title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-12-24
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-12-24

Next game at CGY on Tuesday 27 December 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is who is getting a real chance to play and who isn't, and whether the ones getting chances are earning them.

**Chlup** at 35 games, 20.5 MPG, 28 points on the second line. Full opportunity, producing at 0.80 a night. Nothing to fix. **Nash** mirrors it: 35 games, 15.0 MPG, 21 points. Both are getting what they've earned. **Chistov** 35 games, 20.2 MPG, 24 points on the first line. Same answer.

**Klesla** 35 games, 25.9 MPG, 16 points on the top pair. Full opportunity at 23. Earning every shift.

**Alexeev** is the one that needs correcting. My December 20th note flagged his rate at 0.40, below the 0.45 floor. He's now at 14 points in 28 games, which is 0.50. Two multi-point games pulled the season rate back above the threshold. The breach self-corrected. He stays on the third line at 10.5 MPG. No change.

**Gardener** at POTE 98 has zero points in 23 games on 3.6 MPG. That's the starkest case on the roster. The scratch recommendation stands and should be made permanent. Those minutes are wasted on a player who cannot produce at the NHL level today, and they should go to Spacek.

**Colaiacovo** is 3 points in 25 games at 0.12 a night. POTE 99 again with nothing to show. The scratch holds. He is not earning a spot in any lineup.

**Spezza** at 22 with POTE 99 is in 26 games at 5.4 MPG and 0.19 points per game. **Upshall** is the same story: 26 games, 6.2 MPG, 0.23 points per game, POTE 99. Both are being given spot duty that isn't enough to develop and neither is producing enough to earn more. This is the pattern I flagged in October and it's confirmed: the system buries young forwards in garbage minutes and the production dies. At 22 both are past the age where spot minutes help.

**Spacek** at 20 is the best young option for real ice. Four points in 9 games is 0.44 per game on 6.3 MPG. He's outproducing Gardener, Colaiacovo, Spezza and Upshall by a wide margin per minute. He should have a regular spot on the fourth line or better.

**Gaborik** at 23 has 8 points in 17 games at 22.6 MPG when he plays. He's only in 49% of games. No injuries showing. At his age and with the ice time he commands when dressed, in-and-out status is the wrong use of a 23-year-old. He should be dressing every night.

**Stahle** at 21 with 4 points in 18 games on 12.5 MPG is middling. POTE 96 but 0.22 points per game as a defenceman getting third-pair duty. Not a screaming case either direction. **Eminger** at 22 is only in 9 games but getting 19.4 MPG when he plays, 0.44 per game. His availability is the issue, not his quality.

## Development trends

The question this phase answers is who is actually improving and who is stalling despite getting games, and it matters now because we are 35 games deep and the development window for this season is closing fast.

**Chlup** at 19 is the one whose trend changes plans. 0.79 pts/g on 20.9 MPG after 35 games. He came in at 1.00 in 1 game and has settled into a real number, which is what you want to see: a 19-year-old centring a line and holding 0.79. My April note said he belongs on the first line permanently. The numbers since October confirm it. He should not be sharing first-line centre with anyone.

**Stahle** at 21 is the other quiet riser. Minutes doubled from 6.0 to 12.9 MPG, and his rate went from 0 to 0.24 over 18 games. Still small sample, but the direction is right and he is the only young D producing something. He is the natural replacement for Colaiacovo's minutes.

**Gaborik** at 23 is back. 0.47 pts/g in 17 games at 22.6 MPG. He missed the opening window entirely (0 GP at the first save) and has come in swinging. At 23 with that rate on top-six minutes, he is the winger this team has been looking for.

**Alexeev** at 23 is below the floor I set on November 17th. 0.44 over 28 games at 10.7 MPG, against my 0.45 minimum. The threshold has been breached. He is not developing at this ice time and his minutes should go to Stahle or another young body.

**Colaiacovo** at 22 is 0.12 pts/g over 25 games. Zero goals, 12.6 MPG. I recommended scratching him on November 27th and the numbers since then have gone the wrong way. He is below replacement by a wide margin.

**The depth collapse is confirmed.** Gardener is 0.00 in 23 games. Spacek fell from 1.00 to 0.38 with minutes dropping from 17 to 5. Upshall went 1.00 to 0.20, 16 MPG to 5.8. Spezza is 0.19 at 5.4 MPG. Four young forwards who started with real ice and got nothing from it. The systemic pattern I flagged in October holds for every one of them.

**Jackman** at 24 is at 0.62 pts/g over 35 games, down from 1.00 in the opener. My sell trigger is 0.55. He is 0.07 above it and the trend is downward. If he crosses it before the trade deadline he goes back on the sell list.

**Mogilny** at 36 is 0.82 pts/g on 22.9 MPG. That is outstanding production at his age, but 22.9 minutes a night at 36 is a workload question the GM should be thinking about for the stretch run. **Sundin** is the same problem: 0.76 at 34 on 23.4 MPG. Both are carrying this team. Neither shows decline yet.

**McCabe** at 30 is 0.30 over 10 games, well below the 0.60 threshold I set in March for keeping him off the sell list. He goes back on it.

**No grades moved on the card for anyone in this window.** Every trend I am reading is in production and ice time, not in the rating itself.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy. A winning streak is lifting morale across the board — nearly every player is at 97 and climbing, and the few below that are rising too. No one is in a hole that requires a line change to fix.

**Richards** sits at morale 87 on 12.1 MPG. At his calibre he expects around 17, so he is five minutes short every night. His morale is recovering (+5 from the October baseline) because the team is winning, but the structural gap I flagged in October is still there and the GM has chosen not to close it. I will note it and leave it. If the streak breaks, he is the first forward whose grade will slip by a point on every line.

**Lundmark** is in the same spot: morale 87, 7.4 MPG, well under band at his rating. The GM gave that ice to younger bodies deliberately. No action from me.

**Luongo** at 82 and climbing nine points is the wins doing their job. He is the starter, plays 60 minutes, and there is nothing a line change fixes here. If the room keeps winning he reaches the 90s within two or three saves.

**Spezza** at 82 on 5.4 MPG is below band but the GM is developing him in a reduced role. His morale is up five from baseline, so the current arrangement is not hurting him yet.

No one else in the lineup is under their band with declining morale. The scratched veterans (Tucker, Abid, Roberts, Wallin) are all above 89 and climbing on team results.

## Role composition

Are our units built for their jobs, and do we have enough bodies to fill them? The faceoff gap on L4 and Nash's absence from both penalty-kill units are the two things that need attention before Tuesday.

**L1 and L2** are fine. Sundin (faceoffs 95, clutch 99, playmaking 96) centres a line that can score, check, and win draws. Jackman at 92 checking gives L1 an enforcer who can also produce. Chlup at 80 faceoffs anchors L2 draws. No changes.

**K1** is our strongest unit as a role group: checking mean 80, best 94, anchored by Jackman 92 and McCabe 83. Built correctly.

**K2** has a checking mean of 74. Sundin, Kaberle, Richards, Klesla are a scoring unit asked to kill. **Nash** sits at 82 checking and is on neither PK unit. That's a deployment miss. Moving Nash onto K2 in place of one of the four would raise the checking mean toward 78 and give the second kill a body who actually wants to block shots. Chemistry cost is low because Nash's linemates on L2 (Chlup, Kaberle, Fischer, Afinogenov) stay intact.

**L4** is the structural problem: faceoff mean 54, best 57. Spacek, Koltsov, Upshall collectively lose almost every draw. Koltsov's 99 speed and 85 checking are useful on a 4th line against opposing 4th lines, but the faceoff cost is real. The only faceoff-capable centre we have not already committed is **Wallin** at 88 draws and 78 OVR, currently a healthy scratch. He's the answer if we want it, but at 78 he's a downgrade in every other dimension. This is a roster gap: we have no fourth-line centre who both checks and wins draws.

**Alexeev** remains on L3 at 0.40 pts/g over 26 games, below the 0.45 floor I set on November 17th. My December 20th note stands: he should come out of the regular rotation and those minutes should go to a younger body. Against CGY (3-11-1 last ten) this is a night we can afford to make that change.

## Opponent matchup

The question here is whether CGY's Iginla forces a structural change or whether our depth does the job as-is. The answer is no change: we outclass them on three lines, their power play is 11.8%, and their blue line tops out at 79.

**Iginla** is the only player who scares me. 92 OVR, SHPW 97, SPEE 96, ENDU 91, HERO 94. He plays right wing on their first line with Reinprecht (79) at centre and McAmmond (83) on the left. Our L1 (Sundin/Chistov/Mogilny) auto-pairs with Jackman/Klesla, which is the right D pairing against him — Klesla at CHKG 81 and TOUG 80 is our best shot at containing a 97-shot-power winger, and Jackman at CHKG 94 provides the muscle on the back side. Their supporting cast (79, 83) won't beat us.

**CGY's power play** at 17/144 (11.8%) is irrelevant. No need to shuffle penalty-kill units for this opponent. Our own PP at 12/38 (31.6%) against a 79-74 defensive pair in front of Turek (83 OVR, morale 79) should generate.

**Our blue line matchup by auto-pair:** D pair 1 (Jackman/Klesla, OVR 86/87) against their pair 1 (Salo/Regehr, OVR 79/74). D pair 2 (Kaberle/Fischer, 85/84) against their pair 2 (Klee/Leopold, 73/71). D pair 3 (Eminger/McCabe, 82/84) against their pair 3 (Buzek/Ferguson, 71/68). Every pair is a mismatch in our favour.

**Goalie:** Luongo at 95 is the clear start. Check his fatigue icon on game day per the standing order — I can't see streak icons from the lineup screen. If tired, Ouellet at 86 against a 2.30-goal offence is more than enough.

**No change to lines.** This is a quality mismatch across all four lines and three D pairs. Our record (23-7-1, 4.20 GF/G) against their 2.60 GA/G tells the story. Go all out with veterans, win comfortably.

## Owed

The standing job: analyse our defencemen and update who should go at the end of the season. Here's where things sit as of December 24th.

**Jackman** continues to bleed. 22 points in 35 games is a 0.63 rate, down from 0.68 at 25 games and 0.88 at 16. My sell trigger is 0.55. At his current trajectory he crosses it around game 45, which means the deadline is his last chance to fetch a real return at $0.70M x 2. Nothing changed enough to flip him back to sell yet, but the window is closing week by week.

**Klesla** actually improved. 16 points in 35 games is a 0.46 rate, up from 0.40 at 30 games. Still below the 0.55 threshold that would close the sell window, so the case stays: 87 OVR, expiring at $0.90M, a buyer sees the grade and not the rate. Sell window open, slightly less urgent than when he was at 0.29 in late November.

**McCabe** is the new problem. 3 points in 10 games at 16.4 MPG is a 0.30 rate against $3.00M x 3 more years. He's dressed but clearly a 5th or 6th defenceman. At 30 and producing nothing, that contract is dead weight by summer. Trade candidate, though the value may already be too low to get anything back.

**Eminger** looks fine on the scoresheet: 4 points in 9 games, 0.44 rate at 82 OVR. The problem remains $2.20M x 4. Nobody will take four years of that for a 22-year-old with limited sample. No change, keep developing.

**Hainsey** at 77 OVR, 0.37 rate, $1.40M x 5 more years is a long deal for a bottom-pairing defenceman. Not urgent, but when the season ends the question is whether we want five years of a 77 or find something better cheaper.

**St. Jacques** is done. 66 OVR, zero points in 15 games, expiring. Cut.

**Colaiacovo** is still the same disaster. 3 assists in 25 games, zero goals, 12.3 MPG. Not dressed. My permanent-scratch recommendation holds. $1.40M x 3 more years for a 76 OVR player who cannot produce at any level is a summer problem.

What's changed since the last delivery: Jackman's rate fell from 0.68 to 0.63 and is approaching the trigger. Klesla's rate rose from 0.40 to 0.46, softening the sell urgency slightly. No new injuries among the blue line.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-12-22
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-12-22

Toronto 22-7-1, 53 pts after 34 games.

## Role coverage

The one role genuinely thin on active forward bodies is checking: among lined forwards, only Upshall at 80 CHKG clears the threshold, and the two men who would fill that role (Roberts 86, Tucker 83) are both unlined and both heading out (Roberts at 39, Tucker expiring at $1.30M). Everything else the brief flags as a gap is solved by who is already here.

**Toughness is not a gap.** The brief's role table shows zero at 80+, but the current displayed grades say otherwise: Jackman 93, Nash 92, Roberts 90, Tucker 85, Sundin 83, Eminger 83, Upshall 82, Stahle 82, McCabe 82, Klesla 80, Abid 80. Eleven players at 80 or above. The earlier "zero" reading was against stored grades; on the sheet the GM sees today, this club is physical enough.

**Faceoffs** are covered once the coach puts Wallin in. He sits at 88 FACE with 82 TOUG displayed, currently unlined. With Sundin at 95 and Chlup at 80, that gives three centres clearing 80 across four lines. No acquisition needed.

**Gaborik** at 99 displayed overall, 92 playmaking, 98 speed should be in the top six tonight. The coach already recommends this and the numbers support it without qualification. Every game he scratches is production lost on a $11.90M contract.

**Forward checking** is the one target that survives. Upshall at 80 CHKG is the only lined forward at the threshold. Kurka (CAR, LW, 23, 90 CHKG, 88 TOUG displayed, $0.60M expiring) is the clean fix; he upgrades the checking on L2 or L3 without displacing a scorer. Package remains Upshall plus R3. CAR at 16 points with 14 expiring deals has no reason to keep a 23-year-old with an expiring contract when his ceiling is a bottom-six role.

**Defensive depth** is not a gap but a thin edge. Jackman (24, 87 CHKG, 93 TOUG) and Klesla (23, 80 TOUG) are the first pair. Eminger (22, 82 overall, POTE 99) is the next man and projects above where Klesla is today; McCabe (30, 86 CHKG) slides up if needed. The risk is injury depth, not quality. No trade needed before March, but it is the first hole to fill if a blueliner goes down in the playoffs.

## Trajectory

The club is not aging into a cliff on age. It is aging into a cliff on contracts. The roster skews young — 29 of 34 players are 29 or under, only three are 34 or older — and the manual's 5-7 veteran target is met with exactly three (Sundin 34, Mogilny 36, Roberts 39). The structural risk is contractual: eleven players worth $37.40M all expire in July 2009, and one $11.90M contract is producing nothing while it runs through July 2010.

**Gaborik** is the single largest problem on the books. $11.90M per year for five more years through July 2010, $59.50M of total remaining commitment, against 8 points in 17 games as a healthy scratch. At 23 with POTE 90 and 98 speed he still carries trade value, but every scratched game erodes it. Moving him by the March 2006 deadline frees 13.2% of payroll for renewals that matter (Luongo, Chlup, Klesla) and eliminates the dead-money risk entirely. This cannot be renegotiated mid-contract; the only lever is a trade.

**Mogilny and Sundin** carry 54 combined points over 34 games and will be gone or diminished within two seasons. Mogilny (36, $5.50M, 1 year left) is a deadline chip for a pick. Sundin (34, $8.40M, 4 years left) is locked through 2009 but his POTE 60 says his ceiling is set. No player under 25 on the roster is currently producing at a level that absorbs 50+ points of top-end scoring. Chlup (19, 27 pts/34 GP) is the closest, but he's a year away from proving he can carry a first line.

**Luongo and Chlup** both expire July 2006. Luongo at 91 base and $1.60M needs a 5-year renewal the same summer Chlup at POTE 95 and 27 points in 34 games needs one. If either walks, the backup plan is Ouellet (81 base, $0.90M) or a minor-leaguer, which is a step down the club cannot absorb while rebuilding around the young core.

**The 2009 cluster** is 11 simultaneous expirations at $37.40M, including Richards ($6.70M), Chistov ($5.00M), Kaberle ($4.10M), and Nash ($3.90M). If they all hit the market at once, the club faces either a payroll spike to re-sign everyone or a mass exodus. Extending Richards and Chistov in July 2007 (when they'd have 2 years left) breaks the cluster into manageable pieces. Nash is cheapest to extend early at $3.90M.

**Money is not the constraint.** Profit sits at $32.94M on $78.65M revenue despite $89.94M payroll, so the club can afford new deals. The problem is concentration: the largest single contract (Gaborik, $11.90M) buys zero production, while the two players the club most needs to lock (Luongo at $1.60M, Chlup at $2.34M) are expiring for the cheapest rates they will ever accept.

**Draft capital** is thin: one first, one second, one third, all Toronto's own. At 53 points and first place, the draft position will be late, making these picks worth less as trade chips. The R2 is the most liquid piece for a mid-deadline target.

## Calendar

We are 1st in the East at 53 points in 30 games, and the deadline is 87 days away. The answer is buyers, but the buying is funded entirely by the expiring contracts already on our books. We are not spending real draft capital on a rental; we are converting Mogilny, Tucker, Koltsov, and St. Jacques into players we keep.

**Mogilny** is the non-negotiable move. At 90 base, expiring, and $5.50M, he qualifies for the over-80 pick-recovery mechanic. He walks in July if we do nothing. Trade him to a non-contender in March for a pick, save $5.50M, done. The coach notes he is producing 0.81 per game at 36, which makes him attractive to a contender, but we send him to a team that is not chasing us.

**Tucker** is the GM's designated chip (standing order, 2005-03-19). At 30, $1.30M, expiring, he is the lead piece for Heatley from Atlanta. ATL sits at 27 points with three elite expirers they cannot re-sign on a $40.34M payroll. They will deal.

**Heatley** is the primary acquisition target. At 91 base and 22, he is a keeper. Package: Tucker + R1. This is the one deal where spending a first-rounder makes sense because we get a player who anchors the top line for years.

**Savard** fills the coach's faceoff gap. FACE 88, 26 points in 30 games, $1.00M, expiring, same ATL shop. Package: Koltsov ($1.10M, expiring) + St. Jacques ($0.80M, expiring) + R3. ATL may only do one deal with us; if they force a choice, Heatley wins because he is younger and higher-ceiling.

**Bertuzzi** at 94 base is tempting, but he is 30, $2.60M, and a pure rental. The package costs our R2 plus two young players (Spezza at $1.00M expiring, Alexeev whom the coach is dropping). If Heatley and Savard both land, we have three top-six wings already. Drop Bertuzzi unless both ATL deals collapse.

**Luongo** is the summer priority. One year left, 91 base, $1.60M. Without a five-year extension in July he walks and Ouellet at 81 base is the backup. This is urgent but not a December problem.

**Chlup** at 19 and 82 base on $2.34M is a five-year lock. **Klesla** at 23, 78 base, $0.90M is a four-year deal. **Ouellet** at 24, 81 base, gets two years as the backup. None of these require action before July.

The negotiation window opens in late February per the January standing order. Nothing changes between now and then.

## League scan

Toronto are first in the East at 53 points and heading into March as a contender; the league scan answers one question — who across thirty clubs fills the three gaps (top-six wing scoring, forward checking, defensive injury depth) and can realistically be bought.

**Bertuzzi** is the clearest prize. 94 base, 44 points in 33 games, $2.60M expiring, 87 CHKG and 83 TOUG. He fills the wing gap, brings the checking Toronto lacks, and VAN at 34 points with 13 expiring deals and $46.36M payroll is the most motivated seller in the league. Package: Spezza + Alexeev + R2, which the Coach has already flagged as non-contributors.

**Naslund** (VAN, LW) is the single highest-scoring player on any seller: 50 points in 33 games at 92 base, $4.40M, contract_years=1 (one year beyond this season, so not a pure rental). He has 90 SPEE, 92 SHPW, 94 ACCU — a complete winger. VAN might want a second package because they're rebuilding wholesale, but at 1 year left they will eventually move him. Worth approaching as a companion to the Bertuzzi deal.

**Heatley** (ATL, RW) is 22 years old, 91 base, 36 points in 32 games, 97 SHPW, 98 SPEE, $1.10M expiring, POTE 86. He fills the wing gap AND brings youth — he would carry the first line for a decade after Sundin and Mogilny are gone. ATL at 27 points with $40.34M league-lowest payroll and six expirers cannot re-sign him. Package: Tucker + R1.

**Kurka** (CAR, LW) is the definitive checking fix. 94 CHKG, 92 TOUG, 93 SPEE, 25 points in 34 games, $0.60M expiring, 78 base. He is not just a grinder — he produces. CAR at 40 points with 14 expiring deals and $63.79M payroll must shed salary. Package: Upshall + R3. Upshall is the only lined forward at 80 CHKG; Kurka replaces him AND raises the ceiling.

**Jovanovski** (VAN, D) is 89 base, 92 CHKG, 91 TOUG, $2.30M, one year remaining. He is the only blueliner on a seller above 90 on both checking and toughness. The Coach's first-pair depth gap is real, and Jovanovski closes it. Package from the November note was Klesla + R1, but Klesla is the man being backed up — that doesn't work. Better: a forward body (Spacek, if the Coach won't commit, or a depth D prospect) plus R1. VAN at 34 points will take bodies over a backup goalie.

**Vasicek** (CAR, C) is 82 base, FACE 80, 81 CHKG, 88 SPEE, 23 points in 34 games, $0.40M expiring, 25 years old, POTE 87. Centre depth at the cheapest salary in the league. If Kurka goes to CAR for Upshall + R3, Vasicek needs a separate package — Koltsov + a late pick would do it. PHX at 28 points with 9 expiring also holds **Konowalchuk** (85 base, 86 CHKG, 18pts/34GP, $1.50M) as an alternative two-way winger if Bertuzzi is unavailable.

**Savard** (ATL, C) is 79 base, FACE 89, 29 points in 32 games, $1.00M expiring. A better faceoff centre than Wallin at 88. The same ATL logic that opens Heatley opens him; if Tucker + R1 goes for Heatley, a second smaller package (Koltsov + R3) could land Savard. He and Vasicek address the same gap, so choose one.

**Hartnell** (BUF, LW) at 79 base, 92 CHKG, 91 TOUG, POTE 95, 93 SPEE, $1.10M expiring is the development option. He is 23 and his ceiling is high, but his 10 points in 26 games means he is not a March plug. Better as a summer target if BUF re-signs and then trades him, or at the deadline if nothing better emerges.

**What I would not chase:** Forsberg ($9.90M, COL, 35pts/32GP), Kariya ($10.11M, COL, 35pts/32GP), Alfredsson ($11.40M, OTT, 29pts/31GP). COL at 36 points with 7 expiring might move them, but the salaries are too large for a deadline rental when Bertuzzi gives 94 base at $2.60M. **Komisarek** (MTL) appears at 29pts/33GP in this scan but his base is 77 and the December tracking flagged a production collapse; his season total is inflated by a heater on inflated displayed grades. I would not build around him.

## Trade construction

Can we convert Coach-flagged surplus and a late first-round pick into the top-six wing and checking this roster lacks, before the March deadline?

**Bertuzzi** (VAN, LW, 94 base, 44pts/33GP, $2.60M expiring) fills wing scoring and checking in one move. Give Spezza ($1.00M, POTE 99, 5pts/26GP), Alexeev ($1.50M, POTE 94, 12pts/27GP), and our 2nd-rounder. Both are Coach-flagged non-contributors. VAN at 34 points with 13 expiring deals and $46.36M payroll must shed money they lose in July regardless. They get a POTE 99 centre to develop with real minutes and a 23-year-old winger at 0.44 pts/g. Payroll net: +$0.10M. Acceptance uncertain, but VAN's motivation is the highest of any seller.

**Heatley** (ATL, RW, 22, 91 base, 36pts/32GP, $1.10M expiring, 98 SPEE, 97 SHPW) is a decade-long right wing if we re-sign him in July. Give Tucker ($1.30M, 30, 0 GP, CHKG 92) and our 1st-rounder. These use entirely different assets from Bertuzzi; both deals can close simultaneously. ATL at 27 points, $40.34M league-lowest payroll, six expirers including Heatley, Kovalchuk, and Savard, cannot re-sign any of them. Tucker kills penalties for 30 games; the late 1st-rounder is a lottery ticket for a rebuilding club. Payroll net: -$0.20M.

**Sequencing:** if Bertuzzi lands, his 87 CHKG replaces the need for Kurka (whose availability is uncertain per the November tracking). If Heatley lands too, Mogilny (36, 90 base, $5.50M expiring, 28pts/34GP) becomes a pick-recovery candidate at the March deadline, but only once his production is replaced. Do not trigger that until the wing is filled.

**Do nothing if neither deal closes.** At 53 points and first in the East, the roster's 26-28-27 points from Sundin, Mogilny, and Chlup provide enough scoring. Roberts at 86 CHKG exists if healthy, narrowing the checking gap to one body. Tucker's $1.30M on zero games is dead money but he is 30 at 79 POTE and hard to move. A bad deal is worse than no deal when you lead your conference.

## Owed

**The question this phase answers:** The goalie trade window task from January 2005 — is it still live, and what does it say now?

**Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window** — This task is complete and obsolete. Luongo is on our roster at 95 overall, 16 games played, $1.60M, 1 year remaining. He was acquired during the January-to-February 2005 window the GM set, which is the entire point of the monitoring task. The GM then closed all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19 with the standing order "Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks." That order was never reversed. The February 2005 deadline passed nine months ago.

**DiPietro** sits at 86 overall, 27 GP, $1.10M, 0 years remaining on NYI. He is expiring and could theoretically be available at the March deadline. But we have Luongo at 95 and Belfour staying as our two 90+ goalies through the playoffs per the GM's March decision. There is no roster need DiPietro fills that justifies draft capital or a roster piece, and the GM's standing order is to keep the goalie situation as-is.

**What is live now instead:** Luongo's renewal. He has 1 year left at $1.60M and walks in July 2006 without a new deal. The backup behind him is Ouellet at 81 base. That is the next question on goalies, and it is a renewal task, not a trade-monitoring one.

No action needed on the original task. It is closed.

# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-12-22

Next game vs ATL on Friday 23 December 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question: which young players have earned more games than they're getting, and which are being carried beyond what they've earned?

**Gaborik** is the clearest case of a player being wasted. 22 years old, 17 games played out of 34, 22.6 MPG when he does play, 8 points (0.47/g). He outproduces Upshall (0.24/g, 6.0 MPG) by double and gets nearly four times the ice when dressed. At POTE 90 he's not the highest ceiling in the group, but his actual rate puts him ahead of both other RWs competing for those minutes. He should be in the lineup tonight.

**Eminger** is an inconsistency I own. 8 games, 19.6 MPG, 4 points (0.50/g). When he plays, he's top-pair. That's not a plan — either dress him every night at that role or move him. At 22 with POTE 99, the development case for playing him is strong, but the prior sell recommendation from March was based on a sliding rate in a full season's sample, not this truncated one.

**Alexeev** sits at 12 points in 27 games (0.44/g), one point above the 0.45 floor I set on November 17th. He hasn't breached it cleanly this week, so the prior scratch recommendation doesn't renew yet. One more game without a point and it does.

**Spacek** at 20 has 8 games, 5.9 MPG, and 4 points (0.50/g). Small sample, but he's the youngest body on the roster getting almost no chance to show anything. No obvious slot — Chlup is the only centre with real minutes — but the development case is real.

**No change on Chlup, Nash, Chistov, or Klesla.** All four are at 100% share with production that justifies every minute. **Gardener stays out** — 0 points in 23 games, the GM took that call on December 8th and it's correct. **Spezza, Colaiacovo, and Stahle stay out** — production rates of 0.19, 0.12, and 0.22 respectively don't earn a spot.

## Development trends

The question here is whether anyone's trajectory has changed enough that the GM needs to shift a decision — either give someone more, or start planning around a decline that's now confirmed.

**Chlup** 0.79 at 21.2 MPG at 19. His rate looks down from the 1.00 at 1 game, but that's noise from a one-game sample. The real story is his minutes went from 6 to 21.2 — he's tripled his role and is still producing 0.79. That's the opposite of a stall. No action.

**Gaborik** at 0.47 pts/g over 17 games on 22.6 MPG. This is new and it's a problem. He's getting top-six minutes and producing at a third-line rate. At 23, the expected direction is up, and instead he's below the 0.60 floor I'd want from a winger on 22+ minutes. This is the same shape as the Afinogenov and Richards pattern: flat or rising minutes, falling production. I'd flag it now and watch through January. If he's still under 0.50 at 30 games, the system-fit question applies to him too.

**Jackman** at 0.64 over 34 games, down from 0.68 at 25 games on December 4th. My sell trigger is 0.55. He's 0.09 above it and losing roughly 0.01 per three games. If this slope holds he crosses by mid-January. I'm not calling the trade yet, but the GM should know the window is narrowing and a call is coming within two weeks.

**Klesla** recovered again — 0.45 over 34 games, up from 0.40 at 30 games. The sell window is still wide: 87 OVR, $0.90M expiring, a buyer sees the grade and not the modest rate. Nothing has changed that would make me keep him.

**Richards** at 0.58 over 34 games on 11.8 MPG. The structural decline is now confirmed across three seasons and a full year of data at age 25. He is no longer a top-six centre by output. I'd slot him down permanently and give those minutes to Chlup or another young centre. Reason class: trajectory.

**McCabe** at 0.22 over 9 games since the October save, 15.4 MPG. My March note flagged him in sell territory at 0.45; he's now well below it. At 30 and expiring, he's a rental at best and the rate makes even that a stretch. Planning should assume he's gone in July unless a deadline buyer takes the contract.

**Sundin** 0.79 at 23.3 MPG, age 34. **Mogilny** 0.85 at 23.0 MPG, age 36. Both are carrying the team and both are producing at rates well above their age curves. The GM should build around these two staying at this level; planning around a decline that hasn't materialised would be premature.

**Colaiacovo** 0.12 over 25 games on 12.6 MPG, zero goals. No improvement since the November scratch recommendation. The young-forward-minutes-collapse pattern has claimed him too. If he doesn't move, the development value of 12 MPG at 0.12 is negative — another body would produce more.

**Alexeev** at 0.38 over 27 games. My floor was 0.45; he's now below it and has been for two activations. The minutes belong elsewhere.

**Spezza, Upshall, Gardener, Spacek** — all below 0.43 on under 6 MPG. The season is a write-off for each. Next camp is the only lever, as previously noted.

**Fischer** at 0.67 over 7 games on 21.0 MPG at 25. The GM's instinct is right: he's a keeper. That rate at that ice time at that age is a top-pair D-man emerging.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy. Every regular sits at 95 or above with positive momentum, and the earlier dips from late December have reversed.

**Richards** is the one watch item. He sits at 84 morale on 11.9 minutes a night centring the third line, with 19 points in 34 games. If his grade is 80-plus, his band expects 17 minutes; he is five short. This has been flagged since October. He has climbed from 78 to 84 without any structural change, meaning the winning is doing the work. If the room keeps winning he clears the penalty zone naturally; if it stalls he drops back into the 70s and costs us a point on every grade. The fix remains the same one I filed on December 8th: move him to centre the second line and shift Chlup down to third. The GM has not acted on it and the urgency has eased.

**Luongo** at 82 is results-driven, not minutes-driven. He has started 16 of our 34 games at 60 minutes a night, which is a full workload for a backup sharing the crease. No line change moves him. The GM's fix is wins.

Everyone else in the 97 group (Sundin, Mogilny, Jackman, Klesla, Chlup, Nash, Chistov, Afinogenov, Kaberle, Fischer) has climbed 3 to 8 points in the last save and is showing no concern.

## Role composition

**Tucker and Roberts are both healthy scratches while Spacek plays L4 at checking 57.** That's the role audit failure this activation: the GM named Tucker "our checking guy" back in January, and he sits at 89 checking, 85 toughness, 90 morale. Roberts at 88 checking, 90 toughness, 85 OVR is the same story. Meanwhile Spacek on L4 carries checking 57 and toughness 50, producing 4 points in 8 games at 5.9 minutes a night. That's the single most impactful arrangement problem on the sheet.

**L4** currently runs checking 65 mean: Spacek 57, Koltsov around 53, Upshall 85. Swapping Spacek for Tucker lifts the line's checking mean from 65 to about 76, and gives Koltsov and Upshall a partner who can actually forecheck. One player changes; chemistry cost is minimal because L4 is three forwards in an energy role, not a scoring unit that has developed timing.

**K2** (Sundin, Kaberle, Richards, Klesla) sits at checking 74 mean. Tucker doubling onto the second kill and taking Richards' slot raises it noticeably: Tucker 89 versus Richards 78, the weakest of the four. Richards still keeps P1 and L3, so his ice time doesn't collapse.

**L3** carries Alexeev at checking 69, toughness 54. His rate sits at 12 points in 27 games (0.44), still below the 0.45 floor I set on November 17th, though ticking back up. No forced change tonight — he's producing enough to watch one more week rather than pull him mid-rotation.

**Power play units** are clean. P1 scores 90 mean, 99 best. P2 scores 88 mean, 96 best. Both have two D and strong playmaking underneath. No arrangement problem there.

**Roster gap:** No structural gap on checking or toughness. We have five skaters at 82+ checking (Jackman 92, Tucker 89, Roberts 88, McCabe 83, Nash 82). The problem is deployment, not personnel.

## Opponent matchup

The question: do we change anything for Atlanta, and the answer is no. This is a mismatch from top to bottom, and our current structure already handles the one thing they have.

**Kovalchuk and Heatley** are the entire argument. 92 and 91 OVR on the same line, both with 99 and 97 shot power, both carrying 99 hero. Their first line also has Savard at centre with 89 faceoffs, which is the only place they might win a draw against us. But our first line (Sundin/Chistov/Mogilny) auto-pairs with our first D pair (Klesla/Jackman), which is exactly where I want our two best defencemen against their two best forwards. No rearrangement helps.

**Their power play is 10 for 122** — 8.2%. Historically, embarrassingly bad. Their penalty kill doesn't matter because they can't generate offence. 2.80 goals per game as a team against our 2.10 allowed. Luongo will barely be tested unless we put them on the ice for five minutes of four-on-four.

**Their defence** is Foster 74, Majesky 75, Brule 71, Kaberle 73, Exelby 70, Ratchuk 62. Nobody above 75. Our top six faces the worst defensive group we'll see all month. This is a game where our second and third lines should produce too.

**Deliverable #1 (D-men assessment for end-of-season):** Tonight's matchup is the best test of Klesla and Jackman this week — Kovalchuk and Heatley will be driving the play against them. Klesla at 87 and Jackman at 86 are our sell candidates. If they handle this line cleanly, their card value holds. If they get beaten repeatedly, that's a data point for the GM's deadline review, but tonight is still the right assignment regardless of outcome — I have no better D pair to throw at them.

No change. Lines are set, goalie is Luongo at 95 against a 2.80-offence. Play the game.

## Owed

**Owed item #1 — defencemen analysis and end-of-season sell candidates.**

**Klesla** is the one thing that moved since December 15th. He's put up 3 points in the last 4 games, pushing his season rate from 0.40 back to 0.44 (15 points in 34 games). His card reads 87 OVR at $0.90M expiring. The sell window is at its peak right now — a buyer sees an 87 with a hot streak, and we see a 23-year-old whose season rate is still well below what that grade suggests. My note from November 30th said move before regression; he's proving that right by being hot enough to attract the phone call.

**Jackman** continues his slow bleed. 0.68 at 25 games on December 4th, now 0.65 at 34 games. Still above my 0.55 sell trigger. At 24 years old, 86 OVR, $0.70M x 2, he's cheap with term. No decision change. I'll raise him again if he crosses 0.55.

**Colaiacovo** is unchanged and settled: 0 goals, 3 points in 25 games at 12.3 MPG. 0.12 rate at 76 OVR. He goes at season's end. No young defenceman behind him is being blocked — Eminger (0.50 in 8) and Stahle (0.22 in 18 at 12.5 MPG) are getting their looks above and alongside him.

**Eminger** is the keeper I didn't have on my radar at the start of this run. 3 goals and 1 point of other production in 8 games at 19.6 MPG, 82 OVR, $2.20M x 4. At 22, that's the profile we should be building around on the back end once Kaberle's contract ages.

**St. Jacques** (0 points in 15 games, 66 OVR) remains the deepest scratch. He goes.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-12-20
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-12-20

Toronto 21-7-1, 51 pts after 33 games.

## Role coverage

The question this phase answers: does Toronto have enough bodies at the grades each role demands, and which shortfalls can the coach solve by using his roster versus needing a trade. The answer: two genuine structural gaps (faceoffs and toughness in base grades) plus a checking thinness that Roberts' return fixes, with everything else solvable by better deployment.

**Checking** is the coach's active problem: 5 players at 80+ (Jackman 87, McCabe 86, Tucker 83, Fischer 82, Upshall 80), but Roberts at 86 is out. Two PK units need 8 players above 78. Tucker and Fischer are "not lined" — on the roster, taking no shifts. Dressing them gives the coach K1 as Jackman, McCabe, Tucker, Fischer (all 83+) and K2 anchored by Upshall at 80 plus three men in the 78-79 band who are below the cut shown here but exist. This is a deployment fix, not a trade target.

**Faceoffs** is thin: only Sundin 90 and Wallin 83 carry 80+ base, and Wallin is not lined. Chlup at 75 and Richards at 70 are the third and fourth centre options, both below the threshold where a coach trusts a clutch draw. The Savard package (FACE 88, 26 pts/30 GP, $1.00M expiring, ATL) remains the fix already in motion. No new target needed; this one is being handled.

**Toughness** shows zero at 80+ on base grades — Jackman tops out at 75, McCabe at 73. The GM closed toughness targets in December based on displayed grades showing 11 players at 80+ on a good day. Both readings are true: base toughness is structurally absent, but form modifiers can push multiple players above 80 on any given day. For a seven-game playoff series where form swings, the base-grade void matters, but the GM has made his call and I am not reopening it.

**Scoring, playmaking, speed, clutch, stamina** are all well covered at 9+ players with 80+ grades. No gap.

**Age risk:** Roberts at 39 is the oldest player by five years. If he returns late or re-departs, the checking gap reopens with no internal replacement above 82. Tucker at 30 is expiring and not lined — he is deadline currency per the GM's March 19 standing order. The young defense (Kaberle 27, Jackman 24) carries checking into the future; McCabe at 30 and Tucker at 30 do not. The center group (Chlup 19, Richards 25) is young but weak at the draw.

## Trajectory

The club is not aging into a cliff — the age shape is close to the manual's target — but two structural traps will create one by 2009 if left unaddressed, and Gaborik's $11.90M scratched salary is a hole the club can plug right now.

**Payroll works today, but only because of Gaborik's absence from the ice.** Payroll is $89.94M against $76.98M revenue, and the club is still $34.03M profitable on TV and attendance income. Gaborik alone is $11.90M, 13.2% of the total, for a player at 8 points in 17 games who is a healthy scratch. Remove him and payroll drops to $78.04M, roughly level with revenue. The $34.03M profit is real cushion, but carrying $47.60M of remaining Gaborik dead money for four more years is $47.60M that buys nothing.

**The 2006 renewal summer is small but existential.** Nine contracts expire in one year at $15.44M total. Of those, Luongo ($1.60M, 91 base, POTE 97) and Chlup ($2.34M, POTE 95, 26 points in 33 games) are franchise players who must be locked on 5-6 year deals in the same week in July. Mogilny ($5.50M, 36), Tucker ($1.30M), Koltsov ($1.10M), Spezza ($1.00M), and St. Jacques ($0.80M) all exit before July via deadline trade or release, which is the right outcome. That leaves Luongo, Chlup, Klesla ($0.90M, POTE 97), and Ouellet ($0.90M) to re-sign. The cost of failing on Luongo or Chlup is the dynasty; the cost of failing on the others is depth.

**The 2009 cluster is the cliff.** Eleven players on four-year deals worth $37.40M all expire in July 2009 simultaneously. Richards ($6.70M), Chistov ($5.00M), Nash ($3.90M), Kaberle ($4.10M), and seven others all hit the market the same summer. The manual warns exactly against this: "they all come up for re-signing at the same time." If Chistov (POTE 95, age 22 now) and Nash (POTE 95, age 21) have breakout seasons by 2009, their asking prices will be enormous and Toronto faces eleven simultaneous negotiations. The fix is early extensions starting July 2007: break the cluster by moving Richards, Chistov, and Nash to new deals two years before expiry, even if the salary bump costs more short-term.

**The 30-33 gap means no bridge generation.** The age shape has 13 at ≤23, 16 at 24-29, then just McCabe (30) and Tucker (30) at 30-33, and three at 34+ (Sundin 34, Mogilny 36, Roberts 39). Those three veterans carry the top-six scoring. By 2008, Mogilny is gone, Sundin is 37, Roberts is 42. The players who must fill those roles (Chistov, Nash, Chlup) will be 25, 24, and 22. The bridge exists in potential, but the POTE-to-production jump from 0.73 pts/g (Chistov's current pace) to top-line production is not guaranteed. The Iginla target (CGY, 27, 93 base, 140 points in 73 games, $6.50M expiring) remains the best way to close the gap without gambling on development.

**Draft capital is thin and about to get thinner.** Three picks, all Toronto originals: R1, R2, R3. At 51 points in 33 games, these will land in the 15-30 range if they make the playoffs, or earlier if they miss. The Heatley package (Tucker + R1 to ATL) commits the only high-value pick. After that, Toronto holds an R2 and an R3 and nothing else. Any further deadline acquisition requires player assets, which the GM has protected since February 2005. The club is one trade away from having no draft ammunition.

**Mogilny is the cleanest March chip.** At 36, $5.50M expiring, 90 base overall, he qualifies for the over-80 pick-recovery mechanic. A 26-point season at his age is still 26 points, and a contender will pay a second or third-round pick for him. That pick is the only way Toronto gets draft capital back after the Heatley trade.

## Calendar

**Are we buyers or sellers at the March deadline, and what happens in July?** We are the best team in the East at 51 points, 21-7-1, first place. We are buyers at the deadline and we have nine expiring contracts to sort before July. The deadline is 89 days away; per the GM's standing order, negotiations do not open until late February. This is the plan, not the execution.

**Mogilny** is the deadline engine. At 36 years old, $5.50M, 90 base, expiring, he clears the over-80 pick-recovery mechanic. He is the highest-value chip on the roster for draft capital and the only way to rebuild a pick inventory that sits at a fourth-rounder and below. He moves by March 19 or walks in July for nothing.

**Tucker** at 30, $1.30M, is the trade sweetener. He is not a pick-recovery asset (need to confirm he's above 80 to use that mechanic, but his primary role is as salary filler in a package). He goes with a first-round pick to Atlanta for Heatley, which is the primary acquisition target.

**Koltsov and St. Jacques** together ($1.90M combined) fund the faceoff-centre package. Savard at ATL (FACE 88, 26pts/30GP, $1.00M expiring) is the current primary target over Sillinger at PHX, because ATL's triple-expiring situation makes them a harder retention problem and therefore more willing to sell.

**Spezza** at 22, $1.00M, 5 points in 26 games on 5.4 MPG is replacement-level per the Coach. He is expiring. Either trade him at the deadline for a late pick or release him in July. Given his low value, a late-round pick is realistic; a release saves nothing because his cap hit is minimal.

**Ouellet** at 24, $0.90M, 81 base is the backup for this season. At renewal he gets a 2-year deal as backup; Luongo is the starter and Ouellet is insurance. He stays.

**Klesla** at 23, $0.90M, 78 base is a young defenceman on an expiring deal. Four years at renewal locks him cheaply. He stays.

**Chlup** at 19, $2.34M, 82 base is the franchise centre-in-waiting. Five years at renewal is the only acceptable answer. He is the anchor of the 2006-09 core.

**Luongo** at 26, $1.60M, 91 base is the single most urgent renewal. One year left as of December. Without a 5-year extension he walks and the backup is Ouellet at 81. This is a July 2006 priority above all others.

The 2009 cluster (11 players, $37.40M, all expiring July 2009) is not a this-summer problem but the extension work starts July 2007 for Richards, Chistov, and Nash to stagger the cliff.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: who across thirty clubs fills the gaps that remain after Heatley and Savard land, using only the assets that survive those two deals. After the ATL packages consume Tucker, Koltsov, St. Jacques, R1, and R3, Toronto holds an R2, Mogilny as a rental chip, and four replacement-level young forwards. Every target below must be affordable within that envelope.

**Bertuzzi** is the biggest fish on the board: 94 base, 43 points in 32 games, $2.60M expiring. VAN at 33 points carries 13 expiring deals and the league-lowest payroll at $46.36M. They will sell him. A 30-year-old expiring is a rental to VAN but a playoff weapon to us. Package: Spezza plus Alexeev plus R2. VAN gets two players under 25 at $2.10M combined and a late pick; they dump $2.60M of expiring salary. Both sides improve.

**Havlat** is the best young player on a seller: 87 base, age 24, $0.90M expiring, 29 points in 30 games at 21.2 MPG. OTT at 27 points with only 4 expiring is less desperate, which makes him harder to pry. But if their only realistic re-signing target is Alfredsson (33, $11.40M), they may prefer moving Havlat for young bodies before his value peaks. Package: Mogilny plus R2 works if OTT wants a goal-scorer; Mogilny at 90 base and $5.50M is too rich for a 27-point club to re-sign, so they'd flip him at the deadline themselves. Lower probability than Bertuzzi.

**Vandermeer** is the cheapest quality player in the league: CHKG 90, TOUG 92, POTE 92, age 25, 31.5 MPG, $0.40M expiring. PHI at 34 points with 9 expiring deals is in sell-mode by March. He fills the checking-defense void the coverage phase identified (zero players above 90 on both grades after Roberts). Package: Upshall plus R2. PHI gets a checking wing at low cost and a pick; they shed $0.40M of nothing. Both sides say yes easily.

**Comrie** at EDM: 87 base, age 25, $1.00M expiring, 29 points in 32 games at 22.2 MPG. EDM at 32 points with $42.95M payroll and 5 expiring is rebuilding. He is a second-line centre with top-six scoring at rookie money. Package: Alexeev plus R2 if Vandermeer doesn't go through; otherwise Alexeev plus a late-round swap. EDM gets a 23-year-old with POTE and a pick.

**Nedorost** at FLA: 75 base but POTE 94, FACE 80, age 23, 25 points in 31 games at 22.5 MPG, $1.00M expiring. FLA at 27 points with 5 expiring will sell. He closes the faceoff gap with youth if Savard falls through. Package: Spacek plus R2. FLA gets a young centre at $0.80M and a pick; they shed $1.00M. Probability is medium because his overall is low enough that FLA may simply waive him rather than trade.

**Smyth** at EDM: 89 base, age 29, $2.50M expiring, 33 points in 32 games. Same club as Comrie but older and pricier. Better short-term than Nedorost, worse long-term. Only pursue if Comrie doesn't go through.

**Not pursuing:** Kovalchuk (ATL, 89 base, 22) is the best available player after Heatley but we have no asset left for him after both ATL packages. Hossa (OTT, 89 base, 26, $2.30M with 1 year) is less likely to be moved because OTT has only 4 expiring and he fits their window. Komisarek's 27 points in 32 games at 31.3 MPG contradicts the December collapse note; MTL at 35 points may keep him.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: what can Toronto actually trade for at the March deadline after the Heatley and Savard packages consume Tucker, R1, Koltsov, St. Jacques, R3, and one of our two remaining picks? The answer is that one R2 and three coach-flagged surplus forwards are the entire remaining war chest, which means one big deal plus the Mogilny pick-recovery is the maximum realistic output.

**Bertuzzi** is the clear top target and the one deal that changes our playoff ceiling. At 94 base with 43 points in 32 games, he slots beside Heatley (91 base) and gives Toronto two 90-plus wingers for a playoff run. VAN at 33 points with 13 expiring deals and the league-lowest payroll at $46.36M is the most motivated seller in the league. Spezza (22, POTE 99, $1.00M expiring) plus Alexeev (23, POTE 94, $1.50M) plus our R2 gives them two high-ceiling bodies and a pick; they dump $2.60M of expiring salary and get $2.50M of young contracts they control. Both sides save money. The cost is that Toronto walks into the 2006 draft with zero picks unless Mogilny recovers one.

**Vandermeer** is the structural fix the coverage phase identified: zero current Toronto players carry 90+ on both CHKG and TOUG at base grades. Vandermeer at CHKG 90, TOUG 92, POTE 92, age 25, and $0.40M expiring is the cheapest quality blueliner in the league. But PHI at 34 points with 9 expiring is right on the playoff line; they may not want to move a 31.5 MPG defenceman in March. Upshall (22, $1.50M, POTE 99, CHKG 87) plus R2 is the package, but the R2 is the same pick Bertuzzi needs. These two are mutually exclusive unless PHI accepts Upshall alone, which is a real possibility given Upshall's 5 points in 24 games and PHI's surplus of young bodies.

**Mogilny** at 90 base, $5.50M expiring, 26 points in 33 games qualifies for the over-80 pick-recovery mechanic. He is the safety valve for all three proposals: if Bertuzzi goes through, Mogilny recovers one draft pick for the summer. If nothing else lands, Mogilny alone is the deadline deal and leaves Toronto with the R2 plus whatever pick comes back.

I would not touch Gaborik at the deadline. $11.90M for five more years with 8 points in 17 games as a healthy scratch means no AI will accept that contract at any price in March. This is a summer problem or no problem.

## Owed

**Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window:** Closed by your own order on 2005-03-19 ("Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks"). Luongo is on our roster at **95 overall**, $1.60M, 15 games played. He is not a target anymore; he is our starter. DiPietro was being tracked as a potential replacement package piece, and that question died with the same order. The only live goalie issue is his renewal with one year remaining (already tracked in the summer-2006 renewal list). This item is delivered as closed.
