# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-12-20

Next game vs STL on Wednesday 21 December 2005.

## Development opportunity

Are the young guys getting the games they've earned, 33 into the season? Most of them are, but two are drifting toward the collapse pattern we've seen before, and one is being jerked around in a way that isn't developing anyone.

**Chlup** at 26 points in 33 games on 20.8 minutes is getting every game and should keep getting them. Same for **Chistov** (24 points, 20.3 MPG, first line), **Nash** (20 points, 15.3 MPG, second line), and **Klesla** (14 points, 26.0 MPG, top pair). These four have no development problem. They're earning the ice they get.

**Alexeev** at 12 points in 26 games on 10.9 MPG is a fair third-line fit. His rate is 0.46, slightly up from my last check at 0.40. He's in and out of the lineup, which is right for his production level. No change.

**Gaborik** is the one I'd flag. When he's dressed he plays 22.6 MPG and he's producing at 0.47 pts/g, better than Alexeev (0.46) and well ahead of Upshall (0.21). But he's only been in the lineup 17 times and is currently scratched. In, heavy role, out, in again — that's not development. Either he's part of the plan and gets a consistent spot, or he isn't and we stop pretending. Tonight against STL (20-6) the go-all-out principle says scratch him if there's a stronger veteran winger. Going forward, the pattern needs to stop.

**Upshall** is at morale 82 on 5.8 MPG and 0.21 pts/g. That's the ice-time-morale bleed: POTE 99 at 22, but production says fourth liner. He'll keep sliding unless either the role changes or we accept the number drops below 80. At 0.21 I can't justify raising his role based on what he's done.

**Spacek** at 7 games and morale 82 is at the start of that same road. 0.43 pts/g in seven games is encouraging but small. If he's part of the centre group for the future, he needs more than seven appearances by February, or he follows Spezza's path to 5 MPG and zero production.

**Spezza** at 0.19 pts/g on 5.4 MPG, currently scratched, is the same pattern already confirmed. Morale 82. I said in March the season was a write-off for him and nothing since has changed that.

The scratched group — Gardener (0 points in 23 games), Colaiacovo (0.12 pts/g), Eminger (0.29 pts/g), Stahle (0.22 pts/g) — are correctly out. They're not earning a spot.

## Development trends

This phase asks who is trending up and who is trending down since mid-October, and the answer changes two offseason plans and confirms one deadline call.

**Chistov** is the breakout nobody pencilled in. 0.69 pts/g over 33 games at 20.7 MPG at 22 years old. He went from a one-game flash to a full top-six season without his grade moving on the card, which means the underlying game caught up to the role. He is a real top-six winger now and the GM should plan a third-line spot as his.

**Chlup** holds at 0.78 over 33 games on 21.2 MPG, close to last season's 0.88. At 19, the trajectory is right. No change needed.

**Alexeev** is at the threshold I set on November 17th: 26 games played, 0.40 pts/g. My rule was "if rate stays below 0.45 the dressing recommendation weakens." It did. He is not getting better at 11.1 MPG, and the gap between him and Chistov (0.69 at 20.7) is now a role gap, not a development gap. I would stop dressing him as a regular and give those minutes to a younger body.

**Richards** is the confirmed problem. 0.53 over 33 games at 11.9 MPG, down from 0.71 last year and 1.08 the year before. Three straight years of decline at 25 on flat or falling ice. This is not a slump. Offseason system-fit review before anyone pencils him top-six again.

**Afinogenov** is walking the same road. 0.62 over 33 at 18.0 MPG, continuing the 1.17→0.73→0.62 slide I flagged last spring. At 26, the pattern matches Richards: the system is not extracting what his card says he has. Both need the same offseason look.

**Spezza** is a write-off this year. 0.19 over 26 games on 5.4 MPG with the highest potential ceiling on the roster. He will not recover this season. Next camp is the only lever.

**Gardener, Spacek, Upshall, Brendl** all show the same minutes-collapse signature. Zero or near-zero production, minutes gutted. Gardener is already scratched per my December 8th call. Spacek at 7 games and 3.0 MPG, Upshall at 24 games and 5.3 MPG, Brendl at 10 games and 3.6 MPG: none are developing because none are playing. The GM should decide before camp whether to re-audition them or release.

**Mogilny at 36** is producing 0.81 over 33 games on 23.1 MPG. I have no explanation for it. I have a warning: plan for the decline next year, because 0.81 at 36 is not repeatable. Pair with **Sundin at 34** who is at 0.75 on 23.5 MPG, holding up better but with a shorter runway.

**Roberts at 39** is at 0.29 on 13.7 MPG over 8 games. Natural. No intervention needed.

## Morale watch

The question this phase answers is who needs more or less of the game to keep his morale right before tomorrow's game against STL. The room needs almost nothing: every regular is at 90 or better and the average is 93.

**Richards** is at 84, the lowest of the regulars, on 11.9 minutes a night in 33 games with 17 points from the third line. He is the one regular with a minutes case, and the gap to the 90 line is real. The clean fix is a top-six shift, but that is a bigger intervention, so I would give the third line two or three more minutes a night and lift him without breaking the line.

**Upshall** (82, 24 games, 5.8 minutes), **Spezza** (82, 26 games, 5.4), **Gardener** (82, 23 games, 3.6, no points) and **Spacek** (82, 7 games, 5.0) all sit 8 points under the line. That is the cost of the development rotation, one point off every grade, not something a line change should paper over. **Brendl** at 81 on 3.9 minutes for 10 games is the same story and the lowest number on the sheet.

**Luongo** is at 82, the only man who plays a lot under 90, against **Ouellet** at 97. A goalie's number moves on starts, so that one evens out only if he plays, and that belongs to tomorrow's matchup call, not to this.

**Klesla** (26.0 minutes) and **Jackman** (25.3) are carrying the biggest loads in the room and sit at 97 each. Both are over what a top defenceman expects and neither is showing strain on this sheet. No change.

On duty #1, the end-of-season defence list: no update from the morale sheet alone. Colaiacovo (25 games, 3 points), St. Jacques (15 games, 0 points) and Eminger (7 games, 2 points, the inflated deal) stay on it; the rest are keepers.

## Role composition

The role composition question for tonight: can every unit do what it's asked to do against a 20-6 STL club, or do we have a structural hole the game will expose?

**L4 faceoffs** are the worst unit stat on the board: mean 53, best 57. Against a quality opponent with capable centres, that line will lose draws in their own end all night. Wallin at 88 faceoffs is a healthy scratch. The maximize-quality principle applies to STL — 20-6 is the same class of opponent as Washington was. Reinstating him fixes the worst number on the sheet.

**Wallin** to center L4 costs nothing in chemistry. L4 has no established combo worth protecting — Spacek, Koltsov and Upshall are depth. One swap for one swap, and the faceoff mean jumps from 53 to roughly 67 on that unit.

**L4 checking** (mean 65, best 85) is also the weakest checking unit. Upshall or Koltsov is doing the checking work at best 85, but the unit mean is too low to be a reliable shutdown group. This is partly a roster depth issue — we have Jackman 92, McCabe 83, Nash 82, Roberts 84 (scratched). Four guys above 80 checking, but two of them are on L1 and L2 where they're needed for offense. There is no fifth option.

**K2 penalty kill** uses Sundin, Richards, Klesla and Kaberle — your top centre, best playmaker, top scoring defenceman, and best-stamina defenceman. Checking mean 74 is acceptable, but the opportunity cost is real: two top-six forwards on a PK unit when K1 (checking 80) should be absorbing most of the work. I would not move pieces without knowing the K1/K2 minute split, but if K2 is going out often, this is a misallocation of your best players.

**P1 and P2** are both loaded. P1 scoring 90/playmaking 88/speed 94, P2 scoring 88/playmaking 86/speed 91. No change.

**Roster gap, defensive depth**: Jackman and Klesla carry 56% of defensive minutes (my October note, likely still holding). Colaiacovo is at 0.14 pts/g over 22 games. Hainsey is scratched. If either Jackman or Klesla goes down, the first pair collapses with no quality replacement. That is not fixable by lineup arrangement — the GM needs to hear it.

## Opponent matchup

The question is whether STL's personnel demand a lineup adjustment, and the answer is no — the auto-pairing gives us favorable matchups on every line and their power play at 11.6% (15/129) means we will live at even strength where we are the better team.

**STL's structure.** They win 2-1 games: 2.60 goals for, 2.30 against. Their entire offence runs through the first line. **Tkachuk** at 88 OVR with 93 shot power and 96 puck control is the one man who can beat us on a single shift. **Weight** feeds him (96 pass, 88 puck), and **Reid** at 99 speed provides the breakaway threat. Their second line is Demitra (81) and Berezin (76) — competent but not dangerous. Third and fourth lines are 69-74 OVR players.

**The auto-pairing works for us.** Our first line (Sundin/Chistov/Mogilny) draws their first pair: Pronger (84) paired with **Sekeras at 73**. That is the soft link. Chistov at 99 speed and 94 accuracy should find him all night. Our second line (Chlup/Nash/Afinogenov) gets Junker (74) and Khavanov (77), both beatable. Our third line (Richards/Lundmark/Alexeev) gets Salvador (71) and Timander (70) — the weakest pair on the ice.

**Pronger** at 84 is the shutdown problem. He carries the first pair, kills penalties (PK1 center-adjacent with Weight), and plays the first PP unit. We cannot avoid him, but Sekeras alongside him means the pair has a gap. Our first line is built for that: Sundin's 95 faceoff wins draws, Chistov's 99 speed exploits transitions, and Mogilny's 93 accuracy finishes.

**Goaltending.** **Johnson** at 82 for STL, **Luongo** at 95 for us. That is a 13-point gap and the single biggest edge we carry. I checked for a fatigue icon and see none flagged. Start Luongo.

**No change to the lines.** The system is right against this opponent. Richards on the third line gets Salvador and Timander — that is a gift, not a mismatch to fix. Our fourth line (Spacek/Koltsov/Upshall) can handle their fourth (Kloucek 73, Nedorost 64, Mayers 70) without help.

## Owed

**Standing job #1 — defenceman review for the STL game (December 21st).**

**Klesla** at 14 points in 33 games is now 0.42 pts/g, up from the 0.40 I reported on the 15th. His 87 OVR and $0.90M expiring contract make his card more attractive than it's been all month. The sell window is wide and getting wider — a buyer sees the grade and the cheap cap hit, not the rate history. This remains the primary deadline move.

**Jackman** continues to bleed. 0.67 pts/g over 33 games, down from 0.68 at 25 and 0.88 at 16. My sell trigger sits at 0.55. He's 0.12 above it and the decline rate has slowed (barely half a point in 8 games), so no action. But the direction is unmistakable. If January pushes him under 0.55, he goes back on the list. At $0.70M x 2 he's cheap enough to ride for now.

**Colaiacovo** at 0 goals and 3 assists in 25 games (0.12 pts/g) on 12.3 MPG is still the weakest regular by a wide margin. My November 27th scratch recommendation was right. $1.40M x 4 makes him hard to move, but he should not be on next year's roster. No change from last report — he's not dressed, just sitting there costing cap.

**Kaberle** at 7 points in 14 games on 21.5 MPG is a keeper per the GM's standing order. **Fischer** at 4 points in 6 games same. Both stay.

**Hainsey** at 7 points in 19 games on 20.9 MPG with $1.40M x 6 is the quiet problem. Good MPG, acceptable rate, but six years at that price for a 77-grade defenceman. Not a sell candidate now, but flagged for offseason.

Nothing structural changed since the 15th. Klesla's slight improvement makes the sell case marginally better, not worse.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-12-19
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-12-19

Toronto 21-7-0, 50 pts after 32 games.

## Role coverage

The question this phase answers: given the roster as it stands today, which roles are genuinely unfillable and which are just mis-coached?

**The coach's Dec 17 changes close four gaps without spending a cent.** Dressing Gaborik (SPEE 98, POTE 92, 23 years old) fills the speed slot the team is wasting on scratch. Dressing Tucker (CHKG 83, age 30) on L4 adds the only available 80+ checker the coach isn't using. Moving Spacek (PASS 84, age 20) to L4 gives playmaking depth. Pulling Sundin off K2 stops wasting a 94-clutch, 92-scoring 34-year-old on penalty-kill shifts where his endurance (92) doesn't matter but his hands do.

**Toughness is the structural hole.** Zero players at 80+ on base grade. Jackman tops the list at 75, Roberts at 73. The Dec 4 finding that "11 players carry 80+ on displayed toughness" is true on good days when form and facilities stack, but it means nobody's *standing* toughness is there. In a playoff series, a cold form day leaves the whole roster under 80. The GM's Dec 25 position that Abid is the single toughness target is already resolved — he's on the roster at 25 with 86 scoring but his base TOUG sits below the top-six cutoff, meaning it's under 70. He's not the answer we thought when we targeted him.

**Faceoffs are thin.** Sundin at 90 is the only reliable draw-taker. Wallin at 83 is on the roster but not lined. Chlup at 75, Richards at 70. No team wins a playoff series without second-and-third-line faceoff wins. This is the Sillinger target from December (FACE 96, PHX, expiring, Koltsov + St. Jacques + R3 package) and it remains valid.

**Durability is thin at 5 players and the top one is 39.** Roberts at 98 is the best, but he's the oldest player on the roster and not lined. If he leaves in July, the next-best is Afinogenov at 95 (age 26), which is fine, but the drop from there is steep.

**Age is the quiet gap.** Mogilny (36), Roberts (39), and Sundin (34) occupy the top three slots on scoring, checking, clutch, and stamina simultaneously. They all expire or are expiring. In July 2006, if Mogilny and Roberts leave, scoring drops from 11 players at 80+ to maybe 7, and checking drops from 6 to 4. The coach's current lineup can work tonight; the 2006-07 roster needs bodies behind these men.

**Goalies are solved.** Luongo at 26, 94 GSH, 1 year left, $1.60M. Ouellet at 24 is a capable backup. Task #2 is closed per the November finding.

## Trajectory

The age curve is healthy, but the money is not arranged sensibly. Five veterans (Sundin 34, Mogilny 36, Roberts 39, McCabe 30, Tucker 30), thirteen players under 23, sixteen in the 24-29 prime. That is the manual's shape. The cliff here is financial: one contract eating the future and one summer where eleven players hit the market at once.

**Gaborik** at $11.90M per year through July 2010 is 13.2% of payroll on a healthy scratch with 8 points in 17 games. This is not a player problem anymore; it is a balance-sheet problem. He is 23 with POTE 90, which means he still carries trade value right now, but every scratched game erodes it. His price in March will be lower than his price today. The single most important financial move of this dynasty is converting that contract into a player we dress or picks we can redeploy before value evaporates.

**The 2009 cluster** is the structural bomb. Eleven players on four-year deals worth $37.40M all expire July 2009: Richards, Chistov, Nash, Kaberle, Sundin, Afinogenov, Alexeev, Upshall, Colaiacovo, Abid, Wallin. When that summer arrives, we face re-signing all of them simultaneously or watching half walk. The fix starts two years early: in July 2007, extend Richards (age 27, POTE 88), Chistov (age 24, POTE 95), and Nash (age 23, POTE 95) on fresh five-year deals. That removes three of the highest-value players from the cluster and resets their clocks to 2012.

**Scratch payroll** is the quiet leak. Gaborik $11.90M, Roberts $4.90M, Fischer $3.70M, Eminger $2.20M, Colaiacovo $1.40M, Hainsey $1.40M, Wallin $1.40M, Tucker $1.30M, Abid $1.30M, Koltsov $1.10M: $30.80M in scratched-skater contracts, 34% of total payroll. The GM's October question about keeping players to rotate them has a clear answer: Eminger at POTE 99 and $2.20M is worth parking. Gaborik at $11.90M is not.

**Draft capital** is thin. Three picks, all Toronto's own (rounds 1, 2, 3). No extras from the 2005 deadline moves. Any February acquisition beyond the Tucker trade must send one of these picks or a roster body. The GM's standing order to only trade Tucker and the 4th-rounder from 2005 is long since expired for 2006; but the point stands that we have limited ammunition.

**Luongo** at $1.60M with one year left and POTE 97 is the cheapest franchise asset on the roster. He is 26 with his prime ahead. A five-year extension in July 2006 locks him at whatever number the game generates, which at his current salary level should be reasonable. Missing this is the kind of error that costs a cup.



**On Task #2** (Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time for goalie trade window): This task is closed. Luongo was confirmed on Toronto's roster at 94 overall with one year remaining as of the November save, and the December 17 standing order is "goalies are solved, done, do not revisit." No further monitoring is needed until the July 2006 renewal window, which is recommendation two above.

## Calendar

**Are we buyers or sellers at the March 19 deadline, and what happens to the nine expiring contracts in the summer?**

We are buyers. Toronto sit first in the East on 50 points from 28 games, eight clear of ninth-place Montreal, and five of the nine expiring contracts are trade chips rather than renewal candidates. The deadline plan is straightforward: move Mogilny, Tucker, Koltsov, St. Jacques, and Spezza by March 19, and walk into July needing to re-sign only four players.

**Mogilny** is the deadline engine. At 36, $5.50M, 90 base, expiring, he clears the over-80 pick-recovery mechanic and is the single highest-value asset on the roster. Every contender with a hole on the right wing becomes a buyer. Open negotiations in late February per standing order; the target is a first-rounder plus a young player with potential, not a rental.

**Tucker** is the secondary chip. At 30, $1.30M expiring, the Coach wants him on the fourth line as a checker, but his deadline value to Atlanta (Heatley package) or Vancouver (Bertuzzi package) exceeds his value here. He and Mogilny use entirely different assets and can both move.

**Chlup** and **Luongo** are the two non-negotiable renewals in July. Chlup at 19, 82 base, $2.34M is a franchise centre on a 5-year deal. Luongo at 26, 91 base, $1.60M is the number one goalie on a 5-year deal. Neither goes anywhere, neither is a chip.

**Ouellet** at 24, 81 base, $0.90M stays as backup on a 2-year deal. **Klesla** at 23, 78 base, $0.90M stays as young depth on a 4-year deal. Both are cheap, both are still developing, both are not chips.

**Spezza** is the problem child. The Coach reports 0.20 points per game on 5.4 minutes a night over the season. That is the collapse pattern. At 22 and $1.00M with one year left, he is either a late-round pick dump before March 19 or a July release. He is not a renewal candidate.

**Koltsov** (24, $1.10M) and **St. Jacques** (25, $0.80M) are Sillinger-package filler. Neither is a long-term piece; both move at the deadline.

**Draft capital is intact.** Toronto own all five rounds of their own 2006 draft picks (rounds 0 through 4, holder_team = 0 for all). That is a meaningful change from the January 2005 situation when no pick better than a fourth-rounder was available. We can now fund a package with a first-rounder if the right target appears.

The monitoring task on Luongo's availability and DiPietro's development is complete: Luongo is on this roster at $1.60M with one year left, and the renewal is a July action, not a trade.

## League scan

This phase answers: who across the league fixes Toronto's toughness, faceoff, and depth-scoring holes, and which of their clubs has a reason to say yes before March?

Three players stand above the rest because they close multiple gaps at once or offer elite production at prices that make no sense for their current clubs.

**Savard** (ATL, C, 79 base, FACE 88, 26pts/30GP, $1.00M expiring, age 28) is the single best value in the league. He closes the faceoff gap and adds top-six scoring simultaneously. ATL at 26 points with six expiring players and $40.34M payroll cannot re-sign him, Heatley, and Kovalchuk. The package is Koltsov plus St. Jacques plus R3, which saves us $0.20M in salary.

**Heatley** (ATL, RW, 91 base, POTE 85, 31pts/30GP, $1.10M expiring, age 24) replaces Mogilny's scoring production at 82% of the cost. ATL has no path keeping all three of their elite expirers. Tucker plus R1 is the asking price. If we get both Heatley and Savard from ATL, we send two separate packages — Tucker plus R1 for Heatley, Koltsov plus St. Jacques plus R3 for Savard — and they do not conflict.

**Jovanovski** (VAN, D, 89 base, TOUG 93, CHKG 94, 10pts/20GP, $2.30M expiring, age 29) is the only player in the league above 90 on both toughness and checking on a club that must shed salary. VAN carries 13 expiring deals on $46.36M payroll at 33 points. They will not re-sign him. The December 1 target holds: Klesla plus R1.

**Hartnell** (BUF, LW, 79 base, POTE 94, TOUG 89, CHKG 92, 10pts/26GP, $1.10M expiring, age 23) fixes toughness AND development simultaneously. A 23-year-old with POTE 94 and TOUG 89 is not a rental — he becomes the core. BUF at 30 points with 5 expiring and $57.55M payroll has little reason to keep a depth-scoring tough wing over their own young core. Alexeev plus R2.

**Hejduk** (COL, RW, 91 base, 34pts/31GP, $2.50M expiring, age 29) is the best scoring-for-salary trade available. COL hold Forsberg ($9.90M, 32 years), Kariya ($10.11M, 31 years), and Hejduk ($2.50M, 29 years) all expiring. They cannot keep all three at $22.5M combined on a 35-point team. Hejduk is the cheapest to shed and still worth 91 overall. The question is whether COL sell at 35 points (13-11-5, five games over .500) or believe they can make a run.

**Naslund** (VAN, LW, 92 base, 48pts/32GP, $4.40M expiring, age 32) leads the league in points with 48 in 32 games (1.50 pts/gp). VAN's 13 expiring deals force them to move at least two of Naslund, Jovanovski, Linden, Morrison, and Ohlund. At 32 he is the same age problem Mogilny is, but his production is twice what Mogilny's will be next year. Only pursue if we are not already getting Jovanovski from VAN.

**Comrie** (EDM, C, 87 base, 29pts/32GP, $1.00M expiring, age 25) is the best young-centre value. 29 points at $1.00M at age 25 with POTE 77. EDM at 32 points (10-14-4, .412) with 5 expiring are rebuilding candidates. The risk is EDM fighting for a wildcard at 32 points until February and then deciding to sell late.

**Allen** (VAN, D, 78 base, TOUG 90, CHKG 84, 11pts/27GP at 22.4 MPG, $0.90M expiring, age 25) is the budget toughness-D if Jovanovski proves too expensive. Young, 78 base, TOUG 90, $0.90M. VAN's salary overload makes him available.

**Yonkman** (WSH, D, 74 base, POTE 88, TOUG 88, 8pts/32GP at 19.5 MPG, $0.60M expiring, age 24) fills the toughness gap at development price. WSH at 23 points (7-18-5) with 5 expiring are the most desperate club in the league alongside LA and CHI. $0.60M at POTE 88 with TOUG 88 is depth-pick currency.

**Daze** (CHI, LW, 89 base, 35pts/32GP, $3.00M expiring, age 30) is a rental scorer at a good price. CHI at 23 points (6-17-7) with 8 expiring are the second-worst team in the league. They must move him. But at 30 with POTE 77 he does not improve — he wins us games in April and leaves in July.

**On Gaborik**: every scratched game erodes his value. He is 8pts/17GP at $11.90M. No team in the league carries a payroll low enough to absorb him without also shedding a player. The realistic path is a 3-way or a rebuild team taking on the deal for a first-round pick plus a depth piece. His price in January is higher than March. The GM should decide in January whether to sell or dress him.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: which acquisitions can we actually construct without selling the core defense the GM protected in February, and which packages do the other sides say yes to? The answer is three deals, ranked by certainty and impact, all executable at the March deadline with players we are already scratching plus the three picks we own.

**Savard is the highest-probability deal in the league.** ATL at 26 points hold three elite expirers (Heatley 91 base, Kovalchuk 89, Savard 79) on $3.20M combined at a $40.34M league-lowest payroll. They cannot re-sign even one. Savard at 26 pts/30 GP with FACE 88 fixes our deepest structural hole. The package uses two players with zero games this season (Koltsov, St. Jacques) plus our third-rounder — no picks or core players touched. ATL gets POTE 94 twins and a pick for a player they will lose for nothing in July.

**Jovanovski closes the structural toughness hole.** Zero players on our roster sit above 80 base TOUG or CHKG. He is at 93 and 94, the only player in the league above 90 on both. VAN at 33 points carry 13 expiring deals; they will not re-sign him at $2.30M. The cost is Alexeev (12 pts/25 GP, POTE 94) plus our second-rounder. Alexeev is the player the coach wants scratched; his value to us is declining with every healthy scratch. VAN gets a 23-year-old with real upside and a pick for a rental they will lose in July.

**Heatley is the biggest scoring upgrade available.** 91 base, 31 pts/30 GP, age 24. He replaces Mogilny's production at 20% of the cost ($1.10M versus $5.50M). The price is Tucker plus our first-rounder. ATL gets a 30-year-old with CHKG 92 to occupy a roster spot their young core is about to fill, plus their most needed currency: draft capital for a 26-point rebuild. The risk is whether ATL's AI values Tucker's CHKG 92 highly enough or sees only a 30-year-old rental.

**The draft-capital decision.** Doing deals 1 and 2 uses our second and third rounders and keeps the first-rounder for June. That is the base plan: it fixes both structural gaps (faceoffs, toughness) without touching picks we need for the 2009-cluster rebuild pipeline. Adding Heatley costs the first-rounder as well, leaving zero picks for June. The GM decides in late February whether to go all three.

## Owed

**#2 (Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window):** This was delivered on 2005-02-07 when Luongo was acquired and confirmed on the roster at 91 base. The GM closed all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19 with "Goalies are solved." The task is closed and the window has passed.

What has changed since then: Luongo's contract dropped to 1 year as of December 2005. At 95 displayed, $1.60M, he walks in July 2006 without a new deal. That is no longer a trade-window question; it is a renewal question, and it sits at the top of the July 2006 list I already carry. DiPietro monitoring is irrelevant because Luongo is here and producing.

No action needed on this item. The next step is the Luongo renewal itself, which belongs in the July 2006 renewal cluster and is already tracked.

# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-12-19

Next game at TB on Monday 19 December 2005.

## Development opportunity

Are our 23-and-under players getting the ice they've earned after 32 games? The answer splits cleanly: four are right where they belong, and five are not.

**Chlup** — 25 points in 32 games at 20.9 MPG. First-line centre at 19 earning every shift. No intervention.

**Chistov** — 24 points in 32 games at 20.1 MPG on the first line. Same story. Earned.

**Nash** — 18 points in 32 games at 15.3 MPG, second line, morale 97. Right role, right minutes for a 21-year-old on a second line.

**Klesla** — 14 points in 32 games at 26.0 MPG. Top pairing, top minutes, earned. His trade value is a separate conversation.

**Gardener** — 0 points in 23 games at 3.6 MPG. My December 8th scratch recommendation was taken but he's still dressed and still accumulating games at these numbers. Zero in 23 is not development; it is a roster spot consumed by a player who cannot make the fourth line produce. He should not be active.

**Spacek** — Morale 76, lowest on the roster. 6 games, 5.8 MPG, 3 points. At 20 with POTE 91, six games in a 32-game sample is not developing anyone. Either he gets 12-plus minutes or he comes out and the morale stops bleeding. The GM scratched him in January to give others space; that window closed months ago.

**Spezza** — 5 points in 26 games at 5.4 MPG, morale 82. The collapse pattern is complete: he's a fourth-line depth man producing at 0.19 pts/g. The POTE 99 means nothing when he's on the ice for three minutes of garbage time. He's either a healthy scratch or he plays 10-plus minutes on the third or fourth line.

**Upshall** — 5 points in 23 games at 6.0 MPG, morale 84. Same story as Spezza. Replacement-level production on the fourth line. Not earning a spot.

**Colaiacovo** — Now scratched, which is right. 3 points in 25 games at 0.12 pts/g. Weakest regular D by a distance. Keep him out.

**Gaborik** — 8 points in 17 games but 22.6 MPG when he plays. That's top-pairing ice at 0.47 pts/g. If he returns, his minutes should cap around 16. Right now he's in and out, which wastes both his stamina and the roster spot.

**Eminger** — 2 points in 7 games, scratched. When he plays he gets 19.9 MPG for 0.29 pts/g. The minutes don't match the production. Keep him out unless someone gets hurt.

**Alexeev** — 12 points in 25 games at 0.48 pts/g on the third line. My November note said reassess at 25 games; if the rate held below 0.45 the dressing recommendation weakens. He's just above it. Borderline but still dressing.

## Development trends

The question this phase answers: who is actually getting better or worse under our current deployment, and does any trend change the GM's roster plans. With no grade changes on any card in this window, everything rests on production and minutes.

**Chlup** is the story going the right way. 0.77 pts/g over 32 games on 21.4 MPG at age 19. The sample grew from 1 game last season to 32, and he held nearly a point a night through October before settling. That is franchise-centre production from a teenager and it confirms the April call. Nothing to change, just protect his role.

**Nash** at 0.55 over 32 games on 15.2 MPG is a steady young winger. No spike, no collapse. He is earning his minutes at 21.

**Gaborik** at 0.47 over 17 games on 22.6 MPG is reasonable for a winger coming off injury time. Small sample but the ice-time trust is there.

**Fischer** at 0.80 in only 6 games on 21.8 MPG is hot but too small a sample to read as a trend. The GM has already ruled him a keeper and there is nothing here to challenge that.

**Richards** is the one that changes the GM's plans. Third consecutive season of decline: 1.08, 0.71, now 0.55, at age 25 on 11.6 MPG. No injury, no role change to explain it. This is a system-fit problem. The offseason review I flagged in April is now mandatory.

**Afinogenov** tells the same story. Was 1.17, then 0.73, now 0.61 over 32 games on 18.1 MPG at age 26. Same age, same pattern: flat or rising minutes, falling rate. If Richards is a fit problem, so is he.

**Spezza** at 0.19 over 26 games on 5.4 MPG is a write-off. POTE 99 and he is playing depth-fourth-line minutes. Camp assignment is the only lever.

**Upshall** at 0.18 over 23 games on 5.5 MPG. Same collapse as Spezza. Same offseason decision.

**Gardener** at 0.00 in 23 games on 3.0 MPG. The scratch recommendation from December 8th was the right call. He played one game after that and scored zero. He is done as a development project this year.

**Alexeev** is at the threshold I set. 0.42 pts/g over 25 games on 10.8 MPG. My note from November said: if the rate stays below 0.45 at 25 games, the dressing recommendation weakens. He is at 0.42 at 25 games. It weakens.

**Colaiacovo** at 0.12 over 25 games on 12.6 MPG. Worse than the 0.14 I flagged in late November. He is the weakest regular D on the roster by a wide margin and has not improved.

**McCabe** at 0.29 over 7 games on 14.1 MPG is well below the 0.60 threshold I set in March for selling. Small sample, but he is at 30 and the rate is not recovering.

**St. Jacques** at 0.00 in 14 games on 11.6 MPG. Zero points from a 25-year-old defenceman on real minutes. He is a healthy scratch candidate at season's end if nothing changes.

**Klesla** at 0.45 over 32 games on 25.5 MPG sits above the 0.30 sell floor. The window is open but not urgent. Jackman at 0.65 is above the 0.55 trigger. Both stay for now.

**Sundin** at 0.77 and **Mogilny** at 0.81 over 32 games each are producing at 34 and 36. No decline to flag. They are doing the job.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy: average 93, and every regular in the top nine is at 97. The question is whether anyone below that band needs a minutes adjustment that only I control.

**Richards** is the one name worth a look. Morale 84, up from the low of 78 I flagged in October, but still nine points below the room average. He's on the third line getting 11.7 minutes a night with 17 points in 32 games (0.53 pts/g). If his calibre sits in the 80s band he expects around 17, so the deficit persists at five minutes. However, the structural decline finding says his rate has fallen three seasons running (1.08, 0.71, 0.54), and Chlup is outscoring him at 0.78 pts/g on the second line in 20.9 minutes. Moving Richards up means sitting the better player and breaking a working line. His morale is recovering on its own as the team wins. No change.

**Luongo** at 82 is structural: he's the backup, he's started 14, and no line change gives him starts. That's the GM's roster call, not mine.

**Spacek** (76) and **Brendl** (81) are scratched by design in the development rotation. Their morale is what you'd expect for healthy players not playing. Already the GM's choice, already established.

**Spezza** (82) and **Upshall** (84) are fourth-liners getting 5-6 minutes. At their calibre that's roughly the 7-10 MPG band, slightly under, but both are producing modest points (Spezza 5 in 26, Upshall 5 in 23) and neither is slipping further.

No change. The room is right.

## Role composition

The question is whether each unit is staffed for its job, and whether we have enough bodies to cover every role the season demands. The answer tonight is mostly yes, with one structural gap that matters beyond this game.

**L1 and L2 are built right.** Sundin and Mogilny carry the scoring (94 and 92) while Jackman (92 checking, 78 toughness) does the dirty work at the blue line. Chistov at 93 playmaking links them. L2 has Nash (82 checking) for the grit and Chlup (80 faceoffs) to win draws, with Kaberle and Afinogenov generating. These are role-appropriate and I am not touching them.

**L3 has Richards at 93 playmaking doing third-line work.** I recommended moving him up on December 8th and you did not take it. I accept the call, chemistry is real, and Chlup's 80 faceoffs at the dot on L2 is not nothing. No re-fight tonight.

**PK2 is the structural problem.** Sundin, Kaberle, Richards, Klesla carry a checking mean of 74. Jackman (92) and McCabe (83) are both locked into PK1, so PK2 has no elite checker at all. Tonight against Tampa Bay's 13.4% PP (18 for 134) that risk is negligible. But against a team with a 20%+ PP we have no answer on the second unit.

**Roberts at 85 OVR, 88 checking, 90 toughness, 89 morale is the fix and he is sitting out.** If this is a development rotation for the young guys, fine. But he is the second-best checker on the roster and the only player who pairs with McCabe on PK2 to bring the checking mean above 80 without pulling Jackman out of PK1. When you need a real second PK unit against a strong PP team, he is the man.

**L4 is thin but adequate as a fourth unit.** Checking mean 70, scoring mean 76. That's what a fourth line does. No change needed.

## Opponent matchup

The question is whether to adjust anything for Tampa tonight, and the answer is no: our current structure already mismatches them on every line.

**Lecavalier** is their only real weapon, 86 OVR with 93 speed and 92 shot power. He centers the top line, which means Sundin gets him. Sundin at 92 OVR and 95 faceoff wins every draw against Lecavalier's 62 and out-grades him everywhere it matters. No shutdown assignment needed; Sundin handles him on merit.

**Their defence** is where this game gets decided. Boyle (78) and Malik (74) are their best pair, and after that it drops to Cullimore (72), Tarnstrom (74), Bouillon (70), Lukowich (69). Our first pair Klesla/Jackman at 87 and 86 will eat them alive, and our second pair Kaberle/Safronov at 85 and 68 is a mismatch against Cullimore and Tarnstrom too. The 72-69 range on their third pair means our bottom-six gets quality looks.

**Their penalty kill** is their biggest vulnerability. 18 goals on 134 chances is 13.4%, which is terrible. Our PP at 10/33 is only 30.3% but against a 13% kill, we should convert more than usual. No change to PP personnel needed; Kaberle and McCabe on the second unit against their third pair should produce.

**Khabibulin** at 87 OVR and 85 on all four main grades is the one thing that makes this non-routine. We need our best in net to match, which means Ouellet at 86, not Tellqvist at 73.

**Ouellet** starts. Check his fatigue icon before confirming per the standing order from January.

## Owed

**Standing job #1: defencemen review, who should go at the end of the season.**

**Klesla** is at 14 points in 32 games (0.44 pts/g), up from 0.40 at 30 games when I last checked on December 15th. His 87 OVR and $0.90M expiring make him the top sell before the deadline. The recovery is small but real, and a buyer doesn't see the rate, only the grade and the cheap one-year deal. Window stays open, no change to the recommendation.

**Jackman** sits at 21 points in 32 games (0.66 pts/g), down from 0.68 at 25 games on December 4th. Still well above my 0.55 sell trigger. He keeps. At $0.70M x 2 he's the best value on the blue line.

**Colaiacovo** is the one that hasn't moved and keeps getting worse: 3 points in 25 games (0.12 pts/g), still zero goals. Same case as November 27th when I recommended scratching him. He's on a four-year deal at $1.40M, which means any move needs a partner willing to take that money. Still the weakest regular D by a wide margin, and the case for moving him is only stronger now with more games at zero goals.

**St. Jacques**: 0 points in 14 games, 66 OVR, $0.80M x 1. Let him walk at year end. No reason to re-sign.

**Eminger** and **McCabe** carry heavy deals ($2.20M x 4 and $3.00M x 3 respectively) on low game counts with 0.29 pts/g rates. Not new information since my last review, and the contracts make them hard to move. No change.

**Kaberle** and **Fischer** are keepers by standing order. No change.

Nothing new since December 15th. No injuries to the D group, no rates crossing a trigger, no new sell candidates.

# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-12-17

Toronto 20-7-0, 48 pts after 31 games.

## Role coverage

**Which roles are genuinely thin, and which are only thin because the coach isn't using what he has?** That's the question, and the answer is: almost nothing is missing from this roster, but the deployment is leaving elite talent on the bench.

**The "not lined" problem dwarfs every acquisition target.** Eight players with 80+ grades in at least one role are in no unit at all. Gaborik has 98 speed, 92 scoring, 92 playmaking, and he is sitting out. Fischer brings 89 speed, 82 checking, and 92 durability and is not lined. Roberts at 39 still carries 86 checking, 90 clutch, and 98 durability and is not lined. Koltsov at 92 speed, Spacek at 84 playmaking, Abid at 86 scoring and 90 durability — all out. That is not a roster gap. That is a lineup problem the coach can fix tonight.

**Checking is covered on paper but under-deployed.** Six at 80+ (Jackman 87, Roberts 86, McCabe 86, Tucker 83, Fischer 82, Upshall 80), but only three of those six are lined. Tucker at 83 is the specific player the coach flags for the second penalty kill. Fischer at 82 checking and 89 speed is the other one. Once those two are deployed, checking is adequate.

**Faceoffs are genuinely thin.** Only Sundin (90) and Wallin (83, not lined) are above 80. Chlup at 75 is the next best. Four lines need a faceoff-taker, and having two above 80 across the roster means the third and fourth draws are giveaways. This is the one role that cannot be fixed by reshuffling — there is no one else on the roster to put in the X-slot. The Savard target (FACE 87, 79 base, $1.00M expiring, ATL) and the Vasicek target (FACE 80, 82 overall, $0.40M expiring, CAR) both close this at low cost. Sillinger (FACE 96, PHX) is the premium option if the package works.

**Toughness at base level reads zero at 80+**, with Jackman topping out at 75. But the December 4 finding confirmed 11 players reach 80+ on displayed grades with form and morale applied. The GM has closed toughness targets three separate times. This is not a gap to chase.

**Stamina and durability are adequate now but age-concentrated.** Roberts (98 durability) is 39. Mogilny (91 stamina) is 36. Kaberle at 27 with 97 stamina and 90 clutch is the player who carries these traits into 2009. The young core (Gaborik 23, Chistov 22, Richards 25, Afinogenov 26) need to build durability depth over the next two seasons, but no acquisition is required for 2005-06.

**Scoring, playmaking, speed, and clutch are all covered** with 9 to 25 players at 80+. The issue is that the top names (Mogilny 36, Sundin 34) have a hard expiry window, and the heir (Gaborik) is not playing.

## Trajectory

**No, the club is not aging into a cliff; it is contract-cliffing into 2009, and Gaborik's $11.90M is the hole we are paying into for nothing.** The age curve is healthy (13 players at 23 or under, 16 at 24-29, only 3 at 34+), and profit is $36.23M on $89.94M payroll, so there is no money squeeze tonight. The threats are two specific summers and one contract.

**Gaborik** at $11.90M for 5 more years is $59.50M of future obligation on a player with 8 points in 17 games who sits out 43% of the schedule. At 23 with POTE 90 he still has trade value, but every scratched game erodes it, and the Coach's December 15 report already framed this as "dress him or trade him." He is still scratched on December 17. The Coach's ultimatum and the front office's read converge: trade him by March or he becomes the league's worst dead contract.

**The 2009 cluster** is 11 players carrying $37.40M in contracts that all expire the same July. Richards ($6.70M), Sundin ($8.40M), Chistov ($5.00M), Kaberle ($4.10M), Nash ($3.90M) are the five names whose simultaneous UFA would gut the roster in one offseason. The manual's own warning applies: a roster whose contracts all come up together is a roster that loses its core overnight. The fix is to start signing the young ones on 5-6 year deals in July 2007, three summers early, pushing Richards (then 27), Chistov (24) and Nash (23) past 2009 and shrinking the cluster from 11 to 8.

**July 2006 is the near-term renewal window and it is manageable.** Nine players at $15.44M come due, but most are cheap or leaving anyway. Luongo at $1.60M is the one must-sign; a 97-POTE goalie on that salary is the cheapest insurance on the roster. Chlup at $2.34M needs a 5-6 year extension; 25 points in 31 games at 19 is the kind of player you lock down. Mogilny at $5.50M and 36 should walk; freeing that money pays for both renewals and still leaves surplus. Klesla at $0.90M in 31 games is another cheap keep. The summer is net positive if we are deliberate.

**The 34+ group resolves on its own.** Sundin ($8.40M, 4 years left), Mogilny ($5.50M, 1 year), Roberts ($4.90M, 2 years) carry $18.80M between them. Mogilny walks in 2006, Roberts in 2007, and Sundin's last year lands in 2009 when he is 38. By 2009, the old money is almost entirely off the books, but the young money has clustered right where it should not. The structural problem is the timing collision, not the aging itself.

**Scouting at level 2** is the weakest facility on the sheet, and with 13 players at 23 or under already developed, the next batch of talent arrives through the draft. At three picks (own 1st, 2nd, 3rd), finding late-round value matters more than finding the one good one early. Upgrading scouting costs upgrade points we earn every season, and the draft is still months away.

## Calendar

We are 20-7-0, first in the East, 48 points in 31 games. The deadline is 92 days away on March 19. We are buyers, and the question is which expiring assets fund which upgrades and what the summer renewal list looks like.

**Luongo** is 95 displayed, 91 base, age 26, $1.60M expiring. He is a franchise goalie and the single most important contract on this roster. Sign him to 5 years before anything else. At 26 he is entering his prime; a 5-year deal expires in July 2011, well clear of the 2009 renewal cluster that already holds Richards, Chistov and Nash. This is not a deadline trade target. He stays.

**Mogilny** is 36, $5.50M, 89 displayed, 90 base. He is still producing, but his salary is the largest on the roster by a wide margin and his age means his ceiling is set. He is above 80 and expiring, which means the pick-recovery mechanic works on him: even without a named taker, he can be moved for a draft pick. At the deadline he becomes a chip. Either trade him for a young forward with potential, or let the mechanic pull a pick from him. Either way, $5.50M at 36 does not walk away in July.

**Tucker** is 79 displayed, age 30, $1.30M expiring. He appears in two already-identified deadline packages: Heatley from Atlanta for Tucker plus a first-rounder, and Bertuzzi from Vancouver for Tucker plus a second-round pick. He cannot go to both. The Heatley package is higher-value because Heatley at 91 base is a top-six left wing who changes our scoring profile. Tucker goes to Atlanta.

**Chlup** is 19, 87 displayed, 82 base, $2.34M expiring. He is a first-round talent in his first season. Sign him to 5 years at renewal. A 5-year deal for a 19-year-old is the cheapest way to lock a young centre.

**Klesla** is 23, 87 displayed, 78 base, $0.90M expiring. Young defenceman, still developing. Renew him on 4 years. His base is 78, which means he is likely still climbing; a 4-year deal through July 2010 captures his development without overcommitting.

**Koltsov** is 24, 75 displayed, 68 base, $1.10M expiring. He is already earmarked as a package piece for the Sillinger deal from Phoenix (Koltsov plus St. Jacques plus a third-round pick). Move him in March.

**St. Jacques** is 25, 66 displayed, $0.80M expiring. The coach has him first out at third-pairing D with zero points in 12 games. He is the second half of the Sillinger package. Move him in March.

**Spezza** is 22, 73 displayed, $1.00M expiring. The coach has him in the collapse pattern under 6 MPG with sub-0.21 rates. His trade value is low at 73 overall, but the pick-recovery mechanic requires above 80, so that route is closed. Two options: try to package him in a late-round-pick deal, or release him in July. Do not renew.

**Ouellet** is 24, 86 displayed, 81 base, $0.90M expiring. With Luongo signed long-term and Belfour likely gone after this season (retirement or walk), Ouellet is a cheap backup. If no better goalie materializes through the draft or free agency, renew him on 2 years at $0.90M. If a better option appears, trade him.

**The deadline plan in summary:** three deals, non-overlapping assets. Heatley (Tucker plus R1 to ATL). Sillinger (Koltsov plus St. Jacques plus R3 to PHX). Mogilny moved via the over-80 mechanic or a direct trade for a young asset. Negotiations open late February per the standing order.

**The summer renewal list:** Luongo on 5 years. Chlup on 5 years. Klesla on 4 years. Ouellet on 2 years if he stays. Mogilny, Tucker, Spezza, Koltsov, St. Jacques all gone before July, either via deadline trade or release.

**On the Luongo/DiPietro monitoring task (#2):** Luongo is on our roster at 91 base. He is signed for this season and will be renewed. The monitoring task is complete. DiPietro tracking is no longer relevant to a trade target; he stays a Isles asset.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: which players on selling clubs close our one genuine role gap (faceoffs) and add the scoring depth the Coach's team-wide production decline demands, at a price we can actually pay before March?

The answer: Atlanta, Phoenix, and Ottawa hold four players we want between them, all expiring on clubs with fewer than 30 points. Faceoffs is the only gap that needs a trade; scoring is a question of volume and we have the currency (Tucker, Koltsov, three picks) to address both.

**Heatley** (ATL, RW, 22, 90 overall/91 base, 97 speed, 87 accuracy, POTE 86) is the prize: 31 points in 30 games at $1.10M on a 26-point club that cannot re-sign him. He is the heir to Mogilny's wing, 14 years younger, and costs $1.10M against Mogilny's $5.50M exit. Package: Tucker plus our R1. ATL at $40.34M payroll and 6 expiring deals wants futures, and Tucker's 83 checking gives their rebuild a spine.

**Kovalchuk** (ATL, LW, 91 overall/89 base, 99 speed, 92 accuracy, POTE 86) has 34 points in 30 games, 19 goals, at the same $1.10M. He competes with Heatley for our attention and for ATL's asking price. Kovalchuk is the better scorer tonight; Heatley is the better player in two years (22 versus 23, and his POTE is 86 either way, so the tiebreaker is age). I take Heatley. If ATL will deal both, we take one and let the other go to a different buyer.

**Sillinger** (PHX, C, FACE 96, 87 overall, $1.20M expiring, 8 pts/17 GP from the December tracking) is the faceoff answer. PHX at 26 points with 9 expiring deals and $55.41M payroll cannot keep him. His production is modest but his 96 FACE fixes L3 and L4 draws where Sundin handles L1 and Chlup at 75 handles L2. Package: Koltsov plus St. Jacques plus R3. Koltsov brings 92 speed for their rebuild; St. Jacques is the D-man the Coach says is first out.

**Havlat** (OTT, LW, 86 overall/87 base, 98 speed, POTE 84, $0.90M expiring, 28 pts/28 GP) is the value play nobody has priced. OTT at 25 points with only 4 expiring deals and $59.27M payroll are the least motivated sellers on this board, but 98 speed at $0.90M is cheap insurance if they do move him. FACE 50 and TOUG 69 mean he is a pure winger. Package: Alexeev plus R2, giving OTT speed (Alexeev has 92) and a pick.

**Drury** (BUF, LW, 87 overall/89 base, FACE 85, TOUG 76, CHKG 76, 91 speed, POTE 81, $2.00M expiring, 27 pts/29 GP) is the alternative if Sillinger's package is rejected. BUF at 30 points with only 5 expiring deals are reluctant sellers, and $2.00M is real money. He is a complete player but his FACE 85 only ties Wallin's 83 (who is not lined). I prefer Sillinger's 96 for half the salary.

**Bertuzzi** (VAN, RW, 93 overall/94 base, 42 pts/31 GP, 26 goals, TOUG 85, CHKG 89, $2.60M expiring) has the best season of anyone on this board. But he is 31 with POTE 58 — this is a rental at a rental price. We have scoring from Chistov, Nash, Sundin, Kaberle. His $2.60M and $0.00M in future value do not justify spending a pick on him. Pass.

**Daze** (CHI, LW, $3.00M expiring, FACE 50, TOUG 50, CHKG 80) is a trap. $3.00M for a faceoff specialist who cannot take faceoffs. CHI at 21 points will take almost anything, but so should we, and "anything" here means "not him."

**Marchant** (CBJ, C, FACE 92, 84 overall, $4.88M expiring, 11 pts/15 GP) has the right FACE grade at the wrong price. $4.88M is four times Sillinger's salary for three fewer points per faceoff cycle. CBJ at 34 points with 4 expiring have no urgency. Pass.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: which specific packages do we propose to which clubs, and what do we hand over to get Heatley, Sillinger, and Havlat before the March deadline?

**Heatley from Atlanta** is the headline. He is 90 overall, 91 base, 22 years old, POTE 86, 31 points in 30 games at $1.10M on a 26-point club at $40.34M payroll. They cannot re-sign him, and Tucker at 30 with 92 checking and $1.30M expiring is a rental that helps them develop younger wingers while they tank out the schedule. We give Tucker plus our R1. Payroll effect: we shed $1.30M, take on $1.10M, net saving $0.20M plus we gain a player who is 14 years younger than Mogilny and half his cost. ATL's record (26 points, 8th-worst in the league) and their six expiring deals make them sellers; the R1 is the premium that pushes them past "why not just keep him for 30 games." Acceptance is uncertain, but this is the package that makes the most hockey sense.

**Sillinger from Phoenix** closes the only genuine role gap. His FACE 96 gives L3 and L4 real draws where Chlup's 75 gives nothing. At $1.20M expiring and 87 overall, he is a second-year answer. PHX sits at 26 points with 9 expiring deals and $55.41M payroll; they are shedding everything. Koltsov at POTE 94 with 96 acceleration and 92 speed is a young asset for their rebuild (though he is 0 GP this season, which is a flag PHX will see). St. Jacques at POTE 94 and 84 checking is a D prospect the Coach says is first out anyway. We add our R2 (third round) as sweetener. Total give: $1.90M in expiring contracts plus a pick. We get $1.20M back. Net saving $0.70M. PHX adds $0.70M on a $55.41M payroll, which is a rounding error for them. These two deals are non-competing: they share no assets.

**Havlat from Ottawa** is the fallback if either above fails. 86 overall, 98 speed, POTE 84, 28 points in 28 games at $0.90M. The problem is OTT at 25 points with only 4 expiring deals and $59.27M payroll are the least motivated sellers on this board. They have no urgency. A package of Alexeev plus a pick works on paper (Alexeev brings 89 speed and 90 balance at 23 with POTE 94), but OTT will hold for more unless they decide 98 speed at $0.90M is too cheap to keep. I would wait until late February to open this.

**The Gaborik problem** is the elephant this construction does not solve. $11.90M for five more years, 8 points in 17 games, scratched 43% of the schedule, and still sitting out today. Every scratched game erodes his trade value. The problem is landing spot: no rebuilding team below 30 points obviously needs a 98-speed RW on $11.90M, and contenders who want him won't give up enough to justify us taking on any salary back. I need to identify a specific club with salary flexibility and an open wing before I can build a package. The Coach's "dress or trade" ultimatum means the decision window is January and February, not March.

**What if none land:** Dress Gaborik on L3 or L4 per the Coach's December 15 recommendation. His 98 speed and 98 acceleration should produce points on lower opposition. Koltsov and St. Jacques stay as healthy scratches. The faceoff gap gets managed by rotating Wallin (FACE 83, not lined) into the X-slot on the third line and accepting that L4 draws are a net loss. We are 20-7-0 at 48 points; we are not desperate, and no deal is better than a bad deal.

## Owed

**Luongo availability and DiPietro monitoring for the goalie trade window.** This task was opened in January 2005 with a February delivery date. It is now closed, and the reason is good: Luongo is here.

**Luongo** is on Toronto's roster at 95 overall, 26 years old, 14 games played, $1.60M with 1 year remaining. The January goal — "set a goal to fetch a really good high-90s goalie from a team that will not be a contender" — has been achieved. The GM closed all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19 ("Goalies are solved. Done.").

**DiPietro** is at NYI, 87 overall, 24, 26 GP, $1.10M, 0 years remaining (expiring). He would have been a trade candidate this summer if we still needed one. We do not. The monitoring window is past and the need is filled.

**What has changed and matters now:** Luongo's contract clock. He is on his final year. Without a renewal in July 2006 he walks, and the backup is Ouellet at 81 base. This is the new goalie question, and it is urgent. It is not a trade-window question; it is a re-signing question on the correct timeline (July, when contracts open).

No action needed today. Flagging the renewal as the next goalie item to prepare for.
