# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-12-17

Next game at FLA on Sunday 18 December 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether every player 23 or under is getting the games his production has earned, in both directions: who is being wasted, and who is not worth dressing. With 31 games in the bank, the sample is large enough to call several of these.

**Gardener** has zero points in 22 games at 3.5 minutes a night. Two scratch recommendations, on 4 December and 8 December, were both taken, and he came back each time and still has not registered a point. POTE 98 is a scouting opinion. Zero points in 22 games is the record. He is not a development project any more; he is a roster spot that cannot produce.

**Colaiacovo** sits at 3 points in 25 games, 0.12 per game, at 12.3 MPG. My November 27 call was to scratch him. Twenty-five games is enough rope. He is the weakest defenceman on the roster by a wide margin and has not responded to ice time.

**Gaborik** is the clearest misallocation on the sheet. When he plays, he gets 22.6 minutes — top-four workload — and produces 8 points in 17 games (0.47 per game). He has been scratched 14 times this season. Spezza (0.20 per game, 5.4 MPG) and Upshall (0.23 per game, 6.1 MPG) dress ahead of him on the depth chart while producing half his rate. If Gaborik is healthy, dress him and scratch one of them.

**Spezza** has 5 points in 25 games at 5.4 minutes on the fourth line, morale 82. He is in the same pattern that took Upshall and Gardener: early minutes, a collapse, and now depth scraps that are too small to develop anything. He needs a real camp audition next summer, not 5 minutes a night through February.

**Chlup, Nash, Chistov, Klesla** play every game at 20.9, 15.6, 20.1, and 26.0 MPG respectively. All four are producing at rates that match their role. No change.

**Alexeev** is at 11 points in 24 games, 0.46 per game, one game short of the 25-game reassessment I set in November. He gets 10.5 minutes on the third line. No change today; the answer arrives in one game.

**Spacek** has 3 points in 6 games at 5.8 MPG, morale 76. The lowest morale on the youth list. Six games is too small to judge production, but the morale drop from sitting is real. Watch it.

**D obligation (#1):** Updated from what this brief shows. Klesla at 0.42 pts/g over 31 is the only defenceman above the 0.30 sell floor. Colaiacovo at 0.12 over 25 is confirmed dead. Stahle (0.22 in 18) and Eminger (0.29 in 7) are both below. The sell list is unchanged: Klesla at 0.42 is the only one worth moving, and only if his OVR has held. Full OVR-confirmed update follows in the matchup phase.

## Development trends

This window tells us which young players are earning permanent roles and which are still trapped in the collapse cycle, and it updates the defense review the GM asked me to run after every game.

**Chlup** at 19 has gone from a one-game cameo to 31 games at 0.80 pts/g on 21.4 MPG. The 1.00 left-of-arrow is noise from a single shift; 0.80 over 31 games is the real reading. His minutes nearly quadrupled and his rate held. Franchise centre development on schedule.

**Chistov** at 22 went from scratch to 31 games at 0.67 pts/g on 20.5 MPG. That is a top-six winger's production at a top-six winger's ice time. He earned this role in the window and he keeps it. No change needed, just confirmation for the GM that this isn't a fluke.

**Safronov** at 24 is quietly becoming a top-four defenseman: 0.44 pts/g at 20.9 MPG over 18 games. Compare him to Hainsey (0.37 at 20.9 over 19) and Stahle (0.24 at 12.9 over 18). Safronov leads the young D group in both production and role. This matters for the end-of-season defense review below.

**Alexeev** at 23 is at 0.39 pts/g over 24 games on 10.7 MPG. My threshold from November 17th was 0.45 at 25 games; he is at 24 and already below it. The dressing recommendation weakens. He is not a top-six winger and he is not a depth forward producing above replacement either. I would scratch him and give his slot to someone in the development cycle rather than a player whose rate has faded.

**Lundmark** at 24 is in the collapse pattern: 6.4 MPG over 23 games, 0.18 pts/g. Minutes fell from 11.0 to 6.4, same trajectory as Upshall and Spezza before him. He needs to be scratched or his minutes need to be raised to something meaningful; right now he is neither developing nor contributing.

**Gardener** at 20, **Upshall** at 22, **Spacek** at 20 all confirm the pattern already documented. Gardener: 0 points in 22 games at 3.0 MPG. Upshall: 0.19 at 5.6 over 22. Spacek: 0.40 at 3.6 over 6. All three are write-offs this season.

**Richards** at 25 is at 0.50 pts/g on 11.5 MPG over 31 games. His minutes actually dropped from 13.0 to 11.5 within the window. The structural decline is the third straight season and the role is shrinking, not stabilizing. Offseason review remains the only path.

**Sundin** at 34 (0.77 pts/g, 23.5 MPG) and **Mogilny** at 36 (0.77 pts/g, 22.8 MPG) are producing at elite levels but eating the heaviest forward minutes on the roster. At their ages, 22-23 MPG per night through a December-January stretch risks an endurance slide by February. I would look for spots to take a minute or two off each of them if a game state allows it.

**Jackman** at 24 holds at 0.67 pts/g over 31 games on 24.8 MPG. He is above my 0.55 sell trigger and stable. Keep.

## Defense review (obligation #1, update 11)

Ranking TOR defensemen by this window's evidence for end-of-season decisions:

- **Klesla** (23, 0.43 pts/g, 25.5 MPG, 31 GP, 87 OVR, expiring): Sell window open. His rate recovered above my 0.30 floor. A buyer sees the grade; we see a partner with higher ice time and no long-term future. Move before the deadline.
- **Colaiacovo** (22, 0.12 pts/g, 12.6 MPG, 25 GP): Weakest regular D. Zero goals in 25 games. He should not be in the playoff rotation.
- **St. Jacques** (25, 0.00 pts/g, 11.5 MPG, 13 GP): Zero offense across 13 games. If he does not produce through January he is a healthy scratch candidate permanently.
- **Hainsey** (24, 0.37 pts/g, 20.9 MPG, 19 GP): Solid depth D, not top-four. Keeps his role for now.
- **Safronov** (24, 0.44 pts/g, 20.9 MPG, 18 GP): Emerging top-four. Building the case to keep over Hainsey if we need to choose.

## Morale watch

The room is right. Fourteen players sitting at 97 morale with positive movement, the core lines all trending up 3 to 8 points. One structural problem and one scratch worth revisiting.

**Richards** at 84 morale and rising (+3 to +5) remains the one player whose minutes still don't match his calibre. 11.6 MPG against a 17-MPG expectation is a 5-minute gap, same as October. Morale has climbed from 78 to 84, so the cost is now -1 per grade, manageable. I recommended promoting him on December 8th and the GM didn't take it. The trend is positive without my intervention. I will not re-litigate a declined recommendation while morale is improving.

**Spacek** is the lowest on the roster at 76, up +5. That -2 morale penalty suppresses his grades on the lines screen. At 5.8 MPG and 3 points in 6 games (0.50 rate), he's producing. The -2 costs more than the development value of the scratch is worth at this point. He needs a fourth-line spot to climb out of the 70s.

**Gardener** at 82 morale and +5 is fine emotionally, but 0 points in 22 games at 3.5 MPG is not a development opportunity. I recommended a permanent scratch on December 8th, the GM took it, but Gardener played one more game after that. He is still dressed. The spot should go to Spacek: it gives Spacek the minutes to recover his morale and removes a zero-production slot from the fourth line.

No other concerns. Upshall (84, +7), Spezza (82, +5), Alexeev (97, +5) are all trending well on their current minutes. The goalies are at 82 to 97 and rising. No intervention needed there.

## Role composition

Are our units built from players who suit them? Mostly yes, but the fourth line has a misfit and the centre depth creates a structural problem that no arrangement fixes.

**Tucker** is checking 80 and the GM called him "our checking guy" back in January. He's dressed on the fourth line in this lineup... actually no, he's scratched. Meanwhile **Gardener** is on L4 with zero points in 18+ games at roughly 3 minutes a night. Tucker at 80 checking is the obvious fit on that line. This is a role-fit call: L4 needs a body who can forecheck and kill, not a healthy scratch who produces nothing.

**L1** is fine. Jackman at checking 91 provides the backbone; Sundin, Mogilny and Chistov carry the scoring (93, 92, 92 respectively) and speed (93 best). That's a first line built to score behind a D pair that can also check.

**L2** checks out. Chlup draws at 79, Nash at 81 checking gives the line its grit, Afinogenov at 92 scoring gives the finish. Balanced.

**L3** at checking mean 70 is serviceable. McCabe and St. Jacques provide the defensive presence; Richards at 92 playmaking and 77 faceoffs is the engine. No change.

**Sundin on K2** is the structural issue. He's our best centre for everything — 93 scoring, 95 playmaking, 94 faceoffs, 98 clutch. He's killing penalties on the second unit because we only have three true centres (Sundin, Chlup, Richards) and a fourth-liner in Spezza. A buyer of centre depth would give us something for that surplus role. This isn't fixable by moving players around — it's a roster gap.

## Opponent matchup

**Florida is an 8-15 team with an 8.4% power play and a +7 goal differential in our favour from the one game already played this season.** The only real question is whether Jokinen against Safronov is a mismatch worth a D-pair swap, and against this opponent, it is not.

**Florida's top six breaks down as Jokinen (85), Nedorost (84), Rolston (81), Kozlov (81), Bouwmeester (83) and Lilja (79).** Their bottom six is Weiss (76) and below. Our third line has Richards at 87, Lundmark at 81 and Alexeev at 80. We outclass them on three lines. Their first line's average OVR is 80; our first line's is 89.

**The Safronov-to-Jokinen problem.** Our second defensive pair (Kaberle 85 / Safronov 68) auto-pairs with our second forward line and therefore faces their second line, which is Jokinen-led. Jokinen at 85 with 92 speed and 90 deking against a 68 OVR partner on our second pair is a genuine gap. Swapping D2 and D3 would put McCabe (82, 83 CHKG) against Jokinen, but then Safronov sees Rolston at 81 on their third line. Both pairings expose Safronov. Against a better opponent I would raise this; against Florida it does not justify breaking the D-pair rhythm the players are used to.

**Ouellet should start.** Tellqvist is at 73 and carries no business starting on the road against an 89-OVR Aebischer when Ouellet sits at 86 on the bench. No fatigue flag shown on Ouellet.

**No PP or PK changes.** Their power play is 11 for 131 (8.4%) and their PK will be facing Sundin, Mogilny, Chlup and Richards. Our current special teams units are fine for this night.

## Owed

This is my D evaluation for the 12-18 game at Florida. It's been 3 days since my last update on 12-15, so the movement is minimal, but here's where each defenceman sits.

**Jackman** holds at 0.68 pts/g (21 in 31 games). On 12-04 I flagged 0.68 at 25 games with a sell trigger at 0.55. He's gone 6 games since and scored 4 points in that stretch, holding the rate flat. At $0.70M x 2 he stays unless something breaks. The sell trigger hasn't moved.

**Klesla** ticked from 0.40 to 0.42 (13 in 31 games). One point in game 31. The recovery from the 0.29 low in late November continues, but the sell logic hasn't changed: 87 OVR, expiring, buyer sees the grade not the rate. The window is open now and won't be in August.

**Colaiacovo** is at 3 points in 25 games (0.12) with zero goals. No change from the 11-27 recommendation. He is the weakest player on the roster by production. Gone at season's end.

**Safronov** at 8 in 18 games (0.44) on $0.90M x 2 is fine depth for the price. No reason to move him.

**Hainsey** at 7 in 19 (0.37) on $1.40M x 6 is middling. Not dressed, which is correct with the current group healthy. He stays as long-term third-pair.

**Eminger** has 2 points in 7 games (0.29) at $2.20M x 4. That's the problem contract on the back end. 4 years at that rate and salary means no one will touch it. He stays because he has to.

**St. Jacques** (0 points in 13, 66 OVR, expiring) is gone. No drama.

The sell targets for the deadline remain **Klesla** (window open, 87 on the card) and **Colaiacovo** (0.12 with $1.40M x 4, try to dump the salary). No change since 12-15.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-12-15
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-12-15

Toronto 19-7-0, 46 pts after 30 games.

## Role coverage

**Faceoffs at centre is the one structural gap this roster cannot fill internally; checking and toughness are covered despite the composite metric suggesting otherwise.**

**Toughness.** The role coverage composite shows zero players at 80+, averaging TOUG with aggression and fighting into a diluted number. The Dec 4 audit that pulled displayed TOUG specifically found 11 Toronto players at 80+ on that attribute, which is why Hartnell, Kurka and Jovanovski were all closed. The composite misleads; the attribute is fine. No acquisition needed here.

**Checking.** Six at 80+ on the composite, led by Jackman 87, McCabe 86, Roberts 86, Tucker 83. The Coach's PK concern is about deployment, not talent. Tucker at 83 composite and Roberts at 86 are scratched by choice, not injury. Jackman and McCabe are both available tonight for PK2. This fixes itself if the Coach uses the men he has. The one wrinkle: Tucker is the only designated trade chip from last season, so if he moves his 83 leaves the checking pool thins to three reliable options.

**Faceoffs.** This is the hole. Only Sundin at 90 and Wallin at 83 clear 80, and Sundin plays wing. The centres are Chlup 75, Richards 70, Gardener 72. In a playoff series against a team with an 85+ faceoff centre (Sakic, Niedermayer, St. Louis, Roy), every zone draw in the offensive end becomes a coin flip. Chlup at 75 is the ceiling the Coach can dress, and that is below what wins puck possession in the playoffs. This gap requires an acquisition.

**Scoring, playmaking, speed, clutch.** Deep on every axis. Mogilny 94, Sundin 92, Gaborik 92, Afinogenov 90 on scoring. Gaborik at 98 speed and 92 playmaking sitting unlined is the biggest wasted asset on the roster right now; dressing him solves multiple needs simultaneously.

**Durability.** Five at 80+, but the top three (Roberts 98, Fischer 92, Abid 90) are all unlined. The lined players carry lower endurance grades. In a seven-game series with road trips and back-to-backs, the Coach needs bodies who can absorb knocks. Abid at 90 durability, 86 scoring, and 25 years old is the internal fix.

**Age curve.** Mogilny is 36. Roberts is 39. Sundin is 34. The top-six centre and top-pair defence are held by players whose contracts expire soon and whose bodies are not getting younger. If Gaborik (23), Chistov (22), and Richards (25) do not step into those production slots by 2007, this team loses its top end in one summer. The coverage is fine today; the trajectory says the depth behind these men needs to be real by next season.

**Goalies.** Luongo at 94 overall, 1.99 GAA, .931 SV in 14 games is a true number one. Ouellet at 81 base, .907 in 8 games is adequate backup for a 16-game playoff run. Covered.

## Trajectory

The question is whether Toronto are building toward a window or walking into a cliff. The answer: the age curve is close to ideal, the money is healthy, but two contract problems — one now, one in 2009 — will define the next three seasons if left alone.

**Gaborik** is the single biggest trajectory threat. $11.90M per year through July 2010 on 8 points in 17 games as a scratch. That is 13.2% of payroll earning nothing on the ice. The Coach is now proposing to dress him on the third or fourth line; that's the right call because his trade value only recovers if he plays and scores. But even a productive Gaborik costs $47.60M through 2010, and at 23 with POTE 90, we'd rather own Chistov at $5.00M and POTE 95 producing 0.66 pts/g in the same role. The move that protects three seasons is to dress him, let him rebuild his value for six weeks, then trade him in February for a top-six winger we keep.

**Luongo and Chlup** expire July 2006 and must be locked on 5–6 years the same week. Luongo at $1.60M, 94 overall, 26 years old, is the cheapest elite asset in the league. Chlup at $2.34M, 19 years old, 24 points in 30 games with POTE 95 is the future first-line centre. Neither can walk. Mogilny at 36 and $5.50M should simply not be renewed.

**The 2009 cluster** is the structural trap. Eleven players on four-year deals worth $37.40M all hit the market the same July. Richards, Chistov, Nash, Kaberle, Alexeev, Upshall, Colaiacovo, Abid, Wallin — the entire young core comes up simultaneously. The finding from December recommends breaking this in July 2007 by extending Richards (then 27), Chistov (24) and Nash (23) early. Three players out of that wave, and the renewal calendar becomes manageable.

**Draft capital is thin.** Own R1, R2, and R3 only. The Heatley target (Tucker + R1) and the Jovanovski target (Klesla + R2) compete for the same pool. We can make one deadline move, not two, without a Gaborik return including a pick.

**Money:** $89.94M payroll against $76.98M gate revenue, profit $35.66M. The club is profitable and has spending room. Gaborik's salary is not a cap problem — there is no cap — but it is a revenue-per-point problem. $11.90M buys 0.47 pts/g while Chistov at $5.00M buys 0.66. Rebalancing that frees $11.90M annually for the 2006 and 2007 renewal windows.

**Age shape:** 13 under 23, 16 at 24–29, only 5 at 30+. That is exactly the manual's target (5–7 veterans, 20 young). The roster shape is not the problem. The contracts on that shape are.

## Calendar

**The deadline is 94 days away and we are buyers.** Toronto lead the East at 46 points with 52 games left, and the manual's rule is clear: buy for need when you're contending. The summer question is separate and more urgent than people expect, because Luongo and Chlup both come due in July.

**Gaborik.** His contract runs to July 2010 at $11.90M/year, 13.2% of payroll. At 91 base he's our best player, but 8 points in 17 games while sitting out 43% means his value is eroding every week he watches. This is not a deadline problem — his four-year deal makes him untradeable at this salary. The fix is the Coach's: play him on L3 or L4 at 0.47 pts/g on 22.6 MPG and restore his production. If he's still scratching through February, we have a four-year $47.6M commitment to a man who won't dress, and that's the biggest risk on the roster.

**Mogilny.** 36 years old, $5.50M, 21 points in 30 games at 89 base. He is the deadline sell. Any contender needs a right winger at that level, and he walks in July if we don't move him. His value is at its peak right now — 89 overall base, still producing. Move him by March for a pick or a young player with potential. He is the single highest-value chip on this roster because of the $5.50M salary relief and the age profile that makes him a rental.

**Tucker.** 79 base, $1.30M, age 30. He's the secondary chip. If we can't get Heatley for Mogilny alone, Tucker fills the gap in a package. The Coach wants him on K2 for checking (CHKG 80), which means moving him costs us a PK body. But 79 base at 30 on an expiring deal is exactly what the deadline is for.

**Atlanta still open.** They sit at 24 points (9-15-4) per the query, which confirms they are still a sell team. Heatley (91 base, expiring) is the primary deadline target. The package we discussed in December — Tucker plus R1 — remains the shape. We now own our first, second, and third-round picks fresh for 2006, so the pick constraint from January 2005 ("no picks beyond 4th") is reset.

**Timing.** Standing order: negotiations open late February, not before. It's December. Sellers remain sellers. No urgency to press Atlanta or Vancouver until the season separates from the pack, which will be clearer in February.

## Summer renewals

**Luongo.** 26 years old, 91 base, $1.60M, one year left. This is the most urgent renewal of the summer. Lock him on 5–6 years immediately in July. He is our franchise goaltender and Ouellet (81 base) is a backup, not a successor.

**Chlup.** 19 years old, 24 points in 30 games at 20.9 minutes per night, $2.34M expiring. He is our second-round centre developing into a first-round player. Renew on 5–6 years. This is the renewal that matters most after Luongo.

**Klesla.** 23, 12 points in 30 games (projected 33 over 82), $0.90M. Developing top-four defenceman at a fraction of market value. Renew on 3–4 years.

**Ouellet.** 24, 81 base, $0.90M. He is the backup we need. Renew on 2 years. Cheap, adequate, no drama.

**Koltsov.** 24, $1.10M, 19 points in 38 games last season. If this season matches that pace, renew on 2–3 years. If not, move him at the deadline alongside Tucker to fund a bigger package.

**Spezza, St. Jacques.** Let them go. Spezza is collapsing (5 pts in 46 GP last season, 2 in 24 this season, under 6 MPG). St. Jacques has zero points in 12 games at 11.8 MPG and the Coach says first out. Neither warrants a renewal.

**The 2009 cluster.** Eleven players on four-year deals worth $37.40M expire July 2009 simultaneously. This is the problem to begin breaking in summer 2007 by extending Richards, Chistov, and Nash early. Not this summer, but track it.

## League scan

The faceoff gap is the only structural hole this roster cannot fill internally, and the data confirms it: the top eight faceoff centres on clubs below 35 points are all on expiring or near-expiring deals, meaning the market exists for a February rental.

**Draper** is the single best faceoff centre in the league at FACE 97, 79 overall, 31 points in 26 games for DET at 31 points. He is 34 with POTE 61, so he is a pure playoff rental, but $1.20M expiring with DET down to 3 picks left (actively trading away capital) makes him the cheapest elite faceoff answer available.

**Sillinger** at FACE 96 and 87 overall on 24 points in 27 games for PHX (24 points, 9 expiring, $55.41M payroll) is the best faceoff-and-production combination. He is also 34 with POTE 56, so also a rental, but his 87 overall means he contributes beyond the draw. PHX will dump him for anything.

**Bates** at FACE 89, $0.90M expiring, 30 years old, 37 points in 37 games for NYI is the cheapest viable option. NYI at 37 points with 7 expiring are in no-man's-land and will likely look to shed salary before March.

**Hrdina** (PHX, FACE 88, 77 overall, $1.19M, expiring, 29 years old) is the same seller as Sillinger at a lower price. If PHX moves both, we only need one of them.

**Avery** (LA, FACE 90, 73 displayed / 79 base, $0.40M expiring, 25 years old) is the youngest and cheapest. LA at 20 points will sell anyone. His 79 base says he is a legitimate bottom-six centre who wins draws; he is not a playoff starter but he solves the zone-draw problem at 25 with bridge-contract value.

**Hilbert** (BOS, FACE 86, 82 displayed / 77 base, POTE 95, $0.90M expiring, 24 years old, 38 points in 38 games) is the long-term answer. At POTE 95 with a 77 base and 86 faceoffs, he is a developing two-way centre. The problem: BOS at 38 points with only 4 expiring deals may not sell him. Worth a February conversation but not plan-a.

**Stoll** (EDM, FACE 88, 63 displayed / 67 base, POTE 98, $0.70M expiring, 23) is the highest-ceiling option but cannot help tonight or in April. He is a July development project, not a deadline target.

**Heatley** (ATL, 91 base, expiring) remains the top scoring target. ATL at 24 points cannot re-sign him. Tucker plus R1 is still the proposed return. This move and the faceoff rental compete for the same two assets (Tucker is the only chip, and we need the R1 for Heatley), so the faceoff fix must come from the cheaper pool: Avery, Bates, or Hrdina for a late-round pick or depth player.

**Vasicek** (CAR, 84 overall, FACE 80, POTE 87, $0.40M expiring, 37 points in 37 games) is a better overall player than Avery and costs less than Bates. His FACE is 80, below the 85 threshold, but he contributes on the scoresheet in a way the pure faceoff guys do not. If the goal is a centre who wins draws AND produces, he is the best value.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: what packages actually fix the faceoff hole and add a top-six winger without breaking the defense core the GM has protected? The answer is two independent trades that use entirely different assets: Heatley for Tucker + R1, and Sillinger for three depth players the Coach cannot dress + R3. Both can happen simultaneously.

**Heatley** is the clear first priority. ATL sit at 24 points on a $40.34M payroll (league-lowest) with three elite expirers and no realistic path to re-signing any of them. Heatley's 91 base rating at LW gives us the second elite winger this offense lacks alongside Mogilny's 94. Tucker at $1.30M expiring fills their lineup for the balance of a lost season; the R1 is the real price they want. ATL says yes because they are selling three players they cannot keep and this is the only return that includes a first-rounder. Acceptance is uncertain because ATL might want a young player beyond Tucker.

**Sillinger** is the faceoff answer that actually works. FACE 96, 87 overall, 24 points in 27 games at age 34 — he wins every draw tonight and contributes beyond it. PHX at 24 points with 9 expiring deals and $55.41M payroll have no reason to keep a 34-year-old with POTE 56. We give three players who contributed almost nothing this season: Koltsov (0 GP/0 pts, $1.10M expiring), St. Jacques (0 pts/12 GP, $0.80M expiring), and the R3. Net payroll saving $0.70M. PHX says yes because they are shedding salary and accumulating a late pick; Sillinger's expiring deal means they lose him for nothing in July otherwise.

**Vasicek** is the fallback if PHX wants more. FACE 80 is only a 5-point upgrade over Chlup's 75, but at 25 with POTE 87 and 37 points in 37 games he plays top-six centre, not a rental. CAR cannot re-sign him and will take Koltsov plus the R3. The gap versus elite playoff centres (85-97) persists, but Vasicek is a young piece we can build around.

**If none land:** move Sundin to centre for key draws. His FACE 90 matches anyone in the league, and the role coverage confirmed he clears the threshold the other centres do not. That is the Coach's call, not mine, but the acquisition becomes less urgent if he does it.

## Owed

**The question this phase answers:** is the January 2005 task to "monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window" still live?

**Luongo** is on our roster at 95 overall, 26 years old, $1.60M, 14 games played this season. The original purpose of this task — find a high-90s goalie from a non-contender — is fulfilled. We acquired him. The GM closed all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19. This task is closed.

**DiPietro** is no longer a relevant target. We hold Luongo at 95 and the GM's standing order reads "Goalies are solved." Continuing to track a backup option we no longer need wastes the deadline bandwidth.

**What has changed since last I reported:** nothing on the trade side. The one new fact is Luongo's contract has dropped to 1 year remaining at $1.60M (was 2 in the prior snapshot). That makes his July 2006 renewal the live goalie issue now, not a trade window. I will track that under a renewal heading, not this one.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-12-15
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-12-15

Next game at ATL on Friday 16 December 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether our young players are getting the games they've earned, and there's one clear mismatch on the sheet tonight.

**Gaborik** is the finding that matters. He's at 8 points in 17 games, a 0.47 rate, on 22.6 MPG when he plays — top-line minutes — yet he's dressed only 57% of the time. Alexeev on the third line produces 0.43 (10 points in 23 games) on 10.6 MPG. Gaborik's rate is higher, his minutes when dressed are twice as heavy, and he sits in the pressbox while Alexeev centres the third line. If Gaborik is healthy, he belongs in the lineup ahead of Upshall on the fourth line at minimum, and possibly Alexeev on the third. At 23 with 0.47 production and proven top-line ability, scratching him 43% of games is wasting the season.

**Gardener** is the opposite case. 0 points in 21 games at 3.7 MPG. I recommended scratching him permanently on December 8th and it was taken, yet he still shows 21 games played and 70% share. If he's still in the current lineup, that's a carry with zero production return. No development value at 0 points.

**Chlup, Nash, Chistov, Klesla** are clearly earning everything they get. Chlup at 24 points in 30 games on 20.9 MPG at 19 is the best young player in the club. Nash at 18 points in 15.6 MPG. Chistov at 21 points on the first line. Klesla at 12 points on 25.9 MPG is carrying a heavy load — 25.9 minutes is the highest on the roster — and it's working, but watch his legs in the back half of this schedule.

**Alexeev** at 0.43 on 10.6 MPG on the third line is exactly what he's earning. No change.

**Upshall and Spezza** at 0.21 and 0.24 with 5-6 MPG on the fourth line are getting what they've produced. High potential hasn't translated and their minutes correctly reflect that. No issue.

**Stahle** (0.22 in 18 games) and **Colaiacovo** (0.12 in 25 games) are already scratched and their rates confirm that's right. **Eminger** and **Spacek** are on the block or too young to justify a spot over the current four D. No change needed for any of them.

## Development trends

The question this phase answers: who is climbing and who is sliding, and does any of it change what we plan around for the rest of the season or next offseason. It matters now because we are 30 games in, trends are separating from noise, and several decisions I flagged in November are at their checkpoints.

**Chistov** is the season's biggest gain. 6 MPG in the first sample to 20.2 MPG over 30 games, and 0.66 pts/g over that stretch. At 22 he has made himself a top-six winger. That changes the depth chart behind Nash and Chlup. He is not a depth forward any more and should not be used like one.

**Fischer** came back after missing time and put up 0.80 pts/g on 21.8 MPG in 6 games. The GM called him a keeper and he is proving it. At 25 with that rate on those minutes he is a second-pairing D at minimum and a top-four candidate if the minutes hold.

**Stahle** went from 6 MPG to 12.9 MPG at 0.24 pts/g in 18 games at age 21. That is a defenceman growing into a real role. I would not push him past 14 MPG yet, but the trajectory is the right direction.

**Hainsey** at 0.37 pts/g on 20.9 MPG over 19 games is solid third-pairing work at 24. **Safronov** mirrors him at 0.47 on 21.2 MPG over 17. Both are the reason Jackman and Klesla's minutes came down from 41 and 42 to 24.7 and 25.4. The load problem I flagged in October is fixed.

**Alexeev** is now below my threshold. I set 0.45 as the line on November 17th; he is at 0.36 pts/g over 23 games on 10.8 MPG. Production fell while minutes rose, which is the pattern I watch for. He is not a top-nine winger right now. I would drop him to the fourth line or scratch him for the ATL game and give Brendl or Lundmark a look. Reason class: development, because his growth is stalling and more ice is not fixing it.

**Spezza** and **Upshall** are both in the collapse pattern for the second or third time. Spezza at 0.21 pts/g on 5.6 MPG over 24 games, Upshall at 0.20 on 5.8 MPG over 21 games. Both 22. Neither has shown anything at 5 MPG that would justify more. These are offseason decisions: real training-camp audition or stop dressing them. I will not relitigate it mid-season.

**St. Jacques** has zero points in 12 games on 11.8 MPG at age 25. That is below what a third-pairing D needs to justify dressing over a prospect. **McCabe** has zero in 5 games on 11.8 MPG at 30. Both are replacement-level at best right now. With Safronov and Hainsey outperforming them, they are the first two out when someone returns from injury.

**Colaiacovo** at 0.12 pts/g over 25 games on 12.6 MPG confirms the November 27th scratch call. He is the weakest regular D by a wide margin and has no goal.

On the veterans: **Sundin** at 34 is 0.79 pts/g on 23.3 MPG over 30 games. No decline. **Mogilny** at 36 is 0.72 on 22.7 MPG. Both are producing. **Roberts** at 39 is at 0.29 on 13.7 MPG in 8 games, minutes down from 18. That is the expected slide at his age. Plan for next year without him in a top-nine role.

**Klesla** at 0.41 pts/g over 30 games is above my 0.30 sell floor. The November 30th sell window is still open but his recovery is slowing the urgency. **Jackman** at 0.66 is above the 0.55 sell trigger. Keep. No trade action needed on either this week.

## Morale watch

The room is recovering and no line change fixes anything today. Win streaks have pulled morale up across the board; most guys are at 97 or better with positive trends. Two names sit below the pack for reasons minutes alone won't solve.

**Luongo** is at 82 morale despite playing every minute he's asked to (60.3 MPG over 14 starts). Goalies expect 60; he gets 60. There's no ice-time lever here. That's results or the building, and it's the GM's to solve, not mine to dress around.

**Spacek** sits at 76, the lowest on the roster. He's been scratched most of the season (6 GP, 5.8 MPG, 3 pts). His morale is climbing (+5 from the last save) but he's still well below anyone else. Giving him more minutes means taking them from Chlup, Richards or Alexeev, none of whom can afford to lose ice. The GM needs to decide whether Spacek is a player we're developing for next year or a roster candidate to move. I can't fix that from the bench.

**Richards** is at 84 on 11.5 MPG. He's in the 80-89 band and would ideally see 17, so there's a structural deficit. But three seasons of decline (1.08, 0.71, 0.54 pts/g) mean he's earned the third-line role he's in. I'm not raising his minutes to protect his feelings; he's getting what his game has bought him. Morale is trending up anyway (+5).

Everyone else is at 97 with positive trends. **Jackman** (25.2 MPG) and **Klesla** (25.9 MPG) carry heavy defensive minutes and sit at 97, so the load isn't hurting. **St. Jacques** dropped badly mid-season but has recovered +15 to 97.

No changes. The room is right.

## Role composition

The question here is whether each unit is built from the right pieces, and whether we have enough of each role to cover the season. The answer: the lines are sound, the one gap is the second penalty-kill unit.

**L1 (Sundin, Mogilny, Jackman, Klesla, Chistov)** is built correctly: scoring mean 89, speed mean 93, checking mean 75. This is a first power line with legitimate defensive capability behind it. No change.

**L2 (Chlup, Kaberle, Nash, Afinogenov, Safronov)** is balanced: checking 74, scoring 82, speed 86. Chlup's 79 faceoffs give us a second body at the dot. This line is doing what a second line should. No change.

**L3 (McCabe, Richards, Alexeev, Lundmark, St. Jacques)** is a second skill line, not a checking line. Richards carries 92 playmaking and 77 faceoffs; the checking mean of 70 is below what a shutdown third line needs. But I recommended moving him up to centre L2 on December 8th and the GM kept the arrangement. Chemistry is real — if this line is producing, I leave it alone.

**L4 (Gardener, Spezza, Upshall)** is thin but that's what depth lines are. No structural problem here, just depth.

**K1 (Chlup, Jackman, Safronov, Chistov)** is solid: checking mean 79, toughness mean 68. Jackman's 91 checking anchors it. This is our shutdown kill and it's built right.

**K2 (Kaberle, Spezza, Upshall, Klesla)** is where the problem sits. Checking mean 71, toughness mean 63. Spezza and Upshall are the two weakest skaters on the roster carrying PK duty. **Tucker is at 80 checking and scratched.** The GM himself designated Tucker as "our checking guy" in January. If he's our fourth-best checker, he belongs on the second PK unit to shore up that checking mean from 71 toward 76.

**Roster depth on checking**: Jackman 91, Roberts 83 (scratched), Nash 81, Tucker 80, Wallin (not listed in checking). We have four forwards who can check. Two are in the lineup, two are scratched. That's enough for two PK units if Tucker and Roberts are dressed on PK nights. The gap isn't roster depth, it's deployment.

**Faceoffs**: Sundin 94, Chlup 79, Richards 77. Three bodies over 75, which covers three lines. Wallin 87 is scratched and would be a fourth. Adequate but not deep.

## Opponent matchup

Should our lines change for Atlanta? No. This is a mismatch game where our structure is already set correctly against theirs.

**Atlanta's top line** is the only unit that matters: Kovalchuk (86 OVR, 97 shot power, 95 hero) and Heatley (85 OVR, 98 hero, 91 shot power) flanking Savard at 70 OVR. Our first line with Sundin (92, FACE 94) gets the draw every night against Savard (FACE 83), which means we control possession and limit their zone time. Our first pair Jackman/Klesla at 86/87 handles them cleanly; Klesla's 99 speed/acceleration neutralizes Kovalchuk's 98, and Jackman's 93 checking shuts down Heatley's board game.

**Atlanta's depth is thin.** Their second line centres at 68 (Kotalik, age 19), third line at 68 (MacKenzie), fourth at 62-66. Our third line with Richards at 87 OVR will steamroll MacKenzie's line. No matchup adjustment is needed there because the gap is already enormous.

**Their power play converts at 6.4%** (7 of 110). We can play with some offensive freedom on the back end without fearing the shorthanded rush. No structural defensive adjustment warranted.

**Hnilicka at 75** in net, backup Gerber at 71. Luongo at 95 has no business being pulled or rested for this game. ATL scores 2.30 a game as a team.

**No change to the lines.** Our first line against their first, second against second, all correct by default. The auto-pairing puts Jackman/Klesla against Kovalchuk/Heatley, which is exactly right.

---

**Obligation #1 (D-man season review):** From the brief, Jackman is at 86 OVR with 93 CHKG, Klesla at 87 with 99 speed. I cannot confirm Jackman's production rate without a query; the last reading was 0.68 at 25 games, sell trigger at 0.55. Kaberle (85) is the keeper per the GM. Safronov (68) and St. Jacques (66) are depth D with no trade value at these grades. McCabe (82) is the third-pair workhorse. Klesla remains the sell candidate at 87 with his 59 ENDU and expiring deal. No change to who plays; no change to the end-of-season sell list since October.

## Owed

This is the eleventh delivery of the standing job: how the defencemen have played and who goes at the end of the season.

**Klesla** — 12 points in 30 games, 0.40 pts/g. His rate has continued climbing from the 0.29 low in late November through 0.35 on November 30th to 0.40 now. That makes his card more attractive to a buyer at the deadline, not less. 87 OVR, $0.90M expiring, 23 years old. Still the best trade chip on the blue line, and the improving rate means move him now while the window is wide.

**Jackman** — 20 points in 30 games, 0.67 pts/g on 25.2 MPG. Essentially unchanged from the 0.68 I read at 25 games. Well above the 0.55 sell trigger. Leading D scorer at $0.70M x 2. Keep.

**Colaiacovo** — 3 points in 25 games, 0.12 pts/g, zero goals, 12.3 MPG. I flagged him at 0.14 over 22 games three weeks ago. Three more games and the rate is worse, not better. This is now definitive: he is the weakest regular defenceman and the first one out at season's end.

**Safronov** — 8 points in 17 games, 0.47 pts/g at 21.2 MPG. His 68 OVR is the lowest grade getting top-four minutes, but his production rate is fine for a third-pairing defender. Cheap at $0.90M x 2. Keep for now, but he is the next man out if Stahle or Eminger takes a step.

**Hainsey** — 7 points in 19 games, 0.37 pts/g at 20.9 MPG. Middling production on a $1.40M x 6 contract. Not a trade candidate because nobody absorbs six years for 0.37, but not a keeper beyond that contract either. No change.

**St. Jacques** — 0 points in 12 games at 66 OVR, $0.80M x 1 expiring. Let him walk.

**McCabe** — 0 points in 5 games at $3.00M x 3, age 30. Expendable if anyone takes the salary. No market likely.

**Kaberle, Fischer, Eminger, Stahle** — Kaberle and Fischer are untouchable per the GM. Eminger at 0.29 in 7 games needs more ice before any judgment. Stahle at 0.22 in 18 games is still a project at 21.

**What changed since the last delivery:** Klesla's rate improved from 0.35 to 0.40, raising his trade value. Colaiacovo went from 0.14 to 0.12 and now has 25 games with no goals, confirming the sell case. Nothing else moved enough to change a decision.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-12-11
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-12-11

Toronto 17-7-0, 42 pts after 28 games.

## Role coverage

Is Toronto's roster deep enough to compete through a playoff run, or are there roles where the club genuinely has no answer? The answer: the gaps the Coach flagged this month are almost entirely lineup problems, not roster problems, because the players who fill them are on the roster and sitting out.

**Gaborik** is the single largest waste of talent on this team. 92 overall, 98 speed, 92 playmaking, and he is "not lined" in any unit. The Coach has already flagged him. A man with the best speed grade on the roster and the second-best playmaking grade needs to be on the top line, not on the bench. He is 23. There is no development argument for sitting him.

**Koltsov, Fischer, and Upshall** are all "not lined" and together form a functional fourth line. Koltsov carries 92 speed. Fischer has 89 speed and 82 checking. Upshall has 80 checking. The Coach says the fourth line totals 12 MPG between Gardener, Spezza and Upshall; he should be running Fischer and Koltsov instead of or alongside them, because they give the line the speed and checking that Gardener (3.0 MPG, 0 points in 18 games) cannot.

**Roberts and Tucker** are both "not lined" and both carry 83+ checking (Roberts 86, Tucker 83). The Coach's K2 sits at a 71 checking mean with Klesla at 26 MPG doing double duty. Roberts at 39 with 98 durability is the right answer for penalty-kill minutes specifically; at 39 he will not carry even-strength load, but short PK shifts are exactly where he helps. Tucker at 30 with 83 checking is the same answer with an expiring-contract caveat.

**Wallin** at 83 faceoffs is the second-best draw-taker on the roster and he is "not lined." Sundin at 90 is the only active 80+ faceoff man. The Coach moved Richards up to second-line centre partly on ice-time grounds, but Richards at 70 faceoffs is a liability in the draw. Wallin should centre the third line for faceoff duty, with Chlup (75) dropping to the fourth.

**Toughness shows zero at 80+ on stored grades**, which looks alarming until you remember that displayed toughness has 11 Toronto players at 80+ as of December 4. The base-grade weakness means form dips will expose it, but it is not a gap requiring a trade. The toughness targets stay closed.

**Checking is thin at six players 80+**, but three of the six are "not lined." If the Coach lines Roberts, Tucker and Fischer, the active count rises to six in the lineup, which is adequate for three penalty-kill pairs and top-pair minutes. The problem is deployment, not personnel.

On **task #2** (Luongo and DiPietro monitoring): closed since November. Luongo is on the roster at 94 overall, 12 GP, 9-3, 1.82 GAA, 0.934 SV. Nothing to monitor until the renewal window opens in July 2006, where his one remaining year makes him the club's most urgent re-signing.

## Trajectory

The question this phase answers: can this roster sustain itself financially and age-wise through 2009, or does it collapse under its own contracts? The answer is yes on the age shape and yes on the finances, with two problems that will become three if left unaddressed: Gaborik's $11.90M, the July 2006 expiry wave, and the 2009 cluster.

**Gaborik is the single biggest threat to the next four seasons.** At $11.90M per year locked through July 2010, he accounts for 13.2% of the $89.94M payroll and produces 8 points in 17 games while scratched. That is $47.60M of committed money for a player the Coach does not dress. Mid-contract renegotiation is impossible. If he is not moved by March 2006, his value will have collapsed further (the October note warned about January; it is now December). Even a below-market return clears the largest single financial obligation on the books.

**Luongo is the immediate renewal priority.** He expires July 2006 at $1.60M with POTE 97, age 26, and 94 overall. Chlup expires the same summer at $2.34M with POTE 95, age 19, 20 points in 28 games. Both walk for nothing without a signed extension. Luongo first because the backup behind him is Ouellet at 81 base and also expiring. Lock both on 5-6 years in July 2006, Luongo the same week he becomes eligible.

**The July 2009 cluster is the structural risk.** Eleven players on four-year deals worth $37.40M all expire simultaneously, including Sundin at age 37 ($8.40M locked through his age-37 season), Richards ($6.70M), Chistov ($5.00M), and Nash ($3.90M). The manual warns about exactly this: a roster whose contracts all come up in the same summer. Begin extensions of Richards, Chistov, and Nash in July 2007 to stagger the exposure. Without that, the 2009 off-season requires re-signing or losing ten players at once, and their salaries will have ratcheted upward by then.

**The age curve is not the problem.** Thirteen players at 23 or under, sixteen at 24-29, two at 30-33, three at 34+. That is the manual's target shape: a young core with a few veterans. The 30-33 band is thin (McCabe 30, Tucker 30), but both are effectively out of the lineup, and Tucker is a deadline chip. The veterans carrying production (Sundin 19 pts, Mogilny 18 pts, Roberts scratched at 2 pts in 8 GP) will have rolled off by 2008, but Chistov (22), Nash (21), Chlup (19), and Afinogenov (26) are positioned to absorb that.

**The finances are healthy.** Payroll $89.94M against revenue $75.32M looks alarming until you see profit at $36.12M. The club is spending from a position of strength and can absorb an additional $5-7M contract at the deadline without threatening the books. If Gaborik moves and Mogilny walks (both likely, one forced, one natural), payroll drops to roughly $72.50M before any renewal, creating headroom for Iginla or whoever the summer target turns out to be.

**Draft capital is modest.** Toronto hold their own R1, R2, and R3. No incoming picks from other clubs are visible. Three own-round picks is adequate for a deadline purchase (a first or second buys most players) but thin for a rebuild. Protecting the R1 matters; using the R2 on a rental like Heatley or Jovanovski is the right kind of spend.

**Task #2 (Luongo monitoring):** Closed. Luongo is on the roster at 94 overall with 1 year remaining. No further monitoring needed until the July 2006 renewal window. DiPietro is irrelevant — we already have our franchise goalie.

## Calendar

The question is what we do between now and March 19 and then in July, and it answers itself on the standings: 42 points in 28 games puts us second in the East, and we buy. Ninety-eight days to the deadline, negotiations don't open until late February, so this is target selection and summer renewal planning, not urgent action.

**Luongo** at 95 overall, 91 base, $1.60M with one year left is the entire summer. Without a new deal he walks and we're Ouellet plus Tellqvist. Lock him on five years in July. Nothing else on this list matters as much.

**Chlup** at 19 with a full NHL season on his record and $2.34M expiring is a lock-five-or-six question. The coach already slots him at second- or third-line centre. If the GM believes the ceiling is there — and at 19 playing every night, he has the games — sign five years immediately. The alternative is two years and extend in 2008, which risks a bidding war at 21.

**Klesla** at 23, $0.90M, 26 MPG on both penalty-kill units, is the definition of the roster shape the manual wants: cheap, young, playing every night. Renew four or five years. His $0.90M is what a 23-year-old top-pairing blueliner costs and he is that.

**Ouellet** at 24, $0.90M, 81 base — the GM's February 2005 directive was "we do not want to use Ouellet as the only backup." If Luongo renews, Ouellet is the backup and two years is right. If the GM finds a 90+ backup on the market this summer, Ouellet moves at the deadline instead. Hold the decision until late February.

**Koltsov** at 24, $1.10M, is cheap depth the coach hasn't flagged. If he earns a regular role by February, renew three or four years. If he's still a healthy scratch by then, he's a deadline chip alongside Tucker.

**St. Jacques** at 25, $0.80M, is the same calculus as Koltsov: depth defenseman, cheap, young enough to keep or trade. Decide by February based on ice time.

**Spezza** at 22, $1.00M, is in trouble. The coach says he's at 4 MPG with morale at 79, in a negative spiral costing him 2 points on every grade. That's a trade chip by deadline unless the coach commits him to 10+ minutes, which at this stage of a playoff race he probably won't. His $1.00M and age-22 potential make him attractive to a rebuilding club. Target: move for a later pick at the deadline.

**Mogilny** at 36 and $5.50M is the payroll problem on this roster. The coach doesn't mention him, which tells you he isn't driving the lineup. At that age and salary, do not renew. Move him at the deadline for a pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic, or at minimum find a team to take half his contract.

**Tucker** at 30 and $1.30M expiring remains the designated chip, consistent with the GM's March 2005 call. He clears 80 on checking (81, per the coach's K2 note) so he qualifies for the over-80 expiring-pick mechanic. His best use is in a package that fills the coach's fourth-line gap: Tucker plus a later pick for a young winger or centre the club can keep.

**Draft picks.** The January 2005 note that we owned no pick better than a fourth-rounder no longer holds. We own our own R1 through R5 for the 2006 draft, all unencumbered. The R1 is the funding mechanism for the big package — Heatley or Kovalchuk — that was blocked last season. This changes the deadline board.

**The summer renewal cluster warning still applies.** Eleven players on four-year deals worth $37.40M all expire July 2009. Chlup and Klesla going onto four- or five-year deals in July 2006 would push their expiries into 2010 or 2011 and partially break the cluster. That's a second-order reason to give them the long term now.

## League scan

The question: who across the league should Toronto be targeting for March, given that our gaps are top-six scoring and a shutdown blue-liner, and that Gaborik's $11.90M scratched salary is the largest financial lever we have? The answer is a tiered list led by Atlanta's expiring stars, with Jovanovski as the best single-player upgrade on defense and Savard as the cheapest meaningful move.

**Heatley** at ATL is the clear priority. 91 overall_base, age 22, $1.60M expiring, and Atlanta sit at 22 points with league-lowest payroll and six expiring deals. They cannot re-sign him. He fills the top-six winger gap the Coach's scoring collapse has exposed. Package: Tucker plus R1. This is unchanged from December 8 tracking.

**Kovalchuk** (ATL, 89 overall_base, age 22, expiring) is the same logic on the opposite wing. If Atlanta won't do two deals with one club, or if Heatley's price has crept, he is the alternative. A club that cannot re-sign one elite 22-year-old cannot re-sign two.

**Jovanovski** (VAN, 89 overall_base, TOUG 93, CHKG 94, $2.30M expiring, age 29) remains the only player in the league above 90 on both toughness and checking. He fills the shutdown-D gap directly. VAN at 30 points with 13 expiring and $46.36M payroll will not keep him. The cost is Klesla plus R1, which is real.

**Savard** (ATL, 79 overall_base, FACE 87, 19 pts/22 GP, $1.00M expiring, age 28) closes the faceoff deficit for Tucker alone at zero draft cost. Richards at 70 FACE is the problem; Savard at 87 is the answer on the third line. Cheapest upgrade available.

**Vasicek** (CAR, 82 overall_base, FACE 80, 18 pts/22 GP, $0.40M expiring, age 25) is the value centre. CAR at 33 points with 14 expiring and $63.79M payroll must shed. Koltsov plus R3 nets a $0.70M saving and a centre two years younger than Savard with similar production.

**Hossa** (OTT, 89 overall_base, 86 displayed, 23 pts/25 GP, 18.5 MPG) is the best winger not confirmed expiring. Ottawa at 24 points with only 4 expiring is not yet a seller. If they crater through January, he moves. Track but do not pursue before late February.

**Havlat** (OTT, 87 overall_base, 90 displayed, 26 pts/25 GP) is equally productive but the same availability question. He and Hossa are the prize if Ottawa folds.

**Hartnell** (BUF, 79 overall_base, TOUG 91, CHKG 92, POTE 95, $1.10M expiring, age 23) is the developmental toughness piece. The coverage phase says we have 11 players at 80+ displayed toughness, so this is a depth upgrade, not a gap-fill. Alexeev plus R2 is the cost. Lower priority than the four above.

**Witt** (WSH, 80 overall_base, 17 pts/28 GP, 31.8 MPG, $1.70M) and **Yonkman** (WSH, 74 overall_base, 7 pts/28 GP, 19.8 MPG, POTE 89) remain the shutdown pair if the GM ever releases Eminger. WSH at 22 points with 5 expiring is a sell profile, but the Eminger gate makes this theoretical.

**Gaborik at $11.90M** is the biggest single lever we have. The Coach won't dress him, he's producing 0.47 pts/g in 17 games, and the trajectory phase warns his value collapses monthly. A desperate seller (LA at 20 pts, $15.21M profit, 6 expiring) might absorb his salary for a late pick plus a body. Even a zero-return dump frees 13.2% of payroll for the Luongo renewal and the 2009 cluster work.

## Trade construction

The question: what exact packages do we take to Atlanta, Vancouver, and Carolina when negotiations open in late February? We have three targets that address the three real gaps (top-six scoring, center depth, shutdown defense), and the pieces to pay for them are players the Coach already won't dress or who walk for nothing in July.

**Heatley** is the priority. At 22 years old with a 91 base and $1.60M on an expiring deal, he is the best player available on a club that cannot keep him. Atlanta sit at 22 points with $40.34M payroll, six expiring deals, and no path to re-signing any of their elite players. They need picks and bodies. Tucker at 30 with 92 CHKG gives them a veteran presence for what is effectively a development year, plus our first-rounder accelerates their rebuild. The payroll swing is $0.30M in our direction, noise against $36.12M in profit.

**Savard** at FACE 87 solves the center problem the Coach keeps circling without naming. Richards at 70 FACE is a liability in the draw; Savard at 87 with 19 points in 22 games is the answer on the third line at $1.00M. Koltsov is 0 games played this season, $1.10M expiring, POTE 94 but unused. Atlanta get a speed prospect (ACCE 96) plus a third-rounder for a player they lose for nothing in July. This runs simultaneously with the Heatley deal; the costs don't overlap.

**Jovanovski** is the defense answer, but he competes for the same first-round pick. If Heatley is done, Jovanovski costs Klesla plus the R2 instead. Klesla at 23 with POTE 97 and $0.90M expiring is a fair rental price for a 29-year-old the Canucks will lose anyway. Vancouver sit at 30 points with 13 expiring deals and cannot keep half their roster. Klesla's speed (88) and potential make him sellable even for them, which means they can flip him for a pick if they don't want him.

**If none of these land**, the coverage phase answer is the real answer: line Gaborik, run Koltsov and Fischer as the fourth line, put Roberts and Tucker on the penalty kill. The roster has the pieces; the Coach has not deployed them.

## Owed

**Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window** — this task is obsolete and I'm closing it.

Luongo is on Toronto. He arrived from Florida in January 2005, and the GM explicitly closed all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19: "Goalies are solved. Done." The February 2005 window this task was built around passed eight months ago. There is nothing left to monitor about his availability.

**DiPietro** returned zero rows from the current roster — he is either off the Islanders' roster or has been moved. NYI sit at 14-9-3, 33 points, a playoff team that would not be selling their young goalie regardless. Even if he were available, they are not a non-contender destination.

**What has changed** is the urgency around Luongo's contract, not his availability. He is at 95 overall, $1.60M, with 1 year remaining. Without a renewal in July 2006 he walks, and the backup is Ouellet at 81 base. That is a renewal task, not a trade-window task, and it belongs in the summer plan.

I am marking this item delivered as closed.

markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-12-11

Next game at PHI on Monday 12 December 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question: are our young players getting the games they've earned, given what they're producing and where they sit?

**Gaborik** is the clearest waste. He's 23, gets 22.6 MPG when he plays, and returns 0.47 pts/g in 17 games. That beats every other RW option: Alexeev is at 0.43 on 10.7 MPG, Upshall at 0.21 on 5.5. Yet Gaborik sits in the press box 11 of 28 games while Upshall dresses at 5.5 MPG. If we're going to dress a third RW, Gaborik's production per minute is double Upshall's.

**Spacek** at morale 76 is in the band that costs two points off every grade. He's 20, has played 6 games at 5.8 MPG, and scored 3 points. The 0.50 rate is fine on a tiny sample, but the real problem is the morale spiral: underused, depressed, playing worse because of the morale tax. Either dress him properly at 8-10 MPG or stop carrying him so he can reset.

**Spezza and Upshall** are the same story again. Spezza: 4 points in 22 games, 4.8 MPG, morale 82. Upshall: 4 points in 19 games, 5.5 MPG, morale 82. This is their second consecutive season at this level with no progression visible in the numbers. At 4.8 MPG the fourth line is not a development opportunity; it's a roster spot occupied by a warm body.

**Gardener** at 0 points in 19 games is beyond development. I recommended permanent scratch on December 8th and the GM took it, but he's still dressed and logging 3.2 MPG.

**Chlup, Nash, Chistov, Klesla** are all earning every minute they get. No issue.

## Development trends

The question this phase answers: which young players are improving fast enough to change our plans, and which are stalling despite getting games. The window runs from 12 October to today, so every trend is three months of real data.

**Chlup** at 19 is 0.70 pts/g on 21.5 MPG over 28 games. My April note called him the franchise centrepiece and the data confirms it: he is the best production-to-age on the roster and the minutes are climbing. No change. He is exactly where I want him.

**Nash** at 21 is 0.56 pts/g on 15.6 MPG over 28 games. Chistov at 22 is 0.59 on 20.5 MPG over the same 28 games. Both have earned top-six roles and neither needs a nudge. They are the proof that the development rotation works when a player is actually good.

**Richards** at 25 is the problem. 0.56 pts/g on 11.7 MPG over 28 games extends the three-season slide (1.08, 0.71, 0.54). His minutes are below what a 25-year-old top-six centre should carry. The offseason system-fit review is no longer a "nice to have" — it is the single most important planning item on the club.

**Alexeev** is at 0.35 pts/g over 21 games on 10.9 MPG. My November 17th note set a threshold: below 0.45 the dressing recommendation weakens. He is below it and heading the wrong direction (was 0.40 at 15 games, now 0.35 at 21). At 23, he is running out of rope as a development project.

**Jackman** at 24 is 0.59 pts/g over 28 games. My sell trigger sits at 0.55. He has dropped from 0.88 over 16 games in November to 0.59 now — the hot start is regressing but he is still above the trigger. Not there yet, but one more week of decline puts him on the sell list.

**Spezza, Upshall, Gardener** are the graveyard. Spezza at 22: 0.18 pts/g on 4.8 MPG over 22 games. Upshall at 22: 0.17 on 4.9 over 19. Gardener at 20: 0 points in 19 games on 2.5 MPG. All three confirm the young-player-minutes-collapse pattern. These are offseason decisions now: real camp audition or stop dressing.

**The veterans are defying age.** Sundin at 34: 0.70 pts/g on 23.6 MPG. Mogilny at 36: 0.67 on 23.2. Both are carrying top-minute loads and producing like players ten years younger. No decline to plan around.

**Colaiacovo** at 22 is 0.12 pts/g over 25 games on 12.6 MPG. Confirmed as the weakest regular D by a wide margin. The scratch recommendation from November 27th still stands.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy and no changes are needed. The top nine forwards and the top four defencemen are all at 97 or above, which means the results are doing their job. The only players below 90 are either depth men earning what their production buys, or Richards, whose gap is structural and already flagged.

**Richards** sits at 84 on 11.8 MPG with 15 points in 28 games. I've recommended promoting him twice this month and the GM passed both times. His morale has climbed from 78 to 84, so the bleeding stopped. His OVR sits in the 80s band (expecting roughly 17 MPG), leaving a 5-minute deficit that costs him two points off every grade. The structural decline finding (three straight seasons down) says more ice time alone won't fix his production, so I'm dropping the recommendation until there's a different reason to raise it. If morale dips back below 80, I'll bring it up again.

**Lundmark** at 84, 6.2 MPG, 3 points in 20 games on the third line. If his calibre puts him in the 70s band he expects around 10 MPG and he's 4 short, but he's not producing enough at 6.2 to earn the next shift. Leave it.

**Upshall, Spezza, Gardener** on the fourth line are all at 82 with 3-5 MPG and 4 points or fewer across 19-22 games. This is the young-forward minutes-collapse pattern: they got 13-17 MPG early, production didn't hold, minutes dropped, morale settled at 82. They're depth players at their current level and their morale is stable. Gardener I recommended scratching permanently on December 8th and the GM took it; he still shows 19 GP and 3.2 MPG because the save reflects season totals, not the last two games.

**No change for any unit before Philadelphia.**

## Role composition

The question this phase answers is whether our units are built from the right people for the jobs we're asking them to do, and whether the roster can actually fill every role we need.

**K2 is broken.** The second penalty kill unit reads 72 mean checking and 64 mean toughness. A kill unit needs 80+ mean checking as a floor, and K2 sits eight points below it. Klesla at 86 is the only one who clears the bar, and Kaberle at 72 doesn't belong on a kill. This is not a matchup problem, it's an arrangement problem that costs us goals every time it's on the ice.

**Tucker is the answer to K2.** He carries 81 checking and is the third-best checker on the roster. He's been scratched for development rotation, but our checking depth in the lineup is two deep: Jackman at 92 and Nash at 82. That's it. We cannot build a second kill unit with real teeth without him. Dress Tucker, slot him on K2 with Chlup or Jackman anchoring, and the checking mean jumps to the low 80s.

**L3 is soft for a checking line.** 71 mean checking, 63 toughness. Richards at 93 playmaking makes it a skilled unit but not a defensive one. If Tucker dresses, he belongs on L3 as the forward checker, which pulls it to 74 mean checking. Without him, L3 cannot match opposing second lines physically and we get hemmed in.

**No change to L1, L2, P1, P2.** L1 and L2 are well balanced with Jackman and Nash anchoring respectively. Both power-play units have speed, skill, and a faceoff taker (Sundin at 95 on P1, Chlup at 80 on P2). These are properly constructed.

**The roster gap is real.** We dress 31 skaters and only two of them check above 80. That means one checker per two lines at best, which forces K2 to be soft. This isn't fixable by shuffling. The GM's options are: accept that K2 is a weak kill and hope the PK structure compensates, or dress Tucker every night and accept one fewer development slot. If we want two functional kill units, we need a third 80+ checker.

## Opponent matchup

The question is whether we change anything for this specific Philadelphia club. The answer is no.

**The matchup math is simple.** We are 17-7-0 and they are 10-11-2. We lead the season series 2-0-0, 8 goals to 5. Their top scorer is Roenick at 84 OVR; our top man is Sundin at 92. Every line pairing favors us under auto-match: our first line faces their first, second faces second, and we have the higher-rated centre in each case.

**Their blue line is the game.** Seidenberg (74) has 61 CHKG and 53 TOUG. Giroux (64) on pair three is the weakest skater on the ice. Johnsson (76) and Slaney (66) are no better. They will try to walk the puck out and we should make them pay for it. Nash (87 CHKG, 92 TOUG) and Upshall (85 CHKG, 82 TOUG) can camp on their defenders all night. This is a forecheck game.

**Safronov is the one vulnerability.** At 68 OVR he sits on D2, which auto-pairs against their L2 (Roenick 84, Williams 92 SPEE). He has 90 CHKG to survive with, but Williams' speed will get behind him. Swapping our D3 (St. Jacques 66, McCabe 82) into that slot does not help; St. Jacques is worse than Safronov. The current order is correct.

**Esche at 74 in net is beatable.** Our power play sits at 8/26 (30.8%) and their PP is 9/107 (8.4%). Neither special teams unit will decide this. Even-strength skill and forechecking pressure will.

**Goalie: start Luongo.** At 95 OVR he is 21 points above Esche. The GM's standing order says to check the fatigue icon before I pull the trigger; I cannot see it from here. If he shows tired, Ouellet steps in as usual.

**Defense assessment (deliverable #1, game of Dec 12):** Jackman at 94/94/93 on speed/checking/toughness handles Gagne (92 SPEE, 93 AGGR) physically and wins it. Klesla's 59 ENDU is the usual concern but this is one game, not a stretch. Kaberle's 85 PASS against Roenick's 82 CHKG means he must move the puck quickly; if he holds it, Roenick will strip him. Safronov at 71 SPEE will be exposed by Williams (92 SPEE) on the rush; Kaberle needs to be the second defender on every transition. St. Jacques at 50 ENDU is a third-pair-only man and their L3 (Primeau 77, Brashear 74, Kallio 68) is manageable. McCabe at 84 CHKG is the best fit against Brashear (90 TOUG) and should not be pulled early.

No line changes. No scratches. No D pair reordering. Go all out.

## Owed

This is the standing job: after every game, assess our defencemen and update the end-of-season sell/keep list. Here's the read as of 28 games played, ahead of Monday's game at Philadelphia.

**Jackman** is the movement this week. He's at 17 points in 28 games, which is 0.61 pts/g. My 12-04 note had him at 0.68 at 25 games. He's scored zero points in the last three games (17 points at 25 games, 17 at 28). The decline is accelerating: his games 17-25 rate was 0.33, and games 26-28 are scoreless. My sell trigger is 0.55. He's 0.06 away. If he stays quiet three more games he hits it. At 86 OVR and $0.70M x 2 the card still looks fine to a buyer, which means the window is still open but narrowing. If he crosses the trigger before the deadline I'm back recommending a move; if he doesn't, the 0.70 salary makes him a keeper regardless of the season rate.

**Klesla** is unchanged from my 11-30 note. 10 points in 28 games is 0.36, up marginally from 0.35. Still in the sell window: 87 OVR, $0.90M expiring, the rate is invisible to a buyer. He hasn't dropped below 0.30, so no panic, but nothing has improved to close the window either.

**Colaiacovo** continues to slide. 3 points in 25 games is 0.12. My 11-27 note had him at 0.14 at 22 games; he's added zero points since then. Seven6 OVR, $1.40M x 4. This is the most expensive bad contract on the blue line. He's currently not dressed, which is right. He should go at season end by any means available.

**Safronov** at 68 OVR producing 5 points in 15 games on 21.4 MPG is the best value among the regulars at his level. 0.33 rate from a 68. Cheap, young, producing. Keep.

**Kaberle** only 9 games, 3 points, 0.33 rate. GM has made it clear he's a keeper. No change.

**St. Jacques** at 0 points in 10 games, 66 OVR, $0.80M expiring. Zero contribution. Expiring so no urgency, but he's the seventh D and shouldn't be in the picture.

**McCabe** at 3 games and 9.7 MPG for $3.00M x 3 is the odd man. If he's a veteran on the roster for emergency purposes only, fine. If there's a taker for three years and $3M who sees 82 OVR, take the meeting.

Summary of changes since my last delivery (December 8): Jackman's rate has fallen from 0.68 to 0.61 with three scoreless games, moving him closer to the sell trigger. Everything else holds.
