# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-12-08

Toronto 16-7-0, 40 pts after 27 games.

## Role coverage

The role-coverage question now: with the trade deadline 11 weeks away and Toronto at 16-7-0, which gaps are fixable with bodies already in the building and which require a move? The answer is that checking and faceoffs can be addressed internally, toughness is closed per the GM's standing order, and the one genuinely thin area that cannot be solved internally is depth faceoff coverage beyond one line.

**Checking.** Six players carry 80+ on shipped CHKG: Jackman 87, McCabe 86, Tucker 83, Fischer 82, Upshall 80, Roberts 86. Three of those six are not lined (Roberts, Tucker, Fischer). The Coach's L4 complaint (mean 70) is solvable: put Fischer (82 CHKG, 89 SPEE) on that unit. He's already recommended for Tuesday's NYI game. Tucker (83 CHKG) is the GM's chip and stays available but unplayable; Upshall (80) is already dressed. After Fischer slots in, L4 has at least two 80+ checkers and the Coach's gap closes without an acquisition.

**Faceoffs.** Only Sundin (90) clears 80 among lined players. Chlup at 75 is the next-best, Richards at 70, Gardener at 72. Wallin carries 83 FACE but sits unlined. Dressing Wallin on a third or fourth line gives a second 80+ faceoff man without spending a chip. Below him the drop-off to 75 is steep, and no internal body reaches 80. This is the one gap where the market is genuinely better than the roster, and the Bell target (FACE 88 or 82 depending on which reading is current; the Nov 26 note says 88 FACE, 82 TOUG) remains the cheapest external fix. The GM has not closed this target.

**Scoring and speed.** Both are deep on paper (11 and 25 at 80+ respectively) but the Coach has three 80+ scorers on the bench: Gaborik (92 scoring, 98 speed), Roberts (88), Abid (86). That is the Coach's call, not mine. I note it because if a lineup change is coming, the talent exists to raise the fourth line's ceiling from 70 to 80 without a trade.

**Durability.** Five players at 80+ INJU: Roberts 98, Afinogenov 95, Gardener 92, Fischer 92, Abid 90. Three of those five are not lined. If the playoff run shortens the rotation and injuries come, the durable bodies are on the bench. Spacek at 79 INJU is barely playing (6 GP in 25 games). This is a depth-injury-cover issue, not a starting-role gap.

**Toughness.** Zero at 80+ on shipped grades. The GM closed all toughness targets on December 4 based on displayed grades showing 11 players above 80. I accept that ruling. I note for the record that the gap exists on stored grades and will resurface on a cold-form day.

**Age.** Jackman (24), McCabe (30), Upshall (22) are the current top checkers, all young enough to keep. The toughness "fix" via form is temporary by nature. Sundin (34) and Mogilny (36) are the engine and will need succession planning by next deadline. Nothing here changes the February approach.

## Trajectory

The question this phase answers: does Toronto's contract structure and age curve protect the next three seasons, and where does it threaten to collapse? The answer is the shape is strong but two specific failures — Gaborik's contract and the July 2006 renewal week — could unravel it if not handled by deadline and that summer respectively.

**Gaborik** is the single largest structural problem. $11.90M/year through July 2010 on a healthy scratch who has 8 points in 17 games. Mid-contract renegotiation is impossible. Every month he sits undressed his trade value decays, and the October memory warned that January 2006 is the point where that decay bites. At 23 with POTE 90 he is still tradeable — a contending team needing a right-wing power forward would take him — but by March he is a fire-sale piece if no deal happens before. The alternative is carrying $59.50M of dead money through 2010, which poisons every renewal summer in between.

**July 2006 renewal week** carries nine contracts worth $15.44M. Three are non-negotiable: **Chlup** (19, POTE 95, 20 points in 27 GP at $2.34M), **Luongo** (26, POTE 97, $1.60M), and **Spezza** (22, POTE 99, $1.00M). These are the spine of the next five years. Luongo goes first because Tellqvist behind him is a POTE 91 step down. Chlup next at 19 with 20 points already. Then Spezza, who needs real minutes this season so he develops into a player worth extending. The remaining six are peripheral; Tucker and Koltsov can walk, Ouellet is depth, St. Jacques and Klesla are role players at $0.80–0.90M who are replaceable.

**The 2009 cluster** is the slow-burning trap. Eleven players on four-year deals worth $37.40M all come up at once: Sundin, Richards, Chistov, Afinogenov, Kaberle, Nash, Alexeev, Upshall, Colaiacovo, Abid, Wallin. That is a renewal summer that will force impossible choices. The fix is to begin extending the ones you are certain about — Richards (25, POTE 88), Chistov (22, POTE 95), Nash (21, POTE 95) — in July 2007, pulling them out of the 2009 wave.

**The age curve is healthy.** Thirteen players at 23 or under, sixteen at 24-29. The 30-33 hole (McCabe 30, Tucker 30) does not matter because the young core is deep. Three veterans at 34+ (Sundin, Mogilny, Roberts) are all on short deals and will walk naturally within two seasons.

**Money is not the constraint.** Payroll $89.94M against revenue $73.59M leaves a gap, but profit is $35.56M after TV and prestige income. There is room to absorb a $5-7M addition (the Iginla-class target from prior analysis) without turning the club unprofitable. The answer to the GM's October 16 question is: keep the good players and rotate them. The problem is Gaborik specifically, not the roster's payroll depth.

**Draft capital is thin.** Three picks (R1, R2, R3, all from Toronto). Enough to sweeten a deadline package or a July renewal compensation, but not enough to be a buyer at the March deadline without giving a major piece.

## Calendar

**Are we buyers or sellers at the deadline, and what do we do with the nine expiring players in July?** We are buyers at the deadline — second in the East on 40 points with eight teams making the playoffs — but the deadline action and the summer action are one plan: two salary dumps (Mogilny, Tucker) fund two acquisitions (a checker, a faceoff center), and the summer is a clean re-signing list with no cuts.

**Mogilny** is the deadline's biggest decision. He is 36 on $5.50M, expiring, with 16 points in 27 games. That's productive enough to attract a contender but too expensive and too old to re-sign. He must move by March 19 or we lose $5.50M of rental value for nothing. Last season's attempted Jackman package was the template; this season we need to find a contender short a right wing who will give a pick or a young player for one more year of Mogilny. Even a third-rounder plus a cheap depth piece beats zero.

**Tucker** is already the designated chip (GM, March 19 2005: "Only trading chips left are Tucker and the 4th round pick"). At 30 on $1.30M expiring, he is second-wave deadline currency. He funds the toughness target.

**Chlup** is 19 and on the expiring list because it is his entry contract ending, not because he is leaving. He is 82 base with FACE 80, CHKG 79, TOUG 79, 87 displayed today. Re-sign him on 5-6 years at the first opportunity the game allows (next contract year, when he becomes eligible). He is the franchise center alongside Sundin's eventual handoff. This is the single most important renewal on the sheet.

**Luongo** is 26, $1.60M, and the number-one goalie. The GM closed the goalie file in March 2005: "Goalies are solved." Renew on 5 years. This is non-negotiable and simple.

**Spezza** is 22, POTE 99, $1.00M, but stuck at 4.6 MPG and 0.21 pts/g in 19 games per the coach. The problem is usage, not the player. Give him third-line minutes before the deadline; renew him 5 years in the summer once he shows the POTE. If he is still 4.6 MPG in February, he becomes a development trade target rather than a renewal.

**Koltsov** is 24, $1.10M, flagged by the coach as below the 0.45 pts/g threshold. He is tradeable now. In November 2005 I proposed him as the return in a Vasicek package for CAR. He is the natural package component: a cheap underperformer we will not re-sign, going to a team that needs depth wings. Move him before the deadline as part of a Savard or Vasicek deal.

**Klesla** is 23, D, POTE 97, $0.90M. The GM's February 2005 order protects Eminger and McCabe specifically, not Klesla. In November I proposed him as the return for Jovanovski (VAN) and for Kurka (CAR). His POTE 97 makes him the best defense chip we own. Either he becomes a long-term defenseman or he buys a top-pairing piece; keeping him as a third-pairing 23-year-old with POTE 97 wastes his trade value. Decision at February when targets are priced.

**Ouellet** is 24, $0.90M, 8 games. He is the backup. With Belfour gone and Luongo locked, renew Ouellet on 2 years. He is cheap and provides playoff cover.

**St. Jacques** is 25, $0.80M, D, 0 points in 9 games. He is a seventh defenseman. Renew at current rate or let go; it does not matter. Low priority either way.

**The deadline plan (opens late February):**

1. Mogilny goes to a contender short on right wing. Target: a mid-round pick plus a cheap young player, or a specific need-fill.
2. Tucker + Koltsov fund a single acquisition. **Savard** (ATL, C, 28, FACE 87, 79 overall_base, $1.00M expiring) is the faceoff fix the coach needs on L3. ATL at 16 points with second-lowest payroll cannot re-sign him. Package: Koltsov plus either St. Jacques or a 4th. ATL gets a cheap wing and a depth D for their rebuild.
3. **Hartnell** (BUF, LW, 23, TOUG 91, CHKG 92, POTE 95, 79 overall_base, $1.10M expiring) is the checking fix the coach needs on L4. Package: Tucker plus a 4th. BUF gets a veteran wing for their own playoff push at $1.30M. If the 4th is not enough, add Mogilny as a third piece (BUF gets their RW for a year).

The problem is pick capital. The "no picks beyond a 4th" finding from January 2005 still stands. Every package must be player-funded. That makes Tucker, Koltsov, Mogilny, and possibly St. Jacques the only currency. Four moving parts, two acquisitions. It works if the buyers accept players over picks.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: who across thirty clubs can fill Toronto's one genuine external gap (faceoff depth) and replace the Gaborik RW slot before March, and what does each cost? The answer is that Atlanta's collapse puts the two best options in the league on the same expiring list at $1.10M each, and the faceoff gap closes with a Tucker-only package.

**Heatley** (ATL, RW, 22, 91 overall\_base, $1.10M expiring, 23 pts/25 GP, 23.1 MPG) is the primary target. He fills the Gaborik right-wing role at a ninth of the salary, is 22, carries CHKG 86 and SPEE 96, and sits on the lowest-payroll club in the league ($40.34M) with six expiring deals at 20 points. ATL cannot re-sign all three of Heatley, Kovalchuk and Savard at any price. They will move at least two by March.

**Kovalchuk** (ATL, LW, 22, 89 overall\_base, $1.10M expiring, 27 pts/25 GP, 23.6 MPG) is the alternative if ATL refuses Heatley or prices him too high. 27 goals and assists in 25 games leads the club, SPEE 99. Same contract, same seller logic. If both are available, take Heatley because the RW slot is what's broken; Gaborik's absence leaves no right wing behind Mogilny.

**Savard** (ATL, C, 28, 79 overall\_base, FACE 87, $1.00M expiring, 21 pts/25 GP, 22.5 MPG) is the faceoff fix the coverage phase identified as the one gap the market solves better than the roster. 87 FACE with 21 points makes him a legitimate second-line centre, not a specialist. He's 28 so his ceiling is set, but we need a faceoff man now. Tucker alone ($1.40M, 83 CHKG, 30 years old, the GM's declared chip) is a reasonable package because ATL gets an expiring asset of similar value without touching a pick.

**Havlat** (OTT, LW, 23, 87 overall\_base, $0.90M expiring, 25 pts/24 GP, 21.0 MPG) is the best value on the board. 87 base at $0.90M with 25 points is absurd, and at 23 with POTE 86 he has years left. The problem is OTT: 23 points in 23 games is .500, not desperate, $59.27M payroll with $20.23M profit gives them room, and only 4 players expiring. They may keep him. Ask anyway because his salary at renewal will triple and they may prefer picks over a $3-4M commitment.

**Drury** (BUF, LW, 25, 89 overall\_base, FACE 81, $2.00M expiring, 23 pts/25 GP, 22.1 MPG) is unique: a top-six scorer who takes draws. 89 base with 81 FACE and 23 points fills two gaps at once. The constraint is that BUF at 24 points with only 5 expiring is not a clear seller. Less likely than ATL targets but worth an ask in February.

**Bouwmeester** (FLA, D, 22, 81 overall\_base, POTE 96, $1.20M expiring, 10 pts/20 GP, 33.0 MPG) is the best developmental defense target. 81 base at 22 with POTE 96 on 33 minutes a night is a franchise-D profile. FLA at 27 points and $57.33M payroll are not desperate, but they carry 5 expiring and have other youth on the back end. Monitor whether they drift below .450; if they do, he becomes the top D target for July.

**Hartnell** (BUF, LW, 23, 79 overall\_base, CHKG 90, POTE 95, $1.10M expiring, 9 pts/25 GP, 18.1 MPG) remains the best checking prospect. The coverage phase says Fischer (82 CHKG) closes the L4 gap internally, so Hartnell is insurance, not a fix. Keep him on the board in case Fischer's numbers don't hold by February.

**Daze** (CHI, LW, 30, 89 overall\_base, $3.00M expiring, 29 pts/26 GP, 22.3 MPG) has the best production on any seller — 29 points in 26 games. But he turns 30 in July 2005, carries $3.00M, and at POTE 78 his ceiling is set. He fills a gap we have for two years of a 30-year-old on an expiring deal when our timeline is Chlup, Spezza, and a young core. I would not pursue him.

**Doan** (PHX, RW, 27, 87 overall\_base, CHKG 85, $2.40M expiring, 14 pts/20 GP, 19.8 MPG) was the October target. His CHKG has fallen from 91 to 85 and his displayed overall is 79. At $2.40M with 0.70 pts/g and POTE 78, he is not the same value he was. PHX is a clear seller (19 pts, 9 expiring) but the price does not match the production. Off the board.

**Gaborik's $11.90M** constrains every package. ATL's $40.34M payroll is the league's lowest; they cannot absorb his salary even in a lopsided return. The packages above work because the outgoing assets (Tucker, picks, Alexeev, Koltsov) carry total value without the salary mismatch. Gaborik needs a separate destination — a big-payroll club like NYR ($92.95M) or COL ($66.38M) — and that is a distinct negotiation, not a sweetener for an ATL deal.

The Luongo/DiPietro goalie-monitoring task (#2) was closed by the GM's March 19 standing order: "Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks." I am treating it as delivered by closure.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: what concrete package does Toronto send to Atlanta before late February, and what do they send back? The deadline is 11 weeks away, ATL's three stars are all expiring on a 20-point team with the league's lowest payroll at $40.34M, and Toronto's one structural gap (right wing behind Mogilny) has a name, a number, and a price tag.

**Heatley for Tucker + R1** is the primary proposal. ATL gets a 30-year-old with 83 CHKG they can use for 30 games or flip to a contender themselves, plus the first round pick that a 20-point team will likely have at 4-8 overall. Tucker's $1.30M is expiring, so ATL commits nothing past June. Heatley is 91 base at 22, $1.10M, and Toronto re-signs him in July as a franchise right winger for the next decade. Net payroll: TOR saves $0.20M; ATL adds $0.20M on the league's lowest budget, trivial.

**Savard for Koltsov + St. Jacques** is the cheap insurance deal if the GM decides faceoffs need an external fix despite Wallin (FACE 83) being dressable internally. Koltsov ($1.10M, expiring, 0 GP) plus St. Jacques ($0.80M, expiring, 0 GP) totals $1.90M outgoing against Savard's $1.00M, so TOR saves $0.90M. ATL gets two expiring bodies they can use or release, no draft cost to them. The risk is ATL wants a pick even for this; if so, drop St. Jacques and add R3.

**Kovalchuk for Tucker + R1** is the identical alternative if ATL names Heatley untouchable. Kovalchuk is 89 base, 27 points in 25 games, same contract, same seller logic. The package is unchanged because the value ATL extracts is the pick and the body, not our assessment of which 22-year-old they keep.

**What if none land.** Wallin closes faceoffs internally. Fischer (82 CHKG) closes checking. Mogilny (16 pts/27 GP, $5.50M expiring) and Roberts (8 GP, $4.90M, 39 years old) free cap space in July naturally. The club survives to March without Atlanta, but the RW slot remains a hole that Gaborik must fill by playing, which the last 17 games say he will not. The fallback is Gaborik himself: if he produces at 0.50+ through January, his trade value rises and a February swap for a contending club's expiring RW becomes possible. If he doesn't, $11.90M of dead money through 2010 is the cost of not moving him in July.

## Owed

**Item #2: Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window.**

**Luongo** is on our roster. The monitoring task from January is complete: you closed all goalie trade monitoring on March 19 after confirming "Keeping him and Luongo as two 90+ goalies for the playoffs." He is here, playing, and performing. At 11 GP, 8-3, 1.89 GAA, .933 SV%, 91 base / 94 displayed, $1.60M.

**DiPietro** has played 22 games at NYI, 11-10, 2.61 GAA. He sits at 86 displayed / 79 base, $1.10M expiring. He is not a high-90s goalie and was never a realistic target under the January 15 standing order ("fetch a really good high-90s goalie from a team that will not be a contender"). That goal was Luongo himself, and Luongo is already ours.

What has changed since the task was closed: **Luongo's contract now reads 1 year.** He was acquired during 2004-05 with 2 years left; now 1 year remains. That converts a closed monitoring task into an open renewal question. The January 15 goal is met (he IS the high-90s goalie from a non-contender), but keeping him requires a new deal at renewal. Tellqvist at 77 base, age 24, 6 years left is the development hedge the GM identified, but at 73 displayed today he is not a backup for a playoff run, let alone a replacement.

No further monitoring is needed. The task delivered what it was designed to deliver.

# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-12-08

Next game vs PIT on Saturday 10 December 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether each young player is getting the games he's earned, and three cases stand out this week.

**Gardener** is at 0 points in 18 games on 3.0 MPG. This is the collapse pattern confirmed: no production, no minutes, no path. I recommended a permanent scratch on November 24th and again December 4th, and he played 2 more games scoring zero since the last recommendation. At 20 with a POTE of 98, he has the talent profile, but 18 games of nothing is the answer to whether he's earned more ice time. He hasn't.

**Spezza** (4.2 MPG, 4 pts in 21 GP, morale 79) and **Upshall** (4.8 MPG, 4 pts in 18 GP, morale 79) are both in the same negative spiral. Morale in the 70s costs two points on every grade, which makes them less effective, which keeps them on the fourth line, which keeps morale low. Neither is going to break out of this at 4 minutes a night on the fourth line. The GM needs to decide: accept them as depth and live with the morale drag, or stop dressing them so the ice time goes to someone who'll use it. POTE of 99 on both is a scouting opinion, not a claim on a roster spot.

**Gaborik** is scratched despite producing 0.47 pts/g on 22.6 MPG when he plays. Seventeen games out of 27 available means he's missed 10, and when he's on the ice he gets first-line-caliber minutes. If he's physically available, he belongs in the lineup ahead of Upshall or Spezza. This is the clearest development waste: a 23-year-old winger at 22 minutes a night when he plays, sitting in the press box.

**Chlup**, **Nash**, **Chistov**, and **Klesla** are all dressed every game at full workload. No development concern. **Alexeev** is at 0.40 pts/g on 10.9 MPG in 20 games; my trigger is 25 games before reassessing, so hold.

## Development trends

Which of our young players are actually growing, and which are stalling while we hand them games anyway. This matters now because we are 27 games in and the trends are separating permanently: some of these guys are keepers, some are wasting roster spots we could give to someone else.

**Chlup** at 0.73 pts/g on 21.4 MPG in 27 games. His peak was 0.88 when he was playing 18 minutes a night; the rate dipped as he picked up a full top-line load and the defensive responsibilities that come with it. A 19-year-old centre at 0.73 on 21.4 MPG is a franchise piece. No concern.

**Chistov** has doubled his production from last season's 0.29 to 0.58 on 20.9 MPG at age 22. That is a genuine step forward, not a hot streak in a small sample. He has earned the role he is getting.

**Hainsey** at 0.37 pts/g on 20.9 MPG in 19 games. He took Colaiacovo's minutes in November and immediately separated himself. 0.37 against Colaiacovo's 0.12 is the entire argument made in two numbers. Hainsey is the keeper at that position.

**Nash** is recovering. After bottoming at 0.43 in the last window, he is back to 0.58 pts/g on 15.3 MPG across 27 games. The system-fit concern I raised in March is resolving.

**Alexeev** is the one I flagged and the one who needs attention now. Last season he scored 0.55 pts/g as a scratch. I tracked the fall to 0.40 in November on 11.7 MPG and set 0.45 as the threshold for keeping him dressed. He is now at 0.32 on 11.2 MPG. He has fallen through the floor. Twenty games is a fair sample, and the trend is not a blip. I would stop dressing him and give that spot to a young forward who is actually growing, like Stahle or a call-up, or to a veteran depth option.

**Colaiacovo** remains at 0.12 pts/g in 25 games on 12.6 MPG. I recommended scratching him on November 27th and he is still in the lineup. Hainsey's 0.37 is the direct upgrade at the same position. This is the same recommendation: scratch Colaiacovo, keep Hainsey.

**Spezza** at 0.19 on 4.2 MPG and **Upshall** at 0.18 on 4.1 MPG are both season-lost. Their ice time collapsed and never recovered. Neither has a path back this season. The only decision left is whether to dress them at all or free a roster spot for someone else.

**Gaborik** at 0.47 pts/g on 22.6 MPG in only 17 games is underwhelming for a 23-year-old top-nine winger with high potential. The injury-shortened sample gives him the benefit of the doubt, but if this holds past 25 games he is developing below his projection.

**Jackman** is the sell-watch story. He peaked at 0.88 in October, I reversed the sell call, and set 0.55 as the trigger. He is now at 0.62 over 27 games and trending down. Three more bad games puts him at the trigger and back on the sell list. I am watching him weekly.

**Richards** at 0.54 pts/g on 12.0 MPG is the confirmation of the system-fit problem I flagged last spring. Three consecutive seasons of decline: 1.08, 0.71, now 0.54, at age 25 with no injury. His minutes are 5 MPG below what his grade band expects, which compounds the morale cost. This is not a slump, it is a structural problem in how we use him.

**Afinogenov** tells the same story: 1.17, then 0.73, now 0.65. He is getting 17.9 MPG so the role is not the issue. Same system-fit flag as Richards, both confirmed across a full additional season.

**Sundin** at 0.69 pts/g on 23.9 MPG at age 34 is not declining. He is the most reliable player on the roster and is defying age entirely.

**Mogilny** at 0.62 pts/g on 23.7 MPG at age 36 is remarkable but it is a planning problem. We are relying on a 36-year-old for a top-six role. If he dips next season we have no one ready to step into that spot.

**Roberts** at 0.29 pts/g in 8 games on 13.7 MPG at 39 is winding down as expected. No concern, no surprise.

**Koltsov**, **Wallin**, **Abid** and **Tucker** have not played. Koltsov and Tucker are the GM's explicit non-trade items, so nothing to do here. Abid not playing despite my prior note about his 0.84 pts/g mismatch is strange; if he is healthy, he should be in the lineup somewhere.

## Morale watch

The room is climbing. Most of the roster sits in the 90s with positive momentum, and the deeper numbers are stabilizing after a bad stretch in late November. One player's gap between what he earns and what he's expected is still costing us on the scoresheet.

**Richards** is at 84 morale on 12.1 minutes a night. At his calibre he expects around 20 a night. That's an 8-minute deficit, and the -1 it costs every grade is the same structural problem I flagged in October when he sat at 78. He's recovered to 84 with the wins but the minutes haven't moved. He's 14 points in 27 games on the third line. He deserves more of the game, and the only way to get him out of the 80s is to put him there.

**Luongo** at 79 is the backup goalie situation, not a line problem. 11 games, spec-only role, morale in the 70s costing -2. Nothing I can do with a line assignment fixes that.

**McCabe** at 79, two games played, 10.5 minutes. He's a 30-year-old depth defenceman barely dressing. His morale is what you'd expect from a man who isn't playing. The GM controls his role through roster construction.

**Spezza, Upshall, Gardener** are all at 79, all on 3-5 MPG on the fourth line. This is the known collapse pattern. They're below their 7-MPG expectation but the morale is holding at the floor, not sliding further. No intervention this week.

**Spacek** at 76, scratched, is the lowest number on the sheet but climbing. He scored 3 in 6 before losing his spot. Let him stabilize.

Everyone else is 90+ and rising. No other action needed.

## Role composition

**The core problem: Richards is on the wrong line.** A 93-playmaking centre with 77.6% faceoffs should not be taking 12 minutes a night on the third line while Chlup, also 19, handles the second line at 20.9 MPG. Richards played all 27 games, so this is deployment, not availability. Swapping them puts Richards where his skill belongs and gives Chlup a softer matchup for development.

**Richards at 93 playmaking and 77.6% draws belongs on the second line at 17+ MPG.** He is the roster's best playmaker after Sundin (96) and tied with Chistov (93), yet runs a 12.1 MPG third-line slot behind a line whose best forward (Alexeev) gets 10.9 MPG of his own. The role fit is wrong and the minutes deficit has been compounding since October.

**Chlup to L3 centre is a development move.** At 19 with 79.5% faceoffs, he can win draws against bottom-six centers and grow into the role without being matched against top-pair opposition every night. The GM has kept Chlup on L2 all season, which I respect, but the reason to move him down is different from pushing him up: it is about the opponent he faces, not the quality of his linemates.

**Lundmark on P1 is a filler spot.** He gets 6.2 MPG even strength in 19 games and somehow holds a first-unit PP slot. Nash at 82 checking and 15.4 MPG is the better half-wall presence, and he is not taking draws on the PP so his faceoff deficiency is irrelevant. Swap Nash onto P1 in Lundmark's place.

**The fourth line is a roster gap.** Gardener at 3.0 MPG in 18 games, Spezza 4.2 in 21, Upshall 4.8 in 18. That is 12 total minutes split three ways against opponents who ice a 15-minute fourth line. I cannot fix this by rearranging anyone; the bodies do not exist on this roster. Against Pittsburgh's depth, this is a structural loss.

**K2 penalty kill has no teeth.** Checking mean 71, carried by Klesla who already plays 26 MPG. Tucker at 81 checking and Roberts at 84 are both scratched by the GM's development policy. The second kill needs a body who can actually check, and we do not have one unless the GM reinstates Tucker for it.

## Opponent matchup

The question is whether PIT's first line or any specific matchup forces a lineup change, and the answer is no.

**PIT's defence is thin.** Melichar is out until December 17th. That leaves Rozsival (74) and Salminen (70) on their first pair, Lupaschuk (70) with an unknown partner on the second, and Pushor (65) and Hnidy (63) on the third. Our second and third lines are facing 65-70 defencemen all night. No change is needed to exploit this because the auto-pairing already does it: our second line (Chlup/Nash/Afinogenov) faces that thinned second pair, and our third (Richards/Lundmark/Alexeev) gets Pushor and Hnidy.

**Their first line is the only real threat.** Lemieux at 85 with his hands clearly in form (PASS 93, DEKG 92, SHPW 87) alongside Straka at 83 with similar hand readings. They will generate something. Our first pair (Jackman at 94 checking, Klesla at 99 speed) is built to handle them. Their centres are soft on draws: Lemieux 62, Beech 61, Holzinger 50, Morozov 50. We win faceoffs on every single line tonight, which keeps our defenders from being scrambled before they set.

**PIT's power play is 12 on 112 attempts, 10.7%.** They cannot score short-handed against us, and their 3.30 goals-against per game means they are leaking chances all game. Our PP at 32% (8 on 25) should find looks against that blue line.

**Goalie: start Luongo.** His 94 OVR against a 2.60 offence is not a close call. The brief shows no fatigue flag on him.

**D review (standing obligation #1):** Jackman and Klesla get the Lemieux/Straka line all night, which is the hardest assignment we face this week and the right pairing for it. Their matchup tonight is favorable for us despite the challenge. Safronov's 90 checking is well suited to facing Lefebvre's puck-carrying second line. McCabe on the third pair against Holzinger's third line (65 OVR checking, 50 faceoff) is a comfortable shift. No reason to alter the defensive pair slot order for Saturday.

## Owed

The standing job: how our defencemen played, and who goes at season's end.

**Klesla** — rate has dropped from 0.35 (23 games, November 30th) to 0.33 (27 games, 9 points). He added one point in four games. The sell floor is 0.30; four goalless games puts him below it, which is roughly one week of hockey. The card still shows 87 OVR and $0.90M expiring, which is what a buyer sees, but every empty night tightens the window. Maximum urgency on a trade before the deadline. Nothing has materially changed in his situation, just the clock ticking.

**Jackman** — 17 points in 27 games for 0.63 pts/g. Down from 0.68 at 25 games (two scoreless nights). My sell trigger is 0.55; he's still eight hundredths above it. The recommendation stands: keeps. If he goes cold through December he'll cross it eventually, but not today.

**Colaiacovo** — 0 goals, 3 points in 25 games. 0.12 pts/g. Zero offensive contribution from a 22-year-old on 12.3 MPG. My scratch recommendation from November 27th looks more correct every game he suits up. He goes at season's end. This hasn't changed; it's just confirmed further.

**McCabe** — 81 OVR, $3.00M x 3 years, 2 games played, 10.5 MPG. Carrying third-pairing ice on top-pair money. He's not on the current sell list because I haven't raised it this year, but $3.00M x 3 for a healthy scratch is the sort of contract that needs moving this summer. I'll formally add him to the summer list if the GM wants.

**No change** to the rest. Koltsov is a keeper per the GM. Fischer is a keeper per the GM. Kaberle is a keeper per the GM. St. Jacques is expiring at $0.80M with 66 OVR and zero points in 9 games — he's gone by default, no action needed. Eminger at $2.20M x 4 with 7 games played is untradeable and locked; nothing to do there.

The one actionable item: Klesla's sell window is three to four games from closing. Move him or watch the card become a problem instead of an asset.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-12-04
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-12-04

Toronto 15-6-0, 38 pts after 25 games.

## Role coverage

The toughness gap that has driven our target list since February does not exist. The queries show **Jackman** at 93 TOUG shown (89 stored, age 24), **Nash** at 92 (88, age 21), **Roberts** at 90 (92, age 39), **Tucker** at 85 (88, age 30), and seven more at 80+. The February 24 role coverage that reported "0 at 80+" was wrong. We have eleven players above 80 on displayed toughness. This kills the case for Hartnell (BUF, 93/94) and Kurka (CAR, 88/90) as toughness fixes, which means the package currency spent chasing them should go elsewhere or nowhere.

**Faceoffs** are the real thin role. Only Sundin (95) and Wallin (88) sit above 80 on displayed FACE. Chlup is at 80 at 19, Richards at 78. Sundin is 34 with one year left; when he goes, nobody draws reliably on L1. This is a one-to-two-year cliff, not a tonight problem, but it is the only role where we have a genuine void on the horizon.

**Scoring and playmaking** are deep today but top-heavy by age. Mogilny 94 PASS at 36, Sundin 91 at 34, Roberts 88 at 39. Gaborik (92 PASS, 23, $11.90M) is not lined. Afinogenov (87, 26) is the only young playmaker already contributing. The club needs Gaborik back on a line or traded; at $11.90M dead he is the largest financial problem on the roster.

**Checking** is covered with six players at 80+ on displayed CHKG (Jackman 94, Nash 87, Safronov 90, Tucker 89, Fischer 87, Upshall 85). The coach's "one elite checker" flag is about a forward who plays physical on the PK, not about a raw grade shortage. Nash at 92 TOUG and 87 CHKG on the wing is the best fit for K2 duty, which is what he proposed.

**Depth on defence** is where development matters most. Jackman (24) and Eminger (22) are the future top pair. McCabe (30) and Fischer (25) fill minutes. Klesla (23, 87 overall) is tradeable. Stahle (21) and Safronov (24) are depth. The benching of Colaiacovo for Stahle is correct at 0.13 pts/g.

## Trajectory

Is this club aging into a cliff, and is its money arranged sensibly? The age curve is healthy; the contract calendar is not, and the money is bleeding on one player who doesn't play.

**The shape is fine.** Toronto carry 13 players aged 23 or under, 16 aged 24-29, only 2 aged 30-33, and 3 aged 34+. That sits close to the manual's target of 5 veterans and 20 young players. The three veterans above 34 cost $18.80M combined (Sundin $8.40M, Mogilny $5.50M, Roberts $4.90M) for 34 points between them this season. Mogilny at 36 and Roberts at 39 are done; Mogilny walks in July 2006 at $5.50M, Roberts in July 2007 at $4.90M. That's $10.40M of salary relief the club can bank. Sundin at 34 is still producing 18 points in 25 games, but his 4-year deal runs through July 2009 when he'll be 38.

**Gaborik is the emergency.** He costs $11.90M a year through July 2010, which is 13.2% of total payroll, and the Coach scratched him. 8 points in 17 games at 23 years old, POTE 90. His trade value was highest when he scored 87 points last season and drops every month he sits. The memory from October flagged this: by January 2006, undressed, his value has cratered further. Mid-contract renegotiation is impossible, so there is no lever except a trade. The March deadline is the window. If he is still on the roster after March, this is $47.60M of dead money through 2010 with no path to reduce it.

**The July 2009 cliff is the structural problem.** Eleven players worth $37.40M expire simultaneously: Richards (then 29, $6.70M), Chistov (25, $5.00M), Kaberle (28, $4.10M), Nash (24, $3.90M), Eminger (24, $2.20M), Alexeev (25, $1.50M), Upshall (25, $1.50M), Colaiacovo (25, $1.40M), Wallin (28, $1.40M), Abid (28, $1.30M), and Sundin (38, $8.40M). This is the entire young core plus Sundin all hitting the market the same week. Since no mid-contract renegotiation exists, the only way to flatten this curve is to trade members of the 4-year cluster before it arrives. Upshall (0.21 pts/g, 4.6 MPG, Coach wrote him off), Wallin (0 GP, 0 pts), and Alexeev (0.31 rate, declining) are the first three to move. Each one traded before 2009 removes $1.30M-$1.50M from the renewal bill and frees a roster spot for a cheaper replacement.

**July 2006 is the next urgent window.** Nine contracts worth $15.44M expire. Two are must-locks: **Luongo** at $1.60M, 26, POTE 97, the clear number-one goalie. **Chlup** at $2.34M, 19, 18 points in 25 games, POTE 95, the franchise centre. Both are cheap right now and both need 5-6 year deals the week they open. Behind them, Mogilny ($5.50M, 36) should walk, which is good. Klesla (23, 9 pts in 25 GP, POTE 97, $0.90M) is a third renewal worth considering or a trade chip, but not both.

**The money picture is strained by Gaborik, not by the roster.** Payroll $89.94M against revenue $71.92M leaves $18.02M of spending above hockey revenue, covered by TV, prestige and attendance income that put profit at $36.02M. Remove Gaborik's $11.90M and payroll drops to $78.04M, within $6M of revenue. That single trade fixes the financial profile for three seasons.

**Draft capital is thin.** Three picks: first, second, third round, all Toronto's own. The fourth was traded in March. That is enough to sweeten one meaningful acquisition but not enough to run two rebuild-style packages. Every target from the November and December notes (Jovanovski, Hartnell, Vasicek) demands at least a first or second. The club cannot pursue two of them and also re-sign Luongo and Chlup without giving up a player the Coach values.

## Calendar

The deadline is 105 days away and we are second in the East at 38 points, 10 clear of ninth-place Montreal. We are buying at the deadline, not selling. The summer problem is the reverse: nine contracts expire, three of them are keepers, and one of them (Gaborik) cannot expire because it runs to 2010.

**Gaborik** is the single biggest deadline task. He carries $11.90M for five years through July 2010 at 91 overall_base but produced 8 points in 17 games before going into the current stretch. Any team taking that salary is either desperate or being paid in picks and prospects to take it. The November finding was clear: move him by March or carry $47.60M of dead money for four more seasons. This is harder than a normal trade because he is not expiring, so the over-80 pick mechanic does not apply. The only path is a multi-team or salary-dump package where we attach a pick or young player to make the money work.

**Mogilny** at 90 overall_base, age 36, $5.50M, one year left, is the textbook over-80 expiring pick recovery. Trade him at the deadline for a draft pick. He fills no long-term role at 36 with that salary.

**Chlup** is the most important summer renewal. Nineteen years old, 82 overall_base, POTE 95, $2.34M on one year. Lock him on 5–6 years at renewal. He is the franchise center the entire timeline is built around.

**Luongo** at 26, 91 overall_base, $1.60M, one year left. GM confirmed him as arrived in February 2005. Re-sign on 5–6 years. The risk is a July bidding war if we fumble the renewal, but at 26 with 91 base he will command a star contract. Plan for 5 years at whatever the game demands.

**Tucker** (79 base, $1.30M expiring, age 30) is the deadline chip for the toughness acquisition the coach flagged. Pair him with Koltsov (68 base, $1.10M expiring) in a package for Hartnell at BUF.

**Let-go list for July:** Mogilny (36, $5.50M, trade at deadline instead), Spezza (73 base, write-off per Coach, 0.22 pts/g on 4.6 MPG), Koltsov (68 base, depth), St. Jacques (66 base, depth). Four players cleared, $8.70M in salary freed.

**Ouellet** at 81 base, $0.90M, age 24, one year left. Keep as backup goalie on a 2-year deal. He is cheap and the GM wants a capable second for the playoffs.

**Klesla** at 78 base, 23, $0.90M, one year left. Either trade him at the deadline as part of a larger package (he has tradeable value at 23) or re-sign on 2 years if he stays. Given the coach's defensive depth concern, I lean toward keeping him and re-signing cheap.

**Upshall** has four years left at $1.50M with 78 base and is a write-off (0.21 pts/g, 4.6 MPG). He is not expiring this summer so he is not on the list, but he is dead money for three more seasons unless moved. Flag for the February/March window as a secondary chip.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: who across thirty clubs fills our two real gaps, the faceoff centre behind Sundin and young top-six scoring behind Gaborik's dead contract? The coverage phase killed the toughness gap, so the Jovanovski, Hartnell, and Kurka threads are closed. The ATL Trasher connection is the dominant finding.

**Heatley** (ATL, RW, 24, 91 overall_base, $1.10M expiring, 20 pts/23 GP, 22.3 MPG) is the single best target in the league. He is a Gaborik-priced replacement at $1.10M instead of $11.90M, four years younger than Mogilny, with the same role. ATL at 16 points with second-lowest payroll and six expiring deals cannot re-sign him. A package of Klesla plus R1 is what a rebuilding GM prices a 91-base forward at 24 against a rental with no re-signing path.

**Kovalchuk** (ATL, LW, 22, 89 overall_base, $1.10M expiring, 26 pts/23 GP) is the same story a year younger. ATL has two elite young forwards on expiring deals and cannot keep both. If they deal one, we should be the buyer. Klesla plus R1 works for one of them; a second package of Colaiacovo plus R2 works for the other. Both together is unlikely but ATL at 16 points has no reason to hold either past March.

**Savard** (ATL, C, 28, FACE 87, 79 overall_base, $1.00M expiring, 20 pts/23 GP) remains the cheapest faceoff fix. Tucker alone plus Alexeev gets it done at zero draft cost. ATL at $40.34M payroll cannot re-sign him. He is 28 with a 79 base so this is a two-year solution at best, but it covers the Sundin cliff while Chlup matures.

**Bertuzzi** (VAN, RW, 30, 94 overall_base, $2.60M expiring, 31 pts/24 GP) is the best available rental. 94 base at $2.60M is a top-line winger on a team that will not re-sign him. VAN at 25 points with 13 expiring and $46.36M league-lowest payroll is a pure seller. The cost is that he is 30 with 58 POTE, so he improves nothing long-term. A playoff-only package: maybe Klesla or Colaiacovo plus R2. Only if we miss on Heatley or Kovalchuk.

**Havlat** (OTT, LW, 24, 87 overall_base, $0.90M expiring, 21 pts/22 GP) is the second-best young forward available. OTT at 19 points with 4 expiring and $59.27M payroll will struggle to re-sign at 87 base. The concern is 22 GP suggests a knock or a scratch pattern. A Colaiacovo plus R2 package works if MTL does not bite on him first.

**Hrdina** (PHX, C, 29, FACE 84, 78 overall_base, $1.19M, 1 year left, 14 pts/25 GP) is the budget faceoff option if Savard goes elsewhere. PHX at 15 points is the league's worst. $1.19M is below-slot money. Less production than Savard but cheaper and a year younger than Draper at the same grade band.

**Dropped targets.** Jovanovski (VAN, 89 base, $2.30M) was the toughness fix we no longer need. Kurka did not appear in November queries and the gap is gone. Hartnell (BUF, POTE 95) was a development piece for a role we already fill. None of these should consume draft capital now.

**DiPietro** (NYI, G, 24, 79 overall_base, 20 GP, 60.6 MPG) is developing on schedule for NYI and they are 12-8-3 in the race, so he is not a trade candidate this season. The Luongo monitoring task is resolved: DiPietro is on track, not available, and Luongo is on our roster. No further action needed.

## Trade construction

This phase answers: what packages do we actually put on the table for the two targets that matter most, and what do we hand over that doesn't hurt? The faceoff cliff (Sundin at 34, one year left, no successor above 88 FACE) and the Gaborik problem ($11.90M scratched) define the need; the surplus list (Colaiacovo benched, Upshall and Wallin at 0 GP, Klesla expiring) defines the currency.

**Heatley** (ATL, RW, 24, 91 overall_base, $1.10M expiring, 20 pts/23 GP) is the target that changes the roster most. Package: Klesla plus R1. Klesla is 23, POTE 97, $0.90M expiring, 9 pts/25 GP — a young defenseman on a cheap expiring deal plus a first-rounder is what a 16-point team accumulating pieces accepts. ATL at 16 points with six expiring contracts has no path to re-signing Heatley and every reason to convert him into a player and a pick before July. Payroll effect for us: net +$0.20M (Klesla $0.90M out, Heatley $1.10M in). For ATL: they shed $1.10M, gain a $0.90M defenseman and a first-rounder. Acceptance is uncertain but the logic is clean.

**Savard** (ATL, C, 28, FACE 87, 79 overall_base, $1.00M expiring, 20 pts/22 GP) closes the faceoff gap at the lowest possible cost. Package: Tucker plus Alexeev. Tucker is 30, CHKG 92, $1.30M expiring, 0 GP this season — a physical body on a cheap expiring deal. Alexeev is 23, POTE 94, BALA 90, $1.50M on a 4-year deal, 0.31 pts/g declining. ATL's payroll is second-lowest in the league; they absorb both without strain. For us: we save $1.80M net ($2.80M out, $1.00M in), remove one expiring veteran and one 2009-cliff piece, and get a 87 FACE centre who plays tonight. The concern is that ATL at 16 points may not want a 30-year-old they'll also lose in July; if they refuse Tucker, substitute Wallin (0 GP, $1.40M, 4 years) to give them a younger body.

**Havlat** (OTT, LW, 24, 87 overall_base, $0.90M expiring, 21 pts/22 GP) is the third option if Heatley goes to someone else. Package: Colaiacovo plus R2. Colaiacovo is 22, POTE 99, $1.40M on four years, 0.13 pts/g and benched by the Coach. OTT at 19 points with $59.27M payroll is rebuilding and a 99-potential defenseman on a cheap long deal is exactly what they accumulate. We shed a benched 2009-cliff player and gain a 21-point winger at $0.90M. Net payroll: -$0.50M for us. The 22 GP on Havlat suggests a knock or scratch pattern that may depress his trade value, which cuts both ways — cheaper for us, but OTT may question durability.

**Gaborik** at $11.90M with 8 pts/17 GP and scratched cannot realistically fetch a player. His trade value has collapsed with his production. The best March outcome is pairing him with a cheap asset as a salary dump to a team with cap space, fetching at most a late-round pick. If no team takes him, he walks in July 2010 and we carry the money for four more years. Nothing constructive can be built around him in December; flag it again in February.

**If none land:** Hold Colaiacovo, Upshall, and Wallin through the season rather than selling at a discount to desperate GMs. The 2009 cliff is still 3.5 years away. Develop Chlup (19, 75 FACE, 18 pts/25 GP, POTE 95) into the centre solution rather than buying one — he is the faceoff answer if he stays healthy and plays a full season. Move Gaborik at March even for a fourth-round pick; $11.90M of dead money is the worst asset on the roster and any trade is an improvement.



---

**On the Luongo/DiPietro monitoring task (#2):** Resolved. Luongo is on our roster at 91 overall_base, 26 years old, POTE 97, $1.60M with one year left. DiPietro (NYI) is developing at 20 GP / 60.6 MPG and NYI are 12-8-3 in the race, so he is not available. No further monitoring is needed; the task is complete.

## Owed

**The task "Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window" is obsolete.** The GM closed all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19 ("Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks"), and Luongo is now on our roster: 95 overall, 91 base, $1.60M, 1 year remaining, 9 GP this season. There is no trade window to monitor because the target was acquired.

**DiPietro** is at 86 overall / 79 base with POTE 99, $1.10M expiring, morale 84. He is still a long-term prospect development story, but he is not a trade target anymore — he is a depth piece on someone else's roster, not on ours, and the original task framed him through the lens of a goalie trade window that no longer exists.

**What would replace it, if the GM wants it:** a standing watch on DiPietro's ice time and grade movement as a potential future backup or trade piece, separate from the closed Luongo task. That is a different question with a different deadline.

No action recommended. The task is dead; I am not keeping it alive.
