# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-12-04

Next game at NYI on Tuesday 06 December 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is who has earned ice time and who hasn't, at 25 games. Three players are getting full roles they've justified, three are confirmed collapses the system keeps cycling, and two need a call this week.

**Chlup** at 18 points in 25 games on 20.6 MPG is the team's leading scorer at 19. He plays second-line centre and carries first-line minutes. That's exactly where he belongs and the role is building him. No concern.

**Chistov** at 16 points in 25 games on 20.1 MPG on the first wing is doing what a first-line winger does. **Nash** at 15 points in 25 on 15.0 MPG is a solid second-line winger at 21. Both earning their minutes. No concern.

**Colaiacovo** is the problem. 3 points in 25 games at 12.3 MPG, zero goals. That's 0.12 pts/g, down from 0.14 when I flagged him on November 27th. He's played every single game while Stahle (POTE 96, 0.22 pts/g on 12.5 MPG) sits scratched. The numbers say Stahle is the better option and the rate is moving the wrong way. He comes out.

**Gardener** at 0 points in 16 games on 3.3 MPG is the exact collapse pattern I set the rule for. The GM took my scratch recommendation on November 24th and TOR went 2-0-0, but he's back in the lineup now. The pattern is confirmed: 3.3 MPG with zero production is a player killing time, not developing.

**Alexeev** at 7 points in 18 games is 0.39 pts/g on 10.8 MPG. I set a threshold of 0.45 at 25 games to keep dressing him. He's below it, and he's only at 18 games so the rate is still thin. I'm not cutting him yet, but he's on watch. Another week below 0.45 and the case for Alexeev over Upshall or a recalled Spacek evaporates.

**Spacek** at 6 GP and morale 76 is the lowest morale on the roster. POTE 91, age 20, 3 points in 6 games (0.50 pts/g in brief stints). The GM scratched him in January to give others room. Those others are now Spezza (4.6 MPG) and Upshall (5.3 MPG) at confirmed collapse rates. Spacek deserves a look over either of them if a spot opens.

**Spezza** and **Upshall** have both confirmed the pattern for the second straight season. POTE 99 each, age 22, 4.6 and 5.3 MPG, 0.25 pts/g. They are not developing in 5-minute depth roles and they haven't for two seasons. This is an offseason problem: real audition in camp or move them. For now they're fourth-line filler and that's fine for winning, but nothing is being built here.

**Eminger** at 7 GP and POTE 99 is irrelevant to development at this point. He's a trade asset.

**Gaborik** is scratched at 0.47 pts/g on 22.6 MPG. At 23 he's not developing in the way that matters (his rate doesn't justify those minutes consistently), and he's already out. No action needed from me.

## Development trends

The window shows one clear story: our young players who got real minutes early have mostly held or improved, while those whose minutes collapsed saw nothing but stagnation. Spezza is the loudest case; the veterans are holding, with two notable exceptions.

**Spezza** at 22 is the single worst development outcome on the roster. 0.21 pts/g on 4.6 MPG in 19 games. He has a 99 potential and is rotting on the fourth line. Every game he plays at 4.6 MPG is a game lost to his growth. The choice is dress him at a real slot or stop dressing him; I have no middle ground here.

**Alexeev** at 23 is the case I flagged for reassessment at 25 games. He is at 18 games, 0.29 pts/g on 11.1 MPG. That is well below the 0.45 threshold I set on November 17th. His dressing recommendation is weakening. If he does not cross 0.35 by game 22 I would scratch him for space.

**Chlup** at 19 went 0.71 over 25 games at 21.2 MPG. Below his 0.88 finish last year, but that was a peak. For a second pro season at 19, 0.71 at 21 MPG is ahead of schedule. No concern.

**Nash** at 21: 0.58 pts/g on 14.8 MPG. That is up from last season's 0.43 finish, so he is growing, but still not a first-line winger's rate. My line-change recommendation from November 27th (move him up to first wing) was not taken; I still think it is right but the numbers are moving in our direction without it.

**Gaborik** at 23: 0.47 on 22.6 MPG in 17 games since returning. That is top-six wing production. He is the one young forward on an upward curve without question.

**Hainsey** at 24: 0.37 at 20.9 MPG in 19 games. Solid D development. He is taking over minutes from the tired top pair.

**Stahle** at 21: 0.24 at 12.9 MPG in 18 games. Modest but he is getting real minutes and growing into them. The trajectory is fine.

**Colaiacovo** at 22: 0.12 over 25 games, zero goals. He has not improved since the 0.14 window I flagged on November 27th. He is the same player. My scratch call stands.

**Richards** at 25: 0.58 this year, down from 0.71 last year and 1.08 the year before. That is three straight declining seasons at an age when the expected direction is up. The system-fit problem I flagged in May is confirmed; it is not a hot/cold issue, it is structural.

**Afinogenov** at 26: 0.67 this year, 0.73 last year, 1.17 the year before. Same trajectory. Both he and Richards are sliding while getting stable minutes. Something about how we deploy top-six forwards in this system is suppressing two players who produced elsewhere.

**Eminger** at 22: 0.29 in 7 games on 19.9 MPG. Down from 0.38 last year. He is locked at $2.20M x 4 per the correction, so this is not a trade-by-expiry issue anymore; it is a "do we have a use for a declining 22-year-old on a long deal" issue.

**Sundin** at 34: 0.75 pts/g on 23.9 MPG. He is still playing elite centre production. The load is heavy but he is holding up.

**Mogilny** at 36: 0.58 on 23.5 MPG in 25 games. Still contributing, still taking big minutes. He is not sliding yet, but at 36 the planning for next season should assume he is not here.

**Gardener** and **Upshall** are both dead. Gardener has zero points in 16 games at 2.5 MPG; Upshall 0.20 in 16 at 4.6. Both are in the collapse pattern. Neither is developing.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy. Recent wins have pulled morale up across the board and nobody needs intervention before Tuesday.

**Richards** is the only structural watch. At 87 OVR on 12.1 MPG, he's five minutes below his band, and this was costing him morale in November (dipped as low as -13). He's now climbing steadily (+5, +5) because the wins are doing the work minutes aren't. If the results stall, this reopens immediately. No change today — the ice-time fix would mean taking minutes from the top six, which are producing.

**Spacek** sits at 76, lowest in the room. Scratched with 6 GP on 5.8 MPG. He's been at 76 for weeks but has moved +5 in the latest save, so the winning is reaching him even without ice time. At 76 he loses 2 points off every grade, which makes him harder to dress — a cycle that only wins break. No action available to me.

**Brendl** at 81, scratched, 10 GP on 3.9 MPG. Same story: too low a role for a morale fix, and the +5 in the last save says the results are healing him without intervention.

Everyone else is at 82 or higher and trending flat or up. The fourth-liners (Upshall, Gardener, Spezza, Lundmark) are all at 82, recovering from the November dip, and getting their natural depth minutes. No problem there.

## Role composition

The units are mostly well-built for their roles. L1 through L2 and both penalty-kill units are properly constructed for what they're asked to do. The real issues are L4's identity crisis and a faceoff void below the top two centres.

**L1** — Sundin 94 scoring, 96 playmaking, 95 faceoffs, 99 clutch with Jackman 92 checking behind him. This is a top line that can carry play and kill plays. Well-constructed, no change needed.

**L2** — Nash 82 checking gives a defensive anchor; Chlup 80 faceoffs wins draws; Afinogenov 94 scoring is the offensive engine; Hainsey 99 speed stretches the ice. Balanced for a second line. No change.

**L3** — Richards 93 playmaking, 78 faceoffs is the softest line defensively (checking mean 69, toughness 62). Colaiacovo is the weakest D on the roster (0.14 pts/g in 22 games per my November note). This is the right assignment — Richards needs to be where the playmaking matters most and the defensive burden is lower. But it means L3 cannot be a shutdown line, and that's a roster fact, not an arrangement problem.

**L4** — Gardener, Spezza, Upshall. Checking mean 70, toughness 62. These are L3's numbers with no star. This line is not a checking line; it's a depth line with no identity. The guide calls for "one line with three checkers at 80+" — on the dressed roster, the only players above 80 checking are Jackman (92, needed on L1) and Nash (82, needed on L2). Roberts 84 and McCabe 83 are scratched. Without one of them, no L4 arrangement fixes this.

**PK2** — Hainsey and Klesla both at 99 speed push the checking mean to 93. This is a smart construction: speed kills through pressure and gap control, so a fast second kill is viable even without high checking grades. Keep it.

**P2** — Mogilny 92 scoring, Afinogenov 94 scoring. A PP2 with that much shooting talent is a genuine second weapon. No change.

**Faceoffs** — Below Sundin (95) and Chlup (80), the dressed roster has Richards (78) and nothing else above 78. L4 sits at a 58 mean. Against any team with a competent third-line centre, we will lose draws there consistently. Wallin (88) is scratched; if he's available and healthy, he belongs on L3 or L4 at centre for faceoff coverage.

The structural gaps: one true elite checker (Jackman) and two centres above 80 in the faceoff circle. Roberts and McCabe could patch the checking depth but are being held out. I flag it to the GM as a roster question: do we need them dressed against quality opponents?

## Opponent matchup

The question: can we beat this Islanders team, and does anything need shuffling for Tuesday? The answer: our matchups are favorable up and down the order, Robidas is out of their lineup until the 13th, and their power play is a non-factor. No change.

**Their top line** is Yashin 83, Blake 81, Parrish 81. Sundin at 92 with FACE 95 against Yashin's FACE 70 wins the draw and controls the zone. Chistov 87 and Mogilny 89 both carry the wings over Blake and Parrish. This line should outplay theirs.

**Their second line** drops sharply. Peca 82 is competent but Mapletoft 75 and Simon 72 are bottom-six quality. Chlup 87, Nash 85 and Afinogenov 86 against that unit is a massive gap. We should generate our best offence on this line all night.

**Their third line** has Scatchard 79 with FACE 82, which is his one real weapon. Richards at 87 is too strong for him. Forbes 67 and Weinhandl 71 are soft. Lundmark 81 and Alexeev 80 own that wing matchup.

**Their defence without Robidas** is Aucoin 79 / Hamrlik 82 up top, then Niinimaa 80 paired with Smith 66 or Hawgood 70. Our first pair (Jackman 86, Klesla 87) is overmatched only by Hamrlik. Our second and third pairs face 66-70 quality D. Safronov 68 and Hainsey 77 can handle Niinimaa/Smith.

**Their power play** is 10-for-102, which is 9.8%. No PK adjustment needed. Our first kill unit (Chlup, Chistov, Safronov, Jackman) can play shortened shifts if they want.

**Goalie:** DiPietro at 86 with POKE 93 and AGIL 95 is the reason they allow only 2.40 a game. We need to shoot high-danger. Luongo starts, no fatigue flag showing, morale 84.

**Fourth-line faceoff note (not a matchup change):** Bates FACE 89 against Spezza FACE 54 is the one place they win a clean draw. Same faceoff gap we've carried all season; no lineup fix.

**Defensemen assessment (obligation #1):** Based on my last readings, Jackman at 0.88 pts/g over his first 16 games is a keep, not a sell — confirmed breakout at $0.70M x2. Klesla at 0.35 is still the top sell candidate: 87 OVR with $0.90M expiring is what a buyer sees. Colaiacovo at 0.14 over 22 games remains the weakest regular D. Fischer's contract at $3.7M x4 for second-pair production is the economic problem, not a play problem. Safronov at 68 OVR has no trade value. St. Jacques at 66 is bench fodder. I would need to pull current season production for a full refresh this week, but nothing in this brief contradicts the existing sell order: Klesla first, then Colaiacovo's role review, then Fischer on contract value.

## Owed

**Standing job #1: defenceman analysis and end-of-season sell list, updated for game 25.**

**Klesla** — 87 OVR, $0.90M x 1 yr expiring, 9 pts in 25 games (0.36 pts/g) on 26.3 MPG. Essentially unchanged from November 30 when I put him at 0.35 over 23. Still the top sell: a buyer sees the grade, we see a bottom-six production rate on a top-pair workload. Sell window open, nothing has moved.

**Jackman** — 17 pts in 25 games (0.68 pts/g) on 26.2 MPG. My sell trigger is 0.55 (set November 13 when I reversed the October sell). He was at 0.88 over 16 games and has bled to 0.68 over nine more. Still above the trigger so he stays on the keep list, but this is the direction that kills the card. If he hits 0.55 before the deadline he goes back on the sell list.

**Colaiacovo** — 3 pts in 25 games (0.12 pts/g) on 12.3 MPG, 76 OVR, zero goals all season. Three scoreless games since my November 27 read (then 0.14 over 22). He is the worst regular defenceman on the club by a wide margin. Nobody will take $1.40M x 4 for a 76 with no offense, so he is not a trade candidate — he is a scratch.

**Hainsey** — 7 pts in 19 games (0.37 pts/g) on 20.9 MPG. 77 OVR, $1.40M x 6. Solid second-pair minutes, long and cheap. Keeper.

**Fischer** — 84 OVR, 6 GP, 0.67 pts/g in limited action, $3.70M x 3. Not dressed. The GM's keeper. Tuesday at NYI is a maximize-quality night against a 12-8 club. Dress him, scratch Colaiacovo.

**Kaberle** — 85 OVR, 6 GP, $4.10M x 4. Also not dressed. Same logic as Fischer if we want to maximize this week.

**McCabe** — 0 GP, $3.00M x 3, 84 OVR. Dead money. Still on the sell list from May. Nobody has moved on him.

**St. Jacques** — 0 points in 7 games, 66 OVR, expiring. Depth filler. If we dress Fischer and Kaberle, he comes out.

No structural change from November 30. Klesla and McCabe stay on the sell list; Jackman is trending toward the trigger but not there yet; Colaiacovo's case for scratching has gotten stronger.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-12-01
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-12-01

Toronto 14-6-0, 36 pts after 24 games.

## Role coverage

Toughness and faceoffs are the two roles Toronto cannot fill from within; checking can be fixed tonight by the coach dressing who is already here.

**Toughness** is the only role in the league that Toronto is truly missing. Zero players above 80. The best is Jackman at 75, which is a 4-grade gap from the 80 threshold. Roberts 73, McCabe 73, Tucker 70 are all well short. No amount of role reassignment closes this — the attribute simply isn't on the roster. This is why Kurka (88 TOUG, 90 CHKG, 23, $0.60M) and Jovanovski (93 TOUG, 94 CHKG, 29, $2.30M) have been the February targets since November. It is also why Bell matters more than a pure scorer: he carries 88 TOUG and 82 FACE simultaneously, fixing two gaps in one 25-year-old at $0.90M.

**Faceoffs** is thin by design. Only Sundin at 90 clears 80, and he is 34 carrying 23.6 MPG. Wallin at 83 is not lined, and the next available centre draw is Chlup at 75 — seven grades below the threshold the role needs. Richards at 70 and Gardener at 72 are bottom-of-the-league for centres. There is no faceoff man on this roster who isn't Sundin. The coach can dress Wallin (25, not lined) to get one more body at 83, but that is a band-aid on a role that needs depth across three lines.

**Checking** looks adequate on paper (6 players at 80+) and is a mirage on the ice. Jackman 87 at 24 is the only 80+ checker getting real minutes. Upshall 80 is getting 5.1 MPG per the coach's report. The other four — Roberts 86 (39, not lined), McCabe 86 (30, not lined), Tucker 83 (30, not lined), Fischer 82 (25, not lined) — sit on the bench. The coach can fix this tonight by dressing McCabe and Fischer for penalty-killing shifts; that costs nothing and gives the team two more bodies above 80 in the role. This is the one gap where acquisition is not required.

**Scoring and playmaking** are covered at depth (11 at 80+ in both) but the issue is production, not supply. Mogilny 94 at 36 is the engine and the clock. Gaborik 92 is not lined at all (confirmed collapse, 8 pts in 17 GP per the November finding). Roberts 88 at 39 is not lined. The effective top-six scorers getting ice time are Sundin, Mogilny, Afinogenov, and whatever comes from the bottom six. That is not a coverage gap; it is a development and health problem the coach is already managing.

**Speed** is the club's strength at 25 players above 80. No action needed.

**Stamina** is fine (12 at 80+). Kaberle 97 and McCabe 94 are both not lined, which is the same waste the checking problem describes.

**Durability** is moderate at 5 above 80, with Roberts 98 not lined and Spacek at 79 borderline. Not urgent at 24 games in.

**Goalies** are settled per the March standing order. Luongo at 94, Belfour stays. No gap.

**Age risk**: Sundin 34 and Mogilny 36 carry the top two scoring and faceoff lines between them. When Mogilny is done, the club has no 80+ faceoff centre below 34. Chlup 75 and Richards 70 are the succession plan, and both are below threshold. This makes the February faceoff acquisition (Bell at 82, or Vasicek at 80) not just a this-year fix but a 3–4 year one.

## Trajectory

The question this phase answers is whether Toronto's money and age curve are arranged to survive the next three summers, and the answer is: the shape is good, but one contract is eating the club alive and a second cluster is three years away from exploding.

**Gaborik** is the single largest structural problem in the building. He's 23, scratched, earning $11.90M/year on a deal that runs 5 years through July 2010. That's 13.2% of the $89.94M payroll going to a healthy scratch. Mid-contract renegotiation is impossible. After March 2006, if he's still here, we carry $47.60M of dead money or watch him walk in 2010. His trade value drops every game he doesn't play; at 8 points in 17 games he's already sliding. This deal must be unwound by the deadline. The question is what we can get for a scratched 23-year-old with POTE 90 and no recent production.

**The age curve is close to the manual's target.** Three players over 34 (Sundin 34, Mogilny 36, Roberts 39), two at 30-33 (McCabe, Tucker). Five veterans total, right in the 5-7 window. Thirteen players under 24, sixteen in the 24-29 bracket. The problem isn't the shape; it's that the young players are producing at 0.6-0.7 pts/g while the veterans carry 0.75+. **Chlup** at 17 points in 24 games (0.71) is the closest thing to a bridge over the Mogilny/Sundin void. **Chistov** at 14 in 24 (0.58) and **Nash** at 15 in 24 (0.63) need to reach 0.80+ before the veterans fall off around 2008-09.

**July 2006 walks $15.44M across nine players**, but most are walkable: Mogilny (36, $5.50M), Tucker (30, $1.30M), Koltsov (24, $1.10M), Spezza (22, $1.00M, POTE 99 but 0.22 pts/g), St. Jacques ($0.80M). The two that must be locked are **Luongo** (26, $1.60M, POTE 97, 94 overall) and **Chlup** (19, $2.34M, POTE 95). Both need 5-6 year deals in the same week next July. Tellqvist behind Luongo is POTE 91 at 89 overall, a clear step down. Chlup is the Sundin handoff the Coach already flagged.

**The July 2009 cluster is the long fuse.** Eleven players worth $37.40M expire together: Richards, Chistov, Afinogenov, Kaberle, Nash, Eminger, Alexeev, Upshall, Colaiacovo, Abid, and Gaborik (if he's still here). That's 41.6% of current payroll walking at once. Most are young-core players whose value in 2009 depends entirely on whether they develop. By summer 2008 we'll know if Chistov, Nash, and Eminger are $6-8M players or re-sign-for-minimum candidates. The draft picks we spend in February 2006 and July 2006 determine whether we have depth to absorb departures or are forced into panic renewals.

**Draft capital is thin.** Three picks (rounds 0, 1, 2), all Toronto's own. Scouting at level 2 means auto-draft is adequate for information. These picks are the primary currency for February targets like Komisarek or Jovanovski. Spending all three leaves nothing for the next trade window, which matters if the Gaborik package demands a second pick on top of a player return.

**Fischer** at 25, $3.70M, 3 years left, 4 points in 6 games, scratched, adds another $3.70M of dead weight on top of Gaborik and McCabe ($3.00M, 0 GP). Combined scratched salary is $18.60M, 20.7% of payroll, for zero on-ice contribution. The profit of $35.45M absorbs this, but the roster cost is real: those are three spots that could carry a top-nine forward or a second-pairing defenceman.

**Task #2 (Luongo/DiPietro monitoring)** remains closed. Luongo is on the roster at 94 overall, 8 GP, $1.60M, 1 year. No action until the July 2006 renewal window.

## Calendar

Are we buyers or sellers at March 19, and what do we do with the nine contracts expiring this summer? The answer is buyers with one mandatory sell, and the summer list splits into five renewals, one walk, and two deadline chips.

**We are buyers.** Toronto sits 2nd in the East at 36 points with eight teams qualifying. We are not selling our foundation. The Coach's gaps — toughness on the back end, centre depth, scoring from L3 and L4 — are buy targets, not sell targets. The deadline is 108 days away; negotiations open late February per the GM's standing order.

**The one mandatory sell is Gaborik.** At 8 points in 17 games (0.47 pts/GP) on $11.90M through July 2010, he is the single most dangerous asset on the roster. Mid-contract renegotiation is impossible. If he doesn't move by March 19, we carry $47.60M of dead money for four more seasons or watch him sit. Every other deadline task is optional; this one is not.

**Mogilny** at 36 and $5.50M expiring is the second sell candidate. He triggers the over-80 expiring mechanic (trade for a pick), and $5.50M is the salary we most want off the books. Let him walk only if no team will take him at the deadline.

**Tucker** at 30 and $1.30M was already designated a chip by the GM last March. He's expiring, so move him at the deadline or lose him for nothing.

**Chlup** at 19 and $2.34M is a franchise centre in embryo. Lock him on 5–6 years. He's the oldest player on this list worth that length and the most expensive to let go.

**Luongo** at 26 and $1.60M is our number-one goalie. Five to six years. The GM closed goalie trade monitoring on March 19, 2005 — the task is done, this is a renewal question now.

**Klesla** at 23 and $0.90M with POTE 97: re-sign 4–5 years. Cheap elite-potential defenseman who should not walk. The Coach's move off K2 doesn't change his asset value.

**Koltsov** at 24 and $1.10M: re-sign 3–4 years. Young, cheap, still in development window.

**Spezza** is the hard call. POTE 99 at 22 on $1.00M, but 0.24 pts/GP on 4.4 MPG across two seasons. The Coach has written him off. Either we get the GM to mandate 12+ MPG and genuinely develop him, or we trade him before his POTE carries no value. My recommendation: move him at the deadline while his potential still fetches a return. If the GM disagrees and wants to try one more camp, that's his call.

**Ouellet** at 24 and $0.90M: re-sign 2 years as cheap backup. We need a second goalie who isn't a kid.

**St. Jacques** at 25 and $0.80M: re-sign 2 years or release depending on whether the Coach sees a role for him beyond seventh defenseman.

On **Task #2** (Luongo availability and DiPietro monitoring): the GM closed this on March 19, 2005 — "Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks." Luongo is on our roster at $1.60M expiring. The task is delivered as closed; the action item is now the summer renewal above.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: who across thirty clubs closes Toronto's two structural gaps (toughness at zero players above 80, faceoffs at one man aged 34) at a price the club can pay before the deadline?

**Jovanovski** is still the answer to toughness. 29, TOUG 89, CHKG 90, 89 overall_base, 31.4 MPG, $2.30M expiring. VAN sits at 25 points with 13 expiring deals and $46.36M payroll, the league's lowest. They will not re-sign him. The package from November holds: Klesla (23, POTE 97, $0.90M expiring) plus a first-rounder. He is old and his ceiling is set, but he is the only player in the league above 89 on both grades who is actually going to move.

**Kurka** is still on CAR and still expiring at $0.60M. TOUG 88, CHKG 90, 78 overall_base, 17 points in 24 games at 21.9 MPG. The November note about him disappearing was wrong. CAR at 28 points with 14 expiring and $63.79M payroll must shed him. At 23 and $0.60M, he is the cheapest real toughness fix available. The package (Upshall plus R3) still works because Upshall is confirmed collapse at 0.23 pts/g.

**Hartnell** is the sleeper the October scan missed. BUF, LW, 23, TOUG 91, CHKG 92, 79 overall_base, POTE 95, $1.10M expiring, 9 points in 23 games at 18.0 MPG. BUF at 22 points with 5 expiring. He fills the toughness gap AND carries a 95 potential, which means he is not just a rental. Alexeev (0.33 pts/g at 11.5 MPG, flagged for removal) plus R2 is the package. This is the best value on the board.

**Witt and Yonkman** remain the shutdown-pair option. Witt is 30, TOUG 90, CHKG 94, 80 overall_base, $1.70M expiring, 31.1 MPG. Yonkman is 24, TOUG 90, CHKG 92, 74 overall_base, $0.60M expiring. WSH at 19 points with 5 expiring. Both move together or not at all. Eminger plus R2 remains the proposed return, gated on the GM's final call about Eminger.

**Savard** is the faceoff answer on a desperate seller. ATL, C, 28, FACE 87, 79 overall_base, 19 points in 22 games at 21.9 MPG, $1.00M expiring. ATL at 16 points with $40.34M payroll (second lowest) and 6 expiring. He gives a second 80+ faceoff man who is six years younger than Sundin. Package: Tucker (30, $1.30M, already a GM-designated chip) plus nothing, or Koltsov (24, $1.10M expiring) plus R3.

**Conroy** is the high-end faceoff play with a ticking clock. CGY, C, 34, FACE 95, 85 overall_base, 19 points in 24 games at 20.9 MPG, $2.00M expiring. CGY at 29 points with 9 expiring and $52.08M payroll. 95 FACE and 85 base are elite. At 34 he is a two-year bridge, not a solution. Worth pursuing only if CGY is desperate enough to eat salary or accept a cheap return.

**Bell** at CHI has slid. TOUG now reads 82 (was 88 in November), CHKG 80 (was 82). He still clears the 80 threshold by two grades at each, and his FACE 88 is useful. 25, 80 overall_base, $0.90M expiring, CHI at 17 points with 8 expiring. He is now a depth piece rather than the "fixes two gaps" target from November. Still worth a look if the price stays at Tucker plus R3.

**McLaren and Doan** have both fallen through. McLaren's TOUG dropped from 89 to 81, CHKG from 93 to 85. Doan's TOUG dropped from 86 to 78, CHKG from 91 to 83. Neither clears the 80/88 threshold they carried in October. The grades shifted and the case died with them.

**Komisarek's** value has cratered. 3 points in 24 games at 11.8 MPG, down from 20 points in 23 games at 30.6 MPG last season. MTL is clearly using him in a bottom-pairing role. POTE still reads 92, but any package for him should now be a late-round pick or a bench player, not Eminger plus R2.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: what do we actually put on the table for toughness and faceoffs, and does each other club have a reason to say yes before March? Three proposals, ranked by value-to-us against cost-to-us, each with a concrete reason the other GM picks up the phone.

**Hartnell** is the best package available in the league right now. 23 years old, TOUG 91, CHKG 92, POTE 95, $1.10M expiring, 9 points in 23 games at 18.0 MPG. He is not just a rental. Give Alexeev (23, POTE 94, BALA 90, SPEE 89, 7 pts/17 GP, $1.50M with 4 years control, coach flagged for removal) plus our R2 pick. BUF at 22 points is not making the playoffs. They lose Hartnell for nothing in July unless they move him. Getting a 23-year-old with POTE 94 and four years of control plus a second-rounder is strictly better than watching him walk. Our payroll drops $0.40M.

**Kurka** is the cheapest on-ice solution to the zero-above-80 problem. TOUG 88, CHKG 90, 17 points in 24 games at 21.9 MPG, $0.60M expiring. Give Upshall ($1.50M, 4 years, POTE 99, 4 pts/15 GP, confirmed collapse per the coach) plus Klesla ($0.90M expiring, POTE 97, 8 pts/24 GP, SPEE 88, AGIL 87). We shed $1.80M and swap speed (we have 25 players above 80) for bite (we have zero). CAR at 28 points with $63.79M payroll and 14 expiring deals cannot re-sign Kurka. They get a producing POTE 97 defenceman plus a POTE 99 winger at 22 they can develop or re-flip. Klesla's salary is expiring so the payroll hit is one season.

**Savard** closes the faceoff gap with the cheapest chip we own. 28 years old, FACE 87, 79 overall_base, 19 points in 22 games, $1.00M expiring. Give Tucker (30, $1.30M expiring, CHKG 92, TOUG 88, 0 GP, already a GM-designated chip). ATL at 16 points with $40.34M payroll (second lowest) and 6 expiring will not re-sign Savard. Tucker brings CHKG 92 and TOUG 88, physical presence they need for their young core, and they can flip him to a contender in March for a pick. No draft capital spent. Our payroll drops $0.30M.

**If we do all three:** We give Alexeev + Upshall + Klesla + Tucker + R2. We get Hartnell + Kurka + Savard. We shed $2.50M net, keep R0 and R1 for Gaborik or another move, and go from zero toughness players above 80 to two aged 23 at 88-91, and from one faceoff man aged 34 to two with Savard at 28. The three players we shed are the ones the coach explicitly wants off the ice.

**If none land:** Dress Wallin (FACE 83, 25, currently not lined) for faceoff duty as a band-aid. Accept the toughness gap through the playoffs and attack it in July via free agency and the draft (R0 and R1 both unspent). The Gaborik unwind in March becomes the sole trade priority since it saves $11.90M/year regardless of what comes back.

## Owed

**#2 — Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window.**

**Closed.** This task was opened on 2005-01-19 when we were hunting for a high-90s goalie to acquire at the March 2005 deadline. It was explicitly closed by the GM on 2005-03-19 ("Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks"). Luongo is now on our roster at 95 overall and has been since last season. DiPietro is irrelevant to us because we already have our 95-goalie. The entire premise of the task is discharged.

**The new goalie question is the mirror image.** Luongo is at 95, 26, $1.60M, one year left. That means his contract expires in July 2006. Per the GM's own standing rule, we cannot renegotiate until it expires. The question for the February/March window is now reversed: do we keep him through the playoffs and re-sign in the summer, or do we trade him for value in March if re-signing looks uncertain? At $1.60M for a 95-rated goalie under 27, the incentive is to keep and re-sign. No trade is warranted unless we somehow lose confidence in re-signing him, and at that salary almost every club would want him, making him hard to get and impossible to lose quietly.

No action needed this December. The task is complete. I will flag Luongo's renewal window when it arrives next summer.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-12-01
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-12-01

Next game vs TB on Saturday 03 December 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether our young players are getting the games they've earned, and the answer splits three ways: Chlup, Nash, and Chistov are earning theirs every night; Colaiacovo is not earning his; and Spezza, Upshall, and Gardener are dressed but not developing at fourth-line minutes with nothing to show.

**Colaiacovo** is the problem. 3 points in 24 games at 0.13 pts/g with zero goals, on 12.3 minutes a night. That's below what Stahle produces at 0.22 pts/g in 18 games, and Stahle is sitting out. He's the weakest regular D by a wide margin and he plays every single game. My scratch recommendation from November 27th hasn't been acted on, and every game at this rate makes it harder to justify him to the lineup. He's not growing into the role; he's being carried by it.

**Spezza** (4 pts in 18gp, 4.6 MPG, 0.22 pts/g) and **Upshall** (4 pts in 15gp, 5.3 MPG, 0.27 pts/g) are both in the collapse pattern I flagged in October. Both morale 82, both on the fourth line, both producing nothing. They're occupying roster spots without developing. The GM gave Spezza one block of real minutes on November 20th; the sample was too small to judge. At this point, dressing a third-line winger on the fourth line at 4 minutes helps nobody.

**Gardener** is POTE 98 with zero points in 15 games at 3.2 MPG. I recommended a permanent scratch on November 24th and the GM took it, but he's still showing as dressed at L4. If he's still in the lineup, he needs to come out.

**Spacek** is scratched at the GM's deliberate choice, but his morale has dropped to 76. That costs him 2 points off every grade. At POTE 91 and only 6 games played, the cost of the scratch is becoming visible.

**Gaborik** gets 22.6 MPG and 0.47 pts/g. He's getting the opportunity; the rate is just below what his minutes suggest. Not a "not enough games" problem.

**Chlup** at 17 points in 24 games on 20.6 MPG is the exception to every rule in this phase. He's earned his role and is producing in it.

## Development trends

The window runs 7 weeks, 24 games for the regulars. The story splits: the young core is mostly on track, two depth forwards are dead, and Alexeev has crossed the threshold I set.

**Chlup** at 0.70 pts/g on 21.3 MPG over 24 games at 19 is first-line production. The 1.00 from the first save was one game; 0.70 over 24 is the real number, and it matches last season's 0.88 rate. His role grew from 6 MPG to 21.3 across the window. He belongs where he is.

**Nash** at 0.61 pts/g on 14.7 MPG at 21 is better than last season's 0.43 finish. He is recovering from the slump I flagged in March. No action.

**Stahle** went from 6 MPG to 12.9 over 18 games and from zero to 0.24 pts/g. He is quietly building a second-pair role at 21. If Colaiacovo comes out permanently, Stahle is the natural replacement at the next slot.

**Alexeev** is the one to flag. I set 0.45 as the line at 25 games; he is at 0.31 over 17 games on 11.3 MPG, already below it. Last season he scored 0.55 as a scratch. Give him more ice and his rate fell. His dressing recommendation weakens now, not at 25 games.

**Spezza** (0.22 on 4.6 MPG, 18 games) and **Upshall** (0.21 on 4.6 MPG, 15 games) are the collapse pattern finished. Neither will recover this season. The offseason is the only lever.

**Gardener** at 0 points in 15 games on 2.3 MPG confirmed the scratch decision from November 24th. He is done as a regular.

**Eminger** continues his slide: 0.44 last February, 0.38 last season finish, now 0.29 over 7 games on 19.9 MPG at 22. He is locked at $2.20M x 4 per the correction from May. The slide does not create trade urgency the way an expiring deal would, but it erodes his value every month we hold him.

**Afinogenov** at 0.65 is below last season's 0.73 finish and far from his 1.17 peak. The system-fit issue from the offseason is not resolved. He is still the best right winger on this roster, but the trend is down at 26.

**Richards** at 0.61 over 24 games is flat from last year's 0.71. Same system-fit problem, same answer: not a first-line centre until something changes.

**Sundin** at 0.78 and **Mogilny** at 0.61 are both carrying real production at 34 and 36. Neither shows age decline in this window. No change.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy: the starting core sits at morale 97 across the board, which is the ceiling for a winning club. Two items worth naming, one confirmed action.

**Richards** remains the structural question. He's on L3 at 12.2 MPG against a band that expects about 17 for his calibre. His morale has recovered from 78 in October to 87 now, trending up through a +5 streak in recent saves. The winning is doing the work the minutes deficit should undo. I would not force him to L2 right now: Chlup (17 pts in 24 on 20.6 MPG), Nash (15 pts in 24 on 14.8 MPG), and Afinogenov (16 pts in 24 on 17.5 MPG) are a working unit. The trend is right and chemistry is the bigger intervention.

**Gardener** is the one confirmed action. Zero points in 15 games on 3.2 MPG is the young-player-collapse pattern I flagged on October 22nd. His morale sits at 82 and is recovering, but that's the winning lifting him, not the role. I recommended a permanent scratch on November 24th and the GM took it; the team went 2-0-0. He's still dressed and on L4 at a token 3.2 MPG. Confirm: he comes out. His shift is worth less than a real fourth-liner's.

**Lundmark, Upshall, Spezza** all sit at 5-5.4 MPG on third/fourth lines with morale at 82 and recovering. The same band gap as Richards but smaller players in a smaller role. If the winning continues, their morale climbs and this stays below the radar. The issue is the GM has three quality depth forwards for roughly one line's worth of minutes. That's a roster construction problem, not a coaching one.

No goalie morale concern. Luongo at 86 is the lowest among the three but he's a healthy scratch with a reason; Ouellet and Tellqvist are both at 97.

## Role composition

**K2 penalty kill is the weakest unit we ice.** Mean checking 72 with Upshall at 70 and Spezza at 70 means half the unit cannot actually check. Klesla at 88 is the only anchor, and he's a defenceman trying to cover a hole. If we take a penalty against Tampa Bay on Saturday, that unit gets exposed immediately.

**Nash** at 82 checking is the obvious fix. He's already on L2 at even strength, and putting him alongside Klesla on K2 lifts that unit's mean checking from 72 to roughly 78, giving it two men above 80. Upshall drops off the kill entirely; he keeps his L4 spot at even strength. This costs nothing in chemistry because Nash is not breaking up any existing PK pairing — he's replacing the weakest link.

**L1** is built right: Sundin 94 scoring, Mogilny 92, Chistov 93 playmaking, Jackman 92 checking screening the front. No reason to touch it.

**L2** works. Chlup at 80 faceoffs wins draws, Nash at 82 checking provides the edge, Hainsey at 99 speed stretches the zone. Solid two-way line.

**L3** has no identity but Richards at 93 playmaking is the engine and Alexeev provides secondary scoring. It's a third line. It does not need to be a top-line in disguise. No change.

**P1 and P2** are correctly balanced. P1 runs through Sundin (94 scoring, 96 playmaking) as the hub with Klesla and Jackman at the half-wall. P2 has Afinogenov 94 and Mogilny 92 as dual shooting threats. Both units have a clear first option.

**Checking depth is a roster-level concern, not a lineup problem.** Jackman at 92 is the only player on this club who checks at an elite level. Nash 82 and Klesla 88 are the next men up. If Jackman wears down through a stretch or gets hurt, we have no replacement above 84 in the lineup. Roberts at 84 is already scratched. This is not a Saturday problem but it is a trade-deadline problem that keeps getting more urgent.

## Opponent matchup

**The question:** Does TB's style or personnel demand a lineup change, or do we play the same game that's 14-6-0?

**The answer is no change.** We're 36 points to their 27, we won the first meeting 3-2, and our system matches up well against them without adjustment.

**Lecavalier** at 90 OVR with SHPW 96 and SPEE 97 is their one real threat. He'll auto-pair against Jackman and Klesla (our first D pair) because he sits on TB's first forward line. Jackman's CHKG 94 and Klesla's 99 speed handle him. No adjustment needed; the pairing already solves it.

**St. Louis** at 88 with HERO 97 and AGGR 89 is dangerous on the right side. He'll get Klesla's left point most often. Klesla's ENDU 57 is the one soft spot in our coverage, but replacing him isn't an option and no other D pair handles this better.

**The faceoff situation** is actually good for once. Sundin's FACE 95 against Lecavalier's FACE 66 is a 30-point gap. We control zone starts on the top line, which is where this game will be decided. Chlup at 80 against Halpern at 82 is a wash. Richards at 78 vs Robitaille's 86 is a small loss, but Robitaille's CHKG 51 means even when he wins the draw, he can't protect the puck against our checkers.

**TB's PP is 13 on 105 chances (12.4%).** They cannot score with the extra man. Their volume of PP opportunities (5 per game) means they draw a lot of calls, but they can't convert. Our PK units don't need to be sharper than usual.

**Svitov is out** (returns Dec 7). Their third line loses its best player (77 OVR, TOUG 83). Whoever slots in from the fourth line — likely Battaglia or Svedberg — makes it thinner. Richards already has the skill edge against Robitaille/Hlavac; Svitov's absence widens it. No action required.

**Khabibulin** at 91 with INTE 93 and ENDU 91 is a genuine obstacle. We need our first two lines to sustain zone time and generate second chances. The lines are built for that — Mogilny, Afinogenov, and Nash all have the skill to create from odd angles against a goalie who plays the angles well but will be vulnerable to high-danger traffic.

**Ouellet starts.** 86 OVR, no fatigue icon flagged. He faced them last time and allowed 2. Tellqvist at 73 is a clear downgrade against a 91-rated goalie who will keep them in games.

## Owed

**Standing job #1: defenceman evaluation for end-of-season decisions.** This is the update through 24 games.

**Jackman** at 0.67 pts/g over 24 games has come down from the 0.88 hot streak I noted in November, but that's a regression toward a very good rate, not a collapse. 16 points, 5 goals, 26.1 MPG on $0.70M x 2 years. He stays. No change from my November verdict.

**Klesla** is the one who moved. At Nov 30 I said the sell window reopened at 0.35 after two-point games. Now he has 8 points in 24 games, rate back to 0.33. One assist across three games. At 87 OVR and $0.90M expiring, the card still looks fine to a buyer but the rate is sliding back toward the 0.30 floor I set on November 13th. If he goes without a point in the next two games he hits it again.

**Colaiacovo** at 3 points in 24 games, 0 goals, 12.3 MPG. Still 0.13. My scratch recommendation from November 27th was not taken and the numbers haven't budged. At $1.40M x 4 years he is the worst value on the blue line by a mile.

**Hainsey** at 0.33 over 18 games, 21.0 MPG. Steady, cheap ($1.40M x 6), and does the job we need from a third pair.

**Fischer, Kaberle, Eminger** are all on short samples (6-7 games) because of rotation. Fischer at 84 and Kaberle at 85 are keepers per the GM's standing orders. Eminger at 82 on $2.20M x 4 is locked; his 0.29 over 7 is too small to judge.

**McCabe** hasn't played. 30 years old, $3.00M x 3, OVR 84. If he's healthy, the question is why he's not dressed.

markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-30

Toronto 14-5-0, 36 pts after 23 games.

## Role coverage

The question this phase answers: where does the roster structurally fail, and which failures can the Coach close by playing the men he already has? As of November 30, two roles are genuinely broken, one is thin but improvable with internal moves, and the rest are covered.

**Toughness is zero.** Not thin. Zero at 80+. Jackman tops the roster at 75, Roberts 73, McCabe 73, Chlup 70. The highest-graded player on the entire club in TOUG is below the threshold. This has been true since February and no internal fix exists — nobody is one form swing away from 80. This is the acquisition gap, period. Kurka (CAR, 23, 88 TOUG, 90 CHKG, $0.60M) and Jovanovski (VAN, 29, 93 TOUG, 94 CHKG, $2.30M) are the two targets that close it. Neither package is cheap, but there is no alternative.

**Checking is thin at the top.** Six players at 80+: Jackman 87, Roberts 86, McCabe 86, Tucker 83, Fischer 82, Upshall 80. Two of those six (Roberts 86, McCabe 86) are not lined. Fischer 82 is also not lined but the Coach wants him dressed for PHI. If Fischer goes in, the lined checkers become Jackman 87, Tucker 83, Fischer 82, Upshall 80. That covers a third and fourth pair. What it does not cover is a shutdown pairing to match the league's elite — only Jackman is above 90 on today's display, and he has no partner close. McCabe at 86 is the closest internal option, but he is a 30-year-old on a one-year deal and not currently trusted. The acquisition ceiling matters here: Jovanovski 94 and Komisarek 93 in CHKG would pair with Jackman for a legitimate top shutdown unit.

**Faceoffs are thin below Sundin.** Only Sundin 90 and Wallin 83 are at 80+, and Wallin is not lined. Chlup at 75 is the next option and the Coach just moved him to L1C — he will lose draws against competent centres all night. This is an internal fix: dress Wallin on the third or fourth centre, or accept that L3 and L4 lose the dot. Bell (CHI, FACE 82, TOUG 88) closes faceoffs and toughness in one player at $0.90M, but he is a secondary target behind Kurka.

**Scoring is fine on paper but fragile in practice.** Mogilny 94 at 36 is carrying the top line; Gaborik 92 is not lined and locked at $11.90M for five more years (dead money per the November 20 note). Roberts 88 at 39 is not lined. The lined scorer group is Mogilny, Sundin 92, Afinogenov 90, and whatever Chlup gives at L1C. That is three reliable options for four lines. If Mogilny's minutes drop (the Coach wants 19 MPG), the top-end scoring load falls on Sundin and Afinogenov alone. This is a production concern the Coach handles; it is not a roster gap because the players are here.

**Speed, playmaking, clutch, stamina, durability** are all covered. 25 players at 80+ in speed, 11 in playmaking, 9 in clutch, 12 in stamina, 5 in durability. These are not problems.

**Age trajectory:** Mogilny 36, Roberts 39, Sundin 34. The scoring core is old. Jackman 24, McCabe 30, Tucker 30 on defence. The toughness acquisition targets are all young: Kurka 23, Komisarek 23, Jovanovski 29. The structural fix for toughness also fixes the age curve on the back end.

## Trajectory

Is this club heading for a cliff, or can it keep its young core together when they all get expensive at once? The second question, because the first doesn't apply — 29 of 34 rostered players are 29 or under, and the only 34+ men are Sundin (34, $8.40M x4), Mogilny (36, $5.50M x1), and Roberts (39, $4.90M x2). There is no aging problem here. The problem is a contract cliff in July 2006 and one man costing $11.90M while sitting in the stands.

**Gaborik** is the single biggest financial liability on the roster. At $11.90M x 5 years through July 2010, he consumes 13.2% of a $89.94M payroll while producing 8 points in 17 games as a healthy scratch. There is no renegotiation mechanism mid-contract. The only exit is trade, and his value drops every week he stays undressed. A bad return — a young player with potential and a mid-round pick — is better than carrying $47.60M of dead money for four more years.

**Chlup, Luongo, Klesla, Spezza** all expire in July 2006. Together they are $4.84M today (Chlup $2.34M, Luongo $1.60M, Klesla $0.90M, Spezza $1.00M). Chlup is 19 with POTE 95 and 17 points in 23 games. Luongo is 26 at POTE 97 and 8 starts. Klesla is 23, POTE 97, 8 points in 23. Spezza is 22, POTE 99, still developing. Re-signing these four on 5-6 year deals will cost roughly $12-15M combined per year — a $7-10M annual increase from what they earn now. That is the summer that defines the dynasty. Handle it wrong and the entire future core walks simultaneously.

**The 4-year cluster** ($37.40M across 11 players including Richards at $6.70M, Chistov at $5.00M, Nash at $3.90M, Kaberle at $4.10M) gives stability through 2009 but creates a second wave of expirations in the same summer four years from now. That is a future problem for a future GM conversation, not a 2006 action item.

**Mogilny and Roberts** walk or get replaced within 2 years on their own. Mogilny's 1-year deal means he's either a cheap re-sign or a July 2006 departure. Roberts at $4.90M x2 is scratched at 2 points in 8 games, age 39. Neither needs an intervention; they solve themselves through contract expiry.

**Draft capital** is thin. We hold only our own R1, R2, and R3. The Jovanovski package (Klesla plus R1) and the Komisarek package (Eminger plus R2) each require giving up a developing player AND a first or second rounder. That's the correct price for the blue line but it costs future depth picks. No other teams' picks are in the bank.

**Money check:** $89.94M payroll, $68.53M listed revenue, $36.55M profit. The profit exists (TV and prestige must bridge the gap), but Gaborik's $11.90M is the easiest way to create real headroom for the 2006 renewal wave.

## Calendar

The deadline is 109 days away and we sit 2nd in the East at 14-5-0 with 36 points, so the planning question is what to buy and what to shed by March 19, and which of the nine expiring contracts get renewed versus moved for value. The presumption is buyers, but the roster has enough expiring salary that the summer decisions shape the deadline packages just as much as the deadline itself does.

**Mogilny** is the single biggest decision. He is 36, on $5.50M, and the Coach wants to cut his minutes toward 19 MPG. That salary is the largest on the roster by a wide margin. He must move at the deadline. Carrying him into the playoffs at reduced minutes while paying $5.50M is the worst version of this contract. If we cannot find a landing spot by March, we let him walk in July and save the full amount.

**Tucker** was already a designated chip in the March 2005 window and is still here at 30 and $1.30M. He should go before March, ideally for a pick or a young player with potential. He has no realistic path to a Toronto role given the forward depth.

**Luongo** is 26, 94 overall on the renewal screen, and $1.60M. This is the single most important renewal on the roster. A 5 or 6 year extension is the priority, and the GM should be talking to him the moment contracts open in July. Everything else on this list is secondary to locking the franchise goaltender.

**Chlup** at 19 and $2.34M is the second priority. The Coach moved him to first-line centre this window. At 19, that is a long-term franchise centre being built. 5 or 6 year extension. The current $2.34M will rise on renewal, so locking him early protects us from a bidding war at his next renewal.

**Klesla** at 23, D, $0.90M, was the proposed return in a Jovanovski package in November. If we keep him, he is 4 or 5 years and he is the bottom-pairing D alongside Eminger for the next five seasons. If we trade him at the deadline, we get value now but lose cheap young D depth. I would keep him.

**Spezza** is the wildcard. He is 22, C, $1.00M, and was in a collapse pattern in the November window (2 points in 12 games). If he bounces back to a reasonable pace by February, renew 4-5 years. If he does not, he is a deadline chip: 80+ and expiring, so the pick-recovery mechanic applies. Decision point is late February when we open negotiations.

**Koltsov** at 24 and $1.10M should be renewed on 3 or 4 years if he is in the plans as a middle-six winger. If the Coach does not dress him regularly, he is a deadline chip for the same reason as Spezza.

**Ouellet** at 24 and $0.90M is the backup goalie. If Luongo is locked on a long deal, we need a competent backup. Ouellet fits. Renew 2 years at $0.90M. If his overall clears 80, the pick-recovery mechanic applies and we could also shop him for a pick and use Tellqvist as backup.

**St. Jacques** at 25 and $0.80M has been benched by the Coach in favour of Fischer at 84 overall. He is expendable. Move at the deadline for whatever we can get, or release.

**Colaiacovo** is not expiring, but the Coach scratched him after 3 points in 22 games (0.14 pts/g) on a 76 overall and $1.40M for four more years. His POTE 99 at 22 was supposed to be a cornerstone, but the development clock is the issue. If he is still at this production level in February, he becomes a deadline chip. That is the Eminger problem revisited: a high-potential young D we cannot get ice time into.

On the buy side, the Coach's gap is clear: one 90+ checker (Jackman at 92), next best Nash at 82. We need a shutdown blueliner or a top-six forward with 85+ checking. The tracked targets (Jovanovski, Kurka, Vasicek, Komisarek, Bertuzzi) all sit on struggling clubs, but I need to verify they are still available and still expiring before building the deadline package.

**On task #2** (Luongo/DiPietro goalie monitoring): Luongo is on our roster at 94 overall and expiring. The original task — monitor a goalie trade window to acquire a #1 — is resolved. We have the #1 now. The question has shifted from acquisition to renewal. Closing this task.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: who across the league closes our structural gaps (toughness, elite checking, faceoffs below Sundin) and who would take Gaborik off our books, and on which clubs would they say yes?

Our gaps are clear from the coverage phase: zero TOUG 80+ on the roster, only one CHKG 90+, and faceoffs dead after Sundin. Known targets from prior work (Jovanovski, Komisarek, Doan, McLaren, Vasicek, Bell) need fresh verification, and the Kurka disappearance flags a possible shift. I'm also searching for a Gaborik destination — a contender with a mid-salary forward we want.

**Round 1, broad sweep.** I need to find every player above our gap thresholds on likely sellers, plus contenders who might take Gaborik for a player we actually want.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: what concrete packages do we put on the table for Jovanovski, Komisarek, Vasicek, and Bell, and why would each counterpart GM say yes? I've ranked four proposals by a combination of gap-closing value, cost to our future, and likelihood of acceptance. The Gaborik problem remains unsolved and needs its own destination search; none of these packages solve it.

**Vasicek is the first call.** He's a 25-year-old centre at 82 overall producing 18 points in 22 games, FACE 80, $0.40M expiring, POTE 87. He closes our centre-depth hole AND our faceoff hole in one move for the cheapest package on this list. Carolina sits at 16 points with 14 expiring contracts and $63.79M in payroll. They will not re-sign him at 82 overall and 25 years old with that money situation. We send Koltsov (24, POTE 94, ACCE 96, 0 GP for us, $1.10M expiring) plus our third-rounder. Carolina gets a young winger with elite speed on a cheap expiring deal they can use immediately or flip, plus a draft pick, and they save $0.70M on payroll today. That's three things a desperate GM wants in one call. Acceptance is uncertain but the logic is straightforward.

**Bell is the second call.** He's 25, TOUG 88, FACE 82, CHKG 82, $0.90M expiring. One player closes both our zero-toughness gap and the faceoff gap below Sundin at half the price of Jovanovski. Chicago is 4-10-4 with 18 expiring contracts and cannot re-sign anyone. We send Upshall (22, POTE 99, CHKG 87, 4 pts/14 GP in a confirmed collapse) plus St. Jacques (25, CHKG 84, TOUG 80, $0.80M expiring) plus our third-rounder. Upshall's value is dropping right now because of the collapse — better to use him while POTE still reads 99 than watch his overall follow. Chicago gets a 22-year-old with elite potential at CHKG 87, a 25-year-old D on a cheap deal, and a pick. They're at the bottom of the league; a POTE-99 player at 22 is exactly what they're supposed to want.

**Komisarek is the third call.** He's 23, TOUG 86, CHKG 93, 14 points in 18 games, $1.10M expiring, POTE 92. He gives us a legitimate shutdown partner for Jackman (CHKG 87, TOUG 75) and he's young enough to re-sign. Montreal is 17 points, 8 expiring, $54.89M payroll. They won't re-sign at that number with 8 deals expiring. We send Colaiacovo (22, POTE 99, $1.40M x4) plus our second-rounder. Montreal gets a 22-year-old D with elite potential on a cheap four-year deal plus a pick — that's a rebuild's worth of blue-line depth. The risk: Komisarek is producing (14 pts/18 GP) and MTL might want more for an active producer. I think Colaiacovo's POTE 99 is enough to get them on the phone, but acceptance is genuinely uncertain here.

**Jovanovski is the fourth call, and the most expensive.** He's 29, TOUG 93, CHKG 94, the only player in the league above 90 on both grades. He closes the zero-toughness gap in one swing. But the price is Klesla (23, POTE 97, 8 pts/23 GP, $0.90M expiring) plus our first-rounder. Vancouver at 25 points with 13 expiring and $46.36M payroll (league-lowest) won't re-sign at 29. They get a young D producing at 0.35 pts/g with POTE 97 AND a first-rounder. That's a massive haul. The cost to us: we give up a 23-year-old who's actually playing AND our best pick. If we do both Vasicek AND Jovanovski, we'd need Koltsov for one and Klesla+R1 for the other. That's three picks' worth of capital in one window with only three picks in the bank. I would not do Jovanovski unless Komisarek falls through, because Komisarek gives us 93 CHKG at 23 instead of 29.

**If none land:** We dress Wallin (FACE 83, POTE 97, $1.40M x4) on the third centre and accept Chlup (FACE 75) losing draws at L1C. The toughness gap stays open: Jackman (CHKG 90) carries every shutdown assignment alone, Roberts (TOUG 92, CHKG 86) provides a spark on the fourth line in limited minutes. We survive without a true shutdown pair by leaning on our speed (25 players at 80+) to limit opposition time in our zone. The March deadline makes these players cheaper if sellers panic, but our return also shrinks because their trade value drops to pure rental. February is the window; March is the consolation.

## Owed

The question this phase answers: is Task #2 (monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window) still live, and what does the current picture show?

**Task #2 is closed.** The GM ordered it closed on 2005-03-19: "Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks." The memory note from 2005-11-13 confirms Luongo at 94 overall, 1 year, $1.60M, and the task marked done. There is nothing new to report because there is nothing left to monitor.

**Luongo** reads 95 overall today in the starting table, 8 GP, $1.60M, 1 year left. The one live question tied to him is the renewal window at season end, not a trade window.

**DiPietro** is at NYI, 86 overall, 24, 18 GP, $1.10M expiring. He is developing but the monitoring window the GM opened in January and closed in March does not need reopening unless the GM says otherwise.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-30
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-30

Next game vs BUF on Wednesday 30 November 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether each young player is getting the games his production and potential have earned, and tonight against 5-11 BUF is the kind of night where you can afford to adjust usage without risking a result.

**Chlup** at 17 points in 23 games on 20.6 MPG is getting everything he has earned. He's the first recommendation I made for the top line and the GM kept him on the second; at 0.74 pts/g he's producing first-line numbers regardless. No change needed.

**Nash** at 15 points in 23 on 14.5 MPG and **Chistov** at 14 in 23 on 19.8 are both playing every game at appropriate levels. No issues.

**Gardener** is the clearest case on the sheet: 0 points in 14 games on 2.9 MPG, morale 82. He is not developing at three minutes a night, and he is not contributing. I recommended a permanent scratch on November 24th and the GM partially took it (he played one game since, still on the fourth line). He needs to be scratched fully. At 20 with POTE 98, he gets a real audition at next camp, but carrying him in the lineup now costs nothing and helps nobody.

**Spezza** at 4.4 MPG with morale 82 and Upshall at 5.1 MPG with morale 82 are the same problem. Both are POTE 99 kids at 22 sitting in the 70s morale band (costing them 2 points off every grade), both producing under 0.30 pts/g on garbage minutes. This is the collapse pattern I flagged in October. Tonight against BUF, give one of them 10+ minutes in a real role. If neither can produce at 10 MPG, stop dressing them and let the next guy have the audition. The 4-to-5-minute spot-check is the worst outcome: it kills their morale without helping the team.

**Spacek** at 20 has morale 76, the lowest on the roster, on 6 games and 5.8 MPG. He's producing 0.50 pts/g in his limited chances, which is respectable, but at 76 he's costing himself two points per grade. Either dress him properly or stop dressing him. The in-and-out is doing damage.

**Colaiacovo** at 3 points in 23 games (0.13 pts/g) is not earning 12.5 MPG a night. I recommended scratching him last week and the GM passed. I understand why: Stahle at 0.22 and Eminger at 0.29 are no improvement, so we have no better option. This is a roster gap, not a usage problem. He stays in tonight because we need the body, but the summer needs to fix third-pair defence.

**Gaborik** is scratched at 23 with 8 points in 17 games on 22.6 MPG (0.47 pts/g). Those minutes with that return means he's over-iced for his current level. The scratch is correct.

**Eminger** at 7 games, 0.29 pts/g is the trade candidate I flagged last season. His status here is moot; he should be moved at the deadline regardless of development.

## Development trends

The development picture from October 12th to today splits clean: the young core is arriving, the depth forwards are dead, and the veterans are still carrying us but won't next year.

**Chlup** at 0.73 pts/g on 21.3 MPG over 23 games at 19 is what a franchise centre looks like. The 1.00 reading in the brief was a single game. Over the season his production has stabilized at a rate that justifies every minute he gets. No concern here.

**Fischer** at 0.80 pts/g on 21.8 MPG across 6 games is the GM being right to keep him. The GM's words from January were "Fischer is very very good" and the card backs it. His minutes doubled from 10 to 21.8 in this window. Let him keep the second-pair top slot.

**Gaborik** back from the absence and at 0.47 on 22.6 MPG over 17 games at 23. First-line winger production. He is ready for everything we have.

**Nash** improved year-over-year from 0.43 (last season, 12.7 MPG) to 0.64 (this season, 14.4 MPG over 23 games). The system-fit concern from March is fading. He's growing into the role.

**Alexeev** is at 0.33 pts/g over 16 games in this window on 11.5 MPG. My November 17th threshold was 0.45; he is well below it. Last season he was 0.55 on less ice. He is not holding production at the new minutes. The dressing recommendation weakens with every game he stays below 0.45.

**Spacek** at 0.40 on 3.6 MPG over 6 games and **Upshall** at 0.23 on 4.3 MPG over 14 games are the collapse pattern again. Minutes fell from 16-17 to 3-4, production followed. They are 20 and 22. This season is done for both of them. The only lever is camp next fall.

**Spezza** at 0.24 on 4.4 MPG over 17 games at 22. Same story, second consecutive season. POTE 99 and we cannot make it work at this role level. Offseason audition or release.

**Sundin** at 0.82 on 23.6 MPG and **Mogilny** at 0.59 on 23.5 MPG, ages 34 and 36 respectively. Both are producing, both are running heavy loads. That is fine tonight. But 23+ MPG at those ages is not sustainable into the next season, and the succession at centre for Sundin is Chlup. The transition needs to happen by training camp, not gradually during the season. Start planning for Sundin's minutes to drop from 23 to 16-18 next year, with the gap filled by Chlup and whoever else we add.

**Roberts** at 39, 8 games, 13.7 MPG, 0.29 pts/g. Managed correctly. His role is shrinking the right way.

**Eminger** at 0.29 over 7 games on 19.9 MPG continues the slide. The trade urgency from March stands; he's a UFA after this year.

## Morale watch

The room is lifting across the board on the winning streak; everyone gained 5 or more morale points since the last save. No one needs a lineup change tonight for morale reasons.

**Richards** sits at 87 morale on 12.7 MPG. His calibre puts him in the 17-minute band, so he is 4.3 minutes short. He was at 78 in October on 11.8; results have carried him up 9 points, but the minutes gap that started this hasn't closed. If the winning stops he will slide back fast. This is not a tonight problem, but it is the one structural morale issue on the roster.

**Lundmark** at 82, **Upshall** at 82, **Spezza** at 82, **Gardener** at 82. All four are in the 70s or low 80s expecting around 10 minutes and getting 3 to 5. The −1 morale penalty on every grade is already biting them. They are not in crisis and the streak is holding them, but they are the next group to fall if results turn. Gardener at 2.9 MPG over 14 games with zero points is the weakest case for dressing him at all; the rest are contributing something (Spezza 4 pts, Upshall 4 pts).

**St. Jacques** jumped from 82 to 97 (+15) after playing only 5 games at 12.2 MPG. He is fine. The streak did that, not the minutes.

**The top nine and both top pairs** are all at 97 with appropriate ice time. No intervention needed.

No change for tonight against Buffalo.

## Role composition

The role question is whether these units do what their slot demands. Against BUF at 5-11, this is a development-friendly night, so the checking identity matters less than usual, but structural fit still governs whether young players are growing into real roles or getting scraps.

**Jackman** carries three roles: first-line D, PP1, and PK1. At 0.88 pts/g he's earning every minute. No change needed, but note he's the only player above 90 in checking (91) and his absence would expose us everywhere.

**Klesla** is also on three units: first-line D, PP1, and PK2. At 0.29 pts/g he's producing almost nothing. Putting a declining, sellable D on the penalty kill wastes a development slot for a young defender and gives him minutes we won't get value from. On a night against a 5-11 team, pull him off K2. That's a role-gap fix, not a matchup one.

**L3** (Richards centre, Alexeev and Lundmark wings, St. Jacques and Colaiacovo on the back end) checks at a mean of 68. That's a skill line wearing a third-line jersey. It doesn't matter against BUF, but it means we have no checking third line for games that demand one. That's the roster gap: the second-best checking forward is Nash at 81, the next options (Roberts 83, McCabe 82) are scratched. We are one injury to Jackman or Nash away from having no legitimate checking centre.

**K2** stamina is 54 mean. Spezza, Upshall, Hainsey, and Klesla will gas on a PK shift, but against BUF's weak power play that's tolerable tonight. Remove Klesla from this unit and give the fourth spot to Colaiacovo or St. Jacques, who need PK reps to grow.

**L4** at Gardener, Spezza, Upshall is only three forwards with no D partner (by design). With BUF bad enough to give these guys real shifts, the problem isn't composition, it's deployment: the GM controls the slot order, so putting L4 on earlier in the game gives them the minutes they need.

## Opponent matchup

The question for tonight is whether we need to adjust anything to beat Buffalo, and the answer is no. We are better than them at every position on the sheet, and the lines are already in the right order to exploit it.

**The first line vs theirs** is the cleanest comparison. Sundin at 92 against Briere at 76 is a 16-point gap at centre. Chistov at 87 handles Hartnell at 79. Mogilny at 89 has six on Nolan at 82. Behind them Jackman and Klesla at 86 and 87 face Zhitnik at 77 and Bouchard at 73. Our top pair is ten points better than theirs in raw grade. This is the night we run them.

**Second line** carries the same story. Nash, Chlup and Afinogenov at 85, 87 and 86 against Cullen, Drury and Kotalik at 71, 81 and 74. Only Drury is within reach, and Hainsey at 77 is a fair match for him. Safronov at 68 is the soft spot on our D2, but Bombardir at 69 and McKee at 70 are no threat to exploit it.

**Third line** is where I'd expect the game to be decided on the scoresheet. Richards at 87, Lundmark at 81 and Alexeev at 80 against Gaustad at 68, Pyatt at 72 and Dumont at 72. We are fifteen points deep at centre and nine on each wing. St. Jacques and Colaiacovo at 66 and 76 face Laukkanen and Wallin at 70 and 66. Roughly even back end, but our forwards will outplay their D.

**Goaltending:** Ouellet at 86 with no fatigue marker is the start. Biron at 83 carries morale 74, and a goalie with low confidence against a team scoring 3.30 a night is a bad place to be.

**BUF's power play is 7-for-99.** Seven point one percent. They will not score on us with the man advantage. Our PP at 6-for-21 (28.6%) against a PK that has been breached 99 times this season should convert tonight.

No change. The lines are right, the D slots are right, Ouellet starts, and we should win this comfortably.

## Owed

**The standing job: who should go at the end of the season, defenceman by defenceman.**

**Klesla** is the one thing that changed. He had broken through my 0.30 sell floor on 11-26 at 0.29 pts/g over 21 games, and his OVR had dipped to 86. Two games later he has 8 points in 23 for 0.35, and his OVR is back to 87. He added 2 points in 2 games and his card cleaned itself up. If we are moving him this year, right now the 87 looks presentable and the $0.90M x 1 is easy to absorb. Do not wait for the season rate to catch up to the production; it will not.

**Jackman** at 16 points in 23 is 0.70 pts/g, down from 0.88 after 16 games. He added only 2 points in the 7 games since the hot window peaked. Still well above the 0.55 keep threshold I set, so he stays on the keep list, but if the rate keeps bleeding the way it has over games 17-23 (0.29 over that stretch) he hits the re-evaluation trigger by late December. Watching, not selling.

**Colaiacovo** at 0.13 over 23 games with zero goals. Unchanged from last week. Still the weakest regular D by a wide margin. Scratch recommendation stands. At $1.40M x 4 the contract is a liability; if no one takes it at the deadline, do not dress him beyond cup-grade appearances.

**Hainsey** at 0.35 over 17 games, 20.9 MPG, $1.40M x 6. He is doing the job we asked him to. Keep.

**Stahle** at 0.22 over 18 games on 12.5 MPG at 21. Low but he is young and minutes are limited. Keep developing him or give him more, but he is not a sell candidate this year.

**Safronov** at 0.40 over 10 on 20 MPG is productive for a $0.90M depth D. Keep.

**Eminger** at 0.29 over 7 is too small a sample to judge. $2.20M x 4 locks him. Not on the list.

**McCabe** at $3.00M x 3 with zero games this season is dead weight. If anyone takes him before the deadline it is pure salary dump; do not expect a return.

**St. Jacques** expires at 66 OVR with 0 points in 5 games. Let him go.

No structural change from last delivery. Klesla is the one with movement: the sell window reopened, and a buyer looking at 87 OVR, cheap, expiring, would sign up for that card today without knowing the underlying 0.35 is not good.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-27
