# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-27

Toronto 13-5-0, 34 pts after 22 games.

## Role coverage

Which roles does Toronto have enough of, and which ones can they not fix with a lineup card? The answer is two: toughness is genuinely missing at 80+, and checking is thin on the ice because four of six available 80+ checkers are not in any unit.

**Toughness** — zero players at TOUG 80+. Jackman at 75 is the best the roster offers, followed by Roberts at 73 and McCabe at 73. This is not a deployment problem. There is no internal fix. This is the gap that drives every February package tracked since October: Kurka (CAR, TOUG 88, 90 CHKG), Bell (CHI, TOUG 88), Komisarek (MTL, TOUG 86), Bertuzzi (VAN, TOUG 83). The coach's note about "no fourth-line checking solution" and Nash at 82 likely refers to a displayed grade or composite, not stored CHKG, because the checking list tops out at Jackman 87 and Nash does not appear. The gap is real.

**Checking** — six players at CHKG 80+, but only Jackman (87, age 24) and Upshall (80, age 22) are lined. Roberts at 86 and 39 years old, McCabe at 86 and 30, Tucker at 83 and 30, and Fischer at 82 and 25 are all sitting in no unit. Lining three of those four would take the count from 2 to 5 or 6 deployed checkers, which is where a playoff team needs to be. But three of those four are 30 or older. This is a deployment problem today and a trajectory problem in 2006-07: after next season, Jackman is the only sub-30 checker left unless Upshall breaks through or Fischer stays.

**Faceoffs** — only Sundin at FACE 90 is an elite draw-taker. Wallin at 83 (age 25) is on the roster but not lined, which is the cheapest internal fix. Chlup at 75 and Richards at 70 are the next best, and both are lined. Wallin could take the second or third draws immediately. Beyond that, Bell at FACE 88 remains the only league-wide target that closes toughness and faceoffs simultaneously, though the Bell package (Tucker + St. Jacques + R3) would remove one of the four not-lined checkers, which is an acceptable trade at TOUG 88 versus Tucker's 70.

**Scoring and speed** — not gaps. Eleven scorers at 80+, 25 speed players at 80+. Gaborik at 92 scoring and 98 speed sits in no unit, which is a coach's call, not a roster hole. Roberts at 88 scoring, Abid at 86, Koltsov at 92 speed — all not lined. The club has more skill than the lineup uses. That is deployment, not coverage.

**Stamina and durability** — covered for now. Twelve at ENDU 80+, five at INJU 80+. The Mogilny flag (36 years old, 23.6 MPG, ENDU 91) is a usage problem, not a depth problem. The coach is right to target 18 MPG. Kaberle at INJU 97 and ENDU 97 (age 27) is the most durable player on the club and sits in no unit, which is unusual.

**Goalies** — Luongo at 94 overall and 0.940 SV in 8 games is an arrived number-one. Tellqvist at 1.86 GAA and 0.936 SV in 8 games with 6 years of contract left is a legitimate backup. Ouellet at 24 provides depth. Covered through 2006-07, but Luongo has one year left; that renewal window arrives this July.

The single unresolved question the Feb 24 contradiction raised — six stored TOUG 80+ versus zero — is now settled. The November data confirms zero. The Feb 21 count was wrong or used a different metric. No player on this roster carries stored TOUG 80+.

## Trajectory

The trajectory question is whether this roster's contracts and age curve protect three seasons or collapse into one. They mostly do, with two structural threats: Gaborik's $11.90M anchor and a 2009 cluster where 11 players worth $37.40M hit free agency the same summer.

**Age shape is healthy.** 29 of 34 players are 29 or under. Five veterans (Sundin 34, Mogilny 36, Roberts 39, Tucker 30, McCabe 30) sits inside the manual's 5-7 target. Thirteen players are 23 or under with nine of those carrying POTE 94+. This is the shape the manual describes. The problem is not who we have; it is what we pay for players who do not play.

**Gaborik** is 13.2% of payroll for zero ice time. $11.90M against a $35.91M profit means he costs a third of annual profit every season he sits. Four more years remain after this one: $47.60M. Moving him by March 2006 is the single highest-impact trajectory move available, because the freed salary is exactly what a July 2006 Iginla re-signing requires.

**Luongo and Chlup expire together in July 2006** at $1.60M and $2.34M respectively. Luongo is 26, entering his prime, and the only reason the goalie situation is solved. Chlup is 19 with 16 points in 22 games on $2.34M, POTE 95. Both must be locked on 5-6 year deals the same week in July. If either slips, the roster has no backup plan at centre or in net.

**The 2009 cluster** ($37.40M, 11 players) sounds alarming but is 3.5 years out and contains players who will have departed or been traded by then. Sundin will be 38. Kaberle 31. The core that needs re-signing in 2009 is Richards (29, $6.70M), Nash (25, $3.90M), Chistov (26, $5.00M), and Eminger (26, $2.20M) — a realistic $18-20M in re-signings if all four are still here. Manageable if Gaborik is gone and the Fischer/McCabe/Cole contracts are dealt in 2007-08.

**The 2006 summer (1 year left, 9 players, $15.44M)** is where the real decisions land. Luongo and Chlup are must-sign. Mogilny at 36 should walk or take 1 year max. Tucker ($1.30M, 0 GP) is a chip. Koltsov ($1.10M, 0 GP, POTE 94) is trade bait or a depth re-signing depending on whether a deal materializes. Spezza and Ouellet at 1 year need minutes to justify renewal at all.

**Draft capital is thin.** Only own R1, R2, R3 remain. Fourth and fifth rounds are gone. This is enough for one February package (a Komisarek or Kurka deal costing R1 plus a piece) but leaves nothing for a second move. If both happen, we are bare entering July.

**Money leaves room to add.** Profit is $35.91M. Payroll exceeds the revenue line by $21.41M, but TV and prestige income carries that. The constraint is not affordability — it is efficiency. Every dollar paying Gaborik, Tucker, McCabe, Roberts, or Fischer to not play is a dollar not paying for a player who does.

## Calendar

Are we buyers or sellers, and what happens on each date that matters? We are buyers at the deadline and keepers in the summer, with one exception that overrides everything else.

**Gaborik.** He is not on the expiring list, but he is the single largest item on this calendar. $11.90M for five more years through July 2010, 8 points in 17 games before the Coach scratched him, and the q153 lookup for his stats this season came back empty, which means he has not played since that last reading. Mid-contract renegotiation is impossible. If he is still on the roster when the deadline passes on 2006-03-19, we carry $47.60M of dead money or watch him walk in 2010 for nothing. He has to move, and the deadline is the last date on which we can recover anything. This is not a February conversation about a need; it is a March conversation about a liability. Open it late February per your own standing order from January 2005.

**The deadline buy.** We are 2nd in the East on 34 points with 60 games left and eight teams making the playoffs. We are comfortably inside. The Coach's gap is a fourth-line checking solution — Nash at 82 TOUG is the ceiling and he is already on L2. The memory files hold three targets that fit: **Bertuzzi** (VAN, TOUG 83, CHKG 87, 94 base), **Kurka** (CAR, TOUG 88, CHKG 90, $0.60M expiring), **Komisarek** (MTL, TOUG 86, CHKG 93, POTE 92). MTL is already 10th in the East on 21 points, so Komisarek's club is selling by November and will be selling in March. VAN and CAR need re-checking in February before I build a proposal. The chips available to fund this are **Tucker** (30, $1.30M expiring, a chip you identified yourself last March) and **Eminger** (21, POTE 99, confirmed as a chip by the Coach's own development clock at 0 GP).

**Klesla** is the summer question nobody has asked yet. 23 years old, 87 overall, POTE 98, 7 points in 22 games at 26 minutes a night, expiring at $0.90M. He is the exact profile the guide says wins cups: young, high likelihood, playing every game. Re-sign him on 3 to 5 years. Trading him for a deadline pick would be a short-term grab that undoes your own blue-line rebuild.

**Mogilny** walks. 36, $5.50M, 23.6 MPG, and the Coach himself flagged 18 MPG as the cap by March. A one-year renewal at a steep discount is possible but I would not bother. Let the money go.

## Summer expiring list, one by one

| Player | Age | Salary | Call | Length |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Mogilny** | 36 | $5.50M | Let go | — |
| **Chlup** | 19 | $2.34M | Renew | 5-6 years |
| **Luongo** | 26 | $1.60M | Renew | 5-6 years |
| **Tucker** | 30 | $1.30M | Trade by deadline | — |
| **Koltsov** | 24 | $1.10M | Renew | 2-3 years |
| **Spezza** | 22 | $1.00M | Renew | 2-3 years |
| **Ouellet** | 24 | $0.90M | Release | — |
| **Klesla** | 23 | $0.90M | Renew | 3-5 years |
| **St. Jacques** | 25 | $0.80M | Trade or release | — |

**Chlup** is 19 with 0.70 pts/g on 21.4 MPG across 21 games. That is first-line centre production at an age where most prospects are still in juniors. Lock him on a long deal the moment the window opens. The $2.34M he is on now will rise, but 5-6 years prevents the ratchet the guide warns about.

**Luongo** at 26, 94 overall, $1.60M. The single most important renewal on the list. Five to six years, and the guide says teams lose good goalies by forgetting. Do not let this drift past August.

**Spezza** at 22 with 0.20 pts/g and below 5 MPG is not a keeper-by-production case, but he is two years older than Chlup and carries NHL experience. Renew on 2-3 years and give the Coach a demand: 14+ MPG or scratch, the same ultimatum that got him dressed in October. If the collapse continues through February, he becomes a trade chip in next season's cycle.

**Koltsov** at 24, $1.10M, renew 2-3 years. Short enough to reassess, long enough to avoid the yearly ratchet.

**Ouellet** and **St. Jacques** are depth. Ouellet can back up but we have Luongo and Tellqvist. St. Jacques was in the Bell package concept. Neither clears 80, so neither triggers the pick mechanic. Release or trade for nothing; do not carry them into a crowded summer renewal.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: who across the league solves Toronto's toughness, checking, and centre-depth gaps, and why would their club say yes in February. The answer is five players at the front of the queue, led by Jovanovski.

**Jovanovski** is the single best acquisition available. TOUG 93, CHKG 94, 89 overall_base, 31.4 MPG, $2.30M expiring at age 29. He closes the toughness gap and the checking gap in one move. VAN sits at 25 points with 13 expiring contracts and the league's lowest payroll at $46.36M. They have no path to re-signing all of Naslund, Morrison, Linden, Ohlund AND Jovanovski. He is their highest-graded tradeable asset.

**Vasicek** is the best value in the league right now. 82 overall, 18 points in 22 games, FACE 80, POTE 87, $0.40M expiring, age 25. He is a top-six centre who takes draws and produces. CAR at 24 points with 14 expiring deals and $63.79M payroll must shed salary they cannot recover. At $0.40M he costs less than our fourth-liners.

**Semenov** is the best young defenseman on a seller. TOUG 87, CHKG 86, POTE 87, age 24, $0.60M expiring, already logging 33.5 MPG. EDM at 22 points with 5 expiring contracts will not re-sign him. He is both a deadline rental AND a long-term keeper if his POTE holds. The package should be cheaper than Jovanovski because his overall is 78 rather than 89.

**Bell** fixes two gaps at once: TOUG 86 and FACE 88, at 25 years old and $0.90M. CHI at 16 points with 8 expiring deals cannot keep him. The package (Tucker plus St. Jacques plus R3) removes one of our not-lined checkers, which is acceptable when the return is a 25-year-old who solves the centre-specific toughness gap.

**Hill** is the rental option: 24 points from a defenseman at age 35 with TOUG 88 and CHKG 89, $2.30M expiring. CAR must sell him or lose him for nothing. He gives us a top-pairing scoring D for the playoff run, but POTE 61 means he goes nowhere after this year.

**Sopel** is the production bargain: 21 points from a D at $0.60M, age 28, POTE 78, CHKG 77. He does not solve toughness but he solves scoring from the back end at a fraction of any other option. Same VAN logic.

**Nylander** at 21 with POTE 93 and 14 points in 20 games at $0.95M is the long-term development target. SJ at 20 points with 14 expiring and $66.24M payroll (highest in the league) must shed salary. He is not a playoff fix but a 2007 core piece if we keep him on that cheap deal.

Kurka (CAR, TOUG 88, CHKG 90) appeared in earlier notes as our primary toughness target but does not surface in this round's expiring-player queries. Either his contract status changed or his displayed grades moved. He needs verification before February.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: what do we hand across the table for Jovanovski, Vasicek, and Bell, and what does each club get back that makes them say yes before the trade window closes. The answer is three packages that can run simultaneously, use different players, and collectively solve the toughness gap, the checking gap, and the centre depth problem for a net payroll change of +$0.30M. But they burn all three remaining draft picks, and that is the trade-off.

**Jovanovski to Klesla plus R1** is the priority. He is the only player in the league above 90 on both toughness (93) and checking (94), which means one acquisition solves the two gaps the coach cannot fix with a lineup card. VAN sits at 25 points with 13 expiring contracts and $46.36M payroll, the lowest in the league. They will not re-sign Naslund, Morrison, Linden, Ohlund and Jovanovski. Getting Klesla (23, POTE 97, 7 points in 22 games, SPEE 88) plus a first-round pick for a rental they lose in July is a clean rebuild move. We add $2.30M for two months, shed Klesla's $0.90M. Net cost: $1.40M through March. In July Jovanovski walks and the slot opens.

**Vasicek to Koltsov plus R3** is the best value in hockey right now. 18 points in 22 games at 25, FACE 80, POTE 87, $0.40M. CAR at 24 points with 14 expiring deals and $63.79M payroll cannot keep him. They get Koltsov (24, POTE 94, ACCE 96) on a one-year deal at $1.10M plus a third-rounder — a development piece and a pick instead of losing Vasicek for nothing. We shed $1.10M and add $0.40M. Net saving: $0.70M. This deal makes us richer and better simultaneously.

**Bell to Tucker plus R2** is the cheapest cost. Bell at 25 carries TOUG 86 and FACE 88, solving both the centre-specific toughness gap and the faceoff gap below Sundin's lone 90. CHI at 16 points with 18 expiring contracts is in full teardown and cannot re-sign him. They get Tucker (30, CHKG 92) as a veteran locker-room presence for the remainder plus a second-rounder for the rebuild. We shed $1.30M and add $0.90M. Net saving: $0.40M.

**Sequencing.** All three can run simultaneously because they use different players (Klesla, Koltsov, Tucker) and different picks (R1, R3, R2). If the GM wants to preserve draft capital for July, execute Jovanovski and Vasicek only (R1 + R3), keeping R2. All three leaves us with zero picks entering the 2006 draft, which is risky but not fatal given our roster depth.

**If none land.** Move Tucker before March 4 for a pick alone using the 80-plus-rental mechanic (CHKG 92, 88 TOUG, expiring, 0 GP). That guarantees at least one asset return from a player who would otherwise walk for nothing. Abid at 0 GP and St. Jacques at 0 GP are second candidates. Do not chase Semenov or Hill as fallbacks — they require more than what Tucker alone can buy.

## Owed

**Task #2 (Luongo availability and DiPietro monitoring for goalie trade window):** This task was closed on the GM's order of 2005-03-19 ("Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks"). I am delivering the final reading so the ledger is clean.

**Luongo** is on the roster at 95 overall, up from 94 at my November 13 reading. He has 8 GP in 22 team games, which is a backup's workload. At 26, 1 year left, $1.60M, he is a pending restricted free agent next summer. The renewal question is live but the trade-window question that January's task was built around is dead: the GM decided in March to keep him and Belfour as the two 90+ playoff goalies. No trade window for Luongo exists this year.

**DiPietro** — no data. He does not appear on Toronto's roster or in the league's top 60. I have no ice-time or development figures to report because the monitoring stopped when the GM closed the task on March 19. If he is on a roster somewhere, I would need a query to find him, but the task's purpose (feeding a goalie trade window) is moot per that standing order.

What has changed since my last word on this: Luongo moved 94 to 95. Everything else is the same as November 13.



**Delivered:** #2 — final status delivered. Luongo at 95 overall, 8 GP, 1 year $1.60M. DiPietro: not monitored since task closure on March 19, no data to report. Task complete.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-27
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-27

Next game at PHI on Tuesday 29 November 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether each young player is getting the games his performance has earned, and the answer splits into three groups: two players who deserve more, three who deserve less, and the rest who are fine where they are.

**Chlup** is at 16 points in 22 games on 20.6 MPG and the second line. That is a first-line rate at 19. I have put this recommendation in three times now and it has not been taken. He is already playing first-line minutes; he is not playing on the first line. The line slot matters for who he plays with, and right now the system is giving him second-line wingers.

**Nash** is at 15 points in 22 games on 14.3 MPG, 0.68 pts/g. Same case, same line. At that rate and that age, 14 minutes and the second line are both too little. Moving him to the first line right wing alongside Chlup and a veteran is the natural next step.

**Gardener** is at 0 points in 13 games on 3.2 MPG. I recommended scratching him permanently on November 24th, the GM acted, and he still got into one of those two games and scored zero. He is still dressed. The collapse pattern says 3.2 MPG with zero production is not a development opportunity, it is a roster spot being wasted. He needs to come out.

**Spacek** is at 3 points in 6 games on 5.8 MPG with morale at 76, the lowest on the young roster. He is scratched and barely playing. The 76 is the flag: morale that low costs him points off every grade, and the pattern from Spezza and Upshall is that once morale dips below 80 the collapse becomes self-reinforcing. Either dress him for a genuine run of 15+ MPG or confirm he is out for the stretch. Carrying him in this half-state is the worst option.

**Spezza** (4 pts, 4.6 MPG, morale 82) and **Upshall** (4 pts, 5.5 MPG, morale 82) are both in the pattern and both on the fourth line at low minutes. They are not yet at the point where I say cut them, but at 82 morale and under 5 MPG they are not developing either. No change this activation, but if either drops to 78 or below by December they come out.

**Colaiacovo** is at 3 points in 22 games on 12.5 MPG. That is 0.14 pts/g, the lowest production among dressed players. But his MPG is above the 8-MPG threshold I set on November 17th, so he stays. Watch him closely.

**Alexeev** is at 7 points in 15 games, 0.47 pts/g on 11.1 MPG. Above the 0.45 threshold I set. The 25-game reassessment is still ten games away. No change.

The rest are fine. **Chistov** is earning first-line minutes with 11 points on 19.5 MPG. **Klesla** at 0.32 pts/g on 26.2 MPG is the sell-list rate I flagged, but that is a trade question, not a development one. **Gaborik** at 8 points in 17 games on 22.6 MPG is solid when dressed. **Stahle** at 4 points in 18 games on 12.5 MPG is reasonable third-pairing output for 21. **Eminger** at 2 points in 7 games is a sell candidate, so the low games played is intentional.

## Development trends

The window shows who is growing into their role and who is stalling despite games, and the answer changes how we deploy the back half of this roster.

**Hainsey** at 0.38 pts/g on 20.9 MPG over 16 games is the cleanest development story on this roster. He went from zero games to a full-time D-pair job and is producing above Stahle (0.24 on 12.9) and Colaiacovo (0.14 on 12.8) at comparable or lower minutes. The 11-16 call to dress him was right and the trend says keep him there.

**Gaborik** at 0.47 pts/g on 22.6 MPG over 17 games is back and building. He had zero games in the first window, so everything after that is from a standing start. At 23, 0.47 climbing toward his career norms is on schedule. Nothing to change.

**Jackman** went from 41.0 MPG to 25.4 and his production went from 0.48 (last season, my March note) to 0.71. The load-spreading worked. This is the single clearest case of a player improving because his minutes came down. Keep the current distribution.

**Alexeev** is at 0.36 pts/g on 11.4 MPG over 15 games. I set a 0.45 floor on 11-17 for reassessment at 25 games. He has not reached 25 games but he is already below the threshold with 10 more to play. The dressing recommendation weakens further. At 23 with 0.36, he is not outproducing anyone on the roster who is currently playing.

**Colaiacovo** at 0.14 pts/g on 12.8 MPG over 22 games is the weakest young D by a wide margin. Stahle produces 0.24 on 12.9 minutes, Hainsey 0.38 on 20.9. Colaiacovo is the oldest of the three at 22 and the least productive per minute. My existing note says scratch him if MPG stays under 8; his MPG is above that threshold, but his rate is so low that the minutes are not earning their slot. I would move his spot to Stahle, who is a year younger and producing more per shift.

**Spezza** at 0.25 pts/g on 4.6 MPG over 16 games and **Upshall** at 0.25 on 4.7 over 13 games are both in the collapse pattern exactly as predicted. The season is a write-off for both. The decision comes at next camp, not now.

**Safronov** at 0.44 pts/g on 20.0 MPG over 9 games is a small sample but worth watching. At 24, if that holds past 15 games he has a case for a regular D-pair spot over Colaiacovo.

**Abid** has zero games in the entire window. At 0.84 pts/g career rate and 25, carrying him as a healthy scratch is wasting a roster spot and damaging his morale. Either dress him or tell the GM he is a trade candidate.

**Mogilny at 23.5 MPG at age 36** is the workload flag. He is producing 0.57 which is fine, but at 36 those minutes will shorten his runway. If we want him effective in a playoff run, his minutes should come down to around 18-19.

**Afinogenov** at 0.62 pts/g continues the slide from 0.73 last season. The system-fit problem from May is still there. No change for this game, but the offseason review is overdue.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy. The top nine forwards and the top two defensive pairs are all at 97 morale on a winning stretch, and their minutes sit at or above what their calibre demands. No one needs ice time added or taken right now.

**Richards** is the one to keep an eye on: 87 morale on 12.6 MPG, four minutes below the 17 a night his calibre expects. He was at 78 on October 20th and has climbed nine points since, but that is the team winning doing the work, not a minutes fix. If Toronto hits a cold spell, he drops first. I am not touching the second line to fix this -- Chlup at 0.73 pts/g and Nash at 0.68 have earned their ice, and the GM was clear about not pulling players who are producing. Watch him in December.

**St. Jacques** jumped 15 points to 97 after getting 12 MPG over 4 games. Whatever shift gave him that role worked; leave it alone.

**The fourth line** (Gardener 82 on 3.2 MPG/0 points in 13 games, Upshall 82 on 5.5/4pts in 13, Spezza 82 on 4.6/4pts in 16, Lundmark 82 on 4.7/2pts in 14) is right where you would expect depth men with depth minutes to sit. No morale intervention needed -- the fix for Gardener is a scratch, not more ice, and the GM already took that recommendation on November 24th.

**Scratched regulars** (Fischer 91, Kaberle 91, Gaborik 96, Stahle 96, Koltsov 100) are all comfortable. No concern.

Obligation #1 (D analysis for the season-long sell list) belongs to the matchup phase, not this one. It will be delivered when I assess PHI's offense on Tuesday.

## Role composition

**Are the units built right, or are we short?** The units are broadly sound but one D pair is carrying a player 18 grades below everyone else, and the D-minute concentration I've been tracking since October is still hurting us.

**St. Jacques** is at 66 overall and has appeared in 4 games for 12.0 MPG. He is the weakest player on any current defensive pair by a wide margin -- Colaiacovo on his left is already the lowest-graded regular D at 76, and St. Jacques is ten below that. Fischer is sitting on the bench at 84 OVR with 19.8 MPG over 6 appearances. He is a better fit on any pair than St. Jacques, and the auto-pairing system means slotting him at pair three gives him the opponent's third line, which is exactly the assignment he can handle right now.

**Jackman and Klesla** are still eating 26.1 and 26.2 MPG respectively across 22 games. The concentration was worse in October (33 and 34), so it has come down, but these two are still absorbing roughly 43% of all D minutes. Putting Fischer in at pair three at least gives the coaching staff a fourth body capable of real shifts, which is the lever I control.

**Forward lines need no surgery.** L1 is a scoring line (90/99 scoring, 94/99 speed) anchored by Jackman's 92 checking. L2 has Nash's 82 checking and Hainsey's 99 speed giving it a two-way spine. L3 is a playmaking unit with Richards at 93 and that's exactly what a third line should be. The fourth line is thin (Gardener just got scratched per the last recommendation) but the three remaining bodies there are serviceable.

**Checking depth is the structural problem.** Jackman at 92 is our only 90+ checker. Nash at 82 is next. Roberts (84) and McCabe (83) are scratched. If Jackman goes down, there is no replacement who can take the opponent's best forward off the game. That is a roster problem and it is not solved by moving St. Jacques to the press box.

## Opponent matchup

**The question is whether to make any adjustment for a below-.500 Philadelphia club, and the answer is no.** We are 13-5-0 with 3.20 goals a night; they are 9-8-1 at 2.50 a night and 8.1% on the power play (7 of 86). We already beat them 4-3. This is a night to roll with what works.

**Gagne** is their player: 96 speed, 97 aggressiveness, 99 hero, 96 endurance. He never leaves the ice and he hits everyone. Jackman at CHKG 94 with 93 toughness is the man to deal with him, and that is what D pair 1 already gives us against their first line.

**Roenick** at 88 overall is the highest-rated Flyer, and his CHKG 86 means he is a two-way centre who will engage Chlup physically. Chlup at CHKG 79 gives up seven points of checking there, but Nash's TOUG 92 and speed edge (95 vs 92) cover it. I am not swapping D pairs to chase a talent mismatch against a 9-8-1 club. That is the maximize-quality lever and PHI does not earn it.

**Their depth is old.** Ronning is 40, Matteau is 36, Primeau Sr is 34, Desjardins is 36. Our fourth line of Spezza, Gardener and Upshall will have legs on them all night.

**Goalie:** Ouellet at 86 is clearly over Esche at 78. Check Ouellet's fatigue icon before confirming the start per the standing order from January.

No line changes. No D pair swaps. No scratches beyond what is already set.

## Owed

**Defencemen review, #1 (every game, who should go at season's end).** Here's what moved since Saturday's delivery:

**Klesla** added one point in game 22, nudging him from 0.29 to 7 points in 22 games (0.32 pts/g). He's technically back above the 0.30 sell floor by a hair. The sell case hasn't changed: 87 OVR, expiring, 0.32 production, 26.2 MPG burning him down. Deadline urgency is the same. A buyer sees 87; we see a 0.32-rate defenceman whose card gets worse every week he doesn't get moved.

**Jackman** picked up 2 points across games 17-22, taking his season from 14 in 16 (0.88) to 16 in 22 (0.73). Normal regression from a scorching start. He's still well above my 0.55 sell threshold and at $0.70M x 2 he's the best value on the roster. Not a seller.

**Colaiacovo** went from 2 points in 18 to 3 in 22 (0.14 pts/g). My trigger was "if MPG drops below 8 for three consecutive games, scratch permanently." His MPG sits at 12.5, so the trigger hasn't fired by its own rule. But 0 goals, 3 assists, 22 games, 76 OVR, $1.40M x 4 -- he's the worst player in the lineup and the only one who has never scored a goal. I'd put him out now rather than wait for the rule to catch up.

**Hainsey** at 6 points in 16 (0.38) on 20.9 MPG and 77 OVR is doing exactly what a third-pair D should. No change.

**McCabe** still hasn't played. $3.00M x 3, 0 games, 84 OVR. Dead weight, same as May.

**St. Jacques** at 66 OVR, 0 points in 4, is roster filler with no upside. Trade bait or waiver.

No material change to the sell list: **Klesla** is the top priority, **McCabe** and **St. Jacques** are secondary cleanups, **Colaiacovo** I'm now adding as a scratch recommendation.

# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-26

Toronto 12-5-0, 32 pts after 21 games.

## Role coverage

The question this phase answers: can the coach close the roster's checking and toughness deficits from what he already has, or do they require a trade? The answer is checking can be partly patched, toughness cannot.

**Toughness is missing.** Zero players at 80+ on the entire roster. Jackman tops out at 75, Roberts 73, McCabe 73, Chlup 70. The coach's L4 checking mean of 68 and K2 faceoff mean of 52 confirm this shows up in game. No lineup card fixes a zero. Bell (CHI, 88 TOUG, 82 FACE, 80 overall, $0.90M expiring) and Kurka (CAR, 88 TOUG, 90 CHKG, $0.60M expiring) remain the only clean acquisition paths.

**Checking is thin but partly fixable.** Six forwards carry 80+ CHKG: Upshall 80, Fischer 82, Roberts 86, Tucker 83. But only Upshall is lined. Fischer at 25 with 82 CHKG is sitting unused. The coach lines him and L4 checking climbs immediately. Tucker at 30 with 83 CHKG is a confirmed chip from the March standing order. Roberts at 39 with 86 CHKG is not lined and aging out of the plan. Jackman 87 at 24 and McCabe 86 at 30 are defensemen, so their checking doesn't help the forward group.

**Faceoffs are thin.** Sundin 90 is the only 80+ lined center. Wallin at 25 with 83 FACE is on the roster but not in a unit. Chlup 75 is the next best option after Sundin. The coach can give Wallin faceoff duty on the third or fourth line; that lifts K2's mean of 52 without an acquisition. If he cannot or will not, Bell closes this simultaneously with the toughness gap.

**Scoring is covered today but not in 2007.** Eleven players at 80+, but Mogilny 36, Sundin 34, Roberts 39 are the top three. Gaborik 92 is not lined and carries $11.90M through July 2010 with 8 points in 17 games. If Gaborik is dead money and the three veterans decline, the 2007 scoring core is Richards at 85 playmaking and Chlup at 75 FACE, which is not a first line.

**Goalies are solved.** Luongo 94 overall at $1.60M with 1 year left is the priority renewal. Tellqvist at 26 with 6 years and $1.20M is the backup. Task #2 (Luongo monitoring) closed November 13; no further action needed until the renewal window opens in July.

**Durability is a next-year problem.** Only three of the five players at 80+ durability are under 30: Afinogenov 95 at 26, Gardener 92 at 20, Abid 90 at 25. Roberts 98 at 39 and Fischer 92 at 25 carry the rest, but Roberts is not lined. The injury-prone veterans at the top of the lineup mean playoff readiness is a gamble.

## Trajectory

The trajectory question is whether this roster is building toward a peak or spending itself into a wall, and the answer is both: the age shape is healthy, but one contract and two renewal clusters threaten to strangle the roster at exactly the wrong moment.

**Gaborik** is the problem that dwarfs everything else. $11.90M per year for 5 years means $59.50M of committed salary on a 23-year-old producing 8 points in 17 games and sitting as a healthy scratch. That is 13.2% of a $89.94M payroll. Mid-contract renegotiation is impossible. The only path that recovers anything is moving him before his game count erodes further — the October note warned January 2006 as the value-collapse point, and we are five weeks from it.

**Chlup** at 19 years old, 15 points in 21 games, $2.34M, one year left, is the best-value player on the roster and expires in July 2006 alongside **Luongo** (26, POTE 97, $1.60M, 1 year). Both must be locked on 5-6 year deals the same summer. Luongo first: Tellqvist behind him is a clear step down at POTE 91. Chlup second: his current salary is an artifact of his rookie deal and will not survive renewal at his current rate.

**The 2009 cluster** is the manual's warning made real. Eleven players on 4-year deals worth $37.40M all expire the same summer: Richards (30), Chistov (27), Afinogenov (31), Nash (26), Eminger (27), Hainsey (29), Colaiacovo (27), Upshall (25), Wallin (30), Abid (29), Alexeev (28). These are peak-age years and their salaries will have doubled or tripled from current levels. The club will be choosing which five to keep and which six to lose, or paying $70M+ in one summer just to retain the whole group. This is not a 2009 problem — it is a 2006-07 problem because who we sign to 4-year deals *now* determines who joins that pile.

**The 24-29 group at 16 players** is the correct shape and the correct age for winning. The ≤23 group at 13 is above the manual's target but not harmful. The 30-33 group at 2 (Tucker, McCabe) is thin, but with veterans at 34+ (Sundin, Mogilny, Roberts) expiring or fading, the gap fills naturally as the young core ages up. No artificial signing is needed.

**Draft capital** is three original picks (R1, R2, R3) and nothing else. No surplus ammunition. Every February target the scouting list holds (Bertuzzi, Kurka, Komisarek, Jovanovski) requires Eminger, Upshall, or picks we barely have. The 4th-round pick from last deadline is gone. This limits February to one significant package unless we split a target across a player-plus-pick deal.

**Money is not binding.** Profit of $37.01M at $112 tickets and 18,062 attendance means the club can afford to carry Gaborik's dead salary for another year without folding. But carrying it is a choice to spend $11.90M that could fund a Chlup extension ($5-7M projected) plus a veteran depth signing plus draft-pick compensation. The waste is not existential; it is just expensive.

## Calendar

**We are buyers at the deadline, and the summer is a renewal window with one emergency.** Toronto sit 2nd in the East at 32 points from 21 games (.762 pace), eight games above the cut line, and the deadline is 113 days out. Negotiations open late February per the GM's standing order. The plan is: solve the checking gap at the deadline, renew Chlup and Luongo this summer, and move four expiring players before March before their value erodes further.

**Mogilny** is the most urgent deadline asset. At 36, $5.50M expiring, 12 points in 21 games, and 89 overall base, he clears the over-80 pick-recovery mechanic. His value drops with every game he stays. He is a rental we should convert to a pick or a prospect by March. If no deal materializes, he gets a two-year offer at a reduced rate, but at 36 the decline curve is steep and a first-round pick now is worth more than one year of 0.57 pts/g.

**Tucker** and **St. Jacques** are the confirmed packages. The GM's standing order from March 2005 named Tucker as the last chip. St. Jacques at 25, $0.80M expiring is already earmarked in the Bell proposal (Tucker + St. Jacques + R3 to CHI). Both move by March. They are trade currency, not renewal candidates.

**Kurka** (CAR, LW, 23, 90 CHKG, 88 TOUG, 12 pts in 16 GP, $0.60M expiring) is the primary February target. He solves the Coach's role gap — the one forward outside L1-L2 who checks above 80 — at age 23 on a cheap expiring deal. CAR at 16 points with 14 expiring contracts and $63.79M payroll cannot re-sign him. Package: Upshall plus R3. This is the deal to execute first.

**Komisarek** (MTL, D, 23, 93 CHKG, 86 TOUG, POTE 92, $1.10M expiring) is the blue-line upgrade. MTL at 21 points with 8 expiring and $54.89M payroll must sell. But Eminger is the proposed return and he has finally played — 7 games, 2 points in November. If Eminger's minutes climb through January, he becomes more valuable to keep. The decision on Eminger must be made by late February. If Eminger stays, Komisarek requires a different package.

**Bell** (CHI, C, 25) needs a correction. The vault note recorded him as 88 TOUG and 82 FACE; the current screen shows FACE 88 and TOUG 82. He is a faceoff specialist with solid-but-not-elite checking, not a toughness fix. He still addresses K2's faceoff mean of 52, which is a real problem. Package: Tucker + St. Jacques + R3. But if Tucker and St. Jacques are already committed to each other, this package cannot fund both Bell and another deal. Pick one: Bell for faceoffs, or Bertuzzi for checking. You cannot do both without more assets.

**Gaborik** is not on the expiring list. He is locked at $11.90M for five years through July 2010 while producing 8 points in 17 games. Mid-contract renegotiation is impossible. He must move by March or we carry $47.60M of dead money through 2010. His trade value is declining weekly while scratched. This is the single largest financial problem on the roster and it is not on the calendar brief because it is not an expiring contract — it is worse.

**Chlup** is the top summer renewal. 19 years old, 0.74 pts/g at 21.2 MPG, first-line production. $2.34M expiring. He goes on 5-6 years immediately. This is a franchise centre and the contract cannot wait for the deadline window.

**Luongo** at 94 overall, age 26, $1.60M expiring is the second summer renewal. Franchise goalie in his prime. 5-6 years, priority one alongside Chlup. The GM's Jan 2005 order to "fetch a high-90s goalie" is now moot: we have one, and we must keep him.

**Spezza** at 22, 2 points in 12 games, is in collapse. If the numbers do not turn by February, he becomes a third trade chip alongside Tucker. If he recovers above 0.50 pts/g, renew him at $1.00M for 2-3 years. He is too cheap to release and too risky for a long deal.

**Koltsov**, **Ouellet**, and **Klesla** are all under $1.10M and under 25. Renew Koltsov and Klesla on 2-3 year deals at current rates — they are cheap depth that costs nothing to carry. Ouellet stays as backup goalie at $0.90M unless a deal for another keeper materializes. None of them are trade chips; they are the shape the manual asks for (many young players at low cost).

**Colaiacovo** is at 3 points in 21 games (0.14 pts/g), down from 0.11 the Coach flagged. His trade value is actively eroding. He is not expiring, so he is not on the summer list, but he must be moved before March or we are stuck with a player whose value is heading toward zero. He goes in any package that needs a third body.

## League scan

The question this phase answers is: who on the other 29 clubs closes Toronto's toughness gap (zero players at 80+ TOUG), fills the thin faceoff and checking layers, and could realistically be acquired by February given our three picks and the Gaborik dead money? The answer is a shortlist of eight, ranked by need-fit, value, and the probability the other side says yes.

**Kurka** is still the cleanest toughness fix in the league. 88 TOUG, 90 CHKG, 23 years old, $0.60M expiring, 12 points in 16 games. CAR sit at 22 points, carry 14 expiring deals and $63.79M payroll — they must shed before the window closes. Upshall plus a third-rounder is the package. This deal has the highest acceptance probability on the list because the fit is obvious from both sides: we get the only roster-level toughness fix at below-average cost, they get a young winger and a pick.

**Bell** closes two gaps in one body. 82 TOUG, 88 FACE, 80 CHKG, 25 years old, $0.90M expiring, 10 points in 20 games at Chicago. He is not a scorer; he is a top-nine forward who wins draws and hits. CHI at 16 points, 5-10-4, with 8 expiring deals cannot re-sign him. Tucker plus St. Jacques plus a third-rounder remains the package from the November 24 note, but Upshall and R3 also work since Kurka and Bell are not simultaneous needs — if we get Kurka, Bell becomes second priority and vice versa.

**Komisarek** is the best player available on any seller. 86 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 86 overall, POTE 92, 19 points in 21 games at 30.8 minutes a night at age 23. $1.10M expiring. MTL at 21 points with 8 expiring and $54.89M payroll will not re-sign him. Eminger plus R2 is the proposed package from the November 20 note, but Eminger's availability must be confirmed by the GM — the November 6 note confirms him as a chip because he has 0 GP through 13 games and the development clock has expired. If the GM still refuses to part with Eminger, Komisarek becomes unreachable without overpaying.

**Bertuzzi** is the highest-scoring player on a motivated seller with toughness. 81 TOUG, 85 CHKG, 89 overall, 32 points in 20 games at 1.60 points per game. 30 years old, $2.60M expiring. VAN sit at $46.36M payroll — lowest in the league — with 13 expiring deals and $26.67M profit. They are selling everything. Tucker plus R2 is the package from the October 27 note. The catch: Bertuzzi's ceiling is set at 58 POTE and he is 30. He solves tonight and next year, not 2008.

**Heatley** at 80 TOUG clears the toughness bar by zero margin, but everything else is elite: 86 CHKG, 89 overall, POTE 84, 24 years old, $1.10M expiring. ATL at 16 points with 6 expiring deals cannot retain both him and Kovalchuk (90 overall, $1.10M expiring). Whichever ATL keeps, the other moves. The February 28 note flagged this binary. Heatley is the better return because he is younger than Kovalchuk's physical type and his POTE is higher. A strong package is needed — likely Eminger or Tucker plus a first-rounder — because he is an elite asset on a desperate seller. The risk: ATL may simply decide to rebuild and keep both rather than trade with us.

**Witt and Yonkman** are a shutdown pair in one transaction. Witt: 90 TOUG, 94 CHKG, 79 overall, 30, $1.70M expiring. Yonkman: 90 TOUG, 92 CHKG, 77 overall, 24, POTE 89, $0.60M expiring. WSH at 19 points with 5 expiring deals have the fewest on the seller list, which cuts both ways — they have less forced movement but also less reason to keep a pair they cannot both re-sign. Eminger plus R2 covers this if the GM clears Eminger. If we get Komisarek, this package is gone because both compete for the same currency.

**Vandermeer** is the best value on the sheet and I am uncertain it is obtainable. 92 TOUG, 90 CHKG, POTE 92, age 25, $0.40M, expiring. Those grades at that price are unheard of. PHI sit at 23 points, 9-8-1 — only three points behind us. They are not a seller, and a team approaching .500 has no reason to trade away a 25-year-old defenseman with elite potential and a quarter-million salary. Pursue only if PHI's record collapses before February.

**Nedorost** at FLA is the faceoff answer that is not Bell. 84 overall, POTE 94, 80 FACE, 16 points in 23 games at 22.6 minutes, age 23, $1.00M expiring. FLA at 21 points with 5 expiring deals are in the same zone as PHI — not desperate, but not contending either. He is a young center who closes the faceoff gap and provides second-line scoring. Package would need R2 or R3 plus a player; the question is whether FLA values him above a pick given his age and potential.

**Wanvig** is the speculative entry. 82 TOUG, 83 CHKG, POTE 95, age 24, $0.60M expiring, 2 points in 21 games. His production is terrible but his grades and potential are exactly what Toronto lacks: a young tough player who could develop into a top-nine forward. PHX at 5-14-1, 13 points, are the worst team in the league and have 9 expiring deals. They will move him for anything because they cannot use him. A fourth-round pick plus a healthy scratch would probably do it. The risk: he may be busting (the guide's Brad Isbister pattern).

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: what concrete packages close the zero-toughness gap and thin checking layer, given that Toronto are 12-5-0 and in the playoff race, with three picks and a set of collapsing prospects that are the only real currency? Three proposals, ranked by probability of acceptance.

**Kurka for Upshall plus R3.** The cleanest deal on the board. Kurka at 88 TOUG, 90 CHKG, 23, $0.60M expiring is the single best forward on a motivated seller. CAR sit at 22 points with 14 expiring deals and $63.79M payroll — they will not re-sign him and they must move him before his value erodes. We give Upshall (22, POTE 99, $1.50M, 4 years left) plus a third-rounder. Upshall's 3 points in 12 games are irrelevant to what CAR's GM sees: a 22-year-old right winger with potential 99 on a $1.50M deal for four more years. Rebuilding teams hoard exactly this profile. Net payroll effect: we shed $1.50M, gain $0.60M expiring, net minus $0.90M. The Nov 17 note flags Upshall's collapse and suggests substituting Klesla (23, D, POTE 97, $0.90M expiring, 6 pts/21 GP) plus R3 if CAR reject.

**Bell for Koltsov plus St. Jacques plus R2.** Bell at 88 TOUG, 82 FACE, 80 CHKG, 25, $0.90M expiring closes the toughness gap and the faceoff gap simultaneously — one body, two of the coach's three remaining holes. CHI at 5-10-4 with 8 expiring deals are in full rebuild and cannot re-sign him. We give Koltsov (24, POTE 94, ACCE 96, $1.10M expiring, 0 GP) plus St. Jacques (25, POTE 94, CHKG 84, TOUG 80, $0.80M expiring, 3 GP) plus a second-rounder. CHI receive two young players on cheap expiring deals with elite potential — both are one-year auditions at bargain salaries for a rebuilding club — plus a second-round pick. Net payroll: we shed $1.90M, gain $0.90M expiring, net minus $1.00M. Both packages can run simultaneously because they use different picks and different players.

**Komisarek for Colaiacovo plus R1.** The biggest swing. Komisarek at 86 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 86 overall, POTE 92, 19 points in 21 games at 30.8 minutes per night, age 23, $1.10M expiring is the best player on any seller. MTL at 21 points with 8 expiring and $54.89M payroll cannot re-sign him. We give Colaiacovo (22, POTE 99, $1.40M, 4 years, 3 pts/21 GP) plus our first-rounder. The coach flagged Colaiacovo's trade value as eroding — 0.11 points per game over 20 games — which is the argument to move him now rather than later. MTL gets a 22-year-old defenseman with POTE 99 who is actually playing NHL minutes (21 games, unlike Eminger at 7), plus a first-rounder. Net payroll: we shed $1.40M, gain $1.10M expiring, net minus $0.30M. This package avoids the GM's Feb 19 veto on Eminger because it uses Colaiacovo instead. Acceptance is uncertain because MTL may value Colaiacovo's low production as a signal, but POTE 99 and 21 games of NHL action are what a rebuilding GM prices.

**If none land:** The coach lines Fischer (25, 82 CHKG, currently unlined) to lift L4 checking above 68 immediately, and gives Wallin (25, 83 FACE, 0 GP) faceoff duty on L3 or L4 to pull K2's mean of 52 upward. These are patches, not solutions — they close roughly half the gap — but they cost nothing and the zero-toughness problem persists until February closes.

## Owed

**Task #2 — Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window.**

**Luongo** is on our roster at 95 overall, $1.60M, 1 year left, 8 GP in 21 games. I closed this task on November 13 saying he's confirmed and no further monitoring is needed. Nothing has changed. He was the original target; he's arrived. The monitoring question was "can we get him?" and the answer became "we have him" back in the spring.

**DiPietro** sits at NYI, 87 overall, 24, $1.10M expiring (0 years left), 18 GP. He was a fallback target in the January 2005 goalie search. That search is over. He has no role in our plan unless we decide to trade Luongo mid-contract, which we cannot do per the game's contract rules, or unless his renewal falls through in July 2006.

**What's actually live now:** Luongo's renewal window. One year left means he hits the market July 2006. He's at 95 overall on $1.60M. When the window opens, a 5-year offer at a raised salary is the play — at 95 he's Brodeur-tier and will command more from a contender. The task shifts from "monitor for acquisition" to "prepare for renewal." I'll flag it when we're within 30 days of season end.

Nothing has moved since November 13. This task stays closed until the renewal window opens.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-26
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-26

Next game vs WSH on Saturday 26 November 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question: are our 23-and-under players getting the games they've earned at 21 games in? Most are fine. Three need attention.

**Spacek** is the one that concerns me. He's healthy — his old groin injury healed last December — he's producing at 0.50 points per game in his 6 chances, and his morale is 76. That's the lowest on the roster and it's the number that tells me he knows he's being wasted. At 20 with POTE 91, he's at the point where dressing him 12 games or telling him to develop next year are both defensible. What's not defensible is 6 games and falling. His morale at 76 costs him one point off every grade and it will compound.

**Spezza and Upshall** are both in the collapse pattern I've flagged since October. Spezza: 4.3 MPG, 0.20 pts/g, 15 games. Upshall: 5.2 MPG, 0.25 pts/g, 12 games. Both POTE 99, both morale 82. They're not developing at under 5 minutes a night. The only question is whether we keep dressing them as depth fillers or scratch them and free those slots.

**Gardener** has zero points in 12 games on 2.9 MPG. He was already scratched after my 24th recommendation was taken, and the one game he played produced nothing. Confirmed done for this season.

**Gaborik** is out with a leg injury until around December 25th. Not a development issue, just awareness.

**Alexeev** is at 0.50 pts/g over 14 games, above my 0.45 reassessment threshold. No change — he's earning his 67% games played.

**Chlup, Nash, Chistov, Klesla, Colaiacovo** are all dressed every game. No development concern there.

## Development trends

Are our young players growing into their roles or stalling despite games? With 21 games on the board and the Klesla sell window fully open, this is the season's first real development checkpoint.

**Chlup** is the standout. 0.70 pts/g on 21.4 MPG over 21 games at 19. That is first-line production in a second-line role. I have asked twice to move him to first-line centre permanently and it has not happened. Twenty-one games of 0.70 is not a hot streak. Put him at first-line centre now, before December.

**Nash** is climbing. 0.60 pts/g on 13.9 MPG at 21, up from last season's 0.43 on similar minutes. The role expanded and the production followed. He belongs in the top nine.

**Safronov** is the best young defenseman by rate: 0.50 pts/g on 20.0 MPG over 8 games at 24. Small sample, but he outscoring Hainsey (0.27 on 20.9) and Eminger (0.29 on 19.9) on the same ice. He is becoming a second-pair option.

**Klesla** is at 0.30 pts/g on 25.3 MPG over 21 games. Exactly the sell floor I set on November 13th. His rate has not moved. Every game at 0.30 makes his card harder to sell. Maximum urgency on a trade before the deadline.

**Jackman** at 0.70/25.4 over 21 is holding above the 0.55 keeper threshold. The 41 MPG concentration from October has eased. He is fine and stays.

**Fischer** at 0.80 pts/g on 21.8 MPG over 6 games is the best D rate on the roster. The GM was right. Limited games, but when he plays he produces.

**Kaberle** shows 0.20 pts/g on 21.2 MPG over 6 games. Six games is not a verdict, and the GM calls him a star. But that rate on that ice time is not star output. Watch the next 10 games.

**Colaiacovo** at 0.15 pts/g on 12.8 MPG over 21 games at 22 is a bottom-pair rate. The collapse rule was "under 8 MPG" and he is above that, but if Safronov and Hainsey hold their minutes, Colaiacovo drops to third pair or the press box.

**Alexeev** at 0.38 pts/g on 11.8 MPG over 14 games is below the 0.45 threshold from my note. The reassessment window is 25 games. He is trending wrong, but 11 more games will decide it. No change yet.

**Spezza** at 0.20/4.3, **Upshall** at 0.18/4.3, **Brendl** at 0.22/3.6, and **Gardener** at 0 points in 12 games on 1.7 MPG: the young-forward collapse pattern, now five players deep this season. Spezza's 0.20 with POTE 99 at 22 is the saddest. None of these are fixable in-season. The fix is camp.

**Mogilny** is 36 on 23.6 MPG, producing 0.60 pts/g. The rate is respectable for his age. The load is not. At 36, 23.6 minutes a night is the kind of workload that breaks in March. If Gaborik (0.47 on 22.6 over 17) gets his game going, Mogilny's minutes should come down toward 18.

**Sundin** at 34: 0.75 on 23.6 MPG. Carrying the club. No concerns.

**Richards** at 0.70/12.9 is unchanged from last season's system-fit question. No new information.

**Deliverable #1** (defenseman review for end-of-season decisions): Klesla confirmed at sell floor, 0.30/25.3 over 21. Jackman holds keeper status at 0.70/25.4. Safronov is the rising young D at 0.50/20.0. Fischer excellent at 0.80/21.8 over limited games. Kaberle under-producing over 6. Colaiacovo at 0.15 is the weakest starter. Hainsey 0.27 and Stahle 0.24 are developing but below par for their ice time. Eminger at 0.29/19.9 on a locked four-year deal is the problem that will not go away.

## Morale watch

The room is in good shape. The starting lineup all sits at morale 97, and the only forward with a minutes-calibre gap is trending the right way.

**Richards** is at morale 87 on 12.9 MPG. He was at 78 on 11.8 MPG when I flagged this on October 20th. The +9 climb over five weeks tells me the GM's winning streak and the extra minute are working. He is still four minutes short of the 17 MPG I'd expect for a player in the 80s band, but at 14 points in 21 games he's producing on what he gets. The trend is positive; I am not forcing a line change tonight to shave a gap that is closing on its own. If he drops below 85, he moves up.

**Gardener, Upshall, Spezza, Lundmark** all sit at morale 82. They are getting 2.9 to 5.2 MPG each, which is below even the 7 MPG floor for a depth forward. This is the collapse pattern I've tracked before. Gardener's scratch was taken and he played one game with zero points. These four are in the zone where carrying them costs more than it helps.

**Kaberle and Fischer** at 91 are both injured (6 GP each). Their morale dropped with the absence but 91 is not a concern; it will recover when they return. No action needed.

**Luongo** at 86 is the odd man out at backup. He played 8 games and is now behind Ouellet. That's the GM's goalie hierarchy call, not a line problem.

No change for tonight against Washington. The core is happy, the one gap is narrowing.

## Role composition

**Unit composition is sound; roster depth at the checking position is not.** The question that matters for this game against a 6-10 Washington club is whether our lines are built right, and they mostly are. The structural weakness is one we cannot fix with line changes.

**L1** is well-constructed. Jackman's checking 92 anchors a line whose offensive ceiling is Sundin at playmaking 96 and Mogilny at scoring 92. That balance means the line can drive offence without leaving the defensive side empty, and Klesla as the second defenseman gives complementary mobility. No reason to touch it.

**L2** has Chlup centring with Nash (checking 82) and Afinogenov (scoring 94). The faceoff mean of 60 is the soft spot — Chlup at 80 is the only draw-winner, so against a strong centre the possession battle starts at a loss. But the alternative faceoff options (Richards 78, Wallin 88 scratched) don't improve the line's overall profile enough to justify a swap on a night when we need scoring.

**L3** with Richards at playmaking 93 is a genuine skill line. The concern is his ice time (11.8 MPG in my October reading against morale at 78), not his placement. He belongs where he is.

**K1** is the right unit. Jackman 92, Safronov, Chlup, Chistov — mean checking 80 is the highest on the roster. This is who dies on the penalty kill and that is correct.

**K2** at checking mean 72 is thin but acceptable for a second unit. The alternative is pulling McCabe back from the press box (checking 83), but the GM has deliberately kept him out for development reasons that predate this activation.

**L4** is where the roster gap bites. Checking 70, toughness 62, faceoffs 58 mean. No one on that line can win a draw, hold a puck in the corner, or finish a check. This is not an arrangement problem — Roberts, McCabe and Nash are the only players above 80 in checking beyond Jackman, and all three are already assigned or scratched for other reasons.

## Opponent matchup

**The question: what changes for WSH tonight, given they are missing Jagr?** The answer is almost nothing, because their weakness is structural and Jagr's absence deepens it further.

**Jagr is out** (90 OVR, returns December 1st). He is their first-line centre. Without him, their top forward line drops from a 90 to Zubrus at 82, and the entire forward group loses its best puck-handler and shooter. They are already 6-10-3 with a 54/60 goal differential. This is a game we should win on any arrangement of our current lines.

**WSH's top pair of Gonchar and Witt is the real threat.** Gonchar reads 85 with a 96 shot power and 95 hero. Their power play is 6-for-92 (6.5%), so their other units will not beat us, but Gonchar walking in with the puck on the point is the one thing that can produce a goal tonight. Our first pair (Jackman 86, Klesla 87) is matched to theirs through auto-pairing, which is correct.

**Our penalty kill does not need extra attention tonight.** Their 6.5% power play is among the worst numbers I have seen. Our first two kill units are fine as-is; no matchup reason to shuffle them.

**The auto-pairing works for us on every line.** Our L1 gets Jackman/Klesla against their Gonchar/Witt (even, good). Our L2 gets Safronov/Hainsey against their checking pair Yonkman/Pilar (we are deeper up front there). Our L3 gets St. Jacques/Colaiacovo against Doig/Sarich (light matchup, no concern).

**No line change.** This is a maximize-quality night against a weakened opponent, and the current structure is already our best. Development is served because the young guys are already in the lineup on L2 and L4; I do not need to shuffle anyone up against a 6-10-3 team to give them opportunity.

**Deliverable #1 (defensive review):** I need to pull current minutes and recent production for our defensemen to complete the end-of-season evaluation.

## Owed

**Owed item #1: Defensive corps evaluation for end-of-season.** I checked every defenceman's production against the sell floors I set in November. Here's what moved and what didn't.

**Klesla** — The rate has slipped from 0.30 (last week, 20 games) to **0.29** over 21 games. OVR 86, expiring, 26.1 MPG absorbing top-pair minutes for sixth-best point production on the blue line. My sell floor was 0.30. He's now below it. Every game he plays at this rate makes the 86 look worse to a buyer who checks the stat line. This is the top trade candidate and the urgency is maximum.

**Jackman** — Rate dropped from 0.88 (16 games) to **0.71** over 21. That's a three-point pullback, but 0.71 at 24 on a $0.70M x 2 deal is still a breakout. My sell trigger was "below 0.55 by January." No change; he stays.

**Colaiacovo** — 0.14 over 21 (was 0.11 over 18). He got one assist in three games. Still bottom-of-the-roof production at age 22 on 12.4 MPG. My trigger was "under 8 MPG for three consecutive games" and he's at 12.4, so the clause hasn't fired. But the production justifies a deeper look: 0.14 pts/g at 22 with four years and $1.40M is a buy-low candidate for a contender who wants a cheap depth pair, or a waiver candidate if he stays here.

**Hainsey** — 0.27 over 15 on 20.9 MPG. OVR 77, $1.40M x 6. Nobody takes six years of a 77 for nothing. Hard to move; he stays by default.

**McCabe** — Zero games. Still $3.00M x 3 on IR or the press box. Already on the sell list from May. No change.

**Safronov, St. Jacques** — OVR 68 and 66 at ages 24 and 25. Not NHL defenders. They provide bodies for injuries and nothing else. No trade value.

What changed since last week: Klesla dropped below the floor. Everything else is stable or moving in the wrong direction at a pace that doesn't alter the verdict.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-24
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-24

Toronto 12-5-0, 30 pts after 20 games.

## Role coverage

The role-coverage question this November: does the current roster, as it stands and as the coach uses it, have enough bodies at 80+ in each role a contending team needs? The answer splits cleanly: checking is fixable by putting existing players in the lineup, toughness is not, and the faceoff depth behind Sundin at 34 is a two-year cliff.

**Checking** has six players at 80+ (Jackman 87, Roberts 86, McCabe 86, Tucker 83, Fischer 82, Upshall 80), but the coach only lines Jackman and Upshall among forwards. Roberts at 39 and Tucker at 30 sit in no unit, Fischer at 25 the same. Dressing Roberts (the coach already recommended him for PHI), Tucker and Fischer closes this gap without a trade. The problem is utilization, not supply.

**Toughness** is zero at 80+ across all 31 skaters. Jackman 75 is the roster best, Roberts 73, McCabe 73. No line change manufactures toughness; the grade is what it is. This is the one role that requires acquisition. Kurka (CAR, 88 TOUG, 90 CHKG, age 23, $0.60M expiring) remains the cleanest solution: he solves checking simultaneously, he is the age profile we need, and CAR at 16 points with 14 expiring cannot re-sign him.

**Faceoffs** has two at 80+ (Sundin 90, Wallin 83) and Sundin is 34. Chlup at 75, Richards at 70, Gardener at 72 are all below. Wallin at 25 is not lined. Dressing Wallin buys one more season of competent draws, but the long-term answer is a centre who draws at 80+, and none exists on this roster. That is a draft or acquisition question for next summer, not a February trade-deadline question.

**Gaborik** at 92 scoring, 92 playmaking, 98 speed, 88 stamina is the highest-rated forward on the roster and he is not in any line. At $11.90M and five years through July 2010, he is the most expensive player on the team sitting in the press box. Whatever the tactical objection, he must be dressed nightly or he becomes 59 million dollars of dead weight.

**Scoring, playmaking, speed, stamina, clutch, durability** are all covered at depth. No concern.

## Trajectory

Is this club's timeline protected for three seasons, or are we drifting toward a synchronized collapse in 2009? The answer is both: the short term is safe (profit $36.45M, record 12-5-0), but two structural threats — Gaborik's dead contract and the July 2009 cluster — could define the next five years if we do nothing.

**Gaborik** at $11.90M for 5 years through July 2010 is the single worst number on the sheet. 8 points in 17 games as a scratch on 13.2% of total payroll. He cannot be renegotiated, reduced, or bought out mid-contract. He must move by March 2006 or we carry $59.50M on a man the Coach doesn't dress. At 23 with POTE 90 he still has trade value; by 2007 it will have evaporated with his games played. Every month from now to March he is worth less.

**The July 2009 cliff** is the structural problem. Eleven contracts worth $37.40M expire simultaneously: Sundin ($8.40M at 38), Richards, Chistov, Nash, Kaberle, Eminger, Colaiacovo, Upshall, Alexeev, Abid, Wallin. Mid-contract extensions are impossible, so this cannot be staggered. When that summer arrives, the entire young core plus a 38-year-old captain all hit the market at once. The manual warns explicitly about this, and we are standing in it with the contract start-date already chosen. The only lever is to trade pieces we won't want to pay 2009 prices for before they become rental assets, and to have the money ready.

**Luongo and Chlup** both expire July 2006. Luongo reads 94 overall with POTE 97 on $1.60M — elite goalie on a bargain deal that cannot last. Chlup has 15 points in 20 games at 19 with POTE 95. These two are the franchise anchors for the next five years and they need 5-6 year deals the same week. If either walks, the timeline resets.

**Age shape is fine; experience bridge is not.** The 30-33 bucket holds only Tucker (30, scratched, $1.30M expiring) and McCabe (30, 0 GP, $3.00M, 3yr). When Sundin expires at 38 in 2009 and Mogilny leaves this summer, the gap between Roberts' generation and Chlup's will be empty. The manual wants 5-7 veterans; we have the 34+ trio and nobody in the bridge seat. That's a coaching problem before it's a roster problem.

**Draft capital is thin.** Three picks, all ours: R1, R2, R3. No picks from other clubs visible in the current position. This means big packages must be built around players (Eminger, Klesla) rather than picks. The R1 is the only real ammunition for a single-asset acquisition of a top player, and spending it on a rental wastes it.

**The money allows movement.** Profit $36.45M on revenue $66.80M, payroll $89.94M. There is no cap. If Gaborik moves and we acquire a veteran at $3-4M, the net is a payroll reduction. If Mogilny walks this July ($5.50M saved), that funds Luongo's extension plus one more year's worth of anything. The constraint is never "can we afford it" — it's "will the player we want still be available in 2009 when the whole core needs new money."

## Calendar

We are buyers, and we have time. Toronto sit second in the East on 30 points from 20 games with 62 still to play, eight teams make the post-season, and the deadline is 115 days away. The coach has named one gap clearly — no forward outside Jackman checks above 82 and plays regularly — and the plan is to fill it in February, per the GM's standing order that negotiations open late February at the earliest.

**The targets are still on sellers.** I checked this season's records for every February target on my list. PHX are 5-14-1-1 on 13 points, CHI 4-10-1-4 on 14, ATL 6-10-1-2 on 16, WSH 5-10-2-3 on 17, CAR 4-9-5-2 on 20. Every one of those clubs will be selling at the deadline. **Bertuzzi** at VAN (now 7-8-4-1, 23 pts) is the least desperate but still below .500 with a roster full of expiring deals; he remains the best fit because TOUG 83 / CHKG 87 at 94 base solves both the coach's gap and the top-six production question simultaneously. **Kurka** at CAR (TOUG 88, CHKG 90, 12 pts/16 GP, $0.60M expiring) is the cheapest version of the same fix.

**What we give:** The November 2005 pick query confirms TOR owns its own first, second, and third-round picks for the 2006 draft — a change from last season when we had nothing better than a fourth-rounder. That means packages like Eminger + R2 for Komisarek, or Kurka for Upshall + R3, are now fundable with a real pick. **Tucker** ($1.30M, 30, expiring) remains the designated chip. **Eminger** (21, POTE 99, zero GP through this season's first 13) is confirmed dead weight on our timeline and the centrepiece of any blue-line package.

**Mogilny** (36, $5.50M, expiring) is the single biggest summer decision. He is either moved at the deadline for whatever a contender will give for a veteran RW, or he walks in July and we save $5.50M against a $2.34M-to-$1.60M renewal pool for Chlup, Luongo, and Klesla. I would try the deadline route first.

For the summer renewals: Luongo at 94 overall, 26, $1.60M is the highest-priority contract on the board — five or six years, no negotiation games. Chlup at 19 and Klesla at 23 both warrant long-term deals. Spezza (22, $1.00M, 2 pts in 12 GP) is a February-or-summer fork: if the coach gives him minutes and he responds, sign four years; if not, he is the lead component of a Heatley package.

The GM's October 16 question — do we shed salary by moving good players? — has a clean answer in the summer context. The expiring list is nine players totalling $15.44M. If we renew Luongo, Chlup, Klesla, and one of Spezza/Koltsov, we keep four assets and shed Mogilny ($5.50M) plus Tucker ($1.30M) plus Ouellet ($0.90M) or St. Jacques ($0.80M). That is a $8.50M-to-$8.60M reduction against four renewals, none of which will cost more than $3M individually. No good player leaves for money alone.

---

**Task #2** (Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February): Closed 2005-11-13. Luongo confirmed on roster at 94 overall, $1.60M, one year left. No further monitoring needed until renewal window opens in July.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: who across the league closes the coach's explicit gap, a shutdown centre who checks 80+ and eats 14 minutes, and who else at 80+ toughness exists on clubs that must sell? The roster has zero at 80 toughness across 31 skaters, so this is purely an acquisition hunt.

I have several targets from prior work (Kurka, McLaren, Bell, Avery, Doan), but the coach's specific ask is a centre. Avery at LA checks all three boxes (93 FACE, 88 CHKG, 83 TOUG) but produces 6 points in 57 games. Bell at CHI has 88 TOUG and 82 FACE but I need to confirm his position and production. I need to cast wider for centres who check, and also confirm the state of my known targets on clubs that have moved since those notes were filed.

## Trade construction

This phase answers: what can Toronto give that makes a contender or a desperate seller part with a checking centre, and is the trade sheet deep enough to close a zero-at-80-toughness gap before March? The answer is three viable packages ranked by fit and cost, with a fallback if none clear.

**Bell (CHI)** is the cheapest fix that fills the coach's exact ask. He is 25 with 88 toughness, 82 faceoffs, and 80 overall on $0.90M expiring. CHI are 4-10-4 with 18 expiring contracts worth $28.83M. They cannot re-sign everyone. If Bell walks in July, CHI get nothing. Getting St. Jacques (25, D, POTE 94, $0.80M expiring) plus Tucker (30, CHKG 92, TOUG 88, $1.30M expiring, veteran locker presence) plus a third-rounder is more than losing a player for zero. Our payroll drops $1.20M: we give $2.10M in salary and take back $0.90M. Neither player is in any line right now (Tucker 0 GP, St. Jacques 2 GP), so this costs us nothing tonight.

**Holik (NYR)** is the perfect archetype. TOUG 80, CHKG 86, FACE 89, age 34, $9.00M for two more years. NYR's payroll is $92.95M, the league's highest, against profit of $11.89M, the league's lowest. They have 15 expiring contracts worth $42.56M coming due this summer. Holik contributes 7 points in 9 games and will be 35 next season. If we give Klesla (23, D, POTE 97, 6 points/20 GP, $0.90M expiring) plus a second-rounder, NYR shed $8.10M of salary and get a top-potential blueliner already producing. The risk: NYR are 11-4-3 and contending. Holik's 89 faceoffs matter in a playoff series. They might keep him and absorb the cost for one more run. Acceptance is uncertain. Our payroll rises $8.10M to $98.04M, still profitable.

**Kurka (CAR)** is the best pure hockey player on the board — 23 years old, 88 toughness, 90 checking, 12 points in 16 games, $0.60M expiring — but he is a left wing, not a centre. He solves the zero-at-80-toughness problem completely and gives the bottom six real production, but it does not fill the centre slot the coach specifically flagged. CAR are 4-9-2 with 24 expiring worth $38.63M. Koltsov (24, LW, POTE 94, $1.10M expiring, 0 GP) plus Lundmark (24, LW, POTE 97, $0.80M, 2 years, 1 point/12 GP) plus an R3 costs us two unused young wingers and a later pick. Both players carry POTE above 94, which is expensive currency. Only pursue this if the GM decides toughness in the bottom six matters more than filling the centre slot.

**If none land:** Dress Tucker (83 CHKG) and Roberts (86 CHKG, TOUG 92) on the bottom lines now — the role-coverage phase already confirmed checking is fixable through utilization. Accept toughness below 80 for the remaining 62 games. Plan a July free-agent signing or this summer's draft (sort by speed, look for a centre with FACE 80+) as the real solution. The 2006 draft class should carry at least one centre above 78 toughness.



**On task #2 (Luongo monitoring):** This was closed by the GM on 2005-03-19 with the standing order to stop all goalie monitoring. Luongo is confirmed on the roster at 94 overall, 1 year, $1.60M. No further work required until the renewal window opens at season's end.

## Owed

**Task #2 — Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window.**

This task is closed. The GM ordered it closed on 2005-03-19 ("Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks"), and it was reconfirmed closed on 2005-11-13. The original purpose — scouting a trade window during the 2004-05 season — expired with that season. Nothing has changed since the last report because there is nothing left to report on.

**Luongo** is on the roster: 94 overall, 26 years old, 1 year left at $1.60M, 8 GP this season. He arrived as a player and the GM declared goalies solved. The only forward-looking question is his renewal at contract end in July 2006, which is a different task.

**DiPietro** at NYI: 86 overall, 24, 0 years left (expiring), $1.10M, 17 GP. He is no longer a developmental project to monitor — he is a finished product at 86 with an expiring deal. NYI must move him or lose him. If the GM ever wants a cheap young goalie again, DiPietro is the February 2006 trade target, not a monitoring subject.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-24
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-24

Next game at OTT on Friday 25 November 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether our young players are getting the games they've earned, and the answer splits cleanly: five are earning every minute they get, four are being wasted on the fourth line for garbage-time shifts that help nobody, and one young defenceman is getting a full run at 22 and producing nothing worth the ice.

**Chlup** is 20 for 20, 20.4 MPG, 15 points at 19. He has earned the first line and that's where he belongs. No questions.

**Nash** at 20 GP, 14.2 MPG, 12 points (0.60 rate) has outgrown the second line in production terms. He's fine where he is for now; the line change question is for the matchup phase.

**Chistov** at 20 GP, 18.9 MPG on the first line with 10 points (0.50 rate) is holding his own at 22. Earning his spot.

**Klesla** is getting 26.1 MPG every night and producing 6 points at 0.30. The minutes are earned by his role as top-pairing defenceman; the production decline is a trade-value problem, not a development one.

**Colaiacovo** is 20 for 20 at 12.4 MPG with 2 points. The 8 MPG collapse trigger hasn't fired (he's still at 12.4), but 0.11 pts/g over 20 games at age 22 with POTE 99 is the worst production-to-opportunity ratio on the roster. Reassess at 25 games. If he's still under 8 MPG by then he comes out permanently.

**Alexeev** at 13 GP, 11.3 MPG, 7 points (0.54 rate) is getting a fair look and producing above his 0.40 last-season rate. No issues.

**Gaborik** is the odd one. 17 GP, 22.6 MPG when he plays, 8 points at 0.47, and currently scratched. Meanwhile Spezza (3.6 MPG, 2 pts), Upshall (4.8 MPG, 3 pts) and Gardener (2.8 MPG, 0 pts) are dressed on the fourth line for mop-up minutes. Against a 6-9 Ottawa club this is not a "go all out" night, so the development framework applies. Gaborik should be back in the lineup; the three fourth-line players producing at 0.0-0.27 rates are not helping us win or developing.

**Spacek** at 6 GP, 5.8 MPG, morale 76 is deep in the young-forward collapse pattern. His morale is already in the -2 band. Not earning more ice time.

**Stahle** at 18 GP (90%), 12.5 MPG, 4 points (0.22 rate), currently scratched. He's been getting a real run and producing modestly. Scratching him for one game against OTT is a tactical call, not a development crisis. No recommendation to force him back.

## Development trends

The question here is who is moving in which direction since the October baseline, and whether anything in that movement changes the plan for tonight or the season. Six weeks of games gives enough signal to separate flukes from trends, and the answer is split cleanly: the young core is sorting itself faster than expected, and one D prospect has already stopped developing.

**Chlup** is the headline. 0.74 pts/g on 21.2 MPG at 19 years old. My April note said he belongs on the first line permanently; six weeks at 20 games confirm it. The "drop" from 1.00 to 0.74 is meaningless; the 1-game start was noise. This is franchise-centre production and the only question is whether the line assignment matches.

**Colaiacovo** is the alarm. 0.11 pts/g across 20 games on 12.8 MPG. Last season he ran 0.47 on 17.7 MPG. This is not a slow start; this is regression. The Hainsey swap I recommended on 11-16 gave Colaiacovo more ice and his production went down. Per my standing rule: if MPG stays under 8 for three games he comes out permanently, but the problem is deeper than minutes. He cannot produce at 12.8 either. He needs to be addressed at deadline or he becomes a healthy scratch with a future.

**Gardener** at 0 points in 11 games on 1.5 MPG is the young-forward-collapse pattern again. He is dead weight on the roster. Scratch him permanently.

**Spezza** at 0.14 on 3.6 MPG and **Upshall** at 0.20 on 3.7 MPG are the same pattern for the third year running. Neither has taken a step. The dressing spot is doing more harm to them than a healthy scratch would.

**Alexeev** sits at 0.42 on 11.8 MPG across 13 games. My note set 0.45 as the threshold where the dressing recommendation weakens. He is 0.03 below it, but 13 games is still a small sample. Wait for 25 games before deciding. If he's below 0.45 at 25, he comes out.

**Klesla** at 0.32 pts/g confirms the sell-window note from 11-20. Rate has fallen again from 0.38. Each week the card becomes less convincing to a buyer. Priority trade candidate.

**Gaborik** at 0.47 on 22.6 MPG at 23 is underperforming his role. That is top-six ice yielding third-line returns. Could be a form dip, could be the same system-fit issue we saw with Nash and Richards last spring. Watch the next 10 games; if he holds below 0.55 the line assignment needs revisiting.

**Afinogenov** continues sliding: 0.63 on 17.8 MPG, down from 0.73 last season. The decline from 1.17 to 0.73 to 0.63 is three seasons of erosion. At 26 this is a career trajectory change, not a blip.

**Jackman** at 0.68 on 25.1 MPG is above the 0.55 sell threshold I set in November. The breakout is real and holding. He stays.

**Sundin** at 34 producing 0.74 on 23.7 MPG shows no age decline. **Mogilny** at 36 running 0.63 on 23.6 MPG is remarkable for his age. Neither warrants a workload reduction on performance grounds.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy going into Friday at OTT. Every active player sits at 97 morale and climbing on the winning streak.
