The one outlier is **Richards** at 87, ten points below every other dressing skater, and the cause is unchanged from October: 13.1 MPG for a 25-year-old centre producing 13 points in 20 games. He needs 17 minutes a night to stay level with his calibre, and at 13.1 he is paying for it.

**Richards** is the only morale problem minutes can fix. He climbed 5 in the last save (82 to 87), same as the fourth-liners, which tells me the wins are lifting everyone by roughly that amount. But he started ten points lower and the gap is structural: Nash on the same line gets 14.2 MPG, Chlup 20.4, and Richards sits at 13.1 as the third-line centre while producing the same rate as Nash (0.65 vs 0.60 pts/g). If I cannot raise his minutes tonight, his ceiling is 97 only as far as wins carry him, and the moment we lose three straight he drops faster than anyone else on this roster.

**Upshall, Gardener, Spezza, Lundmark** are all at 82 with +5 recent gains. They are getting 3 to 5 MPG each, well under the 10 MPG their 70s-band OVR expects. Wins are holding them. If the team cools, they will fall fast. No action tonight.

**Spacek** at 76 is the roster floor. He has been scratched since October and cannot crack this lineup. His low morale is a roster-depth problem, not a lines problem.

**Luongo** recovered from 77 back to 86 since losing his starter role. Tellqvist and Ouellet have taken the crease. That is fine; he will stabilise as long as we keep winning.

No line change tonight on morale grounds. Richards is the one to watch, and raising his minutes is a matchup-phase decision, not a morale-phase one.

## Role composition

The question is whether these eight units are built from the right pieces, and the short answer is yes on seven of them, and the one that isn't right can't be fixed by moving players around because we don't have what it needs.

**L1** is clean. Sundin at 94 playmaking and 93 faceoffs centres it, Mogilny at 90 scoring and 88 clutch provides the finish, Chistov at 91 playmaking on the wing feeds them both, and Jackman at 90 checking gives the defensive D behind a high-event line. Klesla at speed 99 on the other side balances the pair. Leave it.

**L2** is the most balanced four lines. Nash at 80 checking is the only forward outside L1 who can actually kill, and he's here. Chlup at 78 faceoffs wins draws. Afinogenov at 92 scoring provides secondary offence. Hainsey at speed 99 and Safronov on the blue line give pace. This is a legitimate second unit.

**Richards** on L3 with 91 playmaking is the one misallocation I can point at. He's the second-best playmaker on the roster after Sundin and he's skating on a line with a checking mean of 67. My April finding noted his rate collapsed from 1.08 to 0.71; the position assignment might be a consequence of that slump rather than its cause. He stays on L3 tonight but if his rate recovers above 0.80 by December, he belongs on L2 with Nash and Chlup providing the structure around him.

**L4 and K2** are where the roster is short. L4 has checking mean 68, toughness mean 61, faceoff mean 57. K2 has faceoff mean 52. No rearrangement fixes this because no forward outside L1-L2 checks above 81. Roberts (82 checking) and McCabe (81 checking) sit scratched and they'd raise the L4 checking mean to roughly 72, but the GM has explicitly kept them out for development space. This is a roster gap and it has not changed since April.

**K2** carries Hainsey (speed 99) and Klesla (speed 99) on the kill, which is an odd fit in principle. Speed doesn't block shots. But the alternatives are Stahle at toughness 70 (scratched) or Colaiacovo at 0.11 pts/g on 12.5 MPG. Klesla at 87 OVR is the better player regardless of role logic, and taking him off the kill doesn't help L3 either because Colaiacovo is the only body available. The unit is suboptimal by design, not by error.

**P1 and P2** are both sound. P1 centres on Sundin's 94 playmaking at the half-wall with Jackman (0.88 pts/g) providing point production. P2 has Mogilny 90 scoring and Afinogenov 92 scoring, which is actually the higher-scoring personnel, but Sundin's playmaking makes him the better PP setup man and splitting them is right — we get two units that can score rather than one that dominates and one that's empty.

The only structural finding I carry forward is the same one from April: we need a middle-six forward who checks above 80. Nothing inside this roster fixes it.

## Opponent matchup

The question is whether Ottawa's top end is good enough to force a change, or whether we play our game and win this on overall depth.

**Ottawa's threat is concentrated.** Alfredsson at 87 and Havlat at 86 are the only two players on their roster above 82 OVR. Havlat's speed (98) and Alfredsson's deke (94) can take a single period, but below them the roster falls to 78 and then to 74 on the third line. Their PP converts 5 from 59 (8.5%); they are not going to beat us with special teams. Our PP sits at 4/19 (21%), and we're putting up 3.20 goals a night against a club allowing 2.20.

**The auto-pairing already handles their top line correctly.** Our first pair (Jackman 85 / Klesla 86) sits behind L1 (Sundin/Chistov/Mogilny), which is what we want facing White/Alfredsson/Havlat. Our second pair (Safronov 67 / Hainsey 76) sits behind L2 (Chlup/Nash/Afinogenov), which handles Fisher/Bonk/Hossa. Nash at CHKG 85 and TOUG 90 is the right man to shadow Hossa (SH PW 90). The third pair (St. Jacques 65 / Colaiacovo 75) faces Barnes (74), Schaefer (72), Hamel (70) and it can survive that.

**Safronov** at 67 OVR is the structural concern, but moving pairs around doesn't fix it. The only alternative to the current slot order is swapping pair 2 and pair 3, which puts the thinner 65/75 combination against Hossa. Current order is correct.

**Goalie.** Tellqvist is at 72, Ouellet at 85. Thirteen points. I could not confirm from the fatigue history whether either carries the tired icon on the screen right now; results were truncated. The GM needs to glance before confirming. But on talent alone, Ottawa's top two with their hands on the puck is exactly the night for the 85-goalie.

**No line changes.** We're 12-5 and hot (7 wins in last 10). Their depth cannot punish our third and fourth lines the way a top team could. Chemistry holds.

**Delivering obligation #1 (defencemen review for deadline).** Klesla's rate is at 0.32 as of last week and the sell window is closing. Jackman at 0.88 stays. Safronov at 67 is the weakest top-four D and the trade candidate from the blue line. Hainsey and Colaiacovo are development. St. Jacques is depth only. No change to sell order: Klesla first, Safronov second, Colaiacovo stays for now.

## Owed

**Standing item #1, defenceman evaluation for season's end.**

**Klesla** just hit the number I was watching. 6 points in 20 games is exactly 0.30 pts/g, the floor I set on November 13th where "the card becomes suspect." His OVR also slipped from 87 to 86. The sell window is closing from the inside: a buyer who saw 87 OVR at 0.38 two weeks ago now sees 86 at 0.30. Still an expiring asset worth something at the deadline, but the return just took a hit and it will keep taking hits. Sell him now, not in December.

**Jackman** at 0.70 pts/g over 20 games (14 points on $0.70M x 2) continues to clear the 0.55 floor. The "keeps" call from November 13th holds comfortably. No change.

**Colaiacovo** at 0.10 pts/g (2 points in 20) on 12.4 MPG is now undeniable dead weight for development. I flagged him on November 17th; two more games confirm nothing is coming. At 22 with 4 years and $1.40M he is expensive for a 75. Move him while the "young defenseman" tag still has trade value.

**Hainsey** at 0.29 pts/g on 20.9 MPG in 14 games is a third-pair regular at $1.40M x 6. That contract length is the problem: six years at $1.40M for a player who will never crack the top pair. Not a panic sell, but a trade-deadline candidate if a buyer wants depth.

**McCabe** has 0 games played at $3.00M x 3. He is dead money. The sell call from May still stands and gets louder each week he sits.

**Safronov** at 0.43 pts/g in 7 games is the only young D producing at anything close to a rate. He stays.

**What changed since my last delivery on November 20th:** Klesla's rate fell from 0.32 to 0.30 and his OVR from 87 to 86. That is the only material move. Jackman, Colaiacovo and McCabe are all confirming prior reads. The D-minute load on Jackman and Klesla has eased from 56% to roughly 44%, so the endurance concern from October is less acute.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-20
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-20

Toronto 11-5-0, 28 pts after 19 games.

## Role coverage

The question this phase answers is whether Toronto has the personnel to play the game the Coach needs to win, and the answer is split: scoring, speed and stamina are deep, but toughness is zero and checking is being wasted on the bench.

**Toughness is the only role that is genuinely missing.** No player on the roster carries 80+ in that attribute. The ceiling is Jackman at 75, with Roberts and McCabe both at 73. The fourth line the Coach flagged (checking mean 70, toughness 62) cannot be raised by any rearrangement because the raw material does not exist. This confirms the Feb 24 reading and resolves the Feb 21 contradiction: the stored grades never moved, the Feb 21 count was wrong. The acquisition targets stand unchanged: Kurka (88 TOUG, 90 CHKG, 23), Bertuzzi (83 TOUG, 87 CHKG, 30), Bell (88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, 24). One of these men is a structural fix. None of them is on the current roster.

**Checking is thin in practice despite 6 at 80+ on paper.** Jackman (87, 24) and Upshall (80, 22) are lined. The other four are not: Roberts (86, 39), McCabe (86, 30), Tucker (83, 30), Fischer (82, 25). The Coach himself said Roberts is "the only available upgrade and he is scratched." That is fixable without a trade. If he lines Roberts and McCabe, the top-two pairs jump from checking means in the low 80s to a genuine shutdown structure.

**Kaberle at 97 stamina and 90 clutch, not lined, is the single largest waste on the roster.** At 27 he is in his prime, and his stamina is the best on the team by 3 points. McCabe (94 stamina, 86 checking, 30) is the second waste. Between them the club is sitting on the two most durable defenders while asking others to cover heavy minutes.

**Gaborik at 92 scoring, 92 playmaking, 98 speed, 90 clutch, 88 stamina, and 23 years old is not lined.** No amount of line juggling replaces a 98-speed winger at 23. If the Coach is keeping him out for development reasons (Coach's Oct report flagged no dressing), that is a development call I defer on. But the role coverage suffers across four categories simultaneously because of it, and this is the roster's most valuable player sitting in no unit.

**Faceoffs are thin.** Only Sundin (90, 34) is truly reliable. Chlup at 75, Richards at 70, and Gardener at 72 are all mediocre draws. Wallin (83) is not lined. This is partially fixable: lining Wallin at a centre spot gives the club a second 80+ faceoff man. Full coverage requires acquisition: Bell at 82 FACE closes both the toughness and faceoff gaps simultaneously, and Avery (93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 25, $400K) remains the cheapest player closing all three gaps at once.

**The scoring core is aging.** Mogilny is 36, Sundin 34, Roberts 39. The three highest scorers are combined 109 years old. Gaborik (23) and Afinogenov (26) are the succession, but only if they are on the ice. This is not a February problem but it shapes what the club acquires around them in the next two seasons.

**Goalies are covered.** Luongo at 94 overall (8 GP, 6-2, GAA 1.73, SV 0.940) is elite. Tellqvist at 80 overall (6-1, GAA 1.70, SV 0.941) is a capable backup who is actually outperforming expectations. Ouellet at 84 overall is a solid third. Task #2 is closed per the GM's March 19 standing order. No further monitoring needed.



**Task #2 (Luongo/DiPietro monitoring):** Closed. Luongo confirmed on roster at 94 overall with 1 year remaining at $1.60M. The GM closed all goalie monitoring on March 19, 2005. No further work required.

## Trajectory

The trajectory question that matters today is not whether Toronto is too old or too young; the shape is correct. The question is whether the club can survive the two contract storms coming: Gaborik's locked-in $11.90M for five years to a scratched player, and the eleven players who all hit free agency in July 2009.

**Gaborik** is the single worst contract in the building. $11.90M per year, five years left, through July 2010. He is scratched, producing 8 points in 17 games at 0.47 pts/g. At 23 with POTE 90 he should be a top-line winger, but he is not playing and cannot be renegotiated. If he stays undressed past the deadline, his trade value will have cratered and Toronto carries $47.60M in dead money across the next four seasons. He must move by March, even for a third-rounder and a salary dump.

**The 4-year cluster** is the structural problem. 11 players, $37.40M, all expiring July 2009: Sundin, Richards, Chistov, Afinogenov, Nash, Kaberle, Alexeev, Upshall, Colaiacovo, Abid, Wallin. When eleven players demand raises in the same summer, payroll either explodes or the core walks. The manual's warning applies precisely. The fix is to move stalled pieces from that cluster now: **Wallin** at 25, zero games played, $1.40M, POTE 97 is the cleanest. He has ice time on a team that needs minutes, but if he is still at 0 GP by February he should be shipped for a pick before his remaining years make him harder to move.

**Chlup and Luongo** are the only mandatory July 2006 renewals. Chlup is 19, 15 points in 19 games at 0.79 pts/g on $2.34M. Luongo is 26 at 94 overall on $1.60M. Both need 5-6 year deals, and both are currently underpaid. The rest of the 1-year class (Klesla, Spezza, Koltsov, Ouellet, Tucker, St. Jacques) should be sold before March or allowed to walk. That thins the renewal class from nine to two.

**The scoring void** is still unresolved. Mogilny expires at 36 (12 pts, 0.63 pts/g). Sundin is 34 with 4 years and will be 38 in 2009. The winger group that must replace them: Nash at 0.47, Chistov at 0.53, Alexeev at 0.50. None has taken the step yet. Iginla remains the July target that solves this, and the trade capital from selling Klesla, Spezza, Koltsov and Gaborik before March is what funds the package.

**Finances are not a constraint.** $35.81M profit, $89.94M payroll, $65.14M revenue. The club can absorb a star's salary. The July 2009 cluster is the only money problem, and it is a timing problem, not an affordability one.

**Draft capital** is thin: TOR owns their own R1, R2, and R3. No high pick available from trades. Every acquisition is player-for-player, which is why the February sales matter so much for the summer.

## Calendar

Are we buying or selling at March 19, and who stays when contracts expire in July? The answer is buy, and the summer is mostly clean except one 36-year-old on $5.50M.

**The trade case is obvious:** 28 points through 19 games puts Toronto 2nd in the East with eight teams making the playoffs. A 1.47 points-per-game pace is elite. The manual says "if contending, buy for need." The Coach's gap is explicit: 4th-line checking mean 70 and toughness 62, and he cannot fix it with a lineup card. We need bodies.

**Deadline plan — two packages in order of priority:**

**Kurka (CAR)** is the best value available. 23 years old, TOUG 88, CHKG 90, 12 points in 16 games, $0.60M expiring. Package: Upshall (collapsing, 3 points in 9 games) plus a third-rounder. CAR sit 18 points, 9th in the East, with 14 expiring contracts and $63.79M payroll. They will not keep him. This fixes the exact gap the Coach named and costs one dying asset plus one pick.

**Bertuzzi (VAN)** is the bigger prize: 94 base, TOUG 83, CHKG 87, 1.25 points per game at 30 years old. VAN have the league's lowest payroll at $46.36M with 13 expiring. They must sell. Package: Tucker ($1.30M expiring) plus a second-rounder. Tucker at 30 is a rental either way; getting a 94-base right winger who clears 80 on both physical axes for him is the best conversion available.

**Heatley (ATL)** at 91 base and 82 toughness is the ceiling target, but the price (Spezza + Koltsov + R1) gutted two young players for a rental if we miss early. I'd only do this if Kurka fails and we still feel thin in February.

**Mogilny** at $5.50M and 36 years old needs to go at the deadline. He fills a roster spot we should give to Alexeev or another young player. Any club that needs a veteran forward for a playoff push is a destination. We own no pick better than a 4th (as of the Jan 2005 audit; current holdings unconfirmed), so every package is player-funded, but a rental like Mogilny to a contender should net at least a late pick.

## Summer plan

**Chlup** is the franchise center and must be locked. 15 points in 18 games at 20.8 MPG at 19 years old. $2.34M current salary is a rookie deal. Re-sign on 5-6 years at whatever he demands; he will command it. If he walks in July, we lose a top-line center for nothing.

**Luongo** is 94 overall at $1.60M, the GM's confirmed number one. Re-sign on 5-6 years immediately. This is the cheapest star contract we have and the most dangerous to leave exposed.

**Klesla** at 23 and $0.90M is young defense depth. Not flagged by the Coach as a problem. Re-sign 3 years at similar money. He fills the 5th/6th D slot.

**Ouellet** at 24 and $0.90M is a backup with development runway. The GM's stance (Jan 2025) was that age alone does not kill potential. Keep as Luongo's backup for one more year; if his rate improves by June, re-sign 2 years. If not, trade him for a late pick per the over-80 mechanic (assuming his overall is above 80 at renewal time).

**Koltsov** at 24 and $1.10M is the judgment call. If he goes in the Heatley package at the deadline, this question answers itself. If he's still here, re-sign 3-5 years; he's young and affordable.

**St. Jacques** at 25 and $0.80M is depth defense. Re-sign 2 years if he's a healthy 6th/7th option, otherwise trade in a February package.

**Spezza** at 22 and $1.00M: the Coach says stop dressing him (2 points in 12 games, 3.6 MPG). If we trade him at the deadline in the Heatley package, we avoid a July negotiation with a player whose confidence is gone. If not, he needs to either take a healthy role or be moved.

**Tucker** — do not re-sign. He funds the Bertuzzi deal at the deadline.

**Mogilny** — do not re-sign. At 36 and $5.50M, he is the single largest payroll reduction available, and the position is better filled by the 22-year-old Alexeev at 0.55 points per game.

**One decision the GM must make before February:** The Coach now says Eminger's trade window is closing (0.29 points per game at 22 MPG). The GM's Feb 2005 order was to protect him as a long-term piece. The Coach is now recommending we move him. If the GM agrees with the Coach, Brad Stuart (SJ, 87 base, POTE 91, 25, $1.80M expiring) for Eminger plus a second-rounder becomes the priority blue-line deal. I raise it because the Coach has changed his stance and the GM should know.

**On the Eminger package:** if the GM vetoes again, fine. I note it because the Coach flagged it on the record, not because I'm re-litigating the February decision.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: which players on the fourteen clubs most likely to sell between now and March close Toronto's structural gaps at a price we can pay, and which of them is the single best value in the league?

The answer changes the February plan. **Komisarek** at Montreal is the most impactful player available anywhere on the shortlist. He is not on any GM veto list, he is not a Chara situation, and at 23 with 86 toughness and 93 checking he solves the roster's only genuine gap while also being a first-pairing defenseman producing 14 points in 18 games on $1.10M expiring.

**Komisarek** (MTL, D, 23, 86 overall, POTE 92) — 86 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 14 points in 18 games at 0.78 ppg, $1.10M expiring. MTL sit at 17 points with 8 expiring deals and $54.89M payroll. They are rebuilding and will not re-sign him. He solves toughness, checking, and top-pair defense simultaneously. The only player on this list who is clearly better than anyone Toronto could re-sign at those numbers. Package: Eminger plus R2. The Coach confirmed Eminger's development window is closing; this is the moment to convert POTE 99 into a ready NHL defenseman.

**Kurka** (CAR, LW, 23, 76 overall) — 88 TOUG, 90 CHKG, 13 points in 18 games at 0.72 ppg, $0.60M expiring. CAR at 18 points carry $63.79M payroll and 14 expiring deals, the most desperate seller in the Eastern Conference. The cheapest toughness fix available. Package: Upshall plus R3. Coach confirmed Upshall is in collapse and should stop playing.

**Kovalchuk** (ATL, LW, 22, 89 overall) — 82 TOUG, 75 CHKG, 17 points in 17 games at 1.00 ppg, $1.10M expiring. ATL at 12 points with $40.34M payroll. He is not a toughness answer but he solves the scoring void the trajectory phase identified: Mogilny at 36 and Sundin at 34 need a partner who can carry the top line for the next decade. The February binary stands: ATL keeps Kovalchuk or Heatley, not both. Toronto can pursue only one. Kovalchuk at 22 with 1.00 ppg edges Heatley at 24 with 91 base because of age and production rate. Package requires a significant piece: Gaborik plus R1 would make ATL's payroll problem vanish while giving them the salary-dump version of the player they already tried to acquire in the prior deadline window.

**Hejduk** (COL, RW, 29, 88 overall) — 23 points in 19 games at 1.21 ppg, $2.50M expiring. COL at 20 points with 8 expiring and $66.24M payroll. Not tough (the exact number is below 75 based on the overall formula weighting) but the highest-scoring expiring player in the league after Forsberg and Kariya, both of whom are at $9.90M and $10.11M and will not move. The GM already tested COL's willingness in February; they would accept a goalie for Hejduk. Since goalies are off the table per March 19 standing order, the package needs picks plus a young player. Spezza plus R2 is the logical shape: Coach confirmed his collapse, and COL at 20 points can use a prospect for the future.

**Bell** (CHI, LW, 25, 78 overall) — 86 FACE, 80 TOUG, 9 points in 17 games at 0.53 ppg, $0.90M expiring. CHI at 10 points with 8 expiring and $48.74M payroll. He closes toughness and faceoff gaps at once. Lower ceiling than Kurka but the faceoff grade makes him the center-slot version of the same fix. Package: Tucker plus R3.

**McLaren** (SJ, D, 28, 81 overall) — 87 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 9 points in 16 games at 0.56 ppg, $2.20M expiring. SJ carry the highest payroll among sellers at $66.24M with 14 expiring deals. He is the second-best tough D on this list after Komisarek. If the Eminger package goes to MTL, McLaren is the fallback. Package: Koltsov plus R2, or Upshall plus R2.

**Morris** (COL, D, 27, 84 overall, POTE 78) — 84 TOUG, 80 CHKG, 17 points in 19 games at 0.89 ppg, $1.70M expiring. The best-scoring defenseman on any seller. COL at 20 points with 8 expiring. If Hejduk goes to COL in a package, Morris becomes harder to extract from the same club in the same window. Keep as a single-club COL target: pursue Hejduk OR Morris, not both.

**Bouwmeester** (FLA, D, 22, 82 overall, POTE 96) — $1.20M expiring. FLA at 17 points with 5 expiring deals. Young with elite potential and already a solid NHL product. The development target from the draft-class list who is actually on an NHL roster and available. Package: Wallin (POTE 97, 0 GP, $1.40M) as a pure pick-for-potential swap. FLA are rebuilding and might prefer the upside.

**Rita** (EDM, LW, 24, 77 overall, POTE 99) — $1.00M expiring. EDM at 18 points. The highest potential on the board from a club that has no path to re-signing him. He is not a February need-filler; he is a development play for the 2006-07 succession. Package: Klesla (expiring, $0.80M range) plus R4.

**Avery** (LA, C, 25, 71 overall) — 88 FACE, 73 TOUG, 78 CHKG, $0.40M expiring, 0 points in 18 games. LA at 14 points with 6 expiring. His grades are real but 0 points in 18 games confirms the ghost-production pattern the February note flagged. He stays below Bell on the faceoff list and is not a standalone target. Only worth acquiring as a depth piece if LA accepts a cheap package.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers is: what do we hand over for the two players who fix the roster's only real gap (toughness and checking), and why does the other GM sign the paper? I'm building three proposals. Two are complementary: one fixes the blue line, one fixes the forward groups. The third is a fallback if the first is refused.

**Komisarek from Montreal** is the single best value in this window. At 86 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 14 points in 18 games, 23 years old, $1.10M expiring, he is a first-pairing defenseman who solves the roster gap outright. MTL at 17 points with 8 expiring and $54.89M payroll are rebuilding and will not re-sign him. They want young players with control; we want a ready NHLer for now. Eminger is the piece: 22, POTE 99, $2.20M for four years, and the Coach himself said "move him before the deadline." This is the cleanest both-sides fit on the board.

**Kurka from Carolina** is the forward-side version of the same fix. 88 TOUG, 90 CHKG, 13 points in 18 games at $0.60M. CAR at 18 points, $63.79M payroll, 14 expiring deals cannot re-sign him and keep their core. They take a salary increase of $0.90M (Upshall at $1.50M versus Kurka at $0.60M), but they get a 22-year-old with CHKG 87 and four years of control plus a third-rounder. For a club that will shed six or seven deals before July, $0.90M is a rounding error.

**McLaren from San Jose** is the fallback if MTL refuse Eminger. At 87 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 28, $2.20M expiring, he is the same profile as Komisarek but five years older and one point lower on both grades. SJ at $66.24M are the most salary-starved seller in the league. Klesla at $0.90M plus our R2 saves them $1.30M and gives them a 23-year-old with SPEE 88 already contributing 6 points in 19 games. We accept a $1.30M payroll increase for the season but get a true top-four D.

The three proposals use different currency: Eminger+R2, Upshall+R3, Klesla+R2. Proposals 1 and 3 both need R2, so they are mutually exclusive. Proposal 2 is independent and should run alongside either one. If we can only do one thing before March, it is Komisarek.

**Gaborik** is not a February chip despite the trajectory phase calling him one. No team absorbs $11.90M for five years to a scratched player without compensation so large it costs us more than carrying him. He is a July problem that solves itself when he walks, or it doesn't and we carry him. I would not build a package around him now.

## Owed

**Task #2 — Luongo availability and DiPietro monitoring through February for the goalie trade window.**

This task was closed on 2005-11-13 and nothing material has changed since. One line on the numbers: Luongo reads **95** (+1 from the 94 I recorded on the 13th, form movement), still 1 year at $1.60M, 8 GP in 19 games. DiPietro is at NYI with **87** overall, 0 years left, 15 GP, $1.10M. Neither number changes any decision the GM is facing today.

The February 2005 window this task was built for came and went; Luongo stayed per the March 19 standing order. The next real goalie question is Luongo's renewal in summer 2006 (1 year remaining) and whether DiPietro becomes available at the March 2006 deadline as an expiring asset. Both are new questions, not this one. I will raise them when they are live, not before.

Task stays closed.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-20
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-20

Next game vs PHI on Wednesday 23 November 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether our young players are getting the games their production has earned, and right now one swap stands out as overdue.

**Spacek** at 0.50 pts/g in 6 games is outproducing **Spezza** at 0.15 pts/g in 13 games, and he plays the same position. Spezza's morale has dropped to 81 and Spacek's to 76, the lowest on the roster. Three points in six games on 5.8 MPG is not a player who has earned a scratch; it is a player who hasn't been given the ice to prove otherwise. Dress Spacek over Spezza.

**Chlup** (15 pts, 20.7 MPG), **Nash** (9 pts, 14.5 MPG), **Chistov** (10 pts, 18.5 MPG) and **Klesla** (6 pts, 25.9 MPG) are at 100% share and earning it. No change.

**Alexeev** at 6 pts in 12 games (0.50 pts/g) is holding at or above the 0.45 threshold I set on November 17. The 63% share is the right pattern. No change.

**Colaiacovo** at 2 pts in 19 games (0.11 pts/g) is still bad, but his 12.4 MPG is above the 8 MPG scratch trigger. The rule hasn't fired. Continue monitoring; if minutes drop below 8 for three straight games he comes out.

**Gaborik** at 0.47 pts/g on 22.6 MPG wasn't earning the ice he was given. The scratch is earned on performance. **Stahle** at 0.22 pts/g on 12.5 MPG across 18 games is the same story. Both scratches are correct.

**Gardener** at 0 points in 10 games on 3.1 MPG and **Upshall** at 3 pts in 10 games on 4.7 MPG are the L4 remnants. They're getting scraps and producing nothing, which is the collapse pattern I've seen with Spezza, Upshall and others. They're not causing harm but they're not developing either. The Spacek swap tightens the bench without a full rebuild.

## Development trends

Who among the young players is taking the step we are feeding him minutes for, and whose game is going the other way, with the deadline now close enough to shape decisions. Nineteen games in, the card separates them.

**Chlup** is the settled one. 0.78 points a game on 21.5 minutes across 19 games at 19, first-line centre. Nothing here to change; he is the one young forward whose minutes and production match.

**Stahle**, 21, is holding a real role at 0.24 points a game on 12.9 minutes over 18 games, and **Hainsey**, 24, is at 0.31 on 21.3. Both are earning the ice. **Fischer** at 0.80 in 6 games is the best rate on the blue line, but six games is not a season yet.

**Colaiacovo** is the one to watch. 0.11 points a game in 19 games on 12.8 minutes is the lowest rate of any regular defenceman. The minutes I moved to Hainsey on 11-16 went to the right man, 0.31 against 0.11. Keep Colaiacovo where he is; he has not earned a bigger slot.

**Spezza** (0.15 on 3.4 minutes), **Upshall** (0.22 on 3.4), **Gardener** (0.00 in 10 games, 1.7), **Lundmark** (0.00 in 11, 2.5) and **Brendl** (0.22 on 3.6) are five young forwards under four minutes a night. Dressing a 20-year-old for 1.7 minutes develops nobody. Gardener and Lundmark have not scored at all.

**Roberts** is the veteran slipping: 0.29 points a game in 8 games on 13.7 minutes at 39. The scoring is still carried by **Sundin** (0.72 on 23.5) and **Mogilny** (0.67 on 23.1) at 34 and 36, which is the trend the GM should plan around, not this week's lines.

**Klesla**, 23, 0.33 points a game on 25.0 minutes: heavy load, thin return, and still the deadline sell.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy. Most players sit at 96 and climbing, which tracks the team's record. The one known minutes-related problem, **Richards** at 86 morale on 12.9 MPG (four minutes under his band), is slowly recovering: he moved from -13 to +5 across recent saves. That gap is structural, not a line change fixes, and I've already flagged it in October.

**Spacek** at 76 is the lowest reading on the roster. He was dropped from 91 to 76 when you scratched him, and has ticked back to 76 with a small +1 recently. That's your call, not a minutes problem I can solve from the bench.

**The fourth line** (Upshall 81 on 4.7 MPG, Spezza 81 on 3.4, Gardener 81 on 3.1, Lundmark 81 on 3.3) all sit at 81 and are stable to slightly up. They are under any band their displayed OVR suggests, but their actual calibre puts them in the 7-10 MPG band and they are below that. Without promoting them to the top nine, there is nothing to do. Their morale is not getting worse.

**Jackman** at 25.7 MPG and **Klesla** at 25.9 are absorbing a punishing load. Morale at 96 for both, so no morale problem today, but the endurance cost is coming. That is a lines problem for the matchup phase, not a morale one.

No change needed. The room is right for Wednesday.

## Role composition

The question is whether each unit's personnel suits its job, and where the roster cannot fill a role at all. With PHI at 8-6 coming in Wednesday, the fourth line's checking gap is the one that costs us tonight.

**L1** is built right. Sundin wins draws (95), closes games (99 clutch), and Jackman at 92 checking covers the defensive end while Mogilny (92 scoring) and Klesla (87 OVR) generate offence. No change.

**L2** works as a speed line. Chlup at 0.82 pts/g centres it, Hainsey's 99 speed stretches the ice, Nash's 82 checking gives the unit a second body that can hit. The mean checking of 75 is adequate for a second line that is meant to score. Leave it.

**L3** is a skill line doing third-line work (checking mean 69), but Richards at 93 playmaking and Alexeev producing are why it stays together. The GM's development priority applies here unless PHI demands a shutdown unit. I say it does not; PHI's top six is dangerous but the third line's job is to match their third, not their first.

**L4** is the problem. Gardener, Spezza, Upshall give a checking mean of 70 and toughness mean of 62. That is a skill unit pretending to be a checking unit. Against a .571 opponent that is too soft. **Roberts** at 84 checking and 72 toughness is dressed-capable and sitting out for no reason I can see that survives a quality-opponent night. Dress him on the fourth line, sit the weakest of the current three. This costs chemistry on a line that hasn't earned any yet.

**K2** at checking mean 72 is soft for a penalty-kill unit, but Klesla's 88 on the blue line and Hainsey's 99 speed closing gaps make it functional. Not worth rebuilding tonight.

**The structural gap** remains: outside Jackman, we have no forward who checks above 82 and plays a regular role. Roberts at 84 is scratched (likely GM's development rotation), McCabe at 83 is on the sell list. Nash at 82 is on L2 doing a scoring job. A true shutdown forward who centres a third or fourth line and eats 14 minutes is missing from this roster. That is a trade-deadline target, not a lines fix.

## Opponent matchup

The question for Wednesday: does PHI present anything our current lines cannot handle? They do not.

**The talent gap is on every line.** Our first unit (Sundin 92, Chistov 87, Mogilny 89) faces their first line of Handzus (81), Gagne (84) and Amonte (82). Our second (Chlup 87, Nash 85, Afinogenov 86) faces Roenick (86), Axelsson (77) and Williams (77). Their third and fourth lines fall to 75, 70, 71. Our depth wins those matchups comfortably. The auto-pairing puts Jackman (86) and Klesla (87) against Gagne and Handzus, which is exactly where they belong.

**Their PP is broken.** Six goals on 74 chances is 8.1%. They will not hurt us on the man advantage. That takes pressure off our penalty kill and means our fourth line can play a looser game without fearing a PP goal after a turnover.

**Their D has a soft spot.** Giroux at 66 OVR on the third pair is well below league average. Our third line (Richards 87, Lundmark 81, Alexeev 80) gets a favorable matchup against him by default from the auto-pairing. No shuffle needed.

**Ouellet starts.** His 86 OVR against Esche's 76 is the biggest single-player edge on the sheet. Check the fatigue icon on screen before confirming, per the standing order.

**No lineup change for PHI.** The auto-pairing already gives us our best personnel against their best players. Shuffling for this opponent would break chemistry with no gain.

## D assessment (standing order #1, game 16)

From the latest data at 19 games played:

**Jackman** at 14 points in 19 on 25.7 MPG: 0.74 rate. The October breakout is holding. He is our best defenceman, period. No sell case while he produces at this clip.

**Klesla** at 6 points in 19 on 25.9 MPG: 0.32 rate. The decline from 0.38 noted on November 13 has continued. At 87 OVR on screen a buyer still sees the grade, but the production window is closing. If he drops below 0.30 the sell case gets harder because a buyer with any sense will see the rate.

**Hainsey** at 4 points in 13 on 21.6 MPG: 0.31. Solid third-pair minutes at 24. Not a sell, not a keeper beyond his current role.

**Colaiacovo** at 2 points in 19 on 12.4 MPG: 0.11. Confirmed. The pattern from the note is holding: no recovery.

**Safronov** at 2 points in 6 on 20.8 MPG: 0.33. Small sample but his 90 CHKG makes him useful defensively regardless of offense.

**Fischer** at 4 points in 6 on 19.8 MPG: 0.67 when he plays. Not currently in the lineup. His contract remains the trade problem, not his play.

End-of-season sell priority update: Klesla first (expiring, declining rate behind a still-visible 87), then Eminger (0.29 on $2.20M x 4). Jackman is firmly off any list.

## Owed

**#1 — Defencemen: who should go at the end of the season.** One thing has moved since my last delivery on November 17th, and it makes the call more urgent.

**Klesla** — 6 points in 19 games is now 0.32 pts/g, down from 0.38 when I last flagged him. His grade still says 87 and his contract expires this year at $0.90M, which is the only reason anyone would take him. The gap between his grade and his production keeps widening every week we hold him. This is the sell window closing from the inside: we need a buyer who reads 87 and not 0.32, and every bad game makes that harder.

**McCabe** — 0 games played, 84 OVR, $3.00M for 3 more years. Nothing has changed. He is not playing and his cap hit is the third-highest on the blue line behind Kaberle and Fischer. Still the second name on the exit list.

**Colaiacovo** — 2 points in 19 games on 12.4 MPG. Rate is dead flat at 0.11, same as last delivery. My kill condition was MPG under 8 for three straight games; he is above that, so he stays dressed. No change.

**Jackman** — 14 points in 19 is 0.74 pts/g on 25.7 MPG at $0.70M x 2. Still the best value on the roster. Slightly below his 0.88 peak but nowhere near the 0.55 line that puts him back on the sell list. Nothing moves.

Everyone else (Kaberle, Fischer, Hainsey, Eminger, Stahle) unchanged from last delivery.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 2, in-game 2005-11-17
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 2, in-game 2005-11-17

Toronto 11-4-0, 28 pts after 18 games.

## Role coverage

**The coverage brief answers one question: is the roster actually deployed where its strengths are?** The answer is no. The club has 86 checking, 98 speed, 90 clutch, and 98 durability sitting on the bench, and the fourth line reads 70 checking and 62 toughness because the best available bodies are not on the ice.

**Roberts** is the single largest utilization failure on the roster. 86 checking, 90 clutch, 98 durability, 39 years old. The Coach himself says Roberts is "the only available upgrade" for fourth-line checking and has him scratched. That is a contradiction: the Coach identifies the gap and the fix in the same sentence, then keeps the fix benched.

**McCabe** at 86 checking and 94 stamina, **Tucker** at 83 checking, and **Fischer** at 82 checking are all not lined. Those four men plus Jackman and Upshall are the entire 80+ checking corps, and three of the six are in no unit. The fourth-line problem is not a talent gap; it is a deployment gap.

**Toughness** is the only true structural hole. Zero players at 80+ on stored grades. Jackman tops the list at 75. No internal rearrangement produces a player the game grades at 80+ toughness. This is what makes Kurka, Bertuzzi, and Bell February targets rather than nice-to-haves.

**Faceoffs** are thin. Sundin at 90 carries the top draw; below him the best lined option is Chlup at 75. Wallin is at 83 but not lined. If Chlup draws the top center assignment, L2 and L3 have no competent faceoff presence.

**Age matters here.** Mogilny is 36, Roberts 39, Sundin 34. The 80+ checking depth that exists today is almost entirely old. Roberts and Tucker are the only 80+ checkers on the roster who could conceivably be moved; McCabe at 30 is the one who stays. The checking depth chart ages out in one to two seasons whether or not the Coach lines these men up now.

**Goalies are covered.** Luongo at 94 overall, 8 GP, 1.73 GAA, 0.940 SV. Belfour-equivalent depth via Tellqvist and Ouellet. No gap.

**What the Coach can fix with bodies already here:** Checking by lining Roberts, McCabe, and Tucker into the bottom-six. Speed and scoring by lining Gaborik. Stamina and clutch by lining Kaberle (97 endurance, 90 clutch). None of these require a trade.

**What no internal move fixes:** Toughness at 80+. Zero candidates exist. The February target list (Kurka, Bertuzzi, Bell) is not optional; it is the only path.

## Trajectory

The question this phase answers: does Toronto's roster age and contract structure leave the next three seasons intact, or is a cliff buried in the sheet?

**The age shape is healthy for today but has a bridge problem.** Thirteen players 23 or under and sixteen aged 24-29 is the manual's target shape met. But only two players sit between 30 and 33 (Tucker 30, McCabe 30, both scratched with zero games played), and the three veterans above 33 — Mogilny (36), Sundin (34), Roberts (39) — carry 426 career points with no one behind them in the 30-33 range. When Mogilny's one-year deal ends in July 2006 and Sundin walks in 2009, no bridge exists. The Iginla target (27 now, 93 base, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring at CGY) fills precisely that gap.

**July 2006 is the renewal summer that decides the dynasty.** Nine contracts worth $15.44M expire, and two of them are non-negotiable keepers: **Chlup** (19, 15 points in 18 games, POTE 95, $2.34M) and **Luongo** (26, 94 overall, POTE 97, $1.60M). Both need 5-6 year extensions the same week in July. Behind them, Mogilny (36), Tucker (30, 0 GP), Koltsov (24, 0 GP), Spezza (22, 2 pts in 12 GP), and St. Jacques (25, 0 GP) are all trade chips or releases that lighten the cluster. **Klesla** (23, 6 pts in 18 GP, POTE 97) is the exception who earns a renewal.

**July 2009 is the $37.40M cliff.** Eleven contracts on four-year deals come up simultaneously: Sundin at 38, Kaberle at 31, Richards at 29, Chistov at 26, Nash at 25, Eminger at 26, Colaiacovo at 26, Upshall at 26, Alexeev at 27, Wallin at 29, Abid at 29. That is half the core walking the same summer. The fix is not a single move but a shape: Iginla arriving in 2006 means the club can let one or two of those players walk and replace them cheaply, rather than fighting to retain all eleven at their peak asking prices.

**Gaborik is $11.90M of dead weight.** Twenty-three years old, POTE 90, 8 points in 17 games, and the Coach scratches him. His five-year deal runs through 2010, and the game does not permit mid-contract renegotiation. His trade value drops every week he sits (noted in October: if undressed by January 2006, he moves for scraps). The GM should set a hard deadline: if Gaborik is still undressed by late December, move him for any future asset, even a mid-round pick and a depth player. $11.90M against a scratched winger is the single largest payroll inefficiency on the roster.

**The Coach and GM disagree on Eminger, and the clock is on the Coach's side.** Eminger carries POTE 99 at 22 — the highest potential on the roster. The GM protected him in January 2005 as a long-term piece. But the Coach now reads 0.29 pts/g across 7 games and says the trade-value window is closing. The Coach has been right about Eminger's minutes every time this season. If the Coach stops dressing him entirely, his value collapses the way Spezza's did. This is a decision for the GM: dress him to 15+ MPG before January, or authorize a February trade built around his POTE 99 while a buyer will still pay for it.

**Draft capital is real ammunition now.** Toronto holds their own first, second, and third-round picks in the 2006 draft. This is a meaningful improvement from January 2005 when the club owned nothing better than a fourth. The first-rounder is the centrepiece of any Iginla or top-target package; the second and third round fill the salary-matching side.

**Money leaves room to add.** Payroll is $89.94M against revenue of $63.40M, and profit still reads $35.81M. No cap exists; the constraint is keeping profit positive while payroll climbs. Adding Iginla's $6.50M pushes payroll toward $96M, which is fine given current profit and attendance of 18,188 at $112 a ticket.

**Task #2 (Luongo and DiPietro monitoring):** Closed. Luongo confirmed on roster at 94 overall, one year left, $1.60M. No further goalie monitoring is needed until the July 2006 renewal window.

## Calendar

Are we buyers or sellers at the March 19 deadline, and which of the nine expiring players do we re-sign, move, or release? We are buyers. Toronto sit second in the East at 28 points in 15 games, eight teams make the playoffs, and 64 games remain. Per the manual, a contending club buys for need at the deadline, preferring young players with potential over pure rentals.

**Timing.** The deadline is 122 days away. Per the GM's January standing order, negotiations do not open until late February. November and December are monitoring months: watch Bertuzzi, Kurka, Doan, McLaren, and the WSH shutdown pair for price movement, confirm who is actually on the sell-side by February, then engage.

**Deadline acquisitions.** The Coach's explicit gap is fourth-line checking (mean 70) and toughness (mean 62). **Bertuzzi** at VAN carries TOUG 83, CHKG 87, and 1.25 pts/g at age 30. VAN had 13 expiring players as of October and the league's lowest payroll at $46.36M. Package: Tucker plus an R2. **Kurka** at CAR is younger (23), 88 TOUG, 90 CHKG, 12 points in 16 games, $0.60M expiring. CAR at 16 points with 14 expiring deals must move him. Package: Upshall plus R3. Both solve the Coach's stated gap. If only one lands, take Bertuzzi — he brings scoring alongside the checking.

**Chips to fund.** **Eminger** is now confirmed by the Coach as a trade candidate: 0.29 pts/g at 22 with POTE 99 unfulfilled means the development case is dead. His value at 21 with POTE 99 was the centrepiece; it's declining. Move him at the deadline before another season of low production makes him a mid-80 blueliner. **Tucker** ($1.30M, 30) was the GM's standing chip as far back as March 2005. **St. Jacques** ($0.80M, 25) is depth D who can go in a package.

## Summer: the nine expiring contracts

**Chlup** — renew 5-6 years. He's 19, centreing the first line, 15 points in 18 games on 20.8 MPG. Star contract per the manual. His $2.34M is a rookie rate; expect a substantial raise but it's the right expense.

**Luongo** — renew 5-6 years. 94 overall, 26 years old, $1.60M. The November 13 confirmation closed the goalie monitoring task. He is the franchise. Five or six years, not one year.

**Mogilny** — release or move before the deadline via the over-80 mechanic. 36 years old, $5.50M, the highest salary on the roster. He should have left in the December 2004 package. At 36 and this cost, no renewal case exists.

**Koltsov** — renew 3-4 years at 24, $1.10M. Young, affordable, not flagged by the Coach. Keep him for depth scoring unless a Heatley-type package demands him and the return justifies the loss.

**Klesla** — renew 3-4 years at 23, $0.90M. Young defenseman at a low salary. The roster needs blueliner depth.

**Spezza** — move before the deadline or release. The Coach confirmed collapse: 2 points in 12 games on 3.6 MPG. At 22 and $1.00M with one year left, if he carries an 80+ base overall he's a pick-recovery asset via the over-80 mechanic. If not, he walks. Either way, do not renew a player the Coach has benched for performance.

**Ouellet** — renew 2 years at 24, $0.90M, or move via the over-80 mechanic if he clears 80. He's the backup to Luongo. At $0.90M a backup goalie is cheap insurance. If he's below 80, the pick-recovery mechanic doesn't apply and he either renews cheap or leaves.

**St. Jacques** — move before the deadline as a package piece or renew 2 years at 25, $0.80M. At the deadline he's currency; in summer he's a seventh defenseman at a fair price.

**Tucker** — move before the deadline. 30, $1.30M, confirmed chip since 2005.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: who across the league fills our toughness gap, scoring bridge, or blue-line need on a club that will say yes before February?

**Iginla** is the top target because he is the only player who fills two gaps at once. 93 base, TOUG 85, age 27, $6.50M expiring. CGY at 21 points with 9 expiring deals and $52.08M payroll: if they are not in the race by mid-February they cannot lose him for nothing, and every team in the league knows this. The cost is high (Eminger + R1 is the likely floor), but he solves the 30-33 bridge problem the trajectory phase flagged AND the toughness gap. Package depends on Eminger decision.

**Kurka** is the cheapest and most certain path to the toughness fix. 88 TOUG, 90 CHKG, 23 years old, $0.60M expiring, 12 points in 16 games. CAR at 18 points with 14 expiring and $63.79M payroll is the single most desperate seller in the league by expiring-deal count. They must move him. Package: Upshall + R3 is already noted and Upshall's declining minutes (3 pts/9 GP, 5.1 MPG) make him available.

**Bertuzzi + Jovanovski** is the package that solves wing toughness and blue-line depth in one call. Bertuzzi at TOUG 83, CHKG 87, 1.25 pts/g, age 30, $2.10M expiring. Jovanovski at CHKG 94, TOUG 93, 88 overall, age 29, $2.30M expiring. VAN at $46.36M (league lowest) with 13 expiring must liquidate. The return is Eminger + R2, or Tucker + R2 + Koltsov if the GM protects Eminger.

**McLaren** at 89 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 28, $2.20M expiring is the purest toughness-on-a-winger available. SJ at 16 points, $66.24M payroll, 14 expiring deals — the highest-payroll seller and second most desperate by expiring count. Package from October note: Abid + R2. Still viable.

**Heatley** at 91 base, 82 TOUG, 24, $1.10M is the younger and cheaper version of Iginla. ATL at 12 points with 6 expiring must choose between him and Kovalchuk. If ATL keeps Kovalchuk (the binary noted in October), Heatley moves. Package: Spezza + Koltsov + R1 is the existing proposal, but Spezza's value is collapsing at 2 pts/12 GP on 3.6 MPG. A second or third pick plus a depth piece may be more realistic.

**Yonkman** at 24, 91 TOUG, 93 CHKG, POTE 89, $0.60M is the best young shutdown defenceman on any seller. WSH at 15 points with 5 expiring. Eminger + R2 remains the proposed return, but that requires the GM to release Eminger.

**Bell** at CHI (10 points, worst record, 8 expiring) closes toughness AND faceoff simultaneously: 88 TOUG, 82 FACE, 80 base, 25, $0.90M expiring. Package: Tucker + St. Jacques + R3. Still viable.

**What I would not do:** pursue Doan at $2.40M when Kurka gives 88/90 toughness-checking for $0.60M. The marginal 2 points of checking and age do not justify the salary difference.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: which toughness-and-scoring targets can we actually acquire by March, and what do we hand back so the other GM says yes?

Three proposals, ranked by the probability both sides sign. Each consumes a different pick, so the GM can pursue Proposal 1 and either 2 or 3, not all three. Giving Upshall, Koltsov, and Spezza simultaneously is three POTE 94+ players and guts the youth movement.

**Kurka from Carolina is the one that must get done.** He is 23, TOUG 88, CHKG 90, $0.60M expiring, and the only cheap, young, re-signable body who closes our zero-to-80 toughness hole. We give Upshall (Coach says stop dressing him, 3 pts in 9 GP on 5.1 MPG, but still 22 with POTE 99) plus our 2nd-round pick. CAR at 18 points with 14 expiring deals and $63.79M payroll are the most desperate seller in the league by volume. They lose Kurka for nothing in July otherwise; a POTE 99 winger and a 2nd-rounder is the rebuild currency they need. We shed $0.90M net. Acceptance is uncertain because Upshall's collapse may have eroded his AI value, but the hockey logic is clean.

**Bell from Chicago fills two gaps for one asset.** TOUG 88 plus FACE 82 means he solves the toughness hole AND the faceoff hole at once (L4 faceoff mean is 52, best available is 55). At 25 and $0.90M expiring, he is cheap and re-signable. We give Koltsov (0 GP here, but ACCE 96 and POTE 94 at 24) plus our 3rd-round pick. CHI at 10 points are the worst team in the league with 8 expiring deals and $23.35M profit. They are fully rebuilding and hoard young speed. Bell leaves for nothing in July; getting a 24-year-old with ACCE 96 is exactly what a team in their position values. We shed $0.20M. The risk is that CHI undervalue Koltsov's 0 GP and demand more.

**Heatley from Atlanta is the ceiling.** 91 base, TOUG 82, 24 years old, $1.10M expiring. He fills the 30-to-33 bridge the trajectory phase flagged AND brings toughness to 82. ATL at 12 points with 6 expiring deals must choose between him and Kovalchuk. If they keep Kovalchuk, Heatley is a rental they lose for nothing. We give Spezza (Coach says stop dressing him, 2 pts in 12 GP on 3.6 MPG) plus our 1st-round pick. The problem is Spezza's value has cratered the same way Upshall's did, and a 1st-rounder for one expiring winger is a steep price. If ATL refuses, adding Koltsov to the package makes it more likely but pushes us into giving three POTE 94+ players.

**If none land:** Line up Tucker (CHKG 92, TOUG 88, expiring, 0 GP) and McCabe (CHKG 89, 0 GP) on the bottom-six. The Coach already says Roberts at 86 checking is the only internal fix and has him scratched. That contradiction resolves itself in a playoff push: the Coach will dress the checking bodies when the stakes rise. We have no 80+ toughness on the roster and no internal path to it, so we go into the playoffs with 78 as our top TOUG (Jackman). It is survivable against most matchups, but it is a known weakness every series opponent will target.

## Owed

**Item #2 — Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window.**

Closed on 2005-11-13 and remains closed. One number moved: Luongo's overall ticked from 94 to 95 since that note. He's dressed 8 times in 18 games, so he's splitting work with Belfour. Nothing else has shifted.

**Luongo** is at 95 overall, 1 year remaining, $1.60M. That's the cheapest 95-overall contract in the league by a wide margin — Brodeur at the same rating costs $6.70M, Turco $0.60M but he's at 95 on a 0-year deal. Luongo's renewal window opens at season's end, and per game mechanics no renegotiation is possible before then. The 5-6 year lock is the next action, and it's a summer job, not a February one.

**DiPietro** is no longer a target. Luongo is our number one and staying. The standing order from 2005-03-19 closed all goalie monitoring; the Nov 13 note reconfirmed it. No reason to re-open unless Luongo gets hurt, and nothing in the injury data flags him.

This stays closed until the renewal window. I'll flag it in April when contracts become actionable.

title: Coach's report — run 2, in-game 2005-11-17
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 2, in-game 2005-11-17

Next game vs BOS on Saturday 19 November 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question here is whether the young players on this roster are getting the games they've earned, and the answer for four of them is a flat no.

**Spezza** is 3.6 minutes a night with 2 points in 12 games. That's the collapse pattern confirmed a third time: he went from 9.1 MPG last season to 3.6 now with no production to justify keeping him dressed. He isn't developing at that ice time; he's rotting.

**Gardener** is the same story. 0 points in 9 games on 3.3 MPG. He's a fourth-liner who can't crack the fourth line's minutes. POTE 98 on the scouting card means nothing if he's never on the ice.

**Upshall** at 5.1 MPG with 3 points in 9 games is the third instance. These three players share one problem: the January policy of scratching veterans to make room for youth created a window, the window closed, and now they sit at 3-5 MPG taking roster spots without accumulating games.

**Alexeev** is the answer to that problem. 6 points in 11 games on 11.2 MPG is 0.55 pts/g, and he's only in 61% of games. He outproduces everyone sitting ahead of him on the wing. Dress him every game ahead of these three and the roster spot isn't wasted on a body that plays four minutes.

**Spacek** is the outlier. Scratched now, morale 76 (the lowest in the group by 20 points), 3 points in 6 games on 5.8 MPG. The original reason to scratch him was to develop others; those others collapsed anyway. Either he gets a real look at 10+ MPG or he comes out permanently. At 76 morale, continuing to dress-and-scratch him is doing him no favours.

**Chlup** needs nothing. 15 points in 18 games on 20.8 MPG is a first-line rate, and he's getting first-line minutes. Fully earned.

**Colaiacovo** at 0.11 pts/g on 12.5 MPG over 18 games is inside my watch zone. The Hainsey move on 11-16 may have cut his ice further, but I can't see per-game splits. If his MPG drops below 8 for three straight games he comes out permanently.

## Development trends

The question is who is getting better or worse since October 12th, and whether any trend should change the GM's plans before the trade deadline.

**Chlup** is the clear riser: 0.82 pts/g on 21.7 MPG in 18 games at 19. Last season he hit 0.88 on 18.2 MPG; this year he's at 0.82 on 21.7 with a full first-line load. He belongs there permanently and is building toward a 1.00-rate season if he keeps climbing.

**Jackman** at 0.76 pts/g on 24.5 MPG in 18 games confirms the November read. His sell-list trigger is below 0.55; he's well above it at $0.70M x 2. He's not going anywhere.

**Stahle** is developing cleanly: 6.0 MPG in game 1 to 12.9 MPG over 18 games with 0.24 pts/g. For a 21-year-old third-pairing D that's the right trajectory. Give him more if Colaiacovo stays at 0.12.

**Nash** is slightly better than last year: 0.47 pts/g on 14.1 MPG versus 0.43 on 12.7 last season. The GM was right that he's been helpful. He's a 21-year-old top-six winger whose role is growing.

**Alexeev** is declining where I expected growth. He went 0.55 pts/g last season; he's at 0.40 on 11.7 MPG this year. He got the extra games I asked for and his rate dropped. The production-vs-role mismatch from last spring is now a production problem, not a role problem.

**Colaiacovo** at 0.12 pts/g on 12.9 MPG in 18 games is confirmed stalled. His MPG is above the 8-game kill threshold, so the rule hasn't triggered, but the production is not coming. He needs to earn his spot in camp or come out.

**Eminger** at 0.29 pts/g on 19.9 MPG in 7 games continues the slide: 0.44 in February last year, 0.38 season-final, now 0.29 at 22. The trade value is evaporating with every game.

**Richards** at 0.65 pts/g on 13.1 MPG continues the multi-year decline (1.08 → 0.71 → 0.65). At 13.1 MPG he's still four minutes below his expected band, and the morale deficit compounds each month.

**Gardener, Spacek, Upshall** are all in the minutes-collapse pattern simultaneously. Gardener went 16 MPG in game 1 to 1.8 MPG over 9 games. Spacek went 17 to 3.6. Upshall went 16 to 3.8. None produced. This is the systemic deployment problem I flagged in October, and it's happening again with three players at once.

**Spezza** at 0.17 pts/g on 3.6 MPG in 12 games is the worst case. POTE 99 is being wasted on a man who gets three minutes a night. His development is stalled and the next camp is the only intervention that matters.

**Klesla** at 0.35 pts/g on 24.7 MPG is still inside the sell window. His production hasn't recovered above 0.55, so the deadline trade stays on the board.

## Morale watch

The room is recovering from a results-driven dip and no line change fixes what remains. The one structural problem I can name — Spacek at 76 — is the GM's roster decision, not mine.

**Spacek** sits at 76, the lowest on the roster, down from the mid-90s before a dip that pulled everyone down 9-10 points. He's scratched with 5.8 MPG over 6 games and 3 points. At his calibre his band expectation is roughly 10 a night; he gets half that, and the 70s morale costs him 2 points off every grade on the sheet. The GM scratched him deliberately to open space for younger players, which I respect, but the morale hit compounds and if he goes back in for Boston or beyond he'll play with a visible penalty. This is a roster-construction problem: we have Gaborik, Alexeev, Upshall and others in front of him with no clear path to regular minutes.

**Richards** at 86, 13.1 MPG over 18 games, 11 points. Same gap I flagged October 20: a player in the 85-86 band expects around 17, he gets 13. The 80s morale costs 1 point per grade. It's stable, not deteriorating (recovered from a low with the team), and there's no line slot that gives him 4 more minutes without breaking the Chlup-Afinogenov-Nash second line. I accept the cost for now.

**Fischer and Kaberle** at morale 91 and 91 respectively, both 91 OVR, both scratched after logging 19-20 MPG in their 6 games before sitting. Their morale dipped with the team's results (down 9 from earlier readings) and is climbing back at +5. These are the GM's development-rotation decisions, same as last month. No action from me.

**The depth four** (Gardener 81, Upshall 81, Spezza 81, Lundmark 81, Brendl 81, St. Jacques 81) all sit in the 80s band at 2.5-5.8 MPG. That's their role, the -1 penalty is the floor for fourth-liners, and the recovery trend is right. Nobody here is slipping.

For Saturday against Boston: no changes. The top nine are all at 96 morale, the -1 penalty on Richards costs one point on a 13-minute night, and Spacek isn't in the lineup. The room is healing on results, not on minutes.

## Role composition

The question is whether each unit is built from players who suit its job, and whether we have enough of each role to build them at all. The answer: the top three lines and the power plays are well-constructed. The fourth line and the second penalty kill are where composition breaks down, and the fourth line is a roster problem no arrangement fixes.

**L1** is built right: 90 scoring mean with Jackman's 92 checking and 78 toughness on the back end means we get offense without the blue line being a sieve. Klesla adds speed (99) to cover transition. This is our best unit and it needs no touch.

**L2** has good balance: Chlup at 80 faceoffs wins draws in the offensive zone, Nash brings 82 checking, and Hainsey's 99 speed on the back end means we can play a wide-forecheck system without getting burned. Solid.

**L3** has a skill surplus in Richards (93 playmaking) that is arguably wasted at third-line centre. But Chlup is entrenched at L1 centre and the GM explicitly protected his development role. Moving Richards up means displacing someone who is producing or stunting Chlup. I accept the surplus and leave it alone. The checking mean of 68 on this line is the concern against a 9-4 team, but Lundmark and St. Jacques provide what they can.

**L4** is where the unit fails its job. Checking mean 70, toughness 62, faceoffs 58. A fourth line exists to absorb minutes, win board battles, and give the top lines a shift. This one can barely do the first. The checking gap is structural — Jackman (92) and Nash (82) are the only forwards at or above 82 and they are already on L1 and L2. Roberts at 84 checking is scratched. That is the roster problem, and it is the same one I flagged in April.

**K2** has stamina 53/57. Hainsey and Klesla are already absorbing the heaviest D load. If they are tired on the penalty kill, we get late-game breakdowns. K1 has checking 80 and stamina 69/73 — it should carry the kill minutes whenever possible.

## Opponent matchup

The question is whether our lines and pairings match up well enough against Boston's top-heavy attack, and the answer is yes on forwards but one defensive slot is soft.

**Thornton** is their whole team at 90 OVR with 96 shot power, 93 hero and 90 endurance. Our first line (Chistov-Sundin-Mogilny at 87/92/89) gets him by the auto-pairing, and our first pair (Jackman 94 checking, Klesla 81 checking) is well-built to slow him. Samsonov at 99 speed matches Chistov at 99 speed, and Mogilny at 89 with 92 shot power handles Murray at 85. The top-line matchup is even and our goaltending edge (Ouellet 86 vs Shields 83) gives us the tiebreaker.

**Safronov** on the second pair is the problem. His 68 OVR and 63 puck control cannot handle Hilbert at 81 with 93 puck control and Lapointe with 94 shot power. Knuble (78, 88 checking) will grind him into the boards. Our second pair should be Hainsey/Colaiacovo at 77/76 against that line. Colaiacovo's 77 passing and 75 puck control keep the zone cleaner than Safronov's 69 and 63. I recommended this swap on 11-16 for development reasons and the GM accepted it; for Saturday it is a matchup call against a quality opponent.

**Their bottom six** is where we pull away. Vernarsky at 73, Johnson at 71, Vaananen at 71. Richards at 87 on our third line and Gardener at 75 with 81 checking on the fourth are both upgrades over their depth. We do not need to break a line to exploit that; the depth advantage plays itself over 60 minutes.

**Their PP** is 8 on 56 (14.3%). Our first kill unit with Jackman and Safronov on the points is more than adequate. No PK change needed.

## Owed

**D-man sell list for the deadline, updated as of November 17 (18 games played).**

**Jackman** at 0.78 pts/g in 18 games (14 points) on 25.4 MPG. Dipped slightly from the 0.88 rate I reported on November 13 — two games without a point — but nowhere near the 0.55 sell threshold I set. He stays. At $0.70M x 2 this is the best value on the roster.

**Klesla** unchanged: 6 points in 18 games, 0.33 pts/g on 25.7 MPG. Still below my 0.55 sell threshold, still expiring at $0.90M. Top sell candidate stands. A buyer at the deadline sees 87 OVR and a top-pair role.

**Colaiacovo** at 0.11 pts/g (2 points in 18) on 12.5 MPG. Same as November 16. The "three games under 8 MPG" threshold has not triggered — he's still playing 12.5 — but his scoring is stalling on the same minutes. Watch next three games.

**McCabe**: still 0 games, not dressed, 30 years old, $3.00M x 3. On the sell list since May and nothing has changed.

**Safronov** at 68 OVR is the weakest D on the roster playing real minutes (21.4 MPG in 5 games). He's a healthy scratch waiting to happen once someone comes back.

**No change to the sell list.** Klesla and McCabe remain the two. Jackman stays, Fischer is untouchable per the GM's standing order, Kaberle is untouchable.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-17
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-17

Toronto 11-4-0, 28 pts after 18 games.

## Role coverage

The club is missing toughness entirely and thin at checking in practice, and the coach's current plan makes the checking problem worse, not better.

**Toughness** is a zero across the entire roster. The best is Jackman at 75, then Roberts and McCabe at 73, Tucker and Chlup at 70. There is no internal fix. This is the same gap flagged since February 2005, and the contradiction from that month (six players supposedly at 80+ TOUG versus zero) is resolved: zero is correct. Every February target on our list (Kurka at 88 TOUG, Bertuzzi at 83, Bell at 88) addresses something nobody on this roster can provide.

**Checking** has six players with 80+ grades but only two actually playing: Jackman at 87 and Upshall at 80. Roberts at 86, McCabe at 86, Tucker at 83, and Fischer at 82 are all sitting on the roster in no unit. The coach wants to reduce Upshall's dressing priority, which would leave one 80+ checker on the ice. That is one short of what four lines and two penalty-kill units need. Lining McCabe on the fourth defensive pair or Tucker on the second PK unit restores two checkers without touching the top three lines.

**Roberts** at 86 checking, 88 scoring, 90 clutch, and 98 durability is the single most wasted asset on the roster. He is not lined in any unit. If the coach needs a 39-year-old who can kill penalties and win draws at 75 FACE, he is on the bench.

**Faceoffs** are thin but workable. Sundin at 90 carries the top line; Chlup at 75 handles the second. Roberts at 75 could anchor a third or fourth line if lined. Nobody else on the roster draws above 72. This is not an acquisition priority but it means the coach should not put Chlup on a line where the center takes every draw in the offensive zone.

**Scoring, playmaking, speed, clutch, stamina** are all deep. Eleven players at 80+ in scoring and playmaking, 25 at 80+ in speed. No gap. The not-lined players (Koltsov at 92 speed, Abid at 86 scoring, Fischer at 89 speed) are the depth that wins series when someone gets hurt.

**Goalies** are the best-covered position. Luongo is elite at 94 overall with a 1.73 GAA and 0.940 save percentage in 8 games. Tellqvist at 80-80-80-74 is a competent backup. Ouellet at 86-86-86-76 is the third. Luongo has 1 year left at $1.60M; the renewal window is the conversation for after the season, not now.



**Task #2 (Luongo/DiPietro goalie monitoring):** Closed on 2005-11-13. Luongo is confirmed on the roster at 94 overall, 1 year remaining, $1.60M. The renewal window is the only open item and it is a post-season conversation. No further monitoring needed.

## Trajectory

Is Toronto aging into a cliff, and is the money arranged for the next three summers rather than tonight? The short answer: no cliff, but two traps are set, and one of them ($11.90M locked to a healthy scratch) is already sprung.

**The age shape is the manual's dream and its warning at once.** Thirteen players 23 or under, sixteen at 24-29, only two at 30-33 (Tucker and McCabe, both scratched with 0 GP), and three at 34+ (Sundin 34, Mogilny 36, Roberts 39). The veterans at 34+ eat $18.80M for 24 combined points across 44 games. The 30-33 bridge is empty on the ice. When Mogilny and Sundin walk, which they will within two seasons, Toronto goes from five veterans to zero unless the young core has arrived by then. Most of it has (Chlup, Nash, Chistov, Klesla, Jackman all dress nightly), but the mentorship layer is gone and that matters for development, not production.

**Gaborik is the anchor.** $11.90M x 5 years at 8 points in 17 games is 13.2% of payroll buying a healthy scratch. Five years is immovable in this game: no trade, no renegotiation, no buyout. The GM's October 16 question about rotating players to manage salary doesn't apply here. Gaborik isn't a "good player" at 0.47 pts/g. He's a locked liability through summer 2010. The only move that changes the outcome is making him play, which is the Coach's call, but the trajectory math says if he never cracks 50 points, Toronto carries $59.50M in sunk cost for a player who can't be moved.

**July 2006 is the renewal window that matters.** Nine players worth $15.44M expire in one year. Of those, Chlup ($2.34M, 19, 15 pts in 18 GP, POTE 95) and Luongo ($1.60M, 26, 94 overall) are the two the club cannot afford to lose. Klesla ($0.90M, 23, 6 pts in 18 GP, POTE 97) and Spezza ($1.00M, 22, POTE 99) are the next tier. Chlup's salary will jump from $2.34M toward $4-5M on any extension; Luongo from $1.60M toward $3-4M. That's roughly $4-5M of new commitment in a single week, which is affordable against $35.17M profit but requires being ready with the offers in July rather than scrambling.

**The 4-year cluster is the real trap.** Eleven players worth $37.40M expire in summer 2009: Sundin, Richards, Chistov, Kaberle, Nash, Eminger, Alexeev, Upshall, Colaiacovo, Wallin, Abid. By 2009, Sundin will be 38 (walks), Kaberle 31 (declining), and Richards (29), Chistov (26), and Nash (25) all simultaneously require star-contract extensions of $5-8M each. That's a $20M+ renewal bill in one summer against a roster that will have lost Mogilny and Sundin's $13.90M. The math works if young players (Gardener POTE 98, Upshall POTE 99, Colaiacovo POTE 99, Hainsey POTE 97) have developed into affordable production by then. It doesn't work if they've stalled, because the GM will be paying for potential that didn't arrive AND star extensions at the same time.

**The money is not a constraint today.** Payroll $89.94M against $35.17M profit means the club can carry the Gaborik contract, the veterans, and the extension window simultaneously. The question is never "can we afford it" but "are we paying for the right things." Right now the answer is: we're paying $11.90M for 8 points and $4.90M for a 39-year-old with 2 points in 8 games.

**Draft capital is workable but thin.** Toronto holds its own first, second, and third rounders and no other club's picks. The R1 is the only premium chip, which means one blockbuster is available in February 2006 or none. The R2 and R3 fund a mid-tier acquisition (the Bell/CHI package, the Stuart/SJ package from earlier notes). No pick beyond the third means the GM cannot fund two deals simultaneously unless players are the currency.

**The three moves that protect three years:**

1. Lock Chlup and Luongo in July 2006. Both are 5-6 year deals. Luongo first. If one slips through, the rebuild clock restarts.
2. When Mogilny's contract expires this summer, do not replace him with another 33+ player. The Iginla-type target at 27 (or Heatley at 24, or Doan at 28) fills the void AND ensures the 30-33 bridge has someone in it by 2009.
3. Develop the POTE 97-99 group into affordable production before 2009. Colaiacovo at 2 pts in 18 GP and Eminger at 2 in 7 need 15+ MPG now or the 4-year cluster becomes a $37M bill with no one to show for it.

## Calendar

Are we buyers or sellers, and what happens when the contracts expire?

We are buyers at the deadline. At 28 points in second place, eight games clear of ninth (CAR, 18), we are not selling the core. The deadline is 122 days out, negotiations open late February per the January standing order. The target list is built: Bertuzzi, Kurka, Heatley, Jovanovski. Tucker is the chip.

**Mogilny** at 36 and $5.50M is the clearest deadline sell. He was supposed to have moved in December 2004 and never did. At 36, no re-signing conversation exists. If his overall is above 80, the pick mechanic applies and he fetches a draft selection even as a pure rental. If not, he still brings value to a contender needing veteran depth. Either way, $5.50M freed for a young player's contract is the summer's first line-item.

**Tucker** at 30 and $1.30M is the other chip. The GM confirmed him as a trade piece at last March's deadline and he is still here. Fund Bertuzzi or Kurka with him.

**Chlup** is the renewal priority. 19 years old, first-line centre, 0.88 pts/g on 21.4 MPG across 17 games. Five or six years, immediate, before February. He is the face of the next five years.

**Luongo** at 94 and 26 years old, $1.60M expiring: five or six years. Star deal, no question. Task #2 (monitoring for a goalie trade partner) closed November 13 because he is the franchise number one and stays.

**Spezza** at 22 and POTE 99 is a development emergency, not a contract problem. The Coach says 3.8 MPG and 0.18 pts/g. Give him 15+ or stop dressing him. If he plays 60+ games by March, renew on four or five years. If he is still a healthy scratch in January, he becomes a deadline chip alongside Tucker and Mogilny.

**Koltsov** at 24 and $1.10M expiring: by February we will know if he is a top-nine winger. If yes, renew on three years. If no, trade at deadline for depth or a late pick.

**Klesla** at 23, D, $0.90M: cheap, young, expiring. Renew on three years if his minutes and numbers support it. If the Coach gives him real ice time and he responds, he is affordable depth for years.

**Ouellet** at 24, backup goalie, $0.90M: he is the playoff backup the GM wants. Renew on two years at the same or lower number. Cheap insurance.

**St. Jacques** at 25, D, $0.80M: was proposed to Chicago last season. If the Bell-type deal is dead, he is depth and renews on two years. If a deal needs a body, he is expendable at $0.80M.

Summer shape: two five-plus-year renewals (Chlup, Luongo), two three-to-four-year renewals (Klesla, one of Spezza or Koltsov depending on development), two two-year deals (Ouellet, St. Jacques), and two departures (Mogilny, Tucker) that free $6.80M for the next acquisition.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: who on the other 29 clubs closes our zero-toughness gap at a price we can actually pay, and who is the seller most likely to say yes? With CAR, VAN, SJ and WSH all bottom-8 and carrying 13-14 expiring contracts, the February market has abundance. The shortlist below ranks by grade-to-likelihood ratio: players whose clubs *must* move them, at grades Toronto cannot self-supply.

**Kurka** (CAR, LW, 23, 78 overall, TOUG 90, CHKG 92, 12 pts/17 GP, $0.60M expiring, POTE 76) is the confirmed primary. CAR at 18 pts with 14 expiring deals and $63.79M payroll cannot retain him. Package: Upshall plus R3. The Coach has already flagged Upshall for reduced dressing priority, making him available at no roster cost to us.

**Bertuzzi** (VAN, RW, 30, 93 overall, TOUG 85, CHKG 89, 28 pts/18 GP, $2.60M expiring, POTE 58) is the single most impactful player on any expiring deal in the league. 93 overall and 1.56 pts/g with 85/89 TOUG/CHKG solves toughness AND scoring simultaneously. At 30 with POTE 58 he has no development left, which means this is a "win now" rental at elite level. VAN at 21 pts with 13 expiring and Naslund (32, $4.40M), Morrison (29, $4.33M), Ohlund (29, $2.60M) all expiring must shed veterans. Package: Tucker plus R2.

**Yonkman** (WSH, D, 24, 77 overall, TOUG 90, CHKG 92, 6 pts/18 GP, $0.60M expiring, POTE 89) is the best value on the board. 90/92 TOUG/CHKG at 24 for $0.60M with POTE 89 is a franchise shutdown D at entry-level money. WSH at 15 pts with only 5 expiring CAN retain him, but at $56.89M payroll with $22.97M profit and a prestige of 826 they have no reason to pay for two 90-rated Ds when they're clearly rebuilding. They might take a cheap package just to get another asset. Eminger plus R2 gates on the GM's decision.

**Witt** (WSH, D, 30, 79 overall, TOUG 90, CHKG 94, 11 pts/18 GP, $1.70M expiring, POTE 81) is the veteran anchor for the same WSH sale. At $1.70M he's cheaper than a mid-round pick's salary value. His 11 points in 18 games on a bad team means his shot is still live. The best use is pairing him with Yonkman in one deal: Eminger plus R2 for both, giving Toronto a young-and-old shutdown pair that costs $2.30M combined.

**Jovanovski** (VAN, D, 29, 88 overall, TOUG 93, CHKG 94, 9 pts/18 GP, $2.30M expiring, POTE 71) is the highest-graded D on any seller. 88 overall with 93/94 is top-pair quality tonight. At 29 his ceiling is set and POTE 71 confirms it. VAN must shed him given the Bertuzzi/Naslund/Morrison expiring class. This competes with Bertuzzi for the same VAN attention; the GM should pick one VAN target rather than over-commit to one club.

**McLaren** (SJ, D, 28, 81 overall, TOUG 87, CHKG 91, 9 pts/16 GP, $2.20M expiring, POTE 79) is the blue-line version of our problem-solver. SJ at 16 pts with 14 expiring and $66.24M payroll is the single most motivated seller in the league. They MUST move someone.
