The package from earlier (Abid plus R2) remains viable but SJ's desperation might open a better deal if we approach with patience.

**Conroy** (CGY, C, 34, 84 overall, FACE 95, 17 pts/18 GP, $2.00M expiring, POTE 80) is the faceoff answer. 95 FACE and 17 points in 18 games on a 21-point team means he's carrying a bad roster. At $2.00M expiring, CGY at 21 pts with 9 expiring will move him for depth pieces. He doesn't solve toughness (TOUG 63) but he solves the L2 or L3 center problem that Chlup's development may create if he moves to L1 permanently.

**Phillips** (SJ, D, 33, 81 overall, TOUG 89, CHKG 92, $1.82M expiring, POTE 82) is a pure rental but 89/92 TOUG/CHKG on the same SJ roster that must shed 14 contracts makes him available. At 33 he's a one-year fix, but for a playoff run that's exactly the profile.

**Komisarek** (MTL, D, 23, 86 overall, TOUG 86, CHKG 93, 13 pts/17 GP, $1.10M expiring, POTE 92) is the best player on the board who will likely NOT move. At 23 with POTE 92 and $1.10M, MTL at 15 pts rebuilding will fight to re-sign him. Worth a phone call in February but do not build around it.

**Semenov** (EDM, D, 24, 77 overall, TOUG 87, CHKG 86, 12 pts/18 GP, $0.60M expiring, POTE 87) is the same story: too good at too cheap for EDM to move with only 5 expiring.

For the high-potential secondary group, **Cammalleri** (LA, RW, 23, 87 overall, POTE 98, $1.10M expiring, 5 pts/9 GP) and **Bouwmeester** (FLA, D, 22, 83 overall, POTE 96, $1.20M expiring) are the two players whose ceiling exceeds anything Toronto currently holds. Neither fills the toughness gap, but LA at 14 pts with 6 expiring and FLA at 17 pts with 5 expiring might not move them. These are February phone calls, not packages.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: what does the GM hand CAR, VAN, WSH and SJ in February, and why do they say yes? With four bottom-8 clubs carrying 13-14 expiring contracts between them, the market has supply. Toronto's constraint is pick depth: one first-rounder, one second, one third. Three proposals, ranked by likelihood-to-impact, with only two executable simultaneously given pick limits.

**Kurka for Upshall plus our third-rounder** is the opening bid and the most likely to land. CAR at 18 pts, $63.79M payroll, 14 expiring deals cannot retain 14 players. Kurka's $0.60M is cheap but his TOUG 90 and CHKG 92 address a gap where our best is Jackman at 75. Upshall at 22, POTE 99, $1.50M x4 with CHKG 87 base gives CAR a developmental piece they can keep or flip. The Coach already flagged Upshall for reduced dressing priority at 3 pts in 9 games on 5.6 MPG, so we lose nothing tonight. We save $0.90M.

**Bertuzzi for Tucker plus our second-rounder** is the highest-impact single move available. At 93 overall, 28 points in 18 games, TOUG 85 and CHKG 89, Bertuzzi solves toughness and scoring in one transaction. VAN at 21 pts with 13 expiring, Naslund at $4.40M, Morrison at $4.33M, Ohlund at $2.60M all leaving, must shed veterans. Bertuzzi at 30 with POTE 58 is a rental for them too; they get zero future value from re-signing him. Tucker provides 88 TOUG and 92 CHKG base for their locker room and a second-rounder is premium currency for a club rebuilding from 21 points. We increase payroll $1.30M but his contract expires this summer.

**Witt and Yonkman for Colaiacovo plus our first-rounder** is the blue-line package. Yonkman at 24, TOUG 90, CHKG 92, $0.60M with POTE 89 is a franchise shutdown defenseman at entry-level money. Witt at 30 brings 94 CHKG and 11 points in 18 games on a bad team for $1.70M expiring. WSH at 15 pts, $56.89M payroll, $22.97M profit are rebuilding; Colaiacovo at 22 with POTE 99, BALA 85, SHPW 84 is exactly the franchise defenseman they're missing. The Coach already flagged him as stalling at 0.06 pts/g in 17 games on 13 MPG, so we're not giving production. The first-rounder is the cost of Yonkman's POTE 89 at 24.

**Combinations:** Kurka (R3) plus either Bertuzzi (R2) or Witt/Yonkman (R1) is executable. Kurka plus both is not: we have one R2 and one R1. If the GM wants toughness AND scoring, take Kurka and Bertuzzi. If he wants toughness AND blue-line construction, take Kurka and Witt/Yonkman.

**If none land:** Line McCabe on the fourth defensive pair (86 CHKG base, 94 ENDU) and Roberts on the fourth line for PK shifts (92 TOUG, 86 CHKG base, 75 FACE). Both are healthy scratches tonight. This does not close the gap at 80 displayed grades but it restores two bodies with real checking pedigree on the ice without spending a chip. The alternative is accepting the gap and going small and fast with our 25 players at 80+ speed. That wins regular-season games but loses playoff series against physical teams.

**On task #2 (Luongo/DiPietro monitoring):** Closed 2005-11-13. Luongo is confirmed at 94 overall, 1 year, $1.60M. No further action until the renewal window opens after the season.

## Owed

**Task #2 — Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window:** This task was closed on November 13 per the GM's March 19 standing order ("Goalies are solved. Done."). Nothing has reopened it.

**Luongo** is still on the roster at 95 overall, $1.60M with 1 year left. He has 8 GP out of Toronto's 18 — that's a 44% workload, meaning the other net is getting 10 starts. This matters for the renewal conversation at season end but does not change the trade question; the task stays closed until the renewal window.

**DiPietro** sits at NYI, 24 years old, 86 overall, 14 GP, $1.10M expiring. No movement from the last reading. NYI are not in a position to sell him at a discount before February, and at 86 he is below the high-90s threshold the GM set in January.

Nothing has moved since November 13. Task remains closed. The next action point is Luongo's renewal at season end, not a trade.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-17
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-17

Next game vs BOS on Saturday 19 November 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether our young players are getting the games they have earned, and right now four of them are caught in a pattern I flagged in October and is now repeating for a second season.

**Chlup** at 15 points in 18 games on 20.8 minutes is getting everything he has earned on the second line. His rate (0.83 pts/g) at 19 is the best on the roster. The only open question is the first line, which I have already raised twice and the GM has kept as-is. Nothing further from me on that tonight.

**Chistov** at 9 points on 17.9 MPG and **Nash** at 9 points on 14.3 MPG are both playing every game and both producing at 0.50 pts/g on the second and third lines. Stable roles, appropriate minutes, morale at 96 for both. They are getting what they have earned. No change.

**Stahle** at 4 points on 12.5 MPG for the third pair and **Colaiacovo** at 2 points on 12.5 MPG on the same pair are the 21-and-22-year-old defensemen sharing the third pairing. The minutes are right for their role. Colaiacovo's production is thin at 0.11 pts/g, but the GM already moved him up the pair order after my November 16 note, so give it more games before judging.

**Gaborik** at 8 points on 22.6 MPG for the first line is exactly where a 23-year-old top winger should sit. His rate is 0.47 pts/g, which is modest, but the role is not the problem. **Klesla** at 6 points on 25.7 MPG for the first pair is the same story. He's a sell candidate at the deadline, not a development question.

**Eminger** at 7 games out of 18 is the odd one out among the defensemen. 19.9 MPG when he plays, POTE 99, 22 years old. The GM has moved on from him as a trade target since the contract correction (locked at $2.20M x 4), so the scratch pattern is his problem to solve, not mine to fight.

The four below are the problem.

**Spezza** at 3.6 MPG in 12 games is the same collapse I wrote about in March and again in October. He was drafted to be a top-six centre and he is getting fourth-line scraps. At 22, with morale at 81 and 0.17 pts/g, dressing him every third or fourth game teaches him nothing and costs him confidence. My October finding called for a hard rule: if minutes stay under 8, scratch permanently rather than carry. Three months later, nothing has changed. Either give him 10-plus minutes in a real role or stop dressing him. The middle ground is the worst option for his development and it is where he sits.

**Upshall** at 5.1 MPG in 9 games, 0.33 pts/g, morale 81. Same pattern, same diagnosis. At 22 with POTE 99, the scouting staff thinks something is there, but he has not shown it in two seasons of being dressed for half the games and playing five minutes. If the GM will not raise his role, scratch him permanently and let a player who will play 10-plus minutes take the spot.

**Gardener** at 3.3 MPG in 9 games with zero points. POTE 98 means the staff sees something, but at 20 he is nowhere close to earning real minutes. Dressed on the fourth line for a shift here and there. The right call is the same: scratch him and let him develop in a role where he actually plays, or keep him home. Dressing a player for 3 minutes a night is not development.

**Alexeev** at 6 points in 11 games on 11.2 MPG (0.55 pts/g) outperforms Upshall (0.33) and Gardener (0.00), both of whom get dressed. His share is up to 61% from the 46% I noted last April, which is progress, but he should be in every game over Upshall. The rate-to-role gap I flagged in the spring is narrowing but not closed.

**Spacek** at 6 games, 5.8 MPG, morale 76. The GM's standing order has him out for development rotation, and I accept that. But 76 is the lowest morale on the roster and he is paying a two-point penalty on every grade for it. If the plan is to develop other centres over him, that is his call, but the morale slide is real.

## Development trends

The window is too short for grade movement — none recorded — so trends rest on production and minutes alone. What matters: the minutes-collapse pattern has claimed another victim, Jackman's load fix is working, and Fischer's small sample is screaming.

**Chlup** at 19: 0.82 pts/g on 21.7 MPG over 18 games. The season opened with one game at 6 MPG; he's since doubled it. His career rate of 0.88 from last season and this 0.82 confirm the first-line centre call. Still sitting on the second line per the record. No change to my position: he goes up.

**Gardener** at 20: 1.8 MPG, 0 points in 9 games. Opened the year at 16 MPG, collapsed to less than 2. This is the fifth young forward caught in the pattern I documented in October. At 0 points there's nothing to develop. Scratch him for good and stop burning a roster slot.

**Spacek** at 20: 3.6 MPG, 0.40 pts/g in 6 games. Same collapse from 17 MPG. But 0.40 in the scraps he gets means he's not helpless. The GM scratched him in January for development and reinstated him for quality nights; this season he got a real audition and lost it. The pattern holds.

**Spezza** at 22: 3.6 MPG, 0.17 pts/g over 12 games. Another season written off before December. No grade movement either. The pattern is now three seasons running.

**Upshall** at 22: 3.8 MPG, 0.25 pts/g in 9 games. Identical to Spezza. Both 22, both invisible.

**Jackman** at 24: 0.76 pts/g on 24.5 MPG over 18 games. His load dropped from 41 MPG to 24.5 and his production went from his career 0.48 to 0.76. The D-minute fix from October worked. The sell window I noted on November 13 (0.88 over 16) has eased slightly to 0.76 but he's still well above the 0.55 sell threshold. Monitor; no action yet.

**Klesla** at 23: 0.35 pts/g on 24.7 MPG. Also down from 42 MPG to 24.7, but his production didn't spike the way Jackman's did. Still the sell candidate at deadline.

**Fischer** at 25: 0.80 pts/g on 21.8 MPG in just 6 games. Small sample, but at 25 with the GM calling him a keeper for his two-way game, this rate says his offensive game is developing. If he holds above 0.50 through 15 games, his role conversation changes.

**Richards** at 25: 0.65 pts/g on 13.1 MPG, flat. The system-fit issue I flagged in May hasn't budged. Fourteen months at roughly 13 MPG and sub-0.75 production. He's not growing into the top centre role; he's stagnating in it.

**Alexeev** at 23: 0.40 pts/g on 11.7 MPG over 11 games. Outproduces Spezza (0.17) and Upshall (0.25) on the sheet but gets similar scraps. My last recommendation to dress him was not taken.

**Sundin** at 34: 0.71 pts/g on 23.2 MPG. Stable. No age-driven decline visible yet.

**Mogilny** at 36: 0.59 pts/g on 22.8 MPG. Respectable for his age but this is the last year anyone should plan around him producing above 0.50.

## Morale watch

The room is stable: nobody below 81 except Spacek, and most starters sit in the 90s. The one actionable issue is Richards, who has been under his minutes band for months and is starting to pay the grade cost. The second is the fourth line, which is in a holding pattern that costs morale without developing anyone.

**Richards** is at morale 86 on 13.1 MPG in 18 games. At his calibre he expects roughly 17 minutes a night, a deficit of about 4. The 80s morale band shaves one point off every grade, and he is producing 0.61 pts/g (11 points in 18) despite the handicap. His morale has been flat at 86 for several weeks now, neither recovering nor dropping further. The fix is minutes on the line, not a line shuffle. If L3 usage rises from 13 to 16 average MPG, Richards gets closer to band and the -1 should lift.

**Spacek** sits at morale 76, the lowest on the roster. The 70s band costs two points off every grade, which partly explains why his production looks thin. He is scratched at the GM's direction for development reasons, so the cost is accepted. No line change fixes this; it resolves when he plays regularly again.

**Spezza, Upshall and Gardener** are all at morale 81 on 3.6, 5.1 and 3.3 MPG respectively. They are fourth-line regulars who get about a third of what their band expects. They are producing almost nothing (2, 3 and 0 points). This is the same collapse pattern I flagged in October: young forwards given token minutes in a sheltered role, morale plateaus in the 80s, production flatlines. Either they get 8 to 10 minutes with real responsibility, or they come out of the lineup. The current middle ground costs one grade point each and develops nobody.

**Nobody else needs attention.** The scratched veterans (McCabe, Tucker, Abid) sit at 90. Luongo is at 86 with no minutes concern as a starter. The top nine forwards and both top pairs are all above 96 and above band.

## Role composition

Are our units built from the right players, and do we have enough of each role to build them? The answer is the units are fine and the roster is not.

**L1** is the best possible configuration with this roster. Sundin (94 scoring, 96 playmaking, 95 faceoffs) plus Mogilny (92) and Gaborik (99/99) with Jackman (92 checking) as the anchor behind them. Nothing to improve.

**L2** works as a speed line. Hainsey at 99 speed gives it separation, Chlup's 80 on draws is acceptable for a second centre, and Chistov's 93 playmaking makes him more useful here than anywhere else on the sheet.

**L3** has the one interesting tension: Richards carries 93 playmaking, the third-best on the club, but sits on the third line. His production collapsed last season and hasn't recovered. I keep him here. The grades say he can play second-line wing; the scoresheet says not yet. Give him the minutes and let the rate earn the promotion.

**L4** is the weakest unit on the sheet. Checking mean 70, toughness mean 62. Roberts (84) and McCabe (83) are the two forwards behind Jackman who could anchor a checking line, and they're both scratched. Nash (82) is already on L3. There is no arrangement of this roster that produces a fourth line with a checking mean above 75. This is the same gap I flagged in April and it hasn't closed.

**P1 and P2** are well-balanced. K1 with Jackman (92) and Chlup (80) is the right shape.

**Kaberle** at 91 clutch and 87 stamina is our best defensive depth piece and he's scratched. Against a 9-4 Boston club this is a maximize-quality night per the framework the GM set in January.

## Opponent matchup

The question is how to shape our lines against a quality Boston club with Gaborik out for six weeks.

**The opponent:** Boston sits at 9-4-2 with a 14.8% power play (8 in 54) — they'll generate chances. Thornton at 91 OVR is their engine (97 SHPW, 94 PUCK, 84 CHKG), flanked by speed (Samsonov 99 SPEE) and veteran scoring (Murray 96 SHPW). Their bottom six is a genuine weakness: Johnson 70, Vaananen 72, Asplund 71. We should outscore them heavily on line four.

**Our advantage in net:** Luongo at 95 versus Raycroft at 85. Ten points of separation. We need him sharp. His morale is 86, no fatigue flag in the brief, but the standing order says to check the icon on screen before confirming.

**The first-line hole:** Gaborik (99 OVR) is out. Mogilny at 89 fills in on the right wing. The left wing spot is the open question. **Nash** (85 OVR, CHKG 87, TOUG 92) is the answer for this opponent specifically — his defensive grade (87) matches Thornton's checking (84), and his speed (92 SPEE) handles Samsonov's 99 better than Alexeev's 94 combined with weaker two-way play. Moving Nash up to the first line is a matchup decision, not a development one. Richards stays at third-line centre.

**Auto-pairing consideration:** When Thornton's line is on, we want line one out because it auto-pairs with Jackman/Klesla (86 and 87 OVR, CHKG 94 and 81). That's our shutdown pair. Klesla's 99 SPEE matches Samsonov directly. We cannot get checking forwards with the top D pair because of the auto-pair system, so we accept Sundin (92 OVR, FACE 95) winning draws against Thornton (FACE 78) as our defensive weapon — we control possession at the dot.

**Discipline is the lever:** Their PP converts at 14.8%. Every minor we take is a real chance against us. The brief doesn't show our PIM history specifically, but the point stands: no change to the lineup changes this. It's an in-game discipline matter.

**Boston's second line** (Hilbert 82, Knuble 79, Lapointe 79) faces our D pair two (Safronov 68, Hainsey 77) when our line two is out. Safronov's 71 SPEE against Knuble's 79 SPEE is a mild concern, but Hilbert at 91 SPEE is the speed threat and Hainsey's 99 SPEE covers. No change needed.

**Bottom line:** Start Luongo, move Nash up to first-line RW to fill the Gaborik gap with a two-way game, leave everything else alone. Our depth advantage on their fourth line should decide this game.

## Owed

D-man trade analysis for Boston game on Saturday. This is the standing job: who should go at the end of the season.

**Klesla** remains the top sell candidate and the window is getting wider, not narrower. 87 OVR with an expiring contract at $0.90M, but his production is now 6 points in 18 games, 0.33 pts/g. My Nov 13 threshold was 0.55 for the window to close. He's well below it and falling. A buyer at the deadline sees the 87 grade and a 23-year-old top-pairing defenceman available cheap. We see a declining rate behind a younger cheaper partner in Jackman. Nothing has changed to argue for keeping him.

**Jackman** stays off the sell list. 14 points in 18 games, 0.78 pts/g, $0.70M x 2. My Nov 13 reversal holds. He is out-producing Klesla at more than double the rate for less than the salary, and he has a year of team control left after this one.

**McCabe** is still a sell target in principle but a practical dead end. 0 games played this season, $3.00M x 4 at age 30, no dressed status. Nobody absorbs that money for a healthy defenceman we won't dress. The GM needs to decide whether to eat the cap hit or find a sign-and-trade or expansion-style dump. My recommendation: try to attach him to a package as filler rather than expecting a return on him alone.

**Eminger** is stuck. 2 points in 7 games, 0.29 pts/g at $2.20M x 4. My May 31 correction that he is not expiring killed the trade urgency. Nobody takes four years of $2.2M for a 0.3 pts/g defenceman at 82 OVR unless we eat a third of the salary. I would not pursue this before the deadline; revisit in the summer when he turns 23 and a rebuilding team might gamble on development.

**Colaiacovo** is producing 2 points in 18 games on 12.5 MPG. That is 0.11 pts/g. Last game I recommended his minutes go to Hainsey and you took it. He is not a sell target -- 76 OVR and $1.40M x 4 will not move -- but he is in the same "young-player-minutes-collapse" pattern I flagged with Spezza, Upshall and Spacek. If his minutes stay under 8 for the next three games, he belongs in the minors or the press box permanently.

**No changes from last delivery except Colaiacovo's situation is now confirmed as stalled rather than uncertain.** Klesla remains the one clear action.

# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-16

Toronto 11-3-0, 28 pts after 17 games.

## Role coverage

The question is: which roles does Toronto have enough of, which are thin, and which are missing? This matters because at 11-3-0 and 28 points through 17 games the club is in a playoff position, and February is six weeks away, so the coverage gaps are now costed in wins.

**Scoring and playmaking** are covered now: 11 players at 80+ in each. But the top is Mogilny at 36, Sundin at 34, Roberts at 39. Gaborik (23, 92) and Afinogenov (26, 90) are the succession. The age curve is fine for two more years, ugly by 2008.

**Speed** is overstocked: 25 at 80+. Koltsov (92, 24) and Fischer (89, 25) are both unlined, which means speed depth the coach is not spending.

**Checking** reads thin only because the coach is not using who he has. Jackman (87, 24) and Upshall (80, 22) are the only 80+ checkers among lined players. McCabe (86, 30), Tucker (83, 30), and Fischer (82, 25) are all on the roster, all 80+, and all in no unit. Dressing McCabe and Tucker lifts checking from two to four above 80. This is the coach's decision, not a trade.

**Toughness** is the only role that is genuinely missing. Zero players at 80+. The best is Jackman at 75, then Roberts at 73. There is no internal fix. The Coach's fourth line reads a toughness mean of 62. This is the single structural gap that no lineup card can close.

**Faceoffs** are thin: one player above 80 who plays (Sundin at 90). Wallin (83, 25) is unlined and would give a second. Chlup at 75 is the next best centre. Lining Wallin at centre makes this thin but serviceable; it does not make it good.

**Clutch** is fine at 9 above 80, though it shares the same Mogilny/Sundin age problem as scoring. **Stamina** and **durability** are fine.

**Goalies**: Luongo at 94, 26, with a .941 save percentage. Tellqvist 6-0 with a 1.48 GAA. Covered.

The only acquisition target the role coverage creates is toughness. Bell (CHI, 88 TOUG role, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, 24) closes toughness and faceoffs in one body. No other single move fixes two gaps at once.

## Trajectory

The question this phase answers: does Toronto's roster age into a cliff, and are its contracts arranged so that the same summer doesn't kill the club twice? It matters now because July 2006 brings the first real renewal crunch after the rebuild loaded up, and the answer determines whether Chlup and Luongo stay.

**Age curve.** The shape is wrong in one specific place: the 30–33 band holds only Tucker (30, scratched) and McCabe (30, scratched). Everyone else is under 26 or over 34. The 34+ trio — Sundin (34), Mogilny (36), Roberts (39) — carry $18.80M and 24 points between them in 42 games. That production has no heir in the 26–33 band because that band barely exists. The gap is structural: there are zero forwards aged 26–33 on this roster except Wallin (25) and Afinogenov (26). The next step after Chlup and Richards is no one, and that's the cliff.

**The July 2006 renewal cluster.** Nine contracts expire, $15.44M total. Two are untouchable and must be locked the same week in July:

**Luongo** is 26, 91 base, $1.60M. He is the franchise goalie. A 5–6 year extension at $3–4M is cheap insurance. Tellqvist behind him at 77 base is a clear step down.

**Chlup** is 19, 82 base, 15 points in 17 games (0.88 pts/g), POTE 95, on $2.34M. He is the future first-line centre. His 4-year comparison is Richards at the same age (25 now, $6.70M, 82 base). Chlup at 19 is ahead of where Richards was. Lock him 5–6 years or lose him.

The remaining seven are either walkable (Mogilny at 36, Tucker at 30) or cheap to keep (Klesla $0.90M, Spezza $1.00M).

**The Sundin question.** He's 34, $8.40M/year, 4 years left, producing 12 points in 17 games (0.71 pts/g). At the end of his contract he'll be 38 on $8.40M. There is no scenario where he's a first-line centre in 2008-09. Either trade him at the February deadline while he still carries a 90 base and has four years of term a contender could use, or accept him as a declining second centre. The GM's question from October 16 — "do we want to get rid of good players just to lower our salary expenses" — applies to Sundin directly. He's not a salary problem yet; he's a role problem arriving slowly.

**Gaborik's cost.** $11.90M/year is 13.2% of total payroll on a single player producing 0.50 pts/g over 16 games. At 23 with POTE 90, the contract pays for the ceiling, not the floor. He's lined now, which is correct, but this is the contract that makes the 30-33 void hard to fill — no free agent at 28 with 20 pts/g comes cheap when Gaborik and Sundin together eat $20.30M.

**Financial room.** Payroll $89.94M against profit $36.27M. The club earns more than it spends. There is room to add a $4–6M player without financial stress. The constraint is not money; it's the absence of a roster spot that isn't someone else's future.

**Draft capital.** First, second, and third rounders from 2006, all TOR's own. At 11-3-0, the first-rounder lands around 25–28th overall. The second and third are the deadline currency. A first-rounder alone buys a mid-80 rental; with a prospect attached (Koltsov, Spezza, or St. Jacques) it buys a young player with term.

## Calendar

Are we buyers or sellers, and what happens to our nine expiring contracts? We are buying, and six of those nine renewals are the work of the summer.

**Where we sit.** Eleven wins, three losses, no ties, 28 points, second in the Eastern Conference with eight teams making the playoffs. The deadline is 123 days out on March 19. We are buyers and there is no plausible scenario where a 17-game lead over eighth-place Carolina (16 points) collapses before March.

**Deadline plan: two acquisitions, one dump.**

**Tucker** is our primary chip and was already a chip last March. At 30, $1.30M, expiring, he is a clean rental package for a contender. The lead target remains **Bertuzzi** at Vancouver (94 base, TOUG 83, CHKG 87, 1.25 pts/g, 30, $1.30M expiring). VAN's payroll was $46.36M with 13 expiring in October; they are the most motivated seller. Package: Tucker plus our best available pick. I do not currently know which picks we hold for 2006 — last season's fourth is confirmed at NYR from the query — so the package shape may need adjusting once we confirm what the June draft left us.

**Mogilny** at 36 and $5.50M is the single largest payroll item and the one move that pays for everything else. If he is still above 80 overall, the pick-recovery mechanic applies: send him to a non-contender for a draft pick with no return player needed. If he is below 80, dump him to a team out of the race (Florida, Tampa, the bottom of the Southeast) for any return at all. Either way, he does not walk in July for nothing. The Coach's notes show our checking depth is non-existent beyond Jackman and McCabe, and Mogilny at 36 is not solving any of that.

**Blue line target:** Brad Stuart (SJ, 25, 87 base, POTE 91, $1.80M expiring). His TOUG is 72, so he is not the toughness fix, but he is the best young defenseman on a desperate seller and fits our timeline. If SAN can be part of a Bertuzzi multi-club package, Stuart becomes reachable. Otherwise, he needs Abid or Koltsov as the return piece, and we are protective of Koltsov. This is the secondary target.

**Summer plan, one by one:**

**Luongo** at 26, 94 overall, $1.60M with one year left. Five to six years. This is the contract that defines the next five seasons and nothing else matters if he walks. Re-sign immediately at renewal.

**Spezza** at 22, $1.00M. The Coach's five-game clock expired in October and he was finally dressed for game 8 at 7 MPG on L4. If he is getting 12+ MPG by February and showing points, he gets 5-6 years. If he is still at 7 MPG on the fourth line in March, he is a trade chip for the blue line and we let this one go.

**Koltsov** at 24, $1.10M. Young, cheap, on the core timeline. Five years if developing, four if middling.

**Klesla** at 23, $0.90M. Same logic: three to five years depending on whether his minutes and grades are moving up.

**Chlup** at 19, $2.34M. The Coach moved him to first-line centre. At 19 and $2.34M he is expensive for a rookie. The decision point is February: if he is producing at top-six rates, he is a keeper on 5-6 years. If he is not, that $2.34M is wasted and he becomes a depth piece on a two-year minimum deal or walks.

**Ouellet** at 24, $0.90M. GM said "give him time" in January 2005. One year has passed. If he is a competent backup (85+), renew on two years. If not, let him walk — Luongo plus a cheap waiver pickup covers us.

**St. Jacques** at 25, $0.80M. Already proposed as a chip in the Bell/CHI package. If we haven't moved him by March, renew on two years or use him as the third piece in a defensive acquisition.

**Task #2 (Luongo/DiPietro monitoring):** Closed November 13. Luongo is on our roster at 94 with one year at $1.60M. No further monitoring needed until the renewal window. The task is delivered.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: who on the other 29 clubs fills Toronto's one structural gap (zero players above 80 toughness) or its secondary gaps (checking depth beyond Jackman, the empty 26-33 age band), and would their club actually say yes? At 11-3-0 we are buying, not selling, so the targets are players on losing clubs who are expiring or overpaid.

**Kurka (CAR, LW, 23)** is the single best value in the league for our exact problem. 88 TOUG, 90 CHKG, 12 points in 16 games at 20.8 minutes a night, $0.60M on an expiring deal. CAR at 16 points with 14 expiring contracts and $63.79M payroll cannot keep him. He is two years younger than Tucker, grades higher in both toughness and checking, costs a third of Tucker's salary, and plays. This closes the gap the Coach has been flagging since October with one body.

**Kovalchuk (ATL, LW, 22)** fills toughness AND the scoring bridge simultaneously. 82 TOUG, 89 overall, 16 points in 15 games, $1.10M expiring. ATL at 12 points with 6 expiring deals cannot retain both him and Heatley. The binary note from February holds: whichever ATL keeps, the other moves. He is younger than Gaborik, cheaper, and grades 82 toughness where Gaborik does not clear 80.

**Witt (WSH, D, 30)** is the shutdown defenseman the Coach says does not exist. 91 TOUG, 95 CHKG, 80 overall, 10 points in 16 games at 32 minutes a night. $1.70M expiring. WSH at 13 points, profitable at $24.36M, with 5 expiring deals. He is a rental (30, no term beyond this year) but he pairs with Jackman immediately and turns the checking gap into a non-issue for the playoffs.

**Yonkman (WSH, D, 24)** is the developmental version of the same package. 91 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 78 overall, POTE 89, $0.60M expiring, 6 points in 16 games at 19.4 MPG. Same seller as Witt. If WSH will not move both, Yonkman is the better long-term fit: he is 6 years younger, carries real potential, and costs $1.10M less. If they will, pairing Witt and Yonkman gives Toronto a shutdown duo that matches any pair in the league on toughness and checking grades.

**McLaren (SJ, D, 28)** remains a valid target: 87 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 81 overall, 9 points in 14 games, $2.20M expiring. SJ at 15 points with 14 expiring and the league's highest payroll at $66.24M are the most motivated sellers. He is a step below Witt in grade (87 vs 91 TOUG) and costs $0.50M more, but carries one more year of usefulness if re-signed at a discount.

**Komisarek (MTL, D, 23)** is the surprise on this list. 80 TOUG, 87 CHKG, POTE 92, 13 points in 15 games at 30.1 minutes, $1.10M expiring. MTL at 15 points with 8 expiring deals. He is not quite an 80-toughness forward equivalent, but his checking and production from the blue line make him the best young defenseman available outside our own Eminger. The GM's February correction said Komisarek had three years left; the current read shows zero, meaning he is now expiring.

**Hejduk (COL, RW, 29)** solves the age gap and the scoring void without touching the toughness problem. 88 overall, 21 points in 17 games, $2.50M expiring. COL at 18 points with 8 expiring and $66.24M payroll cannot keep him and Kariya and Selanne all at once. He is the exact age (29) that Toronto's roster lacks between Gaborik (23) and Sundin (34).

**Hossa (OTT, RW, 26)** is the younger, cheaper version of the same role. 86 overall, 14 points in 14 games, $2.30M expiring. OTT at 11 points with only 4 expiring deals are less desperate, so acceptance is harder. He is the player who slots into the 26-33 void without aging out immediately.

**Caveat on prior notes:** Doan's toughness now reads 80, not 86 as recorded in October. Bell reads 80, not 88. Both are likely form-related drops on displayed grades, but they no longer clear the 80 bar with the same margin the October notes claimed. Kurka and Kovalchuk are superior on every axis to both.

## Trade construction

This phase turns the league scan's shortlist into packages with names, picks and payrolls on both sides, ready for the February window. At 11-3-0 we are buying; the only gap that no lineup card closes is toughness (zero players above 80), and the secondary gap is a shutdown D pair beyond Jackman. Every proposal below gives surplus — players the Coach is not using — and never touches the core the GM has locked.

**Kurka (CAR) is the primary target.** 88 TOUG, 90 CHKG, 12 points in 16 games, $0.60M expiring. Carolina at 16 points with 14 expiring contracts and $63.79M payroll is the most desperate seller in the league; if they do not move him now, he walks in July for nothing. We give Upshall ($1.50M, RW, 22, POTE 99, 4 years left, 8 GP) plus a third-rounder. Carolina gets a 22-year-old with elite potential and four years of control — exactly what a rebuilding club at 16 points needs — and Kurka's salary drops $0.90M on our books. Upshall is surplus: four RWs ahead of him are playing, and his CHKG 87 does not address our specific gap.

**Witt and Yonkman (WSH) as a pair solve the Coach's shutdown-D flag in one move.** Witt is 91 TOUG, 95 CHKG at 30; Yonkman is 91 TOUG, 93 CHKG, POTE 89 at 24. Both expiring, both at Washington who sit at 13 points. We give Eminger ($2.20M, D, 22, POTE 99, 4 years, 7 GP with 2 points) plus a second-rounder. Eminger's Coach clock expired with zero development; he is a chip now per the November 6 finding. Washington gets a defenseman with 99 potential and four years of term plus a pick for two men they are going to lose for free. Net payroll change is +$0.10M, trivial against $36.27M profit.

**Kovalchuk (ATL) is the biggest swing and the hardest ask.** 89 overall, 82 TOUG, 16 points in 15 games, $1.10M expiring at 22. He fills toughness, scoring and the 26-33 void simultaneously. We give Koltsov ($1.10M, speed 96, POTE 94, 0 GP, unlined — pure surplus) plus our first-rounder (25-28th at our record) and second-rounder. Atlanta at 12 points gets two first-and-second-round assets and a year of elite speed for a player they will lose at zero cost in July. Acceptance is the least certain of the three: Atlanta might want a POTE 99 attached, and I would not give Spezza to make this work. If they refuse without Spezza, we walk away and hold Kurka as the deadline target.

**If none land:** dress McCabe (86 CHKG), Tucker (83 CHKG, 88 TOUG), and Abid (80 TOUG) for the playoff run. That lifts the fourth-line toughness mean from 62 to roughly 70 and gives Jackman a checking partner without a single trade. The structural gap above 80 toughness remains, but a playoff pairing of Jackman and McCabe at 87 and 89 CHKG is serviceable for two rounds.

## Owed

**Task #2 — Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window.**

This task was closed on 2005-11-13 because Luongo is on the roster, the goalie situation is solved, and no trade window exists until his renewal. Nothing has changed since then that reopens it.

**Luongo** is at 95 overall (up 1 from the 94 recorded six days ago, within normal form variance), 7 GP, $1.60M, 1 year left. He is playing and healthy. The only future action is renewal at season's end when his contract expires.

**DiPietro** at NYI: 87 overall, 24 years old, 14 GP, $1.10M, 0 years left (expiring). He is getting work and his grade has held at 87. The original logic — target a high-90s-potential goalie from a non-contender — still applies in theory, but DiPietro's 87 base is below Luongo's 95 and there is no vacancy to fill. He remains a "nice to know" rather than an actionable target.

No re-opening until Luongo's renewal window, which is the summer of 2006.
