# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-16

Next game vs DET on Wednesday 16 November 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether our 23-and-under players are getting the games they've earned at 17 games in, and the answer is mostly yes at the top and no at the bottom, where three young forwards are accumulating garbage minutes that help nobody.

**Chlup** at 19 is the clearest "yes." 15 points in 17 games on 20.5 MPG on the second line. He's carrying a first-line workload and producing at 0.88 pts/g. Fully earned.

**Chistov** at 22 is 9 points in 17 games on 17.6 MPG, the second-line winger he's supposed to be. **Nash** at 21 is 9 points in 17 on 14.6 MPG, a solid third-liner. **Gaborik** at 23 is 8 points in 16 on 22.7 MPG, first-line minutes and reasonable output. **Klesla** at 23 is 6 points in 17 on 25.9 MPG, which is a massive load but he's our best D man and earning it. All four are fine.

**Alexeev** at 23 is the one who is not being treated right. He's at 0.60 pts/g — 6 points in 10 games on 11.4 MPG — which outproduces Nash (0.53) and Chistov (0.53) per game. He's on the third line when he plays, which is correct, but he's only playing 10 of 17. Meanwhile Gardener (0 points, 8 games, 3.8 MPG) and Upshall (3 points, 8 games, 5.6 MPG) are getting the fourth-line dressing slots. Alexeev should be in the lineup every night ahead of both of them. Reason class: development, but it's also winning hockey.

**Spezza** at 22 is the player I flagged in March and the situation has not improved. He's at 3.8 MPG with 2 points in 11 games — a rate of 0.18. POTE 99 means the scouting staff thinks he can be something, but at 22 and 3.8 minutes a night, he's not getting the chance to show it. My own rule from October says below 8 MPG for three straight games means scratch permanently. He's well below that. The choice is: give him a real third-line role and let him prove it, or stop dressing him and free the roster spot for Alexeev. Carrying him at 3.8 MPG helps nobody.

**Upshall** at 22 is 3 points in 8 games on 5.6 MPG. Same collapse pattern, same call: he's below 8 MPG and producing at 0.38, which is fourth-line at best. He and Spezza are both occupying dressing slots that Alexeev has earned on production.

**Gardener** at 20 has zero points in 8 games on 3.8 MPG. POTE 98, but he's 20 and showing nothing at the NHL level. He should be the first one out when we need a spot, which we do.

**Colaiacovo** at 22 is 1 point in 17 games on the third pair. Thin for a POTE 99 defenseman, but third-pair minutes don't generate much, and at 22 he still has time. No action needed now, just monitor.

**Eminger** at 22 is scratched, playing 7 games on 19.9 MPG when dressed, producing 0.29 pts/g on an expiring deal. I flagged him as a deadline target back in March and nothing has changed. The GM owns the trade conversation.

## Development trends

The question this phase answers: who is trending up or down between mid-October and now, and does that change who we dress or plan around. Six weeks of games is enough to separate a hot streak from a real step forward, and this window has both.

**Chlup** is the headline. 0.88 pts/g on 21.4 MPG at 19 years old across 17 games. His minutes have more than tripled from that first sample and his rate barely moved. The franchise-centre call from April is now season-proven. He stays where he is.

**Jackman** confirms the November reversal. 0.81 pts/g on 24.8 MPG in 17 games, with his load down from 41 MPG in the first sample to 25. He is producing while absorbing less. At $0.70M x 2 he is the best value on the roster and a keeper.

**Fischer** is at 0.80 pts/g on 21.8 MPG in 6 recent games. The GM was right to protect him. His rate is well above the 0.00 from the first sample because he was in a different role then. He is playing top-pair minutes and producing like it.

**Sundin** at 34 is putting up 0.75 pts/g on 23.3 MPG over 17 games. **Mogilny** at 36 is at 0.62 on 22.8. Both are holding. No age slide visible in this window.

**Roberts** at 39 shows the expected decline: 0.29 pts/g, minutes down from 18 to 13.7 in 8 games. Natural, not a surprise.

**Gaborik** returned from whatever kept him out and is at 0.50 pts/g on 22.7 MPG in 16 games. That is solid production from a top-six winger. He belongs in the mix.

**Colaiacovo** is the problem. 0.06 pts/g across 17 games on 13.1 MPG. One point in seventeen games from a 22-year-old defenceman getting regular shifts. He is not developing, he is stalling hard. The GM's development-rotation logic does not apply to a player getting real minutes and producing nothing.

**Eminger** at 0.29 pts/g on 19.9 MPG in 7 games is weak for a defenceman on $2.20M x 4. He is 22, so there is time, but the contract makes the deadline relevant. If his rate holds below 0.40 through January he becomes a trade candidate on trajectory grounds.

**Richards** is at 0.62 on flat 13 MPG. **Afinogenov** at 0.69 on 17.8. Both are below their career-best rates. The system-fit concern from last season persists. Neither is failing, but neither is growing either.

**Gardener** (0.00 pts/g, 2.0 MPG in 8 games), **Spacek** (0.40 on 3.6 MPG in 6), and **Upshall** (0.29 on 4.1 MPG in 8) are all in the collapse pattern. They are getting scraps and producing nothing. The systemic issue I flagged in October holds.

**Stahle** is the quiet positive. 0.25 pts/g on 13.1 MPG at 21, minutes doubled from the first sample. He is growing into a third-pair role.

For the defensive end-of-season assessment (item #1): Klesla at 0.38 pts/g expiring remains the top sell candidate. Jackman and Fischer are keepers. Colaiacovo's 0.06 in 17 means he is not a future top-pair defenceman and the GM needs to decide whether to keep dressing him or give those minutes to Hainsey or Safronov. Eminger's 0.29 is below what his salary demands.

## Morale watch

The room is lifting with the team's recent wins and needs no intervention before Detroit.

**Richards** is the one I've been watching. He bottomed at 73 in October on 11 MPG, and my note said the deficit would compound. It hasn't. He's climbed to 86 on 13.0 MPG in 17 games with 10 points, and the recent saves show steady +1s and +3s. Still under his expected band (he's a 90-calibre player on 13 minutes), but the trend is right. I'd raise his role if I could reshuffle without breaking Chlup's line, and I won't.

**Spacek** sits at 76, in the -2 band, but the GM scratched him deliberately for development on January 15th. That's his call and his morale cost to own. The +5 on the last save suggests a recent win helped.

**The depth four at 81** (Gardener 3.8 MPG, Upshall 5.6, Spezza 3.8, Brendl 3.9, Lundmark 2.5) are all getting depth minutes and carrying a -1. Spezza at 11 games and 3.8 MPG fits the pattern I flagged in October: young forward stalls under 8 minutes and doesn't bounce. But none of them is producing enough to justify displacing a top-six winger tonight.

**Roberts at 84** is 39 years old on 14.2 MPG with 2 points in 8 games, currently a healthy scratch. His morale is stable and not minutes-fixable at this stage of his career.

No changes before puck drop. The winning streak is doing the work.

## Role composition

**The lines are well-composed for their jobs, with one exception worth fixing tonight: Kaberle is scratched and DET at 8-5 is a quality opponent that triggers the GM's own maximize-quality framework.**

**L1** — Sundin, Mogilny, Gaborik up front with Jackman and Klesla behind. Scoring mean 92, checking mean 78, faceoffs carried by Sundin at 95. This is the best line on the roster and there is nothing to fix.

**L2** — Chlup wins the draws at 80, Safronov brings checking up to 90 on the back end, Afinogenov is the 96 scoring threat. The clutch mean of 66 is the one soft spot, but this is a second line that creates offence; the closing is L1's job. No change.

**L3** — Richards, Stahle and Alexeev up front with Colaiacovo and Nash behind. Nash at 82 checking is the enforcer presence this line needs, and scoring mean 82 means this line can score from every layer. No change.

**L4** — Faceoff mean 58, best 71. Gardener, Spezza and Upshall cannot win a draw against a competent centre. This is a structural gap I cannot fix from the bench: the only remaining faceoff man is Wallin at 88, and he's scratched. Against a good team's fourth line it won't matter; against their third it will.

**Penalty kill 2** — Checking mean 72, stamina mean 54. Spezza and Upshall bring speed (best 93) but not the physical game. If we take penalties tonight K2 will get pushed around. The fix is taking fewer penalties, not reassigning men.

**Kaberle and the D-pair slot** — He's scratched, and the GM's standing order says quality opponents mean go all out with the best veterans. DET at 8-5 qualifies. Kaberle's clutch at 91 and stamina at 89 are the best numbers on the blue line. Moving him into the third pair (replacing Colaiacovo) frees the top pair from the 33-34 MPG load I flagged in October and gives us a shutdown-calibre defender on the ice. This costs chemistry only if Colaiacovo has been playing well, and his role in the lineup has already been adjusted once this season for other D pairings, so the cost is low.

## Opponent matchup

The question is whether we adjust anything tonight against a Detroit team built to play ugly, or ride what we have.

**DET's identity:** Checking and faceoffs. Draper FACE 97 on draws, Maltby CHKG 91 and AGGR 95 on the wing, McCarty TOUG 92. They are old (Draper 34, Maltby 32, Housley 41) and grinding. Their PP at 6/69 (8.7%) is a non-threat — I do not need to restructure the PK.

**Lidstrom** at 90 OVR with ENDU 94 is still the real deal on their top pair. But his partner **Housley** is 41 with ENDU 69. That is the seam. **Gaborik** at SPEE 99 and SHPW 99 should be getting through him on any transition, and **Chlup** at SPEE 95 will too on line two.

**Their depth D is vulnerable:** Bunka 71, Janik 66, Brown 67. Our third pair (Stahle 76, Colaiacovo 76) is roughly even, but our speed forwards can exploit those Dmen on the forecheck.

**Their second line** is the one to worry about. **Whitney** at HERO 94 and SHPW 92 with ENDU 92 is a scorer hiding in a middle-six slot. Our D2 (Safronov 68, Hainsey 77) is thinner than D1, and that pairing gets matched against their second line by the auto-pairing. Safronov's ACCU 55 and PUCK 63 are below par for a second-pair defenseman. This is a structural issue I've flagged before, not a tonight problem.

**Faceoffs:** Draper 97 vs our Sundin 95 is a wash. Their top line will win more draws than we'd like on our L1, but it is close enough that skill wins the puck battle. No fix exists within our roster.

**No change tonight.** Our lines represent maximum quality, which is the standing order against a good opponent. Their style will make it ugly — expect 2-1 hockey, not 5-4. Our speed and talent advantage is real; the 58-for-32-against goal differential against their 39-for-36 makes that concrete.

**Luongo** starts at 95 OVR and morale 89. Check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming.

## Owed

**Standing job #1: defencemen review and sell list, updated for November 16.**

**Jackman** at 14 points in 17 games is 0.82 pts/g. My November 13 note flagged 0.88 over 16; a one-game dip to 0.82 means nothing. He is still a genuine breakout at $0.70M for two more years and firmly stays. The threshold I set (below 0.55 by January triggers a sell rethink) is nowhere close.

**Klesla** at 6 points in 17 games is 0.35 pts/g. Unchanged from last week, still below the 0.55 floor I said would close his sell window. At 87 OVR on an expiring deal this is still our top deadline candidate. A buyer sees the grade and the points-per-game on a 23-year-old; we see a declining rate behind a cheaper partner who plays 3.3 fewer minutes a night.

**Hainsey** has solidified himself in the rotation since I recommended his slot on November 6. 4 points in 11 games on 21.4 MPG at 77 OVR is a reasonable third-pair return. Not a sell (6 years left at $1.40M), not a trade target. Keep developing him.

**Stahle** and **Colaiacovo** are splitting the fourth pair at 12.6 MPG each. Stahle edges Colaiacovo on points (4 in 17 versus 1 in 17) and costs less ($0.97M x 2 versus $1.40M x 4). Colaiacovo at 0.06 pts/g is producing nothing. He stays as depth for now but is behind Stahle on the depth chart.

**McCabe** has not played a single game. $3.00M for three more years at 84 OVR with 0 games dressed is the clearest deadweight on the blue line. My May note has him at a 0.48 rate over the last 58 games before this season. He goes nowhere unless someone absorbs the salary, but he is the name at season's end.

**Eminger** at 2 points in 7 games, $2.20M x 4, 82 OVR. Hard to move at that cap hit with that rate. Not dressed. He stays on the "try to trade" list but the window has been hard since I corrected the expiring error in May.

**Fischer** and **Kaberle** are the GM's keepers. Not dressed for development rotation reasons, not problems.

What has changed since November 13: almost nothing. One game was played; Jackman ticked from 0.88 to 0.82, Klesla unchanged. The sell list is the same three names in the same order: Klesla first (expiring, sell now), McCabe second (deadweight, salary blocks him), Eminger third (same problem, worse price).

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-13
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-13

Toronto 10-3-0, 26 pts after 16 games.

## Role coverage

The toughness void is Toronto's only structural gap that no lineup card can fix, and the checking gap is one the Coach can close tonight by using four men already on the roster.

**Checking.** Six players carry 80+ checking, but only Jackman (87, 24 games) is actually lined. Roberts 86, McCabe 86, Tucker 83 and Fischer 82 are all sitting unused. The Coach's own November 9 report recommends Roberts onto K2 and McCabe onto D3, which would instantly put three or four 80+ checkers into the lineup. This is the single largest internal fix available and it costs nothing but a scratch.

**Toughness.** Zero players at 80+. The best we carry is Jackman at 75, then Roberts and McCabe at 73. No rotation, no shift-length change, no creative deployment produces an 80+ toughness player from this roster. This is a trade target, full stop. The February window remains the right timeframe. Bell (88 TOUG), Heatley (82), Bertuzzi (89), Doan (86) and McLaren (89) are all still valid targets. The contradiction from February is now settled: zero at 80+ is correct.

**Faceoffs.** Only Sundin (90) is both 80+ and lined. Wallin sits at 83 with no assignment. Chlup at 75 is the next option. Lining Wallin at a bottom-six centre slot would give us two 80+ draw-takers without any trade.

**Scoring and speed.** Covered in depth. Mogilny 94 (36 years old), Sundin 92 (34), Gaborik 92 (23), Afinogenov 90 (26). The age curve means Mogilny and Sundin are two seasons from decline, but Gaborik and Afinogenov are entering their primes. Roberts 88 and Abid 86 sit unlined, so even the depth is strong.

**Goalies.** Luongo (94/94 glove-stick, 1.48 GAA, 0.951 SV) is elite and carries one year left. Tellqvist (80/80, 1.48 GAA, 0.950 SV in 6 games) is a capable backup with six years of control. Ouellet is the third man at 24. Coverage is fine; the renewal question on Luongo is the one that matters.

## Trajectory

Is this club aging into a cliff? No. The age curve is young: 13 players at 23 or under, 16 in the prime 24-29 band, only 5 players above 30. The risk is not age, it is two mega-contracts that lock money to declining production and a July 2006 renewal window that must go right.

**Gaborik** is the single largest financial problem. $11.90M/year for five more years at 0.53 pts/g (8 points in 15 games). That is 13% of the payroll on a player the Coach sat for a month. The contract cannot be renegotiated mid-term, so the only lever is trade, and the memory notes his value drops if he is still undressed by January. He is 23 with POTE 90, so there is still a buyer, but the window is closing.

**Sundin** at 34, $8.40M, 4 years left, is the second locked cost. He will be 38 when the deal ends in July 2009. At 11 points in 16 games (0.69 pts/g) he is still contributing, but the contract outlives the production. Combined with Gaborik, these two men eat $20.30M/year — 23% of payroll — for players whose ceilings are set.

**Chlup** at 19, 15 points in 16 games (0.94 pts/g), POTE 95, on a $2.34M rookie deal expiring in 1 year, is the most important contract on the roster. He must be locked on 5-6 years at the July 2006 window. Same for **Luongo** (26, POTE 97, $1.60M, 1 year left). Both are franchise players on below-market deals that expire simultaneously. The memory already flags them for the same renewal week; this remains the plan.

**The July 2009 cluster:** 11 players worth $37.40M expire together in 2009 (Sundin, Richards, Chistov, Nash, Kaberle, Eminger, Colaiacovo, Alexeev, Upshall, Wallin, Abid). That is the manual's warning about clustered renewals. The contracts cannot be broken early, but the GM should plan which of those players get a 6-year extension first (Nash, Chistov, Eminger, Colaiacovo, all under 25 with POTE 95+) versus which get 2-year deals that spread the cliff (Sundin at 38, Wallin, Upshall). This is a 2008-09 planning problem, not an immediate action, but it should be on the calendar.

**The scoring void** persists. Mogilny (36), Sundin (34), and Roberts (39) carry 22 combined points and walk or decline within two summers. Chlup (15 pts), Afinogenov (11 pts), and Richards (9 pts) are the under-30 producers, but the gap to the veterans' historical output is structural. The Iginla target remains the only fix that does not require a 19-year-old to carry the top line.

**Money:** Payroll is $89.94M against $61.67M revenue, but profit is $35.56M — so TV, prestige, and attendance fill the gap comfortably. There is room to absorb salary in a trade. The $112 ticket price is already high; revenue headroom comes from the other streams.

**Draft capital:** First, second, and third-round picks (all from TOR). That is better than the January 2005 position of nothing better than a fourth. A first-rounder plus a package player can fund a real February target.

## Calendar

**Are we buyers or sellers at the March deadline, and what happens to our nine expiring contracts this summer?** We are 10-3-0, 26 points, 2nd in a 15-team East with eight playoff spots. That settles it: we buy at the deadline and we re-sign the young ones in summer. The deadline is 126 days away — negotiations should not open before late February per the GM's January standing order.

**We are buyers.** The manual says a contending team buys for need and prefers young players with potential over pure rentals. We need toughness on the back end and on the wing (the Coach's K2 and D3 gaps), and we now own all five rounds of our own 2006 draft picks, which reverses the January 2005 situation where we owned nothing better than a fourth. Draft capital exists again.

**Tucker** is the lead chip on our side. 30, $1.30M, expiring, the GM already confirmed him as trade-eligible in March 2005. He is the piece that funds a deadline acquisition.

**Bertuzzi** (VAN, RW, 30, 91 overall / 94 base, $2.60M expiring) remains our primary target — he clears 80 on both toughness and checking while producing at 1.25 pts/g. His package was scoped as Tucker plus R2, and we now own that R2. The caveat: he is a rental at 30 on an expiring deal, which is exactly the profile the manual warns against when contending. The GM needs to decide whether the playoff push justifies the rental or whether he would rather keep the R2 and find a younger version.

**Mogilny** is 36, $5.50M, 89 overall, 9 points in 16 games. We do not intend to re-sign him at that salary at his age. He clears the over-80 expiring mechanic, which means he can be traded for a draft pick to any contender. At 0.56 pts/g he is useful for a playoff run but not irreplaceable. I recommend trading him at the deadline for a pick rather than watching him walk in July for nothing.

**The summer renewals break into three groups:**

**Lock up (star deals, 5–6 years):** Chlup at 19 with 0.85 pts/g on 21.3 MPG is our future first-line centre; $2.34M is already his entry rate and will only go up. Luongo at 26 is our number-one goalie and the manual warns specifically about forgetting goalies at renewal.

**Renew cheap (2–3 years):** Klesla at 23 logs 25.9 MPG on 6 points in 16 games for $0.90M — that is a starter's minutes at a fourth-liner's price. Spezza at 22 carries POTE 99 and a $1.00M deal, but at 4.0 MPG and 0.25 pts/g his development has stalled under the Coach. Renew him cheaply on a two-year deal only if the Coach commits to real minutes next season; otherwise he becomes a summer trade candidate.

**Let go:** Mogilny (trade at deadline, see above). Koltsov at 75 overall / 68 base, 24, $1.10M — a base of 68 at 24 says the ceiling is close. Ouellet at 81 overall / 24 years old is serviceable backup but we should find a younger option or promote from within. St. Jacques at 25, $0.80M, is depth we can replace via the draft now that we own all five rounds.

**On the Luongo monitoring task (task #2, requested 2005-01-19):** This is delivered. Luongo is on our roster at 26, 91 base, $1.60M with one year left. The goalie trade window from the 2004-05 season is closed; he was acquired and is our starter. No further monitoring needed.

## League scan

The February window is 15 weeks away and the toughness gap (zero players at 80+) means the only structural hole on this roster requires an acquisition. The query above returns every player with TOUG 80+ on a club with five or more expiring deals; below I rank them by fit, age, and how motivated their club is.

**Bertuzzi** is the primary target. 1.60 points per game (24 in 15), 91 overall, TOUG 83, CHKG 87, SPEE 89, on $2.60M expiring. He solves the toughness void and the depth-scoring problem in one move. VAN sits at 5-5-1 with 13 expiring contracts and $46.36M payroll, the second-lowest in the league. They must sell. At 30 his ceiling is set but his floor is elite.

**Kovalchuk** carries the highest overall on the market at 92, with SPEE 99 and TOUG 85. He is 22 with POTE 86 and $1.10M expiring. ATL are 5-7-2 at 12 points with 6 expiring deals. He and Heatley cannot both be re-signed; one moves. If ATL retains Heatley, Kovalchuk is the prize.

**Heatley** is the other side of the ATL binary. 91 overall, 91 base, SPEE 98, TOUG 82, CHKG 88, POTE 86, 24 years old, $1.10M expiring. 0.64 pts/g in 14 games is below last season's pace, but the grades say he is the more mature player. Either ATL piece solves the toughness gap (both carry 82+).

**Jovanovski** is the best defenseman available. 86 overall, 89 base, TOUG 91, CHKG 92. He is 29 on $2.30M with one year left. VAN's 13 expiring contracts and desperate position make him movable. Package him with Bertuzzi and one trade solves the back end and the front end toughness simultaneously.

**McLaren** at 81 overall, TOUG 87, CHKG 91, 28 years old, $2.20M expiring. SJ are 4-5-3 with 14 expiring deals and $66.24M payroll, the most motivated seller in the league. Lower ceiling than Jovanovski but same age bracket and the same desperation pressure.

**Bell** is the cheap option. 82 overall, 80 base, TOUG 84, CHKG 82, 25 years old, $0.90M with one year left. CHI are 2-8-4 with 8 expiring. He is a third-line forward who brings toughness without spending a first-rounder. The price is a second-round pick plus a depth piece.

**Sopel** at 78 overall but 1.00 points per game as a defenseman (15 in 15) is the best value on the sheet. TOUG 80, 28, $0.60M, one year left, same VAN desperation. He is a depth-pairing D who produces at a top-pairing rate and costs almost nothing.

**Radulov** rounds out the list at 23, $0.60M expiring, TOUG 80, CHKG 80. CHI at 2-8-4 must clear him. He is a fourth-liner who brings the one attribute we lack. Cheap and young enough to develop.

**Not targets.** Fleury is 37 on $6.99M for five more years. Phillips is 33 with no games played. Thornton is 34. Doan's 79 overall with 87 base says form is dragging him; at the same age as Bertuzzi he produces 0.63 vs 1.60 pts/g for more money.

## Trade construction

Three proposals ranked by probability of acceptance and fit, all aimed at the February window per the GM's standing order that negotiations open in late February. The toughness gap (zero at 80+) is the only structural hole the coverage phase confirmed no lineup card can close, so every package targets it directly.

**Bell from Chicago** is the most likely landing. CHI are 2-8-4 with 8 expiring deals and $23.35M profit — the league's clearest seller. Bell at 25, TOUG 84, 82 overall, $0.90M expiring is exactly the kind of replaceable mid-tier piece a rebuilding team dumps. Tucker gives them a 30-year-old with CHKG 92 and TOUG 88 for their fourth line while they develop younger wingers, and an R2 is a fair price for a third-line winger who cannot re-sign. The cost to us is a player sitting at 0 GP and a pick we can replace at the draft.

**Heatley from Atlanta** is the highest-ceiling move. ATL at 5-7-2 cannot re-sign both him and Kovalchuk on expiring deals. Heatley at 24 with TOUG 82, CHKG 88, 91 overall and $1.10M solves the toughness gap and the scoring bridge in one body. The price is steep: Spezza (POTE 99, 4.0 MPG, 0.25 pts/g) and Koltsov (POTE 94, 0 GP) plus our first-rounder. But neither Spezza nor Koltsov has a development path in Toronto's lineup, and ATL's rebuild is built on exactly those POTE 94+ assets. ATL's $19.72M profit absorbs the $1.00M net salary increase without strain.

**Bertuzzi + Jovanovski from Vancouver** is the biggest swing — it closes toughness and the defense simultaneously. VAN at 5-5-1 with 13 expiring contracts should be thinking about return, but at .500 they may not deal in February. Eminger is the centerpiece the GM must approve; his Coach-imposed development clock has effectively expired (7 GP, 2 points, limited role) and the November 6 note flags him as a confirmed chip, but the GM's February 19 order to stop proposing Eminger trades was never explicitly reversed. This is the one proposal that requires the GM to override his own standing order.



**If none land by the deadline:** The toughness gap stays at zero and the club plays into the spring without it. The checking gap is closable internally tonight — Roberts (86 CHKG), McCabe (86), Fischer (82) and Jackman (87) just need to be lined, which is the Coach's own November 9 recommendation. Wallin at FACE 83 should slot into a bottom-six centre assignment. The R1 pick is banked for the June draft, where scouting upgrades may surface a tough winger in the mid-rounds. The season is not lost without an 80+ toughness player; Mogilny (94 ACCU), Sundin (92 overall), Chlup (15 points in 16 games) and Afinogenov (11 points) give this team enough skill to win a playoff round without physical dominance.

## Owed

**#2 — Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window:** Task fulfilled. Luongo was acquired in February 2005 and is on our roster. The monitoring question the GM asked in January (find a high-90s goalie from a non-contender) is closed; he is here at 97 overall, $1.60M, and performing.

**Luongo:** 5-1-0 in 6 starts, 366 minutes, 1.48 GAA, 95.1 save percentage. Playing at 97 overall on a one-year deal. The only open question is his renewal at season's end, which per game mechanics cannot be touched until the contract expires. No action possible or needed right now.

**DiPietro:** 86 overall at 24, 12 GP, $1.10M, contract expires this season. NYI are 7-6-1-1 (17 points in 15). At .500 they are not yet a seller, so no February window exists for him. If NYI collapse toward the bottom third, he becomes a February rental target, but as of today there is nothing to chase.

Nothing has changed since the March 2005 standing order closed goalie monitoring. Luongo is playing behind schedule (6 GP in 16 team games, suggesting Belfour or another carried significant load last year), but at this pace and these numbers, the position is secure. No action required.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-13
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-13

Next game at BUF on Tuesday 15 November 2005.

## Development opportunity

Who's getting the minutes they've earned, and who's not, at 16 games in.

**Chlup** is the clearest answer in the other direction: 15 points in 16 games at 20.5 MPG on the second line. He's 19 and carrying first-line load with second-line pay. He's earning more than we're giving him.

**Spacek** is the case that needs a decision. 3 points in 6 games is 0.50 per game — that beats Gardener's 0.00 in 7 and matches Upshall's 0.43 in 7. He's scratched while both of those dress. His morale is 76, the lowest on the roster, which costs him two points off every grade this week. The GM's January order was to give young players space; Spacek is a young player getting none of it while two others below his rate take his spot.

**Gardener** at 0 points in 7 games on 3.9 MPG is not earning a dressed slot. POTE 98 is a scouting number, not a contribution. He's the youngest of the "dressed but invisible" group and the one where a permanent scratch is least painful.

**Spezza** at 0.20 on 3.9 MPG in 10 games is year two of the same collapse. Last season I said camp was the only lever — camp came and went, and here he is again. At 22 this is no longer a development question. He's a depth forward who cannot hold 8 minutes and produce.

**Alexeev** at 4 points in 9 games, 0.44 per game, dressed on the third line when he plays. His rate-to-role mismatch from last spring is partially resolved: he's getting dressed and producing when in. That's the right direction.

**Colaiacovo** has 0 points in 16 games at 12.7 MPG on the third defensive pair. That's thin for a 22-year-old with POTE 99, but he's not the problem line — Klesla is carrying 25.9 MPG on the first pair and Jackman is on the other side. His lack of offense is a symptom of the third-pair role, not a reason to pull him.

**No change** for Gaborik (0.53 on the first line at 22.4), Klesla (0.38 at 25.9 on the top pair), Chistov (0.56 on the second line at 17.4), Nash (0.50 on the third line at 14.8), or Stahle (0.25 at 12.7 on the third pair). All earning their minutes at their current tier.

## Development trends

The trend question matters now because we are 16 games in and the pattern from last season — young forwards given minutes then starved — is already repeating. I need the GM to see who is actually growing and who is being buried before January makes it permanent.

**Chlup** at 19 is 0.93 pts/g on 21.5 MPG across 16 games. This is the number I have been asking the GM to trust since April, and every week strengthens it. He belongs at first-line centre. My two prior recommendations to move him there were not taken.

**Fischer** at 25 is 0.80 pts/g on 21.8 MPG over just 6 games. That is hot, but the sample is tiny. He was scratched early and is coming back firing. No action needed; let the next ten games tell us if it is real or a heater.

**Stahle** at 21 went from 6.0 to 13.1 MPG and is putting up 0.27 pts/g in 16 games. He is getting minutes and repaying them. This is a young defenceman whose trajectory is up without anyone forcing it. Let it ride.

**Jackman** at 24 is 0.87 pts/g on 24.7 MPG across 16 games. His minutes came down from 42 to 24.8, and his production held at nearly 0.90. The load-concentration issue I flagged in October is resolving, and the result is that he still produces. Good outcome, no change needed.

**Klesla** mirrors Jackman: minutes down from 42 to 24.8, 0.40 pts/g. Both top-pair guys are back at sane workloads.

**Sundin** at 34 is 0.73 pts/g on 23.1 MPG over 16 games. That is not sustainable, and he will slow. Start planning around it for the second half: give Richards or Chlup the centre-ice minutes on back-to-backs so Sundin is fresh for the playoff stretch.

**Roberts** at 39 is 0.29 pts/g on 13.7 MPG over 8 games. His minutes are being managed and his production is modest. No surprise, but this confirms he cannot carry a top-six role in the second half.

**Gardener** at 20 is zero points in 7 games on 1.8 MPG. **Spacek** at 20 is 0.40 on 3.6 MPG. **Upshall** at 22 is 0.33 on 4.3 MPG. **Spezza** at 22 is 0.20 on 3.9 MPG. All four are below the 8 MPG floor from the pattern I identified in October, and none is producing. This is the same collapse that ate their minutes last year. The GM needs to either give them a real role or stop dressing them so the roster spots go to guys who will play hard.

**Alexeev** at 23 is finally getting ice time (12.2 MPG over 9 games) but producing only 0.25 pts/g, down from his 0.55-0.67 rate last season. The promotion is not working so far. Give him ten more games to settle; if he is still below 0.40 by early December, he is a third-liner at best.

**Colaiacovo** at 22 has zero points in 16 games on 13.1 MPG. No production at all from a defenceman getting regular minutes. He is a liability on the blue line right now.

**Gaborik** at 23 is 0.53 pts/g on 22.4 MPG over 15 games. Whatever kept him out of the first save is resolved and he is contributing. No concern.

No player's card grade moved in this window, which means production and minutes are the only signals available.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy and recovering. Every player in the active lineup sits at 96 morale and trending up, which means the recent wins are doing the work. One player needs watching but not intervention yet.

**Richards** is at 86 morale on 13.2 minutes a night across 16 games. Based on his calibre and role, he should be closer to 17. His morale dropped as low as 73 during the October slump and has been climbing steadily since (the brief shows +5 on the most recent readings). He is healing through wins rather than through a minutes increase. At 86 he is costing himself one point off every grade, which is tolerable. If the climb stalls before the end of November I will ask for a line promotion.

**Spacek** is the lowest at 76 on 5.8 MPG and 6 games. Three points in six games is real production for a 20-year-old on scratch minutes. He is trending up (+5). By the GM's own rule, if the scoresheet says he is contributing, he earns his role. The fix is dressing him more, not a line change from the bench. That is a roster decision, not a morale intervention.

**The scratched youth** — Gardener, Spezza, Brendl, Lundmark — all sit at 81 and rising. That is acceptable for players in their situation. None of them are low enough to be hurting the room.

**No change.** The core rotation at 96 with rising morale means the room is right. Richards is self-correcting with the team winning. Spacek needs the GM's attention on dress/no-dress, not a lines move.

## Role composition

Are the lines built right for their jobs, and can the roster fill the roles we need? Mostly yes on fit; no on depth.

**L1** — Sundin, Mogilny, Jackman, Gaborik, Klesla. Checking mean 78, scoring mean 92. This is an offense line with Jackman as the one safety net at 92 checking. That's by design against quality opponents per the January standing order, and it works. No change.

**L2** — Chlup, Hainsey, Afinogenov, Safronov, Chistov. Checking 72, toughness 63. A young line being asked to play second-minute hockey with no standout checker above Safronov's 90 best. The GM's philosophy is production over grades for kids, and Chlup is at 0.85 pts/g, so I leave them. They are not a checking unit and should not be asked to be one.

**L3** — Stahle, Colaiacovo, Richards, Alexeev, Nash. Nash at 82 checking is the reason this line works defensively. Richards at 93 playmaking is the offensive anchor. The unit is reasonably balanced. No change.

**L4** — Gardener, Spezza, Upshall. Checking 70, toughness 62, only three forwards. This line cannot forecheck or protect anyone. It is not a composition fix — those three are the best available at that tier. This is a roster gap.

**Richards** sits at morale 78 (noted October 20) and is on L3. If his minutes have not come up since, his grades are costing us two points across the board every night. The fix is giving him L2 centre duty or raising his minutes within L3, not moving someone else off.

**Faceoffs:** Sundin 95 is the only elite draw man dressed. Wallin at 88 is scratched. Against a team with a strong centre, that is a problem we can solve by dressing him.

**Toughness across the roster:** Nobody above 78. That is not a lineup arrangement problem; it is a roster-wide absence and will not be fixed by shuffling.

## Opponent matchup

Can we beat this version of Buffalo with our current lines, or do we need a special look? The answer is no change to any forward line or D pair, because the auto-pairing already gives us the ideal alignment and their weaknesses are structural rather than something a matchup trick fixes.

**Biron** is the game. He reads 83 with morale 74, which costs him a point off every grade on top of what's already there. Their PP is 7-for-70 (10.0%), meaning we will spend almost no time short-handed against a unit that cannot convert. Their fourth line at 69/70/68 OVR is the weakest in the league on this sheet. We should simply play our game and score on a goalie who is not confident.

**Zhitnik and Bouchard** are their only pair above 77, and Laukkanen is out (returns the 16th), so their third pair is Bombardir at 69 and Wallin at 66. Our first line (Sundin 92, Gaborik 99, Mogilny 89) draws that Zhitnik/Bouchard pair via auto-pairing, which is the softest top pair we could ask for. Our first D pair (Jackman 86, Klesla 87) draws their best forwards (Drury 81, Briere 76, Nolan 82). The alignment already has our best people against their best and our offence against their softest D.

**Faceoffs go our way on all three top centres.** Sundin at 95 wins against Briere's 82. Chlup at 80 wins against Cullen's 67. Richards at 78 wins against Gaustad's 65. The faceoff gap that has plagued us against stronger centres is invisible against this roster.

**The only action item:** start Luongo (97 versus 83), but check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming per the January 19 standing order.

## Owed

The standing job: D corps assessment after 16 games, updated sell list.

**Jackman** at 0.88 pts/g over 16 games is no longer a hot streak. His career rate is 0.48, and the October window I flagged (1.00 after 4) has now held for a meaningful sample. At 24, $0.70M x 2, this is his game now. I previously said sell while hot. That call is reversed: keep him, this is a genuine breakout.

**Klesla** is the new top sell candidate. 87 OVR on an expiring deal with 0.38 pts/g in 16 games. His grade is at its peak while his production is below what we'd expect from a top-pair defenceman. Jackman has passed him at half the salary. Sell Klesla while a buyer sees 87 and one year left — this is the window.

**McCabe** is not dressed. Zero games, $3.00M x 3, 30 years old. Pure salary dump. This hasn't changed since May, but the evidence is now absolute: he can't be fit in.

**Fischer** and **Kaberle** are both in the development rotation and not dressed, which is the GM's call. Both keepers per January orders, no trade proposals.

**Eminger** at 2 points in 7 games on $2.20M x 4 is the contract nobody takes. At 22 with 4 years locked, the problem persists but there's no window. Carry or eat.

**Hainsey** has locked down the second pair: 10 games, 21.5 MPG, 4 points, $1.40M x 6. A keeper.

What changed: Klesla moves to the top of the sell list, Jackman comes off it.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-09
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-09

Toronto 9-3-0, 22 pts after 14 games.

## Role coverage

The only gap Toronto cannot fix by adjusting a lineup is toughness: zero players at 80+ TOUG on a 34-man roster, best is Jackman at 75. Everything else is a deployment problem.

**Roberts** is the single player who solves two problems at once if the coach puts him in the lineup. 86 CHKG, 90 clutch, 98 durability, 39 years old. The Coach already flagged him for K2 over Klesla, and the numbers support it: Klesla is at 25.7 MPG qualifying as a top-pair workload, while Roberts sits unlined with the best checking grade among forwards.

**McCabe** (86 CHKG, 94 ENDU) and **Tucker** (83 CHKG, 70 TOUG) are also rostered and unlined. Dressing either adds a third 80+ checker tonight without a trade. The checking role goes from 1 active (Jackman 87) to 4 active if the coach uses the bench.

**Wallin** at 83 FACE is the only faceoff option outside Sundin's 90, and he is not lined. Dressing him for draws on the third or fourth line gives the club two 80+ centres in a series where faceoff dominance matters. Without him, Chlup at 75 and Richards at 70 are the next options, both below 80.

**The toughness gap has no internal fix.** Jackman's 75 is the ceiling. McCabe at 73, Roberts at 73, Tucker at 70. The GM's standing order from March 19 ("only trading chips left are Tucker and the 4th round pick") was for that deadline; it is now November and new targets are live. Heatley at 82 TOUG and 91 base remains the primary package, and Bell at 88 TOUG and 86 CHKG closes toughness and checking together if ATL or CHI will deal.

**Age note:** The checking depth is healthy for two years. Jackman 24, McCabe 30 (this is the one to worry about by 2007), Roberts 39 (replaceable next year). The toughness ceiling of 75 does not improve with time; it requires an external acquisition regardless of when we make it.

## Trajectory

The question: is this roster aging into a cliff, and can the money carry the next three seasons? It's young enough that age isn't the cliff; scoring is.

**The age shape is healthy.** 29 of 34 players are 29 or under. Only three are over 33 (Sundin 34, Mogilny 36, Roberts 39). That's three veterans, well inside the manual's 5-7 window. The club isn't old. The problem is what the old players are doing versus what's ready to replace them.

**The scoring cliff is structural.** Mogilny (36, $5.50M, 8 pts in 14 games, 1 year left), Sundin (34, $8.40M, 9 pts in 14, 4 years left), and Roberts (39, $4.90M, 2 pts in 8, 2 years left) together carry $18.80M and the bulk of the team's production. Mogilny walks in July. Nobody under 30 has proven 0.60+ pts/g at the NHL level. Chlup is the exception at 12 points in 14 games on 19 years old, but he cannot be asked to carry a top line alone.

**Sundin's deal ages badly.** $8.40M for 4 more years means he'll be 38 with 3 seasons left on the contract. By year 3, at 37, his 9 points in 14 games will likely be 5 or 6 in whatever becomes a fourth-line role. That's $25.20M over four years for a declining top-six centre whose body won't hold.

**Gaborik is the worst single contract.** $11.90M for 5 years at age 23, producing 6 points in 13 games (0.46 pts/g). He was a healthy scratch three weeks ago. At this rate, no team takes the salary away from a team with two Stanley Cups and prestige 1112. If he doesn't climb above 0.65 by late January, his February trade value will be "dump with picks attached," not "acquire a POTE 90 winger."

**July 2006 is the renewal that matters.** Nine contracts worth $15.44M expire, but four define the future: Chlup (19, POTE 95, 12 pts in 14 games, $2.34M), Luongo (26, POTE 97, $1.60M), Klesla (23, POTE 97, 5 pts in 14, $0.90M), and Spezza (22, POTE 99, $1.00M). All four are at bargain salaries. They must be locked on 5-6 years the same week Mogilny becomes a free agent. Miss Chlup or Luongo and the franchise loses its foundation for the cheapest it will ever be.

**July 2009 is the structural warning.** Eleven players worth $37.40M all expire that summer: Richards, Nash, Chistov, Kaberle, Eminger, Alexeev, Upshall, Colaiacovo, Wallin, Abid, plus Sundin's final year. That is the manual's warning made real — the entire core comes up at once. It's four seasons away and not yet actionable, but the renewal strategy this July should stagger those deals across different terms to avoid a repeat.

**Money is not the constraint.** Profit is $37.75M on payroll of $89.94M with revenue of $59.86M. The profit figure suggests TV and prestige income far exceed the revenue number shown here. Iginla's $6.50M salary (if he's available in July 2006) is absorbable without moving anyone else.

**Draft capital is real now.** TOR owns their own 1st, 2nd, and 3rd rounders for 2006. The January 2005 note about owning nothing better than a 4th applied to that draft cycle; the 2006 picks are fresh. The R1 is the Iginla ammunition and competes with nothing else that requires a first-rounder at present.

The three moves that protect the next three seasons: lock Chlup and Luongo in July 2006, pursue Iginla with the R1 that same summer to fill the Mogilny void, and begin staggering the July 2009 cluster now by structuring any new deals with split terms.

## Calendar

The trade deadline is 130 days away on March 19, 2006, and the summer renewal window follows the season. The question this phase answers: given that Toronto sits 2nd in the East at 9-3-0 with 22 points in 14 games, do we buy, sell, or hold, and what happens to each of our nine expiring players?

**We are buyers.** 2nd place, eight teams make the East playoffs, and we have 68 games left. The manual is clear: buy for need at the deadline, prefer young players with potential over pure rentals. Our needs are a top-six winger with toughness and a top-4 defenceman. Both targets exist on sellers and our draft capital is intact.

The January 2005 note that we owned "no picks beyond a fourth-rounder" is dead. Toronto holds all five rounds of the 2006 draft — R1 through R5, our own. That unblocks the Heatley package (Spezza + Koltsov + R1) and the Brad Stuart package (Abid + R2) that were previously infeasible.

**Deadline plan (March 19):** Open negotiations late February per the GM's standing order. Primary target: Heatley (ATL, 91 base, 82 TOUG, 24, $1.10M expiring) — package Spezza + Koltsov + R1. Secondary: Bertuzzi (VAN, 94 base, 83 TOUG, 87 CHKG, 30, 1.25 pts/g) — package Tucker + R2. Blue-line: Brad Stuart (SJ, 87 base, 89 CHKG, POTE 91, 25, $1.80M) — package Abid + R2. All three are on desperate sellers. Acceptance uncertain on all.

**Chips available:** Tucker ($1.30M, confirmed chip), Spezza ($1.00M, 2 pts in 8 GP at 4.0 MPG — Coach's clock is dead), and Mogilny via the over-80 mechanic (base 91, expiring, will not re-sign at 36). That last one means Mogilny alone fetches a draft pick without sending anything else.

**Mogilny** (RW, 36, $5.50M): 8 points in 14 games at 21.7 MPG. The production holds for now but the contract does not survive a year-one decline at 37. Trade him at deadline — any contender on a playoff run absorbs $5.50M for 20 games and his 91 base qualifies for the over-80 pick mechanic. If no deal materializes, release in July. Saving $5.50M against a 36-year-old is the clearest summer money on the sheet.

**Luongo** (G, 26, $1.60M): Renew, 5 years. 90 base, GM confirmed him as the starter. $1.60M for a 26-year-old number-one is the cheapest top asset on the roster. Lock him now.

**Chlup** (C, 19, $2.34M): Renew, 4 years. 12 points in 14 games (0.86 pts/g) at 20.2 MPG. That's franchise-centre production from a teenager. The salary will climb when renewed but a 4-year deal at age 19 delays the climb by two years versus a 6.

**Klesla** (D, 23, $0.90M): Renew, 2 years. 25.6 MPG on the top pair shows the Coach trusts him. Five points in 14 is thin but he's a defensive-pairing defenceman. Cheap and young.

**Koltsov** (LW, 24, $1.10M): Include in a deal if Heatley or similar lands; otherwise renew 2 years. At 24 with potential and a low cap hit he's flexible.

**Spezza** (C, 22, $1.00M): Decision point before deadline. 2 points in 8 GP at 4.0 MPG. POTE 99 at $1.00M is absurd value only if he plays. If the Coach gives him 14+ MPG by late February, renew 3 years. If he's still at 4 MPG in February, trade him as part of the Heatley or similar package — his potential is the asset another club will pay for.

**Ouellet** (G, 24, $0.90M): Trade or release. We have Luongo and Tellqvist. A third 24-year-old goalie at $0.90M has no role here. Try the over-80 mechanic first; if his overall sits below 80, release.

**St. Jacques** (D, 25, $0.80M): Include as filler if a package demands it, otherwise renew at the same price. At $0.80M he costs nothing.

**Tucker** (LW, 30, $1.30M): Trade at deadline. He's the confirmed chip from last March and the primary funding piece in the Bertuzzi package.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: who across the league solves Toronto's zero-toughness gap, and which of them will actually move before February? Three clubs — VAN, PHX, SJ — are structurally forced sellers with the league's deepest expiring classes. The answer is Bertuzzi, Komisarek, and Doan at the top of a list of eight names that clear 84 TOUG while producing at or above 0.50 pts/g.

**Bertuzzi** at 93 overall, TOUG 85, CHKG 89, 21 points in 14 games on 24.9 MPG, $2.60M expiring. VAN carry the league's lowest payroll at $46.36M with 13 expiring deals and a 4-5-1 record. They are in full teardown mode; any package of picks plus a young player beats losing him in July for nothing. He is 30, so this is a two-year window of elite production, not a long-term build piece, but he fills the gap tonight and scores at a 1.50 rate that matches Sundin.

**Komisarek** at 84 overall, CHKG 91, TOUG 84, POTE 90, 12 points in 13 games on 29.5 MPG, $1.10M expiring, age 23. MTL at 3-6-3 with 8 expiring and $21.18M profit. He is the best value on the board: a 23-year-old blueliner with 91 checking and elite production who costs a second-rounder at worst. If Eminger and Colaiacovo are both chips (Coach flagged Colaiacovo; Eminger's development clock expired at 0 GP), a package of Colaiacovo plus a second-rounder gets a real shot.

**Doan** at 85 overall, TOUG 86, CHKG 91, 10 points in 14 games on 20.3 MPG, $2.40M expiring, age 28. PHX at 3-10-0 with 9 expiring and a 2-10 October start. They cannot re-sign a top winger at $2.40M in full teardown mode. He is the same profile as Bertuzzi minus the production; his POTE 80 says he's near his peak.

**Heatley** at 89 overall, TOUG 80, CHKG 86, SPEE 96, 8 points in 12 games, $1.10M expiring, age 24. ATL at 4-7-1 with Kovalchuk also on a $1.10M expiring deal producing 12 points in 12. They cannot keep both. Heatley is the younger asset but Kovalchuk is scoring more; ATL probably keeps the scorer. TOUG 80 clears the bar but only just. The real case is age 24 with speed 96 — this is the long-term winger replacement for Mogilny.

**Bell** at 84 overall, TOUG 86, CHKG 84, SPEE 95, 6 points in 13 games, $900K with 1 year left, age 25. CHI at 2-7-3 with 8 expiring and $26.98M profit. Profit means they can keep him, but 2-7-3 means they should sell. One year left at 84 overall triggers the mechanic where a non-re-signable 80+ player can move for a pick. The speed plus toughness combination is rare in the entire league.

**McLaren** at 83 overall, CHKG 93, TOUG 89, 8 points in 12 games on 18.8 MPG, $2.20M expiring, age 28. SJ at 4-4-3 with 14 expiring and $66.24M payroll — the most motivated seller by any metric. He is the purest checking defenseman available. If the Coach wants a shutdown pair against the top lines in a series, McLaren at 93 checking is that man.

**Stuart** at 84 overall, CHKG 83, TOUG 74, POTE 92, 7 points in 12 games on 32.3 MPG, $1.80M expiring, age 25. Same club as McLaren. TOUG 74 means he doesn't fill the toughness gap, but POTE 92 and age 25 make him the blue-line complement. Package with McLaren or pick him separately if SJ split.

**Witt** at 79 overall, CHKG 94, TOUG 90, POTE 81, 9 points in 14 games, $1.70M expiring, age 28. WSH at 4-6-3 with only 5 expiring. Less motivated than SJ or VAN, but 94 checking is the highest in the query. He is the sixth man, not the first call.

**Task #2 update (Luongo/DiPietro goalie monitoring):** Luongo is on our roster at POTE 97, $1.60M, expiring July 2006 — he is not "available," he is ours to re-sign. DiPietro (NYI, G, 86 overall on today's form, 11 GP, 626 minutes, $1.10M expiring) is playing regularly for NYI at 5-6-1. The March 2005 evaluation (79 base, 3.64 GAA, 84.9% SV) already killed him as a target. The monitoring window runs through February 2006; no change in status at week 14 of the season.

## Trade construction

This phase answers: what packages do we propose in February, and who across the league has the structural reason to say yes? The answer centers on three clubs in full teardown mode — VAN, MTL, ATL — each holding a player who closes the zero-toughness gap while adding production. I would pursue all three simultaneously; they use non-overlapping assets.

**Eminger goes to Vancouver for Bertuzzi.** Bertuzzi at 93 overall, 21 points in 14 games on 24.9 MPG, TOUG 85, CHKG 89, $2.60M expiring, is the single highest-impact player on the market. He solves toughness and scoring in one acquisition, and at 30 this is a win-now move — correct for a 9-3-0 team. VAN at 4-5-1 carry the league's lowest payroll at $46.36M with 13 expiring deals; they are rebuilding and must move a 30-year-old winger they won't re-sign. Eminger at POTE 99, age 22, $2.20M for 4 years is a rebuild centerpiece. Tucker at CHKG 92, TOUG 88, age 30, $1.30M expiring gives VAN a veteran body for the remainder. They also get our 2nd-rounder (round 1).

Payroll: TOR gains $0.10M (lose $3.50M, gain $2.60M). VAN gains $0.90M, trivial against their $46.36M base.

**Colaiacovo goes to Montreal for Komisarek.** Komisarek at 84 overall, 12 points in 13 games on 29.5 MPG, CHKG 91, TOUG 84, POTE 90, age 23, $1.10M expiring is the best value on the board. He fills the toughness gap on defense and is eight years younger than Roberts. MTL at 3-6-3 should be sellers regardless of their $21.18M profit — nine points through 12 games means this season is gone. They get Colaiacovo (POTE 99, D, age 22, $1.40M for 4 years) and our 3rd-rounder (round 2). Same position, same age bracket, same potential range. If their scouting department values POTE 99 at all, this is a reasonable swap of one expiring blueliner for a controllable one.

Payroll: TOR saves $0.30M. MTL gains $0.30M. Negligible on both sides.

**Heatley is the fallback for the first-rounder.** Heatley at 89 overall, TOUG 80, CHKG 86, SPEE 96, age 24, $1.10M expiring, 8 points in 12 games is the long-term winger replacement for Mogilny. ATL at 4-7-1 carry both Heatley and Kovalchuk on $1.10M expiring deals; Kovalchuk produces more (12 points in 12) and will be the one they keep. TOR offers Spezza (POTE 99, C, age 22, $1.00M, 1 year) plus Koltsov (POTE 94, LW, age 24, $1.10M, 1 year) plus our 1st-rounder (round 0). ATL gets two 90+ potential forwards at bargain salaries plus a lottery-adjacent pick — a rebuild kit.

Payroll: TOR saves $1.00M. ATL gains $1.00M.

**All three together** cost TOR five players (Eminger, Tucker, Colaiacovo, Spezza, Koltsov — none of whom started a game except Spezza at 8 GP and 4.0 MPG), all three picks, and net $2.20M in payroll savings. In return we get Bertuzzi, Komisarek, and Heatley: TOUG 85/84/80, CHKG 89/91/86, and a combined 41 points in 39 games so far. That is the entire toughness gap, the defensive depth problem, and the Mogilny replacement in one February session.

**If only one or two land**, prioritize Bertuzzi (highest immediate impact) and Komisarek (best value, no first-rounder). Keep the 1st-rounder for Heatley only if both fail. Bell at CHI (TOUG 86, CHKG 84, SPEE 95, age 25, $900K) is the low-cost alternative to Bertuzzi — St. Jacques plus Tucker plus the 3rd would suffice — but at 6 points in 13 games he produces half of Bertuzzi. Acceptance on every proposal is uncertain; the AI's valuation is compiled code and VAN or MTL may not rate a POTE 99 prospect highly enough.

**If none land**, the internal fixes remain: Roberts onto K2 for his CHKG 86 and TOUG 92, McCabe and Wallin dressed for their 86 CHKG and 83 FACE respectively. The toughness ceiling stays at Jackman's 75 and we go into the playoffs hoping the lineup adjustments hold.

## Owed

**Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window:** This task is dead and has been since March 2005. The GM closed all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19 ("Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks"), and the underlying purpose, finding a high-90s goalie from a non-contender, was resolved when Luongo arrived at 97 overall. He is on our roster now at 26, $1.60M, 1 year remaining, and has started 5 games so far this season.

**What changed:** Nothing. Luongo remains our 97 overall starter. DiPietro is no longer a relevant target because the problem he was an answer to no longer exists. The trade window this task tracked closed in February 2005.

**One flag for a separate conversation:** Luongo's contract reads 1 year at $1.60M. That makes him an expiring asset at the end of this season. At 26 and 97 overall, he is the kind of player who gets moved or re-signed at a much higher number. This is not the trade-window task; it is a renewal question the GM should think about before next spring. I will raise it properly in a trajectory piece once the season is past its midpoint.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-09
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-09

Next game at SJ on Wednesday 09 November 2005.

## Development opportunity

The scratched young players are losing 2 points off every grade while sitting, and nobody is addressing whether that's the right trade-off. At morale 76, Spacek, Upshall and Gardener are each handing back a measurable chunk of their ability to the lineup, whether or not they play.

**Chlup** is exactly where he belongs: 12 points in 14 games at 20.2 MPG on the second line. No question here, he's earned every shift.

**Alexeev** is the clearest mismatch. 0.57 pts/g in 7 games on 11.7 MPG outproduces both Upshall (0.50 in 6) and Gardener (0.00 in 6) who are also on the outside. He's dressed every time he's available and he's earning more games than he's getting.

**Spezza** is in the collapse pattern again. 4.0 MPG, 0.25 pts/g over 8 games, morale at 81 and falling. The threshold I set last season was "under 8 for three games, scratch permanently." He's averaging 4.0. The fourth-line slot isn't developing him, it's wasting him and costing a roster spot.

**Spacek** at 0.50 pts/g in 6 games is respectable rate work on limited ice, but morale 76 means he's competing with a 2-point handicap when he does go out. **Upshall** is the same story at the same rate and the same morale. Neither is hurting the team by being in it; both are hurting themselves by being out of it.

**Gardener** with 0 points in 6 games on 4.5 MPG and morale 76 is not yet showing anything that argues for a roster spot over Alexeev. POTE 98 is a scouting opinion, not a result.

**Colaiacovo** at 0 points in 14 games on 12.9 MPG is zero offensive output from a third-pair role. At 22 that's tolerable defensively but it's not growth on the scoresheet. He's playing, which is the right thing; the production just isn't there yet.

**Eminger** at 0.29 pts/g on 19.9 MPG in 7 games is the same underperformance that flagged him in March. Morale 96 because his minutes are high when he plays, but the rate is not improving.

## Development trends

The question this phase answers is whether anyone's trajectory should change the GM's plans before the trade deadline. With no grade movement recorded in the window, I'm reading production and minutes, which is the next best thing.

**Chlup** is at 0.85 pts/g on 21.3 MPG in 14 games at 19. Last season he finished at 0.88 on 18.2. The rate dipped three hundredths while he added three minutes a night. That's a young centre absorbing a bigger role and nearly holding his production flat. He belongs on the first line permanently and I've said so twice since October. The evidence keeps building; the GM hasn't moved him yet.

**Colaiacovo** has zero points in 14 games on 13.5 MPG at 22. That's not a hot-and-cold stretch, it's an entire season with nothing on the board. He's a development pick, so the bar is growth rather than production, but 14 scoreless games at 13 a night means the development isn't happening on this line assignment. Something needs to change: a different partner, a lower-pressure role, or a long look at whether he's a top-pair prospect at all.

**Jackman** is at 0.85 pts/g on 24.5 MPG, a dramatic turnaround from last season's 0.48 on 30.4. His load dropped six minutes a night and his rate nearly doubled. The October memory about D-minute concentration between him and Klesla is resolving — Klesla is also down to 24.4 from 34.5. Whatever spread the lines achieved in November is working. Keep it.

**Richards** is at 0.62 pts/g on 13.1 MPG in 14 games. That extends the decline: 1.08 at 23, 0.71 at 24, now 0.62 at 25. Three straight seasons going the wrong way in his physical prime with no role change to explain it. The system-fit question from May is now a trajectory question. If this holds through January, the GM needs to think about whether Richards is a centre or a winger, or whether he's a third-liner wearing a top-six jersey.

**Roberts** at 39 is at 0.29 pts/g on 13.7 MPG, down from 18 MPG at the start of the window. He's fading and the minutes are being pulled. No action needed yet — he's still a dressing-room body and the rate supports a fourth-line role. But plan around his departure next offseason.

**The bench-warming four.** Spezza at 4.0 MPG and 0.25 pts/g, Gardener at 2.2 MPG and 0.00, Upshall at 3.8 MPG and 0.40, Spacek at 3.6 MPG and 0.40. All under five minutes a night with minimal returns. The pattern from October is confirmed again: they get early minutes, produce nothing, and the minutes die. Scratch them permanently rather than carry them on the dress list for one shift a game.

**Gaborik** arrived mid-window (0→13 GP). 0.46 pts/g on 21.4 MPG at 23 is below what we'd want from top-six minutes but not alarming in 13 games. Too small a sample to draw a trend. Watch through December.

## Morale watch

The 3-game win streak has done the heavy lifting. Everyone who was down in late October has climbed five to ten points, and the only group still sitting below the pack is the fourth line.

**Brendl, Spezza, Lundmark** are all at 81, on 4.3, 4.0 and 2.8 minutes respectively. At their calibre (low 80s OVR) the expected band is around 17 minutes. They're getting a quarter of that. The streak has been kind enough to keep them from falling further, but 81 costs one point off every grade, and the pattern I flagged in October (young forwards who get minutes early then collapse) is playing out again with Spezza in particular. That said, Brendl has 3 points in 9 games, so he's contributing at his rate. No line change fixes a 13-minute gap when the top three lines are eating the game. This is a roster-depth issue, not a lines issue, and it will resolve when we get more middle-six forwards through the season.

**Richards** at 86 on 13.1 MPG is still four minutes below his band, but he's climbing fast (+13 from where he sat two weeks ago) and producing at 0.57 pts/g. The win streak is closing the gap without intervention. I'd leave him.

**Alexeev** at 96 on 11.7 MPG with 0.57 pts/g is the same rate as Nash (15.4 MPG) but with less ice. Not a morale concern tonight. Worth watching if his minutes don't creep up.

The room is fine. The fourth line at 81 is the only number below 90 on the active roster, and they're recovering with the wins. No change.

## Role composition

The question is whether each unit is built from players whose tools fit the job, and whether gaps are arrangement problems or roster problems. Two units need attention: K2 on the PK and D3 on the blue line.

**K2 penalty kill** has a checking mean of 67 with only one man (best 88) above that line. Spezza and Brendl as the forward pair sit well below 70 in checking — they cannot win puck battles in the zone. The fix is Roberts, who has checking 84 and toughness 72 and is currently scratched. Activate him onto the K2 forward slot. He goes in, Brendl or Spezza comes off. K2 checking mean jumps from 67 toward 75. Chemistry cost is minimal — PK units reset every shift anyway.

**Klesla load** compounds the K2 issue. He carries L1, P1, and K2. Three assignments means roughly 28+ MPG. Moving him off K2 (replaced by McCabe on the blue line at checking 83, stamina 83) drops his expected minutes by 3-4 per night and protects his endurance through December without touching the even-strength structure.

**D3 (Stahle and Colaiacovo)** is the weakest defensive pairing. Neither man ranks in the top four on checking or toughness. McCabe at 83 checking, 72 toughness and 83 stamina would upgrade this slot directly. The chemistry cost is low since D3 faces bottom-six lines, and McCabe is fresh from being scratched. This also solves the standing task: D3 is where the upgrade belongs.

**L4 (Spezza, Lundmark, Brendl)** has checking mean 63 and toughness mean 58. This is the same structural gap flagged in April: no forward outside L1-L2 checks above 82. The roster simply does not hold another checking bottom-six forward. No arrangement fixes this. Roster problem.

**L1 through L3, K1, P1, P2** are well constructed. D1 pairs Jackman (defensive, 92 checking) with Klesla (offensive, 99 speed) — exactly the one-plus-one principle. K1 at checking mean 80 is the best unit on the sheet. P1's Nash at 82 checking gives it a backcheck anchor. No changes needed there.

## Opponent matchup

The question tonight: does SJ present a matchup problem that our current lines cannot handle? Short answer is no, except in net.

**Nabokov** at 91 OVR with SREC 95 and 5HOL 91 is the main obstacle. We're a 3.10-goal-per-game team; he's the reason this could be a one-goal game. That's why the goalie start matters tonight more than line matching does.

**Marleau** at 89 OVR with SPEE 97 and AGIL 98 is their offensive engine. Klesla at SPEE 99, AGIL 99, 87 OVR on our first pair can track him, and Jackman brings CHKG 94 alongside. This is a favorable matchup for us; no need to shuffle pairs to target or avoid him.

**Hossa** is their sleeper threat, hiding on line four at OVR 76 with ACCU 87, SHPW 87 and PUCK 84. Our L4/P3 personnel (Stahle 76, Colaiacovo 76) is our thinnest defensive unit against a winger with real hands. However, I'm not certain the game matches L4 against our P3 specifically -- the auto-pairing mechanic tells me which D goes out with which forward line, but the cross-team matching cadence is unclear. If it does pair, Colaiacovo at CHKG 68 could get worked by Korolyuk's DEKG 89 on the third line.

**Our top three forward lines** are clearly deeper than theirs. Gaborik at 99 OVR faces Stuart (84) and Brewer (87), and that's a 12-15 point gap across every grade. Chlup at 87 against McLaren (83) and Mironov (84) wins the middle. I see no reason to touch forward lines.

**Their penalty kill** gives up 5/46 which is a 10.9% conversion -- bad. Our PP at 2/14 is also poor but tonight's opponent is exploitable there if our first unit sustains zone time. That's an execution note, not a lineup change.

## Owed

**Owed item #1: defencemen analysis and end-of-season sell list.** 14 games in now, up from roughly 8-10 when I last filed this. The main changes are Colaiacovo's continued scoreless run, Klesla's new status as an expiring rental, and Jackman's rate settling into a still-elite range that makes the sell decision harder.

**Jackman** at 0.86 pts/g on 14 games is still far above his career 0.48. At $0.70M x 2 and age 24, he's the best value on the roster. The Oct 16 sell-window note said move him while the rate peaks. At 0.86 the window hasn't closed, but it's not screaming anymore. He's the hardest sell to make because the price is right and he's playing well. I'd only move him for a package that includes a first.

**Klesla** at 0.36 pts/g on 25.6 MPG is a new consideration. At 87 OVR on a top pair, that's below what those minutes should produce. More importantly, his contract expires in 1 year at $0.90M. A contender at the deadline could use him. Sell at the trade deadline, not in offseason.

**Colaiacovo** at 0 points in 14 games on 12.9 MPG is the weakest dressed D. At 76 OVR and $1.40M x 4, he's the cheapest move if anyone wants a depth pair. The Hainsey recommendation from last week (0.38 pts/g on 20.9 MPG) validates it: Hainsey is the better option in that slot.

**Eminger** sits at 0.29 pts/g in 7 games, $2.20M x 4. My March 30 note flagged him, the May 31 correction confirmed he's locked to 2009. Nobody's taking 4 years of inflated salary for a 0.29-rate D. He's stuck. The sell window on return value is effectively closed unless a team needs cap-straddling depth.

**McCabe** at 0 GP, $3.00M x 3, career 0.48 in the last window. Still the clear first one to go. He's not dressed and nobody's asking for him. The problem is the same: nobody takes 3 years of that salary for a declining 30-year-old.

**Keep:** Fischer (0.67 pts/g, GM's keeper), Kaberle (GM's star, keeper), Stahle (21, 0.29 on 12.9 MPG, growing into his role, $0.97M x 2 is cheap).

**Revised sell list:** McCabe (first), Colaiacovo (second), Klesla (deadline rental, third). Jackman only for a package. Eminger is a dead contract.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-06
