# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-06

Toronto 9-2-0, 22 pts after 13 games.

## Role coverage

Toughness is the only gap Toronto cannot fix by dressing different men. Zero players above 80 in that grade; the roster tops out at Jackman's 75. Every other role has enough bodies at 80+, and the ones the Coach flags as weak are sitting on the bench unlined.

**Jackman** at 24 is the only 80+ checker currently in a unit. His CHKG 87 and TOUG 75 make him the best of what we have, but one man does not cover four lines and two penalty-killing units. The Coach's Oct 29 note says "only four checkers above 80" but the sheet lists six: Jackman 87, Roberts 86, McCabe 86, Tucker 83, Fischer 82, Upshall 80. Five of those six are not lined. That is not a roster hole. That is a deployment choice.

**Roberts** is 39 and not lined. His CHKG 86, CLUTCH 90, INJU 98 make him a viable third or fourth defender and a penalty-kill body. He is old, but at 39 with the highest durability grade on the roster (98) he is a legitimate short-shift option who eats minutes without wearing down. Lining him costs nothing and addresses the Coach's checking complaint on K1/K2 immediately.

**McCabe** at 30 with CHKG 86 and ENDU 94 is another unlined checker who can absorb 15 to 18 minutes. The GM locked him in last season for this exact reason. He is on the roster and the Coach is not using him.

**Wallin** at 25 is the roster's second-best faceoff man at 83 FACE, and he is not lined. After Sundin (90 FACE), the next available draw-taker is Chlup at 75, which is below the threshold where a centre reliably wins draws on the third or fourth line. Lining Wallin on a checking line with faceoff duty moves Toronto from one 80+ faceoff man to two.

**Toughness** is the only role that cannot be solved by moving pieces. The Feb 21 count of "six players at stored TOUG 80+" was wrong. The Feb 24 count of zero is correct. Jackman at 75 is the team high. Roberts 73, McCabe 73, Chlup 70, Tucker 70. No one is close to 80. The Coach's Oct 29 flag ("no player above 71 in toughness outside Jackman") is roughly right against displayed ratings and matches the stored picture: 75 is the ceiling here. This is a trade problem, not a lineup problem.

**Scoring and speed** are not close to thin. Eleven players at 80+ scoring, twenty-five at 80+ speed. The concern is not today's depth but who is carrying it. Mogilny is 36, Sundin 34, Roberts 39. Those three hold scoring grades of 94, 92, and 88. The next tier behind them is Gaborik (92, 23), Afinogenov (90, 26), Abid (86, 25). The handoff is coming within two to three seasons and the depth behind the top six is real, but the top six itself will thin if Mogilny and Sundin both depart. That is a trajectory question for next phase, not a coverage gap tonight.

**Goalies** are covered. Luongo at 26, $1.60M, 1 year left, is an elite starter (94/94 glove-stick grades, 0.944 SV). Tellqvist at 26, $1.20M, 6 years, is a serviceable backup at 80-grade. The Luongo contract expiring after this season is a renewal question, not a coverage one.

The pending task on Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time is resolved. Luongo is on this roster at 94-grade and playing. No further monitoring needed.

## Trajectory

The question this phase answers: is Toronto building into a cliff or into a window, and does the money support the plan?

The age curve is young, not top-heavy. 29 of 34 players are 29 or under; only three are 34+ (Sundin 34, Mogilny 36, Roberts 39), all on contracts that end by July 2007. The problem is not old players clinging on. It is the opposite: a contract cluster in July 2009 that, if left unmanaged, releases 11 players and $37.40M simultaneously, and leaves the club rebuilding again with a thin 30-33 bridge (McCabe and Tucker, both 30, are the only two men in that bracket).

**Gaborik** is the single largest risk on the sheet. $11.90M/year for five years, and he is producing 6 points in 12 games (0.50 pts/g) against last season's 1.19. The contract is signed and cannot be renegotiated, so the action is monitoring: if he holds above 0.70 by January, the deal is fine; if he stays at 0.50, he is a $23.80M problem over the next two years on a player POTE 90 who should be better than this.

**The July 2006 renewal cluster** is 9 players, $15.44M. The two must-locks are **Luongo** (26, $1.60M, POTE 97) and **Chlup** (19, $2.34M, POTE 95, 12 points in 13 games). Both on one year. Both must get 5-6 year deals the week their contracts expire. Luongo first because Tellqvist (26, POTE 91, 6 years) behind him is a clear step down and Luongo's market price rises with every playoff win. Chlup second because at 19 with POTE 95, the renewal is cheaper now than in two years when he's a proven 80-point centre.

**The July 2009 cluster** is the structural trap. 11 contracts worth $37.40M all expire the same summer: Sundin, Richards, Chistov, Kaberle, Nash, Eminger, Alexeev, Upshall, Colaiacovo, Wallin, Abid. By then Richards will be 29, Nash 25, Eminger 26, and every one of them a prime-age asset in demand. The fix is to stagger: trade the two who won't get minutes (Wallin 25, $1.40M, 0 GP, POTE 97 and Abid 25, $1.30M, 0 GP, POTE 94) before July 2007 rather than letting them walk into the same bidding war as everyone else.

**The money question answers itself.** Toronto's payroll of $89.94M is the highest in the league, but so is their revenue ($59.86M) and so is their profit ($37.06M). Next closest is Detroit at $30.06M. There is no financial reason not to add a big contract for a target like Iginla or Jovanovski. The constraint is minutes, not dollars.

**Draft capital** has improved since the January 2005 note that said "no picks beyond a 4th." Toronto now owns its own 1st, 2nd, and 3rd rounders. The 1st is the most liquid asset on the sheet and can fund a meaningful February package alongside Tucker ($1.30M, 1 year, POTE 79, already a chip per the GM's March 19 order).

**On the Luongo/DiPietro monitoring task (task #2):** Luongo arrived in January 2005. The GM closed all goalie monitoring on March 19, 2005. This task is complete and obsolete; there is nothing to report.

## Calendar

Are we buyers or sellers at March 19, and what does the summer renewal calendar look like? We are buyers, and the summer is a controlled set of nine decisions that mostly resolve themselves around two anchors: Luongo's five-year deal and Mogilny's exit.

**The deadline call is obvious.** Toronto sit first in the East at 22 points in 13 games. The Coach's gaps (no player above 71 toughness outside Jackman, only four checkers above 80) are fixable at the deadline, and the manual says contenders buy for need. We own our own first, second, and third-round picks this year, a significant change from last season when no pick better than a fourth-rounder existed. That opens packages that were blocked before.

**Bertuzzi** (VAN, RW, 30) is the primary target: 94 base, 1.25 pts/g, TOUG 83, CHKG 87. He solves toughness and production simultaneously. VAN at 2-3-1 with 13 expiring and $46.36M payroll (lowest in the league) are forced sellers. Package: Tucker + R2. He is a rental unless he accepts a reduced deal, but 30 is old for a five-year lock.

**Heatley** (ATL, LW, 24, 91 base, 82 TOUG, $1.10M expiring) is the age-correct version of the same fix. ATL at 2 points cannot keep both him and Kovalchuk. Package: Koltsov + Spezza + R1. This costs the most development capital and should only trigger if Spezza has stalled through January. If Spezza reaches 10+ MPG and 0.5+ pts/g by late February, he stays and the package shifts.

**Brad Stuart** (SJ, D, 25, 87 base, POTE 91, $1.80M expiring) is the blue-line add. SJ carry the highest payroll among likely sellers. Package: Abid + R2. This is the one that improves the foundation long-term rather than patching a gap for April.

**Mogilny** at 36 and $5.50M is the summer's biggest problem. He is the most expensive player on the roster and the oldest by a decade. He is on the expiring list. He should be moved at the deadline as a third chip if a package needs a salary body, or released if not. No renewal.

**Luongo** at 26, 97 overall, $1.60M with two years remaining is the renewal priority. Lock him on five years immediately in July. He is the best player on the roster and the price is absurd for a 97-rated goalie. This is the single most important contract decision in the dynasty right now.

**Chlup** (19, C, $2.34M) and **Klesla** (23, D, $0.90M) are renew candidates. Chlup at 19 needs a five or six-year deal to avoid the annual ratchet. Klesla at $0.90M is cheap depth; renew on four or five years.

**Tucker** (30, $1.30M) and **St. Jacques** (25, $0.80M) are chips. Both appear in active package proposals for Bertuzzi and the Bell/Begin packages respectively. Move them by March.

**Koltsov** (24, $1.10M) is binary: chip in the Heatley package, or renew if Heatley is unattainable. His decision is made by the deadline, not the summer.

**Ouellet** (24, G, $0.90M) is excess goalie depth with Luongo arrived and Belfour still on the books. He is a trade chip for a team with a depleted goalie pool, or a release in July.

**Spezza** (22, C, $1.00M, POTE 99) is the roster's biggest open question. The Coach's October report says 4.5 MPG and morale 76, the same pattern from last year. If he plays 10+ MPG and produces by February, renew five years. If not, he becomes the center in the Heatley package. The deadline forces this choice regardless.

## League scan

The question: who across the league gives Toronto the toughness and checking they cannot manufacture internally, on a club that has reason to say yes before February?

The answer is Bertuzzi first, then Doan, then a defenseman. Toronto have zero players above 75 in toughness and the Coach is explicit that no lineup change fixes this. Three clubs have the profile of a forced seller: VAN (5 points, 13 expiring, $46.36M payroll — the lowest in the league, so they are shedding by structure), SJ (12 points, 14 expiring, $66.24M payroll — the most desperate cutters), and PHX (8 points, 9 expiring, no path to re-signing anyone).

**Bertuzzi** at 93 overall, 94 base, 85 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 71 FACE, 30 years old, $2.60M expiring, 21 points in 13 games (1.62 pts/g) on 25.1 minutes a night. He is the best player on the most motivated seller. VAN at 5 points with 13 expiring deals must move him before July or lose him for nothing. He solves the top-six scoring bridge AND the toughness gap in one body. Package: Tucker plus a second-rounder. VAN gets a cheap forward and a pick; they get picks for a man they cannot keep.

**Doan** at 85 overall, 87 base, 86 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 29 years old, $2.40M expiring, 10 points in 13 games (0.77 pts/g) on 20.2 MPG. PHX at 3-9-0 with 9 expiring will not re-sign him. He is the younger, cheaper version of the same package: top-six winger with legitimate toughness. Less production than Bertuzzi (0.77 versus 1.62) but two years younger and on a $2.40M deal. Package: Tucker plus a third-rounder if VAN gets Bertuzzi.

**Hill** at 77 overall, 81 base, 86 TOUG, 87 CHKG, defenseman, 35 years old, $2.30M expiring, 14 points in 12 games (1.17 pts/g) on 32.2 MPG. CAR at 4-4-2 with 14 expiring are shedding salary. He is the only defenseman in the league combining 86+ toughness with 87+ checking and real offensive production. Age is the concern, but this is a two-season bridge for the blue line. Package: Abid plus a second-rounder.

**Sopel** at 80 overall, 81 base, 82 TOUG, 77 CHKG, defenseman, 28 years old, $600K expiring, 14 points in 13 games (1.08 pts/g) on 23.8 MPG. Same seller as Bertuzzi (VAN). Cheaper than Hill, eight years younger, same point production per game. The trade-off is 5 points lower in checking. If VAN cannot absorb both Sopel and Bertuzzi in one deal, Sopel goes in a separate transaction. Package: Koltsov plus a third-rounder.

**Begin** at 27, $936K expiring, 87 TOUG, 95 CHKG, 86 FACE per the October vault note. BUF at 2-6-2 with 6 expiring. He solves toughness, checking AND faceoff in one body at a salary that barely registers. The concern is whether his production is real — he is not in q151 results, which suggests his overall has dropped since October. Needs a fresh read before approaching. Package: Tucker plus St. Jacques (both expiring, both unlined).

**McLaren** at 89 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 28, $2.20M expiring per the October vault note. SJ at 4-3-2 with 14 expiring and $66.24M payroll (third highest in the league among sellers). The purest checking-and-toughness forward available, but not in q151 results, which means his displayed ratings have shifted below the query threshold since October. If the Oct 22 reading held, he would top this list after Bertuzzi. Needs confirmation.

**Kurka** at 78 overall, 90 TOUG, 92 CHKG, 51 FACE, 23 years old, $600K expiring, 7 points in 12 games on 20.3 MPG. CAR seller (14 expiring, 4-4-2). He is the depth version: fourth-line winger with top-line toughness, cheap and young enough to keep. Package: a third-rounder alone or included as a secondary piece.

**What I would not pursue.** Laraque (EDM, 98 TOUG, 93 CHKG) produces 2 points in 11 games on 9.4 MPG — a fighter, not a hockey player. Hartnell (NSH) has 93 TOUG and 94 CHKG at 23 for $1.10M but NSH at 5-2-1 are not selling. Walker (NSH, 86 TOUG, 1.45 pts/g) is on the same non-selling club. Barnaby (NYR) is on the league's best team.

On the **Luongo/DiPietro monitoring task (#2)**: Luongo is on this roster at 94 overall playing every game. DiPietro at NYI produced 7-12-0 with a 3.65 GAA last season and is not a high-90s goalie. The GM closed all goalie monitoring on March 19, 2005. This task is complete and dead.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: what exact packages convert the toughness targets into offers Toronto can put on the table this month or February, using only surplus pieces the Coach is already not using?

Tucker is the obvious starter for every package. He is 30, $1.30M, one year left, 0 games played, and carries TOUG 88 and CHKG 92. Every seller wants a cheap checking wing for the remainder of this season. Koltsov ($1.10M, expiring, POTE 94, 0 GP) and St. Jacques ($0.80M, expiring, D, TOUG 80, CHKG 84, 0 GP) are the two other zero-ice-time pieces the Coach has not touched. Wallin ($1.40M, 4 years, POTE 97, 0 GP) is the more expensive piece but also the one the trajectory phase flagged for disposal before the 2009 cluster. None of these are players the Coach is deploying, so giving them costs nothing this season.

**Bertuzzi** is the target because he solves two problems in one body. At 93 overall and 85 TOUG, he is not just a toughness patch; he is a first-line winger producing 1.62 pts/g on 25.1 MPG. Toronto's top six is Mogilny at 36 and Sundin at 34, and Bertuzzi gives the immediate answer to who replaces them without waiting for Gaborik to confirm he is healthy. VAN at 5 points with 13 expiring deals and the league's lowest payroll at $46.36M are structurally forced to move him or lose him for nothing in July.

**Doan** is the secondary target. 86 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 29 years old, $2.40M. Less production than Bertuzzi (0.77 versus 1.62 pts/g) but two years younger and the same contract window. PHX at 3-9-0 with 9 expiring have no argument for keeping a man they cannot re-sign.

**Kurka** is the value play. 23 years old, 90 TOUG, 92 CHKG, $600K. He is not a top-six player (7 points in 12 games), but he is exactly what the Coach asked for on L4 and K2: a fourth-liner with elite toughness who costs almost nothing to re-sign at 23. CAR at 4-4-2 with 14 expiring are hoarding assets for their rebuild and would take a young centre with 97 potential over a 23-year-old winger they cannot develop alongside their own youth.

One note on the coverage phase: Nash at 21 carries TOUG 88 and is playing 13 games. The Coach's line "no player above 71 in toughness outside Jackman" is wrong on the sheet as it reads today. Nash IS above 80. That does not eliminate the gap (one 21-year-old winger is not four lines of toughness), but it means the problem is less desperate than the October note suggested, and it means any toughness acquisition is upgrading L4/K2, not plugging a literal zero.

## Owed

**Luongo availability and DiPietro monitoring for the goalie trade window.** This task is complete by virtue of success: Luongo is on our roster at 97 overall, 26 years old, $1.60M with one year remaining. The original question — can we acquire a high-90s goalie from a non-contender — was answered affirmatively last season. The GM's own standing order of 2005-03-19 ("Close all goalie monitoring") already closed this; the reason it still appears as owed is that no one formally marked it done.

**DiPietro** at NYI: 89 overall, 10 GP, 4 wins 5 losses, $1.10M expiring. NYI sit at 11 points in 12 games, 18th in the league, not a contender. He remains theoretically available if we ever needed a backup, but with Luongo at 97 as our starter there is no gap to fill.

**What has changed since last reported:** Everything. The task was designed to track Luongo's availability while he was at Florida. He is now our player. DiPietro has been at NYI all along with 10 starts; nothing about his situation has shifted that would make him more or less attainable. The one forward-looking note: Luongo's contract has one year remaining. He will be a restricted free agent after this season. That renewal question is the next goalie item that will matter, and it is months away (June at earliest).

No action needed. Closing this out.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-06
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-11-06

Next game at DAL on Tuesday 08 November 2005.

## Development opportunity

**The question is whether our young players are getting the minutes they've earned, and the answer splits cleanly:** the ones dressed are mostly right, but the scratched group is stuck in a dead zone that kills development rather than fostering it.

**Spezza** is the worst case. 4.0 MPG on the fourth line at age 22, morale 81, one point in seven games. POTE 99 doesn't matter if he's not on the ice. This is the same collapse I flagged last season, now a full year older with the same result. He needs either 8+ minutes of real work or he stops dressing. Four minutes is neither development nor contribution.

**Gardener** has zero points in six games on 4.5 MPG. He's not earning a roster spot at this rate. The honest call is stop dressing him and give that slot to someone who produces.

**Alexeev** is the counterexample. 0.50 pts/g (3 points in 6 games) on 12.3 MPG when he plays. He outproduces Chistov's rate (0.54) on nearly the same minutes, and he's only been dressed for 46% of games. He deserves every game over Upshall, who sits scratched at 76 morale with 3 points in 6 on 5.8 MPG.

**Spacek and Upshall** are at morale 76 in the scratched group. That's the -2 band. They're not getting enough to develop and the scraps are dragging them down. Same systemic pattern I flagged in October. The GM's January order to give young players space is being honoured in the dressing but not the deployment.

**Chlup** at 12 points in 13 games on 19.7 MPG is exactly where he should be. **Klesla** at 25.7 MPG on the first pair at 23, **Stahle** at 13.3 on the third, **Nash** at 7 points in 13 on 15.9, **Chistov** at 7 in 13 on 17.2, **Gaborik** at 20.9 MPG first-line: all fine. **Colaiacovo** at zero points in 13 on 13.3 MPG is thin production for a 22-year-old with POTE 99, but he's getting his minutes and that's the right thing to watch, not fix yet.

## Development trends

The question this phase answers: who is getting better, who is getting worse, and does any of it change what we do before trades or lineup decisions. Over four weeks, three players have validated a role they earned, and four young forwards are deep in the same minutes-collapse pattern that has wasted three seasons of roster space.

**Chlup** is the headline. 0.92 pts/g on 20.8 MPG in 13 games at 19. The 1.00 was a one-game fluke; 0.92 over 13 is the real number, and it confirms the first-line centre move I have been pushing since April. He is not a prospect developing, he is a top-six centre performing.

**Fischer** has gone from 10 MPG to 21.8 and from no points to 0.80 pts/g in six games at 25. The GM called him a keeper in January and he is proving it. His minutes doubled, his production followed. He is a top-pairing defenceman now.

**Hainsey** at 0.43 pts/g on 20.6 MPG in seven games at 24 is a solid third-pairing result from a player who wasn't even in the lineup four weeks ago. He's earning a regular spot.

**Colaiacovo** is the problem. Zero points in 13 games on 13.9 MPG at 22. A defenceman getting top-four minutes contributing nothing offensively is dead weight. At 22 the ceiling is the issue, not a slump. The GM valued him as development stock in January, but that was before a full 13-game blank. Flag for re-evaluation at the deadline.

**Gardener** at 0.00 pts/g in 6 games on 2.2 MPG is the minutes-collapse pattern again. Sixteenth-minute guy four weeks ago, now invisible. Third young forward this season to burn out in depth.

**Spezza** at 0.14 pts/g on 4.0 MPG in 7 games at 22 is the third consecutive season of the same thing. He is not developing in a meaningful role. He is developing on the fourth line in garbage minutes. This is a problem the GM owns at camp, not at the lines.

**Alexeev** went from 6 to 13.6 MPG but dropped from 0.55 pts/g last season to 0.20 this year. More ice, less production. The role increase hasn't helped.

**Richards** sits at 0.67 pts/g on exactly 13.0 MPG, unchanged. The system-fit question from May is still open. He has neither grown into a top-six role nor been given one.

**Gaborik** is back after missing time, and 0.50 pts/g on 20.9 MPG at 23 is below what his top-six minutes demand. Small sample (12 games), but he needs to trend up or his role will be contested.

The veterans are holding. Sundin at 0.75 on 22.2 MPG at 34, Mogilny at 0.67 on 21.1 at 36, Roberts winding down naturally to 13.7 MPG. No cause for alarm.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy. Core L1 through L3 all sit at 96 and rising with the winning streak; nobody there needs intervention.

**Richards** is the one to watch. 86 morale, 13.0 MPG, third-line centre. He's in the 80-89 band expecting roughly 17 minutes, so he's four short. He's climbed from 78 in late October to 86 now, so the trend is right and team wins are doing the heavy lifting. At 86 he costs himself one point off every grade. He needs to cross 90 to clear that, and the most direct path is a few more shifts a night. I'd nudge him up to the second line if a spot opens; it's not urgent enough to break the Chlup-Chistov-Afinogenov chemistry today, but if that line's production dips, he's the replacement.

**Spezza, Brendl, Lundmark** at 81 on 3.1 to 4.4 MPG. They're depth men in the 70-79 band expecting around 10 minutes, so they're well under, but at 81 they're recovering fine on wins alone. No action.

**Gardener, Spacek, Upshall** frozen at 76, scratched, 6 games each with 4-6 MPG. Seventy-six costs two points off every grade if they do dress. The GM knows this is the cost of the development rotation, and it's not moving without ice time he's not giving them right now. Their problem is his to accept or reverse, not a lines problem.

**Abid, McCabe, Tucker, Safronov, Wallin, Koltsov, St. Jacques** are all at 90+ on zero games. The winning streak carries them. No issue.

No change recommended for this game. The room is right.

## Role composition

The question is whether each unit has the right players for its job, and where the roster simply doesn't hold enough of a role to fill it.

**K2 (second penalty kill)** is the weakest link. Checking mean 66, faceoffs 53 out of 59 best. Klesla is on this unit while playing 25.7 MPG on the first pair. He's our second-best defender by usage and he's burning minutes on a kill where Roberts (83 checking, scratched) would do more good and cost nothing in chemistry since he isn't currently in the lineup. This is the one change that's clearly right.

**L4 (Spezza, Lundmark, Brendl)** carries checking mean 62 and toughness mean 57. This is the same structural gap I flagged in April — no forward outside the top six checks above 75. The GM's answer has been to let them grow into it, and that's fine as a game-plan. But it means we genuinely cannot roll a third checking unit. Any opponent with a second line that can drive play will eat this line alive, and there's no arrangement that fixes it. That's a roster problem, not a lines problem.

**The D minutes** are trending the right way. Klesla 25.7 and Jackman 26.0 at 13 games, down from 33-34 in the first two. Fischer is at 19.8 in 6 games, Kaberle 19.5 in 6, Hainsey 20.6 in 7. The spread the GM wanted is happening. Neither Klesla nor Jackman is a sell candidate on this trajectory — their load is being shared, and both are producing enough to justify it.

**P2** has Mogilny and Afinogenov, which is a lot of offensive talent on a second unit. The faceoff mean of 59 means we're not winning draws there, but against DAL that's manageable. No change warranted before Tuesday.

## Opponent matchup

**Can our current construction beat Dallas?** Yes, and the reason is straightforward: their defence collapses past one pair, and their power play is the worst in the conference at 5/56.

**Dallas D pairs 2 and 3 are a feast.** Erskine sits at 70 OVR with PUCK 53 and ACCU 52 — he is not a hockey player at this level. Berenzweig at 69 and Simpson at 67 are worse. Our second line (Chlup, Chistov, Afinogenov) has three guys above 86 with hands to exploit this. Our third line (Richards, Nash, Alexeev) gets Simpson or Berenzweig and can also produce. No adjustment needed — the talent gap does the work.

**Their top line is the real test.** Arnott at 85, Lehtinen at 86 (AGGR 99, CHKG 85), Morrow at 86 with CHKG 87 and TOUG 85. All three hit. Our D1 (Jackman CHKG 93, Klesla SPEE 99) is built for exactly this. Jackman is the best defensive forward on our D corps and their first line is the best opponent we've seen this stretch. The current D-slot order handles it by default.

**Turco at 97 means volume.** He's 97 OVR with 99 SREC, 98 GSH, 99 GSL. We scored 3.5 per game this season against weaker goaltending. Against a 97, we need our top two lines creating Grade-A chances, which they do when fed against Erskine and Matvichuk. Sundin's FACE 94 wins zone draws against Arnott's 78, giving us territory.

**No PK worry.** DAL is 5/56 (8.9%) on the man advantage. Our second kill unit could give up a goal and we'd still be better off. No PK changes.

**Goalie: start Luongo.** 97 OVR, morale 96, no flag in the brief. Tellqvist at 73 cannot start this game. Check the fatigue icon on screen before confirming per the January 19 order, but the brief gives no reason to doubt him.

**#1 (defensive assessment, standing task):** Current order is right. Jackman/Klesla stay D1 — Jackman covers Klesla's ENDU 59, and both have the speed to match DAL's top line. Eminger/Hainsey stay D2. Stahle/Colaiacovo stay D3; DAL's third line (Kapanen 75, Johnson 74, Lemieux 76) is not good enough to expose them. No sell urgency changes for this game; Eminger is locked $2.20M x4 per my corrected note, and the Klesla question (ENDU 59, 34 MPG load from October) is a November-December endurance conversation, not a Tuesday trade.

## Owed

**Delivering: "analyse how our defencemen played and update who should go at the end of the season" — game 14 of the season, 13 games of data.**

What's changed since October 29th: McCabe has now gone 13 full games without a shift, Jackman's rate has cooled from 1.00 to 0.92 pts/g but remains absurd for $0.70M, and Klesla's production-to-minutes ratio is becoming a pattern rather than a hot start fading.

**Jackman** at 12 points in 13 games (0.92 pts/g) on 26.0 MPG at $0.70M x 2. His career baseline is 0.48. The peak-sell window I flagged October 16th is still open — the rate is cooling but hasn't regressed to earth. If the GM moves him this month, a buyer sees 0.92. By February they'll see closer to 0.60 and offer less. Two years of team control means we're not desperate, but the window closes with the rate.

**Klesla** at 4 points in 13 games (0.31 pts/g) on 25.7 MPG. That is a top-pair investment yielding third-pair production. He's 23 with a year left at $0.90M, so this isn't a fire-sale situation — but if he's still under 0.40 by the deadline, he becomes a trade candidate at a price the GM won't like. Keep watching through November.

**Fischer** at 4 points in 6 games (0.67 pts/g) on 19.8 MPG. GM's keeper, and the numbers agree. He's only had 6 chances and is producing at a second-pair rate on a third-pair schedule. No concern.

**Hainsey** at 3 points in 7 games (0.43 pts/g) on 20.6 MPG. Age 24, $1.40M x 6. Reasonable depth rate. Not a sell target, not a starter. He does his job.

**Eminger** at 2 points in 7 games (0.29 pts/g) on 19.9 MPG. Worse than the March assessment of 0.38 season rate, and the sample is still thin but the direction is down. $2.20M x 4 makes him nearly unmovable — nobody takes four years of a 0.29-rate defenceman at $2.20M. The problem is now: does he get benched (losing the development investment) or do we carry dead cap through 2009?

**Kaberle** at 2 points in 6 games on 19.5 MPG. GM's star, protected. He's played 6 of 13, so his season rate (0.33) is meaningless as a sample. No issue.

**McCabe** at 0 games played, not dressed through 13 games. I cannot tell from here whether that's a healthy scratch decision or something physical — nobody has flagged him with a body part. Either way, he's $3.00M x 3 at age 30 contributing nothing. The sell case from May 2nd is now harder to ignore: at zero minutes his trade value is heading toward zero too. If the GM has any interest in getting a pick or a depth body for him, now is better than January.

**Stahle** at 3 points in 13 games (0.23 pts/g) on 13.3 MPG. Age 21, $0.97M x 2. Cheap third-pair minutes. No sell case.

**Colaiacovo** at zero points in 13 games (0.00 pts/g) on 13.3 MPG. Age 22, $1.40M x 4. The zero is ugly but he's young and cheap. Not a sell target yet — the sell threshold I set in March (0.60) needs production to be absent, not merely low, and zero in 13 at third-pair minutes isn't yet disqualifying. If he's still at zero by 20 games, he joins McCabe on the list.

**Safronov and St. Jacques** at 0 games, not dressed. Depth end. No trade value. Carry them as injury insurance or release in the off-season.

**Updated sell order at season's end:** McCabe (first — value bleeding by the week), Eminger (second — nearly unmovable at his contract, but the rate makes him expendable if anyone bites), Colaiacovo (watch — at zero after 20 games he's on the list). Jackman is not a sell by default; he's a sell only if the GM wants to monetise the hot window before regression.

# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-10-29

Toronto 8-2-0, 16 pts after 10 games.

## Role coverage

**The role that decides whether this team wins a round in June is toughness, and zero players on the roster carry a TOUG grade of 80 or higher.** Every other role has enough bodies at 80+, but most of them are sitting on the bench instead of filling the slot the coach needs.

**Checking** has six players at 80+ (Jackman 87, Roberts 86, McCabe 86, Tucker 83, Fischer 82, Upshall 80) and only Jackman is lined. McCabe at CHKG 86 and INJU 94 is the highest-value player on the bench for a defensive role; the coach wants Klesla's 26.1 MPG reduced and McCabe is the answer that costs nothing. Line him. Tucker at CHKG 83 is a fourth-round chip, so lining him raises his value rather than lowering it. Fischer at CHKG 82 and INJU 92 covers the durability hole too (only Afinogenov at 95 is actually playing among the five players at 80+ INJU).

**Faceoffs** has two at 80+ (Sundin 90, Wallin 83) and only Sundin plays. Wallin is 25, unlined, and draws no trade interest at FACE 83 with nothing else above 80. Put him on a third or fourth line centre slot. That gives two 80+ draw-takers and removes the "Sundin must win every important puck" problem.

**Toughness** cannot be fixed by a line change. Jackman's TOUG 75 is the roster's ceiling, and he is 24 with POTE that will not add toughness points. This is a trade gap and a February gap. The target list is unchanged: Bell (CHI, 88 TOUG, 82 FACE, 25, $0.90M expiring) closes toughness and faceoffs simultaneously, which would also make the Wallin lining a short-term bridge. Bertuzzi (VAN, 83 TOUG, 87 CHKG, 94 base, 30) is the better player but older and pricier. McLaren (SJ, 89 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 28) is the best pure checker on the market. All three are expiring, all three sit on desperate sellers, none are reachable in October.

**Age at the top of the checking depth chart is a problem for next season.** Roberts is 39, McCabe and Tucker are 30. If none of the Bell/Bertuzzi/McLaren packages land in February, the 80+ checker pool in October 2006 shrinks to Jackman, Fischer (26), and Upshall (23). That is thin at the exact moment Roberts walks.

**Luongo is 1.61 GAA, 0.944 SV in 5 games and in the last year of his deal.** Not a coverage gap — the three goalies cover the role — but a renewal task for the summer. Tellqvist has 6 years left; Ouellet has 1.

## Trajectory

**Is this club aging into a cliff?** No — the age shape is correct (13 under 23, 16 at 24-29, only 5 veterans). But two contracts create a money problem the age curve does not: Gaborik's $11.90M for 5 locked years, and Sundin's $8.40M for 4 more years taking him to 38. Neither can be renegotiated. They are structural costs that limit what we can spend on the 2009 renewal wave.

**Gaborik** is at 4 points in 9 games, a 0.44 rate, on $11.90M for 5 years. He is lined now and the Coach has him playing, but his value as a chip has already dropped since October 13. There is no exit until the deal expires in 2010. Every package we build for the next four seasons carries the fact that 13% of our payroll is anchored here regardless of production.

**Sundin** at 34 is producing 0.90 pts/g (9 in 10) on 4 remaining years at $8.40M. The window to recoup value closes at February 2006 when he's 35, and again at July 2006 when he's 35 and one year deeper into decline. After that, a contender pays $8.40M for a 36-year-old centre and gives us almost nothing. If this season's rate holds through January, a mid-season move to a Cup contender buys a young player plus a first-rounder. If it collapses, we eat it to 2009.

**The 2009 summer is the real cliff.** Eleven contracts worth $37.40M expire at once: Nash (25), Eminger (25), Chistov (26), Colaiacovo (26), Richards (29), Kaberle (31), Wallin (29), Abid (29), Upshall (26), Alexeev (27). That is every blue-chip young player we have. We cannot extend them early (no mid-term renegotiation), so 2009 is a single week where we either re-sign all five or lose them to free agency. At $35.20M annual profit we can afford it, but only if Sundin is gone and Gaborik's deal is still on book.

**The 2006 summer is the nearest one.** Nine contracts expire ($15.44M): Luongo, Chlup, Mogilny, Klesla, Spezza, Tucker, Koltsov, Ouellet, St. Jacques. The keepers are Luongo (26, #1 goalie), Chlup (19, 0.88 pts/g, POTE 95), and Klesla (23, POTE 97, 26 MPG). Mogilny walks at 36. Spezza is POTE 99 with 1 point in 4 games — gamble. Tucker is a chip per the GM's March order. These four must be locked the same week, and we must have the $35.20M profit still running by then.

**Draft capital:** TOR own their own R1, R2, and R3 for 2006. That is more than we had in January 2005 (none better than a fourth). The R1 alone funds any Heatley, Bertuzzi, or Doan package. The R2 funds a Stuart or Begin package. Good position.

**Money:** $89.94M payroll against $35.20M profit means the club is healthy and can absorb more salary. No cap exists. The only constraint is profit staying positive, and it will as long as revenue doesn't collapse and we don't sign a third $8M+ deal before 2009.

## Recommendations

## Calendar

Are we buying at the deadline, and what does each expiring contract become? We sit first in the East at 16 points through 10 games, so the answer is buy — the question is what, with whom, and when. The deadline is 141 days out on 2006-03-19, which means negotiations stay shut until late February. The summer's expiring list holds nine names and falls into three groups: three you must lock on long terms, four you renew cheaply, and two you shed.

**Gaborik** is locked. Five years at $11.90M. No decision needed until 2010. The January 2005 note about re-signing him was for the previous season's contract cycle; that ship has sailed and he's yours through his mid-20s at the highest salary on the roster. The money is spent.

**Afinogenov** is also locked, three years at $4.50M. The Coach flags his third year of decline (1.17 to 0.73 to 0.50 pts/g), but the contract runs through 2007-08. The fix is not a re-signing; it's the Bertuzzi target filling the top-six wing spot he can no longer hold. No summer decision.

**Jackman** carries two years at $700K. The Coach is right that 1.00 pts/g against a career 0.48 is regression bait. But selling a core blueliner while Colaiacovo and Stahle sit at 13 MPG each leaves us thin on the back end. If Bertuzzi comes in at a real cost and we need another piece to make it work, Jackman at peak value is the chip. Otherwise keep him.

**Chlup** (C, 19, $2.34M expiring) is the most urgent summer decision. At 0.88 pts/g on 21.2 MPG, he is first-line centre tonight and getting better. Renew on five years. Do not let him hit the market.

**Luongo** (G, 26, $1.60M expiring) is in his prime at a bargain salary. The GM declared him arrived in February 2005. Renew on five years. If he walks, we are rebuilding netminding from Tellqvist and Ouellet upward.

**Spezza** (C, 22, $1.00M expiring) is the POTE 99 gamble. The Coach says there is no in-season fix and next camp is the only lever. At $1.00M on a three-year deal, the risk is minimal. Renew three years. If he busts, we've lost two years of cheap centre depth. If he hits, we have a first-line centre for nothing.

**Klesla** (D, 23, $0.90M) and **St. Jacques** (D, 25, $0.80M) are both cheap depth defencemen. Renew both on two years each. Together they cost $1.70M, less than Mogilny's salary alone.

**Ouellet** (G, 24, $0.90M) is the third goalie. Renew one year. He costs nothing and guards against a Luongo injury.

**Mogilny** (RW, 36, $5.50M expiring) is the deadline asset. He is 36, he costs $5.50M, and if his displayed overall is above 80, the over-80-expiring mechanic means a pick. Even below 80, any contender needs a veteran RW for April. Dump him to a non-playoff team for a pick per the GM's March 4 standing order about avoiding rivals.

**Tucker** (LW, 30, $1.30M expiring) is already a designated chip. He is the lead piece in the Bertuzzi package (Tucker + R2 to VAN). That is the plan. If Bertuzzi falls through, Tucker goes in whatever deadline package materializes, or walks for nothing in July. Either way, do not re-sign him.

**Koltsov** (LW, 24, $1.10M expiring) is the swing piece. If Bertuzzi lands, Koltsov is a trade component (he was part of the Heatley package with Spezza and R1). If Bertuzzi does not land, renew him on two years as a third-line winger at $1.10M. His status depends on whether the February target materializes.

The draft picture matters for package-building: Toronto owns their own R1, R2, and R3 for the 2006 draft. The R4 belongs to NYR and the R5 to CAR. The January 2005 note about "no picks beyond fourth" applied to the 2005 class; we have three rounds to spend in 2006. The Bertuzzi package (Tucker + R2) is affordable.

## League scan

The primary gap is toughness — zero players at TOUG 80+ — and the secondary gap is a top-six winger to replace the declining Afinogenov. Three players on desperate sellers close both simultaneously: Bertuzzi, Hejduk and Doan. The question for February is which package the GM builds first.

**Bertuzzi** is the single best player on the market. 94 base, TOUG 89, CHKG 93, 11 points in 9 games at 27.3 MPG, $2.60M expiring, age 30. VAN sit at 2-3-1 with 13 expiring deals and the league's lowest payroll ($46.36M); they must sell and they have no reason to keep a 30-year-old rental over draft capital. The standing package (Tucker + R2) is fair to VAN — they get a 30-year-old checker with 83 CHKG who fills a hole and a second-rounder, and offload $2.60M. Acceptance is uncertain because VAN could want more for a 94-base player, but Tucker is the only chip the GM authorized for February and the R2 is ours.

**Hejduk** at COL solves the Afinogenov problem directly. 91 base, 12 points in 8 games on 23.5 MPG, TOUG 58 so he does not fix toughness, but he replaces scoring. $2.50M expiring, age 29. COL at 3-2-2 with $68.21M payroll and 8 expiring are the second-most financially stressed sellers. The GM already knows COL would deal Hejduk — in February 2005 they offered him for Belfour. He is still there, still expiring, still producing. He fills one wing; the toughness still needs Bertuzzi or Doan.

**Doan** is the alternate path to Bertuzzi. 87 base, TOUG 88, CHKG 93, 9 points in 9 games on 20.7 MPG, $2.40M expiring, age 29. PHX at 2-6-0 with 9 expiring. The package note says Tucker plus R2 as well. The GM cannot do both Bertuzzi and Doan with a single R2, so this is a choice: Bertuzzi is 7 points better in base and has produced more; Doan is one year younger and PHX are more desperate (2 wins in 8 vs VAN's 2 in 6 with a game in hand). If VAN overask, Doan is the fallback.

**Bell** at CHI is the cheapest toughness-plus-faceoff fix. 80 base, TOUG 88, FACE 82, 5 points in 7 games on 20.3 MPG, $0.90M expiring, age 25. CHI at 2-3-1 with 8 expiring and $25.14M profit — the most profitable seller in the league, meaning they are less desperate. The package (Tucker + St. Jacques + R3) uses a third-rounder we still own. Bell does not produce at a top-six rate, but at 25 with $0.90M he is the kind of player who becomes a permanent L3/L4 fixture.

**Brad Stuart** remains the blue-line target. 87 base, TOUG 80, CHKG 89, POTE 91, 6 points in 7 games on 31.7 MPG, $1.80M expiring, age 25. SJ at 3-2-1 with 14 expiring and $66.24M payroll — the most motivated seller in the league by contract count. Package: Abid + R2. The problem is the R2 is already committed to Bertuzzi. If the GM does Bertuzzi, Stuart waits for a third-rounder package or the summer.

**Komisarek** at MTL is the second young-D target. 77 base, POTE 91, 7 points in 8 games on 28.8 MPG, age 23, expiring. MTL at 2-5-1 with 8 expiring are in freefall. He is not as polished as Stuart but he is cheaper and younger. Abid + R3 is the likely package if we go this route.

**Wanvig** at PHX is the cheap development target with a physical profile. 74 base, POTE 94, TOUG 86, CHKG 87, age 24, $0.60M expiring. Only 1 point in 9 games, so production is absent, but the grade profile matches what we cannot find on our own roster. If PHX are selling Doan, they might take a late pick for Wanvig as a throw-in. Low priority but worth a conversation alongside the Doan package.

**What I would not chase:** Alfredsson ($11.40M expiring) and O'Neill ($6.92M expiring) are productive but their salaries anchor our payroll to a player we will not re-sign. Jokinen has 4 years left at $7.63M. Brewer at $6.21M is the same problem in a different jersey.

## Trade construction

The question is which single package to build first for February, given that all three primary targets cost the same chip — Tucker plus a pick. The answer depends on which seller is most motivated and which gap hurts most in a playoff run.

**Bertuzzi is the clear first call.** 94 base, TOUG 89, CHKG 93, 11 points in 9 games on 27.3 MPG at age 30. He closes the zero-80-toughness gap and adds top-six scoring in one move. VAN sit at 2-3-1 with 13 expiring deals on a $46.36M payroll — the league's lowest, which means they have already cut and must cut further. Tucker at CHKG 92 gives them the checking winger they lack, and the R2 is real draft capital for a team rebuilding. They shed $2.60M and take back $1.30M plus a pick. The risk: VAN could counter for the R1, and 94 base makes them greedy.

**Doan is the identical fallback.** 87 base, TOUG 88, CHKG 93, 9 points in 9 games, age 29, $2.40M expiring. PHX are 2-6-0 with 9 expiring and no path to retaining him. Same package as Bertuzzi (Tucker + R2), slightly less value in base and production, one year younger. If VAN demand the R1, pivot here immediately — PHX have less leverage than VAN.

**Hejduk is the scoring-first alternative.** 91 base, 12 points in 8 games on 23.5 MPG, age 29, $2.50M expiring. COL carry $68.21M payroll — the highest in the league — with 8 expiring deals and a 3-2-2 record. They are financially desperate. The GM already knows COL offered Hejduk for Belfour in February 2005. But he costs the R1, not the R2, and his TOUG 58 means the toughness gap persists. Take this only if the GM decides scoring depth matters more than toughness for a playoff run.

**What we cannot do simultaneously.** Bertuzzi, Doan, and Hejduk all require Tucker. Pick one. Stuart (SJ, POTE 91, age 25) is the next target after the forward deal, and Abid + R3 is the realistic package since the R2 will be spent. Acceptance is uncertain on all of these — the AI's player valuation is compiled code and we cannot model it.

**If none land by February:** Line McCabe at 30 and CHKG 86 on the second pair (Coach wants Klesla's 26.1 MPG reduced). Line Wallin at FACE 83 on a middle centre slot. Give Alexeev the third-line RW role the Coach wants. These three moves cost nothing, close the checking and faceoff complaints internally, and leave the toughness gap for the 2006 draft where we hold the R1.

## Owed

The GM asked on 2005-01-19 to monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro development through February for a goalie trade window. This job is now closed.

**Luongo** is on Toronto's roster at 97 overall, 1 year left, $1.60M, 5 GP in 10 team games. The trade happened. The GM's own Feb 19 order — "Goalies are solved. Done. Do not revisit that issue." — and the Mar 19 confirmation ("Keeping him and Luongo as two 90+ goalies") both stand. Luongo is 97 today with Belfour presumably at 90+ as well. The window is shut.

**DiPietro** at NYI: 87 displayed, 79 base, 24 years old, $1.10M expiring. Save rec 83, rebound 61, consistency 51. Those underlying grades say he is not close to Luongo's level. NYI are 3-4-0-1, 8 points through 8 games — not desperate enough to deal him yet, and even if they were, 79 base does not improve on what Toronto already has.

What changed since the last report: Luongo went from "target" to "on the roster." DiPietro's base is 79, unchanged, and he is one year older with no upward movement in his grades. The trade window the GM set in January has expired both by calendar (February passed) and by roster (we have our answer in Luongo).

No further monitoring needed on this thread.



**Delivered:** #2 (Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window) — closed. Luongo arrived at 97; DiPietro at 79 base is not an upgrade; GM's Feb 19 and Mar 19 standing orders confirm goalies are solved.
