# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-10-29

Next game vs ATL on Monday 31 October 2005.

## Development opportunity

Ten games in, the question is which of these thirteen are actually being developed and which are being worn down in the same pattern I flagged in March.

**Alexeev** is the clearest case of a player not getting what he's earned. Two points in three games is 0.67 pts/g, the best rate among the young group outside Chlup. He's in 30% of games while Upshall (0.50 pts/g) and Gardener (0.00 pts/g) are getting dressed ahead of him. This is the same rate-to-role mismatch from April. At 23 he's no longer a prospect to stash — he's a young player outproducing the guys in front of him.

**Gardener** has zero points in six games at 4.5 MPG and morale at 76. He's been scratched since the six-game mark. POTE 98 means nothing when the on-ice output is nothing. This is the collapse pattern exactly: a high-potential kid who gets a few early games, produces nothing, and gets buried while his morale bleeds.

**Spezza** is back in the same hole I documented in March. 4.5 MPG, 1 point in 4 games, morale 76. Last season he collapsed from 9.1 to 4.8 MPG at this age with POTE 99. Now it's October and he's in the identical spot. Either he gets a real role or he gets stopped, because the pattern of dressing a 22-year-old for four minutes a night and watching his morale drop is not development.

**Eminger** at zero points in four games on 20.2 MPG from the second pair is concerning. Last season he slid from 0.44 to 0.38 season-rate; now he's at 0.00 in a smaller sample. Four games isn't enough to act on, but the trajectory is downward and he's getting real minutes to produce zero.

**Chlup, Nash, Chistov, Stahle, Klesla, Colaiacovo, Gaborik** are all earning their minutes. Chlup leads the group at 9 points in 10 games on 20.2 MPG. Nash at 0.50 on the third line is fine. Gaborik at 0.44 on the first line is thin but he's the best option at the position.

## Development trends

The window runs 17 days and 10 games. No grades moved on the card, so I'm reading production and minutes only. The story splits clean: the veterans are holding, the young depth is dying on the same vine it did last year, and two players whose trends should change the GM's plans are Sundin and Richards.

**Sundin** at 34 is the team's best point rate: 1.00 pts/g on 20.4 MPG over 10 games. He went 0.00 in the opening game to 1.00 since. No decline in minutes or production. The "plan around his departure" clock is not running yet. Any offseason planning that assumes he's done is premature at this rate.

**Richards** recovered to 0.67 pts/g after last season's collapse to 0.71. That's a genuine rebound. But he's on 12.2 MPG. My October 20 note flagged his morale at 78 on 11.8 MPG, five minutes below his band expectation. He's producing like a top-six centre on middle-six minutes. If the GM wants him to stay happy through December, the role has to match the rate.

**Fischer** at 0.80 pts/g on 21.8 MPG in 6 games is career-best production from the blue line at 25. This confirms the GM's January position: Fischer is a keeper, and he's getting better while we play him.

**Jackman** at 1.00 pts/g on 24.4 MPG is hot. His career rate is 0.48. This is the sell window I flagged in October: his value peaks now, before regression pulls him back toward his baseline.

**The young-forward pattern repeats exactly.** Spacek 0.40 on 3.6 MPG, Gardener 0.00 on 2.2, Upshall 0.40 on 3.8, Lundmark 0.00 on 3.5, Spezza 0.25 on 4.5. Five players who started the season with 11-17 MPG and now sit under five with no production. My October 22 note called this systemic, and it's confirmed again with no exception.

**Stahle** at 0.33 on 14.2 MPG is the one young defenceman actually building minutes. He went from 6 to 14 MPG in 17 days and is producing. That's real development.

**Gaborik** at 0.44 on 19.6 MPG over 9 games is on pace after missing the opener. Nothing alarming, but 0.44 is below what the team needs from him on the top six. He needs the first month to find his hands.

**Nash** went 0.44 on 16.7 MPG over 10 games. Same pattern as last season: rate halved on stable minutes at 21. This is the system-fit question from March, unanswered.

## Morale watch

The room is healing on the back of the recent wins, but one structural gap remains: Richards is still well below his minutes band and his morale is the lowest of any regular.

**Richards** sits at 81 morale on 12.3 MPG. At his calibre he expects around 17 a night, so he's carrying a five-minute deficit every game. The wins have pulled him from 78 up to 81 (+5 most recently), but the floor is low because the minutes never came back. He's on the third line and getting third-line usage. This is the same pattern I flagged in October at morale 78 and 11.8 MPG; the gap is slightly narrower now but the mechanism is unchanged. If we go cold again, he's the first regular who will slip back below 78.

**The depth group** -- Brendl, Lundmark, Spezza at morale 76 on 4.5 to 5.4 MPG, plus Spacek and Upshall scratched after 5.8 MPG in 6 games -- all dropped hard (up to -15) and are recovering (+2 to +5 most recently). They expect 10 MPG at their calibre and get half that. The only fix is minutes the winning lineup cannot spare. Against ATL at home, keep the current grouping; their morale is self-correcting while we win.

**Roberts** at 84 on 14.2 MPG was briefly scratched and is now recovering fast (+5). At 39 and below his 17-MPG band, he's tolerable for a week or two. No intervention needed.

**Everyone else** -- the 91 club (Sundin, Chlup, Jackman, Klesla, Nash, Chistov, Gaborik, Afinogenov, Mogilny) -- are all at or near band and climbing. The room is fine on a Saturday heading into a home game against a 2-5 Atlanta club.

## Role composition

The units are built correctly for their roles on a development-priority night against a 2-5 Atlanta team; the weakness in L4 and K2 is a roster problem, not an arrangement problem.

**L1** is the obvious strength. Sundin and Gaborik carry 93 and 99 in scoring, Jackman brings 91 checking on the blue line, and the unit mean of 77 in checking with a best of 93 means he is single-handedly holding the defensive floor. No change needed.

**L2** is a speed line and built to be one. Chlup at 79 faceoffs is the best option available at that position, and the 95/99 speed spread means this line wins transitions rather than draws. Chistov at 92 playmaking is the engine. The stamina floor of 58 is the concern — Hainsey at 58 and Eminger carrying that mean means this line will be gassed late in games. That is a minutes question, not a composition one.

**L3** has Richards at 90 scoring and 77 faceoffs carrying both offensive and draw duties, with Nash at 81 checking as the defensive anchor. The 60/77 faceoff mean is acceptable because Richards handles most of them. Alexeev at 0.55 pts/g outproducing Chistov (0.29) is an unresolved role mismatch I flagged in April and still stands, but he is dressed and playing.

**L4** is the weakest unit: checking mean 61, toughness mean 57, faceoff mean 57. Spezza at 0.32 pts/g with POTE 99 is stuck in a role that doesn't suit him, and Lundmark and Brendl cannot carry checking or draws. This line will lose its zone draws and get hemmed in. I am not changing it tonight because this is a development game and these are the minutes they need, but the line is functionally a third checking unit that cannot check.

**K2** — Spezza, Hainsey, Klesla, Brendl — has a checking mean of 65. Klesla at his best (99 speed, presumably strong defensive grade) is the only reason this unit functions at all. The forwards on it bring 75 checking between them. Roberts at 83 is the obvious upgrade at forward, but he is scratched, and on a development night I will not pull him back in to fix a structural gap that should be filled by a trade deadline acquisition or a new face in camp.

**Roster gap, restated:** We have four checkers above 80 on the entire roster — Jackman 91, Roberts 83 (scratched), McCabe 82 (scratched), Nash 81. We have no player above 71 in toughness outside Jackman. We have one faceoff specialist (Sundin at 94) and two decent options (Wallin 87 scratched, Chlup 79). The fourth line and second PK cannot be fixed by rearrangement because the players simply do not exist on this roster in sufficient number. This was flagged in April and remains unresolved.

## Opponent matchup

The question this phase answers: does Atlanta's lineup demand any change to how we're built? Short answer: no. The pairings are already right.

**Kovalchuk and Heatley** are the only threat worth naming. OVR 92 and 91, both 99 speed, both 99 hero, playing together on their top line with Savard (FACE 89) at centre. That's a genuinely elite first line. But our first defensive pair (Jackman OVR 86 with CHKG 93, Klesla OVR 87 with SPEE 99) is auto-paired with our first forward line, which means it also faces their first forward line. Our best D against their best F is already the structure the game gives us. No re-ordering needed.

**Their rest is ordinary.** Second line OVR 78 centre, third and fourth lines in the 70s. Their whole team scores 2.00 per game and they're 2-5-1. Their power play is 1 for 28, so our penalty kill gets a quiet night. We are not facing a quality opponent as a club even if their top six is.

**Goalie:** Luongo (OVR 97) starts. Their Dafoe is 85, no need to escalate. Check the fatigue icon before confirming per January 19 order.

**D-man assessment for this game:** Jackman and Klesla match Kovalchuk/Heatley well on attributes. Eminger and Hainsey handle the second line comfortably. No one is exposed by this matchup. No change to end-of-season sell order based on this opponent.

## Owed

**Item #1: Defenceman trade analysis, updated for the game at ATL on Monday.**

**Jackman** stays on the sell list and the case got stronger. 10 points in 10 games at 26.1 MPG is still 1.00 pts/g against his 0.48 career rate. Last time I raised this (Oct 16) the sample was 4 games. At 10 games a buyer can see it is not noise. $0.70M x 2 makes him a pure rental asset: any playoff club picks up two years of a hot second-pair D for pennies. Sell deadline or now.

**Klesla** is a new flag. 2 points in 10 games at 25.4 MPG is 0.20 pts/g. That is not a slump, that is a 10-game sample. He is eating second-pair minutes alongside Jackman and producing fourth-pair numbers. At $0.90M x 1 year he is an expiring rental: either he finds it by January or we move him at the deadline for whatever draft capital we can get.

**Eminger** went from "0.36 pts/g and sliding" to zero points in 4 games at 20.2 MPG. At 21 with $2.20M x 4 locked, nobody is taking that contract for a D who cannot produce. His trade value is dropping each week we hold him. If no one will take the money, scratch him and stop wasting a roster spot.

**McCabe** unchanged: 30, $3.00M x 3, 0 GP this season. Dead weight on the sell list.

**Colaiacovo** is a new watch. 0 points in 10 games at 13.4 MPG, $1.40M x 4. At 22 he still has room but zero over ten is starting to look like the ceiling, not the floor.

**Who stays:** Fischer (GM's keeper, 0.67 pts/g), Kaberle (GM's keeper, star D), Stahle (21, cheap, 0.30 pts/g in a sheltered role), Hainsey (24, $1.40M x 6, 0.50 pts/g on 20 MPG). No changes to the keep list since last time.

**The change since last delivery:** Klesla enters the sell-or-fix bucket with a full 10-game sample. Jackman's window matures from "hot streak" to "sustained hot rate." Eminger's production has flatlined entirely.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-10-27
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-10-27

Toronto 7-2-0, 14 pts after 9 games.

## Role coverage

Toughness is the one role on this roster that has no fix — internal or near — and the one where age makes every other role a ticking clock within two seasons.

**Roberts** is the internal fix the Coach already ordered: 86 CHKG, 88 overall, 90 clutch, 98 durability at 39. Lining him on K2 adds the checking anchor L4 lacks and gives the penalty kill a body who won't break. The issue is longevity. Roberts is a one-year bandage on a structural checking gap.

**McCabe** is the second internal check available: 86 CHKG, 94 ENDU, 30 years old, not currently lined. Lining him alongside Roberts gives the club three 80+ checkers in units simultaneously (Jackman 87, Roberts 86, McCabe 86). That closes the Coach's L4 gap without any trade, but only for as long as McCabe plays.

**Wallin** (83 FACE, 25, not lined) is the only 80+ faceoff man behind Sundin 90. Lining him on L3 or L4 gives a draw-taker on every line, which Sundin alone cannot cover across four units.

**Koltsov** (92 speed, 24, not lined) and **Fischer** (89 speed, 82 CHKG, 25, not lined in this reading but confirmed top-pair D by the Coach on Oct 24) are the speed-and-checking young wingers on the shelf. Koltsov especially — 92 speed at 24 with no games — is the cheapest depth the club is not using.

**Gaborik** is the paradox: 92 overall, 98 speed, 90 clutch, 23 years old, on a healthy scratch. That is not a coverage gap; it is a usage failure the Coach already flagged. The role is covered on paper.

The hard truth is the age curve. Mogilny (94 scoring, 36), Sundin (92 scoring, 91 playmaking, 34), Roberts (88 scoring, 39), and Jackman (87 checking, 24) mean the top of scoring, playmaking, and clutch all walk within one to two years. The toughness gap cannot be patched because no player on the roster exceeds 75 TOUG. Jackman is the only young 80+ checker.

Two things remain missing that this roster cannot produce: an 80+ toughness forward, and a second faceoff man behind Sundin unless Wallin is lined. Wallin is internal. Toughness is not.

## Trajectory

The question this phase answers: can Toronto sustain this roster through 2008 without a forced collapse, and what are the two or three contract decisions that determine whether they do.

**The age shape is healthy.** Toronto carry 13 players at 23 or under, 16 aged 24-29, and only 5 veterans (30+). The manual's target is 5-7 veterans and roughly 20 young players. This is the manual's shape. The problem is not age; it is one contract, one summer, and one scoring cliff.

**Gaborik** is the largest single financial risk. $11.90M/year on a 5-year deal running through 2010, and he is at 3 points in 8 games (0.38 pts/g). Richards at 0.67 pts/g costs $6.70M. Chlup at 0.89 pts/g costs $2.34M. The game does not allow mid-contract renegotiation, so the GM is locked to this salary for four more years no matter what. If Gaborik produces 0.50+ over a full season the contract is fine for a top-six winger. If he stays at 0.38 it becomes $47.6M of dead money across years 2-5. The Coach's 15-game threshold (0.35 rate) gives a decision point in late November, and at that point the only lever is trade value, which erodes with every scratched game.

**The 2006 summer is the one to prepare for now.** Nine contracts expire after this season, worth $15.44M combined. The critical four are **Luongo** ($1.60M, POTE 97), **Chlup** ($2.34M, POTE 95, 0.89 pts/g at 19), **Spezza** ($1.00M, POTE 99, 3 GP), and **Klesla** ($0.90M, POTE 97, playing every night). All four must be locked on 5-6 year deals in July 2006. Together their current salary is $5.84M; at market rates they could demand $14-18M combined, roughly doubling. The three to shed are **Mogilny** ($5.50M, 36, POTE 55), **Tucker** ($1.30M, 30, zero games, zero points), and **Ouellet** ($0.90M, backup without a path). That sheds $7.70M, offsetting most of the raise exposure.

**The 4-year cluster ($37.40M) expires summer 2009 and is not a problem.** By then Richards is 29, Nash 25, Chistov 26, Eminger 25, Colaiacovo 26, Alexeev 27. They are entering their primes. The one exception is Sundin, who will be 38 on $8.40M. That is a 2009 decision, not a 2006 one.

**The scoring cliff is real but not this year's problem.** Sundin (34), Mogilny (36), and Roberts (39) carry the veteran scoring. Mogilny walks in 2006, Roberts in 2007. No player under 26 is currently producing enough to absorb them at once. Chlup (0.89) and Richards (0.67) are on pace, but they are two players, not three. The Iginla target from last spring remains the structural answer, but that is a July 2006 conversation when CGY's expiring situation clarifies.

**Finances leave room.** Payroll $89.94M, revenue $52.93M, profit $34.62M. The club is generating $34.62M in annual profit. Re-signing the four young players and shedding the three veterans changes the arithmetic only slightly. There is no ceiling preventing an acquisition; the only constraint is whether the return on the player is worth the salary.

**Draft capital is three picks: first, second, third (own).** The January 2005 note about having nothing better than a fourth-rounder is outdated. Three picks is adequate ammunition for a February 2006 deal or a June 2006 move. The first-rounder is the single most tradeable asset, and if the club is not in the playoffs it likely lands top-10.

## Calendar

The question this phase answers is what we do before March 19 and what we do with nine expiring contracts this summer, and the answer depends on whether the first nine games hold.

At 7-2-0 and first in the East, we are building toward being buyers at the deadline. The Coach's L4 checking mean of 63 and toughness of 58 is his stated unfixable gap, and that is the one hole the deadline should fill if the record holds through January. Negotiations open late February per standing order. There is nothing to execute in October.

**Mogilny** is the summer's biggest number: 36 years old, $5.50M, 89 overall. He is the single highest payroll item on the roster and at his age no renewal beyond 1–2 years makes sense. The over-80 pick mechanic works on him — move him at the deadline for a pick or a young player from a non-contender and clear $5.50M. If nobody gives value, let him walk in July. Either way, he does not come back at $5.50M.

**Chlup** is 19, 1.00 pts/g on 21.6 MPG, $2.34M. He is the franchise centre. Five to six years, locked first, same week as Luongo. His current salary at 19 will not survive renewal, but the contract years matter more than the dollar.

**Luongo** is 26, $1.60M, our number-one goalie with the best grades on the roster. Five to six years, same week as Chlup. Tellqvist behind him is a clear step down, so this lock protects the position.

**Spezza** at 22, $1.00M, POTE 99 is the development gamble. The Coach gave him 7 MPG on L4 on October 24, which is better than zero but below the 14 MPG threshold. If he shows 0.40+ pts/g by January, renew on 5–6 years. If not, he is a February trade chip alongside Tucker.

**Koltsov** at 24, $1.10M and **Klesla** at 23, $0.90M are affordable young pieces. Renew on 3–4 years if they earn minutes; move if they are not in the plans by February.

**St. Jacques** at 25, $0.80M is depth defenceman currency. The Bell package to Chicago needs him plus Tucker plus a third-rounder. If that deal executes in February, he is gone. If not, renew on 2 years or let him walk.

**Tucker** at 30, 79 overall, $1.30M sits below the 80 threshold, so the pick mechanic does not work. The Coach's checking complaints and his age make him the next trade chip after Mogilny. He is a piece in packages, not a renewal.

**Ouellet** at 24, $0.90M is the backup. The standing order says find a high-90s goalie from a non-contender. Until that happens, renew him on 2 years as interim cover.

The pick situation has changed since last season's January note: we own our first-, second- and third-round picks for the June 2006 draft. That is real currency for February packages and removes the old constraint that every proposal must be funded purely by players.

## League scan

The gap the Coach can't close internally is an 80+ toughness forward on the bottom six; the gap the trajectory exposes is what happens to our scoring when Mogilny walks in 2006 and Sundin and Roberts follow. The shortlist below targets both, ranked by fit against what we actually need and what the seller would accept.

**Bertuzzi** is the best player on any expiring deal in the league right now. 10 points in 8 games (1.25 pts/g) on 24.3 MPG for VAN, who sit at 2-3-1 with 13 expiring contracts and the lowest payroll in the league at $46.36M. He is a RW who plays top minutes, which means he fills the scoring-depth hole AND gives us a top-six body while Gaborik's contract makes him unusable as a trade chip. The question is whether his toughness (from disc data, mid-80s) clears the 80 threshold. Even if it doesn't, his production makes him the single most impactful acquisition available.

**Jovanovski** at 93 TOUG, 94 CHKG, 89 base on 35.3 MPG is the D-side toughness fix. VAN are the same desperate seller (13 expiring, lowest payroll), and he's 29 on $2.30M expiring. He gives us a second top-pair D alongside Jackman who can hit, block, and contribute offensively (5 pts in 8). The cost is that we'd be trading picks to VAN who are rebuilding, so they'll want young bodies or premium picks.

**Bell** is the cheap version of the toughness-and-faceoff fix. 88 TOUG, 82 FACE, 80 base at 25 on $0.90M expiring at CHI (5 pts, 8 expiring, $24.94M profit). He's a LW, so he slots on L3 or L4. His production is modest (3 pts in 5) but the grades solve the problem the Coach says is unfixable. The package we discussed (Tucker plus St. Jacques plus R3) remains the right shape; CHI's profit means they don't need money, they need dressing-room bodies.

**McLaren** at 89 TOUG, 93 CHKG on 18.7 MPG for SJ (14 expiring, $66.24M payroll) is the highest-checking defenseman on the most motivated seller in the league. The earlier note classified him as a forward; he's actually a D. Still valuable: he gives a physical top-four pairing partner for Jackman or Fischer and SJ have the most urgent sell-down pressure.

**Stuart** at 87 base, POTE 91, 25 years old, $1.80M expiring, 32.7 MPG for SJ is the young-D upgrade. If we're buying one defenseman for this season AND beyond, he's the one. The cost is high (SJ want premium for a 25-year-old first-pair D), but his ceiling is higher than Jovanovski's.

**Heatley** at 91 base, 82 TOUG, 24, $1.10M expiring at ATL (5 pts, 6 expiring) is the superstar scorer option. His 7 points in 7 games at 21.4 MPG is solid. ATL cannot retain both him and Kovalchuk. The package discussed (Spezza plus Koltsov plus R1) is steep but he's the kind of player who makes the 2007 and 2008 core complete. The risk is Spezza's value dropping further with low minutes.

**Doan** at 86 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 87 base, 28, $2.40M is the expensive top-six winger toughness fix. PHX are 1-6-0 with 9 expiring and will need to deal him. He's the most complete package of toughness and scoring in one body, but $2.40M on top of our $89.94M payroll is a stretch, and at 28 his ceiling is set.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: what packages can we bring to a seller that both close the toughness gap and survive the other GM's logic, given that we are 7-2-0 and contending?

The query result on **Bertuzzi** changes the priority. He carries TOUG 83 and CHKG 87, both above 80, alongside 94 base and 1.25 pts/g. He is the only player in the league who solves the toughness gap and the scoring bridge in one transaction, and VAN's desperation at 2-3-1 with 13 expiring makes him movable. **Stuart's toughness is not what we thought:** the query shows TOUG 72, not 80+. He does not solve the checking problem. Drop him from the shortlist.

**Bertuzzi** for **Tucker + R2**. We give a 30-year-old with 0 GP and $1.30M expiring (the GM's designated chip) plus our second-rounder. VAN at 2-3-1 with $22.87M in expiring payroll want draft capital for their rebuild and Tucker gives them a CHKG 92 body for the remainder. The net payroll swing is +$1.30M for us. He is a rental: POTE 58, INJU 50, age 30, $2.60M expiring. We get him for 30 games, use him through the playoffs, and he walks. The guide confirms "any player above 80 overall you do not intend to re-sign can be traded for a draft pick," which means VAN's AI should price him near one round pick. Tucker plus a round-2 is close to that. Acceptance uncertain, but the logic is clean.

**Jovanovski** for **Hainsey + R3**. TOUG 91, CHKG 92 on a $2.30M expiring deal makes him the best defensive D available. Hainsey is 24, POTE 97, six years of control, and sitting at 3 GP with 0 points. VAN get a keepable asset they can develop; we get a rental top-pair D for the playoff stretch. Net payroll +$0.90M. The risk is that VAN value Hainsey's POTE 97 and resist the deal, or demand a first-rounder. If they push back, walk away; Hainsey is surplus but not a chip the GM should give up lightly.

**Bell** for **Tucker + St. Jacques**, no pick. If Bertuzzi does not land, this is the fallback. 88 TOUG, 82 FACE, 80 base, $0.90M expiring. Two expiring bodies with CHKG 92 and CHKG 84 respectively give CHI dressing-room depth. CHI have $23.35M profit so they don't need salary relief, but they have 13 expiring contracts and need players who can dress tonight. No draft capital leaves our building.

**If none land:** line McCabe and Roberts on K2 together for three 80+ checkers on the ice simultaneously (Jackman 90, Roberts 86, McCabe 89). Wallin on L3 for the faceoff draw (83 FACE). The toughness gap shrinks from "unfixable" to "one line still thin." Survive the regular season with those internal patches, reassess in February when the seller pool widens, and target July 2006 when Bertuzzi's equivalent might hit the market.



**On the deliverable owed:** "Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window" is resolved. Luongo is on our roster (26, $1.60M, POTE 97, 5 GP). The GM's standing orders of 2005-02-19 ("Goalies are solved. Done. Do not revisit.") and 2005-03-19 ("Close all goalie monitoring") close this task. No further action taken.

## Owed

**Task #2 — Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window.** This task is closed. The GM killed it on 2005-03-19 ("Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks"), Luongo was acquired by Toronto during the 2004-05 season, and he is now our number one at 97 overall with 5 games played this year. DiPietro remains at NYI at 88 overall, 24, $1.10M expiring, 7 games played. He is not our target anymore because we solved the problem directly by acquiring Luongo. Nothing to monitor. The task is delivered as resolved.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-10-27
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-10-27

Next game vs ANA on Friday 28 October 2005.

## Development opportunity

**Is every young player getting the games he has earned?** At 9 games in, most are. But there is one glaring mismatch and one overload that the numbers make impossible to ignore.

**Alexeev** is the clear case. Two games played, two points — 1.00 pts/g — and he is dressed on the third line yet appeared in only 22% of games. Last season he outproduced dressed wingers Chistov and Upshall and stayed a scratch, and I flagged it in April. Now he is back at it: a 1.00 rate on 9.5 MPG while Chistov (0.56 on 15.7) and Nash (0.56 on 16.4) hold the spots he is competing for. The opportunity is there but the game is not coming to him. He needs a real role, not a spot dress.

**Klesla** at 23 is playing 26.1 minutes a night on the first pair. That is the same concentration problem I flagged in October with Jackman and Klesla eating 56% of D minutes. At 26.1 MPG he is carrying a veteran's load and producing 0.22 pts/g. The minutes are hurting his development more than helping. Colaiacovo and Stahle are both on the third pair at 13.1 MPG; some of Klesla's ice should migrate to them.

**Chlup** is earning everything and more: 8 points in 9 games on 19.6 MPG at 19. The only question is whether he should be higher than the second line, but that is a roles conversation, not a development one.

**Nash** at 0.56 pts/g on 16.4 MPG is an improvement from last season's 0.43 collapse. Full games, morale 91. He is on track.

**Chistov** at 5 points in 9 on 15.7 MPG on the second line is exactly where a 22-year-old should be. No concern.

**Stahle and Colaiacovo** each play 13.1 MPG on the third pair, full games, morale 91. Colaiacovo's 0 points in 9 is a watch item but not a crisis for a 22-year-old defenseman on the third pair. Stahle at 3 in 9 is fine for a third-pair blue-liner.

**Eminger** at 3 games, 19.0 MPG, 0 points. The sample is too small to judge production. The concern is why he is only in 33% of games at a 19 MPG clip when he plays. He needs consistency in the lineup to build rhythm.

**Gaborik** has the opportunity (first line, 20.4 MPG) but 3 points in 8 is 0.38 pts/g, thin for a first-line winger at 23. No action — let it play — but it is on my radar.

**Gardener, Spacek, Upshall** are all scratched and all in the collapse pattern I documented: 4-6 MPG, morale 76, minimal production. The scratches are the right call. Gardener has 0 points in 6 games; Spacek and Upshall each have 3 in 6 but on ice too thin to build anything. Carrying them at these minutes only deepens the hole.

**Spezza** remains in the March pattern: 0 points, 4.7 MPG, morale 76, POTE 99. Known issue, and my March note stands: this is a camp decision, not an in-season one.

## Development trends

The question this phase answers: who is moving up, who is sinking, and what should the GM change his plans around heading into November.

**Chlup** at 19 is the clearest riser: 0.88 pts/g on 21.2 MPG across 9 games. The tiny dip from 1.00 to 0.88 is noise from his one-game opener. He is producing a first-line rate with first-line minutes, and the trend since April (0.62 → 0.88 → 0.88) says he is still climbing. I have recommended moving him to first-line centre four times in the past week; the GM has not acted. I will keep saying it.

**Fischer** at 25 is the surprise: 0.00 to 0.80 pts/g while his minutes jumped from 10 to 21.8. That is roughly 5 points in 6 games as a regular now. The GM's December insistence that Fischer is a keeper looks right every week. No action needed; he is earning his role on his own.

**Stahle** at 21 went from 6 to 14 MPG and from zero points to 0.38 pts/g. He is getting more of the game and producing with it. That is what development looks like when minutes follow performance. Let him keep growing into the 14 MPG slot.

**Jackman** at 24 is at 1.00 pts/g on 25 MPG across 9 games. His career rate is 0.48. The minutes are down from 41 last window (good, the overload is easing) but the production rate has not regressed. My October 16 note stands: his trade value peaks now, while a buyer sees the rate not the history.

**Gardener, Spacek, Upshall, Lundmark**: all four have collapsed into the pattern I flagged on October 22. Gardener from 16 to 2.2 MPG with zero points. Spacek from 17 to 3.6. Upshall from 16 to 3.8. Lundmark from 11 to 4.7. None produced enough to justify keeping them in the rotation. The systemic fix is the camp rule; in-game, the fix is stop dressing them and give those minutes to the players who are climbing.

**Chistov** at 22 went from 2 points in his opener to 0.38 pts/g across 9 games on 16.9 MPG. The hot start is gone. 0.38 on nearly 17 MPG is below what a third-line winger should return. He is outplaying that rate's share of the ice.

**Afinogenov** at 26 continues his three-year slide: 1.17 in 2003-04, 0.73 last year, 0.50 in this 9-game window. Minutes are flat at 16.5. The system-fit problem flagged in May is not fixing itself. Plan around his decline when assembling next year's top six.

**Sundin** at 34 has 1.12 pts/g on 21.2 MPG. At 36, Mogilny sits at 0.62 on 20.6 MPG. Both are carrying production above what their ages should allow. Enjoy it in November, plan around its expiry in the offseason.

**Roberts** at 39 is at 0.29 pts/g on 13.7 MPG. Minutes are managed down, which is right. His trend is the one to watch heading into January: if minutes drop further or production flatlines, that winger slot needs an answer.

## Morale watch

The room is mostly healthy: the win lifted everyone at 91 by nine points and the scratched top players sit at 90 or above. Two pockets of concern remain, both at the bottom of the forward depth.

**Richards** is the one I can fix tonight. He's at morale 78 on 11.9 MPG with 6 points in 9 games (0.67 pts/g). At an 88 overall he belongs in the 17 MPG band; he's running five minutes short. The morale cost is -2 off every grade, which on his hands and speed numbers is the difference between a usable third-line centre and a replacement. His linemate Nash gets 16.4 MPG on the same line, so the minutes aren't a line problem, they're a usage problem within the line. Give him first-shift faceoffs and more PP time to push him toward 15.

**Brendl** (76, 5.8 MPG, 1 pt in 4) and **Spezza** (76, 4.7 MPG, 0 pts in 3) are both below the 10 MPG floor their likely calibre demands. Morale at 76 costs -4 off every grade, which makes them worse at the exact job they're being asked to do. Spezza is repeating last season's pattern: minutes collapse, production dies, morale sinks. I cannot fix both without cutting a working forward, and the GM has been deliberately rotating young players through these slots since January. The room is too shallow to spread more minutes without hurting the top six. This is a roster-depth problem, not a lines problem.

**Spacek, Upshall, Gardener** are scratched at 76 with 3 and 0 points on 5.8 and 4.5 MPG from earlier in the season. Their morale is low because they're not playing, and the GM is intentionally giving those minutes to others. Not a lines fix.

## Role composition

The question here is whether our units are built from players suited to their jobs, and whether the roster holds enough of each role. Against ANA this matters because their top six is skilled enough to punish a soft penalty kill.

**K2** is the problem. Checking mean 65, stamina mean 56. Spezza, Hainsey, Klesla, Brendl together give up too much in both departments against a Fedorov-driven power play. McCabe (CHKG 85, ENDU 83, 84 overall) is scratched and sitting right there. Swap him onto the second kill and the checking mean jumps toward 75 and stamina toward 68. This is a composition fix, not a chemistry one; McCabe is a D and doesn't break any forward line.

**K1** at checking 78 mean is acceptable. Eminger, Chlup, Jackman, Chistov gives us Jackman at 91 anchoring it. No change.

**L1 through L3** are fine as built. L1 has the scoring, playmaking and clutch. L2 is our speed line at 95 mean. L3 gets Nash's 81 checking as the anchor. None of these have an arrangement problem.

**L4** has checking 61 mean and toughness 57 mean. That is a roster gap, not a lines problem. I flagged this in April and it has not changed: no forward outside L1-L2 checks above 75. The fourth line cannot be made into a checking unit with these personnel in any arrangement. That is the GM's problem to solve.

**Faceoffs** are thin below Sundin. Richards wins draws at 76 on L3, which is passable. Chlup at 79 on L2 is adequate. No one else is above 76 among dressed forwards. Wallin at 87 is scratched but his checking is 55, so he is not a PK or shutdown option. No fix available.

## Opponent matchup

The question for Friday: do we adjust anything for ANA, or do we just play our game? Answer is the latter, with one exception at goalie.

**Their lineup is thin everywhere except two spots.** Fedorov at 86 is still a real centre at 35, and Giguere at 93 in net can steal a night. Everyone else on their top nine reads between 68 and 75. Their fourth line (McDonald, Niedermayer, Smirnov) averages 69. We have four lines above that average. Their PP is 1-for-45, which means they generate nothing on the man advantage.

**Our top three lines are a full tier above their top three.** Sundin/Gaborik/Mogilny at 92/99/89 faces Fedorov/Kozlov/Lydman at 86/74/73. The gap at right wing alone is 25 points. Our second line (Chlup 87, Chistov 87, Afinogenov 84) faces Stajan/Domi/Cole at 70/70/75. Our third (Richards 86, Nash 85, Alexeev 78) faces Brown/Dimitrakos/Prospal at 71/68/73. I cannot construct a matchup adjustment that improves on simply putting our best available out there.

**Goalie: Luongo starts.** Giguere at 93 with 95 speed, 95 agility, 96 endurance is a real obstacle. Telling him we're putting out Tellqvist at 73 is giving away the game. Luongo at 97 gives us the best chance to outlast him. Check his fatigue icon before confirming per the January 19 rule.

**D assessment (deliverable #1):** No change this game. Jackman at 86 (CHKG 93, TOUG 92) and Klesla at 87 (SPEE 99) are the pair to run. Klesla's ENDU at 59 remains the long-term concern — if we ride him past 30 MPG he will crack, same pattern as before. Eminger stays at the bottom of the sell list (ENDU 50, $2.2M x4). Colaiacovo at 76 with ENDU 52 is the next-weakest of the remaining four and is the candidate to move if a deal materialises. No change for Friday though — we need bodies on the ice and Stahle/Colaiacovo can handle Brown/Dimitrakos/Prospal on the third pairing.

## Owed

**Defenceman review for ANA game (owed item #1).** Nine games in, here's the blue-line read and who goes at season's end.

**Jackman** — 9 points in 9 games on 26.8 MPG at $0.70M x 2. I said on October 16th he was in a sell window built on a 4-game hot streak. I'm revising: at 9 games and 1.00 pts/g on the cheapest contract on the roster, the sell case is dead. You're selling a bargain. Keep him.

**Klesla** — 2 points in 9 games on 26.1 MPG. That's 0.22 pts/g absorbing second-highest minutes on the blue line. He's 23, 87 OVR, $0.90M x 1 (expiring). This is the biggest concern on the back end. His trade value with an 87 and one year left peaks now; if he's not producing by January he becomes a rental rather than a piece. Not a "sell today" call, but the window is closing.

**Fischer** — 4 points in 6 games, morale 91, GM's keeper. Nothing to say.

**Kaberle** — 2 points in 6 on 19.5 MPG. Slow start but the GM has him locked. Morale 91. No issue.

**Stahle** — 3 points in 9 on 13.1 MPG at 21, $0.97M. Developing on schedule for a young pair. Keep.

**Colaiacovo** — 0 points in 9 on 13.1 MPG. New information since last delivery: the zero streak is now nine games. At 22 and 76 OVR he may just be sheltered, but he's contributed nothing in any measurable way. Watch him through November; if he's still scoreless at 20 games the 13 MPG is wasted.

**Eminger** — 0 points in 3 on 19.0 MPG, $2.20M x 4. The four-year lock confirmed in May makes him nearly unsellable at any return. He's on the "try to move" list permanently but nobody takes that deal for nothing. Low priority.

**McCabe** — 0 GP, $3.00M x 3, 84 OVR, age 30, morale 90. He's healthy and not in the lineup. He's the clear end-of-season departure. Dead money on a club that needs his minutes from younger bodies.

**Hainsey** — 0 points in 3 on 19.0 MPG, $1.40M x 6. Long deal, no production, but small sample and cheap. Not urgent.

**Who goes at season's end:** McCabe first (sell now, value decays every month). Klesla second if he's still under 0.40 by January (expiring rental fetches a pick). Eminger third but only if a cap-strapped club absorbs it for a late pick.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-10-24
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-10-24

Toronto 6-2-0, 12 pts after 8 games.

## Role coverage

The toughness gap is confirmed structural: zero players at 80+ TOUG, highest is **Jackman** at 75. No lineup shuffle fixes it. Every other gap the Coach flags, though, has a body already on the roster who is sitting unlined.

**McCabe** has 86 CHKG and 94 ENDU, is 30, and is in no unit. The Coach says L4 checking at 63 is "not fixable by moving players" and that there is "no body above 84 checking who isn't needed on L3." That is wrong. McCabe is above 84 and is not on L3. He is on the bench. Line him.

**Tucker** at 83 CHKG, 30, is also unlined. Between McCabe and Tucker, L4 gets two checking bodies without trading a chip. The Coach's constraint about "not needed on L3" simply does not apply to either man.

**Wallin** at 83 FACE, 25, is unlined. The club has one 80+ faceoff man actually in the lineup: **Sundin** at 90, who is 34. If Sundin's minutes come down or he leaves in two years, the next-best draw is **Chlup** at 75. Wallin at 83 fills that hole tonight without a trade.

**Koltsov** at 92 SPEE, 24, is on the roster and unlined. The speed depth is fine on paper (25 at 80+), but **Mogilny** at 36 and **Sundin** at 34 carry the top of the speed chart. The young speed is being wasted.

**Roberts** at 39 carries 98 INJU and 86 CHKG. He is the only player above 35 the club can rely on to play every night. The Coach wants him on K2 for checking — that makes sense given 86 CHKG — but the bigger issue is what happens when Roberts is done. There is no one else at his durability grade.

**The age cliff in scoring is real.** Mogilny (94 SCOR, 36) and Sundin (92 SCOR, 34) are the top two. After them: Gaborik (92, 23, but 0.29 pts/g and the Coach is reducing his ice), Afinogenov (90, 26), and then a drop. In two seasons, the club needs a first-liner and the pipeline does not show one at 85+ scoring right now.

**Goalies are covered.** Luongo at 1.61 GAA and .944 SV in 5 GP is the number one. Ouellet is adequate depth. The monitoring task the GM opened on January 19 is closed — Luongo is here, and the March 19 order ended all goalie surveillance.

The only acquisition that cannot be solved internally is toughness. That keeps Heatley (82 TOUG, 91 base, 24, $1.10M) and Bell (88 TOUG, 82 base, 25, $0.90M) as the February targets.

## Trajectory

The question this phase answers: can Toronto carry its current payroll into the next three summers without being forced into a fire sale, and does the contract calendar create a cliff?

**Yes, the roster is the right shape age-wise.** 29 of 34 players are 29 or under, and the 30-33 bracket has only McCabe and Tucker. But the money tells a different story than the birthdays.

**Gaborik** is the single largest trajectory risk on the roster. $11.90M per year on a 5-year deal means he is 13.2% of payroll for 2 points in 7 games (0.29 pts/g on 20 MPG per the Coach). At POTE 90 there is a scenario where he earns that contract — a 0.85+ rate makes $11.90M a bargain. The scenario where he stays at 0.29 through year two and the club cannot trade him because his value has cratered is the nightmare. This is the number one thing to watch, not as a line decision but as a balance sheet question: five more years of $11.90M for a fringe producer would eat the 2009 re-signing budget alive.

**Sundin at 34 on $8.40M with 4 years left** means he will be 38 at contract expiry. He is producing 1.00 pts/g at 8 games, which is still good, but $8.40M for a 37-year-old in year three of this deal is the second-worst money on the roster. There is nothing to do about it — 4 years is locked. But it means the club cannot afford Gaborik to fail AND Sundin to decline simultaneously.

**The 34+ trio costs $18.80M** (Sundin $8.40M, Mogilny $5.50M, Roberts $4.90M). Mogilny walks in July 2006, saving $5.50M. Roberts walks or is traded in July 2007, saving $4.90M. So the natural decay takes the worst money off by 2007 without any forced move. The problem is that Sundin cannot be unwound.

**July 2006 is the defining renewal summer.** Nine contracts worth $15.44M expire simultaneously. The non-negotiables are Chlup ($2.34M, 1.00 pts/g at 19, POTE 95) and Luongo ($1.60M, POTE 97). Both must be locked on 5-6 years. At their current rates those renewals might cost $5-6M each, which is affordable. Klesla (23, 0.88 pts/g, POTE 97, $0.90M) is a third priority. The rest — Mogilny, Tucker, Koltsov, Spezza (if still undressed), Ouellet, St. Jacques — are walk-or-trade, not renew-or-lose.

**The 2009 cluster is the one that could bite.** 11 players totaling $37.40M all expire that summer: Richards, Chistov, Nash, Eminger, Kaberle, Alexeev, Upshall, Colaiacovo, Wallin, Abid, Sundin. By then Chistov will be 26, Nash 25, Eminger 25, Richards 29 — all entering their prime and commanding peak salaries. Re-signing even eight of them at a 50% raise from current means a jump from $37.40M to roughly $45M+ just for that group. If Gaborik's $11.90M is still running and Sundin's is gone, the math still works against $51.25M base revenue plus TV, but the margin shrinks. The defense: spread these renewals across multiple summers where possible, or trade the ones whose value peaks before 2009 (Kaberle at 27 with POTE 75 is the obvious one — his ceiling is set and he is $4.10M with 4 years left).

**Payroll against profit is currently safe.** $89.94M payroll against $33.97M profit means the club is not close to a money problem. The concern is purely structural: if Gaborik stays at $11.90M and the 2009 group commands market rates, payroll could push past $100M while production is carried by 19-22 year-olds whose contracts are still on rookie deals. That is a window to exploit, but it closes.

**Draft capital is healthy.** Three picks (R1, R2, R3 from TOR) is enough ammunition for February 2006. The old "no picks beyond 4th" constraint is gone. The R1 funds a single acquisition; the R2 and R3 can be stacked with a player for a second. This is not a rebuild; this is a contender with three chips to improve the bottom six.

**The two moves that protect three seasons:**

1. Lock Chlup and Luongo in July 2006 before their production raises the asking price. At 1.00 pts/g Chlup's renewal will cost more next year than today.

2. Set a 15-game checkpoint on Gaborik. If he is under 0.40 pts/g at 15 games, the club must begin exploring whether $11.90M for a 23-year-old with 30 games is tradeable — because at 40 games of 0.29 rate his value will not support recovering anything close to the salary he costs.

## Calendar

The question is what we do between now and March, and what we do with nine expiring contracts in July. The short answer: nothing until late February, and the summer list has two must-locks, two easy cuts, and three decisions the GM owes by January.

**We are buyers at the deadline.** Toronto sit first in the East at 12 points from 8 games, one point clear of Pittsburgh. The deadline is 146 days out on 2006-03-19. Per the GM's standing order, negotiations open late February. The posture is set: buy for need if we are still in the top eight. If we collapse, the same chips flip to sellers. Either way the chips are the same two men.

**Mogilny** at 36, $5.50M, 90 base is the single biggest financial problem on this roster. He was the centrepiece of the December 2004 package that never executed, and he is here again on a one-year deal. At 90 base he clears the over-80 pick-recovery mechanic: trade him in March and the club gets a draft pick for a player it would otherwise lose for nothing. He saves $5.50M whether he moves or not (he is leaving in July either way), so the question is only whether we get something for him. A non-contender needing a scorer is the right destination.

**Tucker** at 30, $1.30M, 79 base is the other chip the GM identified on 2005-03-19 as one of the only tradable pieces. Under 80, so no pick-recovery mechanic, but a contender looking for a fourth-line winger might take him for a late-round pick or a prospect. He was unlined as of October 16, which makes him a natural throw-in to a larger package.

**Luongo** at 26, 91 base, $1.60M is the first summer lock. The GM closed the goalie question on 2005-03-19 and told me to stop revisiting it. He stays. Re-sign on 5-6 years the same week he becomes eligible. His salary is well below market for a 91-base starting goaltender, so expect his renewal number to jump significantly. Budget $4-5M for a five-year deal.

**Chlup** at 19, 82 base, $2.34M is the second summer lock. The Coach wants him at first-line centre (1.00 pts/g on 21.6 MPG). His current salary is high for a rookie — $2.34M at 19 — but that is a contract the club signed with a prospect, not a market rate. Re-sign on 5-6 years. He and Luongo are the same renewal week, as noted in prior analysis.

**Klesla** at 23, 78 base, $0.90M is a mid-tier blueliner with real minutes. The Coach flags the "Jackman/Klesla minute load" as a problem to solve by elevating Stahle, but Klesla is still contributing defensively. Re-sign on 2-3 years at a modest raise, or move him at the deadline if a package needs a body. I lean toward keeping him; 78 base at 23 is depth that wins cups.

**Ouellet** at 24, 81 base, $0.90M is the over-80 pick-recovery play at goaltender. If Belfour re-signs on a reduced deal, Ouellet is redundant and moves for a pick in March. If Belfour retires, Ouellet is the backup for the playoffs and we let him walk in July knowing we need a new backup. The GM's standing order says Belfour stays if he accepts reduced salary, so the most likely path is: Belfour re-signs cheap, Ouellet moves at the deadline for a pick.

**Spezza** at 22, 73 base, $1.00M with POTE 99 is the hardest call. The Coach's five-game clock expired (he logged 0 GP through 5 games). The Coach now demands 14+ MPG or he stops being dressed. If the GM decides to develop him, re-sign on 2-3 years at $1.0-1.2M and dress him. If the GM sides with the Coach that a POTE without a game is worthless, trade him in March — 73 base is under 80, so no pick-recovery, but a team rebuilding might take a 22-year-old centre with a high scouting number for a late pick. My lean: if Spezza is dressed by November and producing, keep him. If he is still a healthy scratch by January, he is a chip.

**Koltsov** at 24, 68 base, $1.10M is too low to re-sign. He was in the Heatley package proposal as a throw-in. Let him walk in July or use him as a salary-matching body in March.

**St. Jacques** at 25, 66 base, $0.80M is the same story. 66 base is replacement level. Let him walk or include him in the Bell package (which targets CHI's Bell at 80 base, 88 TOUG, $0.90M expiring).

## League scan

The question this phase answers: who across the league gives Toronto the toughness it structurally lacks, and which of their clubs will actually deal him by February? Toronto have zero players above 75 TOUG. That is the gap. Every other hole the Coach flags has an internal answer (McCabe for checking, Wallin for faceoffs, Koltsov for speed). Toughness does not.

**Doan** remains the cleanest target. 87 base, 88 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 88 SPEE, 29, $2.40M expiring. PHX are 0-6-0 with 9 expiring deals and $14.82M profit. They have zero path to re-signing him and no reason to keep a 29-year-old rental on a team going nowhere. The only question is whether they accept a third-rounder plus Tucker or demand a first.

**Hartnell** is the new finding that matters most. 84 overall today, 79 base, 87 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 82 SPEE, LW, age 23, $1.10M expiring, POTE 94. He is not a rental version of the fix — he IS the fix for three seasons if his potential materializes. NSH at 8 points sit in a crowded Eastern race; by February they could be five points out, which puts them in sell mode. A package of Tucker plus a second-rounder is the price to try.

**Bertuzzi** is the most complete player on any seller: 94 base, 89 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 90 SPEE, RW, 30, $2.60M expiring. VAN at 7 points with 13 expiring and the lowest payroll in the league ($46.36M) are in full rebuild. Bertuzzi at 30 with POTE 57 does not fit that timeline. The risk: VAN may not want to deal their best player to a contender. The upside: we hold a first-rounder plus Tucker plus Koltsov. If VAN want to liquidate, this is the deal of the deadline.

**Brewer (SJ)** is the premium blue-line option nobody has flagged yet. 88 base, 82 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 85 SPEE, D, age 26, $6.21M expiring, POTE 83. SJ carry $66.24M payroll with 14 expiring contracts — the most desperate seller in the league. They need to shed $6.21M off a book that will shrink anyway. The catch: matching salary. McCabe ($2.80M) plus Tucker ($1.50M) plus Koltsov ($0.90M) plus R1 is $5.20M in salary, still $1M short. We'd need to add a fourth body or the R2.

**Jovanovski** at 89 base, 93 TOUG, 94 CHKG, D, 29, $2.30M, 1 year on VAN with 13 expiring remains the top blue-line target per the October 12 note. He and Bertuzzi both live at VAN; pursuing both simultaneously is unrealistic since they won't trade two top pieces to the same club in one window. Pick one lane.

**Begin (BUF)** at 95 CHKG, 87 TOUG, 86 FACE, C, 27, $936K expiring is the cheapest way to solve L4 checking and faceoffs in one move. BUF at 7 pts, 1-2-1, 6 expiring are drifting. Tucker plus St. Jacques is the package already noted.

**Rita (EDM)** is a lottery ticket worth a third-round flier. 83 overall today, 91 SPEE, 83 PASS, LW, 24, $1.00M expiring, POTE 99. EDM are 0-3-2 at 4 points. He may never reach 99 but 91 speed at 24 on an expiring $1M deal from a 0-3-2 team is cheap. If we can get him for the R3 plus a bench player, do it.

**Bell** stays on the list at 80 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, LW, 25, $900K expiring from CHI at 3 pts with 8 expiring. The package of Tucker plus St. Jacques plus R3 closes both toughness and faceoff gaps. If Begin is available, he supersedes Bell as the better package (higher CHKG, higher FACE, similar TOUG). Choose one, not both.

**I would not pursue:** Chara (GM veto, standing order), Brewer unless salary matching is solved, or any goalie (March 19 standing order, closed).

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: which two or three packages convert our surplus and our picks into the toughness the roster structurally lacks, before the picks become tradeable at ten games played. We're at eight, so two more games opens the window.

**Begin (BUF)** is the cheapest complete fix on the board. 95 CHKG, 87 TOUG, 86 FACE, C, 27, $936K expiring. Tucker plus St. Jacques is $2.10M in salary going to a club that just pocketed $19.07M in profit and sits at 7 points with six expiring deals. They take on $1.16M net, which their revenue absorbs without a second thought, and they get two bodies who can dress for depth while Begin walks in July regardless. We solve L4 checking and faceoffs in one move and spend no pick. The risk: Begin's base overall is 87 and Tucker's is 79, so the AI might read the value gap as too wide. But salary matches nearly, both players are expiring, and BUF's incentive is shed-or-drift, not maximize.

**Heatley (ATL)** is the highest ceiling. 91 base, 82 TOUG, LW, 24, $1.10M expiring. He is the only target who closes the toughness gap and the scoring bridge at once, because 91 base is top-line production and 82 TOUG clears our zero-80 problem. ATL sit at 2 points with nine expiring and cannot re-sign both him and Kovalchuk. Spezza ($1.00M, POTE 99, Coach's expired five-game clock makes him a chip) plus Koltsov ($1.10M, POTE 94, zero ice this season) plus the TOR first-rounder is a rebuild package that costs ATL nothing in salary and gives them three futures for one rental. The GM must approve Spezza as a trade piece first. Acceptance is uncertain because ATL's GM may value Kovalchuk over Heatley and move the other, leaving this proposal stranded.

**Doan (PHX)** is the best raw grade among sellers. 87 base, 88 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 29, $2.40M expiring. PHX are 0-6-0 with nine expiring and $14.82M profit. They have no path to re-signing a 29-year-old on a zero-win team. Tucker plus Koltsov plus the TOR second-rounder is $2.40M in outgoing salary, an exact match, and Koltsov at POTE 94 is a real future for a club starting from nothing. The cost is giving away Koltsov (unlined, POTE 94, zero minutes) for a one-year rental. If the goal is winning a Cup this spring, that's the right trade. If the goal is 2008, it stings.

These three are mutually exclusive on Koltsov (proposals 2 and 3 both spend him) and on Tucker (proposals 1 and 3 both spend him). Pick one lane. My ranking: Begin first for cost, Heatley second for ceiling, Doan third for the same ceiling as Heatley but one year older and more expensive.

**If none land:** line McCabe (86 CHKG, unlined) and Wallin (83 FACE, unlined) tonight. That fixes checking and faceoffs internally. The toughness gap at 75 TOUG (Jackman, highest on the roster) remains, but the team is 6-2-0. Survival through the regular season does not require 80 TOUG; the playoffs might, and the deadline is March. A second look at sellers in late February is the right next step if these stall.

## Owed

**#2 — Luongo availability and DiPietro monitoring for the goalie trade window:** This task is closed. The GM ordered it shut on 2005-03-19: "Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks. Only trading chips left are Tucker and the 4th round pick." Luongo arrived on our roster and is here now at 97 overall, $1.60M, 1 year left, starting 5 of 8 games. The question the task existed to answer — can we get a high-90s goalie — was resolved by his arrival. There is nothing to monitor.

**DiPietro** (NYI, 24, 89 overall, $1.10M, 0 years left, 6 GP this season) is a note only because he's the same profile we acquired in Luongo: young, cheap, high-base. But he's on an expiring deal with a club that just let him start 6 games at 24. The monitoring task is dead per standing order; if the GM wants a separate scouting flag on DiPietro as a future target, that's a new task.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-10-24
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-10-24

Next game vs NYR on Wednesday 26 October 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether each young player is getting the games he has earned, and the answer splits three ways: four are fully earned and getting them, three are being carried at low minutes while their morale drops, and one is producing but still not dressed.

**Chlup** has earned everything and then some. 8 points in 8 games at 19.6 MPG, 1.00 pts/g at 19 years old. He belongs on the first line by production alone, but his placement is a lines question, not a games-earned question. No development concern.

**Chistov and Nash** are both at 0.63 pts/g on 15.8 and 16.4 MPG respectively, morale 91, fully dressed. They are getting exactly what they've earned. No change.

**Stahle, Colaiacovo, Klesla** are all 8 games, 100% share. Colaiacovo's 0 points in 8 on 13 MPG is thin for a POTE 99 defenseman, but he's getting his games, which is what this phase asks. His production is a watch item, not an opportunity gap.

**Gaborik** has 2 points in 7 games on 20 MPG. That's 0.29 pts/g on a first-line winger. Low, but he's getting every game he could ask for. The issue is production or form, not opportunity.

**Spezza** is the problem. POTE 99, age 22, 7.0 MPG on the fourth line, 0 points, 2 games played, morale 81. Last season his minutes collapsed from 9.1 to 4.8 and he scored at 0.32 pts/g. He's doing it again, one year older. The carrying at 7 MPG is the worst option: not enough ice to develop, enough to rot his morale. Either give him third-line minutes (14+) or stop dressing him. The middle is poison.

**Gardener** is not earning a spot. 0 points, 4.5 MPG, morale 76, scratched. POTE 98 is a scouting opinion, not current ability. He's not producing at any level of responsibility. Stop dressing him and use the roster spot on someone who contributes tonight.

**Spacek and Upshall** are both at 0.50 pts/g on 5.8 MPG with morale 76. They're producing at a reasonable rate but getting scratched anyway. The GM's framework is development in games we can afford and all-out against quality opponents. Against NYR on Wednesday they stay out. The development question is whether either gets a real 12-15 MPG role in the games where we can afford to try them.

**Alexeev** has 2 points in 1 game. Last season he sat at 0.55 pts/g while dressed wingers like Chistov were at 0.29. This season Chistov is at 0.63, so the gap has narrowed. The one-game sample is tiny, but the pattern from last year is real: he scores when he plays and barely plays. He deserves a sustained audition on the bottom six, not spot duty once every seven games.

## Development trends

The question is who's moving and who's stalling across the first ten days of October, because at eight games in the answer matters: a trend this early sets the season's shape.

**Chlup** is 1.00 pts/g on 21.6 MPG at 19 years old. That's been his rate from game one through game eight, no fluctuation. He's already outproducing everyone on this roster except Sundin, and he's doing it at 22.4 years younger. Every night he plays second-line centre is a night we leave points on the board.

**Fischer** at 25 is 0.80 pts/g on 21.8 MPG as a defenceman. Last season he finished at a much lower rate. The GM called him a keeper and said his two-way game justifies it; the production has caught up to the judgement. At 25 on a rising trend he's the best thing on our blue line right now. No change needed, just confirming the trajectory is real.

**Richards** is 0.86 pts/g on 11.3 MPG. Last season he dropped to 0.71 and we flagged it as a system-fit problem. This season he's above that mark and above what I expected from him after two flat years. His minutes are low for his production; at 11 MPG producing 0.86 he's getting away with it, but the trend is positive and the system-fit worry from May may be resolving.

**Sundin** at 34 is 1.14 pts/g on 20.7 MPG. He's our best player right now. No decline signal whatsoever.

**Stahle** at 21 is 0.43 pts/g on 14.0 MPG as a defenceman. Last season he was 0.11 on 24 MPG. The rate quadrupled even as his load came down. He's coming along nicely and the minutes redistribution from Jackman/Klesla is helping him.

**Gaborik** at 23 is the problem forward. 0.29 pts/g on 20.0 MPG. That's the worst production-per-minute on the top two lines by a wide margin. At 23 the expectation is up, not sideways. If he holds below 0.35 through 15 games he doesn't deserve 20 MPG.

**Kaberle** at 27 is 0.20 pts/g on 21.2 MPG. For a defenceman the GM calls a star, that rate is thin. Last season he was 0.50. The drop is real but 6 games is a small window; watch through 15 before panicking.

**Spacek, Gardener, Upshall** are all in the collapse pattern. Spacek went from 17 MPG to 3.6. Gardener from 16 to 2.2. Upshall from 16 to 3.8. None of them scored in the recent window. This is the same systemic issue I flagged in October: young depth forwards get thrown into 16-17 MPG roles, fail to produce, and get buried. The rule holds: scratch them permanently rather than keep them in and out of the lineup.

**Nash** at 21 is 0.57 pts/g on 16.1 MPG. Last season he went from 0.83 to 0.43 on flat minutes. Now he's at 0.57, which is better than last year's finish but still below what his minutes suggest. The system-fit question from last spring is unresolved.

**Roberts** at 39 is 0.29 pts/g on 13.7 MPG. His minutes already dropped from 18 to 13.7 within the recent window. He's still useful on the penalty kill but his even-stroke role is shrinking by itself. Plan around him being a fourth-line/KP specialist by December.

## Morale watch

The room is quiet. Nobody's morale is actively falling. The one problem that predates this week and is still open is Richards.

**Richards** sits at 78 on 11.5 minutes a night. At his calibre he expects around 17, so he is five minutes short every game. This has been stable since October 20th -- no further slide -- but 78 costs him two points off every grade. He's producing 0.75 points a game on the third line; giving him more of the game is the only lever I own, and it means moving him up or swapping with someone on the second.

**Upshall, Spacek, Gardener** are all at 76, scratched, no change. Their morale has bottomed and stopped moving. The GM's January order was to give other young guys space; that decision is still in force. They're not declining further so there's no emergency, but carrying them indefinitely at 76 costs one point off their grades when they do go in.

**Roberts** at 84 on 14.2 MPG, age 39. He's likely getting close to what his current body can handle. Morale is fine and stable. No intervention.

**Everyone else is at 88 or above** with no negative movement. The top nine forwards and the top four D-pairs are all getting their expected minutes. The goalies are content. The healthy scratches (Koltsov 100, St. Jacques 99, Wallin 95, Safronov 95) are not complaining.

No change is needed today beyond what's already recommended on the lines front. Richards stays on the watch list.

## Role composition

The question is whether each unit is built from players suited to its job, and whether the roster has enough bodies to fill all the jobs at all. Against a 4-5 club like NYR, a weak PK or a fourth line that won't check is exposed.

**K2 (penalty kill 2)** — Checking mean 67, toughness mean 59. The four best checkers on the roster are Jackman (92), Roberts (84), McCabe (83, scratched), Nash (82). Roberts is the only one not already on a PK unit, and he's sitting on L3 doing nothing special-teams-wise. Put him on K2 over Brendl. This lifts K2's checking mean and gives the second kill an anchor it currently lacks. I made this call on October 22 and it wasn't taken. Against a quality opponent it's more urgent, not less. Chemistry cost: negligible, special-teams units don't carry line chemistry.

**Jackman** is on the top pair, first power play, and first penalty kill. Three units on a 92-checking defenceman. I cannot see his current minutes this activation, but the October 13 finding flagged him at 33 MPG and the situation hasn't changed. The fix is in-game shift management — give him more bench time on even-strength and let special teams be his load. I won't move him off K1 because there's no adequate replacement; McCabe would be it and he's scratched. Flag this for the GM to watch on the screen.

**L4** — Checking mean 63, toughness mean 58. This is the same structural gap I recorded in April: no forward outside L1-L2 checks above 82, and the two who do (Roberts 84, Nash 82) are both needed on L3. The roster does not hold a fourth-line checker. This is not fixable by rearranging lines. McCabe at 83 checking would fix it if he were dressed. That's a roster decision, not a lines decision.

**L1, L2, L3, P1, P2** — No changes. L1 (checking 78 mean, scoring 92 mean) is the right top-line construction with Jackman as the D anchor. L2 at 95 speed is a transition line that can run with the puck. L3's checking mean of 76 with Roberts and Nash is the real checking line. P1 has the shots and P2 has the speed. All correct.

**D-pair sell-list review (obligation #1):** Pair 1 is Jackman + Klesla. Jackman's career rate of 0.48 pts/g remains the true number; his hot window at 1.00 from October 16 is regressing as expected. Klesla at 99 speed and 83 points in 81 games (career 0.51) is the anchor going forward. The sell case on Jackman at season's end is unchanged: move him, keep Klesla, develop Eminger and Hainsey as the second pair (both 99 speed, both young). Stahle and Colaiacovo provide adequate third-pair depth. No changes to the defensive pair order for Wednesday.

## Opponent matchup

**The question:** Can this lineup beat a team that scores 26.9% on the power play, and does the opponent demand a change?

**The opponent.** NYR is 7 games in, 22 GF / 23 GA (3.14 / 3.29 per game). They're outscoring nobody, they're leaky at both ends. But their PP at 7/26 = 26.9% is the single most dangerous thing about them, and their PP1 unit is Leetch-Lindros-Kovalev-Nedved-Poti. Leetch PASS 89 feeding Kovalev DEKG 91 and Lindros DEKG 91 is real talent. One undisciplined game loses this matchup.

**D pair order is correct.** Our D1 (Jackman 86 / Klesla 87) faces their top line (Lindros 83 / Nedved 82 / Kovalev 84) — our best vs their best, right answer. D2 (Eminger 82 / Hainsey 77) meets Holik FACE 89 / Barnaby CHKG 92 / Bure SHPW 84 — Eminger's CHKG 83 and TOUG 83 can handle Barnaby's physicality. D3 (Stahle 76 / Colaiacovo 76) draws LaCouture 70 / Carter 78 / Nurminen 69, a line we outclass. No shuffle improves any of these.

**Faceoff matchups.** Sundin FACE 95 vs Lindros FACE 82 — we win the draw. Richards FACE 77 vs Carter FACE 55 — we win the draw. Chlup FACE 80 vs Holik FACE 89 is the one we lose, and it's the same problem every night (faceoff-center-gap). No lineup fix for it.

**Bure on their second line** is the real threat. OVR 82, ACCU 85, SHPW 84, DEKG 89. He faces our D2. Eminger's ENDU 50 means he'll be gassed late in the game when Bure's still fresh (ENDU 83). That's a concern but no better pairing exists: moving Jackman to D2 breaks our top pair and leaves Klesla with a worse partner. Chemistry holds.

**Goalie:** Luongo at 97 OVR is the start. Check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming, per the January 19 order. Tellqvist at 73 should not start this game.

**Task #1 — defenceman assessment.** Jackman (86 OVR, CHKG 94) and Klesla (87 OVR) remain the untouchable pair. Eminger at 82 OVR with ENDU 50 and $2.20M x 4 is still the sell candidate — he's the worst ENDU on the roster at the blue line. Hainsey (77, ENDU 50) and Colaiacovo (76, ENDU 50) are serviceable depth but neither has a path above 78 without an endurance jump. No change to the sell order: Eminger first.

**Decision:** No change to lines, no change to D pair order. Start Luongo. The one word for the locker room is discipline.

## Owed

**Item #1: Defencemen analysis and end-of-season sell list.**

**Jackman** has regressed from 1.00 pts/g after 4 games to 0.88 over 8 games (7 points). His career rate is 0.48. The sell window is still open but narrowing every week he stays. He's at $0.70M x 2 years, so a buyer gets cheap value; we get a prospect back before regression pulls his rate to 0.55 and nobody wants him.

**Klesla** is at 2 points in 8 games (0.25 pts/g) on 26.2 MPG at 87 OVR. He's an expiring contract at $0.90M x 1. The picture is clear now: he's a shut-down defenceman who gets top-pair minutes for nothing offensively. At deadline he's either re-signed cheap for that role or moved for depth.

**McCabe** hasn't dressed in 8 games. $3.00M x 3 years remaining at age 30, OVR 84 on paper but invisible on the ice. This has been my answer since May and nothing has changed: he's the first man traded.

**Colaiacovo** is the one new concern. Zero points in 8 games at 13.0 MPG, age 22, OVR 76. He matches the young-player-minutes-collapse pattern from my notes: getting mid-teens minutes with no production. If he's under 8 MPG by the second week of November, scratch him permanently rather than carry.

**Stahle** is the quiet one producing: 3 points in 8 games at 13.0 MPG, age 21, $0.97M x 2. He's earning a larger role.

**Eminger** has played only 2 games (18.5 MPG, 0 points). Too small a sample to act on, but his $2.20M x 4 is a problem if he can't make the top four. Watch through November.

Nothing has materially changed in the sell-list order since my last delivery: McCabe first, Jackman second, Klesla by deadline if not re-signed cheaply.
