# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-10-22

Toronto 5-2-0, 10 pts after 7 games.

## Role coverage

The question this phase answers: which of Toronto's role gaps are real roster holes, and which are just players sitting on the bench the coach isn't using? The answer determines whether we spend February currency or simply dress different men.

**Checking** is the clearest example of an internal fix. The Coach flags "we need a second defence pair with 80+ checking to staff K2 without relying on a scratched McCabe." McCabe is at 86 CHKG, 94 ENDU, age 30, and unlined. He is the fix the Coach is asking for. Dressing him staffs K2 and closes the checking gap on the back end tonight without spending a dollar or a pick. Tucker at 83 CHKG and Fischer at 82 CHKG are also unlined and available as secondary checkers.

**Faceoffs** are thin at two players above 80 (Sundin 90, Wallin 83), but Wallin is unlined and available. Dressing him on a bottom-six centre role gives the club a second 80+ draw-taker internally. Chlup at 75 is respectable for a 19-year-old. If we also land Bell (82 FACE) in February, that problem is permanently solved.

**Toughness is the one genuine structural gap.** Zero players at 80+ TOUG. The best is Jackman at 75, Roberts at 73. This cannot be fixed by dressing different men. Bell (CHI, 88 TOUG, 82 FACE, 82 base, age 25, $0.90M expiring) closes both toughness and faceoffs simultaneously. Heatley (ATL, 82 TOUG, 91 base, age 24) closes toughness with elite scoring. These remain the February targets and no internal adjustment substitutes for them.

**Scoring and playmaking are covered but age-concentrated.** Mogilny 94 at 36 and Roberts 88 at 39 anchor the top of both categories. Gaborik 92 at 23 is healthy-scratched and his value decays with every game he sits. The young bridge between the veterans and the prospects is Spezza (0 GP, POTE 99, five-game clock expired) and Chlup (19, 8 pts/6 GP). If the coach does not dress Spezza, he is a February trade chip per his own October language.

**Speed and stamina are absurdly deep.** 25 players at 80+ speed, 12 at 80+ stamina. Kaberle at 97 ENDU is unlined and could log heavy minutes if the coach needs it. Fischer (89 SPEE, 82 CHKG, 92 INJU) is unlined and represents a useful top-nine forward the team isn't using.

**Goalies are solved.** Luongo at 94 GSH_, 0.944 SV, 1.61 GAA in 5 games. Ouellet is adequate backup. No action needed.

## Trajectory

The question this phase answers: does this roster collapse in three seasons, and is the money arranged so it doesn't have to?

The answer is no, not if two contract decisions are made in the next nine months, but the shape has two structural risks that are invisible while the club is winning.

**Gaborik** is the payroll problem. At $11.90M/year for five years, he consumes 13.2% of the roster's $89.94M total while producing 1 point in 6 games. He is lined now, which is better than the October 13 reading, but the dollar-per-point ratio is the worst on the sheet. With five years left there is no mechanism to move him within the game; this is a sunk-cost allocation that will look worse if he stays under 20 points. The GM's October 16 question about whether payroll can be tolerated is answered for everyone except him: yes, it can, because $33.33M in profit leaves headroom for one bad contract.

**The veteran bridge is gone.** Two players sit between 30 and 33: McCabe and Tucker, both scratched, both 30. When Roberts (39) and Mogilny (36) walk in 2006 and Sundin (34) enters year-three decline, the club drops to zero players aged 30-33 by the start of 2007-08. The manual's 5-7 veteran target is met today by 3 players over 34, but none of them will be here in 2007. A 27-29 scoring forward or a veteran defenceman needs to arrive by February 2007 or the experience gap is not a form problem, it is a roster problem.

**July 2006 is the renewal summer that matters.** Nine contracts at $15.44M expire: Luongo ($1.60M), Chlup ($2.34M), Mogilny ($5.50M), Tucker ($1.30M), Klesla ($0.90M), Ouellet ($0.90M), Spezza ($1.00M), Koltsov ($1.10M), St. Jacques ($0.80M). Of these, Luongo and Chlup are untouchable renewals: Luongo at 26 with POTE 97 needs five or six years the same week Chlup at 19 with 8 points in 7 games does. Mogilny and Tucker walk. The remaining five are trade-or-re-sign choices that will define whether the 2009 wall gets worse or better.

**The 2009 wall is $37.40M across 11 players, all 4-year deals signed this summer.** Nash will be 25, Chistov 26, Colaiacovo 26, Richards 29, Kaberle 31. If they have developed into 85+ players, re-signing all eleven at market rate would exceed the current payroll by itself. If they have not, they are too old to trade for rebuilding assets and too numerous to carry. This is not a crisis now, but it is a cliff that becomes unmanageable without a plan formed by 2008.

**Draft capital is three picks: 1st, 2nd, 3rd round of 2006, all their own.** That funds exactly one meaningful deadline rental (a first-rounder is the standard cost) or one young-player-plus-pick package for a February target. The Jovanovski target (Klesla + 2nd) spends a pick and a prospect; the Heatley target (Spezza + Koltsov + 1st) spends all three picks' worth of value and two prospects. The GM cannot fund both.

**Draft capital is three picks: 1st, 2nd, 3rd round of 2006, all their own.** That funds exactly one meaningful February package. The GM needs to decide which target it goes to, because it cannot go to two.

## Calendar

Are we buyers or sellers at the March deadline, and what do we do with the nine contracts expiring this July? The answer depends on where we sit then, but the shape is already clear enough to plan around.

**Buyers.** Toronto sit first in the East at 5-2-0, 10 points in 7 games. The profit sheet reads +$33.33M on $49.49M revenue against $89.94M payroll. There is no cap to dodge and enough money to add. The Coach's gap is explicit: no second defence pair with 80+ checking. That is what we buy, and three targets are already identified (Stuart, Jovanovski, Bell). The deadline is 148 days away, so no negotiation opens before late February per the standing order.

**Mogilny** at 36, base 90, showing 87 on a $5.50M expiring deal is the rental to move. He is the only expiring player who is both over-80 and old enough that a contender would pay for him in March. If we are buying, his salary funds the package. If we are selling, he is the first piece out the door. Either way, he does not come back in July.

**Tucker** (30, $1.30M expiring) was already flagged as a chip in March 2005. He fills the same role as Mogilny but at a fraction of the cost, so he goes with Mogilny or in a separate package for a pick. The 4th-round pick remains the only draft asset Toronto own beyond a 4th.

**Luongo** is the summer priority. Base 91, showing 97, $1.60M, one year left. If he walks we replace a 91-base with Ouellet at base 81. Lock him 5-6 years the day he is eligible, before any other negotiation starts. The GM's 2005-01-15 goal was to "fetch a really good high-90s goalie from a team that will not be a contender" — we already have him, the job is keeping him.

**Chlup** is the second lock. 19, base 82, first-line centre at 22.6 MPG and 1.40 pts/g. Five to six years. At $2.34M he will demand a raise, so a long deal locks the price before he puts up 80 points and asks for what Marleau gets ($7.57M at 89 base).

**Spezza** at 22, $1.00M, POTE 99 is the third young core renewal, but only if he plays. Zero games in seven is still on the GM's desk. If he suits up and shows even 85-level play, lock him 5 years. If the 0 GP stretches to 20, he becomes a trade chip in February and this renewal becomes moot.

**Klesla** (23, base 78, $0.90M) and **St. Jacques** (25, $0.80M) are cheap young depth defenders. Renew both on 2-3 years at flat or slightly raised salary. They cost nothing and staff the bottom pair. **Ouellet** (24, base 81, $0.90M) stays as backup goalie on a 2-year at flat. **Koltsov** (24, $1.10M) is a 2-3 year renew if he produces, or a February chip alongside Tucker.

**The GM's October 16 question** — keep good players and rotate, or cut salary? The numbers say keep. $33.33M profit means payroll is not the constraint. The only players worth moving for money are Mogilny ($5.50M at 36) and anyone on a $10M+ deal who cannot produce (Gaborik at $11.90M for 5 years is the one to watch, though he is not expiring). Everyone else stays.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: who across the league fills our gaps, and would his club actually move him?

The league is shallow on toughness. Only a handful of players above 80 TOUG sit on clubs that are losing enough to sell, and most of them are over 30. That concentrates the market on a few names: **Jovanovski** at VAN with 89 TOUG and 90 CHKG at 29, **Doan** at PHX with 86 TOUG and 91 CHKG at 28, and **Bertuzzi** at VAN with 81 TOUG and a 94 base overall at 30. All three sit on clubs at 2–7 points with many expiring deals.

**Jovanovski** is the single best fit: he closes both the toughness gap and the defence-checking gap in one body, is only 29, and VAN are at 7 points with 13 expiring and the lowest payroll in the league at $46.36M. They are building, not winning, and he is a rental for them.

**Doan** at PHX is the forward version of the same argument. 87 base, 86 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 28 years old, POTE 80, $2.40M expiring from a 0-5-0 club with 9 expiring deals. He is a top-six winger who hits and blocks shots — the profile between Roberts and Nash. PHX have no path to re-signing him.

**Bertuzzi** at 94 base is the highest-overall player on any selling club. He brings 81 TOUG and 85 CHKG with elite scoring, but he is 30 and on $2.60M. A 2-year piece at best. VAN might prefer to keep one of Jovanovski or Bertuzzi; we should target Jovanovski first because he's younger and fills two gaps.

**McLaren** at SJ is a name that wasn't on our radar before: 89 TOUG, 93 CHKG, age 28, POTE 81, $2.20M expiring from SJ who carry the highest payroll among sellers at $66.24M with 14 expiring. SJ are the most desperate club in the league.

**Morrow** at DAL at 26, 88 base, 85 TOUG, POTE 86, $1.30M expiring is the best value if DAL decide to sell from 10 points. They are contending though, so they likely re-sign or keep him until March.

**Cole** at ANA: 84 base, 83 TOUG, 92 CHKG, age 26, $0.60M expiring. The cheapest toughness forward in the league. ANA at 8 points with 11 expiring.

**Brad Stuart** at SJ: his TOUG is only 74, not 80. He fills the D-checking gap (83 CHKG) but not toughness. POTE 92 at 25 means he develops further, but he does not close the structural gap this season.

**Svitov** at TB: POTE 99, 79 TOUG, 90 SPEE, age 22, $1.00M expiring. Raw at 73 base but the development upside is the highest of any available player. TB at 7 points might sell a prospect for a veteran rental.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: which of the February targets can we actually fund with three picks and the chips the Coach has already marked as available, and why would the other GM pick up the phone?

The one structural gap is toughness — zero players above 80 TOUG. The checking gap is internal (dress McCabe at 86 CHKG). The faceoff gap has an internal half-fix (Wallin at 83 FACE, unlined). So the packages below all target toughness first, and the cheapest one that works goes first.

**Bell from Chicago is the proposal that makes sense for both sides with the least cost.** We give Tucker (30, POTE 79, $1.30M expiring, 0 GP, CHKG 92, TOUG 88) plus St. Jacques (25, POTE 94, $0.80M expiring, 0 GP, CHKG 84, TOUG 80) plus our 3rd-round pick. We get Bell (25, 88 TOUG, 82 FACE, 82 base, $0.90M expiring). Net salary effect: we save $1.20M and fill a roster hole. Chicago get a 25-year-old prospect with POTE 94 and a pick for a 25-year-old on an expiring deal they will not re-sign. They carry 13 expiring contracts and $23.35M profit. They are collecting future assets, not competing.

**Jovanovski from Vancouver is the second option, only if Bell doesn't land or the GM wants toughness on the back end too.** We give Klesla (23, POTE 97, $0.90M expiring, 7 GP, 2 pts, SPEE 88) plus our 2nd-round pick. We get Jovanovski (29, 89 TOUG, 90 CHKG, 89 base, $2.30M expiring). Net salary: +$1.40M for a half-season rental. Vancouver at 7 points with 13 expiring and $46.36M payroll (lowest in the league) are collecting youth and picks; a 29-year-old rental at $2.30M is exactly what they flip. The cost is Klesla, who is actually playing. This package is strictly worse than Bell if Bell lands.

**Heatley from Atlanta is the go-big option and I would not lead with it.** Spezza (22, POTE 99, $1.00M expiring, 0 GP) plus Koltsov (24, POTE 94, $1.10M expiring, 0 GP) plus the 1st-round pick for Heatley (24, 91 base, 82 TOUG, $1.10M expiring). Atlanta at 2 points with 9 expiring cannot re-sign both him and Kovalchuk; they want exactly what Spezza and Koltsov represent (POTE 94-99 forwards) plus a 1st. The problem is this spends every piece of development capital the club has. We would be trading our future for a 91-base rental who leaves in July.

**If none of these land by February:** dress McCabe for checking, Wallin for faceoffs, Fischer (89 SPEE, 82 CHKG) for a top-nine forward role, and accept that the toughness gap persists into summer free agency where Bell-type players appear without pick cost.

## Owed

**Luongo availability and DiPietro monitoring** — This task is closed. The GM killed it twice: on 2005-02-19 ("Luongo is arrived. Goalies are solved. Done. Do not revisit that issue") and again on 2005-03-19 ("Close all goalie monitoring"). The original purpose was to find a high-90s goalie from a non-contender before the February 2005 window; Luongo was acquired and is on our roster at **97 overall**, 26, $1.60M with 1 year left.

**DiPietro** at NYI is at 89 overall, 24, $1.10M on an expiring deal with 5 starts logged. He is developing, but he is no longer a target — Luongo is our number one and the monitoring window expired eight months ago.

No action needed. The task was completed in January 2005 and explicitly terminated in February and March.

# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-10-22

Next game vs FLA on Sunday 23 October 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether our young players are getting games that match what they've earned. With seven games gone, the patterns are already clear.

**Chlup** is at 8 points in 7 games on 19.9 minutes a night from the second line centre spot. That is 1.14 pts/g at 19. He has been the best forward on the club since October and he is still not on the first line. I have made this recommendation five times since April. He has earned it now, not projected — 8 points in 7 is not a prospect, it is a first-line centre.

**Spezza** is the biggest concern. POTE 99, age 22, morale 76, and 3 minutes in one game. Last season his minutes collapsed to 4.8 and this season has started worse. At morale 76 he loses 2 off every grade, so he is playing as if he were 2 points worse than his actual ability. If the GM will not dress him on a real line, he should not be dressed at all — the current arrangement wastes his development and rots his morale without giving the team anything.

**Spacek** and **Upshall** both scratched after 6 games at 0.50 pts/g each. Spacek has 3 points in 6 games at 20 with POTE 91. Upshall has the same 3 in 6 with POTE 99. Both are at morale 76. Against Florida at 1-3, this is a game we should develop in. Either of them could take a bottom-six spot and earn minutes.

**Eminger** is dressed every game and has played one. 19 MPG in that one game at 21 with POTE 99, but zero production and zero minutes since. The decision is binary: give him real minutes on the second pair, or stop dressing him so the slot goes to someone who plays.

**Colaiacovo** at 0 points in 7 is not alarming at 22 on the third pair. The minutes (12.6) are appropriate shelter. Let it play out.

**Gardener** at 20 has 0 points in 6 games at 4.5 MPG. POTE 98 is a scouting number, not a current ability claim. Scratched is correct for now.

**Klesla** at 26.6 MPG is the heaviest load among our young D. At 23 that is fine short-term, but if Jackman is also carrying 33+ this feeds the concentration problem from October 13.

## Development trends

Ten days, six or seven games, no grade movement on the card, so this is production and minutes only. The early-season window is short, but the patterns are clear enough to act on.

**Chlup** at 19 is at 1.17 pts/g on 22.2 MPG. That is a first-line rate and he is getting first-line minutes already, just not the first-line slot. I have been telling you since April he belongs on L1C and the numbers keep confirming it. He is not developing, he has arrived. Move him.

**Jackman** is the good news. His minutes dropped from 41 to 25.2 per game and his rate jumped from 0.48 last season to 0.83 now. The load-spreading I called in October is working exactly as predicted. Leave the defensive rotation alone; it is fixing his problem.

**Richards** went from 0.00 in game one to 0.83 over seven games on 12.2 MPG. Last season's collapse to 0.71 looks like it is behind him. Whatever shifted in the offseason is sticking so far. Give him two more weeks before drawing conclusions.

**Fischer** at 0.80 pts/g on 21.8 MPG is a two-way defenceman who just doubled his ice time and scored at a top-pair rate. He was already a keeper on your instructions, and this is confirmation he deserves the slot he's getting.

**Spacek** at 20 is the one worrying me. Minutes fell from 17 to 3.6 and his rate is 0.40. Same collapse as last March when he went from 12 MPG to 8 and never recovered. He is 20 and his window for a real audition is closing. If the minutes don't climb back above 10 in the next week, stop dressing him and give the slot to Gaborik or Alexeev.

**Upshall** is repeating the same pattern: 16 MPG down to 3.8, rate at 0.40. Last season he went from 13.4 to 4.9. This is his second year of the same collapse at age 22. I would scratch him and dress Alexeev, who sat at 2.00 pts/g in his one appearance last season and hasn't played since.

**Gardener** at 20 has zero points on 2.2 MPG. He is a healthy scratch wearing a jersey. Same recommendation: make room for someone who will play meaningful minutes.

**Spezza** at 22 appeared once for 3.0 minutes. The March diagnosis still holds: no path to ice on this roster, the season is about to be another write-off.

**The veterans are fine.** Sundin at 1.00 pts/g on 20.3 MPG at 34 is the best forward on the team right now. Mogilny at 0.50 on 19.7 at 36 is doing his job. Roberts at 0.33 on 15.0 at 39 is a fourth-liner. Nobody is slipping yet.

No changes needed on defence or among the veterans. The only action items are Chlup's slot, and the young-forwards decisions on Spacek, Upshall, and Gardener.

## Morale watch

The whole room dropped together — everyone went down 9 to 15 points since the last save, including players who didn't play a single shift. That pattern is results, not ice time. A -15 on a scratched 20-year-old and a -9 on a 36-year-old playing 20 a night means the losing streak is doing the damage, and no line change I make fixes it.

**Richards** remains the one genuine minutes problem I can address. He's at 81 morale on 12.3 MPG, fifth line-centre minutes for a 25-year-old whose grades put him in the 17-to-20 band. Five points in 7 games isn't a hot hand, but at 81 he's cost two points off every grade in the 70s morale band, which makes him less effective on the ice and harder to trust in close games. I've flagged this since October 20th and nothing moved.

**Spezza** at 76 and 3.0 MPG in 1 game is the same story as last season in miniature. He's dressed but barely touching the ice. At 22 with that potential number, sitting on the bench while the team loses is the worst of both worlds — no development, no win to lift him. The GM scratched him for the January 15 development rotation; that logic doesn't apply anymore with the season underway and losses piling up.

**Upshall, Spacek, Gardener** all hit 76 with -15 drops. They're scratched by design. Their morale cost is the price of the development plan the GM set. I'm not asking to undo that for a Florida game.

The rest of the room is fine. Chlup at 91, Sundin at 91, Jackman at 91, Gaborik at 88. They're getting their minutes and their morale reflects it. If we win two in a row, most of this resets.

## Role composition

The question is whether our units are built from players who suit their job. Most are fine; one PK unit has a hole I can fix, and the fourth line gap is still a roster problem.

**K2 penalty kill** carries a checking mean of 66 and toughness of 59. For a shorthanded unit, that is thin. Jackman (92) anchors K1 at 79 mean, but K2 has no one close. Roberts checks 84 and sits on L3 even-strength only. Moving him onto K2, replacing Brendl, raises the PK checking mean into the mid-70s and gives this unit an actual body who can win a puck battle. He stays on L3 even-strength, so no forward line gets reshuffled.

**L3** (Stahle, Roberts, Colaiacovo, Richards, Nash) checks 76 mean with Nash (82) and Roberts (84) both on it. That is our balanced middle line: Richards plays 93, Nash forechecks, Roberts defends. Leave it.

**L4** (Spezza, Lundmark, Brendl) carries checking 63, toughness 58, faceoffs 58. I flagged this in April as a roster gap, not a lineup problem, and it is unchanged. No arrangement fixes it because every forward who checks above 78 is already deployed on L1-L3.

**P1** (Sundin, Jackman, Gaborik, Klesla, Nash) at 91 scoring mean and 93 speed is loaded. **P2** (Eminger, Chlup, Mogilny, Hainsey, Afinogenov) at 84 scoring and 93 speed is the speed-and-skill second unit. Both fine.

**L2** (Eminger, Chlup, Hainsey, Afinogenov, Chistov) checks 71 mean, toughness 63. Young, thin defensively. But Chlup is at 1.40 pts/g and the GM has made clear that production earns the role. Leave it.

## Opponent matchup

The question: does anything need to change to beat Florida, or do the existing lines exploit the mismatches through auto-pairing on their own? They exploit them. No change.

**Florida's defense** is the worst we will face this season. Nobody above 75. Their top pair is Lilja (75) and Kudroc (72). Their second pair is Krajicek (70) and Biron (68). Their third is Van Ryn (67) and Trnka (67). Through the auto-pairing system our L1 (Sundin 92, Gaborik 99, Mogilny 87) draws their D1, our L2 (Chlup 87, Chistov 87, Afinogenov 84) draws their D2, and our L3 (Nash 85, Richards 87, Roberts 85) draws their D3. Every single forward line we ice is a 15-plus point OVR advantage over the pair it faces. The system is already doing the work.

**Jokinen at 81** is their best forward and he sits on their second line with wingers at 68 and 73. Our D2 of Eminger (82) and Hainsey (77) handles him. I considered swapping our D pair order to put Jackman/Klesla on Jokinen, but their L1 with Nedorost (80) plus Kozlov (77) and Huselius (71) is at least as dangerous in aggregate, and the marginal gain from reordering is nothing against a blue line this thin.

**Their power play is 1-for-24.** Their PK is presumably irrelevant since we'll have plenty of chances at even strength against that D. I see no reason to tweak PP units for a team conceding 3.4 goals per game.

**Goalie:** Luongo at 97 is the start. His morale is 91 and no fatigue flag appears. Standard January 19 order applies: check the fatigue icon on screen before confirming.

**D evaluation (task #1):** Against this blue line our defense should see a quiet night. That's a useful data point for the sell list. If Eminger (82, endurance 50) and Hainsey (77, endurance 50) look comfortable tonight, their value as trade pieces holds because a buyer sees a pair that wasn't exposed. If they look rattled against 70/68 D, the sell window narrows. I'll assess from the result. Klesla's endurance at 57 and Jackman's at 73 remain the concern for December, not tonight.

## Owed

The question: who among our defencemen should go at the end of the season, and has anything moved since my last delivery.

**Jackman** — 6 points in 7 games, 0.86 pts/g on 27.4 MPG. Still well above his 0.48 career rate but cooling from the 1.00 pace I flagged on October 16. The sell window is still open but narrowing; every game he stays close to 0.85 and buyers start pricing the regression. $0.70M x 2 makes him a cheap rental for any contender.

**Klesla** — 2 points in 7 games, 0.29 pts/g on 26.6 MPG. This is the number that changed. He's eating top-pair minutes and producing fourth-pair offence at age 23. Contract is $0.90M x 1 year, expiring. If the rate doesn't climb past 0.50 by late November, he's a February rental at best. His minutes are the other half of the concentration problem I noted October 13.

**Colaiacovo** — 0 points in 7 games on 12.6 MPG. Seven straight scoreless games at 22 with 4 years and $1.40M. At 76 OVR and zero output, he's the first name off the roster if a prospect arrives or we need cap space. He's still developing, but the window where "young and raw" excuses zero production is closing.

**McCabe** — 0 GP, still undressed at $3.00M x 3 remaining. No change since May. He goes the moment a trade partner accepts the contract.

**Kaberle, Fischer** — GM's keepers, unchanged. **Stahle** (2 pts in 7, 0.29 on 12.3) is on schedule for his age. **Eminger** has 1 game and 0 points but $2.20M x 4 is the problem I already flagged in May.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-10-20
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-10-20

Toronto 5-1-0, 10 pts after 6 games.

## Role coverage

The club is covered at speed and scoring depth, thin at checking and faceoffs, and structurally missing toughness with zero players above 75 on the base grade. Most of the thin spots are the coach's fault, not the roster's.

**Toughness** is the only true acquisition gap. Jackman leads the club at 75 TOUG, Roberts sits at 73, McCabe at 73. Nobody on this roster reaches 80 on the base grade, and the gap is not close. The Feb 24 reading of zero players at 80+ TOUG is confirmed here. The only fix is external, and the deadline is March. Bell at 88 TOUG and 82 base remains the cleanest target if he is still available.

**Checking** is thin because the coach is not using who he has. Jackman 87 and Roberts 86 are lined and play. McCabe at 86 CHKG and Tucker at 83 CHKG are both rostered and sitting out. Lining them takes the club from four dressed 80+ checkers to six and costs nothing. Roberts is 39 and will not be here next year; McCabe at 30 and Tucker at 30 bridge two more seasons before the club needs a young replacement like Stuart.

**Faceoffs** show only Sundin 90 and Wallin 83 at 80+. Sundin is 34. Wallin at 83 FACE is unlined. Putting him in at centre or wing on a bottom unit fixes the thinness for this season without any move.

**Gaborik** at 92 overall and 98 speed, age 23, is the single most valuable player on the roster after Sundin, and he is a healthy scratch. Every game he sits costs both wins now and trade value later. He is either dressed within two games or moved before his market dries up.

**Spezza and Eminger** carry POTE 99 and zero games in five. The coach's five-game clock expired. At POTE 99 and ages 21 and 22, they are either developmental investments the coach is wasting or trade chips whose value is decaying by the game. The GM needs to dress them or list them.

**Goalies** are covered. Luongo is 26 with 4 wins, 1.26 GAA, and 0.956 SV in four starts. Ouellet at 24 provides a reasonable backup at 86 GSH_. Tellqvist at 26 is a third-stringer with no games. The depth is fine for a playoff run.

The age profile is the long-term worry. The top three in scoring and playmaking are Mogilny (36), Sundin (34), and Roberts (39). Below them, Gaborik at 23 would carry the torch if he played; Chlup at 19 is the heir apparent at centre. If Gaborik leaves and Chlup stalls, the club falls into the scoring void identified in May with nothing to fill it. That makes dressing Gaborik a trajectory decision, not just a lineup one.

## Trajectory

The trajectory question is whether this roster walks into a simultaneous free-agency cliff or a production void, and the answer is both — but they arrive at different times and the near one is solvable with two renewals.

**Chlup** is the single most important contract on the sheet. 19 years old, POTE 95, 8 points in 6 games at 1.33 points per game, on a one-year deal at $2.34M that expires in July 2006. He is the best forward on the roster tonight and the only player whose growth curve we can project past the veterans. He must be locked on 5–6 years the first day he is eligible. Miss that window and we lose the franchise centre.

**Luongo** is second priority and same summer. 26, POTE 97, $1.60M, one year left. Goalie contracts are the cheapest high-value contracts in this league right now. Lock him on 6 years and we are set at the position for a decade.

**The one-year cluster (July 2006)** holds 9 players worth $15.44M. Of those, we are letting Mogilny (36, $5.50M) walk, moving Tucker (30, $1.30M, trade chip), and deciding on Spezza (22, POTE 99, zero games). The renewal bill is really four or five players, not nine, and Chlup plus Luongo are the two that cannot slip.

**The four-year cluster (2009)** is the structural trap. 11 players worth $37.40M all expire simultaneously: Gaborik, Sundin, Richards, Chistov, Kaberle, Nash, Fischer, Upshall, Colaiacovo, Abid, Wallin. That is more than a third of the payroll hitting the market at once, and it is exactly the warning the manual gives. Every renewal from here should be deliberately staggered — give one player 3 years and his cohort-mate 5, so 2009 never repeats.

**The veterans cliff** is real but three seasons out. Sundin (34, $8.40M, 4 years) will be 38 at expiry. Mogilny (36, 1 year) walks after this season. Roberts (39, 2 years) will be 41 and POTE 52 says he is done. Combined, those three carry the production that nobody under 30 yet matches. Chlup at 1.33, Nash and Chistov at POTE 95 — the potential is there but the actual production gap is 426 points against a young core that produced a fraction of that last year.

**Gaborik at $11.90M** is the highest single salary on the roster, 41% more than the next man. He is 23, POTE 90, and now lined. If he produces 0.8+ points per game, the contract is reasonable for a top-six winger on a 5-year deal. If he sits near 0.2 (1 point in 5 games so far), it is a liability that clogs the 5-year window. The 2005-06 season tells us which.

**Money is not the constraint.** Payroll $89.94M against revenue $47.76M, but profit reads positive at $34.45M. Ticket price is $112, attendance 18,316, prestige 1,100. There is room to add salary. The problem is not spending; it is whether the spending buys the right years.

**Draft capital:** We hold our 1st, 2nd, and 3rd round picks for 2006. This is better than the January situation where we held nothing beyond a fourth. The first-rounder is trade ammunition for a February move (Jovanovski-type package) or a scouting-quality draft pick. Do not spend all three; keep the second and third for depth.

**The three moves that protect 2006 through 2009:**
1. Lock Chlup 5–6 years, July 2006, before anything else.
2. Lock Luongo 5–6 years, same summer.
3. When renewing the 4-year cohort (Richards, Chistov, Kaberle, Nash, Fischer), stagger terms so the 2009 cluster splits across 2008 and 2010.

## Calendar

The question this phase answers is whether we are buying or selling, and what happens to every expiring contract when it comes due.

We are buyers. Toronto is 5-1-0, first in the Eastern Conference, ten points in six games. The deadline is 150 days away. The GM's October 16 question — "do we want to get rid of good players just to lower salary, or keep them?" — answers itself at this record. There is no salary cap; the constraint is profit. At first place with revenue presumably strong, keeping rotation players costs nothing we need back. The only players we move are ones who do not play (Spezza) or who the GM already flagged as chips (Tucker).

## The deadline — March 19, 2006

**Tucker** ($1.30M, 30, LW) is the one confirmed chip. The GM said "only trading chips left are Tucker and the 4th round pick" on March 19 of last season. He has carried that label eight months. At 83 CHKG he fills a checking gap on a contender that needs it, or he becomes draft capital for a contender that needs it. Open in late February per standing order; he does not play, so his trade value only erodes.

**Klesla** (D, 23, $0.90M expiring) is the return piece for Jovanovski (VAN, 89 base, 93 TOUG, 94 CHKG, 29, $2.30M expiring) per the October 12 target list. VAN carry 13 expiring contracts and the league's lowest payroll at $46.36M; they have every reason to convert Klesla for a proven body before he walks. A second-round pick tops it. If Jovanovski does not land, Klesla is still useful as a piece in any package because he is young and cheap.

**St. Jacques** (D, 25, $0.80M expiring) is the Begin (BUF, 87 TOUG, 95 CHKG, 86 FACE, 27, $936K expiring) return per the October 12 target. Tucker plus St. Jacques to Buffalo is the package. BUF have 6 expiring contracts and $19.07M profit; they are in selling mode at this pace. The L4 checking-and-faceoff fix that the Coach keeps demanding arrives in this one deal.

**Spezza** (C, 22, $1.00M expiring) is the wild card. The Coach's five-game clock has expired; per his own language Spezza is now a trade chip. At POTE 99 and morale 88, he is worth something to a club that will play him. If the GM dresses him this week, the case for moving him dies. If he stays scratched through November, he goes at the deadline. I recommend the GM give him one more decision window — dress or deal by mid-November.

**Mogilny** (RW, 36, $5.50M) is the question mark. He was on the December 2004 package that never executed and is still here. At 36 with $5.50M and an expiring deal, he is the textbook "trade an over-80 you won't keep for a pick." If his base overall is still above 80, the mechanic works. If it has decayed, he becomes a July loss with no return. I would test his trade value in February specifically to trigger the pick mechanic. $5.50M is the second-highest salary on the roster and buys nothing if he cannot play 18 minutes a night.

## The summer — July 2006

**Chlup** (C, 19, $2.34M expiring) and **Luongo** (G, 26, $1.60M expiring) both expire the same summer and must be locked on 5-6 years. Chlup first: he is the best forward on the roster at 1.25 pts/g in 23.5 MPG at age 19. Luongo at 90+ base behind Belfour is the continuity piece the GM confirmed. These two renewals are not negotiable items; they are "lock before anyone else notices" items.

**Koltsov** (LW, 24, $1.10M expiring) has no production visible in this save's records. If he has played meaningful minutes and shown something, 2-3 years at similar money is the answer. If he is another undressed piece, he goes before July and the roster thins. The GM needs to tell me whether Koltsov is playing this season, because the data shows nothing.

**Ouellet** (G, 24, $0.90M expiring) is a backup. With Luongo locked and Tellqvist developing behind him, Ouellet is surplus. Trade him in February if a contender needs a third goalie; otherwise let him walk. The $0.90M is trivial but the roster spot is not.

**Klesla and St. Jacques** should already be gone by July (moved at the deadline for Jovanovski and Begin respectively). If either deal collapses, renew Klesla at 2-3 years — he is 23 and $0.90M is cheap insurance on the blue line. St. Jacques at 25 and $0.80M is a depth piece who can walk.

**Mogilny** at 36 walks if not traded. That frees $5.50M, which is the single largest payroll event this summer. The question the GM asked — "keep them and rotate or dump for money?" — is specific to players like Mogilny. My answer: dump him at the deadline for the pick, not in July for nothing. He is 36; every season he ages the value drops.

**Spezza** walks if undressed and untraded. At POTE 99 and $1.00M that is a genuine loss. This is why the decision cannot wait until February. If the Coach will not play him, he must go before his value hits zero with the club.

## The Luongo/DiPietro task

This is the monitoring job you asked for on January 19, 2005. It is closed. Luongo is on our roster at $1.60M, confirmed as the future number one on March 19. DiPietro monitoring is irrelevant because the goalie question is settled. I am not reopening it.

## League scan

The only acquisition gap Toronto has is toughness: nobody on the roster reaches 80 on the base TOUG grade, and the best is Jackman at 75. Every other thin spot — checking, faceoffs — is fixable by dressing McCabe (86 CHKG), Tucker (83 CHKG) and Wallin (83 FACE). The league scan therefore has one primary job: find TOUG 80+ players on clubs that will sell, and rank them by age, salary and what it costs to get them. The secondary job is the scoring bridge — Mogilny walks at 36, Sundin is 34 and carries $8.40M, and no centre behind Chlup produces at a first-line rate yet.

I need to see the full TOUG 80+ market league-wide, the young-potential market on losing clubs, and the high-end expiring class on bottom-half teams. Three queries cover all of it.

## Trade construction

The one true gap on this roster is toughness: nobody reaches 80 base TOUG, and the league scan confirms three players who close it on teams that must sell. ATL is 1-3-0 with two 89+ wingers on expiring deals and cannot keep both, making them the most motivated seller in the league. The proposals below rank by how much of the problem each one solves.

**Heatley** (RW, 24, 91 base, $1.10M expiring) solves toughness and the scoring bridge in one move. He is the older of ATL's two elite wingers, which means ATL will keep Kovalchuk (22, 89 base) and trade Heatley. They are 2 points in 4 games and $17.79M in profit, so salary relief is not urgent, but losing a 91-base winger for nothing at July is.

**Stuart** (D, 25, 87 base, 80 TOUG, 89 CHKG, POTE 91, $1.80M expiring) is the long-term fix at the blue line. SJ carry the highest payroll in this market at $66.24M against 13,558 attendance and 13 expiring contracts. They are shedding. He is two years younger than Jovanovski with 14 more points of potential.

**Bell** (LW, 25, 80 base, 88 TOUG, 82 FACE, $0.90M expiring) is the cheapest path to closing both the toughness and faceoff gaps simultaneously. CHI are 1-1-1, 3 points in 3 games, with 13 expiring and $23.35M profit. They will deal him.

## Owed

**Monitoring Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window.**

This task is closed. Luongo arrived on Toronto's roster in January 2005, and the GM ordered all goalie monitoring stopped on 2005-03-19. There is nothing left to monitor on the acquisition side.

**Luongo** is on our roster at 97 overall, 26 years old, $1.60M, 1 year left, 4 GP so far this season. The live question has shifted entirely from "can we get him" to "will he sign a new deal." He and Chlup both expire July 2006 and must be locked on 5-6 years the same week. Luongo first, because Tellqvist behind him is a clear step down.

**DiPietro** at NYI: 24, 88 overall, $1.10M, expiring, 4 GP. He is no longer a relevant target. We have Luongo at 97 and Ouellet at 86 as a backup, both with one year left. Acquiring DiPietro would mean trading one of them, and the GM's position from March 2005 was to keep the two 90+ goalies. DiPietro's development trajectory (88 at 24) does not justify reopening that.

Nothing has moved since the last report because the task was completed six months ago. The forward obligation is the July 2006 renewal window for Luongo, already on the books.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-10-20
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-10-20

Next game vs BOS on Friday 21 October 2005.

## Development opportunity

Are the young guys getting the games they have earned after six games? Mostly yes, but two situations are wrong and one continues to be a repeat call the GM hasn't made.

**Chlup** at 8 points in 6 games on 19.8 minutes a night is performing at 1.33 points a game. He is 19. He is still on the second line. I have recommended first-line centre since April and the GM has not moved him. At this rate Gaborik on the first line is getting the worse of the two centre options, and it shows: Gaborik has 1 point in 5 games. Chlup belongs between Nash and Chistov's linemates on the top line, or wherever the GM puts him, but he needs to be on the first line.

**Spezza and Eminger** are both scratched with zero games. Spezza is 22, Eminger 21, and both carry the highest potential number the club has on file. Neither is injured. They are simply not part of the plan right now. Two guys with the top developmental upside on the roster are getting nothing. That is the single biggest development problem on this team, and I do not know the answer. Either they need a look in the lineup or the GM needs to tell me why they don't, because right now the sheet says we have zero development happening at those two spots.

**Spacek, Gardener, and Upshall** all sit at morale 76, which is the fourth-line floor when minutes are thin. Spacek has 3 points in 6 games on 5.8 minutes, Upshall has 3 on the same 5.8. Gardener has zero on 4.5 minutes. They are getting fourth-line minutes because their current grade is fourth-line. The morale cost is real but they will recover with team wins. No change for them.

**Stahle, Colaiacovo, Klesla** are all dressed and playing. Klesla at 26.7 minutes on the top pair is the heaviest load among the young defencemen. Stahle at 12.0 and Colaiacovo at 12.3 are fine for their age and role.

**Alexeev** played 1 game, scored 2 points. One game is not a case. His last-season rate of 0.55 was above the guys he was competing with, but Chistov is at 0.83 this year and Upshall at 0.50. The old mismatch argument no longer holds against current numbers.

## Development trends

The window is tiny — 6 games since the first save — so production arrows on the left side are one-game noise. But minutes moved hard, and that's the real story: the GM has redistributed ice time across the roster.

**Chlup** went from 6.0 to 22.6 MPG and scored at 1.40 pts/g over 6 games. He's 19. The minutes jump is everything I asked for. The slot is still wrong: the GM hasn't moved him to first-line centre despite three requests. The ice time says he's already our first-line centre in everything but the lineup sheet.

**Fischer** is the biggest win. Minutes doubled from 10.0 to 21.8 MPG and he's at 0.80 pts/g. He's 25, the GM called him a keeper in January, and he's now playing like a top-pair defenceman. The load-spread away from Jackman and Klesla is working: Jackman dropped from 41.0 to 25.2 MPG, Klesla from 42.0 to 23.6. Fischer, Kaberle (21.2), Colaiacovo (13.6) and Stahle (13.2) all absorbed the difference.

**Spacek** went from 17.0 to 3.6 MPG. The March threshold was "above 10 by season's end or the year is dead." He's at 3.6 after 6 games. He's not playing. Same pattern for **Upshall** (16.0 to 3.8 MPG, 0.40 pts/g) and **Gardener** (16.0 to 2.2 MPG, 0.00 pts/g). Three young players went from meaningful minutes to nothing. If that's a deliberate choice to free ice for the older core, fine, but three players at under 4 MPG means they're not developing.

**Richards** at 0.80 pts/g on 11.6 MPG is better than last season's 0.71 on higher minutes. The system-fit concern from the offseason might be resolving if a smaller role suits him. Worth watching past 10 games before drawing conclusions.

**Afinogenov** at 0.60 on 14.8 MPG is below last season's 0.73. Same system-fit question remains open.

**Kaberle** got the star-D minutes the GM asked for (11.0 to 21.2 MPG) but is producing 0.20 pts/g. Six games is nothing, and January's read was that he's a star. No alarm yet, but if the rate stays under 0.40 through 15 games the "star defenceman" label needs revisiting.

**Sundin** at 34 is 1.00 pts/g on 20.8 MPG. **Mogilny** at 36 is 0.60 on 20.4. **Roberts** at 39 is 0.40 on 16.6. All three veterans are holding their minutes and producing at rates that justify the ice. No decline signal in this window.

**Gaborik** arrived mid-window and is at 19.4 MPG with 0.20 pts/g in 5 games. Thin sample, but the ice time says he's in the top nine immediately.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy, with one exception that needs a move tonight.

**Richards** is the problem. His morale sits at 78, the lowest of any player getting regular shifts, and it hasn't bounced in several saves. He's playing 11.8 minutes a night on the third line. A 25-year-old former first-line centre is squarely in the 80s band, which means he expects about 17. He's five minutes short every night, and the morale has bottomed out in the zone where it costs two points off every grade. That's a real on-ice penalty against Boston.

**Afinogenov** is at 84 on 15.0 MPG, slightly under his band but manageable. He's second-line right wing, scoring at 0.67, and recovering from his dip. Leave him alone.

**Upshall, Spacek, Gardener** are all at 76 on 4.5 to 5.8 minutes. They're young, contributing (3 points in 6 games each for Upshall and Spacek), and the low minutes is the development plan working as the GM intended. Morale at 76 is two points below the band threshold, so they lose a point or two of grade tonight, but that's the cost of the plan. Watch it over the next two weeks — if it drops to 72 or below, they need a spot on the fourth line with real shifts or the grade hit starts compounding.

**Spezza, Abid, McCabe, Tucker** and the other scratches are all at 88 or above. Fine.

No goalie concerns. Luongo is at 91 with 4 starts and 59.8 MPG. Check his fatigue icon before confirming, per January 19.

## Role composition

Are the units built from the right people? Mostly yes — the arrangement is sound given what we have. The problems are depth, not placement.

**L1** — Jackman at 92 checking is the anchor; Sundin, Mogilny, Gaborik and Klesla all above 90 in scoring or playmaking. This line is built to score with one guy who can break the play up. That's the correct shape for a top unit. No change.

**L2** — Checking mean 71, best 87 (Fischer). I flagged this before and the GM's answer stands: Chlup at 19 producing 1.25 pts/g gets the role because the scoresheet says he's earned it. Fischer at 87 is the anchor and the rest grow into it. No change.

**L3** — This is actually our best checking forward group at 76 mean, with Roberts at 84 and Nash at 82. Having them together on the third line means we have a unit that can shut down any opposing second line. Correct placement. No change.

**L4** — Checking mean 70 with only three bodies (Gardener, Spacek, Upshall). Spacek at 84 carries this, but a fourth line with a 70 mean cannot check anyone. This is the gap I raised in April and it remains: no forward outside L1-L2 checks above 82 besides Roberts and Nash, and they belong on L3.

**K1** — Jackman (92) plus Chlup (80 faceoffs) and Fischer (87 checking) gives a kill unit that can both short the play and win the draw going in. Sound. No change.

**K2** — Mean 71 checking with Kaberle and Upshall dragging it down. Klesla at 86 and Spacek at 84 are the only reasons this works at all. We need a second checking defender on the kill, and we have exactly one: McCabe at 83, who is currently a scratch. Against Boston this may shift, but that's a matchup call for Phase 3.

**P1** — Sundin and Gaborik up front, Jackman at the point, Nash net-front. Elite shooting (mean 90) with the speed to generate second chances. Built correctly. No change.

**P2** — Mogilny (92 scoring) on the second unit is a luxury. Chlup at 80 faceoffs can win the draw to set it up. Fine.

The roster gap remains unchanged: we need a second checking defenseman (80+ CHKG) to staff K2 alongside Klesla, and a checking middle-six forward (82+ CHKG) to give L3 rest without losing the shutdown capability. Jackman, Roberts and Nash are the only forwards above 82, and moving any of them breaks something that works.

## Opponent matchup

Can we beat Boston at home on Friday without changing anything? Yes, and I would not touch the sheet.

**Thornton** is their one real weapon at 91 OVR with 97 shot power and 91 endurance. Our first line puts Sundin at FACE 95 against Lapointe at 89, so we win that draw and control possession. Behind him, Murray at 86 is a big body but 50 TOUG is not the problem Jackman and Klesla cannot solve at 93 and 80 checking.

**Their depth is thin.** Third line centres Vernarsky at 74 OVR, fourth line Johnson at 72. Our L3 has Richards at 86, Nash at 85 and Roberts at 85. That is a full ten-point gap across the line, and auto-pairing puts it together. Games open up on lines 3 and 4 when one team has a full twelve points of depth advantage.

**Goalie gap is 12 points.** Luongo reads 97, Raycroft reads 85. Against our shot volume we should convert enough to cover any single lapse.

**No change.** We are 5-1-0 with 1.67 GA per game. They are 2-1-1 allowing 2.75. The line matching already favors us on three of four lines and is competitive on the first. Development priority does not apply (January 15 principle: maximize quality against legitimate opponents), and the sheet already maximizes it.

## Owed

**Owed item #1: D evaluation and sell-list update after 6 games.**

**Jackman** is still the sell. His rate has cooled from 1.00 pts/g at 4 games to 0.83 at 6 (5 points, 27.8 MPG). That's still well above his 0.48 career rate, which means his trade value is elevated right now but the window is closing as he regresses toward mean. At $0.70M x 2 years he's the cheapest quality top-pair minutes in the league. The urgency on this has increased since my October 16 note.

**Klesla** at 26.7 MPG, 0.33 pts/g, 87 OVR, age 23, $0.90M x 1 year. He's the one new name worth raising with the GM. Heavy minutes, modest output, and he's on an expiring deal. If we don't re-sign him he becomes a rental whose value peaks now; if we do, he's a cheap anchor. But losing both him and Jackman would gut the blue line, so it's one or the other.

**The minute spread has improved.** Jackman and Klesla combined now hold 46% of D minutes (54.5 of 118.1 total). At game 4 that was 56%. Fischer (19.8) and Kaberle (19.5) are eating properly. The endurance-crater concern from my October 13 note is easing.

**No change to Fischer or Kaberle.** Fischer at 4 points in 6 on 19.8 MPG and 84 OVR is playing like the keeper the GM wants him to be. Kaberle at 2 points is low-output but 85 OVR and the GM's stated star. Both stay.

**Stahle and Colaiacovo** each play 12 minutes and combined for 2 points. They're the development pair and that's fine for now.

**McCabe** ($3.00M x 3, not dressed) and **Eminger** ($2.20M x 4, not dressed) are salary-dump candidates but neither has a realistic market given their rates and term.

# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-10-18

Toronto 4-1-0, 8 pts after 5 games.

## Role coverage

**Toughness is the only gap this roster cannot fix from within.** Zero forwards and zero defencemen read 80+ on the displayed TOUG scale; the highest is Jackman at 75. Every other role has internal depth the Coach is simply not deploying yet.

**McCabe** sits at 86 CHKG, 94 ENDU, 30 years old, and is in no line. **Tucker** carries 83 CHKG, 30 years old, also unlined. The Coach's standing complaint — "no forward who combines 75+ checking with enough skill to hold a third-line role" — is answered by two men who already wear the jersey. Lining them is a coach-side decision, not a trade target.

**Wallin** at 83 FACE and 25 is the only faceoff draw outside Sundin, and he is also unlined. That gives the club three potential centres (Chlup 75, Roberts 75, Richards 70) all below 80 on the draw. Wallin fixes one slot if he holds the ice.

**The top-end scoring is old.** Mogilny is 36, Roberts 39, Sundin 34. They carry 426 combined career points and no player under 30 is positioned to absorb that production next season. Gaborik at 23 (92 base) and Nash at 21 (1.00 pts/g on 20.7 MPG) are the heirs, but neither has shown 0.80+ pts/g yet.

**Defence checking is thin by count.** Jackman (87 CHKG, 24), Fischer (82, 25), and McCabe (86, 30) are the three 80+ D-side checkers. With Eminger undressed at 21 and Colaiacovo stalling, a single injury to Jackman or Fischer drops the club to two adequate checking D and no true third pair.

**Koltsov** at 92 SPEE, 24, is unlined. He is a speed forward the Coach could dress on the fourth line or a PP unit without displacing anyone.

The only external acquisition that closes two gaps at once is toughness plus checking on a forward who can hold a top-nine role. Bell (CHI, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, 82 base, 24) remains the single best fit from the league scan. Jovanovski (VAN, 89 TOUG, 94 CHKG, 89 base, 29) does the same on defence but costs more and is only one year of control.

## Trajectory

Is this club aging into a cliff? No — the age shape is the healthiest in the league (13 players ≤23, only 5 at 30+) — but the contract architecture creates a July 2009 wall where 11 players and $37.40M expire in one week, and the immediate July 2006 window has two players who cannot walk. The money works today: payroll $89.94M against $33.95M profit means revenue (ticket, TV, prestige bonuses) covers the books, and ticket price at $112 with 18,316 attendance and 1,098 prestige has more room to climb. The risk isn't a single season's payroll. It's four simultaneous contract cliffs arriving between now and 2009, with no picks to paper over them.

**Chlup** at 19, $2.34M, 1 year left, 6 points in 5 games, POTE 95: he is the club's center of the future and he is expiring in nine months. **Luongo** at 26, $1.60M, 1 year left, 97 POTE, 3 wins in 3 starts: same summer, same risk. Both must be locked on 5-6 year deals the first week of July 2006. These are not trade candidates — they are the two contracts the next decade of this franchise is built on.

**Gaborik** is the structural problem nobody can undo. $11.90M/year on a 5-year deal, 13% of the entire $89.94M payroll committed to a player producing 1 point in 4 games at 16 MPG. If he becomes the winger this roster needs, the deal is fine. If he stays a bottom-six scratch, it's dead money for five years and the scoring-bridge void persists while Gaborik eats the budget. The Coach's 16 MPG experiment must resolve within 10 games. If production stays below 0.40 pts/g, he is a February trade candidate despite the salary, because a player who can't produce at 23 won't produce at 25, and four more years of $11.90M with no production poisons every future deal.

**Klesla** is expiring anyway ($0.90M, 1 year, 23, POTE 97). That makes him the cheapest currency on the roster. The Jovanovski target (VAN, 89 base, 93 TOUG, 94 CHKG, 29, $2.30M expiring) fills the toughness gap the Coach has flagged since April. A Klesla-plus-R2 package costs nothing the club wants to keep, since Klesla walks in July regardless. VAN have 13 expiring contracts and the league's lowest payroll — they are rebuilding and a 23-year-old POTE 97 defenseman is exactly what they want. This trade funds the February 2006 deadline from expiring assets, which is how you buy without mortgaging the 2009 cluster.

**The July 2009 cluster** is the real cliff. Sundin at $8.40M will be 38, Mogilny's already gone by then, Kaberle at $4.10M will be 31 and declining, and Gaborik, Richards, Chistov and Nash all come due in the same week at combined salaries of $29.70M in their primes. The fix starts now: the young players getting minutes this season (Chlup, Nash, Stahle, Colaiacovo, Jackman, Gardener) are the 2009 replacements, and every one of them needs to be a regular by February or the depth behind the 2009 cluster won't exist. That's the Coach's problem tonight, but it's the GM's problem in 2009, and the window to grow them is this season.

**Draft capital** is three picks (R1, R2, R3, all their own). The R1 is the only pick worth packaging for a rental; the R2 funds the Klesla-for-Jovanovski deal above. Spending the R1 at the February deadline on a playoff rental for a club sitting at 4-1 is the right call if the return closes the scoring gap, because the R1 from a 4-1 team would be late-round anyway. The R3 is depth-draft fodder and should be used for scouting value.

**The 2-year bucket** (7 players, $10.20M, July 2007) carries a quieter risk: Stahle ($0.97M), Jackman ($0.70M) and Spacek ($1.13M) are all young and developing and all come up two summers from now. If they've earned real roles by then, re-signing three of them alongside the Gaborik/Richards/Chistov cluster creates a renewal queue you can't staff. If they haven't, they walk and the depth collapses. The Coach's demand to give them minutes now is the trajectory play, not just the development play.

## Calendar

The question is whether March 19, 152 days away, finds us buying or selling, and what happens to the nine contracts expiring this summer. We are 4-1-0 and first in the East after five games, which means nothing yet. The deadline decision comes in February when the standings have weight; the summer decision is already clear because seven of nine expiring players are core pieces under 26 who must be locked before July.

**Mogilny** (36, $5.50M, 90 base, POTE 56) is the one unambiguous seller. He is the highest-paid player on a roster whose payroll is $89.94M, he is 36 with 3 points in 5 games, and there is no version of next season that includes him at this price. Move him at the deadline for a first-rounder or a high-potential young player. The over-80 expiring mechanic means he can fetch a pick even if no team "needs" him.

**Tucker** (30, $1.30M, 79 base, POTE 80) was already a chip last March and nothing has changed. He is rostered but unlined, carries no potential upside, and is the cheapest path to a late-round pick. If he is still unlined at the deadline, trade him.

**Spezza** (22, $1.00M, 73 base, POTE 98) is the wildcard. The Coach's five-game clock is running. If Spezza is still undressed when the clock hits zero, he becomes a deadline chip — a 98-potential centre at 22 has value to rebuilding clubs even at 73 overall. If he plays and produces, he becomes a 5-year renewal target. Either way, the answer comes before February.

**Luongo** (26, $1.60M, 91 base, POTE 98) is the priority renewal. Three starts, 179 minutes, and the best base rating on the roster among goalies. Lock him on 5-6 years the same week Chlup's deal comes up. This is the single most important summer signing.

**Chlup** (19, $2.34M, 82 base, POTE 96) needs 5-6 years at once. He is the first-line centre at 19, already at 6 points in 5 games on 20 minutes a night. His current salary of $2.34M will look cheap at renewal; expect his asking price to rise, but the term matters more than the figure.

**Klesla** (23, $0.90M, 78 base, POTE 98) is the cheapest top-potential defenseman in the league. He plays 27 minutes a night already and his base is still 78, meaning the gap between what he is and what he can become is enormous. Lock 5-6 years before that gap closes and his price doubles.

**Koltsov** (24, $1.10M, 68 base, POTE 95) is still raw at 68 overall but 24 with 95 potential. Three years is enough to see if he breaks through without overcommitting at his current level.

**Ouellet** (24, $0.90M, 81 base, POTE 98) is a backup with starter's potential. With Luongo locked long-term, Ouellet is either the insurance policy or a trade piece in a goalie deal. Keep him through the season; reassess in July.

**St. Jacques** (25, $0.80M, 66 base, POTE 95) at 66 overall is the lowest-graded player on the expiring list. The POTE 95 at age 25 is an oddity. Two years at his current salary tests whether the potential is real without blocking a roster spot.

The deadline itself is 152 days away. Per the GM's standing position from January 2005, negotiations open late February. The February priority is the ATL binary: Heatley or Kovalchuk, whichever club cannot keep both. Toughness at 82+ solves the Coach's persistent gap and scoring depth at the same time. The package must be funded by Mogilny's pick value plus possibly Tucker, since we own no picks above the fourth round.

---

On the owed task **#2 (Luongo/DiPietro goalie monitoring)**: This is resolved. Luongo is on our roster (26, $1.60M, 91 base). The GM closed all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19 after acquiring him. The DiPietro tracking that accompanied that task is moot since Luongo is here and Ouellet/Tellqvist provide depth. Task closed.

## League scan

**The question this phase answers: who across the league closes our forward-toughness gap, our scoring bridge, or our D-side checking depth, and which of their clubs will say yes?** We are 4-1-0 and contending, so the direction is buy, not sell. The season is five games old and the deadline is March 2006, so these are February targets, not January ones.

**Jovanovski** (VAN, 29, 89 TOUG, 94 CHKG, $2.30M expiring) remains the top target. VAN carry 10 expiring contracts out of 30 and the league's lowest payroll at $46.36M. They are in full rebuild mode and a 23-year-old POTE 97 defenceman (Klesla) plus our R2 is what they want in return. He closes the D-side checking depth problem in one move. This package was identified on October 12 and nothing has changed.

**Bell** (CHI, 24, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 base, $900K, 2 years left) is the single forward who closes the toughness gap with control beyond this season. CHI now carry 10 expiring out of 30 rostered players at $50.12M payroll. They are a structural seller this year. The GM's January veto was about Bell's faceoff value being irrelevant to a winger; the toughness and checking argument is different and still stands. Price: Colaiacovo plus R2, or Klesla plus R2 if the Jovanovski deal doesn't materialize.

**The ATL binary** — Heatley (91 base, 24) and Kovalchuk (89 base, 21) both sit at Atlanta on expiring deals, with 9 expiring contracts and the league's second-lowest payroll at $39.13M. ATL at 1-2-0 cannot re-sign both. Whichever one moves becomes the scoring-bridge answer simultaneously with the toughness answer, because both carry 82+ TOUG. This resolves by January when ATL either re-signs one and lists the other, or lists both.

**Cammalleri** (LA, 22, POTE 98, $1.10M expiring) is the highest-upside July UFA target. LA carry 12 expiring contracts and $50.80M payroll. He produced 60 points in 61 games last season. This is not a February trade candidate because LA will likely keep him until the deadline and then lose him free; it is a July signing target and the GM should be ready with a 5-year offer the first week of July 2006.

**Avery** (LA, 25, 93 FACE, 88 CHKG, 83 TOUG, $400K, 2 years left) is the cheapest closing-three-gaps option. His production is the problem: 6 points in 57 games last season. He fills a role, not a scoring line. If the Coach's third-line checking problem persists after McCabe and Tucker are lined, Avery at $400K on a controllable deal is the insurance policy. LA are sellers for the same structural reasons as above.

**On the GM's October 16 question about dumping salary versus rotating players:** Keep everyone and rotate. We cleared $33.95M profit on a $89.94M payroll. The constraint is not money, it is development minutes. Every veteran we dump takes a shift from Chlup, Nash, Jackman, Stahle, and the July 2009 replacements never materialize. The only exception is Gaborik at $11.90M — if he hasn't crossed 0.40 pts/g by mid-February, he becomes the next Jovanovski-sized package, because the salary is the one number that poisons every future deal.

## Trade construction

**The question this phase answers: which two or three packages convert our surplus and expiring assets into the toughness and scoring depth the roster cannot manufacture, and why would each counterparty say yes?** We are 4-1-0, contending, deadline is March 2006, and the GM's October 16 answer on salary was "keep everyone and rotate." So every proposal here is a buy funded by players we would lose anyway, never by the Chlup-Nash-Jackman core.

**Klesla plus our second-round pick for Jovanovski** is the cleanest deal on the board. Klesla is 23, POTE 97, $0.90M, and his contract expires in July. We lose him for nothing if we do nothing. VAN carry 10 expiring contracts on the league's lowest payroll at $46.36M; they are in full teardown and a POTE 97 defenceman with four years of development left is exactly the currency they want. We get Jovanovski at 89 base, 93 TOUG, 94 CHKG, which is the only single acquisition that closes the D-side checking gap the Coach flagged in April. We go from $89.94M to $91.34M, a $1.40M increase against $33.95M profit. Acceptance is uncertain but VAN's incentive is structural: they need young defencemen on cheap deals and this is one arriving for a second-rounder.

**Colaiacovo plus our second-round pick for Bell** is the forward-side package. Colaiacovo is 22 with POTE 99 but the Coach wrote him off in May at 0.39 pts/g on 17.9 MPG, and the Coach's October report uses him only to cap Klesla's minutes, not as a projected top-pair defenceman. CHI carry 10 expiring on $50.12M payroll and are structural sellers. A 22-year-old with POTE 99 on four years at $1.40M is a rebuild piece. We get Bell at 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 base, 24 years old, $900K, two years of control. He is the only player in the league whose TOUG is high enough to crack 80 on the displayed scale even with form drag, which is the exact gap the Coach has flagged since April. We actually save $500K net. The risk is that the GM considers Colaiacovo defensive core alongside Eminger and McCabe; if so, this package dies and Bell needs a different price.

**Koltsov plus Tucker plus our second-round pick for whichever of Heatley or Kovalchuk ATL lists** is the scoring-bridge play. Koltsov is 24, POTE 94, $1.10M, expiring, and has played zero games. Tucker is 30, POTE 79, $1.30M, expiring, and also unlined. We are giving two men we are not using on contracts we would lose in July. ATL at 1-2-0 with 9 expiring on $39.13M cannot re-sign both stars; whichever one walks needs to land somewhere that gives ATL something back. Two expiring contracts plus a second-rounder gives them salary relief and a pick. Heatley at 91 base, 24, or Kovalchuk at 89 base, 21, both carry 82+ TOUG, so this closes toughness and scoring at the same time. This will not happen before January when ATL decides who to re-sign, so it is a February proposal. Acceptance is the least certain of the three because we do not yet know which player moves or his salary.

**If none land.** Line McCabe at third pairing (86 CHKG, 94 ENDU, currently unlined) and Tucker on the third line (92 CHKG stored, 88 TOUG stored, unlined). Wallin draws at 83 FACE and is also unlined. These are Coach-side decisions that answer the checking and faceoff complaints without a trade, though they do not answer the 80+ TOUG gap on the displayed scale or the scoring bridge. The toughness gap is a cosmetic problem for one season and a structural one after Mogilny and Roberts retire in 2006; the Jovanovski and Bell packages fix both problems, and the internal stopgaps fix neither cleanly.

## Owed

**#2 — Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window.**

This task is closed. Luongo is on our roster at 97 overall, 26, $1.60M/year, 1 year remaining. The February 2005 trade window passed eight months ago; the GM closed all goalie monitoring on March 19, 2005 with the standing order "Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks." The job was delivered.

**Luongo** at 97 overall in 3 games this season is exactly the high-90s goalie the GM set as the target on January 15, 2005. His $1.60M salary is the lowest of any goalie above 95 in the league (Giguere is $12.56M, Brodeur $6.70M). The live question is now renewal, not availability: 1 year left means he is a UFA in July 2006. Per the existing note, lock him and Chlup the same week, 5-6 years each, Luongo first.

**DiPietro** at NYI reads 88 overall, age 24, $1.10M, 0 years left, 3 GP. He is an expiring pending UFA. He is not a trade target this season because we already have Luongo (97) and Belfour (90+), and the GM's October 16 question about rotating good players suggests we are not shedding depth. If Belfour retires mid-season, DiPietro at 24 and expiring becomes the logical deadline backup for a late-round pick. Otherwise, no action.

Nothing has changed that requires the GM to act this week. The renewal conversation is July 2006. The DiPietro contingency is dormant.
