# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-10-18

Next game at MTL on Wednesday 19 October 2005.

## Development opportunity

Five games in, and the question is simple: is anyone young and useful sitting on the bench while someone less productive plays? The answer is yes, and the names are Spezza, Eminger, and Alexeev.

**Spezza** is the loudest one. POTE 99, morale 88 (lowest of any young player by three points), zero games played. Last season his minutes collapsed to 4.8 MPG and now he is not even dressing. At 22 with a 99 scouting number, six minutes on the fourth line is not a development plan, it is a slow bleed. If he cannot earn a fourth-line role in training camp, we are wasting him and his morale will keep sliding.

**Eminger** is the same shape. POTE 99, zero games, and locked at $2.20M for four more years per my correction. His production was genuinely poor last year at 0.36 pts/g, so his case is weaker than Spezza's, but a 21-year-old on a multi-year deal who cannot get a shift in five games is either a trade candidate or needs a role. Sitting him further helps nobody.

**Alexeev** played one of five games and scored 2 points in it. He outproduced both L4 wingers (Spacek and Upshall, 3 points each in 5 games) on far fewer opportunities. At 23 with POTE 94, the rate-to-role mismatch I flagged in April is still unresolved. He should be dressing over someone on the fourth line.

**Chlup** at 19 is getting exactly what I asked for last season. 20 MPG on the second line, 6 points in 5 games (1.20 per game). He has earned every minute and then some. No change.

**Nash** is at 19.2 MPG on the third line with 4 points in 5 (0.80 per game), up from last season's 0.43 collapse. The rate is back. He is where he belongs.

**Chistov** at 14.2 MPG on the second line with 0.80 per game is a substantial improvement on last year's 0.29. He has moved up because he earned it.

**Gaborik** at 1 point in 4 games (0.25 per game) on the first line with 17.2 MPG looks cold, but we are four games old and I have no way to separate form from inability at this point. He is getting his games. Watch it, do not act on it.

**Klesla** at 27 MPG and **Colaiacovo** at 13.0 MPG are fine. **Stahle** at 12.6 MPG on the third pair at 21 is appropriate. **Gardener** at 4.4 MPG with POTE 98 and zero points in five games is hard to judge, but the minutes are so low that even a hot performance would not show. Flag for re-evaluation at 15 games.

## Development trends

The development question in a five-game window is "who is being used and who is being forgotten," because trends haven't had time to form yet. The answer is stark: Chlup is emerging as a true first-line centre while three other young players got one game and then vanished.

**Chlup** at 19 is at 23.5 MPG and 1.25 pts/g across 5 games. Last season he went from 11.0 to 18.2 MPG and his rate doubled. Now we're at 23.5 and the rate is 1.25. He belongs on the first line permanently. I recommended moving him there on October 13 and it wasn't taken; the numbers are now screaming it. At 23.5 MPG he's already the highest-minute forward on the roster.

**Fischer** went from 10.0 to 21.2 MPG and 0.00 to 1.00 pts/g. At 25, that's a breakout in progress. The GM called him a keeper; this window confirms it. No intervention needed, just keep him where he is.

**Jackman** is at 1.00 pts/g on 25.2 MPG after 5 games. My October 16 sell-window note stands. At 0.48 last season and 1.00 now, any buyer sees the current rate. The window is open today.

**Gardener, Spacek, Upshall** all follow the same pattern: 16-17 MPG in game one, then 1.5, 3.2 and 3.5 MPG respectively over the remaining four. They dressed for the opener and were then forgotten. At 20, 20 and 22, a single game followed by the press box teaches nothing. Either give them a real role or stop dressing them. I would scratch all three and dress Gaborik and Chistov as regular wingers instead.

**Spacek** deserves a separate note. Last season his minutes went from 17 to 3.2 by season's end. This season: 17 to 3.2 in five games. The pattern is identical and repeating. The GM needs to decide if Spacek gets 12+ MPG or the experiment is over.

**Richards** at 0.00→1.00 pts/g on 12.2 MPG is a small-sample bounce, but last season's collapse from 1.08 to 0.71 still haunts this read. Watch him through ten games before drawing conclusions.

**Afinogenov** at 0.25 pts/g on 14.2 MPG is the continuation of last year's decline (1.17→0.73→0.25). At 26 with no minutes collapse, the system-fit problem is unsolved.

**Spezza and Eminger** are not playing at all. Spezza at 22 with POTE 99 sat out last season and is sitting again. Eminger at 21, flagged for trade in March, hasn't played a game. These two need a roster decision from the GM, not a line move from me.

**Sundin** at 34, 19.8 MPG and 1.25 pts/g is not showing decline. Neither is Mogilny at 36 or Roberts at 39.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy. Everyone playing sits at 91 morale and nobody has dropped below 88 across the entire roster. No action needed on this front for MTL.

**Richards** is the one I am watching long-term. 25 years old, 12.4 minutes a night, 4 points in 5 games. If his calibre sits at 90-plus as his past rate suggests, he is 8 minutes below band. Morale at 91 has not cracked yet, and at 0.8 pts/g on those minutes he is efficient enough that I am not forcing an intervention before week ten.

**Afinogenov** is the same situation in milder form: 26, 14.6 MPG, 0.4 pts/g. Morale stable at 91, so no change tonight.

**The defencemen** (delivering on #1): Jackman at 28.4 MPG and 1.0 pts/g in 5 games is the hottest D on the club. Klesla is grinding 27.0 with 0.4 pts/g. Fischer is producing 0.8 pts/g on the second pair at 19.0. Kaberle has been quiet offensively (0.2 pts/g) but his minutes are reasonable. The concentration problem I flagged in early October has eased: Jackman and Klesla were at 33 and 34.5, now at 28.4 and 27.0 as the other pairs absorb more. The load is manageable. For end-of-season evaluation: Fischer at 0.8 pts/g and 19 MPG is the best keeper among the non-top-pair D, and Jackman's current rate is almost certainly unsustainable against his 0.48 career number. He stays on the sell-at-peak list.

No changes tonight. The room is right.

## Role composition

The penalty-kill units are the one place on the sheet where the arrangement doesn't fit the job, and it's fixable without touching a line.

**K2** carries Kaberle and Klesla, two offensive and speed defensemen whose checking grades pull the unit mean down to 72 with a best of 87 (Spacek). They belong on the power play and at 5-on-5, not on the kill. Roberts (86 checking) and Nash (82) are both dressed and available for PK slot assignment without disturbing L3. Moving them onto K2 alongside Spacek and Upshall raises the checking mean from 72 to roughly 84. PK units carry no chemistry cost the way forward lines do, so this is a free swap.

**L1** is built right. Jackman at 92 checking and 78 toughness anchors what is otherwise the most offensive line on the roster (Gaborik 99 scoring, Sundin 96 playmaking). You want him there eating minutes from the opponent's top pair.

**L3** is our shutdown unit and that's correct. Roberts 86, Nash 82, checking mean 77. Richards at 94 playmaking means this line can also exit the zone with the puck, which is what you want from a third unit facing top competition.

**L2 and L4** suit their jobs. Fischer at 87 checking gives L2 enough bite to not be a liability against second pairs. L4 at 72/87 checking is thin but it's a fourth line; Spacek carries it.

**The roster gap is checking depth beyond the top two.** Jackman 92 and Roberts 86 are the only forwards/defensemen above 85. Nash at 82 is third. With McCabe (83) scratched for development purposes, one injury to Jackman or Roberts leaves us with nobody to shadow a top line. This is the same gap I flagged in April and it hasn't closed. It's not a lineup problem; it needs a trade or a draft pick.

## Opponent matchup

**Is there a specific matchup adjustment that gives us an edge against Montreal on Wednesday?** No. Every pairing goes our way, and the only risk is undiscipline or a hot night from Theodore.

**Montreal's roster** tops out at 80 (Komisarek, Zednik). Their first line — Nylander 76, Bulis 75, Zednik 80 — is our second-line assignment at worst. Their power play is 1-for-13, so their special teams will not test us. Theodore at 87 is the one player who can steal this game, but that is a shooting-night problem, not a lineup problem.

**The auto-pairing already gives us what we want.** First line (Sundin/Gaborik/Mogilny) draws Komisarek 80 and Markov 74 — Markov has CHKG 64 and TOUG 50, which is the softest top-pair defence we will face all month. Second line (Chlup/Chistov/Afinogenov) gets Beauchemin 71 and Rivet 73. Third line (Richards/Nash/Roberts) gets Quintal 71 at 36 years old and Spacek 72 at 31. All three defensive pairs are beatable by the line that draws them. No slot reorder improves this.

**Faceoffs go our way on all four lines.** Their centres are 68, 57, 75, 63. Ours are 95, 80, 80, 59. The only line where we are not clearly favored is the fourth (Spacek 59 vs Jaspers 75), and that is a low-danger shift.

**Decision: no change.** The matchups are set in our favor by the current slot order. The D-minute concentration issue (Jackman/Klesla at 56% of defence minutes) is a season problem for later, not a reason to weaken the top pair tonight when Markov is the man we want to attack. Start Luongo at 97; GM checks the fatigue icon before confirming per the January 19 order.

## Owed

**D-man sell review, 11th delivery.** The minute concentration alarm I flagged after four games has eased: Jackman and Klesla now hold 47% of all D minutes (277 of 593 across five games), down from 56%. The pressure valve is working and their endurance risk for December has dropped.

**Jackman** is 5-0-5 in 5 games at 28.4 MPG on $0.70M. His career rate is 0.48. He is at 1.00 right now, which means every GM in the league sees a top-pairing D on a bargain contract. The sell window from my October 16 note is still wide open. If he cools to 0.70 next month his value drops by 30%. Move him at the deadline or early summer.

**Klesla** sits at 2-1-3 in 5 games (0.40 pts/g) on $0.90M with one year left. Below my 0.60 threshold, but five games is noise. He was 0.48 last season over a full sample. He's 23. I'm not pushing a sell here yet — give him to 20 games.

**Fischer** is 1-3-4 in 5 at 19 MPG, 84 OVR. GM called him a keeper on January 15. He is producing. Settled.

**Kaberle** at 0-1-1 in 5 is the lowest scorer among top-pair D, but the GM called him "a star defenseman" on January 15 and shut him down against Washington for that role. Not touching him.

**Stahle** (1-1-2 in 5, 12.6 MPG, 76 OVR, $0.97M x 2) is the cheap young fourth-pairing D doing what he should. Keep developing him.

**Colaiacovo** is 0-0-0 in 5 games at 13 MPG. Zero points, 76 OVR, $1.40M x 4. He's the weakest man in the current rotation by production margin. Not a sell-list emergency at this price, but if a buyer offers anything for a 22-year-old 76-OVR D on a cheap deal, take it.

**McCabe** remains undressed. 84 OVR, $3.00M x 3, recent rate 0.48. The sell case from May stands: a declining 30-year-old taking a top-pairing salary who doesn't dress is a wasted asset.

**Eminger** (82 OVR, 21, $2.20M x 4, undressed) is the most expensive man not playing. His contract correction from May means there's no expiry urgency, but the roster has no room for him and never will. He is a package piece for the next trade, not a trade candidate on his own.

# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-10-16

Toronto 3-1-0, 6 pts after 4 games.

## Role coverage

The one question that matters after four games: can the coach close the checking and toughness gaps with men already on the roster, or does he need a trade? The answer is split — checking is fixable internally, toughness is not.

**Toughness** is the only role with zero players at 80+. Jackman tops the club at 75, McCabe at 73, Tucker at 70. The coach's L3 checking mean of 68 and L4 mean of 72 are symptoms of this: nobody on the bottom two lines can absorb a physical shift without pulling L1 or L2. This is structural. Bell (CHI, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, 24, POTE 81) and Avery (LA, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 93 FACE, 25, $400K, 2 years) are the only targets that close all three gaps at once. Tucker at 92 CHKG is the internal band-aid for checking, but his 70 TOUG means he does not solve the real problem.

**Checking** is thin but not broken. Six players sit at 80+, and two of them — McCabe (86 CHKG, 94 ENDU, 30) and Tucker (83 CHKG, 30) — are on the roster and not lined. Lining McCabe on a defensive pair and dressing Tucker nightly adds two 80+ checkers to the lineup without a trade. That lifts L3/L4 checking without external help.

**Faceoffs** are thin. Only Sundin (90 FACE, 34) and Wallin (83 FACE, not lined) clear 80. Chlup at 75 is adequate for L1C at 19, but L3 and L4 are in the low 70s at best. Wallin being unlined is a waste of the club's only other 80+ draw-taker. Lining him gives a 75–83 range across four centres, which is workable but not good.

**Scoring** looks deep at 11 players 80+, but the age curve is the problem, not the count. Mogilny (94, 36), Sundin (92, 34), Roberts (88, 39) carry the load and are all within three seasons of retirement. Gaborik (92 scoring, 98 speed, 23, POTE 90, $11.90M) is the best young scorer on the roster and he is a healthy scratch. The May 2005 structural void — no under-30 positioned to absorb the veterans' 426 combined points — is now worse because Gaborik isn't playing. Dress him or move him; at 4 games into the season with 0 GP, his trade value is already eroding.

**Speed** is the deepest role with 25 players at 80+. Gaborik 98, Afinogenov 96, Mogilny 94, Koltsov 92 (not lined). No gap here. Koltsov's 92 SPEE and 24 years make him the cheapest internal depth if a winger needs rest.

**Durability** is thin at 5 players 80+, but Roberts (98, 39) and Afinogenov (95, 26) cover the top roles. Klesla at ENDU 63 is the coach's matchup concern against NYR specifically; Fischer and Kaberle carrying more of the load protects him, which is a line problem, not a roster gap.

**Goalies** are solved. Luongo 26 with a 0.50 GAA and 0.983 SV in 2 GP, Ouellet 24 backing him. No action needed.

## Trajectory

The cliff isn't an age cliff — it's a scoring cliff with a contract cluster bolted to it, and the money is fine but pointed at the wrong men.

**Age shape** is healthy in aggregate: 13 players at 23 or under, 16 at 24–29. The manual wants 5–7 veterans and ~20 young players, and at 34 bodies with 5 over 30, Toronto is at the bottom of the veteran count. The problem is the 30–33 bucket holds only Tucker and McCabe. There is no bridge generation between Mogilny/Roberts/Sundin leaving and the Chlup/Nash/Colaiacovo group being proven. The void is structural, not a form dip.

**The scoring cliff.** Mogilny is 36, POTE 55, $5.50M, one year left. Roberts is 39, POTE 52, $4.90M, two years. Sundin is 34, POTE 60, $8.40M, four years — he's locked but declining. Combined, these three carry the bulk of the offence and none of them is getting better. Chlup (19, POTE 95) and Nash (21, POTE 95) are the successors on paper, but neither is yet carrying a 0.70+ pts/g pace. The Iginla target from April — 93 base, 1.92 pts/g, $6.50M expiring at CGY — remains the only single move that fills the gap without requiring a teenager to leap two levels at once.

**The July 2006 renewal cluster.** Nine players expire, $15.44M total, but the four that matter are Chlup ($2.34M), Luongo ($1.60M), Spezza ($1.00M), and Klesla ($0.90M). That's $5.84M walking if not addressed, and four 5–6 year deals simultaneously will push payroll toward $100M. Luongo and Chlup go first (already flagged), Spezza and Klesla second. This is a summer-plan problem, not a trade problem, but it needs planning now because the renewal mechanics require negotiation time.

**Gaborik is the payroll problem.** At $11.90M per year on a healthy scratch, he is the single largest money-to-production mismatch on the roster. His POTE of 90 and age of 23 make him tradeable, but every game he sits devalues him. The Coach's deadline was mid-October; that is now. Either he plays or he moves, and the window for a decent return closes by January.

**The money.** Profit is $35.05M on $89.94M payroll. There is room. Iginla at $6.50M, Chlup at a renewed rate (say $3–4M), and Luongo at a star rate (say $4–5M) together add roughly $12–15M, which the profit absorbs without strain. The constraint is not money; it's the number of players you can renew in the same week and the draft capital to fund any February acquisition.

**Draft capital.** Own R1, R2, R3 for June 2006. The old "no picks beyond a 4th" finding from January is obsolete — the Luongo deal spent the 2005 first, and the 2005 draft replenished the shelf. An R1 is enough to fund a mid-tier February rental (Jovanovski at $2.30M expiring remains the best defensive fit), and the R2 plus a player like Tucker covers smaller needs.

## Calendar

The deadline is 154 days away and we are four games into a season; the only calendar work today is building the summer renewal list and setting conditional deadline intentions we re-test in late February.

**Renewal priority is clear.** Luongo at 26 and $1.60M is a franchise goalie whose contract dies next July. Chlup at 19 and $2.34M is the first-line centre the Coach just installed. Both expire the same week and must be locked on 5-6 years in the same move. Luongo goes first because Tellqvist behind him is a clear step down and losing either one is a season. Klesla at 23, $900K, POTE 98 is the third lock; at 78 base he is still raw, but the trajectory is the whole reason we drafted him.

**Tucker and St. Jacques are chips, not keepers.** The GM already designated Tucker as trade currency on March 19 last season. He is 30, $1.30M, expiring. St. Jacques at 25 and $800K is the second piece in the Buffalo package for Begin. Neither returns in July.

**Mogilny at 36 and $5.50M is the payroll question.** If we are contending in March, he is a rental we ride. If not, he is the biggest salary dump available and the over-80 mechanic likely still works on him for a pick. At 37 next season he is not a re-signing regardless.

**Ouellet is the backup problem.** At 24, POTE 98, 81 base, he is a capable NHL backup on a $900K deal, and the GM's Feb 2005 language ("we do not want to use Ouellet as the only backup") was about playoff depth behind Belfour. Next season Belfour may be gone. Re-sign him on 2 years at current money; he is the best cheap insurance we have.

**Koltsov is a borderline call.** 68 base at age 24 with POTE 95 means the development is slow. He is 75 overall today but that number includes form. A 2-year deal at $900K-$1.00M is fair if he makes the roster; if camp says he does not, let him walk.

**Spezza is the emergency.** The Coach demands L3C immediately; morale at 88 is lowest on the roster; if undressed past 5 games he becomes a deadline chip like Tucker. POTE 98 at 22 and $1.00M means the value is real but decays with every scratched game. The decision is this week, not in March.

**Gaborik at $11.90M on the healthy scratch is a deadline problem.** He is not expiring (not on the list), so the over-80 pick mechanic does not apply. If he is still benched in January when trade talks open, we are looking for any team that will take a large salary for a player whose game count has collapsed. The window for value is now narrowing.

**Eminger at 21, POTE 99, scratched** has the same 5-game clock from the Coach. If he is not dressed or moved, he joins Tucker as a March chip. His base value is enormous and wasting it on the press box is the worst outcome available.

**Draft capital:** we own no pick better than a 4th round. The June draft should target goaltenders per the GM's standing order, and any deadline deal that yields a young high-POTE player is preferable to a pick we cannot convert into a roster player.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: who across the league closes our toughness gap (zero players at 80+ TOUG) and scoring bridge simultaneously, and can we actually get them. The answer: Heatley and Kovalchuk at ATL are a binary choice where we get one, and ATL at 9 expiring with $8.37M in expiring payroll must move one of them. Bertuzzi at VAN is the immediate rental if ATL holds both.

**Heatley** is the top target. 91 base, TOUG 82, CHKG 88, 4 points in 2 games at 20.5 MPG, 24 years old, POTE 86, $1.10M expiring. He is the first player in the league who clears the toughness threshold AND carries elite scoring. ATL at 2 points with 9 expiring deals and $8.37M in expiring salary cannot retain both him and Kovalchuk — my February note established this binary. Whichever ATL keeps, the other moves. Heatley at 91 base and 2.00 pts/g pace this season makes him the more likely keeper, but ATL may prefer the younger Kovalchuk.

**Kovalchuk** is the mirror target. 89 base, TOUG 85, 5 points in 2 games at 20 MPG, 22 years old, POTE 86, $1.10M expiring, 99 SPEE. Same binary, same club, same contract. If ATL keeps Heatley, Kovalchuk is ours for an R1 and a young player. His TOUG 85 is even higher than Heatley's, and at 22 he has three more development years than Heatley.

**Bertuzzi** at VAN is the best available if both ATL players stay. 94 base, TOUG 85, CHKG 89, 5 points in 3 games at 21 MPG, $2.60M expiring. He is 30 with POTE 58 — this is a one-year fix, not a bridge. But 94 base with 85 TOUG and 89 CHKG is exactly the profile the Coach needs tonight. VAN carry 10 expiring, $7.50M in expiring payroll, $46.36M total (lowest in league), and are rebuilding around the Sedins and Jovanovski. Bertuzzi is not part of that future.

**Iginla** at CGY remains the pure scoring bridge from the April plan: 93 base, 1.92 pts/g, $6.50M expiring. CGY at 4 points with 9 expiring and $22.83M profit. He doesn't solve toughness (TOUG unconfirmed but below 85 given his forward frame), but 93 base with real production at 27 makes him the best offensive answer if ATL holds both stars.

**Jovanovski** is the February D-side target already flagged: 89 base, TOUG 93, CHKG 94, 30.3 MPG, $2.30M expiring. He fills toughness on the back end, not the front. VAN will move him if their rebuild accelerates — 10 expiring, lowest payroll in the league, 3 points in 3 games showing they're comfortable without his production.

**Aulin** at LA is the cheap faceoff projection: 71 base, FACE 85, POTE 95, 23, $900K expiring. LA at 12 expiring and $21.73M in expiring payroll (most in league) will deal him for a late pick. He doesn't close the toughness gap, but at POTE 95 and $900K he's the cheapest long-term L3C answer available.

**Drury** at BUF (89 base, FACE 85, 89 pts pace, 29, $2.00M expiring) and **Deadmarsh** at LA (89 base, TOUG 79, CHKG 79, 30, $2.80M expiring) are both close but miss the toughness threshold. Drury at TOUG 76 and Deadmarsh at TOUG 79 leave the primary gap unresolved. They're upgrades over what we have but not answers to the structural problem.

```json

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: what packages close the zero-TOUG gap and the scoring bridge, and why would the other GM say yes? Three proposals follow, ranked by how completely they fix our problems.

**Kovalchuk** is the best target in the league for Toronto's two structural gaps simultaneously. TOUG 85 solves toughness, 89 base with 5 points in 2 games solves scoring, 22 years old with POTE 86 means he's part of the bridge, not a rental past it. ATL at 2 points with 9 expiring and $8.37M expiring payroll cannot re-sign both him and Heatley. We target whoever ATL doesn't keep.

**Bertuzzi** at 94 base, TOUG 85, CHKG 89 is the immediate fix if ATL holds both stars. He's 30 with POTE 58, so he's a one-year answer to tonight's problem, not the long-term solution. VAN at 3 points with the lowest payroll in the league ($46.36M) have no reason to keep a 30-year-old whose ceiling is set.

**Gaborik for Iginla** is the payroll fix disguised as a trade. At $11.90M on the bench he is the largest money-to-production mismatch in the league; at 23 with POTE 90 and 98/99 speed he still has real trade value that erodes every game he sits. CGY at 4 points and $22.83M profit with 9 expiring would rather own a 23-year-old for five years than lose a 27-year-old for nothing in July. This proposal requires the GM to commit to moving Gaborik first.

## Proposals

**1. Kovalchuk (or Heatley) from ATL** — our best package, addresses both gaps

We give: Koltsov (LW, 24, POTE 94, ACCE 96, $1.10M expiring, 0 GP) + R1 2006.
We get: Kovalchuk (RW, 22, 89 base, TOUG 85, 99 SPEE, POTE 86, $1.10M expiring).

ATL says yes because: they are 2 points with 9 expiring and cannot retain both forwards. Koltsov at 24 with POTE 94 and 96 acceleration is a rebuild asset at an expiring price. The R1 funds the next cycle. They keep Heatley at 91 base as their higher-ceiling forward and shed Kovalchuk for equivalent value. Payroll is neutral ($1.10M for $1.10M); they gain a draft pick they'd otherwise not receive.

If ATL moves Heatley instead: swap Kovalchuk for Heatley (91 base, TOUG 82, CHKG 88, POTE 86, 24). The package holds. Heatley is slightly more proven but one year older with lower upside.

**2. Bertuzzi from VAN** — the toughness rental if ATL is stubborn

We give: Lundmark (LW, 24, POTE 97, ACCE 86, AGIL 83, $0.80M, 1 GP) + R2 2006.
We get: Bertuzzi (LW, 30, 94 base, TOUG 85, CHKG 89, POTE 58, $2.60M expiring).

VAN says yes because: they are 3 points and rebuilding. Bertuzzi at 30 with POTE 58 is not part of the Sedin/Jovanovski future. Lundmark at 24 with POTE 97 and 86 acceleration is the kind of young winger they develop around. The R2 adds depth to a draft class. They shed $1.80M net salary ($2.60M out, $0.80M in), which widens their already-lowest payroll advantage. We gain $1.80M in net salary but it's one year only.

**3. Gaborik for Iginla from CGY** — the scoring bridge and payroll reset

We give: Gaborik (RW, 23, 92 scoring, 98 SPEE, 99 ACCE, POTE 90, $11.90M, 5 years).
We get: Iginla (RW, 27, 93 base, 1.92 pts/g, $6.50M, expiring).

CGY says yes because: they are 4 points with 9 expiring. Iginla's contract expires in July — if they don't trade him, they lose him. Gaborik at 23 with POTE 90 and 98/99 speed on a 5-year deal is a better long-term asset at 4 years younger. CGY's $22.83M profit absorbs the $5.40M salary increase ($11.90M in, $6.50M out) without strain. They trade a known quantity losing a contract year for a projection with five years of control.

We shed $5.40M and remove the roster's worst money-to-production mismatch. The risk: Iginla's TOUG is likely below 85, so this doesn't solve toughness. It's a scoring-and-payroll move, not a toughness move. If ATL and VAN both say no, we can pursue this deal AND still need toughness from elsewhere.

## If none land

Dress Gaborik. At 92 scoring and 98/99 speed he is the best young forward we own. Playing him for 10 games on L2 with Sundin/Mogilny doesn't hurt Chlup or Nash (separate lines) and keeps his trade value alive for February, when we can re-approach ATL, VAN and CGY with fresh desperation and a proven game log behind his name.

## Owed

**#2 — Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window.**

This task is dead. The GM closed it himself on 2005-03-19 ("Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks") after Luongo was acquired. We are now in October 2005, the February window passed seven months ago, and Luongo is on our roster at 97 overall, $1.60M, one year remaining. DiPietro sits at NYI at 88 with zero years left, which means he will be a free agent next summer, but we no longer need a goalie trade window — we have two 90+ goaltenders. The renewal of Luongo at contract expiry is a separate live task already recorded in the vault (Luongo first, then Chlup, same week, 5–6 years each). Nothing further owed here.
