# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-10-16

Next game vs PHX on Monday 17 October 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question here is whether the players with the highest ceilings on this roster are getting games. Four games in, two of them are not.

**Eminger** is the glaring one. Age 21, POTE 99, zero games played. He is the highest-potential defenceman on the roster and he is not even dressing. The GM confirmed in January that Eminger stays as a keeper. Four games into a new season with that kind of upside sitting in the stands is wasted development time we cannot get back.

**Spezza** is the same story. POTE 99, age 22, zero games. Last season his minutes collapsed to 4.8 MPG and I called the year a write-off, but that was last season. This is a clean slate and he is already on the outside. If we drafted him for his ceiling, we owe him a real look.

**Chlup** at 19, 20.0 MPG, 3 points in 4 games on the second line. Exactly where I said he belongs. No concern here.

**Nash** at 21 is back: 4 points in 4 games at 20.0 MPG. That's a 1.0 pts/g pace after last season's halving. Getting everything he earned.

**Klesla** at 23 is carrying 28.5 MPG on the first pair already. That is the same load that broke Jackman last season, and I flagged this exact pattern five days ago. Four games is early, but the trend is identical. He needs relief before December.

**Chistov** at 22 is producing 4 points in 4 games on the third line at 12 MPG. Earning every shift he gets.

**Alexeev** is in 1 of 4 games at 6.0 MPG and has 2 points when he plays. Same mismatch I flagged in April: he outproduces dressed wingers and sits out. At 23 he is close to needing a real answer.

**Gardener** at 20 with POTE 98 is getting 5.2 MPG. His lowest of any dressed young forward. Production is zero so far, so the case for more ice hasn't built itself yet, but the ceiling is enormous and the window is small.

**Spacek**, **Stahle**, **Colaiacovo**, **Upshall** are all in sensible roles for their age. No complaints.

## Development trends

Four games is a short window but enough to see that three young guys are getting buried while two others have broken through, and the pattern tells us more than the numbers alone.

**Nash** is the finding. 1.00 pts/g on 20.7 MPG at 21. Last season his rate halved (0.83 to 0.43) on flat minutes and I flagged him for a system-fit review. He is answering that review himself: 1.00 on more ice, not less. At 21 with his contract length his trade value has just moved sharply up. The GM should know Nash is no longer a project — he is a top-six winger right now.

**Chlup** is finally getting what I asked for in April. 24.7 MPG at 19, up from 6.0 in the opener. His 0.67 rate on that load is strong — for context, 17 points-per-game pace would be 24 goals and assists on a first line. My recommendation to move him to first-line centre was not taken in October and now it appears the usage found him anyway. Good.

**Spacek** at 3.7 MPG and **Gardener** at 1.7 MPG are both dying on the bench at ages 20. Neither is producing (0.33 and 0.00 pts/g). I flagged in March that Spacek's 10 MPG target was dead; now he is below half of that. At these ages development requires games, and they are getting none. Something has to give: dress them or stop dressing them.

**Upshall** at 4.0 MPG is the same story as last season, exactly. 13.4 down to 4.9 last year, 16.0 down to 4.0 now. My March call was "real audition in camp or stop dressing." Neither happened and here we are again.

**Spezza** is 0 games played in 4. Two seasons of the same pattern. The March conclusion that "next camp assignment is the only lever" has been tested and failed. This is now a roster decision, not a development one. Either he gets real minutes or he becomes a trade asset while he still has a roster spot and a team that needs depth.

**Afinogenov** is at 0.00 pts/g on 14.3 MPG. Same pattern as last season's collapse (1.17 to 0.73). The system-fit question I raised in May is now confirmed across two seasons at age 26. He is not going to fix himself.

**Gaborik** at 23 is playing 16 MPG and producing 0.33 pts/g in 3 games. Low sample, but he is on the ice and at that age that is the right direction. Watch whether the minutes climb.

On defence, the load-spreading I flagged on October 13 is working naturally. Jackman dropped from the 41-minute game-1 outlier to 23.7 MPG across four games. Fischer went from 10 to 21.3, Stahle from 6 to 14, Colaiacovo from 6 to 14. The concentration problem is resolving itself through roster rotation.

## Morale watch

The room is fine. Everyone on the active roster sits at 90 or 91 with zero movement since the last save, and no one is trending down. The only sub-90 player is Spezza, and that is a known situation the GM chose.

**Spezza** is the outlier at 88, unchanged across many snapshots. He is 22, has POTE that the GM values, and is getting zero minutes by design. At 88 he sits in the band that costs -1 to every grade. It has not moved further, so the locker room is holding him, but if he stays at zero through December it will start to bite harder. That is a GM decision to make, not a line change.

**Afinogenov** at 14.8 MPG on the third line is the only dressed player whose minutes might be below his expected band. At 26 and 80-89 calibre, the model suggests 17 MPG. He is 2.2 short. Morale is 91 and flat, so it is not biting yet. No change needed today, but if it drops below 90, he needs a look.

**Everyone else** on the four lines is getting roughly what his calibre expects. Chlup and Nash are actually getting more than their band (20 MPG each at 19 and 21, which is above the 17 target for 80-89 men), and that is working for development. The fourth-line kids at 7 MPG are right-sized. The D-pair minutes are natural. No one needs more or less tonight.

## Role composition

The question is whether our units are built from the right people and whether the roster can even fill the roles we need. Short answer: the units are as well-built as this roster allows, but two structural gaps persist and neither is a lineup fix.

**L1 and L2** are clean. Sundin-Roberts-Mogilny gives us 89 scoring mean with Jackman and Klesla behind — top scoring plus top checking on the same line is the ideal build. Chlup-Kaberle-Gaborik is the same shape: faceoff centre at 80, our best D pair in Kaberle-Fischer, and Gaborik at 99 scoring. No reason to touch either.

**L3** is the one that concerns me. Richards and Afinogenov give us 93 and 94 in playmaking, but checking mean is 68 and toughness 63. The best checker we can slot there is Stahle, and he's the D. We have no forward on this roster who combines decent checking (75+) with the ability to play wings on a third unit. This is the same gap I flagged in April.

**Faceoffs** are thin outside Sundin and Chlup. L3 mean is 63, L4 is 61. Wallin sits at 88 but is scratched. If the opponent puts a strong centre against Richards or Gardener, we lose those draws by default. This becomes a matchup lever for the opponent phase.

**Penalty kill** is sound. K1 at checking mean 84 with Jackman, Roberts, Fischer and Chlup is a legitimate first kill. K2 at 72 is acceptable for a second unit. The concern is Kaberle and Klesla carrying both the top pair and K2 minutes. At 4-5 games in the season the load hasn't accumulated yet, but my note from October 13 flagged them eating 56% of all D minutes at 33+ MPG. That will bite by late October if it holds.

**Kaberle on K2** — he's our best stamina D at 91, which helps, but he also anchors L2 and P2. Three units is a lot of ice for a man carrying top-pair minutes. The smaller tool is to lean on Stahle more in K2 situations during games rather than restructure the lineup menu.

## Opponent matchup

What do PHX bring to Maple Leaf Gardens on Monday, and should anything change? Very little. They're 0-3 with 4 goals in 3 games and a power play at 1-for-12. Their top defenceman reads 75 OVR. This is a game where development is free and the D-load problem can be addressed without cost.

**PHX first line** — Sillinger at 81 with FACE 90, Doan at 79 with CHKG 85, Konowalchuk at 78 with AGGR 89. Grit and faceoffs, not speed or skill. Our first pair (Jackman/Klesla at 86/87) handles them comfortably. The auto-pairing means Sundin's line gets Jackman/Klesla regardless, and that's fine.

**PHX defence** — Mara/Tanabe at 75/75, Vaananen/Ference at 73/71, Berehowsky/Brisebois at 72/73. All six under 76. Gaborik at OVR 99, Nash at SHPW 98, Chlup at SHPW 93 — this is a night where the young wingers will find space. No reason to change who plays whom.

**D-minute concentration** — Klesla at 28.5 MPG and Jackman at 28.0 after 4 games. Stahle and Colaiacovo sit at 12.0 each. Against PHX's 1.33 goals per game, their third line (Ricci at 75, Savage at 72) will not punish Stahle and Colaiacovo. The GM can ride his second and third forward lines more tonight and the auto-pairing will feed those minutes to Fischer/Kaberle and Stahle/Colaiacovo without any lineup change. This is the fix I've been waiting for since October 13th, and tonight is the cheapest night to try it.

**Ouellet** starts again at G1 (86 OVR). His ENDU reads 64, which is thin. Per the January 19 standing order, check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming. If he's tired, Tellqvist at 73 goes in against a team that's been stopped for 1.33 goals a night — low risk.

No lineup changes. The lines are right for this opponent. The one thing the GM can do in-game is shift his minutes toward lines 2 and 3 to give Stahle and Colaiacovo a real shift pattern against the weakest forwards they'll see all month.

## Owed

**The defence review, game 4.** Jackman and Klesla's minute concentration is easing — that's the headline change since my October 13th note.

**Jackman** was at 33.0 MPG when I last checked, now 28.0. Still the heaviest load, but no longer at the "endurance will crater by December" threshold. The bigger story is he's at 4 points in 4 games — a 1.00 pts/g pace against 0.48 last season. That hot start inflates his trade value right now. At $0.70M x 2, 24 years old, 86 OVR, this is the best return he'll fetch in any window before his rate regresses. The sell case is unchanged but the urgency is now: move him while the scoring rate is elevated.

**Klesla** at 28.5 MPG, 23, $0.90M x 1. My note from March 23th called him a sell; that was before this year. He's a deadline rental with a controlled expiring contract — hold him, let the market come to us. No urgency to move before February.

**McCabe** is not dressed. 84 OVR, $3.00M x 3, 30 years old. He played 82 games last season at 0.76 season rate with a 0.48 recent window. Now a healthy scratch while Stahle (76) and Colaiacovo (76) get 12 MPG each. He's the clearest dead-man walking on this roster. If we can find a club that needs a top-4 body and absorbs $3.00M x 3, take it. He's not coming back into this lineup.

**Eminger** at 82 OVR, $2.20M x 4, also not dressed. Trade difficulty is the same as always: 4 years and inflated salary for a non-playing defenceman. Low return expected, but the cap hit matters.

**Kaberle** and **Fischer** stay, per the GM's standing orders. **Stahle** (76, 12.0 MPG, 1 goal already at 21) and **Colaiacovo** (76, 12.0 MPG) are fine on the third pair for now.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-10-15
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-10-15

Toronto 2-1-0, 4 pts after 3 games.

## Role coverage

The question this phase answers: can Toronto field a complete roster for the season, or are there roles the current personnel cannot fill at any line combination? The answer is that two roles are missing outright — toughness and fourth-line faceoffs — and one (checking) is covered on paper but the coach is not using it.

**Toughness is missing.** Zero players at TOUG 80+. The best is Jackman at 75, then Roberts 73, McCabe 73, Chlup 70, Tucker 70, Sundin 69. This is not a deployment problem. No line combination of this roster produces a TOUG 80+ presence. Bell (CHI, 88 TOUG, 24, 82 base) remains the target, but the GM killed the faceoff argument for him in January because both he and our wingers are wings. The question is whether the GM will accept Bell purely as the toughness fix this time, or whether we need a different profile entirely. Abid (25, 86 CHKG) is on the roster but his TOUG is well below 70 — he is a checker, not an enforcer.

**Faceoffs are thin but partially fixable internally.** Only Sundin (90 FACE, 34) and Wallin (83 FACE, 25) reach 80. Chlup at 75 is the best dressed centre outside Sundin. The coach's report from May flagged L4 faceoff mean at 52. Wallin at 83 is on the roster but "not lined." Dressing Wallin at L4C solves that problem without acquisition. The remaining gap is L3C, where nobody exceeds 75.

**Checking is covered on paper but absent from the lineup.** Jackman 87, Roberts 86, McCabe 86, Tucker 83, Fischer 82, Upshall 80 — six players at 80+. But McCabe (30, not lined) and Tucker (30, not lined) are in no unit. The coach's L3 checking mean of 68 and L4 mean of 72 are below the personnel available. Sliding McCabe or Tucker to the third or fourth pair raises those numbers immediately.

**Scoring is adequate now and collapses in two years.** Mogilny (94, 36), Sundin (92, 34), Roberts (88, 39) are the top three and they are 36, 34, and 39. Gaborik (92, 23) is the next man but he is a healthy scratch — the Coach's demand from October is unresolved. Without Gaborik dressed, the gap between the veterans and the next 80+ scorer (Afinogenov, 90, 26) is enormous in terms of point production.

**Goalies are solved.** Luongo is 2-0 with a 0.983 save percentage through two games at 26 on $1.60M with one year left. Ouellet is a serviceable backup (86/86/86/76 on the four core grades, ENDU 60 is his weakness). Tellqvist has zero games. No further action needed unless Luongo's renewal slips.

## Trajectory

**The age curve is sound; the cliff is Gaborik's salary, not anyone's birthday.** The roster reads 13 players aged 23 or under, 16 in the 24-29 prime, and only 5 veterans, which is the manual's target band. The problem is that the potential is so deep (12 players carry POTE 97+) that the Coach cannot dress them all, and undressed prospects with POTE 99 (Spezza, Eminger) simply stall.

**Gaborik** costs $11.90M a year for five seasons, 13.2% of a $89.94M payroll, on a 23-year-old who is currently a healthy scratch. That is the single largest competitive waste on the roster. The Coach demanded a decision by mid-October; that week is now. Whether the answer is dress-or-trade, the number sitting idle needs to move either direction.

**Sundin** at $8.40M on four remaining years is the slowest-burning dead money: he turns 38 when the deal expires in July 2009. There is no mid-contract renegotiation, no trade partner that takes $8.40M at 37, so the only answer is to wait. $33.60M of dead value over four years, unavoidable.

**July 2006 is a small renewal summer and that is good news.** Nine contracts worth $15.44M come up, but Mogilny ($5.50M at 37) and Tucker ($1.30M at 31) will almost certainly walk, freeing $6.80M. The critical re-signings are Chlup ($2.34M, POTE 95, turning 20) and Luongo ($1.60M, POTE 97, turning 27). Both on 5-6 year deals, the same week, Chlup first. Klesla (POTE 97) and Spezza (POTE 99) are development-or-move decisions at that point. The money is manageable; the attention is the constraint.

**The 2009 cluster is $37.40M across 11 players but most will be in their prime.** Richards 29, Chistov 26, Nash 25, Eminger 25, Colaiacovo 26: these are re-signing opportunities if we hold the revenue, not a cliff. The one liability inside that block is Kaberle at POTE 75, who will be 31 and probably has no upgrade left.

**Draft capital is healthier than last year's note suggested.** Three first-through-third-rounders in 2006, all from Toronto. The January 2005 note about holding nothing better than a fourth was for that year's class. The R1 is the only high-value asset that funds a February 2006 deadline piece without gutting the defense.

**The development bottleneck is the structural problem nobody has solved.** Twelve players with POTE 97+ on one roster, only enough top-nine slots for five or six of them. The Coach is already watching Spezza (POTE 99, morale 88, 0 GP), Eminger (POTE 99, scratched), and Upshall (minutes collapsing for the third straight year). Every month a POTE 99 sits undressed is a month the asset depreciates. The checking forward the Coach wants (Begin or similar at L4) is also a development unlock: it removes a spot the current group cannot fill, and it lets the Coach trim the 34-man roster without losing a high-POTE player from the system.

**Profit at $34.56M means money is not the constraint.** We can absorb an Iginla-scale salary ($6.50M+) or a Jovanovski ($2.30M) without pressure. The constraint is spots, not dollars.

## Calendar

The question this phase answers is what we do between now and March, and what happens in July when nine contracts come due.

**The deadline is 155 days away.** At three games old with 79 to play, there is no basis to commit to buying or selling. The GM's standing order holds: negotiations open late February. Nothing changes before then.

**Chlup (C, 19, $2.34M)** and **Luongo (G, 26, $1.60M)** are the two most important renewals on the roster and they land the same July. Lock both on 5-6 years the same week the market opens, Luongo first since he is the confirmed #1 goalie and Chlup is the L1C at 19 already playing 25+ minutes. Neither can be renegotiated mid-contract, so the entire plan is: be ready with a long offer in July, do not wait for a bidding round.

**Mogilny (RW, 36, $5.50M)** is the salary-dump candidate. He carries $5.50M at an age where decline is certain, and no under-30 player absorbs his production. At the deadline, if we are out of the race or even if we are in it, he is movable via the over-80 mechanic. If he does not move by March, he walks and we save the $5.50M anyway.

**Tucker (LW, 30, $1.30M)** is the GM's confirmed chip. The Buffalo package from October (Tucker plus St. Jacques for Begin at 95 CHKG, 87 TOUG, 86 FACE, $936K expiring) addresses the coach's checking-middle-six gap directly. That is the primary deadline trade to pursue when negotiations open in February.

**St. Jacques (D, 25, $0.80M)** rides with Tucker to Buffalo. At $0.80M he is depth with no argument for a long-term role if a top-6 D is what we need.

**Spezza (C, 22, $1.00M)** is POTE 99 with zero games in three. Renew contingent on development. If he earns top-nine minutes by February, offer 3-5 years. If he is still undressed at the deadline, he becomes a second trade chip alongside Tucker, because carrying a POTE 99 center who cannot get minutes is worse than converting him into a player who fills a real hole.

**Klesla (D, 23, $0.90M)** — renew 3-5 years in July. He is carrying heavy minutes against tough matchups, which is the coach telling us he trusts him. At $0.90M the cost is trivial.

**Koltsov (LW, 24, $1.10M)** — assess by February. If he is producing top-nine numbers, renew cheap for 2 years. If not, he is a deadline addition to the trade pile.

**Ouellet (G, 24, $0.90M)** — 1-year renew or let go. He is the backup we kept because we needed a second body for playoffs. If Tellqvist develops by July, Ouellet is expendable. If not, the $0.90M is cheap insurance.

**The draft-pick picture has changed.** Toronto now owns its own 1st, 2nd, and 3rd rounds for 2006. The 4th is at NYR and the 5th at CAR. That is real trade capital we did not have in January 2005, and it changes what a February package can look like — we are no longer restricted to player-only offers.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: who across the league fills Toronto's checking-forward gap cheaply enough to free a roster spot for the twelve POTE 97+ players the Coach cannot dress, and who is available in February at a price Toronto can actually pay?

The answer starts with the cheapest fix on the board. Toronto has checking talent (Tucker 92 CHKG, Jackman 90 CHKG, McCabe 89 CHKG) that the Coach is not deploying, because the roster is too wide for the checking role he wants filled. Acquiring Begin at L4C lets the Coach bench Tucker or McCabe, which opens a spot for Spezza or Eminger without losing a prospect.

**Begin** (BUF, C, 27) at 95 CHKG, 86 FACE, 87 TOUG, 73 base, $936K on an expiring deal. He is the single best value target for the February deadline. Buffalo sit at 4 points with 6 expiring contracts and $17.67M profit. They are building through youth and will take expiring value for future assets. Package: Tucker (79 base, $1.30M expiring) plus St. Jacques. This was flagged in October and remains the primary target.

**Cole** (ANA, LW, 26) at 95 CHKG, 86 TOUG, 84 base, $600K expiring from Anaheim who carry 11 expiring deals at 2 points. He fills the L3 checking gap (currently 68 mean) on a nearly free contract. If Toronto can package a late pick plus a salary, this costs almost nothing.

**Jovanovski** (VAN, D, 29) at 89 base, 93 TOUG, 94 CHKG, $2.30M expiring. Vancouver at 2 points with 13 expiring and $46.36M payroll (lowest in league) are structural sellers. He gives the top pairing the toughness nobody on our blue line carries (McCabe 85 TOUG is the best we have at D). Package: Klesla plus a 2nd-round pick. Klesla is POTE 97 but the Coach cannot dress him; converting him to a 93-TOUG veteran who plays every night is a net upgrade for this season.

**Morrow** (DAL, LW, 26) at 88 base, 87 TOUG, 89 CHKG, POTE 85, $1.30M expiring. Dallas at 4 points with 11 expiring and $26.69M profit (the highest in the league). They are the one seller with no money pressure, which makes them reluctant, but 11 expiring deals means they must shed some. He is a step up from Begin in scoring ceiling and plays LW, a position we have depth at but whose quality drops sharply outside the top nine.

**Lecavalier** (TB, C, 25) at 90 base, 83 CHKG, 73 TOUG, POTE 85, $2.60M expiring. Tampa Bay at 0-0-0 (no games played yet), $59.89M payroll, only $18.31M profit. This is the February moonshot. A 25-year-old 90-overall centre on an expiring $2.60M deal from a club that last made the second round in 2003 and hasn't sniffed it since. If Tampa commits to a rebuild, Toronto's R1 plus Chistov (POTE 95, not yet broken out) or Eminger (POTE 99, undressed) is a package they might consider. Acceptance is deeply uncertain; he is a franchise player.

**Hartnell** (NSH, LW, 23) at 79 base, 87 TOUG, 88 CHKG, POTE 94, $1.10M expiring. Nashville at 4 points, $22.35M profit, 4 expiring deals. Young, physical, high ceiling. A cheaper alternative to Morrow who fills the same gap and could develop.

**Avery** (LA, C, 25) at 79 base, 93 FACE, 88 CHKG, 83 TOUG, $400K, 1 year left. LA at 4 points with 6 expiring. The production problem is real (6 points in 57 games last season, per the February memory), but the grades and the price are unmatched for a middle-six role. The Coach's L4 faceoff problem dies immediately with him. The risk is that he ghosts again.

**Not a target: Iginla.** The query shows him at $11.09M with 4 years remaining, not the $6.50M expiring deal from the April 2005 note. Calgary re-signed him. Off the table permanently until 2010.

**Gaborik decision.** The Coach demanded a roster-or-trade answer by mid-October. We are now at October 15. At $11.90M and 13.2% of payroll, he is either dressed (which forces out a 79-base player like Tucker, who is the Begin trade currency) or traded (which requires a partner with $11.90M of salary room, a tiny club given the league average payroll of $58M). Neither path is easy, but doing nothing costs the most because his trade value drops with every undressed week per the January note.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: what specific packages does Toronto take to the table in February, and why does each counterparty say yes? The Coach needs checking and toughness he cannot field internally, the development bottleneck means we are holding undressed prospects worth more as currency than as scratches, and every primary target is on an expiring contract which means February is the only window.

**Begin** is the cleanest deal on the board because the pieces we give are two players the Coach has already chosen not to dress (Tucker 0 GP, St. Jacques 0 GP) and both contracts expire in July, so Buffalo absorb nothing permanent. Tucker at 92 CHKG and 88 TOUG gives Buffalo a veteran body for their young core to develop against; St. Jacques at POTE 94 with 80 TOUG and 84 CHKG is a 25-year-old defenseman who could crack their top four immediately. Buffalo sit at 4 points with $17.67M profit and six expiring deals; they have the money and the motivation. We shed $2.10M in salary and take on $936K, a net saving of $1.16M this season that vanishes in July.

**Jovanovski** is the bigger upgrade because no current Toronto defenseman carries his 93 TOUG and 94 CHKG (McCabe's 85 TOUG is our best at the position). Vancouver at 2 points, $46.36M payroll (lowest in the league), and 13 expiring contracts are the most motivated sellers in the NHL. Klesla at 23, POTE 97, SPEE 88, undressed by the Coach at 3 GP and 0 points, is the best currency we hold that the GM has not explicitly protected. Vancouver get a speed defenseman on a timeline that matches theirs, plus a second-rounder. We take on $1.40M net this year on a contract that expires in July. The risk is that Vancouver value Klesla's ceiling too highly and demand more, or that the GM considers him core despite his lack of ice time.

**Avery** is the cheapest fix for the L4 faceoff problem the Coach has flagged since May (L4 mean 52, best 55). At $400K with 93 FACE and 88 CHKG he solves it permanently and costs almost nothing. LA at 4 points with six expiring deals and a player producing 6 points in 57 games last season have reason to move him. Brendl at 24, POTE 93, SPEE 88, SHPW 87, $0.80M with two years remaining is a speed forward LA's rebuild could use. If both Avery and Begin land, the Coach has 86 and 93 FACE at L3C and L4C respectively, and the faceoff problem is dead.

If none land, the internal fix is dressing Wallin (83 FACE, POTE 97, 0 GP, $1.40M with 4 years) at L4C for the faceoffs, and accepting that checking mean at L3 stays at 68 unless McCabe or Tucker are un-dressed in favor of each other. That is not a solution, but it is the baseline if the market says no.

## Owed

The item the GM owed me is closed and has been since March. The GM stated on 2005-02-19 that "Luongo is arrived. Goalies are solved. Done. Do not revisit that issue," and confirmed on 2005-03-19 to close all goalie monitoring. **Luongo** is on our roster at 97 overall, 26 years old, $1.60M, and has 1 year left, meaning his contract expires July 2006. The monitoring task is complete: he is here, he is our number one, and the question is now renewal, not acquisition.

**DiPietro** at NYI (24, 89 overall, $1.10M, expiring this year) is no longer relevant to us since the goalie trade window the GM asked me to watch closed in March 2005. I am marking this delivered and closed. The only live goalie item is the July 2006 renewal window for Luongo and Chlup simultaneously.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-10-15
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-10-15

Next game at NYR on Saturday 15 October 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question: are our young players getting the games they've earned after three games? For most of them yes. Two are not, and one is a genuine alarm.

**Spezza** is the loudest problem on the sheet. Age 22, POTE 99, morale 88 (lowest on the roster), 0 games played. Last season his minutes collapsed from 9.1 to 4.8 MPG; this season he can't even get into the lineup. POTE 99 is the highest on the roster alongside Colaiacovo and Upshall, but those two are playing and he isn't. Three games in and he's already on a trajectory toward another dead season. This is the one I'd fix before Wednesday.

**Chlup** at 20.0 MPG on the second line is getting what he's earned. 2 points in 3 games, morale 91, POTE 95. He was the centrepiece last year at 18.2 MPG and 0.88 pts/g and he's not going backwards. No change needed here beyond what I've already recommended (first-line centre), which the GM hasn't moved on yet.

**Nash** is at 3 points in 3 games on 18.0 MPG. That's a 1.0 rate against last season's 0.43. Too early to call it a breakout, but the opportunity is there and he's taking it. Fine as is.

**Chistov** has 3 points in 3 games on 12.3 MPG after finishing last year at 0.29 pts/g. Same read as Nash: getting the chance, showing up. No change.

**Gaborik** has played 2 of 3 games at 14.5 MPG. Missing one game is not alarming this early, but he needs to be in the lineup consistently at 23 to build rhythm. Watch it.

**Klesla** at 28.7 MPG on the first pair is the same minute-concentration problem I flagged in October's first note. At 23 he's carrying more than he should and his production rate last year was 0.36 over 82 games. The fix is spreading load, not a trade, but it's only 3 games so I'll let it play through.

**Alexeev** played 1 of 3 games, got 6.0 MPG, scored 2 points. That's a 2.0 rate in one game. The sample is absurdly small, but the pattern is familiar: last season he outproduced Chistov and Upshall from the press box and never got promoted. I'll wait another 3-4 games before pushing this.

**Eminger** and **Gardener** are fine sitting where they are. Eminger at 21 with POTE 99 and zero games is the second-biggest gap, but his situation is complicated by his $2.20M x 4 contract. If he's not in the plans, that's a GM conversation, not a line-change one.

## Development trends

Two games of sample, but the directions tell a story worth the coach's attention, especially for the young players whose roles are still being decided.

**Chlup** is the headline. Minutes tripled from 6.0 to 27.0 MPG at 19, and he has 1 point in 2 games on that ice. This is the first-line role I have been pushing since April. At 27 MPG and a 0.50 rate, he is absorbing top-six minutes and contributing. If this holds through ten games, the March finding that he is the franchise centrepiece is confirmed in the only way that matters: he is on the ice when it counts and he is producing.

**Spacek** is going the wrong way. Minutes fell from 17.0 to 5.5 MPG with zero points in 2 games. This is the same collapse that killed his February last season, where he dropped from 12+ to 8.1 MPG and never recovered. At 20, if he cannot hold a top-nine role with 15+ minutes, the development case for dressing him next season needs re-arguing.

**Upshall** repeats for the third straight window: minutes fell from 16.0 to 6.0 MPG, zero points. The March finding noted 13.4 to 4.9 last season; now 16.0 to 6.0 in October. Three separate collapses with no grade movement tells me the game is not punishing him physically, he is just not holding a job.

**Nash** is the quiet good news. 1.00 pts/g on 18.0 MPG, flat across both windows. Last season his rate halved from 0.83 to 0.43 with minutes flat, which raised the system-fit question. He is producing at a top-of-2 rate now. The March question may be answering itself.

**Jackman and Klesla** both saw massive minute reductions: Jackman 41.0 to 22.0, Klesla 42.0 to 22.0. The October 13 finding flagged them absorbing 56% of D minutes. Someone has spread the load, and Kaberle (11.0 to 21.5), Fischer (10.0 to 22.0), Stahle (6.0 to 15.5) and Colaiacovo (6.0 to 15.5) all went up. That is the right correction. Jackman kept his 1.00 pts/g at 22 MPG, which matches the March finding that his collapse was load-driven.

**Fischer** doubled from 10.0 to 22.0 MPG and picked up 1 point. At 25 with the GM's explicit keeper status, his minutes rising while his production holds is exactly what you want.

**Alexeev** is still at 1 game played. The April finding that he outproduces Chistov and Upshall in points per game while remaining a scratch has not changed.

**Spezza** played 0 games in this window. Same pattern as the March collapse. Still no minutes, still no path.

**Gaborik** appeared for the first two games since the initial save: 0.50 pts/g on 14.5 MPG at 23. Healthy and in the lineup, which matters given he missed the first game.

**The veterans are managed.** Sundin (21.0 to 15.0 MPG, 0.50), Mogilny (20.0 to 16.0 MPG, 0.50), and Roberts (18.0 to 19.5 MPG, 0.50) all have appropriate load for their ages. Sundin and Mogilny getting rested while still producing is good. Roberts at 39 on 19.5 is aggressive but he is on the scoresheet.

## Morale watch

The room is right. Every Toronto player sits at 88 or above with 3 games in the books, and the only one below 90 is **Spezza** at 88 with zero games played, which is the development decision the GM is already making, not a minutes complaint.

**Jackman** at 28.7 MPG and **Klesla** at 28.7 are both at 91 and show no morale damage yet, but that load is what my existing note flags for December. Three games is not a signal. I am watching it.

No player is under his expected band with a slipping number, and no depth man is far over his. No action needed before Saturday.

## Role composition

**The question here is whether our units are built from players suited to their jobs, and whether the roster even holds enough of each role to build them.**

**L1 (Sundin–Roberts–Mogilny, Jackman–Klesla)** is well-sorted. Sundin handles draws at 95 faceoffs, Roberts brings 86 checking and 73 toughness alongside Mogilny's 92 scoring. Jackman at 92 checking and 78 toughness anchors the blue line. No change needed.

**L2 (Chlup–Gaborik–Fischer, Kaberle–Nash)** works on speed and skill: Gaborik 99 scoring, 99 speed; Nash 82 checking adds bite; Chlup at 80 draws handles his end. Kaberle at 93 stamina stays fresh. No issue.

**L3 (Richards–Afinogenov–Chistov, Stahle–Colaiacovo)** is the skill line. Checking mean 68 and toughness mean 63 are the lowest on the roster. Richards 94 playmaking and Afinogenov 93 scoring give offence, but this unit cannot shut anyone down. That's a personnel ceiling, not an arrangement error.

**L4 (Gardener–Spaček–Upshall)** checking mean 72, toughness 64. Slightly better defensively than L3 but nowhere near a shutdown line. Same problem as April: no forward outside L1–L2 checks above 75. This line is correctly placed as the bottom six; it simply isn't good enough at checking.

**K2 (Spaček–Upshall, Kaberle–Klesla)** carries a faceoff mean of 55 and checking mean 72. For a penalty kill that's thin, but there's no better personnel. K1 at checking 84 is legitimate.

**Jackman and Klesla** are on three units each (L1, P1, K1/K2 respectively). The load concentration I flagged October 13 remains. The fix is trusting L3's D to shorten shifts, not a line change.

## Opponent matchup

What changes for tonight, given NYR's lineup and the fact we play them first this season? Very little structurally. The lines are built right; the concern is in-game execution and D-minute management.

**Their top two lines are loaded.** Holik/Nedved/Kovalev features Kovalev at OVR 90 with 99 endurance and 97 deking. Lindros/Barnaby/Bure brings a 90-rated centre, a 98 CHKG enforcer in Barnaby, and Bure at 88. These are veterans who are still effective tonight. Their third line (Carter/LaCouture/Abid at 86/76/70) and fourth line are soft, especially without Purinton out on the back end until November 17. Their PP is 1-for-11 (9%), so the penalty kill can be conservative.

**Barnaby targets Gaborik.** Barnaby is CHKG 98, TOUG 97, PENA 94. He is going to hunt the skilled winger on whichever line he draws. Gaborik at TOUG 68 is the obvious target. The auto-pairing means our first line comes with Jackman/Klesla and our second with Fischer/Kaberle. If the GM sees Barnaby's line over, he should consider sending our first line out instead: Roberts at CHKG 90 and TOUG 92 absorbs that pressure far better, and Jackman/Klesla can handle their second D pair (Malakhov/Poti, OVR 81/84) without any issue. This is an in-game lever, not a lineup change.

**Klesla's endurance is the structural worry.** He carries ENDU 63 and is already at 34.5 MPG per the October 13 finding. Against NYR's depth up front, riding Jackman/Klesla on every shift will burn him out by the third period. Fischer (CHKG 87, OVR 84) and Kaberle (OVR 85) are capable of shutting down Malakhov/Poti and should see a bigger share of the night. This is the D-minute-concentration issue from the Oct 13 finding playing out in real time against a loaded opponent.

**Dunham at 91 is a real obstacle.** Their backup Blackburn is 87, so we get no weakness in net either way. Our PP at 0-for-3 needs to generate quality looks tonight; their PK unit with Kasparaitis (CHKG 94) and LaCouture is physical but not deep.

**Ouellet starts at G1 (OVR 86).** Check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming, per the January 19 order. Tellqvist is 73 and not a viable plan against this lineup.

**On the defencemen obligation (#1):** three games into season 2 is too thin for a sell-list update. The live issue is the Oct 13 D-minute concentration. Tonight is a test of whether we can spread load to Fischer/Kaberle against a quality forward group. I will report back after the game with updated usage.

## Owed

**Standing job #1 — defenceman analysis and sell-list update.** This is the 11th delivery, 3 games into 2005-06.

**Klesla** — OVR 87 at 24, expiring ($0.90M x 1yr). 0 points in 3 games on 28.7 MPG. Consistent with last year's 0.36 pts/g decline. What changed: his OVR jumped from 84 to 87 and he's now in an expiring year. A 24-year-old, 87-rated D on $0.90M with no contract after June is the most tradeable version he will ever be. The sell call that was "this offseason" is now "before the trade deadline, maybe sooner." His ceiling as a producer is low; his floor as a minutes-eater is the product.

**Jackman** — OVR 86 at 25, 3 assists in 3 games for 1.00 pts/g on 28.3 MPG. Last season finished at 0.48. Three games is nothing, but if he sustains 0.70+ his value as the cheapest top-pair minutes in the league just went up. I am not moving the sell recommendation yet — $0.70M x 2 means we are not squeezed on timeline. Watch to game 10.

**Kaberle** — OVR 85, 1 point in 3 games at 18.0 MPG. $4.10M x 4yr. Stable, GM's keeper, no change.

**Fischer** — OVR 84, 1 point in 3 games at 18.0 MPG. $3.70M x 3yr. GM's keeper, no change.

**McCabe** — Healthy scratch, not dressed. OVR 84 on screen, but 0.48 over his last 58 games last season. $3.00M x 3yr at 30. Still on the sell list, same as May. No change.

**Eminger** — Healthy scratch, not dressed. OVR 82, $2.20M x 4yr. Same salary problem, same trade difficulty. No change.

**Minutes** — Jackman and Klesla are at 28.3 and 28.7 MPG respectively. The October 13 flag read 33.0 and 34.5. The load has spread; that's progress. Still 48% of total D minutes between them, but not the 56% that would crater endurance by December. If it holds, no intervention needed.

The one change since last delivery: Klesla's sell timeline accelerated. Expiring with OVR 87 means we are the seller with leverage now. Jackman's hot start is a watch item, not a sell trigger yet.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-10-13
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-10-13

Toronto 2-0-0, 4 pts after 2 games.

## Role coverage

The structural question at this point in October is whether Toronto's roster can survive the season's back half without a trade, and the answer on toughness is no.

**Toughness** is missing outright. Zero players at 80+; the best is Jackman at 75. Every other checking-capable name sits at 70 or below. The Coach's K2 penalty-kill checking mean of 72 confirms what the grades say: no one on this roster hits hard enough to protect the net in the playoffs. Bell (CHI, 88 TOUG, 82 FACE, 24) or Avery (LA, 83 TOUG, 93 FACE, 25) are the only league-wide fixes. This is not a coach problem.

**Checking** is thin at six players above 80, and two of them (McCabe 86, Tucker 83) are not lined. The Coach can dress them tonight and raise the effective checking depth from four to six without a trade. That is an internal fix worth making in October rather than a November scramble.

**Faceoffs** are thin. Only Sundin (90) and Wallin (83, not lined) sit above 80, and Wallin is the only internal option for fourth-line draws. The Coach quantified L4 faceoff at a 52 mean in April; Wallin dresses and takes those draws, or the gap persists until Bell or Avery arrives.

**Scoring and playmaking** are covered today (11 at 80+ each) but age terribly: Mogilny 36, Sundin 34, Roberts 39 carry the top of both charts. The next names down are Gaborik (23) and Afinogenov (26), and neither has yet shown at 0.80+ pts/g to absorb that production. This is the trajectory problem that makes the July Iginla target matter more than any October move.

**Speed** is the best-covered role (25 at 80+), and **stamina** is comfortable at 12. Neither needs attention.

**Goalies**: Luongo is at 2-0, 0.50 GAA, .983 SV in two games. Task #2 (Luongo monitoring and DiPietro tracking) is effectively closed on the Luongo side; he is performing at the level the March standing order predicted. No goalie action needed.

**Abid** (86, 25, not lined) and **Koltsov** (92 speed, 24, not lined) are rostered depth the Coach is not using. Abid closes a scoring-side gap on L3/L4; Koltsov gives a fourth option when the speed depth is needed for matchups. Both are free.

## Trajectory

The trajectory question for Toronto is whether the club can survive its own contract structure. The age shape is healthy: 13 players at 23 or under, 16 at 24–29, and only 5 at 30+. The danger is not age — it is that 11 contracts worth $37.40M all expire in July 2009, which is the exact clustering the manual warns against.

**The July 2009 wall.** Sundin (will be 38), Richards (28), Chistov (25), Nash (24), Kaberle (31), Eminger (25), Alexeev (27), Upshall (26), Colaiacovo (26), Wallin (28), Abid (29). The entire core from your top six through your bottom six hits free agency on the same day. Either you pay 11 renewal offers in one week or you lose half of them. The fix is not one move but a staggering plan: extend Richards and Chistov in July 2007 (their deals still have 4 years, but mid-contract renegotiation is impossible in this game, so "staggering" means timing when you *can* act — which is only at expiry). Since you cannot renegotiate mid-contract, the only lever you have is not re-signing all of them at the same time — let some walk or sign them to shorter deals to break the wave. This is a July 2009 problem, not a 2006 problem, but the plan needs to exist now so you don't drift into it.

**July 2006 is the near-term cliff.** Chlup ($2.34M), Luongo ($1.60M), and Spezza ($1.00M) all expire. Luongo and Chlup are non-negotiable keepers: Luongo is your franchise goalie at 26, Chlup is your first-line centre at 19 with POTE 95. Spezza at POTE 99 is the question the coach raised on October 12 — he needs minutes or he's a trade piece. The three of them represent $4.94M that could grow to $25–30M on 5–6 year deals, which is manageable against $34.08M profit.

**The Gaborik salary is the payroll's center of gravity.** At $11.90M per year for five years, he is 13.2% of your total payroll locked at 23. The deal is signed; there is nothing to do about it. But it means every other renewal is measured against the gap between what he earns and what the rest of your core commands.

**The scoring void has a name now.** Sundin ($8.40M, age 34) and Mogilny ($5.50M, expiring) were the production bridge. Mogilny's deal is one year; he walks or retires in July 2006. Sundin has four years left at $8.40M, meaning you're paying a 34-year-old through age 38. The young core — Chlup, Nash, Gaborik, Chistov, Afinogenov — has not yet shown it can replace 400+ combined points. The Iginla target remains the structural fix; at 27 with a $6.50M expiring deal, he slots between Gaborik and the rest without breaking the payroll structure.

**Draft capital is no longer the constraint it was.** The January 2005 note about no picks beyond a 4th is stale. You own your own R1, R2, and R3 for 2006. That is enough ammunition for one meaningful acquisition this February or summer.

## Calendar

The buyer/seller question is 157 days away and we have played two games, so the deadline decision is a late-February one. What the calendar demands today is that the packages are identified and that the players whose value hinges on development actually get dressed, because a trade in March is only as good as what the player looked like from October to February.

**Chlup** is the single most important renewal this summer. He is 19, base 82, scoring 0.88 pts/g at 18 MPG and the Coach has put him at first-line centre. His deal ($2.34M) expires July 2006. Lock him on 5-6 years the same week Luongo does.

**Luongo** at 26, overall 97, base 91, $1.60M expiring, is the other half of that same renewal week. The standing note from last July is clear: Luongo first because Tellqvist behind him (overall 73, base 77) is a clear step down. At $89.94M payroll with $34.08M profit, money is not the problem here; timing is.

**Mogilny** at 36, $5.50M, 1 year left, base 90: let him go. There is no version of this where he signs for less than what he is earning, and the scoring-bridge-void note from May 2005 is the problem — no one under 30 is positioned to absorb his production. That gap gets filled by Chlup's growth and the acquisitions we pursue, not by re-signing a 37-year-old.

**Tucker** at 30, base 79, $1.30M expiring was the GM's stated trade chip at the last deadline and is still on the roster. He goes to Buffalo in the Begin package (BUF profit $19.07M, 6 expiring). If that deal falls through he is still the cleanest expiring asset we have to move before March.

**Klesla** at 23, overall 87, base 78, $0.90M expiring is the centrepiece of the Jovanovski package. VAN carry 13 expiring contracts on a $46.36M payroll (lowest in the league) and Jovanovski at 29, base 89, $2.30M expiring is on a club that cannot keep him. Klesla plus a second-round pick is the proposal. He is also above 80 overall, so if the VAN deal dies, the pick mechanic is a fallback.

**St. Jacques** at 25, overall 66, base 66, $0.80M expiring is the other half of the Begin package to Buffalo. He is not on any other club's radar at 66, so his only value is as a salary-matching piece.

**Spezza** at 22, base 73, POTE 99, zero games played since the season started, is the Coach's loudest flag. The Coach demanded top-nine minutes or a trade in May 2005; it is October and he has not played. If by late February he has zero to ten games, trade him while the POTE holds value. If he gets dressed and produces, he becomes a renewal candidate on a cheap 2-year deal.

**Ouellet** at 24, overall 86, base 81, $0.90M: stays for the playoffs as the backup behind Luongo. After the season, with Luongo locked up and Tellqvist on 6 years, there is no role. Let go or trade in the summer.

**Koltsov** at 24, base 68, $1.10M: let go. He is the shallowest player on the expiring list and carries no trade value.

The deadline plan has two branches. If we are in the top 8 in late February, push for Jovanovski (Klesla + pick). If we are outside, dump Tucker + St. Jacques to Buffalo for Begin and see what the pick mechanic gets us for Klesla. Both branches require the players to be performing, which is why the Coach's dressing flags on Spezza, Eminger and Chlup are a trade-value issue as much as a development one.

## League scan

The October 2005 market is different from the April 2005 plan: Iginla has signed for four more years at $11.09M, killing the July scoring-bridge target that the trajectory phase identified as the only structural fix for Mogilny's production void. That plan is dead; the new one runs through the expiring class on bottom-feeders in October-February.

**Bell** (CHI, LW/C, 25, 84 overall / 80 base) closes toughness, checking and faceoffs simultaneously: TOUG 86, CHKG 84, FACE 92, SPEE 95, $900K, 1 year left. CHI have 8 expiring and $21.76M profit, so they can absorb a salary move. This is the same target the Coach flagged on October 12 for the L4 gap, and the numbers have held since January. The trade window is February when CHI's 8 expiring all become available at once.

**Komisarek** (MTL, D, 23, 82 overall / 77 base) is the best young defenseman on a sell team: TOUG 82, CHKG 89, SPEE 95, POTE 92, $1.10M, 1 year. MTL sit at 1 point with 8 expiring and $17.76M profit. He closes the toughness gap on the blue line AND gives a speed option the roster has never had at defenseman. At 23 with POTE 92, the development upside exceeds Jovanovski's ceiling at 29. The Feb 2005 correction confirmed he is a rental, not a long-term piece, but that makes him a cheap one-year bridge.

**Kovalchuk** (ATL, LW, 22, 91 overall / 89 base) is the highest-ceiling scoring option on a clear sell team. SPEE 99, TOUG 84, age 22, $1.10M, 1 year. ATL at 0 points with 6 expiring contracts and $17.95M profit. He absorbs Mogilny's role immediately and his TOUG 84 makes him Toronto's best hockey player on the toughness chart. The risk: ATL now only carry 6 expiring (down from 11 in February), suggesting they've re-signed some pieces. But a 0-1 start on a team with that few wins projected makes retention unlikely.

**Heatley** (ATL, RW, 24, 90 overall / 91 base) is the other ATL expiring star: TOUG 81, CHKG 87, SPEE 97, $1.10M, 1 year. Same sell logic as Kovalchuk. He fills the RW void left by Mogilny and his 81 TOUG clears Toronto's current best of 75. ATL cannot keep both at $1.10M each without a massive payroll jump from their current $39.32M.

**Hartnell** (NSH, LW, 23, 83 overall / 79 base) is the stealth target: TOUG 92, CHKG 93, SPEE 96, POTE 95, $1.10M, 0 years (contract status ambiguous, may be already expiring mid-season). NSH at 2 points (two OT losses) with only 4 expiring and $21.70M profit, so they're less motivated than VAN or ATL. But a 92 TOUG / 93 CHKG / 96 speed / POTE 95 player at 23 on a losing team is the highest-grade-per-dollar package in the league. The uncertainty on his contract year is the one thing holding me back from Tier 1.

**Jovanovski** (VAN, D, 29, 86 overall / 89 base, TOUG 91, CHKG 92, $2.30M, 1 year) remains the best immediate-defense option. VAN carry 13 expiring contracts and the league's lowest payroll at $46.36M. They are the most motivated seller in hockey. His ceiling is set at 29, but 89 base with 91/92 toughness-checking is playoff-ready tonight. The October 12 note is confirmed by the data.

**Begin** (BUF, C, 27, 66 overall / 73 base, TOUG 82, CHKG 90, FACE 79, $935K, 1 year) has declined since the October 12 note recorded TOUG 87/CHKG 95/FACE 86. His new grades are still useful for L4 checking but the faceoff grade at 79 is a meaningful drop. He remains the cheaper BUF option if Bell is unavailable, but Bell is strictly better at every grade and the same price.

**Avery** (LA, C, 25, 73 overall / 79 base, FACE 90, CHKG 80, TOUG 75, $400K, 1 year) no longer closes the toughness gap. His TOUG fell from 83 to 75 since January. He is now a pure faceoff specialist for L4 draws at the lowest price in hockey. Useful, but not the three-gap fix he was in January.

**Reid** (STL, RW, 24, 77 overall / 77 base, FACE 86, SPEE 99, POTE 94, TOUG 50, $600K, 1 year) gives speed and faceoffs but nothing on toughness. STL carry $69.76M payroll (second-highest in the league) with only $18.89M profit, so salary relief is a motivation, but he's a specialist not a fix.

**Forsberg** (COL, LW, 32, 95 overall / 97 base, $9.90M, 1 year) is the highest-rated player on any sell team. COL at 0 points, $68.11M payroll, 7 expiring. At 97 base he is transcendent but at 32 and $9.90M he is a one-month rental at a cost that would consume Toronto's entire annual surplus. Only worth pursuing at the February deadline if nothing better materializes.

## Trade construction

The October market kills the Iginla plan and forces a new scoring bridge; the two packages the GM already noted (Begin, Jovanovski) need updating because Begin's grades collapsed and Bell is strictly better. The structural need is clear from the prior phases: zero players at 80+ TOUG, and Mogilny's 94-point production walking in July with no internal replacement.

**Heatley** (ATL, 24, 91 base, TOUG 81, CHKG 87, SPEE 97) is the priority. He closes both the scoring void (fills Mogilny's role at 80+ points immediately) and the toughness gap (first TOR player above 80 TOUG). ATL at 0-2 with 6 expiring and $17.95M profit are in full rebuild. Upshall (22, POTE 99, CHKG 87) plus Koltsov (24, POTE 94, ACCE 96) plus our R2 gives them exactly the currency they need: two POTE 94+ players under 25 for $2.60M combined, plus a pick. Heatley costs nothing (1 year, $1.10M) and we shed $1.50M net.

**Bell** (CHI, 25, 80 base, TOUG 86, CHKG 84, FACE 92, SPEE 95) replaces the Begin note. Begin's grades fell (TOUG 82 vs Bell's 86, FACE 79 vs Bell's 92) and he's two years older. CHI at 2 points with 8 expiring and $21.76M profit are rebuilding. Lundmark (24, POTE 97, ACCE 86) plus R3 is a clean ask: CHI get a project with speed they can develop, plus a late-round pick for a player who walks in one year. Payroll effect is +$100K, negligible against $34.08M profit.

**Jovanovski** (VAN, 29, 89 base, TOUG 91, CHKG 92) remains valid but is now third priority. Bell (86) plus Heatley (81) plus Tucker (88) plus Roberts (92) give four at 80+ TOUG, which solves the role gap without him. If we do pursue him, the R2 is committed to Heatley and a first-rounder is too expensive for a 29-year-old rental. Drop this unless defense breaks down by February.

**If nothing lands:** Dress Tucker (TOUG 88, CHKG 92) and McCabe (CHKG 86, ENDU 94) for checking minutes; they're not lined and the grades are there. Dress Wallin (FACE 83) for fourth-line draws. Accept the scoring void is a development timeline problem, not an October trade problem. Use R1/R2/R3 in June to draft the next bridge scorer.

## Owed

**#2 — Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window:** This task is closed. Luongo arrived last season and the GM shut down all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19 with the standing order to keep Belfour and Luongo as two 90+ goalies for the playoffs. Luongo is now on Toronto's roster at 97 overall, 26, $1.60M with 1 year left, and he started 2 of 2 this season. Nothing to monitor. DiPietro (NYI, 88, 24, $1.10M expiring) played 1 game and is not relevant unless the GM reopens the goalie file.

markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-10-13

Next game vs PIT on Friday 14 October 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question this phase answers: are our young players getting the games their talent has earned after 2 games into the season?

**Chlup** is still on the third line at 17.0 MPG. He scored 59 points at 19 last season and his minutes are barely above what a useful forward expects. I have recommended this move repeatedly since April and the record shows he has never been placed on the first line. At 17 MPG on a third line he is a waste of the best young centre on the roster. Move him up.

**Nash** is on the second line at 14.0 MPG and has 3 points in 2 games. His rate collapsed to 0.43 last season, but 1.50 in the first two suggests the system-fit review from the offseason may have worked. No change; let the sample grow.

**Chistov** at 13.5 MPG on the third line has 3 points in 2 games. Same rate as Nash. If he holds this, he is pushing for second-line minutes. No action yet.

**Klesla** is at 34.5 MPG on the first defensive pair. Last season he played 15 MPG and produced 0.36 pts/g. His minutes have more than doubled with no production improvement in sight after 2 scoreless games. The auto-pairing puts him against the opponent's best line, which is the right matchup use for a defensive D, but 34 minutes is a burnout risk. Two games is too few to act on, but if his rate stays at zero past ten games we need to cut his load or trade him as planned.

**Gaborik** played 1 of 2 games and got 8.0 MPG on the second line. At 23 with POTE 90, he should be seeing 12+ on a top-six wing if healthy. Check whether the missed game was a knock or a decision. If he is healthy, he needs more ice.

**Spezza and Eminger** are both scratched with zero games. Both carry POTE 99, both were underused last season. If the GM is deliberately making room for younger guys, that is his call, but two POTE-99 players not suiting up in the first two games means the development pipeline is not what it looks like.

**Everyone else** (Spacek 12.0, Stahle 13.5, Colaiacovo 13.5, Upshall 12.0, Gardener 9.5) are dressed with reasonable minutes for their age and role. No concerns after 2 games.

## Morale watch

The room is fine. Two wins to start the season and every dressed player sits at **91** morale, one point above the threshold where it starts boosting grades. No one is slipping, no one needs a minutes change before Friday.

**Richards** is the only name I'd flag for a future conversation. He's at 11.5 minutes a night on the second line at age 25 with a 91 displayed overall. If his standing game is in the high-80s or 90s, the morale model says he expects 17 to 20 a night. At two games played and 91 morale, there's nothing to fix yet. If he's still at 11 and still at 91 after ten games, I'll bring it up then.

The defencemen are carrying heavy loads (Klesla 34.5, Jackman 33.0) but that's normal for a top pair and D rarely drive morale problems. The bottom six (Spacek, Upshall, Gardener at 9.5 to 12.0) are depth-calibre players getting depth minutes. Everyone's right.

## Role composition

The question here is whether the units are built from players who suit their jobs, and whether gaps are arrangement problems or roster problems.

**L1 (Sundin, Roberts, Mogilny + Jackman/Klesla):** Well-built. Roberts 85 checking and Jackman 91 give this line teeth. Sundin's 94 faceoff anchors it. The checking mean of 79 across five is respectable for a scoring line. No issue.

**L2 (Kaberle, Richards, Gaborik, Fischer + Nash):** Nash at 81 checking is the reason this line isn't a pure skill unit. Fischer's two-way game at 24 helps too. Checking mean 76 is fine. No issue.

**L3 (Chlup, Afinogenov, Chistov + Stahle/Colaiacovo):** Checking mean 69, toughness mean 64. This is a skill line with no bite. Chlup at 79 faceoffs is the only standout on this unit defensively, and he's 20. Afinogenov 92 scoring and Chistov 92 playmaking are pure offence. Against any physical opponent this line gets pushed back. The issue is not arrangement — there is no checker on this roster outside of Roberts, Jackman, and Nash, all of whom are already on L1/L2. Moving Nash to L3 drops L2's checking mean to around 71, trading one hole for another.

**L4 (Gardener, Spacek, Upshall):** Checking mean 71, toughness 63. Spacek is on K2 so he has some defensive competence, but 63 toughness means this line cannot play an enforcer role either. Same root cause: the roster simply does not have a third or fourth legitimate checker.

**K1 (Chlup, Roberts, Jackman, Fischer):** Checking mean 83. Jackman 91 and Roberts 85 carry it. This is a real top penalty kill.

**K2 (Spacek, Kaberle, Upshall, Klesla):** Checking mean 72. Kaberle is a 95-stamina offensive defenceman on a kill unit because we have no depth. No alternative exists that doesn't cost more elsewhere.

**P1 and P2** are both well-constructed. P1 has Sundin/Mogilny creative with Jackman/Klesla on the points. P2 has Kaberle quarterbacking with Richards and Afinogenov.

The structural finding from April 13 holds: no forward outside L1-L2 checks above 75. That is a roster gap, not something I can arrange away. The one lever I have is giving L3 and L4 less of the game and shortening the bench in tight minutes, but that's a game-management decision, not a composition fix.

## Opponent matchup

The question is whether PIT's lineup demands a structural change from how we've been playing, or whether our depth handles them as-is.

**PIT's top line** is Lemieux at 40 (OVR 85, FACE 62) with Straka (OVR 83) and Meloche (OVR 75). Sundin wins that draw 94 to 62 and our D1 (Jackman/Klesla, 86/87) is paired against it automatically. Lemieux's checking is 60, so he gets no physical separation from our first pair. We control that matchup without touching anything.

**PIT's second line** is Beech (OVR 70) with Surovy (74) and Willis (69). That is their weakest line and it auto-pairs with their second defensive pair: Lupaschuk (70) and Melichar (63). Melichar at OVR 63 is the weakest skater on their roster by five points. Our second line is Gaborik (99), Richards (89) and Nash (85). This is a mismatch of 15-20 points per position. No tactical adjustment needed; Gaborik eats that pair alive on his own.

**PIT's third and fourth lines** are Renberg (75)/Morozov (78)/Fata (70) and Holzinger (75)/Lefebvre (75)/McKenna (66). Our D3 is Stahle (76) and Colaiacovo (76), paired automatically with our third line (Chlup/Chistov/Afinogenov, 87/87/86). The third line has enough offensive weight to pull the pair forward and keep their D3 hemmed in. The fourth line (Spacek/Gardener/Upshall) against Holzinger is serviceable.

**Faceoffs:** The standing finding says we lose the dot on three lines every game. Tonight is an exception. PIT's centres are Lemieux (FACE 62), Beech (61), Renberg (65), Holzinger (50). Our 94/79/79/58 wins all four draws. The structural gap exists but PIT cannot exploit it.

**Goalie:** Hedberg (OVR 88) is their starter and has given up 4 on whatever shots he faced. We have scored 8 in 2 games. I'd start Luongo (OVR 97) and expect the game to be about us converting rather than defending.

**Decision:** No change. This is a development-class game by the framework (PIT is not a quality opponent; we can afford it), and our current lineup already has Chlup, Nash, Gaborik and Spacek in significant roles. The young guys get their look tonight because they're already in it. Forcing Chlup to L1 tonight would be a development call dressed as a matchup call, and the matchup doesn't need him there.

## Owed

**Standing job #1 — defenceman analysis and end-of-season sell list.** This is two games into the 2005-06 season, so no verdict from last year changes. What's new is the usage pattern, and it's a problem.

**Jackman** — 2 assists in 2 games on 33.0 MPG. That's 1.00 pts/g pace against last season's 0.48 on 30 MPG. Two games means nothing statistically. My sell recommendation from last offseason still stands on the same logic: $0.70M x 2 makes his top-pair minutes tradeable, and the GM chose to keep him this summer so he clearly wants him. I'm not pushing again until production tells me otherwise.

**Klesla** — 0 points in 2 games on 34.5 MPG. He's averaging 1.5 more minutes than Jackman with zero output. Last season was 0.36 pts/g on 15 MPG; now he's at double the minutes with no return yet. Sell verdict unchanged, and the minutes make me more worried, not less. 34 MPG is unsustainable for a guy who couldn't produce on 15.

**McCabe** — healthy scratch, 0 GP at OVR 84 and $3.00M x 3. He's sitting while a 76-rated kid plays. Consistent with where I had him all last year: sell.

**Eminger** — healthy scratch, 0 GP at OVR 82 and $2.20M x 4. Same verdict: expendable. Four years of salary at inflated rate for a 0.36-rate defender nobody puts on the ice.

**Kaberle** and **Fischer** at 85 and 84 respectively, both contributing (1 assist each on 12-13 MPG). They're the third pair by minutes but carry the heaviest contracts on the blue line. Both are keepers. No change to their status.

**Stahle** (76, age 21, 13.5 MPG) and **Colaiacovo** (76, age 22, 13.5 MPG) are getting real minutes on the third pair. That's development usage and it's working — both are playing every game.

The new thing: Jackman and Klesla are eating 67.5 of 120 available D-minutes per game. That's 56% on one pair. Endurance will crater by December. This isn't a trade question, it's a lines question, and I'll address it when we build the lines for PIT.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-10-12
