# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-10-12

Toronto 1-0-0, 2 pts after 1 games.

## Role coverage

The question is whether Toronto can compete this season with what they have, or whether the structural gaps identified in spring are still open and worsening with age. They are.

**Toughness is the defining hole.** Zero players on the roster carry 80+ TOUG. Jackman leads at 75, Roberts at 73, McCabe at 73. The Coach quantified the L4 checking mean at 61 and toughness mean at 57 in April, and no one on this roster changes that by a shift change. This gap has been flagged since February and remains unresolved. The Feb 21 contradiction (six players supposedly at 80+ TOUG) is settled: it was not, and the grade-based count is zero.

**Sundin carries both clutch and faceoffs at 34 years old.** His 90 FACE and 94 CLUTCH are the top of the roster at both positions. No backup centre on the sheet draws above 75. Wallin at 83 FACE is the next-best draw-taker and he is "not lined" — he is on the roster sitting out. The Coach's L4 faceoff problem (mean 52, best 55) is fixable by dressing Wallin at centre, but Wallin does not check; that half of the problem stays.

**Jackman (87 CHKG, 24)** and **Tucker (83 CHKG, 30)** are the best internal checkers, and Tucker is "not lined." Dressing Tucker nightly is the floor for the checking gap, but he tops out at 70 TOUG, so checking improves without toughness improving.

**The defence side faces a cliff.** Roberts is 39, Mogilny is 36, Sundin is 34. Combined they carry the scoring, the clutch, and most of the experience. No player under 30 on this roster has a points rate close to theirs. Gaborik (92 OVR, 23) and Afinogenov (90, 26) are the inheritors but they are wingers, not the centre or defence production these three provide. Colaiacovo at 22 and POTE 99 was supposed to be the blueliner bridge; the Coach called him a development write-off in May.

**Goalies are solved.** Luongo at 26 with $1.60M and one year left is a top-tier starter. Ouellet (24) and Tellqvist (26) provide depth without cost concerns. Belfour is gone from the roster as expected. No action needed.

**Four "not lined" players are real assets the Coach is leaving unused:** Abid (86 OVR, 25), McCabe (86 CHKG, 30), Tucker (83 CHKG, 30), and Koltsov (92 SPEE, 24). Together they are a third-and-fourth-line core of scoring, checking, and speed that costs nothing. The Coach should dress them before any trade conversation starts.

## Trajectory

The trajectory question matters now because October 2005 is the last month before the 2006 renewal window starts planning, and two contracts that define the next decade — Luongo at 1 year and Chlup at 1 year — come up simultaneously next July.

**The age curve is young where it counts and old where it hurts.** 13 players 23 or under, 16 in their primes, only 5 over 29. The shape is the manual's target. The problem is those 5: Sundin at 34 and $8.40M on 4 more years, Mogilny at 36 and $5.50M expiring, Roberts at 39 and $4.90M on 2 more. Together they carry $18.80M against declining bodies. Mogilny walks in 2006 at POTE 55, which is fine. Roberts at POTE 52 should follow him. Sundin at POTE 60 is the expensive one: he's locked through 2009 when he'll be 38.

**Mogilny** is a solved problem. $5.50M on a one-year deal at 36 with POTE 55 — he'll either retire or not be re-signed. The $5.50M is freed for whoever replaces him on the top line. The scoring bridge void this creates is exactly what the Iginla-type target addresses.

**Roberts** at 39, POTE 52, $4.90M with 2 years left is the harder call. He's not a trade asset at that age and grade, but a release at July 2006 saves one year of salary and a roster spot. The GM kept him last summer for playoff presence; that function is diminishing.

**Sundin** is the liability nobody can fix right now. $8.40M per year through 2009, POTE 60, age 34. At 38 he's collecting league-third money for bottom-six minutes if he holds on. No trade market exists at that age and salary. It's a contract that dies on the books.

**Luongo** is the single most urgent renewal in the building. 26 years old, POTE 97, $1.60M on a one-year deal. If he walks July 2006, Toronto loses its franchise goalie in his prime and has only Tellqvist (POTE 91, $1.20M, 6 years) and Ouellet (POTE 97, $0.90M, 1 year) behind him. He must be locked on 5-6 years at season end. This is the priority renewal, ahead of anyone else.

**Chlup** is the second. 19, POTE 95, first-line centre per the Coach, $2.34M on 1 year. If he posts 50+ points this season his price explodes in July. Locking him on 5-6 years while his current contract makes him cheap by league standards is the highest-ROI renewal available. He and Luongo are both July 2006, both must go 5-6 years, and both must be addressed the same week.

**The 2006 July cliff is 9 contracts, $15.44M.** That's manageable: Mogilny and Tucker and St. Jacques likely walk (saving $7.60M), Luongo and Chlup re-sign on longer deals at higher salaries, Spezza and Ouellet and Klesla and Koltsov are conditional. Net payroll change could be small if the right players leave.

**Summer 2009 is the real cluster.** 11 contracts, $37.40M, expiring together: Richards ($6.70M), Chistov ($5.00M), Afinogenov ($4.50M), Kaberle ($4.10M), Nash ($3.90M), Fischer ($3.70M), McCabe ($3.00M), Eminger ($2.20M), and three more at $1.30-1.50M. By then Richards is 28, Nash 25, Chlup (whoever stays) will be on a different deal. The problem isn't the sum, it's that eleven young cores all hit the market at once and some become unaffordable together. Spreading even two or three of these to 2008 or 2010 renewals at the next opportunity is the fix.

**Tucker** at 30, POTE 79, $1.30M, 1 year, scratched every game — the GM earmarked him as a trade chip in March 2005 and he's still here. He's a rental by July 2006 and worth nothing if not moved by the deadline.

**Money:** $89.94M payroll, $43.00M revenue, $34.08M profit. Profit is healthy; the club can absorb Iginla-type money without restructuring. Ticket at $112 with prestige 1092 suggests revenue headroom exists if the team is winning. No financial constraint blocks the moves above.

**Draft capital:** Own 1st, 2nd, 3rd in 2006. If the club is a contender at the March deadline, the 1st is the ammunition for a backup-centre or depth-D rental. If not, the 1st becomes trade bait for a high-POTE prospect. Either way, not hoarded.

**Task delivery — #2 (Luongo/DiPietro monitoring):** This task is complete. Luongo arrived February 2005, is on the roster at 91 base with POTE 97, and the GM closed all goalie monitoring on March 19, 2005. DiPietro monitoring is moot. The remaining goalie action is a Luongo renewal in July 2006, which is a contract matter not a trade-search matter.

## Calendar

The deadline is 158 days away and Toronto has played one game, so no buy-or-sell posture exists yet. The plan that matters in October is the summer one, because the expiring list is already known and in this game you cannot renegotiate a contract mid-term — every decision below is a July 2006 decision made from a position we build between now and February.

**Chlup** is the single most important contract on the roster. He is 19 years old, carries an 82 base overall at $2.34M on a one-year deal, and the Coach installed him at first-line centre after 59 points at 16.9 minutes a night. Renew on 5–6 years immediately when the contract comes up. At 19 with that production, his price will double by next summer. This is the lock that sets the franchise's centre position for six years.

**Luongo** is 26, 91 base, $1.60M, and the standing order from March 2005 already confirmed him as the number-one goalie. Renew on 5–6 years. He is entering his prime and no contending team trades its starter.

**Mogilny** is 36 at $5.50M with a 90 base overall. The Coach flagged him for step-down within 1–2 seasons in May. He is not returning at that price at 37. Because he is above 80 base and will not be re-signed, he qualifies for the over-80 pick-recovery mechanic at the March 2006 deadline: trade him for a draft pick rather than losing him to free agency. That pick capital is the difference between funding a deadline acquisition and not.

**Klesla** is 23, $0.90M, on the Coach's sell list as of May 2005. Move him before the March 2006 deadline. He is not re-signing and letting him walk in July for nothing is the worst outcome on this list.

**Tucker** was flagged as a trade chip on March 19, 2005 and apparently never moved. He is 30, $1.30M, expiring. Same logic as last season: move him at the deadline for a pick or a young player, or accept he walks in July.

**Spezza** is the conditional case. POTE 99, 22 years old, $1.00M. The Coach said on May 11 either earn real minutes or stop dressing him; he played 46 games at 6.7 MPG last season. If he shows up at camp with top-nine numbers, renew on 3 years at a low rate. If not, trade him at the deadline while his POTE 99 still carries value. His development trajectory from now through February is the deciding input, and I will have it by January.

**Koltsov** is 24, $1.10M, LW. At that age and salary, if he earns a regular role he gets a 2-year renewal at a similar figure. If not, he walks.

**Ouellet** is 24, $0.90M, a backup goalie. With Luongo locked long-term and Tellqvist still developing, he is the cheapest insurance policy in the building. Renew on 2 years or let him walk; either is acceptable.

**St. Jacques** is 25, $0.80M, depth defence. He is replaceable on the market at that price. Let him walk unless injuries make him useful in the stretch run.

**Draft capital** has changed materially since the January 2005 note that said Toronto owned nothing better than a fourth-rounder. For the 2006 draft, Toronto holds its own first-round pick, a second, and an extra first originally belonging to Ottawa. That is enough to fund a February 2006 acquisition without touching the core.

**Deadline posture:** reassess in late January or early February when we have 40+ games. If we are in the top eight, the two extra first-round picks are the currency for a top-four defenceman or a second-line winger. If we are out, Mogilny, Klesla, Tucker and possibly Spezza become the sell list and the picks become the floor rather than the ceiling.

**On task #2** (monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro development for the goalie trade window): this was delivered when Luongo arrived on the roster in February 2005 at 91 base. The March 19, 2005 standing order closed all goalie monitoring. Task is complete and closed.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: who across the other 29 clubs closes Toronto's three structural gaps — zero 80+ TOUG players, no fourth-line centre who both checks and wins draws, and a scoring bridge that does not exist — and whose club has a reason to move them right now.

**Jovanovski** is the single best target. 89 base, 93 TOUG, 94 CHKG, age 29, $2.30M on an expiring deal from Vancouver, who carry 13 expiring contracts, the lowest payroll in the league at $46.36M, and a rebuild underway. He closes the toughness gap and the defence-depth gap in one move, and at 29 he is not a rental — he can anchor a pair for three more years. The price will be real because 89 overall commands it, but VAN's situation is urgent: 13 men leaving next summer means they would rather get something now than nothing in July.

**Ott** is the best developmental asset available. 72 base, POTE 97, TOUG 83, CHKG 84, age 23, $800K, 1 year, Dallas (11 expiring, $27.39M profit). He is not a top-six player today but his grades say he closes the toughness hole while he develops, and $800K is nothing. DAL cannot re-sign 11 expiring players; at $800K he is expendable. This is the manual's shape — young, cheap, high potential, on a seller.

**Begin** is the L4 centre fix the Coach has been asking for since April. 87 TOUG, 95 CHKG, 86 FACE, age 27, $936K, 1 year, Buffalo (6 expiring, $19.07M profit). He is not a long-term core piece at 27, but he solves the checking-and-drawing problem tonight. No internal option comes close: Jackman's 75 TOUG and Tucker's 70 TOUG are the roster bests, and neither draws above 60 FACE. BUF with 6 expiring are moderate sellers; the ask should be a pick or a depth player.

**Hartnell** mirrors Ott's profile on a less motivated club. 79 base, POTE 94, TOUG 87, CHKG 88, age 23, $1.10M, expiring, Nashville. NSH has only 4 expiring contracts and $21.70M profit, so they are less forced than DAL or VAN. Still, at $1.10M and POTE 94, if they listen at all, he should be on the list.

**Malec** is the defence development target. 73 base, POTE 97, TOUG 82, CHKG 84, age 23, $700K, expiring, Carolina. CAR has 14 expiring — the most in the league — and $19.73M profit, so they are shedding aggressively. At $700K and POTE 97 with real toughness grades, he is the cheapest high-upside D on the market. Colaiacovo's May write-off makes this slot urgent.

**Avery** at 25, $400K, 1 year, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 93 FACE, from LA (6 expiring), was already flagged in January. His 6 points in 57 games last season is a problem, but the grades are what the game plays up over a season and he is the cheapest centre on the board who closes all three forward gaps at once.

**Sutton** at ATL offers toughness on D at 94 TOUG, 90 CHKG, age 27, $1.34M on 3 years. ATL are 0-1-0 with $17.95M profit and the second-lowest payroll in the league. The 3 years remaining makes him harder to pry than an expiring deal, but he is young and cheap and ATL are a small-market club that cannot keep everyone.

**Wanvig** at PHX: 74 base, POTE 94, TOUG 86, CHKG 87, age 24, $600K, expiring. PHX have 9 expiring and are 0-1-0. Another cheap young tough forward on a seller. Lower POTE than Ott or Hartnell but still above 90.

**Conroy** at CGY (85 base, 94 FACE, $2.00M, expiring, 9 expiring) remains the March rental option if we are in the race. Not a keeper at 34.

**What I would not chase:** Naslund (32, POTE 52, $4.40M), Selanne (35, $6.94M), Leetch (37, $8.20M), Pronger ($9.50M), Holik ($9.00M) — all expiring from clubs that need the salary relief more than Toronto needs them. Brewer (SJ, 88 base, TOUG 82, $6.21M expiring) is interesting for a July UFA signing but too expensive for a deadline trade. The GM's March 19 order on goalies stands: no goalie targets.

**Internal fixes first:** The Coach should dress Tucker (83 CHKG), McCabe (86 CHKG), Abid (86 OVR, 25) and Koltsov (92 SPEE, 24) before any trade conversation. They cost nothing and give a third-and-fourth-line core of checking and speed that partially bridges the gap while the market works.

## Trade construction

The question is which two or three of the league-scan targets we can actually build a package for, using the surplus the Coach has already flagged as movable. The answer is three deals that don't compete for the same pieces, each argued on the other club's situation.

**Timing matters.** Picks aren't tradeable until game 11, so the two pick-inclusive proposals can't execute for two to three weeks. The GM's Jan 15 2005 stance on opening negotiations late February may still hold; these proposals are built so he can test them when he's ready.

**Jovanovski is the single biggest upgrade available.** 89 base, 93 TOUG, 94 CHKG at 29, on an expiring $2.30M deal from Vancouver, who carry 13 expiring contracts, $46.36M payroll (lowest in the league), and are in full rebuild. They will shed Jovanovski in July for nothing. Getting Klesla, whom the Coach put on the sell list in May, plus a second-round pick is youth plus draft capital for a rebuilding club. Klesla at 23 with POTE 97, SPEE 88 and AGIL 87 is a franchise blueliner if he develops, and $0.90M is nothing against $46.36M. The ask is steep for an expiring rental, but VAN's purge makes a POTE 97 defenceman at 23 the exact thing they should collect.

**Begin is the Coach's April ask in a package.** 87 TOUG, 95 CHKG, 86 FACE at 27, on a $936K expiring deal from Buffalo, who carry 6 expiring and $19.07M profit. Begin walks in July for nothing. We give Tucker ($1.30M, CHKG 92, TOUG 88, the March 2005 chip still unbuilt) plus St. Jacques ($0.80M, POTE 94, CHKG 84, TOUG 80, also expiring and not lined). BUF gets a 25-year-old defenceman with POTE 94 and a veteran checking winger, two real assets for one expiring centre. No pick needed. The two-for-one structure makes the AI's valuation of Begin less important because BUF is getting two bodies.

**Avery is the cheapest fix and prior negotiation confirms it.** 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG at 25, on $400K, from LA. The March 2005 negotiation history says LA wanted a 23-year-old at POTE 94, not a 30-year-old checking wing. Koltsov at 24 with POTE 94 and ACCE 96 fills that exact preference. Add a third-round pick as the sweetener. Avery's 6 points in 57 games last season is ugly, but the grades are what the game plays up, and $400K is below the cost of the 3rd-round pick itself.

**If none land:** Dress Tucker, McCabe, Abid, Koltsov and Wallin as the coverage phase recommends. That partially patches checking and faceoffs through the regular season. The July 2006 UFA market is the real fix: Bell (82 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE from CHI), Iginla (93 base from CGY), and Avery again if LA doesn't re-sign him. The March 2006 deadline with the first-round pick is the fallback for a rental. The structural toughness gap has persisted since February; a failed October only means July carries more weight.

**Malec from Carolina is a bonus suggestion.** 73 base, POTE 97, TOUG 82, CHKG 84, $700K expiring. CAR have 14 expiring, the most in the league. A 3rd-round pick for a POTE 97 blueliner at $700K would be the cheapest upside on the market, but the over-80 pick mechanic doesn't apply (he's 73) and I don't know what CAR would accept for him beyond a pick. Worth testing after the three main proposals.

## Owed

**Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window** — this task is complete. The window closed in February 2005 when Luongo was acquired. The GM closed all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19. Luongo is now on our roster at **97 overall**, 26 years old, $1.60M with 1 year remaining. He played the first game of 2005-06 and is the number one.

**DiPietro** (NYI) finished the window at 88 overall, 24 years old, $1.10M on an expiring deal. He appeared in 1 game this season (the opener). He is still at NYI on a deal that expires in June 2006. Nothing has changed since the file closed in March.

One data point the GM should know without me pushing: Luongo's contract has **1 year left** at $1.60M. That is a renewal question for next July, not this season.

No action needed. The task was completed on 2005-02-19 when Luongo landed, and the GM explicitly killed it on 2005-03-19.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-10-12
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-10-12

Next game vs OTT on Wednesday 12 October 2005.

## Development opportunity

One game is in, so this is purely about who is in the lineup and who is not — no production read is possible yet. The structural question is whether the highest-potential young players are getting dressed and playing, or sitting home.

**Spezza** is scratched with POTE 99 at age 22. Last season his minutes collapsed from 9.1 to 4.8 MPG and his rate fell with them. Now he is not in the lineup at all. That is the same pattern repeating one season later: the highest-potential forward on the roster has no path to ice. I need him playing minutes to find out if last year was a system-fit problem or a real ceiling.

**Eminger** is scratched at 21 with POTE 99. He was locked at $2.20M x 4 per the GM's May correction, so he is not going anywhere. A defenseman with the highest potential on the blue line who cannot dress is a waste of a contract year. He needs top-four minutes or we are burning four years of a valuable asset on the bench.

**Chlup** is on the third line at 6 MPG at age 19. Last season he scored 59 points on 18.2 MPG as the first-line centre. This is game one, so the assignment could be a warm-up, but if he stays on the third line at 6 MPG all season I have buried my best young player.

**Gaborik** at 23, POTE 90, dressed but not playing. At his age the development window is closing. If he is not in the plan, say so and move on rather than carrying him as a healthy scratch.

**Nash** at 21 is getting 18 MPG on the second line. That is the right assignment and I would leave it alone.

**Klesla** at 23 logged 42 minutes in one game on the first pair. That is absurd usage for a 23-year-old and unsustainable. I need to see the next two games before concluding, but if he is eating 40-plus MPG regularly I am burning him out the way I burned Jackman last year.

## Morale watch

**The room is fine after one game, but two usage patterns are creating a morale debt that will come due within a week.**

**Chlup** is at 6 minutes a night on the third line. He scored 59 points at 19 last season; his calibre reads in the mid-80s or better, which means the game expects him to get around 17 minutes. He is 11 minutes short of that band. His morale is 91 right now and climbing, which means the single win is papering over a large deficit. This is the exact setup where a player sits happy for five games and then drops to the 80s all at once when the results cool.

**Richards** is at 13 minutes on the second line. His overall was 91 last season, putting his expected band at 20. That is a 7-minute gap. At 91 morale he is fine today, but it compounds the same way Chlup does.

**Spezza** is the lowest man on the roster at 88, up 3 from last save. He is a healthy scratch with 0 games played. The wins are pulling him back toward 90. If we keep winning he recovers within a handful of games even without ice time. If results slip he is the first to crack. That is the GM's scratch decision, not something a line change fixes.

**The scratched veterans** (Abid, McCabe, Tucker, Eminger, Brendl) sit at 90 with no games. Their morale is stable and the +2 to +6 trend shows wins are carrying them. No intervention needed unless results turn.

No change today. The dressing room is at 91 average, the results are positive, and one game is not enough to move anyone off their number. But if Chlup stays at 6 minutes past the third game, his morale is going to start showing the mismatch.

## Role composition

**The question: do our units suit their jobs, and can I build them from what's available?**

**K2 penalty kill** is the one that bothers me. Checking mean 72 with Kaberle and Klesla on the ice — both offensive defencemen. Klesla's best grade is 99 speed, not a checking or shutdown trait. Kaberle is on P2 as well, so he's the offensive guy asked to do two jobs. Spacek at 81 checking is the only real body on that unit. The alternative would be McCabe at 82 checking, but he's scratched for development and Ottawa at 0-1 doesn't trigger the all-out framework. No arrangement of available players fixes this.

**K1 is solid.** Chlup, Roberts, Jackman, Fischer gives a checking mean of 83 with Jackman at 91 anchoring. That's the unit that kills against Ottawa's top power-play line.

**L1 and L2** are both offensive top-six lines, which is fine for a home game against a 0-1 opponent. The Jackman/Klesla pairing on L1 matches the guide: one defensive D, one offensive D, with three skilled forwards behind them. L2 gets Gaborik's 99 speed and Richards' 94 playmaking. No reason to touch either.

**L3 with Chlup** — I've recommended moving him up four times and the GM hasn't acted. His 0.88 pts/g on 18.2 MPG last season says he's producing on L3 minutes. Per the GM's own philosophy: producing on your minutes is your role. I'm dropping this.

**The fourth line** at checking mean 71 is marginally better than last season's 62 after Spacek came onto it at 81 checking. Still thin, but no player on the roster outside McCabe offers a meaningful upgrade, and he's on the shelf for development.

## Opponent matchup

The question: does Ottawa's top-heavy roster require a lineup change, or do our current lines match them well enough as-is?

**Their top line** is the threat. Alfredsson at 91 OVR with DEKG 98 and PASS 97 is a playmaker who can create from nothing. Havlat at 90 OVR with SPEE 99 and AGIL 99 can beat anyone one-on-one. White at 82 is the soft link (CHKG 66, TOUG 56). Our first line — Sundin 92, Mogilny 89, Roberts 87 — has the size and two-way game to handle them. Roberts specifically (CHKG 89, TOUG 91) is built to body Alfredsson (TOUG 69), and Klesla's SPEE 99, AGIL 99 on our top D pair neutralizes Havlat's speed.

**Their second line** (Fisher 82, Hossa 86, Bonk 82) is solid but our L2 (Richards 89, Gaborik 99, Nash 85) is clearly deeper. Gaborik alone at 99 OVR is an unfair weapon against Fisher's 82. Chara's physicality (AGGR 96, TOUG 90) is the real question on their back end for our second pair (Fischer 84, Kaberle 85), but Chara pairs with Smith at 78 OVR and 57 DEKG, so he has a coverage liability beside him.

**Their bottom six** (Ulmer 70, Schaefer 77, Hamel 74, Barnes 79, Schastlivy 73) is where we win this game. Chlup at 87 against Ulmer at 70 is a 17-point gap. Our depth edges theirs by a full tier on the third line alone.

**No change to the lines.** The auto-pairing puts our strongest units against their strongest units, and the matchups favour us on three of four lines. This is a quality opponent (Alfredsson 91, Havlat 90, Hossa 86), so full veterans out, no development rotation.

**Luongo starts.** OVR 97, no fatigue marker visible. Lalime at 90 is good but not 97.

## Owed

The question: who should go at the end of the season, based on how our defencemen played. This is game 1 of 2005-06 so the sample is thin, but the pair-slot allocation is structural and that's what matters this early.

**Klesla** — The contract situation has changed since my last report. He was at $0.90M x 2 in March when I put him on the sell list. Now it reads $0.90M x 1. He is in his final year of control. The sell window is no longer "next offseason" — it is this season, deadline or bust. He logged 42 minutes on pair 1 last game, which inflates his trade value short-term but risks injury on a player we want to move. His two declining seasons (0.38 at 22, 0.36 at 23) are locked.

**Jackman** — $0.70M x 2 now (one year off from what I noted in March). Still sell this season. He played 41 minutes on pair 1 alongside Klesla. His 0.48 pts/g from last season and cheap contract make him tradeable as top-pair minutes, but he's not the answer going forward.

**Kaberle** — 85 OVR, the GM's stated star, and he got 11 minutes on pair 2 while Klesla and Jackman took all the ice. This is the pairing-slot problem, not a quality problem. He belongs on pair 1. The fix is the slot order in the lines menu: move him to a first-pair slot.

**Fischer** — 84 OVR, $3.70M x 3, and only 10 minutes on pair 2. Same issue as Kaberle: he's a keeper being underutilized because of slot placement. Pair him with Kaberle on the top unit.

**McCabe** — Not even dressed. OVR 84, age 30, $3.00M x 3, and his final season rate was 0.76 over 82 games but the recent window was 0.48. Confirmed sell. The fact that he's already a scratch confirms the game's own evaluation matches mine.

**Eminger** — Not dressed. $2.20M x 4 at age 21. His slide is documented (0.44 to 0.36 over two seasons) but the $2.20M x 4 is the problem nobody else will take. Low trade value; probably stays unless a club bites on the youth.

**Stahle and Colaiacovo** — 6 minutes each on pair 3. Both 76 OVR, young, development minutes. No concern; they're growing in small doses as the rotation intends.

What changed since my last delivery: Klesla's deal flipped from 2 years to 1 (expiring), making this the actual deadline year. McCabe confirmed as a scratch. The pair-slot order needs fixing so Kaberle and Fischer get pair-1 minutes instead of the two guys on the sell list.



---

**Message to GM:**

Defenceman report for the OTT game. The pairing slot order needs fixing: Kaberle and Fischer (85 and 84 OVR) got 10-11 minutes on pair 2 while Klesla and Jackman took 41-42 on pair 1. Swap them in the lines menu so the star pair gets the top minutes. On the sell list: Klesla's deal is now $0.90M x 1, meaning he expires this year. The deadline is this season, not next offseason — his trade window is narrowing fast. Jackman and McCabe unchanged, both still sell. Nothing else moved in one game.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 3, in-game 2005-05-31
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 3, in-game 2005-05-31

Toronto 59-13-5, 133 pts after 82 games.

## Role coverage

The question this phase answers is whether Toronto can fill every role the game demands from what is on the roster, and what has to be bought. The answer: speed and stamina are deep, checking is adequate for now, but toughness and faceoffs are vacant at any usable level, and the scoring core is three players aged 34 to 39 with no proven successor under 30.

**Gaborik** is the single biggest fixable gap on the roster. He carries 92 in scoring, 92 in playmaking, 98 in speed, and 90 in clutch, all at age 23, and the brief lists him as "not lined" in four of eight categories. The coach himself wants him dressed against quality opponents. If he plays L1W or L2W every night, the scoring bridge gains a 90+ carrier in his prime without a trade. This is a coach decision, not an acquisition target.

**Toughness** is the structural void the coach quantified on April 9: L4 checking mean 61, toughness mean 57, and he stated no bench player fixes it. The roster holds zero players at 80+ toughness. Best is Jackman at 75. This cannot be solved internally. Iginla (27, 93 base, TOUG 85, 140 pts/73 GP, $6.50M expiring, CGY) closes toughness and the scoring bridge simultaneously. Bell (CHI, 24, 82 base, TOUG 88, CHKG 86, FACE 82) closes toughness and faceoffs. They serve different gaps.

**Faceoffs** below L3 is the other unfixable-internal gap. Sundin at 90 is the only center above 80 who plays significant minutes; Wallin at 83 is not lined and likely cannot carry L4 duty. Chlup at 75 is the next-best available, and Richards at 70. The coach quantified L4 faceoff mean at 52 with best 55 on May 5. Bell (82 FACE) or Avery (LA, 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, $400K, 2yr) are the only two league-wide solutions. Avery closes toughness too, but at only 83 TOUG he is a partial answer to the toughness gap.

**Checking** is adequate today: Jackman 87 (24), Roberts 86 (39), McCabe 86 (29), Tucker 83 (30), Fischer 82 (24), Upshall 80 (21). But Tucker is a trade chip per the GM's March 19 order, Roberts is 39 and his contract expires, and Upshall is in the camp-audition-or-cut group. After this summer, realistically three 80+ checkers remain: Jackman, McCabe, Fischer. That is thin for a playoff run.

**Scoring and playmaking** look deep at 12 and 13 players above 80, but the top of that list is Mogilny (94, 36), Sundin (92, 34), Roberts (88, 39). Those three carry 426 combined points and all expire or decline within twelve months. Gaborik (23, 92) is the successor if lined. After him the gap drops to Richards (85, 25) and Spacek (84, 19) who is in the camp-audition group. The bridge is one year from structural collapse. Iginla at 27, 93 base, 140 points in 73 games is the single acquisition that prevents it.

**Goalies** are covered. Luongo (26, 94/94 glove-stick grades, 0.889 SV, 1 year left at $1.60M) is the franchise starter. Ouellet (23) and Tellqvist (25, 6 years) provide depth with development upside. The one action item is Luongo's renewal at season's end: 5–6 years, per the star-contract rule.

**Stamina and durability** are not gaps. Kaberle 97, McCabe 94, Sundin 92, Mogilny 91, and 14 others at 80+ in stamina. Durability is thinner at 5 above 80, but the top six lines are covered.

## Trajectory

The July 2005 cluster was resolved; the next one is July 2006, and it is smaller but more dangerous because it holds Luongo, Chlup, and Klesla.

**The shape is right.** Five veterans (Jonsson 30, Tucker 30, Sundin 34, Mogilny 36, Roberts 39) against 28 players under 30. Fourteen players with POTE 94 or higher, six of them playing 68-plus games. The manual calls for 5–7 veterans and at least six high-potential players with three or four dressed nightly; this roster clears every test. The depth is there.

**The scoring cliff is real and specific.** Mogilny (36), Sundin (34), Roberts (39) carry 256 points between them on a roster that produced roughly 550 as a team. No player under 30 scored more than 66 (Richards). Chlup at 59 in 71 games is the closest bridge, but he needs to jump another 30 points to fill Mogilny's seat alone, and Mogilny walks in July 2006 when his contract expires at $5.50M. That is the year the production void becomes unmasked.

**Luongo is the renewal emergency.** He is 26, 91 base, POTE 97, playing 45 games, and carries one year at $1.60M. If he walks in July 2006, the club has Ouellet (POTE 97 but 23 with 13 games) and Tellqvist (POTE 91, 11 games) as goalies. No other 1-year contract on the roster poses a comparable risk. He needs 5–6 years at whatever he'll accept this summer.

**Chlup is second.** He is 19, POTE 95, 59 points in 71 games, $2.34M with one year left. The Coach has already named him L1C. If he signs somewhere else in 14 months, the centre position reopens in a thin market. Lock him on 5–6 years at the same time as Luongo.

**Klesla is third.** 23 years old, 82 games, POTE 97, $0.90M with one year left. He plays every night at 22-plus minutes of defensive duty. Extending him costs pennies relative to what he is worth and removes one more renewal from the 2006 list.

**Sundin is the money trap nobody can solve today.** At $8.40M through 2008-09, he will be 35, 36, and 37 on the three most expensive years. His 91 points this year may be the last 90-point season. There is no trade available that recovers value on a 34-year-old with four years left at that salary; the only decision is whether to build around him or accept that the money is sunk and fill around him cheaply.

**Draft capital is one first-round pick (from OTT) and a fourth.** The fourth is negligible. The first-rounder is the only asset the club can put in a trade without giving up a player.

**Payroll at $95.44M against $128.15M revenue gives $32.71M of unallocated headroom.** The $54.60M profit number includes that gap. Toronto can add $6.50M (Iginla's salary) without touching existing contracts, and if Mogilny's $5.50M walks in July 2006, the total freed space before the 2006-07 season opens is $12.00M. The money is not the constraint. The player to put it on is.

## Calendar

The deadline passed 73 days ago; we're 133 points and first in the East with one game left. There is no deadline plan left to build. The summer is the whole job now, and the clock runs from the first day of July when the nine expiring players hit the market.

**Luongo** is the priority. He's 26, 91 base, $1.60M, and the GM designated him and Belfour as two 90-plus goalies for the playoff push. Belfour may retire; Luongo won't. Lock him 5-6 years before July opens. He is the one asset on this list whose loss would be irrecoverable — franchise goaltending at $1.60M does not exist on the open market.

**Chlup** at 19, L1C assignment, $2.34M. He goes 5-6 years. The coach put him at first-line centre before the season even started. That's a franchise centre on the depth-chart, not a question about whether he stays.

**Spezza** is the hard call. POTE 99 at 21, 6.7 MPG and 0.33 pts/g this year — the coach gave the ultimatum on 2005-05-31: top-six minutes at camp or traded while the 99 still holds value. Renew 5-6 years if he wins a top-nine role in September; if he doesn't, deal him in October. His $1.00M renewal cost is trivial either way.

**Mogilny** at 36, $5.50M. Let him go. The GM's own April target — Iginla at 27, 93 base, 140 points, $6.50M — replaces his production and his toughness in one signing. Mogilny's $5.50M at 36 buys nothing Iginla's $6.50M at 27 doesn't buy, and Iginla buys ten more years. If Iginla walks to another club, the Mogilny money could fund a cheaper alternative, but the direction is clear: replace him, don't renew him.

**Tucker** at 30, $1.30M. The GM already designated him a trade chip on 2005-03-19. He wasn't moved. Let him go. He doesn't fit the timeline or the coach's development plan.

**Koltsov** at 24, $1.10M. No coach flag, no development demand, no camp audition. If he doesn't make the roster in September, release. If he makes it as depth, 2 years at similar money. He is not a priority renewal.

**Ouellet** at 23, $0.90M. He's the backup goalie and we need one. Luongo's career length is the unknown — if Belfour retires, Ouellet is the only other man in the building. Renew 2-3 years. Cheap insurance.

**Klesla** at 23, $0.90M and **St. Jacques** at 24, $0.80M. Both are cheap young defencemen. Renew 2-3 years each. Depth wins cups, and $1.70M for two blueliners under 25 is good value regardless of whether they play every night.

The overall summer shape: lock the two future stars (Luongo, Chlup), decide on Spezza at camp, replace Mogilny with Iginla or equivalent, cut the 30-year-olds (Tucker, Mogilny), hold the cheap depth (Ouellet, Klesla, St. Jacques, Koltsov if he makes it). Total committed money on renewals: roughly $7.64M (Luongo + Chlup at similar money, plus the depth at similar). We free up $6.80M by releasing Mogilny and Tucker. The net is payroll-neutral, and the Iginla signing if it lands adds $6.50M against a club at 133 points with revenue to match.

On the Luongo monitoring task from January: Luongo is on the roster at 91 base. The task is delivered. The GM's March 19 order closed all goalie monitoring.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: which players across the league close Toronto's three structural gaps — zero toughness above 80 on the roster, best L4 faceoff at 55, and 426 points of expiring production from players aged 34 to 39 — and what does it take to get them?

The answer is that the July window is the one that matters, and most of the best available targets hit UFA simultaneously. We have $32.71M of headroom, no cap constraint, and the ability to sign multiple $2M players without touching a contract. The bottleneck is not money. It is which players actually hit the open market versus which their current clubs retain.

**Bertuzzi** is the best player available in this window on any measure. At 30, he carries 94 base, 128 points in 82 games, 83 TOUG and 87 CHKG on a $2.60M expiring deal. No other player closes scoring, toughness, and checking at the same level for the same money. VAN sits at 99 points with 13 expiring contracts; they cannot keep all of them. If he walks in July, we sign him. If VAN trades him before July, we cannot match — he's their leading scorer. The risk is his age: three productive years, not seven. Those are the exact three years Mogilny, Sundin, and Roberts fall off.

**Heatley** (89 base, 131 pts/79 GP, TOUG 80, $1.10M, age 24) and **Kovalchuk** (90 base, 138 pts/79 GP, TOUG 83, $1.10M, age 22) sit in a binary on ATL. The Thrashers cannot re-sign both at $1.10M and keep their roster intact; they have 6 expiring contracts and $37.20M payroll but only 84 points. Whichever one ATL lets go, we pursue. A decade of top-line scoring for $1.10M at 22 or 24 is the single highest-value contract available anywhere. The trade is that ATL knows the value and may not let either walk cheaply.

**Doan** at 28 is the toughness-scoring hybrid nobody else offers at that age: 87 base, 62 points, 86 TOUG, 91 CHKG, ENDU 88, $2.40M expiring from PHX at 93 points. Nine PHX players are expiring; 62 points plus elite checking at $2.40M is within reach if PHX prioritizes retaining younger pieces or Sillinger. He does not solve faceoffs (60 FACE) but he makes every line around him harder to play against.

**Bell** at 24 remains the faceoff solution. 80 base, 92 FACE, 86 TOUG, 84 CHKG, $900K expiring from CHI at 78 points. Only 28 points in 80 games confirms he is a specialist, not a scorer. ENDU 69 caps his shifts at 12 minutes. But he walks into L3C or L4C and the coach's 52-mean problem disappears in one move. At $900K the cost is negligible.

**Iginla's contract changed.** The April note read $6.50M expiring. The sheet now reads $11.09M with four years remaining. That moves him from UFA target to trade-only moonshot. At $11.09M he would be our highest-paid player by a wide margin, more than Sundin's $8.40M. CGY at 70 points with $14.38M profit and 8 expiring deals could still sell him for young pieces and picks, but the price for a 27-year-old with 128 points and four years of control is far beyond our single first-rounder and Tucker. I deprioritize him below the Tier 1 names unless CGY's asking price drops to what we can actually put together.

**Barnaby** at 95 TOUG and 96 CHKG with 53 points in 78 games is the most physical player available at $1.50M expiring. NYR carry $88.18M in payroll against $0 profit; they are shedding salary by necessity. At 32 he is not a bridge player, but he is a two-year fix for toughness and secondary scoring while Heatley or Kovalchuk develops.

**Conroy** scores 102 points in 82 games at 95 FACE for $2.00M expiring from 70-point CGY. But TOUG 63 and age 33 make him a rental with no residual value. He is a depth-scoring add, not a structural answer, and I rank him below every younger option above.

**Holik** at 84 TOUG, 90 CHKG, 93 FACE, 86 points in 82 games is the best pure package in the league for closing three gaps at once. The problem is $9.00M for two more years at age 34. NYR must cut salary — $88.18M payroll, zero profit — but they may need to eat salary to move him. If they offer $4M retention, this becomes the single best deal available. Without it, the money is too much for a 34-year-old when Doan does 70% of the job at $2.40M.

I deprioritize Avery below Bell on every axis: 79 TOUG versus 86, ENDU 50 versus 69, and 9 points in 82 games versus 28. Avery at $400K is a depth piece who cannot survive 10 MPG.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: what concrete packages can Toronto put together in June to close toughness and faceoffs without gutting the depth the GM has built? The answer is two deals, both giving players the Coach himself has said he can't use, and a July UFA plan that handles the scoring bridge without touching a single roster asset.

**Proposal 1: Bell from Chicago.** Bell at 24 is 82 base with 92 FACE, 86 TOUG, and 84 CHKG on $900K expiring. He closes the two structural gaps the Coach quantified on April 9 (L4 checking mean 61, toughness mean 57, faceoff best 55) in a single transaction. We give **Spezza** (21, POTE 99, $1.00M expiring) and **Koltsov** (24, POTE 94, $1.10M expiring, ACCE 96, AGIL 92) plus the 4th-rounder from TOR. Net payroll: we shed $2.10M, take on $0.90M, save $1.20M.

Why CHI says yes: they sit at 78 points with 10 expiring contracts and $29.46M profit. They are rebuilding. Two players aged 21 and 24 with POTE 94+ and elite speed (Koltsov ACCE 96, Spezza ACCE 86) are exactly what a 78-point team hoards. Bell is their 28-point specialist on an expiring deal who doesn't fit a rebuild's timeline. The Coach has already said Spezza should go if top-six minutes don't appear ("6.7 MPG and 0.33 pts/g at POTE 99 is a year wasted"). We are not giving him away; we are selling him to a team that can actually play him.

Risk: Bell's $900K deal expires after 2005-06. We get one year of him, then re-sign in July 2006. Acceptance uncertain because the AI's pricing of two young prospects versus one specialist is unknown, but the hockey logic is clean on both sides.

**Proposal 2: Stuart from San Jose.** Stuart at 25 is 87 base, 89 CHKG, 80 TOUG, POTE 91, with roughly eight years of control remaining. He is the Roberts replacement the coverage phase identified: Roberts at 39 expires after 2006-07 and no blueliner under 30 on this roster carries 80+ TOUG plus 89+ CHKG. We give **Colaiacovo** (22, POTE 99, $1.40M, 4yr) plus the **OTT first-rounder**.

Why SJ says yes: they are at 72 points with 13 expiring contracts on $45.39M payroll. They need to rebuild and a POTE 99 defenceman at 22 on a 4-year, $1.40M deal is a lottery ticket they'd take at any reasonable price. The OTT 1st rounder sweetens it. For us, Colaiacovo is dead weight: the Coach wrote him off on May 15 with 31 GP at 17.9 MPG and 0.39 pts/g. We cannot develop him. Selling his POTE to a team that will give him 20+ MPG converts a zero into an 87-base defenceman.

Risk: SJ at 72 may want to build around Stuart rather than trade him. This is the deal I'm least confident lands. Giving up the 1st rounder also leaves us with zero draft capital until the 2006 draft produces a replacement. I would do this deal but not before Proposal 1 lands, because Bell is cheaper and closes more gaps per asset surrendered.

**Proposal 3 (contingency): Avery from LA.** If Bell falls through, Avery at LA carries 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, $400K with 2 years left. He is a partial answer: faceoffs are closed, toughness moves from 57-mean to about 65-mean. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring has roster clutter. We give Tucker ($1.30M, 1yr, 30, POTE 79, CHKG 92). LA gets a salary to shed and a checking option; we get a cheap faceoff specialist who survives on the fourth line. The Feb 2005 note said LA "wants a 23-year-old at POTE 94, not a 30-year-old," but LA at 79 points is in a different posture than at 48. Acceptance is uncertain; Avery is the fallback, not the target.

**What we do NOT propose:**
- No package for Iginla. At $11.09M with 4 years left, he is $2.69M above Sundin's $8.40M and beyond any combination we can offer without dismantling the foundation.
- No package for Heatley or Kovalchuk. Both are UFA signings at $1.10M, not trade targets. If ATL keeps one and trades the other, we revisit.
- Chistov is off the table. The Coach on May 31 reversed his May 5 stance: "Give Chistov a bigger role next season. He doubled minutes from 9.5 to 14.0 MPG while holding his rate at 0.30 at age 22."

**If none land:** Sign Cammalleri in July at $1.10M (22, POTE 98, 60 pts/61 GP). He solves the scoring bridge without giving a single asset. Keep Tucker as a depth piece or release him to free $1.30M. Accept the toughness gap for one more season and develop Jackman (TOUG 89, 24) into a power role. The gap is survivable for one year; the scoring bridge is not.

## Owed

**Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window** — this task is closed. The GM killed all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19 ("Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks"), and Luongo is on our roster at 97 overall, 26 years old, $1.60M, one year left. He played 45 games this season. The window passed, the target arrived, and the GM made the call.

**DiPietro** finished the season at NYI with 63 games played, 89 overall, $1.10M, expiring. That is a significant workload for a 23-year-old on a rookie deal — more evidence he was a viable target had the window stayed open, but it no longer matters. He will hit the market in July. If the GM ever wants a cheap high-potential backup, DiPietro is the obvious first call now, though our current pair (Luongo 97, Belfour 91) makes that unlikely to be a priority.

Nothing has changed since the task was closed. I am marking it delivered and removing it from the outstanding list.

title: Coach's report — run 2, in-game 2005-05-31
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 2, in-game 2005-05-31

Next game at DAL on Wednesday 01 June 2005.

## Development opportunity

The season's wrapped — 82 games in the books and one playoff game ahead — so this is the offseason verdict: who got the chance, who didn't, and what needs to change before camp opens.

**Gardener** has zero games. POTE 98, age 20, and he hasn't put a shift in all year. That's the most extreme case on the roster. He's not earning games he hasn't been offered, and a season of zero is a season where nobody knows whether he can play. He needs a full camp audition or he's an asset going to waste.

**Stahle** has 4 games and POTE 96 at 21. When he does play he gets 17.8 minutes, which is top-pair minutes, and he hasn't registered a point. Either the coaching staff doesn't trust him or the trust broke early and never rebuilt. A 21-year-old defenceman with that scouting number sitting on the bench for 78 games is the same problem as Gardener in a different shape.

**Colaiacovo** played 31 games at 17.9 MPG. That's a top-pair assignment when he's in, and he scored 12 points on it. POTE 99, age 22. He's been the odd-man-out on the back end while Klesla and Eminger play every night. With Eminger expiring and Klesla on the sell list, next season's top pair should start with Colaiacovo's name on it.

**Spezza** got 46 games but only 6.7 MPG. That's not development — that's dressing him so he doesn't wave a no-moves clause and giving him garbage minutes. POTE 99, age 21, morale 88 (the lowest on the youth group). The season is dead for him; camp is where this gets fixed or stopped.

**Alexeev** scored 30 points in 55 games at 0.55 pts/g and remains a scratch. Chistov (0.29) and Upshall (0.29) get L3 and L4 ice over him. The mismatch has been on file since April and is unresolved. If Klesla and Eminger leave, forward depth changes and he deserves a look at a real role.

**Chlup** earned every shift of his 71 games at 16.9 MPG at 19. Fifty-nine points confirms he belongs on the first line permanently. This isn't a development question anymore — it's a usage question, and I've flagged it repeatedly with no action.

**Gaborik, Klesla, Eminger, Nash** all got their games. Gaborik 82 at 20.5 MPG is exactly right. Klesla and Eminger are on the sell list and their ice time was the asset being preserved for a trade return. Nash got 69 games at 13.1 on the second line; the production decline from 0.83 to 0.43 is a system-fit problem, not an opportunity problem.

**Upshall** got 68 games but only 7.9 MPG on the fourth line. POTE 99, age 21, 0.29 pts/g. Same camp decision as Spezza: real audition or stop dressing.

## Development trends

The development window closes on a season where one teenager confirmed himself, three confirmed they need to start over at camp, and two veterans are now old enough that next year is a planning question rather than a production one.

**Chlup** is the trend of the year. 0.62 to 0.88 pts/g while minutes rose from 11.0 to 18.2. At 19, he is outperforming his card -- no grade moved on the player card all window, yet his rate climbed 42% purely from earning harder minutes. That is the cleanest development signal in this data. I have recommended him at first-line centre four times and it has not been set. The 0.88 on 18.2 at 19 makes the case every time it gets re-run.

**Kaberle** is the only veteran trending up. 0.54 to 0.62 pts/g, minutes up from 19.4 to 21.5. He is 27, the GM called him a star and a keeper, and the numbers agree. No action needed beyond confirming his role next year.

**Spacek** is the stalling problem. 0.55 to 0.28 pts/g, minutes collapsed from 16.0 to 5.2. He went from a regular to a healthy scratch in three months. At 19 with his card unchanged, the issue is confidence or system-fit, not talent. Offseason: real audition at camp or stop dressing him. The same call applies to **Upshall** (0.33 to 0.27, 13.4 to 4.8 MPG) and **Spezza** (0.43 to 0.24, 9.1 to 4.6 MPG). All three need minutes that match their age and potential, and none of them got it this year.

**Mogilny** at 36 went from 1.62 to 0.83 pts/g while minutes rose to 19.1. **Roberts** at 39 went from 1.29 to 0.86 on 21.4 MPG. Both are still contributing -- 0.86 is not nothing -- but the slope is steep and they are still carrying top-nine minutes. Planning around their decline starts now: how much longer do we expect either? That is a contract-year question the GM owns, and he should ask it before August.

**The system-fit trio** remains unresolved. **Afinogenov** 1.17 to 0.73, **Richards** 1.08 to 0.71, **Nash** 0.83 to 0.42, all on flat minutes. Three players whose rates halved with no role change, no injury, and no grade movement points at how they are used rather than who they are. The offseason review is the one thing on my calendar that could fix the top six.

**Gaborik** at 23 reads 1.42 to 1.12 but that is regression from an unsustainable start, not decline. 1.12 on 21.2 MPG over 58 games is elite and he is still improving in minutes. No concern.

**Chistov** got minutes up from 9.5 to 14.0 while holding his 0.30 rate. Small positive -- he earned trust without losing it.

## Morale watch

The room is fine. Every dressed player sits at 100 morale with positive movement, and the only sub-100 readings belong to scratched players, all of whom are climbing. No intervention needed tonight.

**Abid** is the one structural note worth carrying. He's at 100 morale today on 13.8 MPG, but his 0.84 pts/g on those minutes means he's a top-nine forward on fourth-line ice. His morale hasn't cracked yet because the winning is masking it, but I flagged this back in March and it remains true: if a stretch of losses hits, he's the first dressed player who could slide, because the minutes band for a player producing at his rate is 17, not 14. Not a problem tonight, not a change I'd make before Dallas.

**Jackman** is eating 29.6 a night. At 100 morale he's not complaining, and the results mean the load is earning its keep. I'm not touching it.

**Upshall (94) and Spacek (94)** are both dressed on the fourth line at 7.9 and 7.6 MPG respectively. Their calibre is depth-tier, so those minutes are exactly what the model expects for a 70s-rated player. They're rising (+3 and +5 last save) because we're winning. Nothing to fix.

## Role composition

The question here is whether our units are built for what Dallas will throw at us, and whether the roster itself has holes no arrangement can fill.

**L1 through L3 are sound.** Jackman and Fischer on pair one give us checking mean 80 and best 94 against whatever Dallas puts up top. McCabe and Kaberle on pair two carry checking 75 and the highest offensive output on any D pairing. Klesla and Eminger on three are the weakest defensively but they face the weakest opposition line by the auto-pairing, which is the right assignment.

**L4 is the problem.** Faceoff mean 53, best 59. Nobody on that line wins a draw. Upshall at 4.9 MPG and 0.29 pts/g is contributing nothing either way, so we lose nothing by sitting him and gain 29 points of faceoff grade by putting Wallin in. Against a 42-24 team this matters — they will have centers who take draws against us all night.

**The PK units are correct.** K1 has checking 80, stamina 89, and Sundin at 95 faceoffs to win kills. K2 has checking 84, the highest mean on the roster. No change needed.

**The PP units have shot and vision in abundance.** P1 at 88 scoring mean and P2 at 89 with speed 93. Both can score from multiple spots. No structural fix required.

**The roster gap I flagged in April is partially closed but not gone.** L4 checking mean has improved to 72 from 62 (likely due to Spacek's role), but the faceoff hole remains — and Wallin is the only bench player who fills it. He stays a patch, not a solution.

## Opponent matchup

What matters about Dallas on Wednesday: they're a quality opponent with a 95-rated goalie, so this is a maximize-quality night per the January 15 standing order, but our matchups are already favorable and the lines don't need shuffling.

**Turco** at 95 is the only reason this isn't a walkover. Everything else about Dallas is built around an aging core: Modano at 34 still reads 86 with 91 deking, but after him the drop is steep. Arnott at 83 is their 2C, Messier at 44 reads 74, Gilmour at 41 reads 75. We've beaten them 5-1-1 this season, outscoring them 20-11.

**Their defence** is where this game gets won. Pairs two and three are Erskine at 68 and Berenzweig/Descoteaux at 67/64. The auto-pairing puts our second line (Chlup, Nash, Afinogenov) against Matvichuk/Erskine, and our third line (Richards, Chistov, Tucker) against Berenzweig/Descoteaux. Those are punishing mismatches and the system does the work for us. Don't break it.

**Their PP at 10.8%** (32/297) is a non-threat. Our first kill unit with Sundin and Roberts down the middle will handle their first unit easily. No PK adjustment needed.

**Luongo** at 97 starts. Per the January 19 order, check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming. Last recommendation on May 31 was taken and no game intervened, so he should be fresh.

## Owed

**Defenceman season-end review (#1):** The season is done at 82 games. Final rates are locked, and two contract situations have shifted since my last delivery.

**McCabe** finishes at 0.76 pts/g across 82 games on 22.1 MPG. But my May 2 reading stood: the 58-game window was 0.48, meaning his true current level sits near 0.50. At 29 with 3 years at $3.00M, he's a sell. No change to that call, but the window to get value is closing — buyers discount a declining 29-year-old every month.

**Jackman** locks in at 0.46 pts/g on 29.6 MPG across 80 games. Slightly below my March 23 mark of 0.48. The sell call stands. He's now 2 years at $0.70M, which is one year less control than when I first filed. The price makes him attractive to a contender needing a top-pair minute-eater cheap; that window is now before next season starts.

**Klesla** finishes at 0.37 pts/g on 14.8 MPG, 82 games. Second consecutive declining year confirmed (0.38 to 0.37). The key change: his contract has burned to 1 year at $0.90M. If we don't move him this offseason he walks for nothing at 24. Sell urgency has increased.

**Eminger** finishes at 0.36 pts/g on 15.5 MPG across 64 games. I need to correct my March 30 note: I called him "$1.2M expiring" and said we must move him before free agency. The current sheet shows $2.20M with 4 years remaining. He's not expiring. He's locked up long-term at an inflated rate for a 0.36 pts/g defenseman. The trade urgency drops; the problem shifts from "move him or lose him" to "can we get anything back for 4 years of $2.20M?" — which is much harder.

**Fischer** at 0.53 pts/g on 22.4 MPG and **Kaberle** at 0.59 on 20.8 stay protected per the GM's standing orders. No change.

**Jonsson** at 0.49 pts/g on 19.2 MPG, 61 games, $2.80M x 4 at age 30 is the fifth defenseman we don't need. Not urgent, but he's the next name on the list if Klesla and Jackman both move and we want to trim.

**Sell list order:** Klesla (expiring, highest urgency), Jackman (cheap contract, best return), McCabe (declining, big money, hardest to move), Eminger (trapped by long deal, try but don't expect much).

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-31
