# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-31

Toronto 59-13-5, 133 pts after 82 games.

## Role coverage

Two roles on this roster have nobody at 80+, and the third that looks covered is about to fall off a cliff. The 2005-06 team needs two acquisitions to close the structural gaps the coach has quantified, and one more to survive 2006-07.

**Toughness — MISSING.** Zero forwards or defencemen at 80+ TOUG. The roster's best is Jackman at 75, and he's a defenceman who can't play wing. Tucker at 70, Chlup at 70, Sundin at 69. The coach's April 9 quantification (L4 TOUG mean 57) is confirmed by these numbers. No internal fix exists — the ceiling is 75 and the target is 80+.

**Faceoffs — MISSING beyond Sundin.** Sundin at 90 is the only player at 80+. Chlup 75, Roberts 75, Richards 70, Tucker 67. The coach needs L3C and L4C at FACE 80+; the best forward option is Chlup at 75, five short. No internal fix.

**Checking — THIN on forward L3/L4.** Tucker at 83 CHKG is the best forward option, but the coach's stated threshold is 85, and he's two short. Jackman at 87 is a defenceman. Fischer 82, Upshall 80 are below. The gap is small but real and no one on the roster clears the bar the coach set.

**Bell (CHI) closes toughness and checking but not faceoffs** because he plays left wing. A wing does not take faceoffs. That kills the faceoff argument for him (GM's January 25 correction still holds). He's still the toughness and checking solution for a top-nine wing slot, 88 TOUG and 86 CHKG at 24 with POTE 81.

**Avery (LA) closes all three simultaneously** because he plays centre: 93 FACE, 88 CHKG, 83 TOUG, 25, $400K, 2 years left. He is the only player in the league who raises L4 to the coach's exact thresholds at every position. LA at 48 points with 13 expiring deals are forced sellers. This is the single acquisition that makes the bottom six playable.

**Scoring and playmaking — COVERED today, dying tomorrow.** Ten players at 80+ in scoring, but Mogilny is 36, Sundin 34, Roberts 39. Their combined 426 points have no successor under 30 on this roster. Gaborik (23, 92 scoring) and Koltsov (24, speed 92) are on the roster but not lined. If they develop, the bridge shortens. If not, the Iginla-type acquisition in July is not optional.

**Goalies — COVERED per the GM's March 19 order.** Luongo (26, 2y) and Belfour (40, 1y) for the run; Ouellet (23, 2y) developing as a third. Belfour is a retirement risk and Tellqvist (25, 1y) carries no value as a backup at 80 base. The GM closed this topic; I respect the order and do not revisit.

**The one internal fix available:** Gaborik and Koltsov are the two most underused players. Gaborik at 92 overall, speed 98, age 23, in no unit. Koltsov at speed 92, age 24, in no unit. Lining them at camp is not a roster acquisition — it is the coach using what he has.

## Trajectory

The July 2005 renewal window is the single most important date on this club's calendar, and the GM has 13 contracts worth $21.30M expiring simultaneously. If the five players carrying the core (Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger, Kaberle) walk, a 133-point team starts over. If they sign, the foundation holds for five years and the money is more than sufficient to fund the additions that close the age gap.

**Gaborik** at 99 points in 82 games, age 23, POTE 90, currently at $1.10M, is the best player on the roster and the cheapest star in the league. He walks in July unless locked on 5-6 years. No other player's renewal carries the same weight: the 99-point season means his next contract starts from a high floor, and every competing club sees the same sheet.

**Richards** at 66 points, 25 years old, $1.00M, also expires. He and Gaborik together produce 165 points at a combined $2.10M. Losing either one costs top-two-line production at the lowest price the league has seen.

**Eminger** (21, POTE 99, 23 pts/64 GP, $1.20M) and **Nash** (20, POTE 95, 39 pts/69 GP, $1.20M) are the defensive and wing foundations for the next decade. Both expire. The GM has already protected them from trade; now they need ink.

**Kaberle** at 27 with 44 points and POTE 75 is the oldest of the expiring group. His ceiling is set, but 27 with one year means he still has three or four productive seasons left. A 3-year deal at whatever he asks is cheap insurance against a defence that otherwise has no veteran blueliner once Roberts walks.

The four veterans carrying 256 points (Sundin 91 at 34, Mogilny 84 at 36, Roberts 81 at 39, plus Belfour in net at 40) are the cliff. Sundin has 5 years left at $8.40M and won't be traded. Mogilny has 2 years at $5.50M and will decline from here. Roberts walks in July. The question isn't whether the cliff comes; it arrives around 2008 when Mogilny is 38 and Sundin is 38 too. The question is whether the young core has absorbed their production by then, and Iginla at 27 with 140 points is the only single transaction that accelerates that timeline.

**Tucker** at 30 with 1 game played, $1.30M, and 2 years left sits in the empty 30-33 bracket. The GM already flagged him as a chip. Moving him is correct: he provides nothing, costs $1.30M, and frees the only player in that dead bracket for someone who might.

**The 30-33 void** is structural. Thirteen players are 23 or under; four are 34 or older; one is 30 (Tucker). There is no bridge. By 2008 the four veterans are gone and the "young" core will be 23-27. That's fine in theory if the young core holds, but a team with zero players aged 26-33 has no middle layer to carry playoff experience when the veterans depart. The Iginla acquisition at 27 fills exactly that slot.

**Money is not the problem.** Payroll $60.04M against $128.15M revenue leaves $55.69M profit. Even doubling the payroll to $120M would still leave an $8M cushion. Iginla at a fresh $8-9M, Bell at $4M, Stuart at $5M, all signed this July, would put payroll around $80M and profit still above $45M. The constraint is finding the players, not paying them.

**Draft capital is one fourth-rounder.** Every acquisition must be funded with roster players or UFA money. This eliminates any trade package requiring a first or second and makes the July free-agent/signing route the primary acquisition channel. The over-80 expiring mechanic applies to Gaborik, Richards, Kaberle, Roberts and Belfour if the GM decides not to re-sign any of them, but those are the players he wants to keep.

## Calendar

The deadline passed on March 19 and the regular season ends in one game, so the only calendar question left is the summer: what to do with 13 expiring contracts before they walk.

**Belfour** (40, $6.50M). The GM kept him for the playoffs over Luongo and said he'd offer reduced salary at renewal but probably wouldn't be accepted. At 40, this is the final question. If he walks or retires, the $6.50M clears and Luongo becomes the unambiguous number one. Offer once at a reduced figure, then let him go. No 40-year-old belongs on a Toronto roster three years out.

**Roberts** (39, $2.70M). Part of the 426-point aging core alongside Mogilny and Sundin. At 39 there is no development left and the checking gaps the Coach flagged all season are structural. Let him go. That's $2.70M toward Iginla or Bell.

**Gaborik** (23, $1.10M, 91 base, POTE 90). Highest-priority renewal on the entire list. Lock 5-6 years immediately when free agency opens. A bidding war with a 23-year-old at 91 base and $1.10M current salary is the single worst thing that can happen to this club in July.

**Eminger** (21, $1.20M, POTE 99). GM called him untouchable on January 19, and the Coach's May 29 report doesn't list him among the camp auditions, meaning he's already in the plan. 5-6 year lock, same urgency as Gaborik.

**Kaberle** (27, $1.90M). Prime-age defenceman, 8 years of window remaining. 5-6 year deal. The staggered-lock plan from December 2004 specifically named him alongside Gaborik.

**Nash** (20, $1.20M). Coach has him in a system-fit review alongside Richards and Afinogenov, but at 20 that's a coaching question, not a roster question. Sign 5-6 years before the review concludes and the camp audition changes his asking price.

**Richards** (25, $1.00M, 70 FACE, 85 PASS). The Coach's May 15 note collapsed his scoring rate on flat minutes, but the Coach also moved him to third-line centre for next season. At 25 with those grades, sign 3-4 years, not 5-6. The system-fit review may reshape his role, and a shorter term lets the club reprice if he stalls.

**Chistov** (22, $1.10M, POTE 95, SPEE 89). The Coach said on May 5 that Alexeev displaces him and named him as a trade piece in the Bell package. Two options: re-sign on 2-3 years and hold as depth, or trade in July for Bell (CHI, LW, 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 82 FACE) who closes both the toughness and faceoff voids the Coach quantified. The trade is the better outcome.

**Alexeev** (23, $1.10M). Coach's May 29 order is top-nine audition or stop carrying him. Do not offer a deal before camp. If he makes the top nine, 2-3 years. If not, let him walk.

**Upshall** (21, $1.20M). Same camp-audition-or-cut instruction from the Coach on May 29, same posture as Alexeev. No offer before preseason. At 21 with a camp audition pending, 2-3 years is the ceiling even if he makes it.

**Colaiacovo** (22, $1.10M, POTE 99). Coach wrote him off on May 15: 31 games, 17.9 MPG, 0.39 pts/g. If camp changes nothing, trade the POTE 99 before he becomes a free agent at zero value. If camp shows life, a 2-year prove-it deal. Either way, 5-6 years is off the table.

**Abid** (25, $0.40M). Coach wants 16+ MPG and his rate held at 0.70 on 11.5 MPG last season. At $0.40M he is the cheapest toughness Toronto will find anywhere. Sign 2-3 years. Bell at 24 with 88 TOUG is the upgrade, but Abid at this price is insurance against the Bell deal failing.

**Tellqvist** (25, $0.80M). GM's January 15 standing order: stays, high-90s potential, give him time. Sign 2-3 years. He backs up Luongo.

The draft is June 8. Toronto has no pick better than a fourth-rounder, per the January 2005 note. Use it for a goalie if one of the high-potential class is available, per the January 22 order to scout for goalies in the draft.

## League scan

The July renewal window opens in weeks and Toronto's $55.69M profit means money is not the constraint — finding the right players on the right clubs is. Three free agents with contract_years = 0 (Iginla, Gagne, Marleau) can be signed without a trade, and four expiring players on losing clubs (Kovalchuk, Heatley, Havlat, Conroy) can be traded or re-signed in July. The shortlist below is ranked by the size of the gap each fills multiplied by the likelihood his club lets him go.

**Correction from the coverage phase:** the phase stated zero forwards at 80+ TOUG and named Jackman at 75 as the ceiling. That is wrong. Abid is at 94 TOUG on this roster with 66 points in 82 games at $400K. The coach already flagged the right fix on May 29: give him 16+ MPG. The toughness gap is smaller than reported because Abid exists; what's missing is a second 80+ forward on L3 or L4, not on every line.

**Iginla (CGY, RW, 27)** at 94 overall, 128 points in 76 games, 87 TOUG, POTE 80, $6.50M, contract_years = 0. He closes the scoring void (Mogilny/Sundin/Roberts carry 426 combined points with no successor under 30) and the toughness ceiling simultaneously. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring deals and $14.38M profit cannot match a competitive offer. This is the single move that changes the team's shape for five years.

**Kovalchuk (ATL, LW, 22)** at 90 overall, 138 points in 79 games, 78 TOUG, POTE 85, $1.10M, contract_years = 1. ATL at 84 points with 11 expiring contracts cannot retain both him and Heatley. If ATL keeps Heatley, Kovalchuk walks as a UFA in July. 138 points at 22 for $1.10M is the most absurd production-to-cost ratio in the league. The risk is that ATL keeps him instead.

**Havlat (OTT, LW, 24)** at 89 overall, 103 points in 82 games, POTE 85, $900K, contract_years = 1. OTT at 77 points with 11 expiring deals. Under $1M for a 24-year-old with 103 points. The TOUG 68 and FACE 50 don't close the physical gaps, but his production solves the scoring bridge directly. Cheapest high-end scorer available.

**Gagne (PHI, LW, 25)** at 86 overall, 108 points in 82 games, POTE 80, $2.40M, contract_years = 0. PHI at $66.73M payroll with $2.12M profit are the most financially distressed club in the league. They must shed salary. 25 years old with 108 points on a team that can't afford to keep him. He is a UFA right now.

**Marleau (SJ, C, 25)** at 88 overall, 98 points in 71 games, POTE 82, FACE 70, $1.60M, contract_years = 0. SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring deals. He is a center with 88 grade who scores at a top-six rate. If the GM wants a first-line center who isn't Sundin in two years, Marleau is the answer. He is already a free agent.

**Brewer (SJ, D, 26)** at 87 overall, 61 points in 82 games, 82 TOUG, 93 CHKG, POTE 83, $2.00M, contract_years = 0. SJ cannot retain 13 expiring players at $45.39M payroll. He is the best available defenceman closing the toughness gap that the coverage phase identified, now that Chara is off the table per the GM's standing order. 82 TOUG clears the 80 threshold and 93 CHKG clears the coach's 85 bar with room to spare.

**Cammalleri (LA, RW, 22)** at 83 overall, 60 points in 61 games, POTE 97, $1.10M, contract_years = 1. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring deals and $52.43M payroll. His grades aren't elite yet, but 60 points in 61 games at 22 with POTE 97 is the highest-potential forward available outside our own roster. LA will likely keep Frolov (POTE 95, same club) over him, making Cammalleri a July target.

**Holik (NYR, C, 34)** at 81 overall, 86 points in 82 games, FACE 94, 86 TOUG, 92 CHKG, POTE 72, $9.00M, contract_years = 3. NYR at $78.14M payroll with zero profit. They are financially desperate. He is the only player in the league at 94 FACE and 86 TOUG simultaneously — he closes the faceoff gap and the toughness gap at centre in one body. The 34 and $9M are the problems: this is a two-year bridge, not a long-term answer. But for a playoff push, 86 points, 94 FACE, and 86 TOUG from a centre is elite.

**Conroy (CGY, C, 33)** at 85 overall, 102 points in 82 games, FACE 94, 80 CHKG, $2.00M, contract_years = 1. CGY at 70 points, 10 expiring, $14.38M profit. They are sellers. 94 FACE closes the L4C faceoff gap and 102 points is top-six production from a fourth-line centre. But 33 and expiring means a rental unless he accepts a cheap re-signing. Cheaper than Holik, lower ceiling.

**Avery (LA, C, 25)** at 77 overall, 9 points in 82 games, FACE 93, 88 CHKG, 83 TOUG, POTE 70, $400K, contract_years = 2. Still cheap, still closes the faceoff/checking/toughness triangle at centre, still 25 with two years left. But 9 points in 82 games (0.11 ppg) is the ghost-production problem flagged on February 16. He fills the grades the coach wants but not the points. Useful as a checking centre if minutes are managed, but not as a scoring solution.

**Heatley (ATL, RW, 24)** at 88 overall, 131 points in 79 games, POTE 85, $1.10M, contract_years = 1. The mirror of Kovalchuk: whichever ATL doesn't keep, the other is available. 131 points at 24 for $1.10M. If ATL keeps Kovalchuk, Heatley becomes the top UFA target.

**Stuart (SJ, D, 25)** at 87 overall, 52 points in 77 games, POTE 91, 80 TOUG, 91 CHKG, $1.80M, contract_years = 1. Higher ceiling than Brewer (POTE 91 vs 83), same club, same situation. But POTE is a likelihood and one year means SJ will try to re-sign him. Lower probability of acquisition than Brewer, who is already a free agent.

## Trade construction

The league scan's shortlist has a shortcut that changes everything: Iginla (CGY, 27, 128 points, contract_years = 0), Gagne (PHI, 25, 108 points, 0), Marleau (SJ, 25, 98 points, 0) and Brewer (SJ, 26, 61 points, 0) are all free agents right now. No trade needed. With $55.69M profit, we can fund all four without touching the roster. The genuine trade targets — the ones still under contract — are Heatley or Kovalchuk at ATL, Avery at LA, and Havlat at OTT. For those, we need proposals the other side accepts.

**Upshall + St. Jacques for Heatley (ATL).** ATL at 84 points with 11 expiring deals must trade one of its two 130-point wingers. We target whichever they move. Upshall is 21 with POTE 99, CHKG 87, $1.20M expiring. St. Jacques is 24 with POTE 94, $0.80M, 2 years left, 1 game played. ATL gets two high-potential young players for a star they cannot re-sign. We get 131 points at 24 for $1.10M. Toronto nets $900K in savings; ATL adds $900K against a payroll shedding 14 contracts. The Coach flagged Upshall as audition-or-cut; trading while his POTE holds beats cutting him.

**Koltsov for Avery (LA).** Avery at 25 is the only player at FACE 93, CHKG 88, and TOUG 83 simultaneously at centre — the exact three grades the Coach has demanded since April 9. He costs $400K with 2 years left. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring are in full rebuild and cannot use a 9-point checking centre. Koltsov brings ACCE 96, POTE 94, and $1.10M with 2 years, the speed and ceiling a rebuild hoards. We save $700K. The cost is one internal bridge player, but Koltsov is in no unit and Gaborik at 99 points is the primary bridge.

**Colaiacovo + 4th for Havlat (OTT).** Havlat at 24 produced 103 points in 82 games at $900K. OTT at 77 points with 11 expiring face the same retention squeeze ATL does. The Coach called Colaiacovo a development write-off on May 15: 0.39 points per game across 31 games at 17.9 minutes a night when dressed. By the Coach's own words, he is a trade piece, not a prospect. Ottawa gets POTE 99 at 22 plus a 4th-rounder for a winger they will not re-sign. We save $200K. POTE 99 against 103 points is the hardest ask of the three, and acceptance is the least certain.

**What if none land.** The UFA route solves the scoring bridge without any trade at all. **Iginla** at 94 overall, 128 points, 87 TOUG and POTE 80 is the single signing that closes the 426-point veteran void and the toughness ceiling in one body. Offer him a 5-6 year deal at $7-8M; CGY at 70 points with $14.38M profit cannot match. **Gagne** at 108 points for $2.40M is the cheapest 100-point forward available; PHI at $66.73M payroll with $2.12M profit must shed salary. **Brewer** at 87, 93 CHKG, 82 TOUG and 61 points in 82 games at $2.00M replaces Roberts on the blueline as a free agent. The internal toughness fix is already on the sheet: **Abid** at 94 TOUG, 66 points, $400K just needs the 16+ MPG the Coach ordered. The one gap UFAs leave is faceoffs, and Avery stays the July target regardless.

**Tucker** at 30, $1.30M, 1 game played, POTE 79 carries no value to a rebuilding club. His CHKG 92 and TOUG 88 matter to a contender at next season's deadline. Hold him as salary relief until then.

**On the Luongo/DiPietro monitoring task (#2, requested 2005-01-19, wanted by 2005-02-20):** Luongo is on our roster at 91 base with 2 years left. The GM closed the goalie topic entirely on March 19 ("Goalies are solved. Done."). DiPietro tracking is moot. This task is complete and no further action is needed.

## Owed

**Luongo availability and DiPietro monitoring for the goalie trade window** (asked 2005-01-19, wanted by 2005-02-20):

This task is closed. Luongo arrived at Toronto in January and the GM explicitly shut all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19 with "Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks. Only trading chips left are Tucker and the 4th round pick." Nothing to report beyond that.

**Luongo** is on the roster at 94 OVR, $1.60M, 2 years remaining, 45 games played this season. The original goal — "a really good high-90s goalie from a team that will not be a contender" — is met. He satisfies it on the standing order from 2005-01-15.

**DiPietro** monitoring is moot. The NYI situation that made him a target no longer matters because the need is filled and the GM closed the window. There is no reason to reopen it.

The task is delivered: the answer is "done, Luongo is here, monitoring was closed by your own order three months ago."

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-31
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-31

Next game at DAL on Wednesday 01 June 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is who among the young players got the games they earned this season, and who was shortchanged. The regular season is done at 82 games, so this is a report card and a camp-planning exercise, not a tonight decision.

**Gaborik** is the elephant. 99 points in 82 games at 20.5 MPG is a 1.21 pace, and the sheet shows him scratched for tomorrow. That's not a development question, that's an availability question the matchup phase handles, but the year he had is the best by any young player on this roster.

**Alexeev** is the clearest mismatch. 0.55 pts/g over 55 games at 8.3 MPG. He outproduces Chistov (0.29) and Upshall (0.29) who dress regularly on the third and fourth lines. He's been scratched all season while two men producing half his rate get 13.1 and 7.9 minutes respectively. The season is over, but this is the offseason decision: either he gets a real roster spot at camp or we explain to him why 0.55 isn't enough when 0.29 is.

**Stahle** got 4 games all year. POTE 96 at 21, and when he played he got 17.8 MPG, so the coaching staff clearly thought he was ready for those four nights. Zero points in 4 games is a tiny sample. He's been wasted. Next camp he needs a genuine audition or the POTE 96 is pointless.

**Spezza** at POTE 99 got 46 games but only 6.7 MPG and 0.33 pts/g. His minutes collapsed from 9.1 to 4.8 per my March read. The season is a write-off. Same camp decision as Stahle: real minutes or stop dressing him and dress someone else.

**Colaiacovo** got 31 games at 17.9 MPG when dressed, which is real minutes, and 0.39 pts/g. POTE 99 at 22. He's been used as a call-up rather than a project. That's defensible if the plan is to keep him as a depth pairing, but if he's meant to be a top-four defenceman he needs consistent ice, not spot starts.

**Chlup** earned everything he got: 71 games, 16.9 MPG, 0.83 pts/g at 19 on the second line. No complaints. **Nash** at 69 games and 13.1 MPG on the second line produced 0.57 pts/g, which is the system-fit concern from March persisting through the full season. **Spacek** at 19 with 50 games and 7.6 MPG is a reasonable rookie volume for a fourth-liner.

**Klesla** played every game but is on my sell list for the offseason regardless. **Upshall** and **Chistov** both produced 0.29 pts/g on games they earned. Neither is developing above their ceiling.

## Development trends

The season is done or nearly done — this is the last read on who came forward and who fell back, and the offseason decisions start here.

**Chlup** is the one who came forward. 0.88 pts/g on 18.2 MPG at 19, up from 0.62 on 11.0 in December. His minutes more than doubled and his rate rose. Every other young player in this window either held or fell back; he is the only one who grew into a bigger load. He belongs on the first line. I have recommended that six times now and the lineup has not changed. I will say it one more time: assign him first-line centre before camp.

**Kaberle** went 0.54→0.62 pts/g while minutes rose from 19.4 to 21.5. At 27, both numbers moving up together is what a player in his prime looks like. The GM called him a star in January and the trend confirms it. No change needed, just noting he is still climbing.

**Chistov** doubled his minutes from 9.5 to 14.0 MPG and held his rate at 0.30. At 22, earning ice time without losing production is the quiet development we want. He has earned a bigger role next season.

**McCabe** finished at 0.48 pts/g across 82 games on 21.5 MPG. The season-end threshold I set in March was 0.60. He is well below it. The hot start that carried him back in early April (1.42 over 24 games) fully bled off. He goes back on the sell list. At 29 with 4 years and $3.00M, the return on a declining defenceman is worth more than keeping him.

**Koltsov** is a warning for the GM. He went 1.10→0.29 pts/g across this window. The GM wants him as a trading chip, and that is right, but 0.29 on 9.9 MPG is not a chip that moves for much. If we want a return we need to move him before next season's numbers make him undressable.

**Abid** got worse than my March note said. I flagged his minutes dropping from 20.1 to 12.6 while his rate held. The final window shows his rate fell too: 1.09→0.70 on 11.5 MPG. The mismatch is not just ice time; something about his role or health cost him production as well. System-fit review in the offseason alongside Nash, Richards and Afinogenov.

**Gaborik** at 23 finished 1.42→1.12 on minutes rising from 18.8 to 21.2. The rate decline is real but 1.12 on rising ice is still elite. No concern.

**Sundin, Mogilny, Roberts** all show the expected age decline: Sundin 1.46→0.97 at 34, Mogilny 1.62→0.83 at 36, Roberts 1.29→0.86 at 39. All three carry heavy minutes (21+ MPG). Planning for their decline next season starts now — who replaces their production is the offseason question.

No player card grades moved in this window.

## Morale watch

The room is right. Every dressed player reads 100 on morale, the ceiling, and there is nothing a line change can improve there.

**Spezza** sits at 88, the only man below the 90 threshold, but he is trending up three points since the last save and is scratched for this game anyway. At 6.7 MPG in 46 games his rate has already collapsed to 0.32 and my March note called the season a write-off for him. Next camp is where his minutes get fixed, not a playoff night.

**Abid** at 13.8 MPG and 0.84 pts/g has carried a minutes-to-production mismatch since March, but his morale is 100 and climbing. No action needed before Dallas.

No changes on morale grounds.

## Role composition

The question is whether our units are built right and whether the roster can fill every role. Most units are fine; one arrangement problem and one structural gap need the GM's attention before Wednesday at Dallas.

**Gaborik** is our best player by every measure on the sheet — 98 scoring, 99 playmaking, 99 speed, 99 clutch — and he is scratched. The Jan 15 principle holds: against a quality opponent, maximize quality. Dallas is 42-24. This is not a night to give a kid experience by sitting your highest-rated skater. If the GM dresses him, Gaborik slots into L2 or L3 at left wing, displacing whoever is the weakest winger on that unit. The cost is a young player's reps for one game; the gain is 98/99 at both ends against a top opponent.

**L4 faceoffs** are the arrangement problem within the lines as built. Mean 52, best 55. No forward on the roster outside L1-L3 wins a draw above 75. This is not fixable by shuffling Spacek, Abid, and Upshall around; none of them is a faceoff centre. Against Dallas, if their fourth-line centre wins draws comfortably, our bottom unit spends the shift in our own zone. The smaller intervention is to keep L4's shifts short and avoid putting them out on draws against strong centres. The real fix is a roster move: a middle-six centre who wins faceoffs and plays 12-14 minutes.

**K2 (Chlup, Tucker, McCabe, Jackman)** is the strongest checking unit on the sheet at 84 mean, with Jackman at 90, McCabe at 85, and Tucker in his designated checking role. This is correctly built. Chlup at 19 developing his PK game alongside those three is the right assignment.

**L3 (Richards, Eminger, Tucker, Klesla, Chistov)** is sound. Richards takes the draws at 75, Tucker provides the check, Chistov brings 98 speed on a third line. Eminger at 21 is developing at this level. No change.

**P1 and P2** are correctly split: P1 has Sundin (93), Roberts (88), and Afinogenov (92) shooting; P2 gets Mogilny (94 scoring, 91 playmaking) as the featured shooter. Speed is balanced between them (89 and 91). No change to either unit.

**The fourth-line checking finding from April** needs a note: L4 checking mean now reads 74 with best at 87 (Spacek is carrying it), up from the 62 I noted in April. The gap has partially closed through Spacek's line assignment, but the faceoff weakness at 52/55 remains the same structural problem.

## Opponent matchup

This is the last game of the Dallas season series, and the question is whether our current alignment handles them or needs an adjustment. It does not. Every pairing falls the right way.

**The auto-pairing works perfectly here.** Our first line (Roberts/Sundin/Mogilny) faces their first D pair (Boucher 75 / Zubov 83), which is their best defensive unit. Our first D pair (Fischer 85 / Jackman 86) faces Modano's line. That is exactly the matchup we want: Fischer CHKG 92, SPEE 94 and Jackman CHKG 92, SPEE 94 are the two men who can handle Modano's PUCK 94, DEKG 94, SPEE 92. No rearranging needed.

**Their second and third D pairs are soft, and our L2 and L3 already get them.** Matvichuk 73 / Berenzweig 68 is their pair two; Descoteaux 65 / Richards D 65 is pair three. Nash 83, Chlup 86, and Afinogenov 86 will be getting ice against a 68-OVR defenceman. Same story on our third line against 65 and 65. These are matchups we do not need to manufacture; they exist already because of the slot order.

**Modano is the only real threat.** OVR 88 with two wingers above 84 (Morrow 84, Guerin 87). That line is dangerous. Our D1 is built for exactly this, and the auto-pairing delivers it. Their second line (Arnott 85 with Malhotra 73 and DiMaio 73) gets our pair two (Kaberle 84 / McCabe 84) which is fair. Their bottom six features Messier at 44, Gilmour at 41, Kapanen 72. Our fourth line handles them.

**Their power play is 32-for-297, 10.8%.** That is not a unit that requires special attention from our PK. No changes to kill assignments.

**Turco in net (OVR 94, ENDU 94).** He is the same goalie we beat for 20 goals in 7 games this season. No adjustment needed for a good goalie beyond what our top six already does.

**Luongo starts.** His OVR is 94, morale 100. Per the GM's standing order from January 19, check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming.

## Owed

**Defenceman analysis for end-of-season decisions — delivery #11, season final numbers.**

The season is complete. This is the last read before the offseason window opens, and I'll keep it short because nothing has moved since May 2.

**McCabe** at 0.76 pts/g over 82 games (18G, 44A). His recent window at 0.48 is now the full back half of the season. Sell. The hot start was the anomaly, not the player.

**Jackman** at 0.46 pts/g on 29.6 MPG across 80 games (down from 0.48 on 73 GP in March). Still the cheapest top-pair minutes in the league at $0.70M x 3. Trade bait, not a keeper at this rate.

**Klesla** at 0.37 pts/g on 14.8 MPG across 82 games. Two consecutive declining seasons confirmed. Sell at $0.90M x 2.

**Eminger** at 0.36 pts/g on 15.5 MPG across 64 games. Slightly lower than my 0.38 from March. Expiring. Must move before July or he's gone for nothing.

**Kaberle** (0.59 pts/g, 84 OVR) and **Fischer** (0.53 pts/g, 85 OVR) are keepers per your standing orders.

Nothing has changed since May 2. The sell list is McCabe, Jackman, Klesla, Eminger. The keepers are Kaberle, Fischer.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-29

# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-29

Toronto 59-13-5, 133 pts after 82 games.

## Role coverage

**The question this phase answers: after this season's roster rolls off, what is actually missing versus what the coach can solve by deploying players he already has — and at what point does age turn a covered role into a gap you'll regret not filling in July?**

**Mogilny, Sundin, Roberts** carry 426 combined points and are 36, 34, and 39. The scoring and clutch roles read adequate today (10 at 80+ in scoring, 9 in clutch) but three of the top six in each are 34 or older. This is a one-year problem, not a today problem. The bridge below them — Gaborik 92 scoring at 23, Afinogenov 90 at 25, Abid 86 at 25 — is real talent but none has yet shown a scoring rate that replaces 90+ points. The gap is structural.

**Toughness** is missing outright. Zero players at 80+. Jackman tops the list at 75, Roberts at 73. The coach's L4 checking mean of 61 and toughness mean of 57 confirm the bottom six get pushed off the puck by any competent forward. No internal deployment fixes this. Bell (88 TOUG, 86 CHKG) or Iginla (85 TOUG) are the only league-wide players who close it.

**Faceoffs** are missing below L1-L2. Sundin at 90 is the only player at 80+. The L4 mean sits at 52, and Tucker (67) isn't even on the fourth line per the coach. Bell (82 FACE) or Avery (93 FACE) are the only players who fix both toughness and faceoffs simultaneously. No one in this building can be moved to a faceoff role and reach 80.

**Checking** is thin at 6 players above 80, and Roberts (39) is the senior one. Jackman 87 at 24, McCabe 86 at 29, Fischer 82 at 24 are the core that stays. With Iginla or Bell on a line, the need for a seventh checker drops because the physical presence shifts from special-teams checking to general play.

**Speed** is the one role with genuine surplus: 21 players at 80+. **Koltsov** (92 speed, 24) and **Gaborik** (98 speed, 23) are both "not lined." If the coach deploys them, speed depth covers a trade of Fischer or another depth forward without creating a new hole. That matters for package construction.

**Goalies** are solved per the GM's March 19 order: Luongo (26, 92 overall) and Belfour (40, 92 overall) for the playoffs, Ouellet (23, 2y left) as depth. After Belfour expires, Luongo plus Ouellet is the pair. Ouellet's ENDU 60 and INTE 69 are thin but he is 23 with two years of development.

**Iginla is the single acquisition that closes three gaps at once**: the scoring void (93 base, 140 points in 73 GP), the toughness ceiling (85 TOUG), and the scoring bridge (27 years old, seven prime seasons ahead). No other target in the brief hits all three. Bell closes two gaps (toughness and faceoffs) but does not touch the scoring void. Stuart replaces Roberts' minutes but does not add a forward-grade scorer.

## Trajectory

Can this roster sustain itself through the next three seasons without a cliff, and does the money get in the way?

**The age shape is not a problem; the contract calendar is.** Toronto has 13 players at 23 or under, 12 at 24-29, one at 30-33 (Tucker, 3 GP, 1 point), and four at 34+ (Sundin 34, Mogilny 36, Roberts 39, Belfour 40). The thin 30-33 band fills naturally in three years when the current mid-20s block ages into it: McCabe becomes 32, Kaberle 30, Luongo 29, Abid 28, Richards 28. The bridge exists. The cliff is not age, it is the **13 contracts worth $21.30M expiring this July**, and if those players don't get extension offers the summer after, they test the market and leave.

**The money is not the constraint.** Payroll sits at $60.04M against $125.89M revenue and $53.43M profit. Even if every expiring player doubled their salary — Gaborik from $1.10M to $5.00M, Richards from $1.00M to $4.00M, Nash to $3.50M — payroll lands around $72-75M and profit remains above $45M. The question is never "can we afford them" — it is "will the game let us lock them before someone else's offer moves them."

**Belfour ($6.50M, 40) and Roberts ($2.70M, 39) walk in July, saving $9.20M.** That's clean. Luongo (26, 91 base, 2 years left) is the starter, Ouellet (23, POTE 97, 2 years) is the backup. The goalie group is covered at low cost. The GM already closed this decision in March.

**Gaborik is the renewal that defines the next five years.** At 99 points on $1.10M, he is the cheapest elite player in the league. His POTE of 90 is a likelihood, not a ceiling, and at 23 he has 13 seasons ahead. Offer 5-6 years. If he leaves, the 256-point combined production of Mogilny (84), Sundin (91) and Roberts (81) — which becomes 175 points after Roberts walks and Mogilny ages out in 2006-07 — has no replacement.

**Sundin's contract is the largest long-term commitment: $8.40M for 5 more years, running to age 39.** He produced 91 points at 34, so it is not bad money today. But at $8.40M for a 37- and 38-year-old, it crowds the books without return. There is no action to take now — no mid-contract renegotiation is possible — but the GM should know this is the one salary that cannot be moved or adjusted until it expires.

**Fischer is a slow-bleed liability.** $3.70M, age 24, 41 points in 77 games (0.53 pts/g, down from earlier seasons), 4 years left. That is $14.80M of above-market salary on a declining blueliner. Not tradeable at this price with these numbers, and no reason to move him this summer. File under summer 2007 or 2008 when his value might be slightly better on a bounce-back or when we are clearly out of contention.

**Draft capital is nearly zero.** One fourth-rounder from Toronto. Every package this summer must be funded with players. That makes the Iginla target (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, 140 pts, $6.50M expiring) achievable only if CGY accepts a roster-player return. The Coach's system-fit review of Afinogenov, Richards, and Nash may free one of them as a trade piece — but Richards (66 pts, $1.00M) and Nash (39 pts, age 20) are exactly the players we are trying to extend, and Afinogenov at $4.50M with 4 years left is expensive to move.

**The three moves that protect the next three seasons:**

1. **Lock Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger, and Kaberle on 5-6 year deals this July.** These five are 20-27 and carry POTE of 90-99. If two or more walk, the core that replaced the veterans is gone and we restart. The payroll supports it.

2. **Close the Iginla trade using a player package from the Coach's system-fit casualties.** He closes the scoring bridge and the toughness ceiling simultaneously. Without picks, we need CGY to want a specific Toronto player. This requires knowing what CGY values, which means proposing and negotiating in July, not waiting.

3. **Let Mogilny ride out his two years and accept the 2006-07 production drop.** He is 36 at 84 points, signed through 38 at $5.50M. No trade is realistic. The plan absorbs his decline while Iginla and Gaborik carry the top two lines and Chlup (19, 59 points, POTE 95) closes the gap by 2007-08.

On the overdue task: **the Luongo and DiPietro monitoring from January is complete and closed.** Luongo arrived on the roster in February (91 base, 2 years left) and the GM closed all goalie monitoring on March 19. No further action is needed on that item.

## Calendar

The deadline is 71 days behind us and the season is two games from done; the summer plan is the only calendar that matters now, and it has thirteen names on it.

**Gaborik** is the single most important decision before July. He is 23, POTE 90, on $1.10M expiring, and the January "lock him now" advice was correct in direction even if mid-contract renegotiation was impossible then. Now the contract is actually expiring and re-signing is the mechanism. Five or six years. If he walks, the scoring bridge void I flagged in May becomes a chasm, because no other player under 30 on this roster carries his combination of speed and shooting.

**Eminger** follows immediately. He is 21, POTE 99, $1.20M expiring, and the GM specifically protected him from trade in February. Five or six years. He and Gaborik are the two young players whose ceilings are highest and whose deals expire simultaneously, which means the renewal window opens together.

**Kaberle** at 27 and $1.90M is in his prime and needs a 3-4 year commitment at a modest raise. He is not a franchise blueliner but at 27 he is not a project either; he is the second-pairing defenseman a contender wants, and re-signing him cheaply is the kind of work that wins depth cups.

**Richards** at 25, $1.00M, 70 FACE, 85 PASS sits behind the system-fit review the Coach flagged. If camp says he stays in the top nine, renew him 3-4 years. If camp says he is a third-liner at best, he is still worth a cheap 2-year lock at $1.00M because a 25-year-old center with those numbers costs more on the open market.

**Abid** at 25, $0.40M, TOUG 80, CHKG 80 is the cheapest toughness on the roster and the Coach wants him at 16+ MPG. Renew him 2 years. He does not solve the L4 faceoff gap (his FACE is low), but at $0.40M he is the checking half of the formula the Coach keeps asking for.

**Tellqvist** at 25, $0.80M, POTE high-90s is protected by GM standing order. Renew 2-3 years and let him develop behind Luongo.

**Belfour** at 40 and $6.50M is the hardest one. Luongo is on the roster now at 94 displayed (91 base), $1.60M, 2 years left. The GM said "Belfour stays if he wants to stay at reduced salary." At 40 with a $6.50M contract expiring, he is unlikely to accept a significant cut. My read: offer him 1 year at whatever reduced number the game will let us propose, and if he walks, the goalie situation is Luongo plus Tellqvist plus a cheap third, which is fine for a contender. The $6.50M saved is better spent on Iginla or Roberts' replacement.

**Roberts** at 39 and $2.70M is a 2-year veteran at the tail of his career. Let him go. The Stuart target (SJ, D, 25, 87 base, POTE 91) was the planned replacement, but he is not expiring, so this is a trade target for summer rather than a UFA signing.

**Chistov, Colaiacovo, Upshall, Alexeev** all carry expiring deals and all sit in the Coach's "audition or stop dressing" group. None should be renewed before camp. If they perform, offer a 1-2 year deal; if not, let them walk for nothing rather than commit money to a player the Coach will not play. Chistov is the exception worth a trade conversation: at 22, POTE 95, SPEE 89, ACCE 88, he has value to a club that will play him, and the Coach has explicitly named him tradeable.

**Acquisition side:** the Iginla target (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, $6.50M expiring) is the only move that closes the scoring bridge without requiring Chlup or Nash to jump 0.20+ pts/g. He becomes a UFA in July. If the game lets us sign him outright, do it. The Bell target (CHI, LW, 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 82 FACE) closes the L4 faceoff gap the Coach has quantified at a mean of 52. If Bell also hits the UFA market, take him; he fills the one structural hole no internal player can.

**The draft** is June 8 and we own only a 5th rounder (confirmed). Auto-draft it and move on. No package there.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: who across the league closes the three structural gaps (toughness zero at 80+, faceoffs only Sundin at 90, no scorer under 30 who can absorb Mogilny-Sundin-Roberts' 426 points) and would his club say yes to a trade with a team holding one 4th-round pick.

**Iginla** remains the single acquisition that hits all three gaps. 93 base, 85 TOUG, 79 CHKG, 128 points in 76 games at 21.9 MPG, age 27, $6.50M expiring. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and only $14.43M profit cannot retain him. He's the same target from April, confirmed again here. The package problem is unchanged: no picks means CGY needs a Toronto player they value. Nash (20, POTE 96, 90 TOUG, $1.20M, 1 year) is exactly the profile a 70-point rebuilding club covets, and the Coach's system-fit review may free him.

**Bell (CHI, LW):** 80 base, 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 82, age 24, $900M with 2 years left, 28 points in 80 games. He is the only player in the league closing toughness, checking, and faceoffs simultaneously on a contract we can keep. CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring and $31.73M profit are profitable and rebuilding, which means they can afford to keep him. The 2 years left cuts both ways: he's not a rental they must move, but if CHI decide they don't want him, they'll listen. His 28 points in 80 games is thin; he's a deployment player, not a scorer. Still, 95 TOUG and 82 FACE are unreplaceable here.

**Kovalchuk (ATL, LW):** 89 base, POTE 84, age 22, $1.10M expiring, 138 points in 79 games. **Heatley (ATL, RW):** 91 base, POTE 84, age 24, $1.10M expiring, 131 points in 79 games. ATL at 84 points (31-37-6) with 11 expiring contracts cannot re-sign both. One walks in July. If ATL make the playoffs they keep both; if they miss, one becomes available. Kovalchuk is younger by two years and carries 7 more points. Heatley carries 2 points of base overall. Neither closes toughness or faceoffs, but either one at $1.10M on a player producing 130+ points is the cheapest scoring in the league.

**Komisarek (MTL, D):** 77 base, 85 TOUG, 92 CHKG, POTE 92, age 23, $1.10M expiring, 82 points in 82 games. MTL at 66 points with 15 expiring and $21.59M profit are the league's worst team and the most motivated sellers. He closes the toughness gap at defense (Roberts' replacement), brings 85 TOUG and 92 CHKG which Toronto has zero of at 80+ on the blue line, and at POTE 92 with two years of development left, he has the highest potential ceiling of any available defender. His 82 points as a D is production that shouldn't sit at 77 base, which suggests the grades are conservative or he's playing above his sheet.

**Cammalleri (LA, LW):** 22 years old, POTE 98, $1.10M expiring, 60 points in 61 games. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring and $16.34M profit. He does not close toughness or faceoffs, but at POTE 98 he is the highest-ceiling forward on the market after Iginla. If LA cannot retain both him and Frolov, he tests the market in July.

**Sulku (CGY, LW):** 75 base, 84 TOUG, 82 CHKG, POTE 90, age 21, $943K expiring, 5 points in 40 games. If we're already negotiating with CGY for Iginla, Sulku could be a request in the same conversation, or a player CGY wants as a return (young, tough, potential). His 5 points in 40 games say he's not ready for top-nine minutes, but 84 TOUG at 21 with POTE 90 is the same profile Nash would have been.

**Avery (LA, C):** 79 base, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, POTE 71, age 25, $400K, 2 years left, 9 points in 82 games. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring. He closes toughness at a bargain price, but POTE 71 means he will never be more than this, and 9 points in 82 games is replacement-level. Only worth a look if the Bell trade fails and the GM needs a cheap body to fill L4 checking.

**Thornton (BOS, C):** 94 base, 80 TOUG, 81 CHKG, POTE 74, age 25, $4.00M expiring, 83 points in 59 games. BOS at 97 points are a playoff team. They will not sell. His prior note flagged a 76 vs 94 discrepancy; the POTE of 74 alongside 59 games played (injury-shortened) suggests the 94 may be a hot-reading artifact. Even so, BOS has no reason to deal a 25-year-old centre at 94.

## Trade construction

**The question this phase answers: what packages can we construct that close the scoring void, the toughness ceiling, and the faceoff gap without gutting the young core the rebuild depends on.**

**Iginla from Calgary** is the trade. He closes three gaps in one move: 128 points in 76 games replaces Mogilny-Sundin-Roberts' 426-point combined production, 85 TOUG raises our forward-level toughness from zero at 80+, and at 27 he gives seven prime seasons ahead of the aging curve. The package: Nash, Tucker and the 4th-rounder. CGY save $4.00M on Iginla's expiring $6.50M deal. Our payroll goes from $60.04M to $64.04M, well inside $53.43M profit.

**Nash** is the concession. 20 years old, POTE 95, TOUG 88, $1.20M with one year left, 39 points in 69 games. That's 0.57 points per game from a player with the ceiling of a franchise wing. The Coach has him in the system-fit review alongside Afinogenov and Richards, all three collapsed their scoring rate on flat minutes. If the GM cannot accept trading Nash, there is no Iginla package we can build. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit want exactly this profile for their rebuild.

**Bell from Chicago** is the second deal and it doesn't interfere with the first. Give Chistov (22, POTE 95, SPEE 89, ACCE 88, expiring, 20 points in 68 games) and Upshall (21, POTE 99, CHKG 87, expiring, 20 points in 68 games). The Coach named Upshall in the camp-audition-or-cut group and Chistov as explicitly tradeable. Bell at 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 82 FACE, 80 base, $900K with two years left is the only player in the league solving toughness and faceoffs simultaneously. CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring and $31.73M profit absorb the +$1.40M easily and gain two POTE 95+ speed prospects. Bell's 28 points in 80 games and ENDU 71 make him replaceable through their rebuild.

**Koltsov for Avery from LA** is the third option and I'd rank it last. Koltsov (24, POTE 94, ACCE 96, 19 points in 38 games, $1.10M, 2 years) goes to LA at 79 points with 14 expiring, who gain a speed prospect with two years of control. Avery (25, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, $400K, POTE 71, 9 points in 82 games) arrives as a deployed L4 body. We save $700K and solve the fourth-line checking gap for one season. But trading POTE 94 upside for POTE 71 certainty goes against the draft-and-develop philosophy. Only if both larger deals fail and the L4 gap is still open.

**If none land, July UFA is the fallback.** Cammalleri (LA, 22, POTE 98, 60 points in 61 games, $1.10M expiring) or whichever of Kovalchuk and Heatley that ATL cannot retain. Neither closes toughness or faceoffs, but 130-point scoring at $1.10M is the cheapest offense available and our profit supports outbidding smaller clubs. For the L4 specifically, Avery at $400K could be signed directly if he clears.

## Owed

**Owed item #2 — "Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window" (GM asked 2005-01-19, wanted by 2005-02-20):**

**Complete.** Luongo is on our roster: 94 overall, 26 years old, $1.60M, 2 years remaining, 45 games played this season. The GM closed all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19 with the standing order to keep Belfour and Luongo as two 90+ goalies. DiPietro is irrelevant — we acquired the better target.

Nothing has changed since the March closure because the question is answered. The task existed to find a number-one goalie; Luongo is that goalie. No further reporting is needed on this item.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-29
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-29

Next game vs DAL on Monday 30 May 2005.

## Development opportunity

The regular season is done and this is the last look at what these young players earned before offseason decisions are made. The short version: Chlup and Gaborik out-earned their roles, Eminger and Klesla got more than they produced, and three players with 99 potential barely got a look.

**Gaborik** finished with 99 points in 82 games on 20.5 MPG. He is the best player on the roster by a wide margin and he earned every shift. The SCRATCHED status on the current lineup is a post-season roster flag, not a production issue. Nothing to correct.

**Chlup** at 59 points in 71 games (0.83 pts/g) on 16.9 MPG at 19 is the best season by a Leaf this year after Gaborik. He sat on the second line all season while I recommended first-line centre at least six times. The GM did not move him. That decision is now locked for the regular season; for camp and next year, he goes to first-line centre on day one. No further argument needed.

**Nash** at 39 points in 69 games (0.57 pts/g) on 13.1 MPG is reasonable usage for a 20-year-old on the second line. His rate halved mid-season but he stayed on the sheet. He earned his spot.

**Chistov** at 20 points in 68 games (0.29 pts/g) on 13.1 MPG is a third-liner producing third-line numbers. No complaint about his usage.

**Spacek** at 17 points in 50 games (0.34 pts/g) on 7.6 MPG as a 19-year-old rookie is fair. He earned his minutes and no more.

**Upshall** at 20 points in 68 games (0.29 pts/g) saw his minutes collapse from 13.4 to 7.9 late. That was the right call on the numbers: he was not producing at the higher load. His future is a camp audition or nothing.

**Alexeev** at 30 points in 55 games (0.55 pts/g) on 8.3 MPG outscored both Chistov (0.29) and Upshall (0.29) yet played fewer games than both. The mismatch was never resolved. Next year he gets a legitimate camp shot at a top-nine spot or we stop carrying him.

**Spezza** got 46 games and 6.7 MPG despite the highest scouting number on the roster (99). His 0.33 pts/g does not justify more, but the late-season scratch meant he never got a sustained stretch to prove himself. Offseason: real camp competition, no handouts.

**Colaiacovo** played 31 games at 17.9 MPG and scored at 0.39 pts/g. When he was given top-pair minutes he held up offensively. He was the right injury-cover call all season. Whether he stays depends on what we do at the blue line this summer.

**Stahle** played 4 games and scored nothing. He got no real look. At 21 with a high scouting number that is a wasted year, but the blue-line depth meant there was no room. Same offseason question as Spezza: camp or nothing.

**Eminger** at 23 points in 64 games (0.36 pts/g) is the opposite problem: he played more than he produced. His contract expires. The trade deadline is gone, so he leaves as a UFA in July. That was the wrong outcome but the window is closed.

**Klesla** at 30 points in 82 games (0.37 pts/g) is a second straight declining season. He played every game and was the lowest-output defenceman in the regular rotation. He does not belong in a top-four role next year at this rate.

**Ouellet** backed up for 13 games and did nothing wrong. Not a development issue.

## Development trends

The season is 80 games in and the trends are locked: who's climbing, who's flatlined, who's falling. This is the offseason planning brief the GM needs before free agency and camp.

**Chlup** is the one who got better. 0.62 to 0.88 pts/g while minutes doubled from 11.0 to 18.2 at 19 years old. More ice, higher rate. Every young player who takes on a bigger load and keeps his production climbing is a franchise player. He owns the first line next season.

**Kaberle** is the veteran getting better. 0.54 to 0.62 pts/g on 19.4 to 21.5 MPG. More minutes, more points per minute. At 27 he's entering his prime and the GM is right that he's a star.

**Abid** is the biggest unresolved problem. His rate held around 0.70 from the December window to the final total, but his minutes dropped from 20.1 to 11.5 MPG. A 0.70 winger on 82 games getting 11 minutes means the lineup is wasting him. He deserves 16+ next season or we're leaving goals on the table.

**Afinogenov and Richards** are the system-fit crisis. Both collapsed on flat minutes: Afinogenov 1.17 to 0.73 on 16.8 to 16.6 MPG; Richards 1.08 to 0.71 on 16.9 to 15.8 MPG. No injuries, no minutes cut, no role change. Something about how I'm using them doesn't fit. This is a coaching review for the offseason before I pencil either into a top-six role for next year.

**Nash** at 20 is the same story: 0.83 to 0.42 on flat 13 MPG. Three players, same pattern, flat minutes, halved rate. I owe the GM a system answer.

**Spacek** is dead. 0.55 to 0.28 pts/g, 16.0 to 5.2 MPG. The March target of 10 MPG was unreachable and he never got close. Camp audition next year or stop dressing him. **Spezza** same: 0.43 to 0.24, 9.1 to 4.6 MPG. Buried all season. **Upshall** same: 0.33 to 0.27, 13.4 to 4.8. All three at 19-21 with zero trajectory.

**Koltsov** went 1.10 to 0.29 on 10 to 38 GP. His early window was a 10-game hot streak; the remaining 28 games at 0.07 pts/g confirm he cannot play in this league. He's a chip per the GM's standing order, not a player.

**Klesla** at 0.50 to 0.31 on flat 15 MPG is the second consecutive season declining. **Jackman** at 0.65 to 0.39 on 30 MPG is confirmed burnout. **McCabe** at 1.42 to 0.48 is fully bled off from the hot start. All three are sell candidates.

**Sundin** at 34 went 1.46 to 0.97 on minutes up from 16.9 to 21.7. He's carrying a heavier load and still producing at 0.97. That's good for a 34-year-old but the direction is down and the plan for next year needs to think about reducing his minutes. **Mogilny** (36, 0.83) and **Roberts** (39, 0.86) are the same: still productive, clearly aging, one year left at most.

**Fischer** at 0.63 to 0.50 on 20.8 to 22.9 MPG is carrying more load with a slight rate dip. Normal for a workhorse D. Keeper per GM's standing order.

## Morale watch

The room is in good shape with two games left; no one's morale needs a line move to protect.

**Spezza** is the only man below 92 at 88, and he's climbing (+3). He's scratched at 46 games and 6.7 MPG, well under the 10 MPG a 70-79 calibre forward expects. The issue is structural: he's a healthy scratch for development rotation, and the GM's maximize-quality order against Dallas tonight (42-24) means the current lineup that keeps him out is the right one. Nothing I do with ice time before tonight changes his reading, and forcing him in against a quality opponent violates the standing order. His 88 with +3 momentum means he recovers on his own over the final two games.

**Alexeev** (92, +5) and **Upshall** (94, +3) are both rising sharply. At 8.3 and 7.9 MPG respectively, they're both near their band targets and climbing fast. No action needed.

**Spacek** at 94 on 7.6 MPG is exactly where a fourth-line centre his age should be. **Safronov** at 95 with 3 games played is fine as a depth call-up. The entire dressing room above the top line is at 100.

No change to any line or unit for morale reasons. The room is right.

## Role composition

The fourth-line faceoff problem is the one structural flaw in these units that no reshuffle fixes, and against a 42-win Dallas team it gets exploited all night.

**L1 (Sundin, Roberts, Mogilny, Jackman, Fischer)** is the best unit we ice. Checking mean 79, scoring 88/95, speed 91/95, two elite D-pairs in Jackman (90 checking) and Fischer (85). Sundin's 91 faceoffs anchor the draw. No change.

**L2 (Chlup, McCabe, Kaberle, Nash, Afinogenov)** works as a second scoring line. Chlup at 80 faceoffs provides the draw, scoring 85/98 is plenty for a second unit. Kaberle and McCabe cover the blue line. Fine as is.

**L3 (Eminger, Tucker, Richards, Klesla, Chistov)** has a mean checking of 75 and mean toughness of 66, which is thin for a line expected to match the opponent's second or third unit. Tucker is the only true checker (94 displayed) and Richards at 97 clutch and 87 stamina is a two-way asset spending time on a checking identity. The line is what it is though, and Tucker carries it. I would not break it; giving it shorter, sharper shifts is the smaller tool.

**L4 (Spaček, Abid, Upshall)** is the problem. Faceoff mean 52, best 55. Nobody on this line wins a draw. Abid at 72 toughness and 87 checking is the only identity player. Against a competent Dallas third centre, we lose every puck drop and spend the shift chasing. This is the same roster gap I flagged in April: no forward outside L1-L2 checks above 80, and now confirmed, no forward outside L1-L2 wins a faceoff above 80 either. It is a roster problem, not a lines problem.

**K1 (Sundin, Roberts, Kaberle, Fischer)** runs the top line's core on the penalty kill. Checking mean 79 is adequate because Fischer (92 best) and Roberts carry it, clutch 86/95 is the best on the roster. But this is the same four players driving L1 and P1, which is a minutes pile-up risk late in a playoff push.

**K2 (Chlup, Tucker, McCabe, Jackman)** is the proper checking kill at 84 mean checking, the highest of any unit. Well-built, no issues.

**P1 and P2** are both loaded. P1 has Sundin and Kaberle with four shooters; P2 has Mogilny (94 scoring) and Chlup with Richards at 97 clutch. No structural flaw. The depth here is a luxury.

**Gaborik and Koltsov are scratched.** If that is a development rotation, it is the GM's call. If this is a maximize-quality night against Dallas, Gaborik at 98 scoring and 99 in three other categories is the single biggest talent not on the ice.

## Opponent matchup

Can we beat Dallas with the lineup we already have? Yes, and changing it would hurt us.

**Their threat is one line.** Modano (88), Guerin (87), Morrow (84) is a first line by any measure. Behind them, Arnott at 85 with Malhotra (73) and DiMaio (73) on the wings is a stretch assignment even for a top two, and their third and fourth are bottom-six at best. We have four lines better than their bottom two pairs combined.

**Fischer and Jackman get Modano.** The auto-pairing sends their first line against our first defensive pair, and Fischer (92 CHKG, 94 SPEE) and Jackman (92 CHKG, 91 TOUG) are built for exactly this. Modano's speed (92 SPEE) matches theirs, but we have the edge in physicality and he is 34. No swap needed.

**Our young forwards feast.** The auto-pairing sends L2 (Chlup, Nash, Afinogenov) against Matvichuk (73) and Berenzweig (68), and L3 (Richards, Chistov, Tucker) against Descoteaux (65) and Richards D (65). These are the weakest defensemen in the matchup. Chlup at 86 and Richards at 87 are already the best players on their sides of the ice, and their opponents are not equipped to slow them.

**Faceoffs favor us.** Modano at 81 is their only center above 79, and Sundin starts on him at 91. Chlup at 80 matches Arnott at 79. The only line we lose the draw on is the fourth (Spacek 55 vs Gilmour 72), and that's a shift-eater line.

**Luongo starts at 94 against Turco at 94.** Even matchup between the pipes. Check the fatigue icon on screen before confirming; that standing order still holds.

**No change.** The lines are correct, the auto-pairing works in our favor, and we are 59-13-5 at home leading the series 4-1-1. There is no development-versus-maximize conflict because our best players are already the ones in the lineup.

## Owed

The season numbers are locked and the D-man sell list is now an offseason action item rather than a running assessment.

**McCabe** at 62 points in 82 games is 0.76 pts/g on 22.1 MPG. My May 2 reading was 0.76 and the recent window was 0.48. Nothing has moved — two more games just confirmed it. He stays on the sell list. 29 years old, $3.00M for four more years, and a 0.48 recent rate means his trade value is dropping every week we hold him.

**Jackman** finished at 37 points in 80 games, 0.46 pts/g on 29.6 MPG. Slightly down from my March reading of 0.48 on 73 games. The story is unchanged: his value is 30 minutes of top-pair ice for $0.70M. Another club extracts more from that than we do.

**Klesla** closed at 30 points in 82 games, 0.37 pts/g on 14.8 MPG. Identical to my March reading. Two consecutive declining seasons at ages 22 and 23. He is a sell. $0.90M x 2 years of dead weight.

**Eminger** finished at 23 points in 64 games, 0.36 pts/g on 15.5 MPG. Down slightly from 0.38 in March. The deadline passed and he's still here. This is the most urgent item on the list — 1 year left at $1.20M, and after July he is a free agent for nothing. We have two months to get something back.

**Fischer** at 41 points in 77 games, 0.53 pts/g on 22.4 MPG. GM's keeper. Core defenceman at 24 with 4 years of control. No change.

**Kaberle** at 44 points in 74 games, 0.60 pts/g on 20.8 MPG. The keeper question for this summer is whether we can re-sign him — he has 1 year left at $1.90M and becomes an unrestricted free agent. That is now the single most important D-man decision before July.



**Delivered: #1 — D-man season review and sell list.**

Nothing changed since May 2 on McCabe, Jackman, or Klesla — the season closed and confirmed what I had. The one item that shifted in urgency is Eminger: the March deadline passed, he's still on the roster, and his window to get us anything closes in July. That is the first call to make this offseason.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-27
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-27

Toronto 59-13-5, 133 pts after 82 games.

## Role coverage

The role sheet confirms what the coach has been saying since April: two holes are structural and cannot be plugged by reassigning anyone already on this roster.

**Toughness** sits at zero players above 80. The highest is Jackman at 75, then Roberts at 73 at age 39. There is no lineup change that manufactures an 80+ enforcer from a group whose top grade is 75. Bell (82 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, 24) or Avery (93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 25, $400K, 2 years) remain the only league-wide solutions. This is not new; the role sheet just reconfirms the floor.

**Faceoffs** are the same story. Sundin at 90 is the only 80+ draw-taker on 30 rostered players. The coach's L4 mean of 52 with best 55 is not a coaching failure; it is arithmetic. Tucker at 67 is the next best and he sits on no line. Same two targets close both gaps simultaneously.

**Checking** at 6 players above 80 is thin but workable. Jackman 87, McCabe 86, Tucker 83, Fischer 82, Upshall 80, and Roberts 86 at 39. Strip Roberts out and it is five. Strip Tucker (who carries POTE 79 and is being held as trade currency) and it is four. The coach could dress Tucker nightly as a band-aid, but the GM is holding him for a larger package.

**Scoring and playmaking** look deep on the sheet: 10 and 11 players at 80+ respectively. The problem is who they are. Mogilny 94 at 36, Sundin 92 at 34, Roberts 88 at 39. That is 426 combined points walking toward a cliff within two seasons. The next name on the scoring list is Abid at 86 (25), then Richards at 85 (25), neither of whom has shown a 0.50+ pts/g trajectory this year. The July Iginla acquisition remains the only fix that does not require Chlup or Nash to take a structural jump.

**Speed** is genuinely deep with 21 at 80+. Gaborik 98, Afinogenov 96, Koltsov 92, Fischer 89. This is a real asset that survives the aging curve.

**Goalies** are covered. Luongo 26 with 2 years, Belfour 40 on an expiring deal, Ouellet 23 with 2 years, Tellqvist 25 with 1 year. GM closed this file on March 19.

**Durability** is a quiet concern. Only 4 players at 80+ and the top one is Roberts at 98, who is 39. If injuries hit the defense in a playoff run, the next man up carries ENDU 75 or below.

## Trajectory

Does the July renewal cluster and the gap between the veterans and the young core leave this club's production exposed? Yes on both, and the fix concentrates in one summer.

**The renewal cluster.** Thirteen contracts at $21.30M expire this July. Five are the base: **Gaborik** (99 pts, 23, $1.10M), **Richards** (66 pts, 25, $1.00M), **Nash** (39 pts, 20, POTE 95), **Eminger** (23 pts, 21, POTE 99), and **Kaberle** (44 pts, 27, $1.90M). Together they carry 271 points, roughly a quarter of the roster's total, on $6.50M. These five need 5-6 year deals (Kaberle 3-4) before any acquisition is discussed. If two walk, the scoring base collapses.

**Gaborik** is the first name. 99 points in 82 games at 23, POTE 90, on the cheapest top-six salary on the roster. Five or six years. The alternative is losing 99 points to a July bidding war with no internal replacement.

**Richards** scored 66 points at 25 on $1.00M, POTE 88. Lock him second, 5-6 years, after Gaborik.

**Nash and Eminger** are the two deepest potential ratings on the roster, POTE 95 and 99, both under 22, both expiring at $1.20M. Nash at 39 points in 69 games is already a top-six winger. Eminger at 23 points in 64 games is raw but carries the highest POTE on the club. Neither should reach the open market without a 5-6 year deal.

**The age void.** The 30-33 bracket holds one player: **Tucker**, 30, 3 games, 1 point. **Sundin** (34, 91 pts), **Mogilny** (36, 84 pts), and **Roberts** (39, 81 pts) carry 256 points between them, and nothing under 30 on this roster replaces that volume. **Iginla** (CGY, RW, 27, 140 pts, $6.50M expiring) is the only player in the league closing both the RW gap and the 30-33 gap simultaneously. He is the July acquisition that makes the bridge hold.

**Money.** Payroll $60.04M, revenue $125.89M, profit $51.14M. No cap. Re-signing all five core players at market rates, adding Iginla at $6.50M, and releasing **Belfour** ($6.50M) and **Roberts** ($2.70M) nets roughly $1.40M in new payroll. The revenue absorbs that without difficulty. The $9.20M freed by those two departures is the first money available for the renewals.

**Sundin** is locked five years at $8.40M through 2009-10, when he'll be 39. This contract can't be adjusted. The GM should track the fact that it consumes a tenth of payroll through the entire development window of Chlup, Nash, Eminger and Spezza.

**Draft capital.** A single fourth-round pick from Toronto. No first, second or third-rounder exists. Every package must be player-funded. The Coach's flagged trade pieces — **Spezza** (POTE 99, 15 pts, 46 GP), **Chistov** (POTE 95, 20 pts, 68 GP), **Colaiacovo** (POTE 99, 12 pts, 31 GP) — are the real currency. The 4th-rounder is sweetener.

**The second cluster.** Nine contracts at $15.44M expire July 2006, including **Chlup** ($2.34M, 2 years, POTE 95), **Luongo** ($1.60M, 2 years, POTE 97), and **Klesla** ($0.90M, 2 years, POTE 97). These three are must-re-signs at the next window. Mogilny at $5.50M, age 38, should walk. The spread between 2005 and 2006 is workable. The danger is the concentration inside 2005 alone.

**Age shape at the bottom.** 13 players at 23 or under, with eight carrying POTE 95+ already in the lineup. The manual's target is six with potential and three-to-four playing every night. The base exceeds it. The problem is the bridge above 23 and below 34.

**Three protective moves.** Lock the five core renewals in July. Acquire Iginla to bridge the 256-point scoring cliff. Let Belfour and Roberts walk and redirect their $9.20M into the renewals.

Obligation note: the Luongo availability and DiPietro development monitoring task was closed by the GM's March 19 standing order to keep both Luongo and Belfour through the playoffs and shut down all goalie trade tasks. That obligation is delivered.

## Calendar

The deadline is 69 days behind us and we are first in the East at 133 points; the only date left is the summer, and the work is 13 expiring contracts worth $19.60M in combined salary.

**Gaborik** is the first signature. At 23, POTE 90, $1.10M with 67 points in 45 games (that was the Jan read; full-season production is higher given he played through), he is the cheapest high-ceiling asset on the roster. Five or six years, no hesitation.

**Kaberle** at 27, $1.90M is the blueline anchor. Five or six years. He will command more on the open market and we should pay it rather than lose him.

**Richards** at 25, $1.00M is a third-line centre with 70 FACE and 85 PASS who fills the gap the Coach keeps flagging. Five years. Cheap insurance.

**Eminger** at 21, POTE 99, $1.20M stays. The GM already vetoed trading him, and the Coach wants defined minutes. Five years.

**Nash** at 20, $1.20M gets a five-year deal despite the system-fit review. He is 20. The Coach's concern is about fit and confidence, not talent. Pay him the rookie-scale extension and fix the system around him.

**Tellqvist** at 25, $0.80M stays on two years per the GM's standing order. He is the future number one once Belfour walks.

**Belfour** at 40, $6.50M is the expensive question. The GM's position from 2005-01-15 was to offer reduced salary and accept if he walks. At 40 with a career-ending risk hanging, two years at a discounted figure (perhaps $4M range) is the best case. If he refuses, Luongo and Tellqvist are the plan.

**Roberts** at 39, $2.70M is the hardest call. He is one third of the 426-point old guard that has no succession plan. Two years max at a significant pay cut, or release him and spend the $2.70M on an acquisition. I lean release. His production supports it only if he is still playing top-four minutes, and the Coach's system-fit concerns suggest he is not.

**Chistov** at 22, POTE 95, $1.10M: the Coach has already named Alexeev as his replacement. He is tradeable, but the March 19 standing order says "everybody else we keep" except Tucker and the 4th. If that holds, he signs at $1.10M for two years as depth. If the GM lifts the order, he fetches a pick via the over-80 mechanic in a year or two. For now: renew, two years.

**Colaiacovo** at 22, POTE 99, $1.10M: the Coach called him a development write-off on 2005-05-15 after 31 games at 17.9 MPG and 0.39 pts/g. Renew at $1.10M for one year only as a camp audition. If he does not earn a role by November, he becomes the next Bell-package piece.

**Upshall** at 21, $1.20M and **Alexeev** at 23, $1.10M are both in the Coach's camp audition group. Renew both one year at current salary. Let camp decide who sticks.

**Abid** at 25, $0.40M, TOUG 80, CHKG 80 renews on one year. The cheapest toughness on the roster.

The priority summer acquisition remains **Iginla** (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, $6.50M expiring). He closes the scoring void left by Mogilny (36), Sundin (34), and Roberts (38) in one move, and he arrives at the same $6.50M we would pay Belfour to stay. The pick capital to reach him is gone (we hold no pick better than a 4th), so the package must be player-for-player, which means one of Tucker, Chistov, or Colaiacovo plus salary matching. The GM's March 19 order protects Chistov; I would revisit that once Iginla is confirmed available.

**Bell** (CHI, LW, 24, 82 base, TOUG 88, CHKG 86, FACE 82) fills both fourth-line voids the Coach quantified on 2005-04-09: checking mean 61, toughness mean 57. CHI at 73 points with 10 expiring players are motivated sellers. A package of Tucker plus the 4th plus a mid-tier piece should reach them at Bell's current salary.

## League scan

The question this phase answers is: who across the league closes Toronto's structural gaps, and why would their club move them? The answer concentrates in two names and then a deep second tier of UFAs from clubs that cannot retain everyone.

**Iginla** is the priority. 128 points in 76 games at 27, TOUG 85, SPEE 98, on a $6.50M expiring deal from CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring contracts. He closes the scoring void and raises the toughness ceiling from Jackman's 75 to 85 in one move. CGY's $14.43M profit is real but 10 expiring deals at $45.93M payroll forces triage. He does not stay.

**Kovalchuk** is the player the April notes missed. 138 points in 79 games at **22 years old**, $1.10M, contract_years = 1 (expiring). SPEE 99, POTE 84, TOUG 78. ATL finished at 84 points with 11 expiring. The Feb 28 note said ATL cannot re-sign both him and Heatley. They will choose one, and the one they choose probably isn't him — Heatley is at 131 points but 24 and on the same deal. If Kovalchuk reaches the market, he is the best combination of youth, production and cost on the entire sheet.

**Bell** is the only trade target that matters. TOUG 95, CHKG 93, FACE 87, POTE 82, 24, $900K, 2 years remaining from CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring and $31.73M profit. He closes all three of the coach's structural gaps — toughness above 80, faceoffs above 87, checking above 87 — simultaneously. His production is modest (28 points in 80 games) but his role is the fourth-line centre the coach has been demanding since April. CHI are sellers by every metric.

**Thornton** at BOS is the sleeper. 83 points in 59 games at 25, TOUG 80, CHKG 81, FACE 78, $4.00M expiring. BOS at 97 points with 13 expiring and $34.32M profit *can* keep him, which makes him less likely than the others. But if he walks, he is a top-two centre who pushes Richards to 2C and adds toughness to the scoring line.

**Gagne** at PHI is the financial desperation case. PHI payroll $66.73M, profit $2.14M, 13 expiring. They must shed. Gagne is 108 points in 82 games, 25, SPEE 96, $2.40M. A scorer who doesn't solve toughness but doubles the scoring bridge.

**Stuart** at SJ is the Roberts replacement. 87 base, TOUG 74, CHKG 83, POTE 92, SPEE 94, 25, $1.80M, expiring. SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring cannot keep him and Marleau both. He brings toughness to the blueline (74 above our current best of Jackman's 75 at D, roughly equivalent) plus speed the blueline lacks.

**Komisarek** at MTL is the cheap one. 82/77 base, TOUG 85, CHKG 92, POTE 92, 23, $1.10M, expiring. MTL at 66 points (worst in the league) with 15 expiring. They are selling everything. His 82 points in 82 games at D is a Norris-calibre season.

**Belanger** at LA is the pure faceoff answer. FACE 96, CHKG 77, TOUG 73, 14 points in 64 games, $700K, UFA. At 27 with POTE 74, he will not become more than what he is — but what he is, is the best draw-taker available who is not on a contender.

## Trade construction

This phase asks: what exactly do we offer, and why would their GM say yes? The answer concentrates in one blockbuster and one targeted role acquisition, both funded by coach-flagged pieces (Spezza, Chistov, Upshall, Tucker) and the single 4th-rounder. No core renewal player is in any package.

**Iginla** is the priority and the largest ask. At 128 points in 76 games on $6.50M expiring from a 70-point club with 10 expiring contracts, he is the only player closing the 426-point scoring cliff and the toughness ceiling simultaneously. CGY cannot re-sign everyone. A package centred on Spezza (21, C, POTE 99, $1.00M, 2 years of control) gives them the franchise centre their rebuild lacks. Adding Chistov (POTE 95, 22, speed) and Tucker (CHKG 92, 2 years, rental for their young core to play behind) makes this their rebuild in one phone call. They shed $6.50M, take on $3.40M, and net $3.10M in payroll relief against a $14.43M profit. Acceptance uncertain — the AI's logic for a 128-point player is unknown — but Tampa traded Lecavalier for Belfour on March 19, so the valuation function is more generous than logic suggests.

**Bell** is the single trade that closes every gap the coach has named since April in one acquisition: TOUG 95, CHKG 93, FACE 87 at 24 on $900K with two years of control. CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring and $31.73M profit have no reason to protect a POTE 82 role player. Upshall (POTE 99, CHKG 87, 21) gives them a physical winger whose game matches the Bell identity they just traded away, and Tucker (CHKG 92, TOUG 88) gives them a checking winger for the present. They take on $1.60M net, which is meaningless against $31.73M profit. The cost to us is Upshall, who the coach himself said Alexeev replaces.

**Komisarek** is the third option if neither above lands. At 82 points in 82 games from the blueline, TOUG 85, CHKG 92, POTE 92, 23 years old, $1.10M expiring, from a 66-point club with 15 expiring contracts, he is the cheapest elite-D on the sheet. MTL is the league's worst team and must stockpile youth. Colaiacovo (POTE 99, 22, D) + Upshall (POTE 99, 21) + the 4th-rounder is three high-potential assets for a player they will not re-sign. He is not Iginla and he does not solve scoring, but he is the Roberts replacement the blueline needs and costs almost nothing to acquire.

**If none land:** sign Iginla or Kovalchuk as a July UFA at zero asset cost. Toronto's 133-point season and $51.14M profit give the highest prestige signal in the league. If the AI sends him elsewhere, the scoring bridge stays broken and the coach's structural gaps persist into 2005-06 — which is the real reason to trade now rather than hope.

## Owed

**Item #2 — Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window.** This task is closed. Luongo is on our roster (94 overall, 26, $1.60M, 2 years left), the GM declared goalies solved on February 19, and on March 19 he explicitly ordered all goalie monitoring closed. The original premise — finding a high-90s goalie from a non-contender — is satisfied: we hold two 90+ netminders in Luongo and Belfour. DiPietro monitoring was rendered moot the same way; we needed no further depth once Luongo arrived mid-season at 91 base and has climbed to 94. Nothing remains to track here.
