# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-27

Next game at DAL on Saturday 28 May 2005.

## Development opportunity

The season is at or past the 82-game mark with 3 games still on the schedule, so this is the last look at who got a chance and who didn't.

**Stahle** is the starkest case. POTE 96 at 21 and he played 4 games all year, averaging 17.8 MPG in those four. That's a real audition in one game and nothing after. No other club in the league is leaving a POTE 96 defenceman on the bench for 78 of 82 games. The offseason camp tryout is the minimum, but 4 games tells me the coaching staff never even built a case for him. I own that.

**Spezza** at POTE 99 is the other failure. 46 games, 6.7 MPG, currently scratched. His rate fell from 0.43 to 0.32 as his minutes collapsed from 9.1 to 4.8 between February and March. The season is a write-off for him, but POTE 99 at 21 on 6.7 MPG is not a development plan. Camp assignment is the only lever left.

**Alexeev** at 30 points in 55 games is 0.55 pts/g on 8.3 MPG. He's scratched. The dressed wingers Chistov (0.29) and Upshall (0.29) produce roughly half his rate. This rate-to-role gap has been unresolved since April and I still don't see the fix. He's 23, not a prospect anymore. Either he plays or his rate is meaningless.

**Chlup** earned every one of his 71 games: 59 points, 16.9 MPG at 19, morale at 100. He belongs on the first line and I've said that every week for two weeks without action. I'll stop repeating it; the GM knows where I stand.

**Nash** is at 39 points in 69 games, 13.1 MPG. His rate dropped from 0.83 to 0.43 with flat minutes. No injury, no role change. That's a system-fit problem and needs an offseason look.

**Spacek** at 50 games and 7.6 MPG on the fourth line is a depth man getting depth minutes. POTE 91 is respectable but not franchise. His year matches his role. No complaint.

**Eminger** has 64 games and 15.5 MPG but is a confirmed sell (expiring, declining). Development is moot. **Klesla** is a sell too, same reason. **Colaiacovo** at 31 games and 17.9 MPG when he plays is being deliberately rotated behind Svehla per the GM's instruction, and I accepted that in January. **Chistov** at 68 games and 13.1 MPG is earning his third-line spot. **Upshall** is getting 68 games at 7.9 MPG and producing 0.29 pts/g: he's a fourth-liner and that's what he's being asked to be. Same offseason audition flag as Spezza.

**Gaborik** is 82 games, 99 points, 20.5 MPG at 23. He's currently scratched for the next game, which I assume is rest or a minor knock, not a development decision. Nothing to fix.

## Development trends

The season is done and the trends are locked — this is the read that shapes next camp, next lines, and who we try to sell. Everyone moved in one direction or the other, and the picture is clearer than it was in April.

**Chlup** is the only unambiguous riser on the club. 0.62 to 0.88 pts/g while minutes went from 11.0 to 18.2. Both rate and role grew, which means the coaching staff already trusts him and the production followed. At 19, 71 games, 0.88 on 18.2 MPG, he is the first-line centre next season. I have said this since April and the lineup has not moved. This is the one change I need before camp.

**Kaberle** quietly got better. 0.54 to 0.62 pts/g on minutes that rose from 19.4 to 21.5. At 27, that is the right direction at the right age. The GM called him a star defenseman in January and the trend backs it up. He anchors the top pair next year without discussion.

**Gaborik** dipped from 1.42 to 1.12 pts/g, but his minutes went from 18.8 to 21.2, a 2.4-minute jump that would dilute any rate. At 23 and 1.12 on 21.2 MPG over 82 games, he is still an elite winger. No concern. The early-season 1.42 pace was the anomaly.

**Fischer** slid from 0.63 to 0.50 pts/g while his load rose from 20.8 to 22.9 MPG. At 24 and 77 games, that is a heavy workload, and the rate dip tracks the added minutes. He is a keeper. I would just watch that 22.9 doesn't creep higher next season.

**Chistov** is the quiet one nobody is talking about. Minutes went from 9.5 to 14.0 while his rate held at 0.30. At 22, his ice time grew and his production stayed level. That is a young winger earning trust through 68 games. He is a roster piece.

**Abid** is the other quiet one, but going the wrong way. 1.09 to 0.70 pts/g with minutes collapsing from 20.1 to 11.5. He lost half his role and then lost his rate too. At 25, he should be peaking, not shrinking. The minutes cut came first and the production followed. He needs a real role next season or he is another asset bleeding value.

**Koltsov** fell from 1.10 to 0.29 pts/g on minutes that stayed at 8.7 to 9.9. The GM holds him as a trade chip, and his trade value is dropping fast. If we have a window to move him this offseason, it should be early before the market sees another rate collapse.

**Afinogenov** (1.17 to 0.73), **Richards** (1.08 to 0.71), and **Nash** (0.83 to 0.42) all collapsed their scoring rate with minutes flat or barely changed. Three players, same pattern: the system is not drawing the best from them. I flagged all three in May. offseason system-fit review is not optional — it is the single biggest question for next year's forward group.

**Spezza** (0.43 to 0.24, 9.1 to 4.6 MPG) and **Spacek** (0.55 to 0.28, 16.0 to 5.2 MPG) both lost most of their minutes and their production alongside it. Spacek's minutes at 5.2 are well below the 8 MPG floor I set in March, so the year is dead for him. Both are camp auditions next fall. Upshall (0.33 to 0.27, 13.4 to 4.8) is the same story. Three 21-year-olds who got a role and lost it, and camp decides their futures.

**Sundin** at 34 went from 16.9 to 21.7 MPG, **Mogilny** at 36 from 16.9 to 19.1, and **Roberts** at 39 from 16.5 to 21.4. All three saw their scoring rate fall, which is expected at those ages, but the minute increases are the concern. Roberts is 39 and playing 21.4 a night. That is a burnout or injury risk heading into next season, and with his production at 0.86 down from 1.29, he is not the player carrying the load the minutes suggest. We need to plan around these three aging fast.

On the blue line, the sell order for task #1 is settled. **McCabe** at 29 confirmed it: 1.42 to 0.48 on 21.5 MPG over 82 games. **Jackman** at 24 collapsed from 0.65 to 0.39 on 29.4 MPG — the load is too much and the production reflects it. **Klesla** at 23 fell from 0.50 to 0.31 on flat minutes, second consecutive declining year. **Eminger** is flat at 0.37 and his contract expires, so he walks for nothing without a move. That is four defensemen to move. **Colaiacovo** at 22 is a mild dip (0.44 to 0.36) and worth keeping. Kaberle and Fischer are the keepers.

## Morale watch

The room is fine. Morale sits between 88 and 100 on the latest save, with the vast majority of the dressing room at 100. The one player below 90 is Spezza, and his situation is a GM development decision, not a minutes problem I can solve from the bench.

**Spezza** is at 88, the lowest on the roster, which costs him 1 point on every grade. He's scratched and averaging 6.7 MPG across 46 games. The GM chose to sit him for other young players' development, and his morale has been climbing (the latest reading shows +3). At 88 he's not in danger of a slide that affects anyone on the ice since he isn't on it. Next camp is where this gets resolved, not before Dallas tomorrow.

**Alexeev** at 92, 8.3 MPG, scratched: fine. He's in the bonus band (+1 to grades). His production-to-role gap (0.55 pts/g on scratch minutes) is a roster question, not a morale one.

**Spacek** and **Upshall** at 94 on 7.6 and 7.9 MPG respectively, fourth line: exactly where a depth player should be. No adjustment needed.

Everyone else in the lineup sits at 99 or 100. No player's morale is being hurt by insufficient ice. No change.

## Role composition

The role question is whether each unit's pieces suit their job, and if not, whether I can fix it with this roster. Most units are fine. Two problems remain and they share the same root cause.

**L1 (Sundin, Roberts, Mogilny, Jackman, Fischer)** is the best-balanced unit on the team. Checking mean 79 with a 92 best, scoring 88/95, speed 91/95. Nothing to change.

**L2 (Chlup, McCabe, Kaberle, Nash, Afinogenov)** is structurally sound. Chlup at 19 wins draws at 80 (the 80 best in faceoffs on this line), McCabe checks at 85, Afinogenov scores at 92. Good mix.

**L3 (Eminger, Tucker, Richards, Klesla, Chistov)** provides what a third line needs: Tucker as the checking body, Richards at 97 clutch for late-game draws, Chistov at speed 98. Fine.

**L4 (Spacek, Abid, Upshall)** still cannot win a faceoff. Mean 52, best 55. This is the same April 13 gap: no forward outside L1-L2 checks above 75 and no faceoff specialist available. Not fixable by arrangement.

**Chlup on PK2** is my one arrangement concern. He is 19, scoring 0.88 pts/g, and our future first-line center. Putting him on the penalty kill costs him stamina and defensive-zone reps that don't develop his game. But the checking inventory shows only four forwards or D above 85 (Jackman 90, Roberts 85, McCabe 85, Fischer 85) and three of those four are already on PK units. If I pull Chlup off PK2 I have no one to replace him with who keeps that unit's checking above the opponent's second line. I would take him off if I could.

**PP1** has Sundin (93 scoring, 92 playmaking) and Afinogenov (92/92) as the engine pair. Shooters and vision in the right ratio. No change.

**PP2** has Mogilny at 94 scoring and Chlup running the point. Speed 91 mean is the highest of any unit. Fine.

**PK1 (Sundin, Roberts, Kaberle, Fischer)** has Sundin's checking at 79 as the weakest link, but his speed (95) and clutch (95) compensate. Roberts at 85 and Fischer at 85 anchor it. Acceptable.

**PK2 (Chlup, Tucker, McCabe, Jackman)** is the defensive unit: Jackman at 90 checking, McCabe at 85. The Chlup concern above applies here specifically.

**Defensemen obligation (#1):** No changes to my offseason sell list from May 23. Jackman (0.48 pts/g, 30 MPG, $0.70M x 3), Klesla (0.36 pts/g, 15 MPG), Eminger (0.38, expiring UFA), and McCabe (0.48 recent window) are all still on the list. Kaberle and Fischer are keepers per GM standing orders.

## Opponent matchup

**Can we beat Turco and their aged defense, or do we need to adjust?** The matchup heavily favors us as-is; the only question is whether to tweak anything for Dallas specifically.

**Dallas defense is old and slow.** Boucher is 32 at 75 OVR with 62 agility. Zubov is 34. Their second pair of Matvichuk (32, 73 OVR, 70 agility) and Berenzweig (27, 68 OVR, 50 endurance) is soft. Their third pair is 65 and 65 OVR. Our forwards are faster than anyone they can dress.

**Our lines match well already.** Our first line pairs with our top D against their top line (Modano/Morrow/Guerin at 88/84/87). Modano is the one real threat in their lineup, and Sundin on the draw (91 FACE vs Modano's 81) wins the starting possession.

**The Chlup line against Matvichuk/Berenzweig is a mismatch.** Nash shoots 98 and runs at 92 speed; Afinogenov has 98 deking and 95 accuracy. They face a 73 and a 68 OVR defenceman who can barely turn. That's where goals should come.

**Their PP is 32 on 297 for 10.8%.** They draw a lot of penalties but convert poorly. Our PK shouldn't buckle, and even when they get chances, they don't finish them.

**Turco is 94 OVR with 94 endurance.** He won't tire. We need quality chances, not volume. The good news is their defense hands us quality chances.

**No change.** The auto-pairing puts our speed up front against their aging blue line on every line. We're 3-1-1 in the series. Go with what we have.

## Owed

The question this answers: which of our defencemen should we move this offseason, and has anything shifted since my May 2nd delivery? Short answer: the list is unchanged, two of them got slightly more confirmed.

**McCabe** finished his season at 82 GP, 62 pts, 0.76 pts/g on 22.1 MPG. I flagged him back on the sell list on May 2nd based on his 58-game recent window reading 0.48. His season is complete, so that number is locked. Still a sell at 29, $3.00M x 4.

**Jackman** has moved from 73 GP to 80 GP since March, and his rate slid from 0.48 to 0.46 on 29.6 MPG. Confirms the March 23 call. At $0.70M x 3 years and age 24, his value is the cheap minutes a buyer wants, not what he gives us at that rate. Sell stands.

**Klesla** at 82 GP, 30 pts, 0.37 pts/g on 14.8 MPG. Same story as always: second declining season, age 23, $0.90M x 2. Sell confirmed.

**Eminger** has dropped from the 0.38 season rate I noted March 30 to 0.36 (23 pts, 64 GP, 15.5 MPG). The slide continued. Contract expires ($1.20M x 1 yr). If we do not move him this offseason he walks for nothing. Sell stands, urgency unchanged.

**Fischer** (0.53 pts/g, 85 OVR, 24 years, $3.70M x 4) and **Kaberle** (0.59 pts/g, 84 OVR, 27 years, $1.90M x 1 year remaining) are both keepers on the GM's standing order. Fischer's 0.53 rate on 22.4 MPG at age 24 is productive for a top-pairing defenceman. Kaberle's rate is lower but the GM called him a star, and at 27 with an expiring deal he is the kind of player we renew. No change.

Nothing new to move onto or off the list since May 2nd.

# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-25

Toronto 59-13-5, 133 pts after 82 games.

## Role coverage

The role coverage question matters today because the season is over and every gap is now a July decision with no deadline pressure forcing a compromise. The answer: two roles are structurally missing (toughness, faceoffs), one is thin and aging (checking), and the scoring core that carries the team today expires within two seasons.

**Toughness is the club's defining hole.** Zero players at 80+; the best is Jackman at 75, then Roberts 73, McCabe 73. A playoff team needs at least one player clearing 85 TOUG on the third or fourth line to make opponents pay in the corners. No internal combination fixes this. Bell at CHI (88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, 24, POTE 81) closes it alone. This contradiction from February is resolved: the current data confirms zero, and the six-at-80+ claim from Feb 21 was wrong.

**Faceoffs are missing outside one man.** Sundin at 90 carries every important draw at 34. Next best is Chlup at 75, then Richards at 70, Tucker at 67. The Coach is correct that this is a trade/offseason need, not a lines fix. Bell solves it at 82; Avery at LA solves it at 93 FACE for $400K with 2 years left.

**Checking is thin and top-heavy.** Six players clear 80, but Roberts (39) is finished within eighteen months and Tucker (30, POTE 79) is already a trade chip. That leaves Jackman 87, McCabe 86, Fischer 82, Upshall 80 — four usable checkers for a playoff run, two on the power play. Bell adds a fifth at 86 without aging anyone out.

**Scoring looks covered but is a cliff.** Mogilny 94 (36), Sundin 92 (34), Roberts 88 (39) carry 426 combined points. Mogilny already fell from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g this season. No player under 30 is producing above 0.60 pts/g except Chlup at 0.88 on 18.2 MPG, which is a promising but unproven rate. The Iginla target (27, 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP) is the only single acquisition that bridges the scoring void.

**Koltsov and Gaborik are on the roster with no line assignment.** Koltsov carries 92 speed; Gaborik has 92 overall, 98 speed, 90 clutch. Both are usable depth the coach is not deploying. That helps speed coverage (already at 21 players with 80+ SPEE) but does not address toughness or faceoffs.

**Durability is thin at 4 players above 80**, and Roberts at 39 with 98 INJU will not stay on the ice indefinitely. This is not urgent but it narrows the margin if injuries come in a playoff series.

**Goalies are solved.** Luongo 26 with 2 years, Ouellet 23 with 2 years, Belfour 40 expiring. Per the GM's March 19 standing order, no further monitoring needed.

## Trajectory

The question is whether Toronto's age curve is heading toward a cliff, and whether the money supports adding what the roster still lacks. The answer is no cliff and plenty of money, but a single summer does all the work.

**The age shape is healthy.** 25 of 30 rostered players are 29 or under. The only real gap is 30-33, which holds Tucker alone (30, 3 GP, 1 pt). That is a transitional void, not a structural weakness: the 24-29 group (12 players including Luongo at 26, Richards at 25, Kaberle at 27, McCabe at 29) ages into it naturally over four seasons. The 34+ group (Sundin 34, Mogilny 36, Roberts 39, Belfour 40) thins to two after this summer because Roberts and Belfour walk. The club's production is concentrated in the right half of the sheet.

**The problem is July 2005.** Thirteen contracts worth $21.30M expire simultaneously. Roberts and Belfour leave as planned, leaving 11 players and $13.40M to resolve. Four of them define the next five years of this franchise: **Gaborik** (23, 99 pts/82 GP, POTE 90, $1.10M), **Richards** (25, 66 pts/80 GP, POTE 88, $1.00M), **Nash** (20, 39 pts/69 GP, POTE 95, $1.20M), **Eminger** (21, 23 pts/64 GP, POTE 99, $1.20M). Those four produced 227 points last season and all carry potential that makes them trade bait if lost. They must be locked on 5-6 year deals before the summer market finds them.

**The money makes this easy.** Payroll sits at $60.04M against $123.61M revenue and $48.88M profit. Even if Gaborik demands $5M on a five-year deal, Nash $4M, Richards $4M, Eminger $3.50M, the incremental $14.50M against that profit is routine. Adding Iginla at $6.50M as a UFA costs nothing the club cannot absorb. There is no reason to lose a single core player to money.

**The draft capital is empty.** One 4th-rounder. This means the club cannot fund any trade with picks, cannot recover from a failed development path with a high lottery selection, and cannot use the over-80 expiring mechanic to stock the cupboard. It is a vulnerability, but it does not change the July priority, which is all re-signing and free-agency work.

**The second wave comes in 2007.** Nine contracts worth $15.44M expire in two years, including Chlup ($2.34M, age 21 by then), Luongo ($1.60M, 28), Koltsov, Ouellet, and Mogilny (38, clearly finished). If the July 2005 re-signings are all on 3-year deals to "save money," the club faces the same clustering problem again in exactly two summers. Staggering is the whole strategy: stars on 5-6, Kaberle on 4, conditional players on 2-3.

## Calendar

The deadline passed 67 days ago and seeding is locked at 1st in the East (133 points, 19 clear of 2nd-place New Jersey), so every remaining calendar decision belongs to the summer. Thirteen contracts expire, two of them belong to 39-year-olds, and the single most important transaction this club will make is locking Gaborik before July.

**Gaborik** at 23, POTE 90, $1.10M expiring, is the #1 renewal priority. The January standing order on this player — lock him before February — was impossible under the game's no-renegotiation rule, so July is the first and only window. Star-length on 5-6 years, per the manual. If he walks, the scoring bridge void the Coach flagged (Mogilny 36, Sundin 34, Roberts 39 carrying 426 combined points) has no young answer at all.

**Kaberle** at 27, $1.90M expiring, is in his prime and should be locked 5-6 years alongside Gaborik. He is a core piece and the GM has never questioned keeping him.

**Eminger** at 21, POTE 99, $1.20M expiring, is the same story: GM vetoed trading him on January 19, and he is the highest-potential blueliner on the roster. Lock 5-6 years.

**Richards** at 25, $1.00M expiring, is the Coach's designated first-line centre next season (70 FACE, 85 PASS). The system-fit review flagged his collapsed rate, but at 25 with that profile he is a starter, not a camp body. Lock 5-6 years.

**Belfour** at 40, $6.50M expiring, is a release. The GM kept him through the playoffs as the second 90+ goalie (March 19 standing order), and Luongo at 91 base is the starter. The January note was "offer him a reduced contract at renewal but he probably won't accept." Plan on him walking. The $6.50M freed is what makes the Iginla signing possible.

**Roberts** at 39, $2.70M expiring, is a release. No forward line needs a 39-year-old, and $2.70M is the margin between signing Iginla at $6.50M and not signing him. Let him go.

**Tellqvist** at 25, $0.80M expiring, is a 3-4 year renewal. The GM's standing order says give him time to develop, POTE in the high 90s. He is the backup behind Luongo while he matures.

**Abid** at 25, $0.40M expiring, is a 2-3 year renewal. The Coach's fourth-line gap is quantified (checking mean 61, toughness mean 57, faceoffs 50) and Abid at base TOUG 80, CHKG 80 is the cheapest answer available. Renew before July so Bell becomes a luxury rather than a need.

**The camp audition group:** Nash (20, $1.20M), Chistov (22, POTE 95, $1.10M), Upshall (21, $1.20M), Alexeev (23, $1.10M), and Colaiacovo (22, POTE 99, $1.10M) all expire and all carry the Coach's conditional flags. Nash needs the system-fit review to resolve. Chistov is displaced by Alexeev per the Coach's May 25 report. Colaiacovo needs a defined defensive pair role or he becomes a trade piece. Upshall and Alexeev compete for the same wing spot. None should be signed before camp. Sign them on 2-year deals only if they earn a roster spot; otherwise they become trade chips in July packages.

**Iginla** (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, $6.50M expiring) remains the #1 summer target. Belfour and Roberts leaving frees $9.20M, which covers his salary and the Gaborik raise. **Bell** (CHI, LW, 24, 82 base, TOUG 88, CHKG 86, FACE 82) is the fourth-line solution the Coach keeps flagging, but he is a luxury once Abid is renewed.

The four remaining games are seeding exercises. The GM should focus on rest for Sundin (34), Mogilny (36), and the other veterans heading into the playoffs.

**Task #2 (Luongo/DiPietro monitoring):** Closed by the GM's own March 19 standing order — "Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks." Luongo is on the roster at 91 base. DiPietro monitoring is moot with Luongo arrived and Tellqvist developing. This task is complete.

## League scan

The season is over and every gap is a July decision. I need a full league-wide map of who fills the toughness, faceoff, and scoring-bridge voids, and what each club's willingness to move them looks like. I have broad production data from q124 and q125 — now I need the physical profiles and the defensive depth the Roberts departure leaves exposed.

Four queries to paint the picture: all high-toughness players on non-contenders, all high-faceoff players on non-contenders, all young high-potential players on losing clubs, and all defenders with 80+ checking on non-contenders.

## Trade construction

The season is over and every gap is a July decision. Three proposals close all three structural voids — toughness, faceoffs, and the scoring bridge — using only expendable assets and money we already have.

**Bell from Chicago for Chistov plus Abid.** Bell at 24, $900K with 2 years left, 80 base overall, carries 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE on stored grades. He is the only player in the league who closes both the toughness hole (zero TOR players at 80+ today) and the faceoff gap (next best is Chlup at 75) simultaneously. Chistov (22, POTE 95, SPEE 89, ACCE 88, $1.10M expiring) is the piece the Coach already displaced with Alexeev. Abid (25, 66 pts/82 GP, $400K expiring, POTE 94) gives Chicago production they can re-sign cheaply. CHI at 73 points with $29.46M profit are rebuilding; POTE 95 at 22 is a better long-term asset than POTE 81 at 24, and Abid's 66 points at $400K fills their scoring void while they develop. They gain $600K in payroll against a profit margin that makes it invisible.

**Avery from LA for Koltsov.** Avery at 25, $400K with 2 years left, 79 base, FACE 93. He gives the fourth line a real faceoff center, which the Coach quantified at mean 52 with no internal fix. Koltsov (24, POTE 94, ACCE 96, AGIL 92, $1.10M, 2 years, 19 pts/38 GP) is speed and potential that LA at 48 points would prefer over a 79-base center they would likely lose in two years anyway. The March 19 proposal already identified this exact package as LA's stated preference. We save $700K net.

**Iginla as a July UFA signing, not a trade.** His contract reads contract_years = 0, meaning he is already expiring from Calgary. At 27, 93 base, $6.50M, TOUG 85, he closes the Mogilny scoring bridge (140 pts/73 GP against Mogilny's collapse to 0.79 pts/g) and becomes our first player above 85 toughness. CGY at 70 points with $14.43M profit and 10 expiring cannot retain him. We sign him directly — no trade needed. Our $48.88M profit absorbs $6.50M without a flinch.

If Bell doesn't land, fall back to Stuart (SJ, 25, 87 base, $1.80M, 1 year, POTE 91) for toughness on defense, though SJ at 72 points may not deal a POTE 91 blueliner. If Avery doesn't land, Bell's 82 FACE partially covers the wing-side draws but the L4C position stays broken. If Iginla signs elsewhere, Heatley (ATL, 91 base, 24) or Doan (PHX, 89, 25) are the fallbacks, both expiring from non-contenders.

## Owed

The question this phase answers: is the goalie trade window still open, and does DiPietro still need monitoring? It closed on March 19.

**Luongo** is on our roster. 26 years old, 94 overall, $1.60M, 2 years left, 45 games this season. He was acquired in January and has been our starter since. The task was to monitor his availability for a trade; that trade window was opened, worked, and closed. Luongo is no longer an acquisition target — he is the number one we already have.

**DiPietro** monitoring was scoped to the same goalie trade window that the GM closed on 2005-03-19. With Luongo in net and Belfour as the playoff backup, the premise of that sub-task (find a goalie, or find a goalie for us to acquire) no longer applies.

**Belfour** at 40, 93 overall, $6.50M, contract expiring this year is the one goalie item that still matters, but that is a renewal decision at season's end, not a trade-window monitoring task.

Nothing has changed since the last report because the GM shut this job down. I am closing it.

# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-25

Next game vs DAL on Thursday 26 May 2005.

## Development opportunity

The season is over at 82 games, so the development question for each young player is now answerable on a full sample: who got the chance, who did not, and who is not yet ready to take it.

**Chlup** has fully earned the first line. 59 points in 71 games at 16.9 MPG, POTE 95, morale 100. He has outgrown the second line and I have recommended this three times this month. The GM has not moved him. For next season this needs to happen before camp, not during it.

**Gaborik** is currently scratched with 99 points in 82 games and 20.5 MPG. That is the best season on this roster and he is not in the lineup for tomorrow. Either something physical is keeping him out or a decision needs to be reversed immediately. I cannot see what the cause is from here.

**Alexeev** at 0.55 pts/g outproduces both dressed wingers, Chistov (0.29) and Upshall (0.29), yet remains a scratch. This has been unresolved since April 23. The mismatch is now confirmed over a full season: Chistov is 20 points in 68 games, Upshall is 20 in 68, Alexeev is 30 in 55.

**Colaiacovo** got 31 games at 17.9 MPG but POTE 99 and only 12 points. His development is stalled by the rotation he is in, not by a lack of minutes when he plays. He needs a defined pair role next season or this pattern repeats.

**Spezza** got 46 games at 6.7 MPG and 15 points. POTE 99 at 21 with that kind of ice time is a wasted year. The season is done; the only lever left is next camp's assignment.

**Stahle** played 4 games and scored nothing. No evidence of readiness at 21 with POTE 96. He should compete for a roster spot in camp but there is no claim here that he has been wronged.

**Spacek** finished at 7.6 MPG and 0.34 pts/g across 50 games. At 19 that is not damning, but it confirms he is a depth player for now, not a middle-six prospect.

**Upshall** got 68 games but only 7.9 MPG. His minutes collapsed mid-season (noted March 25) and never recovered. He is a healthy scratch in the current lineup, which is the right call based on his production.

**Klesla** played every game at 14.8 MPG. He is getting the opportunity; the issue is his declining rate (0.37 pts/g), which is a performance problem, not a development one.

## Development trends

The season is four games old to go, so these trends are final readings, not early noise. The window is large enough to be honest.

**Chlup** is the only young player whose rate and minutes both rose: 0.62 to 0.88 pts/g on 11.0 to 18.2 MPG at 19. Every other player aged 23 or under on this list saw either their rate, their minutes, or both fall. I have recommended him at first-line centre twice and neither was taken. With four games left this is now a camp decision. He belongs there.

**Kaberle** is the quiet positive story. 0.54 to 0.62 pts/g while his load went 19.4 to 21.5 MPG. At 27, both numbers going up together means he is entering his prime, not leaving it. No action needed, just confirmation the keeper call was right.

**Sundin, Mogilny, Roberts** are declining at the ages you would expect. Sundin at 34: 1.46 to 0.97. Mogilny at 36: 1.62 to 0.83. Roberts at 39: 1.29 to 0.86. All three got more minutes while scoring less per minute, which means the team is leaning harder on men whose legs are going. The GM needs to plan around the fact that this line is a year or two from replacement, not five.

**Afinogenov, Richards, Nash** are the system-fit cluster. All three kept their minutes roughly flat while their rates collapsed: 1.17 to 0.73, 1.08 to 0.71, 0.83 to 0.42 respectively. Ages 25, 25, 20. None injured. The role did not change, the production did. Offseason review of how we use them is still the right call.

**Spacek and Spezza** both lost minutes and rate simultaneously. Spacek 0.55 to 0.28 on 16.0 to 5.2 MPG. Spezza 0.43 to 0.24 on 9.1 to 4.6. The season is finished for them. Camp audition or stop dressing.

**Klesla** at 0.50 to 0.31 on flat 14.9 MPG is the second straight year of decline. He is 23, so the direction is wrong for his age. Sell.

**McCabe** at 1.42 to 0.48 confirms the sell call from May 2nd. His early-season pace was the anomaly. At 29, 4 years, $3.00M on a 0.48 rate, the return on trading him is worth more than keeping him.

**Jackman** at 0.65 to 0.39 on 29.4 MPG is the same story I flagged in March: the load is killing his production. At 24 the expected direction is up and it went the other way. Sell or restructure his minutes.

**Duty #1 — defenceman review.** Kaberle is the one trending up (0.62 pts/g on 21.5 MPG). Fischer dipped slightly (0.63 to 0.50) but minutes rose to 22.9, which is the GM's keeper call and I respect it. The sell list from the blue line: McCabe, Jackman, Klesla, Eminger (expiring, $1.2M, flat at 0.37). Colaiacovo at 22 went 0.44 to 0.36 on slightly lower minutes, young enough that one window is not verdict, but he is not climbing either.

No line changes tonight. These are all offseason decisions.

## Morale watch

The room is right. Every player on the active roster sits at 100 morale. The losing streak to start this stretch (0-1-0, 0-0-1) hasn't dented anyone.

**Spezza** is the lowest on the roster at 88, where he has been for weeks without further decline. He is scratched, carries 15 points in 46 games at 6.7 MPG. His morale is not collapsing, it is stable at a level consistent with being healthy but not playing. That is the GM's development rotation doing exactly what it is supposed to do, and there is nothing I can change on the lines that fixes it.

**Alexeev** at 92 is the same picture: 30 points in 55 games, 8.3 MPG, scratched. Stable.

No player who is dressing has a morale problem that minutes can address. No change.

## Role composition

The question is whether each unit has the right skill profile for its job, and where the roster simply cannot provide what a unit needs.

**L1** is a complete unit. Checking mean 79 with Jackman at 90 and Fischer at 85 gives it real shutdown capability. Sundin's 91 on draws anchors the zone. Speed 91/95 means it can also run. No arrangement fix needed; this is as good as it gets with this roster.

**L2** carries a faceoff liability: mean 59, best 80 from Chlup alone. Nash and Afinogenov are wingers who won't take the dot, and McCabe is a defenceman. Every defensive-zone draw through the centre ice is a coin flip against a competent opposing center. Chlup at 80 is growing into this, but at 19 the ceiling is there. No fix available from the bench; we simply don't have a second 80+ faceoff man to slot in.

**L3** is balanced. Richards at 75 on draws, checking mean 75, speed mean 89 with Chistov at 98 giving it legs. Tucker provides the physical edge. This line does what a third line should.

**L4 is the structural problem.** Faceoff mean 52, best 55. Spacek, Abid, and Upshall cannot win a draw at all. Checking mean 74 sounds acceptable until you notice the best is 87 with no elite checker among them. This line will lose every defensive-zone faceoff it takes and cannot match an opposing checking line's best. My standing finding from April 13 holds: no forward outside L1-L2 checks above 75, and the fourth line has checking mean 62-74 with toughness best at 87. This is a roster gap, not an arrangement error.

**K2 actually outchecks K1.** The second kill has checking mean 84 (Jackman 90, McCabe 85) versus K1's 79 (Fischer 85, Roberts 85). This is correct: K1 handles the draw through Sundin at 91 and matches top-six forwards; K2 is the physical kill. No swap needed.

**P1 and P2 are both legitimate.** P1 leans experience (Sundin 93 scoring, Roberts 91 clutch); P2 leans speed and youth (Mogilny 94 scoring, P2 speed mean 91). Both have point threats and both have a net-front setup. No change.

**Duty #1 (defensemen sell-list review):** Jackman at 0.48 pts/g on 30 MPG across 73 games remains a sell at $0.70M x 3. Klesla's second consecutive decline (0.38 to 0.36) confirms the sell. McCabe's season rate of 0.76 over 82 games is above threshold but his recent 58-game window of 0.48 says the hot start has fully bled off, and he goes back on the sell list at 29 with 4 years and $3.00M. Eminger at 0.38, age 21, $1.2M expiring must move before July or we lose him for nothing. These four positions are unchanged from my April 7 and May 2 notes.

## Opponent matchup

What does this opponent demand that our current setup does not already answer? Short answer: nothing. We are 59-13-5 at home, they are 42-24-7, and the season series is 2-1-1 our way with an 11-8 goal margin. The only pre-game decision that matters is the goalie.

**Modano** is the matchup question, but our first line already answers him. Sundin FACE 91 wins the draw against Modano's 81, Roberts CHKG 88 is the second-best forward checker we dress, and Mogilny's 90 OVR keeps us honest offensively. Their top line (Modano/Morrow/Guerin at 88/84/87) is dangerous, but our L1 at 91/90/88 is the only unit that matches their skill while still having a body to put on them. Moving our checking line (Richards/Tucker) up would win a faceoff battle against a line we'd then be outscored by. Keep L1 where it is.

**DAL's power play** is 32-for-297, which is 10.8 percent. They cannot score a man advantage. No special PK adjustment needed.

**Our power play against their defence** is where the game is won. Zubov at OVR 83 is the only quality D they dress outside Boucher (75). Matvichuk 73, Berenzweig 68, Descoteaux 65, Richards 65. Our PP unit has Sundin FACE 91, Mogilny SHPW 95, Roberts SHPW 90, Jackman SHPW 92, Fischer SHPW 89. We should exploit that bottom four all night. Our 32.3 percent PP against that group is our best scoring path.

**Luongo** goes in net. OVR 94, and he has been sharp enough to warrant a check before every start given the fatigue-icon history. If the tired goalie icon is showing, Ouellet goes in. No way around checking the screen.

## Owed

**Item #1 — defencemen sell-list update, final season read.**

The season is essentially done for this group. McCabe and Klesla have 82 games logged, Jackman 80, Fischer 77, Kaberle 74, Eminger 64. Final rates are locked. Here is where each man stands.

**McCabe** finished at 62 points in 82 games (0.76 pts/g) on 22.1 MPG. His recent window from my May 2 note was 0.48 over the last 58 games, meaning the hot start carried the season average well above his true level. At 29 with $3.00M x 4 years, he stays on the sell list. Nothing has changed since May 2.

**Jackman** ended at 37 points in 80 games (0.46 pts/g) on 29.6 MPG. His $0.70M x 3 makes him the cheapest top-pair minutes in the league, which is the trade value. Sell confirmed. Unchanged.

**Klesla** finished at 30 points in 82 games (0.37 pts/g) on 14.8 MPG. Second consecutive declining season. Sell at $0.90M x 2. Unchanged.

**Eminger** finished at 23 points in 64 games (0.36 pts/g) on 15.5 MPG. His $1.20M contract expires in July. After that he is a UFA loss. He must be moved before free agency opens. Unchanged from March 30, but the window is closing fast.

**Kaberle** finished at 44 points in 74 games (0.60 pts/g) on 20.8 MPG at age 27 with OVR 84. His $1.90M contract expires after this season. The GM said he is a star and a keeper. The urgent action is renewal, not a sell-list decision. If we lose him to UFA, we lose the best defenceman on the roster for nothing.

**Fischer** finished at 41 points in 77 games (0.53 pts/g) on 22.4 MPG at age 24 with OVR 85. The GM's position is clear: keeper. Locked up at $3.70M x 4. No action needed.

What has changed since my last delivery: nothing in the numbers moved, because the season is finished. What has changed in urgency is Kaberle. His contract expires and we are two weeks from July. That renewal conversation needs to happen before anything else on the defence.

# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-23

Toronto 59-13-5, 133 pts after 82 games.

## Role coverage

Toughness is the only role with zero 80+ players on the entire roster, and faceoffs has just one. Both were quantified by the coach and neither has an internal fix. Everything else is covered tonight but ages out fast.

**Bell (CHI, LW, 24)** closes both missing roles at once: 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE at 82 base, POTE 81, $0.90M with two years left. CHI sit at 73 points with 10 expiring deals and $29.46M profit — motivated sellers. No Toronto player reaches 80 on any of those three grades. Avery (LA, C, 25, 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, $400K, 2 years) is cheaper and the better faceoff man but weaker on toughness and has a lower ceiling.

**Sundin at 34** is the only 80+ faceoff man (90 FACE) and the 94 CLUTCH leader. Richards at 70 FACE to L4 was taken three times this season and is the best internal move available, but it caps the fourth line at 70 draws against a league-wide target of 80+. The coach's L4 mean of 52 confirms the gap persists even with Richards down there.

**Tucker at 30** is the internal toughness floor: 83 CHKG but only 70 TOUG, POTE 79. He is already a trade chip per the GM's March 19 order. He cannot close a toughness gap that needs 80+.

**Jackman at 24** is the only blueliner with 87 CHKG and 75 TOUG who is also young. Roberts at 39 (86 CHKG, 73 TOUG, 90 CLUTCH) is the other 80+ checker at defence and he is one or two seasons from retirement. Stuart (SJ, 25, 87 base, 89 CHKG, 80 TOUG, POTE 91) is the target to pair with Jackman and replace Roberts.

**Scoring depth is 10 players at 80+ overall**, but Mogilny is 36, Sundin 34, Roberts 39. Gaborik at 23 (92 base, 1.12 pts/g) and Chlup at 19 (59 pts/71 GP) are the bridge, but the gap between 1.12 and Mogilny's 0.79 on rising minutes says the bridge is not built yet. Iginla at 93 base and 140 points in 73 games on an expiring $6.50M from a 70-point Calgary team remains the July priority.

**Goalies are solved.** Luongo at 26 with two years and Belfour at 40 with one year for the playoff run. Tellqvist at 25 (POTE high 90s per GM) and Ouellet at 23 with two years provide depth. No action needed here.

## Trajectory

The trajectory question is whether this club can keep its young core when 13 deals expire in the same July, and whether the 34+ veterans leaving creates a cliff. The answer: the age curve is healthy, the money is fine, and the single existential risk is the renewal cluster.

**The cliff is not real.** Four players are 34+ (Sundin 34, Mogilny 36, Roberts 39, Belfour 40) carrying $23.10M and 256 points between them. Behind them, 13 players 23 or under and 12 aged 24-29. The roster is structurally young; the old guard is leaving by design, not by collapse. The 30-33 gap (one player, Tucker at 30, who dressed 3 games) is unusual but not a cliff, because Nash (20), Gaborik (23), Richards (25) and Chlup (19) are moving into those roles on their own timeline.

**The renewal cluster is the problem.** Thirteen contracts worth $21.30M expire simultaneously. The players who MUST be locked on 6-year deals are **Gaborik** (99 points, 23, POTE 90, $1.10M), **Richards** (66 points, 25, POTE 88, $1.00M), **Nash** (39 points at 20, POTE 95, $1.20M), and **Eminger** (POTE 99, 23 points at 21, $1.20M). Miss any of those four and the 133-point season becomes a one-off built on expiring veterans.

**The money is not the constraint.** Payroll $60.04M against revenue $121.34M leaves $61.30M of headroom. Even locking all four young stars at a 4x raise adds roughly $15M to payroll. Profit of $48.88M funds the Iginla salary without strain. There is no cap; the only limit is whether the game grants long contracts to players who want them.

**Iginla is the one acquisition that closes the gap.** Mogilny (84 points), Sundin (91), Roberts (81) are leaving. Iginla at 27, 93 base, 140 points in 73 games, POTE unknown but age alone gives him 5-7 better seasons ahead, replaces all three simultaneously. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring contracts and $14.43M profit has no reason to retain him. The cost is players, not picks, because Toronto owns one 4th-rounder.

**Walk Belfour and Roberts in July.** Belfour is 40, $6.50M expiring, CONS 50, and his playoff-purpose standing order is fulfilled. Roberts is 39, $2.70M, and his 81 points at POTE 52 will not repeat. Together they free $9.20M. Keep Kaberle at 27 if the ask is under $2.50M — he is the only bridge-age defenseman available internally.

**Draft capital is nothing.** One 4th-round pick is not ammunition. Every trade package must be player-for-player. This means Chistov ($1.10M expiring, POTE 95, 20 points) and Upshall ($1.20M expiring, POTE 99, 20 points) are the only pieces a contender would want, and neither is worth a 93-base winger alone. The Iginla package likely needs a young defenseman (Klesla at 23, POTE 97, 2 years) or Koltsov plus a depth forward.

## Calendar

The deadline closed March 19 and the season ends in five games, so the only date that matters is the summer, which opens in about two weeks with the draft on June 8 and the next event June 27. Thirteen contracts expire, the scoring bridge (Mogilny, Sundin, Roberts) carries 426 points into decline, and the re-signing queue determines whether Toronto builds around Gaborik or scrambles in July without him.

**Gaborik** is the first call. 23 years old, 1.12 pts/g, POTE 90, $1.10M expiring. If he hits free agency, every contender bids. Lock on 5–6 years the first day it is possible. No negotiation, no leverage argument. This is the highest-value asset on the roster and it walks in July if not signed.

**Kaberle** at 27 and $1.90M is prime-age top-pairing defence on a bargain salary. Lock 5–6 years before his numbers justify a $4M+ ask.

**Eminger** at 21 with POTE 99 and $1.20M is the same logic as Gaborik at lower scale. GM vetoed trading him in January for exactly this reason. Lock 5–6 years.

**Richards** at 25, 70 FACE, 85 PASS, $1.00M is a top-six centre at a fourth-line salary. Lock 5–6 years. The Coach already assigned him third-line centre for next season; the renewal must be the same priority as the lineup spot.

**Nash** at 20 and $1.20M carries the system-fit question (flat minutes, halved rates), but at 20 you lock young players who haven't had a full season to show their game. Renew 5–6 years. The fit review informs his role, not his value to the club.

**Tellqvist** at 25, POTE high 90s, $0.80M: renew 2–3 years per the GM's standing order from January 15. He's the development project behind Luongo.

**Abid** at 25 and $0.40M is the cheapest toughness on the roster. Renew 2 years. No reason to spend more.

**Belfour** at 40 and $6.50M expiring will not accept a reduced deal. Let him go. The GM's January position was "offer reduced, he probably won't accept." That is the answer.

**Roberts** at 39 and $2.70M expiring is the same. Let go. At 39 his production is gone and the money is better spent elsewhere.

**Chistov** at 22, POTE 95, SPEE 89, ACCE 88, $1.10M expiring is a trade candidate this summer. The Coach stated plainly on May 5 that Alexeev displaces him. If he's not re-signed, he walks for nothing. Move him in a package that fills the toughness/faceoff gap.

**Colaiacovo** at 22, POTE 99, $1.10M expiring needs the camp audition the Coach demanded (31 games, 17.9 MPG, 0.39 pts/g). Decision: camp tells us whether he's a top-four defenceman or a trade piece. Hold him through camp, then decide.

**Upshall** at 21, POTE 99, $1.20M expiring gets the same camp audition (0.29 pts/g on 7.9 MPG). Same decision process as Colaiacovo.

**Mogilny** at $5.50M with 2 years left cannot be moved and cannot be cut. He declined from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g at 36. Eat the contract. He has 5 more games this season, then two more years of 40–50 points at most. The $5.50M is the price of the bridge; there is no mechanism to avoid it.

**The money problem.** Sundin at $8.40M for 5 more years and Mogilny at $5.50M for 2 more locks $53M to two players who will combine for perhaps 100 points by 2007. That is the weight the summer must justify. Iginla (93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, $6.50M expiring from CGY) is the acquisition that makes it tolerable because he replaces the Mogilny production outright. Bell (82 base, 88 TOUG, 82 FACE, POTE 81, CHI) closes the faceoff gap the Coach quantified at 52/55 on the fourth line. Both are targets; neither falls in the Tucker + 4th-rounder range, so Chistov's expiring value is the third funding source.

**The plan for the draft on June 8:** scout for goaltending depth per the GM's standing order from January 22. Otherwise take the best player available; Toronto owns no pick better than a fourth-rounder, so this is a depth draft, not a franchise one.

**Playoff ticket prices:** raise per the manual schedule. Roughly 75 in round one given Toronto's home ice and 133-point record.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: who across the league fills our three structural gaps (RW scoring, toughness, faceoffs) on a club that will actually trade or release him. The answer changes from March because one name has emerged that rivals Iginla at a tenth the cost.

**Havlat** is the headline. 24, 87 base, 103 points in 82 games, POTE 85, $900K expiring from Ottawa at 77 points with 11 expiring deals and $32.36M profit. He was shelved in April when Iginla became the RW priority, but Havlat is a LW. He does not compete for the RW slot; he sits beside Nash and behind Gaborik as a third 24-year-old winger with POTE above 80. At $900K, he is the cheapest 87-base, 100-point player on the market.

**Iginla** remains the #1 target. 27, 93 base, 128 points in 76 games, 87 TOUG, $6.50M expiring from CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring deals and $14.43M profit. He closes the Mogilny RW void and carries the second-highest TOUG grade among any realistic target, so he chips at the toughness gap simultaneously. The price is the problem: $6.50M requires a real package, and we own one 4th-rounder. Chistov, Upshall, and Alexeev carry $3.40M combined; we need a defenseman or a bigger salary in the return.

**Bell** stays as the toughness and faceoff answer. 24, 80 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81, $900K, two years left. CHI at 78 points with $31.73M profit is profitable enough that they will not dump him for a 4th-rounder, but with 10 expiring deals they are rebuilding and will listen. He is the only league-wide player closing both missing roles (zero 80+ TOUG, one 80+ FACE) on a contract we keep.

**Stuart and Brewer** are the defense targets from the same club. Stuart: 25, 87 base, 89 CHKG, 80 TOUG, POTE 91, $1.80M expiring, 52 points in 77 games. Brewer: 26, 88 base, 93 CHKG, 82 TOUG, POTE 83, $2.00M expiring, 61 points in 82 games. SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring cannot keep both. Brewer is better tonight (93 CHKG is the highest among defense targets); Stuart has more upside (POTE 91 vs 83). Either replaces Roberts at 39.

**Heatley** is the fallback RW if ATL keeps Kovalchuk (138 pts, 89 base). Heatley: 24, 91 base, 131 points in 79 games, POTE 85, $1.10M expiring. ATL at 84 points, 11 expiring, $25.99M profit. The binary is real; one of those two moves.

**Brewer** edges **Stuart** as the more likely get because SJ has too many expiring blueliners (Brewer, Stuart, McLaren at 82 base with 92/88 CHKG, Mironov at 83) and must shed one. McLaren is the third SJ option at 27, 92 CHKG, 88 TOUG but only 82 base.

**Drury** at BUF is a new LW option: 28, 89 base, 99 points in 82 games, POTE 80, $2.00M expiring. BUF at 84 points, 10 expiring, $24.30M profit. Lower POTE than Havlat but higher base and age-appropriate production.

**Daze** at CHI is the LW rental: 29, 89 base, 127 points in 82 games, POTE 77, $3.00M expiring. The POTE says he is done growing. If we need one-year production after Mogilny leaves, he is available. Not a long-term fix.

**Cammalleri** and **Avery** remain cheap options. Cammalleri (LA, 22, POTE 97, 60 pts/61 GP, $1.10M UFA) is a July signing. Avery (LA, 25, 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, $400K, 2 years) is the cheapest faceoff-plus-toughness combo but produces 9 points in 82 games, which the ice has already proven.

The strategic question: Iginla alone or Havlat + Bell. Iginla costs $6.50M and fills one gap plus partial toughness. Havlat + Bell costs $1.80M, fills LW scoring and both missing roles, but leaves the RW hole for Heatley or Doan on a later trade. Both paths work if ATL releases Heatley.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: what do we hand to Calgary, Ottawa, Chicago and San Jose to get the three players the coverage phase says we are missing? We own one 4th-round pick and roughly $6.70M in non-core trade pieces, so every package is player-for-player. Three proposals follow, ranked by how cleanly they fill a gap versus what they cost us.

**Proposal 1, Bell from Chicago for Upshall and Koltsov.** Bell is 82 base with 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG and 82 FACE at 24 on a two-year deal at $900K. Upshall (21, $1.20M expiring, POTE 99, CHKG 87) and Koltsov (24, $1.10M, two years, POTE 94) give Chicago a $2.30M package against Bell's $900K, meaning we dump $1.40M of salary. Chicago sits at 73 points with 10 expiring deals and $29.46M profit. They are rebuilding and need young players, and Bell at POTE 81 is their lowest-ceiling winger. Upshall at POTE 99 is the kind of piece a 73-point team builds around. Koltsov is a second body with POTE 94 and two years under control. This is the cleanest mutual fit on the board.

**Proposal 2, Havlat from Ottawa for Chistov, Colaiacovo, Tucker and the 4th rounder.** Havlat at 87 base, 103 points in 82 games, POTE 85, age 24, $900K expiring. He slots beside Nash at LW, behind Gaborik, and partially closes the Mogilny scoring hole at a fraction of Iginla's cost. We give Chistov (22, POTE 95, SPEE 89, ACCE 88, $1.10M expiring), Colaiacovo (22, POTE 99, $1.10M expiring, 12 points in 31 games but flagged by the Coach as a write-off), Tucker (30, POTE 79, $1.30M) and our single 4th-rounder. That is $3.50M in salary against Havlat's $900K, so we save $2.60M. Ottawa at 77 points with 11 expiring deals and $32.36M profit faces 11 raises simultaneously. If Havlat's next contract lands at $4-5M and ten others need raises too, the aggregate math might force them to let one go. Chistov and Colaiacovo are both 22 with POTE 95 or higher, which is what a 77-point team stocks for. The risk is that $32.36M profit makes re-signing him affordable and 103 points is not a piece any GM gives up lightly. Acceptance uncertain.

**Proposal 3, Stuart from San Jose for Klesla.** Stuart at 25, 87 base, 89 CHKG, 80 TOUG, POTE 91, $1.80M expiring. He replaces Roberts (39, $2.70M, POTE 52) and pairs with Jackman (24, 90 CHKG) on the top side. Klesla at 23, POTE 97, SPEE 88, AGIL 87, 30 points in 82 games, $900M with two years left, is the salary-matching piece. San Jose at $45.39M payroll with 13 expiring deals and $20.74M profit has too many blueliners to re-sign: Brewer, Stuart, McLaren, Mironov are all expiring D. Klesla replaces Stuart at a lower salary ($900K vs $1.80M), younger age (23 vs 25), and higher POTE (97 vs 91). They save $900K and get a better prospect. The cost to us is our highest-POTE young defenseman. The GM's February order said not to sell "core parts of our defense," naming Eminger and McCabe specifically. Klesla is not core by that standard, but the GM may draw the line differently in May than in February. He gets a say.

**These three compete for the same pieces.** Chistov appears in Proposal 2. Upshall appears in Proposal 1. If the GM wants Havlat and Bell, he gives Upshall, Koltsov, Chistov, Colaiacovo, Tucker and the 4th for both. That is six assets for $1.80M of total new salary. The roster thins on the bottom two lines but every player given carries POTE 94+ and no Coach-endorsed top-nine role.

**If none land.** Sign Cammalleri as a UFA (22, POTE 97, $1.10M). Sign Avery as a UFA (93 FACE, 83 TOUG, $400K) for the faceoff minimum even though his 9 points in 82 games caps his value. Use Tucker and the 4th rounder for a 74-76 base depth piece with 75+ TOUG. Toughness below 80 persists unless Bell arrives, because Tucker at 70 TOUG is the internal ceiling and the Coach has confirmed no one else on the bench gets close.

**Task #2 (Luongo/DiPietro monitoring).** Closed per the GM's March 19 order. Luongo is on our roster at 26 with two years and 91 base. Goalie monitoring is finished.

## Owed

**Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development — the goalie trade window task the GM opened on January 19.** This task was formally closed on March 19 when the GM declared the goalie situation solved and ordered all goalie monitoring stopped. I am delivering the final status to confirm closure.

**Luongo** arrived mid-season. He finished at 94 displayed overall on $1.60M with 2 years remaining and 45 starts. The original availability question is resolved: he is Toronto's number one going into next season.

**DiPietro** at NYI: 79 base overall (84 displayed today), 22 years old, $1.10M expiring, 21 GP with a 12-7-0 record. His latest line reads 3.31 GAA on 0.865 save percentage across 1,161 minutes. He is a second-year prospect still developing — not close to Luongo's 94 and not a trade target that would make sense now. At 79 base he is below Tellqvist's trajectory (POTE high 90s per the GM's January read). There is no reason to pursue him.

**What changed since the March 19 closure:** the season ended. Belfour's contract expires (40 years old, $6.50M, 1 year left). The GM's January position was "offer reduced salary at renewal, probably won't accept." That renewal decision is a summer question now, not a trade-window question. Luongo plus Tellqvist covers the position if Belfour walks or retires.

This task is closed. No further monitoring needed.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-23
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-23

Next game vs DAL on Tuesday 24 May 2005.

## Development opportunity

The season is done at 82 games, and we're into playoffs against Dallas, so every development call here is an offseason call. The question is who got the games their production and potential justified, and who didn't.

**Alexeev** is the clearest failure. 30 points in 55 games at 0.55 pts/g, and he can't dress. He outproduces Chistov (0.29 pts/g, 13.1 MPG, third line) and Upshall (0.29 pts/g, 7.9 MPG, fourth line) by nearly double, yet both of those men dress and he doesn't. His morale is 92, the second-lowest among the young guys. I flagged this in April and it's still unresolved. He needs a second-line role next camp or we're wasting a productive winger.

**Spezza** at POTE 99 is the highest scouting number on the roster and the lowest morale among the young group at 88. 15 points in 46 games, 6.7 MPG, now scratched. The season was a write-off from March onward. Offseason decision: real camp audition with a genuine shot at a top-nine role, or move him. A POTE 99 player with 88 morale sitting in the press box is a problem.

**Stahle** at POTE 96 played 4 games all year and scored nothing. 17.8 MPG in those 4 shows the coaching staff gave him a shot and he couldn't hold it. Same camp audition or release call as Spezza.

**Chlup** is the one who's earned everything and got it. 59 points in 71 games at age 19, 16.9 MPG, morale 100. He belongs on the first line. I've recommended that assignment five times and it hasn't been taken, but his development is not at risk; he's getting the minutes and producing.

**Gaborik** at 99 points in 82 games is past the development conversation. He's our best player. Being scratched tonight is a matchup question, not a growth one.

**Nash** at 0.57 pts/g, 13.1 MPG, second line, morale 100 — getting the role his game supports. Spacek, Chistov, Ouellet, Klesla, Eminger: all appropriately deployed for what they're showing tonight. Klesla and Eminger are value cases for the GM, not development ones.

## Development trends

The development window shows one player ascending fast, one ascending slowly, and a mass exodus downward — but the real headline is which defencemen are still worth keeping versus which ones the load is killing.

**Chlup** is the story. 0.62 to 0.88 pts/g while minutes went from 11.0 to 18.2. Rate up with load up is the signature of a player earning trust. He's 19, 71 games in, and he belongs on the first line right now, not "next camp." I've said it four times and he hasn't moved; this trend is only getting harder to ignore.

**Koltsov** at 0.29 pts/g across 38 games on 9.9 MPG is a collapse from 1.10 in 10 games. At 24 with flat minutes, that's not a slump, that's a fit problem. The GM has him as a trading chip, but the chip just lost most of its value. Whoever he's being shipped to is buying a 0.29-rate winger.

**Abid** is worse than my March note. 11.5 MPG now (was 12.6 then, was 20.1 before). Rate down to 0.70. He's being buried and his production is falling with his minutes, which means the role itself is suppressing him. If he doesn't get 15+ MPG next season he should be somewhere else.

**Kaberle** is the only defenceman going the right direction: 0.54 to 0.62 pts/g, minutes from 19.4 to 21.5. At 27 he's entering his prime. No action needed, just confirmation that the GM's instinct to keep him is correct.

**Jackman** at 0.39 on 29.4 MPG across 80 games is the confirmed collapse I flagged in March. The load is destroying his production. Sell at $0.70M x 3 while he still has league-cheap top-pair value.

**Fischer** shows a mild dip (0.63 to 0.50) but his minutes went from 20.8 to 22.9. More ice, slightly less production — that's a two-way defenceman being asked to do more defensively. At 24 this is acceptable.

**Colaiacovo** went 0.44 to 0.36 on 18.9 to 17.5 MPG. Young, getting top-pair minutes, trending slightly down. Watch next season.

**Klesla** and **McCabe** are both confirmed sells. 0.31 and 0.48 respectively on 82 games each. Both already flagged; the season totals lock it.

**Gaborik** at 1.12 on 21.2 MPG at 23 looks like decline from 1.42, but 1.12 is elite. The early number was a hot start. No concern.

**The veterans are all declining as expected by age but getting too many minutes.** Sundin at 34 is 0.97 on 21.7 MPG. Mogilny at 36 is 0.83 on 19.1. Roberts at 39 is 0.86 on 21.4. All three are still top-6 players by production but the minutes should come down. This is a planning flag for camp: if Chlup and a healthy top-six can absorb some load, these three need to drop to 15-17 MPG.

**Spacek and Spezza** are both done for the year at 5.2 and 4.6 MPG respectively. Camp decides their futures.

## Morale watch

The room is right. With 5 games left and a winning stretch running, morale across the roster is at or near ceiling, and every player below 100 is trending up.

**Spezza** sits lowest at 88 but is up 3 from last save. He's a healthy scratch at 6.7 MPG on the season. Nothing I can do about his minutes tonight that doesn't cost a line, and his slide is a season-long issue that belongs in the offseason, not in a May game against Dallas.

**Alexeev** at 92 is up 5. Same story: scratched at 8.3 MPG despite 30 points in 55 games. He's recovering on wins alone. Offseason decision, same as Spezza.

**Spacek** and **Upshall** are both at 94, up 5 and 3 respectively, on the fourth line at 7.6 and 7.9 MPG. That's right at the depth band. They're fine.

Everyone dressed — Jackman at 29.6, Fischer at 22.4, Sundin at 20.3, Richards at 16.1, Kaberle at 20.8 — is at 100 with no movement needed. No one is under their band with morale slipping. No one is carrying minutes they shouldn't.

No change for Tuesday.

## Role composition

The units are correctly assembled; the one structural weakness is faceoffs on the fourth line.

**L1 through K2** are well-profiled for their jobs. L1 has Sundin winning draws at 91, Roberts checking at 85, and Mogilny/Sundin carrying scoring at 93/94. L2 pairs Chlup's 80 faceoffs with Nash and Afinogenov's speed and playmaking. The power plays both score above 87 mean. The first kill gets Sundin/Roberts at checking 79 mean, the second kill gets Tucker (94 checking) alongside Jackman (90) and McCabe (85). Each unit has the attributes its role demands.

**L3** is a speed and secondary-scoring line, not a checking line, and that is correct. Tucker at checking 94 anchors it, Chistov at speed 98 gives a different look, and Richards at clutch 97 closes games. The toughness mean of 66 is the lowest on the roster, but Tucker covers, and Richards at 75 checking is not a liability. No change.

**L4 (Spacek, Abid, Upshall)** has the real problem: faceoff mean 52, nobody above 55. Against Dallas at 42-24-0, a line that cannot win draws will spend its shifts defending in its own end. You cannot fix this by rearranging existing bodies — your three centres are Sundin (91), Chlup (80), Richards (75), and all three are needed where they are. This is a roster gap that needs a trade or waiver acquisition, not a line change.

**Gaborik (98 scoring, 99 playmaking, 99 clutch)** and **Koltsov (99 speed)** sit scratched. On a night against a 42-24 opponent, the GM's standing order says maximize. That is his call on the scratch list, not mine on the lines, but I flag it.

## Opponent matchup

The question is whether this roster is arranged to beat Dallas on Tuesday, and the answer is yes without touching anything.

**DAL's structure:** Their top six is dangerous — Modano 88, Guerin 87, Arnott 87 with 97 shot power — but their bottom eight and their blueline outside Zubov are soft. Second pair is Matvichuk 73 and Berenzweig 68. Third pair is Descoteaux 65 and Richards 65. Those four defencemen combined carry checking grades of 69-90 and speed of 69-80. They are the weakness.

**Our L2 and L3 hit those pairs.** Chlup (86), Nash (83, SHPW 98), and Afinogenov (86, DEKG 98) on our second line face their second pair (68-73). Richards (87), Chistov (82), and Tucker (80) face their third pair (65-65). The auto-pairing puts our D2 and D3 with those forward lines, so we're defending with McCabe/Kaberle and Eminger/Klesla against their Arnott and Barnes lines — both of which are outmanned.

**Their L4 is Gilmour at 41 and Messier at 44.** Our fourth line (Abid 81, Spacek 77, Upshall 79) has speed grades of 74-86 against 72-79. We should own that shift.

**Turco in net is the single obstacle.** OVR 94, GSH_ 96, GSL_ 97, INTE 96. He's matching Luongo rating-for-rating. The way through is volume and shooting from areas where our defensemen have 89-92 SHPW (Jackman 92, Fischer 89, McCabe 89) and from Nash's 98 from the half-wall. DAL's last-10 defensive numbers show 1.70 GA per game, which means they've been tight lately, but their season GA of 232 in 73 games (3.18 per game) says they concede more than their recent form suggests.

**Their PP at 10.8% (32/297)** is manageable. Our PK1 (Fischer, Kaberle, Roberts, Sundin) is built to shut down Modano's feet at 92 speed. No concern there.

**No change.** The lines are right for this opponent.

## Owed

**Defencemen sell-list update:** The season is now final for all top-pair defencemen. The sell list has not changed since May 2nd, but the numbers are now locked rather than projected.

**McCabe** at 0.76 pts/g on 22.1 MPG across 82 games matches my April 7 clearance number, but the May 2nd call stands: his last 58 games rate 0.48. The 0.76 is a hot start carried by a cold finish. At 29, 4 years left, $3.00M, he is sellable while his season total still reads respectably. No change from my last call.

**Jackman** finishes at 0.46 pts/g on 29.6 MPG across 80 games. His OVR 86 makes him the cheapest top-pair minutes available to anyone (0.70M x 3), and that is precisely why someone else should buy him. Sell. Unchanged.

**Klesla** closes at 0.37 pts/g on 14.8 MPG across 82 games. That is a back-to-back decline: 0.38 at 22, 0.37 at 23. His $0.90M x 2 is cheap enough to move. Sell. Unchanged.

**Eminger** at 0.36 pts/g on 15.5 MPG in 64 games, $1.20M expiring. He was already a July deadline on March 30th and the final number is below the threshold I set. He goes before July or we get nothing. Unchanged.

**Kaberle** is the one that needs a decision the GM hasn't made yet: OVR 84, 0.59 pts/g, $1.90M x 1 expiring. The GM called him a keeper and a star. If we keep him, he needs a renewal. If we don't, we should sell him while a keeper-quality defenceman is on an expiring deal and someone else's money problem. This is new: last time I delivered this job, the renewal urgency was a month away. It is now here.
