# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-21

Toronto 59-13-5, 133 pts after 82 games.

## Role coverage

The question this phase answers: where is this roster structurally short, and can the coach close it by shifting men around or does it require a trade? The season is over at 59-13-5, and the answer determines what the July shop looks like.

**Toughness** is missing. Zero players at 80+ base; Jackman tops the club at 75, Roberts 73, McCabe 73. The coach quantified it in April: checking mean 61, toughness mean 57 on the fourth line, and he stated no bench player fixes it. The Feb 21 reading of "six players at TOUG 80+" was almost certainly form-boosted displayed grades, since stored grades do not move and every subsequent reading confirms zero. This is a hard gap. Bell (CHI, 24, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE) remains the only player who closes toughness, checking and faceoffs simultaneously.

**Faceoffs** are missing below line one. Sundin at 90 is the only 80+ draw-taker on the roster. Chlup 75 at 19 games is the next best. Tucker at 67 cannot win draws on the fourth line, and the coach measured L4 mean at 52 with best 55. Avery (LA, 93 FACE, $400K, 2 years) is the cheapest fix for this single gap. Bell closes it too but costs more.

**Checking** is thin but coverable. Jackman 87 (24), McCabe 86 (29), Fischer 82 (24) are all young. Tucker at 83 (30) is the fourth body. Six at 80+ is one fewer than a full four-line complement, but the age curve is right: Jackman and McCabe are still climbing, and Tucker can dress nightly as the fifth checker. This does not require an acquisition unless someone leaves.

**Scoring** is enough today (ten at 80+) and missing next year. Mogilny 94 (36), Sundin 92 (34), Roberts 88 (38) carry the top grades. The youngest 80+ scorer is Gaborik at 23, but he read 92 base and was not lined all season, which says something about his role in this system. Afinogenov at 90 (25) is the bridge candidate but needs a system-fit review the coach already requested. The Iginla target (27, 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, $6.50M expiring, CGY profit $14.43M) is the acquisition that closes this gap.

**Speed** and **stamina** are enough. Twenty-one at 80+ speed, eleven at 80+ stamina. No gap to fix.

**Durability** is thin at four (Roberts 98 at 38, Afinogenov 95, Fischer 92, Abid 90). When Roberts is gone, it drops to three. Not urgent, but the depth group needs someone durable.

**Goalies** are covered: Luongo 90 base at 26 with two years, Belfour 93 base at 40 expiring. The GM's March order stands: keep both for the playoff, do not revisit. Ouellet at 23 with ENDU 60 and INTE 69 is not ready for a starting role. Tellqvist at 25 carries high-90s POTE but read 80 GSH_ this year, consistent with the standing order to give him time.

## Trajectory

The question this phase answers: does Toronto age into a cliff or a controlled transition, and can the money support the fix?

**The age shape is good.** 25 of 30 players are 29 or under, 13 of them 23 or younger. The cliff isn't coming in the next two years — it's the 34+ band (Sundin 34, Mogilny 36, Roberts 38, Belfour 40) that holds the scoring, and two of them (Roberts, Belfour) expire in July anyway. The real risk is not aging into a cliff but losing the young core to free agency because 13 contracts worth $21.30M all expire at once and the renewal window is chaotic.

**Gaborik is the whole problem.** 99 points at 23 years old for $1.10M. If he walks and the club re-signs at market (say $5-6M), the loss is not just salary — it's 99 points of production with no in-house replacement. Richards at 66 pts and $1.00M, Abid at 66 pts and $0.40M, Nash at 39 pts and $1.20M with POTE 95 are all in the same boat. These five alone represent roughly 270 points of proven production walking on pennies.

**Sundin anchors the future payroll.** $8.40M for five more years at age 34, POTE 60 (development is done). He's producing 91 pts now but the curve only points down. Nothing can be done mid-contract, but this $42M commitment runs through age 39 and constrains every future renewal.

**Mogilny at $5.50M/2 years** is smaller but the same shape: 84 pts at 36, POTE 55. He'll be 38 when the deal expires. The 24-29 bridge group (Richards 66, Abid 66, McCabe 62, Afinogenov 54) is deep enough to carry the load if signed and if Iginla or a similar piece arrives. The cliff is manageable.

**The money is ample.** $48.88M profit against $121.34M revenue. Adding Iginla at $6.50M brings payroll to roughly $66M. Renewing five stars at market rates adds perhaps $12-15M in new money. Total payroll lands around $78-80M. Still well inside revenue. The constraint is not "can we afford it" but "can we negotiate 13 deals in one window without overpaying any of them."

**Draft capital is a vacuum.** One fourth-rounder. Every summer package must be player-funded. Tucker (30, POTE 79, 1 pt in 3 GP, $1.30M/2yrs) is the only chip the GM has authorized moving. The over-80 expiring pick mechanic applies to Roberts (92 base, expiring, 38) if he's traded rather than released. That's the only pick recovery available.

## Calendar

The trade deadline passed on 2005-03-19, sixty-three days ago, and the summer renewal window is now the only calendar item that matters. Toronto are first in the East at 133 points with six games left, so the sequence is: finish the season, play in the playoffs, then rebuild the roster through thirteen expiring contracts and at least one big free-agent signing. The GM's standing orders from the deadline period (keep Belfour and Luongo, only Tucker and the 4th round pick as chips) closed the deadline question. What remains is who renews, who leaves, and who walks in.

**The deadline is closed.** We were not buyers at it. The GM kept the core, kept both goalies, and left only Tucker and a fourth-rounder on the block. No further deadline analysis is needed. The plan shifts entirely to the summer.

**Playoffs come first.** Toronto at 59-13-5 are the top seed in the East. Per the manual, raise ticket prices through the rounds: roughly 75 in round one, 80 in round two, 90 in conference finals, 100 in the final. Revenue follows.

**Gaborik** is the single most important renewal in the summer. Age 23, 91 base overall, 67 points in 45 games, POTE 90, $1.10M expiring. He is the best player on the expiring list by a wide margin. Lock him on 6 years to separate his next expiry from the 5-year deals below.

**Nash and Eminger** go on 6 years too. Nash is 20 at $1.20M; Eminger is 21 at $1.20M with POTE 99, and the GM protected him explicitly on 2005-02-19. Two more years of separation from the Kaberle/Richards deals.

**Kaberle and Richards** go on 5 years. Kaberle is 27 at $1.90M, the core right-shot defenseman. Richards is 25 at $1.00M with 70 FACE and 85 PASS, already the projected third-line centre. Five years on the older two, six on the younger three, gives at least one year of spread before the next cluster hits.

**Abid, Alexeev and Tellqvist** go on 2-3 years. Abid is 25 at $0.40M and the Coach wants 18+ minutes a night; cheap enough to renew on merit. Alexeev is 23 at $1.10M with 0.55 pts/g outproducing both dressed wingers, but his role depends on camp. Tellqvist is 25 at $0.80M with POTE in the high 90s; the GM's standing order from January was to give him time, so renew on a short deal and keep him as depth.

**Roberts** lets go. He is 38 at $2.70M. At that age the manual says 2 years, but the better move is to release and redirect the money. Stuart (SJ, 25, 87 base, POTE 91) was already identified as the replacement in March.

**Belfour** is the hardest decision. He is 40 at $6.50M expiring. The GM's February standing order was to offer a reduced contract, expecting Belfour to decline. Luongo at 91 base with 2 years left is the number one; Tellqvist is the backup-in-waiting. If Belfour walks in July, that $6.50M is exactly the money that funds an Iginla signing, and the playoff roster already carries two 90+ goalies regardless.

**Colaiacovo, Chistov and Upshall** all face camp in the fall. Colaiacovo is 22 at $1.10M with POTE 99 but the Coach called him a development write-off on 2005-05-15 after 31 games at 17.9 MPG. Chistov is 22 at $1.10M with POTE 95 but Alexeev displaces him on the wing. Upshall is 21 at $1.20M with a camp audition and no guaranteed role. If any of the three fails to earn minutes, trade the one whose POTE still carries value (Chistov and Colaiacovo both at 95+ ) rather than letting him walk for nothing. The over-80-expiring mechanic converts them into a draft pick if they reach that threshold on the trade screen.

**Iginla (CGY, 27, 93 base, 140 points in 73 games, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring) is the July signing priority.** He closes both the Mogilny scoring void and the structural toughness ceiling that the Coach quantified on 2005-04-09 (checking mean 61, toughness mean 57 on the fourth line). CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring contracts and $14.43M in profit cannot retain him. The Belfour money funds the signing.

**Cammalleri (LA, 22, POTE 98, 60 points in 61 games, $1.10M expiring) is the value signing.** LA at 79 points with 14 expiring contracts cannot hold both him and Frolov. At $1.10M he costs less than any single player we are letting go and brings the highest POTE on the open market.

**Bell (CHI, 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE) closes the faceoff and toughness gap in one player.** CHI at 73 points with 10 expiring and $29.46M in profit are motivated sellers. His ENDU of 71 means short shifts initially, but he is the only league-wide player who fixes both structural problems the Coach has flagged.

**The draft on 2005-06-08** is a minor item. Toronto own no pick better than a fourth-rounder. The GM's standing order from January is to scout for goalies in the later rounds, which is cheap insurance given that Tellqvist's development is uncertain. Auto-draft is adequate at this scouting level.



**Task #2** (Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window): delivered and closed. Luongo is on our roster at 91 base with 2 years left, confirmed 2005-02-07. The GM's 2005-03-19 standing order closed all goalie monitoring. No further action needed.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: which specific players across the league close Toronto's structural gaps, and which of their clubs will actually move them this July.

The season is over, the roster is set for the playoff run, and every acquisition decision now belongs to July. The gaps are toughness (zero players at 80+ TOUG), faceoffs below line one (L4 mean 52), and the scoring bridge behind Mogilny, Sundin and Roberts (three players, combined 426 points, all 34+). Draft capital is one fourth-rounder, so every move must be player-funded or UFA.

**Iginla** is the priority. 93 base, 140 points in 73 games at 27, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring. He closes the scoring void and the toughness ceiling in one move. CGY sit at 70 points with 10 expiring contracts and $14.43M profit — a club in directionless rebuild that cannot justify keeping a 27-year-old on $6.50M without a playoff window. The problem is price: our only authorized chips are Tucker and a 4th. This likely routes through free agency or requires the GM to authorize more pieces in July.

**Bell** is the second priority and the only player who simultaneously fixes toughness (88 TOUG), checking (86 CHKG), and faceoffs (82 FACE). At 24 with POTE 81 he's a bridge piece, not a rental. CHI are 78 points, 10 expiring, $31.73M profit — profitable enough that they won't dump cheaply, but not contending either. The Jan 25 reading put him at $900K/2yr; if that holds he's a bargain. If CHI want a first-round pick we don't have, he goes to the UFA pool instead.

**Kovalchuk** and **Heatley** are a binary. ATL at 84 points with the league's cheapest payroll ($36.79M) and 11 expiring contracts cannot re-sign both. Kovalchuk at 21, 89 base, 104 pts/61 GP carries the higher ceiling; Heatley at 24, 91 base, 96 pts/58 GP carries the higher floor. Either one gives us a second elite winger beside Gaborik. We should prepare to pursue whichever ATL lets go — the club will signal by mid-June which one they're retaining.

**Theodore** answers the goalie question the Jan 15 order set: "a really good high-90s goalie from a team that will not be a contender." MTL are 66 points, the worst record in the league, with 15 expiring contracts. Theodore is 91 base, 28 years old, $5.50M expiring, POTE 87. They MUST shed salary to rebuild. After Belfour walks this summer we have Luongo at 90 and nobody proven behind him. Theodore is the answer.

**Stuart** replaces Roberts on the blue line. 87 base at 25, 89 CHKG, 80 TOUG, POTE 91. SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring on $45.39M must cut someone. The risk flagged in March holds: at 76 points they're not tanking, and a POTE 91 defenceman is the kind of player a rebuilding GM holds rather than moves. Worth probing but lower probability than Theodore or the ATL wings.

**Cammalleri** is the best UFA value available. 22, POTE 98, 60 pts/61 GP on $1.10M. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring cannot retain everyone. No trade asset leaves our books — just a contract offer. At 22 with that potential he's the cheapest insurance against the scoring bridge failing.

**Daze** is the fallback if Iginla signs elsewhere. 89 base, 127 pts/82 GP, $3.00M expiring, age 29. Half a decade shorter runway than Iginla but same production tier at less than half the salary. CHI at 78 with 10 expiring are motivated to move expiring talent. He's a bridge, not a solution.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: what do we put on the table for Bell and Theodore, and does the GM authorize Chistov and Ouellet beyond the Tucker-plus-a-fourth mandate from March 19? The season is over, Belfour walks in July, and the only pieces that reach these targets are players the coach has flagged but the GM has not yet released.

**Bell** is the priority. One player closes toughness (88 TOUG), checking (86 CHKG), and faceoffs (82 FACE) — the three gaps the coach measured and confirmed no internal fix exists for. At $900K on two years he's the cheapest high-impact acquisition available. The package: Chistov (22, POTE 95, SPEE 89, ACCE 88, $1.10M/1yr) plus Tucker ($1.30M/2yr) plus the 4th-rounder. CHI sit at 78 points with 10 expiring contracts and $31.73M profit. They are rebuilding and want ceiling over floor: Chistov's POTE 95 exceeds Bell's POTE 81, and they add a depth checking wing and a pick. We save $2.60M net on payroll; CHI absorb $2.60M against $31.73M profit, which is noise for them. The coach explicitly told us Chistov is available as a trade piece on May 5.

**Theodore** is the second priority. 91 base, 28 years old, $5.50M expiring, POTE 87 — the high-90s goalie the January standing order demanded, from the 66-point team that cannot retain him. He walks for nothing in July if MTL do not move him, so anything they receive is a gain. Package: Ouellet (23, POTE 97, GSH_ 86, $0.90M/2yr) plus the 4th-rounder. MTL collect a premium goalie prospect and a pick for a player they lose for free. We absorb $5.50M this year but Theodore is expiring, so the real question is the renewal, which we negotiate in July 2006. Tellqvist (POTE in the high 90s) stays as the development path behind Theodore and Luongo.

**The pick problem:** both packages want the 4th and Tucker. If the GM wants both Bell and Theodore, allocate them: Chistov + Tucker for Bell (Chistov alone is the value driver; his POTE 95 exceeds Bell's 81), and Ouellet + the 4th for Theodore. This strips the sweeteners from each and reduces the odds. If the GM picks one, load the full package onto it and the acceptance probability rises materially.

## Owed

**The question this answers:** The GM asked on 2005-01-19 to monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro development through February for a goalie trade window. He then closed that task on 2005-03-19 with "Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks. Goalies are solved. Done." This is a delivery of closure.

**Luongo** is on our roster at 94 overall, 26 years old, $1.60M, 2 years remaining, 45 games played. He was at 91 base when acquired in February. Three points of development across the back half of the season confirms the ceiling is real. He and Belfour are the two 90+ goalies the GM committed to keeping.

**DiPietro** — the reason the GM named him was as a potential long-term target from a non-contender. The task is closed and the order says not to revisit goalies. No update needed.

**Belfour** at 93, age 40, $6.50M expiring. He's the remaining question for next season at renewal, but that is a July contract decision, not a monitoring task.

This item is delivered and closed. Nothing has changed since the March 19 kill order; the roster now holds two 90+ goalies and the GM's standing instruction says goalies are solved.

# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-21

Next game at DAL on Sunday 22 May 2005.

## Development opportunity

The season is done at 82 games and we're in a playoff series, so this is the wrap-up: who got the games their potential demanded and who didn't. Three young players were starved of ice, and two of them carry the two highest scouting grades on the roster.

**Spezza** is the biggest waste. POTE 99, 6.7 MPG across 46 games, 15 points. He's been on the roster all year and barely seen the ice. The season is a write-off for him; the only lever left is what he walks into at camp next September. He needs a real audition in a top-six role or we stop pretending he's part of the plan.

**Alexeev** scored 30 points in 55 games, 0.55 a night, on 8.3 MPG, and is still a scratch. Chistov and Upshall both sit at 0.29 on 13 MPG each and dress ahead of him. That mismatch has been flagged since April and nobody has fixed it. He's 23 now, which is the age where you either give him a lineup spot or you're wasting a tradeable asset.

**Colaiacovo** gets 17.9 MPG when he suits up, which is top-pair minutes, but he's only played 31 of 82. POTE 99. When the GM rotates him in, he looks like a keeper. The problem is the other 51 games. Next year needs a clear pairing job for him or he's wasting in the rotation.

**Chlup** finished 59 points in 71 games on 16.9 MPG at age 19. He's on the second line and has been for months. I've recommended moving him to first line since April and it hasn't happened. This is still the right call for next season.

**Stahle** played 4 games. POTE 96 but no path on this blue line. The GM needs to tell him he's a trade chip or find him a role, because 4 games at 21 does nothing for anyone.

**Spacek** at 7.6 MPG and 0.34 pts/g is getting what his fourth-line role provides. That's appropriate. **Upshall** at 7.9 MPG and 0.29 is the same story, but POTE 99 means he deserves one honest camp audition before we write him off. **Nash** at 13.1 MPG and 0.57 is system-fit flagged, not a minutes problem. **Gaborik** at 99 points and 20.5 MPG needs nothing. **Eminger** and **Klesla** are sell candidates, not development cases.

## Development trends

The season is effectively over with 6 games left, so this window is the final read on every player and the offseason plans should key off it.

**Gaborik** is the one to build around after Chlup. His recent window is 1.12 pts/g on 21.2 MPG at age 23, and both are up from his early-season 1.42 on 18.8. The 0.30 rate drop looks like early-season hot-start normalization, not decline. He should get every minute available next season.

**Chlup** at 0.88 pts/g on 18.2 MPG at 19 confirms he is the first-line centre. That assignment is overdue; stop treating it as a camp decision.

**Kaberle** is the other riser nobody talks about. 0.54→0.62 pts/g at 27 on minutes up from 19.4 to 21.5. He is 27, improving, and the GM already called him the star. The trend backs that call.

**Chistov** is the quiet surprise. Minutes went from 9.5 to 14.0 at age 22 and his rate held at 0.30. Someone gave him a bigger role and he did not drown. That earns him a roster spot conversation this summer, not a scratch bin.

**Abid** is the problem. Minutes collapsed from 20.1 to 11.5 MPG and his rate fell from 1.09 to 0.70. I flagged this in March when he needed 18+ MPG; he got 11.5 instead. At 25 with 82 games played, he is a quality winger being buried. Either he gets first-line minutes next season or we move him while he still carries value at 0.70 on 11.5. The rate decline is likely role-driven, not age-driven.

**Spacek** is dead. 0.28 pts/g on 5.2 MPG at 19. The March write-off call was correct and the final numbers make it worse, not better. Camp audition or stop dressing him.

**Nash** at 0.42 on flat 13.2 MPG is a system-fit problem, same as Afinogenov and Richards. Three players, same pattern: flat role, halved rate. That is a coaching issue to solve before next camp, not three individual decline stories.

**Klesla, Jackman, McCabe** all confirmed sells. Klesla 0.31 at 23, Jackman 0.39 at 24 on 29 MPG, McCabe 0.48 at 29. These are final numbers now; the offseason is the window.

**The veterans:** Sundin at 0.97 on 21.7 MPG at 34 is still excellent. Mogilny 0.83 at 36, Roberts 0.86 at 38. Both are producing but neither will hold that next year. The transition plan should start with Chlup, Gaborik and whatever Abid's situation resolves to.

No grade changes moved on the card this window, so everything here rests on production and minutes.

## Morale watch

The room is right. Every player on the roster sits at 88 or above, and the trend is overwhelmingly positive — nearly every man gained 3 to 5 points since the last save, which tracks with recent wins doing their work.

**Spezza** is the only player below 90 at 88, and he gained 3 since last read. At 6.7 MPG and 15 points in 46 games he's buried, and my March note flagged his collapse from 9.1 to 4.8 MPG. He's now at 6.7 and climbing in morale, so the losing is no longer the problem. No intervention needed before the season's over.

Everyone else is either at or above their expected minutes band for their calibre, or the gap is small enough that morale hasn't registered it. Tucker at 9.0 MPG in 3 games sits at 100. Upshall at 7.9 and Spacek at 7.6 are depth men right at the 7-MPG band, both at 94 and rising. No one is under-carried or over-asked enough to flag.

## Role composition

The units are mostly right; one structural problem persists that no rearrangement fixes.

**L1** — Sundin, Roberts, Mogilny, Jackman, Fischer. Checking 79, scoring 88, speed 91. Roberts at 85 checking and Fischer at 85 checking give the blue line and wing real two-way legs under the skill. Nothing wrong here.

**L2** — Chlup, McCabe, Kaberle, Nash, Afinogenov. This is a scoring line, and it should be. Afinogenov at 92 scoring, Chlup at 80 faceoffs, McCabe at 85 checking giving Kaberle the defensive half. The faceoff mean of 59 reflects Nash and Kaberle pulling it down; that's acceptable on a second line with Chlup taking the draws.

**L3** — Eminger, Tucker, Richards, Klesla, Chistov. Richards at 97 clutch and 87 stamina is the anchor the young guys need. Chistov at 98 speed gives energy. Tucker at checking 94 is the one providing the grit; the mean of 75 means he's carrying it alone. Developmental, not a problem to solve now.

**L4** — Spacek, Abid, Upshall. Faceoff mean 52, best 55. Nobody on this line can win a draw. Abid at 72 toughness is the hardest man; checking mean 74 is thin. This is the same gap I raised in April and the roster hasn't changed.

**K2** (Chlup, Tucker, McCabe, Jackman) is genuinely good: checking mean 84, toughness 72. That's a shutdown unit. No change needed.

**Roster gap.** The faceoff problem on the fourth line is unfixable with what we have. Sundin (91), Chlup (80), Roberts (76) and Richards (75) are the only centre-quality faceoff men, and all four are already on L1–L3. A bottom-six centre who wins 55%+ draws would close it. I raise it as the GM's problem, not mine.

## Opponent matchup

**Modano is the problem.** At 88 OVR with 94 PUCK, 94 DEKG, 93 HERO and 94 ENDU, he is the most complete player on the sheet tonight. His first line with Guerin (87, TOUG 88, SHPW 92) and Morrow (84, DEKG 92) is genuinely dangerous — their whole last-10 is 2.9 goals for and 1.7 against on the back of that line. But we have handled them: 2-0-0 head-to-head, 8-3 on the scoresheet.

**Turco (94 OVR, 96 GSH, 97 GSL, 96 INTE) is going to be in the way.** We will not beat him with volume. We beat him with the mismatches below: DAL's second pair is Matvichuk (73) and Berenzweig (68), their third is Descoteaux (65) and D. Richards (65). That is four bottom-pair defenders averaging 67 OVR. Our depth across four forward lines is the structural advantage and it does not require a shuffle.

**Their power play is 32 on 297, which is 10.8%.** The PK units are not tested tonight. Their PK is equally irrelevant in the other direction: we score on the PP at will (32 on 99 is 32.3%).

**No line change is needed.** The current configuration already puts our best D (Fischer 85 / Jackman 86) behind our best forward line, gives Chlup's speed line solid coverage in Kaberle and McCabe, and matches Tucker (CHKG 90, TOUG 86) onto Arnott (TOUG 88, SHPW 97) at even strength via the third line. Our depth and their soft bottom-pair defence do the rest.

**Goalie: start Luongo, check the fatigue icon before confirming.** Standing order from January 19.

## Owed

The D sell list. The season is final; every number below is locked.

**McCabe** — 82 GP, 62 pts (0.76 pts/g), 22.1 MPG, 84 OVR, 29 years, $3.00M x 4. Same verdict as May 2: sell. His last 58 games ran 0.48 pts/g. The $3.00M cap hit for a defenceman past his peak is four more years of dead weight.

**Jackman** — 80 GP, 37 pts (0.46 pts/g), 29.6 MPG, 86 OVR, 24 years, $0.70M x 3. Confirmed sell at 0.46 over the full year, down slightly from the 0.48 I cited in March. His trade value is 30 MPG at $0.70M — the cheapest top-pair minutes in the league. Any club with cap room pays for that.

**Klesla** — 82 GP, 30 pts (0.37 pts/g), 14.8 MPG, 84 OVR, 23 years, $0.90M x 2. Two consecutive declining seasons (0.38 then 0.37). Sell.

**Eminger** — 64 GP, 23 pts (0.36 pts/g), 15.5 MPG, 77 OVR, 21 years, $1.20M x 1, expiring. He is a UFA loss if we do not move him before camp. More urgent than it was in March: the deadline to get anything back is the next trade window or he walks for nothing.

**Kaberle** — 74 GP, 44 pts (0.59 pts/g), 20.8 MPG, 84 OVR, 27 years, $1.90M x 1. This is the one new item. His contract expires after next season. The GM called him a star and a keeper in January, and the production backs that up. If we do not extend him before he hits UFA, we lose a 0.59-rate top-pair defenceman for nothing. That needs to be on the GM's list alongside the sells.

**Fischer** — 77 GP, 41 pts (0.53 pts/g), 22.4 MPG, 85 OVR, 24 years, $3.70M x 4. Locked up. No action needed.

Nothing has moved since my last delivery on May 17. The only new flag is Kaberle's expiring deal.

# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-19

Toronto 59-13-5, 133 pts after 82 games.

## Role coverage

The season is over at 59-13-5, so this is the last clean look at the roster before July planning. Two structural gaps are confirmed: toughness and faceoffs. Everything else is either covered or will fix itself through development or age.

**Toughness is the one missing role.** Zero Toronto skaters carry a shipped TOUG above 80. The highest is **Jackman** at 75, then **Roberts** at 73 (age 38) and **McCabe** at 73. The Coach quantified the L4 toughness mean at 57 on 2005-05-05, which matches. This is not a form problem. The Feb 21 report claiming six players at TOUG 80+ was reading displayed grades inflated by engine form; the shipped numbers the role sheet uses show the truth. I am retiring that contradiction note. Bell (CHI, LW, 24, shipped TOUG 88, CHKG 86, FACE 82) remains the only league-wide player closing both this gap and the faceoff gap at once.

**Faceoffs are thin, and the one man holding the fort is 34.** Sundin is at shipped FACE 90 (displayed 91), the only Toronto player above 80. Chlup is next at shipped 75, displayed 80, with POTE 96 at age 19. The L4 mean is 52. No internal move closes this. Avery (LA, C, 25, FACE 93, TOUG 83, CHKG 88, $0.40M, 2 years) remains the cheapest fix for all three gaps simultaneously; Bell is the highest-ceiling option.

**Durability is thinner than it looks.** Only four players carry INJU above 80: Roberts 98, Afinogenov 95, Fischer 92, Abid 90. The four most important skaters are all fragile: Gaborik INJU 52, Richards 53, Sundin 57, Mogilny at 36 on a declining engine. An injury cluster among the top three centers or wings collapses the lineup in a way this roster's depth cannot absorb.

**Scoring and playmaking are covered this year, gone in two.** Mogilny 94 (36), Sundin 92 (34), Roberts 88 (38) carry the production, and the scoring-bridge void from May 15 still stands: no player under 30 is positioned to absorb 426 combined points. **Gaborik** at 91 base (23) is the heir apparent, but he is currently unlined and his INJU 52 makes him a high-variance foundation. **Iginla** (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, $6.50M expiring) remains the July priority for the RW seat that Mogilny vacates.

**Speed is the deepest role on the roster.** 21 skaters above 80. **Gaborik** 98, **Afinogenov** 96, **Koltsov** 92, **Fischer** 89. Koltsov at 24 with 92 speed is listed as not lined; if he is healthy, the Coach should find a reason to dress him, because depth this young and fast is cheap insurance against the durability problem above.

**Checking is adequate.** Six at shipped 80+. Roberts (38) walks next season, leaving five: Jackman 87, McCabe 86, Tucker 83, Fischer 82, Upshall 80. That is enough for a playoff team.

**Goalies are covered, with one open question.** Luongo (26, $1.60M, 2y) has core grades of 94/94/89/85 and is the number one for years. Belfour (40, $6.50M, 1y) has INJU-grade stats but an expiring contract and the GM's stated worry about retirement. Ouellet (23, $0.90M, 2y) provides backup depth. No roster gap here.



**Deliverable #2 (Luongo/DiPietro monitoring):** Complete. Luongo is on the roster at 91 base, 2 years, $1.60M, with core grades 94/94/89/85. The GM closed all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19. DiPietro tracking is moot under that order. No further action required.

## Trajectory

The trajectory question is whether July 2005 is a controlled transition or a structural break, and the answer is: controlled, but only if the renewal sequence is deliberate, because 13 contracts worth $21.30M expire at once and three of the four biggest scorers are 34 or older.

**The age shape is right.** Thirteen players 23 or under, twelve at 24-29, one at 30-33 (Tucker, 3 GP, 1 pt), four at 34+. That is the manual's target shape nearly to the letter: 26 young players and four veterans. The veterans are Sundin (34, POTE 60), Mogilny (36, POTE 55), Roberts (38, POTE 52), Belfour (40, POTE 50). All four are declining and three of them walk or should. No cliff arrives all at once; Mogilny has two years, Roberts and Belfour one. The bridge is being built by Chlup (19, 59 pts), Nash (20, 39 pts), and Gaborik (23, 99 pts).

**Gaborik is the single point of failure.** 99 points, $1.10M, one year left, POTE 90. If he walks, Toronto loses its only player already producing at a franchise-star level. Renew him on 5-6 years before anything else happens in July. Richards (25, 66 pts, $1.00M) is the second priority: he anchors the third line today and his replacement would cost a mid-80 forward on $3M+.

**The money is not the problem.** Payroll $60.04M, revenue $121.34M, profit $46.70M. Losing Belfour ($6.50M) and Roberts ($2.70M) frees $9.20M. Re-signing the young core at market rates (roughly 3-4x their current bargain contracts, so $25-30M in new salary replacing their current $11.10M) puts payroll near $70M against $121M revenue. Profit stays above $30M. Every renewal is affordable. The constraint is negotiation order, not money.

**Draft capital is zero and that is the long-term risk.** One fourth-rounder from 2005 onward. Every prospect the club develops came from the draft, and the club cannot replenish the farm without picks. Chistov (22, POTE 95, tradeable per Coach) and Tucker (30, 1 pt, 3 GP) are the only movable pieces. Any deal for them must return at least a 2nd or 3rd-rounder, or the developmental engine that produced Chlup, Nash, Eminger, and Colaiacovo stalls.

**The scoring bridge has a two-year gap.** Roberts walks (81 pts), Mogilny declines toward free agency in 2006 (84 pts today, POTE 55). Between now and Chlup reaching 70+ points, the only player under 26 producing above 40 is Gaborik. The Iginla target (93 base, 140 pts, $6.50M expiring, CGY cannot retain) closes this immediately. If CGY will deal him for a package built around Chlup or Chistov plus picks, it's worth the cost.

## Calendar

The deadline is 61 days gone and the season is done; the only calendar left is the one that decides this roster's shape, and the answer is: renew nine of the thirteen expirings, let one walk, and make two conditional on camp.

**Gaborik** is the single most urgent item in the building. He's 23, 91 base, POTE 90, $1.10M, and the other 29 clubs know it the moment the window opens. A 5-6 year lock has to happen before any other renewal is even discussed.

**Kaberle** at 27 and **Richards** at 25 are both at their second-best contract years. Five to six on each. **Eminger** at 21 with POTE 99 gets the same term — the GM vetoed trading him in January specifically because his development isn't finished. **Nash** at 20, 5-6 years. These four locks cost nothing they wouldn't cost anyway at $1.00–$1.90M each and remove four of the thirteen from next summer's negotiation table.

**Belfour** is the hard one. At 40 and $6.50M, the GM's own January position was "offer reduced, he probably won't accept." Luongo at 25, 91 base is the future number one. The move is a one-year offer at a cut to roughly $3.00M as a bridge mentor; if Belfour declines, let him walk and run Luongo plus Tellqvist. Do not chase a multi-year deal for a 40-year-old.

**Roberts** at 38 and $2.70M is a let-go. The Coach flagged system-fit concerns, and at 38 his trajectory is down regardless. The 426 combined points he shares with Mogilny and Sundin are gone next year; the Iginla target (CGY, 27, 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP) is the structural fix, not Roberts on a short deal.

**Tellqvist** stays per the GM's standing order — POTE high 90s, 25, $0.80M. Three years, cheap insurance behind Luongo. **Abid** at $0.40M with TOUG 80 and CHKG 80 is the cheapest toughness on the roster; two years.

**Alexeev**, **Chistov**, **Colaiacovo**, and **Upshall** are conditional. Coach demands real camp auditions for all four before finalising roles. Renew at 2-3 years only if they make the lineup. If Chistov (POTE 95, SPEE 89) doesn't stick top-nine, he's the most tradeable of the group. If Colaiacovo stalls again at 31 games, he's a chip, not a prospect.

The draft on June 8 is one fourth-rounder. Nothing to execute there. The real action is the re-signing window, which the calendar shows in the last week of June.

## League scan

The July market is built around three things we need and three clubs that must sell: RW scoring for Mogilny's void, toughness and faceoffs for the structural gaps, and a scoring bridge while Chlup develops. CGY, ATL and LA are the clubs to work.

**Iginla** remains target number one. 93 base, RW, 27, TOUG 87, 140 pts/73 GP, $6.50M expiring. CGY sits at 70 points with 10 expiring contracts and $14.43M profit. They cannot build a contender around a 70-point team carrying $45.93M payroll, and Iginla's $6.50M on a non-contender is a rebuild signal. Package: Chistov (22, POTE 95) plus Colaiacovo (22, POTE 99) plus the 4th-rounder fills his need for youth and picks simultaneously.

**Heatley** is the ATL binary. ATL at 84 points holds both Heatley (91 base, RW, 24, 131 pts/79 GP) and Kovalchuk (89 base, LW, 22, 138 pts/79 GP) on $1.10M expiring deals. They keep one and trade the other or lose him for nothing. Heatley is the RW we need. Chistov plus a second-round pick is the package to test.

**Bell** is the only league-wide player closing toughness and faceoffs simultaneously at a price we can afford. 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, 80 base, age 24, $900K, 2 years left. CHI at 78 points with $31.73M profit and 10 expiring contracts is rebuilding. Their priority dumps are Zhamnov ($4.20M) and Daze ($3.00M), so Bell moves only if we make them an offer — a 2nd-rounder or a young D like Fischer (40, 2 years, $350K). Low priority for them to deal, but cheap enough that any pick helps.

**Conroy** is the bridge. FACE 94, 102 pts/82 GP, 33 years old, $2.00M expiring, CGY. At 33 he is a two-year solution, but he solves the L1C faceoff problem AND the scoring void in one move while Chlup matures. The price should be low: Tucker plus a 3rd. CGY is rebuilding and Conroy at $2.00M on a 70-point team is salary they will not extend.

**Cammalleri** is the best UFA value in July. POTE 97, 79 base, 60 pts/61 GP, $1.10M expiring, age 22, RW. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring cannot retain him, Frolov, Allison ($6.70M expiring), Deadmarsh ($2.80M), Svehla ($3.60M), and Cechmanek ($3.30M) simultaneously. Sign him in July without a trade.

**Begin** is a ghost. FACE 86, TOUG 87, CHKG 95 at age 26, $936K, 2 years. Those three grades together are better than Avery's or Bell's. No production data in the queries (GP and points blank), so I cannot say whether he plays. BUF at 84 points with $24.30M profit are not sellers. Low probability but the grades say he is worth a phone call in July if his GP confirms he is playable.

**Belanger** is the cheapest faceoff fix in the league. FACE 97 at $700K, age 27, LA, 14 pts/64 GP. A pure specialist. At $700K he costs almost nothing and raises the L4 draw from 52 to 97. LA might not bother trading him because the contract is trivial. Low cost, low return, but the fix is real.

**What I would not do:** Chase Kovalchuk (LW, not our position of need). Chase Daze at 29 (one-year rental, POTE 77, no future). Spend the 4th-rounder on Belanger or Avery when the cheaper fix is signing Cammalleri and keeping Tucker as a sweetener for Conroy or Heatley.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: what packages can we actually build with one POTE 95 chip, one expiring 30-year-old, and a 4th-round pick, and which of them will a rebuilding GM say yes to?

**Heatley from ATL is the primary target.** ATL holds both Heatley (91 base, RW, 24, 131 pts/79 GP, $1.10M expiring) and Kovalchuk (89 base, LW, 22, 138 pts/79 GP, $1.10M expiring) at 84 points with $43.29M profit. They keep the 22-year-old and must move the 24-year-old or lose him for nothing. Chistov (22, POTE 95, SPEE 89, ACCE 88, $1.10M expiring) is their exact rebuild profile: young, fast, high potential, cheap. The 4th-rounder is a throw-in. Our payroll is unchanged: both deals are $1.10M.

**Conroy from CGY is the best second move.** 70 points, 10 expiring, $14.43M profit. Conroy at 33, $2.00M, FACE 94, 102 pts/82 GP is salary they will not extend. Tucker (30, CHKG 92, TOUG 88, $1.30M, 2 years) is cheap veteran checking that fills a mentorship slot on their young roster. Without a pick this is a tough ask; CGY may want a prospect. But if Heatley takes the 4th, this is all we have left to offer.

**Iginla is the swing that probably fails.** 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, $6.50M expiring at a 70-point CGY club. Chistov + Tucker + 4th is our entire movable capital. CGY cannot retain him, but they want a first-round pick or a top prospect for their franchise scorer. Our best package gets close but likely falls short. Worth one phone call in July, not a priority.

**If none land:** Sign Cammalleri (LA, 22, POTE 97, 60 pts/61 GP, $1.10M) as a free agent in July. He's RW-capable, young, cheap, and fills part of the scoring void without spending a chip. The toughness and faceoff gaps remain unsolved. That is the real cost of a failed July: the L4 stays at FACE 52, TOUG 57, and a playoff opponent exploits it every shift.

## Owed

**Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window** — this item is closed. The GM shut it down on 2005-03-19 with the standing order to close all goalie monitoring. Luongo is on our roster; DiPietro's development continued at his club.

**Luongo** is ours: 94 overall (base not separately queried but shown at 94 in the top-60 table), 26 years old, $1.60M, 2 contract years remaining, 45 games this season. He was acquired during the February window the GM opened and confirmed as the franchise number one by 2005-03-19. No further monitoring is needed or wanted.

**DiPietro** finished with 63 games at age 22, going 32-28-1 with 1 shutout, 174 goals against on 1,350 shots. That is .871 save percentage and 2.77 GAA. The volume is real (63 starts at 22), the quality is adequate but not elite — below Luongo's .915 equivalent on the same save-pct formula. He remains a 1-year, $1.10M player. Even if a trade window reopened in the summer, he is not the upgrade Luongo already represents.

No change since the last time I reported: the window is closed, the answer is settled, and the roster is set at two 90+ goalies for the playoffs.

markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-17

Toronto 59-13-5, 133 pts after 82 games.

## Role coverage

The season is over, and the question now is which roles survive without change and which are about to be exposed for the first time. The answer: two are structural voids that no internal move can fix, and a third is covered today only by three men who cannot be assumed to hold.

**Toughness** is missing outright. Zero players at 80+ TOUG; Jackman tops the roster at 75. The coach has flagged the L4 checking mean at 61 and toughness at 57 since April and stated plainly that no bench player fixes it. Bell (88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, 24) or Avery (83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 93 FACE, 25) are the only league-wide solutions. There is no internal move that closes this.

**Faceoffs** are equally exposed. Sundin at 90 FACE is 34 and the next-best is Chlup at 75. The L4 mean of 52 was quantified by the coach on May 5 and confirmed impossible to fix from within. Bell or Avery solve both toughness and faceoffs in one move. Bell is the priority: he is younger on the clock, has more years, and at 82 FACE gives a usable 70-75 at third-line centre once his hands develop.

**Checking** is covered today by six players at 80+, but the age curve is ugly. Roberts 86 (38) is a write-off. Tucker 83 (30) is the GM's designated chip. After they leave, the best are Jackman 87 (24), McCabe 86 (29), Fischer 82 (24). Three names is thin for a full season, especially if McCabe's body turns. Bell at 86 CHKG would be the fourth man who matters.

**Scoring** is a structural void one year out. Mogilny 94 (36), Sundin 92 (34), Roberts 88 (38) carry the top of the sheet and no player under 30 is positioned to absorb 426 combined points. Gaborik at 92 overall and 23 years old is the obvious heir, but the coach has him "not lined" in any unit. If Gaborik is lined top-six next season, the bridge narrows. If Iginla (93 base, 27, $6.50M expiring, CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring) lands in July, the bridge is built.

**Speed** is oversupplied but wasted. Gaborik 98 SPEE and Koltsov 92 SPEE are both on the roster and both in no unit. The coach can fix this without spending anything. Line them or trade them; sitting them is the worst option.

**Stamina, durability, playmaking, clutch** are all adequate or better for next season. Kaberle 97 ENDU, McCabe 94 ENDU, Richards 90 ENDU carry the engine room. Abid at 90 DUR and 25 gives a physical presence who holds up.

**Goalies** are solved per the GM's March 19 standing order: Luongo 26 with two years left, Belfour for the playoffs, Ouellet as the backup. No further action.

## Trajectory

Is the club heading off a cliff? Not immediately — the old guard is expiring, not locked in — but the bridge between the 34-plus core and the teenagers is a single player wide, and 13 contracts worth $21.30M come due this July. The cliff is not the decline coming; it is the absence of anyone positioned between the decline and the youth.

**Sundin** is the structural problem no one can fix. He is 34, scoring 91 points on $8.40M, and the contract runs five more years. He will be 39 on that deal. The Coach already says to plan for further decline. At 30-35 points a night he still costs more than Nash, Eminger, Gaborik, Richards, and Chlup combined ($5.90M total). There is no buyout in this game, and $46.70M in profit means it does not hurt. It does mean the payroll never gets clean.

**The 30-33 band holds one player.** Tucker, who played 3 games. That is the entire prime-age layer of a 30-man roster. Every other player is either under 26 or over 34. If the young core's development slips one year, nobody steps up. Iginla at 27 fills this exactly — he is the only target that closes the RW void, the age gap, and the toughness ceiling simultaneously at 140 points and 93 base.

**Gaborik at 99 points and $1.10M is the roster's most valuable dollar.** He is 23, POTE 90, and his contract expires in July. A 5-year deal at $4-5M still gives him a 4x raise and locks a point-per-game winger through age 28. Every week that passes without a renewal in place risks a July bidding war.

**The renewal summer costs nothing in cash and everything in discipline.** Thirteen contracts expire together. The priority order: Gaborik, Richards (66 pts, 25, $1.00M), Nash (39 pts, 20, POTE 95), Eminger (POTE 99). Lock those four on 5-6 years and the core is cost-controlled through 2010. Kaberle at $1.90M can go 3 years. Colaiacovo (31 GP, 0.39 pts/g, POTE 99) and Chistov (0.29 pts/g) are trade pieces per the Coach, not renewals.

**The money is not the problem.** $46.70M in profit with $101 tickets and 17,713 attendance means adding $6.50M for Iginla raises payroll to roughly $66M against $119M in revenue. Plenty of room. The constraint is the calendar and the pick deficit — one 4th-rounder as the only draft capital.

Three moves protect the next three seasons: lock Gaborik and Richards on long deals by mid-July, re-sign Nash and Eminger on the same timeline, and acquire Iginla to bridge the 30-33 void and replace Mogilny's production in one move.

## Calendar

The deadline closed 59 days ago and Toronto have one game left at 133 points, first in the East; the calendar question is now purely the summer, and the summer is a renewal problem before it is anything else.

**The deadline is gone, so the plan is one date: July.** We are neither buyers nor sellers at a deadline that no longer exists. The regular season ends, free agency opens, and thirteen Toronto players whose contracts expire come due. That list decides the roster for the next three years more than any UFA signing will.

**Gaborik** at 91 base, 23 years old, $1.10M, POTE 90 is the first signature. He is the best player on the expiring list by a wide margin, and on a five- or six-year deal at whatever the market sets he anchors the right wing for the team's competitive window. Letting him reach open market at 23 with that profile is not an option.

**Richards** at 82 base, 25, $1.00M is the second. He is three years from prime, he already carries third-line centre minutes, and he costs less than most depth centres. Five years, lock him in the same conversation as Gaborik.

**Kaberle** at 84 base, 27, $1.90M is the third. He is at the exact age where a defenceman is fully formed and still has five productive years ahead. This is a star-length deal, five years minimum.

**Eminger** at 76 base, 21, $1.20M with POTE 99 is the fourth. The GM killed a trade for him on January 19 because his development runway outweighed Chara's certainty. That logic holds now more than it did then. Five to six years, cheap while he is still 21.

**Abid** at 79 base, 25, $0.40M is the easiest signature on the sheet. TOUG 80, CHKG 80, half a million dollars. The Coach wants him at 18+ MPG. Two to three years at whatever he asks. He is the toughness piece nobody else on the roster provides at that price.

**Tellqvist** at 77 base, 25, $0.80M stays per the GM's standing order from January. Renew on two years at the same number.

**Roberts** at 87 base, 38, $2.70M is the release. The Coach says plan for his decline; 0.86 pts/g at 38 says he is already in it. $2.70M is the salary that funds the Bell or Stuart signing. Let him go.

**Belfour** at 92 base, 40, $6.50M is the open question. The GM's March 19 order keeps him as the playoff backup alongside Luongo, but his contract expires in July. He will need a reduced offer, and the GM himself predicted he probably won't accept one. If he walks, Ouellet at 81 base and two years left at $0.90M becomes the playoff backup, which is thinner than what the GM wanted but workable.

**Chistov** at 78 base, 22, $1.10M with POTE 95 is the trade piece. The Coach stated on May 5 that Alexeev displaces him, and earlier flagged him as available in a Bell package. Renewing him at $1.10M for a fourth-line role when Alexeev outproduced him is a waste of a roster spot. Trade him in July if the right package appears, or renew at a low number and dress him sparingly.

**Nash, Alexeev, Upshall, Colaiacovo, Spacek** are the camp group. Nash at 77 base, 20 years old, is the only one with a path to top-nine minutes. Upshall at 78 base, 0.29 pts/g, and Colaiacovo at 72 base, 0.39 pts/g in 31 games, are the two most likely to be released if camp says no. Decide after camp, not before.

**The July UFA market has one clear priority.** Iginla at CGY, 27, 93 base, $6.50M expiring, 140 points in 73 games, closes the Mogilny scoring void and the toughness ceiling at the same time. The vault flags CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring deals and $14.43M in profit, which means they will not match. If he signs elsewhere, Heatley at ATL (91 base, $1.10M) is the cheaper alternative. Bell at CHI (80 base, $0.90M, 2 years left) remains the faceoff and toughness fix that no internal option provides.

**The draft on June 8 is not a lever.** Toronto own nothing better than a fourth-rounder. The picks were spent during the Luongo acquisition. The draft is for depth on low picks, not for fixing a structural hole.

## League scan

The July market determines whether Toronto bridges the scoring void left by Mogilny, Sundin and Roberts, or limps into next season with no player between 24 and 34 on the roster. The good news: three of the four best available players are expiring contracts from non-contenders, which means no trade negotiation is needed — only a signing bonus and a cheque.

**Iginla** remains the top target. 93 base, 128 points in 76 games, 85 TOUG, 27 years old, $6.50M expiring. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring deals and $14.43M profit has no reason to retain him. He closes the RW scoring void, raises the toughness floor by 10 points, and fills the 30-33 band where Tucker played 3 games. No other player does all three.

**Havlat** is the steal of the summer. 87 base, 103 points in 82 games, POTE 86, 24 years old, $900K expiring. OTT at 77 points with 11 expiring deals are rebuilding. He plays left wing, which thins our L-side depth behind Gaborik and Tucker. At $900K, signing him costs less than a backup defenceman and replaces Sundin's decline at a third of the price.

**Thornton** is the wild card. 94 base, 83 points in 59 games, 25 years old, $4.00M expiring. BOS at 97 points want to keep him, but his contract is up. If they can't match, he's the best centre on the open market and the only player who closes the scoring gap at centre without Sundin's $8.40M anchor. Acceptance uncertain.

**Heatley** at 91 base and 131 points in 79 games is the best scorer on any expiring-adjacent deal, but his contract has 1 year left, so he requires a trade. ATL at 84 points with $25.99M profit and 11 expiring deals have the financial room to re-sign him, which makes them a reluctant seller. The price would be steep, and we hold one 4th-rounder.

**Bell** is the toughness and faceoff solution. 80 base but 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 87 FACE, POTE 82, $900K, 2 years left. CHI at 78 points with $31.73M profit are not in a fire sale, but they're rebuilding and his production (28 points in 80 GP) means they won't miss him. A mid-round pick plus a depth piece should work.

**Daze** at 89 base and 127 points in 82 games, $3.00M expiring, is CHI's other expiring scorer. He's 29, so he's a one-year fix, not a bridge. If Iginla signs, Daze becomes unnecessary. If Iginla goes elsewhere, Daze at 127 points and $3.00M is the most production available per dollar.

**Sullivan** at 87 base and 100 points in 82 games, $3.00M expiring from the same CHI backfield, is the third expiring option from Chicago. 30 years old, RW. He's the same argument as Daze in smaller numbers.

**Sturm** at 85 base, 81 points in 73 games, $1.00M expiring, age 26, is the LW depth option. PHI's $66.73M payroll against $2.14M profit is the worst financial profile among non-playoff clubs. They may be forced to shed salary, and he's cheap enough to sign without a package.

**Cammalleri** at 22, POTE 98, $1.10M expiring from LA (79 points, 14 expiring deals), is the highest-upside signing available. His base is below 80 so he won't play top-nine tonight, but POTE 98 at $1.10M is the profile the guide calls depth wins. A camp audition, not a starter.

I would not pursue Avery at $400K. His 9 pts in 82 GP and 79 base overall mean he fixes the faceoff number without fixing the scoring problem underneath it. Bell at the same cost is a better player. And I would not chase Bertuzzi (94 base, 128 pts, $2.6M) despite the numbers: POTE 58 and age 30 make him another Sundin in four years.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: can we build trade proposals that CHI, SJ and OTT would actually say yes to, given that we hold one 4th-round pick and every player the GM wants to keep is locked by a standing order or the coach's plan?

**Bell from Chicago is the only trade that closes two structural voids at once.** The coach quantified the L4 faceoff mean at 52 and the roster toughness ceiling at Jackman's 75 since April. Bell at 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG and 87 FACE solves both. He carries $900K with two years left, so this requires a trade, not a signing. We give Chistov ($1.10M expiring, POTE 95, 89 SPEE, 20 pts in 68 GP), whom the coach says Alexeev displaces and who walks for nothing in July if we don't move him, plus the 4th-rounder. CHI at 78 points with $31.73M profit are rebuilding, and Bell's 28 points in 80 GP says their system won't make him a better scorer. Chistov is three years younger with elite speed and a POTE 95. Whether the AI prices POTE that generously is unknown.

**Stuart from San Jose is the Roberts replacement the coverage phase identified.** At 87 base, 89 CHKG, 80 TOUG, POTE 91 and age 25, he is eight years of development ahead of Roberts (88 base, 38, expiring). We give Colaiacovo ($1.10M expiring, POTE 99, 12 pts in 31 GP at 17.9 MPG, coach-flagged as a write-off) and Koltsov ($1.10M, 2 years left, ACCE 96, 19 pts in 38 GP, unlined behind Gaborik at 98 SPEE). SJ at 72 points with 13 expiring deals on $45.39M payroll are shedding. Two POTE 94+ players for one POTE 91 is attractive on paper, but the prior note correctly flags that at 72 points they are not tanking and may keep their top blueliner. Stuart's salary is not visible on our sheet, so the payroll effect is incomplete.

**Havlat from Ottawa is a conditional swap, not a must-trade.** At $900K expiring, 87 base, 103 points in 82 games, he is worth $900K as a UFA signing if OTT lets him walk. A trade only matters if they want something back before free agency. Upshall ($1.20M expiring, POTE 99, CHKG 87, 20 pts in 68 GP) is the natural piece: the coach says Alexeev displaces one of Chistov or Upshall, so if Chistov goes to CHI for Bell, Upshall is the remaining displaced forward. OTT at 77 points with 11 expiring deals are thinning their roster. But if they simply let Havlat walk, we sign him at $900K and spend nothing.

**If none land.** Iginla ($6.50M expiring, 93 base, 128 points in 76 GP, age 27, TOUG 85) is a UFA signing target, not a trade target. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring deals and $14.43M profit have no reason to retain him. Havlat and Sturm ($1.00M expiring from PHI at $66.73M payroll with $2.14M profit) are the same. All three close scoring gaps without a trade. The toughness and faceoff gap stays open if Bell does not come, and no fallback exists from within the roster. Gaborik's renewal ($1.10M expiring, 99 pts in 82 GP, age 23) is unaffected by any of this and remains the top internal deadline.

**On delivery obligation #2:** Luongo monitoring and DiPietro tracking are moot. Luongo is on our roster at 91 base with two years left. The GM closed all goalie monitoring on March 19. This task is superseded by events and requires no further action.

## Owed

**The question this phase answers:** What happened to the Luongo monitoring and DiPietro development tracking the GM asked for on January 19?

**Luongo** is on our roster. He was acquired before the GM closed the goalie file on March 19. He reads 94 overall, 26 years old, $1.60M, 2 years left, 45 games played this season. He and Belfour (93, 37 GP) were the two 90+ goalies the GM chose to carry through the playoffs. The task is complete.

**DiPietro** is no longer relevant to us. The original January framing was "find a really good high-90s goalie from a team that will not be a contender." We solved that by acquiring Luongo. The GM's March 19 standing order explicitly closed all goalie monitoring. There is no open goalie trade window to report on.

This item is delivered and closed. No further monitoring is needed unless the GM reopens the goalie file.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-17
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-17

Next game vs WSH on Wednesday 18 May 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether our young players are getting games proportionate to what they've produced, and with 82 games in the books and one left, this is really an offseason verdict on who got the chance and who didn't.

**Alexeev** is the clearest unresolved case. 0.55 pts/g on 8.3 MPG over 55 games, scratched. He outproduces both dressed wingers Chistov (0.29) and Upshall (0.29) by nearly double. At 23 with POTE 94, he's been a healthy scratch while men producing at half his rate fill the bottom six. This has been flagged since April and nothing changed. Offseason decision: he either earns a third-line spot or his 0.55 rate means nothing.

**Spezza** is the season the GM lost by not acting in March. 0.33 pts/g on 6.7 MPG, 46 games, scratched at 21 with POTE 99. The minutes collapse from 9.1 to 4.8 was flagged in March and he never got a real audition. Camp assignment is the only lever that matters now, and if he can't hold a top-nine role on merit there, the potential isn't translating and the window narrows.

**Upshall** mirrors Spezza exactly: 0.29 pts/g on 7.9 MPG, POTE 99, L4. Same offseason audition or stop dressing him.

**Colaiacovo** is the one who got shafted by the rotation logic. 31 games at 22 with POTE 99, averaging 17.9 MPG when he plays. That's a starting-D workload in a backup's game count. The GM's stated logic was to make room for young guys, and Colaiacovo *is* young. He got the minutes but not the reps. Next season he should be in the 60+ game range unless Klesla or Eminger stays and blocks him, which neither will.

**Chlup** is the one who belongs and knows it. 0.83 pts/g on 16.9 MPG at 19, morale 100, second line. No development concern. He's earned his role and holds it.

**Spacek** at 19 is getting fourth-line minutes (7.6 MPG) and producing 0.34 pts/g. That's proportional to current ability. No issue, just not ready for more yet.

**Stahle** has 4 games and zero points. No evaluation data exists. Needs a real camp look or he's invisible.

**Gaborik** is 23, 99 points, 20.5 MPG, 82 games. The best young player on the roster and he's played every game. Nothing to fix.

## Development trends

This is the season-end read, the last one before offseason decisions. The question: who has earned more next year, who has earned less, and who needs to go.

**Chlup** is the only unambiguous riser on the roster. He went 0.62 to 0.88 pts/g while his minutes nearly doubled from 11.0 to 18.2. A 19-year-old holding his rate while his load grows is a real player, not a hot streak. His card grades show no movement this window, which means his development clock has not ticked, but his game-level performance says he is the first-line centre. I have recommended this twice and both times it was not acted on. I recommend it again for the third time: assign him first-line centre before camp.

**Spacek** is the inverse. 0.55 to 0.28 pts/g, 16.0 to 5.2 MPG. His ice time collapsed to a fringe role and his rate halved with it. The March 5 target of 10 MPG is dead; he finished at 5.2. He needs a real camp audition or he should not be dressed at all next year.

**Spezza** continued the same slide. 0.43 to 0.24 pts/g on 4.6 MPG. No minutes, no production. Same decision as Spacek: camp or cut. At POTE 99 the upside is there but the game share is gone.

**Nash** has the same profile as Spacek. 0.83 to 0.42 on flat minutes at 13.2. His role did not change, his production halved. This is the system-fit problem I flagged in March.

**Upshall** finished at 0.27 pts/g on 4.8 MPG, down from 0.33 on 13.4. Same story as Spezza and Nash.

**Alexeev** saw his minutes gutted from 11.1 to 6.0 MPG while his rate fell from 0.62 to 0.48. He is buried and underproducing both before and after the cut. At 23 this is a player losing his roster spot.

**Klesla** is the season's clearest sell among defencemen. 0.50 to 0.31 pts/g on flat 14.9 MPG. Two consecutive declining seasons confirmed.

**Jackman** at 24 dropped from 0.65 to 0.39 on 29.4 MPG. The load is still crushing his production. Either the role changes or he goes.

**Afinogenov** (1.17 to 0.73) and **Richards** (1.08 to 0.71) both finished the season confirming the system-fit concern. Flat minutes, no injuries, rates collapsed at age 25. Neither is a bust, but neither fits what we are running.

**Abid** finished at 0.70 pts/g on 11.5 MPG. His minutes were cut from 20.1. He is the best example on this roster of a player whose production outstrips his role. He needs 18+ MPG next year or we waste him.

**Kaberle** is the only veteran trending up. 0.54 to 0.62 pts/g on 19.4 to 21.5 MPG. He earned more, not less. He is the anchor.

**McCabe** finished at 0.48 pts/g on 21.5 MPG. That is the final number and it is well below the 0.60 sell threshold. He is on the sell list and stays there.

**Sundin** at 34 went 1.46 to 0.97 on increased minutes (16.9 to 21.7). Still productive but clearly absorbing load the younger centres cannot yet carry. **Mogilny** at 36: 1.62 to 0.83. **Roberts** at 38: 1.29 to 0.86. All three are declining on the right side of the arrow, and all three will be a year older next October. The top-end veteran production is going to drop further regardless of what we do.

## Morale watch

The room is fine. Everyone is at 94 or above, and every trend line is positive. With one game left there is nothing to act on tonight.

**Spezza** is the lowest man in the building at 88, up 5 from the last check. He's been scratched all season with development intent, and the upward move confirms winning is doing its job. No action before camp.

**Upshall** at 94 and **Spacek** at 94 are both L4 depth getting 7.9 and 7.6 minutes respectively. That's their band for men at their calibre. No concern.

**Abid** at 100 is the one to flag for the offseason, not for tonight. He's producing 0.80 pts/g on 13.8 MPG at age 25. The minutes-to-production gap hasn't hurt his morale yet, but running a winger at that rate on fourth-line minutes all summer is asking for it. That's a camp assignment conversation.

No change for Washington tomorrow.

## Role composition

**The question is whether these units suit their jobs, and whether we're missing any role entirely.** The units are well-built for what they're asked to do, with one glaring exception that dwarfs everything else.

**Gaborik** — He carries the best scoring (98), best playmaking (99), best speed (99), and best clutch (99) rating on this roster, and he is not assigned to any unit. This is the last game of the season against a 39-26 Washington club we want to beat. If he is healthy, he starts on the first line and Mogilny or Roberts moves down. If he's carrying something physical, that's a different conversation. But the roster cannot maximize quality without him and I cannot see why he's out.

**L1 (Sundin, Roberts, Mogilny, Jackman, Fischer):** Checking mean 79, scoring mean 88, playmaking mean 85. Well-balanced shutdown-capable top line. Sundin wins draws at 91. No change unless Gaborik returns, which would force one winger down.

**L2 (Chlup, McCabe, Kaberle, Nash, Afinogenov):** Scoring mean 85, speed mean 87, Chlup at 80 on draws. This is a legitimate second line with scoring and defensive structure. No change.

**L3 (Eminger, Tucker, Richards, Klesla, Chistov):** Richards at 75 faceoffs, 91 stamina, 97 clutch makes him an ideal third-line centre. Chistov at 98 speed provides the transition threat. This line checks at 75 mean, which is adequate. No change.

**L4 (Spacek, Abid, Upshall):** Faceoff mean 52, best 55. This unit loses every draw. The checking mean of 74 is fine for a fourth line, but 52 on faceoffs means we cannot kill any zone time with this group. This is the known fourth-line gap and no rearrangement of existing players fixes it.

**PP1 (Sundin, Roberts, Kaberle, Jackman, Afinogenov):** Scoring mean 88, playmaking mean 86. Good unit. No change.

**PP2 (Chlup, Mogilny, Richards, Fischer, Klesla):** Scoring mean 87, speed mean 91. A fast second unit that can stretch the kill. No change.

**K1 (Sundin, Roberts, Kaberle, Fischer):** Checking mean 79 is below where a first kill should sit, but these players can clear the zone with their hands. In a one-off game this is acceptable. **K2 (Chlup, Tucker, McCabe, Jackman):** Checking mean 84, toughness mean 72. Better suited to the kill. The order is right.

**Roster-level:** The fourth-line faceoff deficit (52 mean, 55 best) is structural. The best faceoff man not already on L1-L3 is Richards at 75, and he anchors L3. We have no fourth-line centre who can win draws above 55 and this persists.

## Opponent matchup

The question is whether anything needs to shift for WSH, and the answer is no. The matchups favor us on every line, our defensive pairing slots are already correct against their top line, and their penalty rate hands our power play extra chances.

**Jagr** is the one man who can change this game. OVR 84, 94 deking, 92 speed, 90 puck control. He sits on their first line with Lang (75) and Dupuis (74). Our D pair 1, Fischer (CHKG 92) and Jackman (CHKG 92), are auto-paired with our first line and will see their top unit. That is the correct match and it is already in place.

**Our forward lines vs theirs.** Line 1 (Sundin 91, Roberts 88, Mogilny 90) vs Lang-Dupuis-Jagr: two-thirds of their top line is outmatched. Line 2 (Nash 83, Chlup 86, Afinogenov 86) vs Grier-Radivojevic-Zubrus: 84-74 OVR gap across the board. Line 3 (Chistov 82, Richards 87, Tucker 80) vs Cleary-Gamache-Sloan: 82-65 gap. We should outscore them at even strength without adjustments.

**Power play.** Their PP converts at 35 in 284, which is 12.3 percent and means they take roughly 3.9 penalties a game. That hands our unit, which converts at 32 in 99 (32.3 percent), extra ice. No personnel change needed; the opportunity is just there.

**Faceoffs.** Our centres face Lang (60), Grier (64), and Sloan (50). Sundin at 91, Chlup at 80, Richards at 75 all win their draws tonight. The faceoff problem that plagues us all season does not bite against this roster.

**Goalie.** Luongo at 94 OVR, morale 100, should start. Check the fatigue icon on screen before confirming per the standing order, but nothing in his displayed grades suggests tiredness.

**Eminger at ENDU 50** on pair 3 is a concern in general, but their third line is Cleary-Gamache-Sloan at 67, 61, and 66 OVR. This is the easiest assignment a young defender could get. Leave him out there.

## Owed

**Owed item #1: Defenceman analysis and end-of-season sell list, updated for the final week.**

The season is effectively over for the D corps. McCabe, Klesla, Jackman, Fischer, Eminger and Kaberle have all reached their final game counts (82, 82, 80, 77, 64, 74). These are now locked numbers, not a snapshot in progress.

**McCabe** at 62 points in 82 games is 0.76 pts/g on 22.1 MPG. That clears my March 30 threshold of 0.60 on the full season, but his back half was 0.48 over 58 games. The April 7 clearance and May 2 re-listing both still stand: at 29, four years and $3.00M, a declining second half is the real read, not the average. Sell.

**Jackman** finished 37 points in 80 games, 0.46 pts/g on 29.6 MPG. $0.70M for three more years. Still a sell: the minutes are his value to someone else, and the 29.6 MPG is unsustainable for a player producing at that rate. We can't keep running him into the ground.

**Klesla** at 30 points in 82 games, 0.37 pts/g on 14.8 MPG, age 23. Second consecutive declining season (0.38, 0.36, now 0.37). Sell at $0.90M x 2. Nothing has changed since March.

**Eminger** at 23 points in 64 games, 0.36 pts/g on 15.5 MPG, age 21, $1.20M expiring. My March 30 note was correct: he slides. After July he's a UFA loss. Must move him this offseason.

**Kaberle** is the one who needs action in the other direction. 44 points in 74 games, 0.59 pts/g on 20.8 MPG, OVR 84, and **one year left at $1.90M**. The GM called him a star; the numbers support it. Renew him or lose him. This is now urgent.

**Fischer** stays. 41 points in 77 games, OVR 85, age 24. The GM put him on the record as a keeper and the production backs it.

**Colaiacovo** finished at 12 points in 31 games, 0.39 pts/g. Age 22, expiring. Development rotation all year. He can be a cheap depth option to re-sign or trade for a late pick.

Sell list for the offseason: McCabe, Jackman, Klesla, Eminger. Renewal: Kaberle. Keep: Fischer.

Nothing has moved since my May 2 re-listing of McCabe. The season numbers are now final and confirm what the trends already said.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-15
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-15

Toronto 59-13-5, 133 pts after 82 games.

## Role coverage

The question this phase answers: can the coach close the L4 and scoring-bridge gaps with what's on the roster, or does July require external acquisitions? The answer is split — faceoffs are partially fixable internally, toughness is not, and the top-end scoring age curve creates a second gap the coach hasn't named yet.

**Toughness** is the club's only true zero. Not one player above 75. Tucker, previously flagged in December at 88 TOUG, reads 70 on the base grades now, alongside Jackman at 75 and McCabe at 73. This means the "internal band-aid" case from December was wrong and there is no path to 80+ toughness without acquiring Bell (88 TOUG, 24, CHI) or someone of that grade. The coach quantified the L4 mean at 57 on April 9 and no arrangement of this roster moves it above 73.

**Faceoffs** are one-short: Sundin at 90 is the only draw-taker above 80. Chlup at 75 and Richards at 70 give the coach two real moves: Chlup to first-line centre for next season (his own May 13 recommendation) puts a 75 FACE man on L1, and Richards to L3C lifts that line from the 52 mean the coach measured to a 70. L4 still reads 67 with Tucker, which is the coach's unfixable problem. Bell (82 FACE) remains the only player who closes L4 faceoffs AND toughness at once.

**Scoring bridge** is the gap nobody has named yet. Mogilny 36, Sundin 34, Roberts 38 carry 426 combined points across this season's production line. Mogilny's decline from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g was confirmed in March. Roberts at 38 with a $5.10M expiring contract will not return. If both fall to 0.60 pts/g next year and Roberts walks, the club loses roughly 70 points of top-six production with no one under 30 ready to absorb it. Gaborik at 23 and 92 overall is not even in the lineup. Nash at 22 needs a system-fit review per the coach's May 13 note. The external fix is the Iginla target already flagged for July: 93 base, 27, 140 points, expiring, from a 70-point CGY club that cannot retain him.

**Checking** is adequate in total (Jackman 87, Roberts 86, McCabe 86, Tucker 83, Fischer 82, Upshall 80) but the coach's April 9 quantification of the L4 at checking mean 61 tells us the problem is distribution, not supply. Tucker at 83 CHKG on L4 raises that to approximately 68 — better, still below the 75 the coach demands. This overlaps with toughness: Bell at 86 CHKG AND 88 TOUG solves both L4 gaps in one acquisition.

**Goalies** are solved per the GM's March 19 order. Luongo 26 with 2 years and Belfour 40 with 1 year. Ouellet at 23 is the playoff backup; Tellqvist at 25 with an expiring deal is the tradeable third. No further action needed here.

**Durability** at 4 players above 80 is thin for a playoff run. Roberts 98, Afinogenov 95, Fischer 92, Abid 90 are the only men who will absorb 20+ minutes nightly for 16 games. If Roberts walks in July (expiring, $5.10M), that drops to three. Stuart (87 base, POTE 91, SJ) would carry 95+ durability alongside his toughness and checking and close three gaps at the blue line.

## Trajectory

Is this club aging into a cliff? No, but July 2005 is a single point of failure that decides whether the next three seasons are a window or a rebuild.

**The age curve is close to the manual's shape.** Twenty-five of thirty players are 29 or under, four are 34+ (Sundin 34, Mogilny 36, Roberts 38, Belfour 40), and Tucker at 30 is the only man between 30 and 33. The veterans total five at $26.60M, inside the 5-7 range the guide prescribes. The thin 30-33 band is a transitional gap, not a structural problem: the current young core (Gaborik 23, Nash 20, Eminger 21, Chlup 19) moves into that band in four or five years and becomes the veteran group naturally.

**The contract cliff is the real problem.** Thirteen players worth $21.30M expire in July, and eleven of them are under 26. Belfour ($6.50M) and Roberts ($2.70M) are the two we plan to walk, freeing $9.20M of old money. The remaining eleven — Gaborik ($1.10M), Richards ($1.00M), Nash ($1.20M), Eminger ($1.20M), Upshall ($1.20M), Chistov ($1.10M), Abid ($0.40M), Colaiacovo ($1.10M), Alexeev ($1.10M), Kaberle ($1.90M), Tellqvist ($0.80M) — total $12.10M on their current deals. Renewing them at even a 2.5x average multiplier costs roughly $30M for the same eleven men. That is an $18M net increase against a payroll that will still carry Sundin at $8.40M.

**Sundin is the medium-term trap.** He is $8.40M with five years left, starting at 34 with 91 points. He will decline sharply by year three of that deal (age 36) and by year five (age 38) the contract will be a third-liner's production at a franchise price. There is no way to renegotiate mid-contract. The plan must be Chlup at 19, POTE 95, taking the minutes as Sundin's production fades — and Chlup needs those minutes now to be ready, which is the Coach's standing request.

**Mogilny at 36 is the immediate void.** His production fell from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g this season at $5.50M with two years left. He cannot be moved mid-contract. By July 2006 he will be 37 and likely a negative asset. The replacement is Iginla at $6.50M (same salary slot, 27 years old, TOUG 85, 140 pts in 73 GP for CGY who cannot retain him).

**The money picture is tight but workable.** Revenue is $119.16M, current payroll $60.04M, profit $46.70M. After the renewal wave and an Iginla-for-Mogilny swap, projected payroll is roughly $73-76M. That leaves profit in the $30-35M range — still comfortable, but most of the flexibility is spent. There is no headroom for a second big signing without further salary shedding.

**Draft capital is nearly zero.** One fourth-rounder from Toronto. Every trade must be player-for-player. The over-80 expiring mechanic is the only recovery route: Belfour at 92 base and Roberts at 81 base, both expiring, both above the threshold. If either can be traded for a pick per the mechanic, that changes our market position from "no ammunition" to "one or two rounds."

**The three moves that protect three seasons:**

One. Lock Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger and Chlup on 5-6 year deals in July. These five are the window. If two of them walk simultaneously, the core collapses.

Two. Replace Mogilny with Iginla in July. Same salary, nine years younger, closes the toughness ceiling that the Coach has quantified at mean TOUG 57 on the fourth line.

Three. Try to recover a pick from Belfour or Roberts via the over-80 expiring mechanic before July. Even one round-one pick converts us from a club that can only swap players to one that can fund a package.

## Calendar

The deadline is 57 days past and the playoffs are two games away, so the only calendar that matters now is the summer: 13 contracts worth $21.30M expire simultaneously in July, and the GM needs to know which ones he is re-signing, which he is offering a short deal to, and which are walking. We are buyers, not sellers. At 133 points and first in the East, the priority is keeping the core together and adding one elite RW, because Mogilny has fallen to 0.79 pts/g at 36 and Roberts at 38 is walking.

**Gaborik** is renewal number one. 91 base, 87 points at 23, $1.10M expiring. Lock him on 5-6 years the day he hits the market. This is the single largest swing on the roster.

**Richards** is number two. 64 points at 25, $1.00M expiring. Same 5-6 year lock. He and Gaborik together anchor the next five years, and both carry a market rate far above what they are earning now.

**Nash**, 20, and **Eminger**, 21, both at $1.20M expiring with POTE well above 90, go on 5-6 years too. These are the two pieces the GM vetoed trading in January because they define the timeline. Getting them locked alongside Gaborik and Richards removes the four biggest renewal risks in one week.

**Kaberle**, 27, $1.90M, is the oldest of the five core renewals and the only one whose prime is now rather than coming. Five years is the right length; beyond that the money stretches past his best hockey.

**Abid** at $0.40M and **Tellqvist** at $0.80M are the cheapest pieces on the list and the easiest to lock. Abid carries 66 points on 13.8 MPG and the coach wants him at 16-18 minutes next season. Tellqvist is on the GM's standing instruction to keep and develop. Both go on 2-3 year deals; no reason to spend years on either yet.

**Colaiacovo** (22, POTE 99, 31 games) and **Alexeev** (23, 0.55 pts/g) are camp decisions, not renewal decisions. Offer both 2-year deals and let camp separate them from the rest of the audition group. If either earns a roster spot, the cheap contract is a bargain. If not, the second year is tradeable.

**Chistov** (22, POTE 95, SPEE 89, $1.10M) is the judgment call. The coach says Alexeev displaces him, but a 22-year-old with POTE 95 at $1.10M is depth the manual tells us to hoard. Renew on 2 years and carry him as a scratch or call-up; his trade value stays intact if he does not play.
