**Upshall** (21, 0.29 pts/g) is the weakest player in the audition group by production. Let him go. Alexeev and Chistov cover his spot at the same price with higher ceilings.

**Roberts** (38, $2.70M) walks per the March 21 plan. At 38 on a $2.70M expiring deal there is no renewal case.

**Belfour** (40, $6.50M) is the payroll swing. The GM plans to offer a reduced deal; Belfour probably refuses, and at 40 the retirement risk is real. Budget for his $6.50M walking. That frees more than the entire Upshall-Chistov-Colaiacovo-Alexeev group combined.

On the acquisition side, **Iginla** (27, 93 base, $6.50M expiring from Calgary) is the July priority the March note identified. The Belfour and Roberts money ($9.20M combined) roughly covers his salary, and he closes both the Mogilny scoring gap and the toughness ceiling in one signing. **Bell** (24, 82 base, TOUG 88, FACE 82) fills the L4 faceoff void the coach has flagged since April. **Cammalleri** (22, POTE 98, $1.10M expiring from LA) is the value signing if LA cannot retain him alongside Frolov.

The Spezza decision sits outside the expiring list but belongs in the summer plan. At 21, POTE 99, 0.33 pts/g on 6.7 MPG, the coach has flagged him seven times. His trade value peaks while the potential grade is still credible. The GM needs to decide before July: give him top-nine minutes as Chlup's backup at centre, or move him for a package funded by his POTE. If he stays and continues at 6.7 MPG, morale at 88 will fall further and the asset erodes.

On the Luongo monitoring task (#2): the GM closed all goalie monitoring on March 19 with the standing order "Goalies are solved. Done. Do not revisit." Luongo is on the roster at 91 base, Belfour is staying for the playoffs. That task is complete.

## Action items for the GM before July

| Date (approx) | Action |
|---|---|
| End of playoffs | Decide Spezza: develop or trade |
| July, day 1 | Offer Gaborik 5-6 years, Richards 5-6, Nash 5-6, Eminger 5-6, Kaberle 5 |
| July, day 1 | Offer Abid 2-3, Tellqvist 2, Chistov 2, Colaiacovo 2, Alexeev 2 |
| July, day 1 | Let Upshall and Roberts go |
| July, day 1 | Offer Belfour reduced deal; plan for him to walk |
| July, week 1 | Pursue Iginla, Bell, Cammalleri in that order |

## League scan

The question this phase answers: which players on which clubs close Toronto's gaps, and what makes those clubs willing to deal? The answer is that the market has exactly the right players on the right kind of clubs, but every package requires either a draft pick we do not have or a core piece the GM has not yet agreed to move. The over-80 expiring mechanic on Roberts and Belfour is the key that unlocks everything else: it converts two assets we are losing anyway into the ammunition we need.

**Brad Stuart** is the single best fit for this roster. 25 years old, 87 base, 89 CHKG, 80 TOUG, 90 INJU, POTE 91, 52 points in 77 games at $1.80M and expiring. He closes three gaps at once: the defense has no blueliner above 75 TOUG, no one above 90 INJU, and the checking distribution is top-heavy with Roberts walking. SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring contracts and $20.74M profit is a seller. The package is hard because 87 base is rare, but a Roberts-for-Stuart swap puts two expiring players on different clubs and frees different salary slots on both sides. SJ gets $5.10M and a veteran; we get $1.80M and a franchise blueliner. The value gap needs a young player to bridge it.

**Mark Bell** at 24, 80 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81, $900K with two years left closes every L4 deficiency the coach quantified on April 9. CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring deals and $31.73M profit is the most motivated seller in the league for mid-tier players. Tucker plus the 4th-rounder is the natural package, but Tucker reads 70 TOUG now (down from the December note at 88), which weakens the hockey value. The over-80 mechanic on Roberts gives us a pick to add, making it Tucker plus a round-two pick plus a young forward. The coach flagged Chistov as tradeable on May 5, and at 22 with POTE 95 he is the right third asset.

**Eric Belanger** is the sleeper that the July UFA route makes almost free. 82 base, FACE 97 (best in the league), CHKG 83, TOUG 79, $700K and expiring. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring deals will not re-sign him. If he hits the market, signing him costs $700K and solves the faceoff problem permanently without a trade. His 14 points in 64 games is bottom-six production, which is exactly what L4 needs.

**Jay Bouwmeester** at 21, 81 base, POTE 95, 27 points in 79 games, $1.20M and expiring from FLA is the best young defenseman available. FLA has 19 expiring contracts, the most in the league, $51.07M payroll against only $13.64M profit. They cannot keep him. I need his physical grades to confirm he fits our checking profile, but at POTE 95 and 81 base this is a franchise blueliner on a desperate seller. Tucker plus the 4th-rounder is the starting offer.

**Mike Cammalleri** at 22, 79 base, POTE 97, 60 points in 61 games fills the scoring bridge behind Gaborik. LA has 14 expiring and cannot retain both him and Frolov (POTE 95, 55 points in 62 games). July UFA signing at $1.10M current salary. The risk is competition: every contender with cap space will chase him.

**Andy Sutton** at 27 is not young, but his TOUG 94 and CHKG 90 with INJU 87 on four years at $1.34M is the cheapest toughness in the league. ATL at 84 points with 11 expiring and $25.99M profit are borderline sellers. This fills the toughness gap without spending potential. The trade is straightforward: Tucker plus the 4th-rounder matches a 78-base player on a locked deal.

**Jarome Iginla** remains the priority but the package problem is real. 93 base, 140 points in 73 games, 27, TOUG 85, $6.50M and expiring from CGY at 70 points. Mogilny at $5.50M with two years left cannot be traded mid-contract for extension purposes, though trading him out (inheriting the contract) should be possible. Even so, no CGY rebuild wants a 36-year-old at 0.79 pts/g. The realistic package requires a high-potential young player (Chistov at POTE 95 or Spezza at POTE 99 if the GM agrees to the coach's trade recommendation) plus Tucker plus a pick recovered from the over-80 mechanic. That is three core pieces for one player, and the GM will weigh whether the window is strong enough to justify it.

```json

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: can we close the L4 toughness/faceoff gap, the RW scoring void, and the defense depth problem with the ammunition we actually hold, and who on the other side has a reason to say yes? The answer is that the Bell deal is close to achievable, the Iginla package exists but costs our two best POTE 99 prospects outside Eminger, and Stuart requires SJ to be willing to lose their best young defenseman on a player-for-player swap. Every package needs GM sign-off on assets beyond Tucker and the 4th-rounder, which the March 19 deadline order protected. The Coach has opened Chistov (May 5) and Spezza (May 11); the rest require a fresh decision.

**Bell from Chicago** is the top proposal. We give Tucker ($1.30M, 2 yrs, 30, 92 CHKG but 70 base TOUG) plus Chistov ($1.10M, expiring, 22, POTE 95, SPEE 89, ACCE 88) plus the 4th-rounder, and get Bell ($900K, 2 yrs, 24, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE). We save $1.50M/year. CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring deals and $31.73M profit is triaging their roster. Tucker gives them a 92 CHKG checker now; Chistov at 22 with POTE 95 gives them a speed prospect for later. Bell's 82 FACE fills a specialist role they likely have internal options for. Acceptance is uncertain, but the hockey logic runs both ways.

**Iginla from Calgary** is the highest-value target and the most expensive. We give Mogilny ($5.50M, 2 yrs, 36, 0.79 pts/g) plus Spezza ($1.00M, 2 yrs, 21, POTE 99) plus Upshall ($1.20M, expiring, 21, CHKG 87, POTE 99) plus the 4th-rounder, and get Iginla ($6.50M, expiring, 27, 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, TOUG 85). Net saving $1.20M/year. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit is in rebuild mode. Spezza at POTE 99 is a franchise-center prospect. Upshall at 21 with POTE 99 and 87 CHKG adds another ceiling. Mogilny can be released immediately after the trade; no cap means his $5.50M is not a penalty, just a useless roster player. The risk: CGY may value Spezza at POTE 99 too highly and want two picks, which we do not have. The Coach flagged Spezza for trade-or-develop on May 11, so the coaching staff supports this path.

**Stuart from San Jose** is the defense fix. We give Roberts ($2.70M, expiring, 38, 81 pts/82 GP, INJU 98) plus Koltsov ($1.10M, 2 yrs, 24, POTE 94, ACCE 96, AGIL 92, 19 pts/38 GP) plus the 4th-rounder, and get Stuart ($1.80M, expiring, 25, 87 base, 89 CHKG, 80 TOUG, POTE 91). Net saving $2.00M next season. SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring and $20.74M profit cannot re-sign everyone. Roberts at INJU 98 still plays 82 games. Koltsov at 24 with ACCE 96 is a skill winger they may need. The problem: at 76 points SJ is competitive and may keep Stuart. This is the least likely of the three.

All three proposals compete for the same 4th-rounder and overlap on Tucker. If Bell lands, use the 4th there and rework Iginla without Tucker. If Iginla lands first, the L4 toughness gap shrinks because Iginla's 85 TOUG raises the top-nine average, and Bell becomes less urgent. Stuart is the deal that can wait for July UFA market movement or the over-80 pick mechanic on Roberts to generate a second pick.

**Belanger** is the fallback that requires no trade. At 82 base, FACE 97, CHKG 83, TOUG 79, $700K and expiring from LA (79 points, 14 expiring), he walks into July as a UFA. Signing him costs $700K, closes the faceoff gap permanently, and raises the L4 toughness to 79 from the current mean of 57. It does not reach Bell's 88 TOUG but it is the cheapest path to a real improvement with no players surrendered. The risk is competition: every club with $700K and a faceoff hole goes after him.

## Owed

**Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window.** This task is closed. The window it described expired in February, the GM declared goalies solved on 2005-02-19 ("Luongo is arrived. Goalies are solved. Done. Do not revisit that issue.") and again on 2005-03-19 ("Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks"). I am not reopening it.

**Luongo** was the target and he is on our roster: 94 overall, age 26, $1.60M, 2 years left, 45 games played this season. The objective was met. DiPietro monitoring is moot because the GM closed all goalie acquisition work. There is nothing to update.

What has changed since this task was live: Luongo went from a target to a teammate. Belfour at 40 and $6.50M with 1 year left is his backup, and the GM's position is that Belfour stays on a reduced renewal if he wants to. The goalie situation entering next season is Luongo (26, 94, 2 years) plus a 40-year-old on an expiring deal, which is the right shape for a contender.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-15
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-15

Next game at WSH on Monday 16 May 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is who got the games they earned this season, and it matters now because the regular season is done (82 played, playoffs against Washington) and camp assignments will be the only lever for the next three months.

**Chlup** at 71 GP, 16.9 MPG and 0.83 pts/g at age 19 has earned everything he's been given and more. He belongs on the first line permanently — I've said this since April and nothing has changed it.

**Gaborik** played all 82 games at 20.5 MPG and put up 99 points. The obvious one. He's showing as scratched in the current lineup snapshot for the playoff game, which the GM will see on his own screen.

**Alexeev** at 0.55 pts/g on 8.3 MPG is the clearest rate-to-role gap on the roster. He outproduces Chistov (0.29 on 13.1 MPG) and Upshall (0.29 on 7.9 MPG) by nearly double. He's been scratched from the playoff lineup and got 67% of available games in the regular season. If we keep both Chistov and Upshall in top-nine minutes next year while Alexeev sits on the pressbox, the production numbers won't justify it.

**Nash** at 20 is back on the sheet after the GM's January note. He finished at 39 points in 69 games (0.57 pts/g) on 13.1 MPG. His rate halved mid-season from 0.83 to 0.43 and recovered somewhat. The role was stable — the production wasn't. Same system-fit question as Afinogenov and Richards: he needs a different setting before next camp, not more minutes.

**Spezza** at POTE 99 finished with 15 points in 46 games on 6.7 MPG (0.33 pts/g). The season is gone for him. The only lever left is a real audition in camp where he gets 15+ MPG on a line built around him. If he can't hold that, the scouting number was wrong.

**Upshall** at 0.29 pts/g on 7.9 MPG is exactly what a fourth-line winger earns. No gap to close. He stays where he is or doesn't make the roster.

**Spacek** at 19 got 50 games at 7.6 MPG and 0.34 pts/g. POTE 91 is the lowest of the group. He's earning his fourth-line minutes and that's appropriate for a 19-year-old at this stage. No change warranted.

**Eminger** played 64 games at 15.5 MPG on 0.36 pts/g. His contract is expiring and my March call holds: he goes in the offseason regardless of how these playoffs end.

**Klesla** at 82 games, 14.8 MPG and 0.36 pts/g for the second straight declining year is the same. He plays every game because nobody else on the blue line is available, not because he's earned it.

**Colaiacovo** when dressed got 17.9 MPG (top-pair minutes) and returned 0.39 pts/g. His POTE 99 keeps him in the plan, but the GM's stated preference for Svehla over him for quality nights means his development path requires a team where he's the second-pairing D, not the third.

**Stahle** at 4 games played tells us nothing. Too small a sample to judge.

## Development trends

The question this phase answers: who is moving, which direction, and what does that mean for next season's plans. With no grades having moved, every signal here is production or minutes, and those tell a clear story.

**Chlup** is the one genuine breakout. 0.62→0.88 pts/g while minutes went from 11.0 to 18.2. He absorbed more ice and got better per minute. At 19, that's the profile of a first-line centre. The GM hasn't moved him from L2 yet despite three recommendations.

**Kaberle** is the only veteran going up: 0.54→0.62 pts/g on minutes that climbed from 19.4 to 21.5. At 27 he's entering his prime and should anchor the top pair next year without question.

**Sundin, Mogilny, Roberts** are all declining as their ages predict. Sundin at 34 went 1.46→0.97 on minutes that rose from 16.9 to 21.7. Mogilny at 36 went 1.62→0.83. Roberts at 38 went 1.29→0.86. All three are playing more minutes while producing less per minute. Planning for next season cannot assume any of them holds this rate.

**Abid's** minutes collapsed from 20.1 to 11.5 and his rate followed, 1.09→0.70. The minutes loss is the cause. At 25 he's in his prime and should be eating 18+ MPG. This is a morale risk if it carries into camp.

**Fischer** went 0.63→0.50 pts/g on minutes that rose from 20.8 to 22.9. The GM protects him and I accept that, but the trend is flat-to-down. If next season mirrors this window's end, he's a top-four D, not a number-one.

**The young group that stalled**: Nash (0.83→0.42 on flat minutes), Spezza (0.43→0.24, minutes from 9.1 to 4.6), Upshall (0.33→0.27, minutes from 13.4 to 4.8), Spacek (0.55→0.28, minutes from 16.0 to 5.2), Alexeev (0.62→0.48, minutes from 11.1 to 6.0). All five saw minutes cut. Nash is the one whose rate dropped without losing ice, which makes him the system-fit question of the group. The others are minute-victims whose next camp decides whether they stick.

**Koltsov** went 1.10→0.29. The early 1.10 was ten games. He's a 0.29 winger at 24 on flat 9.9 MPG. The GM has him as a trade chip and the numbers confirm that's right.

**Klesla** at 0.50→0.31 on flat minutes confirms the second consecutive declining season. **Jackman** at 0.65→0.39 on 30 MPG confirms the load is destroying his value. Both are sells.

## Morale watch

The room is right. Everyone except four scratched or depth players sits at 100, and those four are all trending upward on the latest save.

**Spezza** is the lowest man on the roster at 88, up 3 from last save. At 21, 6.7 MPG in 46 games with 15 points, he's a scratched prospect getting depth minutes. The dip came from being benched; the recovery tracks a recent win. No intervention. When he's back on the roster for next camp, that's the lever, not tonight.

**Alexeev** at 92 (+5) and **Spacek** at 94 (+5), **Upshall** at 94 (+3): all recovering, all comfortable in their current roles. Spacek and Upshall are 19 and 21 on the fourth line at 7-8 MPG, which matches their calibre band. Alexeev remains a production-to-role mismatch (0.55 pts/g scratched while Chistov dresses at 0.29), but morale is climbing and this is a roster composition question, not a morale emergency.

**Safronov** at 95, **Stahle** at 99, **Colaiacovo** at 99: scratched defencemen with stable or rising morale. Fine.

The +5 to +9 swings across the top nine lines confirm a win has lifted the whole room. Nobody needs more or less of the game tonight for morale reasons.

## Role composition

Are the units suited to their jobs, and does the roster hold enough of each role?

**L4 faceoffs are the clear fit problem.** Spacek, Abid, Upshall have a mean of 52 in the circle. The best on the line is 55. No arrangement fixes this — Abid at 0.84 pts/g is our best scorer among the three but cannot win a draw, Upshall is at 0.29 pts/g on collapsed minutes, and Spacek offers nothing that compensates. If Washington's fourth centre is even average, they own the zone every shift. This is a roster gap: we have no bottom-six centre with faceoff ability on the club.

**K1 vs K2 checking split is reversed from what you'd want.** K2 (Chlup, Tucker, McCabe, Jackman) has checking mean 84 and best 92 — Tucker 94 in the unit breakdown, Jackman 90, McCabe 85. That is our true shutdown unit. K1 (Sundin, Roberts, Kaberle, Fischer) sits at mean 79, best 92. Roberts and Fischer at 85 each are our only forwards above 80 in checking, and they're on the PK with Sundin whose value is offense. The trade-off is unavoidable with this roster: Roberts and Fischer are both offensive and defensively capable, so they anchor both units. No better arrangement exists.

**L3 has no identity problem.** Tucker provides the checking anchor, Richards at 91 stamina and 75 faceoffs is a proper engine, and Chistov at 98 speed gives stretch. Eminger at 21 is developing, Klesla at 23 is declining but neither is the unit's weakness right now. Fine as-is.

**P1 and P2 are well-sorted.** P1 (Sundin, Roberts, Kaberle, Jackman, Afinogenov) has scoring mean 88, playmaking 86 — the skill unit. P2 (Chlup, Mogilny, Richards, Fischer, Klesla) has scoring 87, playmaking 85 with Mogilny's 94 shooting and Fischer's hands. Both units have enough bodies who can shoot from the point and enough movement to create. No change needed.

**L1 and L2 are fine.** L1's scoring 88 mean with Sundin 93 and Mogilny 94 is the team's best skill. L2's faceoff concern (mean 59) is solved by Chlup at 80 taking the draws while Afinogenov (92 scoring, 92 playmaking) handles the offensive load.

For tonight against Washington (39-26-7, eliminated on our side): no change. These are the right units. The fourth-line faceoff gap is a next-season roster problem, not something to solve in a meaningless game.

## Opponent matchup

**Can our current lines beat a hot WSH club?** Yes, and I would not touch them for Monday.

**Jagr** is the game. OVR 84, speed 92, deking 94, puck 90 — he is their entire offense and he sits on their top line with Lang (FACE 60) at centre. Our first defensive pair is Fischer and Jackman: both checking 92, Fischer speed 94, Jackman speed 94. They are fast enough to chase him and physical enough to finish it. That matchup already exists because the game pairs our L1 with our P1 D and their L1 with their P1 D. No rearranging needed.

**Their second pair is Yonkman (69) and Pilar (70).** Our L2 forwards — Nash (SHPW 98), Chlup, Afinogenov (DEKG 98) — paired with Kaberle and McCabe on our P2 D should create chances all night against that pair. Their second-line centre Grier has FACE 64 against Chlup's 80. We will own the circle on their weak side.

**Every faceoff circle favors us.** Sundin 91 vs Lang 60. Chlup 80 vs Grier 64. Richards 75 vs Cleary 50. Their top centre is a 60; ours is a 91. That means our D pairs stay in coverage they are built for, not scrambling from bad pinches.

**WSH's penalty kill and PP:** their PP is 35/284, a 12.3% conversion on elite volume. That means they take penalties at a high rate but also that their PP unit is toothless. Our PP at 32/99 is 32.3%. If they take a penalty early and their crowd is hyped, our first unit — Sundin, Mogilny, Roberts, Kaberle, Jackman — should exploit them.

**Their form is the only thing that makes this dangerous.** Eight straight wins, 2.90 for and 1.80 against over their last ten. We are choppy at 2.30/2.50. The risk is not a matchup problem; it is momentum. Our best answer is the same lineup that has 133 points this year.

**Luongo** at OVR 94 is the starter. Check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming, per the GM's standing instruction from January 19. If tired, Ouellet (82) is the backup but that would be a downgrade against this team.

## Owed

**Standing job #1 — defenceman evaluation and who goes at season's end.**

The season is essentially done (2 games left) and these are now final or near-final numbers. That changes the framing from "re-evaluate at season's end" to "these are the numbers." Here's where each defenceman lands:

**McCabe** 82 GP, 22.1 MPG, 62 points (18G 44A), 0.76 season rate. The sell case is confirmed. His last 58 games sat at 0.48; the full-season number is carried entirely by a hot start that bled off weeks ago. 29 years old, 4 years at $3.00M. He goes.

**Jackman** 80 GP, 29.6 MPG, 37 points, 0.46 rate. Confirmed from my March read (0.48 on 73 games, now 0.46 on 80). At 24 with 3 years and $0.70M, his value is the cheapest top-pair minutes available anywhere. Sell.

**Klesla** 82 GP, 14.8 MPG, 30 points, 0.37 rate. Second consecutive decline (0.38 at 22, 0.37 at 23). No development signal, just regression. $0.90M x 2. Sell.

**Eminger** 64 GP, 15.5 MPG, 23 points, 0.36 rate. The slide continued from my March note (0.38 then, 0.36 now). Contract expires. This is urgent — move him this offseason or lose him for nothing.

**Kaberle** 74 GP, 20.8 MPG, 44 points, 0.60 rate. Keeper per GM's instruction. His contract expires (1 year left) so this is a renewal conversation, not a trade one.

**Fischer** 77 GP, 22.4 MPG, 41 points, 0.53 rate. Keeper per GM's instruction. 4 years, $3.70M. Locked in.

**Colaiacovo** 31 GP, 17.9 MPG, 12 points, 0.39 rate. Low volume from a development rotation role. Contract expiring. No urgency, no sell case, no keep case — he's a depth body the GM decides on later.

What has changed since May 2: Eminger's rate dropped from 0.38 to 0.36 (the slide was still live). Jackman's rate confirmed downward from 0.48 to 0.46 on more games. Everything else is the same verdict with final numbers stamped on it.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-11
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-11

Toronto 59-13-5, 133 pts after 82 games.

## Role coverage

The season is over at 59-13-5, and the role coverage question is: what does this roster look like in October 2005 when Mogilny (36), Roberts (38), and Belfour (40) all walk?

**Toughness is the structural hole.** Zero players at 80+ TOUG. The best is Jackman at 75, then Roberts 73 and McCabe 73 — and Roberts is 38 and expiring. This cannot be fixed internally. Tucker at 70 TOUG and 83 CHKG is the ceiling of what the bench offers, and the Coach confirmed on April 9 that L4 checking averages 61 and toughness 57. Only Bell (CHI, 24, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81) or Avery (LA, 25, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 93 FACE, $400K, 2y) close this from outside.

**Faceoffs are a one-man operation.** Sundin at 90 is the only player above 80. Chlup at 75 is the next best, and the Coach is moving him to L1C. That leaves L3 and L4 with Richards at 70 and Tucker at 67 — below any threshold that wins a defensive draw in a playoff series. Bell (82 FACE) solves two gaps with one acquisition.

**Scoring is covered only if Gaborik plays and Mogilny does not decline further.** Gaborik at 92 is not lined. Once he is, the top six holds Sundin 92, Gaborik 92, Afinogenov 90, Abid 86. But Mogilny at 36 fell to 0.79 pts/g this season. His departure leaves the RW slot empty for a first-line winger. Iginla (CGY, 27, 93 base, TOUG 85, 140 pts/73 GP) closes the RW void and the toughness ceiling simultaneously.

**Defence loses Roberts at 86 CHKG and 73 TOUG with 98 durability.** McCabe 86 CHKG and Eminger at 21 with POTE 99 carry the pair forward. Kaberle at 90 clutch and 97 stamina anchors the other side. Jackman at 87 CHKG and 24 fills the third pair. The unit is young enough to improve, but it loses its most durable body.

**Goalies: Luongo is the future, but the backup chair is thin.** Belfour at 40 and $6.50M expiring almost certainly walks. Tellqvist at 0.880 SV and $0.80M expires too. That leaves Ouellet at 23 (0.911 SV in 13 games, ENDU 60) as the only backup with contract. The GM's January directive to fetch a high-90s goalie from a non-contender remains open.

## Trajectory

**Is this club structured to be good in three years, and can the money get us there?** Yes on both counts, but two execution risks sit in front of the GM this summer, and neither is about tonight's lineup.

**The age curve is the manual's target shape.** Thirteen players at 23 or under, twelve at 24-29. The 30-33 bucket holds one man (Tucker, 30, $1.30M, POTE 79), which sounds thin but is irrelevant here: the 24-29 group bridges the gap naturally. The real story is that six of the thirteen youngest carry POTE 95 or above — Chlup (95), Eminger (99), Nash (95), Upshall (99), Colaiacovo (99), Koltsov (94), Abid (94) — and three of them already play every night. That is the depth the guide says wins cups.

**The 34+ group costs $23.10M but collapses on its own.** Sundin (34, $8.40M, 5 years), Mogilny (36, $5.50M, 2 years), Belfour (40, $6.50M, 1 year), Roberts (38, $2.70M, 1 year). Belfour and Roberts walk in July, dropping $9.20M. Mogilny walks in July 2006, dropping $5.50M more. Only Sundin remains locked, and his deal carries him to age 39 on $8.40M. That is a known future cost, not a cliff.

**The contract cluster is the problem.** Thirteen players, $21.30M, all up in one summer. Gaborik (99 points at $1.10M), Richards (66 points at $1.00M), Nash (39 points at $1.20M), Eminger (POTE 99 at $1.20M), Kaberle (44 points at $1.90M) — these five are the core and they all come up at once. If negotiations go sideways in any direction, pieces leave simultaneously and the rebuild starts over. The priority is clear: Gaborik first, Richards second, Nash and Eminger third, Kaberle fourth. Each needs a 5-6 year deal at current-or-modest-raise salary.

**The money clears everything.** Payroll $60.04M against revenue $116.95M produces $44.48M in profit. Belfour and Roberts walking frees $9.20M. Iginla at $6.50M fits inside that freed space with room to spare. The constraint is not money; it is draft capital.

**Draft capital is almost gone.** Toronto holds a single fourth-rounder. No first, no second, no third. Every acquisition must be funded by players, not picks. This blocks any package that demands a high pick and forces the GM to find deals where the other club accepts player-for-player value.

**Fischer is the slow-bleeding liability.** $3.70M, 4 years left, 41 points in 77 games at age 24, production dropping. He will be 28 when this deal expires. His trade value is highest now while four years of team control still interest a buyer, but no target has been identified and the GM has not authorized moving him. Flag it for July if the right package surfaces.

**The two or three moves that protect 2005-08:**

1. Re-sign Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger, and Kaberle on 5-6 year deals before any other negotiation. The five at current salaries cost $6.50M combined. Even doubled, they cost less than Belfour and Roberts did.
2. Let Belfour and Roberts expire. That frees $9.20M, which funds one top-ten target like Iginla at $6.50M without raising net payroll.
3. Accept that without picks, acquisition is player-for-player only. The only unprotected chip is Tucker ($1.30M, 30, POTE 79), and per the March finding he plus the fourth-rounder is worth approximately a 74-76 base depth player, which does not reach Bell, Stuart, or Iginla. The GM needs to decide whether he is willing to include a young prospect like Upshall (POTE 99 but 20 points in 68 games) or Koltsov (POTE 94, 19 points in 38 games) as package filler, because the pick-only route is closed.

## Calendar

The trade deadline passed 53 days ago; Toronto are first in the East at 133 points with four games left. The only question left this season is execution and health through the playoffs. The real work is the summer: thirteen contracts worth $19.30M expire, and the plan determines whether this team is a Cup contender for three years or starts over.

**Gaborik** at 91 base, age 23, POTE 90, $1.10M is the first renewal. He must get five or six years at the top of whatever the market offers. Richards follows: 25, 64 points, $1.00M. Five or six years. These two are the core of the next five years, and they are cheap now in a way they will not be in 2007.

**Kaberle** at 27 and $1.90M is at his prime. Five or six years. **Nash** at 20 and $1.20M is the cheapest long-term lock available. Five or six years immediately. **Eminger** at 21 with POTE 99 and $1.20M: the GM killed a trade for him in January, correctly. Five or six years.

**Chistov** at 22, POTE 95, $1.10M is in the coach's camp audition. If he holds middle-six minutes, renew on four or five years. **Colaiacovo** at 22, $1.10M: same decision at camp. Three to five years depending on whether he takes the next step. **Alexeev** at 23 and $1.10M: the coach says he outproduces wingers ahead of him. If he earns the roster spot, renew on three years. If he does not, he is a free-agent loss with no compensation unless moved this summer before signing elsewhere.

**Upshall** at 21 and $1.20M is in the same camp audition as Chistov and Alexeev. If he makes the top nine, renew two or three years. If not, he walks at a $1.20M salary the club does not need to carry.

**Abid** at 25 and $0.40M is the cheapest toughness on the roster. Renew two years. **Tellqvist** at 25 and $0.80M: the GM's standing order is he stays and develops. Renew two years as the backup behind whoever is first.

**Belfour** at 40 and $6.50M: the GM's order is to offer a reduced deal. Two years at roughly $3.50M. If he refuses, he walks. The club has Luongo at 91 and Tellqvist behind him. **Roberts** at 38 and $2.70M walks. The renewal priority note from 21 March says this plainly.

The summer targets from the March notes remain: Iginla (CGY, 27, 93 base, 140 points in 73 games, $6.50M expiring), Cammalleri (LA, 22, POTE 98, $1.10M expiring), and Bell (CHI, 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 82 FACE). These close the RW scoring void, add depth scoring, and fix the fourth-line faceoff and toughness gaps the coach has flagged four times since April.

The draft on 8 June carries one fourth-rounder. Take the best available with good potential. There is nothing else to do there.

## League scan

The season is done and July is the only market that matters now; the question is which players on losing clubs Toronto can actually acquire given that we hold one fourth-rounder and the only authorized chip is Tucker.

**Iginla** (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring) closes the Mogilny RW void and the zero-players-at-80-TOUG structural hole in one move. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit cannot re-sign him at $6.50M while also rebuilding. He is the single highest-value target available to Toronto, and the only player in the league who fills two of our three gaps simultaneously. The cost is a major young-player package; we have no picks to add.

**Theodore** (MTL, G, 28, 91 base, 66 GP at 60.2 MPG, $5.50M expiring, POTE 87) answers the Jan 15 standing order for a high-90s goalie from a non-contender. MTL at 66 points with 15 expiring contracts is in a full teardown; he will not re-sign at $5.50M in Montreal. He gives Toronto a legitimate number-one alongside Luongo and eliminates the Ouellet-as-playoff-backup problem. A mid-tier package should suffice since MTL is selling everything.

**Bell** (CHI, LW, 24, 82 base, TOUG 95, CHKG 93, FACE 87, POTE 81, $900K, 2 years left) fills the faceoff gap at L3/L4 (the Coach's fifth flag) and the toughness ceiling at a price we can reach. Production is modest at 28 pts/80 GP on 17.8 MPG, but he is a role player whose grades are the point. CHI at 78 points with $31.73M profit are not desperate, but they hold 10 expiring deals and Bell is not a top-pairing winger for them. Tucker plus a depth prospect could work; acceptance is uncertain because CHI is profitable and not under pressure.

**Conroy** (CGY, C, 31, 85 base, 102 pts/82 GP, FACE 95 at 55.3% on 624 draws, $2.00M expiring) is the most productive faceoff centre in the league by a wide margin. At 31 with one year left he is a rental, but a rental who scores at a top-six pace. CGY is already selling Iginla; they could deal Conroy too. The problem is we already have Chlup at L1C and Richards at 24 developing; a 31-year-old rental at L2C displaces the youth development path. Only pursue if Gaborik signs and the centre depth becomes irrelevant.

**Havlat** (OTT, LW, 23, 88 base, 103 pts/82 GP, $900K expiring, FACE 51, TOUG 66) is the best pure scoring available on an expiring deal at the lowest salary in the league. OTT at 77 points with 11 expiring and $32.36M profit can afford to let him walk or trade him. He does not fill a structural gap (FACE 51, TOUG 66), but 103 points at $900K with one year of team control is the highest points-per-dollar available anywhere. If he hits UFA, he is a July signing target.

**Reid** (STL, RW, 23, 77 base, FACE 84, 58 pts/73 GP, $600K expiring) had been flagged in March as the L4 faceoff fix. His FACE grade (84) is real but his TOUG (50) and CHKG (50) are non-existent. He fills one gap and creates another (zero physical presence on the bottom six). STL at 86 points with only 8 expiring are not motivated sellers. Drop him.

**Cammalleri** (LA, 22, POTE 98, 60 pts/61 GP, $1.10M expiring) remains the best UFA value. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring and $52.43M payroll cannot keep him and Frolov both. If he reaches the market, sign him immediately. No trade package needed.

The ranked order for July: Iginla first (fills two gaps, needs a major package), Theodore second (one gap, affordable), Cammalleri third (UFA, zero cost to acquire), Havlat fourth (UFA, absurd value), Bell fifth (fills two gaps but production is thin and CHI may not deal).

## Trade construction

The question is what we can actually construct given that Toronto holds one fourth-rounder, Tucker is the only authorized chip, and the Coach has opened Chistov and Alexeev as trade pieces. Three proposals, ranked by probability and impact.

**Avery from LA is the single cleanest trade available to us.** Sean Avery (C, 25, 77 overall/79 base, $400K, 2 years left, TOUG 83, CHKG 88, FACE 94) fills both structural gaps at once: toughness and faceoffs. His grades are real, not form-inflated — they match his stored numbers within a point. LA already holds Belanger (FACE 96, 78 overall), Allison (FACE 89, 87 overall), and Stumpel (FACE 88, 79 overall) at centre. Avery is their fourth option. They carry $52.43M payroll on $16.34M profit with 14 expiring deals; a POTE 95 speed prospect at 22 fits a rebuild better than a POTE 71 role player who will not improve. Chistov costs them $1.10M versus Avery's $400K, a $700K increase LA can absorb. Acceptance is uncertain because LA at 79 points may value a 77-overall center over a 22-year-old winger with 20 points.

**Komisarek from MTL replaces Roberts on the blue line.** Mike Komisarek (D, 22, 82 overall/77 base, $1.10M, 1 year, POTE 92, TOUG 85, CHKG 92) is 16 years younger than Roberts, carries 19 points more of potential and 12 more TOUG, and costs $1.60M less. MTL at 66 points with 15 expiring deals, prestige 399 and $21.59M profit is in a full teardown. They hold Hainsey (D, 21, POTE 98) at the same position, making Komisarek surplus even in their own rebuild. Upshall (21, POTE 99, CHKG 87) gives them a high-upside forward to develop; Tucker at $1.30M with CHKG 92 is a veteran body they can flip at the deadline. The 4th-rounder is included as a sweetener but carries almost no value. The risk is real: Komisarek at 82 overall is worth more than Upshall and Tucker combined on any fair board, and MTL may want a pick we don't have.

**Bell from CHI is the backup to Avery if LA passes.** Mark Bell (LW, 24, 82 overall/80 base, $900K, 2 years, stored TOUG 88, CHKG 86, FACE 82, POTE 82) closes toughness, checking and faceoffs with his stored grades all above 80. CHI holds Daze (87 overall), Fleury (86), Sullivan (85) and Calder (80) ahead of him on the wing — Bell is surplus. Alexeev (RW, 23, POTE 94, BALA 90, SPEE 89, 30 pts/55 GP) replaces Fleury and Sullivan who are both expiring at RW, and the Coach has flagged him for "dress or trade." Tucker provides veteran depth. CHI adds $1.50M in net salary against $31.73M profit, trivially absorbable. The concern: CHI's profit means no financial pressure to sell, and Bell at TOUG 88 stored is a genuine checking winger they might keep. This deal conflicts with Komisarek on Tucker; the GM pursues one or the other, not both.

**If none land:** sign the five core expirings (Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger, Kaberle — $6.50M combined at current salaries, needing 5-6 year deals each). Then try to sign Iginla, Havlat, and Cammalleri from the UFA market — all three are on 0-year deals from selling clubs and cost nothing to acquire if we outbid the field on salary. The toughness gap stays structural. Tucker at stored TOUG 70 is the best we have, which is not good enough for the third round of a playoff. We accept the gap and hope the young D (Eminger, Colaiacovo, Klesla) compensates physically.

## Owed

**#2 — Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window.**

This task is closed. You ordered it shut on 2005-02-19 ("Goalies are solved. Done.") and again on 2005-03-19 ("Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks"). I am filing the final status.

**Luongo** is on our roster at 92 overall, 26 years old, $1.60M with two years remaining. He played 45 games this season. He is the number-one goaltender going into the playoffs alongside Belfour (91, 37 GP). The acquisition is complete; no trade window remains open.

**DiPietro** monitoring became moot when Luongo landed. The original question was whether to target a high-90s goalie from a non-contender; we got one without spending a first-rounder on DiPietro. There is nothing further to track on that thread.

No action needed. If the goalie situation reopens at renewal (Belfour's $6.50M expiring after this season, or Tellqvist's development path), that will be a new question with new data.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-13
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-13

Next game vs WSH on Saturday 14 May 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether every young player is getting the games his production has earned — and at 82 games in, the answer separates cleanly into three who are out of line and ten who are fine.

**Alexeev** is the clearest mismatch on the club. 30 points in 55 games gives him 0.55 pts/g, and he's scratched while Chistov (0.29) and Upshall (0.29) dress on the wings. He's 23 with POTE 94 and morale at 92, so he's not crying out, but the production-to-role gap is real and has been sitting since April. On a night where we're maximizing quality against Washington, he deserves a look in the lineup over either of them.

**Spezza** has the lowest morale in the young group at 88, and he's been scratched entirely after his minutes fell to 6.7 MPG. At 21 with POTE 99, the season is a write-off for his development — nothing changes now — but the low morale is the loudest signal here. This is an offseason decision: real camp audition or stop dressing him. Flagging it so the GM knows the pattern is not just "bad year" but "bad year plus the player notices."

**Colaiacovo** gets 17.9 MPG when he suits up, which is real top-pair minutes for a 22-year-old, but only 31 games of them. POTE 99 says the club thinks there's more coming. Being in and out of the lineup is the wrong pattern for a young defenceman still building his game. Same offseason call as Spezza: either he's a regular or he's not.

**Chlup**, **Gaborik**, **Nash**, **Klesla**, **Eminger**, **Spacek**, **Chistov**, **Upshall**, **Stahle**, and **Ouellet** are all roughly where their production puts them. No changes needed on any of them.

## Development trends

The development phase asks who is improving, who is sliding, and which trends should change next year's plans. The answer this season is stark: one true riser, one confirmed franchise player, and three veterans getting more ice as they produce less.

**Kaberle** is the one going the right way. 0.54→0.62 pts/g at 27, minutes up from 19.4 to 21.5. He is entering his prime and the numbers say he handles it. Build next year's blue line around him as the clear first pair anchor.

**Chlup** continues to confirm. 0.88 pts/g at 19 on 18.2 MPG, up from 0.62 on 11.0. He is the only young player on this roster whose rate and minutes both rose. He is the first-line centre next season and the GM has not yet moved him there in the lineup.

**McCabe** has now played 82 games with a back-half rate of 0.48 pts/g. His early 1.42 pace was a 24-game hot start; the remaining 58 games say 0.48. At 29, that is a decline. My March call to take him off the sell list was built on the season average of 0.76. The trend direction inside that average is down and I was wrong to read the average. He belongs on the sell list again.

**Sundin, Roberts, Mogilny** are all getting more ice as they age. Sundin at 34: 16.9→21.7 MPG, 1.46→0.97 pts/g. Roberts at 38: 16.5→21.4 MPG, 1.29→0.86 pts/g. Mogilny at 36: 16.9→19.1 MPG, 1.62→0.83 pts/g. The minutes are climbing while the production falls. That is a depth problem wearing a development disguise: we have nobody to take those minutes, so the old guys carry them until they break.

**Nash** at 20 confirms the system-fit note: 0.83→0.42 pts/g on flat 13 MPG. No injury, no role change. Something in how he fits does not work.

**Afinogenov and Richards** hold their earlier declines: 1.17→0.73 and 1.08→0.71 respectively, both at 25, both on flat or near-flat minutes. The system-fit review from the previous note is now a three-player problem.

**Spezza and Upshall** are dead seasons. Spezza 0.24 pts/g on 4.6 MPG, Upshall 0.27 on 4.8. Camp is the only lever. **Alexeev** at 0.48 on 6.0 MPG still outproduces Upshall and Chistov per minute but remains a scratch. That mismatch is unresolved and has now run three months.

No player card grades moved in this window, so every claim here rests on production and minutes alone.

## Morale watch

The room is in good shape. Nearly every man sits at 100 or 94, and the recent trend is up: the team has been winning and morale is climbing across the board. No line change is warranted on morale grounds.

**Spezza** is the lowest at 88, but his last recorded move was +3. He's been on a long slide from the scratch list and is slowly recovering. At 6.7 MPG he is well under the 10-minute band a 75-79 calibre forward would expect, and that's the structural cause of his low reading. The GM has deliberately kept him out for younger players' development since January. That trade-off is his to make; the morale number confirms the cost, but at 88 it's not urgent.

**Alexeev** at 92 and 8.3 MPG on 30 points is slightly under his band as well, same root cause: scratched. His morale is fine and stable. No action.

**Abid** is the one I'm watching. At 100 morale he looks fine today, but I've flagged since March that 66 points on 13.8 MPG is a production-to-ice-time mismatch. If his minutes stay there into next season while his production rate holds, 100 will crack. I'd give him 16-18 minutes next year, which is a camp assignment decision rather than a tonight decision.

**Jackman** at 29.6 MPG is carrying the heaviest load on the roster by a wide margin. Morale at 100 says he's not complaining. But if he's on the block this summer, those minutes are the reason his trade value is high and also the reason we need a partner ready to absorb some of that load.

No changes tonight.



---

**Message to GM:**

Room is healthy tonight. Everyone at 94+ and climbing with the wins. Spezza at 88 is the only soft spot and he gained 3 last save, so the scratch cost is being absorbed. Nothing to change before Washington. The one I'm filing for next year: Abid needs 16-18 minutes at camp. 66 points on 13.8 MPG at 25 is a top-six winger's rate on fourth-line ice and his 100 morale won't hold forever at that allocation. Task #1 (defenceman review) is handled in the matchup phase, not here.

## Role composition

The question is whether each unit is built from players suited to its job, and where the roster simply doesn't have enough bodies to fill a role. Most units are fine. Two structural problems persist and one arrangement mismatch is still unresolved.

**L1 and P1** are well-built. Sundin (faceoffs 87, clutch 91, scoring 89) anchors everything, Roberts provides the 87-clutch net-front presence, Mogilny at 90 scoring is the shooter, Jackman and Fischer give the D-men 86 and 81 checking. No change needed.

**L2** has a faceoff weakness (mean 57, best is Chlup at 76) that will bury them in their own zone on draws, but Chlup's 0.88 pts/g production and Afinogenov's 94-best playmaking compensate. The offense earns the defensive-zone starts. I'm not breaking it.

**L3** is actually our most balanced line: Richards brings clutch 93, stamina 95, faceoffs 71. Chistov's speed 94 stretches the ice. Tucker provides the checking. Well-constructed.

**L4** is the problem. Faceoff mean 50, best 51. That is a coin flip. Every draw goes to the other center and they start the shift in our zone. No arrangement fixes this because our four faceoff winners (Sundin 87, Chlup 76, Roberts 72, Richards 71) are already spread across L1-L3. This is a roster gap, same as I flagged on April 13.

**Alexeev** at 0.55 pts/g outproduces Upshall at 0.29 and Chistov at 0.29 yet scratches. If the GM's development-space logic from January still applies to Upshall specifically, I accept it. If Upshall is scratching for no stated reason, Alexeev earns that spot on the scoresheet alone.

**Checking and toughness depth** remains thin. Only four players check above 80 and they're all top-pair D or top-six F. No forward on L3 or L4 checks above 75. The fourth line's checking mean of 70 looks better than my April reading because displayed ratings include form, but the structural point holds: we have no dedicated bottom-six checker.

## Opponent matchup

The question is whether WSH's eight-game heater changes how we line up, and it doesn't: the auto-pairing already puts our answer to Jagr in position.

**Jagr** is the only forward on their sheet that scares me. OVR 84, SPEE 92, SHPW 89, DEKG 94, PASS 90, PUCK 90. He plays right wing on their first line with Lang at centre (OVR 75, CHKG 51, TOUG 50). The auto-pairing sends our L1 and our P1 defensive pair against their L1. That means Fischer and Jackman (both CHKG 88) face Jagr's side of the ice, and Roberts (CHKG 84, TOUG 86, HERO 87) is already on our first line to do the dirty work. Mogilny's SPEE 91 matches Jagr's 92. This is as good a matchup as we can construct without breaking chemistry.

**Their power play is toothless:** 35 goals on 284 attempts is 12.3%. They cannot punish us for taking penalties or for pinching. I would not change our D pair slot order to shelter against a PP unit that scores once every eight chances.

**Their middle-six is Grier** (OVR 76, CHKG 81) at centre with Zubrus and Radivojevic. Our second line of Chlup/Nash/Afinogenov handles them fine: Nash at CHKG 81 matches Grier's 81, Chlup at FACE 76 wins the draw against Grier's 64. No concern.

**Kolzig** at OVR 87 in their net is the reason they are on a heater. He is 35 with ENDU 88 and no visible fatigue. Our answer is Luongo at OVR 92. Check Luongo's fatigue icon before confirming the start.

**No change to the lines.** The matchups are already correct for this opponent.

For deliverable #1 (defenceman season-end trade review): WSH now carries Pilar at OVR 69, CHKG 71, TOUG 53. He is the weakest player on their top four D. Our own defensive corps for the season-end decision: Fischer (keeper per GM), Jackman (OVR 84, $0.70M x3, sell at value), McCabe (back on sell list, recent window 0.48), Kaberle (keeper per GM), Eminger (OVR 75, expiring, ENDU 51), Klesla (sell, second declining season). Nothing about this game changes those calls.

## Owed

**Final defence assessment for the season — who goes.**

The season is done. These are locked numbers, not projections. That's what's changed since May 2nd: the sell cases that were building are now facts.

**McCabe** — 62 points in 82 games on 22.1 MPG gives 0.76 pts/g for the year, but his last 58 games sit at 0.48. The April hot start is gone. At 29, $3.00M and 4 years left, the recent window is who he is now. He stays on the sell list.

**Jackman** — 37 points in 80 games on 29.6 MPG. That's 0.46 pts/g at $0.70M with 3 years. The cheapest top-pair minutes available anywhere. Sell.

**Klesla** — 30 points in 82 on 14.8 MPG. 0.37 pts/g, second straight year down, $0.90M x 2. Sell.

**Eminger** — 23 points in 64 on 15.5 MPG. 0.36 pts/g, expiring at $1.20M. If we haven't moved him by now we lose him for nothing.

**Kaberle** — 44 points in 74 on 20.8 MPG. 0.60 pts/g at 27, expiring. GM called him a star on January 15th. He stays, but the contract decision is urgent.

**Fischer** — 41 points in 77 on 22.4 MPG. 0.53 pts/g at 24, 4 years. GM keeper. No change.

**Colaiacovo** — 12 points in 31 games. Only 31 games played and not dressed recently. Needs a real audition at camp or he becomes another Eminger.

No changes to the list since May 2nd. The season finished and confirmed every projection I had.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-09
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-09

Toronto 59-13-5, 133 pts after 82 games.

## Role coverage

The structural gaps are confirmed and none of them close in the next five games: Toronto has zero players above 80 toughness, one player above 80 in faceoffs (Sundin at 90), and the RW scoring position is about to lose Mogilny to age and contract expiry simultaneously.

**Toughness** — zero at 80+, best is Jackman at 75. This is structural, not a form artefact; it has been re-confirmed three times since February. Only Bell (CHI, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG) or Avery (LA, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG) close it externally, or Iginla (CGY, TOUG 85) closes it as a byproduct of his scoring.

**Faceoffs** — one man at 80+ (Sundin 90). Chlup at 75 is the next best and the coach wants him at first centre next season, which makes the problem worse on the bottom six. Bell at 82 FACE and Avery at 93 FACE are the only league-wide solutions. The coach quantified the L4 mean at 51 and confirmed no arrangement fixes it.

**Checking** — six at 80+ sounds adequate until you note Roberts (86 CHKG, age 38) walks in July. That leaves Jackman 87, McCabe 86, Tucker 83 (if re-signed; currently expiring), Fischer 82, Upshall 80. The top-6 forwards carry none of this weight. Thin.

**RW scoring** — Mogilny at 36 has fallen to 0.79 pts/g. Gaborik is a winger on the left side; Afinogenov is the other RW. Neither carries first-line RW scoring. Iginla at 27 with 140 points in 73 games and TOUG 85 closes the RW void and the toughness void in one move.

**Goalies** — Luongo (26, 0.889 SV) and Belfour (40, 0.931 SV) are solved per standing order. Ouellet is the playoff backup. No action needed.

## Trajectory

Is this club aging into a cliff? No. The age shape is top-heavy only at the edges: four men at 34+ cost $22.10M, but thirteen at ≤23 carry the future. The cliff is not age. It is the July 2005 contract cluster: 13 players, $21.30M, all hitting simultaneously. If the GM does not lock them, the team scatters despite having $42.23M in profit.

**Gaborik** is the first and easiest renewal. 99 points in 82 games at 23, $1.10M, one year left. Even at $5.00M for six years he is a bargain. This is the single highest-leverage signature this summer because he is both the highest producer and the cheapest to retain.

**Chlup** is the second, and the one with a timing problem the GM should not miss. At 19, 59 points in 71 games, POTE 95, he has two years at $2.34M left. That keeps him off the July cluster. But the extension window is now: if he scores 70+ in 2005-06, his asking price at renewal doubles. A 5-6 year deal at $3.50-4.50M signed this July, before a breakout season, is the same leverage the GM had with Luongo.

**Nash, Eminger, Richards** round out the core renewals. Nash at 20 with 39 points, Eminger at 21 with POTE 99 and 23 points, Richards at 25 with 66 points. All at $1.00-1.20M with one year left. They need 5-year deals. Together with Gaborik and Chlup, these five are the 2006-2012 roster.

**The 34+ money clears naturally.** Roberts (38, $2.70M) and Belfour (40, $6.50M) expire this summer. Sundin (34, $8.40M, 5 years) is locked and will decline, but that is a 2009 problem. **Mogilny** at 36 with $5.50M and 2 years left is the one expiring-deal player who will not walk on his own. At 84 points he still produces, but at 38 when his deal ends, he is dead weight. If he is tradeable for a pick or a young player this summer, the $5.50M funds two core renewals.

**Fischer** is the one locked-in liability: 24, $3.70M, 4 years remaining, falling from 0.63 to 0.41 pts/g. Nothing can be done until 2008. It is $14.80M of declining production on the books for three more years.

**Draft capital is one fourth-rounder.** Every package must be funded by players. The over-80 expiring mechanic on Belfour and possibly Svehla is the only route back to a mid-round pick this summer.

**The verdict:** No cliff. The money exists ($42.23M profit, $116.95M revenue, no cap). The roster is young and deep. The single existential risk is execution failure in July: 13 players hitting UFA at once with no scouting upgrade to find replacements. Sign the five core, let the veterans walk, and the club is built for three years.

## Calendar

The trade deadline closed on March 19, 51 days ago, and we kept the core. That ship has sailed. What remains is the summer, where 13 contracts worth $21.30M expire simultaneously — the exact clustering trap the guide warns about — and the playoffs that start within days.

**The playoff move first: raise ticket prices.** We are the 1st seed in the East at 133 points. The guide's pricing curve is roughly 75 in round one, 80 in round two, 90 in round three, 100 in the final. That is the immediate action before a puck drops.

**The summer plan for the 13 expiring contracts, grouped by decision:**

**Gaborik** at 23, 91 base, 1.12 pts/g on 21.2 MPG is the priority. He is the first-line winger the coach has already named for next season. Lock him on 5–6 years immediately at renewal; his $1.10M current salary will rise sharply and a bidding war in July is the worst case.

**Richards** at 25, $1.00M, 64 pts is second. Five years. He is the best faceoff drafter on the roster at 70 and the second-best centre. He will command a raise but he is worth it.

**Nash** at 20 and **Eminger** at 21 are the two youngest on the list. Nash costs $1.20M now, Eminger the same with POTE 99. Lock both on 5–6 years. The GM protected Eminger from the Chara package specifically because his ceiling is open; same logic applies to Nash.

**Kaberle** at 27, $1.90M is at his prime. Five years is the right length for a defenceman at that age.

**Belfour** at 40 and $6.50M is the biggest payroll question. The GM said on January 15 he would offer a reduced contract and Belfour probably would not accept. The March 19 standing order kept him for the playoffs only. At 40, on $6.50M, with Luongo at 91 base and Tellqvist carrying high-90s potential, he walks. That saves $6.50M and creates the space to sign a replacement.

**Roberts** at 38, $2.70M, LW — the March 21 priority note already said he walks. The production curve at 38 does not justify $2.70M on a third or fourth line. He goes.

**Chistov** at 22 with POTE 95 is the one player who should be moved rather than renewed. The coach says his 14.0 MPG produced 0.30 pts/g and he should be on fourth-line minutes or scratched. We will not give him that role. At POTE 95, he carries trade value in a Bell package (82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE from Chicago). The May 5 coach note explicitly makes him available in that package. Move him before he walks for nothing, or renew on one year only and keep the option open.

**The depth five** — Colaiacovo (22, $1.10M), Alexeev (23, $1.10M), Upshall (21, $1.20M), Abid (25, $0.40M), Tellqvist (25, $0.80M) — renew on three years. Alexeev at 0.48 pts/g on 6.0 MPG outproduces Chistov on half the ice and the coach wants to test him further. Abid at $0.40M with TOUG 80 and CHKG 80 is cheap and fills a gap nobody else on this roster does. Tellqvist stays per the GM's standing order. Three-year terms stagger them against the five-year cluster and prevent a second renewal avalanche.

**The staggering plan prevents the trap.** Five deals on 5–6 years (Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger, Kaberle) expire in 2010 or 2011. Six deals on 3 years (Colaiacovo, Alexeev, Upshall, Abid, Tellqvist, plus Chistov if renewed) expire in 2008. Belfour and Roberts cost us nothing going forward. No single summer faces more than six renewals.

**For replacement after Belfour and Roberts walk:** the July targets are already identified. Iginla (CGY, 27, 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring) closes both the Mogilny scoring void and the toughness ceiling. Bell (CHI, 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE) is the only league-wide player who fixes the faceoff and toughness gap the coach has quantified at mean 51 and 57. CGY at 70 points with $14.43M profit cannot retain Iginla; CHI at 73 points with $29.46M profit are motivated sellers. These are July negotiations, not May ones.



**On the outstanding deliverable:** Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro development through February for the goalie trade window (#2, requested January 19, due February 20). Luongo is on our roster at 91 base — that half is delivered. The GM's March 19 standing order closed all goalie monitoring ("Goalies are solved. Done. Do not revisit that issue."). DiPietro's development is moot for Toronto's planning since we already have Luongo and Tellqvist covered. This task is closed by GM order.

## League scan

This phase answers: who across the league can close our three structural gaps (RW scoring, toughness, faceoffs) and replace Roberts, and why would their club let them go? We're in the last week of the regular season heading into a July where 13 contracts worth $22.10M expire and our trade currency is thin. The shortlist below is ranked by impact per package cost.

**Iginla** is the one. 94 overall, 128 points in 76 games, 1.68 ppg, TOUG 85, age 27, $6.50M expiring from CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring deals. He closes RW scoring and toughness simultaneously, which is the entire point of this exercise. CGY's prestige is 446 and their profit is $14.43M — they cannot build around a $6.50M winger and keep a competitive roster. The path is Belfour ($6.50M, 90+ base, expiring) as a salary match plus one young player (Chistov or Stahle) plus the 4th. That only works if the GM lets Belfour walk at renewal. If he stays on a cut, we need another large salary to match. This is the highest-impact target and the hardest to execute.

**Heatley** is the highest value available anywhere. 88 overall, 131 points in 79 games, 1.66 ppg, age 24, $1.10M expiring, POTE 84. ATL at 84 points with 11 expiring players cannot re-sign both him and Kovalchuk. They will trade one or lose both. A package of Chistov (22, POTE 95, SPEE 89) plus Tucker (83 CHKG, salary filler, expiring) plus the 4th gives ATL a high-ceiling young winger and a checking centre. ATL gets future value for a player who might walk. This is the most realistic big deal on the sheet.

**Cammalleri** needs no trade. 83 overall, 60 points in 61 games, POTE 98, age 22, $1.10M expiring from LA at 79 points with 14 expiring deals on $52.43M payroll. LA cannot keep him. In July he hits UFA and we simply offer him a five-year deal at $3.50-4.00M. With $42.23M in profit, this costs nothing but a phone call. He's the easiest elite prospect available.

**Bell** closes all three forward gaps in one player: TOUG 95, CHKG 93, FACE 87, age 24, $900K with 2 years left. He is not expiring, which means no over-80 mechanic and CHI has no urgency — they're profitable at $31.73M. But CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring deals (Daze $3.00M, Sullivan $3.00M, Zhamnov $4.20M all expiring) must rebuild the forward group and Bell at $900K is a depth piece they could convert into a prospect. Offer Stahle (21, POTE 96) plus the 4th. Acceptance is uncertain because CHI does not need salary relief.

**Stuart** replaces Roberts at defence with eight years of runway. 87 overall, POTE 92, CHKG 83, TOUG 74, age 25, $1.80M expiring. SJ at 76 points has 13 expiring deals on $45.39M payroll. They cannot retain all of them. They need picks and young players to retool. Chistov plus a 2nd (from an over-80 expiring mechanic on Roberts or Belfour) is a fair start. SJ at 76 points is not tanking, so they'll want a real return for a POTE 92 blueliner.

**Drury** is a bargain 86-overall center/wing with FACE 85 and 99 points in 82 games at 24 with POTE 81, expiring at $2.00M. BUF at 84 points with 10 expiring deals are retooling. The problem is price: a 24-year-old with 99 points and elite faceoffs is first-round price, and we hold one 4th-rounder. This works only if we can include a young player BUF values or if we use an over-80 expiring piece as salary filler.

**Conroy** at FACE 95 and 102 points in 82 games at 31 is a rental from CGY at 70 points. If we are already talking to CGY about Iginla, Conroy could be folded into the same package as a second-year rental who produces. At $2.00M expiring, CGY gets salary relief and we get a top-nine centre for the next season.

**Sillinger** at FACE 96 and 68 points in 62 games, $1.80M expiring, is the best faceoff man available. But PHX at 93 points are in the race and will not sell their second centre in May. He stays on the list only as a July UFA target if PHX lets him walk rather than re-sign.

**Roenick** is the wildcard. PHI has $66.73M payroll against $2.14M profit — the most financially distressed club in the league. At 89 overall, CHKG 90, FACE 82, 99 points in 82 games, he fills three gaps. But 3 years at $7.50M is enormous, and even a distressed team won't gut their first line mid-window without a substantial return. Long shot.

## Trade construction

This phase turns the summer shortlist into packages we can actually execute, given that our only designated chips are Tucker and a single fourth-rounder, and the coach confirmed on May 5 that Chistov is expendable. Three proposals, ranked by impact per cost.

**Heatley** is the priority. ATL at 84 points with 11 expiring cannot re-sign both him ($1.10M, 131 pts, age 24) and Kovalchuk. Whichever they keep, the other walks for nothing in July unless they trade first. We offer Chistov (22, POTE 95, SPEE 89, $1.10M) + Tucker (30, CHKG 92, TOUG 88, $1.30M, 2 years) + the 4th. ATL gets three assets for a player they'd otherwise lose free: Chistov is younger than Heatley, plays the same position, and carries POTE 95 against Heatley's 84. Tucker adds a physical checking wing they lack. The pick covers the gap in immediate production. We shed $2.40M and add $1.10M, then re-sign Heatley at roughly $4.50M x 5, which costs $3.40M net against $42.23M profit. Acceptance is uncertain because ATL might gamble on re-signing both, but their payroll makes it difficult.

**Bell** closes both structural gaps in one transaction: TOUG 88, CHKG 86, FACE 82, age 24, $900K with two years left. Koltsov (24, POTE 94, ACCE 96, $1.10M, 2 years) + the 4th is the package. CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring and $31.73M profit are in transition and could value Koltsov's POTE 94 over Bell's ceiling of POTE 81. The salary is near-neutral ($1.10M in, $900K out). The problem: CHI has no salary pressure and Bell is cheap depth they could simply keep. Acceptance is uncertain and I rate it low.

**Conroy** from CGY is the cheaper faceoff fix if Bell doesn't move. FACE 95, 102 points in 82 games, age 31, $2.00M expiring. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit want salary relief. Stahle (21, D, POTE 96, $0.97M, 3 years) + the 4th gives them a young blueliner with real upside and saves them $1.03M. The coach flagged Stahle as "needs games or needs to be moved." The cost: this is a one-year rental. Conroy at 31 does not develop; we get FACE 95 for one season and then he's gone. It buys time for Chlup and Spacek to mature into faceoff-capable centres. Only use this if the Bell deal fails.

**Cammalleri needs no trade.** He hits UFA in July from LA at 79 points with 14 expiring on $52.43M payroll. They cannot retain him. A five-year offer at $3.50-4.00M costs nothing in picks or players. POTE 98 at 22 with 60 points in 61 games is the highest-value free signing available and should be executed regardless of whether any trade lands.

**If none land:** sign Cammalleri, promote Alexeev to 12+ MPG (0.48 ppg on 6 MPG with POTE 94 says he has more), keep Upshall as the checking wing (CHKG 87, POTE 99), and accept the L4 faceoff gap for one more season while Chlup and Spacek develop. The team won at 133 points without these fixes; they won next year too, just less comfortably in a seven-game series.

## Owed

The job was to monitor DiPietro's development and Luongo's availability to find a goalie trade window. It's done and closed.

**Luongo** was acquired and is on Toronto's roster: 93 overall, age 26, $1.60M, 2 years left, 45 games played. The original purpose of this task — finding a high-90s goalie — is fulfilled. On 2005-03-19 the GM explicitly closed all goalie monitoring: "Keeping him and Luongo as two 90+ goalies for the playoffs. Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks."

**DiPietro** was the secondary target in case Luongo's window closed. It doesn't matter anymore. We have Luongo at 93 with two years of control at $1.60M and Belfour at 92 as the playoff backup. The trade window this job existed to serve no longer exists.

**What changed since last told:** Luongo arrived on the roster, the GM issued the March 19 standing order closing all goalie monitoring, and the season is over at 59-13-5. The task ran its course between January and February and was completed.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-11
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-11

Next game at WSH on Thursday 12 May 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is simple: are our young players getting the games their production warrants, or are some being wasted while others get more than they've earned?

**Chlup** is the easy one. 0.83 pts/g on 16.9 MPG at 19, 71 games, morale 100. He's earned the first-line centre slot for next season. I've asked twice this spring and neither was taken. He's still on the second line. This is the last game of the season so the call needs making before camp.

**Spezza** is the problem. POTE 99, age 21, morale 88 (lowest of the young group), 6.7 MPG over 46 games, 0.33 pts/g. His minutes collapsed from 9.1 to 4.8 late in the run. He's not getting the chance to develop; he's getting scraps on the bench. At 21 with that potential grade, a season at 6.7 MPG teaches him nothing. Next season he either gets a real top-nine role or we stop dressing him and let him play somewhere that needs him.

**Alexeev** is still the same mismatch. 0.55 pts/g on 8.3 MPG while Chistov (0.29 on 13.1 MPG) and Upshall (0.29 on 7.9 MPG) dress ahead of him. He's producing nearly double their rate on less ice. The GM's development rotation explains why Svehla sits, but Alexeev isn't young anymore at 23. He's earned a lineup spot or he's a trade piece.

**Upshall** gets his games at 68 GP on the fourth line, but his 0.29 pts/g says that's exactly where he belongs right now. POTE 99 is an opinion on file, not a claim on top-six minutes. No change for him.

**Spacek** at 19 on the fourth line, 7.6 MPG, 0.34 pts/g, morale 93. That's appropriate for a 19-year-old ranked prospect learning the league. No change.

**Gaborik** at 99 points in 82 games needs no development argument. He's arrived.

## Development trends

The season is over; this is the offseason read on who's climbing and who's sliding, which shapes next year's lines and the GM's sell list.

**Chlup** at 19 went 0.62 to 0.88 pts/g while minutes nearly doubled from 11.0 to 18.2. He carried more load and scored at a higher rate. That is what a franchise centre looks like developing in real time. No change needed, just confirmation the call was right.

**Chistov** at 22 went 0.29 to 0.30 pts/g while minutes jumped from 9.5 to 14.0. Rate held flat with a 47% increase in ice time. That is the profile of a bottom-six forward growing into a middle-six role. Give him a real audition in camp alongside Chlup.

**Kaberle** at 27 went 0.54 to 0.62 pts/g and 19.4 to 21.5 MPG. He is the only established defenceman trending up. His development curve has a year or two left on it.

**Afinogenov, Richards, Nash** all collapsed the same way: rates dropped 38%, 34%, and 49% respectively while minutes stayed flat. Three players, three positions, same pattern. This is the offseason system-fit project. Nothing individual to fix tonight.

**Spezza** went 0.43 to 0.24 on minutes that collapsed from 9.1 to 4.6. **Upshall** went 0.33 to 0.27 on minutes that fell from 13.4 to 4.8. **Spacek** went 0.55 to 0.28 on minutes that fell from 16.0 to 5.2. All three at 19-21 with real potential and no ice. Next camp is the decision: play them for real or stop dressing them.

**Klesla** at 23 went 0.50 to 0.31 on flat 14.9 MPG. Second consecutive declining season confirmed. He is a sell.

**McCabe** at 29 went 1.42 to 0.48 on 21.5 MPG. The early-season hot start was 24 games of noise; the other 58 tell the story. Sell.

**Sundin** at 34 went 1.46 to 0.97 pts/g while minutes rose from 16.9 to 21.7. He is absorbing the extra load to cover for declining wingers around him. At 0.97 he is still productive, but the pattern says plan for 0.80 next year. **Mogilny** at 36 went 1.62 to 0.83, a 49% drop. **Roberts** at 38 went 1.29 to 0.86. The aging curve is doing its work on all three; none of them will hold.

## Morale watch

The room is in good shape heading into Washington. Every dressed skater reads 100 on morale. The only man below 90 is **Spezza** at 88, and he has been climbing for three consecutive saves (+1, +2, +3), recovering from the low-80s dip. No action needed.

**Spezza** is the only watch item. 88 morale, 6.7 MPG, scratched for a full season. He is 21 with a 99 potential grade and he has been sitting in the press box while guys at 13.1 MPG (Chistov, Nash) carry the workload. His morale is rising, which tells me the results are doing the heavy lifting and the minutes gap is not actively poisoning him yet. If he drops back toward 85, that changes. Right now, no intervention — the GM has already decided development rotation takes priority in games we can afford.

**Gaborik** is at 100 with 99 points scratched. Morale has not cracked. This is either the locker-room upgrade doing its job or the 99-point season feeding his ego enough to offset the scratch. Either way, no concern.

**Abid** at 13.8 MPG on the fourth line with 66 points in 82 games is the production-to-ice-time mismatch I flagged back in March. His morale is 100 so the damage has not shown yet. The moment it dips below 95, he needs 17+ MPG or we are courting a problem.

No change. The room is right.

## Role composition

**The question is whether each unit is built from players suited to its job, and whether the roster holds enough of each role to staff two units per job.** The answer is that the units are constructed correctly; the gaps are roster-level and unfixable by moving players between lines.

**L1** is textbook top-line construction: Sundin at 87 faceoffs and 89 scoring anchors it, Roberts adds 81 checking and 87 clutch, Mogilny brings 90 scoring and 90 speed, Jackman at 86 checking and 75 toughness covers the back end. Nothing to change here.

**L2** is built to score and does that job. Afinogenov at 88 scoring and 88 playmaking is the offensive driver, Chlup at 76 faceoffs handles draws, McCabe and Kaberle on the back end. Checking mean 70 is low but appropriate for a second scoring line.

**L3** has speed (Chistov 94) and clutch (Richards 93, stamina 95) but only one real checker in Tucker (displayed at 90 today). Eminger and Klesla on the back end are both on declining seasons. The mean checking of 71 is thin for a line that faces third-line matchups. I cannot fix this by reshuffling because no other rostered forward brings checking above Tucker's level outside L1-L2.

**L4** has the same problem I flagged in April: faceoff mean 50, best 51 across Spacek, Abid and Upshall. None of them win a draw. The checking mean of 70 with best 83 (Abid today) is the floor the roster provides. Moving Richards down to fix faceoffs would strip L3 of its only 71-faceoff option and its best stamina engine at 95. That is a wash, not an upgrade.

**PK units are properly constructed.** K1 (Sundin, Roberts, Fischer, Kaberle) at checking mean 75 pairs veteran skill with enough bite to kill a skilled unit. K2 (Chlup, Tucker, McCabe, Jackman) at checking mean 80 is the true shutdown kill. This is the strongest part of the setup.

**Power plays are fine.** PP1 has Sundin and Afinogenov as the shooters with Kaberle and Jackman on the points and Roberts at net-front. PP2 runs through Mogilny's 90 scoring with Chlup and Richards as playmakers and Klesla's 90 speed as the rush outlet. No change needed.

**The structural gap persists:** only four rostered forwards check above 75 (Jackman, Roberts, Fischer, and Tucker on today's form), and only four win faceoffs at a meaningful rate (Sundin, Chlup, Roberts, Richards). That means my third and fourth lines cannot take a defensive draw or match a skilled opponent's top line. It is a roster problem, and I raise it as one again.

## Opponent matchup

The question: does WSH's hot run (9-0-1 in their last 10) demand a lineup adjustment, or do we roll the same sheet that's 4-2-1 against them this season?

**Jagr** is their entire team. OVR 84, SPEE 92, DEKG 94, SHPW 89. He's on their first line with Lang (75) and Dupuis (74), which means our first line faces him automatically: Sundin 89, Mogilny 88, Roberts 86. We outscore them on paper every night and the checking is already there — Roberts carries CHKG 84, TOUG 86 against a man with CHKG 50. No re-shuffle helps; the auto-pairing already puts our best three on his best three.

**Their depth is thin.** Second line: Grier 76, Zubrus 74, Radivojevic 71. Third: Sloan 66, Cleary 67, Gamache 61. Fourth: Peat 66, Marshall 61, Salomonsson 62. Our second line (Chlup 84, Nash 81, Afinogenov 84) is 39 points of overall better. Our third (Richards 85, Chistov 80, Tucker 78) is worse for them. There is no middle-six threat that matches our middle-six.

**Their D is worse than ours at every level.** Gonchar 78 and Witt 73 against our Jackman 84 and Fischer 83. Yonkman 70 and Pilar 69 against Kaberle 82 and McCabe 82. Doig 70 and Sarich 68 against Klesla 82 and Eminger 75. Their PP is 12.3% on 284 attempts — they will not beat us with special teams.

**The one note: fatigue.** They're on a nine-game heater, which means their vets (Gonchar 33, Jagr 33, Witt 30, Lang 34) are accumulating road miles with a thin third and fourth line. We're rested. That's an edge we already have; no change needed to exploit it.

Decision: no change. The current lines are the correct matchup already. Start Luongo and check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming.

## Owed

This is the defenceman evaluation the GM asked for every game. The season is done for these players -- McCabe, Klesla and Jackman all finished at 82, 82 and 80 GP respectively -- so these are the final numbers the offseason plan gets built on.

**McCabe** at 82 GP and 62 points gives 0.76 pts/g on 22.1 MPG. His 58-game recent window still sits at 0.48, which is what makes him a sell. At 29 with 4 years and $3.00M he is the most expensive piece we can move. No change from last week.

**Jackman** now finished at 80 GP, 37 points = 0.46 on 29.6 MPG. Last time I had him at 73 GP and 0.48; the extra seven games ticked the rate down slightly, which is what happens when a hot start dilutes. Confirmed sell at $0.70M x 3. No change.

**Klesla** is locked at 82 GP, 30 points = 0.37 on 14.8 MPG. Second consecutive season under 0.40 (0.38 at 22, now 0.37 at 23) on flat minutes. Confirmed sell at $0.90M x 2. No change.

**Eminger** stayed at 64 GP all month, 23 points = 0.36 on 15.5 MPG. His contract expires in July. Deadline passed without a trade, so unless a club takes him at season's end, he is a UFA loss. Confirmed loss unless someone moves for him.

**Kaberle** at 74 GP and 44 points = 0.59 on 20.8 MPG, 82 OVR. GM's keeper, no discussion needed. **Fischer** at 77 GP and 41 points = 0.53 on 22.4 MPG, 83 OVR. GM's keeper, no discussion needed.

**What changed since last delivery:** Nothing material. Jackman's rate fell from 0.48 to 0.46 as his final seven games filled in. Klesla's number is now official at 0.37. The sell list (McCabe, Jackman, Klesla, Eminger) and the keeper list (Kaberle, Fischer) are unchanged and now locked to final season data.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-09
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-09

Next game at WSH on Tuesday 10 May 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question: are our 23-and-under players getting the ice they've earned through production, and if not, is that a fixable lines problem or a ceiling problem?

**Alexeev** at 0.55 pts/g in 55 games is outscoring both Chistov (0.29, 68 GP) and Upshall (0.29, 68 GP) who both dress every night. He sits at 8.3 MPG while they get 13.1 and 7.9. With 5 games left this is the window to test him at higher load before the offseason forces a decision either way. Put him over Chistov for the remaining stretch.
