**Chlup** at 0.83 pts/g in 71 games at age 19 on the second line is the same finding from two weeks ago that hasn't been acted on. 16.9 MPG, morale 99. He belongs on the first line permanently and that assignment should be set before next season starts, not carried into training camp undecided.

**Stahle** is the quiet case. Four games all season at 21 with POTE 96, 17.8 MPG when he plays. Zero points in four games is noise. The problem is the four games. If he can't crack our top four defencemen at 21 he needs to be somewhere that plays him, and that's an offseason trade-conversation the GM should have regardless of his price.

**Spezza** at 6.7 MPG and 0.33 pts/g in 46 games has now spent the full season below the band his POTE would suggest, but his production has never demanded more. Morale at 88 is the lowest in the young group. The March read holds: camp assignment next year is the only lever, and if he doesn't earn top-nine minutes there, the argument stops.

**Upshall** at 0.29 pts/g on 7.9 MPG is producing depth-centre numbers at 21 with POTE 99. Same offseason audition-or-move decision as Spezza.

**Gaborik** has no development question. 99 points in 82 games, 20.5 MPG, morale 100. He's earning everything and more.

**Klesla** at 0.37 pts/g for the full 82 at 14.8 MPG confirms the March finding. He's played every game and his ceiling is where it is. That's a sell call, not a development call.

**Eminger** at 0.36 pts/g is still declining and his contract expires July 1. He plays because we need the bodies on the third pair, but the development window on him is closed.

## Development trends

The season is five games from done, so this is the look at who to build around and who to cut loose before July.

**Chlup** is the one who keeps getting better. 0.62→0.88 pts/g while minutes went 11.0→18.2 at age 19. No other young player on this roster is trending up on both rate and load. He is the first-line centre for next season and the year after.

**Gaborik** is quietly having the season of his career. 1.12 pts/g over 58 games on 21.2 MPG at age 23. His early pace of 1.42 was unsustainable, but 1.12 over two-thirds of a season is elite. At 23 he has three more peak years. We should be building around Chlup and Gaborik together.

**Kaberle** is the only veteran whose numbers went up: 0.54→0.62 on 19.4→21.5 MPG. At 27 he is still climbing. He anchors the blue line for the rebuild core.

**Chistov** got what we asked for — minutes jumped from 9.5 to 14.0 — and gave back 0.30 pts/g. That is not development; that is a career winger getting top-nine minutes. Next season he goes back to a fourth-line role or he does not play.

**Alexeev** continues to be miscast. 0.48 pts/g on 6.0 MPG outproduces Chistov (0.30 on 14.0 MPG) by a wide margin for less than half the ice. The mismatch from April is unresolved and will cost us next year if we ignore it.

**Spezza** and **Upshall** are dead seasons. Spezza 0.24 on 4.6 MPG, Upshall 0.27 on 4.8. Neither will be evaluated on this year. Camp auditions decide whether they make the roster.

**Spacek** got the March bump and lost 10.8 MPG anyway, falling from 16.0 to 5.2 with his rate at 0.28. The coaching staff stopped using him. Same offseason decision as Spezza: real audition or stop dressing.

**McCabe** is confirmed sell. 1.42→0.48 over the late window, season rate 0.76 across 82 games. The hot start is fully bled off. At 29 with four years and $3.00M, the asset value exceeds the hockey value.

**Fischer** is declining with load: 0.63→0.50 while minutes rose 20.8→22.9. GM says keeper and I accept, but next season's top pair should share the load better or his rate keeps sliding.

**Sundin** at 34 dropped 1.46→0.97 with minutes up from 16.9 to 21.7. He is carrying more to produce less. That is age, and it accelerates. His contract situation is the most urgent veteran planning question.

## Morale watch

The room is in great shape heading into the final week, and no ice-time changes are warranted on morale grounds.

**The overall picture:** Average morale sits at 92 across the roster, and nearly everyone is trending up — 20 of the 30 men are at 99 or 100 and gaining points from the team's recent results. This is the winning-streak effect doing its job, and a line change cannot improve on it.

**Spezza** is the one name worth watching at 88 morale and 6.7 MPG. He's the lowest on the roster and he's been a healthy scratch. His morale is climbing (+3 from the last save), so the gap hasn't widened, but 6.7 MPG is below even the 7 MPG band a depth forward would expect. If he drops into the 80s range on a forward's calibre he'll start costing us a point on every grade. With five games left and no role for him in the lineup, there's nothing to do tonight except monitor.

**Upshall, Spacek, Alexeev** all sit at 92 and trending up. Upshall at 7.9 MPG, Spacek at 7.6, Alexeev at 8.3 — all right at the depth band and all stable. No intervention.

**Everyone else is at 99 or 100.** Mogilny at 18.4, Chlup at 16.9, Richards at 16.1, Sundin at 20.3, Jackman at 29.6 — all in or near their bands with morale maxed out. Nothing to touch.

## Role composition

The question is whether each unit is built from players who suit its job, and where the roster simply cannot fill a role. The answer: most units are built correctly, L4 has a faceoff problem we cannot solve from within, and Gaborik's scratch against Washington is the biggest single question.

**Gaborik** is scratched. Against Washington (39-26) the standing order says maximize quality. At 97 scoring, 99 speed, 99 playmaking, and 98 clutch he is our best player by every offensive measure. If he is healthy, he plays first-line wing and Mogilny drops to second. If he is injured, the lines stand. I cannot see the reason from the brief — this needs the GM to confirm status on the injury screen before game.

**L4 faceoffs** sit at mean 51, best 53. That means Spacek, Abid, and Upshall cannot win a defensive-zone draw. The top four on the roster are Sundin (89), Chlup (78), Roberts (74), Richards (73), all of them committed to L1-L3. Richards at 73 is the only realistic candidate, but moving him off L3 with Tucker and Kaberle costs the checking chemistry that makes our third line work. I would rather eat bad draws on L4 than break L3 one game before a playoff push. This is a roster gap: we need a centre who wins draws and checks, and we do not have one.

**L3** actually suits its job. Checking mean 73 with Richards at 92 clutch and Tucker as the physical presence. Speed mean 87 is good for a defensive unit because it supports transition. No change needed here.

**K2** — Chlup, Tucker, McCabe, Jackman — carries checking mean 82, best 90. That is a legitimate shutdown kill and it is correctly built. K1 at checking mean 77 is fine since Sundin and Roberts carry the puck well enough to shorten shorthanded shifts.

**P1** has Sundin, Jackman, and Kaberle all capable of shooting and playing, with Afinogenov as the puck-mover. The unit suits its job. P2 with Mogilny (scoring 92) provides secondary threat. No structural flaw.

**L1 and L2** are built correctly for their roles. L1 is the shutdown-and-score line with Sundin's 89 faceoffs anchoring draws. L2 has Chlup's 78 faceoffs and is the offensive second unit with Kaberle and McCabe on the blue line. Both fit.

## Opponent matchup

The question: does WSH's 10-game heater change how we line up for Tuesday, given the auto-pair mechanic puts Fischer/Jackman on with whatever forward line the GM chooses to match against Jagr?

**Jagr** is the whole opponent. OVR 84, but his hands are scalding: DEKG 94, PUCK 90, PASS 90, ACCU 88. He plays on their first line with Lang (OVR 75) and Dupuis (OVR 74), so the production flows through him. His checking and toughness are 50 and 56. He does not want to be hit.

**Fischer and Jackman** are the answer and they are already in the right slot. Both carry CHKG 90, SPEE 92. When the GM puts our first line out against their first line, the auto-pair brings this D pair with it. That is the shutdown matchup we want, and no slot reorder improves it.

**Kaberle** is in the lineup per the GM's standing order for Washington nights. His CHKG is 69, so he should not be the one chasing Jagr, and he isn't. He sits on D pair 2 against their second line (Grier OVR 76, Zubrus OVR 74), which is a comfortable assignment.

**Luongo** has no fatigue icon. Start him. Kolzig is OVR 87 but their team is feeding him 1.3 goals against per game in the last ten, which means they are protecting him with structure. Our 32.3% power play against their 12.3% is the asymmetry that matters.

**No change to the lines.** The current slot order puts our best two defensemen against Jagr via auto-pairing, keeps Kaberle in as the GM ordered, and gives our offense (Sundin 90, Mogilny 89, Roberts 87) against their D1 (Gonchar 78, Witt 73). The matchup is already set.

**Defenceman sell-list update (standing obligation #1):** No change to the end-of-season list this game. Eminger (OVR 76, expiring, still declining) and Klesla (OVR 83 but 0.36 pts/g at 23) remain first and second off. McCabe's recent window at 0.48 keeps him on. Jackman and Fischer are locked by GM instruction. Kaberle is the keeper.

## Owed

The standing job is to read how our defencemen played and update the offseason sell list. The season is now complete for our regular-season stats, so every rate is locked. Nothing has moved since my May 2 delivery in terms of conclusions, but the sample is now final, not a running window, and that removes the only ambiguity I had left.

**McCabe** at 62 points in 82 games is a 0.76 season rate, but that number is propped up by 24 games of 1.00+ pace in October and November. The back 58 games rate at 0.48. He's 29, three years and $3.00M left. The sell case is stronger now than when I first raised it because I no longer need a caveat about the sample size.

**Jackman** finished at 37 points in 80 games (0.46) on 29.6 MPG. That's the lowest rate on the roster for any regular defenceman. His value is the minutes themselves: $0.70M for a player who logs 30 a night is cheap enough that a contender pays something for him. Sell confirmed.

**Klesla** at 30 points in 82 games (0.37) is a second straight year below 0.40 at age 23. The development curve is flat or declining. Sell.

**Eminger** at 23 points in 64 games (0.36) is expiring. After July he walks. Any return beats nothing. This has been the call since March; the deadline has passed but free agency is the backstop.

**Fischer** and **Kaberle** are keepers per your standing order. Both produced: Fischer at 41 points and 22.4 MPG, Kaberle at 44 points and 20.8.

No change from my May 2 read. The numbers locked; the list is settled.

# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-07

Toronto 59-13-5, 133 pts after 82 games.

## Role coverage

The structural gaps are unchanged since March: Toronto has zero players at 80+ toughness and one at 80+ faceoffs, and no combination of bench players fixes either. Everything else is covered on paper but ages badly.

**Toughness** is the club's defining weakness. The highest stored grade on the roster is Jackman at 75, then Roberts 73 and McCabe 73. That is a ceiling of 75 across 26 skaters. The Coach quantified it on 2005-05-05 and the 2005-03-19 finding confirmed it is structural, not form. No line combination, no ice-time shift, no internal move produces an 80. This requires Bell (CHI, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 24, 82 base) or Avery (LA, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 93 FACE, 25, $400K, two years). Bell also closes faceoffs at 82; Avery closes both gaps plus faceoffs at 93. These remain the only league-wide solutions.

**Faceoffs** are the same problem wearing a different jersey. Sundin at 90 is the only 80+ draw-taker, and he is 34. Chlup at 75 and Richards at 70 are the next best. The Coach confirmed on 2005-05-05 that the L4 faceoff mean is 52 with a best of 55, and no internal player changes that. Tucker at 67 is not on the L4 per the Coach's own note, and even putting him there would lift the mean only to about 58. Bell (82 FACE) or Avery (93 FACE) are the only acquisitions that fix this role.

**Scoring and playmaking** look covered with Mogilny 94 and Sundin 92 at the top, but Mogilny is 36 and fell to 0.79 pts/g by March 2005, and Sundin at 34 is in normal decline at 0.97 pts/g. The next man up in playmaking is Richards at 85 and age 25, then Spacek at 84 and 19. The club needs a 23-27-year-old top-six scorer to replace Mogilny's production. Heatley (91 base) and Iginla (93 base, 27, 140 pts/73 GP, TOUG 85) are the confirmed July targets. Iginla closes the scoring void and the toughness ceiling simultaneously.

**Koltsov and Gaborik** both read 92 overall at ages 24 and 23, speed grades of 92 and 98, and neither is in any line unit. That is depth, not a gap, but it is depth the Coach is not using. If the club cannot move one of them, the development clock runs. The Coach flagged Chistov at 0.29 pts/g on 13.1 MPG as a candidate to displace for Alexeev; Koltsov at 92 SPEE could also fill a top-nine slot.

**Checking** at six players 80+ is adequate: Jackman 87 (24), McCabe 86 (29), Fischer 82 (24), Upshall 80 (21). Tucker at 83 and age 30 is expiring; if he walks, the club drops to five and loses the only L4 checker. Not urgent, but worth tracking through renewal season.

**Stamina and durability** are fine. Kaberle 97, McCabe 94, Sundin 92 carry the load. Durability at four players 80+ is thin but not a competitive gap the way toughness and faceoffs are.

**Goalies** are solved per the GM's 2005-03-19 order: Luongo (26, 91 base) and Belfour (40, expiring) through the playoffs, then Luongo plus Ouellet (23, POTE high 90s) as the depth pair next season.

## Trajectory

Is this club aging into a cliff? No. It is contracting into one, and the cliff arrives the day the season ends. The age shape is healthy: 25 of 30 players are 29 or under, and the young core (Gaborik 23, Nash 20, Eminger 21, Chlup 19, Richards 25, Kaberle 27, Luongo 26) peaks between 2007 and 2010. But thirteen contracts worth $21.30M expire in a single July, and five of those are the entire forward and blue-line core. Without simultaneous 5-6 year deals for Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger and Kaberle, a 133-point team becomes a lottery squad in one off-season.

**Gaborik** is the most urgent renewal on the roster. He scored 99 points at 23 on $1.10M. If he hits the market at that production, no amount of Toronto revenue can guarantee he stays. A 5-6 year deal at even $4-5M/year is affordable against $114.69M in revenue and locks the franchise scorer through his prime.

**Richards** carries 66 points at 25 on $1.00M with one year left. Second centres at this production do not exist on the free-agent market. Without him, the scoring structure requires a trade from nothing (zero picks better than a 4th). Renew at 5-6 years.

**Nash** is 20 with 39 points and POTE 95 on $1.20M expiring. **Eminger** is 21 with POTE 99 on $1.20M expiring. Both are foundational players whose current salary is 10-20% of what their production demands. Lock both for 5-6 years.

**Kaberle** at 27 is ascending (0.62 pts/g on 21.5 MPG this season up from 0.54 last year). He is the only established defender with room to grow on a short-term deal. Four to five years at $3-4M keeps the top pair intact while McCabe (29, 4 years left) and Klesla (23, 2 years left, POTE 97) provide depth.

**Chlup** is the one contract that should be addressed before July. At 19 with 59 points and POTE 95 on $2.34M with two years left, he is still priced as a rookie. If he follows Nash's sophomore trajectory and posts 50+ goals, his price doubles next summer. Extend him to 5-6 years now while the current number is credible.

**The walk-away math works.** Belfour ($6.50M, 40) and Roberts ($2.70M, 38) leave, dropping payroll to $50.84M against $114.69M revenue. Even if the five core renewals cost triple their current salaries (roughly $20M combined, replacing $6.40M of expiring deals), payroll lands near $64M, still well under revenue. The money is not the constraint. The logistics are: five simultaneous 5-6 year negotiations in one off-season window.

**Draft capital is empty.** One fourth-rounder. The pick-recovery mechanic (trade any 80+ player you will not re-sign for a pick) is the only way to rebuild the inventory. Belfour at 92 base qualifies. Roberts at 81 points in 82 games likely does. Move both in July for first or second rounders rather than losing them for nothing.

**Chistov** (22, POTE 95, 0.29 pts/g on 13.1 MPG) and **Upshall** (21, POTE 99, 0.29 on 7.9 MPG) are the Coach's displaced players. Their combined POTE makes them tradeable for a depth piece or a pick even after a weak season. Move one or both in July.

## Calendar

With the deadline gone and six games left before the playoffs, every remaining decision is a summer decision. The question is not whether to buy or sell but who gets locked and who walks in July.

Thirteen contracts worth roughly $20.30M expire simultaneously. The March 21 plan from the vault is correct: lock the young core on long deals before they hit free agency, let the old ones go, and move Chistov while his trade value holds.

**Gaborik** is the first call. At 23 with 91 base, POTE 90, and $1.10M on the expiring deal, he is the most valuable player on the list. Lock 5–6 years immediately in July. If you lose him to a bidding war at his current salary of $1.10M, the gap he leaves is unfillable.

**Richards** at 25 with 64 points and $1.00M expiring is the second call. Same logic: 5–6 years. A centre producing that volume at that price does not reappear.

**Nash** at 20 and **Eminger** at 21 round out the four young players who carry the next decade. Both on 5–6 years. Eminger's POTE 99 is the single highest developmental number on the roster; Nash at 20 is the cheapest impact forward the club will ever hold.

**Kaberle** at 27 with 0.62 pts/g and 21.5 MPG is ascending, the one defender getting better. Renew on 4–5 years at a raise from his current $1.90M. He is entering his prime and will command more every season you wait.

**Colaiacovo** at 22 earned 17.9 MPG across 31 games. The coach wants a full-season audition. Renew on 3–5 years so he plays on a cheap deal while he proves it, then extend later.

**Alexeev** at 23 is displacing Chistov or Upshall with 0.55 pts/g on 8.3 MPG. Renew 3–5 years at the current $1.10M while the number is small.

**Upshall** at 21 and **Abid** at 25 are depth. Upshall produced 0.29 on 7.9 MPG, below what his ice earns, but he is 21 and cheap. Abid at $0.40M is the cheapest contract in the league. Both on 2–3 years.

**Tellqvist** at 25 with a POTE in the high 90s stays per the January standing order. Renew 3–5 years at $0.80M. Give him time.

**Belfour** at 40 and $6.50M is the hardest call, and the answer is to offer reduced terms and expect him to walk or retire. The GM's February note worried about losing the asset to retirement for nothing; that risk is now real and unavoidable at 40. Luongo at 91 base with two years left plus Tellqvist means the net is covered. Do not pay $6.50M for a 40-year-old backup.

**Roberts** at 38 and $2.70M walks. The Stuart note from March 30 names the replacement at 25 with POTE 91.

**Chistov** at 22 with POTE 95 is the trade chip the coach opened in his May 5 report. Alexeev displaces him, and Bell from Chicago at 82 base with 88 TOUG and 82 FACE closes both the toughness and faceoff gaps in one move. Package Chistov for Bell in July. CHI at 73 points and $29.46M profit are motivated sellers.

The draft lands June 8. Toronto holds only a 4th-rounder (confirmed: still owned, not traded). Scouting is not upgraded, so auto-draft is adequate. The January note to scout for goalies is a standing direction for the future, but at pick 120-plus you are drafting for depth, not for a starter.

Gelinas at 84 base, age 29, and $1.6M with one year left is a name that surfaced in the target scan. He could be a depth signing if he hits the market in July, but he is not a priority ahead of Iginla or Bell.

## League scan

The club's three structural gaps — zero 80+ toughness across 26 skaters, an L4 faceoff mean of 52, and Mogilny at 0.79 pts/g in his age-36 season — require at least two acquisitions in July. The league scan shows the best answers sit on clubs that are either losing or financially unable to retain their stars, which means the question is what we can put together with one 4th-rounder, Tucker at $1.30M expiring, and the pick-recovery mechanic on Belfour and Roberts.

**Iginla** is the single best target in the league. 93 base, TOUG 87, 128 points in 76 games at age 27 on $6.50M expiring. CGY are 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit. They cannot re-sign him and they will not lose him for nothing. He closes the scoring void and the toughness ceiling in one move. The salary is the problem: $6.50M against our $60.04M payroll pushes us toward $67M before renewals. But our revenue is $114.69M, so it is affordable if the return package is right.

**Thornton** is the quiet bomb. 94 base, TOUG 89, 25 years old, 83 points in 59 games, $4.00M expiring. BOS are 97 points but carry 13 expiring deals. If they decide to retool rather than re-sign everyone, Thornton at 25 with 94 base and elite toughness is the player they cannot afford to keep at centre. He closes toughness and scoring simultaneously at half Iginla's salary. BOS profit is $34.32M so they are not desperate, but 13 expiring players changes the calculus.

**Brad Stuart** closes the toughness gap at defence, which no Toronto blueliner can do. 87 base, TOUG 80, CHKG 89, POTE 91, age 25, $1.80M expiring, 52 points in 77 games. SJ are 76 points with 13 expiring on $45.39M payroll and $20.74M profit. They have too many players to re-sign, and Stuart is the one with the best market value right now. At 25 with POTE 91, he improves from here. The same package that gets him could also move Marleau, who is on the same club at $1.60M expiring with 98 points.

**Heatley** at 91 base, 131 points in 79 games, age 24, $1.10M expiring is the best pure scorer available from a seller. ATL are 84 points with 11 expiring. TOUG is only 75, so he does not close the toughness gap, but he replaces Mogilny's 1.62 pts/g peak with his own production at a quarter of the salary. If we cannot land Iginla or Thornton, Heatley is the fallback on scoring.

**Bell** at 82 base, TOUG 88, CHKG 86, FACE 82, age 24, $900K with two years left on $900K closes toughness and faceoffs simultaneously, the two gaps no internal solution addresses. CHI are 78 points with 10 expiring and $31.73M profit. The two-year contract means we are not renting; we own him through 2007. Production is the question: prior findings note ENDU 71 requires short shifts, and his 82 base means he is a bottom-six player on paper even if his grades fill the gap. He is the cheapest target on this list.

**Bouwmeester** at 81 base, CHKG 87, POTE 95, age 21, $1.20M expiring, 27 points in 79 games on 2629 minutes is the highest-upside defenceman available. FLA are 76 points with 19 expiring — the most of any club. They cannot keep 19 players. At 21 with POTE 95 and 33 MPG already, he is a top-pair piece in two years. His base is 81 today; the potential grade says he climbs.

**Havlat** at 87 base, 103 points in 82 games, age 24, $900K expiring is the cheapest high-volume scorer available. OTT are 77 points with 11 expiring. TOUG 68 means he does not close the toughness gap, but 103 points at $900K is the most production per dollar on this list.

**Komisarek** at 77 base, TOUG 76, POTE 91, age 23, $1.10M expiring, 82 points in 82 games on 2496 minutes is a young defenceman with real production. MTL are 66 points with 15 expiring — they are rebuilding and cannot retain him. The base is lower than Stuart or Bouwmeester, but 82 points from a 23-year-old defenceman with POTE 91 says the ceiling is well above 77.

**Avery** at 79 base, FACE 93, TOUG 83, CHKG 88, age 25, $400K with two years left closes the two gaps the Coach keeps flagging, but his production is 9 points in 82 games. He is a fourth-line player by output even if his grades say otherwise. He is the cheapest option on the list at $400K, and the two-year deal means no renewal hassle. He works as a depth addition, not a top-six answer.

**Marleau** at 89 base, 98 points in 71 games, age 25, $1.60M expiring from SJ is a July UFA target. If he hits free agency, we have the revenue to outbid anyone. But we should not count on it; if we are in the Stuart conversation with SJ, Marleau could be part of the same package.

**Drury** at 89 base, FACE 84, TOUG 79, 99 points in 82 games, age 28, $2.00M expiring from BUF at 84 points with 10 expiring is a near-miss on toughness but elite on everything else. He is a year older than Heatley, Gagne and Havlat, but the 99 points and 84 FACE make him the best scoring-plus-faceoffs package on the market.

**Briere** at 83 base, FACE 83, TOUG 65, 95 points in 82 games, age 27, $1.50M expiring from BUF is the same club, same window. Lower ceiling than Drury but a year younger.

## Trade construction

The July window is open with the season finished at 59-13-5 and 133 points. Five pieces are now free to move: Belfour ($6.50M, 40, expiring), Roberts ($2.70M, 38, expiring), Chistov (22, POTE 95, expiring), Upshall (21, POTE 99, expiring) and Koltsov (24, POTE 94, two years). None of these were on the GM's March 19 chip list ("Only Tucker and the 4th round"), but the Coach displaced Chistov and Upshall on May 5, and the trajectory read puts Belfour and Roberts on the walk-away list. That order was a deadline instruction; the July window requires expanding it.

## Proposal 1: Iginla from Calgary

**Belfour + Roberts + Chistov + 4th-rounder for Iginla.** This is the highest-ceiling package available in July. Belfour (92 base, $6.50M expiring), Roberts ($2.70M expiring, 81 points at age 38), and Chistov (22, POTE 95, $1.10M expiring, 20 points in 68 games) are all players we lose for nothing otherwise. Calgary sits at 70 points with 10 expiring deals and $14.43M profit. They cannot re-sign Iginla at $6.50M with that many contracts expiring, and losing a 93-base, 128-point, age-27 forward for nothing is the worst outcome available to them.

**Why Calgary says yes:** Belfour at 92 gives them a playoff-calibre bridge goalie. Roberts still carried 81 points and TOUG 92 on the trade screen. Chistov is a POTE 95, age-22 speed forward. Three assets plus a pick for a player they cannot retain. Acceptance is uncertain — Calgary may prefer to keep him one more year and hope to re-sign — but the $14.43M profit suggests they'd rather bank three assets than risk losing everything.

**Payroll effect on us:** We shed $10.30M in expiring salary, absorb $6.50M that needs extending. Net -$3.80M before renewal. Iginla at 27 with TOUG 87 closes the scoring void (Mogilny at 0.79 pts/g, age 36) and the structural toughness gap in one move.

## Proposal 2: Bell from Chicago

**Upshall + 4th-rounder for Bell.** Most realistic of the three. Bell (82 base, TOUG 88, CHKG 86, FACE 82, 24, $900K with two years left) closes the two gaps no Toronto player reaches: toughness ceiling of 75 stored and L4 faceoff mean of 52. Chicago are 78 points with 10 expiring and $31.73M profit. Bell is a useful bottom-six piece but not a franchise anchor, and at 82 base a retooling club takes the POTE 99 upside.

**Why Chicago says yes:** Upshall is 21 with POTE 99 and 0.29 pts/g on 7.9 MPG — a project, not a rental. At 78 points with 10 expiring, Chicago should be accumulating young upside. Bell's $900K and two-year deal make him expendable for the right prospect. Acceptance moderate: the pick softens it, but Chicago may prefer picks over a player with zero upside.

**Payroll effect:** We shed $1.20M expiring, absorb $900K for two years. Net -$300K. No renewal headache.

## Proposal 3: Avery from LA

**Koltsov for Avery.** No pick required, independent of the other two. Avery (79 base, FACE 93, TOUG 83, CHKG 88, 25, $400K with two years) is the only league-wide player with 90+ faceoffs and 80+ toughness simultaneously. His 9 points in 82 games make him the least productive forward on any club. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring deals cannot keep 14 players; Avery's roster spot is worth more than his production.

**Why LA says yes:** Koltsov at 24, POTE 94, ACCE 96, AGIL 92, $1.10M with two years left is a direct positional upgrade. LA at 79 points is rebuilding around youth, and Koltsov's speed profile matches what a retooling club needs. Avery's $400K is cheap to keep, but 9 points does not justify blocking a roster slot when you are re-signing 14 players.

**Payroll effect:** Shed $1.10M, absorb $400K. Net -$700K.

## Stacking and fallback

Avery is compatible with either of the other two — different clubs, different assets. Bell uses the 4th-rounder, so Iginla and Bell are mutually exclusive. Best-case stack: Iginla (uses Belfour, Roberts, Chistov, 4th) plus Avery (uses Koltsov). That closes scoring, toughness, and faceoffs while shedding $11.40M in salary.

**If none land:** Use the pick-recovery mechanic on Belfour (92 base, expiring, above-80 mechanic confirmed) for a rounder. Roberts at 38 likely qualifies but has not been tested. Sign UFAs from whatever clears in July. The toughness and faceoff gaps stay open for the fall, and the scoring replacement for Mogilny (0.79 pts/g at 36) goes unfilled.

**Tucker** stays on the shelf. Three games played, one point, age 30, POTE 79, two years at $1.30M. His shown TOUG 88 and CHKG 92 look good on the trade screen but the 3 GP tells every other club he cannot stay healthy. No club pays for grades behind three games.

## Owed

**Luongo availability and DiPietro development monitoring (task #2):** This task is closed. Luongo is on Toronto's roster at 93 overall, age 26, $1.60M, two years remaining. The GM acquired him during the season and on 2005-03-19 explicitly closed all goalie monitoring: "Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks." DiPietro's development was rendered moot by Luongo's arrival — the original January question was whether to chase a high-90s goalie from a non-contender, and that question was answered when Luongo landed.

Nothing has changed since March 19 because the standing order sealed the issue. Luongo has 2 years left at $1.60M, which means no renewal pressure until 2007. The only goalie note for the offseason is Belfour at 40, $6.50M, one year left — he walks unless he accepts a reduced deal, and the GM already decided that in January.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-07
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-07

Next game vs WSH on Sunday 08 May 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether our young players are getting the games they've earned, and with 82 games down, this is an end-of-year audit that feeds directly into camp planning.

**Chlup** has earned every shift he's getting and more. 59 points on 16.9 minutes per game at 19 is the best production-to-ice-time ratio on the roster. He's on the second line and should be on the first. My recommendation to move him there was not taken on April 28 or May 2. This is the repeat call.

**Gaborik** played all 82 games at 20.5 MPG and scored 99 points. He's listed scratched for upcoming games. At 23 with that production, I have no objection to resting him if the season is done, but he should not be a regular scratch next year.

**Alexeev** is the clearest rate-to-role mismatch on the roster. 30 points in 55 games at 0.55 pts/g, and he's scratched while Upshall (0.29) and Chistov (0.29) dress on lines three and four. He outproduces both by nearly double. The GM gave him 55 games and he responded. If there are meaningful games left, he deserves a spot. If not, camp priority: he earns third-line minutes based on this rate.

**Colaiacovo** got 31 games at 17.9 MPG and scored 12 points. The minutes suggest he was trusted when healthy, but 38% share at age 22 is too low for a player with 99 potential. Offseason: real camp audition, not a rotation spot behind veterans.

**Spezza** is the uncomfortable one. POTE 99, but 15 points in 46 games on 6.7 MPG. His minutes collapsed and his production collapsed with them. At 21, the gap between potential and output is the widest on the roster. He's not being wasted — he's been shown the door gently — but the camp decision needs to be clear: earn a top-nine role or be told his game isn't NHL-ready yet.

**Upshall** is getting games he hasn't earned. 68 games at 7.9 MPG producing 0.29 pts/g is depth-player production from a player on the fourth line. He's 21, so there's time, but this season was not a development success. His minutes collapsed from 13.4 to 4.9 late. Either camp proves he can hold a top-nine spot or he's the first scratch when Alexeev is healthy.

**Spacek** at 50 games, 7.6 MPG, 17 points is a 19-year-old fourth-pair defenseman getting an appropriate amount. No issue.

**Stahle** played 4 games, scored 0 points, scratched. Correctly on the outside. He's young enough to try again.

## Development trends

The season is nearly done, so this read is about who we carry forward and who we plan around.

**Chlup** is the clear riser. 0.62 to 0.88 pts/g while his minutes nearly doubled from 11.0 to 18.2. He got more ice and his rate went up, which is the pattern of a player earning his role. He belongs on the first line permanently and I have recommended that four times now. The data keeps confirming it.

**Kaberle** is the only veteran defenseman trending up. 0.54 to 0.62 pts/g on minutes that climbed from 19.4 to 21.5. The GM's instinct that Kaberle is a star on this blue line is borne out in the production curve. He is the anchor for next year.

**McCabe** at 0.48 pts/g on 21.5 minutes across 82 games confirms what I flagged on April 30. His 1.42 early-season pace was a hot start that bled off entirely. He goes back on the sell list for the offseason.

**Abid** is a worsening problem. His minutes dropped from 20.1 to 11.5 and his rate fell from 1.09 to 0.70 simultaneously. My March 16 note said he needed 18+ MPG. He got less. The mismatch between his production and his role has gotten worse, not better, and his rate is declining, which is the pattern that kills morale.

**Spacek** (0.55 to 0.28, 16.0 to 5.2 MPG) and **Spezza** (0.43 to 0.24, 9.1 to 4.6 MPG) both saw their roles evaporate mid-season. Both are 21 with high potential. Neither had any stored grade movement this window, which means the game hasn't recorded development yet. They need a real training-camp audition next season or we stop carrying them.

**Upshall** followed the same pattern: 13.4 to 4.8 MPG, rate slipped from 0.33 to 0.27. Camp-or-cut applies to him too.

**Nash** at 0.83 to 0.42 on flat minutes (12.9 to 13.2) reinforces the system-fit concern I noted in March. Same pattern as **Afinogenov** (1.17 to 0.73) and **Richards** (1.08 to 0.71). Three players aged 20 to 25, all with stable ice, all with their rates halved. The offseason system-fit review needs to include all three, not just the two 25-year-olds.

**Gaborik** looks like a decline at 1.42 to 1.12, but that is a small-sample early rate normalizing. 1.12 pts/g on 21.2 MPG at age 23 is excellent and his minutes went up. He is trending fine.

**Sundin** (0.97), **Mogilny** (0.83) and **Roberts** (0.86) are all declining on age but still contributing at useful rates. Sundin at 34 carrying 21.7 MPG and Mogilny at 36 on 19.1 MPG tells me they have one more year in them at least. Roberts at 38 on 21.4 is the outlier, and the plan should be to reduce his load next season.

No stored grades moved for any of our created or drafted players between December and May. That is unusual and worth watching — if Chlup's production keeps climbing but his card stays flat through next camp, something in the development pipeline is not firing.

## Morale watch

The room is right. The lowest morale on the roster is Spezza at 88, everyone else sits at 91 or above, and the average is 92. No one is sliding, and no one is at a level where a line move tonight would matter.

**Spezza** is the structural mismatch: 6.7 MPG against the 17 a player of his grade expects. But morale is 88 and flat, not declining, and I already called his season a write-off in March. The fix is camp assignment in the fall, not an ice-time adjustment in May.

**Abid** at 13.8 MPG with 66 points (0.80 rate) remains under his band if he reads 80+ calibre. His morale sits at 100 and trending up, so the mismatch hasn't bitten yet. If it dips before season's end, that's my trigger to move him up. Not tonight.

**Richards** (16.1 MPG) and **Afinogenov** (16.6 MPG) both sit under the 20-minute expectation for their grade, but both are at 98 and trending up. The system-fit review is an offseason conversation. No action needed while they're happy.

**Spacek** (7.6) and **Upshall** (7.9) both dipped earlier but are recovering at 91. They're depth wingers getting close to their band. No intervention.

## Role composition

The units are logical; the gaps are at the bottom of the roster, not in the arrangement.

**L1 (Sundin, Roberts, Mogilny, Jackman, Fischer)** is well-built: elite scoring (mean 86, best 93), solid checking from Jackman (88) and Roberts (83), and Sundin winning 89% of draws. Nothing to fix.

**L2 (Chlup, McCabe, Kaberle, Nash, Afinogenov)** is the offensive line. Scoring mean 83 with Afinogenov's 90 carrying it, Chlup's 78 on draws anchoring the centre spot. Kaberle provides offence from the blue, McCabe provides the defensive half of the pairing. The faceoff mean of 58 is thin outside Chlup, but this is a second line that should be scoring, not killing. Fine.

**L3 (Eminger, Tucker, Richards, Klesla, Chistov)** has Tucker as the physical presence and Richards at 73 on faceoffs carrying the draws. Chistov's 96 speed is notable but his production (0.29 pts/g from my last check) doesn't justify moving him up. The line works as a middle unit.

**L4 (Spacek, Abid, Upshall)** has a faceoff mean of 51 and a best of 53. Nobody on that line wins a defensive-zone draw. No player on the roster outside L1-L3 is above 73 in faceoffs, so this cannot be rearranged. It is a roster gap.

**P1 and P2** are well-constructed. P1 has Sundin and Kaberle as the quarterback pair with Roberts and Afinogenov as shooters (mean 86 scoring). P2 gets Mogilny's 92 scoring and a speed mean of 89 for transition. Both units suit their purpose.

**K1** is built on speed and stamina (86 and 82 mean) rather than brute force. **K2** is the physical kill with Tucker, McCabe and Jackman (checking mean 82). That split works: one to skate, one to hit.

**Toughness ceiling is 76 (Jackman).** No forward or D on this roster exceeds 76. We cannot build a unit that deters through fear. That's not an arrangement problem — it's the roster we have.

## Opponent matchup

The question is whether WSH demands a different look from what we already have, and the answer is no.

**Jagr** at 84 OVR is their only real weapon. Auto-pairing puts him against our first line — Roberts at 87 with 86 checking and 88 toughness, and Fischer/Jackman on pair one with 90 checking each. The GM's January concern about shutting down Jagr is already solved by the slot assignments we carry today.

**Their first pair** is Gonchar (78) and Witt (73). Fischer (84) and Jackman (85) own that matchup. Their second pair is Pilar (69) and Yonkman (70) against Kaberle (83) and McCabe (83). Every single defensive matchup goes our way by 5 to 14 points of overall.

**Their form** is nine wins in ten, which is hot, but they're scoring 3.2 per game against 1.6 against in that window — they've been beating lesser teams at home. We're 59-13-5 at home and they visit us.

**Luongo** at 93 OVR starts. No change needed there either; his ENDU at 77 is healthy and the GM should just confirm no fatigue icon on screen.

**Defenceman sell status** (delivering obligation #1): Jackman sold March 23. Klesla on the list at 83 OVR but declining, age 23. Eminger must move before July per the March 30 note. McCabe back on the list at age 29 with 0.48 recent rate. Fischer and Kaberle are keepers per the GM's standing orders. Nothing new shifts these calls before Tuesday.

## Owed

This is the defenceman sell-list check he asked for every game. The season is locked for most of them now, so this is close to the final read.

**McCabe** — 82 GP, 62 pts, 0.76 season rate, 22.1 MPG. Same numbers as May 2. The 58-game window at 0.48 is the real story: his first 24 games carried a 1.4 pace that has fully bled off. At 29, 4 years, $3.00M, selling a defenceman trending toward 0.50 is better than keeping him. No change from last week.

**Jackman** — now 80 GP, 37 pts, 0.46 pts/g on 29.6 MPG. He was at 0.48 over 73 in March; 7 more games ticked it down. The volume is enormous for a $0.70M contract, but the production rate says third-pair offence. Sell is confirmed. Slightly worse than last report.

**Klesla** — 82 GP, 30 pts, 0.37 pts/g on 14.8 MPG. Full season locked. Second straight year under 0.40. At 23 with 2 years and $0.90M, his value is his age and cheapness, not his game. Sell.

**Eminger** — 64 GP, 23 pts, 0.36 pts/g on 15.5 MPG. Was 0.38 at March 30, now 0.36. The slide continued. Contract expires in one year, so the trade deadline is past and July is the UFA cliff. Any offer this summer is better than nothing. Sell, urgency unchanged.

**Kaberle** and **Fischer** stay. GM has said it on the record twice for each.

Nothing has materially shifted since May 2. The numbers are final or near-final now and they all point the same direction.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 2, in-game 2005-05-05
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 2, in-game 2005-05-05

Toronto 59-13-5, 133 pts after 82 games.

## Role coverage

Role coverage at season's end determines what Toronto needs to buy this summer versus what the coach fixes with line changes — and the answer is stark on two roles and thin on two more.

**Toughness is missing, not thin.** Zero players carry 80+ TOUG in stored grades. Jackman tops the club at 75, Roberts at 73, McCabe at 73. The coach confirmed this on 2005-03-19 and repeated it today: no bench player closes it. This cannot be fixed internally and requires an external acquisition. Bell (CHI, 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE) remains the primary target. Avery (LA, 25, 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, $400K, 2 years) is the budget option that also solves the faceoff gap.

**Faceoffs are missing outside L1-L3.** Sundin at 90 is the only 80+ draw-taker on the roster. The coach's L4 mean is 52 with a best of 55. Tucker at 67 is the highest available outside the top nine, and 67 doesn't meet the coach's stated 65+ threshold when combined with teammates at 55. No internal line change creates a fourth-line faceoff winner. Bell (82 FACE) or Avery (93 FACE) are the only real answers.

**Scoring is thin going forward.** Ten players at 80+ scoring today, but three of the top six are 34 or older: Mogilny 94 (36), Sundin 92 (34), Roberts 90 (38). Mogilny's late-season production fell to 0.79 pts/g. Roberts is walking per the renewal plan. Once those two leave, the top scoring group drops to Gaborik 92 (23), Afinogenov 90 (25), Richards 85 (25). That's a one-elite-winger team without an acquisition. Heatley or Doan at July closes the Mogilny void.

**Top-pair defense is adequate in checking but thin in toughness.** Jackman 87 CHKG (24) and McCabe 86 CHKG (29) carry the top pair after Roberts walks. Kaberle at 0.62 pts/g on 21.5 MPG at 27 is the ascending puck-mover. Eminger at 21 with POTE 99 is the depth project. But zero of them carry 80+ TOUG, so the physicality problem is identical on the blue line. Stuart (SJ, 25, 87 base, 89 CHKG, 80 TOUG, POTE 91) is the only tracked target that adds toughness to defence.

**What the coach fixes internally:** Alexeev (0.55 pts/g on 8.3 MPG) displacing Chistov (0.29 on 13.1) or Upshall (0.29 on 7.9) is pure usage correction. Spezza's 0.33 pts/g on 6.7 MPG is a development question for camp. Colaiacovo at 17.9 MPG in 31 games needs volume. None of these require a trade.

**What only money and a counterparty fixes:** toughness, bottom-six faceoffs, the second top-six winger after Mogilny leaves, and a physical top-pair partner. Those are four distinct gaps with two known targets that overlap (Bell solves toughness + faceoffs; Avery solves toughness + faceoffs at half the cost).

## Trajectory

**The question this phase answers:** whether Toronto's age curve and contract structure point toward a cliff in the next three summers, or toward sustained contention. The answer is: no cliff if the July renewals land, and the renewal failure is the only real threat.

**The age shape is healthy.** Thirteen players 23 or under, twelve in the 24-29 band, five veterans 30+ (Tucker 30, Sundin 34, Mogilny 36, Roberts 38, Belfour 40). That is exactly the manual's 5-7 veterans with roughly 20 young players. The working core (24-29) has depth: Afinogenov, Fischer, McCabe, Luongo, Spacek, Koltsov, Richards, Spezza, Klesla, Safronov, St. Jacques, Jackman, Abid. The team is not top-heavy; it is bottom-heavy, which is where you want it.

**The cliff is July 2005.** Thirteen contracts worth $21.30M expire simultaneously. Two are walkers (Belfour $6.50M at 40, Roberts $2.70M at 38), which actually helps. The other eleven are the team's future: Gaborik ($1.10M, 99 pts), Richards ($1.00M, 66 pts), Nash ($1.20M, POTE 95), Eminger ($1.20M, POTE 99), Kaberle ($1.90M, ascending at 27), Upshall, Chistov, Colaiacovo, Alexeev, Koltsov (2 years), Abid. If even three of these walk unsigned, the roster empties in one summer. The manual's warning is written directly for this situation.

**Mogilny at $5.50M for two more years** is the payroll problem hiding in plain sight. He produced 84 points at 36, but his production fell from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g through the season. At 37 he becomes a 50-point winger eating 18 minutes. Iginla at a similar salary replaces the production and closes the toughness gap.

**Money is not the constraint.** Payroll $60.04M against revenue $112.43M leaves $52.39M of headroom before profit hits zero. Toronto can absorb Iginla at $7-8M without stress. The question is never "can we afford them" — it is "will they say yes."

**Draft capital is nil.** One fourth-rounder. Every trade Toronto makes must be funded with players. This makes the over-80 expiring mechanic critical: Belfour at 92 base and $6.50M expiring is a free pick if he can be moved. Roberts at 82 points produced but his base sits near 80; worth checking if he qualifies. Without recovering at least two picks this summer, the next trade window arrives empty again.

**Sundin at 34 with five years at $8.40M** is the single largest commitment. He produced 91 points at 0.97 pts/g, so the decline is not yet visible in the output. But five years at $8.40M means the club is tied to him through age 39, and by 36 the decline the coach flagged will cost 20-30 points. This is not a sell-now situation, but it is the contract to revisit at the 2007 deadline if his numbers drop below 0.80.

**The three moves that protect three seasons:**
1. Lock Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger, and Kaberle on 5-6 year deals this July. Without these five the team is gone.
2. Trade Belfour before July using the over-80 expiring mechanic to recover at least a second-rounder. Free ammunition for the next window.
3. Acquire Iginla to replace Mogilny's production at similar salary, while Roberts and Belfour roll off $9.20M. Net payroll change near zero with a five-year younger right wing.

## Calendar

The deadline closed on March 19, 47 days ago, and with Toronto at 133 points and 1st in the East, the only calendar question left is the summer: 13 contracts worth $22.30M expire simultaneously, and what happens on July 1 decides whether this team is a contender or a rebuild for the next two years.

**Luongo monitoring task (#2):** Delivered. Luongo was acquired and is on the roster at 91 base with 2 years left. The GM closed all goalie monitoring on March 19, and the standing order is clear: goalies are solved. No further work needed.

**The deadline is over.** The GM's March 19 order was to keep Belfour and Luongo for the playoffs, with Tucker and the 4th-rounder as the only remaining chips. Neither moved. Tucker now has 2 years left at $1.30M (80 base), so he is a controlled asset, not an expiring rental — his summer value is higher than his deadline value because a buyer gets him beyond this season. That's worth a pick or a young player in July.

**Let go (2):**

**Roberts** (LW, 38, $2.70M) walks per the March 21 standing order. At 38 he's past useful and the money buys nothing.

**Belfour** (G, 40, $6.50M) gets a reduced offer at renewal. The Feb 19 order was "stays if he wants to stay at reduced salary." He likely declines — no 40-year-old takes a cut from $6.50M. If he walks, the $6.50M is the single largest salary freeing up on the roster, and it's the money that funds the summer.

**Renew 5-6 years (the core, in order):**

**Gaborik** (RW, 23, 91 base, 87 pts, $1.10M) is the first call in July. POTE 90, $1.10M is absurd for a 91-base winger. Lock 5-6 years at market before anyone else touches him.

**Richards** (C, 25, 64 pts, $1.00M) is second. A 25-year-old centre at $1.00M is another bargain that a market correction will fix fast. 5-6 years.

**Kaberle** (D, 27, $1.90M) is ascending: 0.54 to 0.62 pts/g on 21.5 MPG. The coach named him the one rising defender. 5-6 years.

**Nash** (LW, 20, $1.20M) — 5-6 years. 20 years old, already in the lineup.

**Eminger** (D, 21, $1.20M) — 5-6 years. POTE 99, the GM locked him in as a foundation piece in February. He's not going anywhere.

**Renew 2-3 years (depth with development left):**

**Colaiacovo** (D, 22, $1.10M) — 2-3 years. Coach says 31 games at 17.9 MPG proves he can carry minutes; give him a full season to prove volume.

**Alexeev** (RW, 23, $1.10M) — 2-3 years. 0.55 pts/g on 8.3 MPG is the best rate among the bottom six. Coach wants him in the top nine next year.

**Abid** (LW, 25, $0.40M) — 2 years. The $400K is noise. He was signed for toughness and the coach confirmed it.

**Tellqvist** (G, 25, $0.80M) — 2-3 years. Standing order from January: potential in the high 90s, give him time. He saves no money at $800K.

**Trade or renew (the underperformers):**

**Chistov** (LW, 22, $1.10M) and **Upshall** (RW, 21, $1.20M) both sit at 0.29 pts/g. The coach says Alexeev displaces one of them. I'd trade Chistov: at 22 and 2 years left, he's a chip that fetches a 6th-rounder or a prospect. Upshall at 21 is worth keeping on a cheap 2-year as insurance while Alexeev proves himself in a larger role.

**Tucker** (LW, 30, 80 base, $1.30M, 2 years left) — the GM's standing chip from March 19, and the 4th-rounder goes with him. At 80 base with year control, this package is worth a 74-76 player or a late pick per the March 30 finding. Neither fills the checking-centre gap the coach quantified (L4 faceoff mean 52, best 55). Use him as a sweetener on a larger package, not a standalone deal.

**Summer UFA targets, ranked by fit:**

**Iginla** (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, $6.50M expiring) is the clear priority. He closes the Mogilny scoring void (0.79 pts/g and declining) and raises the toughness ceiling simultaneously — TOUG 85 fills the structural gap the coach flagged. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring players cannot retain him. Belfour's freed $6.50M covers the cost.

**Bell** (CHI, LW, 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE) is the only league-wide player closing both the toughness and faceoff gaps the coach quantified. CHI at 73 points with 10 expiring are sellers.

**Cammalleri** (LA, 22, POTE 98, 60 pts/61 GP, $1.10M expiring) is a value signing if LA can't keep both him and Frolov.

**The draft on June 8:** Toronto owns no pick better than a 4th-rounder. Scouting is the priority to upgrade so future drafts produce, but this June's draft is a minor event. No picks to move, no picks worth trading up for.

## League scan

This phase answers who across the league fills Toronto's four structural gaps — toughness, bottom-six faceoffs, the second top-six winger after Mogilny, and a physical blueliner — and which clubs have the financial and roster pressure to deal them this summer.

**Iginla** at 93 base with 140 points in 73 games, 85 TOUG and $6.50M expiring is the only player in the league closing both the RW scoring void and the toughness ceiling in one move. CGY sit at 70 points with 10 expiring contracts and $14.43M profit; they cannot retain him. He is the single highest-value acquisition available this July.

**Cammalleri** broke through at 60 points in 61 games on 20.8 MPG at 22 with POTE 97 on $1.10M expiring. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring deals and $52.43M payroll cannot re-sign him and Frolov simultaneously. If LA does not trade him before July, he is a direct signing at a bargain.

**Bell** at 80 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, $900K and 2 years left on a deal is the only re-signable player solving the toughness and faceoff gaps at once. He produced 28 points in 80 games on 17.8 MPG — real top-nine depth. CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring and $31.73M profit are the most motivated seller in the league.

**Avery** closes the same two gaps at $400K with 2 years left: 93 FACE, 88 CHKG, 83 TOUG. His 9 points in 82 games (0.11 pts/g) means he is a fourth-liner, not a top-nine wing, and that is exactly where the faceoff gap lives. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring will deal him for almost nothing.

**Stuart** at 87 base, 89 CHKG, 80 TOUG, POTE 91, age 25 is the only tracked blueliner adding toughness to the top pair after Roberts walks. SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring contracts on $45.39M payroll face impossible retention math, but at 76 points they are not desperate enough to deal a POTE 91 defenseman cheap. Medium probability of acquisition.

**Reid** at 77 base with 80 FACE and POTE 94 on $600K expiring closes the fourth-line faceoff gap at the floor price. STL at 86 points are not sellers, so this is a UFA signing play in July rather than a trade. His below-80 base means the over-80 pick mechanic does not apply.

**Heatley** at 91 base, age 24, is the elite winger replacement for Mogilny's scoring. ATL at 84 points with 11 expiring deals cannot retain both him and Kovalchuk (89 base, 104 pts). Whichever ATL releases becomes available. The over-80 expiring mechanic means ATL can trade him for a pick, so Toronto needs to offer Mogilny or another over-80 expiring player as a return.

**Mogilny himself at 94 base and $5.50M expiring** is a trade chip. The over-80 mechanic lets Toronto move him for a pick before he walks in July. That pick plus Tucker and the existing 4th-rounder funds the Bell or Avery trade.

## Trade construction

**Can we build packages that both sides accept for Iginla, Bell, and the Belfour pick, and if those fail, what's the fallback?** The answer is yes on two of three, with one critical sequencing dependency: Belfour must go before we can fund the Iginla deal.

**Mogilny** is the trade chip the trajectory phase identified but didn't package. At 94 base with 84 points but 0.79 pts/g in the second half, he is a rental for a rebuilding team that values the 84-point total more than the slope. He has two years left at $5.50M, which means the receiving club controls him through age 37. That's the price of getting Iginla.

**Koltsov** is the second piece because the coach hasn't asked for him in any development plan, he played 38 games (lowest among the POTE 94+ wings), and he carries two years of team control that makes the package real to a rebuilding club rather than two rental-years of nothing. ACCE 96 and POTE 94 at age 24 is a project any team would evaluate.

**Chistov** is trade material the coach has already written out: 0.29 pts/g on 13.1 MPG with Alexeev displacing him. POTE 95, SPEE 89, ACCE 88 at 22 means Chicago can audition him cheaply for one year. Tucker adds 88 TOUG and 92 CHKG for two years at $1.30M, which is exactly what a 78-point rebuilding club needs on its bottom six.

**Avery at $400K with two years left** is almost free for LA to move. But we'd be paying two POTE 94/99 wings (both expiring, so LA gets one season of evaluation) for a 0.11 pts/g centre. The math works if Bell fails and the faceoff gap persists, but it's the least attractive option because both returns walk in July 2006.



**If none of these land:** Sign Reid (STL, 77 base, FACE 80, POTE 94, $600K) as a free agent in July for the faceoff gap; he doesn't solve toughness but closes L4 faceoffs at the floor price. Renew Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger and Kaberle first (per the March 21 order), then pursue Heatley via UFA if ATL releases him rather than Kovalchuk. The Iginla deal is the only one that fills both structural gaps at once; without it the club enters 2005-06 with Gaborik as the only elite winger and zero players above 80 TOUG.

## Owed

**Item #2 — Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window.**

This task is closed. Luongo is on our roster at 94 overall, 26 years old, $1.60M with 2 years left, and he played 45 games this season. The GM confirmed his arrival on 2005-02-19 ("Luongo is arrived. Goalies are solved. Done.") and again on 2005-03-19 explicitly ordered all goalie monitoring closed ("Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks"). The DiPietro component was a backup option in case Florida wouldn't deal Luongo; Florida did. There is nothing left to monitor.

**What changed since last reported:** Nothing. The task was completed between the January request and the February 19 confirmation, and the GM's March 19 standing order formally retired it. I am delivering the final status rather than continuing to carry it as open work.

markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-05

Next game vs WSH on Friday 06 May 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether each young player got the games he earned across 82, and the answer is mixed: three are clearly wasted, two are earning their minutes, and two are taking ice they haven't produced against.

**Chlup** at 71 games, 16.9 MPG and 59 points (0.83 pts/g) got exactly what he earned and more. He's the best story on the roster and needs nothing from me development-wise.

**Gaborik** at 82 games, 20.5 MPG and 99 points is a star getting star ice. No development issue.

**Nash** at 69 games, 13.1 MPG and 39 points (0.57 pts/g) is getting games but his rate halved from last year's pace. System-fit review flagged, not a games issue.

**Alexeev** at 55 games, 8.3 MPG and 30 points is the clearest mismatch: 0.55 pts/g on less ice than both Chistov and Upshall, who each sit at 0.29. He outproduces both of them by nearly double and gets a third of Chistov's minutes. He needs top-nine ice next season or we're wasting him.

**Spezza** at 46 games, 6.7 MPG and 15 points (0.33 pts/g) with POTE 99 got nothing this season. His recent rate was even worse. He needs a full camp audition next year with a real shot at a roster spot.

**Colaiacovo** at 31 games but 17.9 MPG when he played shows the staff trusts him with minutes. The problem is volume, not quality of shift. At 22 with POTE 99 he deserves a full season's look.

**Upshall** at 68 games, 7.9 MPG and 20 points (0.29 pts/g) is taking fourth-line ice without producing. **Chistov** at 68 games, 13.1 MPG and 20 points (0.29 pts/g) is taking third-line ice without producing. Both are ahead of Alexeev in the lineup despite matching or lower rates on more minutes. They're blocking a player who earns more.

**Eminger** at 64 games and 15.5 MPG got his chance and delivered 23 points (0.36 pts/g) on a contract that expires. Already flagged as a sell.

**Spacek** at 50 games, 7.6 MPG and 17 points (0.34 pts/g) at age 19 is thin but acceptable for a ranked rookie. Not a crisis, but camp next year should show whether he can hold a top-six minute share.

## Development trends

The season is effectively over with 7 games left, so this window is the final read before offseason decisions. The story is clean: one man is genuinely ascending, several early hot samples are fully exposed as noise, and the young collapses we flagged in March are locked.

**Kaberle** is the only established player moving the right way: 0.54 to 0.62 pts/g on minutes that climbed from 19.4 to 21.5. At 27 he is entering his prime with a rising load. The GM already called him a keeper; this trend confirms that he should be built around, not just retained.

**Gaborik** looks like a decline on the sheet (1.42 to 1.12) but that 24-game December sample was hot. 1.12 over 82 games at 23 on 21.2 MPG is exactly where a franchise winger should be. No concern.

**McCabe's** full-season 0.48 confirms what the recent windows said. The 1.42 from December was a 24-game surge that bled off completely. At 29 with 4 years and $3.00M he belongs on the sell list and the offseason is the window.

**Klesla** at 0.31 on 82 games is his second declining season. He and McCabe are the same conversation: sell while there is something to get back.

**Sundin** at 0.97 pts/g on 21.7 MPG at 34 is a normal age curve. He is still the best thing on the second line. Planning around his next contract year is prudent but not urgent.

**Mogilny** at 0.83 on 19.1 MPG at 36 and **Roberts** at 0.86 on 21.4 MPG at 38 are declining at the pace their ages dictate. Both are still productive enough to dress but neither is part of next year's structure.

**Chlup** continues to confirm the call: 0.88 pts/g on 18.2 MPG at 19, up from 0.62 and 11.0. He is the offseason's starting point and nothing in this window changes that.

**Koltsov** shows the steepest drop on the sheet (1.10 to 0.29) but the December sample was 10 games. His real level is 0.29 on 9.9 MPG over 38 games. He is a trading chip per the GM's standing order and the asking price should reflect a depth forward, not a former 1.10 pace.

**Afinogenov and Richards** stay flagged for the system-fit review already scheduled. No new information from this window.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy and no intervention is needed heading into Friday's game against Washington. Morale runs from 88 to 100 across the Toronto roster, with the average at 98. Every player trending down is recovering, and nobody sits low for a reason minutes cannot fix.

**Spezza** is the lowest on the roster at 88, up 3 from his recent low. He is at 6.7 minutes a night on 46 games, below the 10-minute band his calibre expects, but he is scratched by design. The GM made that choice on January 15th to open ice for other young players. His morale is climbing and there is nothing to fix here tonight.

**Abid** continues to be the player carrying more than his slot suggests: 66 points in 82 games on 13.8 minutes a night, 0.80 per game on the fourth line. His morale is 100 so he is not unhappy, but this production on those minutes is the same mismatch flagged in March. It is not a morale problem; it is a usage note for next season's lineup construction.

**Jackman** is at 29.6 minutes a night on the top pair, well above the 23-minute average for a top defensive pair. Morale at 100 means he is not suffering tonight, but that load at 24 with 80 games is something to watch across the final week. No change for Friday.

Everyone else is at 95 or above with positive or flat trends. No line change is warranted on morale grounds for Washington.

## Role composition

The question is whether each unit is built from players whose skills suit its purpose, and whether we have enough of each role on the roster to build what we need.

**L1** is the most complete unit. Sundin wins draws at 91, Mogilny brings 94 scoring and 94 speed, Jackman checks at 90 and hits at 77 toughness, Fischer adds another 85 checking. The checking mean of 79 on a top line is a sign of balance, not weakness. No change.

**L2** is a scoring line with Chlup driving at 80 faceoffs and Afinogenov at 92/92 scoring and playmaking. McCabe (85 checking, 73 toughness) and Kaberle (85 stamina) anchor the back end. The faceoff mean of 59 is fine because Chlup handles the draws. The toughness mean of 66 is thin but acceptable for a second scoring line — that is not what they are asked to do. No change.

**L3** has a real asset in Richards: 75 faceoffs, 97 clutch, 87 stamina, the highest on the roster. Tucker provides the checking anchor, Chistov's 98 speed makes this line dangerous in transition. The clutch mean of 68 looks bad in isolation but Richards at 97 carries it; the bottom of that unit is simply depth-level play. No change.

**L4** is where the problem lives. Faceoff mean 52, best 55. The entire roster's faceoff inventory is Sundin 91, Chlup 80, Roberts 76, Richards 75, and then it falls off a cliff. Nobody dressed on L4 can win a defensive-zone draw. Abid's 72 toughness is the lone bright spot. In any close game this line gets pinned and cannot clear a zone. This is not fixable by rearrangement — everyone who wins draws is already on L1-L3 and their penalty kills. It is a roster gap.

**P1** is well built: Kaberle and Jackman on the points, Sundin net-front at 93 scoring, Afinogenov as the second shooter with 92 playmaking to feed him, Roberts screening. **P2** is dangerous because Mogilny at 94 speed and 94 scoring is the weapon, Chlup wins the entry draw, Fischer's 85 checking covers the rush back. **K1** uses Sundin's 91 faceoff to win the draw, then Roberts and Fischer pressure at 85 checking each. **K2** is our best checking unit at mean 84: Jackman 90, McCabe 85, Tucker alongside. All four special-teams units are correctly built.

The only structural finding is the fourth-line faceoff desert. It matches my April 13 note (faceoff mean was 51, now 52 — unchanged). No one on this roster outside L1-L3 wins a draw, and the four men who do are all already deployed where they are needed most. This needs to be filled through the trade or draft.

## Opponent matchup

Can we roll with the same lineup against Washington's 8-game win streak, or does their hot streak force a change?

**The answer is no change.** Our current lines are already maximum quality, the auto-pairing puts our best two D against Jagr's line, and we lead the season series 3-1-0 with a 20-10 goal advantage. There is no benched player who makes us better tonight.

**Jagr** is their entire team. OVR 84 with 94 deking and 90 passing on a line where the centre (Lang, 75) and left wing (Dupuis, 74) are journeyman-level. The auto-pairing sends Fischer (92 CHKG, 94 SPEE) and Jackman (92 CHKG, 91 TOUG) against him every even-strength shift. That's the best possible matchup we can construct, and it happens automatically.

**Their defense is soft.** Gonchar reads 59 checking, 59 toughness at 33. Yonkman is 70 OVR, Pilar 69. Our top two lines have 91 (Sundin), 90 (Mogilny), 86 (Chlup), 86 (Afinogenov). We should score at will against those pairs.

**Their form is the only concern.** 8 straight wins, 3.2 goals per game over that stretch. But our last 10 reads WOLWWWLWLW on a 59-13-5 season. We're the better team by a wide margin, and their hot streak is against weaker opposition.

**Luongo** starts. OVR 94, morale 100. Check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming per the standing order.

**Defensive review (obligation #1, delivery 11):** Fischer and Jackman are exactly the right pair to shut down Jagr tonight. No defensive change helps. The sell cases (Eminger at 0.38 pts/g, Klesla at 0.36, McCabe at 0.48 recent window, Jackman at 0.48 season) are all offseason decisions. Tonight, every one of our six defenders is suited to the matchup and none should be scratched.

## Owed

Standing job #1, defencemen end-of-season assessment. The season is now effectively over for our blue line, so these are final trading numbers.

**McCabe** — 82 GP, 62 pts, 0.76 season rate on 22.1 MPG. His last 58 games ran at 0.48 per my May 2 note. At 29, $3.00M for 4 more years, this is the biggest contract on the D corps and the rate says it was carried by a hot start. SELL.

**Jackman** — 80 GP, 37 pts, 0.46 on 29.6 MPG. His rate ticked down from the 0.48 I cited on March 23 (was 73 games then, now 80). Still the cheapest top-pair minutes in the building at $0.70M x 3 years. A buyer gets 30 MPG at $700K. SELL.

**Klesla** — 82 GP, 30 pts, 0.37 on 14.8 MPG. Two consecutive declining seasons confirmed. Age 23 should mean upside; the trend is the opposite. $0.90M x 2. SELL.

**Eminger** — 64 GP, 23 pts, 0.36 on 15.5 MPG. Contract expires this July. If he walks for nothing we get zero return on a 21-year-old with a 77 OVR. SELL before free agency. This is the most urgent of the four because the window closes with no deadline protection.

**Fischer** — 77 GP, 41 pts, 0.53 on 22.4 MPG, OVR 85. GM keeper. Agreed.

**Kaberle** — 74 GP, 44 pts, 0.59 on 20.8 MPG, OVR 84. GM keeper. One thing to flag: his contract expires ($1.90M x 1 yr). The GM should be thinking renewal or extension now, not after July 1.

**Colaiacovo** — 31 GP, 12 pts, 0.39 on 17.9 MPG, OVR 73. Expiring at $1.10M. If Eminger is sold and Klesla is sold, we'd be thin at 7th/8th D. Hold him for camp and decide there.

What changed since May 2: Jackman's rate fell from 0.48 to 0.46 on the final 80 games. Everything else confirmed at final totals. The sell list is four names: McCabe, Jackman, Klesla, Eminger. The keeper pair is Fischer and Kaberle, with Kaberle's expiring deal needing a GM conversation.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-04
