# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-04

Toronto 59-13-5, 133 pts after 82 games.

## Role coverage

With 59 wins and the season finished, the only question that matters is whether this roster can repeat — and two structural gaps plus two departures say no without offseason work.

**Toughness** is missing. Zero players carry 80+ in the stored grades. Jackman's 75 is the team high. The coach quantified the fourth line at a mean of 57, and he stated no bench player fixes it. This is the same gap flagged since February and it has not moved. Bell at CHI (88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, 24, POTE 81) is still the single best target — he closes toughness, checking, and faceoffs in one body.

**Faceoffs** are a one-man department. Sundin at 90 is the only draw-taker at 80+. He is 34. The coach flagged L4 faceoffs at 52 mean and 55 best as a roster gap and said no available forward fixes it by moving him in. That is correct — Richards sits at 70, Chlup at 75, Tucker at 67. Bell or Avery (LA, 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, $400K, 2 years) are the only league-wide players who close this alongside toughness.

**Scoring** is covered tonight with 10 players at 80+, but the top of it walks. Mogilny (94, age 36, declining from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g) and Roberts (88, age 38, 86 CHKG, 90 HERO) are both on expiring deals. Losing them removes 182 points of grade-weighted scoring and the team's best check-and-score defenseman. After they go, the scoring list drops to Gaborik 92, Sundin 92, Afinogenov 90, Abid 86, Richards 85 — four forwards and one center carrying the load.

**Koltsov** is 24, 92 speed, and "not lined" — the coach is not putting him in any unit. If his 0.30 pts/g at 7 MPG tells the story, he is a speed prospect who needs a camp audition rather than a fourth spot. Alexeev at 0.48-0.55 pts/g on 6 MPG outproduces both Chistov (0.29, 14 MPG) and Upshall (0.29, 7.9 MPG) and deserves the audition the coach flagged.

**Durability** thins sharply after Roberts leaves. His 98 is the highest on the roster. Afinogenov (95), Fischer (92), and Abid (90) are the only others at 80+, which means the back end has three men who can play a full schedule and nobody else proven.

**The goalie depth chart** has Luongo at 26 with two years and GAA 2.67 as the starter. Belfour (40, expiring, GAA 1.93, SV .931) walks per the March 21 standing order. Ouellet at 23 is the presumptive backup, but his grades say he is not ready: INTE 69, ENDU 60, BRKA 74, REBC 75. Tellqvist (25, expiring, GAA 3.39) is not the answer either. The club needs a second goalie who can hold a playoff series.

## Trajectory

The cliff question has a clear answer: this club is not aging into a cliff, but it is walking into a cliff edge next July unless it splits its renewal deals across two summers. The age shape is almost textbook — 25 players under 30, 5 veterans, matching the manual's target — but 13 of those 25 come due at once for $21.30M, and with no draft pick better than a 4th-rounder, the only way to keep the core is to sign it fast and smart.

**Sundin** is the one contract that cannot be fixed. At 34, $8.40M, five years left, he will be 39 when it ends. That is 14% of payroll for a player whose decline is certain by year three. There is no trade market for it. The move is to build around him for two more years while he still has it, which is exactly why Iginla matters now rather than later.

**Gaborik** is the single most important contract on the sheet. 23 years old, 99 points, 91 base, POTE 90, $1.10M with one year left. If he signs on five or six years at anything under $5M, Toronto has a top-line winger through age 29 at a price the rest of the league cannot match. If he walks, the RW void that Mogilny's decline created stays open and there is no pick to replace him. Lock him first, every summer, before another club offers six years.

**Richards** at 66 points, age 25, POTE 88, $1.00M, needs the same treatment. Nash at 39 points, age 20, POTE 95, the same. These three are the 5-6-year deals. Everything else in the expiring group gets two years.

**The renewal split is the whole summer plan.** Gaborik, Richards, Nash go to five or six years. Eminger at POTE 99 and 23 points in 64 games is the hardest call: his potential is the highest on the roster, but his production is not there yet. I would give him four years, not five, to buy one more year of proof without committing a 29-year-old salary. Upshall, Colaiacovo, Alexeev, Chistov, Abid all get two-year deals. This puts seven contracts up in 2007 instead of thirteen now, which is survivable at $110M revenue.

**Belfour and Roberts walk in July.** That frees $9.20M against a payroll of $60.04M. Roberts at 38 and 81 points is good production, but at POTE 52 he is not improving and $2.70M buys two years of a 40-year-old. Belfour at $6.50M and 40, scratched, with POTE 50, is purely a playoff rental at this point. Walk both, bank the money, and spend it on Iginla.

**Fischer** is the slow leak. $3.70M, four years left, 41 points at 24 on 77 games with POTE 90 and declining production. He is not a problem this summer but he is dead weight by 2008, when he will be 27 and earning $3.70M for a bottom-four slot. Nothing to do about it now; note it for 2007 trade bait.

**The draft-pick situation is the structural weakness.** Toronto holds one 4th-rounder. Every depth addition, every backup, every re-stock after the young core matures must come from player-for-player trades or free agency. That means any trade must return a young player, not a pick, because the club cannot afford to spend picks it does not have and cannot afford to rebuild without them.

## Calendar

The trade deadline passed on March 19, and the regular season ends in one game. The only date that matters now is July. Toronto finished 59-13-5, 133 points, first in the East, and the entire summer plan is about who stays on a new deal and who is brought in with the draft capital we just acquired.

**Pick capital has changed.** As of January, I held that Toronto owned nothing better than a fourth-rounder. That is now stale. The current pick holdings show five slots from New York Islanders (rounds 1 through 5) plus Dallas's fifth. That R1 is the single asset that makes the Iginla pursuit live, which was impossible in January when Florida's R1 demand blocked every high-end package.

**Gaborik** at 91 base, 23, 87 points, $1.10M is the first signature. Five or six years, done before July opens, or he hits the market with 91 base and 23 years of age and the price doubles.

**Richards** at 25, 64 points, $1.00M is second on the same five-year logic. Nash (20, $1.20M) and Eminger (21, POTE 99, $1.20M) are third and fourth. These four renewals lock the core through 2010-11 before any of them gets expensive.

**Kaberle** at 27, $1.90M gets three or four years, not five. At 31 or 32 the production ratchets against him and the salary becomes a cap issue in every future trade discussion.

**Tellqvist** at 25, $0.80M with POTE in the high 90s stays on a three-year deal per the GM's standing order from January 15. **Abid** at $0.40M with TOUG 80 and CHKG 80 is a two-year re-up; he is too cheap to lose.

**Belfour** ($6.50M, 40) and **Roberts** ($2.70M, 38) walk. That frees $9.20M from a $52.47M payroll with $12.46M profit.

**Iginla** is the summer's defining target. 93 base, 27, 140 points in 73 games, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring. CGY sit at 70 points with 10 contracts expiring and $14.43M profit; they cannot retain him and will not tank a R1 for nothing. The Islanders' first now gives Toronto a package Iginla's age and salary can justify. He closes the Mogilny scoring void (0.79 pts/g at 36) and the structural toughness ceiling (zero Toronto players at 80+ TOUG) in one move.

**Cammalleri** at 22, POTE 98, 60 points in 61 games on $1.10M is the UFA value signing if he hits the market. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring cannot hold both him and Frolov.

**Bell** at 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, FACE 82 from Chicago (73 points, 10 expiring, $29.46M profit) closes the fourth-line gap the Coach quantified at checking mean 61 and toughness mean 57. He is a trade target, not a UFA, so the pick capital helps here too.

**Upshall, Alexeev, Chistov, Colaiacovo** all carry expiring deals at $1.10-1.20M. The Coach's report gives them all a camp audition: Upshall POTE 99 at 0.29 pts/g, Alexeev 0.48 pts/g on 6.0 MPG, Chistov 0.29 on 14.0, Colaiacovo 0.39 on 17.9. Renew the ones who show, release the rest. The four slots and $4.50M are not worth carrying if the numbers stay flat.

## League scan

The gaps are toughness, faceoffs, RW scoring after Mogilny walks, top-four defence after Roberts walks, and a backup goalie. Five queries across the league's 30 clubs now return a shortlist, and two names close multiple gaps at once.

**Iginla** (CGY, RW, 27) is the top target on every axis. 93 base, 128 points in 76 games, 87 TOUG. He closes the RW scoring void AND the toughness ceiling simultaneously. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring deals and $14.43M profit cannot retain a $6.50M winger. The payroll math works if Belfour ($6.50M) and Roberts ($2.70M) leave as planned, freeing $9.20M against our $60.04M base. He is the highest-paid player we would ever roster, but he is also the only one who solves two structural problems in one signing.

**Brewer** (SJ, D, 26) is the best value acquisition available. 88 base, 61 points in 82 games, 82 TOUG, 93 CHKG, $2.00M expiring. He replaces Roberts' defensive role and raises the team's toughness ceiling by seven points over Jackman's current 75. SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring deals and $20.74M profit have too many defensemen to keep all of them. At 26, he has four or five good years left.

**Lalime** (OTT, G, 30) solves the backup goalie question at 92 base with a 3.09 GAA in 68 starts. His $1.90M is less than a third of Belfour's, and OTT at 77 points with 11 expiring contracts and $32.36M profit are the most motivated sellers in the league. The GM's March 19 order closed Belfour trade monitoring, not the backup question itself, and Belfour's departure in July reopens it. Ouellet at INTE 69 and ENDU 60 is not a playoff backup.

**Havlat** (OTT, LW, 24) is the cheapest real scorer available: 87 base, 103 points, $900K expiring, POTE 85. Same selling club as Lalime, which means a double-dip package could work. His 68 TOUG does not help the toughness gap, so he is a scoring complement rather than a gap-closer.

**Heatley** (ATL, RW, 24) produces 131 points in 79 games at $1.10M with 91 base and POTE 85. ATL cannot retain both him and Kovalchuk (138 points, also $1.10M expiring). If they keep Kovalchuk, Heatley is the best RW on the market by production. His 75 TOUG is below the team's new ceiling target but well above the current roster's mean.

**Kovalchuk** (ATL, LW, 22) at 138 points in 79 games, 89 base, POTE 85, $1.10M, is the highest-scoring player on any expiring deal in the league. Two years younger than Heatley with higher points and higher potential. The tradeoff: he plays LW, not RW, so he does not directly fill Mogilny's slot. Still, 138 points at $1.10M is the single best value in the league this summer.

**Thornton** (BOS, C, 25) reads 94 base, 89 TOUG, 90 CHKG, 83 points in 59 games at $4.00M expiring. He would close scoring, toughness, and checking in one move. But BOS at 97 points with $34.32M profit are a contender, not a seller. The January note flagging his base as uncertain (76 vs 94 across two readings) adds doubt. Pursue only if they miss the playoffs or if a direct approach costs nothing.

**Brad Stuart** (SJ, D, 25) at 87 base, 52 points, 80 TOUG, POTE 91, $1.80M expiring, is the higher-ceiling alternative to Brewer on the same club. If SJ keeps Brewer, Stuart is the next call. At 25 with POTE 91, he has eight years of development ahead.

**Gagne** (PHI, LW, 25) at 86 base, 108 points, $2.40M expiring, 95 SPEE, is a speed scorer for a club in financial distress: PHI at $66.73M payroll with only $2.14M profit need to shed salary. His 58 TOUG means he adds nothing to the toughness problem.

**Belanger** (LA, C, 27) at 82 base, 97 FACE, $700K expiring is the cheapest faceoff fix in the league. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring deals are sellers. Fourteen points in 64 games means he is a specialist, not a top-nine player, but at $700K he provides insurance for Sundin's age.

**Komisarek** (MTL, D, 23) carries 77 base with POTE 91 and $1.10M expiring from the worst team in the league (66 points, 15 expiring). The 82 GP with 82 points from the season stats is anomalous for a 77-base defenseman and warrants verification before building a case on it, but the club situation makes him available.

## Trade construction

This phase answers: which packages can we actually put together to close the RW scoring, top-four defence, and backup goalie gaps, given that Belfour and Roberts walk in July, we hold one 4th-rounder, and the coach has flagged Spezza, Upshall, Chistov, Koltsov, and Alexeev as players without a roster spot? Three proposals below, ranked by the product of value gained and probability of acceptance.

**Brewer from San Jose for Upshall.** SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring deals and $20.74M profit has too many defensemen to keep them all. Brewer is 88 base, 61 points, $2.00M, and the 93 CHKG he carries is what Roberts provides us tonight. Upshall is 21 years old with POTE 99, CHKG 87 already, $1.20M, and one year left — a player SJ can extend at a low price and build a top-nine role around. We give nothing else. No pick, no second player. The payroll swap saves SJ $800K net. We gain a 26-year-old top-four defenseman who raises our team toughness ceiling from 75 (Jackman) to 93 in checking. The only reason SJ says no is if they want to retain Brewer for a playoff run at 76 points, which is unlikely for a team 7 points from a wild card with 13 contracts to renew.

**Lalime from Ottawa for Ouellet.** OTT at 77 points with 11 expiring deals and $32.36M profit are the most motivated sellers in the league. Lalime is 92 base, 68 starts, $1.90M — a proven number two for any club. Ouellet is 23 with POTE 97, GSH_ 86 and GSL_ 86. Ottawa are 77 points and still building; a 23-year-old with POTE 97 is exactly the crease piece they need for the next four years. They save $1.00M in the swap. We get a playoff-ready backup at 92, which means we don't start next October with Ouellet at INTE 69 and ENDU 60 between the pipes if Luongo needs rest. No pick required.

**Iginla from Calgary for Spezza plus Tucker plus the 4th-rounder.** This is the moonshot. Iginla closes RW scoring AND toughness in one move: 93 base, 128 points in 76 games, 87 TOUG, $6.50M. Calgary at 70 points with 10 expiring deals and $14.43M profit cannot retain a $6.50M winger. A 21-year-old center at POTE 99 with two years of team control at $1.00M is the entire foundation of a rebuild. Add Tucker (30, CHKG 92, TOUG 88) as a veteran locker-room piece and the 4th-rounder. Calgary gets: franchise-center potential, a physical mentor, and a pick. We get: a 27-year-old who produces 128 points and 87 toughness on the same night. Payroll: we go up $4.20M in the swap (Spezza $1.00M + Tucker $1.30M out, Iginla $6.50M in), but Belfour and Roberts walking frees $9.20M, so net we are $5.00M lower than today. The risk: Calgary's AI may value a POTE 99 highly enough to prefer a single player over the package, or may decide to rent Iginla one more year and re-sign later. Acceptance is uncertain.

**If none land.** Sign Brewer or Lalime as UFAs in July if they don't get claimed, since the guide notes skaters are available in free agency and signing them earns experience points. Heatley (ATL, 91 base, 131 points, $1.10M) becomes the RW fallback — he solves scoring but not toughness. Bell (CHI, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 82 FACE) remains the cheapest toughness-and-faceoff fix if his contract structure allows a trade in July rather than a straight UFA signing.

## Owed

**Item #2 — "Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window."**

This task is complete and closed. Luongo is on our roster at 94 overall, 26 years old, $1.60M with 2 years remaining, 45 games played this season. The monitoring was for acquisition purposes; acquisition happened. The GM closed all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19 with the order to keep Belfour and Luongo as two 90+ goalies for the playoffs.

**DiPietro** is no longer relevant to us. He was tracked as a potential return piece to New York Islander in a Luongo package. The deal is done, Luongo is here, and DiPietro belongs to NYI. His development is another club's problem.

Nothing to report on either man because the question that made them worth watching is answered. This task can be struck from the list.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-04
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-04

Next game vs PIT on Wednesday 04 May 2005.

## Development opportunity

The season is over in all but name, 82 played and one game left tonight, so the question is who got their shot this year and who didn't — with a small window tonight to give one look if it costs nothing.

**Chlup** has earned every minute and more. 59 points in 71 games at 16.9 MPG at 19 years old, morale 98. He's not a development case anymore, he's the first-line centre next season. No change needed on him.

**Nash** is 69 GP, 13.1 MPG, 39 points, morale 100. His rate halved but his minutes didn't move and his head is right. He's getting what a 20-year-old on the second line should get. Offseason system-fit note stands, but his games-earned is not the issue.

**Alexeev** is the clearest mismatch on the roster. 30 points in 55 games is 0.55 pts/g, scratched. Upshall produces 0.29 and plays 68 games. Chistov produces 0.29 and plays 68 games. Alexeev nearly doubles both of them and sits out. Tonight's opponent is PIT at 24-34, which is a development game per the GM's own standing order. Put Alexeev in tonight's lineup on the right side in place of Upshall. It costs nothing against a 24-win team and gives the coaching staff one more look before offseason decisions.

**Spezza** at POTE 99 has managed 46 games and 6.7 MPG. His morale at 88 is the lowest of any young player on the roster, and that tracks with the ice-time starvation I flagged in March. 0.33 pts/g is not a number that screams for top-nine minutes, but the combination of POTE 99, collapsing minutes, and morale sagging is the one case this season where a player with obvious upside got squeezed out without an injury or a clear performance failure explaining it. Offseason, he either gets a real camp audition or the roster moves on.

**Klesla** played every single game at 23 and produced 0.36 pts/g on 14.8 MPG. That's two consecutive declining seasons. He's taking minutes a 23-year-old should be earning with production, and he isn't. Offseason sell stands.

**Upshall** is dressed every night on the fourth line, 68 GP, 7.9 MPG, 0.29 pts/g. He's a depth forward getting depth minutes at a depth-forward rate. The POTE 99 is a scouting number, not a contract. At 21 with 0.29, he hasn't earned more than what he's getting.

**Colaiacovo** at 31 GP and 17.9 MPG is in and out. The minutes per game are fine when he plays. The 38% share reflects the GM's rotation, not a development neglect problem.

**Stahle** played 4 games at 21 with POTE 96. The sample is too small to judge anything. He's not a roster decision tonight.

**Spacek** at 19 is on 7.6 MPG on the fourth line, right at the depth band. For his first pro year that's reasonable. 0.34 pts/g is not a number that demands an upgrade tonight.

## Development trends

The season ends tonight, so this is the last read before offseason decisions get made. The trends since December tell us who to build around and who to move.

**Chlup** is the clearest riser: 0.62 to 0.88 pts/g while minutes went from 11.0 to 18.2. He got more ice and got better, which is the opposite of what most 19-year-olds do under a bigger load. He is the first-line centre next season without argument.

**Kaberle** at 27 is the only veteran trending up: 0.54 to 0.62 pts/g on 19.4 to 21.5 MPG. He's getting better as he gets more trust. The GM already called him a star, and the numbers agree.

**Spacek** at 19 went 0.55 to 0.28 on minutes that collapsed from 16.0 to 5.2. He had a role early and lost it entirely. At 19 with potential to develop, next camp audition is the only thing that matters now. Same story for **Spezza**: 0.43 to 0.24 on 9.1 to 4.6 MPG. Both need a real run in camp or we stop dressing them.

**Gaborik** at 23 slid from 1.42 to 1.12 but that 1.42 was a hot 24-game start. He finished at 1.12 on 21.2 MPG, which is a genuine top-line winger. The early pace was the outlier, not the decline.

**McCabe** finished at 0.48 on the 58-game recent window against his season 0.76. The hot start has fully bled off. At 29 with $3.00M and four years, the sell is confirmed.

**Klesla** went 0.50 to 0.31 on flat 14.9 MPG. Second consecutive declining season at 23. Sell stands.

**Abid** is the concern for morale: 0.70 pts/g but minutes halved from 20.1 to 11.5. His rate is respectable for a bottom-six role but he's a 25-year-old who scored 1.09 early in the year now getting fourth-line minutes. If his morale dips this offseason it's because of the ice time.

**Mogilny** at 36 went 1.62 to 0.83 on 16.9 to 19.1 MPG. Normal decline for his age. He's still a capable winger but the trend line says he won't hold 0.83 next year either. Plan for one more year at reduced role, not two.

**Roberts** at 38 is 0.86 on 21.4 MPG, also declining. Sundin at 34 is 0.97 on 21.7, aging better than his linemates. Both are planning-around players at this point, not building-block players.

**Nash** at 20 dropped 0.83 to 0.42 with flat minutes at 13.2. Same system-fit pattern as Afinogenov and Richards. All four need the offseason review to determine whether our style suits them or their usage needs changing.

## Morale watch

The room is fine. Morale averages 92 across the roster with nobody below 72 and the entire dressed lineup at 98 or 100. No one needs a line change tonight for morale reasons.

**Abid** is the one to keep an eye on. He sits at 0.80 pts/g (66 points in 82 games) on 13.8 minutes a night on the fourth line. A player producing at that rate expects around 17 minutes per the morale bands. His morale reads 100 right now, trending up, so nothing has broken. But this gap has been open since March and if results dip he is the first candidate to crack. I am not moving him tonight because there is nothing to fix yet.

**Spezza** at 88 and **Upshall/Spacek** at 91 are the lowest readings on the dressed roster. Spezza is scratched entirely (6.7 MPG season, age 21, potential 99), which is a development decision the GM already made. Upshall and Spacek are at 7.9 and 7.6 MPG on the fourth line, right at the depth-man band of 7-10 minutes they should expect. Their morale is stable. Nothing actionable tonight.

Everyone else: **Jackman** at 29.6 MPG, **Sundin** at 20.3, **Fischer** at 22.4, **Mogilny** at 18.4, **Richards** at 16.1, **Chlup** at 16.9 — all sitting comfortably within or above their expected bands with morale at 98 or 100. The first line is getting what they expect and showing no frustration.

No change.

## Role composition

The units are structurally sound given this roster. One persistent gap remains unsolvable by arrangement: the fourth line cannot win a faceoff.

**L4 faceoffs (mean 51, best 54).** Three forwards on the ice, the best faceoff grade among them is 54. Nobody above 60. Every defensive-zone draw against them is a coin flip we lose. The whole roster only has four centres above 70: Sundin 90, Chlup 79, Roberts 75, Richards 74. Moving any of them to L4 fixes L4 and breaks the line they leave. That's not a rearrangement, it's the same hole moved. This is the same gap I flagged April 13; Abid's arrival helped the checking mean (62 to 73) and toughness (57 to 65), but his faceoff doesn't lift the unit above 54 best.

**L1 is well-built.** Sundin takes draws (90), Roberts checks (84), Mogilny and Sundin score (92 each), Fischer and Jackman bring the best defensive pair (84/89 checking). Speed mean 90, best 94. Nothing to fix here.

**L2 has low faceoffs (mean 59, best 79) but Chlup handles them.** The unit's job is scoring, and Afinogenov at 90 and Chlup at 79 give it two bodies with playmaking. Nash adds energy. Acceptable construction for a second offensive line.

**L3 is the most balanced unit.** Tucker's checking best of 93 on this line is the highest single checking grade we show anywhere. Richards brings clutch 96 and stamina 89. Chistov's speed (97) gives the line zone-exit capability. This is the shutdown group and it's correctly assembled.

**PK units are right given the draw constraint.** K1 carries Sundin and Roberts specifically because a penalty kill starts with a defensive-zone faceoff, and Sundin at 90 is the only reason it can win possession out of the gate. K2 has the better checking mean (83 vs 78) with Tucker, McCabe and Jackman, but can't take the opening draw. That's the correct division of labour, not a mistake.

**PP units are close in quality (P1 scoring mean 86, P2 also 86).** Both have shooting and playmaking. Kaberle on P1 and Klesla on P2 gives both units a point man. No change needed.

**Recommendation: reduce L4's minutes.** With no faceoff on that unit, every start is a possession tax. Give L3 more shifts and L4 less until a centre with a draw above 60 is available. That's a minutes adjustment, not a roster rebuild.

## Opponent matchup

**No change for this game.** We are 133 points against a 24-34-11 club we have beaten seven times, and their power play converts at 11.6% (32 on 276). There is no matchup problem to solve.

**Pittsburgh's top line** is Lemieux at 39 with PASS 99, PUCK 95 and DEKG 98 alongside Straka (SPEE 93, FACE 83). Lemieux can still make plays with his hands, but at 39 with ENDU 82 he is not going to outwork Sundin and Richards for 60. Meloche at 77 is the weak link on that line. Our second and third pairs (McCabe/Klesla, Eminger/Klesla) are more than adequate against their bottom six.

**Their defencemen** read 67-77 across all six slots. Jackman (86), Fischer (85), Kaberle (84) and McCabe (84) will eat them alive on our first PP unit. No adjustment needed; the quality gap is the plan.

**Obligation #1 — defenceman review.** I cannot assess individual games because per-game lines are not available to me. What I can report: all six D carry morale at 100, displayed OVRs range 77-86, and no one is injured or fatigued. Eminger (77, age 21) remains the weakest link and the trade candidate. The rest are in good standing for the playoffs.

**Goalie:** Start Luongo (OVR 94, morale 100). Check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming, per your standing order.

## Owed

The defenceman sell-list update for the end of the season: final numbers are in, and nothing moved from what I said on May 2nd.

**McCabe** — 0.76 pts/g across 82 games on 22.1 MPG, but his recent window is 0.48. He's 29 with 4 years and $3.00M. On the sell list since May 2nd. No change.

**Jackman** — Final season: 0.46 pts/g on 29.6 MPG across 80 games, down from the 0.48 I projected at 73 games. Same conclusion: sell. His value is the bargain contract ($0.70M x 3), not the production.

**Klesla** — 0.37 pts/g on 14.8 MPG over 82 games. Second consecutive declining season (0.38 at 22, 0.37 at 23). Sell at $0.90M x 2. No change.

**Eminger** — 0.36 pts/g on 15.5 MPG across 64 games. The slide continues: 0.44 in February, 0.38 in March, 0.36 now. He's 21 with an expiring contract ($1.20M). Must move before free agency or he's gone for nothing. No change.

**Fischer** and **Kaberle** are keepers per your standing orders. I won't raise them again.

The sell list is McCabe, Jackman, Klesla, Eminger. Nothing has shifted since my May 2nd note. The final season data confirms the calls I already made.

markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-02

Toronto 59-13-5, 133 pts after 82 games.

## Role coverage

This is a post-season look at role coverage, and the question that matters now is what the roster looks like the day after the playoff run ends, not the day of it. Toronto are 59-13-5 with Belfour at 1.93 GAA in 37 games and 32-5; coverage is sufficient for a Cup run. The construction problems are all on the far side of June.

**Toughness** is the only structurally missing role. Zero players at 80+; the ceiling is Jackman 75, Roberts 73, McCabe 73. No internal move fixes this. The gap is confirmed and permanent without a trade or signing.

**Forward checking above 85** is thin and getting thinner. The coach's April 30 flag is right: Roberts (86 CHKG) is the only forward above 85, and he is 38 on an expiring deal. Tucker at 83 and Fischer at 82 are next, then Upshall at 80. After Roberts leaves, the ceiling drops to 83. Bell (CHI, 86 CHKG, 24, POTE 81) or Avery (LA, 88 CHKG, 25, $400K) both reset that ceiling.

**Faceoffs** are a one-man problem. Sundin at 90 is the only forward above 80. Chlup sits at 75, Richards at 70. No internal player draws enough to take a line's worth of draws from Sundin. Avery at 93 FACE closes this immediately; Bell at 82 does most of it.

**Gaborik** reads 92 overall and 98 speed but is listed as unlined. If that is still true entering the playoffs, it is the single largest internal gap. He is 23, $1.10M, and the July renewal priority. Dress him or explain why he is not in a unit.

**Scoring** is covered today (10 players at 80+) but the top two carry age risk. Mogilny is 36 and fell from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g this season. Roberts is 38 and expiring. The next wave is Gaborik 92, Afinogenov 90 (though declining from 1.17 to 0.73 pts/g), and Chlup at 19 producing 0.88 pts/g. The depth exists; the veterans are leaving.

**Durability** is thin. Only four players at 80+, and the best (Roberts, 98) is 38 and expiring. Afinogenov 95 and Fischer 92 are the next two. This is not urgent but it compounds the age problem: the players who stay in the lineup are also the ones who are aging out.

**Goalies** are solved through this season. Luongo (26, 2y, $1.60M) and Belfour (40, 1y, $6.50M) carry the playoff run. Belfour walks after this year. The post-Belfour depth chart is Luongo and then Ouellet (23, 2y) or Tellqvist (25, 1y, 880 SV%). The GM's January standing order to fetch a high-90s goalie from a non-contender is still open.

## Trajectory

The club is in its competitive window, but one $5.50M contract will strangle it by 2007 if left alone.

**Mogilny** is the single largest trajectory problem. He is 36, on $5.50M with two years remaining, and his production fell from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g during this season. At $11.00M total remaining, that is a third-line winger's price with a first-line label. No contender wants a declining 37-year-old at that salary in a rebuild, and non-contenders have no reason to absorb him. The window to trade him is this summer while 84 points in 78 games still looks respectable on paper. After one more decline, the market closes.

**Sundin** is 34 with five years at $8.40M. He scored 91 points in 82 games, so the deal works tonight. But that money runs through age 39. If he declines by year three, Toronto is paying $8.40M for a second-liner from 37 on. There is nothing to do — the deal is locked — but it means the payroll floor stays high regardless of who else walks, and the club cannot shed money quickly.

**The cluster this summer:** 13 contracts at $21.30M expire. Belfour ($6.50M) and Roberts ($2.70M) walk, freeing $9.20M. The remaining 11 must be re-signed or lost. Gaborik (99 pts/82 GP, 23), Richards (66 pts/80 GP, 25), Nash (39 pts/69 GP, 20, POTE 95), and Eminger (POTE 99, age 21) are the foundation of the next five seasons. Each needs 5-6 years. At realistic new-money rates, Gaborik might command $5M, Richards $3.50M, Nash $4M, Eminger $3M, Kaberle $2.50M, Abid $1.50M — roughly $19.50M replacing $6.60M, a net increase of about $13M. After Belfour and Roberts leave, payroll rises from $60.04M to approximately $63-64M. Against $110.33M revenue and $37.86M profit, that is absorbed easily. The money is not the problem. The speed of the re-signings is.

**Draft capital is near zero.** One fourth-rounder. Every acquisition must be funded by players. This means Iginla at $6.50M requires sending back a comparable salary, and with Mogilny (36) the only player near that number, the return package to Calgary looks like a rebuild-killer for them. The Iginla trade works only if CGY accepts a young player plus Mogilny as a short-term rental they can flip again. That is the GM's negotiation to attempt, not mine to close.

**The age curve is healthy.** 13 players at 23 or under, 12 in the 24-29 prime. Four players over 34 (Sundin, Belfour, Mogilny, Roberts), but only Sundin and Mogilny remain after this summer. That is the correct shape. The risk is not aging; it is failing to re-sign the young core before July and watching them scatter.

## Calendar

The deadline passed on March 19 with the roster intact; the GM protected the core, kept Belfour and Luongo for the playoff run, and the only chips left unspent are Tucker and the fourth-rounder. That window is closed. The only date that matters now is July, and the job is a single question: which of the thirteen expiring players come back and on what term, and who walks in.

**Gaborik** is the renewal that starts everything. 91 base overall at 23, POTE 90, 87 points this season at $1.10M. He's a star and gets 6 years. Every day this isn't done is a day a bidding war builds. This is the first phone call in July, not the fifth.

**Richards** is the second call. 25, 64 points, $1.00M. He's the franchise centre alongside Sundin and needs 5-6 years. If Gaborik is locked and Richards isn't, you've kept the wing and lost the centre.

**Kaberle** at 27 and $1.90M is the veteran top-pairing D on 5 years. He's the most expensive renewal on the list but the one least replaceable at his grade this summer.

**Nash** at 20 and $1.20M gets 6 years. He's the cheapest long-term lock on the roster and the one where the game's re-signing mechanics reward early commitment most.

**Eminger** at 21 with POTE 99 gets 6 years. The GM protected him from deadline packages for exactly this reason.

**Colaiacovo** at 22 is the third young D the Coach is still evaluating. 5 years is right if he's in the plans for next camp. If the Coach's May question ("does he need 60+ games or is the rotation enough?") resolves against him, a 3-year deal with a cheaper structure is defensible, but the POTE-grade profile says hold him.

**Alexeev** at 23 producing 0.55 pts/g on 8.3 minutes is better than both Chistov and Upshall at 0.29, and the Coach's April 30 report says exactly that. Renew him on 3 years as a middle-six option. He earns the roster spot the Coach says he deserves.

**Chistov** at 22 and **Upshall** at 21, both 0.29 pts/g, are depth. If Alexeev is kept, one of these two goes. I'd let Chistov walk — the Coach's own numbers put him below Alexeev on every axis and he carries $1.10M against $1.20M for Upshall, who is a year younger and can be traded as a sweetener. Sign Upshall to a 2-year deal at reduced salary or let both go and carry Alexeev plus Tucker as the bottom-six depth.

**Tellqvist** at 25 with high-90s POTE stays on 3-4 years as Luongo's backup and developmental prospect. The GM's January standing order was clear: give him time. He saves no money but he covers the position if Luongo gets hurt in the playoffs or next season.

**Abid** at 25 and $0.40M is the cheapest toughness on the roster. 2 years, keep him. The Coach's gap is structural: zero forwards above 85 TOUG outside Roberts. Abid's 80 TOUG and 80 CHKG are the best the roster carries after Roberts walks.

**Belfour** at 40 and $6.50M walks. The GM's decision is final. We tried to move him before March 19 and chose not to. The money saved is real: $6.50M out of a roster that needs $22.10M of expiring contracts replaced or shed.

**Roberts** at 38 and $2.70M walks. This is the $9.20M the two veterans free for the renewal money Gaborik and Richards will command.

**The RW void is the summer's biggest hole.** Mogilny fell from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g at 36, and his contract situation puts him among those leaving or near-leaving. Iginla (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, 140 points in 73 games, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring) is the target. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring contracts and $14.43M profit cannot retain him. If he hits the market, he closes the scoring void and the toughness ceiling in one signing. That's $6.50M of salary, but it's the Belfour money and more.

**Bell** (CHI, LW, 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81) is the toughness and faceoff fix the Coach's fourth-line gap demands. Chicago at 73 points with 10 expiring are motivated sellers. He's not a star, but he fills a role nobody else on the roster does.

**Stuart** (SJ, D, 25, 87 base, 80 TOUG, 89 CHKG, POTE 91) replaces Roberts' physical presence on the blue line. San Jose at 72 points with 13 expiring on $45.39M payroll can't keep everyone. The risk is they value POTE 91 highly and won't deal cheap.

**Playoff ticket prices** should be raised now. Round one at 75, round two at 80. TOR at 133 points in front of a home crowd in a first-round series is the revenue the season was built to produce.

The draft is June 8. With no picks better than a fourth and the scouting priority the GM set in January (goalies), there's no franchise-changing pick coming. Auto-draft on current scouting levels unless the upgrade has landed.

## Outstanding task

**#2 — Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window.** This is delivered. Luongo is on Toronto's roster at 91 base with 2 years left, acquired during the season. DiPietro monitoring is moot: the GM closed all goalie trade tasks on March 19, Luongo arrived, and the position is solved per standing order. Task closed.

## League scan

The question is who Toronto can acquire this summer to close the four structural gaps: zero players at 80+ toughness, no forward above 85 checking after Roberts leaves, one faceoff taker in Sundin, and the Mogilny scoring void at RW. The summer is when the market opens wide and every seller's motivation is clearest.

**Thornton (BOS, C, 25, 94 base)** is the best player on any likely seller in the entire league. 89 TOUG, 90 CHKG, 79 FACE, 83 points in 59 games at $4.00M and expiring. BOS at 97 points carry 13 expiring contracts and cannot re-sign all of them; if they doubt his extension, they'll deal him for value rather than lose him to UFA for nothing. He closes toughness, checking, and faceoffs simultaneously while adding first-line scoring. The Jan 22 reading of 76 base was an outlier; two later readings including today's confirm 94. This is the move that changes the roster shape more than any other single transaction.

**Iginla (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base)** is the confirmed July priority from the April 12 note. 87 TOUG, 81 CHKG, 128 points in 76 games, $6.50M, expiring. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring and $14.43M profit cannot retain him. He closes the Mogilny scoring void and raises the structural toughness ceiling from 75 to 87 in one move. The problem is matching $6.50M without gutting the prospect base; Mogilny at $5.50M is the closest salary, and he's the piece that must move regardless.

**Lalime (OTT, G, 30, 92 base)** is the best goalie available on the Jan 15 standing order profile. 92 base, POTE 80, $1.90M, expiring, from a 77-point team with 11 expiring contracts and $32.36M profit. Cheapest of the 90+ non-contender goalies by a wide margin. His GAA is 3.09 in 4252 minutes, which reflects Ottawa's defense more than his own play; the grades are what the game trades on. At $1.90M he's absorbable alongside Luongo without Belfour's $6.50M on the books.

**Theodore (MTL, G, 28, 91 base)** is the alternative goalie. POTE 88 is eight points above Lalime's, meaning more development remaining, but $5.50M is $3.60M more per year. MTL at 66 points with 15 expiring are the most motivated sellers in the league. The Jan 15 order says "really good high-90s goalie from a team that will not be a contender"; Theodore and Lalime both fit. Lalime is the better money, Theodore is the better long-term asset.

**Heatley (ATL, RW, 24, 91 base)** is the fallback if Iginla is out of reach. 131 points in 79 games, $1.10M, one year remaining. ATL at 84 points with 11 expiring face a binary with Kovalchuk (89 base, 138 pts, same $1.10M, one year). Whichever ATL keeps, the other becomes available. Heatley at 75 TOUG doesn't close the toughness gap the way Iginla does, but 131 points at $1.10M is the best scoring-for-salary ratio in the league.

**Kovalchuk (ATL, LW, 22, 89 base)** is the other side of that ATL binary. 138 points in 79 games at 22 years old for $1.10M. TOUG 78 is below the 80 threshold so he doesn't close the structural gap, but he's the second-highest point scorer on a likely seller. If ATL extends Heatley, Kovalchuk becomes a trade or UFA target.

**Gagne (PHI, LW, 25, 86 base)** is a July UFA target, not a trade candidate. 108 points in 82 games at $2.40M, expiring from a club at $2.14M profit (the worst in the Eastern Conference). PHI cannot cover his market price. TOUG 58 and CHKG 62 mean he fills a scoring wing, not a toughness role. He's the cheap answer at LW if neither Heatley nor Kovalchuk materializes.

**Bell (CHI, LW, 27, 82 base)** remains the budget toughness option from the March 30 note: 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81, $900K, 2 years. CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring and $31.73M profit are motivated sellers. His data isn't in today's queries because his overall_base of 82 falls below the top-25 cutoffs, but the standing read is unchanged. He doesn't reach 94 base like Thornton but at $900K he raises the toughness ceiling to 88 for a fraction of the cost.

**Avery (LA, C, 25, 79 base)** is the cheapest gap-filler at $400K with 2 years remaining. 93 FACE, 88 CHKG, 83 TOUG. His TOUG is now above our ceiling. The Feb 16 memory deprioritised him below Bell because his production is 9 points in 82 games (0.11 pts/g). He's a fourth-line center who wins draws and plays physical; the production is a known cost. At $400K the risk is negligible.

**Mogilny must move.** He is 36, $5.50M, two years remaining, and fell from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g during the season. His 84-point season in 78 games still has paper value. No contender wants a 37-year-old at $5.50M in a rebuild, and non-contenders have no reason to absorb him. The window is this summer, and he's the salary-matching piece for either Iginla or Thornton. After one more decline, the market closes permanently.

**Spezza needs a decision.** The coach flagged it six times by March and again on April 30: "give him real games or stop dressing him." At 21, POTE 99, he has never exceeded 0.33 pts/g at any ice level. His trade value peaks while the potential grade is credible and the market hasn't seen another dead season. If the coach won't give him top-six minutes, move him in July for a toughness piece like Bell.

## Trade construction

The summer market has three players whose acquisition would reshape Toronto's roster: Thornton at 94 base closing three gaps simultaneously, Iginla at 93 base closing the RW scoring void and the toughness ceiling in one move, and Bell at 82 base filling both faceoffs and toughness for $900K. The problem is funding them. We have one 4th-rounder, Mogilny at $5.50M who must move regardless, and a surplus of POTE 94 young forwards who are blocked in the lineup. The packages below are the cleanest bridges between what we have and what each seller wants.

**Proposal 1: Iginla from Calgary.** This is the confirmed July priority from April 12 and the single highest-impact move available.

TOR gives: **Mogilny** ($5.50M, 36, POTE 55) + **Alexeev** ($1.10M, 23, POTE 94, 30 pts/55 GP, BALA 90). Total $6.60M.
TOR gets: **Iginla** (93 base, 27, 87 TOUG, 81 CHKG, $6.50M, 128 pts/76 GP).
Payroll effect: TOR saves $6.60M, adds $6.50M. Net change: minus $100K. The salary was always going to leave with Mogilny; this converts him into the RW who closes two gaps.
Why CGY says yes: They are 70 points with 10 expiring contracts and $14.43M profit. Money is not their constraint but roster construction is. They cannot re-sign Iginla and all 10 others. Losing him to UFA for nothing is the worst outcome. Mogilny at 84 points in 78 games still projects 30-40 points as a power-play option for one season while they develop, and Alexeev at 23 with POTE 94 and 89 speed is a young piece they didn't have before. They flip Mogilny next summer or keep him as a mentor for a year. Either way, better than nothing.
Acceptance is uncertain. CGY might insist on a first-rounder, which we cannot provide. They might value POTE 94 less than the AI's trade model does.

**Proposal 2: Thornton from Boston.** The highest base available on any likely seller, closing toughness, checking, and faceoffs in one transaction.

TOR gives: **Afinogenov** ($4.50M, 25, POTE 95, 54 pts/67 GP, declining from 1.17 to 0.73 pts/g) + the 4th-round pick. Total $4.50M + pick.
TOR gets: **Thornton** (94 base, 25, 89 TOUG, 90 CHKG, 79 FACE, $4.00M, 83 pts/59 GP).
Payroll effect: TOR saves $4.50M, adds $4.00M. Net change: minus $500K. We give up the player whose development is stalled (coach flagged the decline) and get the player whose grades already reset the structural gaps.
Why BOS says yes: 97 points, 13 expiring contracts, and they must decide who to keep. Thornton at $4.00M with no extension agreed is a liability if he walks for nothing. Afinogenov at 25 with POTE 95 and 54 points is a top-nine winger they could develop into something more, and his contract is 4 years, so they control him. At 97 points they need depth who is already good; he is. The 4th-rounder is a small sweetener.
Acceptance is uncertain. BOS at 97 points may value a 94-base center more than a 54-point winger, even at 25. They might want a defenseman or a goalie instead. This is the proposal most likely to fail on price.

**Proposal 3: Bell from Chicago.** The cheapest path to resetting the toughness ceiling and the faceoff problem simultaneously.

TOR gives: **Koltsov** ($1.10M, 24, POTE 94, ACCE 96, 19 pts/38 GP).
TOR gets: **Bell** (82 base, 24, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81, $900K, 2 years remaining).
Payroll effect: TOR saves $1.10M, adds $900K. Net change: minus $200K. Two years of control at a bargain salary.
Why CHI says yes: 78 points, 10 expiring contracts, $31.73M profit. They are in teardown mode. Koltsov at 24 with 96 acceleration and POTE 94 is the profile of a player they build around. Bell at POTE 81 is useful but not a franchise piece. Swapping one forward prospect for another with a higher ceiling is exactly what a rebuilding GM does. His contract has two years left, so they have no urgency to keep him.
Acceptance is uncertain. The March 30 note says Tucker + 4th is only worth a 74-76 base player, and Bell is 82. But Koltsov at POTE 94 is substantially more than Tucker at POTE 79. The AI's pricing is unknown, and a direct prospect-for-prospect swap has a logic that "depth player plus pick" does not.

**If none land.** The UFA route covers two of the four gaps partially: Gagne (25, 86 base, 108 pts/82 GP, $2.40M) closes scoring at LW but not toughness, and Cammalleri (22, POTE 98, 60 pts/61 GP, $1.10M) adds a long-term winger but also no toughness. The toughness ceiling stays at 75 and the faceoff problem stays with Sundin alone. That is survivable but leaves the structural hole intact, which means the Cup window closes one year earlier than it should. The fallback is to draft toughness in June (the 4th-rounder is gone in Proposal 2; without it we have zero picks). The GM should attempt Proposal 1 before July 1; if Calgary will not engage, move to Proposal 3 as the floor.

## Owed

**Luongo availability and DiPietro development for the goalie trade window** — this task is closed. The GM issued the closing order on 2005-03-19: "Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks." The February window passed, the GM decided to keep Luongo (94 overall, $1.60M, 2 years left) and Belfour (93, $6.50M, 1 year) through the playoffs, and that decision held through the season's end. Nothing to report beyond the closure.

The task was relevant from January through mid-February when we were hunting a high-90s starter from a non-contender. Luongo arrived before that window closed, the need was filled internally, and the monitoring became moot before the deadline itself.
