# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-05-02

Next game at PIT on Monday 02 May 2005.

## Development opportunity

The season is done at 82 games; the only thing left is one meaningless road game at Pittsburgh. This phase is about settling who earned what, so the offseason assignments are clear.

**Chlup** at 19: 59 points in 71 games on 16.9 MPG. That is 0.83 pts/g, the highest rate on the roster outside Gaborik. He has earned the first-line centre slot permanently. He should not start next season on the second line.

**Gaborik** at 23: 99 points in 82 games, 20.5 MPG. He is the best player on this team by a wide margin. Scratched for this final game, which is fine for a 1-0-0 dead rubber, but he stays untouched next season.

**Alexeev** at 23: 30 points in 55 games on 8.3 MPG gives him 0.55 pts/g. Chistov is at 0.29 and Upshall at 0.29, both dressed ahead of him. He outproduces them by nearly double and has been sitting. That rate does not prove he is a top-six winger, but it proves he deserves a serious look in camp next season.

**Spezza** at 21: 15 points in 46 games on 6.7 MPG. 0.33 pts/g. POTE says 99 but the game has not. His minutes collapsed through the back half. The season is a write-off. Next camp decides whether he is still a development project or a reclamation.

**Upshall** at 21: 20 points in 68 games on 7.9 MPG. 0.29 pts/g, POTE 99. Same situation as Spezza: given the chance, did not take it. Same offseason decision.

**Spacek** at 19: 17 points in 50 games on 7.6 MPG. 0.34 pts/g with POTE 91. He got his minutes late and held the fourth line. He is a depth player who earned his dressing spot. No argument for more.

**Nash** at 20: 39 points in 69 games on 13.1 MPG. 0.57 pts/g season, but his recent window is near half that. Rate halved on stable minutes. Offseason system-fit review, same flag as Richards.

**Colaiacovo** at 22: 12 points in 31 games on 17.9 MPG. 0.39 pts/g with POTE 99. When given top-pair minutes he held them at a reasonable rate. He earned a roster audition in camp but has not yet earned a permanent top-four spot.

**Eminger** at 21: 23 points in 64 games on 15.5 MPG. 0.36 pts/g, contract expiring. He is not developing into a top-pair defenceman. He needs to be moved this summer or lost for nothing.

**Klesla** at 23: 30 points in 82 games on 14.8 MPG. 0.37 pts/g, second consecutive declining season. A sell, not a keeper.

**Ouellet** at 23: 13 starts, backup role. Fine as depth behind Luongo.

**Stahle** at 21: 4 games, 0 points. Not in the picture.

## Development trends

Season's wrapping up and this is the last full window to read who's moving before offseason planning. The answer splits clean: one young defenceman ascending, two prime-age forwards sliding when they should be flat or climbing, and three kids whose seasons are over for development purposes.

**Kaberle** is going up, not down. 0.54 to 0.62 pts/g while his load climbed from 19.4 to 21.5 MPG. At 27 he's entering his prime with a rising rate on a rising schedule. He's the best trend on this roster right now.

**Afinogenov** at 25 dropped from 1.17 to 0.73 pts/g on flat minutes (16.8 to 16.6). That's a 38% rate collapse at an age where the expected direction is up. Pair it with Richards (1.08 to 0.71 at 25, same flat minutes) and we have two top-six forwards peaking early or falling through a system-fit problem. Offseason review for both.

**McCabe** at 0.48 over 58 games is now clearly below the 0.60 sell threshold. His 1.42 hot start is long gone and the season total has collapsed to match. The March 30 re-evaluation is done: he goes back on the sell list. 0.48 pts/g on 21.5 MPG at 29 with 4 years and $3.00M is a return we can find elsewhere.

**Klesla** confirms the sell call. 0.50 to 0.31 pts/g on flat 15 MPG, second consecutive declining year. He goes.

**Alexeev** still outproduces his role. 0.48 pts/g on 6.0 MPG versus Chistov's 0.30 on 14.0. The mismatch persists and no line arrangement fixes it from the bench.

**Spacek** and **Spezza** are both done for the year. Spacek at 5.2 MPG and 0.28, Spezza at 4.6 MPG and 0.24. Neither is developing on that schedule. Camp is the only lever.

**Chlup** continues to climb. 0.88 on 18.2 MPG at 19. The breakout is real and permanent.

**Chistov** is getting trusted. Minutes rose 9.5 to 14.0 while his rate held flat at 0.30. Not a scorer but the coaching staff is giving him more of the game and he's not cutting it. That's a role gain.

## Morale watch

**The room is healthy.** Morale ranges from 88 to 100, and the bottom end is climbing. With two games left, nobody needs a minutes change tonight.

**Spezza** at 88 is the lowest man in the building. He's at 6.7 MPG and 0.33 pts/g with 15 points in 46 games. His morale climbed +3 over the last three saves but remains the outlier. The minutes collapse that started in March is not fixable in two games. The lever is next camp, not a line bump now.

**Abid** at 100 is the one I keep an eye on. 66 points in 82 games (0.80 pts/g) on 13.8 MPG from the fourth line. He should be getting 17+ and playing on the second or third unit. Wins have papered over the mismatch so his morale hasn't cracked, but if results dip next season, this is the first player to go south. Not a tonight problem.

**Richards** at 98 gets 16.1 MPG on the third line. If his calibre sits in the 80s, that's his band exactly. If his grades are 90+ as the 66-point season suggests, he's four minutes short. Morale says he doesn't care yet, and I won't break the line for it with two games left.

**Jackman** at 100 on 29.6 MPG is carrying the heaviest load on the roster. His production rate (37 pts in 80 games) doesn't match the minutes. The load is the problem I flagged in March and the sell case stands, but tonight his morale is perfect and I leave him alone.

Everyone else is at 99 or 100. The wins are doing the work.

## Role composition

**Question: do the units fit the players, and do we have enough of each role?** For tonight's game against Pittsburgh this is mostly about whether the current arrangement gives us what we need against a team that can score (125 goals against this season, 24-34 record means they're not a defensive club).

**L1** is correctly built as a scoring line. Sundin at 91 faceoffs handles draws, Mogilny at 94 scoring and Roberts at 95 clutch are the production. Jackman and Fischer on D give it a two-way base with checking at 90 and 85. No reason to touch it.

**L2** is the faceoff-weak line at 59 mean. Chlup at 80 is the only real draw winner, and if Pittsburgh centers their best faceoff man against him, the rest of this unit can't hold a puck clean. The scoring is there though (85/98) so they'll create offense either way. Not broken, just vulnerable on draws.

**L3** has an odd identity. Chistov at 98 speed paired with Tucker at 94 checking makes a line that can run on counters but also shut someone down. Richards at 75 faceoffs and 75 checking is a fine third-line center for it. The 89 mean speed is high for a checking line, which means this unit is more of a matchup flex than a dedicated shutdown line. I'd leave it.

**L4 faceoffs at 52/55** are the real problem. No forward on this roster outside L1-L2 can win a draw. Spacek, Abid, Upshall are 52-55 in the circle. That's a roster gap, not an arrangement problem, because I have no faceoff-capable body to slide in. Every time Pittsburgh gets a zone draw against this line, they win the puck. We need a middle-six center who wins draws above 60.

**Power play units** are both legitimate. P2 scores at 87/95 and Mogilny plus Richards give it real threat. Having two PP units that can actually score is an asset against a team that will take penalties (24-34 teams tend to be undisciplined).

**Penalty kill** looks backwards on paper: K2 checks better than K1 (84 vs 79 mean). But K1's 67 faceoffs beats K2's 64, and winning the zone draw matters more than checking on the kill. Leaving it as is.

## Opponent matchup

**Who is Lemieux tonight, and does it matter that we're already the best team in the league?** It does not. PIT is 24-34-11 and we are 7-2-0 against them this season with the top record locked at 133 points. The only cost of getting this wrong is breaking chemistry the game before the playoffs.

**Lemieux** is 39 but still produces 1.60 pts/g (58 goals, 59 assists, 73 games). His hands read PASS 99, PUCK 95, DEKG 98, HERO 96. He is the entire team — PIT's power play is 32 goals on 276 attempts (11.6%) and without him this lineup is a bottom-third club. Straka alongside him has FACE 83 and 1.60 pts/g in 48 games. Their first line will win draws and generate, but their OVR of 88 against our 91 first line and 86 second line means we match up fine without adjustment.

**Tarnstrom** (0.77 pts/g, 82 games) and **Rozsival** (0.67) are their only D above 75 OVR. Neither threatens our top four. The real problem is Salminen at 71 and Pushor at 67 on the bottom pair — our third line of Richards (0.71 pts/g season) and Chistov will eat them alive if given the ice.

**Luongo's fatigue icon is clear.** Start him. No reason to give Ouellet a meaningless playoff-prep appearance when Luongo is fresh and the streak matters for the locker room.

**No line changes.** We're 7-2-0, the opponent is 24-34, and this is the last game before the playoffs. Running the same units preserves what we've built. The development argument for dressing Alexeev exists (0.55 pts/g beats Chistov's 0.29 and Upshall's 0.29) but breaking the fourth line one night before October is the wrong trade. That's a training-camp decision, not a regular-season last-day one.

**Defensive assessment (#1, standing task):** No change to the sell order. Jackman finishes at 0.48 pts/g on 30 MPG across 73 games at 24 — sell offseason. Klesla's second consecutive declining season is confirmed at 0.36 pts/g on 15 MPG at 23 — sell offseason. Eminger at 0.38 season rate with an expiring contract must go before free agency. McCabe is settled at 0.76 pts/g across 82 games. Fischer and Kaberle are keepers.

## Owed

This is the defenceman sell-list update the GM asked for every game. The regular season is now complete at 82 games for everyone who played, so these are final totals and the case is locked. Nothing has moved since my April 7 confirmation that McCabe cleared the threshold.

**Jackman** is the clearest sell. Final line: 80 GP, 37 points, 29.6 MPG, 0.46 pts/g. His season rate dipped from 0.48 (when he had 73 games) to 0.46 as the final seven went scoreless. The 29.6 MPG is the problem: he is eating top-pair minutes and returning third-pair production. At $0.70M with 3 years left, his value to another club is exactly that volume of cheap top-pair ice. His value to us is a replacement at 24 MPG who puts up 0.55 or better.

**Klesla** is confirmed: 82 GP, 30 points, 14.8 MPG, 0.37 pts/g. Two consecutive declining seasons (0.38, 0.37). At $0.90M with 2 years, he's tradeable for a mid-round pick or a depth piece.

**Eminger** is the urgent one. 64 GP, 23 points, 15.5 MPG, 0.36 pts/g. His $1.20M contract expires in July. After July 1 he walks for nothing. He must be moved this offseason, even for a late-round pick.

**McCabe** at 0.76 pts/g on 22.1 MPG over a full 82 stays as the anchor. **Fischer** and **Kaberle** are the GM's keepers and I do not revisit them.

No change to the recommendation, but the numbers are now season-locked rather than in-progress. The priority order is Eminger (expiring, must move) then Jackman (volume asset with real trade value) then Klesla (lower value, more time to work).



**Delivered: #1** (defenceman sell-list update). Final numbers are locked since the regular season is complete. Eminger is the urgent trade (expiring July 1), Jackman the highest-value one (0.46 pts/g on 29.6 MPG, $0.70M — a volume asset someone else wants), Klesla the lowest-priority sell. McCabe, Fischer and Kaberle stay.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-30
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-30

Toronto 59-13-5, 133 pts after 82 games.

## Role coverage

The season is three games from the regular-season finish and the playoffs are next, so this is the last clean look at the roster before the July rebuilding window opens. Two structural gaps (toughness and faceoffs) are confirmed and unfixable from within; one age cliff (RW scoring behind Mogilny) is visible on the sheet today.

**Toughness.** Zero Toronto players carry 80+ TOUG. Jackman leads the club at 75, Tucker at 70. This was confirmed structurally on March 19 and has not moved since. The coach flagged it again on April 28 with checking mean 61 and toughness mean 57 on the fourth line. No internal lineup change fixes this; the number simply does not exist on the roster. Bell (CHI, 24, 88 TOUG, 82 FACE) or Avery (LA, 25, 83 TOUG, 93 FACE) are the only league-wide players who close both toughness and faceoffs simultaneously, and both were identified as primary targets in late March.

**Faceoffs.** Sundin at 90 is the only player above 80. He is 34. Chlup at 75 is next and the coach has already assigned him first-line centre for next season, so his draws go to the top pair against the other team's top centre. Richards at 70 can cover third line, but neither reaches the 80 threshold a bottom-six centre needs against fourth-line opponents who draw in every shift. The fourth-line faceoff gap the coach names on April 28 has no internal solution.

**Scoring and playmaking.** Ten players at 80+ overall, but Mogilny is 36 and fell from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g (March 23 finding), Roberts is 38 and walking, Sundin is 34. Gaborik at 92 and Afinogenov at 90 are the young core. The RW scoring void behind Mogilny is the single biggest post-season acquisition need, and Iginla (CGY, 27, 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, expiring) supersedes Heatley per the April 12 note.

**Checking.** Six at 80+: Jackman 87 (24), McCabe 86 (29), Roberts 86 (38, walking), Tucker 83 (30, trade chip), Fischer 82 (24), Upshall 80 (21). With Roberts walking and Tucker potentially moving, this drops to four. Jackman, McCabe, Fischer, Upshall are the future and they are adequate if the fourth line gets a body with TOUG 80+.

**Defence after Roberts.** Roberts at 88 overall and 38 is walking per the March 21 renewal order. The top pair becomes Jackman (24) and Kaberle (27) or McCabe (29). Eminger (21, POTE 99) needs a mentor and a spot. Stuart (SJ, 25, 87 base, 80 TOUG, 89 CHKG, POTE 91) fills both the Roberts gap and the toughness gap on the blue line simultaneously.

**Goalies.** Belfour (40, $6.50M, 1yr) and Luongo (26, $1.60M, 2yr) carry the playoff run per the March 19 order. Belfour walks after. Luongo plus Ouellet (23, $0.90M, 2yr) is the post-season pair. The GM closed this file; I will not reopen it.

**Durability.** Only four players at 80+: Roberts 98, Afinogenov 95, Fischer 92, Abid 90. With Roberts walking, three remain. For a seven-game series stretch this is manageable, but it limits the coach's ability to absorb a mid-series injury to a top-pair defenceman.

## Trajectory

The trajectory question here is not whether Toronto ages off a cliff — it's whether they lose their core to a single summer before the young players can sign. The age curve is the best in the league: 25 of 30 players are 23 or under, only 5 are 30+. The money is abundant: $35.74M profit against a $60.04M payroll. The danger is entirely contractual.

**The July 2005 cluster** is 13 players and $21.30M. Of those, the five who must be locked are Gaborik (23, 99 pts, POTE 90, $1.10M), Richards (24, 66 pts, POTE 88, $1.00M), Nash (20, 39 pts, POTE 95, $1.20M), Eminger (21, 23 pts, POTE 99, $1.20M), and Upshall (21, 20 pts, POTE 99, $1.20M). Their combined current salary is $5.70M. Even tripling to $17M is trivial against $108M revenue. The constraint is not money; it's whether the AI clubs outbid us or these players walk unsigned.

**Belfour, Roberts, and Mogilny** carry $14.70M and their minutes are covered. Belfour (40, scratched, $6.50M) and Roberts (38, $2.70M) are one-year deals. Mogilny has one year remaining after this season on $5.50M at 36. All three walk by design and free the payroll for Iginla-class RW acquisition and fourth-line depth.

**Sundin at 34, $8.40M, 5 years left** is the roster's single longest liability. He's producing (91 pts) but POTE 60 means development is finished. He's locked through age 39. If Chlup takes first-centre next season as the coach recommends, Sundin's 19 MPG drops to 14 and the cost-per-point ratio becomes the worst on the club. Nothing actionable now, but it's the contract that will define 2007-08.

**The 2006 cluster** is the next one to watch: Koltsov, Spezza, Ouellet, Klesla, St. Jacques, Luongo, Chlup, and Tucker all have 2 years left ($15.44M total). If we lock the July 2005 core on 5-6 years, we negotiate those 8 deals in a calmer 2006. If we don't, we face 21 concurrent renewals across two summers and the risk grows exponentially.

**Draft capital is nil.** One fourth-rounder. The GM already noted this on January 26. Every acquisition must be funded by players, which makes keeping Abid ($0.40M, POTE 94) and Koltsov ($1.10M, POTE 94) as trade chips more valuable than signing them to long deals.

**Task report — #2 (Luongo monitoring):** Luongo is on Toronto's roster at 26, $1.60M, 2 years left, 45 GP. The GM closed all goalie monitoring on March 19. This task is complete and superseded.

## Calendar

The deadline passed 42 days ago, so the calendar question is now entirely about the summer: 13 contracts worth roughly $20.20M come due, and the order we renew in determines whether the young core stays intact or gets picked apart. Three dates matter: the rookie draft on June 8, unnamed events on June 6 and June 9 (likely free-agency windows, but the game doesn't name them), and a cluster of three unnamed events on June 27–29. Every renewal and signing decision should be made before June 6 so the first offer lands on day one.

**Gaborik** is the first call. At 23, 91 base, POTE 90, and $1.10M, he is the most valuable player on the expiring list and the cheapest. Five or six years, locked before any other Toronto player touches free agency. If another club makes a first-day offer and we lose him, no other move on this list matters as much.

**Richards** follows immediately. He is 24, at $1.00M, and the coach flagged his decline from 1.08 to 0.71 pts/g, which makes him cheaper to re-sign than his age alone would suggest. Five years is the right length: we either get the 1.08 back or we own a cheap asset for five more years and deal him from that position.

**Nash at 20 and Eminger at 21** are the longest-runway pieces. Nash is a 20-year-old left wing at $1.20M; Eminger is 21 with POTE 99, which the GM has protected all season. Both belong on five or six years. The risk is the cluster, and staggering Gaborik/Richards one day and Nash/Eminger the next is the difference between two negotiation sessions and one bad night.

**Kaberle at 27** earns a five-year deal at $1.90M. He is in his prime, not a lottery ticket, and a five-year lock keeps him off the market at 32.

**The depth group** — Upshall (21), Chistov (22), Colaiacovo (22), Alexeev (23), Abid (25) — signs on two- or three-year deals. Upshall and Chistov are 21 and 22, so three years is the better bet; the rest take two. Abid at $0.40M is the cheapest toughness on the roster and costs almost nothing to keep.

**Belfour at 40** gets a one-year offer at a reduced salary, maybe $3.00M. The GM said in January he probably won't accept. If he declines, he walks and we have Luongo (91 base, 2 years left) plus Tellqvist (25, POTE high 90s). That is a workable tandem. If Belfour retires instead of testing the market, we lose nothing we were counting on.

**Roberts at 38, $2.70M** walks. The GM decided this on March 21. Do not offer.

**Tellqvist at 25, $0.80M** renews on two years. He is the backup this coming season and the evaluation case for whether he becomes a starter later.

The RW void Mogilny leaves behind (he is at 36 and fell from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g) points at **Iginla** (CGY, 27, 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, $6.50M expiring). Calgary at 70 points with 10 expiring deals cannot retain him at that salary. If the free-agency window opens on June 6 or 9, he is the first signing target, and Gaborik shifts to first wing while Iginla takes the right side. That combination — Gaborik at 91 base and Iginla at 93 — is the two best wingers on the roster and closes the scoring gap the coach has flagged all season.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: who can we get in July that closes the three structural gaps (toughness, fourth-line faceoffs, RW scoring behind Mogilny) and the defence hole Roberts leaves? We have $14.70M freed by Belfour, Roberts and Mogilny walking, plus a $35.74M profit, so money is not the constraint. The constraint is whether the other GM lets go.

**Iginla** is the single best player available. 93 base, 140 points in 73 games, TOUG 85, SPEE 98, age 27. He closes the RW scoring void and the toughness ceiling at once. CGY at 70 points, 10 expiring, $14.43M profit cannot retain a $6.50M expiring star. He's the July priority per the April 12 note and nothing in this scan displaces him.

**Bell** at 24 closes toughness and faceoffs simultaneously: 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81, $900K. He's the only league-wide player who addresses both gaps with development runway. CHI at 78 points with $31.73M profit and 10 expiring are the most motivated sellers in the league. The price per the March 30 note is R2 plus Colaiacovo, which is fair given their depth.

**Stuart** at 25, 87 base, POTE 92, 59 points in 82 games, TOUG 80, $1.80M expiring fills Roberts' gap and adds 80+ toughness to the blue line in one move. SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring on $45.39M payroll cannot keep everyone. The March 30 note flags that at 76 they are not tanking and may hold, but 13 expiring deals at $45M payroll creates pressure.

**Komisarek** is the cheapest high-ceiling option: 23, 77 base, TOUG 85, CHKG 92, POTE 92, $1.10M expiring. MTL at 66 points, 15 expiring, $21.59M profit are the most desperate sellers in the league. His ceiling is not Roberts-level but at $1.10M and age 23 the risk-reward is the best in the pool.

**Cammalleri** at 22, POTE 98, 60 points in 61 games, $1.10M expiring is the highest-value July UFA. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring cannot retain both him and Frolov. If we sign Iginla, Cammalleri becomes the second RW option on the bottom two lines; if Iginla falls through, he's the starter with growth potential.

**Heatley** at 24, 91 base, 131 points in 79 games, $1.10M expiring is the best RW available if Iginla goes elsewhere. ATL at 84 points with 11 expiring may keep Kovalchuk (22, 89 base, 138 pts) and let Heatley walk. His POTE 84 is lower than Cammalleri's 98 but his production is proven now.

**Avery** at 25, $400K, 2 years left, 94 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG is the cheapest faceoff+toughness solution. His 5 points in 82 games this season confirms the February finding that his production is ghost. He is a fourth-line specialist and nothing more, but at $400K he is nearly free. LA at 79 points, 14 expiring, $16.34M profit will deal him.

**Reid** at 24, 77 base, POTE 94, SPEE 99, FACE 80, 70 points in 76 games, $600K expiring is a speed-forward who can also draw faceoffs. STL at 86 points with only 8 expiring are less likely sellers than the teams above, but at $600K expiring the cost is trivial.

**Belanger** at 27, 82 base, FACE 96, $700K expiring is the pure faceoff answer if we want a dedicated fourth-line centre. LA at 79 points, 14 expiring will move him. 19 points in 73 games means he's a checker who wins draws and nothing else.

**What I would not pursue:** Daze at 29 with TOUG 55 does not fix the toughness gap. Fleury at 36 with POTE 56 is a one-year rental that wastes cap space. Deadmarsh at 29 with 50 GP this season is too injury-prone for a seven-game series team. Chara is forbidden by the February 19 order.

## Trade construction

This phase answers: what packages do we actually put on the table in July, and why would the other GM call yes? The constraint is severe: one 4th-rounder as our only draft capital, a GM order against selling Eminger or McCabe, and a roster whose young core must stay intact. That means our currency is surplus youth (Spezza, Koltsov, Colaiacovo, Abid) and the designated chip (Tucker). The good news is that every target's club is financially desperate enough to take cheap potential over expensive production.

**Iginla** is the priority. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring deals cannot retain a $6.50M player while also re-signing their own young core. They shed $4.40M net in this deal and receive two players under 25 with POTE 99 and 94 on combined $2.10M for two more years. Spezza's trade value is highest right now while POTE 99 remains credible (March 30 finding), and the coach has flagged him six times without a resolution. Koltsov at 24 with POTE 94 is surplus to the forward group. This is the most impactful single trade available and the one the GM should push hardest.

**Bell** closes toughness (88 TOUG) and faceoffs (82 FACE) in one move for $900K. CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring and $31.73M profit are the most motivated sellers in the league. Colaiacovo at 22 carries POTE 99, the highest grade we can give without violating the Feb 19 order. He has 12 points in 31 games and is the odd man out on a blue line with Jackman, McCabe, Klesla and Eminger all ahead. CHI gets a future top-pair D at $1.10M for one year; we get the only player who fixes two gaps simultaneously.

**Stuart** fills Roberts' 88-base hole at 87 with eight years of runway, plus TOUG 80 and CHKG 89 on the blue line where we have zero. SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring on $45.39M payroll physically cannot keep everyone. Abid at 66 points in 82 games on $0.40M is surplus (the coach's April 28 lineup excludes him) and gives SJ immediate production. Tucker at $1.30M adds veteran depth. The risk: at 76 points SJ are not tanking, and the March 30 note flagged they may hold a POTE 91 blueliner. This is the least likely to land.

**If none land:** Sign Cammalleri as a UFA (LA at 79 with 14 expiring cannot keep both him and Frolov; his $1.10M salary is trivial). For toughness and faceoffs, develop Nash (20, TOUG 88, POTE 95) into the fourth-line role and accept the faceoff deficit for one more year. Test Avery from LA at the 2006 trade deadline when he's 26 and LA's window is closing further.

## Owed

**#2 — Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window.**

This task is closed. Luongo is on our roster at 94 overall, 26 years old, $1.60M with two years remaining, 45 games played this season. The GM explicitly terminated all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19: "Keeping him and Luongo as two 90+ goalies for the playoffs. Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks." The February window this job tracked is now two months past, the acquisition happened, and the standing order forbids revisiting the topic. Nothing to report beyond closure.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-30
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-30

Next game vs PIT on Saturday 30 April 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is who is getting the games their potential and production have earned, and who is being left behind without anyone noticing.

**Chlup** is getting everything he's earned: 71 games at 87% share, 16.9 MPG, 59 points at 0.83 pts/g on the second line at 19. He's the one young player with zero ambiguity about his role.

**Gaborik** played all 82 at 20.5 MPG and scored 99 points. At 23 he's the finished product. He's scratched for tonight, which I need to understand separately -- a 99-point player at 100% share doesn't sit for development reasons.

**Spezza** is the clearest case of a player being wasted. POTE 99, 46 games at 56% share, 6.7 MPG, 0.33 pts/g, and morale has dropped to 88 -- the lowest of the young group. He's scratched. The season's minutes tell the story: he went from 9.1 MPG earlier to 4.8 recently. At 21 with the highest scouting mark on the roster, he's getting less than a depth man and his morale is showing it. The chance isn't there.

**Alexeev** produces at 0.55 pts/g on 8.3 MPG and is scratched. Chistov (0.29) and Upshall (0.29) are both dressed and getting more minutes. At 23 and POTE 94, he's outproducing two dressed wingers by double and sitting out. That mismatch hasn't resolved itself all month.

**Colaiacovo** is in a rotation: 31 games at 38% share, but when he plays he gets 17.9 MPG and produces 0.39 pts/g. That's solid top-pair minutes. He's not being wasted when he's in, he's just not getting enough nights. At POTE 99 and 22, the development question is whether the rotation teaches him anything or whether he needs 60+ games to progress.

**Upshall** gets 68 games and 7.9 MPG on the fourth line at 0.29 pts/g. That's a depth-man rate. POTE 99 is a scouting opinion, not a claim on ice time. He's getting games his current level supports, and his morale (91) is fine.

**Eminger** plays 64 games at 15.5 MPG on the third pair, scoring 0.36 pts/g. He's getting real minutes and producing at a bottom-pair rate. His contract expires this summer. That's not a development question, it's a value question for the GM.

**Nash** has 69 games at 13.1 MPG but his rate halved from 0.83 to 0.57 season average without his role changing. He's getting the chance; the production isn't following. That's a system-fit problem, not an opportunity problem.

**Chistov** at 68 games, 13.1 MPG, 0.29 pts/g on the third line is a player getting what his current level has earned. Morale 100. No issue.

**Klesla** plays all 82 at 14.8 MPG on the third pair. 0.37 pts/g is a two-season decline from 0.38. He's getting the chance and the chance isn't producing growth. The sell decision is the GM's.

**Stahle** appeared in 4 games with 0 points. Too little to judge. He's scratched and has been all season. No recommendation.

## Development trends

**This is the last full read of the season before the offseason starts, so it is the moment to set the agenda for camp.** The picture is split: one defenceman getting better under load, one 25-year-old falling apart on flat minutes, and the 21-year-old cohort collapsing together in a way that points to a usage problem rather than three individual failures.

**Kaberle** is the only defenceman on this club going the right way. 0.54→0.62 pts/g while minutes rose from 19.4 to 21.5. At 27, with Jackman at the same age crumbling under 29 MPG, Kaberle proves he handles a bigger role. The GM already called him a star. The numbers confirm it.

**Afinogenov at 25 dropped from 1.17 to 0.73 pts/g on flat minutes (16.8→16.6).** I have not flagged this before and it deserves attention now. At 25 the expected direction is up. A 37% rate drop with no role change is either a system-fit problem or a confidence issue. Offseason review, same bucket as Richards.

**McCabe is confirmed sell at 0.48 pts/g across 82 games.** The 1.42 early pace was noise from a 24-game sample. 0.48 is well below the 0.60 threshold. At 29 with 4 years and $3.00M, his value is the remaining years and the cheap cap hit relative to his peak. Move him while teams still remember the start.

**Chlup finishes at 0.88 pts/g on 18.2 MPG at 19.** My April 28 recommendation to put him on the first line permanently was not taken. The data says the same thing it did then: he belongs there. No change to the argument, just a reminder that the camp assignment should reflect this.

**Chistov quietly earned ice time.** Minutes went from 9.5 to 14.0 while his rate held at 0.30. He is not a scorer, but he is not a liability either, and he has shown he can handle more without drowning. Worth keeping in the plan.

**The 21-year-old group collapsed together.** Spacek 0.55→0.28 on minutes cut from 16.0 to 5.2. Spezza 0.43→0.24 on 9.1 down to 4.6. Upshall 0.33→0.27 on 13.4 down to 4.8. Three players, same age, same pattern, minutes gutted simultaneously. That is a usage decision, not three separate regressions. The season is a write-off for all three. Offseason camp is the audition.

**Eminger's numbers are actually flat, not sliding.** 0.35→0.37 pts/g on 15.0→15.9 MPG. My March 30 note said he was sliding; that was built on a narrower window. The full picture shows stability. He is still expiring and still going, but the urgency is "find a buyer for a steady 21-year-old D," not "dump a collapsing asset."

**No grades moved on the card in this window.** Every production change above is about role, usage, and the cost of a bigger or smaller load. Nobody got measurably better or worse on the card. That makes the offseason about giving young players real minutes, not about worrying whether they can still play.

## Morale watch

The room is comfortable. Every dressed player sits between 98 and 100 morale, and the lowest on the roster is **Spezza** at 88, which costs him one point on his displayed grades but is nowhere near the -2 penalty that hits at 79 or below. No line or minute adjustment helps tonight.

**Spezza** at 88 is the only name worth tracking. He averages 6.7 minutes a night when his calibre expects closer to 10, and he is currently a scratch. The recent movement is positive (the +3 swing suggests it bounced off a low), so there is nothing to fix before Pittsburgh. This is the same offseason decision already flagged: either he gets a real camp audition next year or we stop dressing him. Not a tonight problem.

**Upshall** (91, 7.9 MPG) and **Spacek** (91, 7.6 MPG) are both trending up and both sit in the +1 morale band. They are slightly under their expected 10 minutes but their morale does not reflect it. Leave them where they are.

No one is carrying more than their band should ask. Jackman at 29.6 MPG has 100 morale. The first line at 18-20 MPG all sit at 98-100. The room is fine going into Pittsburgh.

## Role composition

**The question this phase answers is whether these lines are built from players who suit their roles, and whether the roster can even fill the roles we need.**

**L1 and L2 are clean.** Sundin at 91 on faceoffs anchors L1's draws, Mogilny at 94 scoring gives the goal-scoring punch, Roberts at 85 checking provides the two-way floor. L2 has Chlup at 80 on draws — solid for a second-line centre — with Nash and Afinogenov offering 92 and 98 scoring grades. Nothing to move.

**L3 is functional but thin up the middle.** Richards at 75 on faceoffs is the best draw-winner on this line; the unit mean of 61 with a best of 75 means nobody else is stepping up. Tucker's 94 checking is the reason this line works defensively. Chistov brings 98 speed. Eminger and Klesla pair on the back end at 15 MPG each — adequate for a third pairing. No change for tonight.

**L4 faceoffs are 52/55 — nobody wins a draw on that line.** Spacek, Abid, Upshall. The 55 best means even the strongest draw-taker on L4 is below average. In practice, fourth lines don't take many zone-start draws, so this costs us little, but it's another data point on the same structural problem: we have no forward who can check, win draws, and kill simultaneously. The fourth-line-checking-gap finding from April 13 still holds.

**K2 is our better penalty-kill unit.** The checking mean is 84 versus K1's 79, and toughness is 72 versus 69. Chlup, Tucker, McCabe, Jackman is four heavy bodies. K1 has more transition ability with Sundin and Kaberle, which is correct — K1 should break the puck out, K2 should grind it down.

**P1 is the unit that scores on anyone.** Kaberle at 92 playmaking from the point, Sundin and Roberts both above 90, Afinogenov at 92 scoring. P2 with Mogilny and Chlup is a luxury second unit that most clubs would dress as PP1. No change.

**The one roster gap that persists:** we have zero forwards above 85 on checking. Jackman at 90 is a defenceman. Among forwards, Tucker and Roberts top out around 85. This means we can only run one heavy killing line, and it means our fourth line cannot be a true shutdown unit no matter how I arrange it. Offseason problem, not tonight's.

## Opponent matchup

**The question:** Does Pittsburgh's lineup demand any tactical adjustment, or do we run our standard set against a 24-34-11 team we already beat 7 times this year?

**The answer is no change.** The auto-pairing already puts our first line (Sundin-Mogilny-Roberts) with Fischer and Jackman against Lemieux-Straka-Meloche, which is exactly where we want them. Fischer at CHKG 92 and Jackman at CHKG 92 are the two best defenders to contain a 39-year-old Lemieux whose PASS 99 and DEKG 98 are his only remaining threats. He won't outrun them at this stage.

**Lemieux** is the only player on Pittsburgh's sheet who scares anyone. OVR 88, PASS 99, PUCK 95, DEKG 98. But he's 39, ENDU 82, and his line-mates are Meloche at 77 and Straka at 85. We have beaten them seven times this season for 32 goals against 19. Nothing in the matchup profile has changed.

**Pittsburgh's power play** is 32 goals on 276 attempts — 11.6%. They are the worst PP unit in the league by a wide margin. Our penalty kill can play standard without overthinking personnel.

**Hedberg** in net at OVR 87 is competent but not a reason to alter our attack. Luongo at 94 is the right start regardless. Check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming — the standing order holds.

The only lever I would touch is the fourth line: Abid, Spacek, Upshall get the fourth line against Pittsburgh's fourth line (Fata 73, Surovy 74, McKenna 68). That's fine. Their fourth line has no skill and our fourth line has toughness to burn.

## Owed

**Defenceman sell/keep list for the offseason.** The season is at its final three games, so the rates are locked. Nothing has moved since my last delivery.

**McCabe** finishes at 0.76 pts/g on 22.1 MPG across 82 games. Still clears the 0.60 bar. Anchors the top pair at 29 on $3.00M x 4. No change, keeper.

**Fischer** at 0.53 pts/g on 22.4 MPG across 77 games. Below the bar on production, but the GM has him protected and his two-way game at 24 is the reason. Keeper, not my call to reopen.

**Kaberle** at 0.60 pts/g on 20.8 MPG across 74 games. GM said "Kaberle is definitely a keeper. Kaberle is a star defenseman." Off the list permanently.

**Jackman** at 0.46 pts/g on 29.6 MPG across 80 games. The 29.6 MPG is the problem: he carries a load no 24-year-old should at that production. Value is the contract: $0.70M x 3 years of top-pair minutes is the cheapest in the league. Sell, confirmed since March.

**Klesla** at 0.37 pts/g on 14.8 MPG across 82 games. Two consecutive declining seasons. $0.90M x 2. Sell.

**Eminger** at 0.36 pts/g on 15.5 MPG across 64 games, age 21, $1.2M expiring. If he is not moved before July we lose him for nothing. Sell or lose.

Nothing changed. The list is the same three: Jackman, Klesla, Eminger. The rates are now final.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-28

# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-28

Toronto 59-13-5, 133 pts after 82 games.

## Role coverage

The season is done, Mogilny and Roberts are leaving, and the coverage report shows exactly what that costs and where the structural holes sit underneath it.

**Scoring:** 10 players at 80+ SHPW today. Mogilny (94, age 36) and Roberts (88, age 38) leave, cutting it to 8. The remaining group — Sundin 92, Gaborik 92, Afinogenov 90, Abid 86 — is adequate for the top three lines. The gap is that Mogilny's 94 was the best shot power on the roster and nobody inside it is close. This is a replacement problem, not a collapse.

**Checking:** 6 at 80+ today. Roberts (86) leaves, Tucker (83) is a designated trade chip per the March 19 order, and Upshall (80) produces only 0.29 pts/g on 7.9 MPG. That leaves Jackman 87, McCabe 86, Fischer 82 as the only checkers actually in the lineup. Three is thin for a physical playoff series. If Tucker is kept rather than traded, he restores the fourth. That's a GM decision.

**Toughness:** Zero at 80+. Jackman's 75 is the roster best. This has been the structural gap since February and it has not moved because no internal player can close it. The coach's fourth-line mean of 57 TOUG (April 9) confirms the bottom six gets outmuscled every shift. This can only be fixed by acquisition. Bell (88 TOUG, CHI) or Avery (83 TOUG, LA) remain the only candidates.

**Faceoffs:** One player above 80: Sundin at 90, age 34. The next best is Chlup at 75, age 19. Richards sits at 70. Every line below Sundin's loses its opening draw. The coach flagged "no fifth centre who wins faceoffs" on April 26 and the grades agree. This cannot be fixed by a lineup change. Bell (82 FACE) or Avery (93 FACE) close it.

**Playmaking:** 11 at 80+, and Mogilny's departure (93 PASS) drops it to 10. Sundin 91, Gaborik 92, Richards 85, Spacek 84 remain. Covered.

**Speed:** 21 at 80+. Not a concern even after Mogilny leaves.

**Stamina:** 11 at 80+. Covered.

**Durability:** 4 at 80+. Roberts (98 INJU) leaving cuts it to 3: Afinogenov 95, Fischer 92, Abid 90. Thin but all young.

**Goalies:** Luongo (26, GAA 2.67, SV 0.889) is the starter for years. Belfour leaves after the playoffs. The backup becomes Ouellet at INTE 69, ENDU 60, GAA 2.41 in 13 games. That's a weak safety net for a long run. Not urgent in a year with Luongo healthy, but worth watching.

## Trajectory

The July renewal cluster is the whole story. Thirteen contracts worth $21.30M expire after this playoff run, and the four most important players on the roster — Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger — are all on deals under $1.20M. Their production this season says they'll command three or four times that on the open market.

**Gaborik** finished with 99 points in 82 games at age 23 on $1.10M. Richards put up 66 points at 24 on $1.00M. Nash had 39 points at 20 on $1.20M. Eminger, 21, carries POTE 99 on $1.20M. All four need 5-6 year deals signed the first day they're available, because in this game a player on an expiring contract who hits free agency will re-sign at whatever the market offers, not at your number.

**Chlup** is in the next cluster (2 years, $2.34M) but at 19 with 59 points and POTE 95, extending him now locks his rookie-window price. He will be a top-six centre by 21 and will cost $4M+ the moment his deal expires.

**Kaberle** at 27, 44 points, $1.90M, POTE 75 is the judgment call. Colaiacovo (22, POTE 99) and Stahle (21, POTE 96) are waiting behind him. A 3-4 year deal at a modest raise keeps the position covered while they develop, but he's not a 5-6 year player.

**The money is not the problem.** Revenue is $108.20M, profit $35.74M. After Belfour ($6.50M) and Roberts ($2.70M) walk, that's $9.20M freed. Even with raises for the young core and an Iginla acquisition at $6.50M, payroll lands around $65-69M against $108M in revenue. There is room for every move contemplated.

**The age cliff is the opposite of a problem.** After this season the 34+ group shrinks from four players (Sundin, Mogilny, Roberts, Belfour) to two (Sundin, Mogilny), and by July 2007 only Sundin remains. The core ages into its prime: Gaborik turns 24, Nash 21, Eminger 22, Chlup 20, Richards 25. This roster gets better for three seasons before anyone needs replacing.

**The 2006 cluster is real but manageable.** Nine players on 2-year deals worth $15.44M expire next July, including Luongo ($1.60M), Chlup ($2.34M), Klesla ($0.90M), Ouellet ($0.90M). Extending Chlup and Luongo now splits the workload across two summers instead of one.

**Draft capital is nearly empty.** One fourth-rounder. Every trade this summer needs players or picks acquired via the over-80 expiring mechanic. Belfour and Roberts walk, so that's $9.20M of over-80 value leaving for nothing unless someone wants them for picks before July 1.

## Calendar

The deadline passed on March 19 and Toronto are locked in for the playoffs per the GM's standing order: Tucker and the 4th-rounder are the only chips, nobody else moves, Belfour stays for the Cup run. That means the entire calendar question is now a summer question, and the summer has two jobs: re-sign the core before free agency hits, and target the three expiring players the vault has flagged across the league.

**The renewal list, in priority order:**

**Gaborik** (RW, 23, 91 base, $1.10M) is the first conversation in July. 87 points at 23 on $1.10M means his market value will triple the moment he hits the open market. Lock him on 5–6 years immediately. He is the highest-leverage re-signing on the roster.

**Richards** (C, 24, $1.00M, 64 points) second. Centre is the scarcest position, and at 24 he is entering his prime. 5–6 years. He and Gaborik must be done before any other conversation opens.

**Nash** (LW, 20, $1.20M) third. At 20 he is the cheapest long-term cornerstone the club will ever have. 5–6 years, sign in July, do not wait for a breakout year that raises his price.

**Eminger** (D, 21, $1.20M, POTE 99) fourth. The GM protected him from the Chara package specifically because of his upside. 5–6 years.

**Kaberle** (D, 27, $1.90M, 85 base) fills the 2–3 year bracket. He is productive but at 27 his ceiling is set. Renew, but do not give star length.

**Abid** (LW, 25, $0.40M, 80 TOUG, 80 CHKG) is the structural toughness fix the Coach has flagged since February. At 0.70 pts/g on 11.5 MPG he is a top-six contributor who costs pocket change. Renew 2–3 years. This is a cheap fix for a roster gap that no acquisition has filled.

**Alexeev** (RW, 23, $1.10M, 0.55 pts/g) earns a 2-year look. The Coach prefers him to Upshall and Chistov, and his production rate is nearly double theirs.

**The let-go list:**

**Belfour** (G, 40, $6.50M) walks. GM already established he will not accept a reduced deal, and he is worried about retirement. Luongo at 94 base on $1.60M with two years left is the answer. The $6.50M coming off the books is the summer's budget.

**Roberts** (LW, 38, $2.70M) walks per the Coach's own report. At 0.86 pts/g he is finished as a contributor.

**Upshall** (RW, 21, $1.20M, POTE 99 but 0.29 pts/g on 7.9 MPG) is the hardest call. The potential grade says keep, the production says the project is stalled. The Coach gave him an ultimatum: top-nine in camp or drop from the dressing list. Do not renew. Let him walk, or offer a one-year show-me deal at minimum. A POTE 99 who has never played above 8 MPG after two full seasons is not a prospect, he is a paper tiger.

**Chistov** (LW, 22, $1.10M, 0.29 pts/g) walks. Alexeev is better at the same age.

**Colaiacovo** (D, 22, $1.10M) needs a decision after the playoffs. If his minutes and grades improved in the second half, renew 2 years. If he stagnated like Upshall, let him walk and rely on Jackman at $700K, Klesla at $900K, and Eminger at 21 with POTE 99.

**Tellqvist** (G, 25, $0.80M) stays as cheap depth behind Luongo. The GM's January standing order was to give him time to develop. With Ouellet at 82 base on $900K also under contract, the club has three goalies for two slots next season, which is fine at $1.7M combined.

**The acquisition plan:**

**Iginla** (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, $6.50M expiring, TOUG 85) supersedes every other summer target. He closes the Mogilny scoring void and the structural toughness gap simultaneously. Calgary are 26-43-8 at 70 points with $14.43M profit; they cannot retain him and will not re-sign him. Toronto need to find a trade package, but the over-80 expiring mechanic only helps if he is still under contract when the league permits trades. If he hits free agency, Toronto need salary space and he will cost close to $7M on a long deal.

**Bell** (CHI, LW, 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81) is the second target. Chicago at 25-36-14, 78 points, $31.73M profit are motivated sellers. He is the only league-wide player closing both toughness and faceoffs at once, which is the Coach's explicit roster gap: no fifth centre wins draws. Chicago would accept a package around the 0.70-pts/g range — Tucker at 80 base and $1.30M on two years left, or Koltsov at 73 base on two years — plus the 4th-rounder.

**Cammalleri** (LA, 22, POTE 98, 60 pts in 61 GP, $1.10M expiring) is the highest-value UFA available. LA at 25-37-11, 79 points, $52.43M payroll cannot retain both him and Frolov. If he clears waivers or is traded to a non-contender, Toronto should pursue. He needs only a short audition to find out whether POTE 98 is real.

**Payroll math:** Belfour ($6.50M) and Roberts ($2.70M) coming off frees $9.20M. Gaborik, Richards, Nash and Eminger on 5–6 year deals will likely demand $1.50–$3.00M each depending on how the market moves, so the four young locks consume most of that freed space. Iginla at $7M would require a further stretch, which means either Upshall, Chistov, and Colaiacovo must also walk (freeing another $3.40M) or Tucker gets moved. The math works if the GM is disciplined about Abid at $0.40M and the existing cheap deals on Jackman ($700K) and Klesla ($900K).

## League scan

The season is done, and the July board is clear: Mogilny and Roberts walk, taking the roster's best shot power (94) and second-best checking (86) with them, and the structural toughness and faceoff holes the coverage phase identified remain open because no internal player can close them. This query finds the players on other clubs who can, ranked by how many gaps they fill at once and whether their club has a reason to move them.

**Iginla** is the single best answer in the league for two gaps simultaneously. At 27 with SHPW 99 (Mogilny's was 94) and TOUG 85 (our roster best is 75), he replaces the scoring void and raises the toughness ceiling by ten points in one move. 128 points in 82 games on $6.50M expiring. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring contracts and $14.43M profit cannot retain him. Already noted as the July RW priority on April 12; the data confirms he remains the top target.

**Havlat** is the best value on the board. 24 years old, 87 base, SHPW 95, 103 points in 82 games, on $900K expiring. OTT at 77 points with 11 expiring contracts are rebuilding and cannot keep him. He plays LW but can shift to RW, giving Toronto a second top-six wing at a quarter of what Iginla costs. If we get Iginla, Havlat is the third-line scorer behind him. If ATL re-signs Kovalchuk over Heatley, Havlat becomes the primary scoring replacement instead.

**Belanger** is the cheapest gap-closer in the league. FACE 96 at age 27 on $700K expiring from LA at 79 points with 14 expiring contracts. The Coach flagged "no fifth centre who wins faceoffs" on April 26, and Belanger at 96 is the answer the grades demand. He won't score much (82 base), but he wins draws and takes penalties away. He solves the problem for less than the cost of a bag of pucks.

**Cammalleri** hits UFA in July at 22 with POTE 98, 60 points in 61 games, and $1.10M. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring cannot retain both him and Frolov. He is the highest-ceiling young player on the board and costs a rookie salary. The risk is he may not develop (see Isbister), but at 22 and $1.10M the downside is minimal.

**Marleau** is the highest-floor option among the young UFAs. 89 base at 25, 98 points from the March notes. SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring on $45.39M payroll cannot keep everyone. He is arrived, not a project, and fills a top-six wing slot immediately. The concern is he may attract competition in free agency and command more than we want to offer.

**Heatley** at 91 base, SHPW 95, 131 points in 79 games on $1.10M remains available only if ATL re-signs Kovalchuk (22, 138 points) over him. ATL at 84 points with 11 expiring must choose. The younger choice is Kovalchuk. Heatley is the better fit for Toronto because we already have Nash and Gaborik at LW, and he plays RW, but he is conditional.

**Deadmarsh** (LA, RW, 29, 89 base, TOUG 82, SHPW 93, $2.80M, one year after this one) is a trade target, not a UFA. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring will likely deal him next year rather than lose him. He adds toughness and scoring to the right side simultaneously. The age is the cost: at 29 his window is three good years, not five.

**McLaren** (SJ, D, 27, 82 base, TOUG 89, CHKG 93, $2.20M, one year left) gives the blueline the toughness it has never had. SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring are shedding contracts. He is not a power-play quarterback but he is the physical presence our defense lacks, and at 27 he is not finished.

**Barnaby** (NYR, LW, 31, 82 base, TOUG 88, CHKG 89, $1.50M, one year) is the pure bottom-six grit the fourth line needs. NYR at 84 points with $0.00 profit is financially distressed and will dump salary. He scores nothing (53 points in 78 games) but at 88 TOUG and 89 CHKG he is the only player on the board who raises the fourth line's mean toughness by double digits. Age 31 caps him at two years.

**Bell** (CHI, LW, 24, 82 base, TOUG 88, CHKG 86, FACE 82, $900K, two years left) closes toughness, checking, and faceoffs in one player. He is the best hockey answer for the bottom-six problem. The construction problem: he is not expiring, so CHI wants a package. Tucker plus a pick acquired via the Belfour over-80 mechanic is the only offer we can make without breaking the Feb 19 core-protection order. CHI at 78 points with $31.73M profit are not desperate, so acceptance is uncertain.

**Not pursuing:** Daze is confirmed at 29 (born July 1975), which resolves the April 7 low-confidence note. He does not supersede Heatley or Havlat. Conroy at 33 is a one-year rental when Belanger at 27 costs $1.30M less. Fleury at 36 with TOUG 93 is a curiosity, not a plan. Chara is off the table per the February order.

## Trade construction

The question is what we can actually construct with Tucker, a 4th-rounder, and three players already confirmed to be walking, and whether those assets clear the price on the targets the league scan identified. They don't clear Iginla. They do clear Havlat, and they might clear Bell if the GM releases Koltsov from the protected list.

**Havlat from Ottawa** is the proposal that both sides can say yes to without anyone compromising a principle. OTT at 77 points carries 11 expiring contracts on a rebuild calendar. Havlat at $900K expiring will leave in July regardless; getting Tucker's 92 CHKG and 88 TOUG for the bottom six plus a 4th-rounder is a floor, not a gift. We pay $1.30M less than Tucker costs, gain 103 points in 82 games at age 24 with SHPW 95, and have the whole offseason to re-sign him at market. The Feb 26 note flagged this exact package before the season ended.

**Bell from Chicago** is the hockey answer the coverage phase demands: TOUG 88, CHKG 86, FACE 82 at age 24 on $900K with two years left. No other single player closes toughness AND faceoffs simultaneously. The construction problem is that Bell isn't expiring, so CHI has no urgency. At 78 points with $31.73M profit, they are in no pain. Koltsov at 24 with POTE 94 is the only piece that makes a young core piece look like an upgrade to a rebuilding GM, but that requires the GM to release Koltsov from protection. If he won't, this deal has no shape.

**Mogilny, Roberts, and Belfour** all walk July 1. If any of them can be moved via the over-80 mechanic for a pick before that date, it adds a round 3 or 4 to the pile without touching the core. Mogilny at $5.50M and 36 is the hardest to place; Roberts at $2.70M with TOUG 92 and INJU 98 is more palatable to a contender needing depth. The March 19 Belfour order was about finding a trade partner for him as a player return; moving him for a bare pick is a different question, but the GM said to close that monitoring, so I won't push it.

**Iginla at 93 base, 140 points, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring from CGY** remains the dream target but we have nothing that CGY accepts for a franchise right wing. Chlup, Gaborik, Nash, Klesla are the kind of packages that move a 93-base player, and every one of them is protected by standing order. This target lives or dies on whether the GM changes his mind about what the core includes.



**If none of the trades land:** Belanger and Cammalleri as UFAs solve faceoffs and add a high-POTE wing. Toughness remains the open hole — zero players at TOUG 80+, Jackman at 75 is the best — and the only answer becomes system management: short shifts on the bottom six, relying on Abid's 88 TOUG at 11.5 MPG (Coach flagged him for top-six minutes on April 26), and accepting that four-line matchups go against us. That's playable but not ideal in a second-round series against a physical club.

## Owed

**Luongo availability and DiPietro monitoring** — This task is closed and has been since March 19. The GM issued the standing order: "Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks. Only trading chips left are Tucker and the 4th round pick. Everybody else we keep."

**Luongo** is on our roster. He's at 94 overall, 26 years old, $1.60M with 2 years left, 45 games played this season. The acquisition the January 19 task was monitoring for already happened. There is nothing left to track on his availability.

**DiPietro** was eliminated from the target list on March 14: 79 base overall at 52 games played, eleven points below the 90+ threshold the GM set for a high-potential goalie acquisition. No further monitoring was warranted after that reading.

Nothing has changed because the task has been dead for over five weeks. I'm marking it delivered as a formal close.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-28

# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-28

Next game at PIT on Thursday 28 April 2005.

## Development opportunity

The season is winding down with 4 games left. The question is who gets those last shifts, and the answer is the same player I flagged two weeks ago.

**Alexeev** at 0.55 pts/g in 55 games remains scratched while Upshall (0.29, 68 GP) and Chistov (0.29, 68 GP) hold roster spots at double his game count. The rate gap is 0.26 points per game between Alexeev and each of them. PIT is 24-34; these are games where a young guy producing at that rate should earn his chance. Put him in.

**Spezza** (46 GP, 6.7 MPG, 0.33 pts/g, POTE 99) has had his season written off since late March. Scratching him for the last 4 is fine. His case is for camp, not April.

**Colaiacovo** at 0.39 pts/g on 17.9 MPG in 31 games is marginally above Klesla's 0.37 on 14.8 in 82, but the sample is thin. No case to displace Klesla in four games, and Klesla's 82-game workload is already a sell decision made.

**Stahle** has 4 games, 17.8 MPG, zero points. No case.

**Spacek** at 19, 7.6 MPG on the fourth line, 0.34 pts/g in 50 games, is at a fair development pace for his age. Nothing to fix.

**Chistov** at 0.29 pts/g on 13.1 MPG in 68 games is the weakest per-minute yield among dressed forwards. If Alexeev takes his spot for these four, that's the right test.

**Chlup** (0.83 pts/g, 16.9 MPG, 71 games) and **Gaborik** (99 pts, 82 games) have nothing to prove. Keep them where they are.

## Development trends

Season's over in four games. This is the final read before offseason moves, so the question is who has earned more ice next year, who has lost his claim, and whose trend changes what we planned months ago.

**Chlup** is the headline. 0.62 to 0.88 pts/g while minutes went from 11.0 to 18.2. At 19, a doubled load usually drags the rate down. His went up 42 percent. He belongs on the first line next season and I said the same thing in April; the season's data has only strengthened the case.

**Kaberle** is trending up at 27: 0.54 to 0.62 pts/g on minutes that rose from 19.4 to 21.5. More load, better rate, same direction. The GM called him a star in January and the numbers have backed him all season. No change, just protection in the lineup.

**McCabe** is the one that changes plans. Season total locks at 0.48 pts/g across 82 games. I set a 0.60 threshold on March 30; below that he goes back on the sell list, and 0.48 is well below it. His 1.42 early pace was a 24-game hot start. He is a sell this offseason.

**Klesla** confirms the two-season decline: 0.31 this year on flat minutes at 23. Sell with McCabe. The blue line needs a reset.

**Jackman** at 0.39 on 29.4 MPG at 24 is the same story we flagged in March. His role must change next season or his trade value sinks further.

**Richards** dropped from 1.08 to 0.71 on flat minutes at 24. No role change explains it. He needs a system-fit review in the offseason before we pencil him as a first-line centre.

**Abid** is the best underused player on the roster. 0.70 pts/g over 82 games on 11.5 MPG. His early pace was 1.09 on 20.1 MPG; someone took nine minutes a night off him mid-season and he scored at 70 percent of that rate on the reduced load. At 25 with 57 points in 82 games, he is a second-line winger playing fourth-line minutes.

**Alexeev** at 0.48 pts/g on 6.0 MPG still outproduces Chistov (0.30 on 14.0 MPG) and Upshall (0.27 on 4.8 MPG). The mismatch persists. He deserves a real look in camp over both of them.

**Spacek** went from 0.55 to 0.28 pts/g on minutes that collapsed from 16.0 to 5.2. Spezza is the same: 0.43 to 0.24 on 4.6 MPG. Both had lost seasons. Camp is the only lever now.

**The veterans are holding.** Sundin at 0.97 at 34, Mogilny at 0.83 at 36, Roberts at 0.86 at 38. These are aging numbers for players with long histories, not collapses. The window closes within two seasons and everyone knows it.

## Morale watch

The room is happy. Every single player on the roster is trending up in morale, and only four sit below 95. There is nothing to fix tonight.

**Spezza** is the lowest man in the building at 88, up 3 from the last save. He's scratched, carrying 6.7 MPG with 15 points in 46 games. His minutes did tick up from the 4.8 I flagged in March, and his morale is climbing with it. No action tonight; if he stays scratched through the final four games and drops back below 85, we have a conversation about dressing him for development.

**Alexeev** sits at 92, up 5, scratched at 8.3 MPG with 30 points in 55 games. The production-to-role gap is still there (0.55 pts/g on scratch minutes), but his morale has recovered from the 87 I saw weeks ago and is climbing. No action.

**Spacek** and **Upshall** are both at 91 with 7.6 and 7.9 MPG on the fourth line. For 19 and 21-year-olds on the bottom line, those are correct minutes. Rising, not slipping. Fine.

Everyone else on the dressed roster is at 98 or 100 and trending up. Jackman at 29.6 MPG, Sundin at 20.3, Gaborik at 20.5, Fischer at 22.4: all getting the minutes their calibre demands, all at 100. The results are doing the work.

## Role composition

Are our units built from the right pieces, and does this roster have enough bodies for the roles we need?

**L1 (Sundin, Roberts, Jackman, Gaborik, Fischer):** Correct. Checking mean 83 with Roberts at 85 and Fischer at 85 carrying it. The offense is absurd — Gaborik at 98 scoring, Sundin at 93. No change.

**L2 (Chlup, Mogilny, McCabe, Kaberle, Afinogenov):** Offensively elite (scoring mean 87, Mogilny 94, Afino 92). The faceoff mean of 59 is thin — Chlup at 80 carries it alone. Against PIT's 24-34 record this is manageable; I wouldn't restructure for it. The toughness mean of 64 is the weakest in the top three lines, but McCabe at 85 checking and 73 toughness provides some anchor. Leave it.

**L3 (Eminger, Richards, Klesla, Nash, Chistov):** Checking mean 75 is our best of the bottom two, driven by Nash at 94 on the unit. Speed mean 90 with Chistov at 98. Richards adds faceoff at 75 and clutch at 97. This line suits its role. No change.

**L4 (Spacek, Abid, Upshall):** Faceoff mean 52, best 55. Nobody on this line can win a draw. Checking is fine at 74. Against a 24-34 team this is tolerable, but it is a structural gap — see below.

**K1 vs K2:** K2 has checking mean 84 (Jackman 90, McCabe 85) while K1 has 79. K2 is our stronger kill unit by checking. I am not moving them tonight because K1 needs Sundin's 91 faceoff ability to win draws against the opponent's first PP, and the auto-pairing system ties D pairs to forward lines by slot number. The arrangement is a reasonable compromise.

**The roster gap, unchanged:** Only four players check above 80 (Jackman 90, Roberts 85, McCabe 85, Fischer 85). Only four take draws above 70 (Sundin 91, Chlup 80, Roberts 76, Richards 75). We have no fourth-line center who wins faceoffs. This means our fourth line gives up draws all night, every night. It is not a lineup problem; no arrangement of these 26 skaters fixes it. It needs a roster addition at the trade deadline or offseason.

## Opponent matchup

Gaborik is out until June, so the question is who fills first-line right wing against Lemieux tonight, and whether anything else needs to change for a team we beat six times already.

**The lines.** Mogilny goes to L1RW opposite Sundin and Roberts. He's 90 OVR with 95 speed and 95 shot power — the best winger available, and Lemieux's first line (PASS 99, PUCK 95, DEKG 98 on the centre) is no night for Upshall at 79. Chistov moves to L2RW at 82, Upshall to L3RW at 79. Fourth line becomes a three-man line: Spacek centre, Abid left wing, no right winger. That's the strongest 1-2-3 we can ice with 19 healthy forwards.

**PIT's first line.** Lemieux at 39 is still elite on the puck but his endurance reads 82 and he's carrying a 39-year-old engine. Fischer and Jackman on our first pair (CHKG 92 each, SPEE 94 and 94) are already the right answer. No change to D pair slot order needed.

**PIT's power play.** 32 goals on 276 chances is 11.6%. They cannot score a man advantage. No PK adjustment warranted; run the standard units.

**Goalie.** Luongo has no fatigue icon. Start him.

**Defenceman evaluation (obligation #1).** Final season numbers from q74: McCabe 0.76 on 22.1 MPG/82 GP, Kaberle 0.59 on 20.8/74, Fischer 0.53 on 22.4/77, Jackman 0.46 on 29.6/80, Klesla 0.37 on 14.8/82, Eminger 0.36 on 15.5/64. Sell order unchanged: Eminger first (expiring contract), Klesla second (two declining seasons), Jackman third (30 MPG for 0.46 is a role problem we can fix by trading him to a team that needs minutes).

## Owed

The question this answers: who stays, who goes, and what's the final season read on every defenceman. The season is wrapping up — this is the last assessment before offseason decisions get made.

**McCabe** finished at 62 points in 82 games on 22.1 MPG — 0.76 pts/g. That clears the 0.60 bar I set in March. At 29 with $3.00M and 4 years left, he anchors the top pair. No change from my April 7 call.

**Jackman** closed at 37 points in 80 games on 29.6 MPG — 0.46 pts/g. That's worse than the 0.48 I cited on March 23 at 73 games. The load kills him. Sell confirmed, and his $0.70M makes him attractive to a club that needs top-pair minutes cheap.

**Klesla** finished 30 points in 82 on 14.8 MPG — 0.37 pts/g. Two consecutive declining seasons locked in. Sell at $0.90M with 2 years left.

**Eminger** at 23 points in 64 games on 15.5 MPG — 0.36 pts/g. Contract expires this summer. If we don't move him before July we lose him for nothing. He's at 21, so he has trade value to a rebuilding club.

**Kaberle** at 44 points in 74 on 20.8 MPG — 0.59 pts/g. Just under the 0.60 threshold, but he's the GM's star and a keeper by standing order. His contract expires this summer — renewal is the GM's priority on this blue line.

**Fischer** at 41 points in 77 on 22.4 MPG — 0.53 pts/g. Two-way defence at 24, 4 years remaining. GM confirmed keeper. Stays.

**Colaiacovo** finished at 12 points in 31 on 17.9 MPG — 0.39 pts/g at age 22. Small sample. Contract expiring. He's a trade chip for depth help or a camp audition.

Nothing has moved since my last update except Jackman's final rate ticking down from 0.48 to 0.46, which strengthens the sell case. The sell list is Jackman, Klesla, Eminger (urgent, expiring). The keep list is McCabe, Fischer, Kaberle (renewal priority). Colaiacovo is a chip.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-26
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-26

Toronto 59-13-5, 133 pts after 82 games.

## Role coverage

The role coverage gap that decides the summer is faceoffs, and it cannot be fixed from inside the roster. **Sundin** at 90 FACE is the only player above 80, he is 34, and after him the ceiling is Chlup at 75 and Richards at 70. The coach wants a bottom-six centre who wins draws above 60; nobody dressed can do it at a level that changes a shift. This is the same structural gap that has existed all season, and it is one acquisition away from being solved.

**Bell** at CHI (24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81, $0.90M two years) closes toughness, checking and faceoffs in one player. He is the only league-wide candidate who fills all three simultaneously. CHI at 73 points with 10 expiring deals and $29.46M profit are motivated sellers. ENDU 71 means short shifts at first, which is fine for a bottom-six role.

**Avery** at LA (25, 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, $400K, two years left) is cheaper and stronger on draws, but weaker on speed and has no scoring upside. He is the floor option if Bell is out of reach.

**Tucker** (30, 83 CHKG, 70 TOUG, $1.30M) is on the roster and in no unit. Dressing him recovers one 80+ checker and adds a physical 6th on the back end. This is the coach's call and the cheapest move available.

**Checking** is thin once Roberts (38, 86 CHKG) walks at expiry. Jackman 87, McCabe 86, Fischer 82, Tucker 83 if dressed. Four men at 80+, all defencemen or depth forwards. A third-line checking centre would relieve the pressure on this group.

**Toughness** is missing across the board. The ceiling on stored grades is Jackman at 75. Zero players at 80+. The coach's fourth-line average of TOUG 57 confirms this is not a form artefact. No internal solution exists.

**Scoring and playmaking** are adequate now (10 and 11 at 80+ respectively) but age poorly. Mogilny 36, Roberts 38, Sundin 34 carry the top of both lists. Next season Mogilny is 37 and Roberts is 39 if re-signed. The replacement pipeline runs through Gaborik (23, 92), Afinogenov (25, 90) and Chlup, who is stepping into the first-line centre role. That is one fewer top-six winger than there will be roster spots for, which is why Iginla at 27 with 140 points in 73 games is the July priority.

**Durability** drops sharply after Roberts at 98. Afinogenov 95, Fischer 92, Abid 90. That is thin for an eight-month season, and Roberts is the best the club has at the position most likely to wear down.

## Trajectory

The question this phase answers: is Toronto's age curve and contract structure built to sustain contention, or is it one bad July from a rebuild? It matters now because the season is over and every renewal conversation opens in weeks.

The age shape is healthy on its own terms. 13 players at 23 or under, 12 more in the 24-29 band. The gap at 30-33 (Tucker alone) is a feature, not a problem. Four players sit at 34+: **Sundin** (34, $8.40M, 5 years, 91 pts), **Belfour** (40, walking), **Mogilny** (36, $5.50M, 2 years, 84 pts but declining to 0.79 pts/g), and **Roberts** (38, $2.70M, 1 year, walking). Three of those four are gone by next season, leaving Sundin as the sole veteran anchor. That is the correct aging curve for a team built the way the manual describes: youth-heavy with a few veterans.

**The contract cliff is the problem, not the age curve.** Thirteen deals worth $21.30M expire simultaneously this July, and eight of those 13 are lined players carrying the current roster. **Gaborik** at 99 points on $1.10M, **Richards** at 66 points on $1.00M, **Nash** at 39 points on $1.20M with POTE 95, **Eminger** at 21 with POTE 99 on $1.20M — all expire together, all will demand star money. A second cluster follows immediately: nine players worth $15.44M expire in July 2006, including **Mogilny** ($5.50M), **Chlup** ($2.34M, 2 years, POTE 95), **Luongo** ($1.60M, 2 years). Over the next two summers, $36.74M in contracts, 61% of current payroll, come due.

The money can handle it. Payroll is $60.04M against $108.20M revenue, spending 55.5 cents of every revenue dollar on salary. Even if the young core triples on extension — Gaborik to $5M, Richards to $4M, Nash to $4M, Eminger to $3M, Kaberle to $4M — that replaces roughly $5M of existing salary with $20M, pushing payroll to about $75M. Revenue supports it. Profit stands at $35.74M with $108.20M of income, so there is room for Iginla at $6.50M or $7M on top of renewals.

**Draft capital is nearly empty.** Toronto holds only a fourth-rounder. Every acquisition must be funded by roster players, not picks. This means the toughness and faceoff fix (Bell from Chicago) and the right-wing upgrade (Iginla in July) both require giving up a body or two, and there is no pick cushion to make a deal closer.

The three moves that protect the next three seasons, in order:

First, lock the five young core players on 5-6 year deals this July: Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger, Kaberle. This collapses the $21.30M cluster from 13 expirations to maybe 5-6 manageable ones and secures the competitive window. Chlup at 19 with 2 years left and POTE 95 should be addressed in the same conversation, ideally extending before his rookie price evaporates.

Second, sign Iginla in July. He is 27, 93 base, 140 points in 73 games (1.92 pts/g), TOUG 85. He closes the Mogilny scoring void and the structural toughness ceiling in one move. CGY at 70 points with 10 expiring contracts cannot retain him. At $6.50M-$7M, he fits the payroll structure with $35.74M of profit and $48M of revenue headroom.

Third, acquire Bell from Chicago to close the faceoff and toughness gap the Coach quantified at checking mean 61, toughness mean 57. Bell at 24 has 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81. Chicago at 73 points with 10 expiring deals and $29.46M profit are motivated sellers. Toronto has no picks to offer, so a package must include a young player, likely Koltsov or Alexeev (both POTE 94, 1-2 years remaining, scratched).

## Calendar

The deadline passed 38 days ago and we are 5 games from the end of the regular season at 133 points, so the only calendar question left is the summer: who renews, who walks, and which free agents we chase.

**Gaborik** at 91 base, age 23, $1.10M expiring, POTE 90 is renewal priority one. A 5-6 year lock costs more than $1.10M but a bidding war in July costs more than that. Do it first, immediately when free agency opens.

**Richards** at 24, $1.00M expiring, is priority two. Same logic: 5-6 years, lock before someone else names his number. Nash (20, $1.20M) and Eminger (21, $1.20M) follow on the same term.

**Kaberle** at 27 and $1.90M is the one renewal that warrants 2-3 years rather than 5-6. He is still productive but the salary is real and the age curve tilts down after 29.

**Belfour** ($6.50M) and **Roberts** ($2.70M) walk. The GM decided this in March. Belfour's over-80 pick-recovery mechanic required a trade by the deadline, which has passed, so the pick capital is lost. Roberts at 38 is the same. Together they free $9.20M for the summer market.

**Upshall** (21, $1.20M, 0.29 pts/g) and **Chistov** (22, $1.10M, 0.29 pts/g): the coach has flagged both and Alexeev outproduces them both at 0.55 pts/g. Let them go. Their $2.30M is better spent on Bell or Stuart.

**Alexeev** at 23 and 0.55 pts/g is the best of the three fringe wingers but still below roster-average production. Sign 2 years at $1.10M or let him test the market. His $1.10M is not a cost worth keeping him for if he does not break 0.70.

**Colaiacovo** (22, D, $1.10M) and **Tellqvist** (25, G, $0.80M): the GM ordered Tellqvist kept for his high-90s potential. Colaiacovo is the same profile at defence, a young left-shot blueliner cheap to hold. Both on 3-5 year deals at current salary. **Abid** at $0.40M is the cheapest toughness on the roster; 2 years, keep him.

**The summer market.** Three targets that fix what the coach flagged: **Bell** (CHI, 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE) closes both the fourth-line gap and the faceoff void in one signing. **Stuart** (SJ, 25, 87 base, POTE 91) replaces Roberts with eight more years. **Cammalleri** (LA, 22, POTE 98, 60 pts/61 GP) is the highest-ceiling free agent available. All three will command real money.

The June calendar dates are unnamed. June 8 is the rookie draft. The rest are likely free-agency and entry-draft events but I cannot confirm their names from the save.

**The Luongo monitoring task (#2) is closed.** Luongo arrived on February 7 at 91 base. DiPietro was eliminated in March at 79 base with 52 games played. Both questions resolved months ago; nothing further to report.

## League scan

Who across the league can fill the three holes the coverage phase named — a bottom-six centre above 60 faceoffs, an 80+ toughness body, a checking forward — plus the right-wing void Mogilny leaves, and why would his club move him. It matters now because the season is over (59-13-5, 133 points) and this is the board we negotiate the summer from.

**Iginla** is the head of the board. RW, 27, 93 base, 140 points in 73 games at 1.92 pts/g, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring. He closes the Mogilny scoring void and the structural toughness ceiling in one move. Calgary finished on 70 points with 10 expiring deals and $14.43M profit; they cannot retain that cap hit. This is a July signing target, not a deadline one.

**Bell** is the only league player who closes faceoffs, checking and toughness at once. 24, 80 base, showing 93 CHKG, 95 TOUG, 87 FACE, $0.90M with two years left, 28 points in 80 games at 17.8 minutes. Chicago finished 78 points with 10 expiring deals and $31.73M profit, so they will listen. He is the primary target. Koltsov (POTE 95, scratched, 19 points in 38 games) is the chip that funds him.

**Stuart** replaces Roberts' checking minutes on the back end with eight years of runway. 25, 87 base, SPEE 94, CHKG 83, 52 points in 77 games at 30.8 minutes a night, $1.80M with one year left. San Jose finished 76 points with 13 expiring deals and $20.74M profit. Note his TOUG reads 74, below the 80 line, so he is a core add, not a toughness fix.

**Nichol** is the cheap floor if Bell is out of reach. 30, 74 base, FACE 87, CHKG 82, $0.40M and expiring, 4 points in 66 games at 8.7 minutes. A faceoff specialist for the fourth line at no acquisition risk.

**Begin** is depth only. 26, 73 base, FACE 81, CHKG 92, TOUG 84, $0.94M with two years. The flag is ENDU 50; he cannot hold a shift long enough to matter until that recovers.

I would not make a 30-year-old the primary faceoff answer when Bell is 24 and closes two more gaps. The Luongo/DiPietro monitoring task is closed: Luongo is on the roster at 91 base with two years left, and DiPietro finished 79 base with a 3.64 GAA, eliminated on the Jan 15 goalie order.

## Trade construction

The summer board has three targets and one draft pick; the question is what Toronto gives each seller and why they say yes when we cannot cushion any gap with a first-rounder.

**Proposal 1, Bell from Chicago.** Give Koltsov (LW, 24, $1.10M, 2 years, POTE 94, 19 pts/38 GP, ACCE 96, AGIL 92, scratched by the coach) plus Tucker (LW, 30, $1.30M, 2 years, CHKG 92, TOUG 88, 3 GP). Get Bell (LW, 24, $0.90M, 2 years, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81, 28 pts/80 GP). Toronto sheds $2.40M, adds $0.90M, nets $1.50M of relief before the $21.30M July cliff. Chicago at 78 points with 10 expiring deals and $31.73M profit gets a POTE 94 forward whose ceiling is 13 points above Bell's, plus a 92 CHKG veteran body. They are rebuilding on 78 points and Koltsov's development timeline fits their window better than Bell's POTE 81 does.
