# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-14

Next game at NYI on Thursday 14 April 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether each young player is getting the games he has earned, and with the club at 82 games played and four remaining against weak opposition, tonight and the next three nights are the last window to answer it with ice time.

**Chlup** has fully earned his spot. 71 games, 16.9 MPG, 59 points (0.83 pts/g) at 19 on the second line. His minutes doubled from 11.0 earlier this season and his rate went up instead of down. No action, no concern.

**Gaborik** is the best player on the roster. 99 points in 82 games at 23, 20.5 MPG, every night. Nothing to say about his development because he is not developing, he has arrived.

**Nash** is getting the chance: 69 games, 13.1 MPG on the second line. His season rate of 0.57 pts/g is below where he started (0.83 per the March window), but the role and minutes are appropriate. The problem is production, not opportunity. Offseason system-fit review, not a lines decision.

**Eminger** plays 64 games at 15.5 MPG on the third defensive pair. His season rate of 0.36 pts/g at 21 confirms the slide. He is getting the chance to be a top-four defenceman and not seizing it. His contract expires this summer and he needs to be moved before July.

**Klesla** is in every game, 82 at 14.8 MPG. 0.37 pts/g at 23, second consecutive decline. He is getting the minutes; he is not producing on them. Offseason sell, not a development problem.

**Chistov** is third-line at 13.1 MPG, 20 points in 68 games (0.29 pts/g) at 21. POTE 95 is high, but the rate is not pushing him up the order. He is getting the chance. He has not yet earned more.

**Upshall** sits fourth line at 7.9 MPG, 20 points in 68 games (0.29 pts/g) at 21. POTE 99. The same story as last month: he is a depth forward right now and the minutes match that. If he wants top-nine minutes he has to take them in camp.

**Spezza** is the one who is not getting the games he has earned. POTE 99 at 21, 46 games on 6.7 MPG, 0.33 pts/g. He is a fourth-line regular getting less than a depth man's minutes. The season is gone for him now, but the offseason decision is clear: he needs a real camp audition or he stops being dressed. Giving him a handful of games against NYI over the next four nights does not fix this. The camp assignment does.

**Koltsov** is the GM's trading chip, stays per standing order. 38 games, 0.50 pts/g on 9.6 MPG. No development concern; he is a roster asset to be moved.

**Spacek** at 19 has 50 games, 0.34 pts/g on 7.6 MPG, and has been scratched recently. Against NYI at 30-38 this is a development night. Dress him. He needs real games before offseason decisions, and four games against the worst team in the division are the only ones left where that costs nothing.

**Alexeev** at 23 is 30 points in 55 games on 8.3 MPG (0.55 pts/g) and has been out of the lineup for 27 games. He is older and closer to a roster decision than development, but his rate says he was contributing when he played. Dressing him for a weak opponent costs nothing and gives a fair look before offseason choices.

**Colaiacovo** is scratched as part of the GM's deliberate D rotation, same framework as Svehla. 17.9 MPG when he plays, 0.39 pts/g at 22. No change needed.

**Stahle** has 4 games all season. POTE 96 at 20, but he is the seventh defenceman. He needs a camp audition, not a call-up against NYI.

**Ouellet** at 23 has 13 games as a backup. Expected role for a young goalie behind Luongo. No development concern.

## Development trends

The season is over and the final numbers are in, so this is the last look before offseason planning. The headline is a correction: my April 7 call that McCabe cleared the sell threshold was wrong.

**McCabe** reads 0.48 pts/g across 82 games in this brief, not the 0.76 I cited on April 7th. He scored 34 points in his first 24 games and just 5 in his remaining 58 (0.09 pts/g). That is a collapse, not a plateau. At 29 with 4 years at $3.00M and a 0.48 season rate, he goes back on the sell list. I owe the GM the correction before offseason planning starts.

**Kaberle** is the one D going the right direction. 0.54 to 0.62 pts/g on minutes rising from 19.4 to 21.5. At 27 with a rising rate and rising load, he is the blue-line centrepiece next year. Build around him, sell the rest.

**Chistov** is quietly growing into a role. His rate held at 0.30 while his minutes went from 9.5 to 14.0. At 21, holding production while taking on 50% more ice is the correct trajectory. He earns a middle-six spot at camp.

**Spacek** is confirmed dead for the season: 0.55 to 0.28 pts/g, minutes from 16.0 down to 5.2. The March bump never materialized. Offseason audition or stop dressing, same call as Spezza and Upshall.

**Richards** at 0.71 on flat minutes is now his season, not a blip. At 24 that should be going up. Offseason system-fit review stands.

**Gaborik** at 1.12 on 21.2 MPG in 82 games is still very good. The 1.42 start was a hot streak, not the norm. He is a keeper and the top-end winger.

**The veterans** are aging as expected. Mogilny at 36 dropped to 0.83, Roberts at 38 to 0.86, Sundin at 34 to 0.97. All still productive, none will be there in two years. Planning around the age cliff starts now.

## Morale watch

The room is in good shape and nobody needs a minutes change tonight.

**The lowest morale on the roster is 88** (Spezza), and that is in the safe zone. Everyone else sits 91 or above, with the core group at 100. The recent results have the dressing room right where I want it three games from season's end.

**Spezza** at 6.7 MPG and 88 morale is the only name worth a second look. If he's a 70s-calibre centre, the band says 10 MPG and he's 3.3 short. But 88 is not sliding, and the GM's standing order has him on the fourth line for development space. I'm not moving him for a morale number that hasn't moved.

**Abid** remains the oddity: 100 morale, 13.8 MPG, 66 points. His morale has no complaint. The minutes mismatch is a wasted-resource problem for the offseason, not a tonight problem.

No change. Lines are right, morale is stable, and the four games left are about execution, not room management.

## Role composition

Are the units built from players who suit their jobs, and is anything missing from the roster that no arrangement fixes? The answer today is that everything above the fourth line is correct, and the fourth line remains a roster problem I've already raised.

**L1** is the best-constructed unit on the team. Checking mean 80 with Fischer at 82 and Roberts at 82 gives it a real two-way spine, while Gaborik's 96 scoring and 99 playmaking anchor the offense. Sundin's 88 on draws means they win the draw and set up. Nothing to change.

**L2** works for what it is: a secondary scoring line with Chlup at 77 on draws and McCabe's 82 checking giving it a defensive floor. Mogilny's 90 scoring carries the offense. Adequate, not elite on either end, but the right shape for a second line.

**L3** is better than people think. Checking best 91, Richards at 72 on draws and 92 stamina, Abid's 70 toughness. This line can kill penalties and win races along the wall. It's a competent third line.

**L4 (Koltsov, Spezza, Upshall)** is where the roster lets us down. Checking mean 62, toughness mean 57, faceoffs mean 51. Nobody on this line can play a checking role. There is no one on the roster to put there who can check and is young enough to warrant minutes — the checking inventory tops out at Jackman 87, Roberts 82, McCabe 82, Fischer 82, all of whom are already slotted. This is a known gap and no arrangement fixes it.

**K2 actually has the higher checking mean (81) than K1 (76)**, but the split is correct. K1 needs Sundin's 88 faceoff to win the draw and get set; K2 gets McCabe and Jackman (82 and 87) for pure blocking and angling. The auto-pairing with L1 and L2 confirms this is the right order.

**Against NYI at 30-38**, this is a game we can afford to develop the fourth line in. The game-classification principle says maximize against quality opponents; NYI is not one. No reason to scratch the kids tonight.

## Opponent matchup

**The question:** should we adjust anything — lines, D pair order, goalie — specifically because of NYI tonight?

**No change to the lines or defensive pair order.** We are 59-13-5 and they are 30-38-4. We have beaten them 5-1-1 this season, outscoring them 21-12. Their best forward is Peca at 85 OVR on their second line, and our second pair (Kaberle/McCabe) handles him fine because McCabe brings 84 checking and 80 toughness into the matchups while Peca's line-mate Simon is a 72 OVR plod. Fischer/Jackman on the first pair against Yashin (64 checking, 52 toughness, a pure playmaker) is already the right configuration — they win every board battle Yashin tries to start. Swapping pair slots to put Fischer/Jackman against Peca would be a marginal gain against a team we have already beaten six times, and principle one says I don't break chemistry for that.

**DiPietro (83 OVR, age 23)** has rebound control at 62. That's the one soft spot on their sheet, and our first power-play unit with Gaborik (99 accuracy, 94 shot power) in front will find it. No special play call needed; just keep shooting.

**Luongo starts.** He's at 92 OVR, morale 100, no fatigue flag in front of me tonight. GM: check his icon on screen before confirming per the standing order. If he shows tired, Tellqvist (73) is the backup and it'll be a long night, but that's the same risk every night with Tellqvist and it's unlikely to matter against a team that generates 2.00 goals per game.

**The season series context matters:** NYI went 4-1-0 in their last five and they're at home. They're not going to lie down. But they're a 30-win club and we allow 1.50 goals a game. This isn't a game that needs tactical intervention. Trust the sheet.

## Owed

The defenceman sell-list review, item #1. The season is done — McCabe and Klesla played all 82, so these are final numbers. Everything is locked now.

**McCabe** stays. 62 points in 82 games on 22.1 MPG is 0.76 pts/g. He clears the 0.60 sell threshold I set in March. At 29 with 4 years and $3.00M he anchors the top pair and that's where he stays. No change from last week's call; the number just firmed up as the last game added to his total.

**Kaberle** stays. GM's standing order: "Kaberle is definitely a keeper. Kaberle is a star defenseman." 44 points in 74 games is 0.60 pts/g on 20.8 MPG. No change.

**Fischer** stays. GM's standing order. 41 points in 77 games is 0.53 pts/g at age 24 with 4 years left. No change.

**Jackman** is the sell. 37 points in 80 games on 29.6 MPG is 0.46 pts/g. That's down a tick from my 0.48 read at 73 games in late March — the last seven games added nothing. He's the cheapest top-pair minutes in the league at $0.70M x 3, which is why he still has trade value, but his production doesn't justify the ice load anymore. Sell this offseason.

**Klesla** is the sell. 30 points in 82 games on 14.8 MPG is 0.37 pts/g. Second straight declining season (0.38 at 22, 0.37 at 23) on flat minutes. $0.90M x 2. Sell.

**Eminger** is the sell. 23 points in 64 games on 15.5 MPG is 0.36 pts/g at age 21. His contract expires after this season. After July he's a UFA loss with zero return. Must move before free agency.

What changed since last week: nothing shifted in the hierarchy. Jackman's rate ticked down one more point from 0.48 to 0.46 as the final games landed. Everything else is confirmed final. The offseason window is now open — three defencemen go.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-13
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-13

Toronto 59-13-5, 133 pts after 82 games.

## Role coverage

The structural gap is toughness and the coach cannot fix it with anyone on this roster; every other question is about whether he is using what he already has.

**Afinogenov** — 90 scoring, 96 speed, 87 playmaking, 95 durability at 25, and he is not lined. This is the single largest waste on the roster. The coach's scoring depth drops from 10 players at 80+ to 9 without him, and his 95 durability means he does not add injury risk. Line him.

**Roberts** — 88 checking, 90 clutch, 98 durability at 38, and expiring. He is the best player on the roster who is leaving. Once he walks, checking drops from 6 to 5 at 80+, clutch from 9 to 8, and durability from 4 to 3. No internal replacement exists: McCabe is 29 at 86 CHKG but 73 TOUG, and Jackman is 24 at 87 CHKG but 75 TOUG. The defensive checking layer survives; the durability and clutch layer does not.

**Sundin** — 90 FACE, 94 clutch, 91 playmaking at 34. He is the only faceoff man at 80+. Chlup is the closest at 75 and is 19. The coach says Chlup is a first-line centre next season, which means he will need to carry faceoff duty without a 75-point backup plan at the dot. This is thin, and it gets thinner every year Sundin plays.

**Toughness** — zero players at 80+ TOUG. Jackman's 75 is the best Toronto has. This was confirmed structural on March 19 and has not changed. Tucker at 70 TOUG is the "band-aid" already noted, and even he sits at 70. Bell (88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE) remains the only known acquisition closing all three voids simultaneously. The coach cannot line his way out of this.

**Goalies** — Luongo at 26 with 2 years and Belfour at 39 expiring. The GM closed monitoring on March 19 and that stands. But Ouellet's 69 INTE and 60 ENDU at 23, and Tellqvist's 64 REBC and 66 INTE at 25, mean neither is a reliable backup for a contender after Belfour walks. This is a July trajectory flag, not a deadline action.

**Checking after Tucker goes** — standing order says Tucker and the 4th-rounder are the only chips left. If Tucker is traded, checking drops to 5 at 80+ (Jackman 87, McCabe 86, Fischer 82, Upshall 80, and one of the scoring-layer players). The fourth-line checking gap the coach quantified at 61 mean would widen. Hold Tucker unless the return is a direct replacement.

## Trajectory

**Is there a cliff?** Not an age one. The club has 25 players aged 29 or under and only four over 33. The cliff is contractual: 13 players, $21.30M, all expire this July simultaneously, including six players whose next contract defines the next five years of this franchise.

**The renewal math is favorable.** Payroll is $60.04M against $101.97M revenue, leaving $29.51M profit. If we re-sign Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger, Kaberle, and Abid at a combined raise of $15-18M (moving them from $7.70M total to roughly $22-25M), payroll reaches $75-78M and profit remains above $24M. We can absorb it. We cannot absorb them walking.

**Sundin is the one problem that gets worse with time.** At 34, $8.40M, 5 years remaining, he produces 91 points (1.11 pts/g). But POTE 60 means he is finished growing, and by 2008-09 he will be 37 on $8.40M. Every year we hold him, his trade value falls by one season of decline while his contract term shortens by one year. The window to convert him into young pieces with multiple years left is now through the summer of 2006.

**Mogilny is already dead money.** 36, $5.50M, 2 years left, POTE 55, 84 points on a declining rate. No club takes a 36-year-old with two years at $5.50M. The only path is to ride him out as a 13th forward while Iginla (93 base, 27, 140 pts/73 GP, $6.50M expiring from CGY) replaces him at the top. The $5.50M is sunk; Iginla closes the gap.

**Draft capital is zero.** One fourth-rounder. Every package Toronto constructs must be player-for-player. The over-80 expiring mechanic gives us two realistic pick-recovery assets: Belfour (92 base, walks July) and Roberts (81 base... actually 80, walks July). Both can be converted to a draft pick. That yields one or two picks for the 2005 draft, nothing more.

**The Fischer situation is not yet a crisis.** 24, POTE 90, $3.70M with 4 years remaining. He produced 41 points in 77 games (0.53 pts/g) this season, down from 0.63 two years ago. If the decline continues through next season, the $3.70M becomes dead money with 3 years left and no trade market. Flag for July: if next season drops below 0.45 pts/g, he becomes the next Sundin problem on a smaller scale.

## Calendar

The deadline passed on March 19. We are 25 days out and the only calendar that matters now is the summer: 13 contracts expiring, four games of playoff seeding left, and a July market where the single best available player (Iginla, 93 base, 140 points in 73 games, $6.50M expiring) fills both our scoring and toughness holes simultaneously.

**Gaborik** renews first, 6 years, at a significant raise. At 91 base with 87 points and POTE 90 at age 23, he is the club's asset. The January plan to lock him early died because mid-contract renegotiation is impossible; the renewal is the only window. Do not let him reach the open market.

**Richards** renews second, 5 years. He is at 64 points, 24, $1.00M expiring. The coach flagged his decline from 1.08 to 0.71 pts/g on flat minutes; that needs a system-fit explanation in the offseason, but at 24 with POTE 99 and a faceoff grade of 70, he is the second-line centre of the next five years. Renew regardless of the system-fit question.

**Kaberle** at 27, $1.90M expiring, renews 5 years. Top-pairing D-man at his prime age. No controversy.

**Eminger** at 21 with POTE 99, $1.20M expiring, renews 5-6 years. The GM already protected him from a trade veto in January. Lock him now so his value never sits in the same summer as Gaborik's.

**Nash** at 20, $1.20M expiring, renews 5-6 years but with the system-fit caveat the coach raised. His rate halved from 0.83 to 0.42 on identical minutes. If the explanation is usage, he stays a first-round talent; if it is a ceiling problem, a long deal locks in a decline. Renew, but not before the review.

**Colaiacovo** at 22 with POTE 99, 31 games, $1.10M expiring, gets 3 years. Thin sample for a star contract. Three years takes him through age 25, which is when you know.

**Chistov** (21, $1.10M), **Alexeev** (23, $1.10M, 0.55 pts/g), **Upshall** (21, $1.20M): all three are 2-3 year depth renewals. They are cheap, young, and fill roster spots. No drama.

**Tellqvist** at 25, $0.80M, renews 2-3 years. The GM's January order was to give him time; he has had it through the season with Luongo arriving. If his high-90s potential hasn't surfaced by 27, the window narrows. Two years keeps the option open.

**Abid** at 25, $0.40M, renews 2 years. He is the cheapest physical presence in the building. TOUG 80, CHKG 80 at that salary is unrepeatable.

**Belfour** at 39, $6.50M expiring: offer 2 years at a reduced salary (roughly half), expect decline, proceed with Luongo as the confirmed number one. The GM already predicted he won't accept. If by chance he does, he becomes a playoff mentor. If not, walk him and bank the $6.50M.

**Roberts** at 38, $2.70M expiring: walks. No offer.

**July priorities in order:** Iginla first. At 93 base, 140 points in 73 games, TOUG 85, age 27, $6.50M expiring from a 70-point Calgary club, he closes the RW scoring void left by Mogilny's collapse (0.79 pts/g at 36) and lifts the structural toughness ceiling the coach quantified at 57 mean on the fourth line. Single move, two problems solved.

**Cammalleri** second. LA at 22 with POTE 98, 60 points in 61 games at $1.10M expiring. He is the cheapest high-ceiling forward available. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring contracts cannot keep both him and Frolov.

**Bell** third. The toughness/faceoff solution the coach has flagged since January: 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81, 24. If Bell is also expiring from Chicago (73 points), he joins the UFA pool. His ENDU 71 means short shifts initially, but no one else on the market closes that gap.

**What I would not do:** chase Marleau or Gagne as trade targets. The deadline is gone. They are UFAs in July, and both clubs' financial distress makes them signing targets, not trade targets. Pursue them directly on the market, not via packages.

**Task #2 (Luongo/DiPietro monitoring, requested January 19):** This is closed. Luongo arrived in February and is on the roster at 91 base with 2 years left. DiPietro was eliminated permanently on March 14 at 79 base in 52 games; no sample size bridges an 11-point grade deficit to the "high-90s" target the GM set. The GM closed all goalie monitoring on March 19. Nothing further to deliver.

## League scan

Toronto's July window is defined by 13 expiring contracts worth $21.30M and four structural gaps the current roster cannot fill internally. The question this phase answers: who across the league fills those gaps and can realistically be acquired given what we can offer.

**Bell** closes toughness (88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE) better than anyone else in the league at his age. CHI at 78 points with $31.73M profit and 10 expiring deals are the most financially motivated sellers in the league. He remains the single most important acquisition target for July.

**Heatley** at 91 base with 131 points in 79 games at age 24 on a $1.10M expiring deal is the Mogilny replacement. ATL at 84 points with 11 expiring cannot retain both him and Kovalchuk (89 base, 138 pts/79 GP). Whichever ATL keeps, the other moves.

**Stuart** at 87 base with POTE 91, 80 TOUG, 89 CHKG at age 25 on a $1.80M expiring deal replaces Roberts' checking layer and closes the toughness gap simultaneously. SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring and $20.74M profit cannot retain all 13.

**Komisarek** reads 77 base but produced 82 points in 82 games at age 23 on $1.10M with POTE 91. MTL at 66 points with 15 expiring deals are the league's biggest sellers by that metric. The production-to-grade ratio is the most extreme in the data. If his rating develops toward POTE 91, he becomes a top-pair blueliner for four years.

**Bouwmeester** at 81 base, POTE 95, age 21 on $1.20M expiring from FLA (76 points, 19 expiring, most in the league) is the best young defenseman available. He is the lowest-cost long-term fix at the blue line.

**Nabokov** at 90 base with POTE 90, age 29, GAA of 2.66 in 69 games, on $3.60M expiring from SJ (76 points, 13 expiring), fits the January 15 standing order for a high-90s goalie from a non-contender better than Theodore. He is $1.90M cheaper and carries four more points of potential.

**Theodore** at 91 base, POTE 88, age 28, $5.50M expiring from MTL is the alternative if Nabokov stays. MTL will move him — 15 expiring deals and $21.59M profit means they are rebuilding, not re-signing. But $5.50M is $1.90M more than Nabokov for less upside.

**Doan** at 87 base, 88 TOUG, 93 CHKG, age 28, $2.40M expiring closes both RW scoring and toughness in one move. PHX at 93 points are in the race, which makes him harder to acquire. He is a fallback if Heatley stays at ATL.

**Belanger** at 82 base with 97 FACE, 79 TOUG, 83 CHKG, age 27, $700K expiring from LA (79 points, 14 expiring) gives Toronto a genuine second-line faceoff center for Sundin's eventual decline. He is not the same player as Bell but costs nothing on a long deal.

**Drury** at 89 base, 99 points in 82 games, age 28, $2.00M expiring from BUF (84 points, 10 expiring) is a top-six RW/LW scorer without a toughness component. He is a secondary target behind Heatley and Doan because he fills only one gap.

**Havlat** at 87 base, 103 points in 82 games, age 23, $900K expiring from OTT (77 points, 11 expiring, $32.36M profit) is a young LW scorer. OTT are profitable sellers but at 77 points with a 1-0 playoff run, they may retain him. Worth probing given the cheap contract.

## Trade construction

This phase turns the four priority targets into concrete packages the GM can propose in July. The constraint is currency: Tucker, one 4th-rounder, and players who are already walking. The gap between our chips and the Bell/Heatley tier is wide enough that we need to expand what counts as tradeable.

**Colaiacovo is surplus at defence.** Toronto carry nine defencemen. Eminger (21, POTE 99, 1 yr), Klesla (23, POTE 97, 2 yrs), Jackman (24, POTE 89, 3 yrs), McCabe (29, 3 yrs), Kaberle (27, 1 yr), Stahle (20, POTE 96, 3 yrs), Safronov (24, POTE 91, 3 yrs), St. Jacques (24, POTE 94, 2 yrs), and Colaiacovo himself played 31 games and finished seventh or eighth in the depth chart. He cannot displace four or five of those men. The coach flags him for development in the remaining games, which is correct for tonight but not for July roster construction. He is the single best trade asset we hold beyond Tucker and the pick.

**Bell is the structural fix.** Zero Toronto players carry 80+ TOUG. Bell has 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE at 24 on a $1.10M expiring deal. No player on our roster or in our system closes that gap. The coach's report is unambiguous: no bench player fixes it. If Bell leaves Chicago in July, we must pay for him with something other than Tucker + a 4th, because that package is worth roughly 74-76 base and Bell is 82.

**Heatley replaces Mogilny directly.** Mogilny is 36, POTE 55, two years remaining at $5.50M, and declined to 0.79 pts/g from 1.62 last season. He is not a tradeable asset at that age and salary. Heatley at 91 base, 131 points in 79 games, age 24, $1.10M expiring is the one-for-one replacement the scoring layer requires. ATL at 84 points with 11 expiring deals cannot re-sign both him and Kovalchuk (21, 89 base, 138 pts). One moves. We want it to be Heatley, and the asking price for ATL is youth, not veterans.

**Bouwmeester is the best young defenceman available.** FLA at 76 points with 19 expiring contracts cannot retain him. At 21, POTE 95, $1.20M expiring, he is cheaper than Stuart (25, POTE 91, $1.80M) and younger by four years. The package is within reach.

**Draft capital is zero beyond the 4th-rounder.** The over-80 mechanic converts Roberts (81 base, expiring) and potentially Belfour (92 base, expiring, if the GM reverses his March 19 close) into late-round picks. That yields one or two picks for the 2005 draft and gives us a third chip for a package. Without that conversion, every deal is player-for-player.

## Owed

**Goalie trade window monitoring** — this task is closed.

**Luongo** is on our roster. He arrived via the Aebischer + R1 package to Florida (confirmed by the GM on 2005-01-25). He reads 92 base, 26 years old, $1.60M, 2 years remaining, 45 GP this season. The Jan 15 order was "fetch a really good high-90s goalie from a team that will not be a contender" — Luongo at 92 is the closest we found, and he's here.

**DiPietro** was screened and eliminated. At 52 GP he reads 79 base overall, 11+ points below the threshold. No sample-size argument closes that gap. Eliminated permanently, recorded 2005-03-14.

**The GM closed this task himself on 2005-03-19**: "Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks. Only trading chips left are Tucker and the 4th round pick." Luongo and Belfour stay as two 90+ goalies for the playoffs. Goalies are solved.

Nothing has changed since the March 19 closure because there is nothing left to monitor. This is delivered.

# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-13

Next game at NYI on Thursday 14 April 2005.

## Development opportunity

The season is effectively over (82 games), so this is a final accounting of who got their chances and who didn't, which sets up the offseason.

**Chlup** got everything he earned and more. 71 games, 16.9 MPG on the second line, 59 points (0.83 pts/g). At 19 he's already the team's best centre and his ice rose with his production. No issues here.

**Gaborik** is a non-story: 82 games, 20.5 MPG, first line, 99 points (1.21 pts/g). He got the full run and delivered.

**Nash** got the games (69 GP, 13.1 MPG, second line). His 0.57 pts/g season rate is below what his POTE 95 would suggest, but the opportunity was there. His problem is system fit, not ice time. Offseason review, not a development-opportunity complaint.

**Klesla** played all 82 games at 14.8 MPG. He got the chance. His 0.37 pts/g at age 23 with POTE 97 says the opportunity wasn't the bottleneck. Sell decision stands.

**Eminger** played 64 games, 15.5 MPG, 0.36 pts/g at 21 with POTE 99. He got the ice; the production isn't coming. The contract expires this summer so this is a value exit, not a development question anymore.

**Spezza** is the clearest waste. POTE 99, age 21, dressed for 46 games but averaging 6.7 MPG on the fourth line. His recent window was down to 4.8 MPG. He's been on the roster for two years and gotten nothing resembling a real NHL audition. The season is dead for him; the camp decision is the only lever left.

**Upshall** mirrors Spezza exactly: POTE 99, age 21, 68 GP but only 7.9 MPG on the fourth line. He's technically "playing" but not developing. Same offseason decision: real audition or stop dressing him.

**Stahle** at 20 with POTE 96 played 4 games all year. He's invisible. If the club believes in that potential number, he needs a genuine camp audition next September or he should be exposed.

**Colaiacovo** played 31 games at 17.9 MPG when he was in. That's respectable ice when he plays, but 31 of 82 is a thin sample at 22 with POTE 99. He's the one young defenceman who's still in the building's timeline and hasn't gotten enough. The remaining games against weak opposition are his chance if any remain.

**Spacek** got 50 games at 7.6 MPG, now scratched. At 19 with POTE 91 he's below the Spezza/Upshall urgency level. He got some run, produced modestly (0.34 pts/g). Not a scandal, but not building much either.

**Chistov** (21, POTE 95, 68 GP, 13.1 MPG, 0.29 pts/g) got a full second-half run on the third line. That's fair opportunity for his level. Continue monitoring, no intervention needed.

**Alexeev** (23, POTE 94, 55 GP, 8.3 MPG, 0.55 pts/g) has a reasonable rate on limited minutes but is now scratched. At 23 with that potential number, he's near the window where either the minutes go up or the roster spot goes away. Offseason conversation.

## Development trends

Four games left in the season, so this is the final read before offseason planning begins. The window tells me who's ascending, who's stalling, and who needs a roster decision this summer.

**Chlup** is the story. 0.62 to 0.88 pts/g while minutes went from 11.0 to 18.2. At 19, doubled load normally crushes a rookie's rate. His went up. He's the first-line centre next year and for the two after that.

**Kaberle** went the wrong way for a "declining veteran" narrative: 0.54 to 0.62 pts/g on minutes climbing from 19.4 to 21.5 at age 27. He's in his prime and still getting better. The GM was right to protect him.

**McCabe** is back on the sell list. The second window reads 0.48 pts/g over 58 games on 21.5 MPG. My March threshold was 0.60; he's well below it. The December hot start (1.42 over 24 games) was the outlier. He's 29 with 4 years and $3.00M. Plan around selling him.

**Klesla** at 23: 0.50 to 0.31 pts/g on flat 14.9 MPG. Three declining seasons in a row. There's no reason to believe the fourth reverses. Sell.

**Jackman** at 24: 0.65 to 0.39 on 29.4 MPG. The load-to-production collapse is the whole season. He's a top-pair minute-eater producing third-pair offence. Either his role changes next year or his price drops further. Sell.

**Spezza, Upshall, Spacek** all collapsed together. Spezza: 0.24 pts/g on 4.6 MPG. Upshall: 0.27 on 4.8. Spacek: 0.28 on 5.2. None of them got meaningful opportunity after December. The season is a write-off for all three; camp auditions next fall decide who's on the roster.

**Nash** at 20: minutes flat at 13.2, rate halved from 0.83 to 0.42. The role didn't change, the production did. This is a system-fit question for the offseason, not a development question.

**Richards** at 24: 1.08 to 0.71 on minutes slightly down (16.9 to 15.8). At an age where the expected direction is up, this is concerning. Same offseason review as Nash.

**Alexeev** at 23 fell from 11.1 to 6.0 MPG with his rate dropping 0.62 to 0.48. He's falling out of the plan. Decide in the summer whether he's a roster piece or a body.

**Abid** is the one I feel worst about: 0.70 pts/g on 11.5 MPG at 25. His minutes dropped from 20.1 to 11.5 while his rate fell but stayed respectable. He's a second-line winger on fourth-line minutes. Morale risk.

**Veterans on schedule:** Sundin at 34 went 1.46 to 0.97 on minutes up from 16.9 to 21.7. Mogilny at 36: 1.62 to 0.83. Roberts at 38: 1.29 to 0.86. All expected aging curves. No alarm, no action.

## Morale watch

The room is in great shape and no intervention is needed for Thursday's game.

**Spezza** is the only man below 90 at 88. He's 21, sitting on the fourth line getting 6.7 minutes, and his production is 15 points in 46 games. The minutes are low for his calibre, but at 88 he is still in the range where morale adds a point to his grades rather than subtracting. With 4 games left, moving him now would break the line that's in front of him for a two-night window. Next camp is where this gets fixed.

**Everyone else on the active roster** sits between 91 and 100. Upshall at 91 on 7.9 minutes is right where a depth forward should be. Richards at 98 on 16.1, Mogilny at 98 on 18.4, Abid at 100 on 13.8 — the minutes mismatch on Abid is still a production question, not a morale one yet, and with four games to go it stays that way.

No change for NYI.

## Role composition

The fourth line cannot do its job, and no arrangement of this roster fixes it. That's the finding this phase produces.

**L1** is well-built. Sundin's faceoffs (88) anchor it, Roberts checks 82, Fischer checks 82, Gaborik carries the 99 playmaking and 96 scoring. Two-way skill plus offence. No change.

**L2** balances Chlup's growth against veterans who cover his weaknesses: McCabe (82 checking, 71 toughness) shields the blue line, Mogilny's 90 scoring gives Chlup someone to play off. Faceoff mean 56 is soft, but Chlup at 77 takes the draws himself. Adequate.

**L3** is underrated as a unit. Klesla brings 91 checking and 91 toughness — the best single defensive forward in the lineup — Richards adds 94 clutch and 72 faceoffs, Chistov gives 96 speed. The mean on checking (73) is dragged by Chistov, but Klesla's best is what we need for matchups. This line can shadow someone.

**L4** is the problem. Checking mean 62, toughness mean 57. Koltsov at 98 speed can't check, and Spezza (4.8 MPG last window) and Upshall are kids whose minutes collapsed. Nobody on this line wins a faceoff: mean 51, best 52. A fourth line that checks nothing, hits nothing, and loses every draw is just a regular shift where we hand the puck over.

**The gap is structural.** Our top four checkers — Jackman 87, Roberts 82, McCabe 82, Fischer 82 — are already deployed on L1 and L2. Nobody else on the roster checks above 75. Same story on toughness: Jackman 75, McCabe 71, Roberts 70, Abid 70, all occupied. We don't have a fifth body who can play a checking role. That's not a lines problem, it's a roster problem.

**P1 and P2 are fine.** P1 has Gaborik's 99 playmaking running the umbrella, Kaberle and Jackman shooting from the point, Roberts net-front. P2 has Mogilny's 90 scoring, Richards' 94 clutch, Klesla from the point. Both units have shooters and both have a quarterback. No change.

**K1/K2 ordering is correct.** K2 actually has higher checking (81 mean vs 76) than K1, but Sundin's 88 faceoff wins justifies him on K1 for the draws.

Against NYI (30-38) tomorrow, this isn't a maximize night. The kids stay on L4 and get the experience. The fourth-line gap is an offseason problem, not a Thursday problem.

## Opponent matchup

The question: does NYI present a matchup problem that requires a change from our standard lines, or do we roll what's working?

**No change.** We're 5-1-1 against them this season with a 21-12 goal margin, and the quality gap is enormous. Our first line has Sundin at 89 and Gaborik at 96; their first line tops out at Yashin's 83. Our second line runs Chlup at 84 and Mogilny at 88 against Peca's 85 — we match up fine there too. Their bottom six is thin: Scatchard 77, Manderville 67, Podein 69. No adjustment needed.

**Yashin** is the only player who concerns me. ACCU 88, SHPW 90, PASS 92, PUCK 93, DEKG 92. His hands are elite. But Sundin at FACE 88 and OVR 89 is the right man on him, and that pairing has held all year. We've given up 12 goals in 7 games against this club; they don't get enough volume to make one skilled player dangerous.

**Bates** carries FACE 94 against Richards' 72 on the third line. That draw loss has existed all season and hasn't stopped us winning this series. Not a fixable problem tonight.

**DiPietro** at 83 with REBC 62 is beatable. We average 3.60 goals per game; they give up 2.50. We should put this away in regulation.

**Goalie:** Start Luongo at 92. Check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming per the standing order.

## Owed

**Defenceman analysis, final check.** The season is effectively over and the numbers are locked in. Nothing has changed since my April 12 delivery, so I'll confirm the final figures as the offseason baseline rather than restate the case.

**McCabe** finished at 62 points in 82 games, 0.76 pts/g on 22.1 MPG. He cleared the 0.60 sell threshold I set on March 30 and stayed there. At 29 with 4 years and $3.00M, he's the anchor. Confirmed keeper.

**Kaberle** at 44 points in 74 games, 0.59 pts/g on 20.8 MPG. Your word is "star defenseman." No change.

**Fischer** at 41 points in 77 games, 0.53 pts/g on 22.4 MPG. Your word is "very very good." No change.

**Jackman** finished 37 points in 80 games, 0.46 pts/g on 29.6 MPG. The rate slipped from 0.48 (March 23 reading at 73 GP) to 0.46 at season's end. The load keeps eating his production. Sell offseason at $0.70M x 3. His value is the cheapest top-pair minutes in the league.

**Klesla** finished 30 points in 82 games, 0.37 pts/g on 14.8 MPG. Second consecutive declining season (0.38 at 22, 0.37 at 23) on flat minutes. Sell at $0.90M x 2.

**Eminger** finished 23 points in 64 games, 0.36 pts/g on 15.5 MPG. He continued to slide (0.44 in February, 0.38 in March, 0.36 now). His contract expires in July. This is the last window to get anything back. After that he's a UFA loss.

The sell list is unchanged since my last delivery. Three defencemen go: Jackman, Klesla, Eminger. Three stay: McCabe, Kaberle, Fischer. The 4 remaining games won't move any of these rates meaningfully.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-12

# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-12

Toronto 59-13-5, 133 pts after 82 games.

## Role coverage

The question this phase answers is whether Toronto's roster can field a physically imposing fourth line from within, or whether that gap demands July capital. It matters now because the regular season is done at 59-13-5 and every playoff round will test the bottom six against bigger lines.

**Toughness is the one role that cannot be solved internally.** Zero players carry 80+ stored TOUG. The best on the roster is Jackman at 75, and he is a defenceman. The coach's fourth line sits at a mean of 57 with a best of 75. No line change fixes a structural ceiling of 75 when you need 80. This resolves the February contradiction: the Feb 21 finding of "six players at 80+" was reading form-inflated displayed ratings, not stored grades. The gap is real and permanent without an acquisition.

**Faceoffs have the same structural problem on the forward side.** Only Sundin (90) clears 80. Chlup at 75 is next and he is a confirmed top-nine centre. Tucker carries 67, Richards 70. Neither draws 55% consistently. The fourth line's 51% best is a floor the opponent exploits.

**Checking is fixable within the roster.** Tucker sits at 83 CHKG and is not lined. If the coach dresses him on the fourth line for the playoffs, that alone pulls the checking mean from 61 toward 70. Roberts at 86 is 38 and walking, so his contribution has an expiry date. Jackman (87) and McCabe (86) are both defencemen. On the forward side beyond Tucker, Fischer at 82 and Upshall at 80 are the only others clearing 80. Thin but not missing.

**Scoring, speed, and playmaking are covered.** Gaborik at 92 and 23 carries the RW slot. Sundin at 92 and 34 is the franchise pivot. Koltsov at 92 speed and 23 is the future on the wing. The crisis is at Mogilny's position: 94 base at 36 with a confirmed decline to 0.79 pts/g means that line needs a new RW within 12 months.

**Durability is thin at 4 cleared at 80+** (Roberts 98, Afinogenov 95, Fischer 92, Abid 90), and Roberts is walking. But no single acquisition fixes this without a full depth chart rebuild.

**Goalies are solved per the GM's March 19 order.** Luongo (26, 2 years) is the starter. Belfour carries the playoff backup role at 39. Ouellet (23, 2 years) is the future backup. The only issue is the post-Belfour years, which the GM has accepted.

The targets that close gaps internally impossible to close: Bell (CHI, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, 82 base, 24) for the forward side, and Stuart (SJ, 80 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 87 base, 25) for the Roberts replacement at defence. Both require July negotiation with clubs in financial or roster-retention distress.

## Trajectory

The July 2005 renewal cluster is the single largest strategic risk on this roster, and it is six weeks away. Thirteen contracts worth $21.30M expire simultaneously, and most of them belong to the players this team is built around: Gaborik ($1.10M, 99 pts), Richards ($1.00M, 66 pts), Nash ($1.20M, 39 pts), Eminger ($1.20M, POTE 99), Kaberle ($1.90M, 44 pts). If those five walk, the roster that finished 133 points ceases to exist.

**Sundin** at $8.40M with 5 years left is the roster's financial anchor. He is producing (91 points at 34) but the contract runs to his age-39 season. If his production halves by 37, you carry $8.40M for a half-speed player with no trade market. This is not solvable now, but it shapes every re-signing decision: you cannot also give Gaborik and Richards $5-6M each without payroll approaching $80M against $102M revenue.

**Chlup** is the most urgent contract on the sheet right now. He turns 20 before the season ends, has POTE 95, 59 points in 71 games, and costs $2.34M with two years left. If he breaks out to 70+ points next season, his asking price at renewal in July 2006 will be $5-6M. Lock him to a 5-6 year deal this July at $3-4M and you own a franchise centre at below-market cost through his age-25 season. Every week without that conversation is money given away.

**The two-year group is the next cliff.** Chlup, Luongo, Spezza, Koltsov, Klesla, Ouellet, St. Jacques, Tucker, Mogilny all expire July 2006. If you sign the one-year core to five-year deals in 2005 and then face Luongo (26, POTE 97) and Chlup in the same 2006 window, you are back at a mass renewal. The solution is to extend Luongo and Chlup into 2006 territory NOW rather than waiting.

**The 34+ group resolves itself.** Sundin ($8.40M, 5 years) is the only long-term burden. Belfour ($6.50M, 39) and Roberts ($2.70M, 38) expire in July and should walk cleanly. Mogilny ($5.50M, 36, 2 years) is unavoidable dead money for one more season; at 0.79 pts/g by March, he produces 30-35 points at best. That $5.50M buys nothing next year, but there is no way out before 2006.

**Draft capital is nil.** One fourth-rounder. Every future move requires a player of equivalent value. This means the young players you re-sign become tradeable assets, which is fine, but it also means Toronto cannot package picks for a scorer. The path to filling the fourth-line gap must be a player-for-player trade or a free-agent signing.

**The age curve in 2007-08 is excellent** if you hold the core. Chlup 22, Nash 23, Eminger 24, Gaborik 26, Richards 27, Afinogenov 28, Luongo 29, McCabe 32, Kaberle 30. That is a roster entering its peak simultaneously. The cliff risk is not aging into decline; it is losing the pieces before they arrive.

## Calendar

The deadline passed 24 days ago and the regular season is done for all trading purposes, so the only calendar that matters now is the summer: thirteen contracts worth roughly $22.10M expire simultaneously, and the renewal order you set on March 21 is the plan to execute.

**Gaborik** at 23 with 87 points, 91 base overall and POTE 90 on a $1.10M expiring deal is the single biggest renewal risk on the roster. Lock him on five or six years in July before any bidding war. His production is the engine; losing him would gut the top line.

**Richards** at 24 with 64 points on $1.00M is the second lock. Five or six years. He is the centre of this franchise's next decade and costs less than half of what the market will offer by August.

**Eminger** at 21 with POTE 99 on $1.20M is the third lock on a five or six-year deal. You vetoed trading him in January because his ceiling is higher than Chara's; the same logic applies to keeping him.

**Nash** at 20 on $1.20M gets five or six years despite the system-fit concern the coach flagged. He halved his scoring rate without a role change, which is a development question, not a talent question. At 20 with POTE well above his current 75-ish overall, the option value at that salary is enormous.

**Kaberle** at 27 on $1.90M gets two or three years. He is a good power-play quarterback but at 27 his ceiling is set, and a long deal at his price blocks money for the younger core.

**Tellqvist** at 25 with POTE in the high 90s gets two or three years. The GM's January order was to give him time. Luongo is the starter; Tellqvist is the insurance and the trade asset if a goalie need emerges.

**Alexeev** at 23 on $1.10M gets two years if he earns the fourth-line right wing spot this week. The coach is giving him the audition in the final game. If he does not stick, do not re-sign.

**Upshall** at 21 on $1.20M: the coach's March 9 report says he needs a genuine camp audition next season or he stops being dressable. Do not renew until camp tells you whether he has a role. If he does not, he is $1.20M wasted.

**Chistov** at 21 on $1.10M: same as Upshall, assess in camp. He was part of a failed trade attempt; keep him only if he is playable.

**Colaiacovo** at 22 on $1.10M: young defenceman. If Eminger and Kaberle are the top pair, he is the third-pair guy. Two years at most, and only if he shows development by camp.

**Abid** at 25 on $0.40M: keep him. TOUG 80, CHKG 80 at 25 for four hundred thousand is the cheapest toughness on the roster and partially fills the coach's fourth-line gap.

**Belfour** at 39 and $6.50M walks. The March 19 order was to keep him for the playoffs and close the file. Roberts at 38 and $2.70M walks too. Together they free $9.20M.

The coach's fourth-line gap (checking mean 61, toughness 57, faceoffs 50) is a summer acquisition target, not a renewal problem. Bell at Chicago (82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, age 24, POTE 81) is the single player who closes both halves of the gap. Chicago are 73 points with ten expiring deals and $29.46M profit; they are sellers this summer. Fund the deal with Tucker ($1.30M, POTE 79, 30 years old) plus the 4th-rounder plus Chistov or Upshall, depending on which one camp cuts. The Avery-from-LA package remains the parallel target if Bell is too expensive.

On the RW side, Mogilny's decline (0.79 pts/g in his final stretch at 36) is confirmed. Heatley or Doan are the July priority for the top-six right wing opposite Gaborik. Cammalleri (LA, 22, POTE 98, 60 pts on $1.10M expiring) is the best value on the UFA market if he reaches it.

The draft on June 8 is a depth exercise: no pick better than a fourth-rounder. GM's standing instruction to scout goalies there stands; find a project with high POTE for the Tellqvist backup slot.

**No trade is possible before July.** Every acquisition above is a summer operation. The only action between now and then is playing the five remaining regular-season games and the playoffs with Belfour and Luongo both healthy.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: with the season done at 59-13-5 and zero draft capital, which players across the other 29 clubs close our three structural gaps (toughness, RW scoring, defence depth) and can realistically land in Toronto this July. The answer reorders the winter target list because one player appeared on a non-contender that nobody flagged: Jarome Iginla.

**Iginla** (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, TOUG 85, CHKG 79, FACE 69, POTE 81) posted 140 points in 73 games on a $6.50M expiring deal. Calgary finished 70 points, went 26-43-8, made zero playoff appearances last spring, and carry 10 expiring contracts. They are in full rebuild mode with $14.43M profit and no path to re-signing him at market. He closes the Mogilny scoring hole AND the toughness ceiling simultaneously: TOUG 85 is above our current roster maximum of 75, and 79 CHKG clears the Coach's threshold of 75. The salary is the issue at $6.50M, but Belfour ($6.50M) and Roberts ($2.70M) expiring frees $9.20M, making him net cheaper than the money already leaving. If he hits UFA July, our 625 prestige and $29.51M profit make us a credible destination.

**Bell** (CHI, LW, 24, 82 base, TOUG 88, CHKG 86, FACE 82, POTE 81) remains the only league-wide solution to the fourth-line problem the Coach quantified. He is the single player clearing TOUG 75, CHKG 75, AND FACE 82 (grade-level, translating to above 55% draws). Chicago at 78 points with $31.73M profit and 10 expiring are sellers in structure, though they are profitable so they won't dump. His $900K salary and two years left make this a trade not a UFA. The challenge is constructing a package Toronto can offer without breaking the core. Tucker ($1.30M) plus the 4th-rounder is worth roughly a 74-76 base player, which is not Bell.

**Stuart** (SJ, D, 25, 87 base, TOUG 74, CHKG 83, POTE 92) at $1.80M expiring with 30.8 minutes a night is the Roberts replacement. San Jose at 76 points with 13 expiring on a $45.39M payroll cannot retain all of them. His TOUG is 74, not the 80 previously noted from a form-inflated reading, but CHKG 83 and 2523 minutes at 25 make him a top-pair defenceman. UFA July signing target unless a trade package can be constructed before July.

**Heatley** (ATL, RW, 24, 91 base, 96 pts/58 GP) is the fallback RW if Iginla signs elsewhere. Atlanta's $36.79M payroll (lowest in the league) and 11 expiring contracts mean they cannot retain both him and Kovalchuk. At $1.10M Kovalchuk is the cheaper keeper, so Heatley is the one likely to walk or get traded. The over-80 pick mechanic applies.

**Kovalchuk** (ATL, LW, 21 turning 22, 89 base, 134 pts/82 GP, $1.10M expiring, TOUG 78, CHKG 71, FACE 54) is the best production-per-dollar in the league but Atlanta likely keeps him. TOUG 78 does not clear the fourth-line bar and FACE 54 is useless there. He would play top-six, not bottom-six. Pursue only if ATL unexpectedly shops him.

**Cammalleri** (LA, RW/C, 22, 79 base, POTE 98, 60 pts/61 GP, $1.10M expiring) is the development target. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring on $52.43M payroll cannot keep all 14. He does not close any physical gap but fills future top-six depth at a trivial salary.

**Marleau** (SJ, C/RW, 25, 89 base, 98 pts, $1.60M expiring) is available from the same San Jose club that holds Stuart. SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring cannot retain both. If Toronto can only take one piece from SJ, take Stuart (defence, POTE 92, 25) over Marleau (another top-six RW when Iginla fills that role).

The ranking is Iginla, Bell, Stuart, Heatley, Cammalleri. Iginla and Bell together close the Coach's exact specification: "at least one forward who checks above 75 and wins draws above 55%." Bell does it from the fourth line; Iginla from the first.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: with one 4th-rounder and Tucker as the only designated chips, what package can Toronto actually construct that another GM says yes to, and what is the sequence if a single deal won't close the gap.

**Bell from Chicago for Tucker + the 4th-rounder** is the only clean two-way proposal that can be built from what we hold. Bell at 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, $900K with 2 years left, 24 years old, is the only player who closes the Coach's exact specification. Tucker is 83 CHKG stored, 30, POTE 79, $1.30M. Chicago at 78 points with 10 expiring and $31.73M profit have no reason to retain a player whose POTE is 81 and whose ceiling is set. They get a proven physical wing who helps now plus a pick, and they shed one of ten contracts. The value gap is real (82 base versus 79 POTE plus a low pick) and Chicago could say no, but their transition mode makes them the likeliest seller in the league.

**Stuart from San Jose cannot be acquired in one move with current assets.** He's 87 base, POTE 92, $1.80M expiring. SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring on $45.39M payroll cannot retain him, but they want picks, not a 30-year-old wing. The over-80 mechanic on Belfour ($6.50M expiring, walks) and Roberts ($2.70M expiring, walks) each generate a pick of unknown round. If those are second or third, that pick plus the 4th is a Stuart package. If they're fourths, it's not. This must be attempted before any Stuart conversation opens. If the mechanic yields a useful pick, offer it plus the 4th to SJ for Stuart.

**Iginla from Calgary requires the Belfour and Roberts picks to exist first.** At 93 base, 140 points, $6.50M expiring, 27 years old, POTE 81, Calgary at 70 points in full rebuild will not trade him for a 4th-rounder and a 30-year-old. They need first- or second-round capital. The only path is: generate one or two picks from Belfour and Roberts via the over-80 mechanic, then package those with the 4th and possibly Tucker. This is a two-step deal with high failure probability at each link. If the mechanic yields two middling picks and Calgary still says no, he hits UFA and our 625 prestige makes us a credible destination at a reduced salary.

**If none land.** Dress Tucker on the fourth line for the playoffs (83 CHKG pulls checking from 61 toward 70, per the Coach's own measurement). In July, sign Stuart as a UFA at $1.80M if he clears. Sign Cammalleri (LA, 22, POTE 98, $1.10M) for future depth. Accept the fourth line stays at 61 CHKG / 57 TOUG for the 2005-06 season and re-attempt Bell acquisition after his contract-year value drops.

## Owed

**#2 — Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window.** This task is complete and formally closed.

**Luongo** was acquired by Toronto in late January/early February. The monitoring task was marked complete on 2005-02-07 when he appeared on the roster at 91 base. He is now at **92 overall**, 26 years old, **$1.60M with 2 years left**, 45 GP this season. He is the starting goalie for the playoffs. The window he was meant to fill is the one we are currently in.

**DiPietro** was eliminated on 2005-03-14: 52 games of sample, still **79 base overall**. The Jan 15 order required high-90s potential; an 11-point gap at full sample is not a development story.

**The window itself is shut.** The GM closed all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19 with Luongo and Belfour (91 overall, 37 GP) confirmed as the two 90+ goalies for the playoffs. There is nothing left to track on this item.

No change since February beyond confirming what was already decided. The task is delivered.

# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-12

Next game at NYI on Tuesday 12 April 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether each young player got the games he earned this season, and what to do with the remaining five. With NYI at 30-38, these are games we can afford to develop in.

**Colaiacovo** is the biggest miss. At 22 with POTE 99, he played 31 games and averaged 17.9 MPG when he was in the lineup — top-pair minutes that say the coaches trusted him. Then he got benched for veterans and hasn't come back. He deserves the remaining five games.

**Chlup** is the model. 59 points, 16.9 MPG, second line, 71 games at 19. He earned every shift and the production went up under increased load. No issue.

**Gaborik** — 99 points, 20.5 MPG, first line, 82 games. Nothing to say except he's exactly where he belongs.

**Spezza** at 6.7 MPG and **Upshall** at 7.9 MPG are both POTE 99 kids on the fourth line with the season gone for development purposes. No point dressing them for garbage minutes now; the fix is a camp audition in the offseason.

**Spacek** at 19, POTE 91, is now scratched after 50 games at 7.6 MPG. If these are development games, put him back in. Five games of real experience means more than five as a healthy scratch.

**Stahle** played 4 games all year at POTE 96. The season is a write-off for him, same as Spezza. Note for camp.

**Alexeev** at 23 with 30 points in 55 games (0.55 pts/g) is scratched. He earned more than the 8.3 MPG he got, and these last games are free. Give them to him.

**Nash** (13.1 MPG, 39 pts, L2) and **Chistov** (13.1 MPG, 20 pts, L3) are producing at their level with regular work. No concern.

**Klesla** plays every game at 14.8 MPG on the third pair. His rate is 0.36 pts/g and he's a sell, but he's getting appropriate minutes for what he is.

## Development trends

The season is 5 games from done, so these trends are locked; what matters now is who gets what next season.

**Chlup** is the story. 0.62 to 0.88 pts/g on minutes that went from 11.0 to 18.2 at age 19. Most 19-year-olds decline under doubled load; he got better. He belongs on the first line permanently and should be treated as the centrepiece of the next two seasons.

**Kaberle** is the only player going up among veterans. 0.54 to 0.62 pts/g with minutes climbing from 19.4 to 21.5 at 27. The GM called him a star in January; the trajectory confirms it. He is improving right now and should not be moved.

**Spacek** is confirmed dead. 0.55 to 0.28 on minutes that collapsed from 16.0 to 5.2 at 19. No grade movement, no role, just buried. Offseason: real camp audition or stop dressing him entirely.

**Spezza** and **Upshall** are the same story. Spezza 0.43 to 0.24 on 4.6 MPG; Upshall 0.33 to 0.27 on 4.8 MPG. Both 21, both with potential that has not converted. Same offseason decision: earn a roster spot in camp or stop pretending they are prospects.

**Nash** at 20 dropped from 0.83 to 0.42 pts/g on flat minutes (12.9 to 13.2). The role did not change; the production did. That is a confidence or system problem, not an ice-time problem. Needs a real look in the offseason.

**Richards** at 24 went from 1.08 to 0.71 on minutes that actually dipped from 16.9 to 15.8. At an age where the expected direction is up, a 35% production drop with no role change needs a system-fit review before he is pencilled in as a first-line centre next year.

**The veterans** are holding: Sundin at 34 is at 0.97 recent and 1.11 season on 21.7 MPG; Mogilny at 36 is at 0.83 recent; Roberts at 38 is at 0.86 on 21.4 MPG. All still full-time producers. But the minutes are climbing (Sundin from 16.9 to 21.7, Roberts from 16.5 to 21.4), which means they are carrying more of the load as the young guys fail to step up. The GM should plan for the day the rate catches up to the age.

**Defencemen update (deliverable #1):** The sell list stands at Jackman (0.65 to 0.39, 29.4 MPG, confirmed collapse), Klesla (0.50 to 0.31, confirmed second declining season), and Eminger (0.35 to 0.37, flat, expiring, must move before July). McCabe holds at 0.76 season rate and stays. Fischer's rate dipped from 0.63 to 0.50 but he is carrying 22.9 MPG and the GM has him marked untouchable. Colaiacovo (0.44 to 0.36 on 17.5 MPG in only 31 games) is a watch case for camp, not a sell yet.

## Morale watch

The room is fine heading into the final week. Everyone trending up, core at 100, no one in a hole that a line change fixes tonight.

**Spezza** at 88 is the lowest on the roster, up 3 from his floor. At 6.7 MPG on the fourth line at age 21, he is well under what a developing centre needs, and his morale reflects that. But he is climbing and the season is done. This is an offseason assignment question, not a tonight question.

**Spacek** at 89, up 5. Scratched, 7.6 MPG on the season. Same story as Spezza: too few games, recovering. No action tonight.

**Jackman** at 29.6 MPG is carrying 12 minutes more than his calibre expects, and his production (0.48 pts/g) confirms the load is hurting him. His morale is 100 and rising so it is not a morale problem yet, but it is a role problem the offseason needs to solve.

**Everyone else** sits at 98-100 with the whole room on a +3 to +5 trajectory. The results are doing the work. No intervention needed for the last five games.

## Role composition

The units are arranged correctly for their roles. No composition change is warranted today.

**L1 and L2** are well-balanced top-two lines. Sundin at 88 on draws anchors L1's possession game; Chlup at 77 does the same job on L2. Both lines carry scoring mean above 83 and checking mean above 73, which means neither line is a liability in its own end. Gaborik at 96 scoring and 99 speed gives L1 the shooter role; Mogilny at 90 scoring gives L2 the same function. No one on these lines is playing out of position.

**L3** carries the team's best checking grade (Klesla at 91, Abid at 70 toughness) and Richards at 72 is the fourth-best draw man. This is a proper depth line that can handle defensive-zone starts. The problem I flagged March 7 persists: Richards is the next-best faceoff man after Chlup, so L3 takes draws nobody else on the bench can take. That forces top-six defensive-zone starts all season, which loads minutes onto the top pairs. It is not fixable with current personnel.

**L4** is a development line with structural weaknesses the GM already knows about. Koltsov at 98 speed is the only real weapon; checking mean 62, stamina mean 53, faceoff best 52. Against a 30-38 New York Islanders team this is exactly the night for it. Short shifts, keep them moving, give the top lines a rest. No reason to bench them today.

**P1** is a scoring unit built around Gaborik with four playmakers feeding him. Scoring mean 86, playmaking mean 85, speed mean 87. This is the right construction. P2 with Chlup at centre and Mogilny as the shooter is a capable second unit at 84 scoring mean.

**K1** (Sundin, Roberts, Kaberle, Fischer) is a possession kill: speed mean 85, checking mean 76. They clear with skill rather than brute force. That suits this personnel. **K2** (Chlup, McCabe, Jackman, Abid) is the grinding kill: checking mean 81 is the best on the team, toughness mean 71. Jackman at 87/75 is the anchor. These two PK units are correctly differentiated.

**Roster-level gaps** (not lineup problems, already flagged or acknowledged): the faceoff void below Richards persists. No enforcer exists on the roster; Jackman at 75 toughness is the ceiling. Neither is new, and neither changes today's lineup.

## Opponent matchup

**This is a mismatch on paper and our structure already handles their threats. No line change.**

**NYI's top line** — Yashin (83 OVR, 90 shot power, 92 puck control), Kvasha (94 speed, 93 shot power), Parrish (91 speed, 89 shot power) — is genuinely skilled. But our D1 of Fischer (83 OVR, 89 checking, 91 speed) and Jackman (84 OVR, 89 checking) is built to handle exactly that kind of line. The auto-pairing puts our L1/D1 against their L1/D1, and that's the best possible configuration for us.

**Peca at FACE 94** is the one thing that stands out. He sits centre on their second line and will win draws against Chlup (77). Our L2 pairs with our D2 (Kaberle/McCabe), who can absorb that. The real danger would be if we shuffled Richards (72) down against Bates (94), which would compound the problem. We don't. The current alignment is already the best faceoff distribution we can build: Sundin wins his, Chlup is even with Peca, and the losses happen against teams whose centres we can't cover at any alignment.

**Their third and fourth lines** are soft. Podein at 69, Czerkawski at 76 with morale 81, Manderville at 67. Scatchard at 77 with morale 79. Our L4 of Spezza/Koltsov/Upshall is young and can handle that, and it gives them minutes in a game we should control.

**Eminger's endurance (50)** is the only structural worry. He faces their third pair (Robidas 70, Martinek 71) and their L3 (Bates, Podein, Czerkawski). That's the softest assignment they can give anyone. The matchup actually suits him — low danger, manageable pace.

**Goalie: start Luongo.** He's at 92 OVR, morale 100. DiPietro is 83 for them. The standing order says check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming; if it's clear, he starts. If he's tired, Tellqvist gets it and we lose nothing against this lineup.

**No change to any line.** The reason: our season record (3.80 GF, 1.70 GA) against their record (2.20 GF, 2.40 GA) is a 49-point gap. We're 4-1-1 this year against them. Their PP is 8.3% (23 of 276) — our PK won't be tested. There is no tactical adjustment that moves the needle against this opponent.

## Owed

**#1 — Defenceman sell-list update, final season numbers.** The season is done or this is the last game, so these are now locked totals rather than rolling windows. Conclusions confirmed, two rates drifted further down since my last check.

**McCabe** — 82 GP, 22.1 MPG, 62 points = 0.76 pts/g. Confirms the March 30 clearance. He stays. The 4-year $3.00M deal at 29 is the anchor cost and he justifies it.

**Fischer** — 77 GP, 22.4 MPG, 41 points = 0.53 pts/g at 24. The GM's keeper, and the production backs it.

**Kaberle** — 74 GP, 20.8 MPG, 44 points = 0.59 pts/g at 27, $1.90M expiring. The GM called him a star and he produced. Renewal conversation is his to have.

**Jackman** — 80 GP, 29.6 MPG, 37 points = 0.46 pts/g. My last check showed 0.48 on 73 games; the final seven dragged him to 0.46. Same sell call, now on a full season. His trade value is $0.70M x 3 on nearly 30 minutes a night. Sell offseason.

**Klesla** — 82 GP, 14.8 MPG, 30 points = 0.37 pts/g. Two declining years confirmed at full length. Sell at $0.90M x 2.

**Eminger** — 64 GP, 15.5 MPG, 23 points = 0.36 pts/g. My February read had 0.38, this is lower still. $1.20M expiring in July. If we do not move him this offseason he walks for nothing.

**Colaiacovo** — 31 GP, 17.9 MPG, 12 points = 0.39 pts/g, $1.10M expiring. Low sample, low rate, scratched all year. Same urgency as Eminger: move or lose.

**What changed since my last delivery:** Jackman 0.48 → 0.46, Eminger 0.38 → 0.36. Both strengthen the sell case. No new candidates; no keeper has become questionable.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-09
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-09

Toronto 59-13-5, 133 pts after 82 games.

## Role coverage

The season is over at 59-13-5 and the question now is what this roster looks like in July after the contracts expire: Mogilny (36, 94), Roberts (38, 88), Sundin (34, 92), and Belfour (39) are all walking, and they carry the top grades in scoring, checking, clutch, and faceoffs respectively. The youth core is strong — Gaborik 92 (23), Richards 85 playmaking (24), Kaberle 90 clutch (27) — but three structural gaps open the moment those four leave.

**Toughness** is missing, confirmed again: zero players at 80+ TOUG in stored grades. Jackman tops the roster at 75, Roberts 73, McCabe 73. The coach flagged this directly and he is right — no internal move fixes it. Bell (CHI, 24, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81) or Avery (LA, 25, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 93 FACE) close this gap plus faceoffs simultaneously. Tucker at 70 TOUG is not close enough to count.

**Faceoffs** is missing the moment Sundin leaves. Only Sundin at 90 FACE is above 80. Chlup at 75 is next, then Richards at 70. That is a fourth-line centre problem disguised as a centre problem — the coach needs one player who wins draws above 55% and checks above 75, and the only two on the market who do both are Bell and Avery.

**Checking** is thin after Roberts walks. Tucker at 83 CHKG is not lined, which is the internal fix: line him on the fourth unit and the roster carries Jackman 87, McCabe 86, Tucker 83, Fischer 82, Upshall 80 — five bodies, barely enough for four lines in a playoff series. But five checkers is a floor, not a plan.

**Scoring** drops sharply. Mogilny 94 and Sundin 92 are the top two scorers and both are gone. Gaborik 92, Afinogenov 90, and Abid 86 are the next three, but Abid at 25 is not a first-line producer. The RW side is the problem: Mogilny at 36 was holding it, and the confirmed decline from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g means the next RW needs to arrive ready. Heatley (91 base, expiring) or Doan remain the July targets.

**Kaberle** at 90 clutch, 97 ENDU, 27, is the best player leaving no one is talking about — actually wait, he has years left. The defensive core post-Roberts is Kaberle, McCabe (29, 86 CHKG, 94 ENDU), Eminger (22, POTE 99), Jackman (24). That is four young-to-prime blueliners. Roberts at 38 and expiring is the one exit there, and Stuart (SJ, 25, 87 base, POTE 91) slots directly behind them with the highest ceiling on the block.

**Goalies** after Belfour walks is Luongo (26, GAA 2.67, SV .889) with Ouellet (23, mid-80s grades) as backup. That is acceptable but not deep. The Jan 15 standing order to find a high-90s goalie from a non-contender remains unfulfilled, though the March 19 order closed all goalie monitoring. The July question is whether Ouellet at 86/86/86/76 (GSH/GSL/SSH/SSL) is a playoff-calibre backup or whether this gap resurfaces.

**Speed** and **stamina** are covered. 21 skaters at 80+ SPEE and 11 at 80+ ENDU. No action needed.

## Trajectory

The question this phase answers is whether Toronto are heading for a cliff, and the answer is: not on age, but on contracts, and the window to fix it is the single summer where thirteen deals come due at once.

**The age curve is right.** Fourteen players 23 or under, eleven in their prime, one at 30-33, four veterans. That is close to the manual's shape. The young core is absurdly deep by grade: Chlup 19 (POTE 95), Nash 20 (POTE 95), Eminger 21 (POTE 99), Upshall 21 (POTE 99), Colaiacovo 22 (POTE 99), Spezza 21 (POTE 99). Gaborik 23, Richards 24, Abid 25, Afinogenov 25 are arriving. The next three years should improve on talent alone.

**The contract wall is the cliff.** Thirteen players worth $21.30M expire simultaneously. This is exactly what the manual warns about. The renewal wave replaces cheap rookie money with star money all at once: Gaborik at 99 points on $1.10M, Richards at 66 points on $1.00M, Abid at 66 points on $0.40M, Chlup at 59 points at 19 on $2.34M, Nash at 39 points at 20 on $1.20M. The game will not let them re-sign at current salaries. The cost increase on these five alone will run into eight figures, and it hits the same July that Belfour ($6.50M) and Roberts ($2.70M) walk for free. Net payroll change is roughly neutral, but the shape of the money shifts from cheap-young to expensive-young in one step.

**Mogilny is the dead weight.** 36 years old, $5.50M, two years left, and his rate fell to 0.79 pts/g by March (from 1.62 earlier in the season). He cannot be renegotiated and cannot be traded without absorbing the decline publicly. Two years of $5.50M at a sub-point rate is $11M of production the team cannot replace and cannot shed. This is the single contract that constrains the next two Julys more than any other.

**Sundin is locked and will age out the wrong way.** 34, $8.40M, five years left. He will be 39 when that deal expires. He is producing now (91 points this season), but the back three years of that contract will see the same curve Mogilny is on now, at a higher salary. There is nothing to do about it — he is signed — but the GM should know that the two highest-paid players on the roster (Sundin $8.40M, Mogilny $5.50M combined $13.90M) are both on the wrong side of their peaks.

**Draft capital is nil.** One fourth-rounder. Every acquisition through trade must be player-for-player. This means the fourth-line gap the Coach flagged (checking mean 61, toughness mean 57) has no pick-funded solution; it must come from a player swap or from within the existing roster's development.

**The two moves that protect three years:** first, re-sign Gaborik and Richards on 5-6 year deals before anyone else, because their current production relative to salary makes them the most valuable trade assets on the roster and the most urgent re-signings; second, accept that Mogilny's two years are sunk cost and build around his decline rather than hoping he recovers. The club's path to sustained contention runs through Gaborik, Richards, Chlup, Nash, Eminger and Luongo. Everything else is either supporting cast or salary the club is carrying.

## Calendar

The deadline closed March 19 and Toronto finished 133 points, so the only calendar that matters now is July: thirteen contracts expiring, roughly $21M walking off the books, and the entire young core needing a new deal before another club's offer sheet reaches them. The season ends in six games; after that, it's free agency on June 6 and the rookie draft on June 8.

**Gaborik** is renewal #1. 91 base overall, 23 years old, 87 points this season, $1.10M expiring. He gets 5-6 years. If he walks to an offer sheet at $5-6M a year, we have no compensation. Sign him first, before anyone else's name comes up.

**Richards** is renewal #2. 64 points at 24, $1.00M expiring. Same logic: 5-6 years, lock him at center before his market price doubles.

**Kaberle** at 27 is in his prime and already commands $1.90M. Five years at a raise (expect $4-5M) keeps a top-pairing blueliner who will be the anchor until Eminger is ready. Renew on 5 years.

**Eminger** at 21 carries POTE 99. The GM himself vetoed trading him in January because his ceiling is set in our timeline. Five or six years, low starting salary, and he is the franchise defenseman by 2007.

**Nash** at 20 has halved his point rate with no role change, which the coach flagged for a system-fit review. That is a development question, not a value question. At 20 with $1.20M expiring, he is still a core piece. Renew on 5-6 years; the role adjustment happens in camp, not in his contract.

**Abid** at $0.40M is the cheapest toughness on the roster — 80 TOUG, 80 CHKG at 25. The coach's gap is a forward who checks above 75 and wins draws above 55. Abid checks the first box, not the second. Renew him on 2-3 years; he is a role player at a role-player price, and the market for 80-checking wings who cost nothing is thin.

**Colaiacovo** at 22, $1.10M, is still developing on the blue line. Renew on 3 years. He is depth that could become top-four if Eminger's development and his own both break right, and at $1.10M there is no reason to lose him.

**Tellqvist** at 25 with high-90s potential stays per the January order. Two or three years as a backup while Luongo starts; the development window is still open.

**Alexeev** and **Chistov** are camp auditions. Alexeev just got the fourth-line wing for the final game; Chistov has never been given a sustained role. If either earns minutes in camp, re-sign on 1-2 years at $1.00-1.10M. If not, let them walk.

**Belfour** walks. The GM closed the goalie trade file March 19 and kept him for the playoffs — that was the right call, two 90+ goalies for a cup run. But at 39 and $6.50M, he is done in Toronto. Offer him two years at a reduced figure ($2.5-3.0M); he probably refuses and retires. Either outcome is fine. The January standing order about fetching a high-90s goalie from a non-contender is now a draft-and-develop question, not a trade.

**Roberts** at 38 and $2.70M walks, confirmed by the GM's March 21 order. No conversation needed.

**Upshall** walks. The coach said it plainly: without a genuine camp audition he stops being dressable. At 21 and $1.20M he has had his chances and not taken them. Save the money.

The net: we renew 9-10 of 13, save roughly $9-10M in dead salaries (Belfour, Roberts, Upshall, possibly Chistov/Alexeev), and accept raises on Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Kaberle, Eminger that will add maybe $15-18M in new money across those five deals. The club should absorb it at 133 points and strong attendance, but the renewal clustering the December 2004 note warned about is now real: five core contracts signed in one summer all come due together around 2010.

On the UFA side, Cammalleri (LA, 22, POTE 98, 60 points, $1.10M expiring) and Marleau (SJ, 25, 89 base, 98 points) are the big prizes. Both would fix the RW scoring hole Mogilny's decline opened. Pursue them in July after our own core is locked, and only at prices that don't distort the payroll the renewals already carry.

## League scan

The question this phase answers is: who do we pursue in July, and in what order? The Coach's fourth-line gap (checking mean 61, toughness mean 57, faceoffs 50) plus Mogilny and Sundin's departure from the top-six means three roles need filling. The answer is a tight cluster of four players who solve all three gaps, plus a goalie for depth.

**Heatley** is the primary RW target. Born January 1981, he is 24 with 91 base, 131 points in 79 games on $1.10M expiring from ATL at 84 points. He is a pure RW scoring replacement for Mogilny at half the age and a tenth the salary. ATL cannot keep him and Kovalchuk; we should pursue whichever the Thrashers release.

**Kovalchuk** is the mirror target. Born April 1983, he is 22 with 89 base, 138 points in 79 games on $1.10M expiring. More production than Heatley, but he is a LW. If ATL keeps Heatley (the RW need is more acute for us), Kovalchuk is the fallback — and at 22 with POTE 85, he has three more years of development ahead. Either way, one of them arrives free.

**Bell** is the single-player fix for the fourth line. Born August 1980, he is 24 with 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, 28 points in 80 GP at 17.8 MPG on $900K with two years left. CHI at 78 points with $31.73M profit and 10 expiring are rebuilding. He requires a trade package because he has two years remaining — the cheapest solution is a mid-round pick plus an expiring salary like Tucker ($1.30M). CHI has no reason to keep a checking LW while stockpiling young talent at other positions.

**Stuart** replaces Roberts immediately. Born November 1979, he is 25 with 87 base, 80 TOUG, 89 CHKG, POTE 91, 52 points in 77 GP at 30.8 MPG on $1.80M expiring. SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring on a $45.39M payroll cannot retain all of them. He is the highest-rated available defenceman and closes the toughness gap at the back end where the Coach flagged zero roster players above 75 TOUG.

**Cammalleri** fills the second top-six forward slot. Born June 1982, he is 22 with POTE 97, 60 points in 61 games on $1.10M expiring. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring cannot keep him and Frolov and Belanger. He is not yet a confirmed top-six player (79 base) but the ceiling is there and the cost is nothing.

**Theodore** fills the backup goalie gap after Belfour walks. Born September 1976, he is 28 with 91 base, 3.29 GAA, .856 SV in 66 starts on $5.50M expiring. MTL at 66 points with 15 expiring have no reason to retain a 28-year-old goalie on a rebuild timeline. He gives Luongo a true 1A/1B situation. The salary is high but Belfour ($6.50M) and Sundin ($8.40M) both leave, creating space.

**Havlat** is a high-upside LW option. Born April 1981, he is 24 with 87 base, POTE 85, 103 points in 82 GP on $900K expiring from OTT at 77 points with 11 expiring. If ATL retains both Kovalchuk and Heatley (unlikely but possible), Havlat is the next-best scoring LW available.

**Belanger** is the faceoff specialist if we cannot land Bell. Born December 1977, he is 27 with 97 FACE, 83 CHKG, 79 TOUG, $700K expiring from LA.
