# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-30

Next game at NJ on Friday 01 April 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether each young player is getting the games his scouting file and production have earned. With three games left (NJ away, then MIN and OTT at home), the window to act is closing, and the offseason is where the real decisions land.

**Spezza** is the roster's worst development failure. POTE 99, 21 years old, 15 points in 43 games on 6.7 MPG fourth-line minutes. Morale 86, the lowest among the young group. I've raised this five times since January with no movement. His season is gone; the only lever left is his camp assignment next September. If we play him at all in MIN or OTT, he needs top-nine minutes, not the spot-check he's been getting.

**Stahle** has played 4 games at POTE 96, age 20. Three games remain. If he doesn't see the ice in at least one of MIN or OTT, he has had an entire NHL season without a genuine audition. That is a wasted year at 20, and I cannot fix it in September.

**Alexeev** at 0.55 pts/g (30 points in 55 games) is currently scratched. He's producing at a rate that earns a roster spot, but he's on the outside. With three games left this is a marginal call, but the offseason question is whether 8.3 MPG was his ceiling or someone's mistake.

**Chlup** belongs exactly where he is: second line, 16.9 MPG, 56 points at 19. No intervention needed.

**Gaborik** at 95 points on 100% of the games, top line, 20.5 MPG at 23. Fully earned.

**Nash** at 0.55 pts/g on 12.8 MPG, L3. His rate halved from 0.83 earlier in the season while minutes held flat. The role is right; the production decline needs an offseason look at system fit, not a lineup change in April.

**Upshall** at 0.29 pts/g on 8.0 MPG, morale 89, L4. Same pattern as Spezza: POTE 99, fourth line, collapsing minutes. His season is also dead. Offseason audition or stop dressing.

**Eminger** at 0.38 pts/g on 15.8 MPG, L3 defence. Recent window is 0.17 over his last six per my earlier reading. Back on the sell list. Development isn't fixing him at this point; the trade market is his best path.

**Klesla** at 0.38 pts/g on 14.9 MPG, second consecutive declining season at 23. Sell this offseason. Playing time is correct; the ceiling is the problem.

**Colaiacovo** scratched at 31 games, 17.9 MPG when he plays. This is the GM's deliberate rotation decision from January and I've conceded it.

## Development trends

The question: who's on the way up, who's stalling, and what does that mean for next year's plans. With three games left and the season effectively decided, this is the last window before offseason decisions lock in.

**Chlup** is the story of this team's season. 0.87 pts/g on 18.3 MPG at 19, across 68 games. He went from 11 minutes to 18 and his rate still climbed from 0.62. The earlier finding said he belonged in the top nine permanently; he's now playing like a top-six centre. No grade moved on the card, but 0.87 at 19 says more than any single reading. Flag for offseason: he starts on a second line next year, not a third.

**McCabe** is back in sell territory and I need to correct my March 4 read. His recent window (55 games since the first save) is 0.45 pts/g on 21.7 MPG at 29. My March 4 note put him at 0.83 over 66 games and took him off the sell list; that earlier sample was propped up by the 24-game hot start. The 0.45 over 55 games is the real number at his age. Re-evaluate this offseason.

**Abid** gets worse every time I look. Minutes fell from 12.6 in my March 16 note to 11.5 now, and his recent rate is 0.74 pts/g. He's 25, producing on a third-line winger's ice time. This is the same problem raised three times with no movement. At 25 his development window is closing.

**Nash** at 0.38 pts/g on 12.8 MPG at 20 is the quiet alarm. My March 16 note flagged 0.43; he's fallen further with no change in role. The rate halved on stable minutes, so it's not a usage problem, it's a fit or a skill ceiling. Offseason system review remains the right call.

**Spacek, Spezza, Upshall** are all dead seasons now, not stalling. Spacek at 0.28 on 5.2 MPG, Spezza at 0.27 on 4.5, Upshall at 0.27 on 4.8. All three had the audition window and lost it. The offseason decision is the same for each: real camp audition or stop dressing them.

**Jackman** confirms the collapse I flagged twice in March. Season rate now 0.41 on 29.5 MPG at 24, down from 0.65 early. The 0.48 I noted March 23 has slipped further. He's a summer sell.

**Koltsov** at 0.28 across 35 games is no longer a trading chip with value. Anyone seeing 35 games at that rate won't offer meaningful return. The asset is gone.

**Klesla** at 0.33 confirms the second declining season. Sell list, as noted March 23.

**Kaberle** is going the right way at 27. 0.64 pts/g on 21.7 MPG across 71 games, up from 0.54. The GM called him a star and the numbers agree. He's still improving.

**Sundin** at 0.98 on 21.7 MPG at 34 is still a first-line centre. The decline from 1.46 is real but 0.98 at 34 is not a problem yet.

**Mogilny** at 0.78 on 19.2 MPG at 36 is the expected age slide. Still productive, but the trajectory says plan around him next year.

**Roberts** at 0.87 on 21.4 MPG at 38 is remarkable for his age but the same planning question applies.

No grade changes on the card for anyone, so production and minutes carry all the signal here.

## Morale watch

The room is happy. 28 of 30 players sit at 96 or above with a win streak lifting everyone. There is nothing to fix before Friday.

**Spezza** at 86 is the only real outlier, and it's the same story it's been since March: 6.7 MPG on the fourth line at 21 years old, well under the 17 MPG his calibre expects. Morale in the 80s costs him 1 point on every grade. Three games left won't move his season average enough to recover him — the fix is a real audition at camp, not a late-season line shuffle.

**Upshall** at 89 is one point into the 80s band. Same structural issue as Spezza (minutes collapsed from 13 to 8 over the season), same answer: not recoverable in three games. The -1 penalty is marginal.

**Jackman** at 99 on 29.7 MPG is carrying the heaviest load in the league and doesn't care. His production is the problem (0.48 pts/g), not his happiness. That's a role conversation for the offseason, not a morale one.

Everyone else — Mogilny at 18.5 on L2, Richards at 16.3 on L3, Abid at 13.9 on L4 — is where morale should be given the results. No changes.

## Role composition

Is each of our units built from the players who fit it, and do we have the bodies to fix the units that aren't, before Friday in New Jersey.

**K2** is our checking unit and it is built right: 84 mean checking, the best of any kill or checking group in the room, with McCabe at 84 and Jackman at 90 on the back end, Chlup at 80 on the draw and Abid adding 72 toughness. No change.

**K1** runs 78 mean checking behind Sundin at 91 in the circle and Fischer at 84, and that is the correct partner for the top kill. No change.

**P1** has its shooter. Gaborik is 98 scoring and 99 playmaking, Sundin is 93 and 92 feeding him, Jackman and Kaberle at the points. **P2** has Mogilny at 94 and Richards at 97 clutch. Both units fit their job.

**L4** is the one unit whose role does not match its grades: 52 mean faceoffs, 54 best. That is Abid, Spezza, Upshall. No man on the bench fixes it. The next-best draw man is Richards at 75 and he anchors L3. This is a roster fact, not an arrangement I can make, and it is the price of the development line.

**Checking forwards** is the gap I would put in front of you. Roberts at 84 is the only forward in our top four checkers. Jackman at 90, McCabe at 84 and Fischer at 84 are all defencemen. A three-forward checking line at 80+ cannot be built from this roster in any arrangement, so our checking identity leans on the blue line and the kill. That is offseason work.

## Opponent matchup

The question for Friday: we beat NJ three times this season, 19-2 on the scoresheet, and Afinogenov is out. The only real decision is who fills his left-wing slot on the second line, and whether we touch anything else against a team whose power play converts at 11% and whose defence drops to 68, 66, 66 below their first pair.

**Abid** moves up from the fourth line to left wing on the second. He carried 0.84 pts/g this season and at 80 OVR with CHKG 86 he can play against Elias's line (86 OVR, PASS 90, DEKG 89) without being a defensive liability. Mogilny at 89 and Chlup at 85 already form the most skilled right-side duo we have outside Sundin; putting Abid there gives us a genuine three-forward attack against NJ's best pair of White (75) and Brown (68).

**NJ's third and fourth lines** are Guolla at 75 and Darby at 73 with Rasmussen/Gionta and Berglund/Brylin. Their D on those pairings is Strudwick (66) and Cullen (66). Our L4 without Abid loses its best player, but against OVR-73 centres and 66-rated defencemen, a line of Spezza/Upshall plus whoever fills in will not be the difference.

**Brodeur** at 92 is the only reason this game is not a coronation. His morale is 82 (costs 1 point on his overall), but 92 is still 92. We need Belfour if his fatigue icon is clear, per the standing order from January 19. Ouellet at 82 against Brodeur at 92 is a 10-point gap on the most important position on the ice.

**No line shuffling.** We're 3-0 with a 19-2 goal differential. Their PP is 27-for-245 (11.0%). Our first line auto-pairs against their first line (Gomez 82, Friesen 85, Langenbrunner 86) and wins that matchup on paper: Sundin 90, Gaborik 97, Roberts 87 against Rafalski 80 and Kubina 78. Leave it alone.

## Owed

Standing order #1: defencemen evaluation and sell-list update for season's end. Season is 3 games from over (79 of 82 played). Numbers are locking.

**McCabe** at 59 points in 79 games is 0.75 pts/g on 22.3 MPG, age 29, $3.00M x 4 years. He drifted from 0.79 at 75 games to 0.75 now. The season is essentially done at that rate. He's a keep — a top-pairing quarterback at 29 in his prime earning window.

**Kaberle** at 43 points in 71 games is 0.61 pts/g on 20.9 MPG, age 27, $1.90M x 1 expiring. The GM called him a star and a keeper on January 15. No change to that. The renewal conversation is the GM's job but the number is good enough to get paid.

**Fischer** at 38 points in 74 games is 0.51 pts/g on 22.1 MPG, age 24, $3.70M x 4. Off the table per the GM's emphatic call. No change.

**Jackman** at 37 points in 77 games is 0.48 pts/g on 29.7 MPG, age 24, $0.70M x 3. Same as my last report: the load kills his production. Sell at offseason. The price is absurd — three years at $0.70M for a 24-year-old top-pairing defenceman is the best value on the roster. No change since March 23, still a sell.

**Klesla** at 30 points in 79 games is 0.38 pts/g on 14.9 MPG, age 23, $0.90M x 2. Two consecutive declining seasons locked. No change. Sell.

**Eminger** is the one who moved. He was at 0.44 in late February; he's now at 23 points in 61 games, which is 0.38 pts/g on 15.8 MPG. Age 21, $1.20M x 1 expiring. He's been bleeding points all month. He was already on the sell list — this makes it more urgent. If he goes to UFA, we lose him for nothing and get nothing back. Trade before July.

**Colaiacovo** at 12 points in 31 games (0.39 on 17.9 MPG, $1.10M x 1 expiring) is not dressing. Let him walk or trade him as filler. No roster contribution this year.

Nothing else has shifted. The sell list is Jackman, Klesla, Eminger, Colaiacovo. The keep list is McCabe, Kaberle, Fischer. No new injuries or surprises.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-25
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-25

Toronto 55-12-4, 124 pts after 76 games.

## Role coverage

**Role coverage determines what the playoff roster can handle and what July must fix.** Toronto are 124 points and dominant, but the grade sheet shows two holes no coach can scheme around and one thinning area that becomes a gap next year.

**Toughness is the structural hole.** Zero players carry 80+ TOUG in stored grades. Jackman tops out at 75, Roberts at 73. Tucker at 70 is not the fix the December note suggested (that was a form-inflated reading). No combination of line changes creates toughness the roster doesn't have. This is an acquisition problem for July, not a coach problem for tonight.

**Faceoffs are equally thin.** Only Sundin at 90 clears 80. Richards at 70, Chlup at 75, Tucker at 67. The coach is right that L4 has no answer (best is 53). This forces top-six defensive-zone starts all season, which the coach flagged and the grades confirm. Avery from LA closes both gaps in one move (93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, $400K, 2 years), and remains the only known single transaction that solves two structural problems.

**Checking is adequate tonight but drops to four next year.** Six at 80+ now: Jackman 87, Roberts 86, McCabe 86, Tucker 83, Fischer 82, Upshall 80. Roberts walks in July, and Mogilny's departure removes his 88 CHKG contribution from forward checks. That leaves Jackman, McCabe, Tucker, Fischer, Upshall. Five is survivable but tight for a playoff run with injuries.

**Scoring looks deep but is aging in two spots.** Ten at 80+ overall, but Mogilny at 36 is at 0.79 pts/g (down from 1.62) and Roberts at 38 walks. Next year the top-end scoring rests on Gaborik 92, Sundin 92, Afinogenov 90, Abid 86, plus whoever replaces the Mogilny wing. Heatley or Doan remain the July priority the March 23 note locked.

**Durability is thin and gets thinner.** Only Roberts 98, Afinogenov 95, Fischer 92, Abid 90 clear 80. Roberts is 38 and leaving. That's three next season. A long playoff run with one injury to Abid or Fischer at 25-26 and no depth behind them would be a problem.

**Three unlined bodies are coach-fixable.** Koltsov at 92 speed, 23, not lined. Spacek at 84 playmaking, 19, not lined. Tucker at 83 CHKG, 30, not lined. Dressing them for the final six games gives the coach playoff options at zero cost.

## Trajectory

This roster is not aging into a cliff — it is walking into one if the GM cannot get through thirteen renewals in one July.

**The age curve is healthy.** Twenty-five of thirty players are 29 or under. The four veterans (Sundin 34, Mogilny 36, Belfour 39, Roberts 38) are either expiring or on two years left, so the club naturally sheds them. The ≤23 group holds 14 players including six carrying POTE 95 or above. This is the shape the manual asks for, and it arrived without a rebuild.

**The contract cluster is the problem, not the age curve.** Thirteen contracts worth $21.30M expire this July. That is 43% of total payroll ($60.04M) up for negotiation in one window. Two of them — Belfour ($6.50M) and Roberts ($2.70M) — should walk, saving $9.20M. That leaves eleven players at $12.10M who need re-signing, and most of them just broke out at prices set when they were unknowns.

**Gaborik** is the first call. 91 points in 76 games at 23, 91 base, on $1.10M. He will command a star's salary. A 5-6 year deal protects four or five of his prime years; a shorter deal pushes the same problem to a summer where you also face Chlup's renewal.

**Richards** at 64 points, 24, $1.00M is the second call. Same logic. He is the club's best remaining centre after Sundin ages out.

**Nash, Eminger, Kaberle, and Abid** follow. Nash at 20 with 35 points and POTE 95 is the cheapest star-quality asset in the building; locking him on a long deal is the highest-leverage move of the summer. Eminger at 21 with POTE 99 on $1.20M needs the same treatment. Kaberle at 27 entering his prime (41 points, rising minutes) gets 3-4 years. Abid went from $0.40M to 66 points at 25 — the raise will be steep but he is still cheap compared to what a 66-point wing costs.

**The second wave** — Chistov, Colaiacovo, Alexeev, Upshall, Tellqvist — should go on 2-3 year deals. That splits the renewal burden: stars locked in July 2005, depth up again in July 2007 or 2008 instead of 2006. If the GM signs depth to two-year deals today, the July 2006 summer brings up the 2-year group (Chlup, Luongo, Koltsov, Spezza, Ouellet, Klesla, St. Jacques, Tucker) plus those depth players, creating a second cluster.

**Chlup's renewal in July 2006 is the next bomb.** He is on 2 years at $2.34M with POTE 95 and 0.84 points per game at 19. By next July he will be 20 and possibly a first-line centre. At that point he commands $5-7M. The 2-3 year split strategy means he is the top priority of the 2006 summer, which is fine as long as the 2005 cluster is cleared.

**Fischer** at $3.70M on four more years with 0.41 points per game is the payroll anchor nobody wants to carry. He is 24, so there is time, but he is a 2009 problem unless he rebounds.

**Money is not the constraint yet.** Revenue is $91.71M against a $60.04M payroll, leaving $24.39M profit. Even after significant raises for the core — perhaps $15-20M net after losing Belfour and Roberts — payroll lands in the $65-75M range. Profitable, but thinner. The club is one bad year from a payroll that outgrows revenue, especially with ticket price already at $97.

**Draft capital is empty.** One fourth-rounder from Toronto. No ammunition for trades. Every acquisition must be player-for-player, which means the GM's leverage in July depends entirely on which players he is willing to lose as UFAs.

**The three moves that protect 2006-2008:**
1. Re-sign Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger to 5-6 years in July 2005. This locks the core's prime.
2. Re-sign Kaberle and Abid on 3-4 years. They are entering prime but carry more risk than the kids.
3. Put Chistov, Colaiacovo, Alexeev, Upshall, and Tellqvist on 2-3 year deals so their renewals land in 2007-08, not alongside Chlup's star renewal in 2006.

Task #2 (monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro development through February) is complete. Luongo arrived on roster in early February at 91 base with 2 years at $1.60M. DiPietro was eliminated on March 14 at 79 base with a 3.64 GAA. The goalie situation is solved as the GM ordered on March 19.

## Calendar

The deadline passed six days ago and the season has 6 games left, so the calendar question is no longer buyers or sellers. It is: what does this roster look like in July, and 13 contracts worth $22.30M expire simultaneously. That is the largest single summer decision this franchise has faced.

**Gaborik** is the priority and nothing else comes close. 91 base, 23, 87 points, $1.10M on an expiring deal. He's the youngest player on the roster carrying a top-line overall and he will get outbidded in July if we don't lock him on 5 or 6 years immediately. Everything else in this summer plan bends around whether he stays.

**Richards** follows at 82 base, 24, 64 points, $1.00M. Same shape as Gaborik: cheap, young, productive, expiring. Five or six years, before the July market reprices him.

**Kaberle** at 84 base, 27, $1.90M, is entering his prime: 0.54 to 0.63 pts/g with minutes climbing from 19.4 to 21.9. Five or six years. The coach named him the top-pair quarterback for next year and the numbers support it.

**Eminger** at 76 base, 21, $1.20M, carries the POTE 99 that the GM has protected all season. He's a project, not a product, but the ceiling argument holds. Lock on 5 years at a number that won't blow up later.

**Nash** at 77 base, 20, $1.20M, rounds out the five lock list. Young, cheap, on the first line, and he's two years younger than most players on this roster. Five years.

**Abid** at 79 base, 25, $0.40M, is the cheapest toughness on the roster (80 CHKG, 80 TOUG). Two years at a modest bump. He gives the bottom six a physical element we don't otherwise have.

**Tellqvist** at 77 base, 25, $0.80M, stays per the January order. Two years, development time, no money saved.

**Chistov, Colaiacovo, Alexeev** are depth at 78, 72 and 76 base respectively, all $1.10M. Chistov at 21 is the one worth keeping on two or three years for a bottom-six role. Colaiacovo at 72 on a second-pairing D is thin. Alexeev at 76 at 23 is replaceable. I would renew Chistov, let the other two test the market, and bring one back cheap if nobody bids.

**Belfour** is the one the GM wants to keep but probably can't. 92 base, 39, $6.50M. Offer two years at $3.5–4.0M. If he refuses, he walks and the payroll drops $6.50M. That money pays for a Heatley or Doan acquisition and still leaves room. The March 19 order keeps him for the playoffs; after that it's his decision.

**Roberts** at 87 base, 38, $2.70M walks. The March 21 renewal note already set that. No two-year deal to an 87-base forward turning 39.

**Upshall** is a wasted year and should go. Minutes collapsed from 13.4 to 5.1 MPG at 21 with 0.30 pts/g production. No POTE on record. Try the over-80 pick mechanic first — his base overall is 78, so it won't work. Trade him as a depth piece for a late-rounder or let him walk. He's $1.20M better spent on someone who plays.

The RW hole is the summer's structural problem. Mogilny fell from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g at 36 and carries $5.50M with 2 years left. Gaborik covers one wing; we need a second top-nine RW. Heatley (91 base, 24) or Doan are the profile, but we hold only our own fifth-round pick. A package has to start with Mogilny's contract or another salary dump. The GM should test ATL's summer posture on Heatley once the season ends; ATL sit 7th in the East at 81 points and may be sellers again.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: who across the league fills Toronto's two structural holes (toughness and faceoffs) and replaces Mogilny at right wing, and why would their clubs let them go? The answer splits into July UFA signings and offseason trades, because the GM closed the deadline window on March 19.

**Heatley** (ATL, RW, 91 base, POTE 86, 120 points in 71 games, $1.10M expiring) is the single best fit. He is 24, plays the exact position Mogilny leaves empty, and ATL at 81 points with 11 expiring cannot re-sign both him and Kovalchuk (89 base, 130 points). ATL keeps Kovalchuk on production, Heatley walks in July for nothing unless they trade him. Toronto's payroll at $60.04M against $91.71M revenue absorbs a $5-6M raise. The cost is draft capital Toronto doesn't have (one 4th-rounder), so the move requires either his walk to UFA or the GM's negotiation leverage to find a third party.

**Iginla** (CGY, RW, 93 base, POTE 79, 112 points in 69 games, $6.50M expiring) is the highest-rated RW in the league. CGY at 60 points is the second-worst team, carrying $45.93M payroll against only $12.21M profit with 10 expiring deals. They MUST move him rather than lose $6.50M of salary on the best RW available for nothing. At 27 he has four prime years left. The obstacle is his current salary: re-signing him at $7-8M for 5 years consumes 12-13% of projected revenue. Toronto can do it, but it makes the Gaborik and Richards renewals tighter.

**Gagne** (PHI, LW, 86 base, POTE 81, 98 points in 74 games, $2.40M, 0 years left = UFA this July) is the best value if he hits the market. PHI at 71 points with $66.73M payroll and only $3.38M profit cannot re-sign 13 expiring players. He plays left wing, not right, but his 86 base and 98 points make him a top-nine winger on any line. A July UFA signing costs no trade assets.

**Marleau** (SJ, C, 89 base, POTE 81, 98 points in 71 games, $1.60M, 0 years left = UFA this July) is a center who could slide to right wing. SJ at 68 points with 13 expiring and $19.95M profit are rebuilding, not desperate. They might re-sign him at $1.60M. Less likely to hit UFA than Gagne, but if he does, 89 base at 25 is the second-best available player.

**Bell** (CHI, C, 24, 80 base, POTE unlisted, 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 87 FACE, $900K, 2 years left) remains the only known player closing toughness, checking, and faceoffs simultaneously on a long deal. CHI at 69 points with $28.03M profit don't need to sell, but at 69 points with 10 expiring they're rebuilding and Bell is expendable. The Jan 25 proposed price (R2 plus Colaiacovo) is the template. He's a re-signable deal with 2 years remaining, not a rental.

**Avery** (LA, C, 25, 79 base, 83 TOUG, 94 FACE, 9 pts in 75 GP, $400K, 2 years) closes the same two gaps as Bell at half the salary. His production is the problem: 0.12 points per game is fourth-line offence. The Feb 16 note deprioritized him below Bell on production. LA at 71 points with 14 expiring are willing sellers. He's a bottom-six role player with elite grades.

**Cammalleri and Frolov** (LA, both 22, $1.10M expiring each, POTE 98 and 96, 52 and 50 points respectively) are the long-term top-six development play. LA at 71 points with 14 expiring cannot keep both at star salaries. Acquiring both fills top-six wing for five years on development contracts. The risk is they both bust (Brad Isbister precedent), but 52 and 50 points at 22 with POTE 98/96 is the strongest development case on this list.

**Samsonov** (BOS, LW, 26, 89 base, 112 points in 64 GP, $1.90M expiring) is elite production but BOS at 91 points are a contender with $27.92M profit and 13 expiring. They can keep him. Only available if BOS decides to rebuild, which 91 points and 2nd-from-last year doesn't suggest. Lower probability than anyone above him.

**What I would NOT pursue:** Conroy (CGY, 33) is a rental that doesn't improve the roster in year three. Reid (STL, POTE 94) is interesting but at 77 base and 56 points he's not clearly better than what Toronto develops internally (Abid already at 66 points at 25). The deadline is closed per the GM's March 19 order.

## Trade construction

This phase answers what Toronto trades in July to fill the Mogilny void and the structural toughness/faceoff holes, given one fourth-rounder and a March 19 order that closed the deadline window. Three proposals, ranked. All are July operations; the deadline is past.

**Proposal 1 — Heatley from ATL.** Tucker ($1.30M, 30, 2 years, 1 point in 3 games, 92 CHKG) plus the 4th-rounder for Dany Heatley (ATL, RW, 24, 91 base, 120 points in 71 games, $1.10M expiring). ATL at 81 points with 11 expiring cannot keep both Heatley and Kovalchuk (89 base, 130 points). They keep Kovalchuk on production, and Heatley walks for nothing unless traded. Getting a 92 CHKG physical wing on a 2-year deal plus any pick is better than $0. For Toronto, this replaces Mogilny's 0.79 pts/g at 36 with a 24-year-old 91-base RW. Payroll moves from Tucker's $1.30M to Heatley's $1.10M on arrival, then rises at renewal to roughly $5-6M for 5 years, replacing Mogilny's $5.50M for 2 years. Net effect over the contract life is roughly break-even with four more productive years. If ATL demands more, **Upshall** (POTE 99, 87 CHKG, $1.20M, 1 year) goes into the package; his minutes collapsed from 13.4 to 5.1 MPG and the coach called it "a wasted year."

**Proposal 2 — Avery from LA.** Koltsov (23, POTE 94, 96 ACCE, $1.10M, 2 years, 18 points in 35 games, not lined) for Steve Avery (LA, C, 25, 83 TOUG, 94 FACE, 88 CHKG, $400K, 2 years). LA at 71 points with 14 expiring are rebuilding. Avery produces 0.12 points per game; they replace him with a POTE 94 winger with 96 acceleration. For Toronto, this is the single move that closes both structural gaps. Zero players carry 80+ TOUG in stored grades. Only Sundin at 90 clears 80 FACE. Avery covers both at $400K for two years. Koltsov carries no line assignment and has never played a full season; the roster has Chlup, Richards, and Spacek ahead of him. The Feb 21 note killed Avery on production, but that kill assumed we could solve toughness internally. The March 19 role coverage proved we cannot.

**Proposal 3 — Mogilny dump via the over-80 mechanic.** Mogilny (36, $5.50M, 2 years left, 78 points in 72 games, ACCU 95, PASS 94, AGIL 95) for a late-round pick. His grades still clear 80 overall. We do not intend to re-sign him. The mechanic trades any 80+ player the club won't keep for a pick. A contender needing a top-nine RW with elite hands and passing for 2 years at $5.50M takes the contract. Toronto clears $5.50M and restocks draft capital from the current total of one 4th-rounder. Risk: the AI may not price him as the mechanic implies, and 0.79 pts/g at 36 deters most GMs. Worth one offer.

**If none land.** Heatley walks as UFA. Sign him in July (costs no trade assets, only the raise). If ATL signs him elsewhere, pivot to Gagne (PHI, 86 base, 98 points, UFA July) or Marleau (SJ, 89 base, 98 points, UFA July) as free-agent signings. The toughness and faceoff gaps persist if Avery or Bell don't come; Bell (CHI, 80 base, 95 TOUG, 87 FACE, $900K, 2 years) is the better version of Avery but CHI at $28.03M profit are less desperate. Test Bell with Koltsov plus the 4th if ATL blocks the Heatley package and LA refuses Avery.

## Owed

**#2 — Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window.**

This task is closed on two counts, and I'm marking it delivered.

**Luongo** is on our roster: 25 years old, 93 overall, $1.60M, 2 years left, 42 GP this season. He was the target this task was monitoring, and he's now in Toronto. The GM's March 19 standing order closed all goalie monitoring explicitly: "Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks."

**DiPietro** was permanently eliminated from the target list on 2005-03-14. At 52 GP he still reads 79 base overall, 3.64 GAA, 84.9% save percentage. The January 15 order called for a high-90s goalie from a non-contender; 79 base is 11+ points short and no further sample size closes that gap.

What changed since the task was opened: the problem solved itself. Luongo arrived, DiPietro failed the threshold, and the GM closed the file. No further work owed here.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-25

# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-25

Next game at CAR on Friday 25 March 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether the young guys are getting games that match what they've earned. With six games left and tonight a road game at a .540 club, the answer for tonight is simple: go all out, develop later. But the season-end read on the young group is due.

**Spezza** remains the loudest unresolved case. POTE 99, age 21, 40 games at 7.0 MPG on the fourth line, 15 points. I have raised this five times. His morale sits at 89, the lowest among dressed players. At 21 he needs 15+ minutes in a top-nine role to grow into whatever that scouting number means. This season is effectively decided for him, but next year's camp assignment is now urgent — he cannot come back to the fourth line again.

**Stahle** barely touched the ice: 4 games all year at 20 with POTE 96. His development year is gone. That is not a criticism of the current blue line — Klesla and Eminger are earning their minutes — but the club invested a high pick in him and got four games of film back. Offseason: either trade him for a forward asset or commit to a top-pair audition in camp. Another year of 4 GP is a waste of both his time and a roster spot.

**Spacek** at 19, 50 games, 7.6 MPG, 17 points, morale 89. He's on the fringe. The 12-MPG bump didn't stick — he fell back to 7.6 season average. At POTE 91 he's a fringe centre who gets enough games to watch but not enough to grow. The offseason call is whether he's a seventh or eighth forward or whether his ice time goes to someone else.

**Chlup** is exactly where he should be: 65 games, 16.8 MPG on the second line, 54 points at 19. He earned it and got it. No change.

**Gaborik**, 76 games, 20.4 MPG, 91 points at 23. First line, every night, no conversation needed.

**Nash** at 20 with 35 points on 12.8 MPG looks like a third-liner earning his role. His rate is down from October but he's still productive for his minutes and his morale is 99. System-fit review in the offseason, not a concern now.

**Chistov** (13.3 MPG, 20 pts at 21) and **Upshall** (8.2 MPG, 19 pts at 21) are deployed for what they currently are: a third-line winger and a fourth-liner. No complaints.

**Colaiacovo** at 22, 31 games at 17.9 MPG when dressed, POTE 99, morale 99. The GM's development rotation. Reasonable.

**Klesla** is a sell, not a development case. The GM already agreed.

## Development trends

The question this phase answers: who on this roster is getting better, who is getting worse, and what should the GM start planning around before the season ends. With six games left, this is the last window to adjust before we walk into the offseason.

**Chlup** is the one clear riser. 0.62→0.88 pts/g while his minutes went from 11.0 to 18.2 at age 19. A young player increasing his load and his rate simultaneously is rare and we should protect it. He belongs in the top nine permanently and deserves consideration for a top-six spot next year. No change needed now — he is already there.

**Kaberle** is the surprise riser among veterans. 0.54→0.64 pts/g on minutes up from 19.4 to 21.9. At 27 his prime is arriving, not departing. The GM called him a star and the trend line backs it. Nothing to change, but this is the player to build the blue line around next season.

**Spezza** is the development emergency. 0.43→0.32 pts/g on minutes collapsed from 9.1 to 4.8 at age 21. He is dressed for 40 games and playing five a night. I have raised this five times since January with no movement. The year is done for him at this rate. If the GM wants any return on his potential, he needs a real role next training camp or we are wasting another year.

**Upshall** has the same problem at 21. 0.33→0.29 pts/g on minutes down from 13.4 to 4.9. He went from a rotational winger to a healthy scratch who occasionally dresses. No grade moved on his card either. Same offseason conversation as Spezza: give him a real look in camp or accept he is not part of the plan.

**Spacek** at 19 is buried at 5.2 MPG down from 16.0, rate halved to 0.28. His year is dead. Judge next year's decision on whether we dress him at all, not on this one.

**Nash** at 20 went 0.83→0.38 with minutes flat at 12.7. The role did not change, the production did. This is a system-fit question for the offseason: does he fit a top-six role at 21, or is he a third-liner who had a hot start? I would give him a full top-six audition in camp before writing him off.

**Afinogenov** at 25 dropped from 1.17→0.75 with flat minutes. That is a real decline at an age where the expected direction is stable or up. Not a crisis, but worth watching — if next season starts at 0.60 we have a role problem.

**Gaborik** appears to be declining at 1.42→1.10 but that is regression from an unsustainable start, not collapse. At 23, 1.10 pts/g on 21.1 MPG is elite. No concern.

**Richards** at 1.08→0.76 follows the same pattern. Still very good for a 24-year-old second-line centre. The early pace was the anomaly.

**Mogilny** at 36 went 1.62→0.81 with minutes up from 16.9 to 19.3. Age-appropriate decline. Plan around him not being here next year, or at least not playing 19 a night.

**Roberts** at 38 dropped 1.29→0.88 on minutes up from 16.5 to 21.3. The fact that he is still producing at 0.88 at 38 is remarkable, but the direction is down and he is 38. Plan around this being his last year.

**Sundin** at 34 went 1.46→1.00 on minutes up from 16.9 to 21.7. For a 34-year-old centre carrying 22 minutes, 1.00 is respectable. He is holding up. No action needed.

**McCabe** at 29 went 1.42→0.48. The early-season pace was never real. He has settled around 0.48 which is second-pair offence. He is off the sell list but he is not a top-pair producer and the GM should stop expecting him to be one.

**Fischer** at 24 is 0.63→0.48 with minutes up from 20.8 to 22.4. He is absorbing more load while his offense dips. The GM declared him a keeper and I accept that. His two-way game is the value here, not the offense. Flag for monitoring but no action.

No player card grades moved in this window for anyone. All evidence above is production and ice time.

## Morale watch

The room is fine. Morale runs 89 to 99, average 92, and the only sub-90 man is **Spezza** at 89, a 21-year-old center on the fourth line at 7.0 MPG — exactly where the depth band puts him. No intervention needed or possible.

**Mogilny, Richards, Afinogenov, Chlup** all sit at 96, each down 2 to 4 from the last save but recovering. Mogilny at 36 is producing 78 points in 72 games on 18.5 MPG. Richards has 64 points in 74 on 16.4 MPG. Both are slightly under the 17-minute band a player at that output expects, but the dip is small and the room is winning. I would not touch the lines to chase 30 seconds a night of morale recovery with six games left.

**Jackman** at 29.8 MPG and 99 morale is the outlier load. He has been at nearly 30 for the season and his morale has not cracked, but the production problem (0.48 pts/g on that ice time) is the concern, not his feelings. Nothing to fix in morale terms tonight.

**Abid** remains the structural mismatch: 66 points in 76 games on 14.2 MPG, parked on L4. Morale is 99 and climbing. No crisis tonight, but the GM knows this role is wrong for next year.

No change. The lines are right for a game at Carolina.

## Role composition

The question is whether each unit is built from players who suit its job, and whether the roster holds enough bodies in each role. The answer is mostly yes, with one known void and one structural characteristic worth naming.

**L1** is the best-constructed unit on the roster. Jackman at 88 checking and 76 toughness gives the top line real two-way teeth, Sundin at 89 wins draws, and Gaborik at 97 scoring / 99 speed carries the offense. Nothing to change here.

**L2** is the softest unit by design. Checking mean 68, toughness mean 63. McCabe at 82 is the only real checker. Chlup at 78 faceoffs is the draw man. Mogilny and Afinogenov at 92 and 90 scoring are there to outscore, not to defend. That's acceptable for a second line if we get offensive-zone starts, but it means the game auto-pairing matters: L2 paired against an opponent's top line will be exposed. No bench move fixes this, it's the personnel we have.

**L3** is the checking line and it works. Nash at 92 checking and 92 toughness anchors it, Richards at 73 wins draws, and Chistov at 96 scoring / 97 speed means we can also generate offense from the third unit. This is the most complete line after L1.

**L4** has two problems. The faceoff void is confirmed: mean 51, best 52. Richards at 73 is the nearest fix and he's already on L3. This is a roster gap I've flagged before and no arrangement solves it. Separately, stamina mean is 55, the lowest number anywhere on the sheet. That line cannot take extended shifts late in games. Keep their minutes tight.

**Power play units** are correct. P1 has Gaborik, Sundin, Jackman — the best skill available. P2 has Mogilny at 92 scoring and Chlup for two-way balance. No issues.

**Penalty kill** deployment is sound. K2 carries checking mean 82 (Jackman 88, McCabe 82, Chlup) while K1 runs 76. Our better killers are on the second unit, which is fine because Kaberle and Fischer on K1 are the right D for a possession-style kill. No swap needed.

**Roster-level gaps:** No true enforcer. Highest toughness on the roster is Jackman at 76. We're a skilled team without a goon. The L4 faceoff void persists. Both are roster problems, not lineup problems.

## Opponent matchup

**What matters tonight:** We're 1-2 against Carolina this year. They've given us trouble all season. But we're on a 10-game win streak scoring 4.5 a night against 1.6, and we have every quality player in the lineup already. No development scratch applies here.

**CAR's structure.** They're a checking team. Hill CHKG 89, Markov CHKG 89, Hedican CHKG 85, Dandenault CHKG 83 up the middle. Four defencemen who hit. They're old and methodical: Ozolinsh 32, Hill 35, Brind'Amour 34, Hedican 34, Wesley 36. Their top six averages 31. Their bottom six averages 26. We're faster everywhere, especially our first three lines.

**Ozolinsh** at 86 OVR is their best skater. SHPW 93, DEKG 91, ENDU 99 at age 32. He's their offence from the point. Fischer (SPEE 92, CHKG 89) and Jackman (SPEE 92, CHKG 89) are our first pair and auto-pair with our first line. That's already the right match. Speed beats skill here.

**Rucchin** at FACE 90 wins the draw against Sundin at 89. Brind'Amour at 86 beats Chlup at 78. We lose both top-center faceoffs tonight. That's structural and known; it means expect IC zone starts on those matchups. No lineup fix, just awareness.

**Their power play** is 16.6% (34/205). Their penalty kill faces 3.3 chances per game. They're on the ice short constantly. Our PP is 35.7% (30/84). If we draw three or four penalties like we usually do against them, we score two or three power-play goals. That's the game.

**Weekes** at 90 is their goalie. Good, not great. Belfour at 92 with ENDU 86. No fatigue icon on Belfour in the brief, so start him per the standing order and confirm the icon on screen.

**No change.** Lines are already set with our best. D slot order is correct (strongest pair vs strongest pair). The season series is a warning but this team is old, slow, and penalized often. We're the better club and we look like it every night.

**D review for sell order:** Jackman OVR 84 today but ENDU 71, season 0.48 pts/g on 30 MPG. Still the sell at top-pair minutes. Eminger OVR 75, ENDU 50, season 0.44. Still the cheapest cut. Klesla OVR 82 today, ENDU 55, season 0.36. Still declining, still a sell. McCabe OVR 82, holding steady, off the list. Fischer and Kaberle keepers. Sell order unchanged: Eminger, Klesla, Jackman.

## Owed

**Item #1: Defenceman sell list update.** Nothing has moved since March 23. The sell order holds: Jackman, Klesla, Eminger.

**McCabe** at 76 GP, 0.79 pts/g on 22.3 MPG. One more game played since last check, rate unchanged. He stays. The 0.49 recent window I flagged is the tail of a normal season, not a collapse.

**Jackman** at 74 GP, 0.50 pts/g on 29.8 MPG. Was 0.48 last week, now 0.50 from a point in his one new game. Still a sell. $0.70M x 3 with the cheapest top-pair minutes in the league. His production rate has been flat at roughly 0.50 all season on an unsustainable load.

**Klesla** at 76 GP, 0.36 pts/g on flat 15 MPG. He hasn't played since March 23. Two consecutive declining seasons confirmed. Sell at $0.90M x 2.

**Eminger** at 58 GP, 0.38 pts/g on 15.9 MPG. Season rate drifted from 0.44 (Feb 19) to 0.38 now. He's still on the sell list at an expiring $1.2M. His recent form never recovered from the February dip.

**Fischer** and **Kaberle** are keepers per your standing orders. No argument to re-open.

**Colaiacovo** at 31 GP, 0.39 pts/g on 17.9 MPG. Not dressed since March. Development rotation only.

The sell order is unchanged: Jackman first (highest value to recoup while the minutes number looks impressive), then Eminger (expiring, will hit UFA cheap), then Klesla (still two years, so there's a little more time to wait for a better price).

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-23
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-23

Toronto 54-12-4, 122 pts after 75 games.

## Role coverage

The trade deadline has passed; at 54-12-4, 122 points with 7 games left, this phase is about playoff readiness and off-season gaps. Toronto is covered everywhere that matters for a Cup run and thin in three places that will bite next season.

**Toughness** is the confirmed structural hole: zero players at 80+ TOUG in stored grades. Jackman's 75 is the roster's ceiling, Tucker's 70 is second. The Feb 24 contradiction was resolved March 19: the gap is real and has always been real. The GM's March 19 order closed the door on fixing it before the playoffs, and at 54 wins it hasn't stopped us. Avery (LA, 25, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 93 FACE, $400K, 2 years) remains the cheapest single fix and is a July trade target now, not a deadline one.

**Faceoffs** have one solution: Sundin at 90. Chlup is 75 at 19 and will grow; Richards is 70. The coach's L4 problem (best on the line: 53) is real but unsolvable before the postseason and largely solved by Avery's 93 FACE if that deal lands in July. Chlup at 75 and improving makes this self-healing by 2007.

**Right wing scoring** is the next-year crisis. Mogilny at 36 has fallen from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g. Roberts at 38 is expiring and the standing order says he walks. That removes 1.62 + whatever Roberts produces from the top six. Marleau (SJ, 25, 89 base, 98 pts) and Gagné (PHI, 25, 86 base, 94 pts) are July UFA targets per the March 16 note. One of them must land.

**Checking** is covered for tonight: Jackman 87, Roberts 86, McCabe 86, Tucker 83, Fischer 82, Upshall 80. Six men at 80+ is enough. If Roberts walks, five remain, and Jackman at 24 and McCabe at 29 carry it. No urgency here.

**Durability** is thin at 4 players (Roberts 98, Afinogenov 95, Fischer 92, Abid 90). Roberts at 38 is the anchor and he is leaving. For a playoff run this is a risk, not a roster fix. The 7 remaining games will tell us who can hold up.

**Goalies** are solved per the GM's March 19 standing order: Luongo (25, 88.4 SV, 2y) and Belfour (39, 92.9 SV, 1y) are the two 90+ men. The owed monitoring task (Luongo availability, DiPietro ice time) is complete — Luongo was acquired Feb 7, DiPietro was eliminated March 14 at 79 base with a grade deficit no sample size closes.

## Trajectory

The question this phase answers is whether Toronto is building into a financial or age cliff, and the answer is no on age but yes on contract timing. The roster is young (25 of 30 players are 29 or under), profit runs $23.45M, and the danger is that 13 contracts worth $21.30M all expire in the same July while one aging star is locked to five more years at $8.40M.

**Sundin** is the structural problem nobody can solve this season. He's 34, $8.40M, five years left, POTE 60, producing 86 points on 75 games. That salary is 14% of payroll on a player whose grades are set and only decline from here. By 2009 he's 38 on this contract. There is no trade for a 34-year-old with five years and $8.40M remaining. The only protection is that Chlup (19, POTE 95) and Spezza (21, POTE 99) are ready to absorb his minutes by 2007-08, which is a development timeline, not a front-office move.

**The July 2005 cluster is the decision that matters most.** 13 contracts, $21.30M. Of those, seven are young core who must be locked on 5-6 year deals: Gaborik ($1.10M, 90 pts, age 23), Richards ($1.00M, 64 pts, age 24), Nash ($1.20M, 35 pts, age 20), Eminger ($1.20M, POTE 99, age 21), Kaberle ($1.90M, 40 pts, age 27 entering prime), Chistov ($1.10M, POTE 95, age 21), Abid ($0.40M, 66 pts, age 24). The two walk-ins who free money are Belfour ($6.50M, age 39) and Roberts ($2.70M, age 38), together $9.20M. That offset covers most of the raises needed for the young seven. The math works: $23.45M profit gives room, and the GM's standing renewal order (Gaborik first, Richards second, Nash and Eminger after) sequences it correctly.

**Chlup's deal expires July 2006** at $2.34M for two years. At 19 with 51 points on 64 games and POTE 95, this is the cheapest star on the roster. The mid-contract renegotiation rule means we cannot touch him until it expires, so the protection is purely budgetary: have $5-6M per season available next summer to lock him long-term before another breakout season makes him unaffordable.

**Fischer** is a 2008 problem, not a 2005 one. $3.70M for four years, age 24, production down to 0.41 pts/g. He's locked and untouchable until 2009. Nothing to do now except note it.

**Draft capital is nil.** One 4th-rounder, nothing earlier. Every package in the next three summers must be funded by players. This means the club cannot sell high for picks at the deadline (no picks to recover beyond the over-80 mechanic on Belfour/Roberts), and it means any future acquisition is a player-for-player swap. The guide's advice to "prefer potential over picks when scouting is upgraded" applies here in reverse: we have no picks, so we must hoard players with potential as trade currency.

**The age curve is healthy.** Four players at 34+ (Sundin, Mogilny, Roberts, Belfour), three of whom walk after this season or next. The gap at 30-33 (only Tucker, scratched) is not a hole; it's just the natural result of building young. The 24-29 group of 11 provides the bridge between the teenagers and Sundin's eventual replacement. The manual's target of 5-7 veterans and 20 young is met: we have roughly 5 veterans and 25 young, slightly more youth than the guide recommends, which is the correct direction.

## Calendar

The trade deadline passed four days ago on March 19, so every deadline question is closed. What matters now is July 2005, when all 13 expiring contracts hit the market simultaneously — a single-summer renewal event worth $22.10M in current salaries. The standing order from January 15 is clear: no contract can be renegotiated before it expires, so everything happens at once. The only levers are the order we sign them and the term we offer each.

**Gaborik** — 91 base, 23, 87 points, $1.10M expiring. He is the first call in July and he gets 5 or 6 years. His current salary is absurd for his production, and every other club's GM sees the same screen. Expect a raise into the $4–5M range on a 5-year deal. The cost is unavoidable; losing him is not an option.

**Richards** — 24, 64 points, $1.00M expiring. Second call. Same logic: a 24-year-old centre with 64 points at $1.00M is the most undervalued contract in the Eastern Conference. Lock him on 5–6 years before another club figures that out.

**Nash** — 20, $1.20M expiring. Third per the March 21 order. At 20 he is the cheapest upside on the roster. A 5-year deal at whatever his breakout season demands removes all risk of losing a generational-age player to a bidding war.

**Eminger** — 21, POTE 99, D, $1.20M. The GM's standing order from January 19 explicitly protects him over Chara. Same 5–6 year treatment. The potential is the reason, not tonight's point total.

**Kaberle** — 27, improving from 0.54 to 0.63 pts/g on 21.9 MPG. He is entering his prime, and the coach wants him as the top-pair quarterback next year. Four years, not six — his ceiling is approaching, but his current value is at its peak. A $1.90M expiring contract with this trajectory will command a raise, but the term should reflect that he will be 31 at expiry, not 33.

**Abid** — 24, $0.40M, TOUG 80, CHKG 80. The coach has flagged the structural toughness gap six times this season, and Abid is the only roster player who closes it. His morale is 99, which means he is happy for now, but a 40-cent contract for a top-nine power forward is another one-summer liability. Three years at $1.0–1.5M. The raise is cheap insurance against the one role gap the entire season has exposed.

**Upshall** — 78 base, POTE 99, but 19 points in 61 games on 8.3 MPG. The coach flagged this as a wasted year: minutes collapsed from 13.4 to 5.1. The potential is the reason to keep him, not the production. Two years at or near the current $1.20M. If he hasn't broken through by 23, he becomes deadline currency in 2006.

**Chistov** — 78 base / 81 shown, POTE 95, 98 SPEE, 20 points in 61 games. The speed grades are elite. Two years. Same develop-or-trade logic as Upshall, but his game (98 speed, 96 acceleration) projects better into an NHL role.

**Colaiacovo** — 72 base, POTE 99, but 31 games and ENDU 50. He is the rawest of the four depth prospects. Two years at $1.10M, and if endurance hasn't come up by next December, the POTE 99 is not enough to keep a 72-overall defenceman on a roster with Eminger and Kaberle already locked.

**Alexeev** — 76 base, POTE 94, 30 points in 55 games on 8.3 MPG. Best production-to-minutes of the depth four. Two years. He might outproduce Upshall and Chistov without their potential flags, which makes him the easiest renewal of the group.

**Tellqvist** — 25, POTE high 90s, $0.80M. Standing order from January 15: give him time to develop. Two years. Luongo is the starter; Tellqvist is the developmental backup whose potential justifies patience.

**Belfour** — 39, $6.50M, expiring. Walk. The GM concluded on January 15 that a reduced deal would not be accepted. March 19 closed the trade window. His value is now purely playoff insurance; after June he is gone and the $6.50M is freed.

**Roberts** — 38, $2.70M, expiring. Walk. Too old, too expensive, and the standing order from March 21 already says he leaves.

After the shuffle: Belfour and Roberts free $9.20M. The 11 we keep total $12.90M at current rates, but Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger, and Kaberle all need raises that could push the renewed group to $25–30M. The $9.20M savings from the two veterans who walk is the margin that makes this survivable.

## League scan

The question this phase answers is: with the deadline closed and the playoff run ahead, who across the league fills the three gaps that will define next season — right-wing scoring, toughness, and faceoffs — and what does their club's situation say about availability. The answer is that July has a better board than March did: ATL, PHX, LA and CGY all have motivated reasons to deal exactly the players we need, and we enter the summer with $23.45M profit, walk-away money from Belfour and Roberts ($9.20M combined), and one 4th-round pick. The constraint is not money — it is that we have no draft capital and no young players to offer that the sellers haven't already seen.

**Heatley** is the priority. 91 base, 119 points in 70 games, 24 years old, $1.10M expiring. ATL at 80 points with 11 expiring contracts cannot re-sign both him (119pts) and Kovalchuk (129pts, age 21 vs Heatley 24). Kovalchuk is younger and higher-scoring, so he stays. That makes Heatley the most likely top-91-base player to move this summer. He is exactly the right wing Mogilny and Roberts cannot cover anymore. POTE 86 means some growth remains. The package problem is real: we have Tucker, the 4th, and whatever young player the GM is willing to move, and ATL is a small-market rebuild that wants picks and prospects, not 30-year-old rentals.

**Doan** fills two gaps in one player. 87 base, TOUG 82, CHKG 87, 55 points in 73 games, $2.40M expiring, age 28, POTE 80. He is the best RW with real toughness in the league. No Toronto player has 82+ TOUG; Doan has it with 87 checking on top. PHX at 80 points, 14 expiring deals, $47.81M payroll, $13.01M profit. At 80 points they are most likely out of the race, which makes them a seller on an expiring captain-type. His FACE 56 is low but he plays RW where faceoffs don't matter. This is the single best gap-filler on the board.

**Bertuzzi** is the most complete player available at any position. 94 base, 119 points in 75 games, TOUG 89, CHKG 93, $2.60M expiring. A right winger who scores 119 points and checks at 93 does not exist elsewhere. But POTE 58 and age 30 mean the grades are set and declining. VAN at 94 points, $35.16M payroll, $33.24M profit — they have money and are in a race, so they might re-sign him rather than deal. If VAN is out of the race, he becomes the biggest chip in the league. Worth testing in July regardless.

**Morrow** at 88 base, TOUG 84, CHKG 86, 73 points in 58 games, $1.30M expiring, age 26, POTE 86 is better than Doan on every axis: younger, higher grades, better production, cheaper. The problem is DAL at 98 points with only 7 expiring contracts and $8.49M profit. They are a contender in a money squeeze, which could go either way: deal an expiring player to avoid a raise, or re-sign and make a Cup push. Lower probability than Doan but higher ceiling if they sell.

**Cammalleri and Frolov** from LA are the depth play. Cammalleri: 79 base, POTE 98, 51 points in 53 games, $1.10M expiring, age 22. Frolov: 77 base, POTE 96, 50 points in 54 games, $1.10M expiring, age 22. LA at 71 points with 14 expiring deals and $52.43M payroll are a motivated seller. Neither is a proven scorer yet (Cammalleri 0.96 pts/g in 53 GP, Frolov 0.93 pts/g in 54 GP), but the potential grades are the highest available from any seller. Landing both fills two top-six spots for five years at $2.20M combined today. The guide's "depth wins cups" argument applies here directly.

**Havlat** at 87 base, 93 points in 75 games, $900K expiring, age 23, POTE 84 is already flagged from the Feb 26 target list. OTT at 67 points with 11 expiring deals is a clear seller. He plays LW rather than RW, but he's a top-six scorer cheaper than Heatley. If ATL keeps both Kovalchuk and Heatley, Havlat is the next-best scoring target.

**Sillinger** at 86 base, FACE 92, 59 points in 53 games, $1.80M expiring, age 33, POTE 56 is the best faceoff man available. But he is 33 and Sundin is 34. Adding another 33+ centre doesn't help the age curve. He is a two-year bridge at best while Chlup (75 FACE, age 19) grows into the role. Worth keeping warm if a cheap package exists.

**Conroy** at 85 base, FACE 87, 86 points in 74 games, $2.00M expiring, age 33 is better production than Sillinger at a similar price. CGY at 58 points is the worst team in the league with 10 expiring deals. They are the most motivated seller available. Same age concern as Sillinger, but 86 points is real.

**McKenna** at TOUG 95, $400K, 32 GP from PIT at 77 points with 14 expiring is the cheapest toughness fix on the board. He will not play top six (5.3 MPG, 2 points), but he puts a 95-TOUG man on L4 and costs nothing. The coverage phase confirmed our top-six toughness ceiling is Jackman at 75. McKenna at 95 on the fourth line changes the physical profile of a playoff series without touching any core player.

The renewal cluster takes priority over any acquisition. Gaborik ($1.10M, 90pts, 23), Richards ($1.00M, 64pts, 24), Nash, Eminger, Abid, Kaberle, Chlup — all expire in July, and the GM's standing order sequences them correctly. Belfour ($6.50M) and Roberts ($2.70M) walking frees $9.20M that covers the raises. Lock the core before making offers for Heatley or Doan, because those deals cost players and you cannot trade players you haven't signed.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers is: what summer trade proposals can Toronto actually construct given one 4th-rounder, no cap constraint, a core that must be renewed before any piece moves, and three structural gaps (toughness, faceoffs, right-wing scoring)? The answer is two packages that together fill every gap, or one package that fills two of the three in a single move. The currency is Koltsov (23, POTE 94, ACCE 96, $1.10M, 2yr), Alexeev (23, POTE 94, 30pts, $1.10M, 1yr), Tucker (30, $1.30M, 2yr), and the 4th-rounder. Nothing else the GM has protected.

**Avery** fills all three structural gaps in one player: TOUG 83, CHKG 88, FACE 93. The role coverage confirmed zero Toronto players at 80+ stored TOUG; Avery is the only available 83+ man. His FACE 93 is better than Sundin's 90, which ends the L4 faceoff problem the coach flagged every report this season. LA at 48 points with 14 expiring contracts and $52.43M payroll is the most motivated seller in the league. Koltsov gives them a 23-year-old with POTE 94 and 96 ACCE, exactly what a rebuild needs. They also shed $700K in net salary. No pick required.

**Havlat** at 87 base, 93 points in 75 games, 23 years old, $900K expiring, POTE 84 is the top-six scorer the RW crisis demands. He plays LW rather than RW, but he replaces the production Mogilny and Roberts will leave behind. OTT at 67 points with 11 expiring deals cannot re-sign him at the $3-4M he will command. They get Tucker (30, CHKG 92, veteran body) and Alexeev (23, POTE 94, 30 points in 55 games, $1.10M expiring) and the 4th-rounder. OTT gets a prospect with upside and a pick for a player they cannot retain.

**Doan** is the alternative to the two smaller deals. At 87 base, TOUG 82, CHKG 87, he fills right wing and toughness simultaneously, but not faceoffs (FACE 56). PHX at 80 points with 14 expiring contracts and $47.81M payroll is likely out of the race and would rather get assets now than lose him for nothing. The package costs more than Avery alone because Doan is a better player: Koltsov + Alexeev + the 4th.

Proposals 1 and 2 are complementary: together they fill toughness, faceoffs, and top-six scoring for $1.30M combined annual salary (Avery $400K, Havlat $900K). Proposal 3 is the alternative path, consolidating into one bigger swing. Do not do 1 and 3 together; both require Koltsov.

If none land, the July UFA market is the fallback. Marleau (SJ, 89 base, 98 pts) and Gagne (PHI, 86 base, 94 pts) are expiring from distressed clubs per the March 16 note. Both become direct signings with money, not trades. The $9.20M freed by Belfour and Roberts covers either one. McKenna (PIT, TOUG 95, $400K) is the cheapest toughness fix if the Avery deal collapses: he is not a top-six player but he puts a 95-TOUG man on L4 for nothing.

## Owed

The question this phase answers: **the Luongo/DiPietro goalie monitoring task the GM set on January 19, wanted by February 20.** It is now March 23. The task is resolved and closed.

**Luongo** is on our roster. He reads 94 overall at 25 years old, $1.60M, 2 years remaining, 42 GP this season. He was the target the GM set on January 15 ("fetch a really good high-90s goalie from a team that will not be a contender") and he is now in Toronto. The GM confirmed on March 19 that he and Belfour are the two 90+ goalies for the playoffs and closed all goalie monitoring.

**DiPietro** is eliminated. At 52 GP he still reads 79 base overall, 3.64 GAA, 84.9% SV. That fails the high-90s standard by 11+ points at full sample size. I flagged this on March 14 and the finding is recorded.

What changed since I last reported: Luongo went from a trade target to a rostered player at 94. DiPietro went from "watch his ice time" to "permanently eliminated, no sample size fixes this." The GM himself closed the window on March 19 with "close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks."

The task is done. I am marking it delivered.



Delivered: **#2** (Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window) — Luongo is acquired and rostered at 94 overall, 25, 2 years, $1.60M. DiPietro eliminated at 79 base on full 52-GP sample. GM closed the monitoring window on March 19.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-23
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-23

Next game at BOS on Thursday 24 March 2005.

## Development opportunity

**Is every young player getting the games he has earned?** Mostly yes, but Spezza and Upshall are stuck in roles below what the club's own scouting says they can become, and Stahle is getting four games when his number could use forty.

**Chlup** at 19 is the cleanest case of earning it: 51 points in 64 games, 16.7 minutes on the second line, morale 96. He belongs where he is and nobody needs to touch his role.

**Gaborik** plays every game at 20.3 MPG on the first line with 90 points. Nothing to say except he is the team.

**Nash** at 20 has 35 points in 62 games on the third line. He is getting his games. The production question (season rate 0.56, recent window 0.43) is a system-fit issue for the offseason, not a development-opportunity problem tonight.

**Klesla** plays all 75 at 15.0 MPG. At 23 with 27 points he is not declining because he lacks games; he is declining because 0.36 points per game is what he is producing. His opportunity is not the problem.

**Chistov** at 21 gets 61 games and 13.2 MPG on the third line with 20 points. He is in the lineup, he is playing, but 0.33 points per game does not argue for a bump.

**Spezza** at 21 with POTE 99 has played 39 of 75 games at 7.2 MPG on the fourth line. Morale has slipped to 89. I have raised this five times and nothing has moved. He is not getting the chance to prove what the club thinks he can be. Seven games remain: move him to the third line for those games even if it costs us depth on the fourth.

**Upshall** at 21 with POTE 99 has 61 games but only 8.3 MPG on the fourth line and 19 points. He is in the building but invisible. At 0.31 points per game his production does not demand a top-nine role, but his morale at 92 will not hold if he finishes the year here. Give him a look on the third line for the remaining seven and let the result settle the question before the offseason.

**Eminger** at 21 has 57 games, 15.9 MPG and 21 points. His season rate is 0.37, below the 0.45 trade threshold I set in January. He is getting his games, but 0.37 at POTE 99 means the opportunity is not converting. Flag for offseason, not a tonight change.

**Spacek** at 19 with POTE 91 is scratched at 50 games and 7.6 MPG. Morale 89. The minutes target is dead (noted earlier this month), and at 0.34 points per game he has not separated himself from the fourth-line crowd. Accept the year as what it is.

**Colaiacovo** and **Alexeev** are scratched. When Colaiacovo plays he gets 17.9 MPG, which is a real D-pair role compressed into 31 games. That is the GM's deliberate rotation and I have accepted it on the record.

**Stahle** at 20 has 4 games all season with POTE 96. Seven games left, even if he plays all of them he hits 11. The blue line is too deep for him to break in this year. This is a next-season decision, not a this-season one.

**Koltsov** and **Ouellet**: GM's trading chip and backup goaltender respectively. Out of my hands.

## Development trends

The question this phase answers: are our young players getting better fast enough to build around, and are our veterans holding up under the load we've put on them? With 7 games left, the trends visible now decide who starts next October where.

**Chlup** is the season's one clean development story. From 0.62 pts/g on 11 MPG early to 0.84 on 18.1 over 64 games since. At 19, more minutes and better production simultaneously is exactly what you want to see. He's confirmed as a permanent top-nine centre. If anything, 18.1 is light for a guy producing at that rate, but he's ahead of schedule already.

**Kaberle** is the positive surprise among veterans. He went from 0.54 pts/g early to 0.63 recently, while his minutes climbed from 19.4 to 21.9. At 27, he's entering his prime, not leaving it. The GM called him a star in January. The numbers now say the same thing. He's our best defenseman on the rise.

**Upshall** is the story nobody has flagged yet. Early season he played 13.4 MPG at 0.33 pts/g. Since then, over 37 games, he's at 5.1 MPG and 0.30. His minutes collapsed by 8 a night and the production barely budged, which means the ice time we did give him wasn't productive either. At 21, this is a wasted year mirroring Spezza's. Both are 21, both at roughly 5 MPG, both producing under 0.35. The organization is dressing two first-round-level prospects and using them as spare parts.

**Spezza** is still the same problem: 0.33 pts/g on 5.1 MPG over 39 games. Raised five times with no movement. I'll stop raising it this season. Offseason conversation is needed: if he can't earn 10+ MPG in this system at 21 with POTE 99, either the system is wrong for him or he needs to go where it isn't.

**McCabe** needs a re-read. The March 4 note said 0.83 cumulative and off the sell list. The recent window here shows 0.49 pts/g on 21.7 MPG over 51 games since Dec 1. His early season (1.42 in 24 games) was the anomaly, and he hasn't recovered to anything near it since. At 29 with four years at $3M, the planning question changes: is he a top-pair defenseman or a second-pair overpaid? The 21.7 MPG says we still treat him as the former. The 0.49 says maybe he's the latter.

**Mogilny** at 36 is doing what you'd expect. Early season 1.62 pts/g, recently 0.79 on more minutes (16.9 to 19.3). The rate decline is age, the extra minutes mean we're stretching him. He still contributes, but plan the right wing vacancy for next year now. **Roberts** at 38 still at 0.88 on 21.4 MPG is remarkable by any standard, but the same clock runs out on him.

**Abid** remains the production-to-ice-time mismatch flagged March 16. Rate is holding at 0.79, but minutes fell from 20.1 to 12.0. This is now confirmed for the full window, not just a blip. Whatever shifted his minutes in January hasn't reversed.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy; nobody's morale is in trouble.

**Abid** is the one player I'd flag. He's at 14.4 minutes a night with 66 points in 75 games (0.88 pts/g). That's second-line production from a fourth-line winger. His minutes did climb from 12.6 in mid-March, which is progress, but he's still well under the 20 MPG a player of his output-calibre expects. Morale sits at 99 so nothing's broken yet, but the gap between what he puts up and what he gets is a ticking clock. One more month of this and the number drops.

**Nash** at 12.8 MPG and 0.56 pts/g is the reverse: minutes are low for a third-line regular, but his production has cratered (from 0.83 to 0.43 per the earlier finding) and he's only played 62 games. His morale at 99 says he doesn't mind the role right now. No change tonight.

**Spacek** (89 morale, 7.6 MPG) and **Spezza** (89 morale, 7.2 MPG) are the two lowest on the roster. Both are in the GM's development rotation and both are at acceptable levels for a scratch player. No intervention needed.

Everyone else on the active roster sits at 96-99. The record is taking care of the rest.

## Role composition

The role audit asks whether each unit suits its purpose and whether we have enough bodies for each role. The short answer: L1 and L2 are well-built, L3 is Richards plus three men who don't belong there, and L4 has a structural faceoff void that no arrangement fixes.

**L1** is the team's best line in every category that matters. Jackman at 89 checking gives the defensive anchor, Sundin at 90 faceoffs wins the draws, Gaborik at 98/99 scoring and playmaking carries the offense. Fischer's 83 checking adds depth. Mean checking of 81 for a first line is a luxury. No change.

**L2** is an offensive line with thin checking (69 mean, McCabe at 83 the best). That's fine. Lines 1 and 3 can absorb defensive matchups, and L2's job is to score. Kaberle at 86 stamina and Afinogenov at 97 playmaking make this the unit that wears teams down over 60. No change.

**L3** is the problem. Richards at 93 checking is the only reason this unit works defensively. Nash, Eminger, and Klesla all sit well below that. Eminger's recent window at 0.17 pts/g over 6 games means he contributes nothing at either end. Klesla at 22 is declining. Nash is at 0.43 pts/g on 12.7 MPG. The line has a 73 checking mean dragged up only by Richards. However, the bench offers no replacement checker above the low 80s who isn't already deployed, so there's no swap that improves things.

**L4** has a 51 mean faceoff with nobody above 53. Abid at 85 checking is good but his role is a winger, not a center, so he won't take the draws. Spezza at 53 faceoffs as a prospect center is the real concern — if he can't win draws at this level, he needs to build that skill now.

**Power play** is fine. P1 at 86 playmaking and 88 scoring with Gaborik, Sundin, and Jackman is elite. P2 with Mogilny's 92 scoring and Klesla's youth works.

**Penalty kill** is well-arranged. K1 (77 mean checking) uses top players who are on ice anyway; K2 (83 mean checking with Jackman at 89) is the true checking unit. The 6-point gap between them is acceptable because K1's job is short-handed minutes from guys already out there.

**Roster depth on checking:** Jackman 89, Richards 93, Roberts 83, McCabe 83, Fischer 83. That's five forwards and defensemen above 80 checking. Adequate for a full season, but one injury to Jackman or Roberts leaves us exposed badly — we'd have no one at 85+ to anchor both the PK and a shutdown line simultaneously.

## Opponent matchup

**No change to the lines.** This is a game where our depth creates mismatches everywhere and our top pair is built to handle their one real threat.

**Thornton** is Boston's whole offense. 92 OVR, 97 shot power, 97 puck control, 94 hero. He centers Murray (86 OVR, 96 SHPW) and Knuble (a grinder). That line goes to our first pair by auto-pairing, and that is exactly right. Fischer and Jackman both sit at 90 checking, Jackman has 89 toughness and 87 aggression, Fischer has 93 speed to match Thornton's 92. They can hold him.

**Eminger/Klesla on the third pair** face Rolston (82 OVR, 92 SHPW, 89 hero), the one other BOS player who can score. But his wingers Zamuner and McInnis are both 73 OVR with ACCU 58 — they cannot finish what Rolston creates. Klesla alongside Eminger (83 and 76) with 92 speed and 77 checking covers the wing side. The risk is Eminger's 50 endurance fading late and giving Rolston open ice. I accept it for one night; it's three minutes a period he's exposed and only on one player.

**Our top three lines vs their D pairs:** Gaborik (97 OVR) against McGillis/Berard (81/81) is a mismatch in our favor. Nash and Chistov (82/81) against Gill/Moran (72/68) is another. Their third pair has 68 and 72 OVR combined — no other BOS D unit is close. We should score on them.

**Fourth-line faceoffs:** Vernarsky at 82 faceoffs against Spezza at 53. We lose every draw down there, which means BOS L4 gets zone time and our third pair gets more ice. Known structural gap, nothing fixable tonight.

**Belfour in net.** 93 OVR against a team generating 2.90 GA per game — their offense isn't going to test him enough to matter. Check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming.

## Owed

**Item #1 — defenceman analysis and sell-list update.** With 7 games left, this is near-final. The rate has settled enough to call it.

**Jackman** at 35 points in 73 games is 0.48 pts/g on 30.0 minutes a night. On March 14 I flagged this at 0.48 across 69 games and set a condition: hold below 0.50 through season's end and his role must change or he goes. He has held. This is no longer a warning, it is a verdict. At $0.70M x 3 years he is the cheapest top-pair D in hockey, which makes him the most sellable piece on the blue line. Any club gets 30 MPG of 85-OVR defence for pocket change.

**Klesla** at 27 points in 75 games is 0.36 pts/g at 23. My February note said a second consecutive declining season makes him tradeable. That condition is met: 0.38 at 22, now 0.36 at 23, on flat minutes. He is on the sell list for good. At $0.90M x 2 years he carries some value as a young third-pair piece.

**Eminger** at 21 points in 57 games is 0.37 pts/g, $1.20M expiring. Still on the sell list. No change from February.

**McCabe** at 59 points in 75 games is 0.79 pts/g. Was 0.83 on 66 games in early March. A slight drift down, but nowhere near the sell threshold. He stays. No change.

**Fischer** (0.53 pts/g) and **Kaberle** (0.60 pts/g) are both keepers per the GM's standing order. No change.

**Colaiacovo** at 12 points in 31 games is 0.39 pts/g on a small sample. He was the development rotation piece the GM wanted young guys ahead of. With 7 games left he may not get more. His $1.10M expiring makes him a cheap depth piece to move at deadline if a buyer calls.

The sell order is now: Jackman first (cheapest per-point, longest term, biggest value gap), Klesla second (second declining year confirmed, young enough to still draw interest), Eminger third (expiring, no leverage but no cost to let go either).

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-21
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-21

Toronto 53-12-4, 120 pts after 74 games.

## Role coverage

The question this phase answers: with 82 points of cushion and eight games left before the season ends, which holes on this roster can the coach close by redeploying men we already have, and which ones we carry into the playoffs because they require a trade to fix?

**Toughness is the only structural gap that acquisition alone fixes.** Zero Toronto skaters carry 80+ toughness. Jackman tops the club at 75, Roberts at 73, McCabe at 73, Tucker at 70. This confirms the March 19 finding: the gap is not form noise, it has always been there. Avery (LA, 25, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 93 FACE, $400K, 2 years left) closes all three thin roles at once. But the GM's March 19 standing order limits tradeable chips to Tucker and the 4th-rounder, and the only package LA will accept is Koltsov. That package is blocked by the order. The GM needs to decide whether Koltsov is a chip after all or whether we play the whole spring without an 80+ toughness player.

**Faceoffs are thin but survivable.** Sundin at 90 is the lone 80+ draw-taker. Richards at 70 is second-best and already anchored at L3. The fourth line's best option is 52 FACE per the coach's read. Against Buffalo on Tuesday that barely matters; in a playoff series against a centre-heavy opponent it does. Avery at 93 solves it in one move. Without him, Richards sliding from L3 to L4 at least raises two of the four lines to 70+, but it leaves L3 naked on draws. That is a coach call.

**Checking is adequate.** Jackman 87, Roberts 86, McCabe 86, Fischer 82, Upshall 80 — five men at 80+ who are lined. Tucker at 83 sits unlined as depth; dressing him adds a sixth body but does not fix toughness (he is 70). The role is covered.

**Scoring, playmaking, speed, clutch, stamina, durability: all covered.** Ten at 80+ in scoring, eleven in playmaking, twenty-one in speed. No thin role outside the two above. The age overlay matters for next year: Mogilny at 36 and Roberts at 38 are the top of two of those lists, but that is a summer problem, not a March one.

**Goalies are solved per the March 19 order.** Belfour at .930 with 29 wins and Luongo arriving at 94 glove and stick are the two playoff goaltenders. Ouellet backs them up. No action.

## Trajectory

Toronto's age curve is not a cliff; the risk is contract failure, not aging. Fourteen players 23 or under, eleven at 24-29, and only four 34 or older. That is the shape of a team entering its window, not leaving one. The danger is that thirteen contracts worth $21.30M expire this July and every one of them is either a young player about to command a raise or an expensive veteran who can walk.

**Gaborik** is the single most important renewal on the sheet. 87 points in 74 games at 23 years old, on $1.10M with one year left. Every other player on this roster is affordable by comparison, but if he walks, the top line loses its engine and the club has no replacement under 30 with that scoring profile. Five or six years, signed the week the season ends.

**Richards** is 64 points in 72 games at 24, $1.00M, expiring. He is the second renewal priority: a 24-year-old centre producing second-line numbers on a third-line salary. Five or six years. If you get both Gaborik and Richards locked, the center and right-wing depth are secure through 2010.

**Nash** at 35 points in 61 games, age 20, POTE 95, $1.20M, expiring, is the cheapest upside on the roster. Five years, $3-4M per season, is the right deal. Even if he busts, five years of 25-35-point winger depth is cheap insurance at that price.

**Eminger** at POTE 99, age 21, 21 points in 56 games, $1.20M, expiring, carries the highest potential of any defender on the roster. The same five-year logic applies: you are buying the likelihood of a top-four defenseman for less than what a proven third-pairing blueliner costs.

**The 2-3 year tier:** Chistov (POTE 95, 20 pts/60 GP, $1.10M), Upshall (POTE 99, 19 pts/60 GP, $1.20M), Colaiacovo (POTE 99, 12 pts/31 GP, $1.10M), Alexeev (POTE 94, 30 pts/55 GP, $1.10M), and Abid (66 pts/74 GP, TOUG 80, $0.40M) all expire. These five together are $4.90M now. Two or three year deals at modest raises ($1.5-2.0M each) keep the depth without a 2007 cluster. Abid is the cheapest and most valuable of the group; lock him first.

**Belfour** ($6.50M) and **Roberts** ($2.70M) walk after this season. That $9.20M creates the payroll room for the young-core raises.
