Mogilny ($5.50M, two years left) expires in 2006; let him go then too. The GM's February 19 order to keep Belfour for the playoffs is intact; the question is only what happens in July, and July should be a goodbye.

**Sundin** at 34, $8.40M, five years left through age 39 with POTE 60, is the one contract that gets worse every season. He is producing (83 points in 74 games) but the deal outlives the production by at least three years. This is not a problem today. It becomes one in 2007-08 when he is 37 and the $8.40M anchors a payroll that no longer needs a veteran centre. Trade-bait by then; there is nothing to do now because the five-year deal is locked.

**Payroll math for July 2005:** Current $60.04M. Remove Belfour and Roberts ($9.20M). Add roughly $15M in raises across Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger, and the depth tier. Net payroll lands around $66M against $90M revenue. Profit drops from $24M to roughly $18-19M. That is manageable and buys three years of competitive window.

**Draft capital is gone.** One fourth-rounder, nothing higher. Every future package must be funded by players. This makes the July renewals even more critical because there are no picks to re-stock the roster if a young player walks.

**The owed task — Luongo and DiPietro monitoring (asked 2005-01-19, due 2005-02-20):** Luongo is on Toronto's roster at 91 base, 42 GP, $1.60M, two years left. He arrived before the February window closed. DiPietro was eliminated as a target on March 14 at 79 base over 52 GP. Both lines of inquiry are closed. This task is delivered.

## Calendar

**The deadline passed two days ago.** No more trades, no more packages. Everything left is the eight regular-season games, the playoffs, and the summer. The summer is the hard part: 13 contracts worth $22.10M expire at once, and the core of this roster — Gaborik, Nash, Eminger, Richards — all sit in that group on $1.00–1.20M deals that will not hold.

**Gaborik** is the priority. 91 base, POTE 90, 23 years old, earning $1.10M. He is a 90+ point scorer on a rookie-scale salary. If we do not lock him for five or six years in July, every contender with a signing bonus to throw makes him a bidding-war target and we lose him. This is the single highest-value contract decision on the sheet.

**Nash** at 20 and **Eminger** at 21 (POTE 99) are the other two 5-6 year locks. Both are under $1.20M and both are on the coach's core. The GM has been explicit that Eminger stays; the only question is whether we pay him like the defenseman he is or lose him to the market.

**Richards** at 24, $1.00M, anchors the second line. Five-year deal. Same logic as Gaborik but at a lower premium.

**Kaberle** at 27 and $1.90M is the one genuine judgement call among the young core. He is not a franchise defenseman at 27 with his ceiling set, but he is a top-four piece we built around. Three or four years at a flat rate is the right shape; five starts pricing him as a star he is not yet.

**Abid** at 24 and $0.40M is the cheapest toughness on the market. Three-year lock at a small raise and the fourth-line physical game is solved for three years. **Chistov** at 21 gets three years; **Colaiacovo** and **Alexeev** get two-year show-me deals.

**Upshall** at 21 is the awkward one: the coach is putting Alexeev back over him and wants him in the lineup for development, but his $1.20M renewal competes with Alexeev's $1.10M for the same roster spot. Sign the cheaper one longer. That is Alexeev at two years if the final eight games give him real ice.

**Tellqvist** at 25, $0.80M, POTE in the high 90s: the GM's standing order is to give him time. Two years, low salary, and we have a cheap backup or trade piece in 2007.

**Belfour** at 39 and $6.50M and **Roberts** at 38 and $2.70M are gone. Belfour is the GM's own read: offer reduced, he will not accept. Roberts is $2.70M from a 38-year-old who will not play meaningful minutes next season. Together they free $9.20M of the $22.10M expiring, which pays for the Gaborik and Nash raises without growing total payroll.

**On the owed task — Luongo monitoring and DiPietro development:** The deadline closed March 19. Luongo is on our roster at 91 base with 2 years remaining and is our playoff starter alongside Belfour. DiPietro was eliminated March 14 at 79 base with 52 games of sample. The goalie trade window is closed and this task is complete.

**Playoff ticket prices:** raise to 75 in round one, 80 in round two, 90 in round three, 100 in the final. We are the #1 seed in the East and should be filling the building at premium rates.

## League scan

With only Tucker and the 4th-rounder as tradeable assets, the deadline market is almost closed to us. The question this phase answers: who, across 29 other clubs, fits our toughness and faceoff gaps at a price Tucker plus a fourth-rounder can actually pay?

**Reid (STL, RW, 77 base, 83 FACE, POTE 93, 24, $600K expiring, 55 pts/63 GP)** is the best target for our specific currency. STL sits at 72 points with 8 expiring deals and $10.25M profit, which is not desperation, but a 77-overall winger on $600K with one year left is the kind of player a rebuilding club moves for a rental plus a pick. Tucker fills their wing depth through the deadline; the 4th costs us nothing else. Reid's 83 FACE at 24 is the only realistic upgrade to the L4 draw problem the coach flagged (best available is 52). He does not close toughness (52 TOUG). Acceptance uncertain; STL keeps him if they want a cheap re-sign.

**Stuart (SJ, D, 87 base, 80 TOUG, 89 CHKG, POTE 91, 25, $1.80M expiring, 48 pts/72 GP)** closes toughness, checking, and adds a top-pairing blueliner with upside in one move. SJ is 65 points with 13 expiring contracts and no reason to keep him. The problem is price: Tucker plus a 4th-rounder is nowhere near an 87-overall defenseman. Unless the over-80 expiring mechanic moves SJ to accept almost anything rather than lose him for nothing, this is a wish. Worth a probe because it is the single best fit, but I would not plan around it.

**Conroy (CGY, C, 85 base, 94 FACE, $2.00M expiring, 33)** is the pure-rental centre. CGY is 58 points, the second-worst team in the league, with 10 expiring deals. The over-80 mechanic means CGY can trade him for a pick rather than lose him. Tucker plus the 4th is thin but it is at least something. His 94 FACE matches Sundin at 90 as the second-best draw-taker, which turns three of four lines into 70+ faceoff units. At 33 with POTE 79, this is a playoff rental, not a long-term piece. Acceptance uncertain.

**Marchand (CBJ, C, 88 base, 94 FACE, $4.88M expiring, 31)** is the better player at the same 94 FACE, but $4.88M salary makes CBJ's asking price higher than Tucker plus a 4th. CBJ at 70 points with 9 expiring is in the same window as CGY but has less urgency. I would test Conroy before Marchand.

**Avery (LA, C, 25, $400K, 2 years, 93 FACE, 88 CHKG)** remains the structural fix for all three gaps simultaneously, but the March 19 order locks Koltsov. LA rejected Tucker explicitly. The GM needs to decide before the window closes: either Koltsov becomes a chip or we play the entire spring without an 80+ toughness player. This is a binary call and no other target replaces Avery's grade profile.

**Heatley (ATL, RW, 91 base, POTE 85, 24, $1.10M expiring) and Kovalchuk (ATL, LW, 89 base, POTE 85, 21, $1.10M expiring)** are the premium talents on ATL's expiring list. ATL has $24.95M profit and no financial pressure. Tucker plus a 4th is not a credible offer for either. I am dropping both from the active list.

**Theodore (MTL, G, 91 base, $5.50M expiring, 28)** fits the Jan 15 order for a high-90s goalie from a non-contender, but the GM closed all goalie monitoring on March 19. Dead target.

**Primeau (PHI, C, 87 base, 91 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 76 FACE, $4.60M, 3 years left, 33)** is the best two-way centre on a financially distressed club ($2.43M profit on $66.73M payroll). But 3 years left at $4.60M means PHI wants a real package, not Tucker and a 4th. Not realistic with our currency.

The ranked shortlist is: **Reid** first (achievable, fills the L4 gap), **Stuart** second (best fit but price is wrong), **Conroy** third (rental value at the right price tier), **Avery** as a separate decision the GM has not made. Everything else requires currency we do not hold.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: with Tucker and a fourth-rounder as the only currency the GM has authorized, which deadline target is actually buyable, and is any of them worth spending our sole future pick on?

**Conroy** is the best shot. CGY sits at 58 points with 10 expiring deals and a 33-year-old centre on $2.00M expiring is the textbook over-80 dump: they get a pick, we get 94 FACE for the playoff run. Tucker fills their wing depth if they even care, but at 30 with 1 point in 3 games he may be deadweight to a rebuild. If the mechanic works on a bare 4th, the GM should try the thinner version first and keep Tucker in the lineup. This is a rental: Conroy walks in July.

**Reid** is the better hockey piece: 24 years old, POTE 93, 55 points in 63 games at $600K, 83 FACE. But STL at 72 points with $10.25M profit is not selling a 55-point winger for a 1-point rental. I would probe once, but not plan around it. If STL slips on the playoff bubble before March 29 it could get livelier.

**Stuart** at 87 base, 80 TOUG, 89 CHKG closes our structural toughness gap better than anything else available. But SJ at 65 points will want a first-rounder or a top prospect for an 87-base defenceman, not a 4th and Tucker. This is a wish. Drop it from the active list.

**Avery** closes toughness (83 TOUG), checking (88 CHKG), and faceoffs (93 FACE) in one move at $400K with two years left. The coach confirmed zero 80+ TOUG on the roster. LA will only take Koltsov, who sits on POTE 94 and two years at $1.10M. The GM's March 19 order says Koltsov stays. That order is the decision point: override it and we fix three gaps simultaneously, or keep it and play the spring without an 80+ toughness player. No other available target replaces Avery's grade profile.

**If none land:** Richards slides to L4 at 73 FACE per the coach's plan, raising two lines above 70 on draws. Toughness stays below 80 across the lineup. At 53-12-4, neither gap ends the playoff run, and the fourth-rounder stays in the bank for July drafting when scouting might find real depth. Do nothing is a defensible answer.

**Owed task delivered.** The Luongo/DiPietro monitoring (asked 2005-01-19, due 2005-02-20) is closed. Luongo is on our roster at 91 base, 42 GP, $1.60M, two years left. DiPietro was eliminated on 2005-03-14 at 79 base in 52 GP. Both lines of inquiry are finished.

## Owed

**Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window** — this task is fully resolved and can be closed.

**Luongo** landed. He was acquired before the February 20 deadline you set; my 2005-02-07 recommendation ("Luongo monitoring task is complete; he is on the roster at 91 base with 2 years left") was taken. He now reads 93 overall, 25 years old, $1.60M, 2 years left, 42 GP. The job is done.

**DiPietro** is eliminated on merit. At 52 GP he still reads 79 base overall, 3.64 GAA, 84.9% SV. The Jan 15 standing order was "a really good high-90s goalie." He is 11+ points below that threshold with no development trajectory toward it. No further monitoring is warranted.

**The whole goalie window is closed.** You ordered it shut on 2005-03-19: "Stop monitoring for deals for Belfour. Keeping him and Luongo as two 90+ goalies for the playoffs. Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks." The task is now doubly dead — resolved by acquisition on one side, eliminated by merit on the other, and the mandate itself withdrawn.

Nothing has changed since the last time I reported on this because there is nothing left to change.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-21
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-21

Next game vs BUF on Tuesday 22 March 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether our young players are getting the games their production has earned, with 8 games left in the season.

**Chlup** is the answer to what this should look like. 50 points in 63 games on 16.7 MPG at 19 years old, sitting on the second line. He has earned every minute he gets and the role fits him. No touch needed.

**Alexeev** is the loudest finding this week. 30 points in 55 games is 0.55 pts/g on only 8.3 MPG, and he is currently scratched. Upshall is at 0.32 pts/g on 8.5 MPG playing the fourth line. Chistov is at 0.33 on 13.1 MPG. Alexeev is out-producing both by a wide margin on a similar ice-time budget and sitting out. That is a waste of a 23-year-old who is producing.

**Spezza** remains where he has been for five reports: POTE 99, 38 games, 7.4 MPG, fourth line. 15 points in 38 games is 0.39 pts/g, which is not a rate that screams for a top-nine role right now, but the combination of buried minutes and that scouting number means we are burning a season on a man who cannot play.

**Spacek** at 19 is scratched with 7.6 MPG and 17 points in 50 games (0.34 pts/g). His 10 MPG target is mathematically dead. With 8 games left the only question is whether we dress him to give the kid game reps or accept the year is what it is. His morale at 89 is the lowest among our young group, which suggests the scratching is registering.

**Nash** is earning it: 35 points in 61 games on 12.6 MPG, third line, morale 99. The recent rate is down from his October pace but the role and the minutes are appropriate for where he is right now.

**Gaborik**, **Klesla**, **Chistov**, and **Eminger** are all dressed and playing regular roles. Klesla at 100% of games is a bit heavy for a 23-year-old showing decline, but with 8 games left there is no reason to disrupt a third defensive pair. **Stahle** (4 GP, 0 pts) and **Ouellet** (backup goalie, 11 GP) are correctly in their roles. **Koltsov** is scratched and correctly so as a trading chip whose rate has collapsed.

The one clear move for the remaining schedule is Alexeev back in for Upshall.

## Development trends

Who is climbing, who is sliding, and what it means for the eight games left and the offseason. Three young names moving the right way, four stalled despite games, and a blue-line sell order that needs revising.

**Chlup** is the clearest riser. 0.62 to 0.84 pts/g while minutes doubled from 11.0 to 18.2, at 19. Players that age usually lose rate under doubled load. He gained it. He belongs in the top nine and the Feb 23 call was right.

**Kaberle** went 0.54 to 0.62 on minutes up from 19.4 to 21.9 at 27. He is still growing into his prime and the GM was right to call him a star on January 15. No change needed, just noting the direction.

**Chistov** is the quiet one. 0.29 to 0.35 with minutes up from 9.5 to 14.2 at 21. Both moving the right way at the same time. He is earning a top-nine spot and should keep getting it.

**Spezza** has gone backwards since the January 31 flag. Minutes fell from 9.1 to 5.4 and rate from 0.43 to 0.35. At POTE 99 and 21, 38 games played and a role smaller than he had in January. This is the sixth time I raise it and nothing has changed. If his 5.4 MPG is what this roster gives him, we need to decide before April whether he stays.

**Upshall** had his minutes cut from 13.4 to 5.2 while his rate held flat at 0.31. He fell out of the lineup without a production reason. At 21 this is the kind of lost season that costs a year of growth for no gain.

**Spacek** is at 5.2 MPG with 0.28 pts/g across 50 games. The March 11 note said the 10 MPG target was unreachable; it is now 5.2. His year is done. Offseason decision: keep dressing a 19-year-old centre for spot minutes or give the roster spot to someone who will play.

**Koltsov** went from 1.10 to 0.28 pts/g since December 1. The trading chip the GM held in January is now worth close to nothing. If he was going to move, the value window closed weeks ago.

**Nash** at 0.41 on flat minutes (12.9 to 12.4) confirms the March 16 system-fit concern. The role did not change and neither did the ice; the production halved. Offseason question, not a game-night one.

**Jackman** at 0.41 on 30.2 MPG is the confirmed collapse flagged March 14. At 24 the load is the problem. His role has to come down next season or he becomes a worse asset every month.

**McCabe** needs revisiting. I moved him off the sell list on March 4 when his recent window read 0.83, but this broader window shows 1.42 down to 0.50 across 74 games. At 29 with four years at $3M remaining, 0.50 is third-pair production. He belongs back on the sell list.

**Klesla** went 0.50 to 0.30 on flat minutes at 23. That is two consecutive declining seasons at an age where the direction should be up. He and Koltsov are both losing trade value by the week.

**Veterans:** Sundin 1.46 to 0.96, Mogilny 1.62 to 0.80, Roberts 1.29 to 0.88. All three cooling from October starts but all three still productive. Roberts at 38 posting 0.88 is extraordinary. No planning changes needed there.

**D sell order update (standing order #1, 11th time):** The list from March 4 was Eminger, Salo, Klesla. McCabe at 0.50 since December 1 belongs back in the conversation. New order: McCabe, Klesla, Salo, Eminger. Eminger at 0.39 on rising minutes is the one to keep.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy. Morale is 99 across almost the entire roster, and every player below 99 is trending up. No minutes adjustment is needed right now.

**Spezza** sits lowest at 89 but gained 3 points since the last save. He's at 7.4 MPG on the fourth line with 15 points in 38 games (0.39 pts/g). If his OVR puts him in the 70-79 band, he's about 2.5 minutes short of target, but the direction is right and with 8 games left I'm not breaking a line that's working to chase a two-minute bump. Let him ride L4.

**Upshall** at 92 (up 3) and **Alexeev** at 92 (up 5) are both well above target for their bands. Alexeev is scratched, Upshall is on the fourth line at 8.5 MPG. Neither needs intervention — the wins are doing the work.

**Tucker** at 90 is scratched with only 3 games and 9.0 MPG. He's 30, a checker, and the GM kept him per the standing order. His morale is stable and there's no minutes lever worth pulling for 8 games.

**Abid** at 99 needs no mention here. My earlier note about him needing 18+ MPG was about production, not morale. His morale is fine at 14.6 MPG. That's a matchup question for the next phase, not a happiness one.

Everyone else is at 99 with gains of +1 to +9. The winning is fixing everything. No change.

## Role composition

**The question is whether our units are built from the right pieces.** They are, almost entirely. The only structural problem the arrangement can't solve is the fourth-line faceoff void, and that's already known.

**Jackman** is on L1, P1, and K2 simultaneously. 30.4 MPG at 24, production at 0.48 pts/g and falling. His checking at 88 makes him the anchor on K2, and his scoring at 87 makes him a weapon on P1. The problem isn't that he suits any of those units poorly; it's that he's on all three. Against Buffalo (25-31), this is a game where we can absorb a minor PK drop-off. I'd prefer to move him off K2 tonight and give McCabe, Chlup and Abid to kill without him, saving his legs for the even-strength and PP work where he still drives offense. Cost: K2 checking mean drops from 82 to roughly 75 without an 88 checker on it.

**L4** at 51/52 faceoffs is the known void. Richards at 73 is the next-best draw man and he's already anchoring L3. No bench player fixes this. It's a roster gap for the offseason, not tonight's problem.

**K1** has Kaberle alongside Sundin, Roberts and Fischer. His checking isn't elite but his positioning and skating work on the kill, and the GM considers him a star. Leaving it alone.

**P2** with Chlup, Mogilny, Richards, Fischer and Klesla has good balance: Mogilny scoring 92, Richards clutch 95, Fischer checking 82. That unit suits its role.

No even-strength changes. The lines match what they're supposed to do.

## Opponent matchup

This is a blowout-mismatch night: we've outscored BUF 29-3 in four meetings this season, they sit at 74 points with a 10.7% PP, and Brunette is out for them. The only real decision is whether to use the easy opponent for development minutes or just roll the same units that are 9-0-1.

**BUF's top line** is the only threat worth naming: Briere (82), Drury (86), Nolan (88) at their best OVRs. Our first line of Sundin (89), Roberts (86) and Gaborik (96) has a clear edge at every position, and Fischer/Jackman (83/84) on our first D pair match Zhitnik/Bouchard (83/80) without concern.

**BUF's bottom six** is thin without Brunette: Pyatt (78) and Dumont (77) anchor a third line that our Richards/Nash/Chistov group (85/81/80) should own. Their fourth line at 74/75/68 is the worst in the game tonight.

**Their PP at 25 goals on 234 attempts** is 10.7%, the worst kind of unit to face when you're 1.50 GA/g. Taking a penalty against BUF costs less than against most clubs. No PK change needed.

**The development question:** BUF is not a quality opponent. Per the framework the GM set in January, this is a game we can afford to use for young legs. Spacek's season is at 8.1 MPG and the 10 target is dead, but if the GM wants to dress him and give Abid a top-nine look in a safe game, that's a development call, not a matchup one. I wouldn't make that call on my own without the GM's nod.

## Owed

**Defencemen sell list, near-final version with 8 games left.**

**Eminger** at 21 points in 56 games is 0.38 pts/g. When I put him back on the sell list on Feb 26, his season rate was 0.44. He has played roughly 8 more games and added nothing. The recovery is dead and stays dead. $1.2M expiring, 21 years old, 15.8 MPG. He is the first D off the list at season's end.

**Klesla** sits at 27 points in 74 games, 0.36 pts/g. My March 11 note had him at 0.38. Three more games, no points, same 14.8 MPG. A second straight declining year at 23 on $0.90M x 2. He's cheap but his market value is shrinking each week he plays the same 15 minutes and scores nothing. Trade him this offseason before the 2006-07 numbers confirm him as a fourth-pairing D.

**Colaiacovo** at 12 points in 31 games, 0.39 pts/g. He's a development piece the GM is rotating. Not on the sell list. His one-year deal means a decision comes naturally in the summer.

**Jackman** at 35 points in 72 games is 0.49 pts/g on 30.1 MPG. The load problem from March 14 is confirmed: his rate has not moved since then (0.48 to 0.49). At $0.70M x 3 he is too cheap to sell, but if his minutes stay above 28 next year his production will keep stalling and he becomes unsellable at a worse price. This is a role decision for next season, not a trade.

**McCabe** at 59 points in 74 games is 0.80 pts/g. Slight fade from 0.83 at 66 games in March 4 but still a top-pairing number. He stays off the sell list. No change.

**Fischer** at 0.51 pts/g and **Kaberle** at 0.59 pts/g are both keepers per your standing orders. Neither is on the list.

Sell order is unchanged in name: Eminger, Klesla. What has changed is certainty. Eminger has added zero points since I flagged him. Klesla's slide continues with no minutes increase. Neither is moving back off.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-19
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-19

Toronto 52-12-4, 118 pts after 73 games.

## Role coverage

The structural question at three days from the deadline: can the roster cover its own gaps, or do we need to buy someone? The answer is one hard gap that only a trade fixes, one soft gap the coach can partially manage, and one confirmed contradiction finally resolved.

**Toughness is the confirmed structural gap.** Zero players at 80+ TOUG in stored grades. Jackman 75, McCabe 73, Tucker 70, Sundin 69. The Feb 21 reading that showed six players above 80 was inflated by form; the stored numbers have never reached 80 on anyone. The Feb 24 contradiction is resolved: the gap is real, it has always been real. No internal move closes it. The highest TOUG we can dress tonight is 75, and that's Jackman on a top pair.

**Faceoffs are thin.** Sundin 90 is the only player at 80+, and he's 34 with 34 games played. Chlup at 75 and Richards at 70 are the next two centres. The Feb 23 move putting Richards on L3 for faceoff duty helps the matchup but does not create a second 80+ winner. This is a one-deep position, and the one is ageing.

**Avery is back.** The Feb 21 rationale that killed the Avery target was "the toughness gap is a form reading, not structural." The gap is now confirmed structural: 0 at 80+ TOUG. Avery at LA carries 83 TOUG, 93 FACE, 88 CHKG, $400K, and two years left. He closes toughness AND faceoffs simultaneously. LA at 48 points with 13 expiring contracts are the most motivated seller in the league. The original kill condition no longer holds.

**Tucker** at 83 CHKG, 70 TOUG, $1.3M, 30 years old, is on the roster and in no unit. His checking is our fifth-best internal option. The coach's report already flags ice-time issues for others; Tucker is the one internal asset providing nothing at all right now. Dressing him nightly for 15 MPG of fourth-pair and PK work adds checking depth the team has available without spending anything.

**Upshall** at 80 CHKG and 21 is the last young checker. The Coach flagged him needing 10+ MPG. He's the depth behind Tucker and Fischer (82 CHKG, 24). Neither closes TOUG, but both extend our checking bench beyond the top three pairs.

**Abid** at 86 overall, 24, produces 0.84 pts/g on 12.6 MPG. He appears in scoring but not in checking or toughness, which means his CHKG and TOUG are below 80 in stored grades. Earlier notes citing "base 80 TOUG and 80 CHKG" were reading displayed numbers inflated by form. The coach's request to give him 18+ MPG is a production argument, not a physical one.

**The tradeoff to the GM:** our only draft asset (the 4th-rounder) is earmarked for Havlat (Feb 26 note). Avery needs something too. If LA will take a cheap expiring piece plus a late pick, Tucker at $1.3M is the filler, and we keep the 4th for Havlat. If LA demands the 4th, it's a choice between the physical gap and the scoring depth, not both.

## Trajectory

Is this club's future safe, or does it dissolve in one July? The answer: safe only if GM locks 5-6 year deals on the young core the week the season ends. Everything else is secondary to that.

**The cluster is the whole problem.** 13 contracts worth $21.30M expire in one summer. That covers Gaborik ($1.10M, 86 pts), Richards ($1.00M, 64 pts), Nash ($1.20M, 35 pts, POTE 95), Eminger ($1.20M, POTE 99), Abid ($0.40M, 66 pts, POTE 94), Kaberle ($1.90M, 38 pts), Upshall ($1.20M, POTE 99), Chistov ($1.10M, POTE 95), Colaiacovo ($1.10M, POTE 99), Alexeev ($1.10M, POTE 94), Roberts ($2.70M), Tellqvist ($0.80M), and Belfour ($6.50M). The first ten are the franchise. If they walk in July, Toronto goes from 118 points to a rebuild in one offseason.

**The money is there to lock them.** Payroll $60.04M against $90.02M revenue leaves $23.25M profit. Even if every young expiring deal doubles or triples at renewal, the new payroll lands around $70-75M and profit stays in the teens. Revenue is built on prestige 587 and one cup, and that grows with winning. The constraint is not whether Toronto can afford these players; it is whether the GM can actually get them signed before a bidding war.

**Sundin is the long-term anchor and the long-term risk.** $8.40M for 5 years at age 34, POTE 60. That is $42M total for a player who will be 39 when the deal ends and whose grade will only decline. There is no mid-contract renegotiation, so this cost is locked. It is not fatal, but it eats the single largest payroll slot every year while the rest of the roster grows into its prime. The club is buying present production at a premium, which is a legitimate choice at 118 points, but it means the 2008-09 roster carries a 38-year-old at $8.40M doing replacement-level minutes.

**The age shape is good.** 14 players under 24, 11 in the 24-29 band, 4 veterans at 34+. The manual's target is met on both counts. The 30-33 gap (Tucker alone) does not matter because the 24-29 group is thick: McCabe, Kaberle, Afinogenov, Fischer, Luongo, Abid, Richards, Jackman, Koltsov, Ouellet. When the old guard falls away in two seasons, the bridge is already there.

**Draft capital is nil.** One fourth-rounder. Every trade must be player-for-player. The over-80 expiring mechanic applies only to Belfour now ($6.50M, 39, expiring). That is the only source of picks in the next four months. If he walks in July instead of being traded, the club gains zero and loses a potential asset.

**Chlup needs an extension before next July.** He has 2 years left at $2.34M with POTE 95 at age 19. If he repeats this season's 50 pts at higher ice time, his price in July 2006 doubles or triples. Lock him to 5-6 years the moment the game allows it, same as Gaborik.

## Calendar

**Today is the deadline, and the one irreversible decision left is Belfour.** At 52-12-4 and 118 points, Toronto do not need to fix anything on the ice. The risk is not losing the playoff; it's walking away from $6.50M of expiring asset value at zero. Every day past today, the over-80 pick-recovery mechanic dies with him.

**Belfour** at 92 base, 39, $6.50M expiring is the last over-80 pick-recovery asset on the roster. Svehla is confirmed not expiring, so that path is closed. Roberts at 38, $2.70M is the other over-80 expiring piece. If Belfour is not moved today, no pick comes back and he either walks in July or re-signs on reduced terms at the GM's option — but the pick capital is gone permanently either way.

**Colorado** offered Hejduk for Belfour. Morris (COL, D, 26, 85 base, 57 pts/65 GP, $1.70M expiring) is the better return: younger, cheaper, fills blue-line depth. The GM should test Morris before accepting Hejduk. If neither is acceptable to Colorado today, any other over-80 expiring rental on any seller works. The only requirement is that Toronto receive a draft pick, any round.

**Roberts** at 38, $2.70M expiring is the second over-80 pick-recovery candidate. If he's rostered and not protected, move him today to any non-playoff team for a pick. He cannot be re-signed at value anyway.

**Havlat** (OTT, 23, 87 base, 80 pts/63 GP, $900K expiring) remains the lead scoring upgrade. The package is Tucker plus the 4th-rounder. This only works if Belfour goes for a player return (Hejduk or Morris), not a pick, because the 4th is the only pick Toronto owns. If Belfour goes for a pick instead, the 4th is gone and Havlat is unreachable.

**The summer is the real work.** Thirteen contracts worth $21.40M expire. Ten of them are the young core under 25. The plan from December was staggered locks; that plan is still correct.

**Gaborik** at 91 base, 23, 67 pts/45 GP, $1.10M — six years, the first phone call in July. He is the best player on the expiring list and the most likely to start a bidding war.

**Kaberle** at 27, $1.90M, improving — five or six years. He is the first-pair defenseman next season.

**Eminger** at 21, $1.20M, POTE 99 — five or six years. Cheap now, expensive later if he breaks out. Lock him.

**Richards** at 24, $1.00M — five years. He is the third-line center and a 24-year-old with 70 FACE. Reasonable cost for a long-term middle-sixer.

**Nash** at 20, $1.20M — the Coach flagged a rate halving (0.43 pts/g at 20). Renew for three years rather than five or six. Let the next season's production determine whether he earns a star deal later.

**Colaiacovo** at 22, $1.10M — three or four years. He is a second-pair blueliner, not a franchise piece. Do not overpay the length.

**Upshall** at 21, $1.20M, and **Chistov** at 21, $1.10M — two years each. Neither has proven himself. Two years is cheap optionality.

**Alexeev** at 23, $1.10M and **Abid** at 24, $0.40M — two years. Depth roles, cheap, no reason for long terms.

**Tellqvist** at 25, $0.80M — the GM's standing order is to keep him. Two years. He is the development project behind Luongo.

**Belfour** at 39 — if not traded today, do not re-sign. Offer one year at $3.5M max in July; he will likely decline or retire, and that is the correct outcome. Luongo at 91 base with two years left is the number one. Ouellet or a low-cost free-agent backup fills the spare.

**Roberts** at 38, $2.70M — if not traded today, release. There is no role for him next season.

**Marleau** (SJ, 25, 89 base, 98 pts) and **Gagne** (PHI, 25, 86 base, 94 pts) both hit UFA in July from clubs that cannot afford them. If Toronto's revenue supports it, either one is a top-line winger who changes the playoff ceiling. This is a July conversation about payroll, not a March conversation.

**The Luongo and DiPietro monitoring task is complete.** Luongo arrived in February at 91 base with two years left. DiPietro at 52 GP still reads 79 base; the high-90s goalie target requires a grade he does not have and never will. Both are closed.

## League scan

The deadline is within days and the confirmed structural gap is toughness and faceoffs at the same time. No internal move fixes it. The league has two players who close both gaps on re-signable deals at prices that don't cost our only pick.

**Avery** (LA, C, 25) is the primary target. TOUG 83, FACE 93, CHKG 88, $400K, two years left. LA at 69 points with 15 expiring contracts is the most motivated seller in the league. He is cheap, young enough to grow with the core, and his contract does not expire this July. The Feb 16 note deprioritised him on production (0.11 ppg), but the gap we need filled is physical, not offensive. At $400K over two years, even 10 points a season at 12 MPG of fourth-line and PK work is a net positive. Price: Tucker at $1.3M expiring as salary filler. No pick required. LA gets salary relief and a depth D; we get the two grades we cannot produce internally.

**Havlat** (OTT, RW, 23) is the secondary target for scoring depth. 87 base, 80 points in 63 games, $900K expiring. OTT at 67 points with 11 expiring cannot re-sign him. The Feb 26 package is Tucker plus the 4th-rounder. If we ship Tucker to LA for Avery, we lose the Havlat package's salary component. The 4th alone might not be enough for OTT. If we can't get both Avery and Havlat, Avery is the higher priority: Havlat is a rental that walks in July unless re-signed, and at 87 base with 80 points, ATL's Kovalchuk/Heatley conversation (78 pts, 11 expiring) might offer a better wing next year.

**Reid** (STL, RW, 23) is a value alternative to Havlat at lower cost. FACE 80, POTE 94, $600K expiring, 77 base. STL at 71 points with 8 expiring. He does not close the TOUG gap but does close the faceoff gap at the wing, and at POTE 94 he has five more years of development ahead. A cheap expiring piece or the 4th alone might move him.

**Bell** (CHI, C, 24) closes all three gaps (TOUG 95, CHKG 93, FACE 87) better than anyone available. The GM killed him on Feb 25 because the faceoff argument didn't hold when both Bell and our centre were wings. But the coverage phase now confirms zero rostered players at 80+ TOUG, which was the kill's hidden premise. The premise is dead. The problem is CHI: 65 points but $26.71M profit, so they don't need to sell. Any package needs a real piece. With our draft capital at one 4th and our protected core locked by standing orders, we cannot build a package CHI accepts tonight. He stays as a July target if CHI re-signs nobody.

**Theodore** (MTL, G, 28) at 91 base matches the Jan 15 goalie order, but the Feb 19 order is "goalies are solved" and the Feb 21 re-opening was about Belfour's return, not acquiring a new starter. I will not propose this.

**Marleau** (SJ, 25, 89 base, 98 pts, $1.60M expiring) remains a July UFA target per the Mar 16 note. SJ at 63 points with 13 expiring cannot hold him. No deadline path exists without a third party or offering protected pieces.



**Delivered:** Task #2 (Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro for goalie trade window) is complete. Luongo is on our roster at 91 base with 2 years left. DiPietro was eliminated on March 14 after a full 52-game sample still reading 79 base. The standing order for a high-90s goalie remains unfulfilled league-wide; Theodore at 91 is the only candidate and MTL has no deadline motivation to dump him given the goalie situation is closed per standing order.

## Trade construction

The deadline is today and the only confirmed structural gap is toughness and faceoffs simultaneously — zero players at 80+ TOUG in stored grades, one faceoff winner at Sundin (34, 90 FACE). Two proposals close it without touching the protected core, and one exploratory package addresses the Belfour question the GM has been hypothesizing about since February 21.

**Avery from LA via Koltsov** is the primary recommendation. LA at 48 points with 13 expiring contracts is a pure rebuild; they want youth and potential, not a 30-year-old checking wing. Koltsov (23, POTE 94, ACCE 96, AGIL 92, $1.10M, 2 years left) is exactly what a 48-point team wants: cheap, fast, unproven, two years of control. His 18 points in 35 games shows he's not breaking out yet, which means we're not overpaying on production. Avery gives us TOUG 83, FACE 93, CHKG 88 on a two-year deal at $400K. The structural gap closes on both axes. We save $700K/year in salary. LA's GM sees a first-rounder-in-waiting at a bargain price; the record and the payroll both support his side. Acceptance is uncertain — the AI may weight Avery's production (0.11 ppg) higher than the grades suggest it should.

**Havlat from OTT via Tucker plus the 4th** is the secondary. Tucker (30, $1.3M, 2 years, CHKG 92, TOUG 88) plays 3 games and produces 1 point. He is the only roster asset providing nothing while carrying real value to a bottom-feed team. OTT at 67 points with 11 expiring contracts is in sell mode and needs picks and cheap physical depth for their own rebuild. Havlat at 87 base with 80 points in 63 games gives Toronto a legitimate second-line wing for the playoffs alongside Gaborik (86 pts). The risk: this spends our only pick. If the Avery deal lands first, we've paid Tucker for Havlat and kept nothing for July. Both proposals together require the 4th-rounder, so the order matters — attempt Avery first (no pick needed), then decide if the Havlat package is worth the last asset.

**Belfour to Colorado for Morris** is exploratory per the GM's Feb 21 hypothesis. Belfour at 39, $6.5M expiring, 18-3 with a 2.27 GAA in 21 games, is the most attractive playoff goalie rental in the league. Colorado at 72 points with no reliable starter would accept. Morris (26, 85 base, 57 pts/65 GP, $1.70M expiring) is younger and cheaper than Hejduk and fills our blue-line depth. But the GM's own Feb 21 criterion is "someone who is good but is locked on a reasonable salary for a couple of years" — Morris is expiring, so he fails that test. I would not execute this without explicit GM sign-off given the Feb 19 operational stance that "Belfour stays" and the stated need for a second capable playoff goalie beyond Ouellet (11 GP this season).

**If none land:** We go into the playoffs at 118 points with the best record, the fastest roster, Gaborik at 86 points, Luongo at 91 in net, and Chlup breaking out at 50 points in 62 games at 19. The toughness gap makes the playoff series harder but does not eliminate us; no single opponent has a physical advantage large enough to overcome a 118-point team's speed and depth. The real work is July: locking 5-6 year deals on the 13 expiring players worth $21.30M. A missing toughness upgrade costs one round; a missing signature costs the franchise.

## Owed

The task was: monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for the goalie trade window, wanted by 2005-02-20.

**Luongo** is on our roster. 94 overall, 2 years left, $1.60M, 42 GP this season. He arrived in January and was confirmed by 2005-02-07. This is closed.

**DiPietro** was eliminated as a target. At 52 GP he still reads 79 base overall, 3.64 GAA, 84.9%. The January 15 standing order required a "really good high-90s goalie." He fails that by 15+ points, and more sample won't close that gap.

**What changed since last reported:** Nothing. Both answers were final before the February 20 deadline. The GM then closed the goalie file entirely on Feb 19 with "Goalies are solved. Done."

The task is delivered. No further monitoring is needed on either name.

# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-19

Next game at CBJ on Sunday 20 March 2005.

## Development opportunity

Against a 24-34 CBJ club, tomorrow is exactly the kind of game where development takes priority over quality, and that changes who should be in the lineup versus a Wednesday night.

**Spezza** is at 37 games, 7.5 MPG, and 15 points on a POTE 99 scouting grade. I have raised this five times without movement, so I will not pretend this is a surprise. But CBJ is 24-34 and this is not a quality night. Per the GM's own framework from January 15th, development takes priority in games we can afford. Dress Spezza.

**Stahle** at 20 with POTE 96 has four games all season. When he plays he gets 17.8 MPG, which tells me whoever lines him up sees him as a real defenceman. Four games at that age is burying him. Give him a three-game run starting against CBJ and judge from there.

**Alexeev** at 0.55 pts/g on 8.3 MPG is the most productive of the scratched group. At 23 he's past the "needs a chance to grow" stage, but his per-minute rate is better than Upshall's (0.32 pts/g on 8.5 MPG) and he's sitting out while Upshall plays. Worth noting for the GM's roster decisions even if not a development call.

**Spacek** at 7.6 MPG season average is low for a 19-year-old with POTE 91, but I already conceded the 10 MPG threshold is mathematically dead. His 0.34 pts/g is modest and the fourth line is where his minutes live. I am not pushing further.

**The core group is fine.** Gaborik at 20.4 MPG and 86 points owns the first line. Chlup at 16.6 MPG and 50 points on the second line is where he belongs. Nash, Klesla, Eminger, and Chistov are all at 55+ games with substantial minutes. Nobody in that group is being wasted.

## Development trends

The question: who's on an upswing heading into next season and who's slipping off the roster or the lineup? This matters now because the season ends in 9 games and the GM needs to know which young players earned their spot and which veterans to plan around.

**Chlup** is the clear riser. 0.62→0.86 pts/g while his minutes doubled from 11.0 to 18.0. At 19, a player under doubled load should produce less; he produced more. His breakout from February is confirmed over 49 games, not a hot streak. He's a top-nine centre now, full stop.

**Chistov** is the quiet one. 0.29→0.36 pts/g on 9.5→14.3 MPG at 21. His rate went up while his minutes went up, which means he's earning them. Slow, steady, the right direction for a 21-year-old winger.

**Kaberle** is trending up at 27. 0.54→0.61 pts/g on 19.4→21.8 MPG. Peak-age defenceman getting more ice and producing more with it. The keeper decision looks right.

**Spezza** is the problem child. 0.43→0.38 pts/g on minutes falling from 9.1 to 5.3 across 37 games. He's 21 with POTE 99 and he's playing fourth-line minutes in a year that is already dead. This is the eighth time I've raised it. The year is gone; the offseason plan needs to include giving him a real role or moving him.

**Spacek** at 19: 0.55→0.28 on 16.0→5.2 MPG over 50 games. The year is over. Don't dress him for development purposes anymore; there's nothing to develop at five minutes a night.

**Koltsov** is at 0.28 pts/g across 25 games since his early-season hot start of 1.10 in 10 games. The trading chip is evaporating in real time. Any club looking at him now sees a 23-year-old at 0.28 over the last two months, not the October flash. The window to get anything for him closes after this season.

**Nash** at 20: 0.83→0.42 on flat minutes (12.9→12.6). The role didn't change, the production did. This is a system-fit question for the offseason.

**Jackman** at 24: 0.65→0.42 on 30.1→30.4 MPG. 71 games at 30 minutes with declining output. At 24, his body is telling him this load doesn't work. He needs a better partner or a lower-morning role next season.

**Abid** at 24: 1.09→0.82 on 20.1→12.4 MPG. His rate fell as his minutes fell. 0.82 on 12.4 MPG is a top-six winger's rate on a fourth-liner's ice. The minutes cut was wrong.

**Veterans** are aging on schedule. Mogilny at 36 is 1.62→0.82 on 16.9→19.2 MPG. Roberts at 38 is 1.29→0.86 on 16.5→21.4 MPG. Sundin at 34 is 1.46→0.94 on 16.9→21.7 MPG. The first-window numbers are small samples from hot starts; the second-window rates are the real levels. Mogilny at 0.82 and Roberts at 0.86 are still contributing, but they won't hold at 37 and 39. Sundin at 0.94 at 34 with 21.7 MPG is the best of the three but shows age.

**Gaborik** at 1.06 on 21.2 MPG across 49 games is still elite at 23. The 1.42 from his first 24 games was unsustainable. No concern.

**Richards** at 0.81 on 16.3 MPG is solid at 24. The drop from 1.08 in a 24-game sample is mostly regression.

The GM should start offseason planning around replacing Mogilny and Roberts's roles. Both are still effective at 0.82 and 0.86, but neither will repeat at 37 and 39. Chlup and Chistov are the internal answers waiting.

## Morale watch

The room is right. Nearly every player sits at 99 morale, and the trend across recent saves is upward with several showing +5 jumps, meaning results are feeding the model well. No morale-driven line change is needed.

**Spezza** is the lone exception at 86, the lowest on the roster. He's played 37 games at 7.5 MPG and is currently scratched. His minutes when he plays match a 70-79 band, so the ice-time lever isn't the issue here. Being healthy and inactive is the problem, and that's the GM's scratch call, not mine. At 86 he's giving back 1 grade across the board, so if there's a game where we can afford to dress him for a shift or two, it keeps him from sliding into the 70s where the cost doubles.

**Spacek** at 89 is borderline but fine on minutes. He sits at 7.6 MPG on the fourth line, which matches his band. The 89 is almost certainly results-driven and should continue climbing with the current streak. The 10 MPG season-end target is already dead per the March 11 finding, so there's nothing to adjust there either.

**Abid** at 99 and 14.7 MPG with 66 points (0.90 pts/g) remains the production-to-ice-time mismatch already flagged, but morale hasn't moved on him across any save, so there's no morale trigger to act on this week. If he drops into the 90s, the argument for bumping him to 17 becomes urgent.

No changes to the lines for morale purposes.

## Role composition

The question is whether our units are built right and whether we have the roles covered at all. Against a 24-34 CBJ club this matters less than it would against a top team, but it's worth confirming before I tell the GM to hold steady.

**L1** — Sundin, Roberts, Jackman, Gaborik, Fischer. Checking mean 82, speed 92, scoring 89. This is a top line that can carry play, win draws (Sundin 91, Roberts 76), and kill penalties when needed. No arrangement problem here.

**L2** — Chlup, Mogilny, McCabe, Kaberle, Afinogenov. Checking mean drops to 70, toughness to 64. This is a scoring line (87/95) that won't win the puck battle, but that's what a second line does when Mogilny is 94 scoring and Afinogenov 92. McCabe at 84 checking gives one anchor. Acceptable.

**L3** — Eminger, Richards, Klesla, Nash, Chistov. Checking 74 mean is decent, speed 90 is actually higher than L2. Richards at 75 faceoffs is the best draw man outside the top two lines. Nash has been producing at 0.43 pts/g on 12.7 MPG, which is below what a third-liner should carry, but moving him down to L4 takes speed off L3 and Abid is already there. Leave it.

**L4** — Spacek, Abid, Upshall. Faceoff mean 52, best 53. This is the known void. Nobody on this line can win a draw. Abid provides the only physical element (72 checking, 72 toughness). Spacek is at 8.3 MPG season average and playing 12+ when dressed. No bench option fixes this; it's a roster gap.

**K2 is our best checking unit** at 84 mean (Jackman 90, McCabe 84, Chlup 80 draws, Abid physical). That's by design and it's working. K1 is a luxury unit with Sundin and Roberts both on the kill.

**Toughness ceiling** tops out at Jackman 77. Nobody on this roster is an enforcer. We can build checking units (four guys at 84+) but we cannot match a physical fourth line that wants to dump-and-chase and finish checks. Against CBJ at 24-34 this won't cost us tonight, but it's a structural limit worth knowing.

**Decision: no changes for Sunday.** Every unit suits its purpose for what we have. The two gaps (L4 faceoffs, toughness ceiling) are roster-level problems that no line shuffle fixes.

## Opponent matchup

This is a Sunday night game against the worst team we face all year, and the question is whether CBJ demands anything we are not already giving them. They do not.

**CBJ's top line** is Marchant at 82 OVR with a 93 faceoff, flanked by Sanderson at 83 and Vyborny at 78. Marchant wins draws against anyone except Sundin, and our top two centres are Sundin at 91 and Chlup at 80. Their third and fourth lines sit at 67-77 OVR. They score 1.60 goals per game. They are a bottom-five offence in a 24-34-6 record.

**Auto-pairing works for us here.** Our first line faces their first pair (Kalinin/Sydor at 78/74 OVR), and their first line faces Fischer/Jackman at 84/85. Our second line draws their second pair (Yushkevich/Grand-Pierre at 74/75). There is no slot reordering that improves these matchups; they are already favorable across the board.

**CBJ's power play is 21 goals on 267 chances — 7.9 percent.** Our penalty kill is not under any specific threat this game. Our own power play at 37.5 percent (30/80) against a team that will need to take penalties to keep up is the main scoring opportunity.

**This is not a quality opponent**, so the game-classification rule from January 15 says development minutes are available here. That is a choice the GM can make in-game by giving the fourth line more shifts. No lineup rearrangement is needed to enable it.

**Goalie:** Belfour has started the last four wins. He is 39 and carries the fatigue check per the January 19 standing order. If his fatigue icon shows tired on screen, Aebischer starts. If not, Belfour continues.

**Defenceman sell-order update (standing task #1):** Per-game defensive data is not available to me. From season totals, the order remains Eminger (0.44 pts/g), Salo (0.18), Klesla (0.38). Jackman at 0.48 on 30.4 MPG is the structural concern for next year but is not on the sell list — he is 24 and the problem is load management, not the player. McCabe is confirmed off the list at 0.83. No change this week.

## Owed

Standing job #1: defencemen sell list update for the end of the season.

**McCabe** at 59 points in 73 games (0.81 pts/g) and 22.4 MPG. Was 0.83 over 66 games on March 4; now 0.81 over 73. Still off the sell list on production, but the slide is worth noting: 29 years old with four years left at $3.00M. If he breaks 0.75 next season he goes back on the list because the contract makes him unsellable at that point.

**Jackman** at 35 points in 71 games (0.49 pts/g) on 30.3 MPG. Unchanged from March 14 when I called the season collapse confirmed. The $0.70M contract means he's not a payroll problem, but 30 MPG at 0.49 is a role that produces nothing. Next season he either drops to 22 MPG on a second pair or we find someone else to eat those minutes. Not a sell at $0.70M, but a role-change.

**Klesla** at 27 points in 73 games (0.37 pts/g) on 14.8 MPG at age 22. Was 0.38 on February 21, now 0.37. Third consecutive declining season expected-direction is up at 22. Contract is $0.90M x 2, so no urgency, but he belongs second on the sell list.

**Eminger** at 21 points in 55 games (0.38 pts/g) at 21, contract expiring at $1.20M. Season rate has slipped from the 0.44 I cited in February to 0.38 now. Below the 0.45 threshold I set January 26. He's the first man to go.

**Salo** is off the roster. That line item is closed.

**Fischer, Kaberle** stay. The GM made both keepers on the record.

Sell order as of today: Eminger, Klesla. Jackman is a role-change, not a sell. McCabe is a watch-list item for next year, not this one.

# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-16

Toronto 51-12-4, 116 pts after 72 games.

## Role coverage

**Which roster roles are genuinely uncovered heading into the last 11 games and the playoffs, and which gaps are fixable without a trade?**

**Tucker** is the single most important word in this phase. His displayed CHKG is 83, his stored TOUG is 88, and he sits in no unit. Dressing him nightly takes the lined checkers from three to four and brings back the internal toughness the Feb 21 finding identified as the free floor. The coach should use him for the playoff run; he costs nothing and gives the bottom pair a real body.

**Toughness** reads zero at 80+ on displayed grades (Jackman 75 is the best) but six players carry stored TOUG at 80+. Tucker's 88 stored versus 70 displayed is an 18-point drag from engine form. The gap is a form artifact across the whole club, not a roster deficiency. No external toughness trade is needed. This resolves the Feb 24 contradiction permanently.

**Faceoffs** are the one genuine structural gap: only Sundin at 90 clears 80+. Chlup sits at 75, Richards at 70, Tucker at 67. Four lines need three or four faceoff men. The GM killed the Bell trade on Feb 25 for the correct reason (both are wings), and Avery's 0.11 ppg kills him as a value proposition. Richards at 70 is the best available center behind Sundin; sliding him to third-line centre for draw duty is the free fix. No trade should be spent here.

**Scoring depth by age** is a next-season problem, not a deadline target. Mogilny at 94 and 36 years old, Roberts at 88 and 38 — together they carry third and fourth line scoring tonight. Next year Mogilny is 37 and Roberts 39. The top six (Gaborik 23, Sundin 34, Afinogenov 25, Richards 24, Kaberle 27, Abid 24) is young and covered. The bottom-six scoring beyond them is not. That is a summer problem.

**Durability** is thin at four players clearing 80+ (Roberts 98, Afinogenov 95, Fischer 92, Abid 90). With Mogilny and Roberts at the front of the scoring group and a playoff run starting in two weeks, this is a structural concern but not something the trade market solves. Injury resistance is not something another GM prices highly.

**Checking** is adequate with Tucker lined. Jackman 87, Roberts 86, McCabe 86, Tucker 83, Fischer 82, Upshall 80. That is six players at 80+, four of whom can realistically dress in a unit. The Feb 21 finding was correct: the "gap" was a form reading on displayed grades.

**Goalies** are solved per the Feb 19 order. Luongo at 87.7 mean and 2 years, Belfour at 92.1 and expiring, Ouellet at 77.6 as the playoff backup. Tellqvist is depth. No change needed.

## Trajectory

**The July 2005 renewal cliff is the defining problem: 13 players on 1-year deals worth $21.30M come up together, and six of them are the core that must be locked on 5-6 year terms or the roster disintegrates.** The age shape is healthy (14 at ≤23, 11 in 24-29, 4 at 34+), close to the manual's target, but the contract structure puts the whole young core at risk in a single summer.

**Gaborik** is the priority. 85 points in 72 games at 23 with 91 base overall on $1.10M is a franchise winger at a rookie price. He must get 5-6 years in July. A 5-year deal at $5-6M is the realistic ask given his production, and at 23 he has seven more peak seasons.

**Eminger and Nash** are next. Eminger at 21 with POTE 99 has 21 points in 54 games and will grow into a top-pairing defenseman. Nash at 20 with POTE 95 has 35 points in 59 games. Both are locked on $1.20M currently; re-sign before a breakout season erases that price. Upshall (POTE 99, 21, 19 pts) and Chistov (POTE 95, 21) belong in the same batch.

**Richards** is the most expensive of the group at 63 points in 70 games, age 24, POTE 88. He should get 5 years, but his ask will be higher, perhaps $4-5M. That's still a bargain for a second-line center who controls faceoffs.

**Kaberle** at 27, 38 points in 64 games, $1.90M, POTE 75 is a 2-3 year renewal, not a 5-6. His ceiling is set and his value peaks now. Sign him short and cheap.

**Belfour** at $6.50M, 39, 92 base, is the salary-relief target. Letting him walk saves $6.50M and frees a spot for Ouellet or Tellqvist as backup. The GM's exploration of a trade is correct; the over-80 expiring mechanic can recover a pick even if the trade market is soft. The Feb 21 standing order to hedge against retirement is the right frame.

**Roberts** at $2.70M, 38, should walk. His 70 points are valuable tonight but he is on the wrong side of the age curve for the dynasty's next window.

**Fischer** is the slow poison: $3.70M locked for 4 more years at 0.49 ppg, 33 points in 67 games. Not tradeable now at that contract, but it's dead money through 2009 if he doesn't produce. Accept it for now and plan to use him as a salary-matching piece in 2007.

**The money works.** Payroll $60.04M against revenue $88.37M leaves $23.99M profit. If the six young-core renewals add $18-22M in total salary (Gaborik $5M, Eminger $4M, Nash $4M, Upshall $3.5M, Chistov $3M, Richards $5M, offset by losing Belfour $6.5M and Roberts $2.7M), the net payroll jumps to roughly $72-75M. Profit drops to $13-16M. That is still workable, especially with playoff revenue and prestige at 585.

**Draft capital is nil.** A single fifth-rounder cannot fund any deal. All trade ammunition must come from players. This is why the over-80 expiring mechanic on Belfour matters: it's the only way Toronto generates a pick this summer.

## Calendar

**Three days to the deadline and one decision remains unmade.** Toronto are 116 points, first in the East by 19. You are buyers at the deadline per the manual, but with no pick above a 4th-rounder the deadline action is moving assets you will not re-sign, not buying with currency you do not own. The summer is a cluster problem: 13 contracts worth $21.30M expire at once, seven of them young core players who need long deals.

**Belfour** is the keystone and it has been since February. 92 base, 39 years old, $6.50M expiring. If he retires in July you lose all of it. Colorado offered Hejduk on your own Feb 21 read. Morris (COL, D, 26, 85 base, 57 pts/65 GP, $1.70M expiring) is the better return on age, cost and positional need, but Morris is also expiring, which fails your own "locked on reasonable salary for a couple of years" test. Hejduk at least carries term. **Decide by March 18.** If you keep him, you need a second goalie for the playoff because Ouellet (81 base) is the only backup and Belfour's retirement risk hangs over every series.

**Roberts** at 87 base is over the 80 threshold, 38, $2.70M expiring. The over-80 pick mechanic applies. Move him to a non-playoff club for a draft pick. You have no pick better than a 4th, and this is the cheapest one available. Per your March 4 correction, send him away from playoff teams.

**Svehla is not expiring.** The brief lists 13 names and his is not among them. The Feb 23 pick-recovery note is void. Drop him from the target list.

**Havlat** remains the scoring upgrade OTT would accept (60 points, 11 expiring). Tucker plus the 4th is the package. If Belfour goes to Colorado for Hejduk, you get scoring from him instead and the 4th stays home for Havlat. If Belfour stays or walks, the Havlat path still works with Tucker + 4th. Either way, do not spend a pick on both.

---

**Gaborik** — 91 base, 23, $1.10M. Lock 5-6 years at season end. This is the single highest-value renewal on the roster and no mid-contract renegotiation is possible per the Jan 15 order. It must wait for July.

**Eminger** — 76 base, 21, $1.20M, POTE 99. Lock 5-6 years. GM-protected since Jan 19.

**Richards** — 82 base, 24, $1.00M. Lock 5-6 years.

**Nash** — 77 base, 20, $1.20M. Lock 5-6 years. The cheapest potential on the roster.

**Kaberle** — 84 base, 27, $1.90M. Three or four years. Prime age, no urgency to go long but no reason to lose him either.

**Tellqvist** — 77 base, 25, $0.80M. Keep per GM's Jan 15 order. Two or three years. High potential, needs time.

**Abid** — 79 base, 24, $0.40M. Cheap. Two years.

**Colaiacovo** — 72 base, 22, $1.10M. Coach wants him in the lineup. Two years at depth pricing.

**Upshall** — 78 base, 21, $1.20M. Two or three years. Same age band as Eminger and Nash but one tier below them on grade. Renew short and reassess.

**Chistov** — 78 base, 21, $1.10M. Two years or move before expiry if a club offers a pick via the under-80 route. He is expendable; the defence in front of him is not.

**Alexeev** — 76 base, 23, $1.10M. Let go unless a roster spot needs filling at $1.10M or less. Four years on this roster already and still 76.

**Belfour, if not traded** — offer two years at a reduced salary per the Jan 15 order. He probably declines. If he does, he walks.

**The summer problem in one line:** seven players under 25 (Nash 20, Upshall 21, Eminger 21, Chistov 21, Colaiacovo 22, Alexeev 23, Gaborik 23, Richards 24, Abid 24, Tellqvist 25) are all free agents on the same day. The staggered plan from December holds: five 5-6 year locks and five 2-3 year deals. Execute the five long deals first, in the order Gaborik, Eminger, Richards, Nash, Upshall. The short deals and the Belfour/Roberts decision follow.

**Luongo monitoring is complete.** He is on the roster at 91 base, 2 years left. DiPietro at 79 base fails the high-90s order and is eliminated permanently. No further work on that task.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: who across the league can Toronto acquire by Friday or this summer to solve the bottom-six scoring cliff that Mogilny (36) and Roberts (38) create in July, and who can serve as a Belfour return? The league scan surfaces three clusters of sellers with elite young players on expiring deals: Chicago, Philadelphia, and San Jose.

**Eric Daze** (CHI, LW, 29, 89 base) has 111 points in 71 games, 51 goals. Chicago sits at 63 points with 10 expiring deals and $27.19M profit. They are selling. At 29 on $3.00M expiring, he is a playoff rental with bridge-deal potential, not a dynasty piece. The production is the best on the board by 13 points. The age limits the dynasty value.

**Patrick Marleau** (SJ, C, 25, 89 base) has 98 points in 70 games on $1.60M expiring. San Jose at 63 points with 13 expiring deals cannot re-sign him at market. At 25, he is the best dynasty fit in the scan: young, a center, cheap to move, seven more peak seasons. The price is the question because we hold no picks.

**Simon Gagne** (PHI, LW, 25, 86 base) has 94 points in 69 games on $2.40M expiring. Philadelphia carries $66.73M payroll against only $4.87M profit. They must shed salary. Gagne at $2.40M becoming a UFA at 25 would cost them a $6-7M contract next year. They will deal.

**Marco Sturm** (PHI, LW, 26, 85 base) has 75 points in 60 games on $1.00M with 92 speed. Same desperate seller. He folds into a Gagne conversation or works as a standalone cheaper option.

**Evgeni Nabokov** (SJ, G, 29, 90 base, $3.60M expiring) is the closest match to the Jan 15 standing order for a high-90s goalie from a non-contender. SJ at 63 points is rebuilding. He does not carry "locked on a couple of years" because he is expiring, but at $3.60M and 29, a re-signing at $4-5M for 3 years is realistic and fits the GM's Feb 21 desire. The problem: SJ has no reason to take Belfour at $6.50M and 39.

**Steve Sullivan** (CHI, RW, 30, 87 base) has 85 points in 71 games, 95 speed, $3.00M expiring. Same Chicago sell window as Daze. At 30, he is a bridge piece. The speed is the best available on the wing.

**Brad Stuart** (SJ, D, 25, 87 base) carries 30.5 MPG and 47 points on $1.80M expiring. Elite workload at 25. Toronto's blue line is adequate (Kaberle, Eminger, McCabe, Fischer, Colaiacovo, Klesla), so he fills a need only if someone moves. Keep him on the radar for summer.

**Todd Marchant** (CBJ, C, 31, 88 base) has 78 points in 70 games on $4.88M expiring. CBJ at 68 points with $15.41M profit are not desperate. The salary is high for a 31-year-old rental. Deprioritized.

**What I would not do:** Chase Daze at 29 when Marleau at 25 gives 98 points and seven more seasons. Chase Marleau first, Gagne second. If both fail, Daze is the insurance. Nabokov belongs in the Belfour conversation but only if SJ will take salary they don't need.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: with three days until the March 19 deadline and no draft capital beyond a single 4th rounder, which packages give Toronto a realistic shot at acquiring a keeper without gutting the dynasty core?

**Belfour to Colorado for Morris** is the strongest proposal on the board. Belfour at $6.50M, age 39, with 92.1 mean and a 2.27 GAA in 21 games is exactly what Colorado needs for a Cup run, and the GM confirmed on Feb 21 that they "would be glad to accept a good goalie as they don't have one now." Morris is 26, 85 base, 57 points in 65 games, $1.70M expiring. He doesn't meet the GM's "locked on a couple of years" criterion because his deal ends in July, but at $1.70M and age 26 he re-signs for $2.5-3.0M over 3-4 years, which is a franchise top-pairing defenseman at a discount. Toronto sheds $4.80M net salary; Colorado absorbs it from a profitable position. The GM's Feb 5 note already flagged Morris as superior to Hejduk on age and cost; the GM should test this before accepting the Hejduk alternative, which costs $6.10M and buys nothing for the 2005-06 roster.

**Tucker plus the 4th-rounder for Havlat** is the second option. Havlat at 23, 87 base, 80 points in 63 games on $900K expiring is the scoring upgrade that fills the Mogilny/Roberts gap in July. Ottawa sits at 60 points with 11 expiring deals and cannot re-sign Havlat at the $4-5M his production demands. Tucker gives them a veteran body for their remaining games (83 CHKG, 88 TOUG stored) and the 4th is a lottery pick for a rebuild. The cost to Toronto is one lottery pick and a player who has appeared in 3 games. If Havlat re-signs at $2.5-3.0M for 4-5 years, this is the dynasty-building trade. If he walks in July, we've paid the 4th for 10 regular-season games of 87-base wing, which is a bad return but not a catastrophic one.

**Acceptance is uncertain on both.** How the AI values Tucker (a 30-year-old with 3 GP) versus Havlat (a 23-year-old with 80 points) is not known. Colorado's appetite for Belfour's $6.50M against their own payroll is not known. These are argued on hockey and money; the machine may decline.

**If neither lands:** Do nothing. The 4th-rounder is the only draft capital we have. Tucker is the free playoff checker. Preserving both costs nothing and the summer renewal window handles everything the deadline could not. A forced trade that surrenders Chistov, Alexeev, or Koltsov (all POTE 94+) for expiring rentals is worse than standing pat.

## Owed

**Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window.**

This task is complete. I'm closing it here.

**Luongo** is on our roster at 93 overall, 2 years remaining, $1.60M, 42 GP. He was the target from the January window and he landed. The Feb 19 order confirmed him as arrived and the goalies as solved. No further monitoring needed.

**DiPietro** is eliminated. He's now at 52 GP and still reads 79 base overall. That was confirmed on March 9 and re-confirmed March 14. The Jan 15 standing order requires a high-90s goalie; no sample size closes an 11-point base deficit. He is permanently off the list.

**What changed since the February report:** Theodore (MTL, G, 28, 91 base, $5.50M expiring, 58 GP) emerged on March 5 as the live target matching the high-90s-from-a-non-contender requirement. Montreal are sellers. This is the active goalie-trade thread now, not Luongo or DiPietro. Belfour is the chip (Feb 21 order), and the return should be a high-90s goalie on a reasonable deal — Theodore fits that profile except for the salary, which is his problem to shed, not ours.

No action required on this owed item. It is delivered.
