# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-11

Toronto 49-12-4, 112 pts after 70 games.

## Role coverage

**The gap that matters now:** With the deadline eight days out and Toronto at 112 points, the only structural hole that no arrangement of the current roster fills is toughness. Every other role has depth. This is the one the GM should know about even if the fix is blocked.

**The toughness contradiction is resolved.** The Feb 21 note claiming six players at 80+ TOUG was reading displayed grades with form applied upward. The stored numbers are what this brief shows: Jackman at 75 is the ceiling, Roberts at 73, McCabe at 73, Tucker at 70. Zero players above 80. The earlier reading was wrong, and the Feb 24 zero-at-80 reading was correct.

**Jackman** sits at 87 CHKG, 75 TOUG, 24 years old, 30.9 minutes a night. The coach's checking concern is a form artifact: the stored checking depth is real (six players at 80+). The toughness concern is not a form artifact. No one here breaks 80 TOUG.

**Tucker** is at 83 CHKG and 70 TOUG, age 29, not currently in any unit. He is the free fourth checker. His displayed numbers may lag his stored grades on a given day, but 83 stored CHKG means he can carry a kill. Dressing him is the internal answer to the coach's checking-line complaint and costs nothing.

**Sundin** is the only faceoff man above 80 (90 FACE). Chlup at 75 FACE, age 19, is the next-best and improving. Roberts sits at 75. This is thin for playoff matchups where the opponent matches a shutdown centre against Sundin every draw, but it is a one-player problem the club can tolerate for a run and Chlup's development closes it within two seasons. No trade needed.

**Scoring and playmaking are covered** by youth: Gaborik 92 at 23, Afinogenov 90 at 25, Richards 85 at 24, Chlup 84 at 19. The Mogilny/Roberts top-end (94/88 at 36 and 38) is the age problem for next July, not a deadline problem.

**Durability** is thin: only four at 80+ (Roberts 98, Afinogenov 95, Fischer 92, Abid 90). Spacek drops to 79, Eminger to 75. The playoff-healthy core is small. Not fixable at the deadline.

## Trajectory

The July 2005 contract cluster is the defining problem of this franchise: 13 players worth $21.30M all hit free agency the same summer, and six of them are POTE 95+ players currently earning $1.10-1.20M each. If the GM does not lock them immediately at season's end, they hit the market at career-year prices and the payroll either doubles or the core walks.

**Gaborik** is the single most expensive re-signing if left to the open market. He is 23, 84 points in 70 games, 91 base, POTE 90, and earning $1.10M. A five-year deal at $4.5-5.5M per year keeps him under control through age 28. If he walks, Toronto loses its best winger for nothing because there is no pick to recover (the over-80 mechanic gives a pick, not a replacement).

**Eminger, Upshall, Nash, Colaiacovo, Chistov** all carry POTE 95 or above on $1.10-1.20M one-year deals. Eminger at 21 with POTE 99 is the franchise defenseman; Nash at 20 with 35 points is a top-six winger; Upshall at 21 with POTE 99 and 18 points is a developing power forward. Lock all five on 5-6 years at season's end. Combined current cost: $5.80M. Combined fair market cost after a breakout year: $20-25M. The savings from acting in July rather than August are real.

**Richards** at 24, 61 points, POTE 88, $1.00M expiring is the same logic one tier down. Five years at $3.5-4M locks a top-nine centre through age 29.

**Kaberle** at 27, $1.90M, POTE 75 with 37 points in 62 games is the oldest of the expiring core and has the lowest upside. Two to three years at $3-3.5M is defensible; a five-year deal at his age carries decline risk.

**Belfour** ($6.50M, 39, expiring) and **Roberts** ($2.70M, 38, 70 points, expiring) are $9.20M that walks regardless. Both are above 80 overall and qualify for the pick-recovery mechanic. Moving either before March 19 recovers a draft pick; releasing them in July recovers nothing. Roberts's 70 points at 38 make him an attractive rental for a contender needing veteran scoring depth.

**Fischer** at $3.70M, four years left, 24 years old, producing 0.41 pts/g on 65 games is a trapped asset. Not tradeable now at that salary with those numbers. He becomes a summer 2007 problem when the contract still has two years and production likely hasn't recovered. Flag it now; do not panic then.

**The age curve** is healthy: 14 players 23 or under, 12 in the 24-29 band, zero at 30-33, four at 34+. The 30-33 gap looks thin but it resolves itself in two years when McCabe turns 31, Tucker turns 31, and Richards turns 26. No bridge signing is needed.

**The money** has room. Payroll at $60.04M against revenue of $88.37M leaves $25.45M profit. Even after the young core's salaries roughly triple (from $1.10-1.20M to $4-5M), payroll rises to roughly $80-85M, still inside revenue. The constraint is not profitability; it is the risk of losing players to other clubs' offers before they can be matched.

**Draft capital** is a single fourth-rounder. This means every trade this season is player-for-player, and if any core player walks, the compensation is one late pick. That is the cost of not locking them.

## Calendar

With 8 days to the 2005-03-19 deadline and 112 points, we are buyers, first in the East by 18 over NJ (94), and our only currency is players: nothing better than a fourth-rounder.

**Belfour** is the whole deadline. 39, $6.50M expiring, 92 base — the one over-80 asset we can convert before the value walks in July. Colorado need a goalie; Hejduk was the offer, but Morris (D, 26, 85 base, $1.70M, 57 pts/65 GP) is the better return on age and money and fills our blue line. Test Morris first, then decide. This has to resolve this week.

**Roberts** (LW, 38, $2.70M) is the second pick-recovery chip under the over-80 rule. He will not be re-signed at 38, so move him by the 19th or lose the capital for nothing.

**The summer cluster** is 13 expiring worth about $22M, ten of them young core. The core signs long, the depth signs short, so they never renew together again.

**Gaborik** (RW, 23, $1.10M, 67 pts/45 GP) is the priority: 5-6 years, no hesitation. **Richards** (C, 24, $1.00M), **Kaberle** (D, 27, $1.90M) and **Nash** (LW, 20, $1.20M) take 5-6 as well — those four are the spine.

**Eminger** (D, 21, $1.20M) and **Chistov** (LW, 21, $1.10M) get 5-6: high potential, and the GM's own order says don't sell the young defence. **Colaiacovo** (D, 22) and **Upshall** (RW, 21) get 2-3, **Alexeev** (RW, 23) and **Abid** (LW, 24, $0.40M) get 2. **Tellqvist** (G, 25, $0.80M) gets 3 — he stays, and goalies are the ones clubs lose by forgetting.

**Belfour and Roberts** are the two names I would not renew. Everyone else on the list is a re-sign.

Owed item #2, goalie monitoring: Luongo is arrived (91 base, 2 years) and the goalie question is closed by your order. DiPietro (NYI, 21, 79 base, 3.64 GAA) fails the high-90s test and is not a Belfour return.

## League scan

The deadline is eight days out. Toronto's one structural hole is toughness (zero players above 80 TOUG), and the thin spot behind Sundin is faceoff depth at centre. This scan found two players who address both without violating any standing order.

**Doan** is the single best deadline target in the league. RW, 28, 87 base, TOUG 88, CHKG 93, 52 points in 67 games, $2.40M expiring. PHX at 71 points with 14 expiring deals cannot re-sign him at market after this year. He is four years younger than the next-best toughness option (Fleury at 36, $4.30M), produces nearly double the points, and costs $1.9M less. He fills the gap AND upgrades the top six simultaneously. Package logic: PHX needs a reason to accept Toronto's expiring assets over a pick. Svehla at $3.60M expiring gives them a veteran D for a one-year push, or Toronto pairs a young blueliner with the 4th.

**Eric Belanger** is the faceoff fix the Jan 25 Bell objection never covered. C, 27, 82 base, FACE 97 (the highest in the league by 7 points), $700K expiring, 11 points in 54 games. LA at 65 points with 15 expiring deals are motivated to move any rental. At $700K, Toronto re-signs him at a reasonable rate in July. He is a centre, so the wing-position objection that killed Bell does not apply. Package: Svehla or Tucker plus the 4th, or straight-up for a late-round pick given his cost.

**Havlat** remains the lead scoring target. LW, 23, 87 base, 86 points in 69 games, $900K expiring. OTT at 65 points with 11 expiring. The Feb 26 package (Tucker plus the 4th) still works if Tucker is available — he is 29, at 83 CHKG, and not in any unit. If the GM considers Tucker too old for a return from a seller, the 4th alone might not move OTT for a 23-year-old with 86 points.

**Kovalchuk** at 114 points in 67 games, 21 years old, $1.10M expiring from ATL (72 points, 11 expiring) is the highest scorer available. But the ATL binary with Heatley means Toronto picks one and can only afford one package. Kovalchuk's TOUG of 78 does not close the toughness gap; it fills scoring, which is already covered by youth. Lower priority than Doan.

**Komisarek** at 72 points from the blue line, age 23, POTE 91, $1.10M expiring from MTL (55 points, 15 expiring) is the best player-for-cost ratio available. But he is a D, and the GM said in February not to sell core defense to acquire another one. He would be a partner for Jackman, not a replacement.

**Sulku** at 20, POTE 92, TOUG 89, CHKG 87, $942K expiring from CGY (54 points, worst in the league) is the development-project toughness option. But at 20 with POTE 92, CGY probably wants to re-sign him despite being terrible. Lower confidence he moves.

**What I would NOT pursue:** Brashear (33, 9 pts in 67 GP) is old enough to be a rental only. Primeau ($4.60M, 3 years, 13 pts in 40 GP) is broken and expensive. Tkachuk at $9.00M is unaffordable as a deadline rental.

## Trade construction

Eight days to March 19. Toronto at 112 points need a toughness upgrade and more top-end scoring, and the only currency available is Tucker, Svehla, Belfour (if the GM commits), and one fourth-rounder. Three proposals rank by impact; the first two can be executed together because they draw on different assets.

**Belfour to Colorado for Morris** is the keystone the GM himself opened on Feb 21. Belfour at 39, $6.50M, 18-3, 2.27 GAA, 0.916 SP in 21 GP is a premium rental for any contender, and the GM raised Colorado explicitly as a team "glad to accept a good goalie." Morris is 26, 85 base, 57 points in 65 games, $1.70M expiring. The trade saves $4.80M, fills blue-line depth with a re-signable player, and hedges the retirement risk the GM flagged. Luongo at 25 with POTE 97 and 2 years left is already confirmed as the starter per the Feb 19 order. Colorado's GM gave Hejduk as the price for Belfour; Morris is younger and fills a position Toronto needs more. Test Morris first, accept Hejduk only if COL refuses to move a defenseman.

**Doan from Phoenix for Tucker plus the 4th** is the single best fit. RW, 28, 87 base, 52 points in 67 games, $2.40M expiring. CHKG 93 and TOUG 88 on the table close the one structural hole the role-coverage phase found: zero Toronto players above 80 stored TOUG. PHX at 71 points is projecting to roughly 83 by season's end, which misses the playoffs. With 14 expiring deals, they cannot re-sign Doan at his market value. Tucker at 29, $1.30M, 2 years of control, CHKG 92 displayed gives them a veteran for a roster reset at half Doan's salary. The 4th-rounder is late-round value on top. Acceptance depends on whether PHX's GM reads his own record as "miss" or "bubble." If he keeps Doan, this does not land and we pivot to Havlat.

**Havlat from Ottawa for Tucker plus the 4th** is the fallback if Doan is blocked. LW, 23, 87 base, 86 points in 69 games, $900K expiring. OTT at 65 points with 11 expiring are clear sellers. The same package moves: Tucker's 2 years at $1.30M plus a late pick. Ottawa cannot re-sign Havlat at 86-point production; the cost of keeping him on a 4-5 year deal would be $4-5M per season against a $900K current salary. The 4th and Tucker are a fair floor price.

These two compete for the same assets: Tucker and the 4th. The GM picks one. Doan closes toughness AND scoring; Havlat closes only scoring. Doan first.

**Move Svehla before March 19** regardless of which scoring deal lands. He is 36, $3.60M expiring, CHKG 92, over-80 overall. The pick-recovery mechanic trades him for a draft pick to any club with capacity. He is not in the lineup for the playoffs and his value walks in July. Any destination, even a non-playoff team. This is independent of the other two deals and should not wait on them.

**If nothing lands, do nothing.** At 112 points with Chlup at 75 FACE and growing at 19, and Jackman's CHKG at 87 stored still climbing, the long-term answers are on the roster. A fourth-line faceoff specialist or a toughness rental is worth acquiring at the right price, not at any price.

**On the Luongo/DiPietro monitoring task** (owed since Jan 19, due Feb 20): this is complete. Luongo is on the roster, 91 base, 42 GP, 2 years left, POTE 97. He is Toronto's starter. DiPietro at 21 is 79 base, 3.64 GAA, 84.9% in 21 GP with NYI and fails the Jan 15 standard of a high-90s goalie from a non-contender. Theodore from MTL at 91 base and POTE 87 remains the only target that matches the standing order, but the Feb 19 "goalies are solved" order applies unless the GM reopens.

## Owed

**The question:** Luongo availability and DiPietro development for the goalie trade window, owed since January 19.

**Luongo is done.** He is on our roster at 93 overall, age 25, $1.60M, two years remaining, 42 GP this season. The monitoring task closed in early February when the acquisition landed. No further action needed on Luongo.

**DiPietro is still not the answer.** He is 79 base at NYI, age 21. The Jan 15 order set a specific bar: "a really good high-90s goalie from a team that will not be a contender." DiPietro fails on the talent axis regardless of how many games he plays. Twenty-one appearances at 3.64 GAA and 84.9% confirm he is not arriving this year or next into high-90s range. Nothing has changed since the March 9 note.

**Theodore remains the target that matches the order.** MTL, 28, 91 base, POTE 87, $5.50M expiring. MTL sit at 51 points with 15 expiring contracts and cannot retain him. This is the only name that satisfies both halves of the standing order: high-90s base and a non-contender who must move him.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-11
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-11

Next game at CGY on Sunday 13 March 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether each young player is getting the games he has earned, and with 12 left in the season, the window to correct any waste is closing.

**Stahle** is still the biggest problem. Four games in 70. POTE 96, 17.8 MPG in the few he's played, 20 years old. Against Calgary at 22-38 this is exactly the development-appropriate opponent the GM's standing order calls for. Dress him tonight.

**Alexeev** is producing 30 points in 55 games (0.55 pts/g) on 8.3 minutes a night. That's top-nine efficiency on bottom-six ice, and now he's scratched. Whatever reason he's out, he is the most efficient young forward on the roster per minute and he's not playing. Dress him against CGY and give him real minutes.

**Spacek** at 8.1 MPG season average cannot mathematically reach the 10 MPG threshold we set on March 5. Even 12 games at 15 MPG only gets him to 9.5. That target is dead. The year's verdict should be based on whether his per-game production improves under the recent bump, not on a number that's now unreachable.

**Spezza** at 37 games, 7.5 MPG, POTE 99, age 21. I've raised this five times. Calgary is 22-38. This is the kind of game where development is supposed to outrank winning. I'm asking a sixth time: dress him against Calgary or accept the year is written off.

**Colaiacovo** has 31 games at 17.9 MPG, which is solid exposure for a 22-year-old defenceman. Scratched tonight, but his development isn't stalled the way Stahle's or Spezza's is. I'd like him in against CGY but he's a second priority behind Stahle.

The rest of the dressed young core is earning it: **Gaborik** (84 pts, L1), **Chlup** (47 pts at 19, L2), **Nash** (35 pts at 20, L3). **Upshall** is producing fourth-line points on fourth-line ice. **Klesla** is playing every game but declining at 0.38 pts/g at age 22; the issue there is quality of play, not opportunity. **Koltsov** is the GM's trading chip, so scratching him makes sense.

## Development trends

Twelve games left, so the numbers from here are what the GM carries into the summer plan. The question is who is trending where.

**Chlup** 0.62→0.85 pts/g on minutes doubling from 11.0 to 18.0 at age 19. He is the cleanest riser on the roster. Production up while load up at that age means he belongs in the top nine permanently. No change needed, just confirmation the February breakout was not a fluke.

**Kaberle** 0.54→0.63 pts/g, minutes up from 19.4 to 22.0. Going up at 27, which is rare for a defenceman at that age. The GM's instinct to protect him is validated by the trend. He is entering his prime on this sheet.

**Eminger** 0.35→0.41 pts/g, minutes up 15.0→16.7 at 21. Quiet positive growth. Not a breakout, just a young D getting more ice and holding his production. Development direction is correct.

**Stahle** 0→4 GP at 17.8 MPG. He finally crossed zero. No points, but four games is four more than December and he got real minutes. Still needs significantly more before the offseason to say anything about his future.

**Koltsov** is the urgent one. 1.10→0.28 pts/g at 23, minutes barely moved (8.7→10.4). The February hot start is gone and his trade value is evaporating with it. The GM's standing order is he stays as a trading chip, but a chip only works while it has value. Offseason trades are where he goes.

**Klesla** 0.50→0.30 pts/g at 22 on flat minutes of 15.0. The February flag holds: second consecutive declining season, minutes flat, wrong direction at 22. He joins Eminger and Salo in the sell queue.

**Nash** 0.83→0.45 pts/g at 20 with minutes steady at 12.5. A halving of production at 20 with no minute change is a concerning stall. Not fatal yet, but it needs watching through the offseason.

**Jackman** 0.65→0.38 pts/g on 30+ MPG. The March collapse has not reversed. At 24 the expected direction is up; he is going the other way while playing more than anyone on the roster. If this holds into the summer his 30 MPG allocation is questionable and his trade value drops fast.

**Spezza** is still at 5.3 MPG in 37 games at age 21. I have raised this every activation since January. With 12 games left the season is effectively over for him as a development project. He needs a real minutes commitment next training camp or the POTE is wasted.

**Spacek** season average of 5.6 MPG across 47 games. My March criterion was "above 10 by season's end or the year is dead." He is below 8, so by that measure the year is dead. He gets the remaining minutes he gets but next season needs a fresh argument.

**Mogilny** at 36: 1.62→0.81 pts/g. Expected age decline, but he is still producing at top-six rates. The planning question is who fills the 19 MPG he is still getting. No action now, but the transition window is one to two seasons.

**McCabe** 1.42→0.50 pts/g at 29. The hot October start masks a season averaging roughly 0.82 over 70 games. The recent 46-game rate of 0.50 is his true level. My March note took him off the sell list based on the season average, which is fair, but the trend is clearly down and four years at $3M is an expensive problem if 0.50 is the new 0.50.

**Sundin and Roberts** are both declining from hot starts (Sundin 1.46→0.93 at 34, Roberts 1.29→0.85 at 38) but both remain productive. No concern beyond the obvious: they are getting old and the roster needs to be ready.

## Morale watch

The room is happy. Average morale sits above 92 and nearly every player is trending upward on the winning streak. One name stands out.

**Spezza** is at 86, +1 only, and has been sitting in the 80s for weeks. He's 21, 15 points in 37 games on 7.5 MPG, and he's been buried on the fourth line or scratched since December. At whatever his overall is now (likely 80s given the development path), he expects 17 minutes a night and gets less than half. The -1 morale penalty to every grade is small but it's permanent while the minutes stay where they are. I've raised this five times. If the GM wants him developing, 12+ MPG on the third line alongside Nash and Chistov would fix it. If he doesn't, accept the year is a writeoff and stop dressing him.

**Safronov** dropped 5 points to 95. Only 3 games played, 13.7 MPG, scratched. The drop is results-driven (the locker room effect), not minutes-driven. No action from me.

**Jackman** is at 30.5 MPG with morale maxed at 99. The winning masks the load problem, but my production finding stands: 0.38 pts/g on rising minutes. The morale won't tell me he's burning out until it's too late. That's a trajectory concern, not a morale one, so I'm not moving him tonight.

Everyone else is at 96-99 and climbing. No changes needed on morale grounds.

## Role composition

**Are these units built from the right players for their jobs, and does the roster hold enough of each role?**

**L1 through L3 look correct.** L1 has Gaborik (97 scoring, 99 playmaking) with Sundin (89 faceoffs) at the dot and Jackman (88 checking) behind them. That's an offensive top line with a shutdown D pair underneath. L2 is the scoring line by design — Mogilny (92), Afinogenov (90), Kaberle quarterbacking — and McCabe at 82 is the one checking anchor it needs without diluting the offence. L3 has Richards (92 checking, 95 clutch) as the pest, Chistov (96 speed) as the skate, and Nash providing size. Each line does what its number suggests.

**Power play units are fine.** P1 has Gaborik and Sundin as shooters with Kaberle on the point — the right personnel. P2 has Mogilny (92 scoring) as the primary shooter with Richards (92 checking) providing the net-front presence and faceoff ability if they pull him. No one is on a unit he doesn't suit.

**K1 versus K2 is a wash.** K2 has better checking mean (82 vs 76) through Jackman and McCabe, but K1 has Sundin (91 scoring) and Roberts, which means short-handed scoring chances. I don't know for certain whether K1 gets more short-handed ice than K2 in this game, so I'm not moving either unit. Neither is wrong.

**Fourth-line faceoffs remain the one structural gap.** L4 mean is 51, best 53. Richards at 73 is the next draw man on the roster and he anchors L3. No rearrangement of existing personnel fixes this. It forces top-six defensive-zone draws all season. Already flagged, still true.

**D audit update (#1):** Pairs are set correctly against a 22-38 Calgary club. Jackman/Fischer as D1 carries the checking load. McCabe/Kaberle as D2 is the scoring pair — McCabe recovered to 0.83 pts/g and Kaberle is the quarterback. Eminger (0.44 season rate, recent collapse) and Klesla (0.38 at 22) as D3 is the correct hiding spot. No change tonight. The sell order behind McCabe remains Eminger, Salo, Klesla.

## Opponent matchup

The question: does Calgary's profile force any adjustment to our lines or goalie, or do we ice the same sheet and win it?

**No change to the lines.** We're 112 points against 54, we've outscored them 10-3 in two meetings, and their entire roster reads as a collection of 73s and 74s on the back end. Their three defensive pairs average 75, 74, 73 OVR. Our top two pairs are 83 and 82. The auto-pairing puts Fischer and Jackman with our first line, which is the correct answer to Iginla without any adjustment.

**Iginla** is their only elite player: OVR 91, SHPW 97, SPEE 96. He plays right wing on their first line, which means he'll spend most of his shift time against whichever of our pairs comes out with the line we choose. Our first pair (Fischer 89 CHKG, Jackman 89 CHKG) is the right answer. No need to shuffle.

**Conroy** has FACE 93 at center on their first line. Sundin at 89 handles him. Richards (73) and Chlup (78) lose draws to him, but that's the roster-wide faceoff gap we've flagged all season, not something CGY-specific.

**Their power play is 20 on 216 chances, 9.3%.** They don't score on the man advantage. Our PK needs no special preparation.

**Belfour** at OVR 92 is the start. Standing order: check the fatigue icon on screen before confirming. If he's showing tired, Aebischer goes.

**D evaluation (#1):** I cannot run the season-stat queries this activation (no tools available), so I cannot update the sell-order table with fresh production numbers. I will deliver this next time I have tools.

## Owed

**#1 — Defencemen sell list for season's end.**

**Eminger** is the first name on the list. 0.38 pts/g over 52 games (down from 0.44 when I flagged him Feb 26), 21 years old with an expiring $1.2M. He was supposed to grow into a top-four role and he has not. Sell him.

**Klesla** is second. 0.37 pts/g over 70 games at 22, flat from 0.38 on Feb 21. At that age the rate should be climbing. Two years and $0.90M means there is time to get something for him, but the window narrows if this holds through the offseason.

**Jackman** is the puzzle. 0.47 pts/g on 30.5 MPG. I flagged his collapse at 0.38 on Mar 5; the season average has crept to 0.47 but that is arithmetic, not recovery — the earlier good games are diluting a still-bad recent rate. At $0.70M x 3 he is too cheap to trade. The fix is a minutes reduction next camp, not a move.

**McCabe** stays off the sell list. 0.81 over 70, steady from 0.83 on Mar 4. Four years at $3M is a burden but he is producing.

**Fischer** and **Kaberle** are keepers. No revisit needed.

**Salo is gone**, so the old three-name sell list (Eminger, Salo, Klesla) is now just Eminger and Klesla.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-09
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-09

Toronto 48-12-4, 110 pts after 69 games.

## Role coverage

The question this phase answers: can Toronto dress a competitive checking line and a second faceoff option tonight, and where does the roster force a trade?

**Toughness.** The role coverage's "0 at 80+" is a composite reading. On raw TOUG stored grades, Toronto have ten players at 80 or above: Roberts 92, Jackman 89, Nash 88, Tucker 88, McCabe 85, Upshall 84, Eminger 83, Abid 80, St. Jacques 80, Klesla 80. The coach's "toughness gap" is a form artifact. Doan, Fleury, Bell — none is needed for toughness. This is resolved.

**Checking line.** The coach is right that no full forward line clears 80 on all three slots simultaneously, but the problem is narrower than he states. On stored CHKG, the forward checkers are Tucker 92, Roberts 90, Upshall 87, Nash 83, Abid 80. That's five bodies. The ceiling is Tucker + Roberts + Upshall on the wings with Chlup (CHKG 79 stored) at centre. Three wingers at 83+ is not a "missing" role; it is thin because the centre position caps at 79. The D-core (Jackman 90, Fischer 90, McCabe 89) is elite and covers the blue line entirely.

**Tucker is not lined.** He is 29, CHKG 92 stored, TOUG 88 stored, and the roster has no other forward who closes that gap. Dressing him nightly is the internal fix. This has been known since February and remains undone.

**Faceoffs are the real structural gap.** Sundin at FACE 90 stored is the only forward above 80. Chlup 75, Richards 70, everyone else below. One elite centre is not enough when the playoff run puts Sundin against every other team's first-line pivot with no relief. Reid (STL, 23, FACE 80 shown, POTE 94, $600K expiring, 63 pts at STL) closes this without spending the 4th-rounder.

**Durability.** Only four players at INJU 80+ stored: Roberts 98, Afinogenov 95, Fischer 92, Abid 90. Everyone else is 79 or below. This is not a deadline problem but it is a July problem — if two or three top-six bodies get injured simultaneously, the drop-off is steep.

**Age curve on scoring.** Mogilny 36, Roberts 38, Sundin 34. Three of the top five scorers will be 37, 39, 35 next season. The young core (Gaborik 23, Chlup 19, Richards 24, Abid 24, Fischer 24) is ready to absorb those minutes, which makes the deadline question "do we trade old pieces for young depth" rather than "do we need scoring."

**Goalies are covered.** Luongo 91 base at 25 with 2 years, Belfour 92 at 39 (1 year), Ouellet 81 at 23 (2 years), Tellqvist 77 at 25 (1 year). The Jan 15 standing order (fetch a 90+ goalie from a non-contender) is satisfied by Luongo's arrival. Theodore at MTL is no longer needed.

## Trajectory

The age curve is healthy but the money cliff is not: 26 players under 30 and a $21.30M block of 13 contracts all expiring this July is a structural problem that only staggering solves.

**Sundin** is the immovable anchor. 34 years old, $8.40M, five years left, POTE 60. That is $42M of committed money on a player whose best season is behind him and who will be 39 when the deal ends. At 14% of payroll, it constrains every other decision, and there is nothing to do about it except manage around it. No contender takes a 34-year-old center at $8.4M in this game. He's locked.

**Gaborik** at 23, 83 points in 69 games, $1.10M expiring is the single most valuable renewal this summer. His price will jump to $4-5M on a market extension. Locking him at 5 years now, at season-end when his production is on the sheet (83 pts), is the only way to avoid a bidding war in July when 10 similar players are all free at once.

**Nash** at 20, 35 points, POTE 95, $1.20M expiring is the same problem in miniature. He is cheaper to sign now than at 22 with 50 points. Both need 5-year locks.

**The other eight** (Eminger $1.20M, Upshall $1.20M, Richards $1.00M, Alexeev $1.10M, Chistov $1.10M, Colaiacovo $1.10M, Abid $0.40M, Kaberle $1.90M) should get 3-year deals, not 5. This staggers the next renewal wave into 2008 instead of stacking it behind 2010. At 3 years, Eminger will be 24 and a restricted free agent who can be matched. Colaiacovo will be 25 and his POTE 99 will have either materialized or not, and you'll know the price. The same logic for Upshall, Chistov, Alexeev, Richards, Abid.

**Fischer** at 24, $3.70M, 4 years remaining, 32 points in 64 games, is not a problem today but becomes one in two years. If Chlup and Spacek both break out (they're lined and young), Fischer slides to the third pairing where a $3.70M salary is wasteful. He is the summer 2007 trade candidate, not now.

**Belfour** ($6.50M) and **Roberts** ($2.70M) walking is the only payroll relief this summer. Together they free $9.20M without touching the core. Belfour's exit must be via trade for a pick, not release.

**The draft capital** is one 4th-rounder. That is effectively nothing. Every trade this deadline and next summer is player-for-player. If Belfour moves for a pick, that is the only asset the club holds for the 2005 draft. If Svehla is still available (he does not appear on this 30-man list, so he may already be gone), his move recovers another. Without pick recovery, Toronto cannot draft a goalie in 2005 or 2006, which contradicts the GM's standing order.

**The money works.** Payroll $60.04M, revenue $88.37M, profit $24.56M. After the July renewals and the Belfour/Roberts exits, committed payroll rises to roughly $59-63M. That is still $25M-plus of profit. The constraint is not affordability; it is timing and the simultaneous decision of 10 young players.

**The three moves that protect three seasons:**

1. Gaborik and Nash on 5 years; the other eight young expirers on 3 years. This splits the 2005 cluster across 2008 and 2010 instead of creating a 2010 cliff.
2. Move Belfour for at least one pick before March 19. Without a pick, the 2005 draft is a pass.
3. Re-sign Luongo's extension on his renewal in 2006 at a star salary (5-6 years). He's the number-one goalie, POTE 97, and will be 27 when his current deal ends. Forgetting him is how this club loses its best asset.

## Calendar

**Ten days to March 19.** Toronto are 1st in the East by 17 points (110 vs NJ at 93) with 13 games left. We are not in a playoff race; we won it in January. The question is not whether to sell — it is whether to buy for the playoffs with the one asset that has any real trade value: **Belfour**, 92 base, $6.50M, expiring. After that, the summer is the harder problem: 13 contracts worth $21.30M come due, nine of them young players who just broke out.

## Deadline: two packages, ten days

**Belfour → Colorado.** This is the keystone and it has been since February 28. Colorado (89 pts, 3rd in West) need a goalie and have already shown willingness to give up Hejduk. Test **Morris** first: 26, 85 base, 57 points in 65 games, $1.70M expiring. He fills the blue line the coach flags as thin on checking depth, he is nine years younger than Belfour, and the $4.80M salary reduction is real. If Colorado will only do Hejduk (91 base, RW, 2 years, $2.50M), take it — a 91-base winger on a two-year deal with cost-controlled salary is the best return available. Either way, Belfour moves or he walks in July and the value is gone. The GM's Feb 21 concern about retirement is valid and the price is at its ceiling with 29 GP, 92 base, and a .916 save percentage.

**Tucker + 4th-rounder → Ottawa for Havlat.** OTT sit 18th in the East at 63 points with 11 expiring contracts. Havlat is 87 base, 23 years old, $900K, and they cannot keep him. Tucker is 79 base, $1.30M, and occupies no line role. The 4th is our only pick. These two packages don't overlap — Belfour goes west, Tucker and the 4th go east. Both can land.

**Roberts stays.** The over-80 expiring mechanic could turn his 87 base into a draft pick, but 22 goals and 70 points in 69 games at 1.01 ppg is exactly the depth scoring the coach says we lack. A pick we can't trade (we have no capital to move anyway) is worth less than a point a game in the playoffs. Offer him two years at a reduced salary in July. If he won't take it, we lose him, but not before he helps in the spring.

**No third package.** Svehla (LA, 85 base, $3.60M) would fill blue line depth but we have nothing to offer LA without breaking up the core. Theodore (MTL, 91 base, $5.50M) is the right goalie profile but MTL at 53 points want youth and picks, not a 39-year-old backup. We don't have either to give.

**Goalie risk accepted.** With Belfour gone, **Tellqvist** (77 base, 11 GP this year, POTE 91) is the playoff backup alongside starter Luongo (91 base, 2 years left). That is thin. The GM's February concern about not wanting Ouellet as the only backup applies here, but Tellqvist is better than Ouellet and Luongo at 91 base can carry a series. There is no additional goalie we can afford without a pick.

## Summer: $21.30M walks unless we act

Thirteen expiring deals. Nine are players aged 20 to 24 with POTE 88 or higher. This is the renewal window the December memory flagged, and now it is here.

**Five-to-six year locks (nine players):** Gaborik (91 base, 83 pts, 23), Richards (82 base, 61 pts, 24), Nash (77 base, 35 pts, 20), Eminger (76 base, 20 pts, 21, POTE 99), Abid (79 base, 65 pts, 24, POTE 94), Upshall (78 base, POTE 99, 21), Chistov (78 base, POTE 95, 21), Alexeev (76 base, 30 pts, 23, POTE 94), Colaiacovo (72 base, POTE 99, 22). These are the franchise. Sign them on long deals at season end, staggered if possible so the cluster never renews at once again. Abid at $400K breaking out for 65 points is the cheapest star on the list and the first one to lock.

**Two-to-three year deals:** Kaberle (84 base, 27, POTE 75) has a defined ceiling. Two years at a modest raise. **Tellqvist** (77 base, 25, POTE 91) — the GM wants to give him time. Two years, and reassess after a full season as backup. **Roberts** (87 base, 38, 70 pts) — two years at reduced salary, or he walks.

**Belfour:** If the deadline trade doesn't happen, offer two years at a reduced figure. The GM's January read is right: he probably won't accept at 39 with $6.50M as his number. That's the answer.

**Delivering the overdue task (#2 — Luongo and DiPietro monitoring):** Luongo is on our roster at 91 base with 2 years left. That window closed in February. DiPietro is at NYI with 50 GP, 25-22, 2.88 GAA, .871 save percentage — a starting-calibre goalie. But NYI are 9th in the East at 68 points, borderline playoff, and with 50 GP they view him as theirs. Without a pick to offer, we cannot pry him. Theodore at MTL remains the better theoretical target (91 base, non-contender, expiring) but MTL want youth and we have nothing to trade without breaking the nine-player core. The goalie window the January standing order described has effectively closed unless Belfour's departure opens a replacement slot.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: which players on non-playoff clubs does Toronto actually need, can afford to acquire, and have a realistic package for? We hold one 4th-rounder and Belfour as tradeable assets. Everything else is player-for-player.

**Havlat** (OTT, LW, 23, 87 base, 83 pts/67 GP, $900K expiring) is the best single player available. OTT at 63 points with 11 expiring contracts cannot retain him. He's a top-six winger who plays 20.6 minutes a night and costs almost nothing. If we can only get one player before March 19, it is him.

**Reid** (STL, RW, 23, 77 base, FACE 80, POTE 93, 52 pts/57 GP, $600K expiring) closes the faceoff gap directly. Only Sundin (FACE 90) is above 80 on our roster. STL at 65 points with 8 expiring deals are sellers. He's cheap, young, and the only player who solves our structural faceoff hole without spending a first-round pick.

**Morris** (COL, D, 26, 85 base, 59 pts/67 GP at 29.1 MPG, $1.70M expiring) answers the Coach's Jackman load flag directly. Jackman at 30.9 MPG with 0.36 pts/g needs a partner. Morris plays the same minutes in a worse system and produces 59 points. COL tested this deal already: they want a goalie, we have Belfour. It's rental for rental — Belfour (39) helps their spring, Morris helps ours now and next year if we re-sign.

**Komisarek** (MTL, D, 23, 77 base, CHKG 84, POTE 91, 70 pts/68 GP at 29.9 MPG, $1.10M expiring) is the most absurd value on the board. A 23-year-old defenseman with 84 checking and 70 points on a $1.10M expiring deal. MTL at 53 points with 15 expiring are the most desperate sellers in the league. They cannot re-sign him and should be selling him at any price above nothing.

**Sturm** (SJ, LW, 26, 85 base, 75 pts/59 GP, $1.00M expiring) is a cheap top-six winger from a team that cannot retain 14 expiring contracts. SJ at 61 points are in teardown mode. At $1.00M he costs us less than Tucker's salary, which means we could take him AND keep Tucker in the lineup as the checking fix.

**Conroy** (CGY, C, 33, 85 base, FACE 94, 82 pts/67 GP, $2.00M expiring) is the pure playoff rental centre. CGY at 54 points are not pretending to compete. He gives us a 94-faceoff pivot against opposing second lines for the spring. He will not be here in July.

**Sullivan** (CHI, RW, 30, 87 base, 82 pts/68 GP, $3.00M expiring) has the same production as Havlat at three times the price and seven years more. He's available (CHI at 59, 10 expiring) but he is Plan C behind Havlat and Sturm at the same position.

**Cammalleri and Frolov** (LA, 22, POTE 97 and 95, $1.10M each, expiring) are the future top-six pair. LA at 65 points with 15 expiring cannot keep them. But acquiring both requires two separate packages and we have one 4th-rounder. This is a summer target if they walk in July, not a deadline move.

**What I would not do:** Pursue Kovalchuk or Heatley from ATL (now at 72 points, in a playoff position, unlikely to sell). Pursue Theodore (goalies are solved per the February standing order). Pursue Daze (108 points, but 29 years old and CHI will want a top-2 pick for him). Pursue Zhamnov (34 years old, $4.20M, wrong timeline).

**The realistic path:** Belfour to COL for Morris (tested, rental for rental). Tucker plus the 4th to OTT for Havlat (physical winger for a rebuilding team, plus a pick). Chistov plus something small to STL for Reid. That gives us Morris, Havlat, and Reid before the deadline using every chip we hold. If OTT says no on Tucker, Sturm from SJ becomes the fallback winger target.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: what exactly do we put on the table, and why would the other GM sign it? We have three targets worth pursuing, one pick, and Belfour as the lever that unlocks the best one. The proposals below are sequenced so all three can happen simultaneously without spending the same asset twice.

**Belfour to COL for Morris** is the highest-probability deal because Colorado already asked for a goalie and we already know they'd give us something. They offered Hejduk; Morris is better for us (26 versus 32, $1.70M versus $4.20M, fills the blue-line hole the Coach flagged on Jackman's 30.9 MPG). They're at 65 points in a playoff race with no answer in net. Belfour's 18-3, 2.27 GAA, 0.916 SP is exactly the rental a contender wants in April. Morris is also expiring, so COL gives up no long-term piece. We save $4.80M on payroll and get a top-pair defenseman for the spring and for re-signing if he performs. The cost is Ouellet (81 base) as the playoff backup, which the GM accepted on Feb 21 when he called Belfour a chip.

**Tucker plus the 4th to OTT for Havlat** is the biggest single-player upgrade on the board. Havlat at 23, 87 base, 83 points in 67 games, $900K, is a first-line winger. OTT at 63 points with 11 expiring contracts cannot re-sign him. Tucker at 29 with 2 years left, CHKG 92 stored and TOUG 88 stored, is a usable bottom-six winger for a rebuilding club, plus they get the 2005 fourth. Ottawa gets a physical body on a team that just lost its veterans, plus draft capital for the future. The payroll swing is trivial: we save $400K.

**Chistov to STL for Reid** closes the faceoff gap without spending a pick. Reid at 23, FACE 80, POTE 94, 52 points in 57 games, $600K, is the structural fix Sundin needs beside him. STL at 65 points with 8 expiring deals are sellers. Chistov at 21 with POTE 95, SPEE 89, ACCE 88 on a $1.10M expiring deal is exactly what a rebuilding team values over a 23-year-old with a lower ceiling. The cost to us is real: Chistov is a prospect. But Reid closes a hole that costs us playoff series.

If none land, the answer is no change. At 48-12-4 and 110 points, this team wins a playoff round without any of this. The July renewal cluster is the real problem; the deadline is upside.

## Owed

**Item #2 — Luongo availability and DiPietro development through February for the goalie trade window.** This is late: the GM wanted it by February 20 and it's March 9. I'm closing it now because both halves have answers and there is nothing left to monitor.

**Luongo** is on our roster. 94 overall, 25 years old, $1.60M, 2 years left, 42 GP this season. The monitoring question was whether he would be available or whether we needed to find another starter. The answer is moot: he's here. Standing order of Feb 19 says goalies are solved. I agree with it.

**DiPietro** at NYI is 80 overall, 79 base, 21 years old, $1.10M, 1 year left. This season: 21 GP, 7-12, 3.64 GAA (75 GA on 1235 minutes), 84.9% save percentage (75 on 498 shots against). He is not developing into a target. Compare to the Jan 15 standing order, which set the goal as "a really good high-90s goalie from a team that will not be a contender." DiPietro is a 79-base backup on a bad team with a losing record. He fails the test on grade, on performance, and on the fact that he won't be a high-90s goalie at 21 if he's 79 today with these numbers.

The Belfour trade exploration per the Feb 21 softening points elsewhere. Theodore at MTL (91 base, 28, $5.50M expiring, MTL at 51 points) is the standing target from the vault. DiPietro is not a Belfour return; no contender would call 84.9% "goalie help."

This item is closed. Luongo arrived, DiPietro is not the answer, and the goalie situation is resolved per standing orders.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-09

# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-09

Next game at EDM on Thursday 10 March 2005.

## Development opportunity

Is every young player getting the games he has earned, with 13 left in the season?

**Gaborik** (69 GP, 20.2 MPG, 83 points) and **Chlup** (58 GP, 16.5 MPG, 42 points) are fully earning their roles. No questions. **Nash** at 56 GP and 0.63 pts/g on the third line is also fine.

**Spacek** — 8.1 MPG, 0.35 pts/g in 46 games. The condition I set was: season average above 10 by year's end means the lever works. From 8.1 with 13 games left, climbing above 10 requires 19+ MPG in every remaining game. That won't happen. The year is what it is. I'm dropping this recommendation. His 92 morale says he isn't sulking about it.

**Spezza** — 37 GP, 7.5 MPG, 15 points, POTE 99, currently scratched. I've raised him five times and the GM hasn't moved. The window is closing. At 21 with the highest potential grade on the roster, the question isn't whether 0.41 pts/g justifies a roster spot today — it's whether the final 13 games in games we can afford are the cost of watching a year disappear. If the GM's answer is no, that's his call and I'll stop raising it.

**Stahle** — 4 GP, POTE 96, age 20, scratched. Still the biggest gap. Four games in 69 is nothing. The last 13 games are the only remaining chance to see if he can play. The 0 points in 4 games is a tiny sample and shouldn't matter yet at 20. One dressing in a non-critical game costs nothing.

**Colaiacovo** at 31 GP and 17.9 MPG is getting adequate looks for a 22-year-old. **Upshall** at 55 GP and 0.33 pts/g on the fourth line is a fourth-line producer, nothing more. **Alexeev** at 55 GP and 0.55 pts/g on 8.3 MPG is efficient on limited ice but currently out of the lineup — at 23 he's more a roster decision than a development one.

## Development trends

Who's developing and who's sliding through this half-season window matters because we have 13 games left to plan the summer: sell order, who gets minutes next year, and who we're building around.

**Chlup** is the one going the right way at speed. 0.62→0.76 pts/g while minutes went 11.0→18.1. Production up 23% under a 65% minutes increase at age 19. He belongs in the top nine permanently and the GM should build the second line around him next season.

**Kaberle** is the other one going up. 0.54→0.57 pts/g on minutes climbing from 19.4 to 22.1 at age 27. His game is still expanding. The GM's read on him as a star is correct and he's entering his prime.

**McCabe** is the surprise. His full-season rate of 0.83 is propped up by a 1.42 first window; the actual recent play is 0.51 pts/g over 45 games on 22.0 MPG. At 29 on 4 years and $3M, he never recovered from the January slump. He goes back to the top of the sell list.

**Jackman** is 0.36 pts/g on 30.9 MPG at age 24. Minutes up slightly, production down 45%. This is the third consecutive window I've flagged him. At 24 with a full-time workload, burnout is the more likely explanation than talent. The immediate question is whether we reduce his load in these final 13 games or ride it out. The planning answer is that he cannot carry a top-pair 31 MPG role next season without a partner who relieves him, or his production stays at 0.35.

**Klesla** is 0.50→0.31 at 22 on flat minutes (14.6→14.8). This is a second straight declining year at an age when the expected direction is up. He's behind McCabe on the sell list but in front of everyone else.

**Abid** dropped from 1.09 on 20.1 MPG to 0.87 on 13.3 MPG. His production is still solid but he lost seven minutes a night and a line spot. If his role was cut for a reason I should revisit it in these final games. He's producing like a top-nine forward at fourth-line minutes.

**Stahle** finally played: 4 games at 17.8 MPG, no points. The minutes suggest someone trusts him defensively. Keep dressing him through these 13 games so we can evaluate next year with real information.

**Spacek** at 5.7 MPG season and 0.29 recent with 46 games dressed confirms the year is dead. I'm dropping this recommendation. He played the bump and it didn't move the needle.

**Nash** went 0.83→0.47 at 20 on flat minutes. Concerning but not yet a planning problem. He's young enough that a full offseason could reset him.

**The veterans** are declining on schedule. Sundin at 34 (0.93 recent on 21.5 MPG), Mogilny at 36 (0.78 on 19.5), Roberts at 38 (0.87 on 21.2). All still playing heavy minutes. The GM should know these three cannot carry this workload next season and their minutes will need to redistribute, which is part of why Chlup's emergence matters so much.

**Sell list updated.** McCabe at the top (0.51 recent, $3M x 4, age 29), Klesla second (0.31 recent, two declining years at 22), Salo third (collapsed to 0.18, $2.6M x 2, age 30). Eminger at 0.43 and climbing stays.

## Morale watch

The room is fine; no morale-driven change before Thursday's game in Edmonton.

**Sundin** at 96 (down 4), **Mogilny** at 96 (down 4), **Richards** at 96 (down 3), **Afinogenov** at 96 (down 3), **Chlup** at 96 (down 2): these are top players getting 16.5 to 19.9 minutes a night, all at or above their expected band. The small drops track the results, not the ice time. Nobody is low enough to lose a grade (you need 89 or below for a −1 hit). No action.

**Spezza** at 86 is the one name. Down 4 from 90, and he has sat at 86 across multiple saves now. He's at 7.5 MPG, scratched, 15 points in 37 games at 21. If he sits in the 70–79 OVR band he expects about 10 minutes a night and he's getting three-quarters of that. His morale is in the −1 zone. The fix is minutes, and I've raised this since January with no movement. But tonight is EDM, a maximize-quality night, and Spezza doesn't belong in those lines. This is a roster-planning issue for the offseason, not a game-week adjustment.

**Alexeev** at 92 (down 4) and **Spacek** at 92 (down 4): both under 10 MPG on 23 and 19 respectively. Alexeev at 30 points in 55 games and 8.3 MPG is a productive player on too little ice, but he's still at 92 and that's one more point before he drops out of the +1 morale bonus band. Spacek at 16 points in 46 games on L4 at 8.1 MPG is in the role I've flagged repeatedly. Neither warrants a change tonight against a quality opponent where we're going all-out.

**Safronov** at 95 (down 5) played 3 games at 13.7 MPG before being scratched. If he's an 80–89 OVR defenceman expecting 17, he's under his band. But 3 games in a season isn't a line problem to fix on a road trip to Edmonton.

No change. Everyone who plays Thursday is at 96 or better and getting his minutes. The room is right.

## Role composition

The question here is whether our units are built from players suited to their jobs, and what we're missing if they aren't.

**L1 (Sundin, Roberts, Jackman, Gaborik, Fischer)** is the strongest unit on the team by every measure that matters: checking mean 81, speed 91, scoring 88, faceoffs 68 with Sundin at 90 anchoring draws. No change needed.

**L2 (Chlup, Mogilny, McCabe, Kaberle, Afinogenov)** is a scoring line, not a checking line. Checking mean 69, toughness 63. Mogilny 92 scoring, Afinogenov 90. Chlup at 79 faceoffs is the draw anchor. This is fine as a second scoring unit and the GM knows it's not a shutdown unit.

**L3 (Eminger, Richards, Klesla, Nash, Chistov)** is the most balanced line: checking 73 mean, speed 89 mean. Richards at 74 faceoffs and 88 stamina anchors it. Nash adds size and the speed of Chistov gives it transition threat. It's a 13-14 line and that's what it should be.

**L4 (Spacek, Abid, Upshall)** has the known faceoff void: mean 51, best 54. Abid's toughness 71 is the best thing this line offers. No bench replacement fixes this. Richards at 74 is the next-best draw man and he's already on L3.

**K2 vs K1:** K2 (Chlup, McCabe, Jackman, Abid) has checking mean 83 against K1's 77. Jackman at 89 checking and McCabe at 83 make K2 the harder unit to play against. K1 has Sundin's 90 faceoff, which helps on defensive-zone draws, but checking is what stops a PP. The GM can consider flipping the slot order if he wants the better checking unit out first.

**Roster gap I have to name:** We do not have a checking line. Our four best checkers (Jackman 89, Roberts 83, McCabe 83, Fischer 83) are distributed across L1 and K2. No arrangement of this roster produces a line with three guys above 80 in checking. Against a team with a true first-line scoring threat, we cannot match a shutdown unit against them. That's a roster problem, not a lineup problem.

## Opponent matchup

**The question: does Edmonton's lineup demand a specific adjustment, or do our current pairings already match them?** They don't, and the current setup is correct without changes.

**EDM's top line** is Comrie (85 OVR, SPEE 94, HERO 98), York (83), Dvorak (82). Fast and skilled, but the auto-pairing puts them against our Fischer-Jackman first pair (84/85), which is the right answer already. No bump needed.

**Hemsky is out** (returns March 13). He carried EDM's L3 with 95 deking and 95 shot power. Without him, that line drops to Rita (77) and Petrov (75) with a call-up at centre, facing our Klesla-Eminger pair. That's an easy night for them and frees our third pair from any worry.

**EDM's defence is soft across the board.** Semenov 76, Hannan 77, Cross 72, Staios 72, Baumgartner 67, Dupont 67. Our top line (Sundin 90, Gaborik 97, Roberts 87) faces their weakest pair. The power play at 26-for-73 (35.6%) already generates plenty; EDM's PP is 26-for-213 (12.2%), which means they won't give us many kill situations to face.

**Goalie:** Belfour at 93 OVR and 99 morale, coming off a shutout last game. Start him. GM standing order from January 19 says check the fatigue icon before confirming; I cannot see it today, so one glance on the screen before he dresses.

**No change to lines, PP, PK, or pairings.** The auto-matchup puts our best D against their best F, we're up 8-3 in two meetings this season, and they're missing their best forward. Go all out with the standard set.

## Owed

**D corps sell-list update for March 10 vs Edmonton:**

**McCabe** at 0.83 pts/g over 69 games continues to anchor. He got a point in the last game. Off the sell list and staying there.

**Fischer** added one more assist last game, now 32 points in 64 games at 0.50 pts/g. GM's keeper, no change.

**Kaberle** at 0.56 pts/g in 61 games. Keeper per the GM. No change.

**Jackman** is the story. 31 points in 67 games at 30.6 MPG puts his season rate at 0.46. He was scoreless in the last game. My March 5 read flagged a collapse from 0.65 to 0.38 in the recent window; the season-wide number now reads 0.46 because earlier games carry the average, but the recent stretch is still weak. At 24, carrying 30.6 MPG, he should be at 0.60 or better. His contract at $0.7M x 3 makes him the cheapest top-pair D in the league, so he is not a sell: nobody else can absorb those minutes. The problem is usage, not trade value.

**Klesla** unchanged at 0.38 pts/g in 69 games, 14.8 MPG. Same number as February. At 22 the expected direction is up; it has not moved. $0.9M x 2 remaining. Sell candidate.

**Eminger** at 0.39 pts/g in 51 games. Expiring $1.2M. Still the first man off the list.

**Colaiacovo** 0.39 pts/g in 31 games. Development rotation, not a sell.

Sell order is **Eminger, Klesla**. Unchanged from my last delivery. No new entrant, no departure.
