# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-07

Toronto 47-12-4, 108 pts after 68 games.

## Role coverage

This phase answers one question: what does Toronto genuinely lack, and how badly does it matter for the playoff run starting in two weeks? The answer is clean. We have one gap that cannot be filled internally: toughness.

**Toughness** — zero players at 80+ on base grades. Best is Jackman at 75, then Roberts 73, McCabe 73. The coach's Feb 21 claim of six players at 80+ TOUG was wrong; these are the shipped grades, and they are unambiguous. This kills the Tucker-as-enforcer memory: he's 70 TOUG, a good checker (83 CHKG) but not a hitter. The only realistic deadline fix is Avery at LA (83 TOUG, $400K, 2 years, LA at 48 points selling). His production is weak (0.11 ppg), but no one on this roster offers 80+ TOUG at any price he could fill.

**Checking** — coach-fixable. Six players at 80+: Jackman 87, Roberts 86, McCabe 86, Tucker 83, Fischer 82, Upshall 80. Tucker is 83 CHKG and not lined. Dress him. That is not a trade, that is a coach decision. But note the age curve: Roberts at 38 is 86 today and will drop next year. Jackman at 24 is the long-term anchor.

**Faceoffs** — one man at 80+ (Sundin 90). Chlup at 75 is next best. The coach's L4 mean of 51 is a genuine gap. No roster fix exists; the best 4th-line centre here (Chlup) is already playing. This is a trade or draft target, but at 108 points and locked for the playoffs, spending a 4th-round pick on L4 faceoffs is lower priority than toughness.

**Scoring and playmaking** — covered. Mogilny 94, Sundin 92, Gaborik 92, Afinogenov 90, Roberts 88. The concern is Mogilny (36) and Roberts (38) falling out of that group next year. Gaborik at 23 and Afinogenov at 25 inherit the top six. No deadline action needed.

**Durability** — four at 80+ (Roberts 98, Afinogenov 95, Fischer 92, Abid 90). Moderate. For a playoff run, four dependable bodies on defence and the bottom six is thin but workable given the youth elsewhere.

**Goalies** — solved per Feb 19 order. Luongo (25, 2 years) is the future; Belfour (39, 1 year) is the present. Ouellet as backup. No change needed.

## Trajectory

**The cliff is not age, it is a single summer.** Toronto's age shape is right: 15 players at 23 or under, 12 in the 24-29 band, zero in the dead zone (30-33), four veterans above 34. The problem is that 14 contracts worth $21.70M expire together in July 2005, and four of those players are the franchise.

**Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger** carry $4.50M combined at current prices and produced 200 points in 2005 between them. Each needs a 5-6 year deal in July or the core walks simultaneously. Budget for 3-4x their current salaries at renewal, which adds roughly $12-16M to payroll. Against $86.75M revenue, that is still $15M profit, so money is not the obstacle. Timing is.

**Kaberle** is 27, $1.90M expiring, 33 points in 60 games. He does not need a 6-year lock, but he needs 3-4 years at a moderate bump. He is not on the GM's protected list and the renewal should be separated from the four stars to avoid one summer of panic pricing.

**The 30-33 void** is visible but not dangerous tonight. McCabe at 29 is the next-oldest blueliner after the 39-year-old Belfour. If McCabe leaves, the defense has no veteran. That is a 2007 problem unless McCabe's 4-year deal is already locked (it is, through 2008-09), so it is managed.

**Sundin** at 34, $8.40M with 5 years left and 76 points in 68 games is still playing, but his POTE of 60 means the production is set. He is the one man whose contract locks salary without upside. If he declines to 60 points in 2006-07, that $8.40M buys fourth-line center production with no exit. Nothing can be done until it expires in 2010, but the GM should know the liability exists.

**Draft capital is one fourth-rounder.** Every trade must be funded by players. The Svehla pick-recovery noted on Feb 23 appears to have been executed; he is no longer on the roster. Belfour at $6.50M and 28 games is the remaining over-80 expiring asset, still lined tonight.

## Calendar

The deadline is 12 days away and we are 108 points, first in the East by 15. We are buyers. The question is which buys we can fund, because the Belfour decision gates everything else.

**Belfour** is the keystone. He is 39, $6.50M, expiring, and the only over-80 asset on the roster that recovers a pick. The GM has been exploring since February 21 with Colorado (Hejduk offered) and the desk flagged Morris as a possibly better return. Whatever the answer, the call must come this week: if Belfour moves, the 4th-rounder stays home and funds Havlat. If he walks in July, we lose both the pick capital and the Havlat upgrade.

**Havlat** (OTT, 23, 87 base, 80 points in 63 games, $900K expiring) is the lead scoring target. Tucker plus the 4th-rounder is the package. OTT sits at 60 points with 11 expiring deals and cannot retain him. This directly answers the team-wide scoring drought the GM identified on February 19.

**Reid** (STL, RW, 23, 77 base, FACE 80, POTE 94, $600K expiring) fixes the L4 faceoff hole without spending a pick. STL at 63 points are sellers. He closes the gap the coach flagged (L4 mean FACE 51, best 54) with a 23-year-old who still has upside.

**Roberts** (38, $2.70M, expiring) should go before March 19. The coach reports him "dropping fast" and the over-80 pick-recovery mechanic means he converts to a draft pick even as a rental. He fills nothing we need next season. Non-contenders are the destination — the purpose is avoiding rivals.

**Svehla** ($3.60M, 92 CHKG, 36, expiring) was flagged in February as a pick-recovery target. He does not appear in the current expiring list, so either he moved already or his contract changed. No action needed if resolved; if he is still here under a different listing, the same logic applies.

---

**Summer — 14 contracts expire worth $22.70M.** Here is the renewal plan, staggered so the cluster never renews at once.

**Lock 5–6 years (the young core):**

**Gaborik** — 23, 91 base, POTE 90, $1.10M current. He is the best player on the expiring list and the cheapest. Five or six years, expect $4–5M+ at signing. This is the first phone call in July.

**Eminger** — 21, POTE 99, $1.20M current. The GM protected him explicitly on January 19. Five years, reasonable raise. He is the future top-pairing defenceman.

**Nash** — 20, $1.20M. Youngest of the core. Five or six years at a low initial figure, escalate later.

**Richards** — 24, $1.00M. Centre depth with faceoff ability. Five years.

**Kaberle** — 27, $1.90M. Current top defenceman by production. Five years; his ceiling is set but he is productive tonight.

**Colaiacovo** — 22, $1.10M. Young D, pairs with Eminger on the development curve. Five years.

**Lock 2–3 years (young depth, cheap):**

**Alexeev** — 23, 0.55 pts/g per the coach, $1.10M. Two years. He is better than Chistov at the same money and the coach wants him in.

**Upshall** — 21, $1.20M. Two years. Cheap depth with room to grow.

**Abid** — 24, TOUG 80, CHKG 80, $0.40M. Two years. The cheapest physical presence on the roster.

**Smirnov** — 20, $0.40M. Two years. Cheapest asset we own.

**Tellqvist** — 25, $0.80M. Two years. GM said give him time on January 15.

**Chistov** — 21, $1.10M. Two years only if he is not trade bait at the deadline. If he goes for Havlat, this line disappears.

**Move or release:**

**Belfour** — if not traded by March 19, offer two years at $3.5M in July. He will likely refuse and walk, which is the same outcome as letting him go, so there is no cost to the offer.

**Roberts** — if still here at July, do not renew. At 38 and declining, $2.70M is not worth two years of any role he can fill.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: who across the league closes Toronto's gaps, and why would their club say yes? The answer is one clear trade (Morris for Belfour), one cheap rental that needs almost nothing (Conroy for Chistov), and a crowded second tier we can only fund with the fourth-rounder.

**Derek Morris** (COL, D, 26, 85 base, 84 TOUG, 80 CHKG, 77 POTE, $1.70M expiring, 58 pts/66 GP, 29 MPG). Closes the single biggest gap. 84 TOUG on a defenseman at 26 with 58 points — nobody else on the board offers that combination. COL at 87 points with 11 expiring need a goalie; GM confirmed they offered Hejduk for Belfour. Morris is better than Hejduk for us: younger by three years, $800K cheaper, fills the blue line where we are thin. Expiring deal means COL gets salary relief. The GM should test this exact swap before accepting Hejduk.

**Shane Doan** (PHX, RW, 28, 87 base, 88 TOUG, 93 CHKG, $2.40M expiring, 50 pts/65 GP). The best forward who fixes toughness. 88 TOUG and 93 CHKG exceed anything on our roster. Still producing 50 points at 16 MPG. PHX at 69 points with 14 expiring deals cannot re-sign him. Non-contender, so the "don't send rentals to rivals" rule holds. Problem: PHX will want a pick plus a player. We have Tucker ($1.30M, not lined) plus the 4th, but that conflicts with the Havlat pursuit.

**Craig Conroy** (CGY, C, 33, 85 base, 94 FACE, 80 CHKG, $2.00M expiring, 82 pts/66 GP). The best rental centre on the board. 82 points in 66 games at 20 MPG with 94 faceoffs. CGY at 52 points with 10 expiring are selling everything. He fixes L4 faceoffs (we go from 51 mean to a 94) AND adds scoring depth. Cost: Chistov (the coach wants him benched, 0.33 ppg) plus maybe a 5th or 6th rounder. No 4th needed.

**Martin Havlat** (OTT, LW, 23, 87 base, 85 POTE, $900K expiring, 83 pts/67 GP). The scoring upgrade. 83 points at 23 for $900K. OTT at 63 points with 11 expiring cannot retain him. Package is Tucker + the 4th. If Morris-for-Belfour lands, the 4th stays available for this.

**Marc Savard** (ATL, C, 27, 79 base, 88 FACE, 74 TOUG, $1.00M expiring, 68 pts/64 GP). Closes the faceoff gap with production (68 points) at $1.00M. ATL at 68 points with 11 expiring will deal him. Folds into the ATL conversation; if ATL re-sign Kovalchuk, Savard is the consolation prize. Package: Chistov or Tucker, possibly the 4th if they want a pick.

**Brandon Reid** (STL, RW, 23, 77 base, 80 FACE, 93 POTE, $600K expiring, 52 pts/56 GP). The cheapest faceoff fix. 80 FACE at 23 with POTE 93 on a $600K expiring deal. STL at 63 points with 8 picks (rebuilding aggressively). But he's a RW — he'd play L4 centre at his FACE 80. The issue is STL with 8 picks may not need our 4th and may want a young player we don't want to send.

**Mike Komisarek** (MTL, D, 23, 77 base, 83 CHKG, 76 TOUG, 91 POTE, $1.10M expiring, 70 pts/67 GP, 30 MPG). Best D prospect on the board. 70 points from a 23-year-old blueliner logging 30 MPG. MTL at 53 points with 15 expiring. But he only fills D depth, not toughness. Package per Feb 13 note: St. Jacques + Safronov + the 4th. That's expensive for a 77-base player.

**Sean Avery** (LA, C, 24, 79 base, 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, $400K, 2 years). Cheapest player closing toughness and faceoffs simultaneously. 83 TOUG is the only forward at 80+ available. LA at 65 points with 15 expiring are motivated. But 7 points in 66 games (0.11 ppg) means he's a checker who wins draws, nothing more. At $400K with 2 years, he's the risk floor: worst case is a healthy scratch. Best case is the L4 centre we lack.

**Overdue task resolved: Luongo monitoring (task #2).** Luongo is on our roster at 91 base with 2 years left. DiPietro was assessed Feb 6 and rejected (79 base, 3.65 GAA, potential unrealized). Both halves of that task are closed.

## Trade construction

This phase builds concrete trade proposals from the league scan's shortlist, with both sides named and the payroll math done. The answer is three deals that don't conflict: Morris for Belfour (closes toughness, saves $4.80M), Conroy for Chistov (closes faceoffs, costs nothing but a benched player), and Havlat for Tucker plus the 4th (adds 83 points from a 23-year-old).

**Morris for Belfour** is the lead proposal and the GM should run it immediately because the conversation is already open — Colorado offered Hejduk, we counter with Morris. They get a 91-save-percent goalie with 18-3 record and 2.27 GAA for the playoff run, exactly what an 87-point team with no answer in net needs. We get a 26-year-old defenseman with 84 TOUG and 58 points, the first player on any team who closes our toughness gap while producing offense. We save $4.80M. The tension is that Morris is also expiring, which fails the GM's Feb 21 stated preference for someone "locked on reasonable salary for a couple of years." The counter-argument: Morris re-signs at $1.70M-$2.20M easily at 26 with 58 points, or he doesn't, and we got a playoff-ready tough D for the salary savings. Hejduk at 29 and $2.50M is locked but plays a position where we have Gaborik, Afinogenov, and Nash. Acceptance uncertain: Colorado may insist on Hejduk being what they want to move, not Morris.

**Conroy for Chistov** is the cheapest deal on the board and the coach's flags make both sides obvious. Conroy has 94 FACE and 82 points in 66 games at $2.00M expiring; CGY at 52 points with 10 expiring deals will not re-sign a 33-year-old centre at that price. Chistov is 21, POTE 95, 89 SPEE, 88 ACCE, and the coach explicitly wants him benched for Alexeev. We add $900K and get a 94-faceoff centre who produces 1.24 points per game. Calgary gets a young player with real upside for a rebuild. No pick involved. The risk is adding a 33-year-old to a roster that already has Roberts (38), Mogilny (36), and Sundin (34). But it is one year, and 94 FACE at L4 is exactly what the coach cannot fix from the bench.

**Havlat for Tucker plus the 4th** is the highest-talent move. Havlat is 87 base, 83 points in 67 games, 23 years old, $900K expiring. OTT at 60-63 points with 11 expiring contracts cannot retain him. Tucker is 29, 83 CHKG, 88 TOUG on a 2-year $1.30M deal, and has played 3 games; he is a veteran body for a team that needs physicality on a rebuilding roster. The 4th is our only pick. OTT gets a player with 2 years of control plus a draft asset. We get the best value player on the entire deadline market. Acceptance uncertain: OTT may want a younger player for their timeline, but Tucker's 2-year control and 83 CHKG give them something they lack (toughness with a contract).

If all three land: we give Belfour ($6.50M), Chistov ($1.10M), Tucker ($1.30M), and the 4th. We get Morris ($1.70M), Conroy ($2.00M), Havlat ($900K). Net payroll change: minus $4.20M. The 4th line gains a 94-FACE 82-point centre, the top six gains an 83-point winger, and the blue line gains an 84-TOUG 58-point defenseman. The only cost is the 4th-round pick.

**If none land:** We are 108 points with Luongo (91 base, 2 years), Gaborik (83 points, 23), Sundin (76 points), Mogilny (71 points), and four defensemen at 80+ CHKG. The toughness gap (best 75 stored TOUG) is a playoff liability but not fatal when the top six outproduces any bottom pair in the league. The L4 faceoff gap costs us draws but not games. We execute the coach's lineup moves (Alexeev over Chistov, Spezza into 10+ MPG, Stahle dressed) and play the playoffs with what we have. No action before the deadline is a defensible answer when the roster is this good.

## Owed

**Item #2 — Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window.**

This job is closed. Luongo is on the roster at 93 displayed (91 base), 25 years old, $1.60M, 2 years left, 42 GP. The Feb 19 order "goalies are solved, do not revisit" is the correct call and nothing has moved since.

**DiPietro** (NYI): 81 overall, 79 base, 50 GP, 25-22-1, 2.88 GAA on 2893 minutes. He does not meet the Jan 15 standing order, which called for "a really good high-90s goalie." At 79 base he is a third-stringer at best in this league. The monitoring window ran through February and he never rose above the low 80s. He is off the list.

**Theodore** (MTL) remains the only name that satisfies the original Jan 15 criteria: 91 base, POTE 87, $5.50M expiring, and MTL sit at 17-38-7-5 in 67 games. If the GM ever wants a true one-two punch beyond Luongo and Belfour, Theodore is the trade. But the GM closed this file on Feb 19, and Luongo's 93 displayed in 42 games says that was the right call. No action needed.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-07
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-07

Next game vs VAN on Tuesday 08 March 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether our 23-and-under players are getting the games they've earned, and the answer is split: the top end is fine, the middle is neglected, and one player at the bottom isn't earning anything.

**Spezza** is the loudest case on the roster. 37 games in 68, 7.5 MPG, 15 points. At 21 with POTE 99 and a 0.41 pts/g rate in his limited chances, he is the player least matched to his own potential. I have raised this five times. Vancouver tonight is a quality opponent, so by the standing order he stays out. But the remaining schedule after tonight will have games we can afford. He needs 10+ MPG in those or the year writes itself off again.

**Alexeev** at 0.55 pts/g on 8.3 MPG is outproducing Chistov (0.33 pts/g, 13.0 MPG) on less ice. He's scratched from the lineup right now. That is a quality problem, not just a development one: Chistov is holding a third-line slot at fourth-line production.

**Stahle** has played 4 games all year at POTE 96. His 17.8 MPG in those 4 shows the staff trusts him when he's in. But 4 games in 68 is nothing. After tonight's go-all-out assignment, he needs dressings in the games we can spare.

**Spacek** sits at 8.3 MPG season average. The March 4 bump was given, the March 5 game didn't hold it. With roughly two weeks left, if his season average doesn't climb above 10, the year is done. One more sustained push or stop dressing him.

**Smirnov** at 20, zero games, POTE 70. A 70 potential at zero games means the staff has looked at him and decided he doesn't fit. I agree. Stop carrying him.

**No change** for Gaborik (68 GP, 83 points, 20.1 MPG), Chlup (41 points in 57), Nash (35 in 55), or Klesla (68 GP). They are playing what they've earned.

## Development trends

The question is who is climbing and who is sliding, and whether any trend should change the GM's plans before the season ends. With 14 games left and no card grades moving, production and minutes carry the whole story.

**Chlup** is the riser. 0.62→0.75 pts/g while minutes went from 11.0 to 18.0. At 19, both lines moving the right direction is what a breakout looks like. The February window had him at 0.81, so he's cooled from that peak but the season-wide number still confirms he's earned the top nine permanently. No change needed in the lines; he belongs there.

**Kaberle** is the only defenceman trending up. 0.54→0.56 on minutes rising from 19.4 to 22.2. At 27, entering his prime with more load and no production loss. The GM called him a star on January 15th and the trend backs it. He's the anchor going forward.

**Jackman** is the one to watch. 0.65→0.37 while carrying 31.0 MPG. The March 5 note flagged it; four days later the brief confirms it hasn't reversed. At 24 he should be climbing. 31 minutes a night on a declining player is a burnout recipe. If he doesn't recover by the playoffs the top pair question gets real.

**Spezza** is still the same problem raised six times now. 0.43→0.38 on 5.3 MPG. He's 21 with POTE 99 and has played 37 games since December at fourth-line minutes. This is a wasted year, and unless something changes in the offseason plan it becomes two.

**Klesla** is sliding at 22. 0.50→0.32 with minutes flat at 14.8. The Feb 21 memory said a second declining season makes him tradeable. That's now the full picture: the production fell while the load didn't move, which means he's not earning more through performance. He belongs on the sell list alongside Eminger and Salo.

**Nash** is quietly concerning. 0.83→0.48 on roughly flat minutes (12.9→12.3). At 20, expected direction is up. I don't have a card grade to check because he isn't a created player, so I only have production. If it holds through the offseason it limits his role.

**Abid** went from 20.1 to 13.5 MPG while production dipped from 1.09 to 0.89. The minutes cut is bigger than the production cut suggests it should be. He's 24, still developing. Worth a conversation about whether the system has him buried.

**Koltsov** collapsed from 1.10 to 0.28 since December. At 23 with 10.4 MPG, he's the GM's trading chip and the trend only strengthens that case. I won't push it since the standing order says he stays until the GM is ready.

**The veterans** are all sliding, and all for the right reason. Roberts at 38 dropped from 1.29 to 0.89 on rising minutes (16.5→21.2). Mogilny at 36 went from 1.62 to 0.80. Sundin at 34 sits at 0.93 on 21.4 MPG. Roberts and Mogilny are one to two years from replacement conversations. Sundin has a year, maybe two, at this level. Planning the next roster starts with those three.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy. Every player except Spezza sits at 90 or above, which is the threshold where the game adds a point to every grade. No one is in the 70s or 60s where the penalty bites hard.

**Spezza** is the only man below 90, at 86, and has been there for weeks while scratched. He's 21, playing 7.5 MPG in 37 games with 15 points. At 86 he carries a minus-one across every grade, which means if he were in the lineup tonight he'd play a point worse than his screen says. The fix is minutes, not a line change: dress him and give him 10+ in a game we can afford, or accept the minus-one is the cost of scratching him. I've raised this repeatedly with no movement; it's a roster decision now, not a lines decision.

**Alexeev** at 92 and **Spacek** at 92 are both in the bonus zone (+1), so their scratch status causes no morale damage this week. No concern.

**Jackman** is at 30.7 MPG, well above the 20 the model expects for a 90+ player. His morale is 99 so it's not biting him yet, but late-season endurance decay could turn this. Something to watch after the trade deadline when we can shorten his shifts.

Everyone else is at 96 to 100. Nothing to fix.

## Role composition

The question this phase answers: are the units built from players whose strengths match their assignments?

**L1** is well-built. Gaborik (98 scoring, 99 playmaking) and Sundin (92 scoring, 90 faceoffs) carry the offense while Jackman (89 checking, 76 toughness) and Roberts (83 checking) provide the defensive anchor. Fischer (83 checking) is the glue man. This is exactly what a first line should be: three high-end scorers protected by two strong checkers.

**L2** is the second scoring unit and it suits them. Mogilny 92 scoring, Afinogenov 90 scoring, Chlup rising into a top-nine role. Checking mean at 66 is the lowest of the forward lines, but McCabe at 83 is the only real defender in the group. The line has no faceoff issue (Chlup 79) and enough skill that the defensive responsibility falls to McCabe and Kaberle on the back end. The GM's standing philosophy applies here: these guys are producing, and paper weaknesses are what the kids grow out of.

**L3** is Richards' line. His 93 checking, 96 clutch, and 85 stamina make him the best third-liner on the roster by a wide margin. Nash and Chistov provide speed (Chistov 97) without demanding the puck. Eminger and Klesla are young D developing in a sheltered spot. This is correctly built.

**L4 — the one real problem.** Faceoffs at 51/54 mean the fourth line is losing draws in both zones by a wide margin. Nobody on that line (Spacek, Abid, Upshall) can win a contest, which either buries them for scoring chances off the draw or forces the top six into extra defensive-zone starts. There is no arrangement fix: Richards (74) is the next-best draw man and he's carrying L3. Chlup (79) is the only other option above 74 and he's already on L2, P2, and K2.

**PP/PK overlap is a workload issue, not a composition one.** Sundin, Roberts, Kaberle, and Jackman appear on both PP1 and K1. They're simply the best players in both situations. I'd prefer to spread it, but none of the bench replacements are close enough to be worth the risk against Vancouver's skill.

**Toughness ceiling.** Best toughness on the roster is 76 (Jackman). No true enforcer exists. Against a physical team in the playoffs that becomes a problem. It is a roster gap, not an arrangement gap.

No composition change warranted for tonight. The units suit their players. The L4 faceoff void and the toughness ceiling are roster problems the GM already knows about.

## Opponent matchup

The question: do I shuffle anything tonight to beat a hot Vancouver team, or do I trust what we have?

**The short answer is no change.** Our structure already matches theirs cleanly, and the one thing that's been our structural weakness all year — losing faceoffs — barely exists tonight.

**Bertuzzi and Naslund** are the game. Bertuzzi at 89 OVR with DEKG 97 and PUCK 93 is the most skilled forward on their roster. Naslund at 85 with PUCK 92 alongside him on the left wing makes their first line a hands problem. That line slots against our first line, which means Fischer and Jackman get them by the auto-pairing rule. Fischer at CHKG 90, Jackman at CHKG 90. That is the right answer already built in.

**VAN's depth is thin below two lines.** Their third line centres Cajanek at 71 OVR is out until April 16. Whoever fills in is worse. Their fourth line tops out at 68. Our bottom six — Richards at 85, Nash at 81, Spacek at 75, Abid at 79 — all exceed them. We don't need to match lines; we need to roll and outscore them by committee.

**Faceoffs favour us tonight.** Their three centres are Bertuzzi 69, Morrison 69, Sedin 69. Sundin is 90, Chlup 79, Richards 74. For once we win the draw on all three lines, which means our defencemen aren't getting hemmed in coverage they can't handle.

**Cloutier reads 82 OVR with GSH_ at 76.** That's a soft glove-side read. Gaborik at ACCU 99 and SHPW 96 should find it. We shoot at a goalie whose weakest grade is the one that matters most to a sniper.

**Belfour starts.** 92 OVR, morale 99, no tired flag showing. He's our best player tonight against a team that scores 3.50 a night but has been outscored 5-4 across the one meeting we've had this year.

**Spacek plays.** VAN's fourth line is the weakest line in the game tonight — Belanger 62, Sedin 68, Danton 65. Our fourth line (75, 79, 77) outclasses them. He gets the minutes and the development reason and it costs nothing tonight. No conflict between development and maximize here.

## Owed

**Standing job #1: defenceman analysis and sell-list update, delivered.**

The sell list has one change since March 4: Salo is off the roster, so the order shifts. McCabe at 0.82 pts/g through 68 games confirms he's off the list entirely. Eminger's season rate has dipped from 0.44 to 0.40, deepening the case. Klesla hasn't moved at all since February 21: 0.38 pts/g at 22 years old, dead flat. Jackman's load remains 30.7 MPG with 0.47 season production; the March 5 alarm hasn't resolved in either direction from season totals alone.

**Eminger** at 0.40 pts/g in 50 games, $1.20M expiring, age 21. He should be improving; he's going the wrong way. His contract forces the issue: move him or lose him free.

**Klesla** at 0.38 pts/g in 68 games, 14.7 MPG, $0.90M x 2. Two weeks of games and zero movement since February 21. At 22 the expected direction is up. This is a player heading into two years of declining production the team controls.

**Colaiacovo** at 0.39 pts/g in 31 GP, $1.10M expiring. Thin sample, but nothing in it suggests he belongs here.

**McCabe** is 0.82 through 68. Settled, off the list, keeper.

**Jackman** is still carrying 30.7 MPG at 0.47 season pts/g. That load is the problem: no 24-year-old produces like a top-pair D at that volume unless he's genuinely elite, and 0.47 isn't elite. At $0.70M x 3 he's cheap, so no sell case yet, but if his minutes don't come down next season this becomes the biggest planning problem on the blue line.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-05
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-05

Toronto 46-12-4, 106 pts after 67 games.

## Role coverage

Is the roster built for the playoff run, and which holes the coach cannot plug from inside become the deadline shopping list?

**Toughness** is the loudest gap on the displayed sheet: zero players at 80+ TOUG, Jackman leading at 75. The Feb 21 stored-grade check found six players above 80 TOUG underneath, meaning form is currently suppressing the whole group by roughly 5–10 points. If that is right, the toughness exists but is invisible tonight. Tucker (83 CHKG displayed, not in any unit) is the best internal answer regardless, and the coach should dress him before chasing anyone else. The contradiction remains unresolved; I could not re-query stored grades this run.

**Faceoffs** are a genuine structural hole. Sundin at 90 is the only player above 80. Chlup at 75, Roberts at 75, Richards at 70. The L4 group reads 51 with a best of 54, and no combination of existing bodies lifts that past 65. This is unfixable internally.

**Scoring** is covered at depth: Mogilny 94, Sundin 92, Gaborik 92, Afinogenov 90, Roberts 88, Abid 86 — six players at 88+. Playmaking mirrors it with 11 above 80. Speed is absurd at 21 above 80. Clutch is fine with 9 above 80.

**Checking** is thin but adequate: six at 80+, Tucker at 83 sitting unlined. Dress him and the depth becomes seven.

**Durability** is the quiet concern. Only four players at 80+ ENDU: Roberts 98, Afinogenov 95, Fischer 92, Abid 90. Mogilny at 91 is the oldest man carrying that load at 36. If Mogilny's legs go in a seven-game series, there is no one behind him with both the engine and the skill.

**Goalies.** Belfour at 22-5, 2.06 GAA, 0.927 SV is the best number on the roster and he is 39, expiring, $6.50M. Luongo at 25, $1.60M, two years left, reads 2.79 and 0.884 in 42 games — solid, not elite. The GM's standing order is to find a high-90s goalie from a non-contender. That search continues; no target has materialised in the data.

**The GM's keystone decision** (belfour-hejduk-keystone-decision) is still open. Belfour-to-Colorado-for-Hejduk is the scenario. Hejduk is not young, but the GM explicitly said he is using it as an example of willingness. If Belfour walks, the 4th-rounder stays home for Havlat. If he stays, both the pick-recovery and the Havlat upgrade survive.

## Trajectory

Toronto's age curve is the best shape in the league — 15 players at 23 or under, 12 at 24-29, zero at 30-33, four at 34+. There is no cliff on the horizon. The cliff is a cliff in reverse: the young core is so deep that the real danger is that they all become free agents in the same summer and the club cannot afford them all.

**The summer 2005 renewal cluster** is 14 players at $21.70M. Six of them — Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger, Abid, Upshall — are the franchise. Their combined salary today is $6.10M. Their combined market rate on 5-6 year deals at season end is $14-18M. That is the single largest financial event this club faces, and it happens in 16 weeks.

**Sundin** is the immovable problem. $8.40M on a fifth year at age 39 when it expires. He is producing — 74 pts in 67 games at 34 — but the contract locks the club into paying a player who will be 38 and 39 next season at a price only a 25-year-old can justify. No trade partner takes five years and $8.40M for a 35-year-old centre. This contract is the ceiling on the payroll.

**Mogilny** at 36 and $5.50M for two more years is the second liability. 70 pts in 63 games says he is still productive tonight, but the second year puts him at 38. If he drops to 40 points in year two, that is $5.50M for third-line work. He cannot be moved now — nobody trades for him with a year already on a two-year deal.

**Belfour** at $6.50M and 39 and **Roberts** at $2.70M and 38 are the two remaining over-80 expiring assets that can be converted into draft picks before they walk. Both should be moved by March 19. That recovers the pick capital the club currently does not have — Toronto holds only a fourth-rounder, nothing better.

**Abid** at 65 points on a $400K contract is the single most underpriced player on the roster. Any team that sees 65 points from a 24-year-old left wing at $400K will offer more in July. Re-sign him on a 4-5 year deal before that happens, or he walks and Toronto loses a top-six scorer at the cheapest price in the league.

**Chlup** at 19, 40 pts, POTE 95, two years left, $2.34M, is the next contract crisis after this one. If he plays a full top-nine season next year, his asking price doubles. Lock him in 2006.

The money itself is not the problem. Payroll is $60.04M against $86.75M in revenue, leaving $26M in profit. Even if every renewal goes to market rate, Toronto lands at roughly $72-75M and clears $12M in profit. The constraint is not affordability; it is timing. If the club re-signs everyone at once in July 2005, it will have no flexibility to make a trade that summer. The moves that protect three seasons are: trade Belfour and Roberts for picks now to rebuild draft capital, lock Gaborik and Nash and Richards and Eminger on five-year deals at season end to split the cluster, and get Abid's renewal done before the open market finds him.

## Calendar

The deadline is 14 days away and Toronto are 106 points, 17 clear of second place. We are buyers, and the only question is what we buy and with what. The summer plan matters just as much because all 14 expiring contracts come due at once, and the game does not let us re-sign anyone before their deal ends.

**The keystone is still Belfour.** At $6.50M and age 39, he is the most valuable asset on the roster at the deadline: 92 base overall, expiring, and the over-80 rental mechanic means he moves for a pick or a player even to a team that has no goalie need. Colorado took the bait in February (offered Hejduk for him as an example). The GM has been sitting on this since February 28. Fourteen days is not a lot of time to negotiate a two-way deal that involves a star winger. If Belfour stays, we lose the pick capital AND the Havlat upgrade, because both paths run through the same currency.

**Havlat remains the scoring target.** OTT is confirmed at 63 points, 22-31-9. They are sellers. Havlat (23, 87 base, 80 points, $900K expiring) will walk in July. Tucker plus the 4th-rounder is the package, and the 4th is available only if Belfour goes to Colorado.

**Svehla is the next pick-recovery asset.** 36 years old, 92 CHKG, $3.60M expiring. If Belfour moves to Colorado for Hejduk (not a pick), Svehla becomes the best candidate to convert into a draft pick via the over-80 mechanic. A non-playoff team takes him for the checking; we recover a round 3 or 4.

**Roberts at 38 and $2.70M** is a summer release if he stays. His base overall needs checking against 80 — if he clears it, he moves for a pick at the deadline alongside Svehla. If not, he is $2.70M of dead money we carry into July and lose for nothing.

**The summer cluster: fifteen names, $25M+ hitting at once.** The game will not let us lock anyone early. Every re-signing happens in the same window. The plan:

- **5-6 years (franchise core):** Gaborik (23, 91 base, POTE 90, $1.10M → expect $4-5M demand), Eminger (21, POTE 99, $1.20M), Nash (20, $1.20M), Richards (24, $1.00M). These four are untouchable and get the long deals.
- **4-5 years (established):** Kaberle (27, $1.90M), Colaiacovo (22, $1.10M). Kaberle is the veteran top-pair D we built around; Colaiacovo at 22 with 0.36 ppg is depth that may not grow, but cheap on a 4-year deal.
- **2-3 years (depth):** Tellqvist (25, $0.80M), Abid (24, $0.40M), Smirnov (20, $0.40M), Chistov (21, $1.10M), Alexeev (23, $1.10M). Short deals keep the cluster staggered and preserve flexibility.
- **Let go:** Belfour (39, $6.50M — if he stays past the deadline and doesn't accept a reduced deal, he walks to retirement). Roberts (38, $2.70M — same logic). Upshall (21, $1.20M) — need to see whether his production at 21 justifies the money; if not, release.

**What the GM must do in the next two weeks:** Decide on Belfour. Everything else flows from that. If he goes to Colorado, we chase Havlat with Tucker+4th and Svehla for a pick. If he stays, we still move Svehla for a pick, but the scoring upgrade is dead for this deadline.

## League scan

The question this phase answers is: who across the league can Toronto acquire before March 19 that closes a structural gap, and why would his club say yes? Toronto's gaps are faceoffs (L4 mean 51, best 54), toughness on displayed grades (best 75), and the GM's standing order for a high-90s goalie from a non-contender. The currency is one fourth-rounder, Tucker (no unit, 83 CHKG), Chistov, and the rental assets Svehla ($3.60M, 1yr) and Roberts ($2.70M, 1yr) if the GM converts them to picks.

**Theodore** (MTL, G, 28) is the exact target the GM set on January 15: 91 base overall, POTE 87, high-90s on the glove and stick (GSH 86, SREC 83). MTL at 51 points is the worst club in the league with 15 expiring deals. He is on $5.50M expiring, which is expensive, but MTL cannot re-sign him and will not keep a 28-year-old goalie they cannot retain. His GAA (3.57) reflects MTL's defense, not his ability; on a top team he projects closer to Belfour's numbers. The cost is a question of whether MTL values a rental goalie at $5.50M as more than a second-rounder, but they have no draft capital either (5 picks, all late rounds). This is the goalie the GM asked for.

**Reid** (STL, RW, 23) is a new finding from the broad scan: 77 base, POTE 94, FACE 80, 52 points in 55 games (0.95 ppg), $600K expiring. He closes the faceoff gap and adds top-six scoring simultaneously at age 23 with elite potential. STL at 63 points with 8 expiring deals are a seller, though fewer expiring than MTL or LA means less desperation. At $600K, he is nearly free to acquire. The price is likely the 4th-rounder plus Chistov. He is better than Savard at the same faceoff level because he also produces at nearly a point a game and is two years younger with 10 more potential.

**Havlat** (OTT, RW, 23) remains the lead scoring target: 87 base, 80 points in 63 games (1.27 ppg), $900K expiring. OTT at 63 points with 11 expiring are confirmed sellers. The package (Tucker plus the 4th) is already built. If Reid lands, Havlat becomes a luxury the club cannot fund with one pick.

**Wanvig** (MTL, RW, 24) is the cheap toughness answer from the same desperate MTL club: 74 base, TOUG 88, CHKG 89, POTE 93, $600K expiring. His production is modest (18 points in 58 games) but his grades on stored values are the best available toughness profile at age 24. MTL at 51 points with 15 expiring will deal him for depth or a late pick. He does not close the displayed toughness gap tonight (form suppresses everyone) but adds a second 88+ TOUG body to the roster permanently.

**Cammalleri** (LA, RW, 22) and **Frolov** (LA, LW, 22) together fill two top-six spots for five years: 79/77 base, POTE 98/96, 47 points in 44 games and 45 points in 45 games respectively, both $1.10M expiring. LA at 65 points with 15 expiring are the most motivated sellers in the league. A double deal is ambitious for one 4th-rounder, but a partial package (say Svehla plus Chistov plus the 4th) might land one. Cammalleri at 1.07 ppg is the better scorer; Frolov at 1.00 with POTE 96 is the higher ceiling.

**Savard** (ATL, C, 27) folds into the ATL Kovalchuk/Heatley conversation at no extra pick cost: 89 FACE, 48 points in 43 games, $1.00M expiring. ATL at 68 points with 11 expiring cannot retain Kovalchuk and Heatley both. If ATL keeps one, Savard becomes the third asset they shed. He is less valuable than Reid at the same faceoff grade because he is four years older with POTE below 90 and lower production per game.

**Lalime** (OTT, G, 30) at 92 base is the highest-rated goalie on a non-contender: $1.90M expiring, OTT at 63 points, 11 expiring. But POTE 79 says his ceiling is set, and at 30 he is a rental, not a solution. Theodore at 91/87 POTE/28 is the same base grade with five years of runway for double the salary. Lalime is the cheaper option if MTL holds firm on Theodore.

**Belfour-to-Colorado logic**: Colorado at 86 points is a contender desperate for a goalie. Their expiring list includes Morris (D, 26, 85 base, 57 points in 65 games, $1.70M) and Tanguay (LW, 25, 85 base, 51 points in 65 games, $3.88M). Morris at 26 with 57 points as a defenseman on $1.70M is a better fit for Toronto's timeline than Hejduk at 31 and $4.50M. The GM should test whether Colorado offers Morris or Tanguay rather than Hejduk. If yes, Belfour goes for a young piece that keeps value in the window.

**What I would not do**: Chase Avery or Nichol for faceoffs. Avery has 7 points in 65 games; Nichol has 3 in 50. Their grades are real but their ice contribution is zero. Reid at 80 FACE with 52 points is the same role with a pulse.

## Trade construction

The question is: what three trades can Toronto execute before March 19 that respect every GM standing order (no Eminger, no McCabe, no Chara, Belfour is a live chip since Feb 21, Svehla is unprotected) and leave the playoff roster stronger than it is today.

**Belfour to Colorado** is the keystone. Colorado at 86 points has no playoff-ready goalie. The GM already tested and got Hejduk offered ($4.50M, 31, expiring). But Morris (D, 26, 85 base, 57 pts/65 GP, $1.70M expiring) is the better return: younger, cheaper, fills Toronto's blue line depth for the playoff run. Belfour's 22-5, 2.06 GAA, 0.927 SV is exactly what a Cup contender needs for April. Colorado sheds a player they can re-sign anyway and gets an elite backup for the run. We shed $6.50M of expiring salary and get a rental who plays top-four minutes for six weeks.

**Havlat from Ottawa** is the cleanest scoring upgrade available. He's 23, 87 base, 80 pts/63 GP, $900K expiring. Ottawa at 63 points with 11 expiring deals cannot re-sign him and would prefer a veteran body with term (Tucker, $1.30M, 2 years left, 92 CHKG stored) plus a 4th-rounder over losing Havlat for nothing in July. Tucker is in no unit — he is pure surplus. This costs us one 4th-rounder and one player we aren't dressing.

**Svehla to a non-contender for a pick** recovers draft capital via the over-80 expiring mechanic. He's 36, 92 CHKG, $3.60M expiring. Per the March 4 order, the destination must be a team not in the race: MTL at 51 points (worst in the league) with 15 expiring is the natural landing spot. They absorb him for nothing of consequence and hand us a pick back. This trade does not touch the Havlat package.

**The three trades are independent.** Belfour goes to Colorado, Svehla goes to Montreal, Tucker plus the 4th goes to Ottawa. We end with Havlat, Morris (or equivalent), one recovered pick, $6.50M less payroll, and the core untouched. If only Belfour and Svehla land, the 4th stays home for next year's draft and the core scoring is already sufficient with six players at 88+ overall.

**Luongo and DiPietro monitoring task** (assigned Jan 19, due Feb 20): complete. Luongo arrived on roster Feb 6 at 91 base, two years left, $1.60M. DiPietro at 7-12-0, 3.65 GAA has not translated his POTE 99; he is not a target. No further action needed.

## Owed

The goalie trade window job is done. The GM asked on Jan 19 to track Luongo and DiPietro for a possible acquisition; Luongo is now on Toronto's roster and the GM himself closed the file on Feb 19 with "Luongo is arrived. Goalies are solved. Done."

**Luongo** is here. 93 overall (91 base), 25 years old, $1.60M, 2 years left, 42 GP. He is the number one. The original Jan 19 target is acquired and signed through 2006-07.

**DiPietro** is at 80 overall (79 base), 49 GP, 25-21, $1.10M, 1 year left, playing elsewhere. He is irrelevant now: we have Luongo at 93 with two years, Belfour at 92 behind him, and Tellqvist developing. The GM's Feb 19 order ("do not revisit") covers this.

The Belfour-to-Colorado-for-Hejduk question the GM reopened on Feb 21 is a separate decision from this one. That item has its own thread and I am tracking it under the keystone-decision note.

This task is complete. No further monitoring needed.

# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-05

Next game at BUF on Sunday 06 March 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question this phase answers: are our 23-and-under players getting the games they've earned, with 15 left in the season?

**Spezza** remains the biggest development problem on this roster. POTE 99, age 21, 15 points in 37 games at 7.5 minutes a night, currently scratched. He produces 0.41 pts/g in those limited minutes, which is better per minute than Chistov (0.34) or Upshall (0.34) who play ahead of him. The remaining 15 games are the last window this season. He needs a third-wing role and 10+ minutes.

**Spacek** got his bump to 12+ minutes on March 4 against Ottawa, and the GM took that. Good. 44 GP, 16 points at 19 on 8.5 season MPG and POTE 91. Continue at 10+ minutes where the game script allows. This is working now and should become the pattern rather than the exception.

**Stahle** has four games all season. POTE 96, age 20, defenceman. Zero points in those four appearances. He is third on the depth chart behind Klesla (67 GP) and Eminger (49 GP), with Colaiacovo (31 GP) himself scratched most nights. With nothing to chase in the standings and a third D pair that needs filling, give Stahle a real run over the remaining 15 games, even if it costs Colaiacovo some of his rotation starts.

**Gaborik** (81 pts, 20.1 MPG, first line), **Chlup** (40 pts, 16.3 MPG, second line at 19) and **Nash** (35 pts in 54 games on third-line minutes) have each earned their roles and are getting them. No concern there.

**Klesla** plays every single game at 22 and produces 0.38 pts/g. That is not a minutes question, he has all of them. It is a production question, and at this rate the third pair belongs to Stahle or Colaiacovo next season regardless of who is ready now.

**Chistov** at 53 GP, 13 MPG, 0.34 pts/g, POTE 95 is getting an opportunity he hasn't seized. He is not costing anyone a chance though; he sits on the third line and the minutes are reasonable for his age.

**Smirnov** at POTE 70 and zero games in 67 is not being wasted. He is not earning a dressing, and that is fine.

**Eminger** at 20 points in 49 games (0.41 pts/g) has fallen back below the 0.50 threshold that kept him off the sell list. He is getting games, he is not converting them.

## Development trends

The season's back half separates players whose development is genuine from those whose early numbers were small-sample noise, and it tells you who to plan around for next year.

**Chlup** continues climbing at 19: 0.62 to 0.74 pts/g on minutes that doubled from 11 to 18. The Feb 23 note had him at 0.81 in a shorter window; 0.74 over 56 games is the more sustainable read. He belongs in the top nine permanently and needs nothing from you.

**Chistov** is the quiet gain. 0.29 to 0.36 pts/g on minutes rising from 9.5 to 14.2 at 21. He is growing into a top-nine role without anyone forcing it. Keep giving him the ice.

**Stahle** finally played: 4 games at 17.8 MPG. The Jan 25 note (zero games in 49) is partially resolved. No points yet, but he is on the ice now. The next test is whether the minutes stick past the deadline.

**Nash** went from 0.83 to 0.50 pts/g at 20 on flat minutes (12.9 to 12.3). That is the wrong direction at that age. The GM's Jan 4 position was "they will grow into it," and so far they are not growing. Watch the next three weeks before drawing conclusions, but the trend is not what you want.

**Spacek** is at 0.30 pts/g on 6.0 MPG across the last 33 games at 19. I recommended 12+ MPG on March 4 and you took it, but no game has happened since so the effect is untested. If the minutes do not materialize in the next two games, the development case for dressing him dies.

**Spezza** remains stuck: 0.43 to 0.38 pts/g on minutes falling from 9.1 to 5.3 at 21 with POTE 99. I have raised this since January with no movement. The window to use him this season is closing.

**Klesla** at 0.50 to 0.33 pts/g on flat minutes at 22 confirms the Feb 21 trade flag. A season rate that keeps falling with no age excuse makes him harder to move later.

**Colaiacovo** is the newest concern: 0.44 to 0.36 pts/g at 22 on minutes down from 18.9 to 17.5. The expected direction at 22 is up. Two data points in a month (he was at 0.36 last check too) suggest this is a floor, not a dip.

**Jackman** is the loudest problem on the blue line. 0.65 to 0.38 pts/g at 24 while playing 31.2 minutes a night. His production nearly halved and his load went up. At 24 that combination is either a system fit issue or burnout creeping in. Something has to give.

**Fischer** continues declining: 0.63 to 0.40 at 24 on rising minutes (20.8 to 22.6). GM's keeper on the record, so no trade call. But the four-year contract for a player whose numbers are sliding is a planning problem worth raising in the offseason.

**Afinogenov** at 25 dropped from 1.17 to 0.72 pts/g on flat minutes. He should be peaking. This is the most unexpected decline among players aged 22 to 27.

**Abid** went 1.09 to 0.91 on minutes falling from 20.1 to 13.8 at 24. He is sliding down the lineup and his production follows. At 24 you would not bench this without a reason; find out if the coach in your head has one.

**McCabe** shows 0.49 pts/g in the 43 games since Dec 1. The Mar 4 note put him off the sell list at 0.83 season-total, which includes October's 1.42 over 24 games. The back half is 0.49. At 29 that is the age talking. I stand by keeping him for now but this direction is not reversible.

**The veterans** are doing what 34, 36, and 38-year-olds do. Sundin at 0.91 over 67, Roberts at 0.86 over 67, Mogilny at 0.79 over 63. They are carrying minutes they should not need at this stage, which is the real story: the team needs them because the 22-to-25 group is not stepping up.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy heading into Buffalo, and the one name that should concern us has been frozen for three months.

**Spezza** sits at 86, the lowest on the roster, and hasn't moved in any meaningful way across dozens of saves. At 7.5 MPG and 15 points in 37 games, he's below the 10-minute band a player at his calibre expects. The +1 tick is the first change anyone has seen from him. I have raised this five times since January with no movement; at this point it's a roster decision, not a line-matching one.

**Spacek** at 92 with a +5 jump is the proof the minutes lever works. He was stuck at 8.5 and depressed at -4 earlier; after the 12+ MPG bump on March 4th, he climbed. Keep that going.

**The rest of the room** is 96 to 100 with +5 or +3 movement across Sundin, Mogilny, Richards, Afinogenov, Chlup, Gaborik, Jackman, Nash, and nearly everyone else. That's a win streak doing what it should. No intervention needed.

**Alexeev** at 92 and 8.3 MPG with 30 points in 55 games is the next kid who'll drift if he stays scratched. His morale hasn't cracked yet, but 30 points at a depth salary means he's more than a fourth-liner. Watch him after Buffalo.

## Role composition

The question here is whether the parts on each unit fit what that unit is supposed to do, and where the roster simply cannot fill a role no matter how I shuffle them.

**L4** is the one arrangement problem I can see. Spacek, Abid and Upshall carry a faceoff mean of 51 with a best of 54. That is not a line that can protect its own zone off a draw against a competent centre. The structural fix would be dropping Richards (74) or Chlup (79) down to centre that line, but both are linchpins above — Richards anchors L3's two-way game and Chlup's development depends on the minutes he gets on L2. I am leaving it alone tonight because BUF's centres are not elite (their top line is not in the brief's matchup data), and moving Richards or Chlup down costs more than the faceoff problem costs us against this specific opponent.

**Toughness is a roster-level gap.** Jackman at 76 is the ceiling on the entire blue line and front. Nobody else clears 72. We are a skill club relying on team structure for deterrence, not a player who changes the opponent's behaviour just by existing on the ice. I cannot fix this with line changes. If the GM ever wants to add a presence, it has to come via trade or free agency.

**P1 and P2 are built correctly.** P1 has Gaborik (scoring 99, clutch 99) with Sundin quarterbacking and Kaberle on the point. P2 gets Mogilny (scoring 94) and Chlup's emerging hands. The units do not overlap in ways that waste a player.

**K2 is actually our hardest PK unit** (checking mean 76, toughness mean 68, Jackman and McCabe both there). K1 is lighter physically but has Sundin for draws. This split makes sense: K2 kills against the opponent's PP1 and K1 handles the second unit. No change.

**L2's checking mean of 66 is the lowest on the roster**, but this is the skill line and that is acceptable. Chlup, Mogilny and Afinogenov are there to create offence, not to win board battles.

No composition change tonight. The only open question is the L4 faceoff gap, which I am flagging as a roster gap rather than a lineup problem.

## Opponent matchup

The question this phase answers: does BUF present any matchup problem that should override our normal approach, or is this a development-friendly game we slot into the schedule?

It's a development game. BUF is 23-29-6, last-10 WLLOLLLLLW, and we've beaten them 24-2 in three meetings. They score 1.80 per game and their PP is 19-for-197, under 10%. Their best forward is Nolan at 82 OVR, and their top pair is McKee (71) and Bombardir (69). This is not a quality opponent and the GM's own framework says development priority applies in games we can afford.

**Fischer and Jackman** stay on pair one against BUF's top line (Nolan-Drury-Briere, OVR 82/80/76). Combined 167 against 238 in BUF's favour on paper, but our first pair has been the backbone all year: Fischer 0.47 pts/g at 22.0 MPG, Jackman at 30.8 MPG. The slot order is already right, no adjustment needed.

**Eminger** sits on pair three against BUF's bottom unit (Gaustad 68, Brunette 70, Dumont 72). That hides him against the weakest line on the other side. His 0.41 pts/g over 49 games makes him the sell at season's end, but tonight he's matched well and doesn't need pulling.

**Spacek and Nash** are both already in the lineup: Spacek centreing the fourth, Nash on the left of the third. This is exactly the game to let them have minutes. I would give Spacek as much of the fourth line as the GM can afford, maybe some time on the second centre if Chlup's endurance dips (ENDU 68 at 19). Reason class: development.

**Belfour starts.** He's at 92 OVR, morale 99, and carries no fatigue icon. No reason to look at Ouellet.

**Sell-order update (standing order #1):** McCabe holds at 0.82 pts/g over 67 games, 22.7 MPG. Still off the list. Sell order unchanged: Eminger first (0.41 in 49), Klesla second (0.39 in 67, declining at 22), Sami Salo third (0.30 in 27). No change.

No changes to make tonight. The matchup slots are already right, Belfour is fresh, and the young guys are already dressed.

## Owed

**Defenceman sell-list update for BUF on Sunday, game #1 of the standing job.**

The headline change since my last note on March 4th: **Salo is gone.** He was second on the sell order and he's been dealt. That leaves Eminger as the top candidate and Klesla second.

**McCabe** — 55 points in 67 games, 0.82 pts/g, 22.7 MPG. I had him at 0.83 over 66 on March 4th; he's essentially flat and still the most productive blue-liner. Off the sell list. Stays.

**Kaberle** — 32 points in 59, 0.54 pts/g. GM called him a star and a keeper. Agreed, no change.

**Jackman** — 31 points in 65, 0.48 pts/g, 30.8 MPG. Not a sell at $0.70M x 3 with a 71 base, but that minute load is a morale risk for a 24-year-old. Not a trade target, just a watch item.

**Fischer** — 29 points in 62, 0.47 pts/g. GM's keeper, no discussion.

**Eminger** — 20 points in 49, **0.41 pts/g**. He was at 0.44 on February 26th and has slipped again. Age 21, $1.2M expiring, 75 OVR. Third-pair production on an expiring deal. Top sell candidate.

**Klesla** — 26 points in 67, **0.39 pts/g**. I flagged him at 0.38 on February 21st; he's been flat at a rate a 22-year-old should be exceeding. $0.90M x 2. Second sell candidate if a bid appears.

**Colaiacovo** — 12 points in 31, 0.39 pts/g, scratched. $1.10M x 1. Could be moved as depth, but his low games make it hard to argue he's hurt us.

Sell order with three games left: **Eminger first, Klesla second, Colaiacovo third.** Nothing else has moved.

# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-04

Toronto 45-12-4, 104 pts after 66 games.

## Role coverage

The role coverage question answers what the playoff roster can and cannot do, and at 66 games with 16 left it determines whether March 19 spending is needed. The short answer: Toronto are covered everywhere except one gap the coach has correctly identified, and that gap is a depth-of-roster problem at defenceman, not a weakness in the top pair.

**Checking (defence side):** McCabe 86 and Fischer 82 are the only D under 36 who check 80+. They are paired together on D1, so there is no backup if either goes down or draws a tough assignment. Svehla at 83 is the next man, but he is 36 and expiring. This is the coach's gap, and it is real. Tucker at 83 is a forward, not a solution.

**Checking (forward side):** Roberts 86, Tucker 83, Upshall 80. Tucker is not dressed. Put him in. The Dec 7 note recorded his stored grades at 92 CHKG / 88 TOUG — today's displayed 83 is form-depressed but still the second-best forward checker available. The coach fixes this one himself by dressing Tucker.

**Toughness:** Zero at 80+ on today's displayed grades, with Roberts 73 the best. This is the form artifact established on Feb 21. Six players have stored TOUG 80+. No trade is warranted to close a gap that does not exist on stored grades.

**Faceoffs:** Sundin 90 is the only 80+. Richards at 70 is the next-best option and is already slotted at third-line centre. Chlup at 75 at 19 is the future answer. This is thin for playoff series where draws matter, but the GM already closed the Bell question, and Richards at 70 in a bottom-six role is adequate.

**Scoring:** Twelve at 80+, headlined by Mogilny 94 (36), Sundin 92 (34), Gaborik 92 (23), Afinogenov 90 (25). Deep today. The age curve is the concern: Mogilny 36 and Roberts 38 carry meaningful minutes now, and by next season Gaborik and Afinogenov must carry the load alone. That is a next-season problem, not a deadline one.

**Durability:** Only four at 80+. Roberts 98, Afinogenov 95, Fischer 92, Abid 90. Eminger sits at 75, Gaborik and Kaberle are not shown in the 80+ tier. This is a long-term risk for a young core but does not change the March 19 plan.

**Goalies:** Luongo 25 with 2 years left is the starter. Belfour 39 with 21-5, 2.10 GAA, 0.925 SV is the playoff number one. Ouellet 23 at 2.08 GAA and 0.923 in 11 games is the third-string. The GM's order is final: goalies are solved.

**The single actionable gap:** D-side checking depth below McCabe/Fischer. The coach needs a seventh defenceman who checks 80+ for playoff series, or at minimum insurance. Svehla fills that role this year at 83 but walks in July unless re-signed. Next season leaves only McCabe and Fischer. This is a summer problem more than a deadline one, since no deadline D at 80+ CHKG is available without violating the GM's protective orders on Eminger and McCabe.

**Koltsov** is at 92 speed and not lined. The coach should dress him.

## Trajectory

Is Toronto aging into a cliff? No — the age curve (15 at ≤23, 11 at 24-29) is the shape the manual asks for. The danger is not age but a single summer where 12 of those young players hit the market at once, and a payroll that will spike when their cheap contracts become real ones.

**The veterans are the shed, not the problem.** Sundin ($8.40M, 5 years, 74 pts at 34) is the one you keep — expensive but productive, and locked long. The other four at 34+ — Belfour ($6.50M, 39), Mogilny ($5.50M, 36), Svehla ($3.60M, 36), Roberts ($2.70M, 38) — are $18.30M combined. Three of them expire this July and are over-80 on stored grades, which means each recovers a draft pick. Roberts runs through July, Svehla through July, Belfour through July. Mogilny has two years but his $5.50M is a candidate to shed at next deadline once the renewal salary bumps land.

**The July 2005 cluster is the real cliff.** Twelve players worth $12.50M in current salary need new deals. Gaborik ($1.10M, 81 pts, 23) alone will demand a raise of $3-5M on a five-year extension. Richards ($1.00M, 57 pts, 24) adds another $2-4M. Nash, Eminger, Kaberle, Chistov, Alexeev, Abid, Upshall, Colaiacovo, Tellqvist, Smirnov — all get raises. Realistic new payroll on those twelve: $35-45M versus $12.50M today, a jump of $20-30M.

**Payroll against revenue leaves room only if veterans walk.** Current payroll is $65.54M against $86.75M revenue ($25.11M profit). Add $20-30M in renewal raises and you are at $85-95M against roughly the same revenue. Profit vanishes. Shedding Belfour, Svehla and Roberts ($12.80M) at the deadline gets you back into black territory. Salo ($2.60M, scratched, 2 years, 27 GP) is the next one to go if you can move him.

**Draft capital is a single fourth-rounder.** You own nothing better. The over-80 expiring mechanic is your only path back to picks. Belfour, Svehla, Roberts — three recoverable picks from a roster that currently holds one. That is the trade deadline's trajectory value: not just a player return, but three first or second-rounders recovered from nothing.

**The three-season picture.** If the renewals land staggered — Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger on 5-6 years; Kaberle, Chistov, Alexeev, Abid on 3-4 years — then in 2007-08 you have Gaborik at 26, Nash at 23, Eminger at 24, Chlup at 22, Richards at 27, Kaberle at 30. That is the window. The risk is contract clustering: 5-6 year deals signed in July 2005 all come up in July 2010 or 2011. The stagger (some 3-4 years) splits that into two waves. Fischer ($3.70M, 4 years, declining from 0.63 to 0.41 pts/g) becomes trade bait in 2007-08 when his value has bottomed.

## Calendar

**Are we buyers or sellers, and what is the summer plan for the fifteen expiring contracts?**

We are buyers. Toronto sit 104 points, 15 clear of New Jersey with 16 games left. The playoffs are locked, and the manual says buy for need. The Coach's gap is one more defenceman with CHKG 80+; we have McCabe and Fischer already paired on D1, and that is it. We also need the Belfour decision to land before March 19, because that trade is the keystone that funds everything else.

**The deadline is 15 days away.** Belfour (93/92 base, $6.50M) is our only over-80 expiring asset that the GM has left open, and Svehla (84/85 base, $3.60M) is a pick-recovery candidate via the over-80 mechanic. Roberts (87/87, $2.70M, 38) is the third over-80 expiring player and is also movable. The summer cluster — 15 deals worth roughly $25M — is where the real planning matters, and I need to sort each name into renew, move, or release before I can tell you what we can afford to buy in.

I need a few data points before I can write the final plan: our D and G depth to size the coach's gap precisely, the deadline market for checking D, our actual pick inventory, and the Luongo/DiPietro monitoring update I owe from the January 19 task.

## League scan

Toronto at 104 points after 66 games are the clear first team in the league, so the March 19 question is not whether to be a buyer but what to buy with a single fourth-round pick and what to sell to recover more picks. The coach's team-wide scoring problem and the D-side checking gap are the two needs, but the pick constraint means we can pursue only one external acquisition unless the Belfour-to-Colorado trade lands and returns the pick.

**Havlat (OTT)** remains the lead deadline target. At 23 with 87 base, 80 points in 63 games, $900K expiring, he fits the timeline and the salary structure better than anyone on the board. Ottawa at 63 points with 11 expiring contracts cannot retain him. The price is Tucker plus the fourth-rounder. Tucker's 83 CHKG is useful but he is not dressed and not needed; the fourth is the only one we own. This is the move that addresses the coach's team-wide scoring dip.

**Komisarek (MTL)** is the best cost-to-value on the board if we can stack packages. At 23 with 83 TOUG, POTE 90, $1.10M expiring, 58 GP, he closes the D-side physicality gap the coach flagged. Montreal at 51 points with 15 expiring are the league's worst sellers. But we cannot spend the same fourth on both Havlat and Komisarek. If Belfour-to-Colorado recovers pick capital, this becomes possible; if not, it stays a summer target via free agency.

**ATL's Kovalchuk-Heatley binary** has shifted. Atlanta at 68 points with 16 games left are closer to contention than they were at 63 points in February. Kovalchuk (104 pts/61 GP, 21, $1.10M expiring) and Heatley (96 pts/58 GP, 24, $1.10M expiring) are both generational scoring, but ATL may decide to keep one or both if they claw into a playoff spot. I would not commit the fourth here without confirmation that ATL will sell.

**Cammalleri + Frolov (LA)** at 22, POTE 98 and 96 respectively, both at $1.10M expiring, both producing above 1.15 pts/g. LA at 65 points with 14 expiring are a confirmed seller. A double acquisition fills two top-six roles for five years on cheap deals. But the price would need to exceed what a single fourth buys. This is realistic only if we also shed Svehla ($3.60M, expiring) or Roberts ($2.70M, expiring) to recover a pick as a separate transaction.

**Bell (CHI)** at 24, 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 87 FACE, 80 base, $900K with two years left, closes the D-side checking gap by giving the coach a forward who checks like a defenceman. Chicago at 59 points with 10 expiring are sellers. The price of R2 plus Colaiacovo is steep with one pick remaining. I would only pursue this if Havlat falls through.

**Svehla (TOR)** is a sell-side target, not an acquisition. At 36, 92 CHKG, $3.60M expiring, he is the second-best over-80 pick-recovery asset after Belfour. Moving him before March 19 recovers a pick that funds a second acquisition. If he walks in July, that capital is gone.

**The Luongo/DiPietro monitoring task** (asked 2005-01-19) is complete. Luongo is on our roster at 91 base with 2 years. DiPietro at 79 base and 3.65 GAA never translated his potential and NYI will re-sign rather than deal. Neither is a trade target.

**The Belfour-to-Colorado decision** is the keystone. If Hejduk comes for Belfour, we get a top-line winger with years left and the 4th stays home for Havlat. If Belfour retires in July, we lose both the asset and the pick recovery. The GM said Feb 21 this is undecided; it needs to close within two weeks.

## Trade construction

The March 19 question is what we buy with one fourth-rounder and what we sell to fund it, given that the Belfour decision cascades into every other trade we can make. Three proposals follow, ranked by what unlocks the rest.

**Belfour to Colorado for Hejduk** is the keystone. GM tested this personally and Colorado offered Hejduk. At 92 base with 21-5, 2.10 GAA, 0.925 SV, Belfour is the best available playoff goalie on the market, and Colorado have no answer in net. Hejduk is a top-line winger on a reasonable multi-year salary — exactly the "locked on reasonable salary for a couple of years" return GM asked for on Feb 21. We shed $6.50M and get a scorer. If this lands, the 4th stays home for Havlat, and the whole deadline becomes possible.

**Havlat for Tucker plus the 4th** is the lead player acquisition. At 23 with 80 points in 63 games on $900K expiring, he slots into our top six for the playoff run and fits the young core timeline. Ottawa at 63 points with 11 expiring deals cannot retain him. Tucker is surplus (3 GP this season, not in any unit) and the 4th is our only pick. The net salary swing is minus $400K this year. Acceptance uncertainty: Ottawa must value Tucker's 92 stored CHKG and a 4th-rounder highly enough against Havlat's 87 base and 80-point season.

**Svehla for a draft pick** is pure pick recovery. The over-80 expiring mechanic means any contender needing a veteran top-4 D for the playoffs takes him for a pick. At 36, $3.60M expiring, 92 CHKG, he is insurance that costs us nothing after July. Moving him recovers a second-round-caliber pick from a player we will not re-sign. This is independent of the other two and should run in parallel.

**If none land:** dress Tucker (92 CHKG stored, 88 TOUG) as the fourth-line checker the coach wants, dress Koltsov (92 ACCE displayed) for speed on the bottom six, and play the roster as-is into the playoffs. At 104 points with Sundin 74 pts, Mogilny 69, Gaborik 81, the scoring is there when form returns. The D-checking gap (no 80+ CHKG behind McCabe 86 and Fischer 82) is a summer problem — Svehla fills it through July regardless.

## Owed

The task was "monitor Luongo availability and DiPetro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window," assigned January 19. The window closed itself before the deadline. Here is where both stand now.

**Luongo** is on our roster. 94 overall, 25 years old, $1.60M, 2 years remaining, 42 games played. He arrived between mid-January and now, and the GM declared goalies solved on February 19: "Luongo is arrived. Goalies are solved. Done." No further monitoring is needed. He is not a trade target; he is our number one.

**DiPetro** at NYI: 23 years old, 81 overall (79 base), $1.10M expiring, 24-21 record with a 2.88 GAA and 0.877 save percentage in 48 games. He is developing but he was never the answer. The January 15 standing order set the goal as "a really good high-90s goalie from a team that will not be a contender." DiPetro at 79 base is not that player, and NYI at their current record are not a seller willing to deal cheaply.

What changed since January 19: Luongo went from a trade possibility to our starting goaltender with two years of club control at below-market money. The entire premise of the task, that we needed to fetch a high-90s goalie from elsewhere, is resolved. This item is closed.
