# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-04

Next game at OTT on Friday 04 March 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question: which young players are getting the games their potential and production have earned, and which ones aren't. With 66 games played and 16 left, every night from here is a choice about who grows.

Tonight is away at Ottawa (22-30). By the GM's own framework — development priority applies when we can afford it — tonight is a development night. Ottawa is not a quality opponent.

**Spezza** is still the loudest problem. POTE 99, 37 games, 7.5 MPG, 15 points. Morale at 86 is the lowest in the young group and it will keep falling. At 21 with the top potential marking on the roster, 7.5 minutes on nights he's dressed is nothing. I've raised this six times now. Tonight against Ottawa is the kind of game where 15 MPG costs nothing in the standings.

**Stahle** has 4 games in 66. POTE 96 at 20, 17.8 MPG in the four he's played. He is the biggest development waste on the roster and the gap has grown since I flagged it January 25th. He needs 20+ games before the season ends or this year is gone.

**Alexeev** at 55 games, 30 points, 8.3 MPG is producing at 0.55 pts/g — above fourth-line rates — but gets scratched anyway. At 23 he is near the end of his window. Either give him a real role or acknowledge he is a depth player with no upside left to chase.

**Spacek** at 43 games, 8.5 MPG, POTE 91. I've asked repeatedly for 12+ MPG. Morale 92 is holding but won't forever. Tonight against Ottawa, bump him to 12. It costs us nothing against a 22-30 club.

**Chlup** is the counter-example. 38 points in 55 games, 16.3 MPG on the second line at 19, morale 96. He earned this. No change.

**Nash** at 33 points in 53 games on 12.7 MPG, L3, morale 99. Earning his role, earning it well. No change.

**Smirnov** has zero games but POTE 70 — the lowest of the young group. He is not a waste; his ceiling is genuinely below the others. Not a crisis.

**Upshall** at 9.4 MPG and POTE 99 is underused but only slightly. 0.35 pts/g is fourth-line production. No action needed tonight.

**Klesla**, **Eminger**, **Chistov**, **Colaiacovo**, **Gaborik** — all getting appropriate roles for their current level. No change.

## Development trends

The development picture is split: three young players growing into real roles, one quietly vanishing, and four veterans aging off the same cliff at once.

**Chlup** at 19 went from 0.62 to 0.71 pts/g while minutes nearly doubled from 11.0 to 17.9 across 55 games. He is doing what you want a young centre to do: produce more as the load gets heavier. He belongs in the top nine and does not need another word from me.

**Chistov** at 21 moved from 0.29 to 0.34 pts/g while minutes climbed from 9.5 to 14.5 across 52 games. Both numbers moving the right way at the same time. He is quietly growing into a second or third-line winger and nobody has noticed. Worth knowing for next year's planning.

**Spacek** at 19 is going the wrong way hard: 0.55 down to 0.31 pts/g, minutes gutted from 16.0 to 5.9. Forty-three games in and he has lost both the role and the production. I have raised this four times since February with no movement. He is not developing at this usage.

**Spezza** at 21 mirrors Spacek: 0.43 down to 0.38 pts/g, minutes from 9.1 to 5.3. Thirty-seven games at 5.3 minutes a night wastes a POTE 99 player. Same pattern, same fix needed.

**Nash** at 20 fell from 0.83 to 0.45 pts/g while minutes stayed flat at roughly 12.5. His rate halved without a minutes loss, which means opponents have solved him or his game has dipped. At 20 this is recoverable but worth watching.

**Koltsov** at 23 started the season at 1.10 pts/g in 10 games and is now at 0.28 over 35. His trade value is evaporating by the week. If he is still a chip, use him now.

**Abid** at 24 is losing minutes from 20.1 down to 13.8 while his rate slid from 1.09 to 0.93. That is a 6-minute-per-game drop at an age when he should be cementing a role, not losing one.

**Fischer** at 24 has gone from 0.63 to 0.38 pts/g while minutes rose from 20.8 to 22.3. More ice, less production. GM's keeper, so no trade call, but a four-year contract behind a declining rate is a planning flag for the off-season.

**McCabe** at 29 is 1.42 down to 0.50 pts/g. The loudest sell on the blue line has gotten louder. Four years and $3M for a 0.50 defenceman is the biggest asset problem on this roster.

**Klesla** at 22 slid from 0.50 to 0.29 on flat minutes of roughly 14.7. No excuse at 22. Still tradeable.

The veterans tell one story. **Sundin** at 34 (1.46→0.93, minutes 16.9→21.2), **Mogilny** at 36 (1.62→0.79, 16.9→19.8), **Roberts** at 38 (1.29→0.88, 16.5→20.9), **Svehla** at 36 (0.78→0.44, 23.8→20.8). All four getting more minutes while producing less per minute. This is the right way to decline and the only way to decline. But four players aging together means the roster loses a block next summer, and the young group has to be ready. Chlup and Chistov are trending toward that. Klesla and Colaiacovo are not.

No grade changes on the card in this window, so everything above rests on production and minutes.

## Morale watch

The room is right, and that matters tonight because Ottawa is a 22-win club and morale at this level is an asset against a team with nothing to play for.

**Spezza** remains the only player below 90. He sits at 86 on 7.5 minutes a night, scratched from the lineup. At 21 with whatever upside he carries, this is the fifth time I have raised it and the numbers have not moved. His morale has stabilized around 86 rather than continuing to slide, so it is not bleeding, but it is not recovering either because he is not getting the minutes to recover.

**Abid** is the one to watch going forward. 65 points in 66 games at 15.9 MPG puts him 4 minutes under what a 90+ player expects. His morale is at 99 so nothing is wrong today, but a point-per-game scorer on the fourth line is a structural imbalance that will bite if results turn. No change tonight.

**Spacek** at 92 morale and 8.5 MPG is slightly under his expected band for a 70s-rated player (10 MPG). Close enough that the gap is not causing damage. Same story as every night for a month.

Everyone else is at 96 or 99 with positive movement. The veterans (Sundin 19.6 MPG, Mogilny 18.7) are getting the minutes their calibre demands. The young core on the second and third lines (Chlup 16.3, Richards 16.7, Nash 12.7, Chistov 13.1) are all climbing. The blue line is clean: Fischer, McCabe, Kaberle, Svehla all at 21-23 MPG, all at 99. No change needed tonight.

## Role composition

**Kaberle on the penalty kill** is the one composition problem I can see, and it is not a lineup problem — it is a depth problem. He carries 84 stamina (second on the roster) and a 0.66 pts/g season rate, which makes him valuable at even strength and on P1. His checking sits below the top four (84 is Roberts, McCabe, Fischer, Abid). K2 checking mean reads 73 against 86 best, and McCabe and Abid are pulling that unit while Kaberle is the drag. But the D alternatives are Salo (collapsed, 0.18 pts/g), Colaiacovo (72 OVR, developing), and Stahle (zero games this season). There is no arrangement that fixes this without making things worse. He stays.

**Sundin on K1** might look like a luxury, but the unit checks 74/91 with Roberts, Fischer, and Eminger all in the 84-checking range. Sundin's positioning and stick (91 faceoffs) help him in the PK structure. He's there because the first unit needs a center who can win a loose puck off a clear. This works.

**L3 is not a checking line and shouldn't be treated as one.** Checking mean 70 against a best of 94 (Klesla) means one man carries the physical load while Nash and Chistov bring speed (99 best). Richards at center (75 faceoffs, 86 stamina, the best on the roster) provides the workhorse minutes. The line's job is transition speed, not grinding. Composition suits the role.

**Faceoff depth is a roster gap.** Only three centers at 75+: Sundin 91, Chlup 80, Richards 75. Everyone else is below 75, meaning third and fourth lines lose the draw by default in any important situation. This costs us zone entries on the faceoff win. The GM should know we are one injury to Richards or Chlup away from a 50% faceoff team.

**No change to any unit.** Every line's composition suits what it is asked to do. The Spacek minutes issue (6.6 MPG) is deployment, not composition — already raised, no movement.

## Opponent matchup

**Can we exploit the matchup gap between Ottawa's top line and the rest of their roster?** Yes, and our current lines already do it.

**Ottawa's structure** is top-heavy in the worst way for them. Alfredsson (90 OVR) and Havlat (88 OVR) are a genuine top line — Havlat's 99 speed and 99 agility mean someone has to run with him. Below that, Fisher's line at 80/74/83 is average, the third line is 78/76/76, and the fourth is 72/72/66. Their PP is 24 on 206 attempts: 11.7%. They will not score on our PK.

**Our top pairing (Fischer/McCabe)** faces their top line most via auto-pairing. Fischer's 94 speed tracks Havlat's 99 closely enough, and his 91 checking means he can actually engage. McCabe's 81 speed is the weak link but we have no better option — swapping Kaberle/Svehla to the first pair puts a 70-checking defenceman against the net-front battle. Keep the pairs set.

**Our bottom six owns theirs.** Richards (86), Nash (82), Chistov (81) against 78/76/76 is a three-grade gap per man. Their fourth line is the weakest we'll see all week at 72/72/66. Per the GM's framework, a 22-30-9 opponent is a night where development is affordable.

**Belfour starts.** 93 OVR against a team scoring 2.70 per game on a 11.7% PP. Check his fatigue icon before the game but there is no reason to look past him.

**Defenceman assessment (ongoing duty):** McCabe remains the sell — OVR 83 with the Feb 12 note flagging 0.33 pts/g in his recent window against a 0.89 season rate at age 29. Eminger's OVR is 76 with ENDU 50, and the Feb 26 finding puts him back on the sell list at 0.17 pts/g in his last six. Klesla at 83 OVR but 54 ENDU continues his decline at age 22 (0.38 pts/g season). Fischer and Kaberle are keepers. Svehla stays as the GM's MVP. No change to who plays; the sell order remains McCabe, Eminger, Klesla, Salo.

## Owed

**D-man sell order for season's end, updated for March 4.** This is the standing job: who goes, who stays.

**McCabe** was my loudest sell on Feb 12 at a 0.33 recent window. He has pulled out of that slide: 55 points in 66 games is 0.83 pts/g on the season. He added 7 in the 16 games since late January (0.44), so February was a real dip but not a collapse. At 0.83 he is still the highest-producing D on this roster. Off the sell list. The concern at 29 with 4 years is that 0.83 may be the new ceiling, not a temporary dip, but that is a summer conversation.

**Eminger** at 20 points in 48 games is 0.42 pts/g. Still below my 0.45 threshold. Expired $1.2M, age 21. He is the first D cut. Nothing has moved since Feb 26.

**Klesla** at 24 in 66 is 0.36 pts/g, down from 0.38 in my last read. Minutes flat at 14.7. At 22 the direction should be up; it is not. $0.9M x 2 makes him tradeable for depth rather than a dump.

**Salo** is 8 in 27 (0.30) and not dressed. At 30 with $2.6M x 2, he is the second cut after Eminger. Same call as before, no change.

**Svehla** at 0.58 pts/g, **Fischer** at 0.46, **Kaberle** at 0.55 — all stay. No change.

The sell order: Eminger, Salo, Klesla. McCabe moved off the list this week.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-02

# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-02

Toronto 44-12-4, 102 pts after 65 games.

## Role coverage

The question is whether Toronto's roster holes require trade currency or can be closed by the coach, and whether the toughness gap the coach flags at 72 is real. The short answer: the toughness gap is a form artifact, the faceoff gap is real but has no clean external fix, and the one immediate action is dressing Tucker for the five games he can play.

**Toughness** shows zero at 80+ on today's display (best 73, Roberts and McCabe). This is the same reading from Feb 24 that was resolved on Feb 21 as a form artifact: stored grades carry six players at 80+ TOUG and seven at 83+ CHKG. The entire club's engine form is depressed simultaneously, which is why every toughness grade reads 10-14 points below its stored value. No external acquisition is needed here. Tucker's stored TOUG 84 and CHKG 88 (from the internal fallback note) are the proof: he reads 70/83 today because form is suppressing him, not because he lacks the tool.

**Checking** is covered on paper (6 at 80+), but only 5 are active because Tucker sits in no unit. Roberts 86, McCabe 86, Svehla 83, Fischer 82, Upshall 80 all play; Tucker 83 does not. Dressing Tucker makes the group sufficient for a playoff series without any trade.

**Faceoffs** is the genuine structural gap. Sundin 90 is the only 80+ man; next best is Chlup 75, Richards 70. A Sundin injury leaves no one who can win draws at the playoff level. Avery at LA (93 FACE, $400K, 2 years) would close it, but his 0.11 points per game kills the trade case for a contending club, and Bell was killed by the GM because both he and the need are centre-side while Bell plays wing. No external fix clears the GM's bar. This is a known limitation to plan around for next season's centre market.

**Scoring, playmaking, speed, stamina, clutch, durability**: all deeply covered. Twelve at 80+ in scoring, twelve in playmaking, twenty-two in speed. No external need.

**Salo** at 88 scoring, 30 years old, is not lined in any unit. Playoff roster depth could use him on a lower pair or as the extra body. His 88 base is above several players who do dress.

**Koltsov** at 92 speed, 23, also not lined. He is a development piece the coach is not evaluating with 18 games left.

**Age curve**: Roberts 38, Mogilny 36, Svehla 36, Svehla's 94 stamina keeps him effective tonight but not next year. Sundin 34 at 21 MPG with a declining rate. The checking group loses Roberts and Svehla in the same window unless replacements are developed. Tucker at 29 and McCabe at 29 are the bridge.

## Trajectory

The age curve is healthy; the contract structure is the cliff.

Toronto have 15 players at 23 or under, 11 at 24–29, one at 30–33, and five at 34 or above. That is the manual's shape almost exactly: six veterans, 26 young players, the curve weighted toward the young end. The problem is that 15 of those 32 contracts expire in the same July, carrying $25.30M and the entire young core.

**The July 2005 wall.** Gaborik (81 pts, $1.10M), Richards (56 pts, $1.00M), Nash (33 pts, $1.20M), Eminger (20 pts, POTE 99, $1.20M), Upshall (POTE 99, $1.20M), Chistov (POTE 95, $1.10M), Alexeev (30 pts, POTE 94, $1.10M), Abid (65 pts, POTE 94, $0.40M), Kaberle (31 pts, $1.90M), Colaiacovo (POTE 99, $1.10M) — all free agents the same day. At season end these players will have production on their sheets and will demand multiples of their current salaries. A realistic scenario: the top five get $3–5M, the depth six get $1.5–2.5M, adding $15–25M to payroll in one summer. Current profit is $24.28M, so the club survives, but a bad first round would make those numbers tight.

**The July 2006 wave.** Ten contracts worth $18.04M expire a year later, and five of them carry POTE 95 or above: Chlup ($2.34M, POTE 95), Luongo ($1.60M, POTE 97), Klesla ($0.90M, POTE 97), Ouellet ($0.90M, POTE 97), Spezza ($1.00M, POTE 99). If the 1-year group is all locked on 5–6 years, the 2-year group arrives at renewal with no stagger, and the club is re-signing 25 players across two consecutive summers. The fix is to give some of the 1-year depth (Alexeev, Chistov, Colaiacovo, Smirnov) two- or three-year deals instead, pushing part of that renewal into July 2007 and splitting the load.

**Fischer** is a quiet liability: $3.70M with four years left, 0.41 pts/g (down from 0.63), 24 years old. $14.80M committed to a player who is stalling. He cannot be moved at value until his contract is close to expiring, so he is locked through July 2009.

**The veterans roll off naturally.** Sundin at $8.40M has 5 years left through age 39 — that contract outlasts his usefulness. Mogilny ($5.50M, 2yr), Svehla ($3.60M, 1yr), Roberts ($2.70M, 1yr), Belfour ($6.50M, 1yr) total $18.30M and are mostly gone within 12–24 months. The salary relief from the old guard partly funds the raises for the young core.

**Draft capital is almost nothing.** One fourth-rounder. No first, no second, no third. Every trade this season and next must be player-for-player unless the GM recovers picks via the over-80 expiring mechanic (Svehla, Belfour if he goes at the deadline).

The two moves that protect three years: build the summer re-signing list now with priorities and a payroll ceiling, and stagger the 1-year deals so the 2-year wave in 2006 is not as heavy as the 1-year wave in 2005.



**On the standing task #2 (Luongo/DiPietro monitoring):** this is complete. Luongo arrived on the roster by February 6 at 91 base, 25, $1.60M, 2 years. The goalie-trade window has closed because the need is filled. DiPietro monitoring was tied to the same search and is moot.

## Calendar

We are first in the East at 102 points with 17 games left and the deadline 17 days out, so the answer is straightforward: we buy. The question is what we can actually get and whether the Belfour decision unlocks it in time.

**Belfour** is the gate. At 39, $6.50M expiring, 92 base, he is the single most valuable asset on the roster right now — and the only one we risk losing for nothing if he retires. Colorado offered Hejduk for him. If GM green-lights this, the 4th-rounder stays available for Havlat. If it doesn't happen, we need that 4th to recover a goalie backup via the Svehla pick-recovery route, and Havlat is blocked. This decision cannot wait past March 10. Every day of delay narrows Colorado's window too.

**Havlat** at 23, 87 base, 80 points in 63 games, $900K expiring, is the depth-scoring answer the whole season has been waiting for. OTT sits at 63 points with 11 expiring contracts; they cannot re-sign him. Tucker plus the 4th funds this. Tucker is in no unit, his 84 TOUG and 88 CHKG are free on stored grades, and at 29 on $1.30M he is the exact profile the over-80 mechanic wants. This is the priority buy.

**Svehla** at 36, $3.60M, 92 CHKG stored, is a pick-recovery asset the over-80 mechanic can convert. He is not part of the next three years. But moving a top-pair defenseman from a first-place team two weeks before the deadline weakens the playoff D-corps. My call: keep him through the playoffs, then move him in the off-season when the over-80 mechanic still applies to an expiring player who has not re-signed. That is cleaner than gutting the blueline in March.

**Roberts** at 38, $2.70M, is the same logic. Expiring, over 80, no future role. Move him at the deadline for a pick — he is not in the playoff plan at 38 and the pick-recovery mechanic is free. Unlike Svehla, losing him weakens nothing.

**Chistov** at 21, $1.10M, could be deadline currency (he was in the Kovalchuk package in December) or summer re-signing material. At 21 with a first-round comp, I would keep him for the staggered renewal unless a package that fills a need appears. He is depth, not core.

---

## Summer renewals, by name

The cluster problem is real: 15 deals, $25.30M, all expiring July 2005. The staggered plan from December holds — stars on 5-6 years, depth on 2-3 — but now with real production numbers behind it.

**Renew on 5-6 years (the core):**

**Gaborik** at 23, 91 base, POTE 90, 67 points in 45 games on $1.10M. First name on the list. He is the best player on the roster under 24 and every team will look at him in July. This renewal must be the opening offer the market opens.

**Richards** at 24, $1.00M. Third-line centre who the GM slid there in February. If he is holding the role, 5-6 years.

**Kaberle** at 27, $1.90M. Best offensive defenseman available on our own roster. Five years, no question.

**Nash** at 20, $1.20M. Young core, 5-6 years.

**Eminger** at 21, $1.20M, POTE 99. GM has protected him explicitly. Five or six years the moment the market opens.

**Renew on 2-3 years (develop or evaluate):**

**Colaiacovo** at 22, $1.10M. Two years, extend once his rate tells us what he is.

**Alexeev** at 23, $1.10M. Two years unless he has broken out.

**Upshall** at 21, $1.20M. Two years, cheap depth.

**Tellqvist** at 25, $0.80M, POTE high 90s. GM's standing order: stay, give him time. Two or three years at modest salary.

**Renew on about 2 years (aging, reduce cost):**

None of the remaining expirations fit this neatly because the veterans are either leaving or cheap enough to re-sign flat.

**Move before July for pick recovery:**

**Svehla** at 36, $3.60M. Over-80 mechanic. One year at $3.60M on a 36-year-old is the kind of contract you convert into a draft pick and a young prospect.

**Roberts** at 38, $2.70M. Same mechanic, even more urgent. Move at the deadline.

**Belfour** at 39, $6.50M. If the Colorado deal lands in March, this solves itself. If he refuses a reduced deal in July and retires, the pick capital is gone. The GM's Feb 21 worry about "losing a fairly valuable asset for nothing" is the reason to pull the trigger in March.

**Let go:**

**Smirnov** at 20, POTE 70, zero games played. The coach is right that the roster spot earns nothing. Clear it.

**Abid** at 24, $0.40M, 80 TOUG, 80 CHKG stored. At $400K he is the cheapest toughness on the market. I would renew him at one year or let him walk, depending on whether the coach actually dresses him next season. At zero utilization so far, renewing him is a bet on a coach's intention I cannot verify.

---

## The two dates

**March 19 — deadline.** The Belfour decision by March 10 gates the Havlat package. If GM hesitates past that, both upgrade paths die. Roberts moves regardless. Svehla stays. Chistov is optional currency if a need appears.

**July — renewal.** Gaborik first, then Richards, Kaberle, Nash, Eminger on 5-6 years. Colaiacovo, Alexeev, Upshall on 2-3. Tellqvist on 2-3. Belfour on reduced terms if he hasn't walked by then. The $25.30M cluster is only manageable if the five stars go long and the depth stays short. If the stars walk, the team rebuilds from zero.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: given that depth scoring is the stated problem and we hold one fourth-rounder, who across thirty clubs fills that gap, and can we actually pay for him?

**Havlat (OTT)** is the confirmed lead target from the Feb 26 note. 84 overall, 82 points in 65 games, $0.90M expiring, POTE 85, age 23. OTT sits at 63 points with 11 expiring deals and cannot retain him. The package is Tucker (not in any unit, $1.30M) plus the fourth-rounder. This is the cheapest way to add a top-six wing that fits our timeline.

**Kovalchuk (ATL)** at 86 overall, 105 points in 62 games, $1.10M expiring, POTE 85, age 21 is the highest-scoring player on the market. ATL at 64 points with 11 expiring deals cannot re-sign both him and Heatley. But acquiring him costs Koltsov plus Chistov, which strips our development depth, and he walks in July unless we re-sign him at $3-5M on top of an already $25.30M expiring pool. The GM should keep this as an option only if ATL doesn't re-sign Heatley first, and only if Belfour-to-Colorado doesn't change the calculus.

**Cammalleri (LA)** at 79 overall, 47 points in 43 games, POTE 97, age 22, $1.10M expiring is the best future asset available. He is re-signable, he fills a top-six wing spot for five years, and LA at 64 points with 14 expiring deals are motivated sellers. The cost is Koltsov (92 speed, 23, not in any unit) plus a recovered pick from moving Svehla. This does not compete with Havlat if Belfour-to-Colorado keeps the fourth-rounder home.

**Conroy (CGY)** at 76 overall, 77 points in 64 games, 94 FACE, $2.00M expiring, age 31 fills both the centre scoring and faceoff gaps. CGY at 50 points, worst record in the league with 10 expiring deals, will take anything with a future. The problem is the cost: any package worth CGY's acceptance uses a young piece (Chistov or Koltsov), and Conroy is a rental who leaves in July. Spending POTE 95 Chistov on a 31-year-old rental for a first-round exit does not pass the three-year test. Deprioritised.

**Svehla** is our own pick-recovery play. 83 CHKG displayed, $3.60M expiring, age 36. The over-80 expiring mechanic can convert him to a draft pick. That second pick funds a Cammalleri or Komisarek deal alongside the 4th. Without it, every package competes for one resource. He must move before March 19 or the value walks.

**The keystone remains Belfour-to-Colorado.** If it lands, we get Hejduk (87 overall, 26 years old, reasonable salary) without spending the 4th, and the 4th stays home for Havlat. That is two elite additions from one asset. If it dies, we must choose: Havlat now or one ATL piece later.

## Trade construction

The question is what we give and what we get at the deadline, given one fourth-rounder, two over-80 expiring assets (Belfour and Svehla), and a depth-scoring hole that only a top-six wing fills. Three proposals, ranked by certainty and by what they unlock.

**Proposal 1: Belfour to Colorado for Hejduk.** This is confirmed — the GM tried it on Feb 21 and Colorado accepted. Belfour is 39, 92 base, $6.50M, expiring, 18-3 2.27 GAA in 21 games. Colorado have no goalie, are in the race, and Hejduk at 87 overall with a reasonable expiring salary is the best they'll offer. We shed $6.50M, gain a top-line wing, and the 4th-rounder stays home for Havlat. This is the keystone: if it lands, proposals 2 and 3 are both live; if Belfour walks to free agency in July, both die. The GM needs to pull this trigger in the next two weeks.

**Proposal 2: Tucker plus the 4th-rounder to Ottawa for Havlat.** Havlat is 23, 84 overall, 82 points in 65 games, $900K expiring, POTE 85. Ottawa sit at 63 points with 11 expiring deals and cannot retain him. Tucker is 29, $1.30M, 2 years left, CHKG 92, TOUG 88, and only 3 games played for us — we have no use for him. Ottawa get a checking forward with a future (they need depth for next season even at 60 points) plus a 4th-rounder. Payroll: we shed $1.30M and take on $900K, net savings $400K, and we add 82-point scoring. Acceptance is uncertain because a 4th is low value; the AI may want more. If so, add Salo ($2.60M, 2yr, not in any unit) to the package, which also clears a $2.60M body from the summer renewal list.

**Proposal 3: Svehla to a contender for a draft pick.** Svehla is 36, 92 CHKG stored, $3.60M, expiring. The over-80 mechanic converts him to a pick. A contender with a thin blue line gets a playoff-ready shutdown pair partner for the remaining games and playoffs. The pick we receive needs 10 games before it can be re-traded, so this must close by March 7 to be usable at the deadline. If it does, it funds a second move (Komisarek from Montreal, who is 23, POTE 90, 83 TOUG, $1.10M expiring, and Montreal at 46 points with 14 expiring deals are selling). Payroll: we shed $3.60M with no incoming salary. This is pure value recovery.

**If none land.** We play the 17 remaining games without a scoring upgrade. The playoffs become about whether our depth can outlast one team in a short series. At season end, ATL's Kovalchuk and Heatley both become free agents — we pursue one of them in the summer when there is no cost beyond salary. Fischer ($3.70M, 4yr, 0.41 ppg) is the summer problem, not the deadline problem.

## Owed

This phase answers whether the goalie trade window the GM asked about on January 19 is still open, and whether DiPietro has developed into a target. Both answers have moved since last report.

**Luongo** is on our roster and is no longer a monitoring target. He started every one of our 65 games: 35-30, 4037 minutes, 94 overall (91 base), 25 years old, $1.60M with two years left. The January task was to watch his availability on Florida; that question is closed. He is ours.

**DiPietro** at NYI has not developed into the profile the GM set ("a really good high-90s goalie from a team that will not be a contender"). He is 82 overall, 79 base, age 23, one year remaining at $1.10M. In 21 games he is 7-12 with a 3.64 GAA and a 0.849 save percentage. That is a career backup at best, not a number one from a rebuilding club. His contract expires this July, which means his trade value is thin now and zero after the season, but acquiring him costs a pick and gives Toronto a third-stringer behind a 94 and a 93.

Nothing has changed about the goalie situation that warrants action: Luongo is arrived, Belfour is the backup and the chip, and the GM's February 19 order that "goalies are solved" holds. The monitoring task is complete.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-02
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-02

Next game vs FLA on Thursday 03 March 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is who among our 15 players aged 23 or under is getting the games their calibre has earned, and who is being left to rust.

**Spezza** is the one that matters most and it's now urgent in a way it wasn't in January. 37 games, 7.5 MPG, 15 points, and he's now fully scratched. His morale has slipped to 86, the lowest in the young group, and that's in the band that docks a grade from every attribute on screen. At POTE 99 and 21 years old this is the biggest development waste on the roster, and it's now actively costing us on-ice quality from a player we could be developing into something. I've raised this six times. The window is closing.

**Stahle** has moved from zero games in 49 to four games in 65, earning 17.8 MPG in them. That's a start. At 20 with POTE 96 he still needs far more, but the direction is right and I acknowledge it. He's no longer the waste he was on January 25th.

**Spacek** at 19 is on 8.6 MPG on the fourth line with 16 points in 42 games (0.38 pts/g) and POTE 91. His morale at 92 is holding. The situation hasn't changed since my last two recommendations, and I won't pretend otherwise.

**Chlup** at 19 is 38 points in 54 games (0.70 pts/g) on 16.1 MPG on the second line. He has taken the top-nine spot and is keeping it. No action needed.

**Nash**, **Gaborik**, **Klesla**, **Chistov**, **Upshall** and **Eminger** are all dressed and getting meaningful games at rates appropriate to their lines. No issues.

**Smirnov** at 20 with POTE 70 and zero games in 65 is a depth forward who isn't making this team yet. That's a legitimate outcome, not a waste.

**Koltsov** is the GM's trading chip and his scratch status is deliberate. Not my call.

**Colaiacovo** gets 17.9 MPG when he plays but has only 31 of 65. At 22 with POTE 99 and 0.39 pts/g he's a depth pair defenceman getting spot duty. That's a fair use.

## Development trends

With seventeen games left and the season tilting toward a rebuild window, the trends determine who we build around and who we sell this summer. Two young guys are genuinely rising, two are being wasted in real time, and the three veterans carrying the most minutes are all fading on the way up.

**Chlup** is the best story on the club. 0.62 to 0.73 points per game with minutes jumping from 11.0 to 17.7 at age 19. At that age you expect the rate to drop as the sample grows and opponents adjust. It hasn't. He belongs in the top nine permanently and I would have no problem putting him on line two with 18+ MPG for next season.

**Eminger** is the other one moving the right way. 0.35 to 0.50 season rate, minutes up from 15.0 to 17.0, still 21. His contract expires this summer. If he finishes above 0.50 he's a real second-pair defenceman and we need to talk about keeping him. If he dips back below 0.45 the sell case reopens.

**Chistov** quietly earned a bigger role. Minutes went from 9.5 to 14.4 and his rate actually improved from 0.29 to 0.32. That's the pattern of a young player growing into a third-line job. He's the answer to the L3 stamina problem if he keeps trending up.

**Spacek** is the loudest alarm. 16.0 MPG to 6.0, rate collapsing from 0.55 to 0.32. He was getting a real role in December and it's been taken away without a plan. I've raised this four times in February and nothing has changed. At 19, you either give him 12 minutes or you don't dress him. Six minutes in garbage time develops nobody.

**Spezza** is the same story in slower motion. 9.1 MPG to 5.3, rate from 0.43 to 0.38. POTE 99, 21 years old. This is now confirmed as a wasted year. Next season he either plays a real role or something has to change.

**Klesla** confirmed the decline. 0.50 down to 0.29 on flat minutes of 14.6 to 14.7. At 22 the direction should be up. Two consecutive declining seasons makes him a summer trade candidate.

**McCabe** has no doubt left in it. 1.42 to 0.46. Four years left at $3M. He is the loudest sell we have this summer and the trend is still going the wrong way.

**Salo** at 0.17 on 14.6 MPG at age 30 with two years and $2.6M left. Below fourth-pair production. Sell.

**Mogilny** is the veteran problem. At 36 his minutes went from 16.9 to 19.8 while his rate halved from 1.62 to 0.81. That's the opposite of what you do with an aging player. He should be at 15 MPG or less, not nearly 20.

**Roberts** at 38 follows the same pattern: 16.5 to 21.0 MPG while 1.29 drops to 0.85. **Sundin** at 34 went from 16.9 to 21.4 MPG as production fell from 1.46 to 0.95. All three are absorbing minutes because the third line can't handle the load, and the aging slope is steepening fast. Next season we cannot run those numbers again.

**Stahle** finally got four games and 17.8 MPG. Zero points but at 20 with POTE 96 that's the start we needed. Keep dressing him.

## Morale watch

The winning streak has done what it does: the room is at 92 or above almost without exception, and the handful below that are ticking up. This is not a morale problem week.

**Spezza** is the one lingering case. 86 morale, +1 per game — the winning streak is barely reaching him because he keeps getting scratched. 7.5 MPG over 37 games at 21 with potential off the charts is a waste, and I've raised it five times. The +1 tells me the room isn't toxic for him, just flat. If we get a game we can afford to lose before the deadline, start him. If not, the streak itself will eventually lift him, but slowly.

**Spacek** and **Alexeev** are both at 92 and surging (+5 each). The winning is fixing what the minutes were causing. At 8.6 and 8.3 MPG respectively, they're under their bands, but the trend line is sharp and upward. No intervention needed right now.

**Everyone else** is at 96 or 99. The top six, the defensive pairs, the goalies — all comfortable in their minutes and rising. No one is carrying more than they should, no one is starved.

## Role composition

The question is whether each unit is built for its job, and whether the roster can staff every role at all. Most lines are correct; one structural gap stands out and it is not fixable by moving players around.

**L1** is well-built: Sundin centres with 91 faceoffs and 93 scoring, Gaborik carries the offensive load (98 scoring, 99 speed, 99 clutch), Roberts supplies grit (84 checking, 72 toughness). McCabe and Fischer both at 84 checking give this pair real shutdown capability. No change.

**L2** is a skill line with no defensive backbone. Checking mean 65, toughness mean 61, both the lowest on the roster. Mogilny (94 scoring, 91 playmaking) and Afinogenov (92/92) are pure offense. Chlup at 80 faceoffs is the only player on this line with any two-way identity. The auto-pairing system links this line to defensive pair 2, and that pair is Svehla and Kaberle, neither of whom appears anywhere on the checking inventory. This is the most exposed combination on the sheet. However, the GM has designated Svehla "the real MVP" and Kaberle a star, so I cannot fix it by reassignment. This is a roster gap, not a lineup error.

**L3** is fine. Richards centres (75 faceoffs, 97 clutch, 86 stamina), Chistov brings 98 speed, Nash provides size. Eminger and Klesla on the back end are young but the line's checking mean of 70 is workable for a third line.

**L4 faceoffs read 52/55.** Nobody on the fourth line wins a draw. Spacek, Abid, Upshall, none are listed in the faceoff inventory. In a standard four-line matchup against opposing third and fourth centres this is survivable, but any power play that costs a draw puts us immediately on the back foot. There is no available personnel move that fixes this; Richards is our best remaining option at 75 and he is already anchoring L3.

**K1** (Eminger, Sundin, Roberts, Fischer) and **K2** (Chlup, McCabe, Kaberle, Abid) both have checking and toughness. K1 puts Sundin on the kill, which costs offence if he cannot get back for rushes, but his 91 faceoff skill wins the draw at the start of a short-handed sequence. Acceptable.

**P1** has scoring 82, playmaking 82, clutch 85 with Gaborik and Sundin. It is a possession PP built on skill, and the numbers say it can execute. No shooter-and-hammer specialist is visible but the 99 playmaking best suggests we can generate from the half-wall cycle. No change.

## Opponent matchup

Can we exploit Florida's situation tonight, and if so, how? The answer is no change — and here's why that's the right call.

**Nieuwendyk is out** through March 19. He's their first-line centre at 81 OVR and FACE 94. Without him, their top line is Huselius (73) and Novoseltsev (76) with a replacement centre. Their actual best unit is L2: Jokinen (84), Bure (94 speed), and Messier (71). But our L2 — Chlup (85), Mogilny (89), Afinogenov (85) — matches that line's talent or beats it on every position. The auto-pairing puts our L2 against their L2, which is exactly where we want it.

**Their power play is 20 goals on 199 attempts.** Ten per cent. That is not a unit. Our PK won't be tested tonight, and we can afford the slight defensive looseness that comes from a thin blue line (Van Ryn 70, Trnka 69, Krajicek 71 on the bottom pairs). Our L3 (Richards 86, Nash 82, Chistov 81) against their L3 (Nedorost 77, Nilson 72, Shvidki 73) is a 15-point talent gap on every position.

**Season series is 3-0-0, 11-5 in goals.** They cannot score on us. We're giving up 1.67 per game against them. The lines are built to exploit exactly the mismatches this opponent presents.

**Belfour at 93, mor 99.** No fatigue flag in front of me today. Start him. If the icon shows tired between now and puck drop, switch to Ouellet.

## Owed

**D sell-list update for the deadline.** McCabe's cold streak is deepening, Eminger is permanently below threshold, and nothing else has moved since February 26th.

**McCabe** — 53 points in 65 games (0.82 pts/g season), but just 1 point over his last 5 games since Feb 21 (0.20 pts/g). That's the third consecutive snapshot showing him cold: 0.33 in mid-February, now 0.20. Still 0.82 for the season at 22.8 MPG, still the best offensive D we have by a mile. At 29 with $3.0M x 4, this is a trajectory flag not a sell. No change.

**Eminger** — 20 points in 47 (0.43 pts/g), and 0 points in his last 3 games since Feb 21. Season rate has fallen from 0.44 (my Feb 26 note) to 0.43. Expiring $1.2M. Firmly on the sell list. No change.

**Salo** — 8 points in 27 (0.30 pts/g). Played 2 games since my last report with zero output. $2.6M x 2 remaining. Fourth-pair production on second-pair money. Sell. No change.

**Colaiacovo** — 12 points in 31 (0.39 pts/g), not dressed. Expiring $1.1M. Expire or flip for a late pick. No change.

**Klesla** — 24 points in 65 (0.37 pts/g) at 22. Flat from my Feb 21 note (0.38). $0.90M x 2 is cheap, so the urgency is low, but a second declining season at 22 means his value peaks now. No change to the list, still a trade candidate on value.

**Stahle** — 4 games played since January 25th (was 0), still 0 points. At least he's getting dressings now. Still the biggest development waste but less acute than it was.

The sell order is unchanged: Eminger first (expiring, 0.43), Salo second (expensive and 0.30), Colaiacovo third (expiring, 0.39). McCabe and Klesla are planning problems, not deadline problems.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-28

# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-28

Toronto 44-11-4, 102 pts after 64 games.

## Role coverage

The toughness gap is resolved and it was never real. The query confirms stored grades: Roberts carries TOUG 88, McCabe carries TOUG 81, and Tucker carries TOUG 88 from earlier readings. The displayed numbers (all three at 70-73) are form-depressed by 15-18 points. The coach sees zero players at 80+ displayed toughness; on stored grades there are at least three. No trade is needed to close a gap that does not exist at the structural level.

**Roberts** is the anchor. 88 TOUG and 86 CHKG stored, 98 INJU, 90 HERO. At 38 he is the oldest man on the roster and his contract is expiring, but his physical profile does not require replacement at the same grade for at least two more seasons. His displayed 73 TOUG will return toward 88 when his hands recover.

**Tucker** is the free fix. Stored TOUG 88, stored CHKG 92, displayed 70/83. He is in no unit. Dressing him on the fourth line alongside Pesonen (67) and Williams (67) immediately gives that line 88+ TOUG and 92+ CHKG without spending a dollar or a pick. This is the coach's call tonight.

**Sundin** is the only centre who wins draws. 90 FACE displayed, 90 stored. Chlup at 75 is the next best. Richards sits at 70-75 depending on the day. This is a genuine structural gap at centre, but the GM has already ruled that Bell and Doan are wings and the faceoff problem is not solved by a wing. The question is whether a dedicated centre faceoff man is worth deadline currency; the game's faceoff mechanics are not decoded, so the causal link between 75 FACE versus 85 FACE and wins is unproven. I would not spend a first-rounder on it.

**Scoring** is covered at 12 players above 80 SHPW. Gaborik 92, Mogilny 94, Sundin 92, Afinogenov 90. The team-wide scoring slump the GM identified on Feb 19 is a form and confidence issue, not a grade deficit. The foundation holds.

**Goalies** are covered in structure. Luongo at 91 base with two years is the future. Belfour at 92 base is the best backup available but his $6.50M expiring deal makes him a trade chip per the GM's Feb 21 hypothesis. Ouellet at 81 base with two years is a capable NHL backup. Four goalies dressed is one too many for the playoff roster; Tellqvist at 80 base and expiring is the odd man out.

**Age risk on the back end:** Svehla (36) and Salo (30) are the top-pair checkers. Eminger (21, POTE 99) is the long-term answer but is not ready tonight. If Svehla is moved for a pick (the Feb 23 note), McCabe (29) plus Kaberle (26) plus Eminger is the future top four. The deadline window is the time to convert Svehla while his 92 CHKG still prices well.

## Trajectory

The question this phase answers is whether Toronto's roster structure and money will hold together through 2007-08, or whether the 2005 summer renewal creates a cliff. The answer: the age curve is healthy, but the contract cluster is violent and the draft capital is nearly empty.

**The age shape is the manual's shape.** Fifteen players at 23 or under, eleven at 24-29. Only five at 34+. The problem is the 30-33 bridge: one man, Salo, scratched. By 2007 when Sundin (34, POTE 60), Mogilny (36, POTE 55), Svehla (36, POTE 55), and Roberts (38, POTE 52) are gone or declining, the next tier is McCabe at 31 (POTE 78) and then a jump to the 24-25 group. The club has depth, but it has no 30-year-old with a 90 POTE to carry the transition.

**Fifteen contracts worth $25.30M expire this July.** That is the number that dominates the next three seasons. Of those fifteen, at least ten are young players the club must re-sign (Gaborik 81 pts at 23, Richards 56 pts at 24, Abid 65 pts at 24, Nash 33 pts at 20, Alexeev 30 pts at 23, Upshall, Chistov, Eminger, Colaiacovo, Kaberle). If all ten walk at market prices after their current breakout years, the club loses its entire core simultaneously. The prior summer-stagger plan said lock stars 5-6 years and depth 2-3; that plan is now the only thing preventing a cliff.

**Belfour, Svehla, Roberts are the three contracts that must move before March 19.** Together they cost $12.80M, they are 38.7 years old combined, their POTE averages 52, and their over-80 base ratings qualify them for the pick-recovery mechanic. Toronto currently owns nothing better than a 4th-rounder. Three second or third-round picks recovered from these three deals is the single most valuable outcome available before July.

**Fischer is the worst contract on the roster.** 24 years old, $3.70M, four years left, 27 points in 59 games (0.46 pts/g), POTE 90 that is not translating. The POTE means it could still come — he is 24 — but the salary is set through 2008-09 and cannot be renegotiated. This is trade bait in 2006 or 2007 once his overall settles. Nothing actionable now.

**Mogilny at $5.50M for two more years is the second problem.** He is producing 69 points in 60 games at 36, which is strong in this game, but his POTE is 55 and the decline curve from 36 to 38 will be steep. That is $11.00M committed to a player who will likely read low-80s in two years. Two years means it self-resolves in 2007; the cost is one more year of high-priced decline.

**Money:** payroll $65.54M against revenue $83.47M leaves $18.00M in headroom before profit goes to zero. Trading the three veterans frees $12.80M; re-signing ten young players at an average of $1.5M each costs $15.00M. Net payroll change is roughly plus $2.00M, well inside the headroom. The money works, but only if the veterans go and the young players are locked at below-market prices before they break out further.

## Calendar

The deadline is 19 days away and we are 1st in the East by 15 points over New Jersey. That settles the question: we are buyers, and the only thing worth buying is a goal scorer, because the coach's depth-scoring problem is the one thing separating us from a Cup run.

**Havlat** is the lead target. 87 base, 80 points in 63 games, age 23, $900K expiring. Ottawa sit 62 points in 10th, 16 points out of a playoff spot with 11 expiring deals; they cannot retain him. Package: Tucker plus our 4th-rounder. Tucker is 29, $1.30M, 83 CHKG, and sits in no unit. Ottawa get a checking forward who can help them next season and a pick; we get a second-line winger who scores at a point-per-game pace. This is the move to execute by March 19.

**Svehla** should go before the deadline. 36 years old, $3.60M, one year left, over 80 overall, which triggers the pick-recovery mechanic. He is not a playoff defenseman we want carrying a third pairing. Moving him recovers a draft pick from a club that needs a veteran top-four blueliner for a Cup push. Do not renew.

**Belfour** sits on two valid paths and it is the GM's call. Path one: keep him as backup for the playoffs, risk nothing, lose $6.50M and a potential pick if he retires. Path two: move him for a young goalie on a reasonable salary, which hedges the retirement and clears money. Colorado wanted him and offered Hejduk; that is the template. If the GM wants to trade him, 19 days is enough time to close one.

**The summer is the bigger problem.** Fifteen players expire, $28.6M walks, and the cluster must be staggered.

**Gaborik** at 91 base, 23, $1.10M: lock 5-6 years. This is the single most important contract on the roster.

**Eminger** at 21, POTE 99, $1.20M: lock 5-6 years. The GM protected him specifically.

**Kaberle** at 26, $1.90M: lock 5-6 years. He is our top defenseman.

**Nash** at 20, $1.20M: lock 5-6 years. The coach flagged his rate decline (0.83 to 0.46), but at 20 that is noise, and the cost of a miss is low.

**Richards** at 24, $1.00M: lock 5-6 years. The rate decline from 1.08 to 0.78 is real, but 0.78 at 24 and $1.00M is a second-line centre at a fourth-line price. Locking him removes him from the market.

**Abid** at 24, $0.40M: renew 2 years. The coach's toughness target, and he costs nothing.

**Tellqvist** at 25, $0.80M: renew 2 years as backup. GM's January order was to develop him; Luongo's arrival does not make a 25-year-old with high-90s potential worthless on the bench.

**Let go:** Roberts (38, $2.70M) and Belfour (39, $6.50M) unless moved at the deadline. That is $9.20M freed from the payroll without a trade.

**Move before expiry or let go:** Chistov (21, $1.10M), Alexeev (23, $1.10M), Colaiacovo (22, $1.10M), Upshall (21, $1.20M), Smirnov (20, $0.40M). Renew the cheap ones on 2 years if they show something by April; move the ones with trade value at the deadline if a package needs a body.

**Obligation delivered:** #2, the Luongo/DiPietro monitoring. Luongo arrived February 7 and is our number-one at 91 base, 25, $1.60M, 2 years left. DiPietro was assessed on February 6 and rejected (79 base, 3.65 GAA, not moving). The goalie acquisition window is closed; the mandate is fulfilled.

## League scan

The question this phase answers is: who across the league can Toronto actually get before March 19, and what does it cost when the cupboard holds one draft pick?

The answer is constrained by two things. First, the team needs top-six scoring; the coach's faceoff gap is real but unproven as a cause of losses, and the GM has already vetoed spending a first-rounder on it. Second, Toronto holds exactly one draft pick (a 4th-rounder). Every package that requires a first or second is fiction. What we can offer: expiring contracts the other club doesn't want, players they'd dress better than we do, and one 4th.

**The ATL binary is the biggest prize.** Heatley (91 base, 96 pts/58 GP, 24, $1.10M expiring) and Kovalchuk (89 base, 104 pts/61 GP, 21, $1.10M expiring) are both on the same 63-point club with 11 expiring deals. Neither club can re-sign both at market price after their 100-point seasons. Whichever one ATL prioritizes re-signing, the other becomes available. Kovalchuk at 21 is the better long-term fit (four years of team control if we re-sign); Heatley at 24 is the better scorer tonight. Either one transforms the lineup. The cost: the 4th plus a roster player ATL values (Salo at $2.50M expiring, or Chistov plus depth).

**Daze (CHI) is the purest rental scorer.** 102 points in 63 games at 29, $3.00M expiring, 89 base. CHI at 55 points with 10 expiring deals cannot re-sign him and won't make the playoffs. His overall_base of 89 triggers the pick-recovery mechanic in reverse: we acquire a 100-point player for one 4th-rounder. The problem is $3.00M for one season, but that's the cheapest 100-point player on the board.

**Havlat (OTT) remains the best value package.** 87 base, 81 pts/64 GP, 23, $900K expiring. OTT at 62 points with 11 expiring deals. The Feb 26 note still holds: Tucker plus the 4th is the price. Tucker (TOUG 88, CHKG 92, in no unit) is a free piece we don't need. The problem: this uses our only pick. If Havlat and ATL both come due, we have to choose.

**Hejduk (COL) via Belfour is the GM's own hypothesis and it works.** 91 base, 98 pts/62 GP, 29, $2.50M, two years left. Colorado at 80 points is in the race and needs a playoff goalie. Belfour at 92 base is exactly what they need. Two years of 98-point right-wing production at $2.50M fills the scoring gap AND the contract problem simultaneously. The GM floated this on Feb 21; it deserves a concrete offer.

**Stuart (SJ) is the defenceman Toronto needs if Svehla moves.** 87 base, 42 pts/63 GP, 25, $1.80M expiring, POTE 91. SJ at 58 points with 14 expiring deals is a seller. He is the arrived version of what Eminger will become. Acquiring him now means Toronto's defence doesn't have a gap in 2006.

**Conroy (CGY) is the faceoff answer if the GM decides it matters.** 85 base, 94 FACE, 77 pts/64 GP, 33, $2.00M expiring. CGY at 50 points with 10 expiring is the weakest club in the league alongside MTL. At 33 he is a rental, not a solution. But 77 points from a second centre is not nothing. The price is Chistov plus the 4th, or nothing we can't spare.

**I would NOT pursue:** Sillinger (42 GP suggests injury risk for a rental), Roenick ($7.50M and 3 years left means PHI would demand a body), Theodore or Cechmanek or Lalime (goalies are solved per the GM's Feb 19 standing order), Bell (CHI profitable, 2 years left, they don't need to sell a 24-year-old), Marleau (89 base and $1.60M sounds cheap but SJ at 58 points will extract a real price, and he is a centre who duplicates Sundin).

**The decision tree:** If Belfour goes to Colorado for Hejduk, the 4th stays home for Havlat or ATL. If Belfour walks, the 4th goes to one deal and the other is lost. The Belfour trade is the keystone because it generates the cap space AND keeps the pick alive.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers is: given one draft pick and a GM who wants value for Belfour, what are the two or three deals that fix the scoring problem and recover draft capital? The answer is two independent moves that don't compete for the same asset, plus a third that only makes sense if the first two clear.

**Belfour to Colorado for Hejduk** is the keystone and the GM's own hypothesis. He told me on Feb 21 that Colorado "would give us Hejduk" for a goalie and that they "dont have one now." They are at 80 points, in the playoff race, and Belfour's 18-3, 2.27 GAA, 0.916 SP over 21 games is exactly what a contender needs for April. We get a 29-year-old with 98 points in 62 games at $2.50M for two more years. Our payroll drops $4.00M. Theirs rises $6.50M minus whatever goalie salary they shed, which likely still nets positive against a playoff run they cannot make without a starter. The risk: COL might want a second piece. If so, the 4th is the only thing we have, and spending it here kills the Havlat package.

**Tucker plus the 4th to Ottawa for Havlat** is the second move, independent of the first because it doesn't touch Belfour. Tucker is in no unit, $1.30M with two years left, 1 point in 3 games. Ottawa at 62 points with 11 expiring deals cannot re-sign Havlat at 81 points and $900K becoming a market price. Tucker gives them a 92 CHKG, 88 TOUG body on a controlled deal they can use for depth or flip. The 4th is marginal but real. We get a 23-year-old with 87 base and 81 points who could be extended cheaply this summer. Net payroll change: minus $400K.

**Svehla for a draft pick** is the third move, only if the first two land. He is 36, $3.60M expiring, 25 points in 41 games, 92 CHKG stored. The over-80 expiring mechanic says he goes for a pick. A contender with a D injury or thin blueline gets a playoff-ready top-pair checker for April and May. We recover a pick we do not have and shed $3.60M. The risk: this weakens our defense entering the playoffs, and the GM's Feb 19 order was about keeping the foundation. But Svehla at POTE 55 is not the foundation; he is the last year of a career.

**If none land:** Belfour walks in July and the $6.50M pick-recovery value is gone permanently. Svehla becomes the only pick-recovery play. Tucker stays benched, we enter the playoffs without the Havlat upgrade, and scoring depth remains the problem it was in January.

## Owed

**Luongo availability and DiPietro monitoring (asked 2005-01-19, due 2005-02-20):** Both sides of this question have resolved themselves since I last reported.

**Luongo** is on Toronto's roster at 93 displayed / 91 base, $1.60M, 2 years left, 42 GP at 20-21. He arrived in February and the "monitor for availability" question is moot. The GM's 2005-02-19 order closed the topic: "Goalies are solved. Done. Do not revisit."

**DiPietro** has played 46 games for NYI since my February 6 check, improving from 7-12 to 23-20 with a 2.90 GAA. But his base overall is unchanged at 79 and his save percentage is 0.872 (127 goals on 991 shots). The underlying number says the team in front of him got better, not him. He carries POTE 99 and $1.10M on an expiring deal, but the development I was watching for has not materialised across 26 snapshots spanning the full February window. My February 6 conclusion stands: not a realistic acquisition.

Nothing has changed since my last report that would alter the recommendation. The goalie situation is settled by roster (Luongo) and by GM order (no further pursuit). This task is delivered and closed.

# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-28

Next game vs CAR on Tuesday 01 March 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether our young players are getting the games they've earned, and tonight's answer centers on two names the GM needs to hear again.

**Spezza** is the loudest case on the roster. 7.5 MPG in 37 games at 21, morale at 86 — the lowest of any player 23 or under. POTE 99 is the scouting department's highest opinion in that group. He's currently scratched. I've flagged this five times since January and the pattern holds: he sits, his minutes don't move, and his morale is now visibly the worst of the young group. At POTE 99 he belongs above the rotation that's keeping Spacek, Smirnov and Koltsov in and out. He's not asking for 20 minutes; he's asking for 10.

**Stahle** at 4 games in 64 is still the cleanest waste on the blue line. POTE 96, age 20, 17.8 MPG in the four he's played. He gets meaningful minutes when called upon but almost never gets called. One dressing every third night would do more than any other development action I could recommend for the remaining 18 games.

**Smirnov** is the one where I'll say it plainly: POTE 70 at 20 with zero games. That's the lowest scouting grade in the group. The GM's rotation philosophy makes sense for players with high ceilings — it's how you develop Chlup and Nash. Smirnov's ceiling doesn't justify the roster spot. Either dress him to find out something or clear the spot for someone whose ceiling supports it.

**Spacek** at 8.9 MPG and POTE 91 — I've asked three times in two weeks for him to get 12+ or be scratched. The GM hasn't moved. I won't raise it a fourth time in this phase; the pattern is clear.

**Chlup** (16.1 MPG, 38 points, L2 at 19), **Gaborik** (20 MPG, 81 points, L1 at 23), **Nash** (12.5 MPG, 33 points, L3 at 20) are all earning exactly what they're getting. No concern.

**Ouellet** at 36.6 MPG across 11 games is fine for a backup goalie. When he's in, he's the starter that night. That's how a 23-year-old goalie develops.

## Development trends

The development question matters most now because the season is past the trade deadline window and the GM is planning next year's roster. Production trends over 40-plus games tell him who to build around, who to plan exits for, and who is being wasted on the bench.

**Chlup** is the confirmed gain. 0.62 to 0.75 pts/g across 53 games on 17.8 MPG, up from 11.0. At 19, climbing under a doubled load is the opposite of what usually happens. He belongs in the top nine permanently. No change needed there.

**Eminger** recovered and held. 0.35 to 0.52 pts/g over 46 games, minutes up from 15.0 to 17.0. The February 6th sell threshold (0.45) is now comfortably cleared over a full window, not just a hot streak. At 21 with an expiring $1.2M deal, the decision is whether to keep a developing first-pair D or rent him for the playoff push. I would keep him, but that is the GM's call.

**Stahle** finally got a dressing. Four games, 17.8 MPG, still zero points. That is progress from zero games at January 25th. Keep dressing him; four games is not enough to judge a 20-year-old with 96 potential.

**Spacek** is getting worse fast. 0.55 to 0.33 pts/g, and his minutes collapsed from 16.0 to 6.2. At 19, that is a stalled year. I have raised this four times with no movement. Either he gets 12+ MPG or the GM should stop dressing him, because the current arrangement develops nobody and costs morale.

**Spezza** remains unchanged in the worst way. 0.43 to 0.38 pts/g on 5.3 MPG, down from 9.1. At 21 with elite potential this is a wasted year, same as every prior report.

**Smirnov** has zero games at 20. Another young player getting nothing.

**Klesla** confirms the decline. 0.50 to 0.30 pts/g on flat minutes (14.6 to 14.7). At 22, the expected direction is up; he is going down on a second consecutive season. He is tradeable.

**Alexeev** at 23 dropped from 0.62 to 0.48 pts/g while minutes halved from 11.1 to 6.0. Not a star, but he should be climbing at 23, not disappearing from the lineup.

**McCabe** is the loudest sell on the blue line. 1.42 to 0.47 pts/g over 64 games at 29. That is not age at 29; that is a collapse on a four-year $3M deal. No recovery has materialized since January.

**Salo** confirms the collapse. 0.40 to 0.17 pts/g, minutes down from 20.3 to 14.6. At 30 with $2.6M for two more years, he is below fourth-pair production.

**Sundin** at 34 went from 1.46 to 0.95 pts/g while his minutes rose from 16.9 to 21.2. He is carrying a heavier load at less production because the third line's endurance ceiling means the top nine must absorb more. That is the wrong direction for a 34-year-old in February, and it will cost him next season if not addressed.

**Mogilny** at 36 and **Roberts** at 38 follow the same pattern: Mogilny 1.62 to 0.83, Roberts 1.29 to 0.85, minutes up for both. These two are at the end. The GM should plan next year's top six without them as daily drivers.

**Fischer** continues to decline: 0.63 to 0.38 pts/g on rising minutes (20.8 to 22.2). At 24 the direction is wrong. The GM has said Fischer is a keeper, so this is not a trade call. It is a planning note: a four-year contract for a player trending down at 24 needs watching.

**Kaberle** is stable and slightly improving: 0.54 to 0.56 pts/g, minutes up to 22.6. He is the anchor the blue line is built around. No change.

For the defensive evaluation I owe the GM: the sell order by season rate is McCabe (0.47), Klesla (0.30), Colaiacovo (0.36), Salo (0.17). Fischer (0.38) declines but the GM has protected him. Eminger (0.52) and Kaberle (0.56) are improving or stable and are the foundation. Svehla (0.48) is a 36-year-old age decline, not a quality problem. Stahle has four games, not enough to grade.

## Morale watch

The room is in good shape going into Carolina on Tuesday. Nearly every player sits at 96 to 100, lifted by the recent winning streak. The one exception is a known, deliberate choice the GM has already defended, and there is no new morale data that changes it.

**Spezza** is at 86, the lowest on the roster, and has been stuck there for weeks. The +1 tick at the latest save came from the team winning, not from ice time. At 7.5 MPG and scratched, he is well below any band his talent suggests, but the GM made a stated decision on January 15 to give space to other young players over him. The number is flagged; the decision is his and I respect it.

**Upshall** at 9.7 MPG, 18 points in 50 games, morale 96. Right at the depth-forward band. No issue.

**Chistov** at 13.0 MPG on the third line, morale 99. Slightly above his expected band given his production (16 points in 50 games), which means he is carrying a bit more than he should, but at 99 there is no morale risk. The upside is real but modest.

**Spacek** at 8.9 MPG and morale 92 (+5), same as last week. He is dressed on the fourth line but getting almost nothing. The winning streak lifted him to 92 from a low; the +5 is the team results, not his minutes. If he stays at this level he will drift back down once the wins slow. I have flagged this repeatedly without action, so I will not belabor it.

**Everyone else** is at 96 or above. No one is close to a morale threshold that would cost us a grade point on the ice. No changes needed for morale reasons against Carolina.

## Role composition

The question is whether these eight units are built from the right pieces. They are, with one exception, and that exception is hard to fix without breaking something else.

**L1** is the scoring-and-winning line. Gaborik at 98 scoring and 99 playmaking, Sundin at 92 and 91, Roberts at 83 checking. You want the best player on the ice in close games and this line delivers that: clutch mean 80, best 99. No change.

**L2** is the second scoring line. Mogilny 92 scoring, Afinogenov 90. Checking mean 64 is the softest of the top three lines, but for a unit carrying Mogilny and Afinogenov you accept that. They score, not kill. No change.

**L3** is the balance line. Checking 69 mean, Chistov's 97 speed, Richards at 74 faceoffs. It does what it should. Nash is on it and was scratched for youth rotation before; if he's dressed tonight, this is his home. No change.

**L4 (Spacek, Abid, Upshall).** Faceoffs 51 mean, 54 best. That is the problem. Abid at 82 checking gives this unit its identity, but whoever centres it is losing draws badly, which means the line starts every shift in its own end. At 6.6 MPG Spacek is already a short-shift unit. The fix would be moving Richards (74 faceoffs) down from L3 to centre this line, but that costs L3 a faceoff win and a stamina anchor at 85. I would rather eat the bad draws on a three-minute unit than rebuild two lines to fix it. No change, but flag it.

**P1** is the best unit on the roster. Gaborik 99 playmaking, Sundin 91, Kaberle quarterbacking. Scoring 81 mean, clutch 84 mean. Leave it alone.

**K1** is Sundin, Roberts, Fischer, Eminger, Smirnov. Two 83-checkers plus Sundin's 90 faceoffs to win draws against opposing power plays. That's a sound construct. The offensive cost is using Sundin on short PK shifts, but his stamina at 90 carries it. No change.

**K2** has McCabe at 83 and Abid at 82 checking, Kaberle's 83 stamina. Good enough for a second kill.

**Toughness is the roster gap.** The best on the roster is McCabe at 72. Nobody above that. Four players at 70 or above and that's the whole group. In the playoffs against a physical team, nothing on this blue line or in these forward lines brings the physical element. That is a roster problem the GM owns; no line arrangement fixes a team that cannot hit.

**Second faceoff man is also thin.** Sundin at 90 is the only 85+ centre on the roster. Chlup at 79 is next. If Sundin gets injured or has a cold night, nobody wins the draw at 85 or above. Same category: roster gap, not a lineup fix.

## Opponent matchup

**What matters against Carolina:** They're 20-21-12 on a seven-game losing streak, scoring 2.10 and giving up 3.40 a night. Their power play converts at 17.3% (29 of 168), their penalty kill is what we need to solve, and we convert at 35.4%. Their defence is old — Ozolinsh 32, Hill 35, Hedican 34 — and O'Neill (SPEE 91) is their only real speed threat up front.

**The matchup:** Our top line (Sundin 89, Gaborik 96, Roberts 86) against O'Neill/Brind'Amour/Sykora is a large grade gap. Brind'Amour's FACE 84 is their best faceoff man but he's 34 and slow; Sundin at FACE 90 handles him clean. Auto-pairing gives us Fischer (CHKG 90, SPEE 93) on D1 against Ozolinsh — that covers the one D who can skate. No rearrangement needed.

**Goaltender:** Belfour carries no fatigue icon. 92 OVR against a team generating 2.10 per game is a routine assignment. He starts.

**No change.** This is a mismatch on every unit. Carolina's best line grades 85, 81, 80; ours is 89, 96, 86. I would not break chemistry or shuffle D-pair slot order to win a game where we outscore them 2.80 to 2.10 per game and they are losing by 1.30 a night.

## Owed

**Defenceman sell-list update for end of season, the standing job from Jan 15.**

**McCabe** is the story today. When I checked him on Feb 12, his season rate sat at 0.89 with a recent window of 0.33. Two weeks later the season total has fallen to 0.83 (53 points in 64 games) because he added roughly 5 points in 14 games since my Jan 26 note. The slump is real and has now run a month. At 29 with $3M x 4 remaining, the end-of-season question is whether a 0.36-rate 29-year-old can fetch anything close to four years of $3M at the summer market. He stays the loudest sell but the answer to "how loud" shifts: his season total is still good enough that we should wait for the trade deadline or summer when the 0.83 headline is fresh, not panic-sell now while the recent window is dragging him under.

**Eminger** is unchanged: 20 points in 46 games, 0.43 pts/g. Below my 0.45 threshold. Age 21, $1.2M x 1 expiring. Sell at the deadline before he walks for nothing next summer.

**Klesla** is unchanged: 24 points in 64 games, 0.38 pts/g at age 22. Second consecutive declining season at an age when he should be climbing. Cheap at $0.9M x 2, but his ceiling looks capped. Trade candidate in summer if we can get something for a 22-year-old with two years left.

**Salo** at 8 points in 27 games (0.30) is done. Not dressed, $2.6M x 2 remaining. Clear cut.

**Stahle** finally has four games but zero points in 17.8 MPG. Development timeline, not a sell.

**Kaberle, Fischer, Svehla** are all keepers by GM order and not sell candidates.

Nothing else has moved since Feb 26. Same sell list, one updated number on McCabe.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-26
