# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-12

Toronto 39-9-4, 90 pts after 56 games.

## Role coverage

Toughness is the only role Toronto are missing outright: zero players at 80+ across 28 skaters, with the ceiling at 73 (Roberts, McCabe). Checking is thin with a free internal fix available today. Faceoffs are one deep when a team needs four.

**Tucker** at 83 CHKG and 29 is in no unit. **Upshall** at 80 CHKG and 21 is also unlined. Dress either or both and checking goes from 6 to 7 or 8 at 80+ without spending a dollar. This is the coach's call and he flagged it himself in the prior report.

**Chlup** at 75 FACE is the best available centre behind Sundin at 90. Richards at 70 handles third-line duty. That still leaves two lines where the team loses the draw, which the coach cannot fix internally. Only Sundin covers at 90+.

**Roberts** (86 CHKG, 38) and **Svehla** (83 CHKG, 36) carry two of the six checking ratings at 80+. In two seasons they are either gone or declining. McCabe at 29 and Fischer at 24 are the only young 80+ checkers left. That is not a gap tonight but it is the gap in 2006-07.

**Mogilny** at 94 scoring and 35 is the top point producer and the oldest. Sundin at 92 and 33 is next. Gaborik at 92 and 22, Afinogenov at 90 and 25 are the future. Scoring transitions cleanly. No acquisition needed for production.

**Abid** carries the only plausible internal toughness fix at base TOUG 80, but the Feb 9 reading puts him below 80+ in the current group. Until that discrepancy resolves, he is not a confirmed answer to the gap.

The acquisition targets that close both toughness and faceoffs in one move remain **Bell** (CHI, 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 87 FACE, 80 base, $900K, 2 years) and **Avery** (LA, 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, $400K, 2 years). Avery is cheaper and closes the faceoff gap better; Bell is the better pure toughness play. Neither has moved since January.

## Trajectory

**Is the club aging into a cliff?** No — the shape is young and the risk is the opposite: a mass expiration that, if handled badly, loses the core for nothing. The real danger is not 2005 or 2006. It is the summer of 2006 when Fischer's $3.70M deal is the fattest remaining non-core contract on a declining player, and the draft capital is still empty because no one moved an expiring veteran in 2005.

**Gaborik** is the single highest-value renewal on the roster: 76 points at 22 on $1.10M expiring this summer. If he walks in July, the club has nothing. He must go on 5 or 6 years. Nash (32 points, 20, POTE 95, $1.20M expiring) and Richards (54 points, 24, POTE 88, $1.00M expiring) sit in the same window. Kaberle (27 points, 26, $1.90M expiring) is the least urgent of the four but still belongs in the same batch.

**The veteran money is the easy part.** Belfour ($6.50M), Svehla ($3.60M), and Roberts ($2.70M) all expire, all carry 80+ overall, and all qualify for the pick-recovery mechanic. Roberts at 63 points in 56 games is painful to lose for a playoff push, but he walks regardless, and Klesla (POTE 97, 56 GP) plus Eminger (POTE 99, 44 GP) fill the gap next season. All three must be moved by the March deadline or the pick capital is lost permanently.

**The age bridge is thin.** Only two players sit between 30 and 33 (Sundin 33, Salo 30). When Mogilny expires in 2006 at $5.50M and Sundin enters his 34th season, there is no generation between the veterans and the 23-and-under core. That gap is acceptable if the young players are locked long-term and developing; it is fatal if they walk or stall. The Coach's reports about Stahle (2 GP at 20, POTE 96), Spezza (37 GP, 5.3 MPG at POTE 99), and Safronov (3 GP) say the young depth is not yet being developed, which means the bridge is thinner than the sheet suggests.

**Money is not the constraint.** Payroll $65.94M against revenue $76.79M leaves $10.85M of headroom before revenue is touched. If the three veterans walk and are replaced by raises for the young core (say Gaborik to $3M, Nash to $2.5M, Richards to $2.5M, Kaberle to $2.5M, Eminger/Colaiacovo/Upshall at $1.5M each), the payroll rises to roughly $72M. That is workable. Fischer at $3.70M through 2008-09 on declining production (26 points, 0.51 pts/g) is the one contract that will become a liability by 2007.

**Draft capital is empty.** One fourth-rounder from TOR, nothing better. Every trade must be funded with players. The only way to rebuild the cupboard is the over-80 expiring mechanic: move Belfour, Svehla, and Roberts before the deadline for picks, and begin accumulating again for 2006.

**Fischer** at 24, $3.70M, 4 years, 26 points, declining production since January, is a 2007-08 problem. No action is possible now; the note stands.

## Calendar

Are we buyers or sellers at the March 19 deadline, and what happens to the 15 expiring contracts this summer? We are sellers of expiring assets only, buyers of nothing, and re-signers of 12 players in July.

**Belfour** is the single deadline action. 92 base, $6.50M, expiring, 39 years old, redundant with Luongo (91 base, 25, 2 years left) in net. He is the only over-80 asset Toronto must move by March 19 or lose the pick capital permanently in July. A contender needing playoff goalie insurance is the counterparty; they get a proven number one, we get draft compensation. Open that conversation late February per the GM's instruction. No urgency before then.

**Svehla** (36, 85 base, $3.60M, expiring) and **Roberts** (38, 87 base, $2.70M, expiring) are both over-80 walkaways who could theoretically fetch a pick the same way. At 36 and 38, neither will be re-signed regardless. The question is whether keeping them through the playoffs (they still dress and log minutes) is worth more than a pick. With 90 points and a first-round bye likely, the marginal playoff value of two veterans is small. If a contender offers a pick for either in the final week of February, take it. If not, let them walk. Do not spend negotiation bandwidth hunting a return for players this far down the lineup when Belfour is the bigger fish.

**Buying**: There is no gap the coach has flagged that a trade fills. The toughness issue has an internal fix (Abid, 80 TOUG/80 CHKG at $400K). The coach wants young players on the ice, not new ones. The roster depth is sufficient. The only buyer move worth watching is a pure rental centre with elite faceoffs — Conroy at CGY (94 FACE, 63 pts, $2.00M expiring from a 40-point team) fits if CGY is desperate by mid-March — but that is a luxury, not a need, and it costs a pick we can use better on Belfour's return.

**The summer**: 12 re-signings, 3 walkaways (Belfour, Svehla, Roberts, who leave by either route).

**Gaborik** (22, 91 base, $1.10M): five to six years. Most important renewal on the roster. He is a first-line winger at 91 base on a min-exempt salary; letting him hit the market is unthinkable. No mid-contract renegotiation is possible in this game, so this is a July 1 priority.

**Nash** (20, $1.20M): five to six years. Core winger. Same logic.

**Eminger** (21, $1.20M): five to six years. The GM protected him over Chara on January 19 because of POTE 99 at age 21. Lock him long.

**Kaberle** (26, $1.90M): five to six years. Top-pairing defenceman, right-handed, 26 years old.

**Richards** (24, $1.00M): five to six years. Centre, 24, cheap, re-signable. The GM put him at third-line centre on January 25; that is a role for someone the club intends to keep.

**Colaiacovo** (22, $1.10M): three to five years. Young defenceman. If not traded at deadline as part of a Belfour package, he gets a renewal offer.

**Chistov** (21, $1.10M): three to five years if kept; trade bait if Belfour's return requires a player.

**Upshall** (21, $1.20M): three to five years. Young, cheap, re-signable.

**Alexeev** (23, $1.10M): two to three years. Depends on production through the spring; not a star lock.

**Abid** (24, $0.40M): two to three years. Depth at $400K, no urgency to pay more.

**Smirnov** (20, $0.40M): three to five years. Project at minimum salary.

**Tellqvist** (25, $0.80M): two to three years. Backup to Luongo. GM protected him on January 15.

**Mogilny** is not expiring. 90 base, $5.50M, 2 years left. He stays. The December 22 package that would have sent him for Jackman is dead — Jackman is not worth trading a 90-overall centre with 2 years of control for, and the package never executed anyway.

## League scan

The question: which players on losing clubs move Toronto closer to winning in 2005 and 2006 simultaneously? The answer comes down to four players who close the toughness gap (zero at 80+ today) with real hockey value attached, and one offensive swing that changes the franchise's ceiling.

**Chara** (OTT, D, 27) at 94 TOUG, 95 CHKG, 54 points in 56 games, $1.70M expiring from a 52-point club with 11 expiring deals is the best single value in the league right now. He solves toughness and checking from the blue line while producing more points than most top-four D-men. OTT is the clearest seller on the board. The complication: Eminger (POTE 99, 44 GP) and Klesla (POTE 97, 56 GP) already occupy future top-pair minutes, so Chara means Svehla leaves in any scenario, which was always the plan.

**Kovalchuk** (ATL, LW, 21) at 94 points in 54 games on $1.10M expiring is the highest-scoring player available. ATL at 54 points with 11 expiring deals cannot retain him. If re-signed he goes to 5+ years at $3-4M and sits beside Gaborik (76 pts, 22) for half a decade. The binary with Heatley (87 pts, 23, same club, same deal structure) means ATL will only move one. Toronto should pursue Kovalchuk first; his age and scoring rate are better.

**Thornton** (BOS, C, 25) at 92 overall, 94 base, 89 TOUG, 90 CHKG, 73 points in 47 games, $4M expiring is the most complete player on the board. He closes toughness and checking in one move at centre. The obstacle: BOS at 60 points with $30.32M profit has no urgency, and 13 expiring deals means they have other things to move first. Acceptance is uncertain without a large package. Toronto cannot fund this without stripping depth.

**Bell** (CHI, C, 24) at 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, 80 base, $900K with 2 years left is the cheapest player closing all three structural gaps. Only 20 points, but he is not bought for scoring. CHI at 50 points with 10 expiring deals is a seller. At $900K and 2 years, he is low-risk and controllable.

**Conroy** (CGY, C, 33) at 94 FACE and 68 points in 56 games, $2.00M expiring from a 44-point club is the best pure faceoff rental. CGY has nothing to play for and 10 expiring deals. He covers the faceoff gap for the playoff push at the cost of a 3rd/4th-liner we don't keep long-term.

**Avery** (LA, C, 24) at 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, $400K, 2 years, 6 points is the cheapest faceoff fix in the league. The production is almost nil but at $400K and 24 with 2 years left, he is a depth piece that costs nothing and covers a gap for four seasons. LA at 54 points with 13 expiring deals will take almost anything.

I am not pursuing Brashear ($2.10M, 33, 2 years, $8 points) or Domi (ANA at 67 points is not a seller). McCarthy at 32 with 3 points has toughness but no hockey value beyond fighting.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: what concrete packages can Toronto put together right now to close the toughness gap and add playoff depth, and why would each other club say yes? Today is February 12; the GM's standing order is that negotiations open in late February, so these are targets to have ready, not deals to strike this week.

**Bell** is the priority. He closes toughness (95 TOUG on the Jan 25 stored read), checking (93 CHKG) and faceoffs (87 FACE) in one move at $900K with two years of control. He is the only available player who does all three. The restructured price is Colaiacovo plus Safronov: no R2 exists, Eminger and Klesla are untouchable per the GM's veto and the coverage phase respectively, and Colaiacovo at 22 is the most expendable of our three young defensemen. Chicago at 50 points with 10 expiring deals and $26M profit are sellers; they get two blueliners aged 22 and 23 with POTE 99 and POTE 91, which rebuilds their future blue line while they collect nothing of value from Bell's 20 points. Acceptance is uncertain, but the hockey logic is clean on both sides.

**Conroy** is a rental that fills the faceoff hole for the playoffs. At 94 FACE and 68 points in 56 games on $2.00M expiring, he gives Toronto a second center who wins the draw, which only Sundin does today. The cost is Chistov (21, 16 points, $1.10M, POTE 95, expiring) plus our only pick, the fourth-rounder. Calgary at 44 points with 10 expiring deals and nothing to play for get a young forward with upside and a draft slot. The drawback: this is a straight rental, and after the season we have Conroy gone and the fourth-rounder gone, leaving the draft cupboard truly empty. Only worth it if the GM believes the Cup run needs him.

**Avery** is the cheapest gap-closer in the league: 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG at $400K with two years left. His 6 points say he is not a scorer, but at that price he is a four-year depth piece that costs nothing. LA at 54 points with 13 expiring deals are the most motivated sellers in the league. The return is Tucker: 29, $1.30M with two years left, CHKG 92 and TOUG 88, in no unit. LA get a veteran checker for a blueliner they lost to injuries; we offload an unused contract. Avery alone does not justify the ask, so the GM should try pairing him with Belanger (LA, 90 FACE, 82 base, $700K expiring, from the January target list) if LA will bundle two centers.

If none of these land, the fallback is pick recovery: Svehla (36, 83 base, $3.60M, 83 CHKG, expiring) and Roberts (38, 84 base, $2.70M, 63 points, expiring) to a contender for a second or third-rounder each via the over-80 expiring mechanic. Both walk in July regardless. Every week they sit is a week the pick capital is not rebuilt. Belfour ($6.50M expiring) is the same class of asset but must move by the trade deadline; no trades after March 19. These three should be the GM's first calls when negotiations open.

## Owed

**#2 — Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window.** This task is complete and the goalie trade window has been used. Luongo is on our roster and DiPietro was ruled out as a target back on February 6.

**Luongo** arrived and is now showing 93 overall, 40 GP, $1.60M, 2 years remaining. Since the February 7 finding he has added roughly 7 starts. The Jan 15 mandate to "fetch a really good high-90s goalie" is fulfilled; no further monitoring is needed.

**DiPietro** was checked at 79 base / POTE 99, producing 7-12-0 with a 3.65 GAA. Potential has not translated and NYI will re-sign rather than deal. Ruled out on February 6, nothing has changed.

The remaining live item from this thread is the Belfour decision (92 base, 39, $6.50M expiring, 21 GP). That is tracked under the pick-recovery findings and is a separate deadline question, not a monitoring task.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-12
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-12

Next game at CHI on Saturday 12 February 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question: are our young players getting the games they've earned? At 56 games deep with 26 to play, the window for development is closing fast. Most are fine; two are not.

**Chlup** is the good news. 18 years old, 45 games, 14.7 minutes a night on the second line, 32 points (0.71 pts/g). Morale at 92. He's getting everything he's earned and more. Nothing to fix.

**Gaborik** at 56 games, 19.6 MPG, 76 points (1.36 pts/g) needs no development discussion. He's our best player at 22.

**Klesla** has played every single game at 22, 15.3 MPG. That's exactly what a young defenceman needs. On track.

**Nash** is at 43 games, 13.2 MPG, 32 points (0.74 pts/g) on the third line. Getting his chance and producing. Fine.

**Chistov** at 42 games and 13.4 MPG is a reasonable development load for a 21-year-old on the third line. Producing at 0.38, which is depth-level, but he's learning at a pace that won't hurt him.

**Spacek** sits in the GM's rotation philosophy. 33 games, 10.6 MPG, 0.45 pts/g at 19. The GM scratched him deliberately on January 15th to make room for others. Last recommendation about him went unacted. He's getting some games but not enough at 19 to consolidate. I'd like him at 12+ on nights we can afford it.

**Spezza** is the problem I keep raising and nothing has moved. 37 games, 7.5 MPG, 15 points (0.41 pts/g) at 21 with the highest scouting number on the roster. His minutes have fallen again from the January reading. At 21, a year at 7.5 MPG teaches him nothing. I've raised this six times with no movement. I understand the rotation philosophy, but the rotation philosophy is designed for players like Smirnov and Safronov who need a cup of coffee. Spezza is the most talented forward on this roster who isn't in the top six, and he's sitting on the bench.

**Stahle** has played 2 games in 56. At 20, with the same scouting number as Eminger, and Klesla playing every night at 22, Stahle is being starved. His 2 games averaged 17 minutes, so when he plays he's trusted. He just doesn't play.

**Safronov** at 3 games in 56 is a similar issue but less urgent; he's 23, not 20. **Smirnov** at zero games is also nothing, but his scouting number is 70, the lowest of the group, so less to salvage.

**Upshall** is producing at 0.38 pts/g on 10.7 MPG at 21. That's a fourth-line rate on fourth-line minutes. He's getting what he's earned. No promotion warranted.

**Alexeev** at 55 games but only 8.3 MPG is a curious case. 30 points at 0.55 pts/g is solid production for an 8-minute role, but at 23 he should be closer to 10. Not urgent, but worth watching.

## Development trends

Development trends from December to February tell us who to build around and who to plan around by next October. The answer splits clean: two 18- and 21-year-olds are ascending into real roles, a cluster of young players are going backwards despite being rostered, and four veterans are showing clear age decline that changes next season's math.

**Chlup** at 18 is the standout. Rate went from 0.62 to 0.75 while minutes rose from 11.0 to 16.2. He is the only player on the roster whose production climbed alongside his ice time. At 18, a 0.75 recent rate on 16 minutes is second-line centre production. He is ready for more.

**Chistov** is the other riser: 0.29→0.43 on minutes from 9.5→15.3. Same pattern as Chlup, rate up and minutes up, just one step behind. Both are 21 or under and both are telling you they belong on a better line than the one they are on.

**Eminger** is the one that changes a decision. His early-season rate was 0.35 over 23 games. His recent 21 games produce 0.57. The season rate sits at 0.45, right at the trade threshold I set on February 6th. The recent window suggests he has recovered. The GM should consider keeping him rather than selling a player who is ascending at 21 on a cheap deal.

**Spezza** at 21 with POTE 99: recent rate 0.38 on 5.3 minutes a night. I have raised this six times. The pattern is unchanged and the trend is still negative. I will not raise it again. If the GM does not give him 12 minutes before the season ends, the year is written off.

**Koltsov** collapsed from 1.10 in 10 early games to 0.32 in the 22 games since. His trade value has cratered with his production. The GM is keeping him as a chip, but there is very little left on the chip to trade.

**Spacek** went from 0.55 on 16.0 minutes to 0.41 on 7.9 minutes. Rate and role both collapsed. At 19 this could be recovery next training camp, but February's minutes confirm the GM's rotation philosophy has cost him real development this year.

**Klesla** at 22 dropped from 0.50 to 0.34. Colaiacovo at 22 slid from 0.44 to 0.38. Neither should be going backwards at that age. These are not crises but they matter for next season's blue-line depth.

**Fischer** is the one to plan around. 0.44 recent on 21.8 minutes, down from 0.63. He carries four years left. The GM rightly protects him, but a four-year deal for a player trending down at 24 is a structural risk.

**Kaberle** is the keeper confirmed: 0.54→0.58, minutes 19.4→22.4. The only defenceman whose rate and minutes both climbed.

Among the veterans, **Sundin** at 33 moved from 1.46 to 0.97 while minutes rose from 16.9 to 20.4. **Mogilny** at 35 went from 1.62 to 0.89. **Roberts** at 38 went from 1.29 to 1.00 on minutes up from 16.5 to 20.3. All three are taking more ice and producing less. Next season's top nine has to be younger.

**McCabe** at 29: 1.42 early, 0.50 since. At 29 with no age excuse, this slump is either fixable or it is who he is now. The top pair next season should be Kaberle and Eminger if Eminger holds.

## Morale watch

**The room is healthy; the only minutes problem is Spezza, and it is not a morale problem yet.**

**Spezza** sits at 86, down from the mid-90s the room carried in January, on 7.5 MPG as a 21-year-old first-round-calibre centre (POTE 99). His band is 17 minutes a night. He is getting half of it. The drop is small so far and the results are holding his spirits up, but this is the one morale clock on the roster that is running. I have asked five times; the GM's rotation philosophy is the answer, and it is deliberate. I raise it once more, not as a crisis.

**Stahle** (94, 2 games, 17 MPG in them) and **Safronov** (95, 3 games) and **Ouellet** (96, 8 games as backup) all slipped 5-7 points in the recent window because they sit most nights. That is the cost of the GM's development rotation and it is the right cost against weak opposition, but it is why none of these three will dress in Chicago. Their morale is a result of not playing, not of the building or the record.

**Luongo** is at 99 on 61 MPG a night, exactly his band, and Belfour at 99 on 58 is the same. No goalie issue.

**Richards** at 99 is 17.2 MPG at 24, bang on his band. **Nash** at 99 is 13.2 at 20 on the third line, slightly under but his production (32 points) says this is his role. **Mogilny** at 92 is 17.9 at 35, right where a very good veteran belongs. Everyone else dressed sits inside their band.

No line change is warranted on morale grounds. Spezza is the flag I keep waving; the rest of the room is fine.

## Role composition

The question is whether these units are built for their jobs and whether the roster can staff every role. The short answer: the top three lines, both power plays, and both kills are sensible. The fourth line has an identity problem, but it's a roster gap, not an arrangement error I can fix by shuffling names.

**L1 through L3** are built right. L1 pairs Gaborik's 96 scoring and 99 playmaking with Roberts (81 checking), McCabe (81 checking) and Fischer (81 checking) for balance. L2 leans on Mogilny (90 scoring, 91 speed) and Afinogenov (88 scoring) with Chlup winning 77% of draws and Svehla anchoring the blue line at 83 checking. L3 has Richards (72 checking, 94 stamina, 94 clutch) as the engine and Chistov's 95 speed to break out. Nothing wrong with any of these.

**P1** puts Sundin and Kaberle as quarterback/point with Gaborik in shooting position and Roberts/McCabe for net-front traffic. That's a textbook setup. **P2** is Mogilny shooting with Richards at 72 faceoffs to win entries. Both fine.

**K1** has three 81-checking defenders (Roberts, Fischer, Svehla) around Sundin. **K2** has McCabe (81 checking, 71 toughness) and Chlup (77 checking). Both kills are properly staffed with checking bodies.

**L4 (Spacek, Koltsov, Abid)** is the odd one. Checking mean 64, toughness mean 59, faceoff mean 51. This is supposed to be the energy line but Koltsov is a 98-speed player and Spacek is a developing forward. Abid (80 checking, 70 toughness) is doing all the defensive work alone. However, L4 has no paired D and plays against the opponent's fourth line, so 64 checking is probably adequate for the matchup it actually gets. The identity is confused on paper but the minutes are manageable.

**Faceoff depth** is the structural gap. Sundin (88), Chlup (77), Roberts (73), Richards (72). That's it. Nobody behind Richards wins a draw at a meaningful rate. If either Sundin or Chlup goes down, we have no answer in the circle.

**Toughness ceiling** is low across the roster. McCabe 71, Roberts 70, Abid 70, Fischer 69. Nobody above 71. We have checking but not intimidation. No opponent's tough forward needs to worry about our guys making him pay.

**D audit (obligation #1):** Eminger crossed the 0.45 pts/g trade threshold on February 6th (19 points in 42 games). He's 21, on an expiring $1.2M deal, and he is not on any line this week. He is sellable at the deadline. McCabe's recent window shows 0.50 pts/g against a 1.42 season rate, which at 29 is a decline, not a cold streak. He stays for now but the top pair belongs to Eminger's replacement next season, not to McCabe.

## Opponent matchup

**The question:** This is a 50-point team, 18-27-8. Do we go all out or use it for development? Per the GM's standing order, development applies in games we can afford, and this is one we can afford. The current lineup already has young players in every line (Chlup on the second, Nash and Chistov on the third, Spacek on the fourth, Klesla on the third D pair). No structural change is needed.

**Chicago's top line** — Daze (87 OVR), Zhamnov (85), Sullivan (85) — is their only real threat. Zhamnov has CHKG 57 and SPEE 90 but no speed to burn; Fischer's SPEE 91 and CHKG 88 handle him. Auto-pairing puts Fischer-McCabe against them, which is correct.

**Fleury** at 86 on their second line is the other problem, but Svehla (CHKG 83) is the right body for it, and Bell (CHKG 93, TOUG 95) on that line means we want a physical D pair there. Svehla-Kaberle work.

**Their defense** is thin: McCarthy at 77 is their best, and the rest are 70-75. Our top PP (38.5%) should eat alive against that group. No PP adjustment needed.

**Their PP is 22/175** — 12.6%, bottom of the league. Our kill units can relax tonight.

**Goalie:** Luongo at 93 OVR should start. Easy opponent, 25 years old, needs the work. Check Belfour's fatigue icon as standard procedure but no reason to override the G1 slot.

**Spacek** is already on the fourth line with Abid and Koltsov. If we're up by two in the third, give him extended shifts — this is the kind of game where a 19-year-old gets 12+ minutes without consequence. That's an in-game decision for the GM, not a lineup change.

## Owed

**Standing job #1: defenceman analysis and trade candidates.** Here is where things stand for Chicago night.

**McCabe** continues to cool. He was at 48 points in 50 games on Jan 26 (0.96 pts/g); he is now at 50 in 56, meaning 2 points in his last 6 games (0.33 pts/g). Season rate has slipped to 0.89 and the trajectory is clearly downward. At 29 with $3.0M for four more years, this is the loudest sell on our blue line. He is still good tonight (82 OVR, 99 morale, 22.4 MPG), but his window to fetch a real return is closing.

**Eminger** has not moved since Feb 6. He was 19 in 42 then, now 20 in 44 (0.45 pts/g), with 1 point in his last 2 games. The recovery the threshold was waiting for never materialized. 75 OVR, $1.2M expiring, age 21. The sell-at-deadline call stands unchanged.

**Colaiacovo** is quietly the same case at a lower profile: 12 points in 30 games (0.40 pts/g), 71 OVR, $1.1M x1 year expiring, age 22. Teams paying deadline prices for depth blueliners would take him. We have Salo (81 OVR) and Klesla ahead of him on the depth chart.

**Fischer** is stable at 0.51 pts/g on 21.4 MPG, 83 OVR. GM's keeper, not moving. No new information.

**Klesla** has not scored a point since late January (23 in 56, 0.41 pts/g, 56 straight games). Reliable, cheap, not going anywhere.

**Kaberle** at 27 in 48 (0.56 pts/g) remains the keeper the GM declared on Jan 15.

**Stahle** got his third game of the season somewhere between Jan 25 and now (brief shows 2 GP, same as then). Still not getting dressed. The Jan 25 finding on wasted development still stands.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-09
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-09

Toronto 39-9-4, 88 pts after 55 games.

## Role coverage

The roster covers scoring, speed, playmaking, and depth at 80+ across most roles, but toughness and faceoffs are structural holes the coach cannot plug with current personnel, and the age curve at the top of scoring means this problem gets worse by next October.

**Roberts** at 73 TOUG and **McCabe** at 73 are the ceiling on the roster. That is 17 points below Bell's 91 displayed today. A fourth line needs one player at 85+ TOUG to exist as a physical unit; nobody here is close. Tucker's 83 CHKG is useful but his 70 TOUG means he gets out-muscled along the boards by a real enforcer line.

**Abid** was dressed on Feb 6 at the coach's request, and his base grades in our records read TOUG 80 and CHKG 80, but he does not appear in the current 80+ toughness group. Either his displayed grades are below 80 today due to form, or the recorded base was inflated by a reading we cannot confirm now. If he is genuinely at 80 stored and the coach is running him nightly, he partially closes the gap at $400K with zero trade cost. The GM should check his number next screen and confirm before spending capital on Bell.

**Richards** at 70 FACE is the second-best draw man after Sundin's 90. Chlup at 75 and age 18 is the best prospect at the dot. Neither gets a fourth line above 55% on draws. The Coach's complaint about fourth-line faceoffs is a roster problem, not a deployment problem.

**Bell** at 80 base with displayed grades of 91 TOUG, 89 CHKG, and 83 FACE is the cleanest single acquisition that fixes both gaps. At $900K and 2 years left, he is cheap enough to absorb and young enough at 24 to be a keeper rather than a rental. The package is Colaiacovo plus Safronov; Toronto own no pick better than a fourth. Acceptance is uncertain because CHI are profitable at $26M and will want more for a first-round-centre-grade player, but his displayed grades on a neutral day will be lower than 91, which makes him less attractive to a buyer in February.

**Avery** at 79 base with FACE 94, CHKG 88, TOUG 83, $400K and 2 years is cheaper and better at draws. His liabilities are ENDU 50 and PENA 93: he gasses in 12 minutes and takes penalties at an elite rate. He fixes faceoffs outright and toughness to a degree, but the penalty rate makes him a liability on the PK and a risk of giving up power plays on a contending team.

**Mogilny** at 35, **Sundin** at 33, and **Roberts** at 38 carry the top of the scoring chart. Gaborik (22) and Afinogenov (25) are the young core, but the gap between those two and the next scorer down (Richards at 85) means the team is aging into a scoring problem. Bell's 83 TOUG would at least mean the physical burden falls on him rather than Roberts.

**Ouellet** at 23 with a 1.88 GAA and 0.918 SV in 8 games is the best goalie per-minute on the roster and the third stringer. Luongo has locked the top job for two years. The Coach is right: Ouellet needs to be moved if a deal appears. He is a trade chip at 2 years and $900K with POTE 97.

## Trajectory

Is this club aging into a cliff, and is its money arranged sensibly? The age shape is fine — 16 players aged 23 or under — but the money structure is not. Four players aged 34 or older carry $18.30M in combined salary, Sundin locks another $8.40M for five more years at 33, and every core young player on a one-year deal comes up in the same July. Profit at $22.35M means the club can afford the rebuild. The problem is timing and structure.

**The July cluster** hits 15 contracts worth $25.30M. Six are core: Gaborik ($1.10M, 75 pts), Richards ($1.00M, 54 pts), Nash ($1.20M, 32 pts), Eminger ($1.20M, POTE 99), Abid ($0.40M, 63 pts), Kaberle ($1.90M, 27 pts). Current total on those six is $6.80M. On new five-to-six-year deals they will command $15–22M. That is the payroll jump, and it is the right jump to make.

**Sundin** is the hardest contract to fix. 33, $8.40M, five years remaining, POTE 60. Still producing 63 points in 55 games, but he turns 38 when this deal expires. By 2007-08 he costs 12.7% of today's payroll as a 36-year-old. His trade value is highest now and drops every season. The over-80 expiring mechanic does not apply because his deal runs through 2009-10. The window to move him is summer 2005 or summer 2006, and a straight hockey trade is the only route.

**Belfour** at 39, 92 base, $6.50M, one year left is the club's cleanest asset right now. He qualifies for the over-80 expiring mechanic, should be moved before March for a draft pick, and frees $6.50M. That recovers the only meaningful pick capital the club holds beyond a fourth-rounder. Luongo (25, 91 base, POTE 97, $1.60M, two years) is the number-one goalie. The Luongo and DiPietro monitoring task the GM asked for on January 19 is complete; Luongo is on the roster and DiPietro's numbers no longer matter.

**The 30–33 bridge is empty.** Only Sundin (33) and Salo (30) sit in that age band. When Mogilny (35), Roberts (38) and Svehla (36) leave after this summer, the bridge to the young core is Richards at 29, Abid at 29, McCabe at 33 and Tucker at 33. That is four players and two are scratched. Locking Richards and Abid on long deals is what holds the structure together.

**Mogilny** at 35, $5.50M, two years left, POTE 55 is the worst long-term money on the roster. He carries 62 points now, but by 2006-07 he will be 37 on $5.50M. The contract runs to summer 2007 and cannot be renegotiated mid-deal. Ride it out, budget the gap.

**Fischer** at 24, $3.70M, four years remaining is the next Sundin-shaped problem. 25 points in 50 games, declining from 0.63 to 0.41 points per game. Four years means no expiring leverage. Not actionable until he has two years left and can be moved as trade bait.

**Svehla** at 36, $3.60M, scratched, POTE 55 should walk this summer. **Roberts** at 38, $2.70M, 62 points, POTE 52 is a tough call — the production is real, but 38 with POTE 52 is a one-year rental in every sense. Either release him or use the over-80 expiring mechanic for a pick if the market accepts.

**Chlup** at 18, $2.34M, two years left, POTE 95, 31 points in 44 games is the next contract cliff after this summer. His deal expires in 2006 when he turns 19 or 20. Mid-contract renegotiation is impossible under this game's rules, so his price rises before we can act. That is a structural cost, not a management error. Plan the 5-6 year lock for summer 2006.

**Draft capital is gone.** One fourth-rounder from Toronto. The Luongo deal spent the first-rounder. Every acquisition must be funded by players. Belfour's over-80 expiring trade is the pick-recovery play. If it fails, the club enters 2005-06 with nothing worth packaging.

Three moves protect the next three seasons. Lock Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger and Abid on five-to-six-year deals this July — that secures the core and the bridge. Trade Belfour for a pick before March, recovering draft capital and freeing $6.50M. Begin looking for a Sundin trade in summer 2005 while he still carries 63 points and buyers believe it lasts.

## Calendar

**The deadline is 38 days away and we have no reason to be at it; the summer is where the money gets made.** Toronto lead the East by 17 points on 88, own the deepest roster in the conference, and carry only a fourth-rounder as a tradeable pick. There is nothing at the deadline we need that we do not already have, and nothing we can offer a seller that does not cost us a playoff player. The manual's "roster is already strong, do nothing" applies.

**Abid** at 79 base, $400K, and 24 is the coach's toughness answer and he is already on the roster. The coach's report from February 7 says no player carries toughness above 69; Abid's base TOUG is 80 and his CHKG is 80 per January 25 scouting. Either the coach is reading a form-affected displayed grade or he has not checked the sheet since before the trade. This is a lineup problem, not a trade problem, and it does not require 38 more days of window-shopping.

**Belfour** at 92 base, 39, $6.50M, expiring is the single largest pick-recovery asset on the roster. Luongo at 91 base, 25, $1.60M with 2 years is the number one and the standing order from January 15 is fulfilled. Belfour should be kept through the playoffs as insurance — Ouellet at 80 base and Tellqvist at 77 base are thin for a Cup run — then moved in July using the over-80 expiring mechanic. A first- or second-round pick is the realistic return. The same logic applies to **Svehla** (85 base, 36, $3.60M) and **Roberts** (87 base, 38, $2.70M): both are above 80, both are too old to re-sign, both are surplus to our depth chart (we carry eight defensemen and eleven forwards). Moving all three recovers 3–4 picks for a front office that currently owns one fourth-rounder.

## League scan

Which players across the league close Toronto's two structural gaps — toughness and fourth-line faceoffs — and which clubs are positioned to say yes? The answer determines what the GM builds into the late-February negotiation window, and the March deadline behind it.

**Bell** is the #1 target. 91 TOUG, 89 CHKG at 24 on $900K with two years left. CHI at 48 points, 10 expiring, $23.59M profit means they are selling and can afford to take salary back. He is a wing, not a centre, so his 83 FACE does not fix the faceoff gap — that was correctly identified in January. His value is toughness and checking on a top-four minute, and he is the only available player above 90 in both who is young enough to keep. The GM's proposed package (Colaiacovo plus Safronov) is the starting point. Acceptance is uncertain because CHI at $39.27M payroll and $23.59M profit have no salary pressure and may want more than two prospects for a 24-year-old with those physical grades.

**Jackman** is the value play. 86 TOUG, 87 CHKG at 23 on $700K with three years left, 26 points in 53 games from the blue line. STL at 48 points, 9 expiring, $14.63M profit. This is the Chara-type body the GM prefers at a younger age with a longer deal, which respects the January veto on Chara specifically. Three years at $700K means he is still cheap when Eminger is ready, and 26 points at 23 means he plays now. If STL engage, this is the single best value on the board for toughness.

**Avery** is the faceoff fix. 94 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG at 24 on $400K with two years left. A centre who wins draws and hits. His production is ugly — 6 points in 54 games — and the penalty grade (PENA 93) means he will take minors at an elite rate. He is not a top-six player; he is a fourth-line centre who fixes the draw problem immediately. At $400K for two years, the cost of being wrong is negligible. LA at 54 points with 13 expiring and $17.16M profit are selling everything.

**Conroy** is the best pure rental centre. 93 FACE, 67 points in 55 games at 33, $2.00M expiring. CGY at 44 points, 10 expiring, $15.80M profit. He does not close toughness (60 TOUG) but he closes the faceoff gap and adds real scoring in one move. The cost is Chistov plus a 4th — both assets the trajectory phase says the club does not plan to keep. The issue is rental risk: he is 33 with one year, and unless we extend him (which we cannot do mid-contract), he walks in July. If the coach believes Conroy elevates the playoff run, this is the deal. If the priority is roster building, skip it and take Avery at the same cost with two years remaining.

**Cammalleri and Frolov** together are the five-year solution LA is most likely to deal. Both at 22, POTE 98 and 96, on $1.10M expiring deals. Combined: 76 points in 67 games together, both under 1.2 points per game. They do not address toughness or faceoffs, but they fill two top-six spots for half a decade. LA at 54 points with 13 expiring cannot keep both. The package must be substantial — Koltsov plus Chistov plus Ouellet is the depth available without touching the core. The question is whether LA accept prospects with unrealized potential over a proven lineup piece.

**Chara** remains on the board at 88 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 54 points in 55 games from the blue line, 27, $1.70M expiring. The GM vetoed him in January for Eminger's timeline, and that position is sound. But his production has climbed since that conversation — 54 points at 27 is a number-one-pairing output. If a deal can be constructed that costs less than the original Chara+Havlat package the GM killed, it is worth revisiting. I will not re-propose the same package.

**Regehr** (CGY, D, 24) at 84 TOUG, 93 CHKG, $1.26M with three years left and 24 points in 40 games is the next-best tough young D after Jackman. CGY at 44 points, 10 expiring. Same logic as Jackman but slightly more expensive and less productive.

**Daze** (CHI, LW, 29) at 83 overall, 92 points in 54 games, $3.00M expiring is the second-highest scorer available. He does not address either gap. At 29 with an expiring deal, he is a rental with no re-signing upside unless production convinces us to extend. The coach's gaps are physical, not scoring. Daze is not the priority.

The ordering for late February: pursue Bell first (structural fix, keeper). Pursue Jackman second (value, young, long deal). Avery or Conroy third depending on whether the GM wants a keeper at 24 or production now at 33. Cammalleri plus Frolov as a parallel conversation if LA respond positively to a prospect package.

## Trade construction

Which packages both sides can actually sign for the toughness and faceoff gaps, ranked by the chance they close? Three proposals below, each funded by players the coverage phase confirms are not toughness contributors, so giving them costs nothing in the coach's area of need. Negotiations open late February per the GM's standing order; these are the proposals to take into the room.

**Bell from Chicago, package one.** We give Colaiacovo (D, 22, $1.10M, 1yr, POTE 99, 12 pts in 30 GP) and Safronov (D, 23, $0.90M, 3yr, POTE 91, 3 GP). We get Bell (C, 24, $900K, 2yr, displayed 91 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 83 FACE). Net payroll: we shed $1.10M. Chicago gain a 22-year-old with POTE 99 on a one-year deal they can flip or develop, and their $23.59M profit means the salary swing is noise. They are at 48 points with 10 expiring — full sell. The risk: Bell's base overall is 80, not 91. The displayed grades are inflated by current form. Chicago may read the same base we do and want a third piece. Start at two-for-one, be prepared to add St. Jacques (D, 24, $0.80M, 2yr, 0 GP) if they push.

**Jackman from St. Louis, package two.** We give Koltsov (LW, 23, $1.10M, 2yr, POTE 94, 18 pts in 31 GP, 96 ACCE) and St. Jacques (D, 24, $0.80M, 2yr, POTE 94, 0 GP). We get Jackman (D, 23, $700K, 3yr, 86 TOUG, 87 CHKG, 26 pts in 53 GP). Net payroll: we shed $1.20M. STL are at 48 points with 9 expiring and $14.63M profit, in a sell posture. Koltsov gives them a 23-year-old with 96 acceleration and 94 potential — a real rebuilding asset. Jackman's three years at $700K means he is still cheap when Eminger steps up, and his 26 points from the blue line mean he plays tonight. This is the best value on the board: 86/87 physical grades at 23 on a three-year deal below $700K.

**Avery from Los Angeles, package three.** We give Chistov (LW, 21, $1.10M, 1yr, POTE 95, 16 pts in 41 GP, 89 SPEE) and our fourth-round pick. We get Avery (C, 24, $400K, 2yr, 94 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG). Net payroll: we shed $0.70M. LA are at 54 points with 13 expiring and $17.16M profit — every available asset is on the block. Avery's 6 points in 54 games makes him a replaceable depth centre for them, while Chistov at 89 speed and POTE 95 is a young player with upside LA can develop. This fixes the fourth-line faceoff gap outright at the lowest cost of the three proposals. The liabilities are real: PENA 93 means he takes minors at an elite rate, and ENDU 50 caps him at 12 minutes. He is a fourth-line centre who wins draws and hits, not a top-six player. At $400K for two years, the cost of being wrong is negligible.

**Belfour runs as a parallel action.** The over-80 expiring mechanic means he can move for a draft pick without a hockey trade. He does not close a gap, but he recovers the only pick capital Toronto hold beyond a fourth-rounder and frees $6.50M. Identify a contender with a goalie need and propose the one-way deal separately.

**If none land.** Dress Abid nightly on the bottom six and accept his displayed toughness is what it is. The coach reports nobody above 69 TOUG on the roster, which means Abid's recorded base of 80 has not held into February. Check his number next screen. If he reads below 75 displayed, the gap is real and unfixable internally, and the March deadline becomes the last chance before next season.

## Owed

**Goalie trade window monitoring (task #2):** This task is complete. Luongo is on the roster and the mandate from January 15 is fulfilled; DiPietro has not become a trade candidate despite his production rebound.

**Luongo** is at 39 GP on Toronto's roster, 92 displayed (91 base), $1.60M with 2 years left. The monitoring job he was set to track arrival and early performance is done. He has played two more games since the February 7 snapshot. No availability question remains because there is nothing to be available for.

**DiPietro** has the most interesting movement: he went from 7-12-0, 3.65 GAA (early season, per the Feb 6 note) to 22-15-0, 111 GA in 2,245 minutes, which is a 2.97 GAA across 40 starts. His base overall remains 79, unchanged from every snapshot. His displayed overall is 84, meaning he is riding a form cycle, not development. NYI will try to re-sign a goalie who just posted a sub-3.00 GAA at $1.10M. He remains off the acquisition list.

**Turco** is the one new finding worth flagging. He sits at DAL, 94 base, displaying 96 today, $600K with 1 year remaining. That is an elite goalie on an expiring bargain from a club whose record I cannot confirm from the brief. If Luongo's development ever stalls or a playoff injury exposes depth, Turco is the cheapest elite option in the league. This is not actionable now but it is the only goalie who fits the "high-90s from a non-contender" profile with real money attached.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-09
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-09

Next game vs EDM on Friday 11 February 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question this phase answers: which of our 16 players aged 23 or under is getting the games his age and potential warrant, and which is not? With nobody currently injured, every scratch is a choice, so the answer is clean.

**Stahle** is the loudest problem. POTE 96, 20 years old, 2 games in 55. He played 17 minutes in those two appearances, so the coaching staff trusted him when they needed a body, then put him back in the press box. This is the biggest development waste on the roster and it has been going since October. He needs to be in the dressings every night from here to the deadline, even if it means sitting Colaiacovo. At 22 with POTE 99, Colaiacovo has already shown he can handle 18.1 MPG in 30 games. Stahle needs the reps more.

**Spezza** — I have raised this five times and nothing has moved, so I am raising it a sixth. POTE 99, age 21, 7.5 MPG in 37 games, currently scratched. He is 15 points in 37 games, which is 0.41 per game. That is not a player who has beaten out a job, but it is also not a player you sit at 21 when his scouting number is the highest on the roster. The fourth line is his to win. If the answer is he is not good enough yet, then POTE 99 is a number nobody is testing.

**Smirnov** — zero games in 55 at age 20. POTE 70 is modest, and I will not pretend he belongs on a line. But zero games means zero information. The GM's rotation philosophy is about giving young players a chance. Smirnov has had no chance. A ten-game stretch on the fourth line tells us something. Twenty-six more games of scratch tells us nothing.

**Safronov** — 3 games in 55 at 23 with POTE 91. Less urgent than Stahle because he is older, but same pattern: the scouting number says "play him," the games played say "we forgot he's here." At 23 the development window is narrowing.

**Colaiacovo** is fine. 30 games, 18.1 MPG, 12 points, POTE 99. When he is in he plays big minutes on the third pair. His 55% share likely reflects healthy rotation with Eminger and Klesla logging heavier loads. No concern.

**Chlup** at 18 is getting 44 games on the second line at 14.5 MPG with 31 points. That is exceptional for a teenager and there is nothing to fix. **Gaborik** (55 GP, 75 points), **Klesla** (55 GP, 23 points), **Alexeev** (55 GP, 30 points), **Nash** (42 GP, 32 points), **Chistov** (41 GP, 16 points), **Eminger** (44 GP, 20 points) — all dressed, all playing, all producing. No complaints.

**Upshall** is sitting and has earned it. 17 points in 45 games at 10.7 MPG is 0.38 per game. That is fourth-line output on fourth-line minutes. The spot is not being stolen from him; he has not outgrown it.

**Koltsov** stays as a trading chip per the GM's standing order. No development recommendation.

## Development trends

The question is who's growing and who's shrinking over the last ten weeks, and whether any of it should change the GM's February plans. The answer: two young guys are genuinely getting better, one is still not playing, Eminger's trend just flipped against my own trade call, and the top of the lineup is aging visibly.

**Chlup** is the story. 18 years old, 0.62→0.74 pts/g with minutes climbing from 11.0 to 16.0. He's the only young player getting more ice and producing at a higher rate on it. That's the definition of development working. He's earned a second-line look.

**Eminger** has pulled back. My Feb 6 note said he crossed the 0.45 trade threshold on season rate (19 in 42). His recent window is 0.57 pts/g in 21 games since Dec 1, which is pulling the season rate back toward 0.46. The trajectory has reversed. I would not sell him this week. If he finishes above 0.45 season, he stays as a cheap young D on a rebuilt pair. If February collapses again, we revisit.

**Stahle** played 2 games at 17.0 MPG. That's the minimum I asked for on January 25th. Two games is not enough to judge anything, but the dressing happened.

**Spezza** is worse. Minutes have dropped further to 5.3 MPG in the recent window, rate at 0.38. That's below where he was on January 31st when I last flagged this. He is not playing hockey.

**Spacek** at 19 is 0.55→0.43 on minutes that collapsed from 16.0 to 8.3. The GM's rotation philosophy explains part of this, but the rate decline alongside the ice decline is the wrong direction. He needs to be either back at 12+ or benched completely; 8 minutes is neither development nor contribution.

**Fischer** continues to fall: 0.63→0.42 while playing 21.5 MPG. At 24, on a four-year contract, this is the wrong slope. I'm not raising him as a trade candidate — he's a keeper — but the GM should know the trajectory is heading down when it should be at its peak.

**McCabe** is confirmed: 1.42→0.52 on 21.3 MPG. The January 31st note was early; now it's the full picture. He cannot be the top-pair D next season.

**Sundin** (33) and **Mogilny** (35) are 0.90 and 0.85 respectively in the recent window, down from 1.46 and 1.62. Expected at their ages. **Roberts** at 38 is holding at 1.00, better than either of them per point of age. None of these are surprises, but the top six production is thinning and there is no internal replacement for any of them.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy: morale runs 86 to 100 across the roster with an average of 92. No one is crashing, and no line change is needed tonight to fix a morale problem.

**Spezza** is the only player below 90 at 86, flat for weeks. He sits at 7.5 MPG on 37 games and is still scratched. At 21 with POTE 99, that is the same development flag I have raised five times since January. His morale has not slipped further, so it is not an emergency, but the -1 to his grades is costing us a point or two of performance from a player who could grow into something useful. This remains a recommendation to dress him, not a line-move fix.

**Stahle** dropped 6 points to 94 after two appearances. At 20 with POTE 96 and just 2 GP all season, he is the same development waste flagged in January. The morale dip is a signal, but 94 is not a crisis. One dressing before the deadline would stop the slide.

**Safronov** sits at 95 on 3 GP. Same pattern as Stahle: a young defenceman getting scraps. No action required tonight, but worth a look if a defenceman goes down.

**Everyone else is fine.** Luongo at 99 with 61 MPG, Belfour at 99 on 21 starts, Richards at 99 on 17.4 MPG, Abid at 99 on 18.6 MPG carrying fourth-line duty. The top-four defencemen (McCabe 22.3, Fischer 21.3, Kaberle 20.9, Klesla 15.4) are all at 99. The veterans Mogilny (92, 17.8 MPG) and Sundin (96, 18.7 MPG) are stable. No one is carrying minutes far above their band, and no one is sitting below it with a morale reason to complain.

No change tonight.

## Role composition

Are the units built from the right players for their jobs, and does the roster have enough bodies for each role? The answer is mostly yes on construction, with one structural gap that isn't fixable by shuffling.

**L1 (Sundin, Roberts, McCabe, Gaborik, Fischer)** — well-built. Three 80-checking players (Roberts, McCabe, Fischer) alongside Gaborik's 96 scoring. The 77 checking mean on a first line is the kind you want: they can play against anyone. No change.

**L2 (Eminger, Chlup, Mogilny, Kaberle, Afinogenov)** — 64 checking mean is soft, but that's the design. Mogilny (90 scoring) and Afinogenov (88) are here to score. Chlup anchors faceoffs at 76. You can't have a checking line and a scoring line be the same line. Accept the softness, accept that L2 gets sheltered starts or draws the third pair. No change.

**L3 (Colaiacovo, Richards, Klesla, Nash, Chistov)** — 68 checking mean, 90 best from Klesla the defenceman. Among forwards on this line, nobody checks above 72. Richards (71 faceoff) is the only draw man. This is a speed line (Chistov 94), not a checking line. It does what it's built for. No change.

**L4 (Spacek, Alexeev, Abid)** — **51 faceoffs, both mean and best.** Nobody on the fourth line wins a draw. Abid (79 checking) is the only real checker on the unit. The faceoff gap matters only if this line takes defensive-zone starts, and fourth-liners naturally don't get many. I'd accept it for now but watch if Edmonton rolls their fourth line against ours on cycles.

**K1 (Eminger, Sundin, Roberts, Fischer)** — 76 checking mean, three 80s among the four. This is the right unit. Sundin's faceoff (87) is a bonus if the kill involves a defensive-zone draw. No change.

**K2 (Chlup, McCabe, Kaberle, Chistov)** — 70/82 checking. McCabe's 80 is the anchor. Workable second kill. No change.

**P1 and P2** — P1 has Sundin, Gaborik (96 scoring, 98 playmaking), Kaberle and McCabe at the points. Four offensive weapons and Roberts for balance. Strong. P2 has Mogilny (90 scoring) and Eminger shooting from the back end. Fine for a second unit. No changes.

**Roster gap: toughness ceiling.** McCabe tops out at 70 toughness. Abid 69. Nobody above 70 on the entire roster. Against a physical opponent, we can't match their hitting from any line. That's not fixable by shuffling — we don't have the bodies. Flagging it.

## Opponent matchup

**What changes for EDM:** Nothing should change. We are superior on every line, their power play is broken, and the auto-pairing gives our top units the weakest D they'll see all week. This is a maximize-quality night per the GM's own framework, and the lineup already is maximum quality.

**EDM's structure:** They score 2.40 goals a game against our 2.40 against, and their power play is 17 for 157, which is 10.8%. They cannot kill penalties into offense. Their three D pairs read 70/71, 66/66, and 61/61. Our first three forward lines read 88/95/85, 83/83/87, and 84/80/79. The auto-pairing puts our best line against their 70-71 pair and our second line against their 66-66 pair. That's the easiest matchup on our schedule.

**Sundin's line vs Comrie:** Sundin at 88 against Comrie at 79, with Gaborik (95) against Semenov (70) and Hannan (71). The only question is whether we blow them out or grind it. We won the only meeting 4-0.

**Richards' line vs Hemsky:** Hemsky at 21 has 89 shot power and 89 deking, so he's a real scorer in the making, but he's 71 OVR and centring the third line. Richards at 84 handles him. Their third D pair is Baumgartner (61) and Dupont (61). Our Klesla/Colaiacovo at 81/70 can eat alive against those two.

**Faceoffs:** Against EDM specifically, the faceoff gap that usually bites us disappears. Their bottom-two centres are Hemsky (50 FACE) and Rita (50). Richards at 71 and Spacek at 51 win or split those draws. Only Reasoner (77) against Chlup (76) is even. This is one of the few nights the faceoff hole costs us nothing.

**Goaltending:** Luongo at 92 OVR against Salo at 82. EDM scores 2.40 a game. Luongo started Feb 7 and the GM took it. No fatigue flag on him in the brief. Belfour was tired on Jan 19; the GM should check his icon if he wants the veteran in, but Luongo is the clear choice on the numbers.

**No change on defense either.** Kaberle is already reinstated on the second pair. McCabe/Fischer on the top. Klesla/Colaiacovo get a free ride against 61-61 and should be encouraged to join the rush.

## Owed

This is the 11th update on **how our defencemen have played and who should go at the end of the season**.

**McCabe** — His slump since late January is continuing. He went from 48 points in 50 games (0.96 pts/g) on Jan 31 to 50 points in 55 games (0.91) now. That's 2 points in 5 games, a 0.40 rate over the recent stretch. At 29, $3.0M for 4 more years, and 22.3 MPG, this is no longer a blip — it's a decline. He still carries an 81 OVR and his season total is good, but the direction is wrong. He stays on the top pair now because nothing else on this roster matches his production, but next summer he becomes the question at the top of this list.

**Eminger** — No change from Feb 6. He's at 20 points in 44 games (0.45 pts/g), exactly at the trade threshold I set. He's 21, $1.2M expiring, 74 OVR. Sell at the deadline. Nothing has moved him above the line.

**Fischer** — Static. Still 25 points in 50 games (0.50 pts/g), 21.3 MPG. GM's keeper, no proposal made. My declining-age-24 flag holds: at 24 with a four-year $3.7M deal and a rate going the wrong way, this is a planning problem for next October, not a trade call now.

**Kaberle** — 27 points in 47 games (0.57 pts/g), 26 years old, 81 OVR, $1.9M expiring. Keeper per the GM. His renewal is the offseason priority on this blue line.

**Klesla** — 23 points in 55 games (0.42 pts/g) at 22, 81 OVR, $0.9M for 2 more years. Young, cheap, plays top-four minutes. No reason to move him.

**Colaiacovo** — 12 points in 30 games (0.40 pts/g) at 22, 70 OVR, $1.1M expiring. Low production, low grade. He's a candidate if a mid-round pick comes up, but no urgency.

**Svehla** — 0.68 pts/g at 36 on an expiring deal. The GM has called him the MVP and that's settled. Not raising him again.

**Stahle** — Now 2 GP (was 0 on Jan 25). Still the biggest development asset sitting idle with 0 points in 2 games and 68 OVR. He needs to be dressed and playing every remaining game, or we're wasting the asset.

Nothing structural has changed since my last delivery. The only new fact is McCabe's slump extending into February, which strengthens the "question mark next summer" flag.
