The SJ cluster (Marleau, Stuart, Brewer, Sturm, Hossa, all 25 or under, all expiring or 1-year) is a one-stop shop for multiple needs. But we have one R1 and it goes to either ATL or FLA. Everything else must be player-for-player.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: given one round-4 pick and a roster that is 35-8-3, which trades are worth constructing and does the other side have a reason to say yes.

**Belanger is the best deal available.** LA hold him at 90 FACE, 82 base, age 27, $700K expiring, on a 13-20-5 club with 13 expiring deals. They lose him for nothing in July unless they deal him. We give Safronov, a POTE-91 defenseman with three years of control who has sat on our bottom pair at 3 games played. LA are rebuilding and need exactly what Safronov is: a young blueliner they develop for three seasons. We save $200K and close the faceoff gap without spending our only pick. Acceptance is uncertain, but the logic is clean on both sides.

**Savard is the alternative.** ATL hold him at 89 FACE, 48 points in 43 games, age 27, $1.00M expiring, on a 13-24-2 club with 11 expiring deals. He carries more proven production than Belanger. The cost is Chistov plus our round-4. Chistov at POTE 95 with 89 speed is attractive to a rebuilding front office, but spending our last pick on a player we then need to re-sign is the risk. This ranks behind Belanger because it burns the pick.

**Bell is the keeper option if both faceoff deals die.** At 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 87 FACE, age 24, $900K with two years left, he closes all three remaining gaps in one move and stays. The price is Colaiacovo (POTE 99, D, 21, $1.10M, 2 years) plus the R4. We have Eminger at POTE 99 and Klesla at POTE 97 on the back end, so Colaiacovo is surplus on the depth chart even if he is not surplus on the talent sheet. CHI at $26M profit are not desperate. A POTE-99 blueliner is a real piece, and I would not be surprised if they want more. Low confidence on acceptance.

**Decision: open the Belanger conversation in late February.** It is the cheapest proposal, uses a surplus defenseman, saves money, and keeps the R4 in reserve. If LA pass, move to Savard. Bell is the fallback only if we decide toughness above 80 is a playoff-round requirement that Abid at 80 cannot cover.

**If none land:** Dress Abid nightly. He carries base 80 TOUG and 80 CHKG with 63 points in 49 games at $400K. Line Tucker on the penalty kill. Accept Richards at 70 FACE on the third line; we are 35-8-3 and have managed. Release Smirnov (POTE 70, zero games, $400K). No deal is a defensible answer.

title: Coach's report — run 2, in-game 2005-01-25
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 2, in-game 2005-01-25

Next game vs COL on Tuesday 25 January 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether our 23-and-under group is getting games they've earned, and the answer splits into three clear stories: two players are being wasted, one is earning his spot at the top, and the rest are roughly right.

**Stahle** is the clearest waste on the roster. POTE 96 at age 20, a defenceman, and zero games in 49. Colaiacovo is in the rotation at 27 games, and Safronov got 3, so the GM is willing to develop young D. Stahle has been given none of that. He's the second-highest potential defenceman on the club after Colaiacovo's 99 and he hasn't put on a jersey once. That needs fixing this week.

**Spezza** at POTE 99 is stuck at 7.5 minutes a night across 37 games with 15 points (0.41 pts/g). Morale has dropped to 86, the same band as Chlup. A player with the second-highest ceiling on the roster, getting fourth-line minutes and showing the signs. He needs 12+ to consolidate what the rate suggests he can do, and he hasn't had it since October.

**Alexeev** has been underused all season and nobody flagged it. 27 points on 8.8 MPG across 49 games is 0.55 pts/g — that's second-line production on fourth-line minutes. At 23 with POTE 94, he's the most efficient young forward on the club and he's getting the least ice of anyone who plays.

**Smirnov** has POTE 70, zero games, and nothing to show. Unlike Stahle, his scouting number doesn't support pushing him ahead of anyone else in the rotation. The right answer here is probably a release at season's end or a trade to a team that can use a ninth defenceman prospect. No recommendation to dress him tonight.

**Colaiacovo** at POTE 99 getting 55% share is the GM's rotation working as designed. He's producing 0.44 pts/g on 18 MPG at 21. Acceptable, and the POTE means the ceiling justifies patience.

**Chistov** is the weakest dressed regular. 13 points in 35 games is 0.37 pts/g on third-line wing with 12.8 MPG. That's fourth-line production on second-tier ice. At 21 with POTE 95 there's time, but tonight's third line is thin if Colorado's top pair is strong.

## Development trends

The development question this season: are the young players we drafted growing, and are the veterans we rely on sliding toward a cliff we have to plan for in February? Both things are happening at once, and the second one is accelerating because the first group cannot absorb their minutes.

**Spezza** at 21 is at 5.3 minutes a night and 0.38 pts/g across 37 games. His rate is down from 0.43 and his ice has been cut in half from 9.1. I have flagged this three times. At 21 with 37 games played and 5 minutes a night, his development window is closing. He is not a future second-line centre on this usage; he is a depth piece. The GM needs to either give him 12+ minutes or treat him as trade material this summer.

**Chlup** at 18 is the opposite story: 15.2 MPG, 0.72 pts/g over 38 games, up from 0.62. His rate climbed while his minutes went up, which is the pattern that matters. He is developing into a middle-six centre. The problem is he is there while Spezza sits, and the GM's rotation logic has no room for both at the same time.

**Chistov** at 21 went from 0.29 to 0.43 pts/g while minutes nearly doubled from 9.5 to 15.0. Still modest production, but the trend is real. He is growing into a middle-six winger and his speed plays on the top line with Sundin.

**Abid** at 24 jumped from 1.09 to 1.44 pts/g on 21 MPG. This is a top-six power winger emerging in his second full season. He belongs where he is.

**Eminger** at 21 went from 0.35 to 0.69 pts/g on 17.4 MPG, confirming the January note. He is outscoring McCabe (0.56 on 21.1 MPG) by 0.13 per game while playing 3.7 fewer minutes. Eminger is the better producer on the blue line right now.

**Fischer** at 24 dropped from 0.63 to 0.40 on 21.7 MPG. The GM has said clearly Fischer is a keeper for his two-way game and I respect that. But his production is second-pair level on first-pair ice, and it has not recovered.

**Alexeev** at 23 is going backwards: 0.62 to 0.48 pts/g and 11.1 to 6.5 MPG. A 23-year-old declining on both production and usage is unusual. He has no role on this roster at 6.5 minutes and 0.48.

**Sundin** at 33 dropped from 1.46 to 0.84 pts/g while his minutes went from 16.9 to 19.9. He is playing 3 more minutes a night and producing 43% less. This is the aging curve arriving, and the L3 stamina ceiling means the top nine must carry the load. He might need to come off 20 minutes in February or he will have nothing left in the playoff push.

**Mogilny** at 35 shows the same pattern: 1.62 to 0.90, 16.9 to 18.6 MPG. Nearly halved his rate while absorbing more ice. At 35 this is terminal decline, not a slump.

**Roberts** at 38 went from 1.29 to 1.04 on 20.0 MPG. Expected for his age but 20 minutes is a lot for a 38-year-old and he is not getting any younger.

## Morale watch

The room is in good shape overall: average morale is 92, most players sit at 96 or above, and the recent trend is up across the board after the win streak. One player stands out.

**Spezza** sits at 86, the lowest on the roster alongside Chlup, and he's been there for weeks without recovering. He's getting 7.5 minutes a night on 37 games and is currently scratched. At 21, with 15 points in 37 games (0.41 pts/g on those limited minutes), he's producing at a second-line pace while living on fourth-line ice. Whether his calibre puts him in the 70-79 band (10 mpg) or 80-89 (17 mpg), 7.5 is below what he's owed. The fix is minutes, and minutes are mine to give. The GM's rotation philosophy is why he's sitting tonight, and I respect that against weaker opponents, but a 21-year-old former top pick at 86 morale with a -1 grade penalty needs to come back into the mix soon.

**Chlup** at 86 is the other low mark. He's 18, on the second line, with 26 points in 38 games on 13.8 mpg. His calibre at 18 is almost certainly in the 70s, putting his band at 10 minutes, and he's already 4 minutes above that. Minutes aren't the issue here. His low morale likely tracks the team's point streak before the recent win run, or just the frustration of a teenager watching the game from the bench when other guys rotate through. His recent +3 trend tells me he's recovering on his own. No intervention needed.

**Luongo** dipped to the low 80s earlier this season and has bounced back to 87 with a +5 on the latest save. That tracks the goaltending results and needs no action. He's the starter at 61.2 minutes a game; there's no lever to pull.

**Alexeev** at 89 on 8.8 mpg, L4, 27 points in 49 games. If his overall is in the high 70s his band is 10 and he's close enough. At 89 he's fine.

Everything else is at 90+ and stable. The room is healthy.

## Role composition

**Unit construction is sound tonight; the one gap is structural and not fixable by shuffling lines.** Every line does what it's supposed to do on paper, and the three defensive pairings follow the guide's principle of pairing one offensive with one defensive defenceman.

**Pair 1 (McCabe + Fischer):** McCabe is the offensive driver at 48 points in 49 games on 22.4 MPG; Fischer is the checking anchor at 83 checking and 93 speed. Classic pairing. McCabe carries P1, Fischer carries K1 and P2. Heavy but not overloaded for a top pair.

**Pair 2 (Svehla + Kaberle):** Svehla checking 90 on K1, Kaberle stamina 85 and the GM's stated star. Svehla on K1 and P2 gives us two checking D on the penalty kill. This works.

**Pair 3 (Klesla + Eminger):** Klesla checking 93 (unit best on L3), Eminger producing 0.79 pts/g over his last stretch. One stays home, one walks the line. Correct construction.

**L4 (Spacek, Alexeev, Upshall):** Faceoffs 52 mean, 54 best. Nobody on this line wins a draw. Every line change against a competent centre is a possession giveaway. The top four faceoff men are Sundin 90, Chlup 77, Roberts 75, Richards 74, and all four are already deployed on lines where moving them would break something. Richards on L4 would strip L3 of its best player (playmaking 89, clutch 96). Nash cannot centre. This is a roster gap, not a lineup fix.

**K1 uses Roberts, Sundin, Fischer, and Svehla.** That is three of our four best checkers plus our best centre. It makes K1 the strongest PK in the league (checking mean 79) but it also means Sundin's even-strength rest is non-existent when we're short-handed. The trade-off is deliberate and worth it.

## Opponent matchup

**Is this a "go all-out" night, and do the lines answer it?** Colorado's top line is elite — Forsberg 95, Sakic 90, Hejduk 89 — so yes, maximize quality applies. The lines already do; no change needed beyond the goalie check.

**Sakic-Forsberg-Hejduk** is the only unit on their sheet that threatens us. Sakic wins draws against everyone except Sundin, but Sundin's displayed FACE today is 90 against Sakic's 82, so he takes the draw. Roberts at CHKG 86 and TOUG 88 is the man to make Hejduk (TOUG 51) earn it along the wall. Gaborik at 99 speed against Clark (69 OVR) and McAllister (69) who skate at 77 SPEE is a mismatch the other way.

**Their depth is thin below line one.** Stephens (73), Aubin (75), Hinote (78) on L3; Willsie (72), Battaglia (77), Krestanovich (72) on L4. Our third line is Richards at 85 with Nash's 97 SHPW on it. We should be outscoring their bottom six on any night. Their third-pair defence is the worst on the ice: two 69 OVR players with 50 endurance.

**Their PP is 14.2% (17/120), ours is 32.5% (13/40).** They get more chances (120 to our 40) but we convert twice as well. Their PK first unit is Foote, Forsberg, Sakic, Hejduk — elite but the K2 is Skrastins (75) and Hinote (78). That's where the Gaborik-Sundin unit feeds.

**Storr in net has morale 78**, which subtracts 2 from every grade. At 83 OVR before that penalty he's at 81 today. Luongo at 91 or Belfour at 92 are both clearly superior.

**Goalie:** Belfour carried the tired icon six days ago on January 19. I cannot see today's fatigue status in this brief. Check the icon before the game: if clear, start him (92 OVR, best chance against their top line). If still showing tired, start Luongo (91, no downside against a 83-OVR opponent).

## Owed

**Standing job #1: Defenceman evaluation and who goes at season end.**

**McCabe** is fully settled. 48 points in 49 games, 0.98 pts/g, 22.4 MPG. The January collapse I flagged on January 4th is a dead memory. He stays on the top pair and off every list. No change from last delivery.

**Svehla** at 23 points in 33 games is 0.70 pts/g, slightly above the 0.66 I had last noted. The GM's rotation logic holds. His deal expires this summer ($3.60M, 1 year), so he's a summer decision, not a trade candidate. No change.

**Kaberle** at 23 points in 41 games (0.56 pts/g) is the quiet question mark on a star label. But the GM said "Kaberle is definitely a keeper" on January 15th. I accept that. No change.

**Fischer** is 22 points in 44 games (0.50 pts/g) on $3.70M x4. The economic problem remains. The GM killed this conversation on January 15th. I am not reopening it. No change.

**Klesla** is the value finding. 82 OVR at 22, 49 games played, 23 points, $0.90M for two more years. He is untradeable at a fair price because no one will match the value. No change.

**Eminger** at 19 points in 39 games is a season rate of 0.49, but his recent rate confirmed the breakout. At 21 and $1.20M expiring, he is either signed by summer or moved. He stays on this list as a "sign or trade" decision, not a "must move." No change from last delivery.

**Salo** is the clearest trade candidate at season end. 8 points in 21 games (0.38 pts/g), $2.60M for two more years, 30 years old, and not even being dressed. He is behind four younger defencemen who all play more and score more. This is unchanged in character but now clearer in evidence: 21 games and a healthy scratch is the staff telling you he is not part of the plan.

**Colaiacovo** at 12 points in 27 games (0.44 pts/g), 71 OVR, not dressed, expiring at $1.10M. His trade value is low because of the OVR and the production, but he's a body a contender needs on a third pair. The return would be a late pick or a depth prospect.

**Stahle, St. Jacques, Safronov**: non-factors. St. Jacques at 65 OVR and zero games is the first one to clear if a roster spot tightens.

**What has changed since last delivery:** Nothing material. McCabe's recovery is now fully confirmed rather than recent. Colaiacovo continues to sit out, which confirms he is behind Eminger and Klesla permanently. The season-end trade list is the same: **Salo first**, Colaiacovo second, Eminger depends on whether he is re-signed.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-25
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-25

Toronto 35-8-3, 79 pts after 49 games.

## Role coverage

The roster has too much skill and too little muscle. Speed (25 players at 80+) and scoring (13 at 80+) are absurd; toughness (0 at 80+) and faceoff depth (1 at 80+) are holes that will show in a playoff series against a structured team.

**Tucker** is the cheapest fix available and he is already on the roster. 83 CHKG, 70 TOUG, 29 years old, $1.30M, currently in no unit at all. Dressing him closes the checking gap from 6 players to 7 and puts a second 80+ checker on the penalty kill alongside McCabe (86). He will not fix toughness — 70 TOUG is the best the roster offers — but he is the floor the Coach flagged in December.

**Koltsov** at 92 speed, 23, not lined, is the same problem in a different form. He is producing 1.09 pts/g when dressed. The Coach's own January report flagged this. He gives the fourth line real speed without needing a trade.

**Faceoffs** are a structural weakness: Sundin at 90 is the only player above 80. Chlup at 75 is next, then Richards at 70 (the Coach reads him at 75 today, likely form-boosted). One man cannot win draws on all four lines. Belanger (LA, 90 FACE, 82 base, 27, $0.70M expiring) from the standing notes remains the cheapest external fix and pairs with a seller in full rebuild mode.

**Toughness** cannot be fixed internally. The roster's best is 73 (Roberts, McCabe). This is the same hole flagged since December. The Chara package was vetoed by the GM on January 19 (Eminger at 21/POTE 99 was preferred over Chara at 27), so the gap persists by choice. The question for the GM is whether that veto was about this specific package or about trading for a 27-year-old blueliner at all. If the latter, the gap stays open and the playoff run faces a physical problem with no answer.

**Durability** at only 3 players above 80 (Roberts 98 at 38, Afinogenov 95, Fischer 92) is a second-order concern. A long run thins the body count. Roberts carries checking, clutch, and durability simultaneously; if he goes down, three roles collapse at once.

## Trajectory

Is this club aging into a cliff, and can its money support the next three seasons? No cliff, but one summer is a minefield. The age shape is strong: 25 of 32 players are 29 or under, and the payroll naturally declines through 2009 as old contracts expire. The single threat is 17 contracts hitting UFAs in the same July. Handle that and the trajectory points up. Fail and the core walks.

**The old money rolls off in stages, not a cliff.** Svehla ($3.60M, 36, POTE 55) and Roberts ($2.70M, 38, POTE 52) expire summer 2005 and should not be re-signed. Renberg ($2.00M, 32, 7 points in 12 games) is a fourth. That is $8.30M of payroll gone without giving up anything. Belfour stays per standing order, but Mogilny's $5.50M falls off in 2006 and Sundin's $8.40M in 2009. Payroll steps down each year.

**Sundin is the one exposure with no fix.** $8.40M per year through 2009, POTE 60, and his production has halved to 0.88 pts/g. He will be 37 when that deal expires. No trade partner takes a 35-year-old at $8.40M in a no-cap league where the AI values picks and prospects. The only play is to absorb the salary within a growing revenue base. It is annoying but survivable.

**Chlup is the contract to watch in 2006.** He is on a 2-year deal at $2.34M with POTE 95 at age 18, and the game mechanics prevent renegotiation until the deal expires. By summer 2006 he will be 20 and potentially a top-nine centre, at which point $2.34M disappears and the new ask could be $5M+. Nothing to do now, but mark the summer.

**The 17-contract cluster is the whole game.** $28.60M in deals expiring the same summer covers Gaborik ($1.10M, 70 pts), Richards ($1.00M, 51 pts), Nash ($1.20M, POTE 95, age 20), Eminger ($1.20M, POTE 99, age 21), Kaberle ($1.90M, POTE 75), and eight more depth players. If they all enter July unprotected, Gaborik alone could go from $1.10M to $5M+, Richards from $1.00M to $3.50M, Nash and Eminger to similar. A simultaneous raise across all 17 pushes payroll past $80M in one step.

**The stagger solves it.** Lock the six star-tier players on 5-6 years now: Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger, Kaberle, Chlup (when eligible). Lock the depth tier — Upshall ($1.20M, POTE 99), Colaiacovo ($1.10M, POTE 99), Alexeev ($1.10M, POTE 94), Chistov ($1.10M, POTE 95), Klesla (already 2yr, $0.90M, POTE 97) — on 2-3 years. The renewal wave splits across summer 2005 and summer 2007, and the payroll step-up is gradual.

**Draft capital is thin and about to get thinner.** TOR holds their own R1, R2, R3, R4. The R1 is committed to Luongo or an ATL package. If the R2 goes in the December fallback, the club is left with two late-rounders for a team that wants to stay competitive for four more years. At scouting level 2, the late picks still have value for depth, but there is no margin left after those two go. The club should not trade the R2 unless the return is a player it would re-sign, not a rental.

**The money has room.** Payroll is $66.97M against $71.86M revenue and $25.51M profit. The profit comes from TV contracts, prestige (519) and a 35-8-3 record selling out at $97. Even if the record drops to 38-40-4 next season, attendance at 17,566 and the existing TV deal sustain the base. The stagger plan raises payroll to perhaps $72-75M by 2006, which revenue at a 100-point pace absorbs. The plan is not reckless.

**What I would not do:** I would not spend the R2 on a deadline rental. The December package (Mogilny + R2 for Jackman) spends it on a rental the club will not re-sign, since Mogilny already expires in 2006. If Jackman is on an expiring deal too, the club gets one playoff run from him and loses the second-best pick it has. Better to keep the R2 unless the target is a young player on a multi-year deal.

## Calendar

The deadline is 53 days away on March 19, and we sit at 79 points with 33 games left, 12 clear of second place. We are buyers. The GM's standing order puts negotiations at late February, which is the right timing: sellers like ATL (13-24-2), PIT (12-21-5), and FLA will still be sellers in four weeks, and we have nothing to prove before then.

**The deadline plan is three moves, not five.** The Luongo package (own R1 plus Chistov) is the priority and fulfills the GM's mandate for a high-90s goalie. The ATL binary (Kovalchuk or Heatley, whichever they do not re-sign) fills the top-six gap the Coach flagged — Sundin at 0.88 and Mogilny at 0.85 have both halved. Abid at $400K for R3 plus Holden is cheap depth. Those three spend one R1, one DET-2nd, one R3, and move two young forwards (Chistov, Holden) who are depth, not core.

**Svehla and Roberts are deadline sellers regardless.** Svehla at 36 and $3.60M, Roberts at 38 and $2.70M — both are above 80 base and will not re-sign at those numbers. The game's mechanic lets us convert any player above 80 we will not keep into a draft pick. Moving both clears $6.30M and yields two picks for the 2005 draft class.

**Belfour stays through the deadline** per GM order. At 39 and $6.50M he is the present number one while Luongo develops. The summer question is whether he accepts a reduced renewal or walks; either way Luongo and Tellqvist (POTE high 90s) are the future.

**Summer renewals, tiered by value and timeline:**

- **Gaborik** (22, 67 pts/45 GP, $1.10M expiring): five or six years. This is the one that matters. If he's still at 91 base when the market opens in July, every contender bids.
- **Nash** (20, POTE 96+): five or six years. Same logic, slightly less urgent because he's a year younger.
- **Richards** (24, $1.00M): five or six years.
- **Kaberle** (26, $1.90M): five years.
- **Eminger** (21, POTE 99, $1.20M): five or six years. GM wants him.
- **Colaiacovo** (21, $1.10M): three years, see him play before locking.
- **Tellqvist** (25, POTE high 90s, $0.80M): three years. GM standing order: give him time.
- **Smirnov** (20, $0.40M): three years, developing.
- **Aebischer** (26, $0.50M): one year as insurance, or let go if Luongo signs.
- **Belfour** (39, $6.50M): offer two years at reduced. If he declines, walk.
- **Svehla, Roberts, Renberg**: do not renew. Svehla and Roberts move at deadline; Renberg at 32 and $2.00M is the one to evaluate on production.
- **Alexeev, Upshall**: two years, depth re-signings.

## League scan

Which players on losing clubs solve Toronto's two structural gaps — zero toughness above 80, and one faceoff win — at a price the GM would pay, with term he'd keep?

**Abid** is the answer before it's complicated. 63 points in 49 games at age 24 with 87 toughness and 87 checking, on a $400K expiring deal at a 15-23-5 club with 14 expiring players. He fills the toughness hole and replaces Sundin's halved 0.88 with a man producing 1.29 pts/g. POTE 95 means he's not a rental — he's a keeper. PIT must move him or lose him for nothing. The standing return (TOR 3rd-rounder plus Holden) spends the weakest asset the club holds and frees a dressed spot. Best value on the board.

**Bell** at CHI is the one a GM should be embarrassed he hasn't moved on yet. 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 87 FACE, 80 base, 24 years old, $900K, two years left. He fixes toughness, checking, and faceoffs simultaneously and is on a long enough deal to re-sign. CHI at 13-26-7 are the worst club in the league. The only reason he hasn't moved is that CHI are profitable at $26.01M, so they don't need to sell cheap. A first-rounder and a young prospect would probably do it. He is more expensive than Abid in the asset column but cheaper in the long run because of the two remaining years.

**Avery** at LA is the faceoff fix the Coach has been asking for since December. 94 FACE, 88 CHKG, 83 TOUG, 79 base, age 24, $400K, two years left. Only 5 points but that's a fourth-line centre who wins draws and hits, which is exactly the role Toronto is missing. LA at 14-22-6 with 13 expiring are motivated. He pairs with Belanger (95 FACE, $700K, expiring, age 27) in the same LA conversation if the GM wants a two-for-one.

**Jackman** at STL is the young blueliner version of the toughness fix. 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 80 base, age 24, $700K, three years left. STL at 12-26-3 have 9 expiring and only $13.87M profit — the weakest seller's position in the league. Three years of term means the GM gets a top-pairing physical D and then controls his next contract. This is what the Chara package was supposed to be, except younger, cheaper, and under the GM's veto timeline.

**Thornton** needs to be flagged. The January 22 note pulled him off the target list at base 76. Today the sheet reads base 94 with 73 points in 47 games, 82 TOUG, 80 FACE, age 25, $4M expiring at BOS (19-20-4, 13 expiring, $26.05M profit). If 94 is correct, he is the best available player — he solves scoring, toughness, and faceoffs in one move. If 76 was correct, he's $4M of nothing. Before late February, the GM should confirm this number. If it holds, he outranks everything above.

**Kovalchuk** (ATL, 87 pts/48 GP, 89 base, age 21, $1.1M expiring) remains the highest-upside target but the R1 is committed to Luongo or him, not both. The GM's choice between a franchise goalie and a franchise winger is for him to make in February.

**Komisarek** (MTL, 58 pts/49 GP from D, age 23, 83 TOUG, POTE 91, $1.1M expiring) is still the best young blueliner on a rebuilding club. MTL at 13-27-4 with 14 expiring cannot keep him. He adds toughness to the blue line while producing first-pair offence.

## Trade construction

Which sellers give Toronto the toughness and faceoff depth the roster has zero of, at a price the GM would actually pay, and why would each club say yes?

**Abid** is the first call. 63 points in 49 games at age 24 with 87 TOUG and 87 CHKG, on a $400K expiring deal at a 15-23-5 club. PIT have 14 expiring players; if they do not move him he walks for nothing in July. We give R3 plus Holden ($1.20M, age 27, 0 GP, POTE 81, not dressed). PIT get a late pick and a cheap depth centre they can dress or waive; the alternative is $0 return. We get the roster's first 80+ toughness player and a 1.29 pts/g winger who covers Sundin's halved 0.88. Net payroll saving: $800K. Acceptance is uncertain, but PIT's record and expiring pile make them the most motivated seller on the board.

**Bell** is the expensive fix that solves three gaps in one transaction. 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 87 FACE, 80 base, age 24, $900K, two years left. We give R2 plus Colaiacovo ($1.10M, age 21, POTE 99, 2 years). CHI at 13-26-7 are the worst club in the league and are rebuilding; a POTE 99 blueliner with two years of control plus a second-rounder is exactly the asset shape a franchise in this position collects. Bell at 80 base is replaceable with draft lottery luck. They have $26.01M profit so they do not need the money, but they need the young bodies. The R2 spend is justified because Bell gives two years of control, which the trajectory phase flagged as the condition for touching that pick. Payroll effect: we save $200K net.

**Avery** is the cheap faceoff specialist. 94 FACE, 88 CHKG, 83 TOUG, 79 base, age 24, $400K, two years left. We give R4 plus Chistov ($1.10M, age 21, POTE 95, 89 SPEE, 1 year). LA at 14-22-6 with 13 expiring are collecting assets for a rebuild. A speed winger with 95 potential and a fourth-rounder is a reasonable price for a 79-base faceoff centre who scores 5 points. LA keeps Chistov or re-trades him in July; either way they gain a pick. We fill the fourth-line draw hole the Coach has flagged since December. Net payroll: we save $700K.

All three stack without overlapping assets: R3 goes to PIT, R2 to CHI, R4 to LA. Together they spend the three lowest picks and three players we are not re-signing or are happy to move (Holden, Colaiacovo if forced, Chistov), and they close the toughness, checking, and faceoff gaps simultaneously while saving $1.70M in payroll.

If none land, the R2 stays home, we enter the playoffs with 70 TOUG as our ceiling, and we address the gaps through the summer draft and free-agent market instead. The December fallback (Mogilny + R2 for Jackman) is not recommended: Jackman at $700K on three years is a keeper, but Mogilny at $5.50M with POTE 55 is the salary we should let walk, not dump into a trade.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-25
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-25

Next game vs COL on Tuesday 25 January 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is who's earning games and who isn't, and tonight's answer centres on one name: **Spezza** is still stuck at 7.5 MPG with POTE 99 and morale down to 86.

**Gaborik** — 49 of 49 games, first line, 19.1 MPG, 70 points (1.43/g). He is exactly where he should be. Nothing to fix.

**Klesla** — 49 of 49, 15.3 MPG, 23 points (0.47/g). Full-time regular at 22 on the third defensive pair. His development is on track.

**Eminger** — 39 of 49, 16 MPG, recent rate 0.79/g. First-pair minutes at 21. The best development story on this roster right now.

**Chlup** — 38 games at 18, second line, 13.8 MPG, 0.68/g. Heavy load for a first-year player, and his morale at 86 is the joint-lowest among the young core alongside Spezza. Not an emergency, but worth watching in February when the legs go.

**Nash** — 36 games, 12.9 MPG, 0.83/g, third line. He sits some nights by design. When he plays he produces at top-six rates. No issue.

**Spezza** — 37 games, 7.5 MPG, 0.41/g, morale 86, POTE 99. This is the same flag from January 5th and he has moved nowhere. 7.5 minutes is fourth-line usage for the highest-potential centre on the roster. The GM's rotation philosophy is about giving *space* to develop, and 7.5 MPG is not space. He needs 12+ minutes in a meaningful role. I know this has been proposed three times and not taken; I'm raising it again because the numbers haven't budged and the morale is now visibly affected.

**Colaiacovo** — 27 games, scratched, 18 MPG when playing, 0.44/g, POTE 99. Deliberate rotation. When he gets the ice he gets real minutes. No change needed; the production will come with the games.

**Upshall** — 45 games, 10.7 MPG, 0.38/g, fourth line. Already noted as faded. Getting his fourth-line usage and producing at fourth-line rates. No promotion earned.

**Alexeev** — 49 of 49, 8.8 MPG, 0.55/g, morale 89. Playing every game on minimum minutes. At 23 this is a fourth-line role, and he's accepting it (morale 89 is mild concern but not alarming). No action.

**Smirnov** — 20, zero games, POTE 70. The lowest potential in the young group and he hasn't suited up once. At 20 with no games and the weakest scouting grade, he's not earning a roster spot. This is the GM's call to make, but I'll say it plainly: that jersey could go to someone the club believes in more.

**Safronov** — 23, 3 games, 0 points, 13.7 MPG. No output in the tiny sample he's been given. POTE 91 says the club liked him once; three games at zero doesn't change that, but he isn't earning more ice on what we've seen.

**Koltsov** — 31 games, 10.9 MPG, 0.58/g. The GM's standing order keeps him as a trading chip. No development argument here; he stays on the sheet until he moves.

**Chistov** — 35 games, 12.8 MPG, 0.37/g, third line, POTE 95. Low production for his potential, but he's on a line that carries Nash and Klesla and the third-line stamina ceiling caps everyone's minutes. No individual fix.

## Development trends

The development window from December 1st to now splits this roster cleanly: the 18-to-21 group is ascending, the 33-and-over group is falling, and two guys in the middle (Spezza, Afinogenov) are going the wrong way for entirely different reasons.

**Chlup** is the best story on the team. At 18, he's gone from 0.62 pts/g on 11 minutes to 0.72 pts/g on 15.2 minutes. Rate up 16%, minutes up 38%. He's not just getting thrown in to fill a gap, he's producing while the load grows. He's ready for a top-nine role permanently, not rotationally.

**Spezza** is the alarm. At 21, his rate dropped from 0.43 to 0.38 while minutes collapsed from 9.1 to 5.3 per game. My January 5th note said "if he gets 12+ and maintains 0.60+, he's a second-line centre for next season; if not, the window closes." He's at 5.3 and falling. The window is closing in real time. At this point the question isn't line assignment, it's whether this roster has a role for him at all.

**Alexeev** is following the same slide at 23: 0.62→0.48 pts/g, 11.1→6.5 MPG. Less urgent because he's a year older and has less upside, but the direction is identical to Spezza's.

**Afinogenov** at 25 dropped from 1.17 to 0.92 pts/g on flat minutes (16.8→16.7). That's a 21% rate loss at an age when production should still be climbing. Worth watching through February. If it continues, it's not a slump, it's a ceiling.

**McCabe** is gone as an offensive force. 1.42→0.56 pts/g at 29. His minutes haven't collapsed (23.7→21.1), so the coaching staff is still using him, but the production isn't there. The season is written. Offseason planning must treat him as a depth pair defenceman.

**Sundin** dropped from 1.46 to 0.84 pts/g while minutes rose from 16.9 to 19.9. He's being asked for more and delivering less. At 33, that's the aging curve. **Mogilny** mirrors it exactly at 35: 1.62→0.90 pts/g on rising minutes (16.9→18.6). Together they're producing 1.74 pts/g combined versus 3.08 in October. The top line is carried by Gaborik (1.44 and flat) and Richards (1.09 and flat).

**Roberts** at 38 is holding up better than expected: only 1.29→1.04. But he's on 20 MPG at 38, and the L3 stamina ceiling means the team can't give him relief.

**Fischer** declined from 0.63 to 0.40 pts/g, but the GM has ruled him a keeper. Noted, no action.

**Svehla** at 36 dropped from 0.78 to 0.60 pts/g with minutes down (23.8→20.2). The GM called him MVP. I respect that; the trend is what it is, and planning should account for it being lower next season.

## Morale watch

The room is in good shape. Morale moved up across the board since January 18 — Sundin, Richards, Roberts, Chistov and Chlup all gained 3 or 4 points, and most of the roster gained 1. That's results doing the work. Nobody is at a point where I'd change their minutes to protect their head space before tonight's game against Colorado.

**Aebischer** sits at 81, eleven points below the next-lowest player and eleven below the team average of 92. This is not a minutes problem: he's playing 58 a night, the maximum a goalie gets. He went from 80 to 81, so at least he's climbing. Whatever is dragging him — the goals against, the losses between the pipes — is not something I can fix by moving a forward up or down a line. Flagging it for the GM to watch; if it drops below 80 his grades lose a point each and every save gets harder.

**Alexeev** at 89 with 8.8 minutes on the fourth line is the one to keep an eye on. At 23, if his game is low-80s calibre he expects the 10-minute band. He's slightly under it and his morale is sitting right at the 80s threshold where the -1 kicks in. Not urgent tonight; if it slips below 88 before February, he earns a top-nine wing spot over whoever is on the fourth line.

**Spezza** at 86 is fine. He dropped to 85 mid-window but recovered with the team. He's scratched tonight and 7.5 MPG across 37 games is below the 10-minute band for his age, but his development is the GM's deliberate rotation choice, and at 86 he's not suffering. No change needed.

**Chlup** at 18 getting 13.8 minutes on the second line is over the 10-minute band by nearly four minutes, but his morale rose 3 points this week to 86. He's thriving on the load. Leave him exactly where he is.

No lineup or rotation change justified on morale grounds for tonight.

## Role composition

Are our units built from players who suit them, and does the roster hold what they need? The answer is mostly yes on forwards, and the one structural problem is on the penalty kill.

**K2** — Chlup, McCabe, Kaberle, Chistov. **Kaberle** is at checking 69 and toughness 56 on a unit whose job is to keep the puck out of the net. McCabe (85/81) carries the defensive load alone. **St. Jacques** at checking 80, toughness 76 is purpose-built for this slot even at 65 OVR — a PK unit needs those two grades, not the overall. If he is available to dress, swap him for Kaberle on the second kill. That keeps Kaberle fresh for even strength and P1 where his playmaking actually earns him ice time.

**McCabe + Fischer (L1 pair)** — McCabe at 48 points in 49 games on 22.4 MPG is carrying the top pair as both our first power-play shooter and our best two-way defender. Fischer's checking 90 is the highest on the roster and makes this a legitimate shutdown pair. No change.

**Svehla + Kaberle (L2 pair)** — This is the guide's formula: one offensive (Kaberle 23 pts in 41 GP) with one defensive (Svehla checking 85). The mean checking is 77 and Svehla is carrying it. Acceptable for a second pair.

**Eminger + Klesla (L3 pair)** — Eminger at stamina 50 and Klesla at stamina 55 cannot take more minutes than the 16 and 15 they already carry. This is the l3-stamina-ceiling finding confirmed again in the displayed grades. Neither exceeds 79 in checking. They are a third pair that won't hold up against top opposition in a long playoff run. The production is fine (Eminger 0.50, Klesla 0.47) but the physical ceiling is real and won't grow at these numbers.

**Eminger (season-end, obligation #1)** — At 75 OVR, 19 points in 38 games, 16.2 MPG, and stamina 50, he is confirmed as a second-pair player, not a first. His checking 79 and toughness 79 are respectable but the stamina is a ceiling he carries. Cheap and young (21), so keep him unless a trade gets value, but he's not the answer to "who plays 22 a night beside McCabe next season."

**Colaiacovo** — 71 OVR, checking 64, 12 points in 27 games on 18 MPG. A defenceman at checking 64 is the weakest on the roster. Development is happening (up from earlier snapshots) but the floor is low. Trade candidate at season's end if a package presents.

**Salo** — 81 OVR, 8 points in 21 games, 19.3 MPG. He is the odd man out on this blue line and sitting healthy. He's the most obvious trade candidate: a club looking for a third-pair D who can score would pay something for 81 OVR and 3 goals.

**The roster gap.** We have four D who can check above 80 (Fischer 90, Svehla 85, McCabe 85, St. Jacques 80). That is adequate for two shutdown pairings on a given night. The real gap is a top-pair left-shot defender with both checking 85+ and the stamina to hold 22 MPG — we only have McCabe, and he's 29 and declining. Eminger and Colaiacovo will not grow into that. The GM knows this from the trade conversations already.

## Opponent matchup

The question this game answers: can we keep our home dominance (4.00/2.00) against a team with two of the best players in the league? Colorado's top line of Forsberg (95), Sakic (90), and Hejduk (89) is the most talented forward group we'll see this week, but their club gives up 3.60 per game and their third pair is Clark (69) and McAllister (69).

**Sundin vs Sakic** is our faceoff advantage. Sundin FACE 90 against Sakic 82. Richards at 74 handles Stephens at 51 easily. The one problem is Chlup (FACE 77) against Oates (FACE 95) on the second line. Oates will win draws, but at 42 with checking 50 and toughness 50 he cannot punish possession — he's a passer, not a scorer. The zone-entry cost is acceptable; moving Sundin down to centre Oates would break up the best line in the league (Sundin 89, Gaborik 96, Roberts 86).

**The first pair vs Forsberg/Sakic** is the key test. Fischer's checking 90 and speed 93 make him our best answer to Forsberg (99 HERO, 99 DEKG, 98 PUCK). McCabe at 85 checking and 84 aggression provides the physical element. This pair holds up on paper. Svehla and Kaberle handle Selanne (87, DEKG 96) and Tanguay. No reason to shuffle.

**Our power play at 32.5%** (13/40) against a club whose third pair reads 69/69 is the biggest matchup edge we have. Their PP at 14.2% (17/120) is poor. No adjustment needed.

**Belfour** at 92 OVR is the best netminder on the ice and this is a "maximize quality" opponent given Forsberg and Sakic. He carried the tired icon six days ago. If that icon is clear today, start him. If not, Aebischer rested since the Buffalo game on January 22 and can handle a 3.20-per-game attack.

**Deliverable #1, defence assessment for end-of-season:** Fischer stays (GM's call, checking 90, 0.50 pts/g at 24). Kaberle stays (GM's "star defenseman"). Svehla at 36 is the trade piece — he produces (0.66 pts/g) but is old and the minutes must eventually go to Klesla or Eminger. McCabe's rate collapse noted January 4th hasn't reversed; his displayed OVR of 82 says he's still contributing but the production trend matters for off-season decisions. Klesla at 82 with speed 92 and shot power 90 is the long-term partner for whoever stays. Eminger's confirmed breakout (0.79 pts/g in last 14) makes him the best depth D we own.

## Owed

**Owed item #1: defenceman analysis and trade candidates.** The headline since last time: McCabe has recovered. He was at 0.80 pts/g when I flagged the collapse on January 4th. He's now at 0.98 in 49 games, 48 points. The top pair is intact.

**McCabe** is back. 48 points, 22.4 MPG, 82 OVR. $3.0M x 4. He stays. The January 4th note is retired.

**Svehla** at 0.70 pts/g on 22.2 MPG in 33 games. Expiring at $3.6M. GM has him on record as the MVP. No change from me.

**Kaberle** at 0.56 pts/g, 26 years old, $1.9M x 1. GM's keeper, and the numbers support it.

**Fischer** at 0.50 pts/g, $3.7M x 4. Off the table per standing order. The contract is ugly but that's settled.

**Eminger** at 0.49 season pts/g (19 in 39). My January 19th note flagged his last-14 at 0.79. The season rate ticking down from 0.51 to 0.49 means that hot stretch has cooled. He's still cheap at $1.2M x 1 and 21 years old, but the "trade candidate before his expiring deal" threshold (under 0.65 by February) is met. That call belongs to the GM at deadline.

**Klesla** at 0.47 pts/g on 15.3 MPG, $0.9M x 2. Cheap, young, producing on his minutes. Keep.

**Salo** is the one who should go. 30 years old, $2.6M x 2, 0.38 pts/g in 21 games, not dressed. He's the fifth or sixth defenceman at a top-four salary. That's the trade I'd push at deadline.

**Colaiacovo** and **Safronov** are development depth. No trade case for either.

No change in the verdict since last time except McCabe's recovery, which removes the only structural worry about our blue line.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 2, in-game 2005-01-22
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 2, in-game 2005-01-22

Toronto 34-8-3, 77 pts after 48 games.

## Role coverage

**The Coach's L4 endurance flag has an internal fix that is already sitting on the roster.** Kaberle at ENDU 86 and Richards at ENDU 88 are both listed as "not lined" — the Coach is sitting on two players who clear his stated threshold of 65 by more than twenty points each. Dressing one of them on the fourth line costs nothing and closes the gap tonight. A trade for a fourth-liner with stamina is unnecessary while both are available.

**The toughness gap is narrower than the shipped grades suggest.** On the numbers the GM sees today, Roberts reads 89 TOUG, Tucker 85, McCabe 82, Fischer 80. Four players at 80 or above. The brief's "0 at 80+" used shipped grades before form and facilities. Three of those four are currently lined; Tucker at 89 CHKG and 85 TOUG is the fourth and he is not in any unit. Dressing him is the single cheapest move available and the Coach has already recommended it.

**Roberts** at 87 CHKG, 89 TOUG, 71 ENDU, age 38 is the best all-around checker on the roster but is running on a short clock. His endurance is already the lowest of any regular forward on the ice. He cannot carry 15+ minutes a night through a playoff run. Tucker at 89 CHKG, 85 TOUG, 70 ENDU, age 29 is the internal answer to the same role with nine more years on it, if the Coach puts him in.

**Fischer** at 91 CHKG and 80 TOUG, age 24, is the most productive young checker and should not be traded. McCabe at 86 CHKG and 82 TOUG is producing 0.61 pts/g on 20.8 MPG according to the Coach. The Coach wants to trade him in March. I agree on timing but not on the reading — his TOUG is 82 displayed, not the 73 the shipped grade implies, and his CHKG at 86 is the second-best on the blue line. He is a tradeable piece in a window, not a declining asset this month. His slide is from 0.79 (Eminger) to 0.61 on first-pair minutes, which says Eminger should take those minutes now and McCabe moves back or gets moved.

**Faceoffs are the one role with no internal fix.** Sundin at 90 FACE is alone above 80. Chlup reads 75 shipped and is the next best. Richards at 70 FACE, Holden at 71, Renberg at 68 — nobody else on the roster wins draws. Against a Cup run, a centre who cannot win a faceoff in the defensive zone is a liability. Belanger at LA (90 FACE, 82 base ovr, 27, $0.70M expiring) remains the cheapest external answer on a confirmed seller. This is a late-February conversation, not a January one.

**Age and trajectory by role:** Scoring is covered with three players under 26 (Gaborik 22, Afinogenov 25, Richards 24) plus Mogilny 35 and Sundin 33 as the veterans. Checking has Fischer 24 and Upshall 21 young, with McCabe 29 and Svehla 36 as the current starters. Toughness at 80+ averages 32 across the four (Roberts 38, Tucker 29, McCabe 29, Fischer 24). The 38-year-old is the linchpin. If Tucker does not play, there is no succession plan. Durability at 80+ is three names (Roberts 38, Afinogenov 25, Fischer 24), which is thin for a full season but adequate through a healthy stretch.

## Trajectory

The question this phase answers is whether the roster's age shape and money are heading toward a collapse or building toward a window, and the answer is: the age curve is healthy but the contract structure is a cliff that either gets managed in July 2005 or becomes an emergency.

**The good shape.** Fourteen players aged 23 or under against four at 34 or above is the right pyramid. The youth group carries the potential: Eminger (21, POTE 99), Colaiacovo (21, POTE 99), Upshall (21, POTE 99), Spezza (21, POTE 99), Klesla (22, POTE 97), Chlup (18, POTE 95), Nash (20, POTE 95), Spacek (19, POTE 91). That is eight players with potential above 90 inside the under-23 bracket, well above the manual's threshold of six. The curve is not top-heavy. It is bottom-heavy, which is the right problem to have.

**The problem is not age, it is synchronisation.** Seventeen contracts worth $28.60M expire the same July. Of those, $14.80M belongs to four players who should not come back: Belfour (39, $6.50M, CONS 50), Svehla (36, $3.60M), Roberts (38, $2.70M), Renberg (32, $2.00M, 7 pts in 12 games). Letting those four walk is the single largest payroll lever available this season. It frees $14.80M to fund raises on the young core.

**Mogilny is the next domino.** At 35, $5.50M, two years left, POTE 55, he produces (56 pts/44 GP) but that salary is the second-largest on the roster and it buys nothing for 2006-08. He has a full no-trade likely given the five-year structure, but with two years left he is a trade candidate at the deadline for a pick plus a young player. If he moves, $5.50M comes off next season's payroll and a top-six wing opens for Upshall (21, POTE 99) or Chistov (21, POTE 95).

**Sundin is the anchor nobody can move.** $8.40M for five more years means Toronto pays him through age 38. At POTE 60 and 56 pts on 48 games, his ceiling is set and his floor is declining. This is the single largest contract on the roster at $8.40M/year and it is locked. It cannot be fixed, only planned around: the club must become profitable enough on revenue growth (attendance at 17,566 on a $97 ticket, prestige 517) that $42.00M over five years for one player is a cost the structure absorbs. It does, because profit is $24.67M. But it is the one number that makes the payroll feel large.

**McCabe is the March decision the coach already flagged.** 29, $3.00M, four years left, 48 pts in 48 games on the season but 0.61 pts/g recently on 20.8 MPG. Eminger is producing 0.79 pts/g on 18.6 MPG with POTE 99. Trading McCabe frees $3.00M/year through age 33 and hands first-pair ice to a 21-year-old who is better. He is worth something now and worth less in July when his expiring partner Kaberle walks and the pair dissolves anyway.

**Money has room.** Payroll $66.97M against revenue $71.86M leaves $4.89M in headroom before profit turns, but the real number is profit at $24.67M. Letting $14.80M of veterans expire and adding moderate raises to thirteen young players (average $1.06M now, maybe $1.8M-2.5M at renewal) replaces $13.80M with roughly $22-28M. Net payroll change from the cluster: roughly break-even to slightly up, offset by the $14.80M in walkaways. The club can afford to re-sign everyone from the young group. The question is whether to, and that is a hockey call for late February.

**Draft capital is thin.** Toronto holds four picks: own R1, R2, R3, R4. No other clubs' picks. That is enough to make one deadline trade with the first-rounder as the centrepiece (the Kovalchuk or Chara packages both spend it), but leaves nothing for a second big move. If the GM executes the Chara package (Eminger + Colaiacovo + own R2 for Chara + Havlat, already vetoed per standing order) or the ATL Kovalchuk package, the first-rounder is gone and the remaining ammunition is the R3 and R4 plus players.

**Three moves that protect 2005-08:**

Let Belfour, Svehla, Roberts and Renberg expire or trade them for picks before July. That is $14.80M of salary the club should not carry into next season. The above-80 expiring-asset mechanic on Belfour is a bonus: trade him for a pick rather than losing him for nothing in July.

Trade Mogilny at the deadline if a taker exists. $5.50M for a 35-year-old with two years left is money that could become a second-rounder plus a young forward instead.

In July, stagger the young core deliberately: Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Kaberle, Eminger on 5-6 years; Colaiacovo, Upshall, Alexeev, Chistov, Spezza, Tellqvist, Holden on 2-3 years. This splits the next cluster into a small 2007 renewal and a manageable 2008 one.

## Calendar

We are 34-8-3 with 77 points, first in the East by 12. We are buyers at the deadline, and the plan is to address the bottom-six gaps the Coach has flagged while shedding salary we will never re-sign. The deadline is 56 days away; negotiations open late February per the GM's standing order.

**The deadline plan (March 19):**

**Abid** is the priority target. PIT at 12-21-5 with 14 expiring are confirmed sellers. At 86 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 54 points in 43 games and $400K expiring, he is the cheapest impact player available and fills the L4 endurance hole the Coach flagged (50 across the board is the scale floor). Return: our R3 plus Holden at $1.20M expiring.

**Mogilny** at $5.50M and age 35 is the salary dump. The December template (Mogilny + R2 for STL's Jackman) was agreed but never executed. At 2 years remaining on his deal, he is a long-term liability on a contender that needs that money for the young core coming up. Move him for a pick or a young blueliner.

**Svehla, Roberts, Renberg** ($3.60M + $2.70M + $2.00M = $8.30M combined, all expiring, all 32 or older). These are the "above 80, won't re-sign, can trade for a pick" mechanic. If any club at the deadline wants a veteran body, we move them for a conditional or a future pick. If nobody bites by mid-March, we simply don't re-sign.

**Kovalchuk** from ATL is the ceiling target if they engage, but the GM vetoed Eminger from the package and the only other acceptable return is the R1. At 77 points we are one good player from being dangerous in the second round, but I would not spend the first-rounder unless ATL are desperate. Late February decides this.

**Belfour stays.** No package involving him goes forward.

---

**The summer plan (17 contracts expiring, $28.5M in salary):**

**Gaborik** (22, 91 base ovr, 67 pts/45 GP, $1.10M). The single most important renewal. Lock 5-6 years. If he walks, we have no replacement. This cannot wait until July.

**Eminger** (21, POTE 99, 0.79 pts/g recent on 18.6 MPG). The future top-pair defenceman. Lock 5-6 years. The Coach already wants his minutes above McCabe's.

**Richards** (24, $1.00M). Centre depth, cheap to keep. Lock 5 years.

**Kaberle** (26, $1.90M). The established top-pair D. Lock 5 years.

**Nash** (20, $1.20M). Young winger, first-round talent. Lock 5 years.

**Upshall** (21, $1.20M). Coach's flag says he is earning more ice at 0.47 pts/g. Give him 3 years after the deadline test.

**Colaiacovo** (21, $1.10M). Young D with development upside. 3 years.

**Tellqvist** (25, $0.80M). GM says high 90s potential, give time. Sign 3 years as the projected starter once Belfour is gone.

**Belfour** (39, $6.50M). Offer reduced to $3.0-3.5M on 2 years. He probably refuses. If he does, we have Tellqvist and Aebischer.

**Holden** (27, $1.20M). Use in the Abid deal at the deadline. If that falls through, re-sign 2 years as depth.

**Chistov** (21, $1.10M). Keep if Kovalchuk falls through; deal as a package piece if ATL engage.

**Alexeev** (23, $1.10M), **Smirnov** (20, $0.40M), **Aebischer** (26, $0.50M). Re-sign all three on 2 years. Cheap depth, no urgency.

**Svehla, Roberts, Renberg.** Let go if not moved at the deadline. $8.30M freed for the core locks.

## League scan

The question is which players on the fifteen clubs outside the playoff race Toronto should pursue before the March deadline, and whether the club's own capital (one first-rounder, three more picks) can cover the two or three best moves. The short answer: Luongo at the top for the GM's standing mandate, Komisarek for the best value on the board, and Abid at $400K as the cheapest impact player in the league. The expensive names like Kovalchuk and Heatley carry a rental trap that changes how much a first-rounder should cost for them.

**Luongo** at 91 base overall, POTE 96, age 25, $1.60M, two years left on his deal, 15-19-1 with a 2.86 GAA through 35 starts. FLA sit at 17-24-4 with 18 expiring contracts, the deepest teardown in the league. This is the exact target the GM set on January 15: a high-90s goalie from a non-contender. Two years on the deal means no rental risk. Belfour carries the playoff run this spring, Luongo inherits the net in July. A package of own R1 plus a young forward (Chistov, POTE 95) plus a third would be fair to FLA's rebuild.

**Komisarek** at 77 base overall, POTE 92, 92 CHKG, 85 TOUG, 89 SPEE, 58 points in 48 games on 29.8 minutes a night, $1.10M expiring. MTL at 13-26-4 with 14 expiring are the second-most desperate seller. He replaces McCabe (0.61 pts/g recent, 29, $3.00M) on the first pair and produces at 1.21 pts/g as a 23-year-old defenceman. Mogilny ($5.50M, 2 years) or McCabe's contract plus a second rounder gets him. His potential is a high likelihood of development into a top-pair blueliner.

**Kovalchuk** at 89 base, POTE 86, 82 points in 46 games, age 21, $1.10M expiring. ATL at 15-25-2 cannot keep both him and Heatley. The problem is contract structure: one year means he walks in July if ATL or any other club outbids us, and we cannot renegotiate mid-contract. Trading the own R1 for a rental of an expiring player is exactly the trap the guide warns about. Use Mogilny plus R2 or R3 instead, keeping the first for Luongo.

**Heatley** at 91 base, POTE 86, 75 points in 43 games, age 24, $1.10M expiring. Same ATL situation, same rental risk, but his base is two points higher than Kovalchuk's. If ATL re-sign Kovalchuk, Heatley becomes the sole target. Same package logic: mid-round pick plus a salary, not the first-rounder.

**Abid** at 79 base, POTE 95, 86 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 61 points in 47 games, age 24, $400K expiring. PIT at 15-21-5 with 14 expiring must move him. At $400K, even if he walks in July, a third-round pick is a price the club absorbs without flinching. POTE 95 at 24 means the likelihood he develops well beyond 79 is high. He scores at 1.30 pts/g and carries his own zone. The single best expected-value deal available.

**Havlat** at 87 base, POTE 84, 64 points in 47 games, age 23, $900K expiring. OTT at 15-24-4 with 11 expiring are rebuilding. A top-six wing at 23 with 1.36 pts/g and under a million. He pairs with Chara from the same club but should be pursued separately with different assets than the vetoed Eminger package.

**Conroy** at 85 base, 95 FACE, 59 points in 48 games, age 33, $2.00M expiring. CGY at 15-25-6 with 10 expiring. He is the faceoff answer the roster lacks, and at 1.23 pts/g he still produces second-line offence. Age limits him to a bridge deal, but 95 FACE against a Cup run changes zone-entry math. If Conroy is too old for a long-term fit, Savard from ATL (79 base, 88 FACE, 49 points in 46, $1.00M expiring, age 27) folds into any ATL conversation at no extra pick cost.

**Chara** at 85 base, 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 49 points in 47 games, age 27, $1.70M expiring. OTT again. The GM vetoed the package that sent Eminger for him, and that was correct: Eminger at POTE 99 is worth more than Chara at POTE 71. But Chara as a rental for a pick plus a player the club is shedding (Svehla, $3.60M expiring, age 36) is a different question. He is the best defensive defenceman available and his grades at 90/91 on toughness and checking are the highest on any D-man in the league.

**Thornton** needs a correction. The January 10 note listed him at 91 overall, but that was the displayed number inflated by form and facilities. His base overall is 76, and his potential is also 76. At $4.00M/year, the contract is bad for what the player is. He should come off the target list.

**Gagne** at 86 base, POTE 81, 71 points in 47 games, age 24, $2.40M, listed with no remaining contract years, which in this save marks him as a UFA. PHI at $69.34M payroll and $8.58M profit are the second-most expensive roster in the league and barely profitable. They may not be able to retain him. If he reaches July, he is a top-six winger at 24 for a contract, no pick needed. A July signing target, not a deadline trade.

## Trade construction

The question is which trade packages Toronto should be ready to execute in late February, given that the club is 34-8-3 and contending, which changes the calculus from "dump salary" to "buy for need with young players you would keep." Three proposals stack without overlapping assets, spend the R1 on the GM's standing mandate, and leave two picks for the summer.

**Luongo** is the first call. He answers the GM's January 15 instruction to fetch a high-90s goalie from a non-contender: 91 base, POTE 96, 25 years old, $1.60M with two years of term, 15-19-1 with a 2.86 GAA. FLA at 17-24-4 with 18 expiring contracts are the deepest teardown in the league and have no reason to build around him at that record. Own first-rounder plus Chistov (21, POTE 95, $1.10M, 89 SPEE) gives FLA a top-100 prospect and a first pick. They are getting two rebuild assets for a goalie whose window in Sunrise is closing. Payroll moves $500K toward us. Belfour carries the playoff run this spring, Luongo inherits the net in July.

**Abid** at 24, base 79, POTE 95, 86 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 61 points in 47 games for $400K is the cheapest impact player in the league. PIT at 15-21-5 with 14 expiring deals must move him. Own third-rounder plus Holden (27, $1.20M expiring, 0 GP) gives PIT depth and a pick for a player they will not re-sign. Net payroll: we shed $800K. Even if Abid walks in July, losing a third-rounder on a $400K rental is absorbable. At POTE 95 he is a re-signing target in July.

**Belanger** at 27, base 82, 90 FACE, $700K expiring on a confirmed LA seller is the only faceoff answer on the board, and the role coverage phase identified faceoffs as the one gap with no internal fix. Safronov (23, POTE 91, $900K, 3 GP, 0 pts, scratched 44 times) is the return. He is not in the plan; the Coach flagged dress-or-remove. LA gets a young project on a three-year deal. We get the 90 FACE we need for a Cup run. This costs no pick and resolves a roster decision the Coach asked us to make.

**Komisarek** is the next target if any of the above die. McCabe ($3.00M, 4 years, 48 pts, 89 CHKG) plus own R2 for him at 22, POTE 92, 58 pts/48 GP, $1.10M expiring. MTL at 13-26-4 with 14 expiring would take a top-pair blueliner with term plus a second-rounder, though $3.00M for four years is salary bloat in a rebuild. Execute only if the R2 is still available (meaning the Luongo deal did not escalate).

All three proposals should be drafted now and negotiated in late February. January is for preparation.



**If none land:** dress Kaberle (ENDU 86) or Richards (ENDU 88) on the fourth line tonight, closing the Coach's endurance flag internally. Dress Tucker (89 CHKG, 85 TOUG) for the toughness the Coach says is thin. Move Spezza to the third line for 12+ MPG as he has requested three times. McCabe stays until July or moves for a late pick. The December package (Mogilny + R2 for Jackman) remains the fallback but Mogilny at 56 pts/44 GP is helping a Cup run right now; he should stay through the spring and be traded in July when his value is still real and his remaining year has less urgency.

# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-22

Next game at BUF on Monday 24 January 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether each young player is getting the games his production and upside have earned, and the answer is mostly yes with one glaring exception.

**Spezza** is the problem. 15 points in 37 games on 7.5 minutes a night, morale 86, POTE 99. At 21 he needs 12-plus minutes to consolidate anything, and the fourth-line stamina ceiling (endurance mean 51) means he cannot get them there. My last two recommendations moved him to third-line centre and both were not taken. Chistov is producing 0.35 pts/g on the third line at 12.9 MPG. Spezza replaces him and goes from 7.5 to roughly 13 minutes, a development priority. This has been recommended before and the GM did not act, so I will not repeat it endlessly, but the situation has not improved: 7.5 MPG and 86 morale at POTE 99 is the kind of drift that turns a first-round talent into a healthy scratch by March.

**Nash** is producing 30 points in 35 games, 0.86 per game on 13.1 minutes, morale 96. He is back in the lineup after the rotation period and getting a real third-line role. That rate says he could move up, but in a development frame he is being given the chance he needs. No change.

**Eminger** is where I expected him to be: 19 points in 38 games on 16.2 minutes, second pair, morale 96. His recent rate is 0.79 per game. POTE 99, and the ice matches it. No change.

**Klesla** and **Gaborik** are at 48 of 48 games. Gaborik at 70 points in 48 games on the first line needs no development discussion. Klesla at 22 points in 48 on 15.5 minutes is a regular defenceman and being treated like one. Both fine.

**Colaiacovo** has POTE 99 at 21 and is getting 18.0 MPG when he plays, 27 of 48 games. The rotation between him and Svehla limits his games, but the minutes he gets are second-pair. His 0.44 per game is modest but he is a defenceman. He is getting the chance.

**Spacek** at 25 of 48 games, 0.60 per game, POTE 91, 13.2 MPG. In and out of the third line, which is the GM's rotation working as intended. Fine.

**Alexeev** at 27 points in 48 games on 8.8 MPG, POTE 94. He is producing at a useful rate on fourth-line minutes. He could absorb a bit more but there is no urgency.

**Upshall** has faded to 0.39 per game on 10.8 MPG. He is exactly what his minutes say he is: a fourth-liner. No promotion case.

**Smirnov** has zero games at 20 with POTE 70. The scratch is correct. There is no upside on file that justifies taking a spot from someone producing.

**Safronov** played 3 games, scored nothing, and has been scratched since. At 23 with POTE 91 but no production, he is a healthy scratch, not a development candidate.

**Koltsov** is scratched with 18 points in 31 games, 0.58 per game. His production is not the issue; his checking grade of 55 is the worst on the roster and his role does not fit anywhere on this team. The GM has designated him a trading chip, and the development phase confirms that is the right call. He is not being wasted; he is being kept available for a deal.

## Development trends

The question: who on this roster is getting better, who is getting worse, and does anything I see change the GM's plans. The window is eight weeks of production data with no stored grade movement, so this is all ice time and points per game.

**Spezza** is the alarm. On January 5th I flagged him at 0.62 pts/g on 6.2 minutes and said he needed 12+ or the window closes. Three weeks later he's at 0.38 pts/g on 5.3 minutes. Rate down, minutes down, both at the same time. He is not stalling anymore. He is regressing. At 21 with potential that says he should be growing, this is a problem. I would sit him for a full week or two to reset and see if fresh legs bring back the 0.60 rate, because at 5.3 MPG we cannot tell whether his game has declined or whether he is simply too cold on the bench to produce when he gets his shift.

**McCabe** at 29 is at 0.58 pts/g on 20.8 minutes, down from 1.42 on 23.7 in the first quarter of the season. That is a 59% drop. I flagged this on January 4th and it has continued. He is no longer a first-pair defenceman by production. Eminger at 0.73 on 18.2 has passed him. The question for the GM is whether we ride McCabe through a slump or hand the first pair to Eminger and Colaiacovo for the remaining 34 games.

**Sundin** at 33 went from 1.46 to 0.88 pts/g. **Mogilny** at 35 went from 1.62 to 0.85. Both rates have roughly halved. Both are still playing 19+ minutes a night because we have nobody to take those minutes from. The top six is carrying two men whose production is in the rear-view and the l3 stamina ceiling (endurance mean 56) means we cannot push more load down the lineup. This is a structural problem heading into February.

**Eminger** at 21 is the confirmation I was waiting for. 0.35 to 0.73 pts/g on minutes rising from 15.0 to 18.2. The January 1st breakout was real and it is holding. He is a first-pair defenceman now.

**Richards** at 24 sits at 1.14 pts/g on 18.8 minutes, up from 1.08 on 16.9. Quietly becoming a second-line centre with first-line production. No action needed, just the note that he is approaching Sundin's output while being nine years younger.

**Gaborik** at 22 is at 1.50 pts/g on 19.4 minutes. Still climbing. Elite.

**Chlup** at 18 went from 0.62 to 0.71 on minutes climbing from 11.0 to 14.9. More ice, more production. He is developing on schedule.

**Smirnov** at 20 has zero games played in the entire window. If he is healthy, he is not being used at all, and the GM's rotation philosophy is meant to give young guys games. I cannot tell if he is injured or simply not being dressed.

**Koltsov** at 23 is at 0.33 pts/g on 12.0 minutes. The 0.60 threshold is not close. As I noted January 15th, the GM keeps him as a trade chip. Fine. He is not developing.

**Alexeev** at 23 went from 0.62 to 0.50 on minutes dropping from 11.1 to 6.5. He is losing his role. At 23 he is not a project anymore; either he gets minutes or he becomes available.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy overall, average morale around 92 with most players trending up on recent wins, but one player's morale is now visibly cracking from insufficient minutes.

**Spezza** — 86 morale, down 4 since the last save, 7.5 MPG on the fourth line. He's 21 with 15 points in 37 games, a first-round centre who should be in the 80-89 band expecting 17 minutes a night. He's 9.5 minutes short of that target and his morale is the clearest minutes-driven slide on the roster. I've recommended moving him to the third line three times; the morale number now confirms the case. If he stays at 7.5 another two weeks he drops into the 80s for real and you lose the +1 bonus every grade carries at 90 and above.

**Alexeev** — 89 morale, down 4, 8.8 MPG on the fourth line. 27 points in 48 games at age 23 is a useful winger's production, and his calibre says 17. He's 8 minutes under. Morale is still tolerable at 89, but he moved the same way Spezza did, which says the results aren't why. Same fix: find him top-nine minutes when the development rotation allows.

**Sundin** — 93 morale, down 4, 18.2 MPG. At 33 and a 90+ player he expects 20. The 1.8-minute gap is small, and at 93 morale he's nowhere near a problem. Just noting the direction since he moved the same amount as players with real deficits, which suggests the streak moved him too.

**Afinogenov** — 93 morale, down 3, 16.7 MPG. At 93 OVR he expects 20, so he's 3.3 under. Still comfortable at 93. If his minutes don't recover by February he'll join the list.

**Aebischer** — 81 morale, unchanged. That's a backup goalie watching the starter play. No line change fixes it. The GM's call on the goalie hierarchy is the only lever.

**Safronov** — 95 morale, down 5, only 3 games played. He's a scratched defenceman in the development rotation. The drop is the cost of sitting, and at 95 it's not urgent. No action needed.

## Role composition

The faceoff gap below the second line is the one structural arrangement problem that matters, and it's not fixable within the players currently dressed.

**L1** is correctly built. Sundin (91 faceoffs, 93 scoring), Roberts (84 checking, 76 faceoffs), Gaborik (99 speed, 98 scoring), Fischer (94 speed, 84 checking), McCabe (84 checking, 73 toughness). Four of five have checking above 80, and the two centres can win draws. Nothing to change.

**L2** is a scoring line wearing checking numbers. Mogilny (92 scoring, 92 playmaking) and Afinogenov (92 scoring, 92 playmaking) are the point, and Chlup (78 faceoffs) takes the draws. The 69 checking mean and 62 toughness mean reflect the personnel correctly: this unit exists to score, not to shut anyone down. Fine for a second line.

**K1** is the best-built unit on the roster. Four players with checking above 80 (Sundin, Roberts, Fischer, Svehla all at 80+), speed mean 90, stamina 78. This is a proper shutdown kill. No change.

**K2** is reasonable. Eminger, Chlup, McCabe, Chistov give a checking mean of 75 and speed mean of 88. Chistov's 98 speed lets the unit short-shift. Adequate.

**L3** has the faceoff problem. Mean 54, best 60. Nash and Chistov are the forwards who take draws, and neither is a specialist. Against a team that wins its own zone starts, this line will be hemmed in and its stamina ceiling of 70 will make that worse. The only fix within the roster is Richards (75 faceoffs), who is currently scratched. On maximize nights, he belongs on this line at centre.

**L4** is a three-man unit with a stamina best of 53 and a faceoff best of 54. There is no centre on it who can take a draw. This is the thinnest part of the roster: when the top three lines are grinding, the fourth cannot hold the ice for a full shift cycle.

**P1** and **P2** are both fine. P1 has Gaborik and Sundin as the threats with Roberts and McCabe screening. P2 has Mogilny and Fischer carrying the puck, Chlup taking the draw.

**The roster gap**: four lines need draws, and only two centres who can take them are in the lineup (Sundin at 91, Chlup at 78). Richards (75) is the third, but he's scratched for development reasons. On nights where we're maximizing, the faceoff gap on L3 and L4 is a real tactical cost against good draw-winning teams.

## Opponent matchup

**Goalie:** The question before puck drop is who starts, since both our netminders flagged tired as recently as January 19 and the current streak cell shows neither as fatigued now. Belfour carried the icon three days ago; even with it cleared, he is 39 and this opponent gives no reason to push him. Aebischer has the hot hand and this is a beatable team without him. Start Aebischer.

**The opponent:** Buffalo is 17-18-5, outscored 164-187, and their power play is 15 for 118 (12.7%). They have no player above 84 overall. Their top line (Briere 78, Drury 82, Nolan 84) is respectable but their blue line is the worst I have seen all season: McKee at 73 is their best defenceman, and their second and third pairs sit at 69, 66, and 65. We have outscored them 21-1 in two games this year. There is no specific matchup problem to solve here.

**This is not a maximize night.** Per the GM's framework, development rotation applies against teams we can afford to give space to, and Buffalo at 2.70 goals per game is exactly that. The young guys (Chlup, Spacek, Spezza, Nash, Colaiacovo, Eminger) play their normal roles. No one gets scratched or promoted specifically for this opponent.

**No line changes.** Sundin (FACE 91) will win the draw against Briere (FACE 80) on every shift that matters. Chlup (FACE 78) against their second centre Connolly (FACE 66) is another advantage. Our third and fourth lines will face their third and fourth, who offer nothing that requires adjustment. Fischer and McCabe face a blue line that cannot move the puck through the neutral zone cleanly (McKee has PUCK 61, Bombardir 62). This is a game where our top nine scores and we coast.

## Owed

**Item #1: Defencemen analysis, who should go at the end of the season.**

**McCabe** is the big change. In my January 4th note I flagged his rate collapsing from 1.42 to 0.80 pts/g with ice dropping to 19.3 MPG. That flag is dead. He is now at 48 points in 48 games (1.00 pts/g) on 22.2 MPG. He scored 18 points in his last 11 games, which is a 1.64 pace on a hot streak. The 29-year-old top-pair defenceman with the $3.00M x 4 contract has stabilised, and his stock is at its highest point since the slump began. Not a trade candidate this week.

**Salo** is the one who should go. 3 years of data on the sheet: 8 points in 21 games (0.38 pts/g), 19.3 MPG when he plays, 82 OVR, and he is barely being dressed at all. $2.60M x 2 years remaining. He is the worst contract-to-production ratio on the blue line by a wide margin. He was available to play 48 games and only suited up in 21. Trade him or bury him; he has no path back into the top four and his money buys nothing.

**Eminger** continues to look like a keeper. The Jan 19 finding stands: 0.79 pts/g in his last 14 games on 18.6 MPG. Season total (19 in 38, 0.50) is diluted by the October slog. At 21 years old on an expiring $1.20M deal, he is the most cost-effective young defenceman we have. Extension target.

**Svehla, Fischer, Kaberle, Klesla, Colaiacovo:** All unchanged from the January 15th assessment. Svehla at 0.69 on 32 games (the GM's rotation, not decline). Fischer at 0.51 on 43. Klesla at 0.46 in 48 games for $900K is a keeper at that price and age. Colaiacovo at 0.44 on 27 games is cheap depth. No moves needed from anyone on this list.

**Pilar** is already on the GM's list. No re-raise needed.

The "who goes" list is one name: Salo. Everything else is either untouchable by GM decree or young value we should be extending.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-19
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-19

Toronto 34-8-2, 76 pts after 47 games.

## Role coverage

The question this phase answers: can Toronto's roster survive a playoff series with what it already has, and where does it absolutely need new bodies? The answer is that scoring, playmaking, speed and clutch are covered in depth, but toughness is nonexistent, faceoffs rest on one man, and checking thins sharply below the top pair.

**Roberts** at 38 carries the team's identity: 88 scoring, 86 checking, 90 clutch, 98 durability. He is a one-man army. Svehla at 36 provides the other aging pillar (83 CHKG, 94 ENDU). Together they are the entire checking infrastructure. Fischer at 24 and Upshall at 21 are the successors, but at 82 and 80 they are not yet reliable shutdown answers. The coach is right that there is no Plan B.

**Sundin** at 33 is the only player above 70 in faceoffs. Richards at 70 is the nearest alternative, and he sits unlined. Chlup at 75 is serviceable but limited. A third or fourth line that cannot win draws will be pinned in its own zone against any structured club. This is a one-man role with no backup.

**Toughness is zero.** The best on the roster is Roberts at 73, then McCabe at 73, Tucker at 70. No player carries 80+ toughness. The December memory listed Tucker at 88 TOUG, but the current read shows 70, meaning the internal fallback that was supposed to cover this gap does not exist. No lineup change fixes a missing attribute.

**Salo** at 88 scoring and **Kaberle** at 90 clutch and 97 stamina both sit unlined. If Salo's 88 scoring can be used on the second line or PP unit, that partially offsets Mogilny's decline (1.62 to 0.83 pts/g). Kaberle's 97 stamina means he can absorb third-pair minutes without fading. These are coverage the coach already owns and is not deploying.

**Goalies** follow the GM's standing order. Belfour is elite at 19 GP, 16-3, GAA 2.35, SV 0.910 but 39 and expiring. Aebischer at 26 is the likely future (15-3, GAA 2.62, 0.898). Tellqvist's 64 REBC and 66 INTE are below NHL-averaging and need more than patience. The "fetch a high-90s goalie from a non-contender" target remains unfilled.

## Trajectory

The contract cluster is the defining trajectory problem, not the age curve. Fourteen players under 23 and only five veterans means the roster is built right — but seventeen of those twenty-five young players are one year from free agency on July 1st, and $28.60M walks out the door at once if the summer is mishandled.

**Gaborik** at 22, 69 points in 47 games, $1.10M, is the franchise cornerstone. Richards (24, 51 pts in 46 GP), Nash (20, 30 pts in 34 GP, POTE 95), and Kaberle (26, 22 pts in 40 GP, top-pair D) are the other four who cannot be allowed to hit the market. These four cost $5.20M combined today; in a free-agent pool they'll demand $14–16M on 5–6 year deals. Lock them all in July or the core fractures.

**The veterans coming off** — Belfour ($6.50M), Svehla ($3.60M), Roberts ($2.70M), Renberg ($2.00M) — total $14.80M. The GM has Belfour staying through the season, which is right for the playoff push. At renewal his $6.50M at 39 is the single largest line item the club can shed.
