# Coach's report — run 2, in-game 2005-01-15

Next game at WSH on Monday 17 January 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether each young player is getting the ice his production has earned, and the answer is mixed: one elite producer is benched, two promising centres are starved of minutes below the level they need to develop, and one 23-year-old is invisible.

**Nash** at 20 is sitting on the bench with 30 points in 34 games (0.88 pts/g). This is the same healthy-scratch pattern flagged on December 29, now recurring. The GM's standing order is clear: production wins over what a kid looks like on paper. Nash has earned a top-nine role and he's not getting one.

**Spezza** is at 7.8 minutes a night on the fourth line with morale at 86. His season rate is 14 points in 34 games (0.41), but the January 5 note recorded his recent rate climbing to 0.62 before minutes were cut again. At 21 with a POTE the club rates at 99, the Jan 5 threshold still applies: 12+ minutes and a sustained 0.60+ rate makes him a second-line centre next season. He hasn't gotten the minutes to prove it.

**Upshall** is at 11.4 MPG and 17 points in 41 games (0.41 season rate). His recent clip (0.69 per the Jan 8 note) has earned him the bulk of fourth-line minutes. The problem is structural: L4 endurance averages 51, so putting both Spezza and Upshall on 12+ simultaneously risks a fatigue spiral by February. This means rotation, not promotion for both. Upshall keeps the 12-minute spot now; Spezza rotates in when Upshall's legs go.

**Spacek** at 19 produced at 0.61 pts/g (14 points in 23 games) before being scratched. His morale is 96, which means the scratch hasn't hurt him yet, but at 19 every week sitting is a week not developing. He's behind Nash in the queue but deserves a look once Nash is back in and one of them settles in.

**Safronov** is 23 with 3 games played, 0 points, and a POTE of 91 that nobody has tested. The December 15 note said to keep this in front of the GM. It's now January 15 and the answer still hasn't come. At 23, three games in 45 is not development. It's a roster spot being consumed without either contributing or growing. The GM needs to name him in or out.

**Koltsov** is interesting. The January 1 note said he failed the 0.60 recovery threshold at 0.42 pts/g. His season rate is now 18 points in 29 games (0.62), meaning his recent production has been very strong — likely over 1.0 in the stretch since that note. The old assessment may be stale. I can't call it development without snapshots, but I can say his current numbers look like a player earning his role, not one who lost it.

**Gaborik, Klesla, Chlup, Alexeev, Chistov, Eminger** are all playing their share and producing at rates consistent with their minutes. No issue there.

## Development trends

The question this phase answers is who is getting better and who is getting worse between December 1st and now, because the trade deadline and the February collapse window are both close and the trends determine who gets minutes and who gets traded.

**Gaborik** at 22 is still climbing: 1.42 to 1.57 pts/g on minutes up from 18.8 to 20.0. He is the only young forward whose rate and ice are both rising simultaneously. Nothing to change here, just don't slow him down.

**Nash** at 20 broke the point-per-game mark: 0.83 to 1.00 on steady 13-minute shifts. That is a second-line winger emerging. He should be getting closer to 15 minutes by now given the rate.

**Chlup** at 18 went from 0.62 to 0.71 pts/g with ice climbing from 11.0 to 14.7. The kid is earning the centre spot by performance. His minutes are finally where a 0.70-rate centre belongs.

**Eminger** at 21 continued the breakout: 0.35 to 0.92 pts/g on minutes up from 15.0 to 19.3. The memory from January 1st called it then; this confirms it is not a hot streak. He is a first-pair defenceman now and the pairing should reflect it permanently.

**Richards** at 24 went 1.08 to 1.14 pts/g on minutes up from 16.9 to 19.0. Steady ascent into a true second-line centre. No intervention needed.

**Chistov** at 21 went 0.29 to 0.41 pts/g with minutes jumping from 9.5 to 14.8. Rate up with more ice, which is the sign of a checking forward developing into a real third-liner. Keep feeding him.

**Colaiacovo** at 21 crept from 0.44 to 0.53 pts/g on slightly fewer minutes (18.9 to 17.3). Quiet improvement. If McCabe's slide continues, Colaiacovo is the next man up on the first pair.

**Spezza** at 21 is now declining on both axes: 0.43 to 0.38 pts/g with minutes collapsing from 9.1 to 5.7. The December 5th note said 12 MPG and 0.60 rate was the threshold to keep the window open. He is at half the minutes and well below the rate. The window is closing fast. He needs 12+ MPG now or this kid's development is being killed by a lack of ice, not a lack of ability.

**Spacek** at 19 has the same pattern Spezza had in December: rate up (0.55 to 0.67) but ice down from 16.0 to 10.2. He was getting 16 minutes, got cut to 10, and his production rate actually rose. That means he can handle the ice and is being underused. Restore him to 14+ MPG.

**Upshall** at 21 sits at 0.53 pts/g with minutes down from 13.4 to 8.5. The January 8th memory set a floor of 0.55 for the promotion signal. He is at 0.53. The signal is gone. He is a bottom-six forward, and the minutes drop reflects that honestly.

**Koltsov** at 23 went from 1.10 to 0.37 pts/g while his minutes went up from 8.7 to 11.5. More ice, much worse rate. The January 1st note already said the roster has no role for him. This confirms it. GM needs to move him or dress someone else.

**Alexeev** at 23 dropped from 0.62 to 0.48 pts/g with minutes falling from 11.1 to 6.8. Both axes declining. He is losing his grip on a roster spot.

**Safronov** at 23 has 3 games and 0 points on 13.7 MPG. He finally got dressed and produced nothing. That is one sample, but at 23 with a 91 scouting number, three scoreless games does not make the case for more ice. Either commit to dressing him consistently for 10 games to get a real read, or stop treating him as a prospect and let someone else take the slot.

**Fischer** at 24 is confirmed broken: 0.63 to 0.38 pts/g on stable 21 minutes. The December 29th note said no patience fixes this. It still does not. He needs off the first pair permanently.

**McCabe** at 29 went from 1.42 to 0.67 pts/g on minutes down from 23.7 to 20.3. At 29 this is not aging. The January 4th note flagged it and the trend continues. If this holds past the All-Star break, the first pair is Eminger and Colaiacovo and McCabe becomes a second-pair option.

**Sundin** at 33 is the biggest number on the page: 1.46 to 0.90 pts/g while his minutes went up from 16.9 to 19.0. He is getting more ice to compensate for producing less, which is exactly the aging-top-six-minutes-crisis the December 19th note predicted. His minutes need to come down and go to Richards, Nash, or Gaborik. Running him at 19 minutes on a declining rate burns him for February.

**Mogilny** at 35 went from 1.62 to 0.76 pts/g on minutes up from 16.9 to 18.0. He is done as a top-six forward. Every minute above the second line is a minute better spent on a young player who is actually ascending.

**Svehla** at 36 is where the January 4th note said he would be: 0.78 to 0.45 pts/g on declining minutes (23.8 to 20.9). Age-appropriate. The transition away from him should already be happening.

**Roberts** at 38 slipped from 1.29 to 1.10 pts/g on minutes up from 16.5 to 18.8. Still contributing, but the pattern is the same as Sundin: more ice, less production. At 38 that is the most you can ask, and his minutes should be managed down to 15-16 by February.

**Salo** at 30 dropped from 0.40 to 0.33 pts/g with minutes down from 20.3 to 16.8. He is fading and getting less ice as a result. Reasonable trajectory.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy overall: 24 of 32 rostered players sit at 96 or above, and the upward swings this save (Richards +3, Roberts +3, Chistov +3, the whole blue line +1) track a winning streak. Three names still need attention.

**Spezza** sits at 86, the lowest of any dressed player, and dropped 4 points before stabilising. He's 21, on the fourth line, averaging 7.8 minutes a night. A kid at his calibre expects 10, and my development note from January 5th says he needs 12+ to consolidate. He's at 14 points in 34 games on those scraps. The morale is telling me what the scoresheet already does: he's better than the minutes he's getting. I asked for this on January 8th and it wasn't acted on. I'm asking again.

**Aebischer** at 81 is the lowest number on the whole roster. He's the third goalie, currently scratched, but he's played 19 games at 57.9 a night this season. At 81 his grades lose 2 points, so when he comes in relief he's worse than his sheet suggests. This isn't a minutes problem I can fix by moving someone between lines. It's a goalie-depth question: either he plays somewhere or his numbers stay depressed until the trade deadline.

**Safronov** dropped 5 to 95. He's 23, scratched, 3 games played, zero points. The morale tells me he knows he's not in the plan. I flagged his window closing in December. This is the GM's call to make: dress him regularly or move him. Sitting him indefinitely at 95 and dropping is wasting an asset.

Everyone else is fine. The dips from Sundin (-4, recovered +4), Richards (-3, recovered +3) and Alexeev (-3, recovered +1) all bounced back, which means they were results-driven and the streak is fixing them.

## Role composition

The question this phase answers: are the units built from the right pieces, and if not, can I fix it by rearranging or only by adding?

**Mogilny on K1 is the one arrangement error.** He's a 92 scoring winger at 36 taking penalty-kill minutes while Tucker at 81 checking sits on the bench. K1's checking mean is 76 with a best of 90 (Roberts); Mogilny is the reason that mean is not higher. Roberts and Fischer carry the kill; Mogilny's value is in his stick and his hands, not his willingness to eat a shot. Moving him off the PK costs nothing in PK chemistry — units of four rebuild fast on a kill — and frees him from a third role that drains his engine.

**Tucker scratched is the other half of that problem.** Checking 81, toughness 69. He's the fourth-best checker on the roster and the third-best forward checker behind Roberts and McCabe. Dressing him gives K1 a genuine body to put in front of the net and gives me a second line I can deploy on the penalty kill. I cannot see from the brief why he is out — if it is production, that is a different conversation, but on role fit alone he belongs in the lineup.

**L3's stamina at 56 mean, best 68, has no fix.** Koltsov, Klesla, Chistov, Chlup, and Colaiacovo are all low-endurance players. By the third period this line is skating on fumes. The only tool is shorter shifts, which the GM controls with line changes. Composition won't fix a physiological floor.

**Faceoffs remain the known roster gap.** Sundin 89, Chlup 78, Richards 75. Three centres below 80, meaning two lines lose the draw every game and our defencemen start shifts under pressure. This is unchanged since December and remains a trade target, not a lineup fix.

**L1, L2, P1, P2, K2 are right.** The first line has Sundin for draws and Roberts for the physical game. P1 gives Gaborik 99 scoring and 99 playmaking the most of the ice in the offensive zone. K2 has Eminger's 94 checking anchoring it with Chistov's 98 speed to chase. No reason to touch them.

## Opponent matchup

Do we need to adjust anything for Washington, or do our current lines already match them well?

**The answer is no change.** Here's why.

**Jagr** at OVR 89 with SPEE 98 and DEKG 99 is their whole team in one man. He plays right wing on their first line with Lang at centre (FACE 66) and Dupuis at left. Sundin at FACE 89 against Lang at 66 means we win those draws routinely and sustain offensive zone time against Jagr's own line. Fischer with CHKG 90 and SPEE 94 on the first pair has the speed to stay home on Jagr. The matchup already covers him.

**Halpern** at FACE 85 on their second line is their best faceoff man and he beats Richards at 75. That gives them zone entries on second-line draws. I have no answer for this that doesn't burn Chlup against their top nine, and Chlup at 78 barely helps anyway. It's a 10-point faceoff deficit, not a game-changer, and our second line has Gaborik at OVR 97 against Bondra at 86. We win that battle on the scoresheet even if they win the draw.

**Their PP is 12 on 122, which is 9.8%.** They cannot score on the man advantage. Our PK personnel is irrelevant for this game. They get 2.9 PP chances a night and convert one in ten. I would not swap a single penalty-killer for this opponent.

**Their depth after two lines is poor.** Third line: Zubrus OVR 79, Metropolit OVR 68, Cleary OVR 72. Fourth line: Gamache OVR 66, Sutherby OVR 72, Sloan OVR 71. Our third line (Chlup OVR 83, Chistov 81, Koltsov 72) and fourth (Upshall 78, Alexeev 77, Spezza 71) are better across the board. We can roll four lines against their bottom two and get secondary scoring.

**Belfour starts.** Kolzig is OVR 93 and the game is on the road, but their shots come from Jagr (SHPW 95) and Gonchar (SHPW 93, HERO 95) off the point. Belfour's BRKA 95 and REBC 94 are exactly what you need against a team that generates power rather than volume (251 for, 120 against for us says we control the play). No reason to go with Tellqvist.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-15
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-15

Next game at WSH on Monday 17 January 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether our young players are getting the games they have earned, and the answer is that we have a 20-year-old with 30 points sitting on the bench and a 21-year-old with 99 potential getting fourth-line minutes. Both are development failures I can see clearly from the sheet.

**Nash** is the loudest problem on this list. 30 points in 34 games at age 20 is 0.88 points per game. He's been healthy enough to dress 34 times but he's now scratched, and the club has played 45 games total, meaning he's been out for 11. This is the same pattern flagged December 29. A kid producing at nearly a point a game does not belong in the press box.

**Spezza** is at 7.8 minutes a night on the fourth line with 14 points in 34 games. His rate has been climbing — 0.62 per game over the recent stretch — and he carries 99 potential. The note from January 5 set 12 minutes as the floor for his development. He's still at 7.8. He's earning a top-nine role and getting depth minutes. That's the underuse that costs the most because nobody reacts to it.

**Spacek** has 14 points in 23 games (0.61 per game) at 19 years old and 91 potential, and he's scratched. When he plays he gets 13 minutes, which is a regular's ice, but he only plays half the games. If his production when dressed is a fair read of his ability, the scratch is wrong.

**Chlup** is 18 with 23 points in 34 games on the third line. 0.68 per game. He's getting his chance and taking it. No action needed.

**Gaborik, Klesla, Alexeev, Eminger** are all playing every game or close to it. No issues. Gaborik at 67 points is the team's best player and plays 19.3 a night.

**Upshall** is at 11.4 minutes, just below the 12 I said he needed in the last note. His season rate is 0.41 but that's dragged down by a slow start. Close enough to the threshold that it's not a crisis, but if he drops further it is.

**Koltsov** is 18 points in 29 games, 0.62 per game. That's actually above the 0.60 threshold the note from January 1 set. But that note was based on his recent rate at 0.42, and the season number includes a hot start. I can't tell from here whether he's recovered or the early games are propping up the average. Flag it but no action.

**Safronov** is the one I have to raise again. Three games played, zero points, scratched, at 23 years old and 91 potential. This has been in front of us since December 15. He is either part of the plan or he is not, and right now the answer by default is "not" while he occupies a roster spot.

**Smirnov** at 0 games and 70 potential is a depth player on this roster. He does not have a realistic path to games behind Nash, Chistov, and Koltsov. Saying it plainly is kinder than dressing him for nothing.

## Development trends

This phase asks who is getting better and who is getting worse, because three veterans are falling off a cliff simultaneously and I need to know if the young guys are stepping up to fill the holes they leave. Some are. Some are not, and one is getting the opposite of what his numbers earned.

**Chlup** at 18 is the best story on the roster. Rate up from 0.62 to 0.71, minutes up from 11.0 to 14.7. He is getting more of the game and producing at a higher clip. At 18 that is not luck; that is a kid who is outplaying his role. He and Richards (1.08→1.14 pts/g, 16.9→19.0 MPG) are both climbing, and that pair is the future centre two.

**Gaborik** at 22 went from 1.42 to 1.57 pts/g on 20.0 MPG. He is a top-line winger right now, not next year. The GM should know that our best player is also our youngest first-line forward.

**Spacek** at 19 is a problem I created. Rate went up (0.55→0.67) but I cut his minutes from 16.0 to 10.2. A 19-year-old producing at 0.67 pts/g should not be losing ice. I am penalising a kid who is getting better. I need to restore his time.

**Upshall** at 21 has a rate of 0.53, which is above the 0.55 threshold from the Dec 8 note, and minutes at 8.5. The note said he earned 12+ MPG. I have not given it to him. Same coaching error as Spacek, same fix.

**Spezza** at 21 is the one who worries me most among the young group. Rate is down (0.43→0.38) and minutes are down from 9.1 to 5.7. Both falling at once is what happens when a player loses confidence and the coach loses patience. He is on a two-way path at 21: either he gets 12 minutes and we find out who he is, or this season ends with him at 5 MPG and we never learn. I am giving him the minutes.

**Alexeev** at 23 went from 0.62 to 0.48 pts/g and from 11.1 to 6.8 MPG. The rate drop is mild but the minutes collapse suggests I do not trust him. At 23, he is not a development project anymore. Either he fills a role or he is not part of the plan.

**Safronov** finally got dressed — 3 games, 13.7 MPG, zero points. The sample is too small to judge, but the window flagged in December is now closing. Three games without a point means either I need to keep running him or we need to admit he is not ready.

**Fischer** continues to confirm the structural-failure note: 0.38 pts/g on 21.1 MPG. He is what he is, and what he is does not belong on a first pair.

**McCabe** at 29 dropped from 1.42 to 0.67 pts/g on minutes falling from 23.7 to 20.3. This is not aging — this is a collapse. Our top pair heading into the final stretch is Eminger (0.92, rising) paired with whoever survives, and McCabe is not it.

**Sundin** (1.46→0.90) and **Mogilny** (1.62→0.76) are both losing more than half their rate while getting more minutes. The memory from December said this becomes a scoring collapse by February. We are in January and it is happening. The GM needs to plan the top six around two veterans who will not get their pace back.

**Roberts** at 38 is holding at 1.10 pts/g on 18.8 MPG. He is the only veteran in his age bracket who is not in free fall. Remarkable, but I cannot build the next season around 38-year-olds.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy: average morale 92, most starters at 96 and climbing with the recent wins. Three players broke from that pattern and need attention.

**Spezza** sits at 86, down 4 since Dec 28. He's getting 7.8 MPG on L4 with 14 points in 34 games (0.41 pts/g). If he's a 70-79 guy, he expects 10 MPG; if 80+, he expects 17. Either way he's under. My standing note says he needs 12+ MPG to consolidate development at 21, and the morale drop confirms he knows it. Give him more of the fourth line's shifts or promote him over Chlup on the third.

**Alexeev** at 93, down 3. He's producing 25 points in 45 games (0.56 pts/g) on 9.1 MPG on L4. For a 23-year-old wing putting up those numbers, that's second-line production trapped in fourth-line minutes. If he's 80-89 overall, his band is 17 MPG. He's 8 short. His rate and his morale both say he's earned more than he's getting.

**Safronov** dropped 5 to 95 with 3 games played all season and a scratched status. I cannot fix this from the bench. I need the GM to tell me whether Safronov is in the plan or out of it, because a 23-year-old with real ability watching from the press box every game burns both morale and development capital.

**Sundin** dropped 4 to 89 but bounced back up 4 in the latest save. At 17.9 MPG he's slightly under his likely 20 MPG band (33 years old, 54 points, first-line centre, probably 90+ overall), but the recovery tells me the recent wins fixed what was bugging him. No action.

**Chlup** at 86 is below the room average. 23 points in 34 games at 13.3 MPG on L3 as an 18-year-old. If he's 70-79 he's already over his 10 MPG band and the morale is results-driven. If he's 80+ he's under. I'd watch it rather than act.

The room is winning, the numbers back that up, and almost everyone is happy. Two ice-time adjustments fix the only two players whose minutes don't match their production.

## Role composition

The question is whether each unit's personnel suits what we ask it to do, and where the arrangement can't paper over what the roster doesn't have.

**L1** carries the entire defensive load. Checking 76 mean with Fischer 84 and Roberts 83 as the only 80+ options below McCabe's 84. Faceoffs 64 mean with Sundin's 89 the sole player above 80 on the whole roster. Scoring 87, speed 88, clutch 85 — this line does everything because the next line down can't do any of it at a high level. That's not an arrangement error; it's the only configuration the roster supports.

**L2** is a speed and skill line (speed 91, scoring 87, playmaking 87) with checking at 72 mean. Eminger's 94 on the PK sheet carries that number up. Gaborik 99 scoring, Afinogenov 92 — this unit does what it should. Richards at 75 faceoffs is the best we can do on a second line. No change needed.

**L3** is the problematic unit. Checking 67, toughness 62, stamina 56 — those are bottom-of-the-roster numbers on what should be a sheltering line. Speed is 91 because Chistov (98) and Koltsov (99) are fast, not because the line is built for transition. This line cannot check and cannot win draws. **Koltsov** at 99 speed doesn't compensate for 0.42 pts/g and a failed recovery threshold. He has no role here.

**L4** has a stamina crisis. 51 mean, 52 best. That's the line you need fresh in the third period, and they're the most fatigued unit on the sheet. Spezza and Upshall are both climbing (my notes put them at 0.62 and 0.69 pts/g) but at low minutes. More ice would help development and morale but their bodies say otherwise right now.

**K1** uses Mogilny at 35. His speed still reads 94 but my earlier note has his production halved. He's the only option alongside Roberts/Fischer with enough game sense to not be a liability on the kill. It works short-term; it won't in February.

**P2** scores through Mogilny (92) and Fischer's shot (84 checking, but his speed 94 creates open ice). Alexeev as the fifth man is development. No better option exists.

**The Tucker question:** 81 checking, 69 toughness, scratched. He's the only player who raises L3's checking mean. I don't see a reason on the sheet why he's sitting. If it's not injury, he belongs on the third line over Koltsov to lift the unit's checking from 67 to a workable level.

## Opponent matchup

The question is whether Washington's shape demands any lineup adjustment. It does not. Our current construction already covers their threats better than any shuffle could.

**Jagr** is their whole first line. OVR 89, SPEED 98, DEKG 99, PUCK 96, but TOUG 62 and CHKG 52. Roberts at CHKG 86 and TOUG 88 is the man to make Jagr's night miserable, and that's exactly where he sits on our first line. Sundin's FACE 89 versus Lang's 66 means we own the draw on their top line and can sustain pressure. No change needed.

**Halpern** is their best faceoff man at FACE 85, and Richards sits at 75. We lose that draw, but Richards has AGGR 94 and HERO 97 — he'll win it on the puck, not the draw. And Gaborik at OVR 97 against Bondra at 86 is the best player-vs-player mismatch on the sheet. We want that line out there together, and it already is.

**Witt** is their problem. OVR 78, CHKG 94, TOUG 90, SHPW 93, but PUCK 64, DEKG 55, PASS 69. He's a hitter who can't handle forechecking pressure. Their blue line behind him and Gonchar is Yonkman 75, Doig 75, Fortin 66, Belak 68. That's a soft third and fourth pair. Our second and third lines (Chistov at SPEED 99, Chlup at 83 OVR, Koltsov at SPEED 99) should eat them alive.

**Their power play is 12 on 122.** Under 10%. We can play aggressive without fearing the penalty kill. The 122 attempts also tells you they draw or take a ton of penalties — 2.9 per game. We should ride the whistles, not avoid contact.

**No line changes. Belfour starts.** The matchups are already right, their blue line is soft from position three down, and our top six has the skill and speed to exploit Witt's puck-handling. The only thing the GM controls here is the forecheck aggression, and the answer to that is "yes, more."

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-15
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-15

Toronto 33-8-1, 73 pts after 45 games.

## Role coverage

**Toughness is the one role with no coverage at all: zero players above 73.** Every other role on this roster is deep enough to contend; this one isn't close, and the coach's flags since December are aimed at exactly this.

**Roberts** at 38 is the closest thing to a power forward with 86 CHKG and 73 TOUG, but he's also the oldest player on the roster with 98 INJU, which means he won't carry the checking load next year either. **Svehla** at 36 has 83 CHKG but 69 TOUG. The two under-30 checkers are **McCabe** (86 CHKG, 73 TOUG, 29) and **Tucker** (83 CHKG, 70 base TOUG, 29). Tucker isn't even lined. That's the entire checking core, and two of four are in their mid-30s with base toughness at 73 or below.

**Sundin** is the only faceoff man above 80. Chlup at 75 is next best, then Roberts at 75. That means three lines lose the draw. Holden at 71 is on the roster but not lined, and 71 doesn't help. For a team playing 45 games already and headed into the playoffs, this is a real liability against centres who win draws at 60%+.

**Kaberle** at 97 ENDU, 90 CLUTCH and 84 ODBI (passing) is sitting unlined. The brief doesn't say why, and that's a coach question. A 26-year-old with that engine and clutch grade is the kind of depth that wins playoff series.

**Spacek** at 19 with 84 PLE and 79 INJU is also unlined. The coach already flagged him for a dressed spot. Development says put him somewhere.

**Aebischer** at 26, 2.62 GAA and .898 SV over 19 starts has made the Belfour question urgent rather than distant. The coverage is fine tonight; the plan is what matters.

## Trajectory

This club is not aging into a cliff on the ice; it is sitting on a contract cliff that renews almost everyone in the same July, and that is the trajectory problem to solve now because the deadline and the summer run into each other.

**The age curve is healthy, not top-heavy.** Fourteen players are 23 or under, eleven more are 24–29, only three sit in the 30–33 bridge, and four are 34+: Belfour (39), Svehla (36), Mogilny (35), Roberts (38). The thin 30–33 band looks like a gap until you read the names behind it, McCabe (29, $3.00M, 48 pts), Afinogenov (25, $4.50M) and Fischer (24, $3.70M) already bridge the jump. The real top-heavy line is money: those four veterans carry $18.30M, and three of them are on one-year deals.

**Belfour is the single biggest lever.** At 39 and $6.50M expiring with CONS 50, he is the most expensive asset on the sheet and the one most worth converting. Aebischer (26, $0.50M) and Tellqvist (25, $0.80M) are both young and expiring and can share the crease now, so trading Belfour for a pick before March frees $6.50M and hands the position to two players you can keep.

**Roberts and Svehla walk for nothing if you wait.** Roberts (38, $2.70M, 54 pts) and Svehla (36, $3.60M, 19 pts) are both expiring and both 35-plus; above-80 or near it, they fit the expiring-asset-for-a-pick mechanic. Moving them with Mogilny's 35-year age in mind thins the 34+ line without touching the 20–23 core.

**The July cluster is the actual cliff.** Seventeen contracts worth $28.60M expire in the same summer, and that group holds Gaborik (22, $1.10M, 67 pts), Richards (24, $1.00M, 50 pts), Nash (20, $1.20M), Kaberle (26, $1.90M) and the rest of the under-23 talent. If they all hit the market together you re-sign them against each other's rising prices. The fix is terms, not money: lock the five on 5–6 years, split the depth across 2–3.

**Chlup is the most urgent single signature.** He is 18, POTE 95, 23 pts in 34 games, on $2.34M with two years left, and still priced like a rookie. A full top-nine season erases that price, so a 5–6 year extension now is the cheapest star lock on the roster.

**The money leaves room.** Payroll $66.97M against revenue $70.20M and profit $25.53M, so there is no profit-driven reason to stand still. The constraint is the renewal wave, not today's payroll.

## Calendar

The deadline is 45 days away and Toronto sit 12 points clear of second place at 73 points; the question is what to buy, what to move before expiry, and how to survive seventeen expiring contracts in the same July.

**Deadline: buy.** The three stacked proposals from the January 14 report are the plan. They don't overlap in assets and net $4.80M in payroll relief if all three land. **Belfour** at $6.50M and 39 years old is the engine: the above-80-expiring mechanic makes him tradeable for a pick, and he must go before March whether or not the Chara deal executes. If OTT won't take the Belfour+R1 for Chara+Havlat, Belfour still moves for a second-rounder on his own. The Kovalchuk and Abid packages fill the top-six scoring and toughness gaps the coach has flagged; the December fallback (Jackman, Sillinger, Sutton) stays as insurance if ATL or OTT go quiet by mid-February.

**Chistov** (LW, 21, $1.10M, 0.33 pts/g in 27 games) is the asset going to ATL for Kovalchuk. He's a pick in the Kovalchuk package; if that deal dies, he's expendable at summer re-signing anyway given the Nash development path. **Holden** (C, 26, $1.20M) goes to PIT for Abid; if PIT decline, Holden is a depth centre who can be re-signed on a cheap two or moved for a late pick in July.

**Safronov** at 23, 3 games, 0 points, morale down 5 to 95: he's already the package-3 piece in the December fallback (Safronov+R4 for Sutton). Execute that fallback or move him somewhere else before March. The coach is right that sitting him further costs nothing but goodwill.

**Summer: stagger the seventeen.** $28.60M expiring at once is the single biggest roster-management problem in front of us. The split:

**5-6 year locks (stars and core, July 2005):** Gaborik (22, $1.10M), Richards (24, $1.00M), Nash (20, $1.20M), Kaberle (26, $1.90M), Upshall (21, $1.20M), Eminger (21, $1.20M), Colaiacovo (21, $1.10M). That's seven deals locking the young core at current rates before their value spikes.

**2-3 year deals (evaluation tier, July 2005):** Alexeev (23, $1.10M), Chistov if not traded, Smirnov (20, $0.40M), Tellqvist (25, $0.80M). Cheap term, re-evaluate in two years.

**Older players on 2 years (July 2005):** Roberts (38, $2.70M), Renberg (32, $2.00M), Svehla (36, $3.60M) if not traded. These three cost $8.30M combined; if any of them go at the deadline for picks, that's money back immediately.

**Goalies:** Aebischer (26, $0.50M, 2.62 GAA, 0.898 SV in 19 starts) re-signs on 3 years at $0.70-0.80M as the clear number one post-Belfour. Tellqvist (25, $0.80M) is the backup or the trade bait; his morale is not flagged so no urgency, but decide before July 1.

**Not renewing / move for value:** Belfour (goes at deadline). Svehla at $3.60M and 36 is the next candidate if his play drops; a 2-year re-sign at $2.50M is the generous case. Renberg at $2.00M and 32 is a rental who should be moved at the deadline if a taker exists, or let walk.

## League scan

The question this scan answers: who across the league fills Toronto's three real gaps (toughness at zero above 73, faceoffs with only Sundin above 80, top-six scoring depth) and sits on a club that will say yes. I ran toughness leaders, faceoff leaders, and high-potential players on losing clubs, then merged against what we already tracked. The result is a board that stacks cleanly without overlapping assets, and one sleeper nobody has flagged yet.

**Ramzi Abid** at 24, 56 pts in 44 GP, 87 TOUG, 87 CHKG, $400K expiring remains the single best value on the board. PIT are 12-21-5 with 14 expiring contracts. He solves toughness and adds a top-nine second-line scorer at the salary of a 13th forward. No change from the January 14 proposal: 3rd rounder plus Holden.

**Marc Savard** is new to this scan and the sleeper of the league scan. He is 27, 89 FACE, 48 pts in 43 GP, $1.00M expiring on ATL (13-24-2, 11 expiring). That grade and that point total at that price solves the faceoff gap and adds secondary scoring in one move. ATL have 11 expiring deals; they are in full rebuild and will deal him. He should go into the ATL conversation alongside Kovalchuk and Heatley as a cheaper add-on or alternative package.

**Mike Cammalleri** at 22 with POTE 98, 27 pts in 23 games (1.17 pts/g pace), 89 SPEE, 88 SHPW, $1.10M expiring is the best young player on a seller. LA are 13-20-5 with 13 expiring. The same LA roster holds **Alexander Frolov** at 22, POTE 96, 40 pts in 34 GP, 86 SPEE, 88 SHPW, $1.10M expiring. A double acquisition from LA fills the top six for the next five years. The December proposal (Holden plus DET 2nd for Cammalleri) should be extended to include Frolov if LA will do both.

**Mark Bell** at 24 is the purest toughness available: 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 90 SPEE, 82 ovr, $900K with two years left. CHI are 12-23-6 but profitable at $24.48M, and two years left means they are not forced. He is the fallback if Chara or Abid stalls. Do not spend a first or second on him.

**Matt Walker** at 24, $500K expiring, 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG on STL (10-24-3, 9 expiring) is absurd value for a checking defenceman. Five points in 33 games confirms he is not an option, but a 7th-pair blueliner who hits everything on a 35-point team is a playoff asset at $500K. This costs a late pick or nothing.

**Joe Nieuwendyk** at 95 FACE, 51 pts in 44 GP is the best faceoff man available by any measure. At 38 and $4.10M expiring on FLA (16-22-4, 18 expiring), he is a pure rental. If we need to win a playoff series in April, he is the answer; if we want him in October, he is not. **Craig Conroy** at 33, 91 FACE, 55 pts in 45 GP, $2.00M expiring on CGY (14-24-6) is the younger, cheaper version at 91 FACE. **Mike Sillinger** at 92 FACE, $1.80M expiring on PHX (16-23-4) is already in the December package. All three solve the same problem at different price and age points.

**Jay Bouwmeester** at 21, POTE 96, 78 ovr, 18 pts in 44 GP, 90 SPEE, $1.20M expiring on FLA (16-22-4, 18 expiring) is the best long-term defenceman available. FLA with 18 expiring deals are in full teardown. A 21-year-old already playing 44 games on a 40-point team with that profile is a franchise blueliner. This would cost a first or second rounder plus a prospect.

The existing three-package stack from January 14 (Belfour+R1 for Chara+Havlat, DET-2nd+Chistov for Kovalchuk, R3+Holden for Abid) still stands as the lead architecture. Savard slots into the ATL conversation at no extra cost. Cammalleri+Frolov is a separate negotiation from LA. Walker is a seventh-day target who costs nothing and should be picked up regardless of what else happens.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: which deadline packages do we propose, what do we give, what do we get, and why does each club across the table say yes. Toronto's gaps are toughness (zero above 73), faceoffs (only Sundin above 80), and top-six scoring depth beyond Gaborik. The board stacks three negotiations that don't overlap on assets, and Belfour's $6.50M expiring contract is the engine that opens the biggest one.

**Belfour** is the single most important decision on this sheet. At 39 with CONS 50, 18 GP, and Aebischer already at 2.62 GAA in 19 starts, he is a rental we are paying $6.50M for. The above-80 expiring mechanic means any club values him for a pick even without wanting him long-term. Giving him with our 1st-rounder converts the biggest liability on the roster into two players who fix two gaps at once.

**Abid** at $400K with 87 TOUG and 87 CHKG on a 56-point pace is the cheapest impact player in the league. PIT at 12-21-5 with 14 expiring deals cannot hold him. Holden is lined nowhere, played zero games, and costs $1.20M. The swap saves $800K and fills the left-side checking slot that the coach has flagged since December.

**Kovalchuk** at 78 points in 41 games, age 21, $1.10M expiring, is the highest-scoring player on a rebuilding club. ATL with 13-24-2 and 11 expiring deals face a choice: re-sign him at $5M+ next year or take a first-round asset plus a 95-potential 21-year-old now. Chistov's 0.33 pts/g in 31 games means the coach is done with him; he is the logical piece to send.

The three packages stack without double-spending: the 1st goes to OTT, the DET 2nd to ATL, the 3rd to PIT. Remaining picks are the TOR 4th and 5th, which leave room for Walker (STL, 95 TOUG, $500K expiring) as a late add-on at nothing.

# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-14

Toronto 32-8-1, 71 pts after 44 games.

## Role coverage

The toughness gap is the only role on this roster with zero players at 80, and it will cost you a series in the spring.

**Roberts** is your best toughness player at 73, and he is 38. McCabe is also 73 at 29. Tucker's displayed 92 TOUG is a form spike over a 70 base grade. Chlup sits at 70. There is no path to an 80 enforcer without a trade.

**Sundin** carries the entire faceoff workload at 90. Chlup is next at 75, Holden at 71, Renberg at 68. One elite draw man at 33, and no internal replacement above 75. This is thin but not fatal in the regular season; it becomes a problem in a playoff series where the opponent targets your second-center draws.

**Checking** is thin at 6 players above 80, and the top two (Roberts 86, Svehla 83) are 38 and 36. Tucker at 83 CHKG is the immediate fix the coach can make by lining him. That gets you to 7 checkers, which is adequate, but the age curve means you need a young replacement within 18 months regardless.

**Scoring, speed, playmaking, stamina** are all deep and young enough. Gaborik 92 SPD at 22, Afinogenov 96 at 25, Nash at 20 going in over Chistov per the coach's report. No acquisition needed in these roles.

**Salo** at 88 scoring and 30 years old sits unlined. If the coach trusts him, he is a fourth-line scorer who costs nothing. He does not fill the grit gap though.

The December package (Sutton, Bell, Bell at 93 TOUG and 24 with two years left) and Chara (88 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 27) both directly address toughness. The coach cannot fix this with internal personnel.

## Trajectory

The cliff is in the top six, not the age shape: the club has the right skeleton, but three of its four best scorers are 33 or older and their production walks this July.

**Age shape is fine.** Fourteen players 23 or under, eleven at 24–29, seven at 30+, four at 34+. That is close to the manual's 5–7 veterans with a young core behind them. The problem is not how old the roster is; it is which old men are carrying the offence.

**Sundin, Mogilny, Roberts** are the cliff. Sundin (33) has 52 points, Mogilny (35) 51, Roberts (38) 51. The only young man among the top four is Gaborik (22, 64 points). Roberts and Belfour are 1-year deals, Svehla (36) is 1-year, Mogilny (35) carries two years and will be 36. The engine of the top six is on a short fuse.

**Sundin** is the one deal I cannot undo and must flag. He is 33 on five years at $8.40M, the single largest long-term lock on an aging body in the building. That contract is fine through his prime years and heavy at 36 and 37. It is the reason the post-Sundin centre (Spezza, 21, or Richards, 24) has to be groomed now, not in 2007.

**The July wall is the dominant threat.** Seventeen contracts worth $28.60M all expire the same summer, and they are the future: Gaborik (64 pts), Richards (47), Nash (30), Kaberle, Upshall, Alexeev, Chistov, Eminger, Colaiacovo, plus the whole crease depth (Aebischer, Tellqvist). Left alone, the entire young core is on the block in one window, at prices set by their best season, all at once.

**Chlup** is the most urgent single renewal. He is 18 on $2.34M and two years left, POTE 95, 23 points in 33 games. Extend him to five or six years before a full top-nine season erases the rookie-window price. This is the cheapest lock on a star the club will ever sign.

**Belfour and the crease** line up for one move. Belfour is 39, $6.50M, one year, CONS 50. Trade him for a pick before March using the above-80 expiring mechanic, not release him in July. That hands the next three seasons to Aebischer (26, $0.50M, 1 year) and Tellqvist (25). Re-sign Aebischer to a term this summer; the guide loses goalies by forgetting, and we have just watched it happen to a good one.

**Money leaves room to add.** Payroll is $66.97M against $68.54M revenue and profit of $26.35M. There is no cap; the only real constraint is profit, and profit is healthy. A deadline buy or a few above-market re-signings fit without straining the books, so the July wall is a discipline problem, not an affordability one.

**Draft capital is the ammunition.** The club holds two first-rounders (its own round-0 plus the DET round-1) and a round 2, 3 and 4. That funds two young expiring sellers for March (the Kovalchuk and Chara tracks), not old rentals. Spend the firsts on players we keep, and keep at least one pick for the next June.

## Calendar

**We are buyers at the deadline.** Toronto sit at 71 points after 44 games, ten clear of second place. The question is not whether to make a move but which one gets us a Cup, and the summer cluster determines whether this window stays open.

**The deadline plan runs on three tracks.** First, trade Belfour before March — he's 39, carries $6.50M on an expiring deal, reads 91 overall, and the above-80-asset mechanic converts him to a draft pick. Aebischer is ready (2.62 GAA, 0.898 SV in 19 starts at $0.50M). Second, close on Thornton or Chara. BOS at 16-19-3 and OTT at 15-21-4 are both confirmed sellers with expiring assets; Thornton (91 ovr, 66 pts/40 GP, $4.00M) is the best available player on a motivated seller. Third, the December package (Mogilny+R2 for Jackman, R3 for Sillinger, Safronov+R4 for Sutton) has been sitting for three weeks without executing. If it dies, that's fine — Thornton fills toughness (82 TOUG) and scoring in one negotiation and is better than Jackman. If those talks fail by late February, fall back to the package as-is.

**Svehla** (D, 36, $3.60M expiring) and **Roberts** (LW, 38, $2.70M expiring) should also be moved before March if any club takes them. Both are above 80 overall-eligible and carry salary that clears with them gone.

**Renberg** (LW, 32, $2.00M) is the same class of player. Let go in July at the latest, or include in a Belfour package to sweeten it.

**The summer re-signing list is the real problem.** Seven players on 5-6 years, four on 2-3, and six released. That staggers the next renewal wave.

**Gaborik** (RW, 22, $1.10M) is the single most important contract on the sheet. Lock 5-6 years immediately. **Richards** (C, 24, $1.00M) and **Nash** (LW, 20, $1.20M, 0.88 pts/g) are the same class. **Kaberle** (D, 26, $1.90M) gets 5-6 years as the top-pairing left defenseman.

**Aebischer** (G, 26, $0.50M) becomes the number one. Lock 3-4 years at a number well below market. **Chlup** already has two years left; extend him to 5-6 before his sophomore season erases his rookie price.

**Eminger** (D, 21, $1.20M) and **Colaiacovo** (D, 21, $1.10M) are both young blueliners. Lock 4-5 years. They fill the depth chart behind Kaberle and prevent the 2007 cluster.

**Upshall** (RW, 21, $1.20M, 0.69 pts/g on 9.7 MPG) is developing. The coach wants him up a line. Lock 3 years — not 5-6 yet, because we need to see him at 12+ MPG before committing long term.

**Holden** (C, 26, $1.20M) stays as third/fourth-line centre on 2-3 years. **Smirnov** (LW, 20, $0.40M) is cheap depth on 2-3 years.

**Let go:** Chistov (LW, 21, 0.33 pts/g in 27 games — the coach already benched him), Alexeev (RW, 23), Tellqvist (G, 25 — redundant once Aebischer starts and Belfour is traded), Svehla, Roberts, Renberg, Belfour.

## League scan

Which players on losing clubs close the toughness gap, the faceoff gap, or add top-six scoring this March, and which clubs are motivated enough to deal. The bottom ten all carry 9 or more expiring contracts; the five worst clubs each have 10 or more. The board is deep.

**Chara** (OTT, D) is the single best player on the board. 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 82 overall, 46 points in 43 games, age 28, $1.70M expiring. OTT at 15-21-4 with 11 expiring deals has no reason to keep him. He closes the toughness gap on his own and adds top-pair offence. No other player addresses both our worst gap and our second-worst in one body.

**Abid** (PIT, LW) is the best value on the board by a wide margin. 86 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 77 overall, 54 points in 43 games at age 25, $400K expiring. PIT at 12-21-5 with 14 expiring deals must sell. He fills toughness and checking while providing 1.26 pts/g secondary scoring. At $400K he is the cheapest impact available.

**Doan** (PHX, RW) fills toughness (84), checking (89), and top-six scoring (39 pts/44 GP) at age 29 with 84 overall. PHX at 16-23-4 with 14 expiring deals and $13.33M profit are sellers. At $2.40M expiring he is a rental, but a rental that makes us better in the top six than anything we have behind Gaborik.

**Komisarek** (MTL, D) is the best keeper target the scan produced. 88 CHKG, 81 TOUG, 92 POTE at age 23 with 52 points in 43 games at $1.10M expiring. MTL at 12-23-4 with 14 expiring deals and $53.20M payroll should be shedding salary. He fills checking and toughness now and has the upside to be a long-term top-pair defenceman.

**Kovalchuk** (ATL, LW) remains the highest-scoring target: 86 overall, 80 points in 42 games at age 22, $1.10M expiring. ATL at 13-23-2 with 11 expiring deals cannot keep both him and Heatley. He does not fill the toughness gap, but 80 points from a 22-year-old is the best scoring addition available anywhere.

**Jackman** (STL, D) is the most underpriced keeper on the board. 86 TOUG, 87 CHKG, 90 SPD at age 24 with 24 points in 42 games, $700K and three years left. STL at 9-24-3 is the worst club in the league. The December package already targets him; this scan confirms he belongs at the top of that package.

**Havlat** (OTT, LW) is the bundle partner for Chara: 86 overall, 61 points in 43 games at age 24, $900K expiring. Two OTT players, one negotiation, toughness and top-six scoring solved simultaneously. OTT has 11 expiring deals; they will sell.

**Bell** (CHI, LW) offers 91 TOUG, 89 CHKG at age 25 on a two-year deal at $900K. CHI at 11-23-6 with 10 expiring deals are sellers, though profitable at $24.96M so they are not desperate. He is a keeper, not a rental, which makes him more valuable than the deadline-only options.

**Belanger** (LA, C) is the faceoff answer. 92 FACE, 69 TOUG, 73 CHKG at age 28, $700K expiring. LA at 13-19-5 with 13 expiring deals. His scoring is negligible (9 pts/43 GP), but he wins draws and is physical, which is exactly what the second centre needs behind Sundin. Cheapest path to the faceoff fix.

**Cammalleri** (LA, RW) remains the highest-potential target at 98 POTE, age 23, $1.10M expiring, 26 points in 22 games. At his healthiest pace that is 1.18 pts/g. LA cannot keep him. A keeper play for the post-Sundin era.

**Bouwmeester** (FLA, D) is the depth defenceman with upside: 96 POTE, 89 SPD, 82 CHKG at age 22 with 31 MPG already, $1.20M expiring. FLA at 16-22-3 carry 18 expiring deals, the most in the league. They must sell, and a 22-year-old with 96 potential on a 31-MPG workload is exactly what a rebuilding FLA club should convert into picks.

## Trade construction

The question is what packages the three identified sellers (OTT, ATL, PIT) would actually accept for the players who close our zero-above-80 toughness gap and add top-six scoring, and what we give from surplus. The answer is two proposals that use different assets and can stack, with a cheap third as insurance.

**Belfour** is the engine of every proposal. At 91 overall, 39 years old, $6.50M, one year left, he qualifies for the above-80 expiring mechanic, meaning he is worth at least a draft pick on his own. Every proposal that moves him helps July because it frees $6.50M from a roster already facing a $28.60M renewal wall.

**Proposal 1 (Chara + Havlat, OTT):** Give Belfour plus our own first-rounder. Get Chara (28, $1.70M expiring, 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 46 pts/43 GP) and Havlat (24, $900K expiring, 86 ovr, 61 pts/43 GP). This is the single move that fills the toughness gap on its own AND adds a top-six winger. OTT at 15-21-4 with 11 expiring deals is in full rebuild; they want picks and salary relief. Belfour gives them a 91-overall stopper they can start behind young defencemen or flip to a contender before March for more picks. The first-rounder is their franchise player. They shed $2.60M in salary. We save $3.90M net and get 107 combined points of production for a rental window.

**Proposal 2 (Kovalchuk, ATL):** Give the DET second-rounder plus Chistov ($1.10M, 21, 1yr, 11 pts/30 GP, 95 POTE, 89 SPEE, being benched by the coach behind Nash). Get Kovalchuk ($1.10M, 22, expiring, 86 ovr, 80 pts/42 GP). ATL cannot keep both him and Heatley. They keep Heatley (base 91 vs Kovalchuk's 89, same salary), take the second-rounder, and get a 21-year-old with 95 potential and elite speed who slots into their own rebuild. Kovalchuk walks in July for nothing if they try to retain both. The risk is ATL re-signs Kovalchuk and the target dies; if that happens, the proposal is moot.

**Proposal 3 (Abid, PIT, fallback):** Give our third-rounder plus Holden ($1.20M, 26, 1yr, 0 GP, 81 POTE, not playing). Get Abid ($400K, 25, expiring, 86 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 77 ovr, 54 pts/43 GP). PIT at 12-21-5 with 14 expiring deals must clear bodies. A 3rd plus a depth forward is adequate return for a 77-overall expiring winger. At $400K, he is the cheapest 86-toughness player in the league.

**Stacking:** Proposals 1 and 2 use different assets (Belfour + 1st vs 2nd + Chistov) and can execute simultaneously. Both landing gives us Chara, Havlat, and Kovalchuk while saving $4.80M in payroll. After both, we still hold the 4th and 5th for a depth piece or keep them for June.

**If nothing lands:** Execute the December package (Mogilny + R2 for Jackman, R3 for Sillinger, Safronov + R4 for Sutton). It nets $2.56M in savings and lifts toughness from 73 to 90/92 via Jackman and Sutton, but it gives up Mogilny's 51 points and uses three lower picks instead of two top ones.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-12
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-12

Toronto 32-7-1, 71 pts after 43 games.

## Role coverage

**Which roles does this roster actually have, and which ones only the trade market can fix?** Toronto's 32-7-1 record covers up the holes, but two roles are genuinely absent from the roster and will be exposed in the playoffs: toughness and faceoffs.

**Toughness is missing, not thin.** Zero players at 80+ in the grade. The ceiling is Roberts at 73 (age 38) and McCabe at 73 (age 29). Tucker's displayed 92 is a form spike over a 70 base, already confirmed. No internal reassignment raises the best available toughness by a single point because the highest base grade on the roster is 73. Every contender Toronto will face in April carries at least one 80+ enforcer; this roster has none.

**Faceoffs are a one-man operation.** Sundin at 90 is the only player above 80, and he is 33. Next best is Chlup at 75 (age 18) and Roberts at 75 (age 38). A 10-point cliff from the first faceoff man to the second means every opposing centre wins the draw against Richards, Chlup, or whoever centres line two. Holden at 71 is not lined either. This is an acquisition gap with a clear internal upgrade path via Chlup's development over two seasons, but not for this spring.

**Checking is thin at the top but fixable tonight.** Six players at 80+, but Tucker (83 CHKG) is not lined. Line him and the count goes to seven. The real problem is age: the top three are Roberts (38), McCabe (29), Svehla (36). Fischer (24) and Upshall (21) are the next wave but cap at 82 and 80. If both Roberts and Svehla slide, the checking group drops to McCabe-led with a ceiling of 86 and only two other bodies. This is a trajectory concern for next season, not this one.

**Kaberle (26, 97 ENDU, 90 CLCH) shows as unlined in every role listing.** If he is genuinely in no unit, that is a 26-year-old blueliner with elite stamina and clutch wasting away. The coach's Jan 8 report does not mention him, so this needs confirming with the coach before any move.

**Scoring, playmaking, speed, stamina, and clutch are all covered** with 8-25 players at 80+ in each. The age transition on scoring is clear: Mogilny (35) and Roberts (38) sit atop two roles, but Gaborik (22), Richards (24), and Afinogenov (25) are the succession and they are already carrying 80+ grades.

**Goalies are covered for now.** Belfour at 91 overall and 2.28 GAA is elite but 39 and expiring at $6.50M. Aebischer (26, 2.62 GAA, 0.898 SV) is ready. The gap is not coverage, it is that both contracts expire in the same July.

## Trajectory

The question this phase answers is whether Toronto are about to fall off a cliff and whether the books let the GM steer around it; the answer is no cliff three seasons out, but a hard two-summer window in which $28.6M of contracts come due and the GM must lock the right players before their prices move.

**The age shape is the right shape with one thin seam.** Fourteen players are 23 or under, eleven are 24–29. That matches the manual's target of 20 young players. The four veterans at 34+ — Belfour (39), Svehla (36), Mogilny (35), Roberts (38) — carry $18.2M and all expire within two years. The seam is the 30–33 bracket: Sundin (33), Salo (30), Renberg (32) are the only three, and Renberg is a scratched 12-game depth piece. When the four veterans leave, the bridge to the 21–25 core is Sundin alone. That is manageable if the 24–29 group holds, and it mostly does: **Afinogenov** is 25 on 4 years at $4.50M with POTE 95, **Fischer** is 24 on 4 years at $3.70M with POTE 90, **McCabe** is 29 on 4 years at $3.00M with POTE 78, **Pilar** is 27 on 4 years at $1.20M with POTE 88. Those four are the bridge. They are locked and they are young enough to carry 2007–08.

**The $28.6M summer is the problem to solve now, not in July.** Seventeen deals carry one year left: Belfour ($6.50M), Svehla ($3.60M), Roberts ($2.70M), Renberg ($2.00M), Kaberle ($1.90M), Nash ($1.20M), Eminger ($1.20M), Holden ($1.20M), Upshall ($1.20M), Colaiacovo ($1.10M), Alexeev ($1.10M), Gaborik ($1.10M), Chistov ($1.10M), Richards ($1.00M), Tellqvist ($0.80M), Aebischer ($0.50M), Smirnov ($0.40M). If all seventeen re-sign at their current prices, Toronto keep $66.97M. If the stars get top-nine production and their prices double, the summer becomes a $50M+ commitment all at once. The fix is staggered locks this month, not a scramble in July.

**Chlup** is the most urgent single contract on the roster and it has two years left, not one. He is 18, POTE 95, $2.34M, 23 points in 32 games. If he finishes the season with a full top-nine line and another 15 points, his extension price moves. Locking him at 5–6 years at his current number is the cheapest star deal the club will ever do. This is more urgent than any of the seventeen, because it is not yet on the deadline clock.

**Belfour** at 39, $6.50M, CONS 50, expiring is the single best lever on the whole roster. Trading him before March removes the largest salary the GM would otherwise face this summer, brings a pick via the above-80 expiring-asset mechanic, and forces the goalie transition to Aebischer (26, $0.50M, 2.62 GAA in 19 starts) and Tellqvist (25, $0.80M) on the GM's schedule instead of July's.

**The money is workable but the margin is thin on payroll.** Revenue is $68.54M, payroll $66.97M, profit $27.17M. Profit is healthy because of TV and prestige income, not because payroll-to-revenue is comfortable. The club can absorb additional salary in a trade — there is no cap — but every dollar added in January is a dollar added against a revenue base that only grows with attendance and prestige. The GM has room to take on salary for a deadline buy, but not to re-sign all seventeen at inflated prices.

**Draft capital is tight.** The December package already commits R2 (for Jackman), R3 (for Sillinger) and R4 (for Sutton), and it has not executed as of January 8. That leaves the own first-rounder and the DET second as free ammunition. Per the guide, a first or second is enough for a deadline rental. The GM has exactly that: one round-one pick to spend on a rental or a keeper, and a second-rounder from Detroit to sweeten.

The three moves that protect the next three seasons, in order: extend Chlup on 5–6 years at his current number before his production erases his price; trade Belfour for a pick before March to cut $6.50M and open the crease; and begin the summer stagger now with Gaborik (22, 62 pts, POTE 90, $1.10M), Richards (24, 46 pts, POTE 88, $1.00M) and Nash (20, 30 pts, POTE 95, $1.20M) on 5–6 year deals while the depth pieces (Holden, Upshall, Chistov, Alexeev, Colaiacovo) go on 2–3 to split the renewal load across two summers.

## Calendar

We are buyers at the deadline, and the plan has to clear 17 expiring contracts by July; those are the two dates that matter and both need decisions now. Toronto sit 32-7-1 with 71 points, 12 clear of second-place Tampa Bay (59) with only 39 games left and eight playoff spots to fill. The club is in a contender's window, so the manual's contending rule applies: buy for need, prefer young players with potential over pure rentals, and spend the cheap draft capital on the way out of expiring value, not on a two-month rental. The deadline is early March, about 48 days away; the summer cluster is the bigger bill.

**Kovalchuk** (ATL, RW, 92, 69 pts in 38 GP, 21, $1.10M expiring) is the best fit for the contending rule: a 21-year-old top scorer on a seller, and ATL is outside the Eastern top ten. He fills the third top-six slot the coach flagged as declining, and his age means he is a keeper, not a rental. Own first-rounder plus Koltsov is the proposed price; acceptance is uncertain.

**Chara** (OTT, D, 80, 45 pts in 41 GP, 88 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 27, $1.70M expiring) is a confirmed seller: OTT are 15-20-4, 10th in the East, 11 expiring deals, rebuild mode. He answers the coach's toughness gap at the blueline, where our true ceiling is 73. Trade before March while his value is at 80, not on a rental deadline.

**Thornton** (BOS, C, 91, 66 pts in 40 GP, 25, $4.00M UFA) is the ceiling target but the weakest yes: Boston are 16-19-3, eighth, possibly still in the race, so the reason-for-selling is thin. Approach only if they engage; do not break the first-rounder for a maybe.

**Belfour** is the cleanest deadline action regardless of the buyer targets. He is 39, $6.50M, 91 overall, expiring, and qualifies for the above-80 expiring-asset mechanic: move him before March for a draft pick rather than releasing him in July and getting nothing. **Aebischer** (26, $0.50M, 2.62 GAA, 0.898 SV over 19 starts) is the successor; re-sign him 2-3 years before July so we never enter the season on a goalies-only gamble.

**The pending December package** (Mogilny+R2 for Jackman, R3 for Sillinger, Safronov+R4 for Sutton) is the fallback. It is unexecuted as of the last read, costs the own first-rounder nothing, and fills exactly what the coach flags: toughness up toward 90 and a 96 faceoff man beside Sundin. Run Kovalchuk and Chara first; if neither club engages by late February, execute the package so the deadline is not wasted.

## The summer: renew the core, move the old, clear the cluster

Seventeen deals worth $28.6M expire at once; renewing them all at one sitting ratchets every price. Split the renewals and stagger them so the cluster never renews in a single July.

**Gaborik** (22, $1.10M), **Richards** (24, $1.00M), **Nash** (20, $1.20M, 0.88 pts/g) and **Kaberle** (26, $1.90M) are the four to lock on 5-6 years now; their rookie-window prices are the asset. **Chlup** (18, $2.34M, two years left, POTE 95) is not expiring this summer but is the most urgent single extension on the sheet, and should not wait for the cluster.

**Colaiacovo** (21, 18.5 MPG when dressed), **Eminger** (21, $1.20M), **Upshall** (21, 0.69 pts/g on 9.7 MPG) and **Smirnov** (20, $0.40M) are the develop-or-keep depth: lock the first three on 3-5 years to get them past restricted, Smirnov on 2-3. **Holden** (26) and **Alexeev** (23) get 2-3 years as cost-controlled middle-nine bodies.

**Let go or move before expiry for value:** **Svehla** (36, $3.60M), **Roberts** (38, $2.70M) and **Renberg** (32, $2.00M) are old, expensive and off the three-year plan; if a seller will take a pick or cheap prospect for them by March, take it, otherwise release and free $8.30M. **Chistov** (21, $1.10M, 0.33 pts/g in 27 GP) is the one young man off the plan, the coach wants him out, so move him for the coach's target (Spacek) or let him walk. **Tellqvist** (25, $0.80M) becomes the Aebischer backup or the trade bait; decide once Aebischer is signed.

## League scan

This phase answers which players on seller clubs fill Toronto's two real gaps (toughness and faceoffs) and which young players on losing clubs are worth a first-rounder for the long term. The shortlist is ranked by the product of grade, contract leverage, and club motivation. The December package remains the priority because it solves both gaps without spending the R1; these targets are what the GM does with the R1 and the DET second on top of it.

**Thornton (BOS, C)** is the best player on the seller board. 94 base overall, 89 TOUG and 90 CHKG displayed, 79 FACE, 25 years old, $4.00M expiring, 70 points in 42 games on 20.7 minutes a night. He fills the toughness ceiling (Toronto's best is 73) and arrives as a second-line centre who could eventually replace Sundin. BOS at 16-19-3 with 13 expiring deals and $24.85M profit are not desperate, but they have no reason to re-sign Thornton at $4M+ when they can't make the playoffs. Acceptance is uncertain; BOS have the payroll to keep him if they want.

**Heatley (ATL, RW)** is the highest-base player on the seller list: 91 base overall, 74 points in 38 games, 23 turning 24 in nine days, $1.10M expiring. ATL at 13-22-2 with 11 expiring deals cannot keep him. He does not fill the toughness gap (75 TOUG displayed), but 91 base on $1.10M is the cheapest elite scoring the market offers. Package with Kovalchuk or take him instead: ATL have two 89-plus base players expiring and will not keep both.

**Chara (OTT, D)** fills toughness at 94 TOUG and 95 CHKG displayed (base overall 85), 27 years old, $1.70M expiring, 45 points in 42 games on 31.0 minutes a night. OTT at 15-20-4 with 11 expiring deals are confirmed sellers. He is a top-pairing defenceman who closes the toughness gap outright. Already confirmed as a target; the December 15 stale read has been corrected.

**Kovalchuk (ATL, LW)** is 89 base, 78 points in 41 games, 21 years old, $1.10M expiring. Does not fill the toughness gap (78 TOUG), but he is a generational scorer on the cheapest expiring deal in the league. ATL's situation means they move him or Heatley or both. If the GM can only take one from ATL, Kovalchuk is younger and Heatley is older but more established. The own first-rounder plus Koltsov remains the proposed package.

**Abid (PIT, LW)** at 79 base, 53 points in 42 games, 24 years old, $0.40M expiring. The displayed 80 TOUG and 80 CHKG have come down from the 87s noted in late December (form has cooled), but even at 80 he is above Toronto's 73 ceiling. At $0.40M and 53 points, he is the best pure value on the board. PIT at 12-21-5 with 14 expiring deals are motivated. Koltsov remains the proposed return.

**Havlat (OTT, LW)** is a new discovery from the expiring-on-sellers scan: 87 base, 61 points in 42 games, 23 years old, $0.90M expiring. OTT at 15-20-4 will not keep him alongside Chara and Lalime expiring. He does not fill the toughness gap (68 TOUG), but 61 points on $0.90M at 23 is the best value-per-salary dollar on the board. He is the natural package partner for a Chara acquisition: take both from OTT in one deal.

**Brad Stuart (SJ, D)** is 87 base, 80 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 25 years old, $1.80M expiring, 35 points in 42 games on 29.8 minutes. SJ at 15-20-4 with 14 expiring deals. He fills the toughness gap at 80 on a top-pairing blueliner. The 80 displayed is below Chara's 94 but above Toronto's ceiling. If the GM wants toughness on defence without paying a first-rounder, Stuart is the secondary option.

**Bell (CHI, LW)** is the most underappreciated target: 80 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, 24 years old, $0.90M, two years left. He fills toughness AND faceoffs simultaneously. CHI at 11-23-6 are the worst team in the league and have 10 expiring deals; they should be open to moving a 24-year-old for future assets. Two years left means they get something back rather than losing him for nothing. His 15 points in 42 games is low, but the grades are the point.

**Belanger (LA, C)** solves the faceoff problem outright: 97 FACE displayed, the highest in the league. 82 base overall, 27 years old, $0.70M expiring. His 9 points in 42 games is low but irrelevant for a fourth-line faceoff specialist. LA at 13-18-5 with 13 expiring deals will move him. A late-round pick gets him.

**Avery (LA, C)** at 79 base, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 93 FACE, 24 years old, $0.40M, two years left. He fills both gaps at $0.40M. The 5 points in 42 games is dreadful but his role is draws and physical play. LA will not fight for a 4C on $0.40M. Two years left is a slight complication versus Belanger (expiring), but the price is right.

**Komisarek (MTL, D)** is the best young defenceman available: 77 base, POTE 91, 52 points in 42 games (7 goals, 45 assists), 23 turning 24 in a week, $1.10M expiring. MTL at 12-23-4 with 14 expiring deals are in full rebuild. He does not fill the toughness gap (76 TOUG), but POTE 91 with a 52-point season at 23 is a franchise blueliner. He is the trajectory target: trade for him now, lock him on 5 years, and the position is solved through 2010.

**Conroy (CGY, C)** is the faceoff rental: 85 base, 94 FACE, 51 points in 42 games, 33 years old, $2.00M expiring. CGY at 13-22-6 with 10 expiring deals. He brings faceoffs and secondary scoring for a playoff push. At 33, this is a one-year solution; Chlup (18, FACE 75, POTE 95) is the long-term answer. A second-rounder gets him.

**Cammalleri (LA, RW)** remains the best keeper target if the GM has a second pick to spare: 79 base, POTE 97, 22 years old, $1.10M expiring, 26 points in 21 games. LA at 13-18-5 cannot keep him. The package is Holden plus the DET second-rounder.

## Trade construction

This phase answers what package Toronto send for each top target, what it costs in payroll, and why the other side's record and balance sheet make them say yes. With the own 1st-rounder and DET's 2nd the only free picks left after the December package claims TOR's 2-3-4, every proposal competes for the same two assets.

**Thornton** is the best fit and the only deal that makes payroll go down. Give Mogilny ($5.50M, 2yr) plus the own 1st-rounder, take Thornton (94 base, 89 TOUG, 70 pts/42 GP, $4.00M expiring, 25). Our payroll drops $1.50M because we sell $5.50M and buy $4.00M. He fills the toughness ceiling (Toronto's best is 73, Thornton is 89) and the centre position, and he replaces one of the three declining top-six forwards the coach flagged. BOS at 16-19-3 with 13 expiring deals and $24.85M profit could re-sign Thornton, but they'd be paying $4M+ for a player on a team going nowhere. A 1st-rounder from a 71-point club plus a 95-overall RW on two years at 51 points is the better business. Mogilny's ACCE 95, PASS 94, and 51 points give BOS two seasons of real offence while they reset.

**Kovalchuk** is the backup if BOS say no. Give Koltsov ($1.10M, 2yr, POTE 94, coach-flagged as surplus) plus the own 1st-rounder, take Kovalchuk (89 base, 78 pts/41 GP, $1.10M expiring, 21). Payroll is unchanged: $1.10M in, $1.10M out. ATL at 13-22-2 with 11 expiring deals cannot keep Kovalchuk on a July walk. Koltsov at 23 with POTE 94, ACCE 96 and AGIL 92 is a speed-forward for their rebuild, and a 1st-rounder from the best team in the league is the best pick ATL will see this year. Heatley (91 base, 74 pts/38 GP, $1.10M expiring, 23) is the swap if ATL signals they're keeping Kovalchuk; ATL won't retain both 89-plus players on expiring deals.

**Komisarek** is the trajectory play, but it competes with Kovalchuk for Koltsov. Give the DET 2nd-rounder plus Koltsov, take Komisarek (77 base, POTE 91, 52 pts/42 GP, 45 assists, $1.10M expiring, 23). Payroll unchanged. MTL at 12-23-4 with 14 expiring deals are in full rebuild; Komisarek walks in July for nothing. They get a 23-year-old winger with POTE 94 on 2 years and a 2nd-rounder from Detroit. Then lock Komisarek on 5 years at a reasonable number and the blueliner position is solved through 2010. This deal is better for 2007-08 than the ATL rental; the GM must choose between tonight's Cup run and the next window.

**Belfour** is the separate sell that should happen regardless of which buy lands. At 91 overall, $6.50M, 39, expiring, he qualifies for the above-80 expiring-asset mechanic and trades for a draft pick. Cutting $6.50M is the largest single payroll reduction available this season and forces the goalie transition to Aebischer (26, $0.50M, 2.62 GAA, 19 starts) on the GM's timeline.

If none of the buy targets land, execute the December package (Jackman for Mogilny+R2, Sillinger for R3, Sutton for Safronov+R4), which fills toughness and faceoffs at low-round picks and has been pending since December 22. Then pursue Belanger (LA, 97 FACE displayed, $0.70M expiring) for a late-round pick and Bell (CHI, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, $0.90M, 2yr) for mid-round picks. Both fill the gap roles at low cost.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-10
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-10

Toronto 32-6-1, 71 pts after 42 games.

## Role coverage

The toughness gap is the only role on this roster where no internal fix exists, and it's the one the coach can't line his way out of. Everything else is either covered or closable by dressing someone.

**Toughness** tops out at 73 (Roberts, McCabe) on stored grades. Tucker's displayed 92 is a form spike over a 70 base, confirmed by development tracking. Six players, none above 73. A team with zero players at 80 toughness in any single role will get out-muscled in a seven-game series. This requires an external acquisition. Chara (OTT, 92 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 27, $1.70M, 1yr) remains the cleanest target if Ottawa are still below .500; Bell (CHI, 93 TOUG, 24, $0.90M, 2yr) is the cheaper fallback.

**Faceoffs** are one-deep. Sundin 90 is the only player above 80. Chlup sits next at 75, and at 18 with POTE 95 he could develop into a second option, but not by March. The gap is real for this season's playoff push. Avery (LA, 94 FACE, 88 TOUG, $0.40M, 2yr) fills both this and the toughness need in one body if the price is a late pick.

**Checking** is covered today: Roberts 86 (38), McCabe 86 (29), Svehla 83 (36), Tucker 83 (29), Fischer 82 (24), Upshall 80 (21). Six bodies is adequate. But Roberts is 38. When he leaves, this drops to four and the ceiling is McCabe's 86. The coach should line Tucker (83 CHKG stored, 70 base TOUG, not currently in a unit) immediately to get a sixth body into games and evaluate whether his engine holds at full minutes.

**Scoring and playmaking** are well-covered now: Mogilny 94, Sundin 92, Gaborik 92, Afinogenov 90 give four 90+ options. The trajectory problem is that Mogilny (35, expiring) and Roberts (38, 90 clutch) carry the top end, and Sundin is 33. Gaborik (22), Richards (24), and Spacek (19, 84 PASS, not lined) are the succession plan. The coach should dress Spacek now per his own flag — at 19 with 0.61 pts/g in 23 games he has earned it, and getting him above 12 MPG is how the transition actually happens.

**Speed** is no issue. Twenty-five players above 80 speed. Gaborik 98 and Afinogenov 96 at 22 and 25 are the best pair on the club and both are under contract.

**Durability** is thin: only three above 80 (Roberts 98 at 38, Afinogenov 95, Fischer 92). This is largely an age problem, not a trade problem, but it means the club needs body count on the bottom pairs. Colaiacovo at 18.5 MPG when dressed should be full-time as the coach says.

**Goalies** are covered with a clean handoff. Belfour at 91-grade and 2.28 GAA is the best goaltender in the league, but he's 39, $6.50M, and expiring. Aebischer (26, $0.50M, 2.62 GAA, 0.898 SV in 19 starts) is ready. The job is to trade Belfour for a pick before March per the standing finding, and re-sign Aebischer before July.

**Salo (88 scoring, 30)** and **Kaberle (90 clutch, 97 stamina, 26)** are on the roster with no unit assignment. Salo at 30 is not a development piece; if the coach won't line him, he's trade bait with 30 games of value. Kaberle at 26 with 97 stamina is the kind of depth player who wins series in late May — the coach should find him a spot on a pair or the penalty kill.

## Trajectory

**Is the club aging into a cliff?** No — the age curve is healthy. The cliff is the contract structure: 17 deals worth $28.60M expire the same July, and the club will either stagger them or lose pieces of the young core to free agency.

**Chlup** is the most urgent single contract action. He is 18, $2.34M, two years remaining, POTE 95, 23 points in 31 games. Two years left means he isn't in the July cluster, but if he plays a full top-nine season and posts 50-60 points, his renewal in 2006 will demand $4-5M+. Extend him to 5-6 years now while the current price still anchors the negotiation. This is cheaper in 2005 than in 2006 and the window is open today.

**Gaborik and Richards** are the two biggest July risks. Gaborik is 22, 61 points in 42 games, $1.10M expiring. Richards is 24, 46 points in 42 games, $1.00M expiring. Both are top-six producers leaving on one-year deals. If they hit free agency untagged, the AI may price them well above what the club can match in a single-summer scramble against 15 other renewals. Lock both on 5-6 years the moment July opens. Nash (20, 30 points, $1.20M) and Upshall (21, 17 points, $1.20M) follow on 5 years. Depth players like Chistov, Smirnov, Holden go on 2-3.

**Belfour** is the single largest payroll lever. 39 years old, $6.50M, expiring, CONS 50. He qualifies for the above-80 expiring-asset mechanic and should be moved by March for a pick, not released in July. Aebischer at $0.50M, 26, 2.62 GAA and .898 SV over 19 starts is the successor. That removes $6.50M of dead weight and opens a pick.

**The old guard walks cleanly.** Svehla (36, $3.60M), Roberts (38, $2.70M), Renberg (32, $2.00M) are all expiring. Let them go. That's $12.30M of salary relief from players the club will not miss. With Belfour moved, total relief from the July cluster's veterans is $18.80M against roughly $12.80M in young-core contracts that need extending at a raise. Net payroll stays flat or drops.

**Mogilny and Sundin** are the only veterans worth keeping. Mogilny at 35 and $5.50M on 2 years is a short-term rental; if the December package with St. Louis executes, he's gone by March and the club saves on re-signing. Sundin at 33 and $8.40M on 5 years is locked through his career. Salo (30, $2.60M, 2 years) and Renberg can be moved or released as depth permits.

**Money is not the constraint.** Payroll $66.97M, revenue $68.54M, profit $27.98M. Total income exceeds payroll by roughly $28M through TV, prestige, and gate. Even re-signing the young core at a 50% raise, the club absorbs it. The constraint is the number of simultaneous negotiations and whether the club can lock the players it needs before the AI-driven market resets.

**Draft capital:** Two first-round picks (own and DET), plus rounds 2-4. The DET first is the deadline ammunition; keep the own first for the June draft. Two firsts is the best trade value on the board and the deadline targets (Kovalchuk at ATL, Abid at PIT) are both worth one first-rounder, not two.

**The three moves that protect 2005-08:**

1. Extend Chlup to 5-6 years now. The price advantage disappears the moment he has a 60-point season.
2. Move Belfour before March. $6.50M freed, a pick gained, the crease handed to Aebischer.
3. Lock Gaborik and Richards on 5-6 years at July opening. These two are the difference between a sustainable top six and a rebuild by 2007.

The age shape is right. The money is there. The risk is a single summer where the club tries to renegotiate 17 players and loses three or four of the ones it cannot afford to replace.

## Calendar

The deadline is 50 days away and the summer cluster is 17 deals and $28.60M landing the same month. The answer is clear on both dates: buy for need in March, lock the young core in July on staggered terms.

**We are buyers.** 32-6-1, 71 points, 14 ahead of second place. The only question is what we add and what we can get for free by moving players we are losing anyway.

**Belfour** (39, $6.50M, 91 ovr, expiring) is the single best value on our own roster. The above-80 expiring mechanic gets a pick for him without giving up a roster player. Aebischer is 26 at 2.62 GAA and 0.898 SV and ready for the number-one job. Trade Belfour at the deadline, not in July.

**Svehla** (36, $3.60M, 85 base, expiring) also qualifies for the above-80 mechanic. The coach wants Colaiacovo (21) on the second pair full-time and has Eminger (21) behind him. Svehla blocks that timeline. Move him for a pick and the young pair inherits the minutes.

**Roberts** (38, $2.70M, 87 base, expiring) is the third above-80 expiring asset. Three picks for three players we lose anyway costs nothing on the ice if the December package brings in Jackman and Sillinger to cover the top-nine minutes. Roberts is the player the coach flags in "post-35 top six."

**The December package** (Mogilny+R2 for Jackman, R3 for Sillinger, Safronov+R4 for Sutton) remains the priority deadline action. It fills toughness from 73 to 90 and adds a 96 faceoff man alongside Sundin at 90, and it does not spend our first-rounder. Execute it in February so the new players have games together before March.
